cards.pattern: People assume there's a much more [X] than there is.
cards.quote: I think people assume that there's a much more detailed semantic understanding of everybody's interests and preferences in the algorithm than there is.
cards.zh: 我覺得大家會以為演算法對每個人的興趣和偏好，有一套比實際上細膩得多的語意理解。
cards.why: 用「people assume... than there is」直接指出集體誤解，但主詞是 people 不是 you，不會讓聽的人覺得被打臉。台灣人常直接說「That's wrong」，這句是資深的替代寫法。
swaps: There's a common misconception that...
People tend to overestimate how much...
cards.pmNote: 破除利害關係人對系統能力的想像，是 PM 對齊期望的第一步。
cards.episode: Adam Mosseri: AI is a tailwind for authenticity

alts.quote: And the reason for that is, I don't think there's any reason to assume that human skill level is the cap on anything.
alts.zh: 原因是：我不覺得有任何理由要假設「人類的能力水準」就是天花板。

alts.quote: I don't think there's any one thing that has happened. I think that a lot of times people ascribe a lot of momentum to a one time change or a single person.
alts.zh: 我不覺得有哪一件事是關鍵。很多時候大家會把一整段動能歸給某一次改動、或某一個人。

alts.quote: Where I've seen people get lost is they assume that if you do that alone, it will work.
alts.zh: 我看過很多人卡住的地方是：他們假設光做這件事就會成功。

cards.pattern: In a world where [前提], it's more important to [主張].
cards.quote: In a world where it's easier to build things, it's more important to make sure that your time is spent figuring out what you should be building in the first place.
cards.zh: 在一個「東西越來越好做」的世界裡，更重要的是先確保你把時間花在想清楚「到底該做什麼」。
cards.why: 「In a world where X, it's more important to Y」把主張架在一個對方已經同意的前提上，聽起來像推論而不是意見。這是矽谷提案最常見的開場結構。
swaps: Now that X is cheap, the bottleneck shifts to Y
As X gets easier, Y becomes the real constraint
cards.pmNote: 「做得出來」不再是瓶頸時，機會判斷 (opportunity assessment) 才是 PM 的核心價值。
cards.episode: Adam Mosseri: AI is a tailwind for authenticity

alts.quote: Most people are missing the most important slide of their presentation. The most important slide of your presentation is the first slide. This slide is going to be presented for the longest period of time.
alts.zh: 大部分人都漏掉了簡報裡最重要的那一頁。你簡報最重要的一頁，是第一頁。因為那一頁會在螢幕上停留最久。

alts.quote: Know that it's coming and make sure you land the plane.
alts.zh: 先知道它一定會來，然後確保你把飛機落好。

alts.quote: There are periods of time where you have to make judgment calls that are not going to be the consensus view. You got to have confidence in your convictions on how to best play the hand.
alts.zh: 有些時期你必須做出不會是主流看法的判斷。你得對自己怎麼打這手牌有信心。

cards.pattern: What's clearly happening is [現象], and [誰] is wrestling with what that means.
cards.quote: What's clearly happening is all of the functions are starting to bleed into each other, and the whole industry's wrestling with what that means.
cards.zh: 很明顯正在發生的是，各個職能開始互相滲透，而整個產業還在摸索這代表什麼。
cards.why: 把「事實」和「解讀」切開講：現象很確定（clearly happening），意義還沒定論（wrestling with）。這讓你既顯得有觀點，又不會把話說死。
swaps: The trend is clear; what it means is still an open question
We can see X happening. What we don't know yet is Y
cards.pmNote: 定義問題時分開「觀察」與「詮釋」，能避免團隊在還沒對齊事實前就吵解法。
cards.episode: Adam Mosseri: AI is a tailwind for authenticity

alts.quote: We can have really good conversations about something that's a year plus from now. And we can have really good conversations about what's happening in weeks. But there's this awkward middle ground.
alts.zh: 我們可以很好地討論一年以後的事，也可以很好地討論接下來幾週的事。但中間那一段就很尷尬。

alts.quote: And the difference between v0 and a lot of other tools is that yes, you do have the code and code is very important, but I call it code last rather than code first.
alts.zh: v0 跟很多工具的差別在於：對，你確實有程式碼，程式碼也很重要，但我把它叫做「程式碼最後」而不是「程式碼優先」。

alts.quote: So we did this recent reorg where now we have what I call the fast thinking group, which officially is called AI platform, but it really means we want to just ship a bunch of new capabilities on a near weekly basis.
alts.zh: 我們最近重組，現在有一個我叫做「快思考小組」的團隊，正式名稱是 AI 平台，但它真正的意思是我們想每週左右就出一批新能力。

cards.pattern: We try to [做法] a bit, but then end up with [結果].
cards.quote: So we try to build a team based on the needs of the work a bit, but then end up with a much smaller core.
cards.zh: 所以我們會盡量照工作本身的需求去組團隊，最後就會收斂成一個小很多的核心。
cards.why: 句尾那個 a bit 是母語者的減壓閥——把「我們照需求組隊」這種可能被質疑的說法先自己打個折，反而更可信。台灣人寫英文常常忘了加這種緩衝詞。
swaps: to some extent
more or less
roughly speaking
cards.pmNote: 團隊編制跟著工作型態走，而不是先定編制再塞工作。
cards.episode: Adam Mosseri: AI is a tailwind for authenticity

alts.quote: So if you take that viewpoint, then pricing needs to sit in the product function. This is my strong-held belief, one that probably won't change now.
alts.zh: 如果你接受那個看法，那定價就必須放在產品這一側。這是我很堅定的信念，大概不會再改了。

alts.quote: Maybe my best advice here is for founders to put themselves in the shoes of investors and just imagine what their life is like and how if you are in their shoes you would make decisions.
alts.zh: 我最好的建議大概是：創辦人去站在投資人的位置上，想像他們的日子長什麼樣、如果換成你會怎麼做決定。

alts.quote: People often think that I get hired into later stage companies because I'm supposed to teach them how to operate like a big company, and in fact, I say I'm hired to remind them they can operate like a startup.
alts.zh: 大家常以為，公司找我去後期階段是要我教他們怎麼像大公司一樣運作；但其實我都說，我是被找去提醒他們，他們還可以像新創一樣運作。

cards.pattern: That is a function of [原因].
cards.quote: And that is a function of you want to have, for anybody who's running code, someone who can review their code and who's familiar with that code base.
cards.zh: 而那是因為：只要有人在寫程式，你就會希望有另一個熟悉那個 codebase 的人能 review 他的程式。
cards.why: 「That's a function of X」比「That's because X」更冷靜、更像在做結構分析。用在解釋現狀成因時，會讓你聽起來像在拆系統而不是找藉口。
swaps: That comes down to...
That's driven by...
That falls out of...
cards.pmNote: 組織設計的限制往往來自協作成本，而非人力預算。
cards.episode: Adam Mosseri: AI is a tailwind for authenticity

alts.quote: I think that becomes a bit of a strategic conversation of do we want to have a better chance of surviving, going after a niche that we know we can serve well?
alts.zh: 我覺得這時候就變成一個策略層級的討論了：我們是要提高存活機率、去打一個我們服務得很好的利基市場嗎？

alts.quote: But what's really interesting is it's not a universal thing. The amount of detail that the team is going to feel helps them is a dial that we can turn that depends on who's on the team.
alts.zh: 但有趣的是，這件事沒有通則。要給多少細節其實是一個可以轉的旋鈕，看團隊裡是誰。

alts.quote: Not all of these variables is created equal and the manager is the most important variable in the environment, because a great manager who is empathetic, who is aware of what's going on, has the ability to move the chess pieces around.
alts.zh: 這幾個變數的份量不一樣，主管是環境裡最關鍵的那一個——因為一個有同理心、狀況清楚的好主管，是有能力幫你把棋子移一移的。

cards.pattern: I don't think we should [X]. I think we should [Y]. That's hard, by the way.
cards.quote: I don't think we should filter out AI content. I think we should let you know if content is AI content or not. That's hard, by the way.
cards.zh: 我不認為我們該把 AI 內容濾掉。我認為該做的是讓你知道這則內容是不是 AI 產的。順帶一提，這很難。
cards.why: 先給明確立場，再補一句 That's hard, by the way 承認執行難度。這種「立場堅定＋誠實承認困難」的組合，比只講立場更有說服力，也預先擋掉了「你講得太簡單」的質疑。
swaps: ...which is easier said than done
...and I'll be the first to say we haven't solved that
cards.pmNote: 主張與可行性分開陳述，是資深 PM 建立信任的方式。
cards.episode: Adam Mosseri: AI is a tailwind for authenticity

alts.quote: So if we can rebuild systems to let the agent be default useful, we'll start unlocking hockey sticks. Unfortunately, I don't think that's going to be binary.
alts.zh: 所以如果我們能把系統重建成讓 agent 預設就有用，成長曲線就會開始往上翹。可惜我不覺得這會是一刀切的事。

alts.quote: So I think it has to come with a place of knowing that you don't know everything and humility to say, "Hey, I need help." And it actually earns you a lot more credit than you think.
alts.zh: 我覺得這要來自一個認知：你不可能什麼都懂，還要有那個謙虛去說「嘿，我需要幫忙」。而且這其實比你想像的更會替你加分。

alts.quote: So those will be custom for anything. And I hate to use the word, it depends because I think whenever consultants say it depends, they're just throwing their hands up and saying, "I don't really know."
alts.zh: 這些每家都不一樣。我很不想講「看情況」，因為顧問一講「看情況」，通常就是兩手一攤說「我其實不知道」。

cards.pattern: The risk you take if you [不做 X] is that [後果]
cards.quote: So the risk you take if you're not telling stories is that you will be forgotten. 100%. You will be forgotten.
cards.zh: 所以你不講故事的風險就是：你會被忘記。百分之百，你一定會被忘記。
cards.why: 把「你應該做 X」翻譯成「不做 X 的風險是什麼」，責任從說話者轉到聽者身上。後面把同一句短短重複一次，是英文口語裡加重語氣的固定手法，中文直譯會覺得囉唆，英文聽起來卻很有份量。
swaps: The downside of not doing this is...
What you're risking here is...
If we don't, what happens is...
cards.pmNote: 提案時講「不做的代價」通常比講「做的好處」更能推動決策——這就是 loss aversion 的實務用法。
cards.episode: How to tell better stories | Matthew Dicks (Storyworthy)

alts.quote: My one piece of advice is when you're early on, your mindset should almost be like you're trying to create a word of mouth machine. If you can get that part right, everything else becomes significantly easier.
alts.zh: 我唯一的建議是：早期你的心態應該是在打造一台「口碑機器」。這件事只要做對，其他所有事都會變得輕鬆很多。

alts.quote: I would argue that the more power you have, the more moral responsibility you have to actually pause and figure out what it is that you're doing.
alts.zh: 我會主張：你握有的權力越大，你就越有道德責任停下來，搞清楚自己在做什麼。

alts.quote: I think with hiring, it's funny, man, there's so much hiring advice online and you read it and you're like, "Yeah, this is super obvious." And then when you live it, you're suddenly like, "Aah, this is why people say this."
alts.zh: 招人這件事很好笑，網路上一堆建議，你看的時候都覺得「這不是廢話嗎」。等你真的經歷過，才會突然懂「喔，原來大家是這個意思」。

cards.pattern: If [對象] isn't [X], they're no longer [Y].
cards.quote: If your audience isn't wondering what you're about to say, they're no longer listening to you.
cards.zh: 如果台下的人沒有在好奇你下一句要講什麼，他們其實已經沒在聽你講話了。
cards.why: 用 if...they're no longer... 把「注意力」這種抽象東西變成一個可以當場檢查的條件。no longer 比 don't 多了時間感——他們本來在聽，是你把他們弄丟的，語氣更狠但不指責。
swaps: The moment they stop wondering, you've lost them.
If they're not asking themselves X, they've checked out.
cards.pmNote: 簡報設計的檢查點：每一頁都該讓聽眾產生下一個問題，而不是結束一個問題。
cards.episode: How to tell better stories | Matthew Dicks (Storyworthy)

alts.quote: I'd say that was the beginning of chapter two where it was we went from the company that could do no wrong to the company that could do no right, which was a big flip.
alts.zh: 我會說那就是第二章的開始——我們從「怎麼做都對」的公司，變成「怎麼做都錯」的公司，整個翻過來。

alts.quote: I often use this analogy of if you're doing a home renovation, you can have the most beautiful rendering of the new bedroom. But if you haven't checked if there's electricity in that wall there or not, it's going to drastically change the cost and the time and everything.
alts.zh: 我常用一個比喻：你在裝修房子，臥室的效果圖可以做得美到不行。但如果你沒去確認那面牆裡到底有沒有電線，成本跟時間都會整個變樣。

alts.quote: You kind of come up thinking you're the protagonist. You can be the protagonist in your life, but in the story of your work of a company, you are probably not the protagonist.
alts.zh: 你一路長大都以為自己是主角。你在自己的人生裡可以是主角，但在公司這個故事裡，你多半不是主角。

cards.pattern: I assume, 100% of the time, that [對自己最不利的前提].
cards.quote: I assume all the time, 100% of the time, that no one wants to hear anything I have to say.
cards.zh: 我永遠都假設——百分之百的場合都假設——沒有人想聽我講任何話。
cards.why: 先自己承認最不利的前提，後面講的方法就不像自我感覺良好，而像是有備而來的專業判斷。這種「先把自己放到最低」的開場，在英文簡報裡是資深講者的標記。
swaps: My default assumption is that nobody's paying attention.
I start from the assumption that I have to earn their attention.
cards.episode: How to tell better stories | Matthew Dicks (Storyworthy)

alts.quote: You really cut out all the parts that make people go dead in the eyes and just say the parts that make their eyes light up.
alts.zh: 你要做的就是把那些讓人眼神死掉的段落全砍掉，只留下讓人眼睛發亮的部分。

alts.quote: So time becomes a convenient excuse for us where we say, 'Well, it's not me. It's just, I don't have time to work on it.'
alts.zh: 時間就變成一個很方便的藉口，我們會說：「不是我的問題，我只是沒時間做這件事。」

alts.quote: You wouldn't want to be in a commercial airplane and hear the tower say to the pilot, 'I'm giving priority to the following three planes on runway five.' Right away, you know there's something wrong.
alts.zh: 你不會希望自己坐在飛機上，聽到塔台跟機師說：「我要給五號跑道上這三架飛機優先權。」你馬上就知道哪裡不對。

cards.pattern: The good news is [X]. The bad news is [同一件事的代價].
cards.quote: The good news is, you're just like everybody else. The bad news is, you're mediocre just like everybody else.
cards.zh: 好消息是，你跟大家一樣；壞消息是，你跟大家一樣平庸。
cards.why: good news / bad news 拿同一件事翻兩面，是英文簡報裡最順手的轉折。厲害的地方在於 bad news 重複了同一組字（just like everybody else），聽眾以為在聽安慰，結果被刺了一下。
swaps: The upside is X. The catch is X.
That's the comfortable part. Here's the uncomfortable part.
cards.episode: How to tell better stories | Matthew Dicks (Storyworthy)

alts.quote: But human beings are notoriously good at trading off the long run just to feel good in the short run. That's why we're all eating chocolate and cupcakes and stuff that we know is bad for us because it feels good.
alts.zh: 人類非常擅長犧牲長期，只為了短期舒服。所以我們才都在吃明知不好的巧克力跟杯子蛋糕。

alts.quote: He thinks that a lot of the best recruiters in the world or the companies that attract talent, they put out this distinctive bad signal and it has to turn some people off. That's the key of a good, bad signal.
alts.zh: 他認為最會吸引人才的公司，都會刻意放出一個「不討喜的訊號」，而且一定要有人被勸退。這才是好的壞訊號的重點。

alts.quote: My one piece of advice is when you're early on, your mindset should almost be like you're trying to create a word of mouth machine. If you can get that part right, everything else becomes significantly easier.
alts.zh: 我唯一的建議是：早期你的心態應該是在打造一台「口碑機器」。這件事只要做對，其他所有事都會變得輕鬆很多。

cards.pattern: To her credit, [她做了 X]（即使那不是我建議的）
cards.quote: And to her credit, she didn't put it in, and it still worked brilliantly.
cards.zh: 而且說句公道話，她確實沒放進去，結果一樣做得很漂亮。
cards.why: to her credit 是在講「她沒照我說的做」之前，先把功勞給對方的緩衝墊。英文商業對話裡要說別人做了不同選擇時，幾乎都會先墊這一句，台灣人多半直接跳到結果。
swaps: To be fair to her,...
In fairness,...
Credit where credit's due,...
cards.episode: How to tell better stories | Matthew Dicks (Storyworthy)

alts.quote: Credit our CEO with this, that I shared the data with him and he basically told the product team, "We are putting a complete freeze on the product development roadmap."
alts.zh: 這件事要歸功給我們執行長：我把數據給他看，他就直接跟產品團隊說「產品路線圖全面凍結」。

alts.quote: Joanne's really special. I got to just take a moment to give her a giant shout out. She is the only person that I've worked with that has as much technical depth as she does have product taste.
alts.zh: Joanne 真的很特別。我一定要停下來大聲說一下她有多厲害——她是我合作過唯一一個技術深度跟產品品味一樣強的人。

alts.quote: Thank you for giving me more of that answer.
alts.zh: 謝謝你願意把那個答案講得更完整。

cards.pattern: It's not because [直覺的解釋]. It's because [真正的原因].
cards.quote: It's not because my life is more interesting. It's because I have a better lens and I understand what to look for.
cards.zh: 不是因為我的生活變得比較精彩，是因為我的鏡頭變好了，我知道該找什麼。
cards.why: 先否定聽眾腦中最順的那個解釋，再給真正原因。這比直接講真因難反駁——因為你已經替對方把反例講過一次了。data review 上解釋數字變化時特別好用。
swaps: That's not down to X. That's down to Y.
The difference isn't X — it's Y.
cards.pmNote: 指標變好時，先排除「大環境變好」這種懶惰歸因，才是可信的成效敘述。
cards.episode: How to tell better stories | Matthew Dicks (Storyworthy)

alts.quote: It's about saying, okay, if we have these themes of stuff that we want to work on, what do we know with confidence because the data tells us and what do we need to understand because we don't have the data?
alts.zh: 重點是要問：在我們想做的這些主題裡，哪些是數據講得夠清楚、我們有把握的？哪些是因為沒數據，所以還得先搞懂的？

alts.quote: And it's not bad because it's not well-intentioned, but it's bad because it's not contextual.
alts.zh: 它不好，不是因為對方沒有善意，而是因為它沒有考慮你的處境。

alts.quote: Well, to be clear about my brand promise, because it's true, every word that has my name on it, I wrote.
alts.zh: 先把我的品牌承諾講清楚：每一個掛我名字的字，都是我寫的。

cards.pattern: People say [常識], and it doesn't. What happens is [真實機制].
cards.quote: People say that time flies and it doesn't. What happens is it goes by unaccounted.
cards.zh: 大家都說時間過得很快，其實不是。真正發生的是：那些日子根本沒被記下來。
cards.why: What happens is... 是把「我不同意」包裝成「我來說明實際上發生什麼」的萬用開關，聽起來像在描述事實，不像在吵架。挑戰團隊共識時，這句比 I disagree 安全太多。
swaps: The usual explanation is X, but what's actually happening is Y.
That's the story we tell ourselves. The mechanism is actually...
cards.pmNote: 拆穿一個團隊共識時，重點不是否定它，而是給出更精確的機制描述。
cards.episode: How to tell better stories | Matthew Dicks (Storyworthy)

alts.quote: It's one thing to say you're spending a lot of time looking outside the building. It's a whole other thing to hear from the places you don't normally hear from.
alts.zh: 說自己花很多時間在公司外面看，是一回事；真的去聽那些你平常聽不到的聲音，完全是另一回事。

alts.quote: We're all sitting talking about it, and Tate says, "It's a low margin reseller, one time sells." "You can say dotcom all you like, it's a low margin reseller."
alts.zh: 大家在車上討論，Tate 說：「它就是個低毛利的經銷商，一次性買賣。你要講幾次『.com』都可以，它還是個低毛利經銷商。」

alts.quote: I challenge it and I say, "First of all, I don't think there's evidence for that. Is there evidence for that? And even if there is, it doesn't really matter."
alts.zh: 我會直接反問：「首先，我不覺得這件事有任何證據。你有證據嗎？就算有好了，其實也不重要。」

cards.pattern: …, which means we're not going to [X]. Instead, we're going to [Y].
cards.quote: speaking with adjacency, which means we're not going to match content to content. Instead, we're going to match theme, meaning or message.
cards.zh: 我把它叫做「鄰近敘事」，意思是我們不去對內容，而是去對主題、意義或訊息。
cards.why: 自創一個名詞後，馬上用 which means 拆解，再用 not... instead... 給出對照。這三步是把一個新概念塞進別人腦袋的標準流程，少任何一步都會被問「所以你到底在說什麼」。
swaps: ...— by which I mean we stop doing X and start doing Y.
The shift here is from X to Y.
cards.pmNote: 新框架要能被團隊複述，必須「命名 → 定義 → 對照舊做法」一次講完。
cards.episode: How to tell better stories | Matthew Dicks (Storyworthy)

alts.quote: Speaking is not a specialized skill, it's a meta skill. That means that the better you get at speaking, the better your life gets.
alts.zh: 說話不是一項專門技能，它是一項後設技能。意思是：你說話越強，你的人生就越好。

alts.quote: I think a lot of people think about markets almost like these bodies of water. And it's like, "Oh, it's this big body of water that we're going after." And I actually think that the most interesting markets, you have to think of them like currents.
alts.zh: 很多人把市場想成一片水域，覺得「喔，我們要去攻的是這一大片水」。但我覺得最有意思的市場，你得把它想成水流。

alts.quote: These are things we're going to do, not goals we're going to achieve. These are things we're going to do, action steps.
alts.zh: 這些是我們要做的事，不是我們要達成的目標。就是要做的事，是行動步驟。

cards.pattern: I'm going to disagree with [某人] a little bit.
cards.quote: So I'm going to disagree with Sedaris a little bit.
cards.zh: 這點我要跟 Sedaris 有一點不一樣的看法。
cards.why: 先宣告「我要小小反對一下」，a little bit 把力道預先調小，聽者有心理準備、對方面子也保住。台灣人不同意時常整段沉默或直接跳結論，缺的就是這句預告。
swaps: I'd push back on that slightly.
I see it a bit differently.
I'm going to take the other side on this one.
cards.episode: How to tell better stories | Matthew Dicks (Storyworthy)

alts.quote: This is maybe going to come across a little bit flippant, but they can't stop you from sending an email technically. So I'm just going to send the email.
alts.zh: 這樣講可能有點輕佻，但嚴格來說他們也不能阻止我寄信。所以我就照寄。

alts.quote: I would soften it a little bit... I wouldn't say I'm not a fan of creating category.
alts.zh: 我會講得軟一點——我不會說我不喜歡做品類（category）這件事。

alts.quote: I'd maybe put it a little bit differently.
alts.zh: 我可能會換一個講法。

cards.pattern: What you're essentially saying is [把對方立場翻譯成更難辯護的版本].
cards.quote: If you don't say yes, what you're essentially saying is, I am so presumptuous that I understand what's on the other side of that door already.
cards.zh: 你如果不答應，你其實等於在說：我狂妄到已經知道那扇門後面是什麼了。
cards.why: 把對方的行為翻譯成一句他自己不會承認的話，是英文辯論裡最有力也最危險的一招。用 essentially 讓它聽起來像整理不像扣帽子——不加這個字就會變成人身攻擊。
swaps: The implicit assumption there is...
What that position commits us to is...
cards.pmNote: 把反對意見還原成它隱含的假設，比逐點反駁更能推進討論。
cards.episode: How to tell better stories | Matthew Dicks (Storyworthy)

alts.quote: To me, I think it's a great accelerant when it's already working, but it can't fix it if people don't want to talk about your product.
alts.zh: 對我來說，那在本來就跑得動的時候是很好的加速器，但如果根本沒人想談論你的產品，它救不了你。

alts.quote: One of the comments was, "Benedict, this is 80 slides of saying we don't know," which is slightly facetious, but also kind of true.
alts.zh: 有人留言說：「Benedict，你這 80 張投影片就是在講『我們不知道』。」講得有點壞，但也算是實話。

alts.quote: I still think that things that we interviewed for in the past, a critical mindset, the ability to really understand deeply the technical nature of a problem is still much more important than whether you're a fully AI native programmer or not.
alts.zh: 我還是認為我們過去在面試裡看的那些東西——批判性的思維、能真正深入理解問題技術本質的能力——遠比你是不是一個完全 AI 原生的工程師重要得多。

cards.pattern: They don't want to [X]. They want to have [X 的完成式].
cards.quote: But that's really not actually what they want. They want to have been funny, because being funny means you must take a risk.
cards.zh: 但那其實不是他們真正想要的。他們想要的是「已經很好笑」這個結果，因為要好笑就得冒險。
cards.why: 用完成式 to have been 把「想要結果」和「願意付代價」切開——一個時態就完成整個洞察，中文得繞好幾句才講得清楚。這是英文裡罕見、但一學就能用的高階招式。
swaps: They want the outcome, not the process.
What they want is to have already done it.
cards.pmNote: 利害關係人說「我要創新」時，往往要的是創新的成果，不是創新的失敗率。
cards.episode: How to tell better stories | Matthew Dicks (Storyworthy)

alts.quote: I really try and stay away from better, because that's really hard to define, and better means something different to everyone.
alts.zh: 我盡量不用「比較好」這個字，因為它很難定義，而且每個人心中的「比較好」都不一樣。

alts.quote: You keep using the word advice, and I just want to, so for anybody who's listening, do not take my advice.
alts.zh: 你一直在用「建議」這個詞，我想借這個機會講一句：不要照我的建議做。

alts.quote: So, I don't really care how high quality the initial MVP is because quality is defined by the customer. And if we don't know who our customer is, we literally don't know what the word quality means.
alts.zh: 所以第一版的 MVP 品質多高，我其實沒那麼在意，因為品質是由客戶定義的。如果我們連客戶是誰都不知道，我們根本不知道「品質」這兩個字是什麼意思。

cards.pattern: People don't [大範圍的問題]. They [精準的小問題].
cards.quote: Most people don't forget their talk. They forget the transitions in their talk.
cards.zh: 大部分人不是忘記整場講稿，是忘記段落之間怎麼接。
cards.why: 用「不是 A，是 A 裡面的某一小塊」把問題縮小到可以動手解決的尺寸，這是 PM 定義問題最常用的收斂句型。而且否定句在前，聽眾會先放下自己的誤判再接收新資訊。
swaps: It's not X that breaks — it's the seam between X and Y.
The failure isn't in A, it's at the handoff.
cards.pmNote: 問題定義得越窄越好解；「使用者流失」不是問題，「第三步驗證後流失」才是。
cards.episode: How to tell better stories | Matthew Dicks (Storyworthy)

alts.quote: And so then the first few pages became very much more problem-based because if people don't understand the problem then they can't understand or care about your solution.
alts.zh: 所以前面幾頁後來就大改成以「問題」為主，因為人如果不懂那個問題，就不可能懂、也不可能在乎你的解法。

alts.quote: I think most people don't like product managers often because they haven't experienced good product managers.
alts.zh: 我覺得多數人不喜歡 PM，多半是因為他們沒遇過真正好的 PM。

alts.quote: I don't know that we even talk about problems without a qualifier. Are we talking about a business problem? Are we talking about a customer problem?
alts.zh: 我們大概不會不加限定詞就講「問題」這兩個字。我們現在講的是商業問題？還是客戶問題？

cards.pattern: That's fine, but [代價].
cards.quote: That's fine, but you're going to need me the next time too. You're going to keep needing me because you're not really becoming a storyteller.
cards.zh: 這樣也行，但下次你還是得找我。你會一直需要我，因為你並沒有真的變成一個會說故事的人。
cards.why: That's fine 先接受對方的選擇，再講出後果——不否定人，只點出代價，讓對方自己重新決定。比 that's wrong 好用一百倍，是英文職場最實用的一句軟釘子。
swaps: That works, but it does mean...
Totally your call — just know that...
cards.pmNote: 擋需求時，把「不行」換成「可以，但代價是」，決策權還給對方，責任也一起還回去。
cards.episode: How to tell better stories | Matthew Dicks (Storyworthy)

alts.quote: You're focused on recent and I'm just going to push back. No, there's nothing terribly recent.
alts.zh: 你一直扣在「最近」這個點上，我要反過來擋一下——沒有，最近沒什麼特別的。

alts.quote: This is a tricky one. So, you're right that it's implied, but the thing is, in real life, if you make a commitment and you get alignment that we are going to spend six weeks of engineering time building this thing…
alts.zh: 這題很麻煩。你說得沒錯，那個確實是言下之意，但問題是，現實裡如果你已經做出承諾、也拿到共識要花六週工程時間……

alts.quote: I don't know that that's how it's going to play out.
alts.zh: 我不確定事情會這樣發展。

cards.pattern: I often say [對現況的一句意象式評語].
cards.quote: I often say most communication in business is round white and flavorless, intentionally so, because a lot of people are afraid to stand out.
cards.zh: 我常說，商業場合的溝通大多是圓的、白的、沒有味道的——而且是故意的，因為大家都怕突出。
cards.why: 用三個感官形容詞（圓的、白的、沒味道）取代 boring，把抽象的批評變成畫面。I often say 則把這句包裝成他的招牌說法，聽眾會直接記住並轉述。
swaps: Most of it is beige.
It's all the same shade of safe.
cards.episode: How to tell better stories | Matthew Dicks (Storyworthy)

alts.quote: I think most people don't like product managers often because they haven't experienced good product managers.
alts.zh: 我覺得多數人不喜歡 PM，多半是因為他們沒遇過真正好的 PM。

alts.quote: To me, I call it candor and not truth because if I march into a room and I say, "Lenny, I'm going to tell you the truth." I'm kind of implying I've got a pipeline to God and you don't know anything.
alts.zh: 對我來說，我叫它「坦率」而不是「真相」，因為如果我走進一個房間說：「Lenny，我要告訴你真相。」我等於在暗示我有一條直通上帝的專線，而你什麼都不懂。

alts.quote: The way I learned how to pitch in business school, and I think the way most people did, is what I call the arrogant doctor.
alts.zh: 我在商學院學到的提案方式——我想大部分人學的也是——就是我說的「傲慢醫生」那一套。

cards.pattern: …is what I call the [自創的名字].
cards.quote: The way I learned how to pitch in business school, and I think the way most people did, is what I call the arrogant doctor.
cards.zh: 我在商學院學到的提案方式——我想大部分人學的也是——就是我說的「傲慢醫生」那一套。
cards.why: 用 what I call 幫一個現象命名，等於把討論的主導權拿到手上：之後大家只能用你的詞來討論這件事。中間插一句 and I think the way most people did，把個人經驗擴大成普遍現象。
swaps: I've started calling this the...
There's a pattern here I label...
cards.pmNote: 替一個反面模式命名，是策略敘事的第一步——Andy 整套方法都建立在「先命名舊遊戲」上。
cards.episode: The power of strategic narrative | Andy Raskin

alts.quote: Then finally I did what I call the cocktail party test, which is to look at the cocktail parties and to watch how people pitch your product to other people.
alts.zh: 最後我做了一件我叫做「雞尾酒會測試」的事——去看那些雞尾酒會，觀察別人怎麼把你的產品推薦給其他人。

alts.quote: The way that I think of Entrepreneur is that it's not even a magazine about business. It's a magazine about thinking.
alts.zh: 我自己是這樣看《Entrepreneur》的：它根本不是一本講商業的雜誌，而是一本講「怎麼想事情」的雜誌。

alts.quote: One of the things that I think when you're doing interviewing, one way to think about it, I call it home court, away court, neutral court, you want interviews to balance in all those different spheres.
alts.zh: 面試的時候有一個思考方式，我把它叫做「主場、客場、中立場」，你會希望面試在這幾個場域之間取得平衡。

cards.pattern: Not to say [對方可能的反駁], but just [你的重點].
cards.quote: Not to say it's not better, but just this is the structure of it, and it kind of sets you up for bragging.
cards.zh: 我不是說它不好，我只是在講它的結構——這個結構會把你逼到一直自誇。
cards.why: 在對方開口反駁之前，先自己把反駁講一次，再把話題拉回自己的重點。這是英文口語裡最常見的 pre-empt，也是台灣人最常漏掉的一步（漏掉就會被打斷）。
swaps: I'm not saying X isn't true — my point is just that...
That's not a knock on X. The issue is the structure.
cards.pmNote: 預先處理反對（pre-mortem）不只在文件裡做，講話時也要一句一句做。
cards.episode: The power of strategic narrative | Andy Raskin

alts.quote: And I always write them back and say like, "Please tell me the better term and popularize it and I'll use it. It's a great idea."
alts.zh: 我都回信說：「請你告訴我更好的講法，然後把它推廣開，我就會改用。這主意很好。」

alts.quote: Sometimes I feel the need to defend that the process is not for process' sake, it's ultimately to help us all move faster and work better.
alts.zh: 有時候我得替流程辯護一下：流程不是為了流程而存在，它最終是要讓大家跑得更快、做得更好。

alts.quote: So they would say, "Oh, your market's not big enough." And I would say, "It's going to be huge." And I'd add a new page in my pitch deck that said how big the market I believe was.
alts.zh: 他們會說：「你的市場不夠大。」我就說：「它會變超大。」然後我就在簡報裡加一頁，講我認為這市場有多大。

cards.pattern: You'd think after [經驗] I'd have [答案] — and I don't.
cards.quote: You'd think, I've been doing this for 10 years, I'd have a very snappy definition of it there, and I don't.
cards.zh: 你會以為我做了十年，應該早就有一句俐落的定義——結果我沒有。
cards.why: 先講出聽眾心裡的期待（You'd think...），再自己承認落差。承認不知道反而顯得誠實又資深，因為你證明了你知道「好答案應該長什麼樣」。
swaps: I still don't have a clean answer for that, and I've been at it a while.
I wish I had a crisper way to put it.
cards.pmNote: 知識誠實：能說出「這題我還沒有好答案」的人，其他答案才可信。
cards.episode: The power of strategic narrative | Andy Raskin

alts.quote: I don't think we should filter out AI content. I think we should let you know if content is AI content or not. That's hard, by the way.
alts.zh: 我不認為我們該把 AI 內容濾掉。我認為該做的是讓你知道這則內容是不是 AI 產的。順帶一提，這很難。

alts.quote: So I think it has to come with a place of knowing that you don't know everything and humility to say, "Hey, I need help." And it actually earns you a lot more credit than you think.
alts.zh: 我覺得這要來自一個認知：你不可能什麼都懂，還要有那個謙虛去說「嘿，我需要幫忙」。而且這其實比你想像的更會替你加分。

alts.quote: So those will be custom for anything. And I hate to use the word, it depends because I think whenever consultants say it depends, they're just throwing their hands up and saying, "I don't really know."
alts.zh: 這些每家都不一樣。我很不想講「看情況」，因為顧問一講「看情況」，通常就是兩手一攤說「我其實不知道」。

cards.pattern: In making it [A], you're losing [B].
cards.quote: And it's hard because in making it compact you're losing completeness.
cards.zh: 這很難，因為你把它壓得越精簡，就越不完整。
cards.why: 把取捨壓成一句 in doing X you're losing Y，不用先鋪陳一大段就能把 trade-off 講清楚。開頭那句 it's hard because 也很關鍵：先承認難，對方才不會以為你沒想過另一面。
swaps: Every bit of X we gain costs us Y.
The price of making it sharper is that it's less accurate.
cards.pmNote: 命名一定會犧牲精確度；策略敘事寧可被說「講得太滿」也不要模糊。
cards.episode: The power of strategic narrative | Andy Raskin

alts.quote: So yeah, no hard and fast rule, but I think it's always you need to have this matrix of options in your mind and be very deliberate about which one you are going with and why.
alts.zh: 沒有什麼鐵則，但你腦中要有一張選項矩陣，而且要很清楚自己選了哪一格、為什麼。

alts.quote: Is it a better outcome to just ship more faster now, but most of the things aren't impactful? Or is it a better outcome to ship fewer things but really work on making sure that you're shipping them in the best way?
alts.zh: 到底哪個結果比較好：現在拚命多出貨，但大部分都沒什麼影響力？還是少做幾件，但每一件都確保做到最好？

alts.quote: There's definitely a trade-off. I think sometimes when companies specialize roles a lot it's because it's more efficient.
alts.zh: 這確實有取捨。公司把角色切得很細，通常是因為那樣比較有效率。

cards.pattern: I would soften it a little bit — I wouldn't say [對方替你下的定論].
cards.quote: I would soften it a little bit... I wouldn't say I'm not a fan of creating category.
cards.zh: 我會講得軟一點——我不會說我不喜歡做品類（category）這件事。
cards.why: 主持人替他把立場講死了，他沒有否認也沒有接受，而是說「我會講得軟一點」再重講一次自己的版本。要修正別人替你下的定論，這是最不傷和氣的做法。
swaps: I'd put it less strongly than that.
That's close, but I'd phrase it differently.
cards.episode: The power of strategic narrative | Andy Raskin

alts.quote: This is maybe going to come across a little bit flippant, but they can't stop you from sending an email technically. So I'm just going to send the email.
alts.zh: 這樣講可能有點輕佻，但嚴格來說他們也不能阻止我寄信。所以我就照寄。

alts.quote: So I'm going to disagree with Sedaris a little bit.
alts.zh: 這點我要跟 Sedaris 有一點不一樣的看法。

alts.quote: And the way Reid records, which I'm not sure I would recommend this, but he does it a little bit differently than you do.
alts.zh: Reid 錄音的方式——我不確定我會推薦這樣做——跟你的做法有點不一樣。

cards.quote: Lenny, are you trying to get me in trouble?
cards.zh: Lenny，你是想害我惹麻煩喔？
cards.why: 被問到會得罪人的問題時，用一句玩笑先把問題的殺傷力拆掉，同時替自己爭取幾秒鐘思考，之後再認真回答。英文會議裡處理尖銳提問的第一動作，通常是幽默而不是防衛。
swaps: You're going to get me in trouble here.
Am I allowed to answer that honestly?
cards.episode: The power of strategic narrative | Andy Raskin

alts.quote: The basic idea is bootstrapping is for lifestyle businesses that want to cash flow. Funding is for companies trying to create a billion dollars in annual revenue. And that answer offends everybody.
alts.zh: 基本想法是：自力經營是給想要現金流的生活型事業，募資是給要做到年營收十億美元的公司。而這個答案會得罪所有人。

alts.quote: Yes and no. It depends on how you define that really.
alts.zh: 算是，也不算。要看你怎麼定義。

alts.quote: Probably going to get slapped for saying all this stuff, by the way.
alts.zh: 順帶一提，我講這些大概會被電。

cards.quote: I mean, I almost see them as orthogonal.
cards.zh: 我幾乎覺得這兩件事是正交的（彼此不衝突、也不互相決定）。
cards.why: orthogonal 一個字就擋掉「所以你是反對 X 嗎」這種二選一的逼問——不是對立，只是不同軸。前面加 I almost 讓語氣不那麼絕對，是理工背景的人在英文會議裡很吃得開的用法。
swaps: Those are two different axes.
They're not in tension — they're just separate questions.
cards.pmNote: 討論策略時分清「互斥」與「正交」，能省掉大量無效爭論。
cards.episode: The power of strategic narrative | Andy Raskin

alts.quote: And that is a function of you want to have, for anybody who's running code, someone who can review their code and who's familiar with that code base.
alts.zh: 而那是因為：只要有人在寫程式，你就會希望有另一個熟悉那個 codebase 的人能 review 他的程式。

alts.quote: I think it's the difference between oversimplification and focusing. You can have a complex problem and be like, "You know what? I need to hold some things constant."
alts.zh: 我覺得差別在於「過度簡化」和「聚焦」。面對複雜問題你可以說：好，我需要先把某些變數固定住。

alts.quote: So before you price discount, think about what value can you exchange to actually justify that price discount.
alts.zh: 所以在你打折之前，先想想你可以「交換」掉什麼價值，來讓這個折扣說得過去。

cards.pattern: I'm really hesitant to [做對方要求的事]. What I'd say is these are [X], not [Y].
cards.quote: I am really hesitant to recommend any template. And what I'd say is these are principles for building it, not any prescribed formula.
cards.zh: 我真的很不願意推薦任何範本。我會說，這些是建構的原則，不是一套規定好的公式。
cards.why: hesitant 把拒絕包裝成「我個人的保留意見」，不是「你的要求不合理」。後半用 X not Y 提供替代品——拒絕時一定要留東西在對方手上，不然對方只會再問一次。
swaps: I'd rather not give you a template — here's the principle instead.
I'm wary of turning this into a checklist.
cards.pmNote: 擋需求的標準結構：拒絕 + 說明為什麼 + 給一個對方拿得走的東西。
cards.episode: The power of strategic narrative | Andy Raskin

alts.quote: So I say no to almost anything that isn’t furthering these priorities.
alts.zh: 所以只要不是在推進這幾個優先事項的，我幾乎都會拒絕。

alts.quote: I don't think it's particularly productive to say, "Well, is it 20% bigger than the internet or 100%?" Those aren't productive conversations.
alts.zh: 去爭「它比網路大 20% 還是 100%」我覺得沒什麼意義，那種對話不會有產出。

alts.quote: I would say wait until it hurts more. If the unfamiliarity is the big problem with it, then maybe the things are fine.
alts.zh: 我會說：等到更痛再來。如果你最大的問題只是「不熟悉」，那可能表示現在其實還好。

cards.pattern: Having [不完美的 X] is a million times more valuable than having [完美的 Y].
cards.quote: So having a shit draft is a million times more valuable than having all these great ideas. But it's also really painful.
cards.zh: 有一份爛草稿，比手上一堆很棒的點子有價值一百萬倍。但那個過程真的很痛。
cards.why: a million times more valuable 這種誇張比較在英文口語是常態、不是失禮；台灣人習慣保守講 is better，力道差很多。後面補一句 but it's also really painful，先認了痛，主張才不像空話。
swaps: A rough draft beats a great idea every time.
One bad version on paper is worth ten good ideas in the room.
cards.pmNote: 先做出可以被批評的東西，團隊才有東西可以收斂；空討論只會累積意見。
cards.episode: The power of strategic narrative | Andy Raskin

alts.quote: Focus is not about what we are doing, it's about what we are not doing. These are the hard decisions.
alts.zh: 專注不是關於我們在做什麼，是關於我們不做什麼。那才是難的決定。

alts.quote: Not having things be your idea I think is really powerful. I just talked to 50 customers who all yelled the same thing.
alts.zh: 讓這件事「不是你的點子」其實非常有力。我剛跟五十個客戶談過，他們全都在吼同一件事。

alts.quote: That sounds cliche. I think a lot of founders and startup people like to talk about the mission, and I get it, and I think it's real. But I really mean it.
alts.zh: 我知道這聽起來很老套。很多創辦人都愛談使命，我懂，我也覺得那是真的。但我是真心這樣講。

cards.quote: I always ask, "What worked? What didn't work?"
cards.zh: 我每次都會問：哪裡有用？哪裡沒用？
cards.why: 固定兩問比 any feedback? 有效太多——問題越窄，回答越具體。而且拆成正反兩題，對方講完好話後幾乎一定會補上壞話，你就拿到真正想要的那一半。
swaps: What landed and what didn't?
What would you keep, what would you cut?
cards.pmNote: 回顧會議（retro）最小可用版本就是這兩題。
cards.episode: The power of strategic narrative | Andy Raskin

alts.quote: You ask questions like, what's the hardest you've ever worked to get something done and why? And that does differentiate a lot of people, a lot of people don't actually have a great answer to that.
alts.zh: 你可以問這種問題：你這輩子為了完成某件事最拚的一次是什麼？為什麼？這題真的很能分辨人，很多人其實答不太出來。

alts.quote: So it's not always the right thing to ask questions, but I would've tried to ask it before I had examined the work when I noticed that he looked uncomfortable himself.
alts.zh: 所以問問題不見得永遠是對的，但我會希望在我檢視他的作品之前就先問——就在我注意到他自己也很不安的那個時候。

alts.quote: What we ask people in general is we say, what do you think? We don't say, what do you know? We often say, what do you think?
alts.zh: 我們一般會問人「你怎麼想？」我們不會問「你知道什麼？」我們最常問的就是「你怎麼想？」

cards.pattern: So put another way, [用白話重講一次].
cards.quote: So put another way, it defines what are the alternatives to what you do? How are you different?
cards.zh: 換個講法：它定義的是——你的替代方案有哪些？你跟它們差在哪？
cards.why: 講完一句比較抽象的定義，馬上 put another way 換白話重講，是英文簡報裡「怕你沒聽懂、但不讓你尷尬」的標準補位動作。比 do you understand? 高明太多。
swaps: In other words,...
Said differently,...
The practical version of that is...
cards.episode: April Dunford on product positioning, segmentation, and optimizing your sales process

alts.quote: And so what I'm hearing is when you come into a project and the way you simplify is you start putting together a doc that describes these things you're talking about...
alts.zh: 所以我聽到的是，你進到一個專案時，你簡化的方式就是先寫一份文件，把你剛講的那些東西寫下來。

alts.quote: I'm not saying that we should not take customer feedback, that's very different.
alts.zh: 我不是說不要聽客戶回饋——那是完全不同的兩件事。

alts.quote: Please note that don't mix transparency and fairness with being predictable. Those are very different things.
alts.zh: 請注意，不要把「透明與公平」跟「可預測」混為一談。這是兩件很不一樣的事。

cards.pattern: This is my long-winded way of [X], but this is the only way I know how to [Y].
cards.quote: This is my long-winded way of doing it, but this is the only way I know how to get positioning done.
cards.zh: 這是我比較囉唆的做法，但這是我唯一知道能把定位做出來的方法。
cards.why: 先自嘲講太長（long-winded），再用 the only way I know 把自嘲翻回權威。謙虛和自信各放一半，是英文裡講自己方法論時最好的比例。
swaps: That was the long version, but it's the version that works.
Sorry, that's a mouthful — but I don't know a shorter route.
cards.episode: April Dunford on product positioning, segmentation, and optimizing your sales process

alts.quote: And I'm now doing stuff that I love, and in some strange way, I guess it even pays better.
alts.zh: 我現在在做我喜歡的事，而且莫名其妙地，好像還賺得更多。

alts.quote: Beyond those cosmetics, the biggest thing I see particularly at higher levels is people talk about what they have done but not why it mattered.
alts.zh: 撇開那些表面功夫，我在比較資深的層級看到最大的問題是：大家只講自己做了什麼，不講那件事為什麼重要。

alts.quote: And I raised my hand and I said, "I'll IC this. I think I know what we need."
alts.zh: 我就舉手說：「這個我自己下去做。我大概知道我們需要什麼。」

cards.pattern: We can't just [某部門] cook up [X] and then heave it over the wall to everybody else.
cards.quote: We can't just have the marketing department sit down and cook up new positioning and then heave it over the wall to everybody else. It's a team sport.
cards.zh: 不能讓行銷部門自己關起門想一套新定位，然後往牆外一丟就沒事了。這是團隊運動。
cards.why: heave it over the wall（丟過牆）是英文職場批評跨部門甩鍋的固定意象，比 didn't communicate well 精準，又因為講的是行為不是人，不會變成點名。收尾 It's a team sport 給出正面替代。
swaps: throw it over the fence
hand it off and walk away
cards.pmNote: 定位／策略要能落地，marketing、product、sales、CS 必須在同一個房間裡產出，不是收文件。
cards.episode: April Dunford on product positioning, segmentation, and optimizing your sales process

alts.quote: It's like we heard you and then we parse them into these 10 and everybody agreed with these 10 and therefore that's why we came up with this solution.
alts.zh: 人最在意的是知道你有聽進去。「你這個願景是怎麼來的？」這種質疑就消失了——我們聽了大家的意見，收斂成這 10 條，而且大家都同意。

alts.quote: Or if the meeting is not under the context of buying it all, it's like, "We're working on something cool. We have a great vision. It aligns with what you're doing. Maybe there's a partnership here."
alts.zh: 或者那場會根本不是在談收購，而是：「我們在做一件很酷的事，我們有很好的願景，跟你們在做的方向對得上。也許這裡有合作的空間。」

alts.quote: He's just got to sit in meetings you are, quiet, observe, just by observing you, he will be a rockstar. No stress, nothing to give.
alts.zh: 他只要坐在你會出席的會議裡，安靜、看就好，光是看你怎麼做他就會變很強。你完全不用出力，也不用有壓力。

cards.pattern: I need to put a stake in the ground and say [暫定結論].
cards.quote: So I need to be able to put a stake in the ground and say, "I got to beat all that in order to win a deal."
cards.zh: 所以我得先釘一根樁，說：我必須打贏這些，才拿得到這筆生意。
cards.why: put a stake in the ground＝先立一個暫定結論好往下走，隱含「之後可以再改」。討論卡住時用它推進，比 let's decide 少壓力、比 let's discuss more 有進展。
swaps: Let's take a position on this for now.
I'll commit to an answer so we can move.
cards.pmNote: 定位第一步不是講自己多好，是先定義「我們要打敗誰」——包含 status quo（客戶什麼都不換）。
cards.episode: April Dunford on product positioning, segmentation, and optimizing your sales process

alts.quote: So there's, I wouldn't say a checklist, but there's a series of questions that I asked to diagnose why is growth slowing in this order, because it's one of these things where the first one that's a problem, if you don't fix that, it doesn't matter if you fix one of the ones below.
alts.zh: 我不會說那是一張檢查清單，但我確實有一組問題，會照順序問下去診斷成長為什麼變慢——因為只要最前面那個沒修，後面修再多都沒用。

alts.quote: The way to summarize that is if you look at all the startup stories that we have at YC and all the companies we funded over all the years, the underlying theme is that rationally the founder should have given up at some point.
alts.zh: 要總結的話：如果你看 YC 所有的創業故事、這些年投的所有公司，底下共通的主題是——照理性判斷，創辦人早就該在某個時間點放棄了。

alts.quote: I just felt this pull, of this huge interest of people caring about this. The point was, I was able to double down on this pull.
alts.zh: 我就感覺到一股拉力——一大群人真的在乎這件事。重點是，我有辦法對這股拉力加碼。

cards.pattern: So it works like this. I start with [第一步]…
cards.quote: Yeah. So it works like this. I start with competitive alternatives.
cards.zh: 對，運作方式是這樣：我從「競爭替代方案」開始。
cards.why: So it works like this. 是講框架前的一句路標，聽眾一聽就知道接下來是有順序的清單，注意力會自動排隊。沒有這句，同樣的內容會被聽成一團。
swaps: Here's how it goes.
The sequence is this:
Let me walk you through it in order.
cards.episode: April Dunford on product positioning, segmentation, and optimizing your sales process

alts.quote: So maybe this is a way to come back to your question about what's the output of the shaping session, it's like it's shaped if we can give this to a technical person and they say, "Yeah, I know what to go build now."
alts.zh: 所以回到你剛剛問的「shaping session 的產出是什麼」：判準是——把它交給一個技術的人，他會說「好，我知道要蓋什麼了」。

alts.quote: Let me just try to summarize what you shared, this five step framework.
alts.zh: 我試著把你剛剛講的整理一下，這個五步驟的框架。

alts.quote: Here's what I heard from all of you. I'm listening, I hear this and here's what I want to do about it.
alts.zh: 以下是我從各位那裡聽到的。我有在聽，我聽到了，接下來我打算這樣做。

cards.quote: So for positioning work, I'm going to say something that is contentious, but I don't think it is at all.
cards.zh: 講到定位這件事，我要說一句大家可能覺得很有爭議的話——但我完全不覺得有爭議。
cards.why: 先預告「我要講有爭議的話」，聽眾會坐正；後半又補「但我不覺得該有爭議」，等於同時立了場、也留了退路。這種一句話兩層的操作，是英文裡拋出強觀點的高階做法。
swaps: This might be an unpopular opinion, but I'd defend it.
Hot take, though I don't think it should be.
cards.episode: April Dunford on product positioning, segmentation, and optimizing your sales process

alts.quote: Now, I'm biased when I'm going to say this, so take this with a pinch of salt, but I think the Accordion Method might be one of the things I'm the most proud of in my entire life.
alts.zh: 我要講的這件事我是有偏見的，所以你打個折聽——但我覺得手風琴法可能是我這輩子最引以為傲的東西之一。

alts.quote: I'm going to tell my boss, on Monday, that I think we should do that. I'm going to use a little social capital and say we should do this.
alts.zh: 我禮拜一會跟我主管講，我覺得這個該做。我會動用一點我的政治額度，去替它說話。

alts.quote: You don't have to do the thing I'm asking, but it is something that I would do if I were you, or at least I would consider if I were you.
alts.zh: 你不一定要照我說的做，但如果我是你，我會做這件事——至少會認真考慮。

cards.quote: Yes and no. It depends on how you define that really.
cards.zh: 算是，也不算。要看你怎麼定義。
cards.why: 對方用一句話把你歸類時，Yes and no 既不吵架也不照單全收，接著把球丟回去要求先定義用詞，主導權就回來了。短、好背、幾乎萬用。
swaps: Sort of — depends what you mean by that.
Both, actually. Define X first.
cards.episode: April Dunford on product positioning, segmentation, and optimizing your sales process

alts.quote: Yes, there are nuances. But for the most part, you get from most... Zero to 10, you can get to step eight by just doing the best practices.
alts.zh: 對，是有很多細節。但大多數情況下，從 0 到 10，你光靠基本功就能走到第 8。

alts.quote: And yes, there's certainly a tax or things we have to do now as a publicly traded company that we didn't have to do as a privately traded company. But there are actually benefits.
alts.zh: 而且沒錯，身為上市公司確實有一些「稅」、一些我們以前不用做的事。但其實也是有好處的。

alts.quote: I remember somebody on social media said the problem with Benedict is his answer to everything is it depends. It's like, yeah, it does. It depends.
alts.zh: 我記得有人在社群上說：Benedict 的問題就是他對什麼都回答「看情況」。呃，本來就是啊。就是看情況。

cards.pattern: I think it is an utter waste of time to [X].
cards.quote: So I think it is an utter waste of time for marketing to build these stupid little one pager persona things.
cards.zh: 所以我覺得行銷花時間做那些一頁式的 persona 小卡，根本是浪費時間。
cards.why: utter waste of time 是重砲，但前面加 I think 就還在「意見」的範圍內。英文允許用很強的形容詞表達立場，中文直譯會顯得太衝——關鍵是那個 I think 的免責前綴。
swaps: I think that's effort we're throwing away.
Honestly, I'd cut that entirely.
cards.pmNote: B2B 真正要吃透的只有 champion 那一個 persona，其他人的卡片多半是自我安慰。
cards.episode: April Dunford on product positioning, segmentation, and optimizing your sales process

alts.quote: It's funny that everyone complained about Google as this really, really smart, all-knowing LLM, and at the same time, they think they're dumb enough to fall for these guest posts.
alts.zh: 很好笑的是，大家一邊抱怨 Google 是那種超級聰明、什麼都知道的 LLM，一邊又覺得它笨到會被這些客座文章騙過去。

alts.quote: I think sometimes people think that craft is about perfecting things and perfecting them in a very organized way or very early on. The downside with this perfection mindset is that it can be sometimes hard to put anything out because nothing is ever fully perfect.
alts.zh: 大家常以為所謂「工藝」就是把東西做到完美，而且要很有條理、很早就開始做。這種完美心態的代價是：你可能什麼都出不了貨，因為沒有東西是真正完美的。

alts.quote: I think maybe on the flip side of less positive is what it definitely learned is most of the time you hear it's really complex, it isn't. Leadership's just weak.
alts.zh: 我確實學到的是：多數時候你聽到「這件事很複雜」，其實它不複雜。只是領導層軟弱而已。

cards.quote: I can then translate those capabilities into value, the so what for the customer.
cards.zh: 然後我把這些能力翻譯成價值，也就是對客戶來說的「所以呢」。
cards.why: the so what 被當名詞用（那個「所以呢」），一個詞就代表「這件事對客戶到底有什麼意義」。商業英語裡高頻，但台灣人幾乎不會主動講，聽到也常聽不出是名詞。
swaps: What's the so-what here?
the payoff for the customer
why they'd care
cards.pmNote: 功能 → 價值的轉換：每個 feature 後面都要問一次 so what，問不出來就別寫進簡報。
cards.episode: April Dunford on product positioning, segmentation, and optimizing your sales process

alts.quote: As an entrepreneur, a company, you actually don't have a choice whether you'll have a pricing conversation with your customer. The only thing in your control is when you will have it.
alts.zh: 身為創業者或公司，你其實沒有「要不要跟客戶談價格」的選擇權。你唯一能控制的是「什麼時候談」。

alts.quote: So I think if you take all those steps back and you look at this from a journey perspective, there's no way that it won't be impacting search. It's just going to be hard to find.
alts.zh: 所以我覺得，只要你退開幾步、用「使用者旅程」的角度看，它不可能不影響搜尋。只是那個影響很難被指認出來。

alts.quote: Intrinsically strategy has no business value. It's basically a document with a few words. And I think it starts accumulating value as you generate business impact and results.
alts.zh: 策略本身沒有任何商業價值。它就是一份寫了幾個字的文件。它是在你做出business impact 之後，才開始累積價值的。

cards.pattern: Better how? You've got to be able to articulate [模糊的字].
cards.quote: But better how? You got to be able to articulate better.
cards.zh: 但「比較好」是好在哪？你得有辦法把「比較好」講清楚。
cards.why: 兩個字的反問 Better how? 就逼對方把模糊形容詞拆開，比 Could you elaborate? 有力得多，而且完全不失禮。articulate 這個動詞（把某個感覺講成可說明的東西）也很值得學。
swaps: Faster how?
Better in what way, exactly?
Can you make that concrete?
cards.pmNote: 會議上遇到「更好／更快／更彈性」這類形容詞，先問 how，再談要不要做。
cards.episode: April Dunford on product positioning, segmentation, and optimizing your sales process

alts.quote: How do we know there's an ROI to a better design here?
alts.zh: 我們怎麼知道在這裡做更好的設計是有投報率的？

alts.quote: I really try and stay away from better, because that's really hard to define, and better means something different to everyone.
alts.zh: 我盡量不用「比較好」這個字，因為它很難定義，而且每個人心中的「比較好」都不一樣。

alts.quote: Your belief is that if we add buy now pay later, a lot more people will be able to buy and transact, and so it's going to pay off. Do I have that right?
alts.zh: 你的認定是：只要我們加了先買後付，會有更多人買得下去、成交量會上來，所以這筆投資划得來。我這樣理解對嗎？

cards.pattern: What matters is [真正的判準].
cards.quote: What matters is, does it resonate for your buyers?
cards.zh: 真正重要的是：它能不能打中你的買家？
cards.why: What matters is... 一句話把離題的討論拉回判準；後面直接接一個問句，等於順手給了對方檢查方式。開會發散時最省力的收斂工具。
swaps: The only question that matters here is...
What we should be judging this on is...
cards.episode: April Dunford on product positioning, segmentation, and optimizing your sales process

alts.quote: Most people don't forget their talk. They forget the transitions in their talk.
alts.zh: 大部分人不是忘記整場講稿，是忘記段落之間怎麼接。

alts.quote: Everyone that I know says they have a bottom of funnel problem. It's never a bottom of funnel problem. It's a top of funnel problem.
alts.zh: 我認識的每個人都說自己是漏斗底部有問題。從來都不是漏斗底部的問題，是漏斗頂端的問題。

alts.quote: The way I think about this is that emotions are like a tube, let's say, and there's water moving through the tube.
alts.zh: 我自己是這樣想這件事的：情緒像一根管子，裡面有水在流。

cards.pattern: The true test of whether [X] is working is [具體場景]. That's the real test.
cards.quote: The true test of whether the positioning's working is, if I'm sitting across from a qualified prospect and I tell the story, does the prospect get excited and want to buy something?
cards.zh: 定位有沒有效，真正的檢驗是：我坐在一個合格的潛在客戶對面把故事講完，他會不會眼睛一亮、想買東西？
cards.why: The true test of X is... 用來否定一堆假指標、只立一個真指標，是資深者在會議上收斂爭論的招牌句。而且他給的是一個場景不是一個數字——當沒有好指標時，這是誠實又有力的替代。
swaps: The real test is whether...
If you want one signal, it's this one:
cards.pmNote: 沒有好量測時，用一個可重現的場景當判準，好過硬湊一個假指標。
cards.episode: April Dunford on product positioning, segmentation, and optimizing your sales process

alts.quote: If you tell someone, 'This is the problem I'm going to address,' and they will tell you, 'Oh, I know someone that has this problem,' it's not a real problem.
alts.zh: 如果你跟人說「這是我要解決的問題」，對方回你「喔，我知道有誰有這個問題」——那它就不是真問題。

alts.quote: The test for me, of whether you're building a product that has the ingredients to create a retentive product on a micro level, just at the user level, is that the product should get better the more you use it, and you'll have more to lose by leaving it.
alts.zh: 我判斷一個產品有沒有留存體質的標準是：用得越多它越好用，而且你越難離開它。

alts.quote: I want to be clear that I had seen that idea somewhere else, someone else, a blog post about it or something like that.
alts.zh: 我想講清楚，那個點子我是在別的地方看到的，是別人寫的一篇部落格之類的。

cards.quote: And so here's where I think we go off the rails in marketing.
cards.zh: 而我覺得行銷就是在這一步脫軌的。
cards.why: go off the rails（脫軌）加上 here's where，精準指出是「哪一步」出錯，不是整件事全盤否定。批評一旦有座標，就不像人身攻擊；而且用 we 不用 you，責任共同承擔。
swaps: This is the step where it breaks down.
Here's where I think we lose the plot.
cards.episode: April Dunford on product positioning, segmentation, and optimizing your sales process

alts.quote: And I honestly think saying, "You are not doing a good job," is much kinder than, "I think you can improve on this aspect or that aspect."
alts.zh: 老實說我覺得直接講「你做得不夠好」，其實比「我覺得你在某某方面可以再進步」還要仁慈。

alts.quote: And I think the error that people make more often than not is they are actually too stuck on their own product vision. That's the mistake I've seen a little bit more actually than the other way around.
alts.zh: 我覺得大家最常犯的錯，是太黏著自己原本的產品願景。這個錯我看到的，其實比反過來的那種多一點。

alts.quote: Hey, here's what I'm seeing and tell me what's going on for you.
alts.zh: 我先講我這邊看到的狀況，然後換你講講你那邊發生了什麼事。

cards.pattern: At that stage, what you've got is a [X] thesis.
cards.quote: At that stage, what I think you've got is a positioning thesis... But it's just a thesis.
cards.zh: 在那個階段，你手上有的其實是一個「定位假設」……但它就只是個假設。
cards.why: 把還沒驗證的判斷叫 a thesis 而不是 a decision，一個字就標示了不確定的程度，之後改變主意也不算打臉。這是英文裡管理期望最省力的做法：先幫自己的結論標好熟度。
swaps: Treat that as a working hypothesis.
That's our current best guess, not a decision.
cards.pmNote: 早期定位刻意留鬆，讓市場把你拉向你沒想到的客群（April 的漁網比喻）。
cards.episode: April Dunford on product positioning, segmentation, and optimizing your sales process

alts.quote: I think this is a nuanced question and it's hard for me to say something on a podcast that'll actually be useful to people, but here's a couple of thoughts.
alts.zh: 我覺得這是個很有層次的問題，要在 podcast 上講出真的對別人有用的東西很難，不過我有幾個想法。

alts.quote: I mean, look, I don't know that it's a perfect answer, but I think the reality is just that what kills most projects most early companies is stamina.
alts.zh: 我是說，我不確定這是不是完美的答案，但我覺得現實就是：殺死大多數專案、大多數早期公司的，是續航力。

alts.quote: Now, to be clear, this is hard for me. I think it's hard for everybody.
alts.zh: 先講清楚，這件事對我來說也很難。我覺得對每個人都很難。

cards.pattern: A lot of [某群人] get tripped up because they're taking [不適用的建議].
cards.quote: A lot of early stage founders get tripped up as they're taking late stage sales advice.
cards.zh: 很多早期創辦人會踩坑，是因為他們套用了後期階段的銷售建議。
cards.why: get tripped up 把「做錯」講成「被絆倒」，責任落在建議來源、不落在人身上。要指出別人做錯又不想傷人時，這個被動意象非常好用。
swaps: That's where people usually come unstuck.
A lot of teams trip over this.
cards.pmNote: 引用最佳實務前先問：這是哪個階段、哪種規模的公司驗證出來的？
cards.episode: "Sell the alpha, not the feature": The enterprise sales playbook for $1M to $10M ARR | Jen Abel

alts.quote: Here's the mistake that 99% of founders and sales reps make. We're not really selling in B2B, we're solving problems.
alts.zh: 99% 的創辦人跟業務都犯同一個錯。B2B 我們其實不是在賣東西，是在解問題。

alts.quote: And so the anti-pattern I see is there are lots of founders that are very familiar with your awesome work.
alts.zh: 所以我常看到的反模式是：很多創辦人非常熟你那些很棒的內容（然後在錯的階段照做）。

alts.quote: And so I think a lot of it comes down to not the things you try, but how you deeply understand the problem that's preventing someone from using your product effectively.
alts.zh: 所以我覺得關鍵不在你試了哪些招，而在你有多深地搞懂「是什麼擋住使用者用好你的產品」。

cards.pattern: I try and stay away from [某個字], because it's hard to define.
cards.quote: I really try and stay away from better, because that's really hard to define, and better means something different to everyone.
cards.zh: 我盡量不用「比較好」這個字，因為它很難定義，而且每個人心中的「比較好」都不一樣。
cards.why: 把異議指向「用詞」而不是「人」，是會議上要擋掉含糊字眼時最安全的做法。I try and stay away from 又是個人習慣的講法，聽起來像分享而不是糾正。
swaps: I'd avoid the word X here.
I've stopped using that word because it doesn't survive follow-up questions.
cards.pmNote: 定位不要說「更好」，要說「不一樣」——better 會被要求定義、被要求量測，然後被拖一年。
cards.episode: "Sell the alpha, not the feature": The enterprise sales playbook for $1M to $10M ARR | Jen Abel

alts.quote: But that's really not actually what they want. They want to have been funny, because being funny means you must take a risk.
alts.zh: 但那其實不是他們真正想要的。他們想要的是「已經很好笑」這個結果，因為要好笑就得冒險。

alts.quote: So, I don't really care how high quality the initial MVP is because quality is defined by the customer. And if we don't know who our customer is, we literally don't know what the word quality means.
alts.zh: 所以第一版的 MVP 品質多高，我其實沒那麼在意，因為品質是由客戶定義的。如果我們連客戶是誰都不知道，我們根本不知道「品質」這兩個字是什麼意思。

alts.quote: They would write principles such as move fast and I would always be, "Everyone likes to move fast." It is not a good principle actually because nobody can really disagree with this reasonably.
alts.zh: 他們會寫「快速行動」這種原則，我都會回：誰不喜歡快速行動？那其實不是好的原則，因為沒有人會合理地反對它。

cards.quote: The only thing that's different is the insight that the founder has on the market, which is a hard pill to swallow. And I know that's hard to hear too.
cards.zh: 唯一的差別是創辦人對市場的洞察——這顆藥很難吞。我也知道這話很難聽。
cards.why: 講完刺耳的結論，立刻承認「這很難接受」，等於先把對方的防衛心說出來。比 sorry to say this 高一階：它不是道歉，是同理，結論一點都沒有收回。
swaps: I know that's not what anyone wants to hear.
That one stings, and I don't have a nicer version of it.
cards.pmNote: 轉換率低通常不是通路問題，是「你講的事情不夠有趣」——這是最難承認的診斷。
cards.episode: "Sell the alpha, not the feature": The enterprise sales playbook for $1M to $10M ARR | Jen Abel

alts.quote: And I think the error that people make more often than not is they are actually too stuck on their own product vision. That's the mistake I've seen a little bit more actually than the other way around.
alts.zh: 我覺得大家最常犯的錯，是太黏著自己原本的產品願景。這個錯我看到的，其實比反過來的那種多一點。

alts.quote: This is how we think about things. This is how we handle this type of behavior here. If that's hard for you, let's find you another job.
alts.zh: 我們就是這樣想事情的。這種狀況我們在這裡就是這樣處理的。如果你覺得很難接受，那我們一起幫你找個別的工作。

alts.quote: And one thing that I noticed, a lot of people just don't know what you built.
alts.zh: 我注意到一件事：很多人根本不知道你做了什麼。

cards.pattern: There's this thing in my head, I haven't fully validated it, but I'm going to share it with you.
cards.quote: There's this thing in my head and I haven't fully validated it but I'm going to share it with you.
cards.zh: 我腦中有個想法，還沒完全驗證過，但我還是講給你聽。
cards.why: 先幫想法標好成熟度（還沒驗證），就能大膽拋半成品又不用負全責。矽谷會議的常態，台灣人多半覺得「沒想清楚不要講」而錯過整個討論。
swaps: This is half-baked, but bear with me.
I don't have data on this yet — just a pattern I keep seeing.
I don't know, it's just a thought.
cards.pmNote: 把未驗證的觀察講出來，團隊才有機會幫你驗證；憋著就只是你一個人的直覺。
cards.episode: "Sell the alpha, not the feature": The enterprise sales playbook for $1M to $10M ARR | Jen Abel

alts.quote: I'm going to make a bold statement here. There is no such thing as a long feedback loop.
alts.zh: 我要講一句很大膽的話：世界上沒有「很長的回饋迴圈」這種東西。

alts.quote: You don't have to do the thing I'm asking, but it is something that I would do if I were you, or at least I would consider if I were you.
alts.zh: 你不一定要照我說的做，但如果我是你，我會做這件事——至少會認真考慮。

alts.quote: So for positioning work, I'm going to say something that is contentious, but I don't think it is at all.
alts.zh: 講到定位這件事，我要說一句大家可能覺得很有爭議的話——但我完全不覺得有爭議。

cards.pattern: Probably going to get slapped for saying this, by the way.
cards.quote: Probably going to get slapped for saying all this stuff, by the way.
cards.zh: 順帶一提，我講這些大概會被電。
cards.why: 講完不主流的建議補一句「我大概會被打」，先自嘲就把可能的攻擊接住了，聽起來也更敢講。by the way 放句尾，讓這句像隨口一提而不是討拍。
swaps: I'll probably get hate for this one.
This is going to be unpopular, I know.
cards.episode: "Sell the alpha, not the feature": The enterprise sales playbook for $1M to $10M ARR | Jen Abel

alts.quote: And that is never, ever, ever the reason. How do I know? Because they already looked at your homepage, read all the stuff, saw what you promised, looked at the pricing page and decided to buy it.
alts.zh: 那絕對、絕對不會是真正的原因。我怎麼知道？因為他們早就看過你的首頁、讀完那些內容、看過你承諾了什麼、也看過定價頁，然後決定買了。

alts.quote: But if they come in on day one saying your strategy is all wrong, raises the question of, "Well then why did you join my team if you didn't believe in my strategy?"
alts.zh: 但如果他第一天就說你的策略整個都錯了，那就會讓人想問：既然你不相信這個策略，當初為什麼要加入我的團隊？

alts.quote: It's all the other stuff. And the PowerPoint is just like the task, but that's not what you hired them for.
alts.zh: 價值在其他所有事情上。投影片只是那個「任務」，但那不是你花錢請他們來做的事。

cards.quote: Yes, such a great point, Lenny. You absolutely need to time box this.
cards.zh: 對，這點問得很好。這件事你一定要設一個時間框。
cards.why: time box 當動詞用（把它框在一段時間內）是英文職場高頻詞。前面先給對方一句 such a great point——即使是同意，也要先把功勞遞出去，這是英文會議的潤滑劑。
swaps: Cap it at 90 days.
Put a hard end date on it.
cards.pmNote: 接服務型合約要以 90 天為單位切，到期重新 scope，才不會被綁死。
cards.episode: "Sell the alpha, not the feature": The enterprise sales playbook for $1M to $10M ARR | Jen Abel

alts.quote: Be careful. If you need to spend a little time on the problem, fine, but don't spend a lot of time because you need to save as much time as possible to come up with the winning solution.
alts.zh: 小心一點。你要花一點時間在問題上沒問題，但別花太多，因為你得盡量把時間留給「想出會贏的解法」。

alts.quote: So yeah, no hard and fast rule, but I think it's always you need to have this matrix of options in your mind and be very deliberate about which one you are going with and why.
alts.zh: 沒有什麼鐵則，但你腦中要有一張選項矩陣，而且要很清楚自己選了哪一格、為什麼。

alts.quote: Not all of these variables is created equal and the manager is the most important variable in the environment, because a great manager who is empathetic, who is aware of what's going on, has the ability to move the chess pieces around.
alts.zh: 這幾個變數的份量不一樣，主管是環境裡最關鍵的那一個——因為一個有同理心、狀況清楚的好主管，是有能力幫你把棋子移一移的。

cards.pattern: If you [先讓步] just to [達成目標], you're negotiating with yourself.
cards.quote: So discounting just to get the deal over the line, you're negotiating with yourself.
cards.zh: 為了把案子推過線就先給折扣，那你是在跟自己談判。
cards.why: negotiating with yourself（跟自己談判）＝對方還沒開口你就先讓步。一句話就替一個常見錯誤命名，之後團隊會直接拿這個詞互相提醒——這就是好命名的價值。
swaps: Don't bid against yourself.
You're conceding before they've even asked.
cards.pmNote: 折扣要換東西（設計夥伴、兩年推薦背書），不能只換簽約。
cards.episode: "Sell the alpha, not the feature": The enterprise sales playbook for $1M to $10M ARR | Jen Abel

alts.quote: Give yourself two to three months at the minimum, ideally more like six months, to really optimize it back to a good standing where it can potentially outperform.
alts.zh: 至少給自己兩到三個月，最好是六個月，把它優化回到好的水準、甚至超越原本的表現。

alts.quote: So instead of just sending the link, I usually start the email with something like looking forward to connecting, feel free to share, sometimes you're available or if easier, you can choose to find time on my calendar using the Calendly link here.
alts.zh: 所以我不會只丟一個連結，我通常這樣開頭：很期待跟你聊，你可以直接給我幾個方便的時間，或者比較省事的話，也可以用這裡的 Calendly 連結直接約。

alts.quote: So find some friend of yours that's like, "I'm tweeting about your podcast on Friday, or I'm going to include you in my newsletter next month." And give yourself an artificial deadline or even a real deadline to just put a stake in the ground.
alts.zh: 去找一個朋友，讓他說「我週五要發推介紹你的 podcast」或「我下個月電子報會提到你」，然後給自己一個人造死線——甚至真的死線——先把樁打下去。

cards.pattern: It's never a [對方以為的] problem. It's a [真正的] problem.
cards.quote: Everyone that I know says they have a bottom of funnel problem. It's never a bottom of funnel problem. It's a top of funnel problem.
cards.zh: 我認識的每個人都說自己是漏斗底部有問題。從來都不是漏斗底部的問題，是漏斗頂端的問題。
cards.why: 用 never/always 這種絕對句先推翻對方的自我診斷，再給新診斷。重複同一組名詞（bottom / top of funnel）讓對比極好記——換掉名詞就能套用到任何「大家都以為是 X 其實是 Y」。
swaps: It's rarely X. It's almost always Y.
People call it a X problem. It's a Y problem.
cards.pmNote: 轉換率的病灶通常在 qualification（找錯人講錯話），不在成交技巧。
cards.episode: "Sell the alpha, not the feature": The enterprise sales playbook for $1M to $10M ARR | Jen Abel

alts.quote: The problem is not like what should my goal be or how should I figure out what to do with my life? They usually know, but it's very hard to actually make time for those things.
alts.zh: 問題不在於「我的目標該是什麼」或「我這輩子要幹嘛」。這個大家其實都知道。問題是很難真的挪出時間去做那些事。

alts.quote: And so in that case, someone like me who's an advisor comes in and is like, "That's right, it's not a marketing problem, it's company strategy problem.
alts.zh: 所以那種情況下，像我這種顧問進去就會說：「沒錯，這不是行銷的問題，這是公司策略的問題。」

alts.quote: It's never about one finding in isolation.
alts.zh: 重點從來都不是單獨一個發現。

cards.pattern: So which [選項] do you want to play? Let's just start there.
cards.quote: So which game do you want to play? Let's just start there.
cards.zh: 所以你想玩哪一種賽局？我們就從這裡開始。
cards.why: 不給答案，先丟一個二選一的框，再用 Let's just start there 把問題縮到只剩一步。帶人、帶會議都能用——對方一旦選了框，後面所有討論就有邊界。
swaps: Which of the two are we optimising for? Start there.
Pick a lane first, then we'll work the details.
cards.pmNote: 企業銷售與中小企業銷售是兩種 go-to-market，不能同時打——這是策略即取捨的典型。
cards.episode: "Sell the alpha, not the feature": The enterprise sales playbook for $1M to $10M ARR | Jen Abel

alts.quote: Sometimes I even start the conversation by asking them, "What do you want to do? Where do you want to go in your career?"
alts.zh: 有時候我甚至會用這個開場：「你想做什麼？你的職涯想往哪走？」

alts.quote: I'm like, "Let's say we weren't in the room as the leadership team," which is the one the team wants to get behind. Then you'll sometimes see the team hasn't even done the work between themselves talking.
alts.zh: 我會問：「假設我們這些主管不在這個房間，你們團隊自己最想投哪一個？」有時候你會發現他們彼此之間根本還沒討論過。

alts.quote: What else can people do to become better storytellers in business? I know this is a big question, but let's see where it goes.
alts.zh: 在商業場合還可以怎麼把故事講得更好？我知道這題很大，但我們就看看會聊到哪。

cards.quote: Hopefully I'm not making this sound too daunting. I'm just really trying to lay out all the mistakes I've made.
cards.zh: 希望我沒有把這件事講得太嚇人。我只是想把我自己踩過的坑全部攤出來。
cards.why: 講完一長串壞消息，先照顧對方情緒（怕嚇到你），再把自己的失敗當成資訊來源。用「我犯的錯」而不是「你會犯的錯」，可信度最高、防衛心最低。
swaps: I don't want this to sound discouraging —
None of this is theory; it's a list of things I got wrong.
cards.episode: "Sell the alpha, not the feature": The enterprise sales playbook for $1M to $10M ARR | Jen Abel

alts.quote: I'm just going to bump you up to the 100-video plan. Let me know if you have any questions.
alts.zh: 我就直接幫你升到 100 支影片的方案囉。有問題再跟我說。

alts.quote: Then you're pushing deadlines out, and you're making your marketing team very sad.
alts.zh: 然後你就開始一直往後延，把行銷團隊搞得很難過。

alts.quote: We feel it’s trying to drive urgency via artificial deadlines versus via value to the customer.
alts.zh: 我們覺得它是在用人造的死線去製造急迫感，而不是用對客戶的價值。

cards.quote: It's so hard to give a founder hard feedback. Who wants to be the bearer of bad news?
cards.zh: 要給創辦人難聽的回饋真的很難。誰想當那個報壞消息的人？
cards.why: 用反問 Who wants to...? 把「沒人願意講真話」講成普遍人性，既替不肯給你壞消息的人開脫，也順便解釋了你為什麼收不到真實回饋。bearer of bad news 是固定說法，直接背起來。
swaps: Nobody wants to be the one to say it.
It's an awkward message to be the messenger for.
cards.pmNote: 客戶「很客氣」通常不是好訊號；要看行為（有沒有拉人進下一場會）而不是措辭。
cards.episode: "Sell the alpha, not the feature": The enterprise sales playbook for $1M to $10M ARR | Jen Abel

alts.quote: Nobody wants to hear it. Everybody wants to just think about these really cool models and how smart they are. But really it's just the hard work of getting really good data to the LLMs.
alts.zh: 沒有人想聽這個。大家都只想談那些很酷的模型有多聰明。但說到底，這就是把好資料餵給 LLM 的苦工。

alts.quote: You know what? We should ship. It's embarrassing, but that's strictly less bad than not getting the feedback you wanted.
alts.zh: 我覺得就出吧。是很難看沒錯，但這比拿不到你要的回饋還是好一點。

alts.quote: And the good news bad news is that's true. That is absolutely true.
alts.zh: 好消息也是壞消息：那是真的。千真萬確。

cards.quote: In most cases, you can ask them, is that a hard line? Or how negotiable is that?
cards.zh: 大多數情況你都可以直接問：這是硬性規定嗎？還是有多少討論空間？
cards.why: 遇到「制度就是這樣」不要爭辯，先問這條線有多硬。how negotiable is that 把對抗改成資訊詢問，對方回答時就自己把彈性講出來了——這是談判裡最划算的一句話。
swaps: Is that fixed, or is there room?
How much flexibility do you have on that?
cards.pmNote: 面對採購／法務的規則，先確認硬度再決定要不要投入時間繞路。
cards.episode: "Sell the alpha, not the feature": The enterprise sales playbook for $1M to $10M ARR | Jen Abel

alts.quote: And it's hard because in making it compact you're losing completeness.
alts.zh: 這很難，因為你把它壓得越精簡，就越不完整。

alts.quote: So yeah, no hard and fast rule, but I think it's always you need to have this matrix of options in your mind and be very deliberate about which one you are going with and why.
alts.zh: 沒有什麼鐵則，但你腦中要有一張選項矩陣，而且要很清楚自己選了哪一格、為什麼。

alts.quote: And I think people don't understand that in a competitive environment, being right is good, but being quick is necessary.
alts.zh: 我覺得大家沒搞懂：在競爭環境裡，做對是加分，做得快是必要條件。

cards.pattern: I fundamentally do not believe in [X], which is [為什麼重要的比喻].
cards.quote: I fundamentally do not believe in outsourcing the heartbeat of the organization, which is sales.
cards.zh: 我從根本上不相信可以把一家公司的心跳外包出去——而銷售就是心跳。
cards.why: I fundamentally do not believe in... 講的是原則不是偏好，語氣很重但不針對任何人。後面接一個比喻（the heartbeat of the organization）當理由，讓強硬立場有畫面可以站。
swaps: I don't think you can delegate that away.
That's not something a company should hand off.
cards.episode: "Sell the alpha, not the feature": The enterprise sales playbook for $1M to $10M ARR | Jen Abel

alts.quote: There's a saying that Mike and Kevin had at Instagram which is we may not be right, but at least we're not confused.
alts.zh: Instagram 的 Mike 跟 Kevin 有一句話：我們不見得是對的，但至少我們不是一團混亂。

alts.quote: I think so many folks don't know where to begin on starting a startup, and my tactical advice is start doing customer validation first versus building a PowerPoint deck.
alts.zh: 很多人根本不知道創業要從哪裡開始，我很具體的建議是：先去做客戶驗證，而不是先做一份簡報。

alts.quote: When we talk about pricing strategies, we hear many buzzwords, and it's irrelevant. So when we take a step back and look at it, there's literally only three types of pricing strategies.
alts.zh: 談定價策略的時候會聽到一堆流行詞，那些都不重要。退一步看，定價策略其實就只有三種。

cards.pattern: I always assume [對方] knows way more than I do.
cards.quote: I always assume that the buyer I'm speaking to is highly educated and knows way more than I do.
cards.zh: 我永遠假設坐在對面的買家很懂，而且懂的比我多很多。
cards.why: 先把對方設定成比自己懂，是英文商業對話裡低姿態高效率的開場。knows way more than I do 的那個 way（加強語氣的「多很多」）讓語氣自然、不做作，這個小字台灣人很少用。
swaps: I assume they've already done the homework.
I go in assuming they're ahead of me on this.
cards.episode: "Sell the alpha, not the feature": The enterprise sales playbook for $1M to $10M ARR | Jen Abel

alts.quote: Those are just numbers I'm putting out there. It's always going to be a gut call based on where you are.
alts.zh: 那些數字只是我隨口丟出來的。這終究是看你所在的位置做的直覺判斷。

alts.quote: So I'll give you a contention and a plausible way we get there, but as for how it happens, who knows?
alts.zh: 我可以給你一個主張，還有一條看起來說得通的路徑，但實際上會怎麼發生，誰知道。

alts.quote: Is this positioning good or not?" And the problem with B2B tech companies is, well, unless I'm your buyer, I'm not the right person to ask.
alts.zh: 「這個定位到底好不好？」B2B 科技公司的問題在於——除非我就是你的買家，不然我根本不是該問的那個人。

cards.pattern: We have a lot to learn. Can we gain your insight into how this problem is manifesting on your side?
cards.quote: Hey, I'm an early stage startup. We have a lot to learn. Can we kind of gain your insight into how this problem is manifesting on your side?
cards.zh: 嗨，我們是很早期的新創，還有很多要學。能不能請教你，這個問題在你們那邊是怎麼呈現的？
cards.why: 先自曝短處再請教，對方就從「被推銷」變成「被請教」，回饋才會誠實。how this problem is manifesting on your side 又把問題講得很中性——不是預設你有病，是問症狀長什麼樣。
swaps: We're still figuring this out — how does it show up for you?
I'd love your read on how this plays out on your side.
cards.pmNote: 早期銷售不是為了成交，是為了拿到 insight，先取得賣的資格（earn the right to sell）。
cards.episode: "Sell the alpha, not the feature": The enterprise sales playbook for $1M to $10M ARR | Jen Abel

alts.quote: Hey, I'm really enjoying working with you. I'm wondering is there some way I could help you that would also help me reach my goal?
alts.zh: 嘿，跟你合作我覺得很愉快。我在想，有沒有什麼事我可以幫你、同時也能幫我朝目標前進的？

alts.quote: It might actually mean a proactive conversation with your manager or the leadership to say, "I love what I'm doing here, and I would also like to learn a little bit more. And here's what I'm interested in."
alts.zh: 這可能只是主動找主管或高層談一次，跟他說：「我很喜歡現在做的事，同時我也想再多學一些，這是我有興趣的方向。」

alts.quote: This is people you used to work with before, go ask them, "Hey, what did I do well, what do you think my strengths are? What do you think I'm a fit for?
alts.zh: 去問以前的同事：「我哪裡做得好？你覺得我的強項是什麼？我是這樣想的——你覺得我對自己的認知準確嗎？」

cards.pattern: Let me just try to summarize what you shared, this [N] step framework.
cards.quote: Let me just try to summarize what you shared, this five step framework.
cards.zh: 我試著把你剛剛講的整理一下，這個五步驟的框架。
cards.why: Let me just try to 三個字把「我要總結」變成「我試試看」，就算整理錯了對方也只會補充不會糾正你。英文會議想確認自己有沒有聽懂，這是最安全的入口。
swaps: Let me play that back to you.
So if I've got this right, it's...
Let me see if I can summarise that.
cards.pmNote: 會議收斂的第一步是複述，複述能同時檢查理解與逼出隱含分歧。
cards.episode: The power of strategic narrative | Andy Raskin

alts.quote: But before we do that, let me just summarize maybe the top five attributes and kind of traits you just shared, and then I have a two part question around this.
alts.zh: 在進到那個之前，我先把你剛剛講的五個特質整理一次，然後我有一個兩段式的問題。

alts.quote: I still may insert myself and say, "Hey, let me pause here for a second and try to capture what has been said." This is what I've heard.
alts.zh: 我還是會切進去說：「欸，我先暫停一下，把剛剛講的整理一下。」以下是我聽到的。

alts.quote: So just to summarize so people can have just a very short definition of this framework.
alts.zh: 所以快速總結一下，讓大家可以有一個很短的定義知道這個框架是什麼。

cards.quote: I'm taking us off track, but I want to go a little deeper with this.
cards.zh: 我知道這樣會離題，但我想在這裡多挖一點。
cards.why: 自己先承認「我要岔題了」，聽起來就不像失控而像刻意選擇，別人也不會急著把你拉回去。這是英文會議裡爭取時間的合法手續。
swaps: Slight detour, but —
Can I take us sideways for a second?
cards.episode: The power of strategic narrative | Andy Raskin

alts.quote: Before you actually move on to the next one, I want to spend a little time on this one
alts.zh: 在你跳到下一點之前，我想在這一點上多待一下。

alts.quote: It gets easier. I don't want to go off too much of a tangent, but the thing you have to remember is that pricing is not this knob that you can turn separate from the rest of your strategy.
alts.zh: 是會變簡單。我不想扯太遠，但有件事一定要記得：定價不是一個可以單獨轉的旋鈕，它跟整套策略是連在一起的。

alts.quote: I'm not going to interrupt the flow conversation. I'm just going to summarize in Zoom chat this is what I've heard, and this is what I think we're saying in this conversation.
alts.zh: 我不打斷大家的討論節奏，我直接在 Zoom 聊天室整理一下我聽到的、以及我認為我們在談的東西。

cards.pattern: Let me take us back on track and let's talk about [主軸].
cards.quote: So let me take us back on track and let's talk about just the high level framework here.
cards.zh: 我們把話題拉回來，來談一下這個框架的高層次架構。
cards.why: take us back on track 用 us 不用 you，收線的同時把責任分攤掉，不會像在指責誰講太多。這是主持會議最常需要、台灣人卻最不敢做的動作。
swaps: Let's bring it back to...
Coming back to the main thread —
Parking that, let's return to...
cards.episode: The power of strategic narrative | Andy Raskin

alts.quote: I know we'll talk more about this, but let me go back to the question I was going to ask...
alts.zh: 我知道這個我們等下會再聊，不過讓我先回到我原本要問的問題。

alts.quote: So I think we talked about how to decide whether to resource SEO, but we didn't talk about how to understand what the expectations are from SEO.
alts.zh: 我覺得我們談了「要不要投資源做 SEO」，但還沒談「對 SEO 的期待該怎麼設定」。

alts.quote: Maybe that's another podcast for another day, but I fundamentally believe in when products take on some kind of persona.
alts.zh: 這可能要另開一集才講得完，但我真的相信產品應該要有某種人格。

cards.pattern: So to quickly recap a few of the key things I've written down as we're talking.
cards.quote: So to quickly recap a few of the key things that I've written down as we're talking.
cards.zh: 我快速把剛剛邊聽邊記下來的幾個重點整理一下。
cards.why: 加上 that I've written down as we're talking，等於證明你全程有在聽、而且只挑重點——比乾巴巴的 to recap 多了可信度與參與感。
swaps: Quick recap of what I've got so far:
Let me read back the key points.
cards.episode: "Sell the alpha, not the feature": The enterprise sales playbook for $1M to $10M ARR | Jen Abel

alts.quote: So just to summarize what you shared, which I was just writing as you were talking about the things that essentially help Stripe build this incredible team.
alts.zh: 所以總結一下你分享的——你講的時候我就在寫——那些讓 Stripe 能建出這支超強團隊的東西。

alts.quote: So to your question, you're a feature team. You want to give it a shot, be in a real product team. These are the four things you need to go out and do.
alts.zh: 回到你的問題：你在一支功能團隊，想試試看真正的產品團隊怎麼運作——那你要去做的就是這四件事。

alts.quote: I still may insert myself and say, "Hey, let me pause here for a second and try to capture what has been said." This is what I've heard.
alts.zh: 我還是會切進去說：「欸，我先暫停一下，把剛剛講的整理一下。」以下是我聽到的。

cards.pattern: Backing up a little bit — we jumped right in. I'm curious how you'd even describe [基本概念].
cards.quote: Backing up a little bit, we jumped right in. I'm curious how you even describe positioning, what the heck is positioning?
cards.zh: 稍微倒回去一下——我們一開始就直接跳進來了。我很好奇你會怎麼定義「定位」這件事？
cards.why: 問一個很基本的問題之前，先說 we jumped right in（是我們跳太快，不是我沒跟上），把「不懂」的責任轉成流程問題。要在英文會議裡問笨問題，這是最漂亮的包裝。
swaps: Can we rewind a step?
Before we go further, can we define terms?
cards.pmNote: 對齊（alignment）常常敗在沒人敢問「我們講的是同一個東西嗎」。
cards.episode: April Dunford on product positioning, segmentation, and optimizing your sales process

alts.quote: The reason I'm a little confused, just because I want to get it right, is what I'm hearing, which maybe isn't what you said
alts.zh: 我有點不確定，純粹是想弄清楚——我聽到的（可能不是你講的意思）是……

alts.quote: And if it's helpful, let me break down the question a little bit.
alts.zh: 如果有幫助的話，我把這個問題拆開來講一下。

alts.quote: What I'm hearing is basically you give those responsibilities to the engineers, designer, and maybe other functions within the team. Is that right?
alts.zh: 我聽到的意思基本上是：你們把那些責任分給工程師、設計師，可能還有團隊裡其他角色。我理解對嗎？

cards.pattern: I want to talk about [新主題], but just to close the loop on that…
cards.quote: I want to talk about public speaking skills, but just to close the loop on that.
cards.zh: 我想聊聊公開演講的技巧，不過在那之前先把剛剛那題收尾。
cards.why: close the loop（把迴圈關起來）是英文職場最常用的收尾動詞片語。先預告下一個主題再回頭補完上一題，聽者知道你沒忘、也知道還要多久。
swaps: Before we move on, let me close this out.
One last thing on that, then we'll move on.
cards.episode: How to tell better stories | Matthew Dicks (Storyworthy)

alts.quote: And kind of on a note, I want to call an audible, and so we were going to talk through all of your favorite frameworks.
alts.zh: 順著剛剛那個點，我想臨時改一下流程——我們原本要把你最愛的框架全部走一遍。

alts.quote: So I think we talked about how to decide whether to resource SEO, but we didn't talk about how to understand what the expectations are from SEO.
alts.zh: 我覺得我們談了「要不要投資源做 SEO」，但還沒談「對 SEO 的期待該怎麼設定」。

alts.quote: "I need 20 minutes of focused time to interrogate something that I've done. We're not going to talk. I'm literally going to force us into a room or Zoom.
alts.zh: 「我需要二十分鐘的專注時間來拷問我做的東西。我們不用講話。我就是要把大家關進一個會議室或 Zoom。」

cards.pattern: Just to calibrate — what [規模／範圍] are we talking about here?
cards.quote: Just for folks that are listening, just to calibrate what size of company you're talking about selling to here.
cards.zh: 為了讓聽的人有個基準——你剛剛講的是賣給多大規模的公司？
cards.why: calibrate（校準）把「你講的到底適用在哪」問得很專業，而且不是質疑對方，是幫大家對準刻度。加一句 for folks that are listening，等於替全場問，自己不用承認沒聽懂。
swaps: Just so we're calibrated on scale —
What size are we talking about, roughly?
cards.pmNote: 任何建議都該附上適用條件（階段、規模、市場），否則就是無法執行的口號。
cards.episode: "Sell the alpha, not the feature": The enterprise sales playbook for $1M to $10M ARR | Jen Abel

alts.quote: For folks that haven't worked at a company with this kind of on the ground ops team, can you just unpack what that is?
alts.zh: 對於沒待過有這種第一線營運團隊的人來說，你可以幫忙拆解一下那是什麼嗎？

alts.quote: Okay, what do you mean by this? Are you talking about inner and outer loop? Are you talking about friction?
alts.zh: 好，你指的是什麼意思？你講的是內外迴圈嗎？還是講摩擦成本？

alts.quote: You're sitting in the meeting and you're like, "This is a dumb question. Everyone's going to think I'm an idiot." But then you get brave and you ask it and it turns out it wasn't a dumb question.
alts.zh: 你坐在會議裡想：「這問題也太蠢，問了大家會覺得我是白痴。」結果你鼓起勇氣問了，才發現根本不是蠢問題。

cards.quote: What else can people do to become better storytellers in business? I know this is a big question, but let's see where it goes.
cards.zh: 在商業場合還可以怎麼把故事講得更好？我知道這題很大，但我們就看看會聊到哪。
cards.why: 先承認問題太大，等於免除對方「必須給完整答案」的壓力，對方反而會放鬆講出好東西。let's see where it goes 把一個模糊的問題變成一場共同探索。
swaps: That's a huge question — take it wherever you want.
Big one, but I'll throw it out anyway.
cards.pmNote: 1:1 帶人時，開放式大問題要先鬆綁期待，對方才敢想。
cards.episode: How to tell better stories | Matthew Dicks (Storyworthy)

alts.quote: People call me sometimes they're like "I want to know if I have product market fit." Well, the fact that you have time to call me and ask me this question already tells me the answer.
alts.zh: 有人打給我說：「我想知道我們有沒有 PMF。」嗯，你有空打這通電話問我，這件事本身就給了答案。

alts.quote: I often think about this phrase, which is people don't care what you know until they know that you care.
alts.zh: 我常想到這句話：在別人知道你在乎之前，他們不會在乎你懂什麼。

alts.quote: What we ask people in general is we say, what do you think? We don't say, what do you know? We often say, what do you think?
alts.zh: 我們一般會問人「你怎麼想？」我們不會問「你知道什麼？」我們最常問的就是「你怎麼想？」

cards.quote: I'd maybe put it a little bit differently.
cards.zh: 我可能會換一個講法。
cards.why: 整句沒有一個否定詞，卻已經把對方的說法擋掉了。maybe + a little bit 是雙重緩衝，讓「我不同意」聽起來像「我來補一個角度」，是英文會議裡最安全的反對開場。
swaps: I'd frame it slightly differently
Let me put that another way
cards.pmNote: 接住別人的總結再微調，比直接推翻更容易保住後續的合作關係。
cards.episode: How embracing emotions will accelerate your career | Joe Hudson (executive coach, Art of Accomplishment)

alts.quote: This is maybe going to come across a little bit flippant, but they can't stop you from sending an email technically. So I'm just going to send the email.
alts.zh: 這樣講可能有點輕佻，但嚴格來說他們也不能阻止我寄信。所以我就照寄。

alts.quote: So I'm going to disagree with Sedaris a little bit.
alts.zh: 這點我要跟 Sedaris 有一點不一樣的看法。

alts.quote: And the way Reid records, which I'm not sure I would recommend this, but he does it a little bit differently than you do.
alts.zh: Reid 錄音的方式——我不確定我會推薦這樣做——跟你的做法有點不一樣。

cards.quote: Yeah, it's definitely a huge part of it. There's a couple of things that I noticed get in the way.
cards.zh: 對，那絕對是很大一塊。不過我有注意到幾件事會卡住。
cards.why: 先給一個「不是敷衍」的實質認可（definitely a huge part），再用 get in the way 把異議說成「有東西擋路」而不是「你錯了」。台灣人習慣的 but 在這裡被換成一個新句子，火藥味整個降下來。
swaps: That's a big piece of it. What I'd add is...
Agreed on that. A couple of things complicate it though
cards.pmNote: 先確認共識再談分歧，是跨部門對齊時省下最多來回的順序。
cards.episode: How embracing emotions will accelerate your career | Joe Hudson (executive coach, Art of Accomplishment)

alts.quote: Both things can be true. It's like, yeah, there's nothing perfect in product. However, it is true that some companies are healthier than others.
alts.zh: 這兩件事可以同時成立。對，產品這行沒有什麼是完美的；但同樣真實的是，有些公司確實比其他公司健康得多。

alts.quote: Yeah, sorry. Buy-in doesn't feel quite right to me, because buy-in feels like, oh, I've come to agree with you. And that's different from it's a part of me.
