alts.zh: 抱歉，我覺得「buy-in（買單）」這個詞不太對。buy-in 聽起來像「我最後被你說服了」，那跟「這東西本來就是我的一部分」是兩回事。

alts.quote: I agree with you. I totally agree with you. Now, I think it's the human aspect though of boldness, seeing the future in a way that a thing trained on priors cannot.
alts.zh: 我同意你，完全同意。不過我覺得，人的那一塊——那種膽識、那種能看見未來的能力，是只學過去資料的東西做不到的。

cards.pattern: The other thing that's a little bit different about what you said is [差異].
cards.quote: The other thing that's a little bit different about what you said is that emotions do need to be felt.
cards.zh: 還有一點跟你剛剛講的稍微不一樣，就是情緒是真的需要被感受到的。
cards.why: 把「你錯了」重寫成「這裡有個 different」，差異變成一個中性的名詞，不指向任何人的對錯。a little bit 再把差距縮小，聽起來像微調而不是推翻。
swaps: Where I'd diverge slightly is...
One nuance I'd add to that is...
cards.pmNote: 把分歧描述成「差異」而非「錯誤」，是評審別人方案時最不傷關係的說法。
cards.episode: How embracing emotions will accelerate your career | Joe Hudson (executive coach, Art of Accomplishment)

alts.quote: So, I think one needs to be a little bit cautious on what Dario says. And that's setting aside the cynical view that he's just doing that department stock, which I don't believe at all.
alts.zh: 我覺得對 Dario 講的話要保留一點。而且我這裡還先撇開那種比較酸的解讀——說他只是在替自家股價講話——那我完全不相信。

alts.quote: I would soften it a little bit... I wouldn't say I'm not a fan of creating category.
alts.zh: 我會講得軟一點——我不會說我不喜歡做品類（category）這件事。

alts.quote: Yeah, sorry. Buy-in doesn't feel quite right to me, because buy-in feels like, oh, I've come to agree with you. And that's different from it's a part of me.
alts.zh: 抱歉，我覺得「buy-in（買單）」這個詞不太對。buy-in 聽起來像「我最後被你說服了」，那跟「這東西本來就是我的一部分」是兩回事。

cards.pattern: Clearly, [反證], so I'm not buying it.
cards.quote: Clearly, you're not so scared that you can't do anything, so I'm not buying it. I don't do it quite like that, I do it with a lot more love than that.
cards.zh: 很明顯你沒有害怕到什麼都做不了，所以這個說法我不買單。我實際上不會講得這麼硬，我會帶更多善意。
cards.why: I'm not buying it 是用「消費者拒買」的比喻拒絕一個說法，比 that's not true 輕，因為否定的是「說詞」不是「人」。後半句是母語者自我標註語氣的習慣——先講重話，再說明真實情境下我會更溫和。
swaps: I'm not sure I buy that
That doesn't quite square with what I'm seeing
cards.pmNote: 用對方自己的行為當反證，比用你的判斷當反證更難反駁。
cards.episode: How embracing emotions will accelerate your career | Joe Hudson (executive coach, Art of Accomplishment)

alts.quote: I know you're mad at me today, but it is your fault. A hundred percent your fault if any of your hires fail. Don't blame them.
alts.zh: 我知道你今天會氣我，但這是你的錯。招進來的人陣亡，百分之百是你的錯。別怪他們。

alts.quote: I'm not saying Google's bad, but Google used to have this don't be evil ethos, and it got lost.
alts.zh: 我不是說 Google 很爛，但 Google 以前有「不作惡」那套精神，後來弄丟了。

alts.quote: Look, I don't have time to sugarcoat any feedback, and frankly, the best people I've worked with are the people who come into one-on-ones with me and yell at me and tell me I'm messing up.
alts.zh: 老實說，我沒空把回饋包糖衣；而且說真的，我合作過最好的人，都是會在一對一裡對我吼、直接說我哪裡搞砸了的人。

cards.quote: I'm like, "Oh, cool. Tell me what I'm missing."
cards.zh: 我會說：「好啊，跟我說我漏掉了什麼。」
cards.why: 被罵之後的標準反應句。Tell me what I'm missing 假設「錯的是我的視野不是我的能力」，一句話把對抗轉成資訊交換，而且逼對方講具體的東西而不是情緒。
swaps: Walk me through what you're seeing
What am I not seeing here?
cards.pmNote: 接住批評的第一句話決定對方後面願不願意講真話。
cards.episode: How embracing emotions will accelerate your career | Joe Hudson (executive coach, Art of Accomplishment)

alts.quote: Hey, here's what I'm seeing and tell me what's going on for you.
alts.zh: 我先講我這邊看到的狀況，然後換你講講你那邊發生了什麼事。

alts.quote: Look, I don't have time to sugarcoat any feedback, and frankly, the best people I've worked with are the people who come into one-on-ones with me and yell at me and tell me I'm messing up.
alts.zh: 老實說，我沒空把回饋包糖衣；而且說真的，我合作過最好的人，都是會在一對一裡對我吼、直接說我哪裡搞砸了的人。

alts.quote: I care so much about you and I'm giving you this feedback because I want you to be successful and I want you to be able to reach the pinnacle of what I know you can accomplish.
alts.zh: 我非常在乎你，我給你這個回饋是因為我希望你成功、希望你能走到我知道你能到的高度。

cards.quote: Give me a day and I'll come back to you.
cards.zh: 給我一天，我再回來找你談。
cards.why: 不是拒絕、也不是硬撐，而是把「我現在接不住」轉成一個有期限的承諾。come back to you 隱含「這件事我認領了」，是英文職場最常見的緩衝兼認領句。
swaps: Let me sit with that and get back to you tomorrow
Can I take a day on this?
cards.pmNote: 當場答不出來時給出時間點，比硬給一個爛答案更能保住信任。
cards.episode: How embracing emotions will accelerate your career | Joe Hudson (executive coach, Art of Accomplishment)

alts.quote: By the way, a very, very successful company for a new set of products has a 50% hit rate. So half of you are going to come back in a year and have a different job. Do you have the resilience to do that?
alts.zh: 順帶一提，一家非常成功的公司做新產品的成功率大概是五成。所以你們有一半的人一年後會換一份工作。你們有那個韌性嗎？

alts.quote: It's so hard to give a founder hard feedback. Who wants to be the bearer of bad news?
alts.zh: 要給創辦人難聽的回饋真的很難。誰想當那個報壞消息的人？

alts.quote: These are reaching millions of people, their websites get many, many, many millions of unique visitors each month. That does not mean that your story is going to be read by millions of people.
alts.zh: 這些媒體確實觸及上百萬人，網站每個月幾百萬不重複訪客。但這不代表你那篇報導會被上百萬人看到。

cards.pattern: You keep using the word [X], and I just want to [反轉].
cards.quote: You keep using the word advice, and I just want to, so for anybody who's listening, do not take my advice.
cards.zh: 你一直在用「建議」這個詞，我想借這個機會講一句：不要照我的建議做。
cards.why: 把攻擊點放在「用詞」而不是「人」，是英文裡最安全的挑戰法。You keep using the word X 同時做了兩件事：指出對方的預設，以及取得重新定義的發言權。
swaps: We keep saying 'growth' — can we define what we mean?
I notice we keep calling this a bug
cards.pmNote: 團隊反覆使用的詞，往往藏著沒對齊的假設；拆詞就是拆假設。
cards.episode: How embracing emotions will accelerate your career | Joe Hudson (executive coach, Art of Accomplishment)

alts.quote: But that's really not actually what they want. They want to have been funny, because being funny means you must take a risk.
alts.zh: 但那其實不是他們真正想要的。他們想要的是「已經很好笑」這個結果，因為要好笑就得冒險。

alts.quote: We're going to get to work on that, but can you tell me how are you measuring success? We want to make sure that what we do, you consider it successful.
alts.zh: 這件事我們會開始動工，不過可以先跟我說你是怎麼衡量成功的嗎？我們想確保做出來的東西，在你眼中算是成功。

alts.quote: That is an artificial timeline introduced by Google Calendar or whatever calendar you use. It's not a real thing, and so I want to put us on real timelines.
alts.zh: 那只是 Google 日曆——或你們用的任何行事曆——生出來的假期限，它不是真的。所以我希望我們回到真正的時間軸上。

cards.pattern: I definitely would not [對方的說法]. What I would say that's a close cousin to that is [你的說法].
cards.quote: I definitely would not want anyone to feel joy. What I would say that's a close cousin to that is that enjoyment is such an important tool for productivity.
cards.zh: 我絕對不會要求任何人去感受喜悅。跟那個很接近、但我會這樣說的是：享受是生產力非常重要的工具。
cards.why: a close cousin to that 是把自己的立場「掛」在對方的問題旁邊，既不接受錯誤前提、也不讓對方覺得問題被打槍。台灣人碰到被誤解時常只會 no, that's not what I meant，這句是專業版。
swaps: That's not quite it, but here's the neighboring idea
The version of that I'd actually defend is...
cards.pmNote: 被問到一個前提錯誤的問題時，重新定義問題比硬答更有價值。
cards.episode: How embracing emotions will accelerate your career | Joe Hudson (executive coach, Art of Accomplishment)

alts.quote: If you’re uncomfortable, you could say something like “Normally, I want you all to feel great about the direction, but I feel strongly about this path, so can we just try it and see how it goes?
alts.zh: 如果你會不好意思，可以這樣說：「平常我希望大家都認同這個方向，但這條路我立場很強，我們就先試試看，看結果如何，好嗎？」

alts.quote: So this kind of behavioral framing and nudging becomes important, it's not about deceiving your customers, but it's just about framing the products in such a way that it also appeals to the irrational side of the brain.
alts.zh: 這種行為框架跟推力很重要——它不是要騙客戶，而是把產品呈現得也能打到大腦不理性的那一面。

alts.quote: And many of my design friends will push back on this and they'll say design should be its own thing and it should be an independent group and we should have three co-equal branches of government, and that's a solid argument as well
alts.zh: 我很多設計圈的朋友會反對，他們會說設計應該獨立成一個部門，跟產品、工程三權分立——那也是很有道理的論點。

cards.pattern: Love him or hate him, [引用有爭議的人].
cards.quote: Another one, love him or hate him, one of the things that Elon Musk has said that I found it very valuable in my time.
cards.zh: 還有一個，不管你喜不喜歡他啦——馬斯克講過一句話，我覺得對我很受用。
cards.why: love him or hate him 是預先處理反對（pre-empt）：在對方跳出來說「引用這個人？」之前，先承認爭議，把焦點鎖回內容。一句四個字省掉一整段離題。
swaps: Whatever you think of the company, they got this right
Setting aside the controversy for a second
cards.pmNote: 引用有爭議的來源時先承認爭議，能避免討論被身分之爭綁架。
cards.episode: How embracing emotions will accelerate your career | Joe Hudson (executive coach, Art of Accomplishment)

alts.quote: It's like these things that seem so common sense are actually hard with what they're doing… a lot of the advice is common sense. That doesn't mean it's easy to put in motion.
alts.zh: 這些看起來根本是常識的東西，真的做起來很難……很多建議都是常識，但常識不代表容易落地。

alts.quote: I often tell people that I hate the word 'favorite' because it tells me to become limited in my mind. So I stay away from 'favorite', but I learn all the time from everybody.
alts.zh: 我常跟人說我討厭「最喜歡的」這個詞，因為它會逼我的腦袋變窄。所以我不用這個詞，但我隨時都在跟每個人學東西。

alts.quote: Most of the time they will say, "Thank you. I am cool with six of these. This one freaks me out.
alts.zh: 多數人會回：「這裡面有六點我可以接受。但這一點讓我很不安，可以再聊聊嗎？」

cards.pattern: What I'm hearing is [你的理解].
cards.quote: What I'm hearing is the core issues, we're not able to feel our emotion.
cards.zh: 我聽到的重點是：核心問題在於我們沒辦法真的感受到自己的情緒。
cards.why: What I'm hearing is 把「我沒聽懂」變成「我來覆述確認」，聽起來像在整理不像在求救——對英文非母語者是保命句。而且覆述錯了對方會直接更正，資訊反而更完整。
swaps: So if I'm following you correctly...
Let me play that back to you
cards.pmNote: 把聽到的內容覆述一次，是會議上成本最低的對齊動作。
cards.episode: How embracing emotions will accelerate your career | Joe Hudson (executive coach, Art of Accomplishment)

alts.quote: The reason I'm a little confused, just because I want to get it right, is what I'm hearing, which maybe isn't what you said
alts.zh: 我有點不確定，純粹是想弄清楚——我聽到的（可能不是你講的意思）是……

alts.quote: So kind of what I'm hearing is a lot of the work is giving humans more information versus giving machine learning algorithms more information and there's a lot more leverage potentially there, giving humans more ways to tweak and dial.
alts.zh: 所以我聽到的大概是：很多工作其實是給人更多資訊，而不是給機器學習演算法更多資訊，而那裡的槓桿可能大得多。

alts.quote: What I'm hearing is step one is just get your kind of peer leaders aligned behind something that may not obviously be something your leaders want you to do, is that right?
alts.zh: 我聽到的是：第一步就是先把同層的主管拉到同一邊，就算那件事你的上面不見得想要你做——是這樣嗎？

cards.pattern: The way I think about this is [比喻].
cards.quote: The way I think about this is that emotions are like a tube, let's say, and there's water moving through the tube.
cards.zh: 我自己是這樣想這件事的：情緒像一根管子，裡面有水在流。
cards.why: The way I think about this is 先聲明「這是我的思考模型」，比 This is 更容易被接受；後面接 let's say 又進一步標示這只是暫時的比喻。兩層 hedge 讓比喻不用背負「必須正確」的壓力。
swaps: The mental model I use is...
Here's the analogy I keep coming back to
cards.pmNote: 給抽象問題一個具體比喻，是策略溝通裡最省時的對齊工具。
cards.episode: How embracing emotions will accelerate your career | Joe Hudson (executive coach, Art of Accomplishment)

alts.quote: Let's just say there's a product manager and nobody's ever coached this poor person, and so they really don't know much.
alts.zh: 我們就假設有一個產品經理，從來沒有人帶過他，所以他其實懂得不多。

alts.quote: Think about press the same way that you think about raising money, which is to say you do it when you know what the money is for, and you should do it when you know what the press is for.
alts.zh: 把「找媒體報導」想成「募資」：你會在知道這筆錢要幹嘛的時候才去募，那你也該在知道這次曝光要幹嘛的時候才去找。

alts.quote: And that's the thing they used to say, "Hey, leadership, this is the problem statement. Here's what we think how might we solve this big problem and here's what we think it looks like when we ship it." That's a mini-vision.
alts.zh: 「各位主管，這是問題陳述。我們認為可以怎麼解這個大問題，還有我們認為做出來會長什麼樣。」這就是一個小型願景。

cards.pattern: We start our meetings with: what are you scared to say?
cards.quote: We start all of our meetings with what are you scared to say in our business?
cards.zh: 我們每場會議都從這個問題開始：在這家公司裡，你不敢講的是什麼？
cards.why: 把「請大家踴躍發言」換成一個具體到讓人不好閃躲的問題。scared to say 直接指名情緒門檻，比 any concerns? 有效十倍——後者的標準答案永遠是沉默。
swaps: What's the thing nobody wants to say out loud?
What are we all avoiding here?
cards.pmNote: 會議開場的問題設計，決定了那場會能不能碰到真問題。
cards.episode: How embracing emotions will accelerate your career | Joe Hudson (executive coach, Art of Accomplishment)

alts.quote: Now that you've agreed among yourselves that you're going to do that for a fixed period of time, everyone go around the room and say, "If I could start this company over again the thing I wish we were doing was."
alts.zh: 既然大家已經同意用一段固定的時間來試，那就一個一個講：「如果能重來一次，我希望我們在做的是＿＿＿。」

alts.quote: And kind of on a note, I want to call an audible, and so we were going to talk through all of your favorite frameworks.
alts.zh: 順著剛剛那個點，我想臨時改一下流程——我們原本要把你最愛的框架全部走一遍。

alts.quote: So I'd say practically just try to look for places where it seems the team's having the same debate over and over and have it once, get it done, and put it behind you.
alts.zh: 很實際的做法是：找出團隊一再重複爭論的那幾件事，把那場辯論一次辯完、定案、然後永遠翻過去。

cards.pattern: If it's helpful, let me break that down a little bit.
cards.quote: And if it's helpful, let me break down the question a little bit.
cards.zh: 如果有幫助的話，我把這個問題拆開來講一下。
cards.why: if it's helpful 是英文裡最禮貌的「取得繼續講的許可」，把主導權形式上交給對方，實際上你已經接著講了。比 Let me explain 少了說教感。
swaps: If it's useful, I can unpack that
Happy to go deeper if that helps
cards.pmNote: 在會議上展開細節前先確認需求，可以避免把時間花在沒人要的深度上。
cards.episode: How have I been complicit in creating the conditions I say I don’t want? | Jerry Colonna (CEO of Reboot, executive coach, former VC)

alts.quote: Let me refine that a little bit more. It's more about giving people the information that they can use for decisions that they alone are good at...
alts.zh: 我把那個講法再修得精準一點。重點比較是：給人們他們才擅長的那類決策所需要的資訊。

alts.quote: Let me back up and just dissect a little bit the way you described design, you described it in really tactical terms.
alts.zh: 先讓我退一步，拆解一下你剛剛描述設計的方式——你講的是很戰術層次的東西。

alts.quote: Backing up a little bit, we jumped right in. I'm curious how you even describe positioning, what the heck is positioning?
alts.zh: 稍微倒回去一下——我們一開始就直接跳進來了。我很好奇你會怎麼定義「定位」這件事？

cards.pattern: I purposely chose the word [X] because [X] does not mean [Y], and that's a really important distinction.
cards.quote: So I purposely chose the word complicit because complicit does not mean responsible, and that's a really important distinction.
cards.zh: 我是刻意選「共謀」這個詞的，因為共謀不等於負責，這個區別非常重要。
cards.why: 先宣告「我是刻意選這個字的」，等於預先擋掉「你用詞太重」的反彈，再用 X does not mean Y 精準劃界。這是把定義權拿在手上的高階做法。
swaps: I use 'X' deliberately — it's not the same as 'Y'
The word matters here: X, not Y
cards.pmNote: 問題定義用哪個字，會決定團隊往哪個方向找解法。
cards.episode: How have I been complicit in creating the conditions I say I don’t want? | Jerry Colonna (CEO of Reboot, executive coach, former VC)

alts.quote: So there's, I wouldn't say a checklist, but there's a series of questions that I asked to diagnose why is growth slowing in this order, because it's one of these things where the first one that's a problem, if you don't fix that, it doesn't matter if you fix one of the ones below.
alts.zh: 我不會說那是一張檢查清單，但我確實有一組問題，會照順序問下去診斷成長為什麼變慢——因為只要最前面那個沒修，後面修再多都沒用。

alts.quote: And we are, I mean we are busy, but we call it the busy bandwagon because it feels like you should be busy.
alts.zh: 我們確實很忙，但我們把它叫做「忙碌從眾車」，因為那感覺就像你應該要很忙。

alts.quote: But that's the wrong question, because you can do a lot of bad things that will improve revenue.
alts.zh: 但那是錯的問題，因為你可以做很多爛事，一樣能讓營收變好。

cards.quote: So let's just pause, Lenny.
cards.zh: 我們先暫停一下。
cards.why: 用 let's（我們）而不是 you，把打斷包裝成共同行動，對方就不會覺得被叫停。加上名字更軟——這是英文裡搶回發言權而不失禮的標準做法。
swaps: Can we pause there for a second?
Let me stop us right there
cards.pmNote: 會議失焦時，打斷的時機比打斷的措辭更重要。
cards.episode: How have I been complicit in creating the conditions I say I don’t want? | Jerry Colonna (CEO of Reboot, executive coach, former VC)

alts.quote: I'm taking us off track, but I want to go a little deeper with this.
alts.zh: 我知道這樣會離題，但我想在這裡多挖一點。

alts.quote: Oh, one thing I forgot that I learned from Guy Rosen, he is our chief security officer, is when you have three options and a recommendation...
alts.zh: 喔對，我忘了講一件我從 Guy Rosen（我們資安長）那邊學到的：當你有三個選項加一個建議的時候⋯⋯

alts.quote: I'm not going to interrupt the flow conversation. I'm just going to summarize in Zoom chat this is what I've heard, and this is what I think we're saying in this conversation.
alts.zh: 我不打斷大家的討論節奏，我直接在 Zoom 聊天室整理一下我聽到的、以及我認為我們在談的東西。

cards.quote: Does that resonate at all?
cards.zh: 這樣講有打中什麼嗎？
cards.why: resonate 問的是「有沒有共鳴」而不是「對不對」，對方就不必為了保住面子而說 yes。at all 又把門檻降到最低，連「有一點點」都算數，很難尷尬地回答不出來。
swaps: Does any of that land?
Is that anywhere close?
cards.pmNote: 驗證你的假設時，問「有沒有共鳴」比問「我說得對嗎」拿到的訊號更真。
cards.episode: How have I been complicit in creating the conditions I say I don’t want? | Jerry Colonna (CEO of Reboot, executive coach, former VC)

alts.quote: I want to follow that thread, but first of all, I want to also add, and correct me if you disagree with this.
alts.zh: 我想追那條線，但首先我想補充一點——你不同意的話就說。

alts.quote: Just for folks that are listening, just to calibrate what size of company you're talking about selling to here.
alts.zh: 為了讓聽的人有個基準——你剛剛講的是賣給多大規模的公司？

alts.quote: Please note that don't mix transparency and fairness with being predictable. Those are very different things.
alts.zh: 請注意，不要把「透明與公平」跟「可預測」混為一談。這是兩件很不一樣的事。

cards.pattern: Let's take a step back. If I can reflect back your original question, [重述].
cards.quote: So let's take a step back. The fear is, if I can reflect back to your original question, the fear is if I go there, I don't know what's going to happen as a consequence of that.
cards.zh: 我們退一步看。如果我把你原本的問題回映給你，那個恐懼是：如果我真的往下探，我不知道會發生什麼後果。
cards.why: reflect back 是教練用語，意思是「把你的話整理後還給你」。它跟 summarize 的差別在於它承認這是「我的版本」，所以對方可以修正——是英文裡收斂發散討論最不霸道的方式。
swaps: Let me reflect that back to you
Zooming out for a second, the underlying question is...
cards.pmNote: 把散開的討論收回原始問題，是主持人最該練的一招。
cards.episode: How have I been complicit in creating the conditions I say I don’t want? | Jerry Colonna (CEO of Reboot, executive coach, former VC)

alts.quote: So maybe this is a way to come back to your question about what's the output of the shaping session, it's like it's shaped if we can give this to a technical person and they say, "Yeah, I know what to go build now."
alts.zh: 所以回到你剛剛問的「shaping session 的產出是什麼」：判準是——把它交給一個技術的人，他會說「好，我知道要蓋什麼了」。

alts.quote: I know I keep saying we're going to wrap this up, but here's a question and if it doesn't work, we'll get rid of it.
alts.zh: 我知道我一直說要收尾了，但這裡有個問題——如果行不通，我們就把它砍掉。

alts.quote: Sometimes I'm like, "Who's owning this?" And it's like people don't know. That's why I think it's very important to have a single-threaded owner.
alts.zh: 有時候我問「這件事誰在 own？」結果大家都不知道。這就是為什麼一定要有一個單一負責人。

cards.quote: Thank you for giving me more of that answer.
cards.zh: 謝謝你願意把那個答案講得更完整。
cards.why: 肯定的不是內容而是「你多說了一點」這個行為。當對方剛剛講了一段有點難堪的實話，這句是最精準的獎勵——它鼓勵的是坦白本身。
swaps: I appreciate you going there
Thank you for being that honest about it
cards.pmNote: 有人在會議上說出不好聽的真話時，公開謝他，下次才還會有人講。
cards.episode: How have I been complicit in creating the conditions I say I don’t want? | Jerry Colonna (CEO of Reboot, executive coach, former VC)

alts.quote: I said, "Hi, my name's Camille. I'm interning here this summer. It's my first day. I just wanted to say thank you for spending your time doing that speech for us on Saturday."
alts.zh: 我說：「嗨，我叫 Camille，今年夏天在這裡實習，今天是我第一天。我只是想跟你說謝謝，謝謝你週六花時間為我們做那場演講。」

alts.quote: Well, thank you for sharing the real talk. I think you made the right choice.
alts.zh: 謝謝你講了實話。我覺得你那個選擇是對的。

alts.quote: And to her credit, she didn't put it in, and it still worked brilliantly.
alts.zh: 而且說句公道話，她確實沒放進去，結果一樣做得很漂亮。

cards.pattern: The good news / bad news is [事實].
cards.quote: And the good news bad news is that's true. That is absolutely true.
cards.zh: 好消息也是壞消息：那是真的。千真萬確。
cards.why: 把壞消息和好消息綁成同一個東西，聽者的防衛就先卸下一半。這比 unfortunately 高明，因為它沒有替對方決定該不該難過。
swaps: The good news and the bad news are the same thing
There's an upside and a downside to that, and they're identical
cards.pmNote: 報壞消息時同時指出它帶來的資訊價值，比純道歉更能推進決策。
cards.episode: How have I been complicit in creating the conditions I say I don’t want? | Jerry Colonna (CEO of Reboot, executive coach, former VC)

alts.quote: It's so hard to give a founder hard feedback. Who wants to be the bearer of bad news?
alts.zh: 要給創辦人難聽的回饋真的很難。誰想當那個報壞消息的人？

alts.quote: You know what? We should ship. It's embarrassing, but that's strictly less bad than not getting the feedback you wanted.
alts.zh: 我覺得就出吧。是很難看沒錯，但這比拿不到你要的回饋還是好一點。

alts.quote: Nobody wants to hear it. Everybody wants to just think about these really cool models and how smart they are. But really it's just the hard work of getting really good data to the LLMs.
alts.zh: 沒有人想聽這個。大家都只想談那些很酷的模型有多聰明。但說到底，這就是把好資料餵給 LLM 的苦工。

cards.quote: Say more.
cards.zh: 多說一點。
cards.why: 兩個字，沒有問號，也沒有指定方向——對方會自己挑最想講的往下講。台灣人習慣問 Can you give me an example，那會把對方導到你想要的方向；Say more 不會。
swaps: Tell me more about that
Keep going
cards.pmNote: 1:1 時最好用的一句話：什麼都不引導，訊號最乾淨。
cards.episode: How have I been complicit in creating the conditions I say I don’t want? | Jerry Colonna (CEO of Reboot, executive coach, former VC)

alts.quote: I always ask, "What worked? What didn't work?"
alts.zh: 我每次都會問：哪裡有用？哪裡沒用？

alts.quote: So which game do you want to play? Let's just start there.
alts.zh: 所以你想玩哪一種賽局？我們就從這裡開始。

alts.quote: What else can people do to become better storytellers in business? I know this is a big question, but let's see where it goes.
alts.zh: 在商業場合還可以怎麼把故事講得更好？我知道這題很大，但我們就看看會聊到哪。

cards.pattern: I want to offer a different possibility. What if [替代方案]?
cards.quote: Now, I want to offer a different potential. What if what drove you was not quieting that voice, but what drove you was, oh, this is just fun?
cards.zh: 我想提供另一種可能。如果驅動你的不是想壓掉那個聲音，而是「這件事就是好玩」呢？
cards.why: offer 這個動詞是關鍵：把不同意見說成「我遞一個東西給你，你可以不拿」。搭配 What if 假設句，整段話沒有一個字在否定對方，但方向已經被換掉了。
swaps: Can I offer another way to look at it?
Here's an alternative read — what if...?
cards.pmNote: 提替代方案時用「提供」而非「反對」的框架，決策者比較不會進防衛狀態。
cards.episode: How have I been complicit in creating the conditions I say I don’t want? | Jerry Colonna (CEO of Reboot, executive coach, former VC)

alts.quote: The other thing that's a little bit different about what you said is that emotions do need to be felt.
alts.zh: 還有一點跟你剛剛講的稍微不一樣，就是情緒是真的需要被感受到的。

alts.quote: And again, I just want to make a huge caveat, this is not a judgment on any of these particular perspectives. It's more like I noticed a lot of it.
alts.zh: 再強調一次，我要先加一個很大的但書：我不是在評判這些觀點的好壞，比較像是我注意到它們特別多。

alts.quote: I agree with you. I totally agree with you. Now, I think it's the human aspect though of boldness, seeing the future in a way that a thing trained on priors cannot.
alts.zh: 我同意你，完全同意。不過我覺得，人的那一塊——那種膽識、那種能看見未來的能力，是只學過去資料的東西做不到的。

cards.quote: Now, to be clear, this is hard for me. I think it's hard for everybody.
cards.zh: 先講清楚，這件事對我來說也很難。我覺得對每個人都很難。
cards.why: 給完建議後補一句「我自己也做不好」，把 advice 從高處拉平。to be clear 在這裡不是澄清事實，而是澄清姿態——是英文裡拆掉權威感的常用開關。
swaps: For the record, I struggle with this too
I'm not saying I've got this figured out
cards.pmNote: 給建議時承認自己也在掙扎，對方採納的機率反而更高。
cards.episode: How have I been complicit in creating the conditions I say I don’t want? | Jerry Colonna (CEO of Reboot, executive coach, former VC)

alts.quote: I think this is a nuanced question and it's hard for me to say something on a podcast that'll actually be useful to people, but here's a couple of thoughts.
alts.zh: 我覺得這是個很有層次的問題，要在 podcast 上講出真的對別人有用的東西很難，不過我有幾個想法。

alts.quote: I don't think we should filter out AI content. I think we should let you know if content is AI content or not. That's hard, by the way.
alts.zh: 我不認為我們該把 AI 內容濾掉。我認為該做的是讓你知道這則內容是不是 AI 產的。順帶一提，這很難。

alts.quote: At that stage, what I think you've got is a positioning thesis... But it's just a thesis.
alts.zh: 在那個階段，你手上有的其實是一個「定位假設」……但它就只是個假設。

cards.pattern: Far be it from me to disagree with [權威], but I think he's wrong.
cards.quote: So far be it from me to disagree with Mike Tyson, but I think he's wrong.
cards.zh: 我哪敢跟泰森唱反調——但我覺得他錯了。
cards.why: Far be it from me to 是誇張的自貶，用來替後面的硬話買保險，語氣還帶點幽默。這種「先跪再打」的結構台灣人幾乎不會用，但在英文會議裡挑戰資深者非常好用。
swaps: Who am I to argue with X, but...
With all due respect to X, I'd push back
cards.pmNote: 挑戰高階或名人的觀點時，先明確承認地位差，反而讓內容被聽見。
cards.episode: How have I been complicit in creating the conditions I say I don’t want? | Jerry Colonna (CEO of Reboot, executive coach, former VC)

alts.quote: So, I think one needs to be a little bit cautious on what Dario says. And that's setting aside the cynical view that he's just doing that department stock, which I don't believe at all.
alts.zh: 我覺得對 Dario 講的話要保留一點。而且我這裡還先撇開那種比較酸的解讀——說他只是在替自家股價講話——那我完全不相信。

alts.quote: Instead, it's my instinct to go the wrong way on challenge directly and to pretend that I agree when I disagree, and then I wind up in the worst place of all, manipulative insincerity.
alts.zh: 我的本能反而是在「直接挑戰」這件事上走錯邊——明明不同意卻裝作同意，最後掉進最糟的那一格：虛偽的操弄。

alts.quote: The stability is important, don't get me wrong, but I do think that as a faster growing company, we need to consistently to reiterate not only the product but also our teams.
alts.zh: 穩定當然重要，別誤會，但我確實認為以一家成長更快的公司來說，我們要不斷迭代的不只是產品，還有團隊。

cards.quote: So is that my legacy? Yeah, and maybe there's some ego implicit in that, but can I go on for just a bit on this?
cards.zh: 所以那算是我的 legacy 嗎？算吧，裡面可能也有一點自我——不過我可以再多講一下嗎？
cards.why: 自己主動要求延長發言時間，而且先承認「這段可能有點自戀」。just a bit 界定範圍，讓主持人容易點頭。英文會議裡想多講一段而不被打斷，這是最有效的一句。
swaps: Can I take one more minute on this?
Mind if I keep going for a beat?
cards.pmNote: 要多要一點時間就明講並給出界線，比偷偷超時更容易被允許。
cards.episode: How have I been complicit in creating the conditions I say I don’t want? | Jerry Colonna (CEO of Reboot, executive coach, former VC)

alts.quote: I want to come back real quick to the activation metric because it's something that a lot of people somewhat misuse and think maybe incorrectly about.
alts.zh: 我想快速回到啟用指標那件事，因為很多人其實在誤用它、想錯方向。

alts.quote: So yeah, anyway, sorry, that's just a rant, but you should try it.
alts.zh: 總之，抱歉，剛剛那段只是我在碎念——但你真的該試試看。

alts.quote: Yeah. I actually have a better one for you.
alts.zh: 對。不過我有一個更好的例子可以給你。

cards.pattern: A year ago, I thought [舊看法]. We're clearly not. This is different.
cards.quote: A year ago, I thought we were going through a similar kind of transition. We're clearly not. This is different.
cards.zh: 一年前我以為我們正在經歷類似的轉型。顯然不是。這次不一樣。
cards.why: 收回立場的教科書結構：時間標記 + 舊看法 + 一句話撤回 + 新判斷。三個短句沒有一句在解釋或道歉，收得乾淨俐落，這正是英文裡改變想法該有的節奏。
swaps: I used to think X. I've changed my mind
Six months ago I'd have argued the opposite
cards.pmNote: 公開更新自己的判斷並標上時間點，是 strong opinions, loosely held 的實作方式。
cards.episode: How have I been complicit in creating the conditions I say I don’t want? | Jerry Colonna (CEO of Reboot, executive coach, former VC)

alts.quote: Transparently, I thought this was going to be an apocalypse. So I shared about a year ago that it's going to be an apocalypse. We have not seen it yet.
alts.zh: 老實說，我本來以為這會是世界末日。我一年前也是這樣公開講的。到目前為止並沒有發生。

alts.quote: Fast-forward to the middle of 2023, everything looks like it's going to be a transformer. So now our hypotheses are just wrong.
alts.zh: 快轉到 2023 年中，看起來全部都會走向 transformer。所以我們原本的假設就是錯的。

alts.quote: Four or five years ago, I would've said, well, personal skills, nothing. It's all the environment. I used to be one of those particular people.
alts.zh: 四五年前我會說：個人能力根本不重要，全都是環境造成的。我以前就是那一派的人。

cards.pattern: What I come back to — and I could be wrong — is [立場].
cards.quote: Now, what I come back to, and I could be wrong, but what I come back to is we're talking through a medium, a mediated experience.
cards.zh: 我一直會回到的一點——我也可能是錯的——就是：我們是透過一個媒介在對話，一種被中介過的經驗。
cards.why: and I could be wrong 插在句子中間而不是句尾，是母語者的習慣：先聲明不確定，再把立場講完，聽者就不會把它當成事後補救。what I come back to 又暗示這是反覆想過的結論，不是隨口。
swaps: I keep landing on — and I may be wrong here —
My current read, subject to change, is...
cards.pmNote: 把「不確定」放在主張前面，比放在後面更像自信而不是心虛。
cards.episode: How have I been complicit in creating the conditions I say I don’t want? | Jerry Colonna (CEO of Reboot, executive coach, former VC)

alts.quote: Now that may be completely wrong, and one of the points I make in the presentation is like, imagine having this conversation about the internet in 1997, what would you have got right?
alts.zh: 當然，這可能完全錯。我在簡報裡就有提到：想像我們在 1997 年談網路，你當時猜對過幾題？

alts.quote: We're going to go off and make this two-year, five-year, whatever, 10-year vision even, and we're going to point us towards something." But the way that the technology is changing now, we don't know what's going to happen in two years.
alts.zh: 我們本來會去做那種兩年、五年甚至十年的願景，把大家指向某個方向，但以現在技術變化的速度，我們根本不知道兩年後會發生什麼事。

alts.quote: So I think it has to come with a place of knowing that you don't know everything and humility to say, "Hey, I need help." And it actually earns you a lot more credit than you think.
alts.zh: 我覺得這要來自一個認知：你不可能什麼都懂，還要有那個謙虛去說「嘿，我需要幫忙」。而且這其實比你想像的更會替你加分。

cards.pattern: Here's what I have a problem with. First of all, [X] is a very helpful thing.
cards.quote: Here's what I have a problem with. First of all, having a growth mindset is a very, very helpful thing.
cards.zh: 我要說的是我對它的哪一點有意見。首先，擁有成長心態本身是非常非常有幫助的事。
cards.why: 先宣告「我有意見」再立刻讓步一大步，聽者的防衛值會被這個順序打亂。Here's what I have a problem with 也把批評範圍限縮成一個點，不會被理解成全盤否定。
swaps: My issue isn't with X itself — it's with how it gets used
Let me be precise about what I object to
cards.pmNote: 反對一個廣受認同的概念時，先承認它的價值再限縮攻擊面。
cards.episode: How have I been complicit in creating the conditions I say I don’t want? | Jerry Colonna (CEO of Reboot, executive coach, former VC)

alts.quote: Now, obviously if you live in a small town and they capped the well and gave all the water to the data center, then you're really pissed off. But that's a planning problem. That's not a data center problem.
alts.zh: 當然，如果你住在小鎮上，井被封了、水全給了資料中心，那你當然火大。但那是都市規劃的問題，不是資料中心的問題。

alts.quote: One, what a problem to have. Of all the problems in the world, "I'm overwhelmed by customer interest," is on the top list of problems I want to have.
alts.zh: 第一，這是多好的問題啊。世界上這麼多問題，「客戶熱情多到我應付不來」是我最想要的那幾個之一。

alts.quote: First let's examine the counterfactual, right? So let's start with the opposite of your question and say, "How would the world be sadder if we all just gave up on this?"
alts.zh: 我們先看反面情況吧。從你問題的相反面開始想：如果大家乾脆全都放棄這件事，世界會變得多糟？

cards.pattern: So, put succinctly, [一句話結論].
cards.quote: So put succinctly, stay attached to the growth and hold mindset a little loosely.
cards.zh: 簡單講就是：緊抓成長，心態就抓鬆一點。
cards.why: 講了一大段之後用 put succinctly 明確標記「以下是懶人包」，聽的人會自動提高注意力。這個標記詞比 in summary 更口語、更有份量。
swaps: To put it simply
If I had to boil it down to one line
cards.pmNote: 任何長論述最後都該留一句能被別人轉述的版本，不然對齊只到你為止。
cards.episode: How have I been complicit in creating the conditions I say I don’t want? | Jerry Colonna (CEO of Reboot, executive coach, former VC)

alts.quote: I think that's the key part, but let me pause there and then I'll talk a little bit about ChatGPT and some of my reasoning behind that.
alts.zh: 我覺得那是關鍵的部分，但我先停在這裡，然後再來講一點 ChatGPT 和我背後的理由。

alts.quote: Sometimes I'm like, "Who's owning this?" And it's like people don't know. That's why I think it's very important to have a single-threaded owner.
alts.zh: 有時候我問「這件事誰在 own？」結果大家都不知道。這就是為什麼一定要有一個單一負責人。

alts.quote: Is everyone in agreement with that or is there some dissent about whether that's an accurate portrayal of where we've landed with this conversation?
alts.zh: 大家都同意嗎？還是有人覺得我這樣描述我們的結論並不準確？

cards.pattern: Okay, I'm seeing something happen here. Every time we [情境], [模式].
cards.quote: Okay, guys, I'm seeing something happen here. Every time we get close to talking about something that's really painful, somebody makes a joke and all the energy disappears.
cards.zh: 好，我看到一個現象。每次我們快要談到真正痛的事情，就會有人開個玩笑，然後所有能量就消失了。
cards.why: 描述行為模式（every time... somebody...）而不指名任何人，讓整組人一起面對同一面鏡子。I'm seeing 又標明這只是我的觀察，不是判決。這是處理團隊動力最安全也最有效的句型。
swaps: I want to name a pattern I'm noticing
This is the third time we've done this — can we look at it?
cards.pmNote: 點名「模式」而不是點名「人」，是跨團隊卡關時唯一不會引爆的說法。
cards.episode: How have I been complicit in creating the conditions I say I don’t want? | Jerry Colonna (CEO of Reboot, executive coach, former VC)

alts.quote: I was like, "First of all, I don't even think I can work with you anymore given this environment you're creating, but I need to understand why you are talking to your team like that."
alts.zh: 我就說：「老實講，看到你製造出來的這種氣氛，我覺得我沒辦法再跟你合作下去了。但我還是想先搞懂，你為什麼會這樣跟你的團隊講話。」

alts.quote: The rule with the Waterline Model, which is very memorable, is you snorkel before you scuba. So, 80% of problems on teams actually happen because of structural issues or dynamics issues.
alts.zh: 這個模型的規則很好記：先浮潛，再深潛。團隊上八成的問題其實出在結構或運作方式，不是出在人。

alts.quote: I'm not interested in litigating the things that happened already when we can move forward.
alts.zh: 已經發生的事我沒興趣再打官司，我們可以往前走。

cards.pattern: I would argue that the more [X] you have, the more [Y] you have.
cards.quote: I would argue that the more power you have, the more moral responsibility you have to actually pause and figure out what it is that you're doing.
cards.zh: 我會主張：你握有的權力越大，你就越有道德責任停下來，搞清楚自己在做什麼。
cards.why: I would argue that 把主張標記成「經過論證的立場」而不是感想，聽者會準備接收理由。後面的 the more X, the more Y 是英文裡最好記的說理骨架，換內容就能重用。
swaps: My argument would be that...
The case I'd make is...
cards.pmNote: 資源與責任成正比的論證，是爭取或推辭跨組任務時的通用槓桿。
cards.episode: How have I been complicit in creating the conditions I say I don’t want? | Jerry Colonna (CEO of Reboot, executive coach, former VC)

alts.quote: The good news is, you're just like everybody else. The bad news is, you're mediocre just like everybody else.
alts.zh: 好消息是，你跟大家一樣；壞消息是，你跟大家一樣平庸。

alts.quote: I'm just trying to argue this advice applied to a startup that's too early is actively not helpful.
alts.zh: 我只是想主張：把這套建議套在太早期的新創身上，是「主動有害」而不只是沒用。

alts.quote: I think with hiring, it's funny, man, there's so much hiring advice online and you read it and you're like, "Yeah, this is super obvious." And then when you live it, you're suddenly like, "Aah, this is why people say this."
alts.zh: 招人這件事很好笑，網路上一堆建議，你看的時候都覺得「這不是廢話嗎」。等你真的經歷過，才會突然懂「喔，原來大家是這個意思」。

cards.pattern: How can you [期待 X] if you can't tolerate [X 的必然後果]?
cards.quote: How can you hire people whom you expect to make decisions without running them through you if you can't tolerate them making a decision that you disagree with?
cards.zh: 如果你受不了他們做出你不同意的決定，你怎麼可能招到那種不需要事事回報你就能決策的人？
cards.why: 把對方的抱怨和他自己的行為擺進同一個句子，矛盾自己浮出來，你一個字都不用評論。這種 Socratic 反問是英文裡最有力也最不失禮的挑戰方式。
swaps: You can't ask for X and also refuse Y
Those two things can't both be true — which one do you want?
cards.pmNote: 授權失敗多半不是人不行，是主管無法忍受不同意的決定。
cards.episode: How have I been complicit in creating the conditions I say I don’t want? | Jerry Colonna (CEO of Reboot, executive coach, former VC)

alts.quote: They're not useful as decision-making tools because nobody would ever argue the opposite. Nobody ever sat in a meeting and said, "Oh, forget clear. Let's try to make it as confusing as possible."
alts.zh: 這些東西沒辦法拿來做決策，因為根本不會有人主張反面。從來沒有人在會議上說：「別管清楚了，我們把它做得越難懂越好。」

alts.quote: One thing I've learned is that I think people are really good at coming up with very rational sounding reasons to not do things that just make them uncomfortable.
alts.zh: 我學到一件事：人非常擅長替「其實只是讓自己不舒服的事」找出聽起來很有道理的理由。

alts.quote: when you're making decisions that could be described as hostile towards your customers, but a net positive for the business, you're probably not thinking long-term enough
alts.zh: 當你在做的決定可以被形容為「對客戶不友善、但對公司淨正面」時，多半代表你想得還不夠長。

cards.pattern: One thing to ask yourself is: what draws me to this in the first place?
cards.quote: One of the things to ask oneself is what draws me to this position in the first place?
cards.zh: 有個可以問自己的問題是：當初到底是什麼把我吸引到這個位置的？
cards.why: in the first place 是英文裡把時間軸拉回起點的關鍵詞組，逼人回頭看最初的動機。用 one of the things to ask oneself 包裝，等於把問題輕輕放在桌上，不指定誰要撿。
swaps: What made you take this on originally?
What was the appeal at the start?
cards.pmNote: 抱怨環境之前先問自己為何選擇它，能區分「該修的問題」和「該離開的局」。
cards.episode: How have I been complicit in creating the conditions I say I don’t want? | Jerry Colonna (CEO of Reboot, executive coach, former VC)

alts.quote: And one of the things I'll often ask is, if you had another couple days, what would you do with this?
alts.zh: 我很常問的一個問題是：如果再多給你幾天，你會拿這個東西做什麼？

alts.quote: One of the things I ask a lot in product review when someone says, "Hey, we want to run an experiment," is, "Okay, what do we do if it's green? What do we do if it's red?"
alts.zh: 有人說「我們想跑個實驗」，我在產品評審上最常問的就是：「如果結果是綠的我們做什麼？紅的又做什麼？」

alts.quote: I ask them, "What are your goals when it comes to coaching? Roll it forward six months, what have you gotten done in your coaching experience."
alts.zh: 我會問他們：「你找教練的目標是什麼？把時間快轉六個月，那時候你在教練這件事上完成了什麼？」

cards.quote: If this job were open, I'd like to be considered for it.
cards.zh: 如果這個職位有空缺，我希望能被列入考慮。
cards.why: 用假設語氣（were / I'd）把野心講出來，但不逼對方現在回應，所以被拒絕也不傷。be considered for 是被動式的關鍵：你要的是「進入名單」，不是「給我」——這個分寸台灣人很難自己抓出來。
swaps: I'd love to be in the mix if that ever opens up
Keep me in mind for that role
cards.pmNote: 沒說出口的職涯意願，主管永遠不會替你猜到。
cards.episode: How to own your career growth and become a powerful product leader | Deb Liu, Ancestry (ex-Facebook, PayPal)

alts.quote: What you do is up to you, but by the next time we talk, you should have made a move.” We considered our options: shut down, restart, or sell the company.
alts.zh: 「怎麼做由你決定，但下次我們談之前，你應該已經動了。」我們評估了選項：關掉、重來，或把公司賣掉。

alts.quote: Hey, I'm an early stage startup. We have a lot to learn. Can we kind of gain your insight into how this problem is manifesting on your side?
alts.zh: 嗨，我們是很早期的新創，還有很多要學。能不能請教你，這個問題在你們那邊是怎麼呈現的？

alts.quote: Hey, I'm really enjoying working with you. I'm wondering is there some way I could help you that would also help me reach my goal?
alts.zh: 嘿，跟你合作我覺得很愉快。我在想，有沒有什麼事我可以幫你、同時也能幫我朝目標前進的？

cards.pattern: The thing a lot of [對象] don't realize is that you can love something to death.
cards.quote: The thing that I think a lot of large companies don't realize is that you can love something to death.
cards.zh: 很多大公司沒意識到的一件事是：你可以把一個東西「愛到死」。
cards.why: love something to death 用一個反直覺的搭配，一句話擋掉「多給資源、多開會、多關注」的好意。要拒絕善意的介入時，這比 please leave us alone 有效得多。
swaps: Too much attention can kill a new product
We'd rather have less oversight and more room
cards.pmNote: 早期產品最需要的不是資源，是不被檢視的空間。
cards.episode: How to own your career growth and become a powerful product leader | Deb Liu, Ancestry (ex-Facebook, PayPal)

alts.quote: If none of those companies are using it, I'm like, "Don't bother me. It's either snake oil or it's not proven yet."
alts.zh: 如果那些公司一家都沒在用，那我的反應就是：別來煩我，這東西不是江湖偏方，就是還沒被驗證。

alts.quote: We are about to launch something and then for example I or someone else goes to look at it and sees, "Oh, this doesn't feel right and we should fix it so I don't think we should launch this now."
alts.zh: 我們正要上線，然後我或別人去看了一眼，就會說：「這感覺不對，應該修一下，我覺得現在還不能上。」

alts.quote: It's like, I don't think I can predict that. I think a much better use of my time is being very flexible and adaptable at a time like this.
alts.zh: 我不覺得我預測得了那個。我覺得我的時間花在保持彈性、快速調整上，回報高得多。

cards.pattern: By the way, [殘酷數據]. So half of you are going to [後果]. Do you have the resilience to do that?
cards.quote: By the way, a very, very successful company for a new set of products has a 50% hit rate. So half of you are going to come back in a year and have a different job. Do you have the resilience to do that?
cards.zh: 順帶一提，一家非常成功的公司做新產品的成功率大概是五成。所以你們有一半的人一年後會換一份工作。你們有那個韌性嗎？
cards.why: 用 By the way 淡化開場，再丟出殘酷數字，最後用一個問題把選擇權交回去。這三拍是英文裡「期望管理」的完整結構：不恐嚇、不美化、要求對方自己決定。
swaps: Just so you go in with eyes open, the base rate is...
Half of these bets won't survive the year — are you okay with that?
cards.pmNote: 先講清楚失敗率再讓人選，事後就不必處理被騙的感覺。
cards.episode: How to own your career growth and become a powerful product leader | Deb Liu, Ancestry (ex-Facebook, PayPal)

alts.quote: There is literally no faster way to demoralize high performers than going back on a promise.
alts.zh: 要讓高績效的人瞬間心死，沒有比毀約更快的方法了。

alts.quote: Give me a day and I'll come back to you.
alts.zh: 給我一天，我再回來找你談。

alts.quote: This is exactly where we are. This is what we're going to do and the next hour, and this is when you'll get your next update. I will update you again at 9:00 AM.
alts.zh: 目前的狀況就是這樣。接下來一小時我們要做的是這些，下一次更新會在什麼時候。我九點會再跟你更新一次。

cards.pattern: If you had to write a spec for your career, what's in there? What are your milestones?
cards.quote: But if I said you had to write a spec for your career, what's in there? What are your milestones? What are the skills?
cards.zh: 如果我要你替自己的職涯寫一份 spec，裡面會有什麼？你的里程碑是什麼？需要哪些技能？
cards.why: 把對方每天在用的專業框架（spec）反過來套在他自己身上，一秒讓抽象的職涯焦慮變成可填的欄位。這種「借用對方的語言」是教練式提問最強的一招。
swaps: What would the roadmap for your own career look like?
If your career were a product, what's the north star metric?
cards.pmNote: 會替產品訂目標的人，常常忘了替自己訂；1:1 時借用他的框架最有效。
cards.episode: How to own your career growth and become a powerful product leader | Deb Liu, Ancestry (ex-Facebook, PayPal)

alts.quote: Most work is wasted in AEO, so how do you know what's not wasted?
alts.zh: AEO 上大多數的工都是白做的——那你怎麼知道哪些沒白做？

alts.quote: Walk me through what's living in your head right now.
alts.zh: 帶我走一遍你現在腦子裡裝的東西。

alts.quote: Okay, so I noticed that I needed to change that at some point, and actually found a solution, again, late in my career, but I found a solution, because I asked myself this question, which is, "Why am I so busy?
alts.zh: 我注意到我某個時間點需要改掉這個，後來真的找到解法——雖然是職涯很後期才找到——因為我問了自己一個問題：「我為什麼這麼忙？」

cards.pattern: I noticed that you never [行為] when we [情境].
cards.quote: I asked her once, I said, "I noticed that you never answer questions when we do these presentations."
cards.zh: 我有一次問她：「我注意到，我們在做這些簡報的時候，你從來不回答問題。」
cards.why: I noticed 只陳述可觀察的行為，不含評價與推論，對方沒有東西可以否認，只能解釋。這是 radical candor 在句型層級的落實，比 You should speak up more 安全太多。
swaps: I've noticed a pattern in meetings
Something I've observed a few times now
cards.pmNote: 回饋只講觀察到的行為，對方才會告訴你背後真正的原因。
cards.episode: How to own your career growth and become a powerful product leader | Deb Liu, Ancestry (ex-Facebook, PayPal)

alts.quote: At one point I noticed I was spending six to 7% of my week on these areas, these areas where I can truly be world-class at.
alts.zh: 有一陣子我注意到，我一週只花百分之六到七的時間在這些領域上——那些我真的能做到世界頂尖的領域。

alts.quote: Direct is kind. And it feels kind or, really, honestly, easy to avoid these things or to work around them.
alts.zh: 直說才是善意。避開不談、繞過去，感覺很體貼，其實只是比較輕鬆而已。

alts.quote: I noticed we have this opportunity.
alts.zh: 我注意到我們有這個機會。

cards.pattern: What if I called it [重新命名]? What if I called it [重新命名]?
cards.quote: What if I called it educating your manager about all the great work your team has been doing? What if I called it helping people see why your team should get more resources?
cards.zh: 如果我把它叫做「讓主管了解你的團隊做了哪些很棒的事」呢？如果我把它叫做「幫大家看見為什麼你的團隊該拿到更多資源」呢？
cards.why: 重新命名一件事，就重新分配了它的道德重量：self-promotion 變成 educating，主角從「我」換成「團隊」。用 What if I called it 而不是直接改名，等於邀請對方一起換框，抗拒最小。
swaps: What if we called it visibility instead of self-promotion?
Try thinking of it as advocating for your team
cards.pmNote: 自評與績效簡報寫的是團隊拿資源的理由，不是個人邀功。
cards.episode: How to own your career growth and become a powerful product leader | Deb Liu, Ancestry (ex-Facebook, PayPal)

alts.quote: When somebody is using AI to solve a problem that they wouldn't have used AI before, give them a shout-out in the team meeting, let them demo that. Again, make them feel like a million bucks for doing the thing.
alts.zh: 只要有人用 AI 解掉一個他以前不會這樣解的問題，就在團隊會議上點名讚美他，讓他 demo 一次。就是要讓他爽到不行。

alts.quote: Credit our CEO with this, that I shared the data with him and he basically told the product team, "We are putting a complete freeze on the product development roadmap."
alts.zh: 這件事要歸功給我們執行長：我把數據給他看，他就直接跟產品團隊說「產品路線圖全面凍結」。

alts.quote: And that means being very clear when people are not meeting expectations, making it very clear that questioning ideas is not questioning innate talent.
alts.zh: 這代表在別人沒達到期待時要講得很清楚，同時也要講清楚：質疑一個想法，不等於質疑一個人的天賦。

cards.quote: And I said, "Well, then why do you put yourself in his category instead of mine?"
cards.zh: 我就說：「那你為什麼把自己歸到他那一類，而不是我這一類？」
cards.why: 先讓對方承認一個他認同的反例，再問他為何不把自己放進去。整段沒有安慰、沒有說教，用一個問題就拆掉自我設限，是教練式提問的高階示範。
swaps: Why assume you'd be the bad version of that?
What makes you the exception in the wrong direction?
cards.pmNote: 帶人時找到對方自己認同的正面樣本，比你講一百句鼓勵有用。
cards.episode: How to own your career growth and become a powerful product leader | Deb Liu, Ancestry (ex-Facebook, PayPal)

alts.quote: So if your partner comes to you and says that marketing plan or that product roadmap that you put together, not good, do you take it as the plan is not good and let's talk about what we can actually do to fix it?
alts.zh: 如果你的夥伴跟你說，你做的行銷計畫或產品路線圖不好，你會理解成「這份計畫不好，我們來談怎麼修」嗎？

alts.quote: People call me sometimes they're like "I want to know if I have product market fit." Well, the fact that you have time to call me and ask me this question already tells me the answer.
alts.zh: 有人打給我說：「我想知道我們有沒有 PMF。」嗯，你有空打這通電話問我，這件事本身就給了答案。

alts.quote: put a calendar invite, let it renew every three months. You're going to snooze it a couple of times, I get it, I've seen this many, many times before. But just do something, even if it's super small.
alts.zh: 開一個行事曆邀請，每三個月自動重複。你一定會按掉個幾次，我懂，我看過太多次了。但就是做點什麼，再小都好。

cards.pattern: I think we do a disservice when we say [說法], because it's a skill like any other.
cards.quote: I think we do a disservice when we say we're not good at speaking up because it's a skill like any other.
cards.zh: 我覺得我們說自己「不擅長發言」是在害自己，因為那跟其他技能沒有兩樣。
cards.why: do a disservice 指的是「好意造成的傷害」，用來反駁一個大家習以為常的自我開脫，語氣是心疼不是責備。把「個性」改講成 skill，責任就從天生變成可練。
swaps: Calling it a personality trait lets us off the hook
That's a skill, not a fixed trait
cards.pmNote: 把「我就是這種人」翻譯成「這是一項還沒練的技能」，才有帶人的著力點。
cards.episode: How to own your career growth and become a powerful product leader | Deb Liu, Ancestry (ex-Facebook, PayPal)

alts.quote: The only answer I think one can have is, don't stick your head in the sand and say, "I hate all of this stuff," because that gives you a great feeling of moral superiority.
alts.zh: 我覺得唯一的答案是：別把頭埋進沙子裡說「我討厭這些東西」，因為那只會讓你很有道德優越感。

alts.quote: And it's not because people are bad people. I think most people are really well-intentioned. But what happens when you have people that join and you didn't really need them?
alts.zh: 這不是因為誰是壞人，我覺得大多數人動機都很好。但問題是：當你招了一批其實不需要的人，會發生什麼事？

alts.quote: Of course, I don't want to be cruel to the people who are putting their hearts into that work, because the Figma file is beautiful. It's just coming a little early.
alts.zh: 當然，我不想對那些真心投入的人太苛刻——那些 Figma 檔真的很漂亮。只是它來得太早了一點。

cards.quote: So especially when you're meeting with a new engineering team for the first time, actually ask them, what is one thing I can do to help you this week?
cards.zh: 尤其是第一次跟新的工程團隊碰面時，真的去問他們：這禮拜我可以幫上哪一件事？
cards.why: one thing 和 this week 兩個限制詞是精髓：把一個容易被敷衍的客套問句，變成一個小到不能拒絕的具體請求。沒有這兩個限制，答案永遠是 nothing, we're good。
swaps: What's one thing I could take off your plate this week?
Give me one small thing I can help with
cards.pmNote: 新人建立信任最快的方式是先付出一次可交付的小忙。
cards.episode: How to own your career growth and become a powerful product leader | Deb Liu, Ancestry (ex-Facebook, PayPal)

alts.quote: So first of all, when you're in the early innings, you'll actually get more useful advice often from your peers because they're going through the same thing.
alts.zh: 首先，在很前期的階段，你從同輩那裡拿到的建議其實比較有用，因為他們正在經歷一模一樣的事。

alts.quote: Say, "Hey, let's have a workshop first. I have this problem. I think that you can help me fix it."
alts.zh: 你就說：「嘿，我們先辦一場工作坊吧。我手上有這個問題，我覺得你可以幫我解。」

alts.quote: And don't ask them, "Should I do it?" Ask them, "Tell me for each thing, can you give me the pros and cons of doing it?"
alts.zh: 不要問他們「我該不該做？」要問他們「每一個做法的利弊分別是什麼？」

cards.pattern: I would like to carve [X%] of my time for [目的], and I'm happy to do this work [Y%] of the time.
cards.quote: Okay. I would like to carve 20% of my time listening and I'm happy to do this work 80% of the time.
cards.zh: 好，我想切出兩成的時間去聽，另外八成的時間我很樂意投入手上的工作。
cards.why: carve 是「切出一塊」，比 spend 更有守住邊界的意味。先講你要拿走的比例，再立刻交出剩下的比例，主管聽到的是交易而不是討價還價。
swaps: I'd like to protect one day a week for this
Can we ring-fence 20% for discovery?
cards.pmNote: 要時間時同時承諾產出比例，通過率遠高於只說「我需要時間」。
cards.episode: How to own your career growth and become a powerful product leader | Deb Liu, Ancestry (ex-Facebook, PayPal)

alts.quote: It might be easier if I just go, I might be able to save you some time and some energy if I just joined you.
alts.zh: 也許我直接去比較快，我一起進去的話，說不定可以幫你省下一些時間跟力氣。

alts.quote: So instead of just sending the link, I usually start the email with something like looking forward to connecting, feel free to share, sometimes you're available or if easier, you can choose to find time on my calendar using the Calendly link here.
alts.zh: 所以我不會只丟一個連結，我通常這樣開頭：很期待跟你聊，你可以直接給我幾個方便的時間，或者比較省事的話，也可以用這裡的 Calendly 連結直接約。

alts.quote: And then I propose a little contingency plan, like hey, if that doesn't work out, here's the rollback plan, here's the maximum impact it will have done in a negative way, which is not going to be too much.
alts.zh: 然後我會提一個小小的備案：如果沒成，這是回滾計畫，這是最壞情況下的負面影響——而且不會太大。

cards.quote: Here's what I heard from all of you. I'm listening, I hear this and here's what I want to do about it.
cards.zh: 以下是我從各位那裡聽到的。我有在聽，我聽到了，接下來我打算這樣做。
cards.why: 三段式收斂：我聽到什麼 → 我確實有在聽 → 我要做什麼。中間那句看似多餘，其實是整段的關鍵——它回應的是情緒，不是資訊。
swaps: Here's what I took away from those conversations
This is what I heard, and this is what happens next
cards.pmNote: listening tour 做完一定要公開回饋摘要，否則等於沒做。
cards.episode: How to own your career growth and become a powerful product leader | Deb Liu, Ancestry (ex-Facebook, PayPal)

alts.quote: So to your question, you're a feature team. You want to give it a shot, be in a real product team. These are the four things you need to go out and do.
alts.zh: 回到你的問題：你在一支功能團隊，想試試看真正的產品團隊怎麼運作——那你要去做的就是這四件事。

alts.quote: I still may insert myself and say, "Hey, let me pause here for a second and try to capture what has been said." This is what I've heard.
alts.zh: 我還是會切進去說：「欸，我先暫停一下，把剛剛講的整理一下。」以下是我聽到的。

alts.quote: So just to kind of recap, you want it to feel like it's core and critical to the company. You want it to feel like it's everyone's success.
alts.zh: 所以簡單複述一下：你希望它讓人覺得對公司是核心、關鍵的；你希望它是所有人的成功。

cards.quote: And so I always say diagnose before you treat.
cards.zh: 所以我常說：先診斷，再開藥。
cards.why: 借醫療的動詞對比，四個字就把「別急著解決」講完，而且沒有指責誰躁進。這種可以被別人轉述的短語，在會議裡的傳播力遠勝一整段道理。
swaps: Let's diagnose before we prescribe
We're treating symptoms before we know the cause
cards.pmNote: 跳過問題定義直接做方案，是新任 PM 最貴的錯誤。
cards.episode: How to own your career growth and become a powerful product leader | Deb Liu, Ancestry (ex-Facebook, PayPal)

alts.quote: So there's, I wouldn't say a checklist, but there's a series of questions that I asked to diagnose why is growth slowing in this order, because it's one of these things where the first one that's a problem, if you don't fix that, it doesn't matter if you fix one of the ones below.
alts.zh: 我不會說那是一張檢查清單，但我確實有一組問題，會照順序問下去診斷成長為什麼變慢——因為只要最前面那個沒修，後面修再多都沒用。

alts.quote: The way I think about this is that emotions are like a tube, let's say, and there's water moving through the tube.
alts.zh: 我自己是這樣想這件事的：情緒像一根管子，裡面有水在流。

alts.quote: Let's just say there's a product manager and nobody's ever coached this poor person, and so they really don't know much.
alts.zh: 我們就假設有一個產品經理，從來沒有人帶過他，所以他其實懂得不多。

cards.pattern: What they're saying is not [誤讀], it's that [真正的意思].
cards.quote: No, no, no. What they're saying is not that you're a bad product person, it's that you need to do a better job communicating or connecting.
cards.zh: 不不不。他們講的不是你是個爛 PM，而是你在溝通、在建立連結這件事上要做得更好。
cards.why: not X, it's Y 的對照結構，一句話把人身評價和行為建議切開。幫別人翻譯他收到的回饋時，這是最好用的句型——先擋掉最痛的誤讀，再放回可行動的版本。
swaps: That's feedback about the behavior, not about you
They're not questioning your judgment — they want more context
cards.pmNote: 把回饋從「你這個人」翻譯成「這個行為」，對方才有辦法改。
cards.episode: How to own your career growth and become a powerful product leader | Deb Liu, Ancestry (ex-Facebook, PayPal)

alts.quote: And it's not because people are bad people. I think most people are really well-intentioned. But what happens when you have people that join and you didn't really need them?
alts.zh: 這不是因為誰是壞人，我覺得大多數人動機都很好。但問題是：當你招了一批其實不需要的人，會發生什麼事？

alts.quote: And I honestly think saying, "You are not doing a good job," is much kinder than, "I think you can improve on this aspect or that aspect."
alts.zh: 老實說我覺得直接講「你做得不夠好」，其實比「我覺得你在某某方面可以再進步」還要仁慈。

alts.quote: I'm not saying Google's bad, but Google used to have this don't be evil ethos, and it got lost.
alts.zh: 我不是說 Google 很爛，但 Google 以前有「不作惡」那套精神，後來弄丟了。

cards.quote: Hey, I'm really enjoying working with you. I'm wondering is there some way I could help you that would also help me reach my goal?
cards.zh: 嘿，跟你合作我覺得很愉快。我在想，有沒有什麼事我可以幫你、同時也能幫我朝目標前進的？
cards.why: 整句的重量在 that would also：把自己的需求掛在「幫你」後面，變成雙贏的搜尋題而不是索取。I'm wondering 又讓它保持在探詢語氣，主管沒答應也不尷尬。
swaps: Is there something you need that would also stretch me in this direction?
What could I take on that helps you and builds this skill for me?
cards.pmNote: 把個人成長需求綁在主管的痛點上，是升遷談判成功率最高的框架。
cards.episode: Taking control of your career | Ethan Evans (Amazon)

alts.quote: Hey, I'm an early stage startup. We have a lot to learn. Can we kind of gain your insight into how this problem is manifesting on your side?
alts.zh: 嗨，我們是很早期的新創，還有很多要學。能不能請教你，這個問題在你們那邊是怎麼呈現的？

alts.quote: It might actually mean a proactive conversation with your manager or the leadership to say, "I love what I'm doing here, and I would also like to learn a little bit more. And here's what I'm interested in."
alts.zh: 這可能只是主動找主管或高層談一次，跟他說：「我很喜歡現在做的事，同時我也想再多學一些，這是我有興趣的方向。」

alts.quote: This is people you used to work with before, go ask them, "Hey, what did I do well, what do you think my strengths are? What do you think I'm a fit for?
alts.zh: 去問以前的同事：「我哪裡做得好？你覺得我的強項是什麼？我是這樣想的——你覺得我對自己的認知準確嗎？」

cards.quote: Two things I'd love to clarify.
cards.zh: 有兩件事我想澄清一下。
cards.why: 先報數字（two things）讓聽者知道要留多少注意力，再用 I'd love to 把「更正」講得像貢獻。這是英文簡報和會議裡最容易上手的結構標記。
swaps: A couple of things worth clarifying
Let me clean up two points
cards.pmNote: 開口前先報項目數，聽眾才知道你什麼時候會講完。
cards.episode: Taking control of your career | Ethan Evans (Amazon)

alts.quote: Just to reinforce this point, what are the three things again? In case folks didn't catch it all.
alts.zh: 為了把這個重點再壓一次——那三件事到底是哪三件？怕大家剛剛沒全部聽清楚。

alts.quote: Just to be clear, I love Claude.
alts.zh: 先說清楚，我很愛 Claude。

alts.quote: Please note that don't mix transparency and fairness with being predictable. Those are very different things.
alts.zh: 請注意，不要把「透明與公平」跟「可預測」混為一談。這是兩件很不一樣的事。

cards.pattern: I'd be honest with people and say some patience is required. However, there is a lot you can do.
cards.quote: I would be honest with people and say some patience is required. However, there is a lot you can do. A lot is in your control.
cards.zh: 我會誠實地說：這需要一點耐心。不過，你能做的事很多，很多都在你的掌控裡。
cards.why: 報壞消息的雙拍結構：先不粉飾（patience is required），再立刻把 agency 還給對方（in your control）。少了後半句是打擊，少了前半句是畫大餅，兩句一起才是專業。
swaps: I won't sugarcoat it — this takes time. But here's what's in your hands
Realistically we're waiting. Meanwhile, here's what we control
cards.pmNote: 延期或凍結的消息一定要配上「現在能做什麼」，否則團隊只會空轉。
cards.episode: Taking control of your career | Ethan Evans (Amazon)

alts.quote: We can't just cut the scope and say, "Oh, well now, we managed to ship inside of six weeks." That's going to kill everybody's morale.
alts.zh: 我們不能就這樣砍掉範圍，然後說「你看，我們六週內出貨了」。那會把所有人的士氣打死。

alts.quote: And at Uber, I learned this because, it pains me to say this, but really the price and the ETA at Uber was the product.
alts.zh: 我在 Uber 學到這件事——講出來我自己都有點痛——但價格跟預估時間，那才是 Uber 真正的產品。

alts.quote: I definitely don't think it was obvious to everyone, and I can definitely say that because we were given a pretty strict deadline that we needed to launch by and I pushed it out three times.
alts.zh: 我完全不覺得這對所有人來說是顯而易見的，我敢這樣說是因為我們當初拿到一個很硬的上線死線，而我把它往後推了三次。

cards.pattern: The first thing I did was I owned it. Yes, it's not working. It's my fault. I will deal with it.
cards.quote: Yes, it's not working. It's my fault. I will deal with it.
cards.zh: 我做的第一件事就是認下來。我說：「對，它現在是壞的。是我的錯。我會處理。」
cards.why: 三個短句、零解釋、零形容詞：承認事實、認領責任、宣告行動。台灣人（和多數人）出事時的直覺是先解釋原因，而在英文語境裡，任何在 It's my fault 之前出現的解釋都會被聽成推卸。
swaps: This one's on me. I'm on it
That was my call and it was wrong. Here's what I'm doing
cards.pmNote: 事故當下的第一句話決定你之後有沒有機會解釋來龍去脈。
cards.episode: Taking control of your career | Ethan Evans (Amazon)

alts.quote: And the big epiphany, we already talked about it, it shouldn't have taken me this long to realize that anytime an employee fails, it's your fault.
alts.zh: 我最大的頓悟——其實前面也提過——是我不該這麼晚才明白：只要有員工陣亡，那都是你的錯。

alts.quote: And guess what? It's all okay. It's not a loss, it's a lesson.
alts.zh: 然後你知道嗎？那都沒關係。那不是損失，那是一課。

alts.quote: So it's someone that as a leader, you are in the hot seat and you can take accountability. So if some of these things don't pan out, it's on you and not on your team, and give your team permission to fail.
alts.zh: 身為領導者，你就是坐在火線上、要負起責任的人。如果這些事沒成，那是你的責任，不是團隊的責任——同時給團隊失敗的許可。

cards.pattern: This is exactly where we are. This is what we're going to do in the next hour. I will update you again at [時間].
cards.quote: This is exactly where we are. This is what we're going to do and the next hour, and this is when you'll get your next update. I will update you again at 9:00 AM.
cards.zh: 目前的狀況就是這樣。接下來一小時我們要做的是這些，下一次更新會在什麼時候。我九點會再跟你更新一次。
cards.why: 危機溝通的三欄位：現況、下一小時的動作、下次更新時間。第三欄是最多人漏掉也最關鍵的一欄——主動給下次更新時間，就是在買時間，而且對方不會來微管理你。
swaps: Status, next step, next update — I'll ping you at the top of the hour
Nothing new to report yet; next update in 60 minutes
cards.pmNote: 事故期間的節奏承諾（每小時一次）比事故內容本身更能穩住上層。
cards.episode: Taking control of your career | Ethan Evans (Amazon)

alts.quote: By the way, a very, very successful company for a new set of products has a 50% hit rate. So half of you are going to come back in a year and have a different job. Do you have the resilience to do that?
alts.zh: 順帶一提，一家非常成功的公司做新產品的成功率大概是五成。所以你們有一半的人一年後會換一份工作。你們有那個韌性嗎？

alts.quote: In those stages, the experience can be a little janky or it's not that polished, but we're okay with it because we are saying, "It's not finished. We just want to get your feedback early so we can make it better."
alts.zh: 那個階段體驗可能有點卡、不太精緻，但我們可以接受，因為我們有先講清楚：「這還沒完成，我們只是想早點拿到你的回饋，好把它做得更好。」

alts.quote: We can't just cut the scope and say, "Oh, well now, we managed to ship inside of six weeks." That's going to kill everybody's morale.
alts.zh: 我們不能就這樣砍掉範圍，然後說「你看，我們六週內出貨了」。那會把所有人的士氣打死。

cards.pattern: We've all been there, we know it's miserable. What can we do to help?
cards.quote: We've all been under Jeff's Eye of Sauron, we know it's miserable. What can we do to help?
cards.zh: 我們都被那道索倫之眼盯過，知道那有多難受。我們能幫上什麼？
cards.why: 先用共同經驗把對方從「犯錯的人」拉回「我們這群人」，再問要什麼幫助。少了前半句，後半句會像上級查勤；有了前半句，才是同盟。
swaps: Been there. What do you need?
We've all had one of these. How can we help?
cards.pmNote: 有人在火線上時，先表達同盟再問需求，對方才敢說出真正缺什麼。
cards.episode: Taking control of your career | Ethan Evans (Amazon)

alts.quote: It's not that one of my PM counterparts couldn't bring a lot to the design table, it's just I need you to play that position.
alts.zh: 不是說 PM 對設計沒有貢獻——他們當然有；只是我需要你守住你的位置。

alts.quote: I was like, "First of all, I don't even think I can work with you anymore given this environment you're creating, but I need to understand why you are talking to your team like that."
alts.zh: 我就說：「老實講，看到你製造出來的這種氣氛，我覺得我沒辦法再跟你合作下去了。但我還是想先搞懂，你為什麼會這樣跟你的團隊講話。」

alts.quote: This stress between product and sales is a good thing. It's a sign of a well-run B2B company when there is stress between product and sales.
alts.zh: 產品跟業務之間的緊張是好事。B2B 公司如果產品跟業務之間有張力，那才叫營運健康。

cards.quote: So how are you doing? I bet it's been a hard week.
cards.zh: 所以你還好嗎？我猜這禮拜很難熬吧。
cards.why: 衝突之後的修復句：不提事故、不再追責，只認可對方的處境。I bet 是英文裡替對方說出感受又不強加的句型——比 Are you okay? 更貼近，也更難拒絕。
swaps: That can't have been fun. How are you holding up?
Rough week, I imagine
cards.pmNote: 衝突後主動修補關係的人通常是層級較高的那一方，這一步決定信任會不會回來。
cards.episode: Taking control of your career | Ethan Evans (Amazon)

alts.quote: We're not better than you, you're not better than us, it's just this is how we do things here.
alts.zh: 我們沒有比你好，你也沒有比我們好，就只是我們這裡是這樣做事的。

alts.quote: It's not that one of my PM counterparts couldn't bring a lot to the design table, it's just I need you to play that position.
alts.zh: 不是說 PM 對設計沒有貢獻——他們當然有；只是我需要你守住你的位置。

alts.quote: This stress between product and sales is a good thing. It's a sign of a well-run B2B company when there is stress between product and sales.
alts.zh: 產品跟業務之間的緊張是好事。B2B 公司如果產品跟業務之間有張力，那才叫營運健康。

cards.quote: Yeah, I messed up. But I know I'm still a good person and a good worker. Yes, I made a mistake, but I'm going to move on.
cards.zh: 對，我搞砸了。但我知道我還是個好人、也還是個好的工作者。對，我犯了錯，但我要往前走。
cards.why: 承認錯誤與維持自我價值同時成立——這是英文職場語言裡很重要、台灣人卻常常做不到的分離。連續用兩次 Yes...but 的節奏，讀起來像在對自己宣誓，可以直接照抄。
swaps: I own the mistake, but I'm not going to live in it
Bad call, not a bad career
cards.pmNote: postmortem 的目的是修系統不是修人；把羞恥留下來只會讓人隱瞞下一個錯。
cards.episode: Taking control of your career | Ethan Evans (Amazon)

alts.quote: And I'll tell you, ProfitWell, this was a big mistake. Yes, it was a great exit, we sold for over $200 million, et cetera, but we probably, if we had taken money, we could have had a billion-dollar exit
alts.zh: 老實說 ProfitWell 這件事是個大失誤。是啦，出場很漂亮，賣了兩億多美元，但如果我們當初有拿錢，可能會是十億等級的出場。

alts.quote: But basically what happened is that we pushed out an update that made the model more likely to tell you things that sound good in the moment.
alts.zh: 簡單講就是，我們推了一個更新，結果讓模型更容易講出那種當下聽起來很順耳的話。

alts.quote: The biggest mistakes I've made have been going into business models where other people have repeatedly failed and thinking, I can do this better.
alts.zh: 我犯過最大的錯，都是跳進那種別人一再失敗的商業模式，然後心想：我可以做得比他們好。

cards.quote: Paul, that's excellent leadership. I really appreciate what you're doing. Please step out of the way.
cards.zh: Paul，這是很好的領導。我很感謝你這麼做。不過請讓開。
cards.why: 先給一個具體且真誠的肯定，再下一個不容商量的指令——肯定不是為了鋪墊拒絕，而是確保對方被否決時不會誤讀成被貶低。這種「先表揚後否決」的節奏在英文高階場合很常見。
swaps: I respect you protecting your team. I still need to talk to them directly
That's the right instinct — I'm going to override it this once
cards.pmNote: 推翻部屬的判斷時先肯定他的動機，才不會讓他下次不敢再擋。
cards.episode: Taking control of your career | Ethan Evans (Amazon)

alts.quote: What if I called it educating your manager about all the great work your team has been doing? What if I called it helping people see why your team should get more resources?
alts.zh: 如果我把它叫做「讓主管了解你的團隊做了哪些很棒的事」呢？如果我把它叫做「幫大家看見為什麼你的團隊該拿到更多資源」呢？

alts.quote: When somebody is using AI to solve a problem that they wouldn't have used AI before, give them a shout-out in the team meeting, let them demo that. Again, make them feel like a million bucks for doing the thing.
alts.zh: 只要有人用 AI 解掉一個他以前不會這樣解的問題，就在團隊會議上點名讚美他，讓他 demo 一次。就是要讓他爽到不行。

alts.quote: It's not often I use a product and I'm like, "This thing is 10 times better than anything that's come before it." It's one of those for me.
alts.zh: 我很少用到一個產品會覺得「這東西比之前所有的東西好上十倍」。這個對我來說就是其中之一。

cards.pattern: Well, two things. First, you were wrong. Second though, [轉折].
cards.quote: He said, "Well, two things. First, you were wrong. You were wrong to prioritize date over our reputation."
cards.zh: 他說：「兩件事。第一，你錯了。你不該把時程放在我們的商譽前面。」
cards.why: 先報數量再逐條講，重話就有了結構感，聽的人知道還有下一點、不會當場崩潰。You were wrong to [動詞] 這個句型精準鎖定「哪個決定錯」，而不是「你這個人錯」。
swaps: Two things. One, that was the wrong call. Two, here's what saves you
You were wrong to trade X for Y
cards.pmNote: 重話分點講並預告總數，對方才聽得完而不是聽到一半就防衛。
cards.episode: Taking control of your career | Ethan Evans (Amazon)

alts.quote: I'm not saying that one or the other was right or wrong, but as leaders in the organization, we've got to get some of the basic stories straight, including how do we fundamentally prioritize growth versus engagement versus monetization?
alts.zh: 我不是要說哪一邊對哪一邊錯，但身為組織的領導者，我們得先把一些最基本的故事講清楚——比如成長、互動、變現到底怎麼排順序。

alts.quote: Hey, well this is how other people perceive you including me, but maybe this is not what you are intending...
alts.zh: 其他人——包括我——是這樣看你的，但這可能不是你原本想呈現的樣子。

alts.quote: And I said, "Is it okay if I show you an alternative way of communicating that?"
alts.zh: 我就說：「我可以示範一種不一樣的講法給你看嗎？」

cards.quote: Yes, you wrote the bug, but that's not on you. The system failed you.
cards.zh: 對，那個 bug 是你寫的，但這不算在你頭上。是制度沒接住你。
cards.why: that's not on you 是英文裡把責任從個人移回系統的標準說法，短、明確、沒有安慰的味道。先承認事實（yes, you wrote it）再免責，比一開口就說「不是你的錯」可信得多。
swaps: That's on the process, not on you
We set you up to fail there
cards.pmNote: 事故檢討時明確講出「這不是你的責任」，是留住人的關鍵一句話。
cards.episode: Taking control of your career | Ethan Evans (Amazon)

alts.quote: The only thing that's different is the insight that the founder has on the market, which is a hard pill to swallow. And I know that's hard to hear too.
alts.zh: 唯一的差別是創辦人對市場的洞察——這顆藥很難吞。我也知道這話很難聽。

alts.quote: And I think the error that people make more often than not is they are actually too stuck on their own product vision. That's the mistake I've seen a little bit more actually than the other way around.
alts.zh: 我覺得大家最常犯的錯，是太黏著自己原本的產品願景。這個錯我看到的，其實比反過來的那種多一點。

alts.quote: I respect that, and I relate to it in some ways with my own trying to get attention for my own work. But, "I deserve this" that's not a good tactical decision for your business.
alts.zh: 我尊重這種心情，我自己在推廣作品時也有過。但「我值得」不是一個好的商業決策理由。

cards.pattern: [X] is good, but [Y] is necessary.
cards.quote: And I think people don't understand that in a competitive environment, being right is good, but being quick is necessary.
cards.zh: 我覺得大家沒搞懂：在競爭環境裡，做對是加分，做得快是必要條件。
cards.why: good / necessary 的對比把兩個都「重要」的東西分成不同層級，一句話解決優先順序的爭論。這個結構可以無限套用：X is helpful, but Y is non-negotiable。
swaps: Quality is table stakes; speed is the differentiator
Nice to have versus non-negotiable
cards.pmNote: 排優先順序的爭論常常卡在「兩個都重要」，分成加分項與必要項就解開了。
cards.episode: Taking control of your career | Ethan Evans (Amazon)

alts.quote: And as long as your decision is like 70% right, you can iterate on that 20, 30% in either direction, but if you don't commit, then you don't actually get any new information that is high fidelity and high quality.
alts.zh: 只要決策有七成對，剩下的兩三成你都可以往任一邊修；但你不下注，就拿不到任何高品質的新資訊。

alts.quote: So I think a lot of times we just think, okay, this is the scope of it for now and we are okay launching this and the execution is good. But we know that this is not the fully figured out version.
alts.zh: 很多時候我們就是這樣想：現階段範圍就到這裡，執行品質夠好，可以上。但我們知道這還不是完整想通的版本。

alts.quote: And then the last thing I would say about this detection is if you don't know what to do, or all else being equal, then focus on onboarding.
alts.zh: 關於怎麼提早偵測，我最後想講的是：如果你不知道該做什麼，或其他條件都差不多，那就去弄 onboarding。

cards.quote: Beyond those cosmetics, the biggest thing I see particularly at higher levels is people talk about what they have done but not why it mattered.
cards.zh: 撇開那些表面功夫，我在比較資深的層級看到最大的問題是：大家只講自己做了什麼，不講那件事為什麼重要。
cards.why: what you did / why it mattered 是英文績效與面試語言裡最重要的一組對照。台灣人受的訓練多半停在前者，這句給了一個可以自我檢查的鉤子：講完事情就問自己 so what。
swaps: Don't tell me what you shipped — tell me what changed
Impact, not activity
cards.pmNote: 升遷簡報與面試都吃 impact；同樣一件事，量化的後果才是敘事的主詞。
cards.episode: Taking control of your career | Ethan Evans (Amazon)

alts.quote: I think those people tend to get lost in organizations. So if that describes you, just remember to say what you did.
alts.zh: 這種人在組織裡很容易被淹沒。所以如果你就是這種人，記得一定要把你做過的事講出來。

alts.quote: It was just such a rare opportunity, but I wouldn't have gotten those opportunities if I just let them promote me or I followed a strategy where I was just focused on trying to get the biggest title.
alts.zh: 那真的是很難得的機會，但如果我當初只是讓他們幫我升職、或只想著拿最大的頭銜，我根本拿不到那些機會。

alts.quote: I think the other thing is really asking yourself, "What do I do that no one else in this organization can do?" There are lots of things that I do that other people in the organization can do.
alts.zh: 另外一件事是問自己：「我做的哪些事，是這個組織裡其他人做不到的？」我做的很多事，其實別人也能做。

cards.quote: And what I say about that is what your manager should do and $4 will get you a cup of coffee at Starbucks.
cards.zh: 我對這件事的回答是：你主管「應該」怎麼做，加四塊美金可以在星巴克換一杯咖啡。
cards.why: 美式的招牌冷嘲句型「X and $Y will get you Z」，意思是「X 本身一文不值」。用來擋掉「這本來就該是別人的責任」這類抱怨，殺傷力強但有幽默感，屬於聽得懂就很有用、講出來要看場合的等級。
swaps: That's true, and it changes nothing
Fair — but you still have to deal with reality
cards.pmNote: 把注意力從「誰該負責」轉回「我能控制什麼」，是卡住的職涯最快的解法。
cards.episode: Taking control of your career | Ethan Evans (Amazon)

alts.quote: When I first started out in PM somebody, it's obviously a chestnut, but he pointed out that realistically when you're a product manager, your job is to say no to 90% of things that get brought your way.
alts.zh: 我剛入行做 PM 的時候，有人跟我說——雖然是老生常談——現實是，PM 的工作就是把送到你面前的事拒絕掉九成。

alts.quote: I am really hesitant to recommend any template. And what I'd say is these are principles for building it, not any prescribed formula.
alts.zh: 我真的很不願意推薦任何範本。我會說，這些是建構的原則，不是一套規定好的公式。

alts.quote: I don't think it's particularly productive to say, "Well, is it 20% bigger than the internet or 100%?" Those aren't productive conversations.
alts.zh: 去爭「它比網路大 20% 還是 100%」我覺得沒什麼意義，那種對話不會有產出。

cards.quote: Hey, I noticed that we have this problem. I fixed it.
cards.zh: 嘿，我注意到我們有這個問題，我把它處理掉了。
cards.why: 兩個短句就完成一次向上回報：發現 + 已解決。沒有請示、沒有邀功、也沒有請對方決策——這是英文裡展現 seniority 最經濟的說法。
swaps: Heads up — saw this, handled it
FYI, this came up and it's taken care of
cards.pmNote: 越資深，回報就越該從「請示」變成「知會」。
cards.episode: Taking control of your career | Ethan Evans (Amazon)

alts.quote: I think the other thing is really asking yourself, "What do I do that no one else in this organization can do?" There are lots of things that I do that other people in the organization can do.
alts.zh: 另外一件事是問自己：「我做的哪些事，是這個組織裡其他人做不到的？」我做的很多事，其實別人也能做。

alts.quote: But now I am making more in compensation that I made at Uber. Part of it is just luck, part of this is situational.
alts.zh: 但我現在的收入比在 Uber 的時候還高。其中一部分純粹是運氣，一部分是時機造成的。

alts.quote: It's not about you, it's about the idea. And don't be afraid to stand behind the idea.
alts.zh: 重點不是你，是那個想法。而且不要怕站在那個想法後面。

cards.quote: We're going to get to work on that, but can you tell me how are you measuring success? We want to make sure that what we do, you consider it successful.
cards.zh: 這件事我們會開始動工，不過可以先跟我說你是怎麼衡量成功的嗎？我們想確保做出來的東西，在你眼中算是成功。
cards.why: 先用「我們會做」拿掉對方的防衛，再用「你怎麼衡量成功」把一個指定好的功能悄悄翻譯成一個問題。整句沒有一個字在反對，卻拿回了解法的主導權——這是 PM 擋需求最安全的開場。
swaps: Happy to pick this up — how will we know it worked?
Before we scope it, what does success look like for you?
We can start on that. What outcome are you hoping to move?
cards.pmNote: 把 output（做某功能）反推回 outcome（解某問題）是 empowered team 的第一步；stakeholder 給的功能其實只是他心中的一個解法假設。
cards.episode: The nature of product | Marty Cagan, Silicon Valley Product Group

alts.quote: You keep using the word advice, and I just want to, so for anybody who's listening, do not take my advice.
alts.zh: 你一直在用「建議」這個詞，我想借這個機會講一句：不要照我的建議做。

alts.quote: Obviously never say never. Sometimes it might work, and if it worked for you, I am so glad. But that's an outlier and don't treat it as a pattern.
alts.zh: 當然，凡事沒有絕對。有時候真的會成功，如果你成功了我真的替你高興。但那是特例，不要把它當成通則。

alts.quote: Where I've seen people get lost is they assume that if you do that alone, it will work.
alts.zh: 我看過很多人卡住的地方是：他們假設光做這件事就會成功。

cards.pattern: Your belief is that if we [做 X]，[結果 Y] will happen. Do I have that right?
cards.quote: Your belief is that if we add buy now pay later, a lot more people will be able to buy and transact, and so it's going to pay off. Do I have that right?
cards.zh: 你的認定是：只要我們加了先買後付，會有更多人買得下去、成交量會上來，所以這筆投資划得來。我這樣理解對嗎？
cards.why: 把對方的要求複述成一句「假設」，再加上 Do I have that right? 交還發球權。假設一旦被講出口就變成可以被驗證的東西，你不必反駁，對方自己會開始鬆動。
swaps: So the assumption is that…, right?
If I'm hearing you right, you're betting that…
The thinking is …— am I reading that correctly?
cards.pmNote: 這是 assumption mapping 的口語版：把需求拆成「價值假設」，才有辦法用最小成本驗證它。
cards.episode: The nature of product | Marty Cagan, Silicon Valley Product Group

alts.quote: Well, I mean this is the irony of growth, is people think growth is overnight success and it's not. It is a lot of short wins and short-term execution for a longer-term gain.
alts.zh: 成長最諷刺的地方就在這：大家以為成長是一夜爆紅，其實不是。它是一堆短期的小勝仗，堆出長期的結果。

alts.quote: It's one thing to say you're spending a lot of time looking outside the building. It's a whole other thing to hear from the places you don't normally hear from.
alts.zh: 說自己花很多時間在公司外面看，是一回事；真的去聽那些你平常聽不到的聲音，完全是另一回事。

alts.quote: I think sometimes people use data a lot or too much because they're worrying or they're afraid that, will I make the wrong choice? And I'm using data to make the choice for me.
alts.zh: 我覺得有時候大家用數據用得太兇，是因為他們在怕：萬一我選錯了怎麼辦？於是就讓數據替他們做決定。

cards.pattern: What do you think about us running an experiment? Let us try [做法] for [期間] — if it goes well, great; if it doesn't, no harm.
cards.quote: What do you think about us doing an experiment? For the next quarter or two, why don't you let us try running like this? If it goes well, great; if it doesn't, no harm.
cards.zh: 我們來做個實驗你覺得如何？接下來一兩季，讓我們試著用這種方式跑跑看。順利的話很好，不順利也沒損失，我們就退回原本的做法。
cards.why: 把「改變組織做法」這種高風險提案包裝成「實驗」，再自己先講出退場條件（no harm），主管要拒絕的成本就變得很高。台灣人常直接要求授權，忘了先幫對方把風險降到零。
swaps: Could we treat this as a two-sprint experiment?
What if we time-boxed it to one quarter and reviewed?
Would you be open to us piloting this on one team?
cards.pmNote: 組織轉型不要一次動整個 BU，先找一個 product team 當試點——風險小、可回復、有成功案例才好擴散。
cards.episode: The nature of product | Marty Cagan, Silicon Valley Product Group

alts.quote: And I want you to say, "This is great. I want to talk about money, but before we do, I want to think about some of the things that will set me up to see succeed in this role.
alts.zh: 我要你這樣說：「這很好。我想談薪水，但在那之前，我想先談談有哪些東西能讓我在這個角色上成功。」

alts.quote: Instead of saying, "Look, your span of control, you have nine direct reports, you need leverage here. I have a lot of credibility with this side of the product organization. I think we could be doing more if this position existed."
alts.zh: 換成這樣講：「你看你的管理幅度，你手下有九個直屬，你需要有人幫你分擔。我在產品組織這一邊累積了不少信任。我覺得如果有這個職位，我們可以做得更多。」

alts.quote: So feel free to reach out to us if you have questions, but don't feel like that's required to be a good YC applicant.
alts.zh: 有問題歡迎來找我們，但不要覺得一定要這樣做才算是好的申請人。

cards.quote: I've learned that some of the companies we admire are not working the way we are, and maybe we should try this.
cards.zh: 我發現我們很欣賞的那幾家公司，做事方式跟我們並不一樣，也許我們可以試試看他們的做法。
cards.why: 用「我們共同欣賞的對象」當外部權威，避免把提案變成「我覺得 vs 你覺得」的個人對決；結尾用 maybe we should 留一個很低的門檻，讓對方是「同意嘗試」而不是「承認錯誤」。
swaps: The teams we look up to do it differently — worth a look?
I noticed a pattern at companies like X; maybe there's something for us there.
cards.pmNote: 推動改變時，外部標竿（best practice benchmark）比內部主張更容易被採納，因為它把爭論從立場移到證據。
cards.episode: The nature of product | Marty Cagan, Silicon Valley Product Group

alts.quote: My sense is if you want work-life balance, don't join one of these companies, because that's just not the way they work.
alts.zh: 我的感覺是，如果你想要工作生活平衡，就別加入這種公司，因為它們就不是那樣運作的。

alts.quote: And again, everything I've just described, by the way, is just a very straightforward extrapolation of very basic economics. I'm not making any bold predictions of what I just said.
alts.zh: 我剛剛講的這一整串，其實只是最基本的經濟學往下推而已。我沒有在做什麼大膽預測。

alts.quote: The way I think about this that I've heard well described is just there's no silver bullets, just many lead bullets.
alts.zh: 我對這件事的想法——我聽過一個說得很好的講法——就是沒有銀色子彈，只有很多顆鉛彈。

cards.pattern: Don't get me wrong, I love [X], but [保留意見]
cards.quote: And don't get me wrong, I love those cultures, but they're all different cultures. They're very different cultures.
cards.zh: 別誤會，那些文化我都很欣賞，但它們彼此其實非常不一樣，真的差很多。
cards.why: Don't get me wrong 是英語裡最好用的「防誤解緩衝器」：先預告我不是要攻擊你喜歡的東西，再說出真正的保留。台灣人常直接接 but，聽起來像否定對方的品味。
swaps: Don't get me wrong — I'm a fan, but…
I'm not knocking it, but…
To be clear, I like it; my concern is…
cards.pmNote: 抄大公司做法時要把「文化」和「技法」拆開——Amazon 的 working backwards 可以學，Amazon 的文化不見得能移植。
cards.episode: The nature of product | Marty Cagan, Silicon Valley Product Group

alts.quote: Don't get me wrong, all that's very important.
alts.zh: 別誤會，那些都很重要。

alts.quote: But the other thing is I don't really love some of that thinking process just in general.
alts.zh: 另外還有一點：那整套思考方式，我其實不是很喜歡，講一般情況啦。

alts.quote: In terms of evaluating the options, I don't love pros and cons. It's a flat list of text. It's hard to just get the big picture from that.
alts.zh: 在評估選項這件事上，我不太喜歡用優缺點列表。它就是一串平鋪的文字，很難一眼看到全貌。

cards.pattern: If none of [可信對象] are using it, it's either snake oil or it's not proven yet.
cards.quote: If none of those companies are using it, I'm like, "Don't bother me. It's either snake oil or it's not proven yet."
cards.zh: 如果那些公司一家都沒在用，那我的反應就是：別來煩我，這東西不是江湖偏方，就是還沒被驗證。
cards.why: 拒絕時把標準（誰在用）講在前面、結論擺後面，聽起來像在套用規則而不是針對人。snake oil（蛇油＝江湖假藥）是母語者常用、台灣人幾乎講不出來的貶義詞。
swaps: If the teams we trust aren't using it, I'd wait.
Until someone credible has shipped with it, it's unproven.
That's a solution looking for a problem.
cards.pmNote: 評估新工具/新流程的最低門檻：有沒有幾支好團隊已經在真實情境下用出結果，而不是白皮書說得漂亮。
cards.episode: The nature of product | Marty Cagan, Silicon Valley Product Group

alts.quote: I don't think it's particularly productive to say, "Well, is it 20% bigger than the internet or 100%?" Those aren't productive conversations.
alts.zh: 去爭「它比網路大 20% 還是 100%」我覺得沒什麼意義，那種對話不會有產出。

alts.quote: I'm like, "You have not earned that yet. That's not a statement about your worth. It's just you're not ready for that conversation."
alts.zh: 我會說：「這個你還沒掙到。這不是在評斷你的價值，只是你還沒到可以進行那場對話的階段。」

alts.quote: The thing that I think a lot of large companies don't realize is that you can love something to death.
alts.zh: 很多大公司沒意識到的一件事是：你可以把一個東西「愛到死」。

cards.pattern: If you need to spend a little time on [X], fine — but don't spend a lot, because you need to save as much time as possible for [Y].
cards.quote: Be careful. If you need to spend a little time on the problem, fine, but don't spend a lot of time because you need to save as much time as possible to come up with the winning solution.
cards.zh: 小心一點。你要花一點時間在問題上沒問題，但別花太多，因為你得盡量把時間留給「想出會贏的解法」。
cards.why: 「fine, but」是談優先順序的黃金句型：先承認對方要的東西有價值（不是零），再用「因為要留給更重要的」轉移資源。比直接說 don't do that 溫和太多。
swaps: A little is fine; a lot is expensive.
Worth some time, not worth weeks.
Timebox it — the leverage is downstream.
cards.pmNote: problem discovery 與 solution discovery 要分開看：多數產品的勝負在解法端，過度驗證早已確知的問題等於燒掉窗口期。
cards.episode: The nature of product | Marty Cagan, Silicon Valley Product Group

alts.quote: Yes, such a great point, Lenny. You absolutely need to time box this.
alts.zh: 對，這點問得很好。這件事你一定要設一個時間框。

alts.quote: I think it's the difference between oversimplification and focusing. You can have a complex problem and be like, "You know what? I need to hold some things constant."
alts.zh: 我覺得差別在於「過度簡化」和「聚焦」。面對複雜問題你可以說：好，我需要先把某些變數固定住。

alts.quote: There's definitely a trade-off. I think sometimes when companies specialize roles a lot it's because it's more efficient.
alts.zh: 這確實有取捨。公司把角色切得很細，通常是因為那樣比較有效率。

cards.pattern: You can hand off [這些]. But never [那三件核心的事].
cards.quote: Pulling off other responsibilities is no problem. It's a good thing to do, especially as you grow, but never when you touch those three sacred things.
cards.zh: 把其他職責分出去完全沒問題，隨著規模變大這反而是好事——但前提是不能碰到那三件神聖不可讓的事。
cards.why: 先大方讓步（很多事都可以拿走），再用 never 把一條線劃死。給出讓步清單會讓那條紅線顯得合理而不是難搞，這是守住範疇時最有效的結構。
swaps: Happy to give up X and Y — Z I can't move on.
Everything else is negotiable; that one isn't.
Take the rest, but that one stays with the team.
cards.pmNote: PM 三條命脈：直接接觸使用者、直接接觸工程師、直接接觸 stakeholder；把任何一條交給 product owner 或 product ops，創新就停了。
cards.episode: The nature of product | Marty Cagan, Silicon Valley Product Group

alts.quote: I don't think it's particularly productive to say, "Well, is it 20% bigger than the internet or 100%?" Those aren't productive conversations.
alts.zh: 去爭「它比網路大 20% 還是 100%」我覺得沒什麼意義，那種對話不會有產出。
