alts.quote: I would say wait until it hurts more. If the unfamiliarity is the big problem with it, then maybe the things are fine.
alts.zh: 我會說：等到更痛再來。如果你最大的問題只是「不熟悉」，那可能表示現在其實還好。

alts.quote: You've got to do HIPAA, you got to do SOC 2, you've got to do all those things if you want to be a serious player. And those are just non-negotiable.
alts.zh: HIPAA 要做、SOC 2 要做，這些全都得做，你才算是玩真的。這些就是沒得談。

cards.pattern: That one always makes me laugh, because [反問]
cards.quote: That one always makes me laugh because I was thinking, "Do you know how many hours a week I'd need to work if that was my only job?"
cards.zh: 這種說法每次都讓我笑出來，因為我心想：如果那真的是我唯一的工作，你知道我一週只需要上多少小時的班嗎？
cards.why: 用「這讓我笑了」＋自嘲式反問來反駁一個廣為流傳的錯誤觀念，火力很強但沒有指名任何人。幽默在英語會議裡是合法的反對武器，台灣人往往只會硬碰硬或乾脆不講。
swaps: That one always gets me, because…
I have to smile at that one — if that were true, …
That always makes me laugh; think it through and…
cards.pmNote: 「PM 只管 what、不管 how」是最常見的角色誤解——valuable 與 viable 這兩個風險本來就落在 how 裡面。
cards.episode: The nature of product | Marty Cagan, Silicon Valley Product Group

alts.quote: And I know this is going to trigger some people, but the truth is they don't want to work.
alts.zh: 我知道這句會讓一些人不爽，但事實就是——他們不想做事。

alts.quote: I actually say I disagree with Naval on this because often, when you're part of a large organization, it's really hard to do great work and get recognized for it.
alts.zh: 我其實在這件事上跟 Naval 意見不同，因為在大組織裡，你常常很難既做出好成果又被看見。

alts.quote: That's fine, but you're going to need me the next time too. You're going to keep needing me because you're not really becoming a storyteller.
alts.zh: 這樣也行，但下次你還是得找我。你會一直需要我，因為你並沒有真的變成一個會說故事的人。

cards.pattern: If [關鍵的人] can't be there, cancel it.
cards.quote: If the product manager and the designer are not available to be there during their product test, cancel the test. They need to be there.
cards.zh: 如果產品經理和設計師沒辦法到場，那這場使用者測試就取消。他們一定要在現場。
cards.why: 把「拒絕」寫成一條前置條件式的規則（if…, cancel it），對事不對人，下次不必再吵一次。這種「規則化的 no」是資深者最省力的擋人方式。
swaps: No decision-maker in the room, no meeting.
If the owner can't join, we move it.
Let's not run it without them.
cards.pmNote: 使用者研究的價值不在報告，在團隊親耳聽到；報告太容易被忽略，現場的震撼才會改變決策。
cards.episode: The nature of product | Marty Cagan, Silicon Valley Product Group

alts.quote: Realistically when you're a product manager, your job is to say no to 90% of things that get brought your way. And so you're saying no to 90%, so you can say yes to 10%.
alts.zh: 說穿了，當產品經理的工作就是把送到你面前的九成東西拒絕掉——你拒絕九成，才有辦法對那一成說好。

alts.quote: if you want to change during the course of the quarter, if you want to disrupt our whole engineering product team, you can do it, but understand there's a high cost, and the later you do it in the quarter, the less successful it's going to be
alts.zh: 你想在季中改、想打亂整個工程團隊，可以啊，但你要知道代價很高——而且愈晚改，效果只會愈差。

alts.quote: You can say, "Yes, I agree. That is a real problem. Yes, I think we could test this design with users."
alts.zh: 你可以說：「對，我同意，那確實是個真的問題。對，我覺得這個設計我們可以拿去跟使用者測。」

cards.pattern: I hate the idea of [做法], because [理由]
cards.quote: I hate the idea of those companies that have separate product owners because product owner is just an administrative role.
cards.zh: 我很不喜歡那些另外設 product owner 的公司，因為 product owner 本質上只是個行政角色。
cards.why: I hate the idea of X 攻擊的是「這個做法」而不是「做這件事的人」——英語裡用 the idea of 當緩衝墊，強度可以很高但不會變成人身攻擊。
swaps: I'm not a fan of the idea that…
I really don't like the setup where…
The idea of splitting that role bothers me.
cards.pmNote: 把 PM 一分為二（PO 對工程、PM 對市場）看起來減負，實際上切斷了發現解法所需的資訊迴路。
cards.episode: The nature of product | Marty Cagan, Silicon Valley Product Group

alts.quote: Both things can be true. It's like, yeah, there's nothing perfect in product. However, it is true that some companies are healthier than others.
alts.zh: 這兩件事可以同時成立。對，產品這行沒有什麼是完美的；但同樣真實的是，有些公司確實比其他公司健康得多。

alts.quote: I'm not trying to diss anyone, but you'll see things that become fashionable really quickly because someone found success in this unfashionable space and then it becomes fashionable.
alts.zh: 我不是要酸誰，但你會看到有些東西紅得很快——因為有人在一個沒人做的領域做成了，然後它就變成流行。

alts.quote: So I think it's an unnecessary addition, but maybe I'm just being protective of my original idea.
alts.zh: 我覺得那是多此一舉的補充，不過也可能只是我在護著自己原本的想法啦。

cards.pattern: Let's just say [情境設定]，and [推論]
cards.quote: Let's just say there's a product manager and nobody's ever coached this poor person, and so they really don't know much.
cards.zh: 我們就假設有一個產品經理，從來沒有人帶過他，所以他其實懂得不多。
cards.why: Let's just say 讓你把一個真實但敏感的狀況（例如「我們公司的 PM 很弱」）搬到假設世界討論，聽的人不必對號入座。談人的問題時這是最好用的去人格化裝置。
swaps: Say for the sake of argument that…
Imagine a team where…
Suppose nobody's ever coached them.
cards.pmNote: empowered team 最常失敗的一環不是流程，而是 PM 本人準備不足（不懂使用者、數據、商業、產業）。
cards.episode: The nature of product | Marty Cagan, Silicon Valley Product Group

alts.quote: The way I think about this is that emotions are like a tube, let's say, and there's water moving through the tube.
alts.zh: 我自己是這樣想這件事的：情緒像一根管子，裡面有水在流。

alts.quote: So there's, I wouldn't say a checklist, but there's a series of questions that I asked to diagnose why is growth slowing in this order, because it's one of these things where the first one that's a problem, if you don't fix that, it doesn't matter if you fix one of the ones below.
alts.zh: 我不會說那是一張檢查清單，但我確實有一組問題，會照順序問下去診斷成長為什麼變慢——因為只要最前面那個沒修，後面修再多都沒用。

alts.quote: The editor, the writer, I'll just say it as plainly as possible, they don't care about you. They don't care about you. They care about their reader, or their listener, or their viewer.
alts.zh: 編輯也好、記者也好，我把話講到最白：他們不在乎你。他們真的不在乎你。他們在乎的是他們的讀者、聽眾、觀眾。

cards.pattern: So to your question: [重述問題]. These are the [N] things you need to do.
cards.quote: So to your question, you're a feature team. You want to give it a shot, be in a real product team. These are the four things you need to go out and do.
cards.zh: 回到你的問題：你在一支功能團隊，想試試看真正的產品團隊怎麼運作——那你要去做的就是這四件事。
cards.why: 講久了要收線時，用 So to your question 把話題拉回提問者，再用「這 N 件事」把散開的內容重新打包。這是英語會議裡把發散變收斂的標準動作。
swaps: Coming back to your question…
So, to answer what you actually asked…
Back to your point — here's the short version.
cards.pmNote: 從 feature team 轉成 product team 的四件事：拿到問題而非功能、PM 補足知識、拿到策略脈絡、學會 discovery 技法。
cards.episode: The nature of product | Marty Cagan, Silicon Valley Product Group

alts.quote: So I was taking notes as you were talking and there's kind of these four items just to summarize.
alts.zh: 你講的時候我一直在記筆記，總結起來大概是這四項。

alts.quote: So maybe this is a way to come back to your question about what's the output of the shaping session, it's like it's shaped if we can give this to a technical person and they say, "Yeah, I know what to go build now."
alts.zh: 所以回到你剛剛問的「shaping session 的產出是什麼」：判準是——把它交給一個技術的人，他會說「好，我知道要蓋什麼了」。

alts.quote: So just to wrap things up, is there anything else that you thought would be fun to share or maybe a piece of wisdom you want to leave listeners with before we get to a very exciting lightning round?
alts.zh: 那就準備收尾了——還有什麼你覺得好玩、想分享的，或想留給大家的一句話，然後我們才進快問快答？

cards.pattern: My purely anecdotal guess is [數字], something like that.
cards.quote: My purely anecdotal guess is maybe 10 to 15% are good product companies, something like that.
cards.zh: 我純粹憑印象猜，大概一成到一成五算是好的產品公司吧，差不多這個量級。
cards.why: 先給數字（對方要的），再用 purely anecdotal 標明資料等級，最後 something like that 留誤差。敢給數字又標清楚可信度，是資深訊號；台灣人常常是乾脆不給，反而顯得沒觀點。
swaps: Gut feel, no data behind it: maybe 10–15%.
Anecdotally, I'd guess…
Ballpark, and I could be way off…
cards.pmNote: 回答沒有資料的問題時，給出「估計值＋可信度標籤」比拒答有用，這也是 opportunity sizing 的基本禮貌。
cards.episode: The nature of product | Marty Cagan, Silicon Valley Product Group

alts.quote: Is this positioning good or not?" And the problem with B2B tech companies is, well, unless I'm your buyer, I'm not the right person to ask.
alts.zh: 「這個定位到底好不好？」B2B 科技公司的問題在於——除非我就是你的買家，不然我根本不是該問的那個人。

alts.quote: And if you push a really experienced product director like that, they're going to go, "Good point, I don't. I'm going to go find out."
alts.zh: 你這樣逼一個真正資深的產品總監，他會說：「說得對，我確實不知道。我去查清楚。」

alts.quote: If something is just purely code planning, there's not a great reason why we would be the best at that. I can't come up with a coherent argument for that.
alts.zh: 如果只是純粹的程式規劃，我想不出我們憑什麼會是最強的。這個我實在提不出一個站得住腳的論證。

cards.pattern: Just to reinforce this point — what are the [N] things again? In case folks didn't catch it.
cards.quote: Just to reinforce this point, what are the three things again? In case folks didn't catch it all.
cards.zh: 為了把這個重點再壓一次——那三件事到底是哪三件？怕大家剛剛沒全部聽清楚。
cards.why: 把「我要你再講一次」包裝成「這點很重要值得再講」＋「怕別人沒聽到」，完全不暴露自己沒跟上。英文會議裡最實用的一句自保台詞。
swaps: Can we land that one again for everyone?
Worth repeating — what were the three?
Say that once more for the room.
cards.pmNote: 會議尾聲把關鍵清單複述一次，是最便宜的 alignment 動作。
cards.episode: The nature of product | Marty Cagan, Silicon Valley Product Group

alts.quote: Two things I'd love to clarify.
alts.zh: 有兩件事我想澄清一下。

alts.quote: So I'm not saying they didn't get the exact monthly number wrong. I'm saying they got it wrong by many factors.
alts.zh: 我不是在說他們只是月份的確切數字抓錯。我是說他們錯了好幾個量級。

alts.quote: Just for folks that are listening, just to calibrate what size of company you're talking about selling to here.
alts.zh: 為了讓聽的人有個基準——你剛剛講的是賣給多大規模的公司？

cards.pattern: [名字], you have to stop [具體行為].
cards.quote: And he's like, "Jackie, you have to stop shutting me down."
cards.zh: 他就直接說：「Jackie，你不能再這樣把我的話擋回去了。」
cards.why: 叫名字＋you have to stop＋一個動作名詞，短到沒有閃避空間。難聽的回饋在英語裡反而要更短：拉長修飾只會讓對方抓不到重點。shut someone down 精準指「當場把人堵死」。
swaps: You need to stop cutting people off.
I need you to stop shooting things down so fast.
That's the third time you've shut that down — let's not.
cards.pmNote: PM 用「效率」當理由快速否決，久了會被讀成防衛心，真正的代價是別人不再帶想法來找你。
cards.episode: Jackie Bavaro on getting better at product strategy, what exactly is strategy, PM pitfalls to avoid, advancing your career, getting into management, and much more

alts.quote: And so here's where I think we go off the rails in marketing.
alts.zh: 而我覺得行銷就是在這一步脫軌的。

alts.quote: The only thing that's different is the insight that the founder has on the market, which is a hard pill to swallow. And I know that's hard to hear too.
alts.zh: 唯一的差別是創辦人對市場的洞察——這顆藥很難吞。我也知道這話很難聽。

alts.quote: Clearly, you're not so scared that you can't do anything, so I'm not buying it. I don't do it quite like that, I do it with a lot more love than that.
alts.zh: 很明顯你沒有害怕到什麼都做不了，所以這個說法我不買單。我實際上不會講得這麼硬，我會帶更多善意。

cards.pattern: Yes, I agree that's a real problem. Yes, we could test [做法] with users.
cards.quote: You can say, "Yes, I agree. That is a real problem. Yes, I think we could test this design with users."
cards.zh: 你可以說：「對，我同意，那確實是個真的問題。對，我覺得這個設計我們可以拿去跟使用者測。」
cards.why: 把「不做」換成兩個真心的 yes：同意問題存在、同意驗證方式。你沒有承諾任何排程，但對方感覺被接住了——這是擋需求最不傷關係的版本。
swaps: I agree the problem's real — let's test the solution.
Yes to the problem, let's validate the approach.
That pain is real; let's see what the data says.
cards.pmNote: 把 stakeholder 給的解法當成「他在描述問題的方式」，你就永遠有東西可以同意，而不必先開戰。
cards.episode: Jackie Bavaro on getting better at product strategy, what exactly is strategy, PM pitfalls to avoid, advancing your career, getting into management, and much more

alts.quote: Realistically when you're a product manager, your job is to say no to 90% of things that get brought your way. And so you're saying no to 90%, so you can say yes to 10%.
alts.zh: 說穿了，當產品經理的工作就是把送到你面前的九成東西拒絕掉——你拒絕九成，才有辦法對那一成說好。

alts.quote: So yeah, I think the only way you build something that matters that's going to change the world is if you find a big idea you believe in and you say no to everything else.
alts.zh: 我覺得要做出真正有份量、能改變世界的東西，唯一的路就是找到一個你相信的大想法，然後對其他所有東西說不。

alts.quote: I don't think it's particularly productive to say, "Well, is it 20% bigger than the internet or 100%?" Those aren't productive conversations.
alts.zh: 去爭「它比網路大 20% 還是 100%」我覺得沒什麼意義，那種對話不會有產出。

cards.quote: And I can interpret their solution as a way of sharing the problem and exploring and brainstorming around that.
cards.zh: 我可以把他們提出的解法，理解成他們在用自己的方式描述問題、順便一起發想。
cards.why: interpret A as B 是很高段的重新框架：不否定對方講的內容，只調整它的身分（從「指令」變成「線索」）。學會這一句，很多對立會直接消失。
swaps: I read that as them describing the pain.
Their fix is really a symptom report.
Behind that request there's a real problem.
cards.pmNote: 需求背後幾乎都藏著真實痛點；解法可以否決，痛點不要否決。
cards.episode: Jackie Bavaro on getting better at product strategy, what exactly is strategy, PM pitfalls to avoid, advancing your career, getting into management, and much more

alts.quote: Here's what I have a problem with. First of all, having a growth mindset is a very, very helpful thing.
alts.zh: 我要說的是我對它的哪一點有意見。首先，擁有成長心態本身是非常非常有幫助的事。

alts.quote: Now, obviously if you live in a small town and they capped the well and gave all the water to the data center, then you're really pissed off. But that's a planning problem. That's not a data center problem.
alts.zh: 當然，如果你住在小鎮上，井被封了、水全給了資料中心，那你當然火大。但那是都市規劃的問題，不是資料中心的問題。

alts.quote: I will say if you're like, the hardest problem I have is that I need to build a new unicorn business, obviously that's not going to work. Not yet.
alts.zh: 當然啦，如果你說「我最難的問題是要生出一家獨角獸」，那顯然行不通。目前還不行。

cards.pattern: It might be easier if I just [做 X] — I might be able to save you some time and energy.
cards.quote: It might be easier if I just go, I might be able to save you some time and some energy if I just joined you.
cards.zh: 也許我直接去比較快，我一起進去的話，說不定可以幫你省下一些時間跟力氣。
cards.why: 想擠進一個自己沒資格參加的會議，卻把理由完全放在「幫你省事」。用 might＋just 把要求縮到最小，聽起來像順手幫忙而不是爭取權力。
swaps: Might be quicker if I just came along.
Want me to sit in so you don't have to relay it?
I could take that off your plate if I joined.
cards.pmNote: 爭取進到更高層的會議時，賣點是「減少傳話損耗」，不是「我也想聽」。
cards.episode: Jackie Bavaro on getting better at product strategy, what exactly is strategy, PM pitfalls to avoid, advancing your career, getting into management, and much more

alts.quote: So instead of just sending the link, I usually start the email with something like looking forward to connecting, feel free to share, sometimes you're available or if easier, you can choose to find time on my calendar using the Calendly link here.
alts.zh: 所以我不會只丟一個連結，我通常這樣開頭：很期待跟你聊，你可以直接給我幾個方便的時間，或者比較省事的話，也可以用這裡的 Calendly 連結直接約。

alts.quote: Okay. I would like to carve 20% of my time listening and I'm happy to do this work 80% of the time.
alts.zh: 好，我想切出兩成的時間去聽，另外八成的時間我很樂意投入手上的工作。

alts.quote: And I want you to say, "This is great. I want to talk about money, but before we do, I want to think about some of the things that will set me up to see succeed in this role.
alts.zh: 我要你這樣說：「這很好。我想談薪水，但在那之前，我想先談談有哪些東西能讓我在這個角色上成功。」

cards.pattern: Here are the [N] questions I want you to get answered — and if they say X, ask Y.
cards.quote: Hey, you have your planning committee today. Here are the three questions I want you to go in and get answered at that committee.
cards.zh: 你今天有規劃委員會對吧？這是我希望你進去幫我問到答案的三個問題。
cards.why: 進不去的會議，就把自己的問題塞進去。用「三個問題」這種有限、具體的形式，主管容易答應；久了你就從外圍變成議程的作者。
swaps: Could you bring these two questions in for me?
If it comes up, can you ask about…?
Here's what I'd love to know from that room.
cards.pmNote: 影響力常是從「幫決策者準備問題」開始累積的，不必等到有席次。
cards.episode: Jackie Bavaro on getting better at product strategy, what exactly is strategy, PM pitfalls to avoid, advancing your career, getting into management, and much more

alts.quote: I very quickly just sent her a note that said, "Wanted to build on this idea you had today. I really liked that idea, by the way. I saw this article, I saw this research about this other emerging thing."
alts.zh: 我很快就傳了一則訊息給她：「想接著你今天那個想法往下延伸。順帶一提，我真的很喜歡那個點子。我看到一篇研究提到另一個正在浮現的現象……」

alts.quote: What does the CEO want to hear more? Growth or saves money? Both are good, but I know which one is healthier for the company, increases market share, is better competitively.
alts.zh: CEO 比較想聽哪一個：成長，還是省錢？兩個都好，但我知道哪一個對公司比較健康、比較能拉市佔、比較有競爭力。

alts.quote: We can't just have the marketing department sit down and cook up new positioning and then heave it over the wall to everybody else. It's a team sport.
alts.zh: 不能讓行銷部門自己關起門想一套新定位，然後往牆外一丟就沒事了。這是團隊運動。

cards.pattern: I'd really love to become [目標] someday. What do you suggest I work on now so I'll be ready when the opportunity comes up?
cards.quote: I would really love to become a people manager someday. What do you suggest that I work on now so that I'll be ready when the opportunity comes up?
cards.zh: 我以後很想帶人。你建議我現在可以先練哪些東西，等機會來的時候我已經準備好了？
cards.why: 把野心放在未來式（someday）就不會逼主管當場評價你「現在夠不夠格」，再用 what do you suggest 把他拉到你這一邊當教練。整句沒有要求任何東西，卻同時完成了宣告目標和取得路線圖。
swaps: Down the road I'd like to grow into X — what should I be building now?
When that door opens, what would make me ready?
What gaps should I close before that comes up?
cards.pmNote: 升遷回饋要主動聚焦：不聚焦時你會收到一堆都對但無關升遷的小建議。
cards.episode: Jackie Bavaro on getting better at product strategy, what exactly is strategy, PM pitfalls to avoid, advancing your career, getting into management, and much more

alts.quote: It might actually mean a proactive conversation with your manager or the leadership to say, "I love what I'm doing here, and I would also like to learn a little bit more. And here's what I'm interested in."
alts.zh: 這可能只是主動找主管或高層談一次，跟他說：「我很喜歡現在做的事，同時我也想再多學一些，這是我有興趣的方向。」

alts.quote: This is people you used to work with before, go ask them, "Hey, what did I do well, what do you think my strengths are? What do you think I'm a fit for?
alts.zh: 去問以前的同事：「我哪裡做得好？你覺得我的強項是什麼？我是這樣想的——你覺得我對自己的認知準確嗎？」

alts.quote: So instead of just going to someone saying, "Hey, can you be a mentor?" Coming to me and say, "Do you know someone who's actually really good at changing the way teams work or really good at communicating a new vision that I can talk to?"
alts.zh: 與其跑去問人家「你可以當我的 mentor 嗎」，不如問：「你認識誰特別擅長改變團隊運作方式、或特別會傳達新願景，可以讓我請教一下嗎？」

cards.pattern: I agree — I've changed my mind. You're right. You saw it in a way I hadn't seen.
cards.quote: I agree, I've changed my mind. You're right. You just saw it in a way that I hadn't seen.
cards.zh: 我同意，我改變想法了。你是對的，你看到的角度是我原本沒看到的。
cards.why: 改立場時最怕顯得沒主見。這裡用「你看到的角度是我沒看到的」把轉向歸因於新資訊而非自己軟弱，既給對方面子也保住自己專業感。三句話乾淨俐落，不拖泥帶水。
swaps: You've convinced me — I hadn't looked at it that way.
Fair point, I'm changing my position.
I was wrong on that; your framing is better.
cards.pmNote: strong opinions, loosely held：立場要清楚，但新證據出現時要能公開換邊，這是資深而非動搖。
cards.episode: Jackie Bavaro on getting better at product strategy, what exactly is strategy, PM pitfalls to avoid, advancing your career, getting into management, and much more

alts.quote: I think that's the biggest major fundamental 180 degree change that I've changed my mind on, but I changed my mind all the time.
alts.zh: 那大概是我立場整個一百八十度翻過來、最大的一次改變，不過我本來就一天到晚在改想法。

alts.quote: By the way, I will say on the Peter one, I've come much more around to Peter's point of view. I would probably argue that one quite a bit differently today than I did, and I would give his view, I think, a lot more credit.
alts.zh: 順帶一提，Peter 那場辯論，我現在比較站到他那邊了。同樣的題目今天要我講，我會講得很不一樣，也會給他的看法多很多分數。

alts.quote: Even if I don't agree with the feedback, what is the insight that I'm missing? How am I wrong about this? What would be true for this other person to be right?
alts.zh: 就算我不同意那個回饋，我也會問：我漏掉了什麼洞見？我哪裡想錯了？要怎麼樣，對方才會是對的？

cards.pattern: I think really [選項] is the only reasonable one, for these reasons.
cards.quote: And then our CEO gets in, and he's like, "I think really number four is the only reasonable one for these reasons."
cards.zh: 然後我們執行長進來說：「我認為真正合理的其實只有第四個，理由如下。」
cards.why: the only reasonable one 火力很強，但前面加 I think、後面立刻接 for these reasons，就從獨斷變成「我有推論、歡迎檢驗」。強勢意見要能被接受，關鍵是理由必須同句出現。
swaps: To me only option four holds up, and here's why.
I'd argue three of these are non-starters because…
I think there's really only one viable path here.
cards.pmNote: 定價這類高槓桿決策，講清楚淘汰其他選項的理由，比宣布結論更能建立共識。
cards.episode: Jackie Bavaro on getting better at product strategy, what exactly is strategy, PM pitfalls to avoid, advancing your career, getting into management, and much more

alts.quote: I think my only build on that would be to say I think those core PM skills aren't necessarily the things that we have rewarded PMs for over the last five years, versus storytelling, alignment, strategy.
alts.zh: 我唯一想補的是：那些核心 PM 能力，其實不是我們過去五年在獎勵的東西——我們獎勵的是說故事、跨部門對齊、講策略。

alts.quote: So far be it from me to disagree with Mike Tyson, but I think he's wrong.
alts.zh: 我哪敢跟泰森唱反調——但我覺得他錯了。

alts.quote: So, I think one needs to be a little bit cautious on what Dario says. And that's setting aside the cynical view that he's just doing that department stock, which I don't believe at all.
alts.zh: 我覺得對 Dario 講的話要保留一點。而且我這裡還先撇開那種比較酸的解讀——說他只是在替自家股價講話——那我完全不相信。

cards.quote: And he's like, "Can you create a strategy for the platform team?" And I was like, "Great, here it is." And he's like, "That's not a strategy."
cards.zh: 他問：「你能幫平台團隊做一份策略嗎？」我說：「好啊，這就是了。」他說：「這不是策略。」
cards.why: 四個字的否決，沒有任何緩衝——這種強度只有在資深、關係穩、而且接著會給定義時才能用。值得學的是它的效果：把模糊的爭論一刀切開，逼出「那什麼才算」的對話。
swaps: That's a goal, not a strategy.
That's a plan — where's the choice in it?
I don't think that clears the bar for a strategy.
cards.pmNote: 策略＝願景＋策略框架（市場、致勝賭注）＋路線圖；只有目標數字或功能清單都不算策略。
cards.episode: Jackie Bavaro on getting better at product strategy, what exactly is strategy, PM pitfalls to avoid, advancing your career, getting into management, and much more

alts.quote: So, I think one needs to be a little bit cautious on what Dario says. And that's setting aside the cynical view that he's just doing that department stock, which I don't believe at all.
alts.zh: 我覺得對 Dario 講的話要保留一點。而且我這裡還先撇開那種比較酸的解讀——說他只是在替自家股價講話——那我完全不相信。

alts.quote: The other thing that's a little bit different about what you said is that emotions do need to be felt.
alts.zh: 還有一點跟你剛剛講的稍微不一樣，就是情緒是真的需要被感受到的。

alts.quote: It's like, "well, I'm not telling you that you should pivot. I'm just saying that is what it's called when you change the strategy, but try to have fidelity to the vision."
alts.zh: 我不是在叫你去 pivot。我只是說，當你改策略但盡量守住願景的時候，那件事就叫這個名字。

cards.pattern: Anytime a disagreement feels like a disagreement in values, that's a sign it's really a disagreement in strategy.
cards.quote: Anytime you have these disagreements that feel really thorny or they feel like a disagreement in values, that's a sign that you really have a disagreement in strategy.
cards.zh: 每當某個爭執特別棘手、感覺像是價值觀的衝突，那通常是個訊號：你們真正在吵的是策略。
cards.why: 把僵持的衝突重新命名（不是人不合，是策略沒定），衝突就從人身層級被抬到議題層級。that's a sign that… 是把情緒轉譯成診斷的萬用句型。
swaps: If we keep relitigating this, the real gap is upstream.
This feels like values, but I think it's strategy.
Repeated fights usually mean a missing decision above.
cards.pmNote: 反覆爭同一個功能，是策略或產品原則缺席的症狀；解法是把爭論寫成一條原則，而不是一次一次投票。
cards.episode: Jackie Bavaro on getting better at product strategy, what exactly is strategy, PM pitfalls to avoid, advancing your career, getting into management, and much more

alts.quote: This stress between product and sales is a good thing. It's a sign of a well-run B2B company when there is stress between product and sales.
alts.zh: 產品跟業務之間的緊張是好事。B2B 公司如果產品跟業務之間有張力，那才叫營運健康。

alts.quote: Okay, guys, I'm seeing something happen here. Every time we get close to talking about something that's really painful, somebody makes a joke and all the energy disappears.
alts.zh: 好，我看到一個現象。每次我們快要談到真正痛的事情，就會有人開個玩笑，然後所有能量就消失了。

alts.quote: That's the whole ball game. No one had to lose in order for us to win.
alts.zh: 這才是重點。我們要贏，不需要有人輸。

cards.pattern: If you come in on day one saying [X] is all wrong, it raises the question of why you joined.
cards.quote: But if they come in on day one saying your strategy is all wrong, raises the question of, "Well then why did you join my team if you didn't believe in my strategy?"
cards.zh: 但如果他第一天就說你的策略整個都錯了，那就會讓人想問：既然你不相信這個策略，當初為什麼要加入我的團隊？
cards.why: It raises the question of… 是把反對包成「一個自然會被問到的問題」，不是「我要質問你」。用問句回擊，殺傷力保留、姿態卻很低。
swaps: That raises a fair question…
It begs the question of why we hired for this then.
Which makes me wonder what you signed up for.
cards.pmNote: 新人前六個月先學既有策略並交付，六個月後再提策略草稿，才有信用可用。
cards.episode: Jackie Bavaro on getting better at product strategy, what exactly is strategy, PM pitfalls to avoid, advancing your career, getting into management, and much more

alts.quote: Now, obviously if you live in a small town and they capped the well and gave all the water to the data center, then you're really pissed off. But that's a planning problem. That's not a data center problem.
alts.zh: 當然，如果你住在小鎮上，井被封了、水全給了資料中心，那你當然火大。但那是都市規劃的問題，不是資料中心的問題。

alts.quote: And then there's this question of, well, would you rather be in the room and making this better or not?
alts.zh: 然後就有一個問題：你是寧願待在那個房間裡把它變好，還是乾脆不在？

alts.quote: And I think one of the monikers we use internally is no, then go. As in just think through all the things that could go wrong, understand where scale will break, understand the things that might happen, and then move on anyway.
alts.zh: 我們內部有個口號叫「先說不，然後走」。把所有可能出錯的地方都想過一輪，知道規模在哪裡會斷，然後照樣往前。

cards.pattern: OK, great — what does [模糊的詞] actually mean?
cards.quote: I got the feedback that I needed to be more strategic. I was like, "Okay, great. What does being more strategic mean?" And nobody could tell me.
cards.zh: 我收到的回饋是「要更有策略性」。我心想：好啊，那「更有策略性」到底是什麼意思？結果沒有人講得出來。
cards.why: Okay, great 先接受回饋、不辯解，再追問定義。這一組（接受＋要定義）能把空泛評價逼成可執行的東西，而且不會被讀成在辯護。
swaps: Happy to work on it — what would 'more strategic' look like day to day?
Got it. Can you give me an example of someone doing that well?
What would I be doing differently if I nailed that?
cards.pmNote: 收到抽象的績效回饋時，追問「具體行為」與「範例人物」，否則你會改到錯的地方。
cards.episode: Jackie Bavaro on getting better at product strategy, what exactly is strategy, PM pitfalls to avoid, advancing your career, getting into management, and much more

alts.quote: Okay, what do you mean by this? Are you talking about inner and outer loop? Are you talking about friction?
alts.zh: 好，你指的是什麼意思？你講的是內外迴圈嗎？還是講摩擦成本？

alts.quote: I'm not saying that we should not take customer feedback, that's very different.
alts.zh: 我不是說不要聽客戶回饋——那是完全不同的兩件事。

alts.quote: Just to clarify what you just said, what do you mean when you say citation strategy is different?
alts.zh: 我釐清一下你剛剛講的：你說引用策略不一樣，是什麼意思？

cards.pattern: The right answer to a narrowly scoped problem is not to invent a whole new [大東西].
cards.quote: And the right answer to these narrowly scoped defined problems is not to invent a whole new print dialogue.
cards.zh: 面對這種範圍很窄、已經定義清楚的問題，正確答案並不是重新發明一整套列印對話框。
cards.why: The right answer to X is not to Y——先立標準再排除做法，比直接說「你做太多了」不傷人。這是替別人（或自己）縮範疇時很好用的句型。
swaps: This doesn't need a redesign — it needs to ship.
The win here is doing the simple thing well.
Big creative swings are the wrong tool for this one.
cards.pmNote: 初階 PM 最常見的傷：拿到小任務卻硬做大改造，把「值得信任」的分數花掉。
cards.episode: Jackie Bavaro on getting better at product strategy, what exactly is strategy, PM pitfalls to avoid, advancing your career, getting into management, and much more

alts.quote: And as long as your decision is like 70% right, you can iterate on that 20, 30% in either direction, but if you don't commit, then you don't actually get any new information that is high fidelity and high quality.
alts.zh: 只要決策有七成對，剩下的兩三成你都可以往任一邊修；但你不下注，就拿不到任何高品質的新資訊。

alts.quote: In product, I like to joke, there's no right answers. There's only wrong answers, and you're just trying to execute well on the least wrong answer that's available to you.
alts.zh: 做產品這行我常開玩笑說：沒有對的答案，只有錯的答案；你能做的就是把眼前「最不錯」的那個做好。

alts.quote: And I think people don't understand that in a competitive environment, being right is good, but being quick is necessary.
alts.zh: 我覺得大家沒搞懂：在競爭環境裡，做對是加分，做得快是必要條件。

cards.pattern: That person needs to step up and be a multiplier on everybody else's work.
cards.quote: That person needs to step up more, to be somebody who's really contributing and adding and being a multiplier on the work of everybody else on their team.
cards.zh: 那個人需要更站出來一點，成為真正有貢獻、有加分，能把團隊其他人的產出放大的角色。
cards.why: step up 指出不足、multiplier 給出目標畫面，一句話同時完成批評與方向。給難聽回饋時，最好的收尾永遠是一個具體的、可以想像的角色形象。
swaps: I'd like to see you take more of the lead here.
You're adding less than you could — let's fix that.
I want you multiplying the team, not just tracking it.
cards.pmNote: PM 的績效不是自己做了多少，而是讓團隊產出被放大多少；當旁邊有強設計師時最容易退化成記錄員。
cards.episode: Jackie Bavaro on getting better at product strategy, what exactly is strategy, PM pitfalls to avoid, advancing your career, getting into management, and much more

alts.quote: I always start with, "Does this person actually know what you expect of them?" If not, go back to step one.
alts.zh: 我一定先問一句：這個人到底知不知道你對他的期待是什麼？如果不知道，那就回到第一步。

alts.quote: I respect that, and I relate to it in some ways with my own trying to get attention for my own work. But, "I deserve this" that's not a good tactical decision for your business.
alts.zh: 我尊重這種心情，我自己在推廣作品時也有過。但「我值得」不是一個好的商業決策理由。

alts.quote: It's like they know what to do, but they don't understand how to tie it back to the business context and the overall strategy needs and so where to prioritize.
alts.zh: 他們知道該做什麼，只是不知道怎麼把這件事接回商業脈絡跟整體策略，所以也就排不出優先順序。

cards.pattern: Yes it failed — but what I learned from that is [具體做法改變], and since then [結果].
cards.quote: I don't want them to leave it at, "It was a big loss." You want to say, "What I learned from that is now I always run a load test, and I've had many successful launches since then."
cards.zh: 我不希望他只停在「那是一次很大的損失」。你應該說：我從那件事學到，現在我一定會先跑壓力測試，後來的好幾次上線都沒再出過同樣的問題。
cards.why: 談失敗一定要有第三段：損失→新做法→之後的證據。少了最後那段證據，聽起來就只是懺悔；有了它，失敗反而變成能力證明。
swaps: We lost X. What changed after was Y, and it's held since.
That failure gave us the checklist we still use.
Since then I've never shipped without…
cards.pmNote: postmortem 的產出應該是一條被寫進流程的規則，不是一份心得。
cards.episode: Jackie Bavaro on getting better at product strategy, what exactly is strategy, PM pitfalls to avoid, advancing your career, getting into management, and much more

alts.quote: So there's probably just too many specific examples of times I've screwed up in my career, but there probably is a really common thread to it. And I think it's probably an easy trap for any PM to fall into, which is averages mean nothing to the individual is probably the thing that I've really scarred by.
alts.zh: 我職涯搞砸的例子多到講不完，但它們有一條很明顯的共通線：平均值對個別使用者毫無意義——這是我被燙傷最深的一課。

alts.quote: We get a lot of crap for the model chooser, and I own it. I've tried to say that to everyone who will listen.
alts.zh: 模型選單被罵翻，這我認。我逢人就講這件事是我的責任。

alts.quote: So it's someone that as a leader, you are in the hot seat and you can take accountability. So if some of these things don't pan out, it's on you and not on your team, and give your team permission to fail.
alts.zh: 身為領導者，你就是坐在火線上、要負起責任的人。如果這些事沒成，那是你的責任，不是團隊的責任——同時給團隊失敗的許可。

cards.pattern: I just want to make a huge caveat — this isn't a judgment on any of these.
cards.quote: And again, I just want to make a huge caveat, this is not a judgment on any of these particular perspectives. It's more like I noticed a lot of it.
cards.zh: 再強調一次，我要先加一個很大的但書：我不是在評判這些觀點的好壞，比較像是我注意到它們特別多。
cards.why: 在批評整個產業風氣之前先立一道免責聲明，把「我在觀察」和「我在批判」分開。想講重話又不想樹敵時，caveat 是最重要的前置動作。
swaps: Big caveat up front: I'm not knocking any of this.
To be clear, this isn't a criticism — just an observation.
With the obvious disclaimer that…
cards.pmNote: 產品建議大多預設了矽谷新創的脈絡；照抄到別種公司常常比不做還糟。
cards.episode: What differentiates the highest-performing product teams | John Cutler (Amplitude, The Beautiful Mess)

alts.quote: Yeah, it's definitely a huge part of it. There's a couple of things that I noticed get in the way.
alts.zh: 對，那絕對是很大一塊。不過我有注意到幾件事會卡住。

alts.quote: I'm not saying that having a large market someday doesn't matter, of course it does eventually. But trying to be super pedantic about market size when it's a pre-seed company, it's just not something I'd put a lot of thought.
alts.zh: 我不是說市場總有一天要夠大這件事不重要，當然重要。但在一家 pre-seed 公司還在糾結市場規模算得多精確，我不會花太多心思在上面。

alts.quote: So this might mean that I think... I don't want to say that if you don't have experience, don't start one, but it's kind of true. So become an expert somewhere, somehow, before you start.
alts.zh: 我不想說「沒經驗就別開始」這種話……但其實有點是真的。所以動手前，先想辦法在某個地方變成專家。

cards.pattern: Both things can be true. Yes, [讓步]. However, it is true that [你的重點].
cards.quote: Both things can be true. It's like, yeah, there's nothing perfect in product. However, it is true that some companies are healthier than others.
cards.zh: 這兩件事可以同時成立。對，產品這行沒有什麼是完美的；但同樣真實的是，有些公司確實比其他公司健康得多。
cards.why: 先把對方的話完整承認一次（yeah, …），再用 however it is true that 把自己的重點放回桌上。讓步不是輸，而是換取對方接住你下一句的注意力。
swaps: Both can be true at the same time.
Sure, and at the same time…
Agreed — that said, it's still the case that…
cards.pmNote: 區分 chronic（長期慢性）與 acute（急性）問題：把慢性債還掉的公司，遇到景氣衝擊時才撐得住。
cards.episode: What differentiates the highest-performing product teams | John Cutler (Amplitude, The Beautiful Mess)

alts.quote: Yeah, it's definitely a huge part of it. There's a couple of things that I noticed get in the way.
alts.zh: 對，那絕對是很大一塊。不過我有注意到幾件事會卡住。

alts.quote: You're focused on recent and I'm just going to push back. No, there's nothing terribly recent.
alts.zh: 你一直扣在「最近」這個點上，我要反過來擋一下——沒有，最近沒什麼特別的。

alts.quote: And don't get me wrong, I think there's a lot of product folks out there who enjoy that modality of work, I'm not one of them.
alts.zh: 別誤會，我知道有很多產品人是真的喜歡那種工作方式的——我不是。

cards.quote: Go and talk to that executive and say, "Look, I know you've told me to do this, but what would we observe if this was working versus not working? I'm here to help you with that."
cards.zh: 你可以去找那位主管說：「我知道你已經指定要做這個了，但如果它有效跟沒效，我們會分別看到什麼？這部分我可以幫你。」
cards.why: 先明確認輸（我知道這已經拍板），換取問一個真正關鍵的問題的權利，最後用「我來幫你」把自己放在同陣營。這是對付上對下命令最漂亮的一招——沒挑戰決定，只挑戰未定義的成功條件。
swaps: Decision's made, I get that — what would tell us it's working?
I'm on board. How will we know if it lands?
Since we're doing it: what signal should we watch?
cards.pmNote: 在自主權很低的組織裡，仍然可以爭取到「定義成功指標」這一格——這是把 output 文化撬開的最小施力點。
cards.episode: What differentiates the highest-performing product teams | John Cutler (Amplitude, The Beautiful Mess)

alts.quote: You write this document and I'm sorry, who actually reads it? You know what I mean? I know it's painful, but it's like that.
alts.zh: 你寫了那份文件——不好意思，但到底有誰真的會讀？你懂我意思吧？我知道這很刺耳，但事實就是這樣。

alts.quote: People say that time flies and it doesn't. What happens is it goes by unaccounted.
alts.zh: 大家都說時間過得很快，其實不是。真正發生的是：那些日子根本沒被記下來。

alts.quote: It's one thing to say you're spending a lot of time looking outside the building. It's a whole other thing to hear from the places you don't normally hear from.
alts.zh: 說自己花很多時間在公司外面看，是一回事；真的去聽那些你平常聽不到的聲音，完全是另一回事。

cards.pattern: It's the difference between oversimplifying and focusing — I need to hold some things constant.
cards.quote: I think it's the difference between oversimplification and focusing. You can have a complex problem and be like, "You know what? I need to hold some things constant."
cards.zh: 我覺得差別在於「過度簡化」和「聚焦」。面對複雜問題你可以說：好，我需要先把某些變數固定住。
cards.why: 用一組對照詞（oversimplification / focusing）把「我要縮小範圍」講成方法論而不是偷懶。hold things constant 借自科學，很適合在會議上為砍範疇辯護。
swaps: Let's hold those variables constant for now.
That's focusing, not dumbing it down.
We can't move unless we freeze a few things.
cards.pmNote: 複雜系統裡要有進展，就得刻意凍結一部分變數；分不清「簡化」與「聚焦」的團隊，會在無限討論裡打轉。
cards.episode: What differentiates the highest-performing product teams | John Cutler (Amplitude, The Beautiful Mess)

alts.quote: So yeah, no hard and fast rule, but I think it's always you need to have this matrix of options in your mind and be very deliberate about which one you are going with and why.
alts.zh: 沒有什麼鐵則，但你腦中要有一張選項矩陣，而且要很清楚自己選了哪一格、為什麼。

alts.quote: I think that becomes a bit of a strategic conversation of do we want to have a better chance of surviving, going after a niche that we know we can serve well?
alts.zh: 我覺得這時候就變成一個策略層級的討論了：我們是要提高存活機率、去打一個我們服務得很好的利基市場嗎？

alts.quote: Be careful. If you need to spend a little time on the problem, fine, but don't spend a lot of time because you need to save as much time as possible to come up with the winning solution.
alts.zh: 小心一點。你要花一點時間在問題上沒問題，但別花太多，因為你得盡量把時間留給「想出會贏的解法」。

cards.pattern: That's the trillion-dollar question, so I don't really have an answer — I have a couple of thoughts.
cards.quote: That's the problem. I mean, that is the trillion dollar question so I don't really have an answer. I have a couple thoughts on it.
cards.zh: 問題就在這。這是那種價值一兆美元的問題，所以我其實沒有答案，但我有幾點想法。
cards.why: 先把問題捧高（trillion-dollar question），承認沒答案就不再像無能，而像誠實；再用 a couple of thoughts 把發言權留住。承認不知道又不失分量，全靠這個順序。
swaps: If I knew that, I'd be retired — but here's how I think about it.
No clean answer; a few observations though.
That's the hard one. I've got partial answers.
cards.pmNote: 「人 vs 流程哪個決定績效」沒有定論；能講清楚兩邊的證據，比硬給比例更有價值。
cards.episode: What differentiates the highest-performing product teams | John Cutler (Amplitude, The Beautiful Mess)

alts.quote: So again, I don't mean to overstate this, and I certainly don't mean to claim that there's some answer that's right for everybody, of course, but surely this is the right kind of question.
alts.zh: 我不想把這件事講得太滿，也絕對不是說有一個答案適用所有人——但這絕對是該問的那類問題。

alts.quote: I think this is a nuanced question and it's hard for me to say something on a podcast that'll actually be useful to people, but here's a couple of thoughts.
alts.zh: 我覺得這是個很有層次的問題，要在 podcast 上講出真的對別人有用的東西很難，不過我有幾個想法。

alts.quote: I mean, look, I don't know that it's a perfect answer, but I think the reality is just that what kills most projects most early companies is stamina.
alts.zh: 我是說，我不確定這是不是完美的答案，但我覺得現實就是：殺死大多數專案、大多數早期公司的，是續航力。

cards.pattern: Four or five years ago I would've said [舊立場]. I used to be one of those people.
cards.quote: Four or five years ago, I would've said, well, personal skills, nothing. It's all the environment. I used to be one of those particular people.
cards.zh: 四五年前我會說：個人能力根本不重要，全都是環境造成的。我以前就是那一派的人。
cards.why: 把過去的自己拿出來當反例，是最不傷人的反駁方式——你批評的是曾經的自己，而不是現場的誰。同時也證明你會隨證據更新。
swaps: I used to believe exactly that.
Past me would've argued the same thing.
I've flipped on this over the last few years.
cards.pmNote: 對「環境決定論 vs 能力決定論」保持流動立場，才不會在招募與組織設計上做出極端決策。
cards.episode: What differentiates the highest-performing product teams | John Cutler (Amplitude, The Beautiful Mess)

alts.quote: When I was younger and I was starting off, I used to think it's all about the product.
alts.zh: 我年輕、剛入行的時候，以為一切就是產品而已。

alts.quote: And I used to think leadership was the same, which is, well, it's not about you as a leader, it's about who are you bringing along on your journey?
alts.zh: 我以前也以為領導力是同一回事——就是說，重點不在你這個領導者身上，而在你把誰一起帶上路。

alts.quote: Yeah, I used to think it was versus, but now I realize that they combine really well.
alts.zh: 對，我以前覺得這兩個是互斥的，但現在我發現它們其實搭得很好。

cards.pattern: A lot of this advice is common sense. That doesn't mean it's easy to put in motion.
cards.quote: It's like these things that seem so common sense are actually hard with what they're doing… a lot of the advice is common sense. That doesn't mean it's easy to put in motion.
cards.zh: 這些看起來根本是常識的東西，真的做起來很難……很多建議都是常識，但常識不代表容易落地。
cards.why: 對方還沒說出口的「這不是廢話嗎」，你先幫他說完，再把重點移到執行。搶先承認顯而易見的部分，是化解 so what 質疑的標準手法。
swaps: I know it sounds obvious — obvious isn't easy.
Simple to say, hard to run.
Everyone agrees with it; almost nobody does it.
cards.pmNote: 高績效團隊的差異往往不在知不知道，而在有沒有把常識制度化（例如 Amazon 的 bar raiser）。
cards.episode: What differentiates the highest-performing product teams | John Cutler (Amplitude, The Beautiful Mess)

alts.quote: Actually, all feedback I think is valid. People's feelings are valid, but it doesn't mean that you need to do something about all of those things.
alts.zh: 其實我覺得所有回饋都是有效的。別人的感受都是真的，但這不代表你每一項都得去處理。

alts.quote: But before that, I think getting to product-market fit, obviously there's a lot of methodology for doing it today that might make it a bit easier for people, but I still think it's fairly random and pretty dang hard.
alts.zh: 在那之前——我覺得要走到 PMF，現在當然有很多方法論可能讓大家輕鬆一點，但我還是認為它相當隨機，而且真的很難。

alts.quote: That's a good idea, but we don't actually understand these three things before we start working on that. So maybe we should do understand work to make sure that that is actually the right idea.
alts.zh: 這個想法不錯，但在動手之前有三件事我們其實還沒搞懂。也許先做點「理解型的工作」，確認這真的是對的方向。

cards.pattern: The last thing I want to do is say you either have [X] or you don't.
cards.quote: The last thing I want to do is be like you have a product mindset or you don't.
cards.zh: 我最不想做的事，就是把它講成「你要嘛有產品思維、要嘛沒有」。
cards.why: The last thing I want to do is… 用「我拒絕做某件事」的方式反對一個流行說法，不必點名任何人。要拆掉別人的二分法，先宣布自己不玩這個分類。
swaps: I don't want to turn it into a binary.
I'd hate to frame it as haves and have-nots.
That's the framing I'm trying to avoid.
cards.pmNote: 把「product sense」拆成可教的能力（建模、系統思考、不確定下決策、引導），才有辦法培養人。
cards.episode: What differentiates the highest-performing product teams | John Cutler (Amplitude, The Beautiful Mess)

alts.quote: So this might mean that I think... I don't want to say that if you don't have experience, don't start one, but it's kind of true. So become an expert somewhere, somehow, before you start.
alts.zh: 我不想說「沒經驗就別開始」這種話……但其實有點是真的。所以動手前，先想辦法在某個地方變成專家。

alts.quote: And I know this is going to trigger some people, but the truth is they don't want to work.
alts.zh: 我知道這句會讓一些人不爽，但事實就是——他們不想做事。

alts.quote: We're very interested in folks who have already been thinking about what the future should look like with agents. And we don't have to agree on where we're going, but we want people who are very passionate.
alts.zh: 我們很想找那種已經在思考「agent 的未來該長什麼樣」的人。方向上我們不一定要有共識，但我們要真的在乎這件事的人。

cards.quote: I took us off track a little bit. I think you were going to go onto a second piece of advice.
cards.zh: 我剛剛好像把話題帶偏了一點。你原本要講的第二個建議是什麼？
cards.why: 把偏題的責任攬到自己身上（I took us off track），對方就不會覺得被指責話多。這是主持人把會議拉回主線最沒有摩擦的方式。
swaps: That's on me — you were on point two.
I derailed us; please continue.
Let's get back to where you were.
cards.pmNote: 會議主持的成本大多花在收斂；用自我歸責的方式回主線，能維持發言者的安全感。
cards.episode: What differentiates the highest-performing product teams | John Cutler (Amplitude, The Beautiful Mess)

alts.quote: he'll sit in a review and be like, "I don't think this is right." And then he'll pause and say, "I'm going to clear the rest of my day. Let's sit and figure it out."
alts.zh: 他會在評審會上說：「我覺得這不對。」然後停一下說：「我把今天剩下的行程清掉，我們一起坐下來把它弄清楚。」

alts.quote: So let me take us back on track and let's talk about just the high level framework here.
alts.zh: 我們把話題拉回來，來談一下這個框架的高層次架構。

alts.quote: So I think we talked about how to decide whether to resource SEO, but we didn't talk about how to understand what the expectations are from SEO.
alts.zh: 我覺得我們談了「要不要投資源做 SEO」，但還沒談「對 SEO 的期待該怎麼設定」。

cards.pattern: Let me just summarize the top [N] things you shared, and then I have a two-part question.
cards.quote: But before we do that, let me just summarize maybe the top five attributes and kind of traits you just shared, and then I have a two part question around this.
cards.zh: 在進到那個之前，我先把你剛剛講的五個特質整理一次，然後我有一個兩段式的問題。
cards.why: 先預告動作（我要整理）、再預告下一步（然後我要問），聽者知道會被帶去哪裡。長討論之後不做這個動作，共識就會蒸發。
swaps: Let me play that back to make sure I've got it.
Quick recap before we move on.
So the five things I'm hearing are…
cards.pmNote: 把對方講的東西複述成編號清單，是最有效的 alignment 檢查，也順便取得議程主導權。
cards.episode: What differentiates the highest-performing product teams | John Cutler (Amplitude, The Beautiful Mess)

alts.quote: Let me just try to summarize what you shared, this five step framework.
alts.zh: 我試著把你剛剛講的整理一下，這個五步驟的框架。

alts.quote: So I was taking notes as you were talking and there's kind of these four items just to summarize.
alts.zh: 你講的時候我一直在記筆記，總結起來大概是這四項。

alts.quote: So maybe this is a way to come back to your question about what's the output of the shaping session, it's like it's shaped if we can give this to a technical person and they say, "Yeah, I know what to go build now."
alts.zh: 所以回到你剛剛問的「shaping session 的產出是什麼」：判準是——把它交給一個技術的人，他會說「好，我知道要蓋什麼了」。

cards.pattern: I'm not an expert in this — [某人] wrote about it and they're much smarter than I am.
cards.quote: And again, I'm not an expert in this and I think Erin Meyer wrote that book, The Culture Map. So you should just find what those people wrote because they're much smarter than I am about this.
cards.zh: 再說一次，我不是這方面的專家。Erin Meyer 寫過《文化地圖》那本書，你們應該直接去看他們寫的，他們比我懂太多了。
cards.why: 承認不懂之後立刻指路，就從「不知道」變成「知道去哪找」。轉介比硬答更能建立信任，而且保住了你在自己專業區的可信度。
swaps: Not my area — X has done the real work on this.
I'd point you to someone who actually knows.
I only know enough to be dangerous here.
cards.pmNote: 知道「這是一門有人專精的學問」本身就是能力；PM 的價值常在於認得出邊界並接上專家。
cards.episode: What differentiates the highest-performing product teams | John Cutler (Amplitude, The Beautiful Mess)

alts.quote: So those will be custom for anything. And I hate to use the word, it depends because I think whenever consultants say it depends, they're just throwing their hands up and saying, "I don't really know."
alts.zh: 這些每家都不一樣。我很不想講「看情況」，因為顧問一講「看情況」，通常就是兩手一攤說「我其實不知道」。

alts.quote: And if you push a really experienced product director like that, they're going to go, "Good point, I don't. I'm going to go find out."
alts.zh: 你這樣逼一個真正資深的產品總監，他會說：「說得對，我確實不知道。我去查清楚。」

alts.quote: I'll admit I'm definitely not an SEO expert. I've been fortunate to work with some of the best marketers in the world who I think are bonafide legends at this point
alts.zh: 我坦白說我絕對不是 SEO 專家。我只是很幸運跟一些世界頂尖的行銷人共事過，那些人到今天都算是真正的傳奇。

cards.pattern: It's one thing to say [X]. It's a whole other thing to [真正做到的行為].
cards.quote: It's one thing to say you're spending a lot of time looking outside the building. It's a whole other thing to hear from the places you don't normally hear from.
cards.zh: 說自己花很多時間在公司外面看，是一回事；真的去聽那些你平常聽不到的聲音，完全是另一回事。
cards.why: It's one thing… it's a whole other thing… 是英語裡拆穿「自我感覺良好」最漂亮的對稱句型：先承認宣稱，再把標準提高一級。不指名、不指責，但沒人躲得掉。
swaps: Saying it and doing it are different things.
It's one thing to care; another to build a system for it.
Easy to claim, hard to evidence.
cards.pmNote: 避開 availability bias：永遠找同一批熟客講話，等於用同一組資料反覆確認自己。
cards.episode: Why great AI products are all about the data | Shaun Clowes (CPO Confluent, ex-Salesforce, Atlassian)

alts.quote: I don't think there's any one thing that has happened. I think that a lot of times people ascribe a lot of momentum to a one time change or a single person.
alts.zh: 我不覺得有哪一件事是關鍵。很多時候大家會把一整段動能歸給某一次改動、或某一個人。

alts.quote: We're all sitting talking about it, and Tate says, "It's a low margin reseller, one time sells." "You can say dotcom all you like, it's a low margin reseller."
alts.zh: 大家在車上討論，Tate 說：「它就是個低毛利的經銷商，一次性買賣。你要講幾次『.com』都可以，它還是個低毛利經銷商。」

alts.quote: I think maybe on the flip side of less positive is what it definitely learned is most of the time you hear it's really complex, it isn't. Leadership's just weak.
alts.zh: 我確實學到的是：多數時候你聽到「這件事很複雜」，其實它不複雜。只是領導層軟弱而已。

cards.pattern: Your job is to say no to 90% of what comes your way, so you can say yes to 10%.
cards.quote: Realistically when you're a product manager, your job is to say no to 90% of things that get brought your way. And so you're saying no to 90%, so you can say yes to 10%.
cards.zh: 說穿了，當產品經理的工作就是把送到你面前的九成東西拒絕掉——你拒絕九成，才有辦法對那一成說好。
cards.why: 把拒絕定義成職務內容而不是個人態度，同時給出「為了說好」這個正當理由。要在文化上習慣說好的環境裡守住範疇，先立這個框最有效。
swaps: Every no here is protecting a yes somewhere else.
Saying no is most of the job.
We can't say yes to this without dropping that.
cards.pmNote: scope control 的本質是機會成本：每一個 yes 都在偷走另一件事的工程時間。
cards.episode: Why great AI products are all about the data | Shaun Clowes (CPO Confluent, ex-Salesforce, Atlassian)

alts.quote: If the product manager and the designer are not available to be there during their product test, cancel the test. They need to be there.
alts.zh: 如果產品經理和設計師沒辦法到場，那這場使用者測試就取消。他們一定要在現場。

alts.quote: You can say, "Yes, I agree. That is a real problem. Yes, I think we could test this design with users."
alts.zh: 你可以說：「對，我同意，那確實是個真的問題。對，我覺得這個設計我們可以拿去跟使用者測。」

alts.quote: Yeah, total waste of time. Yeah, I mean, unless there's a reason for it. So if you're a media company and traffic means that that number keeps going up, then yes, it matters.
alts.zh: 對，純粹浪費時間。嗯，除非真的有理由啦。如果你是媒體公司、流量就是那個一路往上的數字，那當然有意義。

cards.quote: Is the juice worth the squeeze? And now I would say that it's pretty clear that the juice is worth the squeeze.
cards.zh: 這個果汁值得你這樣擠嗎？以現在來看，我會說很明顯是值得的。
cards.why: 一句話把 ROI 討論口語化，比 is it worth the investment 生動很多，母語者在會議上常用。台灣人講成本效益時常太正式，這句能讓你聽起來像局內人。
swaps: Is the payoff worth the effort?
Does the return justify the lift?
Is that worth the squeeze for us?
cards.pmNote: 評估投入前先問這句，能擋掉大量「做了也不會改變結果」的專案。
cards.episode: Why great AI products are all about the data | Shaun Clowes (CPO Confluent, ex-Salesforce, Atlassian)

alts.quote: And now, it's not like, "Okay, now, we're screwed and the project is going to be bigger." Now, we can have a really cool conversation about trade-offs.
alts.zh: 所以現在不是「完了，這專案要爆了」。現在我們可以來一場很棒的取捨對話。

alts.quote: Now, again, don't hear this as antagonistic. We're not antagonistic here. We're trying to say, "What's going to help me succeed?"
alts.zh: 再說一次，不要把這聽成對立。我們不是在對抗。我們是在問：什麼能幫我把這件事做成？

alts.quote: And it's hard because in making it compact you're losing completeness.
alts.zh: 這很難，因為你把它壓得越精簡，就越不完整。

cards.pattern: First let's examine the counterfactual — let's start with the opposite of your question.
cards.quote: First let's examine the counterfactual, right? So let's start with the opposite of your question and say, "How would the world be sadder if we all just gave up on this?"
cards.zh: 我們先看反面情況吧。從你問題的相反面開始想：如果大家乾脆全都放棄這件事，世界會變得多糟？
cards.why: 被問「這東西還值得做嗎」時，不直接辯護，而是把問題倒過來問一次。反事實框架讓對方自己走到你的結論，這是最高段的接招方式。
swaps: Let's flip it: what happens if we don't?
What's the cost of doing nothing?
Take the opposite case for a second.
cards.pmNote: 辯護一項投資時，先算「不做的代價」往往比列出好處更有說服力。
cards.episode: Why great AI products are all about the data | Shaun Clowes (CPO Confluent, ex-Salesforce, Atlassian)

alts.quote: First of all, maybe just to set the record straight, if AI is writing over 90% of the code, that doesn't mean engineers are 10X as productive.
alts.zh: 首先，我先把話講清楚：就算 AI 寫了九成以上的程式碼，也不代表工程師的產出就變成十倍。

alts.quote: Here's what I have a problem with. First of all, having a growth mindset is a very, very helpful thing.
alts.zh: 我要說的是我對它的哪一點有意見。首先，擁有成長心態本身是非常非常有幫助的事。

alts.quote: But if they come in on day one saying your strategy is all wrong, raises the question of, "Well then why did you join my team if you didn't believe in my strategy?"
alts.zh: 但如果他第一天就說你的策略整個都錯了，那就會讓人想問：既然你不相信這個策略，當初為什麼要加入我的團隊？

cards.quote: Data is more like a compass than a GPS. If you look at data as a way of giving you the answer, you're always wrong. Wrong or slow, or sometimes both.
cards.zh: 數據比較像指南針，不是導航。如果你把數據當成會給你答案的東西，你不是錯就是慢，有時候兩者都有。
cards.why: 一個比喻同時完成主張與反駁（compass vs GPS），比長篇論述好記十倍。要挑戰「數據至上」文化時，用比喻比用理由安全，因為沒有人被說錯。
swaps: Data points the direction; it doesn't drive.
It narrows the uncertainty — it doesn't decide.
Think compass, not autopilot.
cards.pmNote: 資料的功能是把不確定性降到可以做下一個決策的程度，而不是取代判斷。
cards.episode: Why great AI products are all about the data | Shaun Clowes (CPO Confluent, ex-Salesforce, Atlassian)

alts.quote: The basic principle with laser is that willpower is never going to win, and there's great research on this, but for now just trust me, you're not going to white-knuckle your way through not looking at Twitter when you're trying to work.
alts.zh: laser 的基本原理是：意志力永遠贏不了。這方面有很多很好的研究，但現在你先信我——你不可能靠硬撐來讓自己工作時不看 Twitter。

alts.quote: I think Peter Thiel actually says it more simply and elegantly, which is, 'You need to be right about something that other people think you're wrong about for a very long time.'
alts.zh: 我覺得 Peter Thiel 講得更簡潔漂亮：「你得在一件別人認為你錯的事情上，長時間地正確。」

alts.quote: Whenever you talk to people who are at the company, they're always try to tell you the best version of the company. It's on you to triangulate that information, but you need both sides.
alts.zh: 你去問還在公司裡的人，他們永遠給你公司最好的那個版本。要交叉比對是你自己的責任，但兩邊的說法你都得聽到。

cards.pattern: It'd be better not to show up with an analysis than to show up with one that's dumb.
cards.quote: If you present data with authority and that data is ridiculous, you don't just not get benefit for that. You lose a whole bunch of brownie points.
cards.zh: 如果你很有底氣地端出一份數據，結果那份數據很荒謬，你不只是沒加到分，還會倒扣一大堆好感度。
cards.why: brownie points（好感點數）是台灣人幾乎不會用但母語者很常講的說法。整句用「不只沒好處、還倒扣」的雙層結構，把警告講得比單純說 be careful 有力得多。
swaps: A shaky analysis costs you more than no analysis.
You'll lose credibility, not just the argument.
Better to say 'I don't know yet' than to bring this.
cards.pmNote: 帶分析進會議前先自問樣本、選擇偏誤、上下游是否合理，否則被當場拆穿的代價是長期信用。
cards.episode: Why great AI products are all about the data | Shaun Clowes (CPO Confluent, ex-Salesforce, Atlassian)

alts.quote: It's about saying, okay, if we have these themes of stuff that we want to work on, what do we know with confidence because the data tells us and what do we need to understand because we don't have the data?
alts.zh: 重點是要問：在我們想做的這些主題裡，哪些是數據講得夠清楚、我們有把握的？哪些是因為沒數據，所以還得先搞懂的？

alts.quote: So there's a different metric that I like to use, which keys off of this idea that I think, again, people don't appreciate, which is cancellations grow faster than marketing.
alts.zh: 我比較喜歡用另一個指標，它是從一個大家常常沒放在心上的觀念推出來的：取消的成長速度比行銷快。

alts.quote: If we just acknowledge reality and this person looks bored, they look bored, that is data. Don't ignore that data.
alts.zh: 如果我們願意面對現實——這個人看起來很無聊，那他就是很無聊。那是資料。別忽略那筆資料。

cards.quote: Oftentimes when I see analysis from different product leaders or even data teams, you can drive a truck through it, literally drive a truck through it.
cards.zh: 我常看到一些產品主管、甚至數據團隊做的分析，那個漏洞大到可以開一台卡車過去，真的。
cards.why: 英語裡形容論證漏洞用「洞大到可以開卡車」，比 there are holes 具體且好笑。批評分析品質時用誇飾的成語，殺傷力強但語氣還是輕鬆的。
swaps: There are holes you could drive a truck through.
That argument leaks in three places.
It doesn't hold water.
cards.pmNote: 常見的三個洞：樣本不具代表性、有選擇偏誤、只看單點沒看上下游。
cards.episode: Why great AI products are all about the data | Shaun Clowes (CPO Confluent, ex-Salesforce, Atlassian)

alts.quote: Now even if they had the best of experiences with your answer, now they're looking at everything you said through the lens of, oh, this person was kind of uncertain.
alts.zh: 就算他們原本對你的回答感受很好，現在他們也會透過「這個人好像沒把握」這個濾鏡，重新看你剛剛講的每一句話。

alts.quote: To me, I think it's a great accelerant when it's already working, but it can't fix it if people don't want to talk about your product.
alts.zh: 對我來說，那在本來就跑得動的時候是很好的加速器，但如果根本沒人想談論你的產品，它救不了你。

alts.quote: I was like, "That's the product. The thing you're talking about is the product."
alts.zh: 我就說：「那就是產品啊。你正在講的那個東西，就是產品本身。」

cards.pattern: I don't really love that thinking process, just in general.
cards.quote: But the other thing is I don't really love some of that thinking process just in general.
cards.zh: 另外還有一點：那整套思考方式，我其實不是很喜歡，講一般情況啦。
cards.why: I don't really love… 是英語裡最溫和的否定之一：用喜好語氣（而非對錯）表達異議，再加 just in general 把它從針對現場的人拉開。台灣人常在這種場合直接說 that's wrong，成本高很多。
swaps: I'm not sold on that way of thinking.
That framing doesn't sit right with me.
I'd push back on the logic a bit.
cards.pmNote: 實驗效果不能長期維持，不代表當初那個效果沒有價值——可能是後續沒接住的問題。
cards.episode: Why great AI products are all about the data | Shaun Clowes (CPO Confluent, ex-Salesforce, Atlassian)

alts.quote: I think this is an interesting thing that technical founders sometimes don't really like. They think sales is a very negative part of the process. I think it's not that black and white.
alts.zh: 技術背景的創辦人常常不太喜歡這件事，他們覺得業務是整個過程裡很負面的一塊。我覺得沒那麼非黑即白。

alts.quote: And don't get me wrong, I love those cultures, but they're all different cultures. They're very different cultures.
alts.zh: 別誤會，那些文化我都很欣賞，但它們彼此其實非常不一樣，真的差很多。

alts.quote: In terms of evaluating the options, I don't love pros and cons. It's a flat list of text. It's hard to just get the big picture from that.
alts.zh: 在評估選項這件事上，我不太喜歡用優缺點列表。它就是一串平鋪的文字，很難一眼看到全貌。

cards.pattern: This idea that [X] just seems like a fantasy to me.
cards.quote: And so from my perspective, this idea that this just completely destroys the differentiation of these business process SaaS applications just seems like a fantasy, a crazy fantasy.
cards.zh: 所以就我的角度來看，「這會徹底摧毀這類商業流程 SaaS 的差異化」這種說法，聽起來根本是幻想，而且是很扯的幻想。
cards.why: 強度極高的否定，但開頭 from my perspective 與 this idea that 兩層緩衝，讓你打的是「這個說法」而不是「說這話的人」。想在英文會議上表達強烈不同意，這是安全的最高檔。
swaps: That story doesn't hold up for me.
I think that's wishful thinking.
From where I sit, that's not how it plays out.
cards.pmNote: AI 讓做出「表單＋資料庫」變便宜，反而強化既有系統的地位，因為 lock-in 來自流程不是介面。
cards.episode: Why great AI products are all about the data | Shaun Clowes (CPO Confluent, ex-Salesforce, Atlassian)

alts.quote: So I would expect that if you have a startup and that startup is not B2B in some way, that it would be possibly very reasonable that business publications might not be your target right now.
alts.zh: 所以我會預期，如果你的新創不算 B2B，那商業媒體現在可能不是你該鎖定的對象——這樣想其實滿合理的。

alts.quote: I hate the idea of those companies that have separate product owners because product owner is just an administrative role.
alts.zh: 我很不喜歡那些另外設 product owner 的公司，因為 product owner 本質上只是個行政角色。

alts.quote: And then our CEO gets in, and he's like, "I think really number four is the only reasonable one for these reasons."
alts.zh: 然後我們執行長進來說：「我認為真正合理的其實只有第四個，理由如下。」

cards.pattern: Nobody wants to hear it, but really it's just the hard work of [不性感的事].
cards.quote: Nobody wants to hear it. Everybody wants to just think about these really cool models and how smart they are. But really it's just the hard work of getting really good data to the LLMs.
cards.zh: 沒有人想聽這個。大家都只想談那些很酷的模型有多聰明。但說到底，這就是把好資料餵給 LLM 的苦工。
cards.why: 先承認這個訊息不討喜（Nobody wants to hear it），聽眾的防衛就會鬆掉，然後你才有空間講出真正無聊卻正確的結論。報壞消息前的最佳暖身。
swaps: This is the unglamorous part, but…
Nobody likes this answer, and it's still the answer.
It's less exciting than it sounds: it's mostly plumbing.
cards.pmNote: AI 產品 90% 的力氣花在資料管線：拿到對的、即時的、結構化的資料，模型本身反而可替換。
cards.episode: Why great AI products are all about the data | Shaun Clowes (CPO Confluent, ex-Salesforce, Atlassian)

alts.quote: It's so hard to give a founder hard feedback. Who wants to be the bearer of bad news?
alts.zh: 要給創辦人難聽的回饋真的很難。誰想當那個報壞消息的人？

alts.quote: And maybe this is a... I don't want to be very negative, but it's very hard inside a company like ours to task our best engineers to build a best in class sales product.
alts.zh: 我不想講得太負面，但在我們這種公司裡，要把最好的工程師派去做一個頂尖的業務工具，是非常困難的。

alts.quote: You know what? We should ship. It's embarrassing, but that's strictly less bad than not getting the feedback you wanted.
alts.zh: 我覺得就出吧。是很難看沒錯，但這比拿不到你要的回饋還是好一點。

cards.quote: A decision with too little data is fatal. A decision that takes too long and collects too much data is also fatal. So it's about trying to find the balance.
cards.zh: 資料太少就下決策，是致命的；拖太久、蒐集太多資料才決策，一樣致命。所以重點是抓到那個平衡。
cards.why: 用完全對稱的兩句把兩端都封死，聽眾就不會把你的話當成偏向哪一邊。談取捨時，先證明你看得到兩種失敗，你的中間值才有說服力。
swaps: Too early is a guess; too late is a miss.
Both under- and over-researching kill you.
The risk cuts both ways.
cards.pmNote: Colin Powell 的 30/70 法則：低於三成資訊就決策太魯莽，等到七成以上才決策已經太慢。
cards.episode: Why great AI products are all about the data | Shaun Clowes (CPO Confluent, ex-Salesforce, Atlassian)

alts.quote: And as long as your decision is like 70% right, you can iterate on that 20, 30% in either direction, but if you don't commit, then you don't actually get any new information that is high fidelity and high quality.
alts.zh: 只要決策有七成對，剩下的兩三成你都可以往任一邊修；但你不下注，就拿不到任何高品質的新資訊。

alts.quote: There's definitely a trade-off. I think sometimes when companies specialize roles a lot it's because it's more efficient.
alts.zh: 這確實有取捨。公司把角色切得很細，通常是因為那樣比較有效率。

alts.quote: And it's hard because in making it compact you're losing completeness.
alts.zh: 這很難，因為你把它壓得越精簡，就越不完整。

cards.pattern: If you let your calendar rule you, nothing good will happen.
cards.quote: One is that if you let your calendar rule you, then nothing good will happen. It's really hard to be successful unless you find a way to force that to happen.
cards.zh: 第一，如果你讓行事曆牽著你走，就不會有什麼好事發生。除非你想辦法強迫它發生，否則很難做出成績。
cards.why: 把「拒絕會議」這件難以啟齒的事，講成一條普遍法則，你就不必針對任何一場會議說不。let X rule you 是很有畫面的說法，比 be too busy 有力。
swaps: My calendar can't be the thing deciding my priorities.
If I don't block it, it doesn't happen.
I'm protecting time for outside-in work.
cards.pmNote: 把 80% 思考時間留給「公司外面的世界」是理想值，實務上要靠固定的行事曆保護區才守得住。
cards.episode: Why great AI products are all about the data | Shaun Clowes (CPO Confluent, ex-Salesforce, Atlassian)

alts.quote: So yeah, I think the only way you build something that matters that's going to change the world is if you find a big idea you believe in and you say no to everything else.
alts.zh: 我覺得要做出真正有份量、能改變世界的東西，唯一的路就是找到一個你相信的大想法，然後對其他所有東西說不。

alts.quote: Pulling off other responsibilities is no problem. It's a good thing to do, especially as you grow, but never when you touch those three sacred things.
alts.zh: 把其他職責分出去完全沒問題，隨著規模變大這反而是好事——但前提是不能碰到那三件神聖不可讓的事。

alts.quote: if you want to change during the course of the quarter, if you want to disrupt our whole engineering product team, you can do it, but understand there's a high cost, and the later you do it in the quarter, the less successful it's going to be
alts.zh: 你想在季中改、想打亂整個工程團隊，可以啊，但你要知道代價很高——而且愈晚改，效果只會愈差。

cards.pattern: It should have been obvious, and we should have been able to call a spade a spade and speak truth to power.
cards.quote: I feel really bad because I'm like, it should have been obvious. We should have been able to call a spade a spade and I guess speak truth to power.
cards.zh: 我到現在還是很懊惱，因為這件事本來就該一眼看穿。我們應該有辦法直話直說，向上把真話講出來。
cards.why: 承擔錯誤時用 we should have been able to（我們本來做得到）而不是找藉口，語氣真誠又不自我鞭笞。call a spade a spade（有話直說）與 speak truth to power（對權力說真話）都是高分片語。
swaps: We should have named it earlier.
I should have said the quiet part out loud.
That was on us — we all saw it and stayed quiet.
cards.pmNote: 殭屍產品（zombie product）最貴的成本不是失敗，而是沒人願意在第六個月宣布它死亡。
cards.episode: Why great AI products are all about the data | Shaun Clowes (CPO Confluent, ex-Salesforce, Atlassian)

alts.quote: truth be told, when I interviewed with Fareed that first time, I think back to the interview and I think I bombed it. I actually don't think I would've hired me back then.
alts.zh: 老實講，我第一次跟 Fareed 面試的時候，現在回想起來我覺得我搞砸了。換成是我，當時我大概也不會錄取我自己。

alts.quote: Yeah, I messed up. But I know I'm still a good person and a good worker. Yes, I made a mistake, but I'm going to move on.
alts.zh: 對，我搞砸了。但我知道我還是個好人、也還是個好的工作者。對，我犯了錯，但我要往前走。

alts.quote: And then the second piece of advice I would give I think we should have been talking to potential acquirers from the beginning and sharing our vision and what we were trying to accomplish because we started those quite late in our journey as a company.
alts.zh: 我要給的第二個建議是：我覺得我們一開始就該去跟潛在的收購方聊，分享我們的願景跟想達成的事。我們啟動得太晚了。

cards.quote: It was pretty obvious after six months this thing was a bit of a zombie product walking, and the least I could have done is said, "This thing is dead." We could have called it dead way earlier.
cards.zh: 半年後就很明顯這是個活死人產品了，我至少可以做的，就是講一句：這個東西已經死了。我們早就該宣布它死亡。
cards.why: call it dead 是英語裡宣布終止的乾脆說法（來自急診室宣告死亡），比 we should sunset this 更果斷。報壞消息時，用最短的句子把結論放在最前面反而最有尊嚴。
swaps: Let's call it: this isn't working.
I think we should sunset it now, not in six months.
Time to pull the plug.
cards.pmNote: 砍產品要設早期的 kill criteria，否則團隊會一路投資到有人願意付錢才被迫面對。
cards.episode: Why great AI products are all about the data | Shaun Clowes (CPO Confluent, ex-Salesforce, Atlassian)

alts.quote: Look, we haven't shipped any. Last three years, the only thing our customers have really meaningfully seen from our product is a price increase. What the hell are we doing?
alts.zh: 你看，我們什麼都沒出。過去三年，客戶從我們產品上真正感受到的只有一件事：漲價。我們到底在幹嘛？

alts.quote: I definitely don't think it was obvious to everyone, and I can definitely say that because we were given a pretty strict deadline that we needed to launch by and I pushed it out three times.
alts.zh: 我完全不覺得這對所有人來說是顯而易見的，我敢這樣說是因為我們當初拿到一個很硬的上線死線，而我把它往後推了三次。

alts.quote: By the way, a very, very successful company for a new set of products has a 50% hit rate. So half of you are going to come back in a year and have a different job. Do you have the resilience to do that?
alts.zh: 順帶一提，一家非常成功的公司做新產品的成功率大概是五成。所以你們有一半的人一年後會換一份工作。你們有那個韌性嗎？

cards.pattern: It's not often I use a product and think: this is 10x better than anything before it.
cards.quote: It's not often I use a product and I'm like, "This thing is 10 times better than anything that's come before it." It's one of those for me.
cards.zh: 我很少用到一個產品會覺得「這東西比之前所有的東西好上十倍」。這個對我來說就是其中之一。
cards.why: 稱讚前先講「我很少這樣」，讚美的可信度立刻上升——因為你先證明自己標準很高。這是給推薦、給肯定時最值錢的鋪陳。
swaps: I don't say this often, but…
Rarely does something clear that bar for me.
I'm hard to impress here, and this did it.
cards.pmNote: 10x better 是判斷產品能否取代既有習慣的粗略門檻，微幅改善通常換不動使用者。
cards.episode: Why great AI products are all about the data | Shaun Clowes (CPO Confluent, ex-Salesforce, Atlassian)

alts.quote: I said, "Hi, my name's Camille. I'm interning here this summer. It's my first day. I just wanted to say thank you for spending your time doing that speech for us on Saturday."
alts.zh: 我說：「嗨，我叫 Camille，今年夏天在這裡實習，今天是我第一天。我只是想跟你說謝謝，謝謝你週六花時間為我們做那場演講。」

alts.quote: I do not believe in being liked. I believe in being loved, right? And that's a very, very different thing.
alts.zh: 我不追求被喜歡。我追求被愛。這是兩件非常、非常不一樣的事。

alts.quote: When somebody is using AI to solve a problem that they wouldn't have used AI before, give them a shout-out in the team meeting, let them demo that. Again, make them feel like a million bucks for doing the thing.
alts.zh: 只要有人用 AI 解掉一個他以前不會這樣解的問題，就在團隊會議上點名讚美他，讓他 demo 一次。就是要讓他爽到不行。

cards.pattern: My career has been a bit like a bingo card — I've been filling in the boxes I didn't have.
cards.quote: Looking back, my career has been a little bit like a bingo card. I've always been looking to fill in boxes I didn't have filled because I felt like that would make me a better professional.
cards.zh: 回頭看，我的職涯有點像一張賓果卡。我一直在補那些還沒被填滿的格子，因為我覺得那會讓我變成更好的專業工作者。
cards.why: 用一個具體比喻把看起來很亂的資歷講成有意識的策略。面試被問「你的經歷怎麼跳這麼多」時，一個好的比喻比逐段解釋有效太多。
swaps: I've been collecting the experiences I was missing.
Each move filled a gap I knew I had.
I optimized for range, not for title.
cards.pmNote: 刻意選擇「相鄰但不同」的職位（不同銷售模式、不同使用者、不同技術層）會讓你在新問題上有更多可比對的樣式。
cards.episode: Why great AI products are all about the data | Shaun Clowes (CPO Confluent, ex-Salesforce, Atlassian)

alts.quote: What I didn't tell is that there was at least six years of accidental work behind this. I started a blog six years before... Actually, I've always been blogging since I graduated.
alts.zh: 我沒講的是，這背後至少有六年、不是刻意規劃的累積。我在那之前六年就開始寫部落格了——其實我從畢業就一直在寫。

alts.quote: I don't want to make it seem like it was me against everyone because that was definitely not the case. I think the starting engineers and designers on that team really cared about the quality of what they built too.
alts.zh: 我不想講得好像是我一個人對抗全世界，完全不是那樣。那個團隊的工程師跟設計師本來就很在乎品質。

alts.quote: I was going to start by saying, I've been wrong about tons of things, but I buried those out back behind the shed.
alts.zh: 我本來想說，我看走眼的次數多到數不清啦，只是那些我都埋在後院工具間後面了。

cards.pattern: I've rarely regretted going deep on something that isn't quite my job.
cards.quote: I've rarely regretted going deep in something that isn't quite my job. The worst case scenario is I've learned something new that I will never use.
cards.zh: 去深入研究那些不完全屬於我職責的東西，我幾乎沒後悔過。最糟的情況也不過是學到一個以後用不到的東西。
cards.why: I've rarely regretted… 是談自己選擇時很成熟的語氣：不吹噓成果，只講「我幾乎沒後悔」，再自己算出最壞情況有多便宜。談職涯決策時這種風險語言很有份量。
swaps: The downside is small; the upside is occasionally huge.
I've never lost by understanding the next function over.
Worst case I learn something I never use.
cards.pmNote: 最好的產品人不是 T 型而是「塗鴉型」：在好幾個不同領域都能往下鑽三層，遇到問題時能從別的角度辨識模式。
cards.episode: Why great AI products are all about the data | Shaun Clowes (CPO Confluent, ex-Salesforce, Atlassian)

alts.quote: But where I started understanding deeply the dynamics of the marketplace was actually my experience and the one job I've had that not been in the creator or art or these big consumer platforms.
alts.zh: 但我真正開始深入理解市集的運作機制，其實是在那份唯一不屬於創作者、藝術或大型消費平台的工作裡。

alts.quote: And for us, even at scale, again going back to more than 50% of new signups still come through word of mouth.
alts.zh: 對我們來說，就算做到這個規模，還是有超過一半的新註冊是從口碑來的。

alts.quote: I was going to start by saying, I've been wrong about tons of things, but I buried those out back behind the shed.
alts.zh: 我本來想說，我看走眼的次數多到數不清啦，只是那些我都埋在後院工具間後面了。

cards.quote: I often think about this phrase, which is people don't care what you know until they know that you care.
cards.zh: 我常想到這句話：在別人知道你在乎之前，他們不會在乎你懂什麼。
cards.why: 用 know / care 的對仗把一整套影響力理論壓成一句。這種押韻式格言在英語職場很容易被記住、被轉述，是把觀點植入別人腦中的高效載體。
swaps: Trust first, then the argument lands.
Relationship before rightness.
Being right isn't enough on its own.
cards.pmNote: 跨部門推動事情時，先確認對方的 outcome 和 incentive，你的資料才會被聽進去。
cards.episode: Why great AI products are all about the data | Shaun Clowes (CPO Confluent, ex-Salesforce, Atlassian)

alts.quote: What we ask people in general is we say, what do you think? We don't say, what do you know? We often say, what do you think?
alts.zh: 我們一般會問人「你怎麼想？」我們不會問「你知道什麼？」我們最常問的就是「你怎麼想？」

alts.quote: What else can people do to become better storytellers in business? I know this is a big question, but let's see where it goes.
alts.zh: 在商業場合還可以怎麼把故事講得更好？我知道這題很大，但我們就看看會聊到哪。

alts.quote: You ask questions like, what's the hardest you've ever worked to get something done and why? And that does differentiate a lot of people, a lot of people don't actually have a great answer to that.
alts.zh: 你可以問這種問題：你這輩子為了完成某件事最拚的一次是什麼？為什麼？這題真的很能分辨人，很多人其實答不太出來。

cards.pattern: People only do what their incentives tell them to do. You get what you set out to measure.
cards.quote: In economics, people only do what their incentives told them to do. Broadly speaking, that is what they do. You get what you set out to measure.
cards.zh: 在經濟學裡，人只會做他們的誘因叫他們做的事。大致上就是這樣。你量什麼，就會得到什麼。
cards.why: 先借一個學科當靠山（in economics），再用 broadly speaking 幫自己留退路，最後收在一句好記的結論。這種「權威＋緩衝＋金句」三段式，是把主張變成共識的標準結構。
swaps: Show me the incentive and I'll show you the outcome.
If nobody's measured on it, it won't happen.
Behaviour follows incentives, not memos.
cards.pmNote: 沒有人的 KPI 綁在終端使用者的成功上，PLG 就只會是興趣（a hobby），不會變成成果。
cards.episode: Why great AI products are all about the data | Shaun Clowes (CPO Confluent, ex-Salesforce, Atlassian)

alts.quote: If I told you, I'm going to build an autonomous vehicle, and I said our team is 10 people, you should rightfully say, Varun, you're not serious. And you'd be right.
alts.zh: 如果我跟你說我要做自駕車，然後說團隊只有 10 個人，你完全應該回我：Varun，你不是認真的吧。而且你會是對的。

alts.quote: And if you don't have them on your growth roadmap, you are going to be in some really big trouble over the next year to two years because your cost of acquisition is only going to go up.
alts.zh: 如果你的成長路線圖上沒有這些東西，未來一到兩年你會陷入大麻煩，因為你的獲客成本只會一路往上。

alts.quote: And again, everything I've just described, by the way, is just a very straightforward extrapolation of very basic economics. I'm not making any bold predictions of what I just said.
alts.zh: 我剛剛講的這一整串，其實只是最基本的經濟學往下推而已。我沒有在做什麼大膽預測。

cards.pattern: By definition, it's only [X] if it seems like it isn't
cards.quote: By definition it is only a tarpit if it seems like it's not. If it's just a regular idea that is hard, that is not a tarpit.
cards.zh: 照定義來說，只有在它「看起來不像陷阱」的時候，它才是陷阱。如果只是一個大家都知道很難的點子，那不叫陷阱。
cards.why: 用「By definition」把定義權搶回來，先重新界定名詞，再讓對方的反駁自動失效——這是資深 PM 面對「我覺得這個沒那麼糟」時最有力的一招：不吵事實，改吵定義。
swaps: By definition, X only counts as Y if...
The whole point of calling it X is that...
cards.pmNote: tarpit idea（焦油坑點子）＝很多人想得到、又能拿到早期正面回饋、但十年來沒人做成的題目。
cards.episode: Lessons from 1,000+ YC startups: Resilience, tar pit ideas, pivoting, more | Dalton Caldwell (Y Combinator, Managing Director)

alts.quote: The problem is not like what should my goal be or how should I figure out what to do with my life? They usually know, but it's very hard to actually make time for those things.
alts.zh: 問題不在於「我的目標該是什麼」或「我這輩子要幹嘛」。這個大家其實都知道。問題是很難真的挪出時間去做那些事。

alts.quote: Communication isn't about being able to convey a message. It's about being able to convey a message in a way that the listener receives it and understands it and remembers it. And that's really hard to do.
alts.zh: 溝通不是把訊息送出去。溝通是用一種方式送出去，讓聽的人接收到、聽懂、而且記得住。這超級難。

alts.quote: I think that the issue is, it's not just about product market fit, it is about achieving a product market pricing fit.
alts.zh: 我覺得問題在於：重點不只是 product-market fit，而是要做到 product-market-pricing fit。

cards.pattern: I completely agree with [對方], but to look at this from a different frame, [你的角度]
cards.quote: I completely agree with what Gustav said, but to look at this from a different frame, I think is that the founders lose hope.
cards.zh: 我完全同意 Gustav 講的，但換一個框架來看，我覺得真正的原因是創辦人失去了希望。
cards.why: 先百分之百同意，再說「換個框架看」——不是反駁，而是把同一件事移到另一個座標系。台灣人常直接說 But I think...，聽起來像否定；frame 這個字讓你在不否定任何人的情況下換掉整場討論的軸。
swaps: to look at it from another angle
if you reframe it slightly
another way to cut this is
cards.pmNote: 同一組事實可以有多種 problem framing，框架選錯，後面所有解法都會歪。
cards.episode: Lessons from 1,000+ YC startups: Resilience, tar pit ideas, pivoting, more | Dalton Caldwell (Y Combinator, Managing Director)

alts.quote: One of the things that I think when you're doing interviewing, one way to think about it, I call it home court, away court, neutral court, you want interviews to balance in all those different spheres.
alts.zh: 面試的時候有一個思考方式，我把它叫做「主場、客場、中立場」，你會希望面試在這幾個場域之間取得平衡。

alts.quote: And if you look beyond the short term and like, "Okay, what are the numbers for this quarter?" And you zoom out and you think about what are the very best products out there, you realize this is how they all operate.
alts.zh: 如果你不只看短期、不只問「這一季的數字怎樣」，而是往外拉、去想想市面上最好的產品是怎麼運作的，你會發現它們全都是這樣做的。

alts.quote: When we talk about pricing, many people quickly gravitate to dollar figures. That's just a price point. But when we think about price, we think about it as a measure.
alts.zh: 談定價的時候，大部分人馬上跳到金額。那只是一個價格點。但我們看「價格」是把它當成一種度量。

cards.pattern: If you look at [全部案例], the underlying theme is that [共同結構]
cards.quote: The way to summarize that is if you look at all the startup stories that we have at YC and all the companies we funded over all the years, the underlying theme is that rationally the founder should have given up at some point.
cards.zh: 要總結的話：如果你看 YC 所有的創業故事、這些年投的所有公司，底下共通的主題是——照理性判斷，創辦人早就該在某個時間點放棄了。
cards.why: 「the underlying theme is」是把一堆零散案例壓成一句洞見的收束句型。台灣人講案例常一路平鋪，缺的就是這種「所以底層的東西是什麼」的收尾動作。
swaps: the common thread is
what they all have in common is
the pattern underneath all of it is
cards.pmNote: 從 N 個案例抽出 pattern，是資深工作者跟資淺最明顯的差別。
cards.episode: Lessons from 1,000+ YC startups: Resilience, tar pit ideas, pivoting, more | Dalton Caldwell (Y Combinator, Managing Director)

alts.quote: Right now we kind of have this dichotomy between what I call investor controlled companies and founder controlled companies.
alts.zh: 我們現在有一個二分：我稱之為「投資人控制的公司」跟「創辦人控制的公司」。

alts.quote: And then we also don't obsess over absolute numbers, because if we're successful, if you zoom out and out and out, any point in time will be inconsequential and small.
alts.zh: 我們也不會執著於絕對數字，因為如果我們成功了，你一直往外拉、再往外拉，任何一個時間點都會顯得無足輕重。

alts.quote: One of the things that I think when you're doing interviewing, one way to think about it, I call it home court, away court, neutral court, you want interviews to balance in all those different spheres.
alts.zh: 面試的時候有一個思考方式，我把它叫做「主場、客場、中立場」，你會希望面試在這幾個場域之間取得平衡。

cards.pattern: The anti-pattern I see is [常見錯誤做法]
cards.quote: And so the anti-pattern I see is there are lots of founders that are very familiar with your awesome work.
cards.zh: 所以我常看到的反模式是：很多創辦人非常熟你那些很棒的內容（然後在錯的階段照做）。
cards.why: anti-pattern 是矽谷用來「批評一種做法但不指名任何人」的安全詞。你不是說「你做錯了」，你是說「這是一種已知的錯誤模式」，被指的人比較容易接受。
swaps: the failure mode I keep seeing is
the trap here is
where I see teams go wrong is
cards.pmNote: 把個案講成 anti-pattern，回饋才會變成組織知識而不是人身批評。
cards.episode: Lessons from 1,000+ YC startups: Resilience, tar pit ideas, pivoting, more | Dalton Caldwell (Y Combinator, Managing Director)

alts.quote: A lot of early stage founders get tripped up as they're taking late stage sales advice.
alts.zh: 很多早期創辦人會踩坑，是因為他們套用了後期階段的銷售建議。

alts.quote: Wait, why do I have 1 search box at home, and 10 search boxes at work? Why is it easier to search all of human knowledge than my company's knowledge?
alts.zh: 等等，為什麼我在家只有一個搜尋框，在公司卻有十個？為什麼搜全人類的知識，比搜我自己公司的知識還簡單？

alts.quote: So, what you can see here is it's not like, what is a calendar? It's not a calendar. It's a two-month dot grid with scrolling agenda view underneath.
alts.zh: 所以你看，重點不是「什麼叫行事曆」。它不是一個行事曆，它是「兩個月的圓點格線，下面搭一個可捲動的議程檢視」。

cards.pattern: The prompt here is to [行動方向]
cards.quote: And so the prompt here is to try to go more off the beaten path either from your personal experience, like in the case of Brex and Retool or Whatnot.
cards.zh: 所以這裡給你的思考提示是：試著走出那條被踩爛的路，從你自己的經驗裡挖，像 Brex、Retool、Whatnot 那樣。
cards.why: 把「建議」講成 prompt（思考提示），語氣從命令降級成觸發器——你不是規定方向，你只是丟一個引子。給資深同事或創辦人建議時特別好用。
swaps: the nudge here is to
the question I'd plant is
what I'd have you go explore is
cards.pmNote: off the beaten path＝避開所有人資訊來源相同而產生的同質題目。
cards.episode: Lessons from 1,000+ YC startups: Resilience, tar pit ideas, pivoting, more | Dalton Caldwell (Y Combinator, Managing Director)

alts.quote: I use it as an input into ideation, but I never use it as a destination for the result, if that makes sense.
alts.zh: 我把它當成發想的「輸入」，但絕不把它當成結果的「終點」，這樣講你懂我意思嗎？

alts.quote: And what Canva really does is we're literally smack bang in the middle of that Venn diagram of creativity and productivity, rather than making our customers have to make a choice between those two suites.
alts.zh: Canva 真正在做的事，就是不偏不倚站在「創意」跟「生產力」這兩個圈的交集正中央，而不是逼客戶在兩邊二選一。

alts.quote: We should probably not do things that would've been invented by everybody else 10 minutes later. Where are the problems that are not solving themselves?
alts.zh: 我們大概不該去做那些晚十分鐘別人也會做出來的東西。真正該問的是：哪些問題是不會自己被解決的？

cards.pattern: My tactical advice is [先做 A] versus [B]
cards.quote: I think so many folks don't know where to begin on starting a startup, and my tactical advice is start doing customer validation first versus building a PowerPoint deck.
cards.zh: 很多人根本不知道創業要從哪裡開始，我很具體的建議是：先去做客戶驗證，而不是先做一份簡報。
cards.why: tactical advice 這個標籤先幫聽眾降低期待（我不是要給你大道理），再用 A versus B 把「該做的」跟「你正在做的」直接對撞。比 You should... 少了說教味。
swaps: the practical move is to
concretely, I'd start with X rather than Y
cards.pmNote: 先預售、先驗證，再寫程式；customer validation 排在募資與美化簡報之前。
cards.episode: Lessons from 1,000+ YC startups: Resilience, tar pit ideas, pivoting, more | Dalton Caldwell (Y Combinator, Managing Director)

alts.quote: And then just the nature of the future is like we just don't know all the answers and that's okay. And then the right way to deal with that is to run as many experiments as possible.
alts.zh: 未來的本質就是我們不會知道所有答案，這沒關係。面對這件事正確的做法，是盡可能多跑一些實驗。

alts.quote: When we talk about pricing strategies, we hear many buzzwords, and it's irrelevant. So when we take a step back and look at it, there's literally only three types of pricing strategies.
alts.zh: 談定價策略的時候會聽到一堆流行詞，那些都不重要。退一步看，定價策略其實就只有三種。

alts.quote: Often people have a mission that's kind of on the wall somewhere and then what they're actually doing and the way they actually make money and the way people actually spend their time is in a very, very different direction from that original mission.
alts.zh: 很多公司的使命就掛在牆上某個地方，可是他們真正在做的事、真正賺錢的方式、大家真正把時間花在哪，跟那個使命的方向差超多。

cards.pattern: Put yourself in the shoes of [對方] and just imagine what their life is like
cards.quote: Maybe my best advice here is for founders to put themselves in the shoes of investors and just imagine what their life is like and how if you are in their shoes you would make decisions.
cards.zh: 我最好的建議大概是：創辦人去站在投資人的位置上，想像他們的日子長什麼樣、如果換成你會怎麼做決定。
cards.why: 解釋「為什麼對方會拒絕你」時，不講對方的動機（那會變成猜測與抱怨），而是請對方自己走進去演一次。這是化解怨氣、把情緒問題變成結構問題的標準手法。
swaps: flip it around and imagine you're them
run the exercise from their side of the table
cards.pmNote: 投資人說 no 多半不是不信你，而是他一年只投得下幾個。
