cards.episode: Lessons from 1,000+ YC startups: Resilience, tar pit ideas, pivoting, more | Dalton Caldwell (Y Combinator, Managing Director)

alts.quote: Yeah. Imagine, no such thing as a request from sales, yeah? No such thing as pressure of like, "We need this thing in order to upsell or to close this deal." Never.
alts.zh: 你想像一下：完全沒有業務來提需求，好嗎？也完全沒有那種「我們需要這個功能才能升級方案、才能成交」的壓力。從來沒有。

alts.quote: And for me, that just felt completely backwards. I should be spending 90% of the time on the content, 10% maybe on the design and formatting.
alts.zh: 對我來說那整件事根本是反過來的。我應該把 90% 的時間花在內容上，設計排版頂多 10%。

alts.quote: So we try to build a team based on the needs of the work a bit, but then end up with a much smaller core.
alts.zh: 所以我們會盡量照工作本身的需求去組團隊，最後就會收斂成一個小很多的核心。

cards.pattern: And this is the big but, [關鍵轉折]
cards.quote: But, and this is the big but, no one has this at the early stages when they don't have a good idea and they don't have customers and it's objectively not working.
cards.zh: 但是——而且這是很大的一個「但是」——在最早期、還沒有好點子、沒有客戶、客觀上根本不 work 的時候，沒有人會有那種信念。
cards.why: 先用「this is the big but」替接下來的轉折立牌子，聽眾知道重點來了、會提高注意力。這種先預告再講的手法，在英文會議裡是掌控節奏的關鍵，台灣人幾乎不會用。
swaps: here's the caveat though
and this is the important part
with one big asterisk
cards.pmNote: 信念是結果不是前提——先有一點成績，信念才長出來。
cards.episode: Lessons from 1,000+ YC startups: Resilience, tar pit ideas, pivoting, more | Dalton Caldwell (Y Combinator, Managing Director)

alts.quote: That's a good idea, but we don't actually understand these three things before we start working on that. So maybe we should do understand work to make sure that that is actually the right idea.
alts.zh: 這個想法不錯，但在動手之前有三件事我們其實還沒搞懂。也許先做點「理解型的工作」，確認這真的是對的方向。

alts.quote: And optics is a good thing. So I'm not saying don't think about optics whatsoever, I think it's actually important to think about optics.
alts.zh: 而且「對外呈現」本身是好事。我不是說完全不要管呈現，我覺得那其實很重要。

alts.quote: To me, I think it's a great accelerant when it's already working, but it can't fix it if people don't want to talk about your product.
alts.zh: 對我來說，那在本來就跑得動的時候是很好的加速器，但如果根本沒人想談論你的產品，它救不了你。

cards.pattern: I'm not saying [X] doesn't matter, of course it does. But [你的真正立場]
cards.quote: I'm not saying that having a large market someday doesn't matter, of course it does eventually. But trying to be super pedantic about market size when it's a pre-seed company, it's just not something I'd put a lot of thought.
cards.zh: 我不是說市場總有一天要夠大這件事不重要，當然重要。但在一家 pre-seed 公司還在糾結市場規模算得多精確，我不會花太多心思在上面。
cards.why: 先把對方的立場完整交還（of course it does），再限縮到「時機」而不是「對錯」。這是英文異議最常用的降溫結構：不否定命題，只否定它現在適用。
swaps: it's not that X is wrong, it's that it's premature
X matters eventually, just not now
cards.pmNote: 同一條建議在 seed 跟 series B 可以完全相反，先問這是給哪個階段的。
cards.episode: Lessons from 1,000+ YC startups: Resilience, tar pit ideas, pivoting, more | Dalton Caldwell (Y Combinator, Managing Director)

alts.quote: It's like, "well, I'm not telling you that you should pivot. I'm just saying that is what it's called when you change the strategy, but try to have fidelity to the vision."
alts.zh: 我不是在叫你去 pivot。我只是說，當你改策略但盡量守住願景的時候，那件事就叫這個名字。

alts.quote: It's super boring, but the biggest hot take is you just have to do something once a quarter.
alts.zh: 這超無聊，但最辣的評論就是：你每一季至少得動一次。

alts.quote: Again, don't get me wrong, I'm not trying to talk people out of doing it. But for me, a lot of this was luck.
alts.zh: 先說清楚，我不是想勸大家不要做。但對我來說，這裡面有很大一部分是運氣。

cards.pattern: I'm not trying to diss anyone, but [批評]
cards.quote: I'm not trying to diss anyone, but you'll see things that become fashionable really quickly because someone found success in this unfashionable space and then it becomes fashionable.
cards.zh: 我不是要酸誰，但你會看到有些東西紅得很快——因為有人在一個沒人做的領域做成了，然後它就變成流行。
cards.why: diss 是很口語的「酸／貶低」。先聲明「我不是要酸誰」，等於買一張批評的保險。台灣人講到批評時常整段吞掉，這個前綴能讓你照講不誤又不樹敵。
swaps: no shade to anyone, but
I don't mean this as a knock on anyone, but
cards.pmNote: 題材的 fashionable 程度跟報酬率通常成反比。
cards.episode: Lessons from 1,000+ YC startups: Resilience, tar pit ideas, pivoting, more | Dalton Caldwell (Y Combinator, Managing Director)

alts.quote: So Lenny, I don't see it as a pivot because as we were joking in the beginning, I've been an employee, I was an operator there at early stage startups and now I'm a founder and I'm a VC.
alts.zh: Lenny，我不覺得那是轉彎——就像我們一開始開玩笑講的，我當過員工、在早期新創當過操盤手，現在是創辦人，也是投資人。

alts.quote: Again, don't get me wrong, I'm not trying to talk people out of doing it.
alts.zh: 再說一次，別誤會，我不是要勸大家別做這件事。

alts.quote: Actually, it's not that it's harder to find, your stuff becomes less relevant. And that's the part about SEO that I'm excited about.
alts.zh: 其實不是變得比較難被找到，是你的東西變得沒那麼相關了。而這正是 SEO 讓我興奮的地方。

cards.pattern: I'm just trying to argue that [主張] is actively not helpful
cards.quote: I'm just trying to argue this advice applied to a startup that's too early is actively not helpful.
cards.zh: 我只是想主張：把這套建議套在太早期的新創身上，是「主動有害」而不只是沒用。
cards.why: 兩個關鍵：I'm just trying to argue 把強硬主張降級成一個論點（留餘地），actively not helpful 又把「沒幫助」升級成「有害」。一句話裡同時軟化語氣、強化內容，這是母語者的高階操作。
swaps: my claim is narrower than that: ...
not just unhelpful — counterproductive
cards.pmNote: 早期公司做 A/B test 與成長駭客，通常是拿後期工具解前期問題。
cards.episode: Lessons from 1,000+ YC startups: Resilience, tar pit ideas, pivoting, more | Dalton Caldwell (Y Combinator, Managing Director)

alts.quote: My one piece of advice is when you're early on, your mindset should almost be like you're trying to create a word of mouth machine. If you can get that part right, everything else becomes significantly easier.
alts.zh: 我唯一的建議是：早期你的心態應該是在打造一台「口碑機器」。這件事只要做對，其他所有事都會變得輕鬆很多。

alts.quote: And one of my main takeaways of that entire process is that it's always too early until it's too late.
alts.zh: 我從那整段過程裡學到最重要的一件事是：這種事永遠都「太早」，直到它「太遲」。

alts.quote: In fact, I would argue that what we're seeing in the industry is us trying to use mature playbooks from the end stage of the last tech era in one that doesn't really fit yet.
alts.zh: 事實上我會說，我們在業界看到的，是大家拿上一個科技時代末期的成熟劇本，套進一個還不適合的新時代。

cards.pattern: This is a nuanced question and it's hard to say something that'll actually be useful, but here's a couple of thoughts
cards.quote: I think this is a nuanced question and it's hard for me to say something on a podcast that'll actually be useful to people, but here's a couple of thoughts.
cards.zh: 我覺得這是個很有層次的問題，要在 podcast 上講出真的對別人有用的東西很難，不過我有幾個想法。
cards.why: 承認問題複雜、承認自己給不出通解，然後還是給——這是資深的訊號。台灣人遇到這種題目常直接給一個過度簡化的答案，或整個推掉；正確做法是「降低承諾、照樣交付」。
swaps: there's no clean answer here, but a couple of things I'd look at
I'll caveat this heavily, but
cards.pmNote: bespoke advice：需要看個案的問題，講通則反而誤導人。
cards.episode: Lessons from 1,000+ YC startups: Resilience, tar pit ideas, pivoting, more | Dalton Caldwell (Y Combinator, Managing Director)

alts.quote: So I think it has to come with a place of knowing that you don't know everything and humility to say, "Hey, I need help." And it actually earns you a lot more credit than you think.
alts.zh: 我覺得這要來自一個認知：你不可能什麼都懂，還要有那個謙虛去說「嘿，我需要幫忙」。而且這其實比你想像的更會替你加分。

alts.quote: Now, to be clear, this is hard for me. I think it's hard for everybody.
alts.zh: 先講清楚，這件事對我來說也很難。我覺得對每個人都很難。

alts.quote: That's the problem. I mean, that is the trillion dollar question so I don't really have an answer. I have a couple thoughts on it.
alts.zh: 問題就在這。這是那種價值一兆美元的問題，所以我其實沒有答案，但我有幾點想法。

cards.pattern: I can't promise it works for everyone, but in [具體情境] it worked really well
cards.quote: Yeah, I mean, I can't promise that works for everyone, but again, in the very bespoke situation with Rujul, it worked really well.
cards.zh: 我不能保證這對每個人都有效，但在 Rujul 那個很特定的情況下，效果非常好。
cards.why: 先自己標出證據的邊界，再講成果——反而更可信。台灣人分享成功案例時常無意間過度推論（所以大家都該這樣做），這句是最短的免責＋可信度加成。
swaps: your mileage may vary, but
n of one, but it worked
I wouldn't generalize it, but in that case
cards.pmNote: 單一案例可以當靈感，不能當通則。
cards.episode: Lessons from 1,000+ YC startups: Resilience, tar pit ideas, pivoting, more | Dalton Caldwell (Y Combinator, Managing Director)

alts.quote: Obviously in this case, it worked out great and there's survivorship bias and that doesn't mean that everyone should pivot all the time.
alts.zh: 當然這個案例後來結果很好，但這裡有倖存者偏誤，不代表每個人都該一直轉型。

alts.quote: Well, to be clear about my brand promise, because it's true, every word that has my name on it, I wrote.
alts.zh: 先把我的品牌承諾講清楚：每一個掛我名字的字，都是我寫的。

alts.quote: And it's not bad because it's not well-intentioned, but it's bad because it's not contextual.
alts.zh: 它不好，不是因為對方沒有善意，而是因為它沒有考慮你的處境。

cards.pattern: Just to pull on this thread a little bit more, [追問]
cards.quote: Just to pull on this thread a little bit more, what is the general advice you share there for people that also don't want to die?
cards.zh: 順著這條線再拉一下：對那些也不想死掉的人，你通常會給什麼建議？
cards.why: pull on this thread＝順著剛剛那條線再挖深。比 Can you say more? 更精準，也對對方是一種肯定（你剛剛講的那條線值得挖）。開會時追問而不打斷氣氛的最佳句。
swaps: staying on that thread for a second
I want to go one level deeper on that
cards.episode: Lessons from 1,000+ YC startups: Resilience, tar pit ideas, pivoting, more | Dalton Caldwell (Y Combinator, Managing Director)

alts.quote: Let me refine that a little bit more. It's more about giving people the information that they can use for decisions that they alone are good at...
alts.zh: 我把那個講法再修得精準一點。重點比較是：給人們他們才擅長的那類決策所需要的資訊。

alts.quote: Let me back up and just dissect a little bit the way you described design, you described it in really tactical terms.
alts.zh: 先讓我退一步，拆解一下你剛剛描述設計的方式——你講的是很戰術層次的東西。

alts.quote: The reason I'm a little confused, just because I want to get it right, is what I'm hearing, which maybe isn't what you said
alts.zh: 我有點不確定，純粹是想弄清楚——我聽到的（可能不是你講的意思）是……

cards.pattern: Many people quickly gravitate to [表象]. But we think about it as [本質]
cards.quote: When we talk about pricing, many people quickly gravitate to dollar figures. That's just a price point. But when we think about price, we think about it as a measure.
cards.zh: 談定價的時候，大部分人馬上跳到金額。那只是一個價格點。但我們看「價格」是把它當成一種度量。
cards.why: 重新定義一個大家以為自己懂的詞：先描述大眾的直覺反應（gravitate to），再說「但我們是這樣看的」。這是整場策略對話裡最值錢的三十秒，因為定義換了，後面的結論就跟著換。
swaps: most people jump straight to X. We treat it as Y
the instinct is to think X — we think of it as Y
cards.pmNote: 價格是價值的度量單位，不是一個數字；先問客戶願不願意付，再決定收多少。
cards.episode: Pricing your AI product: Lessons from 400+ companies and 50 unicorns | Madhavan Ramanujam

alts.quote: People come to search for a ridiculously wide set of things. They want a phone number, a price, directions. I think the vastness of that is underappreciated by many people.
alts.zh: 大家來搜尋的東西範圍寬到誇張——找電話、查價格、要路線。我覺得這個「廣度」被太多人低估了。

alts.quote: The way I learned how to pitch in business school, and I think the way most people did, is what I call the arrogant doctor.
alts.zh: 我在商學院學到的提案方式——我想大部分人學的也是——就是我說的「傲慢醫生」那一套。

alts.quote: And so I think a lot of it comes down to not the things you try, but how you deeply understand the problem that's preventing someone from using your product effectively.
alts.zh: 所以我覺得關鍵不在你試了哪些招，而在你有多深地搞懂「是什麼擋住使用者用好你的產品」。

cards.pattern: It's not just about [大家熟的概念], it's about [升級版概念]
cards.quote: I think that the issue is, it's not just about product market fit, it is about achieving a product market pricing fit.
cards.zh: 我覺得問題在於：重點不只是 product-market fit，而是要做到 product-market-pricing fit。
cards.why: 在一個大家已經接受的名詞上加一個字，就造出自己的概念——這是矽谷造詞法的核心。用「it's not just X, it is Y」的節奏，聽眾會覺得你只是把他既有的知識往前推了一格，接受度極高。
swaps: X is table stakes; the real bar is Y
everyone talks about X — the version that matters is Y
cards.pmNote: 沒有把價格放進 PMF 驗證，你聽到的都是你想聽的。
cards.episode: Pricing your AI product: Lessons from 400+ companies and 50 unicorns | Madhavan Ramanujam

alts.quote: And so I think a lot of it comes down to not the things you try, but how you deeply understand the problem that's preventing someone from using your product effectively.
alts.zh: 所以我覺得關鍵不在你試了哪些招，而在你有多深地搞懂「是什麼擋住使用者用好你的產品」。

alts.quote: I think most people don't like product managers often because they haven't experienced good product managers.
alts.zh: 我覺得多數人不喜歡 PM，多半是因為他們沒遇過真正好的 PM。

alts.quote: Also, price is not just the number on the webpage. It's easy to think that, but how it's structured is just as important, how the product's positioned is just as important.
alts.zh: 還有，價格不是只有網頁上那個數字。很容易這樣以為，但怎麼收費、產品怎麼定位，重要程度完全一樣。

cards.pattern: You don't have a choice whether [X] happens. The only thing in your control is when
cards.quote: As an entrepreneur, a company, you actually don't have a choice whether you'll have a pricing conversation with your customer. The only thing in your control is when you will have it.
cards.zh: 身為創業者或公司，你其實沒有「要不要跟客戶談價格」的選擇權。你唯一能控制的是「什麼時候談」。
cards.why: 把 whether 的辯論直接關掉，只留 when——對方一旦接受前提，就已經站在你這邊了。這是說服句型裡效率最高的一種：不爭論該不該做，只討論早做還晚做。
swaps: this conversation is happening either way — the only question is when
it's not if, it's when
cards.pmNote: willingness-to-pay 對話越早做，越能反過來設計產品。
cards.episode: Pricing your AI product: Lessons from 400+ companies and 50 unicorns | Madhavan Ramanujam

alts.quote: I would argue that the more power you have, the more moral responsibility you have to actually pause and figure out what it is that you're doing to be complicit in creating the conditions you say you don't want.
alts.zh: 我會說，你擁有的權力越大，你就越有道德責任停下來，弄清楚你到底做了什麼，才讓你嘴上說不想要的那些狀況得以成立。

alts.quote: And if you don't have them on your growth roadmap, you are going to be in some really big trouble over the next year to two years because your cost of acquisition is only going to go up.
alts.zh: 如果你的成長路線圖上沒有這些東西，未來一到兩年你會陷入大麻煩，因為你的獲客成本只會一路往上。

alts.quote: And the third thing is that I really believe that... I don't believe. I think we all know at this point that the most important thing for the growth of anything tech is retention.
alts.zh: 第三件事是我真的相信——不，不是相信。我覺得到這個時間點大家都已經知道了：科技產品成長最重要的就是留存。

cards.pattern: When we take a step back, there are literally only [N] types of [X]
cards.quote: When we talk about pricing strategies, we hear many buzzwords, and it's irrelevant. So when we take a step back and look at it, there's literally only three types of pricing strategies.
cards.zh: 談定價策略的時候會聽到一堆流行詞，那些都不重要。退一步看，定價策略其實就只有三種。
cards.why: 先把噪音掃掉（buzzwords, irrelevant），再宣布一個很小的數字。「literally only three」給聽眾一個可掌握的世界，是策略簡報最有效的開場。
swaps: strip away the jargon and there are really only three
at the end of the day it collapses into three options
cards.pmNote: 定價策略只有三種：skimming（高開低走）、penetration（低價衝量）、maximization（中間最大化）。
cards.episode: Pricing your AI product: Lessons from 400+ companies and 50 unicorns | Madhavan Ramanujam

alts.quote: I think so many folks don't know where to begin on starting a startup, and my tactical advice is start doing customer validation first versus building a PowerPoint deck.
alts.zh: 很多人根本不知道創業要從哪裡開始，我很具體的建議是：先去做客戶驗證，而不是先做一份簡報。

alts.quote: There's a saying that Mike and Kevin had at Instagram which is we may not be right, but at least we're not confused.
alts.zh: Instagram 的 Mike 跟 Kevin 有一句話：我們不見得是對的，但至少我們不是一團混亂。

alts.quote: And what Canva really does is we're literally smack bang in the middle of that Venn diagram of creativity and productivity, rather than making our customers have to make a choice between those two suites.
alts.zh: Canva 真正在做的事，就是不偏不倚站在「創意」跟「生產力」這兩個圈的交集正中央，而不是逼客戶在兩邊二選一。

cards.pattern: The point is not [選哪個], it's [執行你選的那個]
cards.quote: The point is not about picking, just picking one, but it's about executing the one that you actually pick.
cards.zh: 重點不是「選哪一個」，而是你選了之後有沒有真的執行到底。
cards.why: 當團隊在幾個選項上鬼打牆時，用「the point is not X, it's Y」把討論的重心整個搬走。這是主持策略會議最實用的一句——不裁決選項，直接換掉爭論的題目。
swaps: the choice matters less than the follow-through
any of these can work — what kills us is half-executing
cards.pmNote: 策略即取捨，但取捨的價值來自貫徹，不是來自比較。
cards.episode: Pricing your AI product: Lessons from 400+ companies and 50 unicorns | Madhavan Ramanujam

alts.quote: Often people have a mission that's kind of on the wall somewhere and then what they're actually doing and the way they actually make money and the way people actually spend their time is in a very, very different direction from that original mission.
alts.zh: 很多公司的使命就掛在牆上某個地方，可是他們真正在做的事、真正賺錢的方式、大家真正把時間花在哪，跟那個使命的方向差超多。

alts.quote: People and teams don't really reach... They don't actually reach their goals. They fall to the level of their systems.
alts.zh: 人跟團隊其實不會「達成」目標。他們會掉到自己系統的水準。

alts.quote: If it's not an alternative, it doesn't need to exist.
alts.zh: 如果它不是一個「另一種選擇」，那它根本沒必要存在。

cards.pattern: How you [做法] is way more important than how much [量]
cards.quote: We usually say how you charge is way more important than how much you charge.
cards.zh: 我們常說：「怎麼收費」比「收多少」重要得多。
cards.why: 用同一個動詞（charge）做兩種問法的對比，句子短、對仗強、聽一次就記住。這種 how vs how much 的結構可以搬到很多場合：how you ship it vs how much you ship。
swaps: the model matters more than the number
we spend too long on the number and not enough on the metric
cards.pmNote: 計價單位（per seat / per mile / per tracked user）決定客戶怎麼感受價值。
cards.episode: Pricing your AI product: Lessons from 400+ companies and 50 unicorns | Madhavan Ramanujam

alts.quote: And then just the nature of the future is like we just don't know all the answers and that's okay. And then the right way to deal with that is to run as many experiments as possible.
alts.zh: 未來的本質就是我們不會知道所有答案，這沒關係。面對這件事正確的做法，是盡可能多跑一些實驗。

alts.quote: Often people have a mission that's kind of on the wall somewhere and then what they're actually doing and the way they actually make money and the way people actually spend their time is in a very, very different direction from that original mission.
alts.zh: 很多公司的使命就掛在牆上某個地方，可是他們真正在做的事、真正賺錢的方式、大家真正把時間花在哪，跟那個使命的方向差超多。

alts.quote: If it's not an alternative, it doesn't need to exist.
alts.zh: 如果它不是一個「另一種選擇」，那它根本沒必要存在。

cards.pattern: The number one lesson — and I hope this is the biggest takeaway — is you cannot [X] without [Y]
cards.quote: Literally, for your product folks, the number one lesson, and I hope this is the biggest takeaway for your audience, you cannot prioritize a product roadmap without having a willingness to pay conversation.
cards.zh: 對做產品的人來說，第一號的教訓——我希望這是聽眾最大的收穫——就是：沒有做過付費意願對話，你根本沒辦法排產品路線圖的優先順序。
cards.why: 中間插入的「and I hope this is the biggest takeaway」是在替聽眾標重點，等於口頭版的螢光筆。長段落結束前用它，資訊才不會被沖走。
swaps: if you remember one thing from today, make it this
everything else is optional — this isn't
cards.pmNote: 20% 的功能帶來 80% 的付費意願，先找出那 20%。
cards.episode: Pricing your AI product: Lessons from 400+ companies and 50 unicorns | Madhavan Ramanujam

alts.quote: Is everyone in agreement with that or is there some dissent about whether that's an accurate portrayal of where we've landed with this conversation?
alts.zh: 大家都同意嗎？還是有人覺得我這樣描述我們的結論並不準確？

alts.quote: A really interesting takeaway here is that your sense is over time the foundational model companies, their margins will get squeezed, and the bigger opportunities in the application layer.
alts.zh: 所以一個很有意思的結論是：你的判斷是，長期來看基礎模型公司的毛利會被壓縮，比較大的機會在應用層。

alts.quote: So let's take a step back. The fear is, if I can reflect back to your original question, the fear is if I go there, I don't know what's going to happen as a consequence of that.
alts.zh: 我們退一步看。如果我把你原本的問題回映給你，那個恐懼是：如果我真的往下探，我不知道會發生什麼後果。

cards.pattern: Don't mix up [A] with [B] — those are very different things
cards.quote: Please note that don't mix transparency and fairness with being predictable. Those are very different things.
cards.zh: 請注意，不要把「透明與公平」跟「可預測」混為一談。這是兩件很不一樣的事。
cards.why: 會議裡最有價值的插話，往往不是提出新意見，而是拆開兩個被混用的概念。這句的第二段「Those are very different things」很重要——它給你的區分一個明確的收尾，不會被當成挑字眼。
swaps: let's not conflate X with Y
those two often get bundled, but they pull in different directions
cards.pmNote: 客戶要「公平」不等於要「帳單金額穩定」，兩者會導向完全不同的計價模型。
cards.episode: Pricing your AI product: Lessons from 400+ companies and 50 unicorns | Madhavan Ramanujam

alts.quote: The support's not going to be good enough. They probably don't have good governance policies or other things that we need. Whether that's true or not, this is what it looks like.
alts.zh: 他們的客服大概不夠好、治理政策大概也不合我們要求。這是不是事實不重要——重點是看起來就是這樣。

alts.quote: I think they're very related concepts that people sometimes conflate, but I see them as being different. So related, but different.
alts.zh: 我覺得這是常被混用的相關概念，但我把它們看成不同的東西。所以是——相關，但不同。

alts.quote: Just to pull on this thread a little bit more, what is the general advice you share there for people that also don't want to die?
alts.zh: 順著這條線再拉一下：對那些也不想死掉的人，你通常會給什麼建議？

cards.pattern: It's not about [對方擔心的壞事], it's just about [你真正在做的事]
cards.quote: So this kind of behavioral framing and nudging becomes important, it's not about deceiving your customers, but it's just about framing the products in such a way that it also appeals to the irrational side of the brain.
cards.zh: 這種行為框架跟推力很重要——它不是要騙客戶，而是把產品呈現得也能打到大腦不理性的那一面。
cards.why: 在對方開口質疑之前，先把最可能的道德指控講出來並否認（pre-emption）。這是提出爭議性做法時的標準保護動作：你先講，殺傷力就沒了。
swaps: to be clear, this isn't about tricking anyone
before anyone asks — this isn't manipulation, it's framing
cards.pmNote: 誘餌方案（decoy）與心理門檻是包裝手法，不是欺騙，但界線要自己守。
cards.episode: Pricing your AI product: Lessons from 400+ companies and 50 unicorns | Madhavan Ramanujam

alts.quote: But the only way to build long-term enduring value with a marketplace is to corner the demand side. And so it's kind of a little bit that evolution of a marketplace that ends up changing who you focus on.
alts.zh: 但要做出長期能留住價值的市集，唯一的路是掌握需求端。所以那有點像是市集的演化，會慢慢改變你該把重心放在誰身上。

alts.quote: I definitely would not want anyone to feel joy. What I would say that's a close cousin to that is that enjoyment is such an important tool for productivity.
alts.zh: 我絕對不會要求任何人去感受喜悅。跟那個很接近、但我會這樣說的是：享受是生產力非常重要的工具。

alts.quote: One of the comments was, "Benedict, this is 80 slides of saying we don't know," which is slightly facetious, but also kind of true.
alts.zh: 有人留言說：「Benedict，你這 80 張投影片就是在講『我們不知道』。」講得有點壞，但也算是實話。

cards.pattern: Before you [讓步], think about what value you can exchange to justify it
cards.quote: So before you price discount, think about what value can you exchange to actually justify that price discount.
cards.zh: 所以在你打折之前，先想想你可以「交換」掉什麼價值，來讓這個折扣說得過去。
cards.why: 把「讓步」重新定義成「交換」——這一個字的替換，就是談判裡守住價格完整性的關鍵。任何要求你讓步的場合都能用。
swaps: if we move on price, what do we get back?
no concession without an exchange
cards.pmNote: price integrity：折扣要用「拿掉功能」來換，否則折扣價六個月後就變成新定價。
cards.episode: Pricing your AI product: Lessons from 400+ companies and 50 unicorns | Madhavan Ramanujam

alts.quote: But now I think we're getting to this point where actually if I could only choose one thing to understand, it would be really meaningful understanding of the problems that a certain customer has.
alts.zh: 但我覺得我們現在走到一個階段：如果只能挑一件事搞懂，那就是真正深刻地了解某一群客戶的問題。

alts.quote: I think it's the difference between oversimplification and focusing. You can have a complex problem and be like, "You know what? I need to hold some things constant."
alts.zh: 我覺得差別在於「過度簡化」和「聚焦」。面對複雜問題你可以說：好，我需要先把某些變數固定住。

alts.quote: I think that becomes a bit of a strategic conversation of do we want to have a better chance of surviving, going after a niche that we know we can serve well?
alts.zh: 我覺得這時候就變成一個策略層級的討論了：我們是要提高存活機率、去打一個我們服務得很好的利基市場嗎？

cards.pattern: Most people who claim to have a [X] strategy are only doing half of it
cards.quote: 90% of customers or people who we meet who claim to have a land and expand strategy are only landing. They're not expanding because they gave their farm away in the land.
cards.zh: 我們遇到宣稱自己有 land and expand 策略的人，九成其實只有 land。他們沒辦法 expand，因為一開始就把家當全給出去了。
cards.why: 挑戰假設最漂亮的方式：不說「你們沒有策略」，而是說「你們只做了策略的前半段」。對方沒有被否定，但缺口被指出來了。give the farm away（把家當全送出去）也是很道地的說法。
swaps: everyone says they do X — most stop halfway
we're landing fine; we've never actually expanded
cards.pmNote: land and expand：入門版給太多，就沒有東西留給後面的升級。
cards.episode: Pricing your AI product: Lessons from 400+ companies and 50 unicorns | Madhavan Ramanujam

alts.quote: I think sometimes people use data a lot or too much because they're worrying or they're afraid that, will I make the wrong choice? And I'm using data to make the choice for me.
alts.zh: 我覺得有時候大家用數據用得太兇，是因為他們在怕：萬一我選錯了怎麼辦？於是就讓數據替他們做決定。

alts.quote: I really try and stay away from better, because that's really hard to define, and better means something different to everyone.
alts.zh: 我盡量不用「比較好」這個字，因為它很難定義，而且每個人心中的「比較好」都不一樣。

alts.quote: So, I don't really care how high quality the initial MVP is because quality is defined by the customer. And if we don't know who our customer is, we literally don't know what the word quality means.
alts.zh: 所以第一版的 MVP 品質多高，我其實沒那麼在意，因為品質是由客戶定義的。如果我們連客戶是誰都不知道，我們根本不知道「品質」這兩個字是什麼意思。

cards.pattern: If you take that viewpoint, then [結論]. This is my strong-held belief
cards.quote: So if you take that viewpoint, then pricing needs to sit in the product function. This is my strong-held belief, one that probably won't change now.
cards.zh: 如果你接受那個看法，那定價就必須放在產品這一側。這是我很堅定的信念，大概不會再改了。
cards.why: 先把結論掛在一個前提上（if you take that viewpoint），再表態這是自己的堅定信念——條件句讓你不強迫別人，後半句讓你不顯得沒立場。台灣人常只有其中一半：不是太軟就是太硬。
swaps: follow that logic and you end up at...
that's a hill I'll die on
cards.pmNote: 定價該歸產品還是財務，取決於你認為定價是「防守」還是「設計」。
cards.episode: Pricing your AI product: Lessons from 400+ companies and 50 unicorns | Madhavan Ramanujam

alts.quote: Virtual office could get pretty good, but we would never beat that. And so we were almost limited in our own imagination about how good could this product be.
alts.zh: 虛擬辦公室可以做到不錯，但我們永遠贏不過真實見面。所以我們等於是被自己的想像力上限卡住了——這個產品最好能到哪裡。

alts.quote: So we try to build a team based on the needs of the work a bit, but then end up with a much smaller core.
alts.zh: 所以我們會盡量照工作本身的需求去組團隊，最後就會收斂成一個小很多的核心。

alts.quote: And I would just say generally, until you see pull, just people pulling the product out of your hands, you don't want to be spending money.
alts.zh: 我會說一個通則：在你看到「拉力」之前——就是人家把產品從你手上搶走那種——你都不該開始花錢。

cards.pattern: We can go deep into this — you can pull me back or ask me to go deeper
cards.quote: Yeah, we can go deep into this and you can pull me back or ask me to go deeper, whatever. It doesn't matter.
cards.zh: 這題我們可以講得很深，你隨時可以把我拉回來，或叫我再講細一點，都行。
cards.why: 在長回答之前先把「打斷我」的權力交給對方——這是英文會議裡展現從容的高階動作，也順便解決了自己講太久的風險。pull me back 這個說法台灣人幾乎想不到。
swaps: stop me whenever
wave me off if this is too much detail
cards.episode: Pricing your AI product: Lessons from 400+ companies and 50 unicorns | Madhavan Ramanujam

alts.quote: I know we'll talk more about this, but let me go back to the question I was going to ask...
alts.zh: 我知道這個我們等下會再聊，不過讓我先回到我原本要問的問題。

alts.quote: So let me take us back on track and let's talk about just the high level framework here.
alts.zh: 我們把話題拉回來，來談一下這個框架的高層次架構。

alts.quote: And stop me if I'm getting too wonky, I can really get into this.
alts.zh: 如果我講得太細節控你就打斷我，這個主題我可以講到停不下來。

cards.pattern: I'll try to see what I can talk about without getting too detailed
cards.quote: Sure. I will try to see what I can talk about without getting too detailed, but the thesis of the book is...
cards.zh: 好，我盡量在不講太細的前提下講一點，這本書的主軸是……
cards.why: 被問到還不能公開的東西時，不要說 I can't talk about that（會冷場），而是先答應要講、同時劃出深度上限。答應＋設限，是保密與合作之間的最佳平衡。
swaps: I can share the shape of it, not the numbers
let me stay at the level I'm allowed to
cards.episode: Pricing your AI product: Lessons from 400+ companies and 50 unicorns | Madhavan Ramanujam

alts.quote: For what it's worth, we're not really motivated to try to create a self-improvement empire. This is not our full-time job. We just hope it works for you and is useful.
alts.zh: 順帶一提，我們並不是想搞一個自我成長帝國。這不是我們的正職。我們只是希望這對你有用。

alts.quote: that's too easy to come to me and be like, "Oh, here's A and B. You do the work and tell me which you one to pick." No way.
alts.zh: 「這裡有 A 案和 B 案，你來想、你來選」——這太輕鬆了。不行。

alts.quote: And if with all of that it didn't work, then you can say, "Hey, we're not going to try this again because we literally did try everything that we could to test this hypothesis.
alts.zh: 如果做到那樣還是沒用，你就可以說：「我們不會再試一次了，因為我們真的已經把能測的都測過了。」

cards.pattern: It comes down to not [表面動作], but how deeply you understand [問題]
cards.quote: And so I think a lot of it comes down to not the things you try, but how you deeply understand the problem that's preventing someone from using your product effectively.
cards.zh: 所以我覺得關鍵不在你試了哪些招，而在你有多深地搞懂「是什麼擋住使用者用好你的產品」。
cards.why: 「comes down to not X, but Y」是把功勞從戰術移到理解的萬用句。當團隊一直在討論要做哪個實驗時，用這句把大家拉回問題本身。
swaps: the win wasn't the tactic, it was the diagnosis
less about what we tried, more about what we finally understood
cards.pmNote: 轉換率卡住時，先做質化訪談找出真正的疑慮，再設計實驗。
cards.episode: The original growth hacker reveals his secrets | Sean Ellis (author of “Hacking Growth”)

alts.quote: And so in that case, someone like me who's an advisor comes in and is like, "That's right, it's not a marketing problem, it's company strategy problem.
alts.zh: 所以那種情況下，像我這種顧問進去就會說：「沒錯，這不是行銷的問題，這是公司策略的問題。」

alts.quote: So there's, I wouldn't say a checklist, but there's a series of questions that I asked to diagnose why is growth slowing in this order, because it's one of these things where the first one that's a problem, if you don't fix that, it doesn't matter if you fix one of the ones below.
alts.zh: 我不會說那是一張檢查清單，但我確實有一組問題，會照順序問下去診斷成長為什麼變慢——因為只要最前面那個沒修，後面修再多都沒用。

alts.quote: Don't think of users as using your product. Think of users as hiring you to do something for them.
alts.zh: 別把使用者想成「在用你的產品」。要想成他們是「雇用你」去替他們完成某件事。

cards.pattern: Your two big levers on [目標] are [A] and [B]
cards.quote: I mean your two big levers on driving a conversion are increase desire, reduce friction.
cards.zh: 驅動轉換率，你只有兩根大槓桿：提高慾望、降低阻力。
cards.why: lever（槓桿）是英文商業語彙裡描述「可操作變因」的核心字。把一堆選項壓成兩根槓桿，是讓團隊立刻能行動的講法——句子越短，執行力越高。
swaps: there are really only two dials here
everything we do falls into one of two buckets
cards.pmNote: 轉換率＝慾望 ÷ 阻力；多數團隊只做後者。
cards.episode: The original growth hacker reveals his secrets | Sean Ellis (author of “Hacking Growth”)

alts.quote: I fundamentally do not believe in outsourcing the heartbeat of the organization, which is sales.
alts.zh: 我從根本上不相信可以把一家公司的心跳外包出去——而銷售就是心跳。

alts.quote: I think so many folks don't know where to begin on starting a startup, and my tactical advice is start doing customer validation first versus building a PowerPoint deck.
alts.zh: 很多人根本不知道創業要從哪裡開始，我很具體的建議是：先去做客戶驗證，而不是先做一份簡報。

alts.quote: When we talk about pricing strategies, we hear many buzzwords, and it's irrelevant. So when we take a step back and look at it, there's literally only three types of pricing strategies.
alts.zh: 談定價策略的時候會聽到一堆流行詞，那些都不重要。退一步看，定價策略其實就只有三種。

cards.pattern: What we're trying to do is build a flywheel around [核心價值]
cards.quote: And that ultimately, we understand what makes it a must-have product. And then what we're trying to do is build a flywheel around that must-have value.
cards.zh: 最終我們要弄清楚是什麼讓它變成「非有不可」的產品，然後圍繞那個非有不可的價值，去打造一個飛輪。
cards.why: flywheel（飛輪）是英文商業裡描繪「會自己越轉越快的機制」的標準意象。用 build a flywheel around X 講願景，比 We want to grow 具體十倍，而且暗示成長是機制而不是努力。
swaps: build a loop around that value
make that moment compound
cards.pmNote: 成長飛輪：啟用 → 參與 → 推薦 → 再啟用，圍繞 must-have 價值設計。
cards.episode: The original growth hacker reveals his secrets | Sean Ellis (author of “Hacking Growth”)

alts.quote: We should be cannibalizing the existing state of our product every six to 12 months. Every six to 12 months, it should make our existing product look silly.
alts.zh: 我們應該每六到十二個月就把自己現有的產品吃掉一次。每六到十二個月，新的東西就該讓舊的看起來很蠢。

alts.quote: But I think that I'd like to change that. I'd like to help change the mood. I'd like to help change the way we're thinking about things.
alts.zh: 但我會想去改變這件事。我想幫忙改變那個氛圍。我想幫忙改變我們思考事情的方式。

alts.quote: You want your product to live in their brain somewhere where when they think about, "Hey, I have to create a presentation." They come to you as the default tool.
alts.zh: 你會希望你的產品住在他們腦中的某個位置：當他們想到「我得做一份簡報」的時候，預設就是來找你。

cards.quote: So if I got a 37%, am I going to be like, "Oh no, this would be impossible?" It's more nuanced than that.
cards.zh: 如果我拿到 37%，我會覺得「完蛋、沒救了」嗎？沒那麼一刀切。
cards.why: 「It's more nuanced than that」是英文會議裡最有教養的反對句：你沒有說對方錯，你說的是對方的版本太粗。四個字就能把一個二元問題重新打開。
swaps: it's not that binary
there's more texture to it than that
I'd resist a hard line there
cards.pmNote: PMF 的 40% 門檻是參考點不是及格線。
cards.episode: The original growth hacker reveals his secrets | Sean Ellis (author of “Hacking Growth”)

alts.quote: I don't know that that's how it's going to play out.
alts.zh: 我不確定事情會這樣發展。

alts.quote: And it's kind of building a house that you want every brick in the house to match. And if you go and try and take some bricks from someone else's house and stick it in your house, it's probably going to not look very matched.
alts.zh: 這有點像蓋房子，你會希望每一塊磚都是搭的。如果你跑去人家家裡搬幾塊磚塞進自己家，看起來大概就是不搭。

alts.quote: So I'm going to disagree with Sedaris a little bit.
alts.zh: 這點我要跟 Sedaris 有一點不一樣的看法。

cards.pattern: Just one quick interjection there — [補充]
cards.quote: Just one quick interjection there is that when I coined growth hacking, I did not think of it as a bunch of one-off hacks.
cards.zh: 這邊我快速插一句：我當初造 growth hacking 這個詞的時候，並不是指一堆一次性的小花招。
cards.why: 插話最安全的三件事：宣告很短（quick）、宣告只有一個（one）、指定位置（there）。台灣人最怕在英文會議插話，這句把打斷包裝成「幫忙補位」，幾乎不會被討厭。
swaps: quick footnote on that
one small correction before we move on
can I jump in with one thing?
cards.episode: The original growth hacker reveals his secrets | Sean Ellis (author of “Hacking Growth”)

alts.quote: I want to come back real quick to the activation metric because it's something that a lot of people somewhat misuse and think maybe incorrectly about.
alts.zh: 我想快速回到啟用指標那件事，因為很多人其實在誤用它、想錯方向。

alts.quote: Real quick on Yahoo because it makes me think about it.
alts.zh: 快速講一下 Yahoo，因為它讓我想到這件事。

alts.quote: It gets easier. I don't want to go off too much of a tangent, but the thing you have to remember is that pricing is not this knob that you can turn separate from the rest of your strategy.
alts.zh: 是會變簡單。我不想扯太遠，但有件事一定要記得：定價不是一個可以單獨轉的旋鈕，它跟整套策略是連在一起的。

cards.pattern: Maybe I picked the wrong [X], but at least it [正面效果]
cards.quote: And so maybe I picked the wrong term in calling it growth hacking, but I think it at least opened the conversation to getting more people thinking about growth in a different way.
cards.zh: 所以也許我當初取 growth hacking 這個名字是取錯了，但至少它打開了對話，讓更多人開始用不同的方式想成長這件事。
cards.why: 認錯 + 保住成果的雙段結構。承認的是「用詞」這個小的、可讓的部分，守住的是「影響力」這個大的部分。這比整段道歉或整段辯護都成熟。
swaps: I'd name it differently today, but
the label aged badly — the idea didn't
cards.episode: The original growth hacker reveals his secrets | Sean Ellis (author of “Hacking Growth”)

alts.quote: The biggest mistakes I've made have been going into business models where other people have repeatedly failed and thinking, I can do this better.
alts.zh: 我犯過最大的錯，都是跳進那種別人一再失敗的商業模式，然後心想：我可以做得比他們好。

alts.quote: I came in thinking I was supposed to behave the way I behaved at Apple, which is very direct, fighting hard.
alts.zh: 我進去的時候以為我該照在 Apple 的那一套來——非常直接、硬碰硬地爭。

alts.quote: truth be told, when I interviewed with Fareed that first time, I think back to the interview and I think I bombed it. I actually don't think I would've hired me back then.
alts.zh: 老實講，我第一次跟 Fareed 面試的時候，現在回想起來我覺得我搞砸了。換成是我，當時我大概也不會錄取我自己。

cards.pattern: I think it's [評價], but maybe I'm just being protective of my original idea
cards.quote: So I think it's an unnecessary addition, but maybe I'm just being protective of my original idea.
cards.zh: 我覺得那是多此一舉的補充，不過也可能只是我在護著自己原本的想法啦。
cards.why: 先講反對意見，再自己點出自己可能有的偏見——這叫 disclosing your bias。奇妙的是，這反而讓你的反對更有份量，因為聽的人知道你已經自己檢查過一輪了。
swaps: take this with a grain of salt, it's my own framework
I have an obvious conflict of interest here, but
cards.pmNote: RICE 的 R（reach）Sean 認為已經含在 ICE 的 I（impact）裡。
cards.episode: The original growth hacker reveals his secrets | Sean Ellis (author of “Hacking Growth”)

alts.quote: By the way, I'm being very mean to Figma so far in this conversation. There is a time when it's the right time for the Figma file.
alts.zh: 順帶一提，我到目前為止對 Figma 有點太兇了。Figma 檔是有它對的時機的。

alts.quote: I'm curious what you think. I still don't think ideas are worth as much as maybe a lot of people think. I still think execution is really hard.
alts.zh: 我反而想聽你怎麼看。我還是不覺得點子有大家講的那麼值錢，我還是覺得執行才難。

alts.quote: In fact, if I'm being brutally honest, I think loops are kind of hard to achieve in B2B SaaS.
alts.zh: 其實老實不客氣地講，我覺得在 B2B SaaS 要做出成長迴圈是滿難的。

cards.pattern: If there's anything I'd be accused of, it would be [自己的弱點]
cards.quote: And so I think if there's anything that I would be accused of, it would be being over simplifying things.
cards.zh: 如果說我有什麼會被人批評的，大概就是我把事情簡化過頭了。
cards.why: 把最可能的批評自己先講出來，而且用「被指控」這種略帶自嘲的框架——對方之後再提就沒有力道了。這是英文裡處理已知弱點的標準先手。
swaps: the fair criticism of my approach is
if you want to knock this, knock it on X
cards.episode: The original growth hacker reveals his secrets | Sean Ellis (author of “Hacking Growth”)

alts.quote: I think there's this stigma that brand marketing and performance marketing are sort of at odds with each other. I very much follow the sort of thought that brand marketing is performance marketing.
alts.zh: 大家有一種成見，覺得品牌行銷和成效行銷是互相對立的。我個人非常認同的說法是：品牌行銷就是成效行銷。

alts.quote: I still think that things that we interviewed for in the past, a critical mindset, the ability to really understand deeply the technical nature of a problem is still much more important than whether you're a fully AI native programmer or not.
alts.zh: 我還是認為我們過去在面試裡看的那些東西——批判性的思維、能真正深入理解問題技術本質的能力——遠比你是不是一個完全 AI 原生的工程師重要得多。

alts.quote: Actually, all feedback I think is valid. People's feelings are valid, but it doesn't mean that you need to do something about all of those things.
alts.zh: 其實我覺得所有回饋都是有效的。別人的感受都是真的，但這不代表你每一項都得去處理。

cards.pattern: Credit [人] with this — [事情經過]
cards.quote: Credit our CEO with this, that I shared the data with him and he basically told the product team, "We are putting a complete freeze on the product development roadmap."
cards.zh: 這件事要歸功給我們執行長：我把數據給他看，他就直接跟產品團隊說「產品路線圖全面凍結」。
cards.why: 在講自己成功案例的中途，用一句 Credit X with this 把功勞明確分出去——不只是禮貌，也讓你的敘述更可信（願意分功的人聽起來沒在膨風）。
swaps: that call was hers, not mine
hat tip to X for that one
cards.pmNote: 註冊→實際使用率從 5% 拉到 50%，同樣的通路花費才從月 1 萬美金變成月 100 萬。
cards.episode: The original growth hacker reveals his secrets | Sean Ellis (author of “Hacking Growth”)

alts.quote: And to her credit, she didn't put it in, and it still worked brilliantly.
alts.zh: 而且說句公道話，她確實沒放進去，結果一樣做得很漂亮。

alts.quote: What if I called it educating your manager about all the great work your team has been doing? What if I called it helping people see why your team should get more resources?
alts.zh: 如果我把它叫做「讓主管了解你的團隊做了哪些很棒的事」呢？如果我把它叫做「幫大家看見為什麼你的團隊該拿到更多資源」呢？

alts.quote: Joanne's really special. I got to just take a moment to give her a giant shout out. She is the only person that I've worked with that has as much technical depth as she does have product taste.
alts.zh: Joanne 真的很特別。我一定要停下來大聲說一下她有多厲害——她是我合作過唯一一個技術深度跟產品品味一樣強的人。

cards.pattern: I don't want to overstate it, but [你的貢獻]
cards.quote: Yeah, I mean, I don't want to overstate it, but they basically said all the early stuff we did to grow TikTok was based on your writing.
cards.zh: 我不想講得太誇張，不過他們基本上是說：TikTok 早期做的成長工作，都是照你寫的東西做的。
cards.why: 談自己的成績時最難的就是分寸。I don't want to overstate it 先自降一格，後面再把事實原封不動講完——聽起來既不吹牛也沒縮小。績效面談的萬用開場。
swaps: I won't claim more than my share, but
I had a hand in it — how big a hand, others can judge
cards.episode: The original growth hacker reveals his secrets | Sean Ellis (author of “Hacking Growth”)

alts.quote: I don't want to make it seem like it was me against everyone because that was definitely not the case. I think the starting engineers and designers on that team really cared about the quality of what they built too.
alts.zh: 我不想講得好像是我一個人對抗全世界，完全不是那樣。那個團隊的工程師跟設計師本來就很在乎品質。

alts.quote: So we cut down basically 50% of test runs this way, which is pretty great, and we're not warming the planet as much with all these unnecessary CPU cycles being wasted on tests.
alts.zh: 我們用這個方法把測試執行次數砍掉大概一半。

alts.quote: I just want to say, I'm this Nigerian girl. I don't have an MBA, I didn't work in consulting, and I'm here, right?
alts.zh: 我只想說：我就是個奈及利亞女生。我沒有 MBA，也沒做過顧問業，但我人就在這裡。

cards.pattern: At first I gave the smart-ass answer '[舊立場]'. But I started finding that [新發現]
cards.quote: And at first I gave the smart-ass answer, "I don't care what they say, I care what they do." But I started finding that my experiments were so much better the more I talked to customers.
cards.zh: 一開始我回了一句欠揍的話：「我不在乎他們說什麼，我在乎他們做什麼。」但後來我發現，我越常跟客戶聊，實驗設計就越好。
cards.why: 改變立場的最佳講法：把舊的自己演出來（連當時的臭屁語氣一起），再讓證據把自己翻過來。自嘲式的 smart-ass answer 讓「我錯了」不再需要痛苦地講出口。
swaps: my glib answer back then was...
I used to push back with X — until I noticed Y
cards.pmNote: 質化與量化混用，實驗品質才會提升。
cards.episode: The original growth hacker reveals his secrets | Sean Ellis (author of “Hacking Growth”)

alts.quote: If you had asked me when I first started the company, it would've been an enthusiastic hell yes. I totally recommend. Now, I have a couple asterisks on top of it.
alts.zh: 如果你在我剛創業的時候問我，答案會是超級肯定的「絕對推薦」。現在的話，我會加上幾個但書。

alts.quote: By the way, I will say on the Peter one, I've come much more around to Peter's point of view. I would probably argue that one quite a bit differently today than I did, and I would give his view, I think, a lot more credit.
alts.zh: 順帶一提，Peter 那場辯論，我現在比較站到他那邊了。同樣的題目今天要我講，我會講得很不一樣，也會給他的看法多很多分數。

alts.quote: Even if I don't agree with the feedback, what is the insight that I'm missing? How am I wrong about this? What would be true for this other person to be right?
alts.zh: 就算我不同意那個回饋，我也會問：我漏掉了什麼洞見？我哪裡想錯了？要怎麼樣，對方才會是對的？

cards.pattern: If you give a team [X], they'll take [X]. If you give them [Y], they'll take [Y]
cards.quote: But I think it's really important for it to be a time capped group conversation. And if you give a team 30 days, they'll take 30 days. If you give them six months, they'll take six months.
cards.zh: 我覺得這一定要是一場有時間上限的團體討論。你給團隊 30 天，他們就會用滿 30 天；你給六個月，他們就會用滿六個月。
cards.why: 用重複同一句型的對稱句把一個抽象的管理道理講到不可反駁。time-capped（設上限的）這個形容詞也很值得學——它把「限制」講成一種設計，不是不信任。
swaps: let's timebox this to 30 minutes
work expands to fill the time you give it
cards.pmNote: 北極星指標的討論給團隊 30 分鐘就夠，前提是原料與檢核清單齊備。
cards.episode: The original growth hacker reveals his secrets | Sean Ellis (author of “Hacking Growth”)

alts.quote: So I've used up basically all our time talking about Make Time. I think we should have a follow-up episode just to talk about Sprint. What I think we do is let's cut off the lightning round.
alts.zh: 我基本上把時間都花在 Make Time 上了。我覺得我們該再錄一集專門講 Sprint。現在我的想法是：閃電問答就先砍掉。

alts.quote: It's a day long podcast on its own. So some other time.
alts.zh: 那個講一整天都講不完，改天再說吧。

alts.quote: Now that you've agreed among yourselves that you're going to do that for a fixed period of time, everyone go around the room and say, "If I could start this company over again the thing I wish we were doing was."
alts.zh: 既然大家已經同意用一段固定的時間來試，那就一個一個講：「如果能重來一次，我希望我們在做的是＿＿＿。」

cards.pattern: It's a great accelerant when it's already working, but it can't fix [根本問題]
cards.quote: To me, I think it's a great accelerant when it's already working, but it can't fix it if people don't want to talk about your product.
cards.zh: 對我來說，那在本來就跑得動的時候是很好的加速器，但如果根本沒人想談論你的產品，它救不了你。
cards.why: accelerant（加速劑）這個字精準劃出一種工具的能力邊界：它只能放大既有的東西。當老闆要求「加個推薦機制就會成長」時，這句是最有禮貌的擋箭牌。
swaps: it amplifies what's there; it doesn't create it
that's an accelerator, not an engine
cards.pmNote: Dropbox 推薦計畫成功的前提是它本來就有很強的口碑。
cards.episode: The original growth hacker reveals his secrets | Sean Ellis (author of “Hacking Growth”)

alts.quote: I don't really agree and I still think it's wrong, but I'm committed to it." That's not actually commitment.
alts.zh: 「我其實不同意，我還是覺得這是錯的，但我會照做。」那並不是真正的承諾。

alts.quote: But, and this is the big but, no one has this at the early stages when they don't have a good idea and they don't have customers and it's objectively not working.
alts.zh: 但是——而且這是很大的一個「但是」——在最早期、還沒有好點子、沒有客戶、客觀上根本不 work 的時候，沒有人會有那種信念。

alts.quote: I also think it would be easy to use all what I just said as an excuse not to eventually build a great product.
alts.zh: 我也覺得，我剛剛講的那些很容易被拿來當藉口，變成「反正最後也不用做出好產品」。

cards.pattern: That becomes a bit of a strategic conversation of whether we want [A] or [B]
cards.quote: I think that becomes a bit of a strategic conversation of do we want to have a better chance of surviving, going after a niche that we know we can serve well?
cards.zh: 我覺得這時候就變成一個策略層級的討論了：我們是要提高存活機率、去打一個我們服務得很好的利基市場嗎？
cards.why: 當一個問題其實沒有正確答案時，最好的動作是把它「升級」成策略對話，而不是硬給答案。這句同時保護了你（我不會亂拍板）跟團隊（這件事值得認真討論）。
swaps: that's a leadership call, not a data call
this one's above my pay grade to decide alone
cards.pmNote: 小而狂熱的族群 vs 大而溫吞的族群，選哪個取決於你募了多少錢。
cards.episode: The original growth hacker reveals his secrets | Sean Ellis (author of “Hacking Growth”)

alts.quote: I think it's the difference between oversimplification and focusing. You can have a complex problem and be like, "You know what? I need to hold some things constant."
alts.zh: 我覺得差別在於「過度簡化」和「聚焦」。面對複雜問題你可以說：好，我需要先把某些變數固定住。

alts.quote: So yeah, no hard and fast rule, but I think it's always you need to have this matrix of options in your mind and be very deliberate about which one you are going with and why.
alts.zh: 沒有什麼鐵則，但你腦中要有一張選項矩陣，而且要很清楚自己選了哪一格、為什麼。

alts.quote: So I think a lot of times we just think, okay, this is the scope of it for now and we are okay launching this and the execution is good. But we know that this is not the fully figured out version.
alts.zh: 很多時候我們就是這樣想：現階段範圍就到這裡，執行品質夠好，可以上。但我們知道這還不是完整想通的版本。

cards.pattern: Why would I possibly mortgage [長期資產] for [短期小利]?
cards.quote: I had this reputation that's, like I randomly pulled the number and said, my reputation worth $5 million. Why would I possibly mortgage that reputation for $20,000?
cards.zh: 我隨便抓個數字，說我的名聲值五百萬美金。那我幹嘛為了兩萬塊去把這個名聲抵押掉？
cards.why: mortgage（抵押）把「短期得利、長期受損」的抽象概念變成金融動作，聽的人立刻感覺到代價。談任何長短期取捨（技術債、砍測試、對客戶硬拗）都能套。
swaps: that's borrowing against next year
we'd be trading a dollar of trust for a dime of revenue
cards.episode: The original growth hacker reveals his secrets | Sean Ellis (author of “Hacking Growth”)

alts.quote: In product, I like to joke, there's no right answers. There's only wrong answers, and you're just trying to execute well on the least wrong answer that's available to you.
alts.zh: 做產品這行我常開玩笑說：沒有對的答案，只有錯的答案；你能做的就是把眼前「最不錯」的那個做好。

alts.quote: The number one thing to figure out when you're thinking about the different pricing pieces, pound for pound, it's the pricing metric or the value metric.
alts.zh: 定價的各個環節裡，論投入產出比，最該先搞定的就是計價單位（價值指標）。

alts.quote: Is the juice worth the squeeze? And now I would say that it's pretty clear that the juice is worth the squeeze.
alts.zh: 這個果汁值得你這樣擠嗎？以現在來看，我會說很明顯是值得的。

cards.pattern: I want to put a pin in that and come back to it
cards.quote: Okay. I want to put a pin on that and come back to that because a really important topic.
cards.zh: 好，這個我先插個旗、等一下再回來講，因為這題真的很重要。
cards.why: 會議控場最實用的一句：暫時擱置一個好議題，但同時肯定它的重要性，讓被打斷的人不覺得被忽略。標準說法是 put a pin in it（Lenny 講成 on that，口語常見）。
swaps: let's park that for now
I'll come back to that — flagging it
let's table that
cards.episode: The original growth hacker reveals his secrets | Sean Ellis (author of “Hacking Growth”)

alts.quote: But I think it's really important for it to be a time capped group conversation. And if you give a team 30 days, they'll take 30 days. If you give them six months, they'll take six months.
alts.zh: 我覺得這一定要是一場有時間上限的團體討論。你給團隊 30 天，他們就會用滿 30 天；你給六個月，他們就會用滿六個月。

alts.quote: So I'd say practically just try to look for places where it seems the team's having the same debate over and over and have it once, get it done, and put it behind you.
alts.zh: 很實際的做法是：找出團隊一再重複爭論的那幾件事，把那場辯論一次辯完、定案、然後永遠翻過去。

alts.quote: So let me take us back on track and let's talk about just the high level framework here.
alts.zh: 我們把話題拉回來，來談一下這個框架的高層次架構。

cards.pattern: [方案] might be a solution, but it can never be a problem on its own
cards.quote: You're never trying to solve a problem of simplifying. And simplifying might be a solution, but it can never be a problem on its own.
cards.zh: 你不會是在解決「簡化」這個問題。簡化可能是一種解法，但它本身永遠不會是問題。
cards.why: 這是整批語料裡最鋒利的一句。它給了你一把刀，去切開所有「把解法當成目標」的路線圖項目——把 simplifying 換成 redesign、migrate、AI 化，句子照樣成立。
swaps: that's a solution wearing a problem's clothes
what's the problem that would make this the answer?
cards.pmNote: roadmap 上寫「簡化 onboarding」＝沒定義問題；要寫的是「新用戶在第三步搞不懂要做什麼」。
cards.episode: Elena Verna on how B2B growth is changing, product-led growth, product-led sales, why you should go freemium not trial, what features to make free, and much more

alts.quote: And so then the first few pages became very much more problem-based because if people don't understand the problem then they can't understand or care about your solution.
alts.zh: 所以前面幾頁後來就大改成以「問題」為主，因為人如果不懂那個問題，就不可能懂、也不可能在乎你的解法。

alts.quote: But you take the thing you're responsible for and you just do one zoom out of the problem you're solving and question that.
alts.zh: 你就拿你負責的那件事，把你在解的問題往外拉一層，然後質疑那一層。

alts.quote: Everyone that I know says they have a bottom of funnel problem. It's never a bottom of funnel problem. It's a top of funnel problem.
alts.zh: 我認識的每個人都說自己是漏斗底部有問題。從來都不是漏斗底部的問題，是漏斗頂端的問題。

cards.pattern: If you ever have a line item on your roadmap that says [X], please cross it out
cards.quote: But if you ever have a line item on your roadmap that says simplified onboarding, please cross it out.
cards.zh: 如果你的路線圖上有一條寫著「簡化 onboarding」，拜託把它劃掉。
cards.why: 用 please 開頭的祈使句在英文裡不是禮貌，而是一種帶感情的強調（像在求你）。擋需求時比 We shouldn't do this 更有記憶點，也不那麼官僚。
swaps: strike that line
that one doesn't survive the cut
cards.episode: Elena Verna on how B2B growth is changing, product-led growth, product-led sales, why you should go freemium not trial, what features to make free, and much more

alts.quote: And so even though I really like a lot about this, I'm going to say no." And I often think that founders think that there's some secret truth that's being held from them on why someone says no or they want more feedback.
alts.zh: 「就算我真的很喜歡這個東西的很多地方，我還是要說不。」我也常覺得，創辦人以為別人說不的背後藏著什麼沒告訴他的秘密，或想再要更多回饋。

alts.quote: We're not going to interrupt you with a popup that says like, "Do you want to save your changes," or any of that kind of stuff.
alts.zh: 我們不會用那種「你要儲存變更嗎？」的彈窗打斷你，那類東西都不會有。

alts.quote: I am really hesitant to recommend any template. And what I'd say is these are principles for building it, not any prescribed formula.
alts.zh: 我真的很不願意推薦任何範本。我會說，這些是建構的原則，不是一套規定好的公式。

cards.pattern: That's an outlier — don't treat it as a pattern
cards.quote: Obviously never say never. Sometimes it might work, and if it worked for you, I am so glad. But that's an outlier and don't treat it as a pattern.
cards.zh: 當然，凡事沒有絕對。有時候真的會成功，如果你成功了我真的替你高興。但那是特例，不要把它當成通則。
cards.why: 先把例外整個讓給對方（甚至說我替你高興），再一刀把它釘死成 outlier。outlier / pattern 這組字是英文商業討論裡分辨「軼事」跟「規律」的標準工具，台灣人常缺這一層。
swaps: that's the exception that proves the rule
one data point isn't a trend
cards.pmNote: 改版／重新設計官網幾乎不會帶來成長，成功案例是離群值。
cards.episode: Elena Verna on how B2B growth is changing, product-led growth, product-led sales, why you should go freemium not trial, what features to make free, and much more

alts.quote: It's one thing to say you're spending a lot of time looking outside the building. It's a whole other thing to hear from the places you don't normally hear from.
alts.zh: 說自己花很多時間在公司外面看，是一回事；真的去聽那些你平常聽不到的聲音，完全是另一回事。

alts.quote: I challenge it and I say, "First of all, I don't think there's evidence for that. Is there evidence for that? And even if there is, it doesn't really matter."
alts.zh: 我會直接反問：「首先，我不覺得這件事有任何證據。你有證據嗎？就算有好了，其實也不重要。」

alts.quote: People say that time flies and it doesn't. What happens is it goes by unaccounted.
alts.zh: 大家都說時間過得很快，其實不是。真正發生的是：那些日子根本沒被記下來。

cards.pattern: Never ever once have I seen [X] produce [Y]
cards.quote: Never ever once have I seen a rebrand or redesign, especially of a marketing site, produce good performance results.
cards.zh: 我從來、一次都沒看過品牌重塑或改版——尤其是行銷官網——帶來好的成效數字。
cards.why: 把否定詞放句首造成倒裝（Never once have I seen...），這是英文裡最強的強調結構之一。用自己的親身統計當證據時，倒裝句能把「我的經驗」講出「這是規律」的份量。
swaps: not once in fifteen years have I seen
I've yet to see a single case where
cards.episode: Elena Verna on how B2B growth is changing, product-led growth, product-led sales, why you should go freemium not trial, what features to make free, and much more

alts.quote: If you say, 'I think this is going to take three months to launch' and I was thinking four weeks, you're never going to hear four weeks from me, ever.
alts.zh: 如果你說「我覺得要三個月」，而我原本想的是四週，那你永遠不會從我嘴裡聽到四週。永遠不會。

alts.quote: The basic principle with laser is that willpower is never going to win, and there's great research on this, but for now just trust me, you're not going to white-knuckle your way through not looking at Twitter when you're trying to work.
alts.zh: laser 的基本原理是：意志力永遠贏不了。這方面有很多很好的研究，但現在你先信我——你不可能靠硬撐來讓自己工作時不看 Twitter。

alts.quote: prospects who meet you in person have 10 to 30% higher willingness to pay than those who didn't. Churn for those folks who you meet in person is typically 20% lower than those folks who have never met you.
alts.zh: 跟你當面見過的潛在客戶，付費意願會高出 10 到 30%；見過面的客戶流失率通常比沒見過的低 20%。

cards.pattern: I use it as an input, but never as a destination
cards.quote: I use it as an input into ideation, but I never use it as a destination for the result, if that makes sense.
cards.zh: 我把它當成發想的「輸入」，但絕不把它當成結果的「終點」，這樣講你懂我意思嗎？
cards.why: input vs destination 這組對比一次解決「參考競品該參考到什麼程度」這個永恆爭論。結尾的 if that makes sense 是母語者在講完抽象區分後的標準緩衝，不是真的在問你懂不懂。
swaps: it informs the work, it doesn't define it
it's a starting point, not an answer
cards.pmNote: 拆競品可以當靈感，但不能跳過使用者研究與設計流程。
cards.episode: Elena Verna on how B2B growth is changing, product-led growth, product-led sales, why you should go freemium not trial, what features to make free, and much more

alts.quote: And so the prompt here is to try to go more off the beaten path either from your personal experience, like in the case of Brex and Retool or Whatnot.
alts.zh: 所以這裡給你的思考提示是：試著走出那條被踩爛的路，從你自己的經驗裡挖，像 Brex、Retool、Whatnot 那樣。

alts.quote: And what Canva really does is we're literally smack bang in the middle of that Venn diagram of creativity and productivity, rather than making our customers have to make a choice between those two suites.
alts.zh: Canva 真正在做的事，就是不偏不倚站在「創意」跟「生產力」這兩個圈的交集正中央，而不是逼客戶在兩邊二選一。

alts.quote: We should probably not do things that would've been invented by everybody else 10 minutes later. Where are the problems that are not solving themselves?
alts.zh: 我們大概不該去做那些晚十分鐘別人也會做出來的東西。真正該問的是：哪些問題是不會自己被解決的？

cards.pattern: My rule of thumb: if we can't [條件], we shouldn't [行動], period
cards.quote: My rule of thumb, if we cannot collect the sample size in the month, we shouldn't test it, period.
cards.zh: 我的判準是：如果一個月內收不到足夠樣本數，那就不要測，就這樣。
cards.why: rule of thumb（經驗法則）＋句尾的 period（就這樣、不討論了）是一組黃金搭配：前者表示這是經驗不是真理（謙虛），後者表示現在不接受討論（果斷）。同時軟又硬。
swaps: my bar is simple:
hard line for me:
..., full stop
cards.pmNote: 樣本數一個月內收不齊的實驗，改用前後期比較（pre vs post）就好。
cards.episode: Elena Verna on how B2B growth is changing, product-led growth, product-led sales, why you should go freemium not trial, what features to make free, and much more

alts.quote: I fundamentally do not believe in outsourcing the heartbeat of the organization, which is sales.
alts.zh: 我從根本上不相信可以把一家公司的心跳外包出去——而銷售就是心跳。

alts.quote: I think so many folks don't know where to begin on starting a startup, and my tactical advice is start doing customer validation first versus building a PowerPoint deck.
alts.zh: 很多人根本不知道創業要從哪裡開始，我很具體的建議是：先去做客戶驗證，而不是先做一份簡報。

alts.quote: When we talk about pricing strategies, we hear many buzzwords, and it's irrelevant. So when we take a step back and look at it, there's literally only three types of pricing strategies.
alts.zh: 談定價策略的時候會聽到一堆流行詞，那些都不重要。退一步看，定價策略其實就只有三種。

cards.pattern: ..., but the question is, how much time do you have to [X]?
cards.quote: Success is an output of a lot of failures, but the question is, how much time do you have to fail?
cards.zh: 成功是一堆失敗的產物，但問題是：你有多少時間可以失敗？
cards.why: 先同意一句所有人都同意的話，再用 but the question is 把真正的限制條件換上去。這是把空泛的價值觀討論（要允許失敗）拉回可管理問題（我們有幾次機會）的最快路徑。
swaps: sure — the real constraint is
agreed in principle; the binding question is
cards.pmNote: 失敗次數是資源，市場不會等你把每個坑都自己踩一遍。
cards.episode: Elena Verna on how B2B growth is changing, product-led growth, product-led sales, why you should go freemium not trial, what features to make free, and much more

alts.quote: But that's the wrong question, because you can do a lot of bad things that will improve revenue.
alts.zh: 但那是錯的問題，因為你可以做很多爛事，一樣能讓營收變好。

alts.quote: Finding a new manager is always an option, but I guess sometimes the real question is, is actually spending time to try to understand what is your manager optimizing?
alts.zh: 換一個主管永遠是個選項，但我想有時候真正的問題是：要不要花時間去搞懂你的主管到底在最佳化什麼？

alts.quote: So we can accidentally spend a lot of our time thinking about features that are very deep in the user adoption journey. And so we can kind of end up oversolving for that.
alts.zh: 我們很容易不小心把時間都花在使用者旅程很後段的功能上，結果就在那一段過度投入了。

cards.pattern: I'm very sorry to break it to you, but [難聽的事實]. I'm 99% sure of that
cards.quote: I am very sorry to break it to all of you, but your problem is not unique. I am 99% sure of that.
cards.zh: 很抱歉要這樣說，但你的問題一點都不特別。我有 99% 的把握。
cards.why: break it to someone＝把壞消息告訴某人。前面的道歉是社交緩衝，後面的 99% 卻不留餘地——先給糖再給刀，是給難聽回饋最有效的順序。台灣人常兩邊都軟，話就傳不到。
swaps: I hate to be the one to say it, but
this is going to sting, but
cards.pmNote: 你的成長問題別人解過，先去找人問，不要從零重造解法。
cards.episode: Elena Verna on how B2B growth is changing, product-led growth, product-led sales, why you should go freemium not trial, what features to make free, and much more

alts.quote: And I think I want to be clear, in my mind the problem is obviously not about the practitioners, it's systemic.
alts.zh: 我想講清楚：在我看來問題不在第一線的人身上，是系統性的。

alts.quote: I would say there are a few things that PMs do that annoy engineers and to be clear, I am sure that engineers annoy PMs, just as much.
alts.zh: 我會說有幾件事是 PM 做了會惹惱工程師的——先講清楚，我相信工程師惹惱 PM 的程度也不遑多讓。

alts.quote: The only answer I think one can have is, don't stick your head in the sand and say, "I hate all of this stuff," because that gives you a great feeling of moral superiority.
alts.zh: 我覺得唯一的答案是：別把頭埋進沙子裡說「我討厭這些東西」，因為那只會讓你很有道德優越感。

cards.pattern: Once you stand that up, it's a gift that keeps on giving and nobody can take it away from you
cards.quote: Obviously, I skew very heavily towards earned channels just because once you stand that up, that's a gift that just keeps on giving and nobody can take that away from you.
cards.zh: 我明顯偏向自有通路，因為那個東西一旦架起來，就是一份會一直給你回報的禮物，而且沒有人拿得走。
cards.why: 描繪願景不需要形容詞疊加，只需要一個對比：會一直給 vs 沒人拿得走。前半講複利，後半講防禦性——兩句話講完一個策略資產的全部價值。stand up 當動詞用（把某個機制建立起來）也很值得學。
swaps: it compounds, and it's ours
that's an asset, not a spend
cards.pmNote: Dropbox 超過 50% 的獲客來自分享機制——競爭對手買不到那些眼球。
cards.episode: Elena Verna on how B2B growth is changing, product-led growth, product-led sales, why you should go freemium not trial, what features to make free, and much more

alts.quote: And it doesn't matter how small that first step is or how seemingly inconsequential if it is working towards that future that you want to will into existence
alts.zh: 第一步有多小、看起來多微不足道，都沒關係——只要它是朝著你想召喚出來的那個未來走。

alts.quote: I still feel like ChatGPT feels a little bit like MS-DOS, like we haven't built Windows yet. And it'll be obvious once we do.
alts.zh: 我還是覺得 ChatGPT 有點像 MS-DOS——我們的 Windows 還沒做出來。而且一旦做出來，大家馬上就會知道那就是了。

alts.quote: And he would say, you have to aim for Chartres. You have to make something that is better than that. That should be your goal, not to just turn in something that's what you feel is good enough.
alts.zh: 他會說：你要對準夏特大教堂。你要做出比它更好的東西。那才是你的目標，而不是交出一個你自己覺得「還可以」的作品。

cards.pattern: If you don't have [X] on your roadmap, you're going to be in real trouble over the next [時間]
cards.quote: And if you don't have them on your growth roadmap, you are going to be in some really big trouble over the next year to two years because your cost of acquisition is only going to go up.
cards.zh: 如果你的成長路線圖上沒有這些東西，未來一到兩年你會陷入大麻煩，因為你的獲客成本只會一路往上。
cards.why: 把急迫性綁在一個具體的時間窗（next year to two years）＋一個單向的趨勢（only going to go up）。沒有時間窗的警告，聽起來永遠都可以明年再說。
swaps: the window on this closes in about 18 months
this only gets more expensive from here
cards.episode: Elena Verna on how B2B growth is changing, product-led growth, product-led sales, why you should go freemium not trial, what features to make free, and much more

alts.quote: And so ever since then, we've been automating jobs and creating new jobs, and you can always see the job that's going to go away, and you don't know the new job because it doesn't exist yet.
alts.zh: 從那時候到現在，我們一直在自動化舊工作、也一直在長出新工作；而你永遠看得到那個要消失的工作，看不到新的，因為它還不存在。

alts.quote: And it seems like it would be a huge deal because it changes others expectations, and that is true. But the real power of it is in changing our own expectations about what we are going to do.
alts.zh: 看起來它之所以有用，是因為它改變了別人的期待——這也沒錯。但它真正的威力，在於改變我們自己對自己的期待。

alts.quote: And the third thing is that I really believe that... I don't believe. I think we all know at this point that the most important thing for the growth of anything tech is retention.
alts.zh: 第三件事是我真的相信——不，不是相信。我覺得到這個時間點大家都已經知道了：科技產品成長最重要的就是留存。

cards.pattern: [X] can amplify [好的狀況], but [X] can't fix [壞的狀況]
cards.quote: The point is growth can amplify great product market fit and growth can help you grow faster once you are already growing. But if you are slowing down, growth is going to be absolutely helpless to do anything.
cards.zh: 重點是：成長團隊可以放大本來就好的 PMF，可以讓已經在成長的東西長更快。但如果你正在衰退，成長團隊完全無能為力。
cards.why: 拒絕一個不合理的期待，最有效的方式不是說「做不到」，而是精準定義「什麼情況做得到、什麼情況做不到」。amplify vs fix 這組動詞是關鍵：放大器不是修理工。
swaps: we can multiply what works; we can't manufacture it
hiring for this won't reverse the trend
cards.pmNote: 業績下滑時招成長負責人＝注定失敗；先讓核心產品與行銷把曲線打平。
cards.episode: Elena Verna on how B2B growth is changing, product-led growth, product-led sales, why you should go freemium not trial, what features to make free, and much more

alts.quote: We're not going to get people necessarily building integrations just for us out of the gate unless we have a really compelling product around that.
alts.zh: 除非我們先把周邊產品做到真的夠有說服力，不然一開始不會有人專門為我們做整合。

alts.quote: And then we're like, "Well, does it help the customers? Does it help the product?" This sounds like a side quest to me, and basically means we shouldn't do it.
alts.zh: 然後我們就會問：「這對客戶有幫助嗎？對產品有幫助嗎？」這聽起來像支線任務，那基本上就是不該做。

alts.quote: if you want to change during the course of the quarter, if you want to disrupt our whole engineering product team, you can do it, but understand there's a high cost, and the later you do it in the quarter, the less successful it's going to be
alts.zh: 你想在季中改、想打亂整個工程團隊，可以啊，但你要知道代價很高——而且愈晚改，效果只會愈差。

cards.pattern: It's a step back, but there's a much bigger upside — and you'll have to work to get there
cards.quote: It's like a stepping stone back, but there is a much bigger room for upside that you can get to, but you are going to have to work to get to that upside.
cards.zh: 它其實是往後退一步，但後面有大得多的上升空間可以拿——只是你得努力才走得到。
cards.why: 三段式的取捨敘述：先承認退步、再指出更大的天花板、最後補一句「這不是免費的」。第三段最重要，它讓你的樂觀聽起來不是在推銷。
swaps: we're trading a local max for a shot at a global one
short-term dip, bigger ceiling
cards.pmNote: local maxima vs global maxima：改版的價值在打開新天花板，不在改版當下的數字。
cards.episode: Elena Verna on how B2B growth is changing, product-led growth, product-led sales, why you should go freemium not trial, what features to make free, and much more

alts.quote: And now, it's not like, "Okay, now, we're screwed and the project is going to be bigger." Now, we can have a really cool conversation about trade-offs.
alts.zh: 所以現在不是「完了，這專案要爆了」。現在我們可以來一場很棒的取捨對話。

alts.quote: You get to these points of just diminishing marginal return in every system where it feels like you could put 50 people on this project, it's just not going to dramatically move the needle.
alts.zh: 每個系統都會走到邊際效益遞減的那個點——你感覺得出來，就算再丟 50 個人下去，也不會讓數字有什麼大變化。

alts.quote: So yeah, no hard and fast rule, but I think it's always you need to have this matrix of options in your mind and be very deliberate about which one you are going with and why.
alts.zh: 沒有什麼鐵則，但你腦中要有一張選項矩陣，而且要很清楚自己選了哪一格、為什麼。

cards.pattern: Give yourself [X] at the minimum, ideally more like [Y]
cards.quote: Give yourself two to three months at the minimum, ideally more like six months, to really optimize it back to a good standing where it can potentially outperform.
cards.zh: 至少給自己兩到三個月，最好是六個月，把它優化回到好的水準、甚至超越原本的表現。
cards.why: 談時間資源時同時給下限與理想值，比只給一個數字聰明：對方要砍，也只能砍到你的下限。而 Give yourself 的語氣是替對方著想，不是在跟對方要東西。
swaps: three months buys us X; six months buys us Y
the floor is two months — I'd argue for six
cards.pmNote: 改版之後要預留三到六個月的優化期，這段常被團隊忘記編進計畫。
cards.episode: Elena Verna on how B2B growth is changing, product-led growth, product-led sales, why you should go freemium not trial, what features to make free, and much more

alts.quote: So find some friend of yours that's like, "I'm tweeting about your podcast on Friday, or I'm going to include you in my newsletter next month." And give yourself an artificial deadline or even a real deadline to just put a stake in the ground.
alts.zh: 去找一個朋友，讓他說「我週五要發推介紹你的 podcast」或「我下個月電子報會提到你」，然後給自己一個人造死線——甚至真的死線——先把樁打下去。

alts.quote: So discounting just to get the deal over the line, you're negotiating with yourself.
alts.zh: 為了把案子推過線就先給折扣，那你是在跟自己談判。

alts.quote: So are you able to share what went down there with the story of what happened, how it went, and where things are at now?
alts.zh: 所以你方便說一下那邊發生了什麼事嗎——事情經過、後來怎麼樣、現在到哪了？

cards.pattern: It has to come from knowing you don't know everything and the humility to say 'I need help'
cards.quote: So I think it has to come with a place of knowing that you don't know everything and humility to say, "Hey, I need help." And it actually earns you a lot more credit than you think.
cards.zh: 我覺得這要來自一個認知：你不可能什麼都懂，還要有那個謙虛去說「嘿，我需要幫忙」。而且這其實比你想像的更會替你加分。
cards.why: 後半句是關鍵：It actually earns you a lot more credit than you think——直接對抗「求助＝示弱」的直覺。對害怕在英文環境暴露不懂的台灣人，這句是心理支撐也是實用句。
swaps: asking buys you more credibility than bluffing
I'd rather look green now than wrong later
cards.episode: Elena Verna on how B2B growth is changing, product-led growth, product-led sales, why you should go freemium not trial, what features to make free, and much more

alts.quote: So those will be custom for anything. And I hate to use the word, it depends because I think whenever consultants say it depends, they're just throwing their hands up and saying, "I don't really know."
alts.zh: 這些每家都不一樣。我很不想講「看情況」，因為顧問一講「看情況」，通常就是兩手一攤說「我其實不知道」。

alts.quote: I don't know about you, but literally every time I think to do this, there's a fight in my head of like, "Ah, do I really need to work out today?
alts.zh: 我不知道你怎麼樣，但我每次想到要做這件事，腦子裡都會吵一架：欸，我今天真的需要運動嗎？

alts.quote: I don't think we should filter out AI content. I think we should let you know if content is AI content or not. That's hard, by the way.
alts.zh: 我不認為我們該把 AI 內容濾掉。我認為該做的是讓你知道這則內容是不是 AI 產的。順帶一提，這很難。

cards.pattern: Let's do a workshop first. I have this problem — I think you can help me fix it
cards.quote: Say, "Hey, let's have a workshop first. I have this problem. I think that you can help me fix it."
cards.zh: 你就說：「嘿，我們先辦一場工作坊吧。我手上有這個問題，我覺得你可以幫我解。」
cards.why: 請教高手時不要問「可以跟你聊聊嗎」，而是帶著一個具體問題並指定形式。這三句話的結構是：提議形式 → 給出問題 → 說明為什麼是你。短、具體、有誠意。
swaps: can I bring you a real problem to work on together?
I'd rather pay you for one working session than a intro chat
cards.pmNote: 找顧問／advisor 前先付費做一場工作坊，等於實戰面試。
cards.episode: Elena Verna on how B2B growth is changing, product-led growth, product-led sales, why you should go freemium not trial, what features to make free, and much more

alts.quote: So especially when you're meeting with a new engineering team for the first time, actually ask them, what is one thing I can do to help you this week?
alts.zh: 尤其是第一次跟新的工程團隊碰面時，真的去問他們：這禮拜我可以幫上哪一件事？

alts.quote: So instead of just going to someone saying, "Hey, can you be a mentor?" Coming to me and say, "Do you know someone who's actually really good at changing the way teams work or really good at communicating a new vision that I can talk to?"
alts.zh: 與其跑去問人家「你可以當我的 mentor 嗎」，不如問：「你認識誰特別擅長改變團隊運作方式、或特別會傳達新願景，可以讓我請教一下嗎？」

alts.quote: Hey, I'm an early stage startup. We have a lot to learn. Can we kind of gain your insight into how this problem is manifesting on your side?
alts.zh: 嗨，我們是很早期的新創，還有很多要學。能不能請教你，這個問題在你們那邊是怎麼呈現的？

cards.pattern: I want to call an audible here — [改變議程]
cards.quote: And kind of on a note, I want to call an audible, and so we were going to talk through all of your favorite frameworks.
cards.zh: 順著剛剛那個點，我想臨時改一下流程——我們原本要把你最愛的框架全部走一遍。
cards.why: call an audible 來自美式足球（四分衛在開球前臨時改戰術），現在是會議室裡「臨時變更議程」的標準說法。用它比 Let's change the plan 更有掌控感，也順便顯示你是有意識地改，不是失控。
swaps: let me audible here
I'm going to switch gears on the agenda
change of plan — bear with me
cards.episode: Elena Verna on how B2B growth is changing, product-led growth, product-led sales, why you should go freemium not trial, what features to make free, and much more

alts.quote: "I need 20 minutes of focused time to interrogate something that I've done. We're not going to talk. I'm literally going to force us into a room or Zoom.
alts.zh: 「我需要二十分鐘的專注時間來拷問我做的東西。我們不用講話。我就是要把大家關進一個會議室或 Zoom。」

alts.quote: I want to talk about public speaking skills, but just to close the loop on that.
alts.zh: 我想聊聊公開演講的技巧，不過在那之前先把剛剛那題收尾。

alts.quote: We start all of our meetings with what are you scared to say in our business?
alts.zh: 我們每場會議都從這個問題開始：在這家公司裡，你不敢講的是什麼？

cards.pattern: To make this even more concrete for people, can you [具體要求]?
cards.quote: To make this even more concrete for people that are starting to like, oh, shit I got to do this. Can you just give us a list that doesn't have to be exhaustive?
cards.zh: 為了讓大家更具體一點——那些正在想「糟糕我得開始做了」的人——你可以給我們一個清單嗎？不用列很完整沒關係。
cards.why: 要求對方講具體時，先把理由掛在「聽眾」身上（for people），不是「我聽不懂」。後面的 doesn't have to be exhaustive 是降低對方負擔的關鍵——你越說不用完美，對方越願意馬上給。
swaps: can you ground that in an example?
off the top of your head, what would that look like?
cards.episode: Elena Verna on how B2B growth is changing, product-led growth, product-led sales, why you should go freemium not trial, what features to make free, and much more

alts.quote: To set the answer up, I'll give you a super brief history of Make Time.
alts.zh: 為了鋪陳我的答案，我先講一段 Make Time 的超簡短來歷。

alts.quote: Let me refine that a little bit more. It's more about giving people the information that they can use for decisions that they alone are good at...
alts.zh: 我把那個講法再修得精準一點。重點比較是：給人們他們才擅長的那類決策所需要的資訊。

alts.quote: And I might even ask them to define what product-led means to them that we can get on the same page of what we're even talking about.
alts.zh: 我甚至會請他們先定義一下「產品驅動成長」對他們來說是什麼意思，這樣我們才知道彼此在講的是不是同一件事。

cards.quote: And so what I'm hearing is when you come into a project and the way you simplify is you start putting together a doc that describes these things you're talking about...
cards.zh: 所以我聽到的是，你進到一個專案時，你簡化的方式就是先寫一份文件，把你剛講的那些東西寫下來。
cards.why: 「So what I'm hearing is…」是英文會議裡最安全的確認句：它把「我可能聽錯」的責任攬在自己身上，而不是質疑對方講不清楚。台灣人常直接說 "You mean...?"，聽起來像在挑錯；這句則同時完成「我有在聽」＋「請幫我確認」兩件事。
swaps: What I'm taking away from this is...
If I'm following you correctly...
So the way I understood that is...
cards.pmNote: 在跨職能會議裡覆述對方的話，是最低成本的對齊 (alignment) 動作——它讓誤解在會議中就暴露，而不是在交付前才爆炸。
cards.episode: Meta’s Head of Product (and 29th employee) on working with Mark Zuckerberg, early growth tactics, why PMs are like conductors, and more | Naomi Gleit

alts.quote: I say something to you like, "Lenny, I think what I'm hearing you say is you're off and you're thinking, screw you, Matt.
alts.zh: 我會對你說：「Lenny，我想我聽到你在說的是——你火了，你心裡在想：去你的，Matt。」

alts.quote: Just for folks that are listening, just to calibrate what size of company you're talking about selling to here.
alts.zh: 為了讓聽的人有個基準——你剛剛講的是賣給多大規模的公司？

alts.quote: I often go into a project, everyone's operating at a PhD level, I'm coming in at a kindergarten level...
alts.zh: 我常常進到一個專案時，大家都在博士班的水準討論，而我是幼稚園程度進來的。

cards.quote: Just to double click on that one real quick, so what you're describing for the visual is you're presenting here's our options, here's our three options on a slide.
cards.zh: 這點我很快追一下——你剛說的那個視覺化，意思是你把三個選項放在一張投影片上對吧？
cards.why: 「double click」是矽谷會議的高頻動詞，意思是「把這一點放大來看」。加上 "real quick" 等於先承諾「我不會佔太久」，所以打斷不會惹人厭。這是台灣人最缺的一招：不是搶話，而是宣告「我只借三十秒」。
swaps: Can I double click on that for a second?
Let me pull on that thread real quick
Quick follow-up on that before we move on
cards.pmNote: 會議中即時追問細節，比會後私訊確認省下一整輪往返。
cards.episode: Meta’s Head of Product (and 29th employee) on working with Mark Zuckerberg, early growth tactics, why PMs are like conductors, and more | Naomi Gleit

alts.quote: I'm going to jump in real quick just to highlight what you're talking...
alts.zh: 我快速插一下，只是想把你剛剛講的重點標出來……

alts.quote: Can I double click on that though for a second?
alts.zh: 我可以就那一點再往下鑽一下嗎？就一下下。

alts.quote: Oh, one thing I forgot that I learned from Guy Rosen, he is our chief security officer, is when you have three options and a recommendation...
alts.zh: 喔對，我忘了講一件我從 Guy Rosen（我們資安長）那邊學到的：當你有三個選項加一個建議的時候⋯⋯

cards.pattern: I'm going to come back to X. I want to take a tangent to Y.
cards.quote: I'm going to come back to what you've learned about what makes super successful PMs, what makes you really successful. I want to take a tangent to Zuck.
cards.zh: 成功 PM 的特質這題我等一下會繞回來。我想先岔題聊一下 Zuck。
cards.why: 厲害在「先寄放、再岔題」：他不是隨便跳題，而是當場替被跳過的議題留一個位子，讓對方知道「你講的沒被丟掉」。這是主持人控場的核心技巧——會議的議程焦慮，多半來自「不知道還會不會回來談」。
swaps: Let's park that and come back to it
I want to bookmark that — first, a quick detour
Hold that thought, I want to go sideways for a second
cards.pmNote: 把離題「命名」出來（tangent / detour），比硬壓住離題更能維持會議節奏。
cards.episode: Meta’s Head of Product (and 29th employee) on working with Mark Zuckerberg, early growth tactics, why PMs are like conductors, and more | Naomi Gleit

alts.quote: Now that you've agreed among yourselves that you're going to do that for a fixed period of time, everyone go around the room and say, "If I could start this company over again the thing I wish we were doing was."
alts.zh: 既然大家已經同意用一段固定的時間來試，那就一個一個講：「如果能重來一次，我希望我們在做的是＿＿＿。」

alts.quote: "I need 20 minutes of focused time to interrogate something that I've done. We're not going to talk. I'm literally going to force us into a room or Zoom.
alts.zh: 「我需要二十分鐘的專注時間來拷問我做的東西。我們不用講話。我就是要把大家關進一個會議室或 Zoom。」

alts.quote: he'll sit in a review and be like, "I don't think this is right." And then he'll pause and say, "I'm going to clear the rest of my day. Let's sit and figure it out."
alts.zh: 他會在評審會上說：「我覺得這不對。」然後停一下說：「我把今天剩下的行程清掉，我們一起坐下來把它弄清楚。」

cards.quote: And this may not be a direct answer to the question, but it didn't really necessarily come from Mark.
cards.zh: 這可能不算直接回答你的問題，不過這件事其實不見得是 Mark 起頭的。
cards.why: 先自曝「我知道我沒正面回答」，反而讓聽者放心——因為最惱人的不是答非所問，是講的人沒發現自己答非所問。面試、被老闆抽問時特別好用：它買到繼續講下去的許可。
swaps: This is a bit adjacent to your question, but...
I'm going to answer a slightly different question first
Let me come at that from another angle
cards.pmNote: 當問題本身框錯了，資深的人不會硬答，而是先標示「我要換個框」。
cards.episode: Meta’s Head of Product (and 29th employee) on working with Mark Zuckerberg, early growth tactics, why PMs are like conductors, and more | Naomi Gleit

alts.quote: That's the problem. I mean, that is the trillion dollar question so I don't really have an answer. I have a couple thoughts on it.
alts.zh: 問題就在這。這是那種價值一兆美元的問題，所以我其實沒有答案，但我有幾點想法。

alts.quote: Okay, that's a difficult and different question.
alts.zh: 好，這是個困難、而且性質不太一樣的問題。

alts.quote: I mean, look, there is literally no magic answer to that. I wish that there was, but there is not. There's no format.
alts.zh: 老實說，這題沒有什麼神奇答案。我也希望有，但就是沒有。也沒有什麼固定格式。

cards.quote: And stop me if I'm getting too wonky, I can really get into this.
cards.zh: 如果我講得太細節控你就打斷我，這個主題我可以講到停不下來。
cards.why: 把「要不要繼續聽」的控制權主動交給對方，是專業感很強的一招——講細節前先給對方煞車。"wonky" 指「鑽進技術細節的書呆子勁」，母語者常用來自嘲。台灣人往往一路講到底，或乾脆不敢展開；這句讓你可以放心展開。
swaps: Cut me off if this is too in the weeds
Tell me if this is more detail than you need
Stop me if I'm going too deep here
cards.pmNote: 簡報時主動交出中斷權，比事後道歉「講太久」更有掌控感。
cards.episode: Meta’s Head of Product (and 29th employee) on working with Mark Zuckerberg, early growth tactics, why PMs are like conductors, and more | Naomi Gleit

alts.quote: I always say that my superpower is being a professional moron. Because I'm the one that shows up in a room and is like, “Do we have goals? Why are we having this meeting?”
alts.zh: 我常說我的超能力就是當一個專業級的蠢蛋。我就是那種進到會議室會問：「我們有目標嗎？我們現在在幹嘛？這個會到底為什麼要開？」

alts.quote: I'm going to come back to what you've learned about what makes super successful PMs, what makes you really successful. I want to take a tangent to Zuck.
alts.zh: 成功 PM 的特質這題我等一下會繞回來。我想先岔題聊一下 Zuck。

alts.quote: "I need 20 minutes of focused time to interrogate something that I've done. We're not going to talk. I'm literally going to force us into a room or Zoom.
alts.zh: 「我需要二十分鐘的專注時間來拷問我做的東西。我們不用講話。我就是要把大家關進一個會議室或 Zoom。」

cards.pattern: Before we wrap, is there anything we haven't covered that you wanted to cover?
cards.quote: So before we get to our very exciting lightning round, is there anything else that we haven't covered that you wanted to cover or share?
cards.zh: 在進到最後的快問快答之前，還有什麼我們沒聊到、但你想講的嗎？
cards.why: 會議結尾的標準收口句。它做兩件事：宣告「快結束了」（讓大家收心），同時開最後一扇門（避免有人帶著沒講的話離開）。台灣人常用 "Any questions?"，那是要別人問你；這句是請對方補你漏掉的。
swaps: Anything we should have talked about and didn't?
Before we close out — anything I missed?
Is there anything you were hoping I'd ask?
cards.pmNote: 收尾前留一個「補件視窗」，能撈回會後才被提出的隱藏需求。
cards.episode: Meta’s Head of Product (and 29th employee) on working with Mark Zuckerberg, early growth tactics, why PMs are like conductors, and more | Naomi Gleit

alts.quote: Yeah. So it works like this. I start with competitive alternatives.
alts.zh: 對，運作方式是這樣：我從「競爭替代方案」開始。

alts.quote: Let me just try to summarize what you shared, this five step framework.
alts.zh: 我試著把你剛剛講的整理一下，這個五步驟的框架。

alts.quote: Here's what I heard from all of you. I'm listening, I hear this and here's what I want to do about it.
alts.zh: 以下是我從各位那裡聽到的。我有在聽，我聽到了，接下來我打算這樣做。

cards.pattern: Oh, one thing I forgot — [X] is that...
cards.quote: Oh, one thing I forgot that I learned from Guy Rosen, he is our chief security officer, is when you have three options and a recommendation...
cards.zh: 喔對，我忘了講一件我從 Guy Rosen（我們資安長）那邊學到的：當你有三個選項加一個建議的時候⋯⋯
cards.why: 話題已經往前走了，還想補一段——"one thing I forgot" 是最不失禮的回頭插話法。它把插話包裝成「我的疏漏」而不是「你講得不完整」。順帶示範一個母語習慣：人名後面立刻補職稱，讓聽眾不必猜這人是誰。
swaps: Sorry, one thing I meant to mention earlier
Oh — I should have said this before
Can I back up for one second? I skipped something
cards.episode: Meta’s Head of Product (and 29th employee) on working with Mark Zuckerberg, early growth tactics, why PMs are like conductors, and more | Naomi Gleit

alts.quote: Just to double click on that one real quick, so what you're describing for the visual is you're presenting here's our options, here's our three options on a slide.
alts.zh: 這點我很快追一下——你剛說的那個視覺化，意思是你把三個選項放在一張投影片上對吧？

alts.quote: It gets easier. I don't want to go off too much of a tangent, but the thing you have to remember is that pricing is not this knob that you can turn separate from the rest of your strategy.
alts.zh: 是會變簡單。我不想扯太遠，但有件事一定要記得：定價不是一個可以單獨轉的旋鈕，它跟整套策略是連在一起的。

alts.quote: I'm taking us off track, but I want to go a little deeper with this.
alts.zh: 我知道這樣會離題，但我想在這裡多挖一點。

cards.pattern: I don't love X. It's [problem].
cards.quote: In terms of evaluating the options, I don't love pros and cons. It's a flat list of text. It's hard to just get the big picture from that.
cards.zh: 在評估選項這件事上，我不太喜歡用優缺點列表。它就是一串平鋪的文字，很難一眼看到全貌。
cards.why: 「I don't love X」是英文裡殺傷力最小的否定：不是「這是錯的」，是「我個人不偏好」。但後面立刻接一句具體理由，所以不會顯得任性。台灣人反對時常兩極——要嘛不講，要嘛講成 "That's not good"；這個句型剛好落在中間。
swaps: I'm not a huge fan of...
I've never loved...
That's never quite worked for me because...
cards.pmNote: 否定一個既有做法時，一定要立刻給替代方案，否則只是製造真空。
