cards.episode: Meta’s Head of Product (and 29th employee) on working with Mark Zuckerberg, early growth tactics, why PMs are like conductors, and more | Naomi Gleit

alts.quote: And don't get me wrong, I love those cultures, but they're all different cultures. They're very different cultures.
alts.zh: 別誤會，那些文化我都很欣賞，但它們彼此其實非常不一樣，真的差很多。

alts.quote: But the other thing is I don't really love some of that thinking process just in general.
alts.zh: 另外還有一點：那整套思考方式，我其實不是很喜歡，講一般情況啦。

alts.quote: I think this is an interesting thing that technical founders sometimes don't really like. They think sales is a very negative part of the process. I think it's not that black and white.
alts.zh: 技術背景的創辦人常常不太喜歡這件事，他們覺得業務是整個過程裡很負面的一塊。我覺得沒那麼非黑即白。

cards.pattern: If there's a decision, I need three options and a recommendation.
cards.quote: So if there is a decision, I need three options and I need a recommendation that should hopefully help focus the meeting.
cards.zh: 如果這場會要做決定，我要三個選項加一個推薦方案，這樣才有辦法讓會議聚焦。
cards.why: 會議前設「入場費」的句型：不是拒絕開會，而是說清楚「符合什麼條件我才開得下去」。"help focus the meeting" 是很體面的理由包裝——你不是在刁難，你是在保護大家的時間。
swaps: Can you come with a recommendation, not just options?
I'd like a point of view, not just a menu
What would you do, if it were your call?
cards.pmNote: 「三選項＋一推薦」是主管最愛的提案格式：既展示你想過取捨，又不把決策丟回去給對方。
cards.episode: Meta’s Head of Product (and 29th employee) on working with Mark Zuckerberg, early growth tactics, why PMs are like conductors, and more | Naomi Gleit

alts.quote: "I need 20 minutes of focused time to interrogate something that I've done. We're not going to talk. I'm literally going to force us into a room or Zoom.
alts.zh: 「我需要二十分鐘的專注時間來拷問我做的東西。我們不用講話。我就是要把大家關進一個會議室或 Zoom。」

alts.quote: I always say that my superpower is being a professional moron. Because I'm the one that shows up in a room and is like, “Do we have goals? Why are we having this meeting?”
alts.zh: 我常說我的超能力就是當一個專業級的蠢蛋。我就是那種進到會議室會問：「我們有目標嗎？我們現在在幹嘛？這個會到底為什麼要開？」

alts.quote: Every additional person in a meeting has a cost, because every additional person in a meeting makes the people in that meeting less candid than they would have been if there were fewer people in that meeting.
alts.zh: 會議每多一個人都是有代價的，因為人越多，在場的人講話就越保留。

cards.pattern: Who's owning this? / Every workstream has a single-threaded owner.
cards.quote: Sometimes I'm like, "Who's owning this?" And it's like people don't know. That's why I think it's very important to have a single-threaded owner.
cards.zh: 有時候我問「這件事誰在 own？」結果大家都不知道。這就是為什麼一定要有一個單一負責人。
cards.why: "own" 當動詞用（誰 own 這件事）是矽谷會議的日常，台灣人常直譯成 "Who is responsible for this?"，語氣偏究責；"Who's owning this?" 問的是歸屬，不是罪責。散會前問這句，是把口頭共識變成可追蹤決議的最短路徑。
swaps: Who's the DRI on this?
Who's driving this one?
Whose name goes next to this?
cards.pmNote: single-threaded owner（單一負責人）＝ Amazon 的 DRI 概念：一件事只能有一個人的名字，兩個人負責等於沒人負責。
cards.episode: Meta’s Head of Product (and 29th employee) on working with Mark Zuckerberg, early growth tactics, why PMs are like conductors, and more | Naomi Gleit

alts.quote: I'm in too many conversations where I'm like, "Who is on the hook for this decision? Who cares if this decision is made?" It's not like six people with consensus. Who is the person?
alts.zh: 我參加過太多會議，我會問：「這個決定是誰扛？誰真的在乎它有沒有被做出來？」不是六個人共識，是哪一個人？

alts.quote: Okay, so let me summarize things that you've taught us so far. One is think about publications that go to people that will buy your thing. Two is don't think of it broad thing.
alts.zh: 好，我來把你目前教我們的整理一下。第一，挑那些會接觸到你買家的媒體。第二，不要只想到媒體這個層級。

alts.quote: So maybe this is a way to come back to your question about what's the output of the shaping session, it's like it's shaped if we can give this to a technical person and they say, "Yeah, I know what to go build now."
alts.zh: 所以回到你剛剛問的「shaping session 的產出是什麼」：判準是——把它交給一個技術的人，他會說「好，我知道要蓋什麼了」。

cards.quote: I often go into a project, everyone's operating at a PhD level, I'm coming in at a kindergarten level...
cards.zh: 我常常進到一個專案時，大家都在博士班的水準討論，而我是幼稚園程度進來的。
cards.why: 這是「問笨問題」的通行證。她不是說「我不懂」（示弱），而是說「我是新進場的人」（角色說明）——把知識落差重新框成情境問題，不是能力問題。對非母語者尤其好用：你聽不懂時，可以借這個框自然要求對方降階解釋。
swaps: Can you take me back to first principles on this?
Assume I know nothing here — walk me through it
Let me ask the naive question
cards.pmNote: 資深的人敢問基本問題，因為簡化本身就是產出：問題被拆到幼稚園程度，通常也就找到真正的癥結。
cards.episode: Meta’s Head of Product (and 29th employee) on working with Mark Zuckerberg, early growth tactics, why PMs are like conductors, and more | Naomi Gleit

alts.quote: You're sitting in the meeting and you're like, "This is a dumb question. Everyone's going to think I'm an idiot." But then you get brave and you ask it and it turns out it wasn't a dumb question.
alts.zh: 你坐在會議裡想：「這問題也太蠢，問了大家會覺得我是白痴。」結果你鼓起勇氣問了，才發現根本不是蠢問題。

alts.quote: And so what I'm hearing is when you come into a project and the way you simplify is you start putting together a doc that describes these things you're talking about...
alts.zh: 所以我聽到的是，你進到一個專案時，你簡化的方式就是先寫一份文件，把你剛講的那些東西寫下來。

alts.quote: The reason I'm a little confused, just because I want to get it right, is what I'm hearing, which maybe isn't what you said
alts.zh: 我有點不確定，純粹是想弄清楚——我聽到的（可能不是你講的意思）是……

cards.pattern: X is not for X's sake — it's ultimately to [benefit].
cards.quote: Sometimes I feel the need to defend that the process is not for process' sake, it's ultimately to help us all move faster and work better.
cards.zh: 有時候我得替流程辯護一下：流程不是為了流程而存在，它最終是要讓大家跑得更快、做得更好。
cards.why: 「not for X's sake」是預先拆掉對方最可能的攻擊角度：對方還沒說「你在搞官僚」，你已經先替他說了，再翻轉成效益。這叫 pre-empting——先講出反對意見，反對意見就失去殺傷力。
swaps: This isn't process for the sake of process
I'm not adding this to add ceremony — it's so that...
The point isn't the doc, the point is...
cards.pmNote: 推流程時，一定要把它翻譯成「更快」而不是「更嚴謹」，否則工程團隊會直接判死刑。
cards.episode: Meta’s Head of Product (and 29th employee) on working with Mark Zuckerberg, early growth tactics, why PMs are like conductors, and more | Naomi Gleit

alts.quote: Not to say it's not better, but just this is the structure of it, and it kind of sets you up for bragging.
alts.zh: 我不是說它不好，我只是在講它的結構——這個結構會把你逼到一直自誇。

alts.quote: Actually, all feedback I think is valid. People's feelings are valid, but it doesn't mean that you need to do something about all of those things.
alts.zh: 其實我覺得所有回饋都是有效的。別人的感受都是真的，但這不代表你每一項都得去處理。

alts.quote: And I always write them back and say like, "Please tell me the better term and popularize it and I'll use it. It's a great idea."
alts.zh: 我都回信說：「請你告訴我更好的講法，然後把它推廣開，我就會改用。這主意很好。」

cards.pattern: You can imagine [audience] hearing this and thinking...
cards.quote: You can imagine an engineer hearing me talk about how to run a meeting and all the canonical docs and just be like, "What? This sounds terrible."
cards.zh: 你可以想像一個工程師聽我在講怎麼開會、講那堆權威文件，心裡大概是：「蛤？這聽起來超糟。」
cards.why: 自己先演出反對者的台詞，還用對方的語氣（"What? This sounds terrible."）。這比「有些人可能不同意」高明得多——它證明你真的懂對方的痛，聽眾就會願意聽你解釋。會議中被質疑前先自嘲，等於把子彈接走。
swaps: I know how this sounds to an engineer
Some of you are probably thinking...
If I were sitting where you are, I'd be rolling my eyes
cards.pmNote: pre-mortem 的口語版：先把最強的反對意見說出來，再回應它。
cards.episode: Meta’s Head of Product (and 29th employee) on working with Mark Zuckerberg, early growth tactics, why PMs are like conductors, and more | Naomi Gleit

alts.quote: This sounds like a commodity feature and on all surface level it is.
alts.zh: 這聽起來像個誰都有的功能，表面上看也確實是。

alts.quote: First let's examine the counterfactual, right? So let's start with the opposite of your question and say, "How would the world be sadder if we all just gave up on this?"
alts.zh: 我們先看反面情況吧。從你問題的相反面開始想：如果大家乾脆全都放棄這件事，世界會變得多糟？

alts.quote: To me, I think it's a great accelerant when it's already working, but it can't fix it if people don't want to talk about your product.
alts.zh: 對我來說，那在本來就跑得動的時候是很好的加速器，但如果根本沒人想談論你的產品，它救不了你。

cards.pattern: It doesn't mean we agree — it means we have the same understanding of the facts.
cards.quote: Extreme clarity means everyone's on the same page. It definitely doesn't mean that they all agree with each other, but they just have the same understanding of the facts.
cards.zh: 極度清晰的意思是大家在同一頁上。它絕對不是說大家都同意彼此，而是大家對事實的理解是一致的。
cards.why: 「It doesn't mean X, it means Y」是英文最有效的定義句型，專治雞同鴨講。這句本身也解決一個台灣職場常見誤會：把「對齊」當成「要大家同意」。對齊的門檻其實只到事實層，不到立場層。
swaps: Alignment isn't agreement
We don't have to agree, but we do have to be looking at the same facts
Let's separate the facts from the positions
cards.pmNote: 把會議切成「事實層」與「立場層」：事實不一致造成的爭吵最浪費時間，而且最容易解決。
cards.episode: Meta’s Head of Product (and 29th employee) on working with Mark Zuckerberg, early growth tactics, why PMs are like conductors, and more | Naomi Gleit

alts.quote: Or if the meeting is not under the context of buying it all, it's like, "We're working on something cool. We have a great vision. It aligns with what you're doing. Maybe there's a partnership here."
alts.zh: 或者那場會根本不是在談收購，而是：「我們在做一件很酷的事，我們有很好的願景，跟你們在做的方向對得上。也許這裡有合作的空間。」

alts.quote: I very quickly just sent her a note that said, "Wanted to build on this idea you had today. I really liked that idea, by the way. I saw this article, I saw this research about this other emerging thing."
alts.zh: 我很快就傳了一則訊息給她：「想接著你今天那個想法往下延伸。順帶一提，我真的很喜歡那個點子。我看到一篇研究提到另一個正在浮現的現象……」

alts.quote: She used to have this saying, which is like, "Repetition doesn't spoil the prayer."
alts.zh: 她有一句話我一直記著：「重複並不會壞了那句禱告。」

cards.quote: "Where can I learn what I need to learn about this project?" I ask five different people, get five different answers. That is unacceptable.
cards.zh: 我要去哪裡搞懂這個專案？我問五個人，得到五種答案。這是不能接受的。
cards.why: 描述「團隊沒對齊」最生動的一句話，而且結構可複製：用一個具體場景取代抽象抱怨。台灣人常說 "There is no alignment"，聽的人無感；"five people, five answers" 讓每個人腦中都浮現畫面。
swaps: Ask three people and you get three roadmaps
Everyone has a different version of the truth here
There's no single source of truth on this
cards.pmNote: canonical doc（權威文件）：一個專案只能有一份「總表」，其他文件都從它連出去。
cards.episode: Meta’s Head of Product (and 29th employee) on working with Mark Zuckerberg, early growth tactics, why PMs are like conductors, and more | Naomi Gleit

alts.quote: And if you're on different pages, you're heading in completely different directions.
alts.zh: 如果大家不在同一頁上，那就是往完全不同的方向前進。

alts.quote: The way I would say it is, say you're going to do the thing, say that you're doing the thing, and then say that you did it.
alts.zh: 我的講法是：先說你要做這件事，做的過程中說你在做，做完再說你做完了。

alts.quote: We can't just have the marketing department sit down and cook up new positioning and then heave it over the wall to everybody else. It's a team sport.
alts.zh: 不能讓行銷部門自己關起門想一套新定位，然後往牆外一丟就沒事了。這是團隊運動。

cards.quote: I think the thing you really need to know is that for under 16-year-olds, if they want to change any of these defaults, they're going to have to get their parents' permission.
cards.zh: 我覺得你真正需要知道的是：未滿 16 歲的用戶如果想改這些預設值，必須先拿到父母同意。
cards.why: 在一堆細節裡替聽眾標紅線。母語者很習慣用這種「資訊分級」句型帶聽眾——不是全部倒給你，而是先告訴你哪一句最重要。台灣人簡報常平鋪直敘，缺的就是這種語氣上的粗體字。
swaps: If you only remember one thing, it's this
The headline here is...
The part that actually matters is...
cards.episode: Meta’s Head of Product (and 29th employee) on working with Mark Zuckerberg, early growth tactics, why PMs are like conductors, and more | Naomi Gleit

alts.quote: Yeah. Imagine, no such thing as a request from sales, yeah? No such thing as pressure of like, "We need this thing in order to upsell or to close this deal." Never.
alts.zh: 你想像一下：完全沒有業務來提需求，好嗎？也完全沒有那種「我們需要這個功能才能升級方案、才能成交」的壓力。從來沒有。

alts.quote: It is just so natural for our internal mindset and lingo to flow into the application over time. And you need some counterbalance to get there. And I think it has to be an unnatural counterbalance.
alts.zh: 內部的思維和黑話會很自然地慢慢滲進產品裡。你需要某種抗衡的力量。而且我認為那必須是一種「不自然」的力量。

alts.quote: People often think that I get hired into later stage companies because I'm supposed to teach them how to operate like a big company, and in fact, I say I'm hired to remind them they can operate like a startup.
alts.zh: 大家常以為，公司找我去後期階段是要我教他們怎麼像大公司一樣運作；但其實我都說，我是被找去提醒他們，他們還可以像新創一樣運作。

cards.pattern: One of the development areas for me is...
cards.quote: Candidly, one of the development areas for me, and it could be downstream because I do have this analogy of how to be a PM, is that the growth feedback or the constructive feedback for me is really learning when to lead from the front more.
cards.zh: 老實說，我自己的成長項目之一——這可能跟我對 PM 的那套比喻有關——別人給我的建設性回饋是：我要學會什麼時候該站到前面帶。
cards.why: 談自己的弱點時，母語者不用 weakness，而用 development area / growth feedback / constructive feedback，把缺點放進「還在長」的框架。面試「你的缺點是什麼」時，這組詞就是分水嶺。"lead from the front" 也是台灣人想不到的說法。
swaps: An area I'm actively working on is...
The feedback I keep getting is...
Where I still have room to grow is...
cards.pmNote: 績效面談把缺點講成「發展方向」，比講成「我不擅長」更容易換到資源與教練。
cards.episode: Meta’s Head of Product (and 29th employee) on working with Mark Zuckerberg, early growth tactics, why PMs are like conductors, and more | Naomi Gleit

alts.quote: We doubled our growth rate and last year we were in the low double digits.
alts.zh: 我們把成長率翻倍，去年大概是十幾趴那個區間。

alts.quote: Looking back, my career has been a little bit like a bingo card. I've always been looking to fill in boxes I didn't have filled because I felt like that would make me a better professional.
alts.zh: 回頭看，我的職涯有點像一張賓果卡。我一直在補那些還沒被填滿的格子，因為我覺得那會讓我變成更好的專業工作者。

alts.quote: My one learning there that has stuck with me, and I think can work for other people too, is that it's not just about doing things that actually matter, and learning. It's about being able to tell the story.
alts.zh: 那段經驗裡有一個一直留在我身上的體悟，我覺得對別人也適用：重點不只是去做真正重要的事、去學東西，還要能把這件事講成一個故事。

cards.quote: If there's nothing here, totally cool. But is there something that you changed Mark's mind about?
cards.zh: 如果沒有的話完全沒關係。不過，有沒有哪件事是你改變了 Mark 的想法的？
cards.why: 問敏感問題前先給對方一個下台階，對方就不必為了面子硬編一個答案。這在跨文化會議特別重要：台灣人被問到答不出來時容易硬撐，而母語者其實習慣先鋪「可以說沒有」。
swaps: Feel free to pass on this one, but...
No pressure if nothing comes to mind, but...
This might be a dead end, but I'm curious...
cards.pmNote: 使用者訪談同理：先允許受訪者說「沒有」，資料才不會被禮貌污染。
cards.episode: Meta’s Head of Product (and 29th employee) on working with Mark Zuckerberg, early growth tactics, why PMs are like conductors, and more | Naomi Gleit

alts.quote: You ask questions like, what's the hardest you've ever worked to get something done and why? And that does differentiate a lot of people, a lot of people don't actually have a great answer to that.
alts.zh: 你可以問這種問題：你這輩子為了完成某件事最拚的一次是什麼？為什麼？這題真的很能分辨人，很多人其實答不太出來。

alts.quote: And then there'll be some other thing that happens that causes you to reinstall it, and that's totally fine, because you're being deliberate about it and you're paying attention.
alts.zh: 然後某天會發生某件事讓你又把它裝回來——那完全沒問題，因為你是刻意這樣做的，你有在注意。

alts.quote: You usually need a goal in mind, like what are you optimizing for?
alts.zh: 你通常心裡得先有個目標，也就是——你到底在最佳化什麼？

cards.quote: I still may insert myself and say, "Hey, let me pause here for a second and try to capture what has been said." This is what I've heard.
cards.zh: 我還是會切進去說：「欸，我先暫停一下，把剛剛講的整理一下。」以下是我聽到的。
cards.why: 這是整批素材裡最值錢的一句。它同時解決台灣人在英文會議的兩個痛點：插不上話、以及不知道怎麼展現貢獻。你不需要提出新想法，只要當那個「按暫停＋做總結」的人——Anneka 說，別人會直接把這個動作認定為「有策略思維」。
swaps: Let me play back what I'm hearing
Can I stop us here and summarize?
Before we go further — here's where I think we are
cards.pmNote: 在發散的討論裡做即時 summarization，是最容易被誤認為策略能力的行為（她的原話：people actually view that as strategy）。
cards.episode: Becoming more strategic, navigating difficult colleagues, harnessing founder mode, and more | Anneka Gupta (Chief Product Officer at Rubrik)

alts.quote: Let me just try to summarize what you shared, this five step framework.
alts.zh: 我試著把你剛剛講的整理一下，這個五步驟的框架。

alts.quote: I think that's the key part, but let me pause there and then I'll talk a little bit about ChatGPT and some of my reasoning behind that.
alts.zh: 我覺得那是關鍵的部分，但我先停在這裡，然後再來講一點 ChatGPT 和我背後的理由。

alts.quote: Here's what I heard from all of you. I'm listening, I hear this and here's what I want to do about it.
alts.zh: 以下是我從各位那裡聽到的。我有在聽，我聽到了，接下來我打算這樣做。

cards.pattern: Is everyone in agreement, or is there some dissent about where we've landed?
cards.quote: Is everyone in agreement with that or is there some dissent about whether that's an accurate portrayal of where we've landed with this conversation?
cards.zh: 大家都同意嗎？還是有人覺得我這樣描述我們的結論並不準確？
cards.why: 總結完一定要用問句結尾，否則就變成「我替大家做決定」。關鍵在 "or is there some dissent"——主動邀請反對，讓沉默的人有位子。"where we've landed"（我們落在哪）是會議收斂的標準說法，台灣人幾乎不會用。
swaps: Does that land for everyone?
Anyone see it differently?
Is that a fair read of where we are?
cards.pmNote: 結論以問句收尾，能把「表面同意、會後翻案」的風險提前引爆。
cards.episode: Becoming more strategic, navigating difficult colleagues, harnessing founder mode, and more | Anneka Gupta (Chief Product Officer at Rubrik)

alts.quote: I think that's the key part, but let me pause there and then I'll talk a little bit about ChatGPT and some of my reasoning behind that.
alts.zh: 我覺得那是關鍵的部分，但我先停在這裡，然後再來講一點 ChatGPT 和我背後的理由。

alts.quote: And again, just to summarize where we're at, just to give people the advice we've shared so far.
alts.zh: 再一次，快速摘要一下我們現在講到哪，把目前分享過的建議整理給大家。

alts.quote: Sometimes I'm like, "Who's owning this?" And it's like people don't know. That's why I think it's very important to have a single-threaded owner.
alts.zh: 有時候我問「這件事誰在 own？」結果大家都不知道。這就是為什麼一定要有一個單一負責人。

cards.pattern: I'm not going to interrupt the flow — I'll just summarize in chat what I've heard.
cards.quote: I'm not going to interrupt the flow conversation. I'm just going to summarize in Zoom chat this is what I've heard, and this is what I think we're saying in this conversation.
cards.zh: 我不打斷大家的討論節奏，我直接在 Zoom 聊天室整理一下我聽到的、以及我認為我們在談的東西。
cards.why: 給「真的插不進話」的人一條後門：把總結打在聊天室，通常會被主持人念出來、拉回主線。對非母語者是黃金策略——書寫沒有口音、沒有搶麥壓力，卻拿到同樣的存在感。
swaps: Dropping a quick summary in the chat
I'll put my read in the chat so I don't derail us
Noting in chat — feel free to correct me
cards.pmNote: 遠端會議的低風險發言管道：chat 的門檻遠低於搶麥，但被引用的機率很高。
cards.episode: Becoming more strategic, navigating difficult colleagues, harnessing founder mode, and more | Anneka Gupta (Chief Product Officer at Rubrik)

alts.quote: I'm going to jump in real quick just to highlight what you're talking... what you just said, which I think is extremely important and powerful, and people might kind of move on too quickly.
alts.zh: 我很快插一下，只是想把你剛剛講的那句畫個重點，我覺得那非常重要、非常有力量。

alts.quote: And I'm like, "Time out. What you're going to do is raise prices again. You just told me you 12x-ed the price and nothing observable changed."
alts.zh: 我就說：「等一下。你接下來要做的是再漲一次價。你剛剛才跟我說你把價格拉了十二倍，結果什麼都沒變。」

alts.quote: So a downside we haven't mentioned, but I'm just going to call it out, is holiday.
alts.zh: 有一個我們還沒提到的缺點，我就直接講出來——就是休假。

cards.pattern: I agree with 90% of that — I'm 10% off.
cards.quote: But then inviting people to discuss and say "Yes," or "No, I agree with 90% of that or 10% off."
cards.zh: 然後邀請大家討論，回一句「同意」，或者「不完全，我同意九成，有一成不太一樣」。
cards.why: 用百分比表達部分不同意，是英文會議極常見、中文卻很少的招。它避免了 yes/no 的二元對立，也自動把討論聚焦到那 10%——不用重新吵整件事。台灣人自己想不出來，但學會後馬上能用。
swaps: I'm with you on most of that, except...
I'd agree with everything but the last part
90% yes — let me push on the other 10%
cards.pmNote: 把異議量化，能防止一個小分歧升級成全案重議。
cards.episode: Becoming more strategic, navigating difficult colleagues, harnessing founder mode, and more | Anneka Gupta (Chief Product Officer at Rubrik)

alts.quote: You know what, I'll say yes and, right.
alts.zh: 這樣說吧，我要用「是，而且」來回答。

alts.quote: We're very interested in folks who have already been thinking about what the future should look like with agents. And we don't have to agree on where we're going, but we want people who are very passionate.
alts.zh: 我們很想找那種已經在思考「agent 的未來該長什麼樣」的人。方向上我們不一定要有共識，但我們要真的在乎這件事的人。

alts.quote: It sounds wonderful, having one person to deal with across all these functions. — It is and isn't. I'll just say, I've done both.
alts.zh: 「有一個人統管這些功能聽起來很棒。」——是也不是。我只能說，兩種我都做過。

cards.quote: Hey, look, I know this is what you're trying to do, but maybe instead of looking at option A here of how we go about tackling this, we should have explored these three other options instead.
cards.zh: 欸，我知道你想達成的是什麼，只是與其走 A 這條路，也許我們該把另外三個選項也攤開來看。
cards.why: 反對老闆的標準結構：先確認他的目標（我知道你要什麼），只反對手段（不是 A 這條路）。台灣人反對時容易連目標一起否定，聽起來像不服；這句把爭點縮到「方法」，老闆的面子完全不受傷。
swaps: I'm bought into the goal — I'd challenge the approach
Same objective, different path: what if we...
Can we pressure-test the mechanism, not the goal?
cards.pmNote: 跟創辦人 disagree 前先還原他的 objective：多數「爛點子」其實是好目標配錯手段。
cards.episode: Becoming more strategic, navigating difficult colleagues, harnessing founder mode, and more | Anneka Gupta (Chief Product Officer at Rubrik)

alts.quote: I don't know that I would look back at what I shipped back then or what we shipped back then, and say they were the best possible solutions or best possible product.
alts.zh: 我不確定我會回頭看當年出的東西，然後說那是最好的解法、最好的產品。

alts.quote: I think if you're building a product where it's not necessarily an AI- first product and you have some AI features that are on the side, but it's not the core of your value, I don't know that I would operate this way.
alts.zh: 如果你做的不是 AI 優先的產品，只是旁邊掛幾個 AI 功能、AI 不是核心價值，那我不確定我會這樣做。

alts.quote: The other thing that's a little bit different about what you said is that emotions do need to be felt.
alts.zh: 還有一點跟你剛剛講的稍微不一樣，就是情緒是真的需要被感受到的。

cards.pattern: What's the hill I'm going to die on?
cards.quote: What's the hill that I'm going to die on and is this something that I can shift or is this something that is not worth shifting?
cards.zh: 哪座山是我願意死守的？這件事我推得動嗎？還是根本不值得去推？
cards.why: "the hill to die on" 是英文職場最常見的取捨隱喻，台灣人聽得懂但幾乎不會主動用。它把「該不該堅持」變成一個可以放上桌面討論的問題，而不是私下悶著生氣。
swaps: Is this a hill worth dying on?
Is this a two-way door or a one-way door?
Do I spend capital here, or save it?
cards.pmNote: 產品領導的核心不是每場都贏，而是選對要贏的那幾場——政治資本是有限資源。
cards.episode: Becoming more strategic, navigating difficult colleagues, harnessing founder mode, and more | Anneka Gupta (Chief Product Officer at Rubrik)

alts.quote: But what's really interesting is it's not a universal thing. The amount of detail that the team is going to feel helps them is a dial that we can turn that depends on who's on the team.
alts.zh: 但有趣的是，這件事沒有通則。要給多少細節其實是一個可以轉的旋鈕，看團隊裡是誰。

alts.quote: Not all of these variables is created equal and the manager is the most important variable in the environment, because a great manager who is empathetic, who is aware of what's going on, has the ability to move the chess pieces around.
alts.zh: 這幾個變數的份量不一樣，主管是環境裡最關鍵的那一個——因為一個有同理心、狀況清楚的好主管，是有能力幫你把棋子移一移的。

alts.quote: Now, again, don't hear this as antagonistic. We're not antagonistic here. We're trying to say, "What's going to help me succeed?"
alts.zh: 再說一次，不要把這聽成對立。我們不是在對抗。我們是在問：什麼能幫我把這件事做成？

cards.pattern: I heard this piece of feedback, and here's what it made me think about our strategy — what do you think?
cards.quote: I was talking to security leaders in our customer advisory board recently and I heard this piece of feedback and this is what it made me think about our strategy, what do you think about that?
cards.zh: 我最近跟客戶顧問委員會的資安主管聊，聽到一個回饋，這讓我重新想我們的策略——你怎麼看？
cards.why: 資深的人挑戰下屬的策略時，不會直接說「這錯了」，而是「丟一個資料點＋問你怎麼看」。她的理由很直白：她一開口，房間裡就沒人敢反駁。這個句型把「主管的意見」降級成「一個可以被反駁的假設」。
swaps: Here's a data point that's been nagging me — how does it square with your plan?
Let me put a hypothesis on the table
I might be wrong, but here's what I keep hearing
cards.pmNote: 位高的人講話會壓縮討論空間，所以要刻意把結論降級成假設（seed an assumption），保留反駁的餘地。
cards.episode: Becoming more strategic, navigating difficult colleagues, harnessing founder mode, and more | Anneka Gupta (Chief Product Officer at Rubrik)

alts.quote: I think I made the product better, but is anyone using it? Does anyone care? Or are we just congratulating ourselves?
alts.zh: 我覺得我把產品做得更好了——可是有人在用嗎？有人在乎嗎？還是我們只是在自我感覺良好？

alts.quote: I think that you need to understand in the event that it's a top-down strategy, what are the assumptions that led to folks believing that that is the right idea?
alts.zh: 我認為，如果那是一個由上而下的策略，你得去弄懂：是哪些假設讓大家相信那是對的方向？

alts.quote: I think people assume that there's a much more detailed semantic understanding of everybody's interests and preferences in the algorithm than there is.
alts.zh: 我覺得大家會以為演算法對每個人的興趣和偏好，有一套比實際上細膩得多的語意理解。

cards.quote: I care so much about you and I'm giving you this feedback because I want you to be successful and I want you to be able to reach the pinnacle of what I know you can accomplish.
cards.zh: 我非常在乎你，我給你這個回饋是因為我希望你成功、希望你能走到我知道你能到的高度。
cards.why: 重點在她強調的一件事：這段話要「明講出來」，不能只是希望對方感受到。台灣主管習慣用暗示和婉轉，結果對方只接收到批評沒接收到善意。把動機說白，是硬回饋能被聽進去的前提。
swaps: I'm telling you this because I think you can go further than this
This comes from a good place — I want you to win
I wouldn't spend this time if I didn't think you had it in you
cards.pmNote: radical candor：關心對方 × 直接挑戰。少了前半段，後半段就只是攻擊。
cards.episode: Becoming more strategic, navigating difficult colleagues, harnessing founder mode, and more | Anneka Gupta (Chief Product Officer at Rubrik)

alts.quote: So when the feedback is coming like raw, they know that it's in their best interest because I've shown them enough times that I genuinely care about the person behind the role.
alts.zh: 所以當回饋很生硬地丟過來，他們知道那是為他們好——因為我已經用夠多次證明，我在乎的是角色背後那個人。

alts.quote: Of course, I don't want to be cruel to the people who are putting their hearts into that work, because the Figma file is beautiful. It's just coming a little early.
alts.zh: 當然，我不想對那些真心投入的人太苛刻——那些 Figma 檔真的很漂亮。只是它來得太早了一點。

alts.quote: Look, I don't have time to sugarcoat any feedback, and frankly, the best people I've worked with are the people who come into one-on-ones with me and yell at me and tell me I'm messing up.
alts.zh: 老實說，我沒空把回饋包糖衣；而且說真的，我合作過最好的人，都是會在一對一裡對我吼、直接說我哪裡搞砸了的人。

cards.pattern: This is how you're being perceived — which may not be what you're intending.
cards.quote: Hey, well this is how other people perceive you including me, but maybe this is not what you are intending...
cards.zh: 其他人——包括我——是這樣看你的，但這可能不是你原本想呈現的樣子。
cards.why: 把「你是這樣的人」換成「你被這樣看」，對方就不會為了辯護人格而關上耳朵。而且它自帶一個善意假設：你的本意是好的，只是傳達出了落差。討論就自然轉向「怎麼改變觀感」這個可執行的問題。
swaps: The perception is X — I don't think that's your intent
Here's how it's landing, which may not be how you meant it
The gap I see is between intent and impact
cards.pmNote: 回饋談「觀感落差」而非「本質缺陷」，對方才有可改的著力點。
cards.episode: Becoming more strategic, navigating difficult colleagues, harnessing founder mode, and more | Anneka Gupta (Chief Product Officer at Rubrik)

alts.quote: And I think the error that people make more often than not is they are actually too stuck on their own product vision. That's the mistake I've seen a little bit more actually than the other way around.
alts.zh: 我覺得大家最常犯的錯，是太黏著自己原本的產品願景。這個錯我看到的，其實比反過來的那種多一點。

alts.quote: Hey, Lenny. You probably didn't know, but I don't really like when people comment on my shirt.
alts.zh: 嘿 Lenny，你可能不知道，我其實不太喜歡別人評論我的衣服。

alts.quote: And it's not because people are bad people. I think most people are really well-intentioned. But what happens when you have people that join and you didn't really need them?
alts.zh: 這不是因為誰是壞人，我覺得大多數人動機都很好。但問題是：當你招了一批其實不需要的人，會發生什麼事？

cards.pattern: All feedback is valid — that doesn't mean you need to act on all of it.
cards.quote: Actually, all feedback I think is valid. People's feelings are valid, but it doesn't mean that you need to do something about all of those things.
cards.zh: 其實我覺得所有回饋都是有效的。別人的感受都是真的，但這不代表你每一項都得去處理。
cards.why: 「承認＋但不照做」的標準句型。先給對方情緒上的完全認可（valid），再把行動決定權留給自己。台灣人常誤以為承認對方有道理就等於答應要改；這句示範兩者可以拆開。
swaps: That's fair, and I'm still going to prioritize elsewhere
I hear it, but it's not where we're putting the effort
Valid — just not a must-have this quarter
cards.pmNote: 回饋分 must-have 與 nice-to-have：must-have 太多時，nice-to-have 就是明確地不做。
cards.episode: Becoming more strategic, navigating difficult colleagues, harnessing founder mode, and more | Anneka Gupta (Chief Product Officer at Rubrik)

alts.quote: It's like these things that seem so common sense are actually hard with what they're doing… a lot of the advice is common sense. That doesn't mean it's easy to put in motion.
alts.zh: 這些看起來根本是常識的東西，真的做起來很難……很多建議都是常識，但常識不代表容易落地。

alts.quote: And I think one of the monikers we use internally is no, then go. As in just think through all the things that could go wrong, understand where scale will break, understand the things that might happen, and then move on anyway.
alts.zh: 我們內部有個口號叫「先說不，然後走」。把所有可能出錯的地方都想過一輪，知道規模在哪裡會斷，然後照樣往前。

alts.quote: First of all, maybe just to set the record straight, if AI is writing over 90% of the code, that doesn't mean engineers are 10X as productive.
alts.zh: 首先，我先把話講清楚：就算 AI 寫了九成以上的程式碼，也不代表工程師的產出就變成十倍。

cards.quote: How do I make this idea one click better? It's not about how do you do something radically, radically different, but taking ideas and then making it slightly better, slightly better.
cards.zh: 我要怎麼把這個想法再往上推一格？重點不是做出天差地遠的東西，而是接手別人的想法，再讓它好一點點。
cards.why: "one click better" 是很好用的提案框：你不是推翻別人，你是在他的基礎上加值。這讓「提出想法」變成低風險行為——尤其適合會議上不敢拋大構想的人。
swaps: Can I build on that?
What if we took that one step further?
Yes — and here's a small twist
cards.pmNote: 策略常不是憑空生出來的大點子，而是把現有的想法一格一格往上推（betterment）。
cards.episode: Becoming more strategic, navigating difficult colleagues, harnessing founder mode, and more | Anneka Gupta (Chief Product Officer at Rubrik)

alts.quote: I would argue that just by breaking the question to these two questions we usually have a slightly better discussion than just my idea is better than yours.
alts.zh: 我會說，光是把這個問題拆成這兩個問題，我們通常就能有比「我的點子比你的好」稍微好一點的討論。

alts.quote: None of this is going to blow anyone's minds, I think, because it's very best practices. But it's easy to overlook when you're so focused on so many different steps of a process.
alts.zh: 這些應該不會讓誰驚呆，因為都是很基本的最佳實務。但當你同時盯著流程裡一大堆步驟時，就是很容易漏掉。

alts.quote: Speaking is not a specialized skill, it's a meta skill. That means that the better you get at speaking, the better your life gets.
alts.zh: 說話不是一項專門技能，它是一項後設技能。意思是：你說話越強，你的人生就越好。

cards.pattern: As long as the decision is 70% right, you can iterate on the rest.
cards.quote: And as long as your decision is like 70% right, you can iterate on that 20, 30% in either direction, but if you don't commit, then you don't actually get any new information that is high fidelity and high quality.
cards.zh: 只要決策有七成對，剩下的兩三成你都可以往任一邊修；但你不下注，就拿不到任何高品質的新資訊。
cards.why: 用一個數字（70%）把「先決定再修正」變成可以說出口的原則，而不是聽起來很草率的直覺。開會卡在分析癱瘓時，這句是最有效的推進器。
swaps: Let's make the call and learn our way to the rest
We're at 70 — that's enough to move
The cost of not deciding is higher than deciding wrong
cards.pmNote: 不做決定＝零學習。承諾之後拿到的資料，品質遠高於假設階段的推演。
cards.episode: Becoming more strategic, navigating difficult colleagues, harnessing founder mode, and more | Anneka Gupta (Chief Product Officer at Rubrik)

alts.quote: And I think people don't understand that in a competitive environment, being right is good, but being quick is necessary.
alts.zh: 我覺得大家沒搞懂：在競爭環境裡，做對是加分，做得快是必要條件。

alts.quote: And the right answer to these narrowly scoped defined problems is not to invent a whole new print dialogue.
alts.zh: 面對這種範圍很窄、已經定義清楚的問題，正確答案並不是重新發明一整套列印對話框。

alts.quote: It's important to obsess about the details of craft, while simultaneously having the perspective and wisdom of which details don't actually matter.
alts.zh: 你要對細節的講究到近乎偏執，同時又要有那個判斷力，知道哪些細節其實根本不重要。

cards.pattern: Before I give feedback: what do you want to do? Where do you want to go?
cards.quote: Sometimes I even start the conversation by asking them, "What do you want to do? Where do you want to go in your career?"
cards.zh: 有時候我甚至會用這個開場：「你想做什麼？你的職涯想往哪走？」
cards.why: 給回饋前先問目標，回饋就從「我對你的評價」變成「我幫你導航」。同一件事，對想當 CPO 的人跟想當技術專才的人，回饋內容完全不同——不先問，回饋就注定錯位。
swaps: Where are you trying to get to?
What does the next version of your career look like?
Before I dive in — what would be most useful to you?
cards.pmNote: 1:1 先校準對方的目標函數，回饋才有槓桿。
cards.episode: Becoming more strategic, navigating difficult colleagues, harnessing founder mode, and more | Anneka Gupta (Chief Product Officer at Rubrik)

alts.quote: So which game do you want to play? Let's just start there.
alts.zh: 所以你想玩哪一種賽局？我們就從這裡開始。

alts.quote: People call me sometimes they're like "I want to know if I have product market fit." Well, the fact that you have time to call me and ask me this question already tells me the answer.
alts.zh: 有人打給我說：「我想知道我們有沒有 PMF。」嗯，你有空打這通電話問我，這件事本身就給了答案。

alts.quote: I'm like, "Let's say we weren't in the room as the leadership team," which is the one the team wants to get behind. Then you'll sometimes see the team hasn't even done the work between themselves talking.
alts.zh: 我會問：「假設我們這些主管不在這個房間，你們團隊自己最想投哪一個？」有時候你會發現他們彼此之間根本還沒討論過。

cards.quote: Let me refine that a little bit more. It's more about giving people the information that they can use for decisions that they alone are good at...
cards.zh: 我把那個講法再修得精準一點。重點比較是：給人們他們才擅長的那類決策所需要的資訊。
cards.why: 當別人幫你總結卻總結歪了，直接說 "That's not what I meant" 會讓對方難堪。"Let me refine that" 把糾正包裝成「我來把它磨得更準」——是你在補完，不是他理解錯。這招在英文會議每天都用得到。
swaps: Let me sharpen that a bit
Close — let me put it slightly differently
I'd nuance that one degree
cards.episode: Humanizing product development | Adriel Frederick (Reddit, Lyft, Facebook)

alts.quote: And if it's helpful, let me break down the question a little bit.
alts.zh: 如果有幫助的話，我把這個問題拆開來講一下。

alts.quote: Just to pull on this thread a little bit more, what is the general advice you share there for people that also don't want to die?
alts.zh: 順著這條線再拉一下：對那些也不想死掉的人，你通常會給什麼建議？

alts.quote: Let me back up and just dissect a little bit the way you described design, you described it in really tactical terms.
alts.zh: 先讓我退一步，拆解一下你剛剛描述設計的方式——你講的是很戰術層次的東西。

cards.quote: So I think about it as designing an interface and make it an extension of yourself rather than a black box on its own that you just need more information to. Is that helpful?
cards.zh: 所以我把它想成在設計一個介面，讓它成為你的延伸，而不是一個你只能不斷餵資料的黑盒子。這樣講有幫到你嗎？
cards.why: 講完一段長解釋後回頭確認，把「你聽懂了嗎」（帶著居高臨下）換成「我講得有用嗎」（責任在講者）。這個責任轉移是母語者的細膩處，台灣人常用 "Do you understand?"，語感其實很傷人。
swaps: Does that answer it?
Is that the level you were after?
Did that land?
cards.episode: Humanizing product development | Adriel Frederick (Reddit, Lyft, Facebook)

alts.quote: And if it's helpful, let me break down the question a little bit.
alts.zh: 如果有幫助的話，我把這個問題拆開來講一下。

alts.quote: To set the answer up, I'll give you a super brief history of Make Time.
alts.zh: 為了鋪陳我的答案，我先講一段 Make Time 的超簡短來歷。

alts.quote: So I don't know if I answered your question, but that's the scope of that problem I think
alts.zh: 我不確定有沒有回答到你的問題，但這大概就是這個問題的範圍。

cards.pattern: So just to kind of recap — you want X, you want Y.
cards.quote: So just to kind of recap, you want it to feel like it's core and critical to the company. You want it to feel like it's everyone's success.
cards.zh: 所以簡單複述一下：你希望它讓人覺得對公司是核心、關鍵的；你希望它是所有人的成功。
cards.why: "just to kind of recap" 裡的 kind of 是關鍵的緩衝詞——它讓總結聽起來像隨手整理，而不是「我來替你定調」。台灣人講英文常缺這類軟化詞，導致語氣比本意強硬。
swaps: So if I zoom out for a second...
Let me play that back
Quick recap before we move on
cards.episode: Humanizing product development | Adriel Frederick (Reddit, Lyft, Facebook)

alts.quote: So to quickly recap a few of the key things that I've written down as we're talking.
alts.zh: 我快速把剛剛邊聽邊記下來的幾個重點整理一下。

alts.quote: Here's what I heard from all of you. I'm listening, I hear this and here's what I want to do about it.
alts.zh: 以下是我從各位那裡聽到的。我有在聽，我聽到了，接下來我打算這樣做。

alts.quote: So to your question, you're a feature team. You want to give it a shot, be in a real product team. These are the four things you need to go out and do.
alts.zh: 回到你的問題：你在一支功能團隊，想試試看真正的產品團隊怎麼運作——那你要去做的就是這四件事。

cards.quote: For folks that haven't worked at a company with this kind of on the ground ops team, can you just unpack what that is?
cards.zh: 對於沒待過有這種第一線營運團隊的人來說，你可以幫忙拆解一下那是什麼嗎？
cards.why: 這是「我聽不懂但不想顯得沒跟上」的最佳解：把問題掛在別人身上（for folks who haven't...），你就從「不懂的人」變成「替大家問的人」。"unpack" 也比 "explain" 更專業、更不像在挑戰對方沒講清楚。
swaps: Can you unpack that a bit for the room?
For those of us not close to this — what does that mean in practice?
Say more about what that looks like day to day
cards.pmNote: 會議裡沒人敢問的術語，通常有一半的人也不懂——先問的人反而拿到主持權。
cards.episode: Humanizing product development | Adriel Frederick (Reddit, Lyft, Facebook)

alts.quote: Just for folks that are listening, just to calibrate what size of company you're talking about selling to here.
alts.zh: 為了讓聽的人有個基準——你剛剛講的是賣給多大規模的公司？

alts.quote: And that's the classic explanation of what they do. So, they sell a data platform. So, that's the capsule answer, but there's lots to unpack in there.
alts.zh: 這是最制式的講法：他們賣的是一個資料平台。這是濃縮版的答案，但底下還有很多可以拆。

alts.quote: So kind of what I'm hearing is a lot of the work is giving humans more information versus giving machine learning algorithms more information and there's a lot more leverage potentially there, giving humans more ways to tweak and dial.
alts.zh: 所以我聽到的大概是：很多工作其實是給人更多資訊，而不是給機器學習演算法更多資訊，而那裡的槓桿可能大得多。

cards.quote: And so we had this idea that we came up with that would do it. I'm not going to let that one out.
cards.zh: 我們後來想到一個做得到的點子。那個我就不外流了。
cards.why: 拒絕透露而不失禮的漂亮示範：語氣輕鬆、不解釋、不道歉。台灣人碰到不能講的事常支支吾吾或編理由；"I'm not going to let that one out" 反而顯得有分寸又有趣。
swaps: That one I'll keep to myself
I'll have to leave that one out
Can't go into that one, sorry
cards.episode: Humanizing product development | Adriel Frederick (Reddit, Lyft, Facebook)

alts.quote: But if a PM came to me with something that was drawn and kind of fully baked, my response was like, thanks for giving me that. Now I know exactly what we're not going to do.
alts.zh: 如果 PM 拿一張畫得很完整的圖來找我，我的回應是：謝謝你給我這個，現在我很清楚我們「不會」做成這樣。

alts.quote: And so even though I really like a lot about this, I'm going to say no." And I often think that founders think that there's some secret truth that's being held from them on why someone says no or they want more feedback.
alts.zh: 「就算我真的很喜歡這個東西的很多地方，我還是要說不。」我也常覺得，創辦人以為別人說不的背後藏著什麼沒告訴他的秘密，或想再要更多回饋。

alts.quote: We're going to have salespeople helping you through it, but we're not going to let you hire someone.
alts.zh: 我們會派業務協助你走完這段，但我們不會讓你去請一個人。

cards.pattern: Now, don't get me wrong — [credential that pre-empts the misread].
cards.quote: Now, don't get me wrong, I've built the experimentation platform at Lyft. I'm a guy who loves data and loves using it and looking at experiments.
cards.zh: 先別誤會我的意思——Lyft 的實驗平台就是我建的。我是個超愛用數據、愛看實驗的人。
cards.why: 當你批評某件事（這裡是「只看數據」），聽眾很容易把你歸類成反對派。"Don't get me wrong" 立刻堵住這條誤讀，還順手把自己的資歷放上桌。批評與立場切割，論點才站得住。
swaps: To be clear, I'm not anti-data
Don't hear this as me saying X
I say this as someone who...
cards.episode: Humanizing product development | Adriel Frederick (Reddit, Lyft, Facebook)

alts.quote: Now, obviously, I'm not saying don't do SEO, or don't do SEM, so organic search or paid search.
alts.zh: 當然，我不是說不要做 SEO、也不是說不要做 SEM——就是自然搜尋跟付費搜尋。

alts.quote: So the idea is, basically, you write up a two-page plan for the project. You invite three or four smart folks who don't know anything about the project and their job is just to tear apart your plan.
alts.zh: 做法是：你先寫一份兩頁的專案計畫，然後找三四個完全不懂這個專案的聰明人來，他們的任務就是把你的計畫拆爛。

alts.quote: I don't really agree and I still think it's wrong, but I'm committed to it." That's not actually commitment.
alts.zh: 「我其實不同意，我還是覺得這是錯的，但我會照做。」那並不是真正的承諾。

cards.quote: I think some controversy is necessary and so I may be at a different point on that one.
cards.zh: 我覺得某種程度的爭議是必要的，所以這一題我的位置可能跟大家不太一樣。
cards.why: 把「我不同意」重寫成「我站的位置不同」——不預設誰對誰錯，只是座標不同。這是英文裡殺傷力最低的異議表達之一，非常適合對上級或客戶用。
swaps: I might land somewhere different on that
I probably sit further along that spectrum
I hold that one a bit differently
cards.episode: Humanizing product development | Adriel Frederick (Reddit, Lyft, Facebook)

alts.quote: I think if you're building a product where it's not necessarily an AI- first product and you have some AI features that are on the side, but it's not the core of your value, I don't know that I would operate this way.
alts.zh: 如果你做的不是 AI 優先的產品，只是旁邊掛幾個 AI 功能、AI 不是核心價值，那我不確定我會這樣做。

alts.quote: He just had an episode recently about a skeptical take on AI that I disagreed with a lot, but it was really interesting to think about it from a different perspective.
alts.zh: 他最近那集講了一個對 AI 很懷疑的觀點，我非常不同意，但從另一個角度想這件事真的很有意思。

alts.quote: So far be it from me to disagree with Mike Tyson, but I think he's wrong.
alts.zh: 我哪敢跟泰森唱反調——但我覺得他錯了。

cards.quote: Where I've seen people get lost is they assume that if you do that alone, it will work.
cards.zh: 我看過很多人卡住的地方是：他們假設光做這件事就會成功。
cards.why: 指出對方的錯誤假設，卻不指名對方——主詞是「我看過的人」，不是「你」。這個第三人稱轉移是拆假設時最好用的緩衝，會議上幾乎不會引起防衛。
swaps: The trap I see teams fall into is...
Where this usually breaks down is when people assume...
The mistake I keep seeing is...
cards.episode: Humanizing product development | Adriel Frederick (Reddit, Lyft, Facebook)

alts.quote: It's actually one of the things I see people fail on the most is they assume something working for one system will work in your world.
alts.zh: 我看到最多人栽的地方就是：他們假設在別的系統上行得通的東西，在你這邊也會行得通。

alts.quote: I think people assume that there's a much more detailed semantic understanding of everybody's interests and preferences in the algorithm than there is.
alts.zh: 我覺得大家會以為演算法對每個人的興趣和偏好，有一套比實際上細膩得多的語意理解。

alts.quote: One thing I've learned is that I think people are really good at coming up with very rational sounding reasons to not do things that just make them uncomfortable.
alts.zh: 我學到一件事：人非常擅長替「其實只是讓自己不舒服的事」找出聽起來很有道理的理由。

cards.pattern: Something I caution people against is...
cards.quote: Something I caution people against though is don't use the data alone to figure out who the marginal user is.
cards.zh: 不過有件事我會提醒大家小心：不要只靠數據去判斷誰是邊際使用者。
cards.why: "caution against" 比 "don't do" 專業得多，語氣是提醒不是命令。它把你放在「有經驗、替你擋坑」的位置，而不是「來管你」的位置——資深感就是從這種措辭累積出來的。
swaps: One thing I'd be careful about here is...
The thing I'd watch out for is...
I'd push back gently on...
cards.pmNote: marginal user＝差一步就會轉換的那群人；找到他們就找到最高槓桿的優化點。
cards.episode: Humanizing product development | Adriel Frederick (Reddit, Lyft, Facebook)

alts.quote: We're very interested in folks who have already been thinking about what the future should look like with agents. And we don't have to agree on where we're going, but we want people who are very passionate.
alts.zh: 我們很想找那種已經在思考「agent 的未來該長什麼樣」的人。方向上我們不一定要有共識，但我們要真的在乎這件事的人。

alts.quote: And I know this is going to trigger some people, but the truth is they don't want to work.
alts.zh: 我知道這句會讓一些人不爽，但事實就是——他們不想做事。

alts.quote: Again, don't get me wrong, I'm not trying to talk people out of doing it.
alts.zh: 再說一次，別誤會，我不是要勸大家別做這件事。

cards.quote: Those are just numbers I'm putting out there. It's always going to be a gut call based on where you are.
cards.zh: 那些數字只是我隨口丟出來的。這終究是看你所在的位置做的直覺判斷。
cards.why: 他剛講完 80/20 的分配，主持人追問「這是你的原則嗎」，他立刻承認那是隨口說的。這一招保護你不被自己的舉例綁架——台灣人被追問時常硬撐把即興數字說成方法論，反而失信。
swaps: Don't quote me on the exact split
That's directional, not precise
I'm making that number up to illustrate the shape
cards.pmNote: 報數字時要標示信心水準：拍腦袋的比例就說是拍腦袋的，別讓它變成別人的規劃基準。
cards.episode: Humanizing product development | Adriel Frederick (Reddit, Lyft, Facebook)

alts.quote: So I'm giving some heuristics, I'm giving some benchmarks, but your mileage is going to vary.
alts.zh: 我給的是一些經驗法則、一些對照基準，但你們的狀況一定會不一樣。

alts.quote: I'm obviously limited on what exactly I can share, but it is true that our retention numbers are really exciting and that is actually the thing we look at.
alts.zh: 我能講的東西確實有限，不過可以說的是，我們的留存數字真的很好看，而且那正是我們在看的指標。

alts.quote: I haven't seen their CAD, so I don't know what it's like inside their device, but they do have a lot of things going on.
alts.zh: 我沒看過他們的 CAD 圖，所以我不知道他們裝置裡面長怎樣，但他們確實塞了很多東西進去。

cards.quote: Okay, good tangent, I wanted to chat about your learnings at Facebook.
cards.zh: 好，這段岔題不錯——我想聊聊你在 Facebook 學到的東西。
cards.why: 把離題拉回主線的最短句：先肯定（good tangent），再直接轉。先給一句正面標籤，轉場就不會顯得你在嫌人家講太久——這是台灣人主持英文會議最常缺的兩秒鐘。
swaps: Great detour — let's get back to...
Love that, and I want to make sure we cover...
Good rabbit hole. Coming back to the agenda...
cards.episode: Humanizing product development | Adriel Frederick (Reddit, Lyft, Facebook)

alts.quote: So let me take us back on track and let's talk about just the high level framework here.
alts.zh: 我們把話題拉回來，來談一下這個框架的高層次架構。

alts.quote: Well, first a pairing, and then one more. The pairing is reset expectations and slow your inbox.
alts.zh: 好，先講一組配套的，再講一個。配套的是：重設期待，還有讓你的收件匣慢下來。

alts.quote: So I think we talked about how to decide whether to resource SEO, but we didn't talk about how to understand what the expectations are from SEO.
alts.zh: 我覺得我們談了「要不要投資源做 SEO」，但還沒談「對 SEO 的期待該怎麼設定」。

cards.quote: Okay. I know I have to let you go and you have to get back to real work.
cards.zh: 好，我知道我該放你走了，你還有正事要忙。
cards.why: 結束會議的體面說法：把「時間到了」翻譯成「我尊重你的時間」。"let you go" 是母語者收尾的固定用法，台灣人通常只會說 "Time is up"，語感生硬又像在趕人。
swaps: I want to be respectful of your time
I'll give you your time back
Let's not run over — last thing before we close
cards.episode: Humanizing product development | Adriel Frederick (Reddit, Lyft, Facebook)

alts.quote: So let me take us back on track and let's talk about just the high level framework here.
alts.zh: 我們把話題拉回來，來談一下這個框架的高層次架構。

alts.quote: Yeah, we can go deep into this and you can pull me back or ask me to go deeper, whatever. It doesn't matter.
alts.zh: 這題我們可以講得很深，你隨時可以把我拉回來，或叫我再講細一點，都行。

alts.quote: Well, first a pairing, and then one more. The pairing is reset expectations and slow your inbox.
alts.zh: 好，先講一組配套的，再講一個。配套的是：重設期待，還有讓你的收件匣慢下來。

cards.quote: Okay, that's a difficult and different question.
cards.zh: 好，這是個困難、而且性質不太一樣的問題。
cards.why: 被問到棘手問題時，先替問題貼標籤，等於合法地買到三秒鐘思考時間，還順便暗示「答案不會簡單」。比 "Um... let me think" 專業非常多。
swaps: That's a harder question than it looks
That's a fair question, and a tricky one
Let me think about how to answer that properly
cards.episode: Humanizing product development | Adriel Frederick (Reddit, Lyft, Facebook)

alts.quote: That's the problem. I mean, that is the trillion dollar question so I don't really have an answer. I have a couple thoughts on it.
alts.zh: 問題就在這。這是那種價值一兆美元的問題，所以我其實沒有答案，但我有幾點想法。

alts.quote: And this may not be a direct answer to the question, but it didn't really necessarily come from Mark.
alts.zh: 這可能不算直接回答你的問題，不過這件事其實不見得是 Mark 起頭的。

alts.quote: So again, I don't mean to overstate this, and I certainly don't mean to claim that there's some answer that's right for everybody, of course, but surely this is the right kind of question.
alts.zh: 我不想把這件事講得太滿，也絕對不是說有一個答案適用所有人——但這絕對是該問的那類問題。

cards.pattern: The hardest part isn't getting into their shoes — it's taking my own off.
cards.quote: The hardest part of it is they say getting in somebody else's shoes. The hardest part is taking my own shoes off.
cards.zh: 大家都說最難的是站到別人的鞋子裡。其實最難的是先把自己的鞋脫掉。
cards.why: 改寫一個人人都會的老比喻，就是母語者製造記憶點的手法。這句在跨團隊卡關的場合特別好用——它把「同理心」講成一個具體動作，而不是道德要求。
swaps: I have to put my own agenda down first
Before I can hear you, I have to stop arguing in my head
Step one is letting go of what I came in wanting
cards.pmNote: 跨團隊衝突多半不是資訊不對稱，而是雙方都沒放下自己原本要的東西。
cards.episode: Humanizing product development | Adriel Frederick (Reddit, Lyft, Facebook)

alts.quote: Instead of getting mad at Lenny for his really stupid idea or getting mad at Nicole because this was a really bad idea, we can say, "This was problematic. What's wrong here?"
alts.zh: 與其去氣 Lenny 出了個爛點子、或氣 Nicole 這主意很糟，我們可以說：「這裡有問題。是哪裡出錯了？」

alts.quote: Okay, guys, I'm seeing something happen here. Every time we get close to talking about something that's really painful, somebody makes a joke and all the energy disappears.
alts.zh: 好，我看到一個現象。每次我們快要談到真正痛的事情，就會有人開個玩笑，然後所有能量就消失了。

alts.quote: We've all been under Jeff's Eye of Sauron, we know it's miserable. What can we do to help?
alts.zh: 我們都被那道索倫之眼盯過，知道那有多難受。我們能幫上什麼？

cards.quote: Now can I jump in here, please? Because then people are like, "But how do I do this?"
cards.zh: 我可以在這邊插一句嗎？因為接下來大家一定會問：「那我到底該怎麼做？」
cards.why: 插話的黃金結構：請求＋理由。"please" 讓它保持禮貌，"Because..." 立刻交代插話的價值，對方就不會覺得被搶麥。台灣人插話常只有請求沒有理由，於是聽起來像打斷。
swaps: Can I come in on that?
Mind if I jump in here?
Sorry — can I add one thing before we move on?
cards.episode: How to measure AI developer productivity in 2025 | Nicole Forsgren

alts.quote: I'm going to jump in real quick just to highlight what you're talking... what you just said, which I think is extremely important and powerful, and people might kind of move on too quickly.
alts.zh: 我很快插一下，只是想把你剛剛講的那句畫個重點，我覺得那非常重要、非常有力量。

alts.quote: Can I actually jump in real quick because that's a really cool framework that I haven't heard before, this idea of fuel and engine from a marketing perspective.
alts.zh: 我可以插一下嗎？因為這個框架真的很酷，我以前沒聽過——就是行銷上「燃料 vs 引擎」這個想法。

alts.quote: I'm taking us off track, but I want to go a little deeper with this.
alts.zh: 我知道這樣會離題，但我想在這裡多挖一點。

cards.quote: I'm going to jump in real quick just to highlight what you're talking... what you just said, which I think is extremely important and powerful, and people might kind of move on too quickly.
cards.zh: 我很快插一下，只是想把你剛剛講的那句畫個重點，我覺得那非常重要、非常有力量。
cards.why: 最容易被接受的插話理由：不是要反對，是要把對方的話放大。稱讚型插話幾乎零風險，而且能讓你在會議裡累積存在感——對不敢搶話的人來說是最好的第一步。
swaps: Can I underline that for a second?
I want to make sure that doesn't slide by
Let me flag that — it's the key point here
cards.episode: How to measure AI developer productivity in 2025 | Nicole Forsgren

alts.quote: I'm not going to interrupt the flow conversation. I'm just going to summarize in Zoom chat this is what I've heard, and this is what I think we're saying in this conversation.
alts.zh: 我不打斷大家的討論節奏，我直接在 Zoom 聊天室整理一下我聽到的、以及我認為我們在談的東西。

alts.quote: And I'm like, "Time out. What you're going to do is raise prices again. You just told me you 12x-ed the price and nothing observable changed."
alts.zh: 我就說：「等一下。你接下來要做的是再漲一次價。你剛剛才跟我說你把價格拉了十二倍，結果什麼都沒變。」

alts.quote: Real quick on Yahoo because it makes me think about it.
alts.zh: 快速講一下 Yahoo，因為它讓我想到這件事。

cards.quote: Help me understand more what your concerns are. Are your concerns around reliability when you move faster?
cards.zh: 幫我多理解一下你的顧慮是什麼。你擔心的是加快之後穩定性會出問題嗎？
cards.why: 碰到阻力時，最有效的不是反駁而是「請對方教我」。"Help me understand" 把姿態放低，卻同時逼對方把模糊的反對具體化。第二句再給選項，讓不擅表達的人有梯子可下。
swaps: Walk me through what's worrying you
What's the concern underneath that?
Say more — what would make this feel safe?
cards.pmNote: 反對意見多半是模糊的焦慮；把它逼成具體問題，才有辦法設計解法。
cards.episode: How to measure AI developer productivity in 2025 | Nicole Forsgren

alts.quote: I read the email, I'm like, "What do you want me to do? Is this an FYI? Are you saying there's a problem? Do you want me to help?"
alts.zh: 我讀完信心想：「你到底要我做什麼？這是知會嗎？你是在說有問題嗎？還是你要我幫忙？」

alts.quote: Just to make sure I understand what you're saying there, you're saying generally maybe third party tools limit what you can do, which set you up for hardship later.
alts.zh: 我確認一下我有聽懂你的意思：你是說一般來說第三方工具會限制你能做的事，之後會讓你很痛苦。

alts.quote: Just to make sure we understand, when you say judgment, what should people be thinking of when you talk about judgment?
alts.zh: 我們確認一下：你說的 judgment，大家該想到的是什麼？

cards.pattern: What do you mean by this? Are you talking about X? Are you talking about Y?
cards.quote: Okay, what do you mean by this? Are you talking about inner and outer loop? Are you talking about friction?
cards.zh: 好，你指的是什麼意思？你講的是內外迴圈嗎？還是講摩擦成本？
cards.why: 光問 "What do you mean?" 常換到一句更含糊的回答。厲害的是後面連續丟兩三個具體選項——讓對方用「選」的，而不是用「重講一次」的。這對非母語者尤其有效：你不必聽懂全部，只要問對選項。
swaps: When you say X, do you mean A or B?
Which of these are we actually talking about?
Give me the concrete version of that
cards.pmNote: 80% 的專案走偏，起因是主管一句沒被追問的模糊指令。
cards.episode: How to measure AI developer productivity in 2025 | Nicole Forsgren

alts.quote: I got the feedback that I needed to be more strategic. I was like, "Okay, great. What does being more strategic mean?" And nobody could tell me.
alts.zh: 我收到的回饋是「要更有策略性」。我心想：好啊，那「更有策略性」到底是什麼意思？結果沒有人講得出來。

alts.quote: Just for folks that are listening, just to calibrate what size of company you're talking about selling to here.
alts.zh: 為了讓聽的人有個基準——你剛剛講的是賣給多大規模的公司？

alts.quote: And I might even ask them to define what product-led means to them that we can get on the same page of what we're even talking about.
alts.zh: 我甚至會請他們先定義一下「產品驅動成長」對他們來說是什麼意思，這樣我們才知道彼此在講的是不是同一件事。

cards.pattern: They're related concepts that people conflate — so, related but different.
cards.quote: I think they're very related concepts that people sometimes conflate, but I see them as being different. So related, but different.
cards.zh: 我覺得這是常被混用的相關概念，但我把它們看成不同的東西。所以是——相關，但不同。
cards.why: "conflate"（把兩件事混為一談）是台灣人幾乎不用、但會議裡超常出現的動詞。最後那句三字收尾 "related, but different" 示範母語者的節奏感：長句解釋完，用一個極短句釘住。
swaps: People use those interchangeably, but they're not the same thing
Adjacent, not identical
Same neighborhood, different house
cards.pmNote: canonical nomenclature：先把詞定義好再討論，否則整場會都在為同一個詞吵不同的意思。
cards.episode: How to measure AI developer productivity in 2025 | Nicole Forsgren

alts.quote: A lot of people see product market fit as this binary, "I have it or I don't." What you're describing is what I often hear, it's more of this spectrum of more and more confidence.
alts.zh: 很多人把 PMF 看成二元的：不是有就是沒有。而你在描述的，是我常聽到的另一種——它比較像一條逐漸累積信心的光譜。

alts.quote: Please note that don't mix transparency and fairness with being predictable. Those are very different things.
alts.zh: 請注意，不要把「透明與公平」跟「可預測」混為一談。這是兩件很不一樣的事。

alts.quote: At the top of the interview, Lenny, you asked, "What do most people get wrong when they think about this productivity, time management, whatever?" And I'll frame my answer in those terms.
alts.zh: Lenny，你一開始問過：「大家在生產力、時間管理這些事情上最常搞錯什麼？」我就用那個框架來回答。

cards.pattern: I will admit I only have [X] top of mind.
cards.quote: So I will admit I only have the 2019 benchmarks top of mind.
cards.zh: 我得承認，我腦中現在只記得 2019 年那版基準數字。
cards.why: "top of mind"（此刻記得起來的）是漂亮的限縮詞：她沒說「我不知道」，而是精確標示自己資訊的邊界。這是專家承認不足的方式——縮小範圍，而不是否定自己。
swaps: Off the top of my head...
I'd have to check the latest, but as of last I looked...
Don't hold me to the current numbers
cards.episode: How to measure AI developer productivity in 2025 | Nicole Forsgren

alts.quote: So I'm giving some heuristics, I'm giving some benchmarks, but your mileage is going to vary.
alts.zh: 我給的是一些經驗法則、一些對照基準，但你們的狀況一定會不一樣。

alts.quote: I'll admit I'm definitely not an SEO expert. I've been fortunate to work with some of the best marketers in the world who I think are bonafide legends at this point
alts.zh: 我坦白說我絕對不是 SEO 專家。我只是很幸運跟一些世界頂尖的行銷人共事過，那些人到今天都算是真正的傳奇。

alts.quote: I don't know how to do it off the top of my head, but I can go and look at the code or I can have Claude look at the code and combine that with other things to solve new problems.
alts.zh: 我沒辦法直接憑印象講出來，但我可以去看程式碼，或叫 Claude 去看，再結合其他東西來解新問題。

cards.pattern: I can't tell you why. If I were to guess / I would surmise...
cards.quote: In a research paper, we'd have a discussion section, and this is where you get to guess. I would surmise, and we do this in the report, that it's probably because retail went through the retail apocalypse, right.
cards.zh: 我沒辦法告訴你原因。在論文裡這叫討論章節，也就是可以猜的地方。我的推測是——報告裡也是這樣寫的——大概是因為零售業經歷了那場零售末日。
cards.why: 把「知道」與「猜」明確分開，反而讓人更信任你。她甚至先示範分界（這一段是可以猜的），再開始猜。台灣人被問到不確定的事時常含糊帶過，聽起來像在唬；這種明講分界的方式是資深訊號。
swaps: I don't have data on that — but my hypothesis would be...
If I had to guess, and this is a guess...
That's speculation on my part, but...
cards.pmNote: intellectual honesty：把事實、推論、猜測分層說清楚，是資料型工作者最重要的信用來源。
cards.episode: How to measure AI developer productivity in 2025 | Nicole Forsgren

alts.quote: And I guess it's kind of an embarrassing thing to say because everyone who's a startup founder thinks, my startup moves super fast and the talent bar is super high.
alts.zh: 說這話其實有點難為情，因為每個新創創辦人都覺得「我們超快、人才標準超高」。

alts.quote: I don't know how many customer support folks we have, but it's not very many, 30, 40, I'm not sure, way smaller than you would have at any comparable company, and it's because we've automated a lot of our flows.
alts.zh: 我不知道我們有多少客服人力，但沒有很多，三十、四十吧，我不確定，總之比任何同等規模的公司都少很多，因為我們把很多流程自動化了。

alts.quote: My guess is because I'm not a psychologist, I'm not a therapist, that you are modeling something that's happened in your life.
alts.zh: 我猜——因為我不是心理學家、也不是治療師——你其實是在複製你人生中發生過的某個模式。

cards.pattern: The common knowledge was X. Turns out that's not right.
cards.quote: The common knowledge was that you had to have at least a two-week wait for change approvals in order to get that stability. Turns out that's not right. It was just kind of an old wives' tale, right.
cards.zh: 過去大家都認為，變更審核至少要等兩週才能確保穩定。結果那是錯的。那就是個以訛傳訛的老說法。
cards.why: 推翻共識的標準三段式：先複述共識（讓大家點頭）→ 一句短的翻轉（Turns out that's not right）→ 貼標籤（old wives' tale）。攻擊的是「集體迷思」而不是在場任何人，所以沒人需要防衛。
swaps: The received wisdom is X — the data says otherwise
That's the folklore. It doesn't hold up
We all believed that. It turned out not to be true
cards.episode: How to measure AI developer productivity in 2025 | Nicole Forsgren

alts.quote: I really try and stay away from better, because that's really hard to define, and better means something different to everyone.
alts.zh: 我盡量不用「比較好」這個字，因為它很難定義，而且每個人心中的「比較好」都不一樣。

alts.quote: Your belief is that if we add buy now pay later, a lot more people will be able to buy and transact, and so it's going to pay off. Do I have that right?
alts.zh: 你的認定是：只要我們加了先買後付，會有更多人買得下去、成交量會上來，所以這筆投資划得來。我這樣理解對嗎？

alts.quote: Obviously never say never. Sometimes it might work, and if it worked for you, I am so glad. But that's an outlier and don't treat it as a pattern.
alts.zh: 當然，凡事沒有絕對。有時候真的會成功，如果你成功了我真的替你高興。但那是特例，不要把它當成通則。

cards.quote: You know what, I'll say yes and, right.
cards.zh: 這樣說吧，我要用「是，而且」來回答。
cards.why: "yes, and" 來自即興劇，現在是矽谷會議的固定用法：先接受對方的前提，再加上你的補充——實質上是不同意，但語感是共建。台灣人想不到可以用一個「劇場術語」當作反對的外衣。
swaps: Yes — and here's the wrinkle
True, and also...
I'd say both things are true
cards.episode: How to measure AI developer productivity in 2025 | Nicole Forsgren

alts.quote: I know we all release 28 times a day, but the reality is, software still goes on quarterly release cycles no matter what we say
alts.zh: 我知道我們嘴上都說一天出 28 版，但現實是，不管我們怎麼講，軟體對客戶來說還是季度發版。

alts.quote: I don't know that I would look back at what I shipped back then or what we shipped back then, and say they were the best possible solutions or best possible product.
alts.zh: 我不確定我會回頭看當年出的東西，然後說那是最好的解法、最好的產品。

alts.quote: But then inviting people to discuss and say "Yes," or "No, I agree with 90% of that or 10% off."
alts.zh: 然後邀請大家討論，回一句「同意」，或者「不完全，我同意九成，有一成不太一樣」。

cards.quote: One, I hate to be this person, but I'll point to a few of my papers.
cards.zh: 第一，我很不想當那種人，但我還是要推薦一下我自己的幾篇論文。
cards.why: 自我推薦最尷尬的一刻，用 "I hate to be this person" 先自嘲就化解了。這是英文裡處理「自誇焦慮」的通用開關——台灣人多半選擇乾脆不提自己的成果，結果貢獻沒人知道。
swaps: At the risk of being that guy...
Shameless plug, but it's genuinely the best source
Forgive the self-reference —
cards.episode: How to measure AI developer productivity in 2025 | Nicole Forsgren

alts.quote: And I raised my hand and I said, "I'll IC this. I think I know what we need."
alts.zh: 我就舉手說：「這個我自己下去做。我大概知道我們需要什麼。」

alts.quote: So at any given point in time, I probably give myself a B to B-, and sometimes it's a C and sometimes it's a D, and sometimes it's an A, and I'm really plugging away, but it's totally an ongoing challenge.
alts.zh: 任何時間點上，我大概給自己 B 到 B-，有時候 C、有時候 D，偶爾也有 A，我真的一直在努力，但這就是個持續的挑戰。

alts.quote: Conversion rates go from 60% to 90% over the course of a few weeks of just optimizing that and putting more content there.
alts.zh: 轉換率會在幾週內從 60% 上到 90%，就只是把那塊優化一下、多放點內容進去。

cards.quote: I know we'll talk more about this, but let me go back to the question I was going to ask...
cards.zh: 我知道這個我們等下會再聊，不過讓我先回到我原本要問的問題。
cards.why: 回到議程的乾淨句型：前半句先安撫（這題沒被丟掉），後半句才拉回。少了前半句就會像在打斷；有了前半句，對方會覺得你在幫忙管時間。
swaps: Let's come back to that — first, the question I parked
Holding that thought, back to where we were
We'll return to this. To finish the earlier point...
cards.episode: How to measure AI developer productivity in 2025 | Nicole Forsgren

alts.quote: So let me take us back on track and let's talk about just the high level framework here.
alts.zh: 我們把話題拉回來，來談一下這個框架的高層次架構。

alts.quote: "I need 20 minutes of focused time to interrogate something that I've done. We're not going to talk. I'm literally going to force us into a room or Zoom.
alts.zh: 「我需要二十分鐘的專注時間來拷問我做的東西。我們不用講話。我就是要把大家關進一個會議室或 Zoom。」

alts.quote: Yeah, we can go deep into this and you can pull me back or ask me to go deeper, whatever. It doesn't matter.
alts.zh: 這題我們可以講得很深，你隨時可以把我拉回來，或叫我再講細一點，都行。

cards.pattern: This is a great segue to something I was going to get to later — let's just get into it.
cards.quote: This is a great segue too, something I was going to get to a little bit later, but let's just get into it, which is the DORA framework...
cards.zh: 這剛好可以順下去——我本來排在比較後面，不過我們直接進去談吧，就是 DORA 框架。
cards.why: 議程可以往前調，但要說出來。這句把「我臨時改順序」講成「你的話剛好接得上」，等於把主導權的行使包裝成順水推舟——主持會議時最實用的一種面子工程。
swaps: You've teed up my next question perfectly
That's a natural bridge to...
Let's jump ahead in the agenda since we're here
cards.episode: How to measure AI developer productivity in 2025 | Nicole Forsgren

alts.quote: "I need 20 minutes of focused time to interrogate something that I've done. We're not going to talk. I'm literally going to force us into a room or Zoom.
alts.zh: 「我需要二十分鐘的專注時間來拷問我做的東西。我們不用講話。我就是要把大家關進一個會議室或 Zoom。」

alts.quote: he'll sit in a review and be like, "I don't think this is right." And then he'll pause and say, "I'm going to clear the rest of my day. Let's sit and figure it out."
alts.zh: 他會在評審會上說：「我覺得這不對。」然後停一下說：「我把今天剩下的行程清掉，我們一起坐下來把它弄清楚。」

alts.quote: So let me take us back on track and let's talk about just the high level framework here.
alts.zh: 我們把話題拉回來，來談一下這個框架的高層次架構。

cards.quote: You can't fund everything. You don't get to pick everything.
cards.zh: 你沒辦法什麼都投資。你也沒有權利什麼都選。
cards.why: 兩個短句、平行結構、沒有任何緩衝——擋需求時偶爾就是需要這種硬度。注意她用的是 "you"（泛指所有人），所以聽起來像原則，不像針對某個人。
swaps: If we fund everything, everything fails
Saying yes to this means saying no to that
We don't have the capacity to bet on all of it
cards.pmNote: 策略的本質是取捨：全部都做＝全部都做不好。
cards.episode: How to measure AI developer productivity in 2025 | Nicole Forsgren

alts.quote: So if you can't answer the question about what is it that someone's going to do a search on, then don't do SEO, because SEO is about appealing to that user.
alts.zh: 所以如果你答不出「別人會搜什麼」這個問題，那就不要做 SEO——因為 SEO 就是在對那個使用者說話。

alts.quote: let's say somebody commenting about your business, who does not understand the nuance of it, you can't be reacting to everything.
alts.zh: 假設有人在評論你的生意，但他根本不懂裡面的細節——你不可能每件事都去回應。

alts.quote: We are about to launch something and then for example I or someone else goes to look at it and sees, "Oh, this doesn't feel right and we should fix it so I don't think we should launch this now."
alts.zh: 我們正要上線，然後我或別人去看了一眼，就會說：「這感覺不對，應該修一下，我覺得現在還不能上。」

cards.pattern: This is where I'm data informed, not data driven.
cards.quote: Now this is where I'm data informed, and I'm not data driven.
cards.zh: 這就是我所謂的「被數據啟發」，而不是「被數據驅動」。
cards.why: 一組字的差別（informed vs driven）就劃出立場，而且不必否定數據的價值。當你要在數字之外做判斷、又不想被說「憑感覺」時，這句是最省力的辯護。
swaps: The data has a vote, not a veto
I let the numbers inform the call, not make it
Data in one hand, judgment in the other
cards.pmNote: 數據給你一個選項清單（class of options），最後那一步還是人的判斷。
cards.episode: How to measure AI developer productivity in 2025 | Nicole Forsgren

alts.quote: I now use, I'm an investor, so I'm biased, but Aura, A-U-R-A, which is a marketplace app.
alts.zh: 我現在用的是——我有投資，所以我立場不中立——Aura，A-U-R-A，一個市集型的 app。

alts.quote: The true test of whether the positioning's working is, if I'm sitting across from a qualified prospect and I tell the story, does the prospect get excited and want to buy something?
alts.zh: 定位有沒有效，真正的檢驗是：我坐在一個合格的潛在客戶對面把故事講完，他會不會眼睛一亮、想買東西？

alts.quote: Data is more like a compass than a GPS. If you look at data as a way of giving you the answer, you're always wrong. Wrong or slow, or sometimes both.
alts.zh: 數據比較像指南針，不是導航。如果你把數據當成會給你答案的東西，你不是錯就是慢，有時候兩者都有。

cards.pattern: Instead of getting mad at [person], we can say: this was problematic — what's wrong here?
cards.quote: Instead of getting mad at Lenny for his really stupid idea or getting mad at Nicole because this was a really bad idea, we can say, "This was problematic. What's wrong here?"
cards.zh: 與其去氣 Lenny 出了個爛點子、或氣 Nicole 這主意很糟，我們可以說：「這裡有問題。是哪裡出錯了？」
cards.why: 對事不對人的具體操作法：把爭論的對象從「人的名字」搬到「框裡的東西」。她甚至拿自己當反例（getting mad at Nicole），主動把自己放進可被批評的位置，房間的防衛心就降下來了。
swaps: Let's put the problem on the whiteboard, not on a person
The idea failed, not the person
What broke here — not who broke it
cards.pmNote: 把假設寫成外部化的框（四宮格、假設卡），失敗時就能檢討框而不是檢討人。
cards.episode: How to measure AI developer productivity in 2025 | Nicole Forsgren

alts.quote: The hardest part of it is they say getting in somebody else's shoes. The hardest part is taking my own shoes off.
alts.zh: 大家都說最難的是站到別人的鞋子裡。其實最難的是先把自己的鞋脫掉。

alts.quote: The rule with the Waterline Model, which is very memorable, is you snorkel before you scuba. So, 80% of problems on teams actually happen because of structural issues or dynamics issues.
alts.zh: 這個模型的規則很好記：先浮潛，再深潛。團隊上八成的問題其實出在結構或運作方式，不是出在人。

alts.quote: We've all been under Jeff's Eye of Sauron, we know it's miserable. What can we do to help?
alts.zh: 我們都被那道索倫之眼盯過，知道那有多難受。我們能幫上什麼？

cards.quote: And if you're on different pages, you're heading in completely different directions.
cards.zh: 如果大家不在同一頁上，那就是往完全不同的方向前進。
cards.why: 一句話講完「沒對齊的代價」，而且是可以直接搬去說服老闆開對齊會議的說法。"on the same page / on different pages" 是英文職場最高頻的對齊隱喻，台灣人聽得懂卻很少主動用。
swaps: We're solving two different problems right now
We're not aligned on what 'done' means
Let's make sure we're pointed at the same thing
cards.pmNote: 對齊做在前面是幾小時，做在後面是幾個月的返工。
cards.episode: How to measure AI developer productivity in 2025 | Nicole Forsgren

alts.quote: "Where can I learn what I need to learn about this project?" I ask five different people, get five different answers. That is unacceptable.
alts.zh: 我要去哪裡搞懂這個專案？我問五個人，得到五種答案。這是不能接受的。

alts.quote: The way I would say it is, say you're going to do the thing, say that you're doing the thing, and then say that you did it.
alts.zh: 我的講法是：先說你要做這件事，做的過程中說你在做，做完再說你做完了。

alts.quote: Or if the meeting is not under the context of buying it all, it's like, "We're working on something cool. We have a great vision. It aligns with what you're doing. Maybe there's a partnership here."
alts.zh: 或者那場會根本不是在談收購，而是：「我們在做一件很酷的事，我們有很好的願景，跟你們在做的方向對得上。也許這裡有合作的空間。」

cards.pattern: I'm not saying that's the thing that made it happen, but I will say [後續發生的事實]
cards.quote: And I'm not saying that's the thing that made it happen, but I will say very quickly after that, we became very close partners and ultimately they acquired me.
cards.zh: 我不是說就是因為這件事才成的，但我可以說，那之後我們很快就變成很緊密的夥伴，最後他們把我們買下來了。
cards.why: 把「因果」降級成「時序」——先主動放棄過度歸功（I'm not saying that's the thing that made it happen），再用 but I will say 把事實原封不動放上桌。結果是聽者自己去連因果，你既拿到功勞又完全沒有吹牛的姿態。這是英語職場「講成績」最高階的一招。
swaps: I won't claim that caused it, but the timeline speaks for itself
I can't prove the two are connected, but what I can tell you is...
cards.pmNote: 談 impact 時，只要你講的是 correlation 而非 causation，就該用這種降級句型——否則被追問「你怎麼證明」會很難看。
cards.episode: Bending the universe in your favor | Claire Vo (LaunchDarkly, Color, Optimizely, ChatPRD)

alts.quote: But probably the stat I'm most proud of, and the hardest thing to make happen out of all of that was we acquired 70% of the users that found out about Wise last month through word of mouth.
alts.zh: 大概是我最自豪、也最難做到的一個數字：上個月知道 Wise 的使用者裡，有 70% 是靠口碑來的。

alts.quote: Well, first of all, thank you for saying all that. That's giving me too much credit, but I like the idea that it's going to balance out the too little credit I ostensibly get somewhere else, that's great.
alts.zh: 首先謝謝你這樣說。你太抬舉我了——不過我喜歡這個說法，就當作是補回我在別的地方被低估的部分吧。

alts.quote: Yeah, this is not something I'd ever say about myself. It's nice that someone else would say it, but it's a mysterious thing.
alts.zh: 這種話我自己絕對講不出口。有別人這樣說當然開心，不過這東西其實挺玄的。

cards.pattern: The short of it is [三個關鍵字]. And the longer version is that...
cards.quote: The short of it is, it was a promise to myself, and COVID, and Uber doing layoffs. And the longer version is that, when I joined Uber, before Uber I was...
cards.zh: 簡單講，就是我對自己的一個承諾、COVID，還有 Uber 裁員這三件事。比較長的版本是，我剛進 Uber 之前……
cards.why: 先給一個「三個名詞」的壓縮版答案，再自己開權限講長版。對聽者是禮貌（你隨時可以喊停），對講者是保險（就算被打斷，重點已經送出去了）。台灣人面試最常見的死法就是直接進入長版、講到一半被打斷，結論還沒出來。
swaps: The short answer is X. The longer answer is...
Short version: X. Want the long version?
cards.pmNote: 這是 BLUF（bottom line up front）的口語版；PM 對高層報告一律先給 short of it。
cards.episode: Leaving big tech to build the #1 technology newsletter | Gergely Orosz (The Pragmatic Engineer)

alts.quote: So I gave myself this rule where I had to go out once a week for a couple of months, go to an external event, and I would count out 10 business cards.
alts.zh: 所以我給自己訂了一條規則：連續幾個月每週出去一次，去參加外部活動，然後數出十張名片。

alts.quote: I like to ask people to tell me about something they're really proud of that they accomplished and take me through the process and talk to me about why they're proud of it.
alts.zh: 我喜歡請對方講一件他真的很自豪的成就，帶我走過整個過程，並告訴我為什麼他覺得自豪。

alts.quote: When you walk into a room as a product manager, engineers, designers, researchers go to market. Nobody owes you anything. It's very similar skillset, just different domain expertise.
alts.zh: 你以 PM 身分走進一個房間，工程師、設計師、研究員、GTM——沒有人欠你什麼。技能其實一模一樣，差別只在領域知識。

cards.pattern: I picked you because [具體理由]. Do you mind spending a couple of minutes and just giving me some thoughts on this?
cards.quote: I picked you because I really trust you to be a sound source of truthful advice and give me some feedback. So I really value that. Do you mind spending a couple of minutes and just giving me some thoughts on this?
cards.zh: 我會找你，是因為我真的很信任你會給我誠實的建議跟回饋，這對我很有價值。可以請你花個幾分鐘，給我一點想法嗎？
cards.why: 三段結構：說明為什麼是你（不是群發）→ 講出你重視的價值 → 把 ask 縮到「a couple of minutes / some thoughts」這種心理成本極低的量詞。台灣人請教常犯的錯是問題很大、理由很空，對方讀完不知道要回什麼。
swaps: I'm reaching out to you specifically because...
Would you be up for giving me your quick take on this?
cards.pmNote: Ada 稱這套流程為 curiosity loop：好問題＋精選對象＋輕量 ask＋事後回報結果。
cards.episode: How to make better decisions and build a joyful career | Ada Chen Rekhi (Notejoy, LinkedIn, SurveyMonkey)

alts.quote: My uncle and aunt were coming in, and they're encouraging me, "This is all up to you, but try not to lose it all on night number one," which was good advice to give me.
alts.zh: 我叔叔阿姨要來，他們鼓勵我說：「這都是你自己決定，不過盡量不要第一晚就全輸光。」後來覺得這建議給得很好。

alts.quote: So first of all, when you're in the early innings, you'll actually get more useful advice often from your peers because they're going through the same thing.
alts.zh: 首先，在很前期的階段，你從同輩那裡拿到的建議其實比較有用，因為他們正在經歷一模一樣的事。

alts.quote: And don't ask them, "Should I do it?" Ask them, "Tell me for each thing, can you give me the pros and cons of doing it?"
alts.zh: 不要問他們「我該不該做？」要問他們「每一個做法的利弊分別是什麼？」

cards.pattern: I love what I'm doing here, and I would also like to [想要的]. And here's what I'm interested in.
cards.quote: It might actually mean a proactive conversation with your manager or the leadership to say, "I love what I'm doing here, and I would also like to learn a little bit more. And here's what I'm interested in."
cards.zh: 這可能只是主動找主管或高層談一次，跟他說：「我很喜歡現在做的事，同時我也想再多學一些，這是我有興趣的方向。」
cards.why: 關鍵在 and，不是 but。「I love X, but I want Y」會被聽成抱怨，「I love X, and I would also like Y」是把新需求疊加在肯定之上。結尾再用 here's what I'm interested in 把球做給對方——你不是丟問題，你是丟一份可執行的清單。
swaps: I'm happy where I am, and I'd love to stretch into...
This is working well for me — and here's where I'd like to grow next
cards.pmNote: 要成長機會前先確認自己現在的產出無可挑剔；否則這句會被讀成「本份沒做好還想挑工作」。
cards.episode: How to make better decisions and build a joyful career | Ada Chen Rekhi (Notejoy, LinkedIn, SurveyMonkey)

alts.quote: Hey, I'm an early stage startup. We have a lot to learn. Can we kind of gain your insight into how this problem is manifesting on your side?
alts.zh: 嗨，我們是很早期的新創，還有很多要學。能不能請教你，這個問題在你們那邊是怎麼呈現的？

alts.quote: Hey, I'm really enjoying working with you. I'm wondering is there some way I could help you that would also help me reach my goal?
alts.zh: 嘿，跟你合作我覺得很愉快。我在想，有沒有什麼事我可以幫你、同時也能幫我朝目標前進的？

alts.quote: If they had reached out to me and said, "I know you don't know me. I have this small software company. I'm not well-connected, but I would love your advice on how to grow this business and what you would do if you were in my shoes,"
alts.zh: 如果他們寫信說：「我知道你不認識我。我有間小軟體公司，我人脈也不廣，但我很想聽聽你對怎麼把它做大的建議——如果你是我會怎麼做？」

cards.pattern: I wouldn't have gotten [成果] if I had just [被動的預設路徑]
cards.quote: It was just such a rare opportunity, but I wouldn't have gotten those opportunities if I just let them promote me or I followed a strategy where I was just focused on trying to get the biggest title.
cards.zh: 那真的是很難得的機會，但如果我當初只是讓他們幫我升職、或只想著拿最大的頭銜，我根本拿不到那些機會。
cards.why: 用「反事實」（counterfactual）講成績：不說「我很厲害所以拿到 X」，而說「如果我沒有做那個選擇，我就拿不到 X」。功勞落在你的判斷力上，聽起來像在分析而不是在誇耀。這是亞裔講者最好用的一招。
swaps: None of that would have happened if I'd taken the default path
That only came about because I deliberately chose not to...
cards.pmNote: 面試的 STAR 裡，Action 最有說服力的講法就是講「你放棄了什麼預設選項」。
cards.episode: How to make better decisions and build a joyful career | Ada Chen Rekhi (Notejoy, LinkedIn, SurveyMonkey)

alts.quote: Beyond those cosmetics, the biggest thing I see particularly at higher levels is people talk about what they have done but not why it mattered.
alts.zh: 撇開那些表面功夫，我在比較資深的層級看到最大的問題是：大家只講自己做了什麼，不講那件事為什麼重要。

alts.quote: I was going to start by saying, I've been wrong about tons of things, but I buried those out back behind the shed.
alts.zh: 我本來想說，我看走眼的次數多到數不清啦，只是那些我都埋在後院工具間後面了。

alts.quote: We hadn't even gotten there and the trial-to-paid conversion rate increased 40%, and we didn't touch it.
alts.zh: 我們根本還沒做到那一步，試用轉付費的轉換率就漲了 40%，而且我們完全沒動它。

cards.pattern: I'm here to [你真正的目的]，even if it costs [別人以為你要的東西]
cards.quote: I even told my manager this when I first came in, "I'm here to learn to be a better founder." So if I can make my LinkedIn experiences match to that, that would be a huge win for me independent of promotion, or compensation.
cards.zh: 我一進去就跟我主管講了：「我來這裡是為了學會怎麼當一個更好的創辦人。」所以只要 LinkedIn 的經歷能配上這個目標，對我就是大勝利，跟升職或薪水無關。
cards.why: independent of promotion, or compensation 這半句是全句的重量所在——你先放棄了對方最容易拿來跟你交換的籌碼，反而讓你的請求變得可信、也讓主管不需要防你。「a huge win for me」則把個人目標翻譯成對方聽得懂的成敗語言。
swaps: I'm optimizing for learning here, not title
What I want out of this role is X — the promotion piece is secondary
cards.pmNote: 跟主管講清楚你要什麼，主管才有辦法把對的專案給你；沒講的人只會拿到剩下的專案。
cards.episode: How to make better decisions and build a joyful career | Ada Chen Rekhi (Notejoy, LinkedIn, SurveyMonkey)

alts.quote: As head of fan monetization, I have a team of folks who are really passionate about figuring out new ways to help artists and fans connect and also figure out ways to make those connections result in new monetization opportunities for the artists.
alts.zh: 我的職稱是 head of fan monetization，我帶一群很熱衷於「幫藝人跟粉絲建立連結」的人，同時想辦法把這些連結變成藝人新的收入來源。

alts.quote: I'm potentially world-class at this other thing. Let me see what it feels like to double down on this area."
alts.zh: 比較好的說法是：「那些事我做得還行。但這件事我可能可以做到世界級。那就往這邊押吧。」

alts.quote: I'll be honest, I didn't really enjoy being a manager of managers. It felt a bit too abstract. I didn't like being in the meetings, not doing the work.
alts.zh: 老實說，我沒有很喜歡當「管理主管的主管」。感覺有點太抽象了。我不喜歡一直在開會、卻沒有真的在做事。

cards.pattern: I respect you so much as [角色]. I want to tell you that [我這一端的觀察落差]
cards.quote: I shared a lot of my impressions with her and I told her, "I respect you so much as an operator. I want to tell you that in the physical meeting that we had together, there was this disparity on how I would've potentially perceived you."
cards.zh: 我把我的印象跟她說了：「我非常尊敬你作為一個經營者的能力。我想跟你講，我們那次實體見面時，我對你的印象跟我原本認識的你有落差。」
cards.why: 整句都掛在「我」上：my impressions、how I would've perceived you。沒有一句是「你錯了」，全部是「我這一端看到什麼」，對方沒有東西可以反駁、也不必防衛。disparity（落差）比 problem 更中性，把事實留給對方自己去解讀。
swaps: I want to name something I noticed, and it's just my read
There's a gap between how I know you and how you came across that day
cards.pmNote: radical candor 的操作定義：先證明你在乎（care personally），才有資格直接挑戰（challenge directly）。
cards.episode: How to make better decisions and build a joyful career | Ada Chen Rekhi (Notejoy, LinkedIn, SurveyMonkey)

alts.quote: I said, "The way you are operating is not meeting our leadership expectations. If you do not change, you cannot be part of this organization anymore. I believe you can operate differently."
alts.zh: 我跟他們說：「你們現在的做事方式沒有達到我們對領導者的期待。如果不改變，你們就不能繼續留在這個組織。我相信你們有能力用不同的方式做事。」

alts.quote: So you have engineers now who are working on optimizing short form videos for higher engagement, and you sort of want to say to them like, "Hey, are you thinking about what this is doing to the brains of young children?"
alts.zh: 現在有一群工程師在優化短影音的互動率，你會有點想跟他們說：「欸，你有想過這對小朋友的腦袋在做什麼嗎？」

alts.quote: Of course, I don't want to be cruel to the people who are putting their hearts into that work, because the Figma file is beautiful. It's just coming a little early.
alts.zh: 當然，我不想對那些真心投入的人太苛刻——那些 Figma 檔真的很漂亮。只是它來得太早了一點。

cards.quote: Her reaction was like, "Oh my God, Ada. No one has ever connected the dots for me. Thank you so much."
cards.zh: 她的反應是：「天啊 Ada，從來沒有人幫我把這些點連起來。真的太謝謝你了。」
cards.why: 接難聽回饋的高分答案。connect the dots 把對方定位成「幫我補上了缺的那條線」，而不是「指出我的缺點」——你不但沒有防衛，還把這次回饋重新定義成一份禮物。往後對方會更願意告訴你真話。
swaps: That's the first time anyone's put it that way — thank you
I really appreciate you saying the hard thing
cards.pmNote: 回饋的供給量取決於你上一次怎麼接。接得好，別人下次才敢講。
cards.episode: How to make better decisions and build a joyful career | Ada Chen Rekhi (Notejoy, LinkedIn, SurveyMonkey)

alts.quote: I'm like, "Oh, cool. Tell me what I'm missing."
alts.zh: 我會說：「好啊，跟我說我漏掉了什麼。」

alts.quote: I asked her once, I said, "I noticed that you never answer questions when we do these presentations."
alts.zh: 我有一次問她：「我注意到，我們在做這些簡報的時候，你從來不回答問題。」

alts.quote: Yes, you wrote the bug, but that's not on you. The system failed you.
alts.zh: 對，那個 bug 是你寫的，但這不算在你頭上。是制度沒接住你。

cards.pattern: If you had asked me [某個時間點], it would've been [當時的答案]. Now, I have a couple asterisks on top of it.
cards.quote: If you had asked me when I first started the company, it would've been an enthusiastic hell yes. I totally recommend. Now, I have a couple asterisks on top of it.
cards.zh: 如果你在我剛創業的時候問我，答案會是超級肯定的「絕對推薦」。現在的話，我會加上幾個但書。
cards.why: 改變立場的標準句型：先誠實還原舊立場（而且講得很生動：enthusiastic hell yes），再用 asterisks（星號、但書）這個視覺化的名詞承接。asterisk 比 but 高明得多——它暗示主結論還在，只是要看註腳，不是自打嘴巴。
swaps: A year ago I'd have said X without hesitating. These days I'd caveat that
My answer used to be a flat yes — now it comes with conditions
cards.pmNote: strong opinions, loosely held：更新立場時保留舊立場的合理性，別假裝自己一直都是對的。
cards.episode: How to make better decisions and build a joyful career | Ada Chen Rekhi (Notejoy, LinkedIn, SurveyMonkey)

alts.quote: And at first I gave the smart-ass answer, "I don't care what they say, I care what they do." But I started finding that my experiments were so much better the more I talked to customers.
alts.zh: 一開始我回了一句欠揍的話：「我不在乎他們說什麼，我在乎他們做什麼。」但後來我發現，我越常跟客戶聊，實驗設計就越好。

alts.quote: Fast-forward to the middle of 2023, everything looks like it's going to be a transformer. So now our hypotheses are just wrong.
alts.zh: 快轉到 2023 年中，看起來全部都會走向 transformer。所以我們原本的假設就是錯的。

alts.quote: But I no longer have to provide the first-round feedback I once did, since the draft has already undergone several rounds of what are essentially my suggestions before I even touch it.
alts.zh: 但我已經不必再給以前那種第一輪回饋了，因為草稿在我碰到之前，已經跑過好幾輪等同我意見的修改。

cards.pattern: Roll it forward six months — what have you accomplished?
cards.quote: I ask them, "What are your goals when it comes to coaching? Roll it forward six months, what have you gotten done in your coaching experience."
cards.zh: 我會問他們：「你找教練的目標是什麼？把時間快轉六個月，那時候你在教練這件事上完成了什麼？」
cards.why: roll it forward 是教練式提問的萬用開關：把對方從「我現在很卡」的情緒狀態，硬拉到未來的完成式，逼出可驗收的具體成果。動詞用 gotten done 而不是 want——want 會拿到願望，done 才會拿到標準。
swaps: Fast-forward six months — what does good look like?
