alts.quote: So there's, I wouldn't say a checklist, but there's a series of questions that I asked to diagnose why is growth slowing in this order, because it's one of these things where the first one that's a problem, if you don't fix that, it doesn't matter if you fix one of the ones below.
alts.zh: 我不會說那是一張檢查清單，但我確實有一組問題，會照順序問下去診斷成長為什麼變慢——因為只要最前面那個沒修，後面修再多都沒用。

alts.quote: I think most people don't like product managers often because they haven't experienced good product managers.
alts.zh: 我覺得多數人不喜歡 PM，多半是因為他們沒遇過真正好的 PM。

alts.quote: And so I think a lot of it comes down to not the things you try, but how you deeply understand the problem that's preventing someone from using your product effectively.
alts.zh: 所以我覺得關鍵不在你試了哪些招，而在你有多深地搞懂「是什麼擋住使用者用好你的產品」。

cards.pattern: It's kind of like [比喻]. And if you go and take [別人的做法] and stick it in [你這裡], it's probably not going to look very matched.
cards.quote: And it's kind of building a house that you want every brick in the house to match. And if you go and try and take some bricks from someone else's house and stick it in your house, it's probably going to not look very matched.
cards.zh: 這有點像蓋房子，你會希望每一塊磚都是搭的。如果你跑去人家家裡搬幾塊磚塞進自己家，看起來大概就是不搭。
cards.why: 反對「照抄大公司做法」卻完全沒有點名任何人，也沒有說 that won't work——只描述一個誰都看得出來不對勁的畫面，再用 probably 和 not very matched 收尾。要在會議上擋掉別人帶進來的舊公司 playbook，這是殺傷力最低、成功率最高的講法。
swaps: Borrowed practices tend not to match the rest of the house.
That worked there because of everything else that was true there.
cards.pmNote: 引進外部流程前先問：我們是不是也要引進讓它成立的那些前提？
cards.episode: The woman behind Canva shares how she built a $42B company from nothing | Melanie Perkins

alts.quote: So this might mean that I think... I don't want to say that if you don't have experience, don't start one, but it's kind of true. So become an expert somewhere, somehow, before you start.
alts.zh: 我不想說「沒經驗就別開始」這種話……但其實有點是真的。所以動手前，先想辦法在某個地方變成專家。

alts.quote: And I know this is going to trigger some people, but the truth is they don't want to work.
alts.zh: 我知道這句會讓一些人不爽，但事實就是——他們不想做事。

alts.quote: We're very interested in folks who have already been thinking about what the future should look like with agents. And we don't have to agree on where we're going, but we want people who are very passionate.
alts.zh: 我們很想找那種已經在思考「agent 的未來該長什麼樣」的人。方向上我們不一定要有共識，但我們要真的在乎這件事的人。

cards.pattern: Often people have [使命] kind of on the wall somewhere, and then what they're actually doing and the way they actually spend their time is in a very different direction.
cards.quote: Often people have a mission that's kind of on the wall somewhere and then what they're actually doing and the way they actually make money and the way people actually spend their time is in a very, very different direction from that original mission.
cards.zh: 很多公司的使命就掛在牆上某個地方，可是他們真正在做的事、真正賺錢的方式、大家真正把時間花在哪，跟那個使命的方向差超多。
cards.why: 三個 actually 連發（actually doing / actually make money / actually spend their time），一次把「說的」和「做的」拉開對照。actually 在英文口語裡就是揭穿的訊號詞，用它比用 but 或 however 更不像指控、卻更有力。
swaps: The mission is on the wall; the roadmap says something else.
What we say we're about and where the time actually goes are two different things.
cards.pmNote: 檢查策略是否真實：看時間與預算的流向，不要看願景頁。
cards.episode: The woman behind Canva shares how she built a $42B company from nothing | Melanie Perkins

alts.quote: People and teams don't really reach... They don't actually reach their goals. They fall to the level of their systems.
alts.zh: 人跟團隊其實不會「達成」目標。他們會掉到自己系統的水準。

alts.quote: And then just the nature of the future is like we just don't know all the answers and that's okay. And then the right way to deal with that is to run as many experiments as possible.
alts.zh: 未來的本質就是我們不會知道所有答案，這沒關係。面對這件事正確的做法，是盡可能多跑一些實驗。

alts.quote: I think so many folks don't know where to begin on starting a startup, and my tactical advice is start doing customer validation first versus building a PowerPoint deck.
alts.zh: 很多人根本不知道創業要從哪裡開始，我很具體的建議是：先去做客戶驗證，而不是先做一份簡報。

cards.pattern: Just because [X] is all the rage and [某群人] really like it doesn't necessarily mean it should be front and center.
cards.quote: Just because AI is all the rage and investors really like AI doesn't necessarily mean it should be front and center
cards.zh: AI 現在很紅、投資人也很愛，但這不代表它就該擺在最前面。
cards.why: Just because A doesn't mean B 是英文最好用的拆假設句型：先大方承認 A 是真的（不跟人吵事實），只否定那個沒人講出口的推論。加上 necessarily 又再軟一層，聽起來像在提醒而不是打臉。
swaps: Just because everyone's doing it doesn't mean it's right for us.
That it's popular doesn't automatically make it a priority.
cards.pmNote: 熱門技術要進 roadmap，判準是「有沒有幫使用者把事情做完」，不是「投資人愛不愛聽」。
cards.episode: The woman behind Canva shares how she built a $42B company from nothing | Melanie Perkins

alts.quote: Just because somebody can use your product doesn't mean that they will buy it. Just because they can use it doesn't mean they will choose it.
alts.zh: 會用你的產品，不代表他會買。會用，也不代表他會選你。

alts.quote: I don't like the word sprint because how do you feel after a sprint? Exhausted.
alts.zh: 我不喜歡「衝刺」這個詞——你衝刺完是什麼感覺？累爆。

alts.quote: Exactly. Did they succeed because of that or in spite of that?
alts.zh: 沒錯。他們成功是「因為」那個做法，還是「儘管」有那個做法？

cards.pattern: One of the most important things we did was we didn't really worry about [對手] at all. We just asked where is there a gap that we can uniquely fill.
cards.quote: One of the most important things that we did was we didn't really worry about competitors at all. We actually just saw where is there a gap in the market that we can uniquely fill
cards.zh: 我們做過最重要的一件事，就是根本不太管競爭對手。我們只看市場上哪裡有一個缺口，是我們可以獨一無二補上的。
cards.why: 先講「我們刻意不做什麼」再講「我們只做什麼」，一放一收就把策略講完了。uniquely fill 的 uniquely 是重點，它把 gap 從「沒人做的事」升級成「只有我們能做的事」——少了這個字，整句就變成單純的市場空白論。
swaps: We spent almost no time on competitors and all of it on the gap.
The question wasn't who else is here, it was what only we can do.
cards.pmNote: 競品分析容易變成 feature 對照表；真正該產出的是「我們獨有的缺口」。
cards.episode: The woman behind Canva shares how she built a $42B company from nothing | Melanie Perkins

alts.quote: We should probably not do things that would've been invented by everybody else 10 minutes later. Where are the problems that are not solving themselves?
alts.zh: 我們大概不該去做那些晚十分鐘別人也會做出來的東西。真正該問的是：哪些問題是不會自己被解決的？

alts.quote: I think so many folks don't know where to begin on starting a startup, and my tactical advice is start doing customer validation first versus building a PowerPoint deck.
alts.zh: 很多人根本不知道創業要從哪裡開始，我很具體的建議是：先去做客戶驗證，而不是先做一份簡報。

alts.quote: The point is not about picking, just picking one, but it's about executing the one that you actually pick.
alts.zh: 重點不是「選哪一個」，而是你選了之後有沒有真的執行到底。

cards.pattern: We're literally smack bang in the middle of that Venn diagram of [A] and [B], rather than making our customers have to make a choice between those two.
cards.quote: And what Canva really does is we're literally smack bang in the middle of that Venn diagram of creativity and productivity, rather than making our customers have to make a choice between those two suites.
cards.zh: Canva 真正在做的事，就是不偏不倚站在「創意」跟「生產力」這兩個圈的交集正中央，而不是逼客戶在兩邊二選一。
cards.why: 定位一句話講完：座標（Venn diagram 的交集）＋ 敵人（逼客戶二選一）。rather than 後面接的不是競品名字，而是客戶的痛，所以聽起來是在幫客戶說話而不是在自誇。smack bang in the middle 是很口語的加強語，可換成 right in the middle。
swaps: We sit right at the intersection of A and B.
Instead of asking people to pick a side, we cover both.
cards.pmNote: positioning 的黃金句型：先給座標，再給你替使用者消除的那個選擇題。
cards.episode: The woman behind Canva shares how she built a $42B company from nothing | Melanie Perkins

alts.quote: Incremental feels very safe. But that is not the reason why we're going to win. That's almost table stakes.
alts.zh: 有個很微妙的張力：漸進式改動感覺很安全，多加一顆按鈕嘛。但那不是我們會贏的原因，那幾乎只是入場資格。

alts.quote: When we talk about pricing strategies, we hear many buzzwords, and it's irrelevant. So when we take a step back and look at it, there's literally only three types of pricing strategies.
alts.zh: 談定價策略的時候會聽到一堆流行詞，那些都不重要。退一步看，定價策略其實就只有三種。

alts.quote: There's a saying that Mike and Kevin had at Instagram which is we may not be right, but at least we're not confused.
alts.zh: Instagram 的 Mike 跟 Kevin 有一句話：我們不見得是對的，但至少我們不是一團混亂。

cards.pattern: You fast-forward [50 年] and you say: Are we in a safer world? Is this the [X] that we want?
cards.quote: Are we in a safer world? Is the world the place that we want our kids to grow up in? Is this the humanity that we want?
cards.zh: 我們有活在一個更安全的世界嗎？這是我們想讓小孩長大的世界嗎？這是我們要的人類文明嗎？
cards.why: 三個平行問句、一句比一句大（safer → our kids → humanity），完全不下結論。願景講到最後不給答案而給問句，聽者才會自己回答「不是」——那個「不是」由他們自己講出來，說服力才夠。
swaps: Fast-forward five years — is this the product we'd be proud of?
Is this the team we want to be in three years' time?
cards.pmNote: long-term vision 的檢查點：把時間軸拉遠到現有 KPI 全部失效，剩下的才是真的方向。
cards.episode: The woman behind Canva shares how she built a $42B company from nothing | Melanie Perkins

alts.quote: You want your product to live in their brain somewhere where when they think about, "Hey, I have to create a presentation." They come to you as the default tool.
alts.zh: 你會希望你的產品住在他們腦中的某個位置：當他們想到「我得做一份簡報」的時候，預設就是來找你。

alts.quote: Imagine two years there's a newspaper, there's a journalist that covers this work, and there's a newspaper article that comes out. I want you to imagine the progress on all these strategic pillars and what the headline of that newspaper article looks like.
alts.zh: 想像兩年後有個記者來報導我們這段工作，寫成一篇報導。我要你想像那篇報導的標題會長什麼樣子。

alts.quote: And what blew my mind is, it's not priced in, to any of these companies out there. And it's not reflected in the org charts of all the software companies in the world right now. That is going to completely change.
alts.zh: 最讓我震驚的是：這件事根本還沒被 price in。它完全沒有反映在現在全世界軟體公司的組織圖上。而這會徹底改變。

cards.pattern: Rather than just being fearful of [你擔心的事], I started to think what would the alternative be?
cards.quote: And then rather than just being fearful of the things that I'm worried about for society and for humanity, I started to think what would the alternative be?
cards.zh: 與其一直害怕那些我替社會、替人類擔心的事，我開始想：那另一種版本會長什麼樣？
cards.why: 把「反對什麼」轉成「想要什麼」的標準轉軸句。Rather than being fearful of X 先承認情緒是真的（不裝理性），再用 I started to think 把自己從受害者切換成設計者。抱怨型的同事最需要被丟這一句。
swaps: Instead of listing what worries us, let's describe the version we'd want.
Rather than fighting the thing we hate, what's the alternative we'd build?
cards.pmNote: 把 risk list 翻成 target state，團隊才有東西可以往前做。
cards.episode: The woman behind Canva shares how she built a $42B company from nothing | Melanie Perkins

alts.quote: It's going to take us years to do, but if we do it, we think this will change everything for design.
alts.zh: 這件事會花我們好幾年；但如果做成了，我們認為這會徹底改變設計這件事。

alts.quote: You want your product to live in their brain somewhere where when they think about, "Hey, I have to create a presentation." They come to you as the default tool.
alts.zh: 你會希望你的產品住在他們腦中的某個位置：當他們想到「我得做一份簡報」的時候，預設就是來找你。

alts.quote: So you can quit your job on a Sunday night, get the Sunday scaries, I'm done with this thing, and on Monday morning fill out this form and the next day be able to run a billion-dollar business.
alts.zh: 所以你可以星期天晚上辭掉工作——那種週日症候群發作、受夠了的心情——星期一早上填完這張表，隔天就能開始經營一間十億美金等級的公司。

cards.pattern: It's not something that I alone can achieve. I'd like to help change [X]. I'd like to help change [Y].
cards.quote: But I think that I'd like to change that. I'd like to help change the mood. I'd like to help change the way we're thinking about things.
cards.zh: 但我會想去改變這件事。我想幫忙改變那個氛圍。我想幫忙改變我們思考事情的方式。
cards.why: 三句 I'd like to 排比把野心堆高，但第二句起插進 help（我只是幫忙，不是我一個人扛），姿態瞬間壓低。野心大＋姿態低是英文講願景最難的平衡，這個 help 就是那顆調節鈕。
swaps: I'm not going to solve this alone, but I'd like to help shift how we think about it.
I'd like to help move the conversation, not own it.
cards.pmNote: 跨部門提大方向時，用 help 當動詞可以避免踩到別人的地盤。
cards.episode: The woman behind Canva shares how she built a $42B company from nothing | Melanie Perkins

alts.quote: It's going to take us years to do, but if we do it, we think this will change everything for design.
alts.zh: 這件事會花我們好幾年；但如果做成了，我們認為這會徹底改變設計這件事。

alts.quote: And so we felt like that was the wrong, that didn't feel right, and so could we help democratize visual storytelling, visual communication? That was sort of our north star.
alts.zh: 我們覺得這件事不對勁，所以問：我們有沒有辦法讓視覺敘事、視覺溝通變得人人可用？那就是我們的北極星。

alts.quote: And that ultimately, we understand what makes it a must-have product. And then what we're trying to do is build a flywheel around that must-have value.
alts.zh: 最終我們要弄清楚是什麼讓它變成「非有不可」的產品，然後圍繞那個非有不可的價值，去打造一個飛輪。

cards.pattern: It was like [遠處的蘑菇雲] — you see it, but you don't hear or notice it.
cards.quote: But weirdly, it was like you see the videos where there's the mushroom cloud in the distance. You see it. But you don't hear, or notice it.
cards.zh: 但很怪，那感覺就像影片裡遠方升起的蘑菇雲。你看得見。可是你聽不到，也沒真的感覺到。
cards.why: 三句短到不能再短，節奏是「畫面 → 停 → 反轉」。You see it. 獨立成句就是刻意的停頓，讓聽眾以為講完了，下一句 But you don't hear it 才把整個意思翻過來。要描述「威脅已經來了但當時沒人有感」，這比任何形容詞都準。
swaps: You could see it coming and still not feel it.
It registered visually, but nothing actually changed for us.
cards.pmNote: 競品發表當下往往看不出數據影響；真正的衝擊是綁定與迭代後才出現。
cards.episode: Behind the founder: Drew Houston (Dropbox)

alts.quote: So time becomes a convenient excuse for us where we say, 'Well, it's not me. It's just, I don't have time to work on it.'
alts.zh: 時間就變成一個很方便的藉口，我們會說：「不是我的問題，我只是沒時間做這件事。」

alts.quote: You wouldn't want to be in a commercial airplane and hear the tower say to the pilot, 'I'm giving priority to the following three planes on runway five.' Right away, you know there's something wrong.
alts.zh: 你不會希望自己坐在飛機上，聽到塔台跟機師說：「我要給五號跑道上這三架飛機優先權。」你馬上就知道哪裡不對。

alts.quote: At Facebook in particular, I would find that every so often I would have to have what I called a Legos talk with someone where I would just see them start to ask these questions like, why are we hiring that person?
alts.zh: 特別是在 Facebook，我發現每隔一陣子就得跟某個人來一場我叫做「樂高談話」的對話——我會看到他們開始問：我們為什麼要招那個人？

cards.pattern: People write about [X] like it's [一槍斃命的散彈]. Later I would learn it's more of a [慢慢絞緊的蟒蛇].
cards.quote: When, later, I would learn it's more of a boa constrictor.
cards.zh: 後來我才學到，它比較像一條蟒蛇慢慢把你絞緊。
cards.why: 媒體把競爭寫成「散彈槍一轟」，他改用蟒蛇——換比喻就是換模型，兩個比喻的差別剛好就是時間軸，而時間軸正是他的論點。要糾正別人對一件事的理解，找一個比對方更精準的比喻，比列三點理由有效十倍。
swaps: People talk about it like a single event; it's actually a slow squeeze.
It's not a shock, it's a slow compression.
cards.pmNote: 被大廠夾擊很少是單次事件，而是綁定＋迭代累積出的擠壓，數據上要看趨勢不是看發表日。
cards.episode: Behind the founder: Drew Houston (Dropbox)

alts.quote: It's a bit like this really smart intern that refuses to read Slack and doesn't check Datadog or Sentry unless you ask it to.
alts.zh: 它有點像一個超聰明、但死不看 Slack、你不叫他他就不會去看 Datadog 或 Sentry 的實習生。

alts.quote: You want to be that tree in the storm that is not so rigid that if the wind is too strong it's going to break in half, but not so flexible that it's going to swing every which direction as soon as there's a gust.
alts.zh: 你要當風暴裡的那棵樹——不要硬到風一大就攔腰折斷，也不要軟到一陣風來就往每個方向亂晃。

alts.quote: We call it the bow and arrow technique because we think you can only remember one thing out of a talk and that it's very powerful to go through that framework or that kind of thinking when you're building a talk.
alts.zh: 我們把它叫做「弓與箭技巧」，因為我們認為一場演講聽眾只記得住一件事，而在準備演講時走過這套思考非常有效。

cards.quote: I'd say that was the beginning of chapter two where it was we went from the company that could do no wrong to the company that could do no right, which was a big flip.
cards.zh: 我會說那就是第二章的開始——我們從「怎麼做都對」的公司，變成「怎麼做都錯」的公司，整個翻過來。
cards.why: 只換一個字（wrong→right）就把整段起落講完，這是英文裡最省字的對比法。而且 could do no wrong / could do no right 兩個都是現成慣用語，母語者一聽就懂；台灣人多半會講成 people used to love us, now they criticize everything，長三倍又沒力。
swaps: Overnight we stopped being the team that could do no wrong.
The narrative flipped completely.
cards.pmNote: 敘事（narrative）本身會影響招募、留才與媒體，是需要主動管理的資產。
cards.episode: Behind the founder: Drew Houston (Dropbox)

alts.quote: I always say you should have, what I call an elephant at the beginning of the story, which is actually a big spaceship shooting at a little spaceship or a police officer chasing a guy across a roof.
alts.zh: 我一直說你應該在故事開頭放一隻我稱為「大象」的東西——實際上就是一艘大太空船在射一艘小太空船，或是警察在屋頂上追一個人。

alts.quote: You wouldn't want to be in a commercial airplane and hear the tower say to the pilot, 'I'm giving priority to the following three planes on runway five.' Right away, you know there's something wrong.
alts.zh: 你不會希望自己坐在飛機上，聽到塔台跟機師說：「我要給五號跑道上這三架飛機優先權。」你馬上就知道哪裡不對。

alts.quote: Now, you have to be careful, let's say, I'll give you an example where this can go wrong.
alts.zh: 不過這裡要小心，我給你一個會出事的例子。

cards.pattern: Suddenly [一個很小很具體的畫面：員工不想再穿公司的 T-shirt 了].
cards.quote: You've started this company, it's been super successful, and then suddenly your employees don't want to wear your T-shirt anymore.
cards.zh: 你創了這家公司，它一路很成功，然後突然間，員工不想再穿你們公司的 T-shirt 了。
cards.why: 「士氣崩了」是抽象的，「員工不再穿公司 T-shirt」是看得見的。母語者講低潮幾乎一定會落到一個生活畫面上，聽眾才會有身體感。挑細節的原則：要能被拍下來，而且不需要解釋。
swaps: People stopped putting the company on their LinkedIn headline.
Nobody was handing out referrals anymore.
cards.pmNote: 士氣的領先指標常常是這種小訊號，比 engagement survey 早三個月出現。
cards.episode: Behind the founder: Drew Houston (Dropbox)

alts.quote: So time becomes a convenient excuse for us where we say, 'Well, it's not me. It's just, I don't have time to work on it.'
alts.zh: 時間就變成一個很方便的藉口，我們會說：「不是我的問題，我只是沒時間做這件事。」

alts.quote: I just started to feel this and it became like a pebble in my shoe. I started just to go through that process that you've gone through many times before of writing and distilling it, and that's where I came up with this hierarchy.
alts.zh: 我一直有這個感覺，它就像鞋子裡的一顆小石頭。後來我就照那個寫下來、把它蒸餾的過程走一遍，這個框架就是這樣長出來的。

alts.quote: I hate Jobs-to-be-Done, I think it is a terrible framework, I think no successful company has ever been built on top of JTBD and if you pick JTBD, you're probably doomed and I'll give you an example.
alts.zh: 我討厭 Jobs-to-be-Done，我覺得那是個爛框架，沒有一家成功公司是靠 JTBD 建起來的；你要是選了它，大概就完了——我給你一個例子。

cards.pattern: [強大的外部對手] did not kill us. We killed ourselves.
cards.quote: And he's looked at me, he laughed at and snorted and he's like, "Microsoft did not kill us. We killed ourselves."
cards.zh: 他看著我，笑了一聲、鼻子哼了一下，說：「不是微軟弄死我們的。是我們自己弄死自己的。」
cards.why: 兩句話、同一個動詞（kill）、主詞對調，就把責任從外部搬回內部。這種句型的威力在於它先幫對方講出那個最好用的藉口，再一刀否決——比直接說 we made mistakes 更難反駁，因為它示範了「我已經想過怪別人這條路了」。
swaps: The market didn't beat us — we beat ourselves.
That wasn't done to us. We did it to ourselves.
cards.pmNote: postmortem 開場先把外部因素講完再封起來，剩下的時間才會花在可控項上。
cards.episode: Behind the founder: Drew Houston (Dropbox)

alts.quote: Yes, it's not working. It's my fault. I will deal with it.
alts.zh: 我做的第一件事就是認下來。我說：「對，它現在是壞的。是我的錯。我會處理。」

alts.quote: I came in thinking I was supposed to behave the way I behaved at Apple, which is very direct, fighting hard.
alts.zh: 我進去的時候以為我該照在 Apple 的那一套來——非常直接、硬碰硬地爭。

alts.quote: And guess what? It's all okay. It's not a loss, it's a lesson.
alts.zh: 然後你知道嗎？那都沒關係。那不是損失，那是一課。

cards.pattern: The root cause was that I was too busy firing to aim, and then I thought I would do my aiming on [週末／假期].
cards.quote: I was too busy firing to aim, and then I thought I would do my aiming on vacations and things like that.
cards.zh: 我太忙著開槍，忙到沒空瞄準；然後我還以為瞄準這件事可以放到放假的時候再做。
cards.why: firing / aiming 是同一個動作系統的兩端，用它們就不必解釋「執行 vs 思考」的差別。第二句更狠：不是不知道要瞄準，是把瞄準排到了不可能發生的時段——這是承認錯誤時最高階的一手，你連自己的自欺都說出來了。
swaps: I was executing far more than I was deciding.
I kept deferring the thinking to a week that never came.
cards.pmNote: 策略時間如果沒有排進行事曆，就等於不存在。
cards.episode: Behind the founder: Drew Houston (Dropbox)

alts.quote: And so I think a lot of it comes down to not the things you try, but how you deeply understand the problem that's preventing someone from using your product effectively.
alts.zh: 所以我覺得關鍵不在你試了哪些招，而在你有多深地搞懂「是什麼擋住使用者用好你的產品」。

alts.quote: The problem is not like what should my goal be or how should I figure out what to do with my life? They usually know, but it's very hard to actually make time for those things.
alts.zh: 問題不在於「我的目標該是什麼」或「我這輩子要幹嘛」。這個大家其實都知道。問題是很難真的挪出時間去做那些事。

alts.quote: So there's, I wouldn't say a checklist, but there's a series of questions that I asked to diagnose why is growth slowing in this order, because it's one of these things where the first one that's a problem, if you don't fix that, it doesn't matter if you fix one of the ones below.
alts.zh: 我不會說那是一張檢查清單，但我確實有一組問題，會照順序問下去診斷成長為什麼變慢——因為只要最前面那個沒修，後面修再多都沒用。

cards.pattern: [挑戰] is not optional. You're going to be challenged, but [受苦] is optional.
cards.quote: I think the hardest thing for a founder, challenge is not optional. You're going to be challenged, but the suffering is optional.
cards.zh: 對創辦人來說最難的是：挑戰不是選項，你一定會被挑戰；但要不要痛苦，是選項。
cards.why: 把兩件常被綁在一起的事拆開，用同一個字（optional）當支點。這個句型可以套到任何你想幫人卸下不必要負擔的場合：加班、被罵、改版都適用。難度在於必須先承認前半是真的，否則後半會變成風涼話。
swaps: The deadline isn't negotiable; the panic is.
Pressure comes with the job. Misery doesn't have to.
cards.pmNote: 高壓專案的溝通重點：把不可控（挑戰）與可控（工作方式）明確分開。
cards.episode: Behind the founder: Drew Houston (Dropbox)

alts.quote: We call it the bow and arrow technique because we think you can only remember one thing out of a talk and that it's very powerful to go through that framework or that kind of thinking when you're building a talk.
alts.zh: 我們把它叫做「弓與箭技巧」，因為我們認為一場演講聽眾只記得住一件事，而在準備演講時走過這套思考非常有效。

alts.quote: I often use this analogy of if you're doing a home renovation, you can have the most beautiful rendering of the new bedroom. But if you haven't checked if there's electricity in that wall there or not, it's going to drastically change the cost and the time and everything.
alts.zh: 我常用一個比喻：你在裝修房子，臥室的效果圖可以做得美到不行。但如果你沒去確認那面牆裡到底有沒有電線，成本跟時間都會整個變樣。

alts.quote: And then the basic advice to a climber is if you can't do the crux, don't do the climb, because you're going to fall off there.
alts.zh: 攀岩最基本的建議是：如果你過不了關鍵段，就不要爬這條路線，因為你一定會在那裡掉下去。

cards.quote: Yeah, every time you move up a league, your reward is a stronger and better opponent and potentially more unlevel playing field.
cards.zh: 每升上一個聯盟，你的獎賞就是一個更強的對手，而且場地可能還更不公平。
cards.why: reward 這個字用得很反常——獎賞應該是好事，這裡卻接一個壞消息，一句話就把「成功會帶來更難的問題」講完。要安慰正在被降維打擊的團隊，這比 it's normal to struggle 有力太多。後面接 Easy to say, hard to do 可以再把姿態放低。
swaps: The prize for winning is a harder game.
Every level up buys you a tougher opponent.
cards.pmNote: 產品做起來之後的競爭強度是階梯式跳升的，資源規劃要提前一級。
cards.episode: Behind the founder: Drew Houston (Dropbox)

alts.quote: He was asked whether or not he was sleeping well at night and he said, 'Oh, yeah, I slept like a baby. I woke up every two hours and cried.'
alts.zh: 有人問他晚上睡得好不好，他說：「喔，超好，我睡得跟嬰兒一樣——每兩小時醒來哭一次。」

alts.quote: I assume all the time, 100% of the time, that no one wants to hear anything I have to say.
alts.zh: 我永遠都假設——百分之百的場合都假設——沒有人想聽我講任何話。

alts.quote: The more massive an object, the more energy it takes to change its direction. This is why big companies move slowly.
alts.zh: 物體越重，要改變它的方向就要越多能量。這就是為什麼大公司動得慢。

cards.pattern: Owning it ends up being more painful in the short run, but some painful hours can save painful years.
cards.quote: And just owning things ends up being more painful in the short run, but then some painful hours can save painful years.
cards.zh: 把責任認下來，短期一定比較痛；但幾個難熬的小時，可以省下難熬的好幾年。
cards.why: hours / years 同字根對照（painful hours → painful years），把成本效益比壓進四個字裡。前半先老實承認會痛（不假裝認錯很容易），後半才給理由——順序反過來就會變成說教。
swaps: It costs more today and a lot less over the year.
A hard conversation now beats a hard quarter later.
cards.pmNote: 壞消息越早上報越便宜，這是期望管理的核心算式。
cards.episode: Behind the founder: Drew Houston (Dropbox)

alts.quote: So it's someone that as a leader, you are in the hot seat and you can take accountability. So if some of these things don't pan out, it's on you and not on your team, and give your team permission to fail.
alts.zh: 身為領導者，你就是坐在火線上、要負起責任的人。如果這些事沒成，那是你的責任，不是團隊的責任——同時給團隊失敗的許可。

alts.quote: I don't want them to leave it at, "It was a big loss." You want to say, "What I learned from that is now I always run a load test, and I've had many successful launches since then."
alts.zh: 我不希望他只停在「那是一次很大的損失」。你應該說：我從那件事學到，現在我一定會先跑壓力測試，後來的好幾次上線都沒再出過同樣的問題。

alts.quote: I got to tell you, I had no idea how unique we were until I was outside and there are so many things.
alts.zh: 我得說，直到我離開之後，我才知道我們當時有多特殊——太多事情都是。

cards.pattern: Why do I have [1 個 X] at home and [10 個 X] at work? Why is it easier to [大範圍的事] than [自己身邊的事]?
cards.quote: Wait, why do I have 1 search box at home, and 10 search boxes at work? Why is it easier to search all of human knowledge than my company's knowledge?
cards.zh: 等等，為什麼我在家只有一個搜尋框，在公司卻有十個？為什麼搜全人類的知識，比搜我自己公司的知識還簡單？
cards.why: 兩個 Why 問句都內建一組荒謬的對照（家裡 vs 公司、全人類 vs 一間公司），完全不需要下結論，聽眾自己就得出「這不合理」。定義問題最有效的方式不是描述它，是找到一組讓它顯得荒謬的對照。
swaps: Why is the consumer version of this better than the one we pay for?
Why does this get worse every year instead of better?
cards.pmNote: 好的 problem statement 通常長得像一個沒人能回答的 Why。
cards.episode: Behind the founder: Drew Houston (Dropbox)

alts.quote: One of the things that I think when you're doing interviewing, one way to think about it, I call it home court, away court, neutral court, you want interviews to balance in all those different spheres.
alts.zh: 面試的時候有一個思考方式，我把它叫做「主場、客場、中立場」，你會希望面試在這幾個場域之間取得平衡。

alts.quote: So I need to be able to put a stake in the ground and say, "I got to beat all that in order to win a deal."
alts.zh: 所以我得先釘一根樁，說：我必須打贏這些，才拿得到這筆生意。

alts.quote: The way to summarize that is if you look at all the startup stories that we have at YC and all the companies we funded over all the years, the underlying theme is that rationally the founder should have given up at some point.
alts.zh: 要總結的話：如果你看 YC 所有的創業故事、這些年投的所有公司，底下共通的主題是——照理性判斷，創辦人早就該在某個時間點放棄了。

cards.quote: We should probably not do things that would've been invented by everybody else 10 minutes later. Where are the problems that are not solving themselves?
cards.zh: 我們大概不該去做那些晚十分鐘別人也會做出來的東西。真正該問的是：哪些問題是不會自己被解決的？
cards.why: 先給一條刪除規則（不做什麼），再給一個定位問句（做什麼）。not solving themselves 是很漂亮的判準——它把「市場空白」重新定義成「連時間都解決不了的空白」，門檻一下子拉高，而且很好在會議上重複引用。
swaps: If someone else would build it anyway, it's not ours to build.
Which of these problems won't fix itself in two years?
cards.pmNote: 選題判準：這個問題會不會被平台方、時間或競爭者自然解決？會的話就別投人力。
cards.episode: Behind the founder: Drew Houston (Dropbox)

alts.quote: One of the most important things that we did was we didn't really worry about competitors at all. We actually just saw where is there a gap in the market that we can uniquely fill
alts.zh: 我們做過最重要的一件事，就是根本不太管競爭對手。我們只看市場上哪裡有一個缺口，是我們可以獨一無二補上的。

alts.quote: You absolutely should polish things like the model output, but you won't know what to polish until after you ship.
alts.zh: 該打磨的東西當然要打磨，像是模型輸出；但你要磨哪裡，得等出貨之後才會知道。

alts.quote: I think so many folks don't know where to begin on starting a startup, and my tactical advice is start doing customer validation first versus building a PowerPoint deck.
alts.zh: 很多人根本不知道創業要從哪裡開始，我很具體的建議是：先去做客戶驗證，而不是先做一份簡報。

cards.pattern: When you open up your laptop in [2030], what do you see?
cards.quote: In deciding to turn Dropbox into this lab for distributed work, we're like, "Okay, when you open up your laptop in 2025, 2030, what do you see?"
cards.zh: 我們決定把 Dropbox 變成遠距工作的實驗室時，問的是：「二〇二五、二〇三〇年，你打開筆電的那一刻，看到的是什麼？」
cards.why: 願景問題落到一個具體動作（打開筆電）跟一個具體感官（看到什麼），團隊就答得出來。相對地「五年後我們想成為什麼」這種問法只會收到空話。要讓 vision workshop 有產出，先把問題縮到一個畫面。
swaps: What's on the screen when they start their day in 2030?
Walk me through their first five minutes three years from now.
cards.pmNote: product vision 的可操作版本＝使用者未來某一天的具體場景，不是形容詞的堆疊。
cards.episode: Behind the founder: Drew Houston (Dropbox)

alts.quote: You kind of want to have a ladder that goes all the way up to the moon, which is your crazy, wild vision. And then you want to have rungs that just work its way up step by step.
alts.zh: 你會希望有一把直達月球的梯子，那就是你那個瘋狂的大願景。然後你要有一階一階的橫桿，讓人可以一步一步往上爬。

alts.quote: And he would say, you have to aim for Chartres. You have to make something that is better than that. That should be your goal, not to just turn in something that's what you feel is good enough.
alts.zh: 他會說：你要對準夏特大教堂。你要做出比它更好的東西。那才是你的目標，而不是交出一個你自己覺得「還可以」的作品。

alts.quote: Imagine two years there's a newspaper, there's a journalist that covers this work, and there's a newspaper article that comes out. I want you to imagine the progress on all these strategic pillars and what the headline of that newspaper article looks like.
alts.zh: 想像兩年後有個記者來報導我們這段工作，寫成一篇報導。我要你想像那篇報導的標題會長什麼樣子。

cards.pattern: [某個 buzzword] means a lot of things to a lot of people. So it's a bit of a Rorschach test — the part that resonates with me is [你的定義].
cards.quote: So founder mode means a lot of things to a lot of people. So it's a bit of a Rorschach test
cards.zh: 「founder mode」這個詞，每個人講的都不太一樣，有點像羅夏克墨漬測驗——但真正打到我的部分是⋯⋯
cards.why: 會議上有人丟出一個大家其實各自解讀的流行詞時，這句可以在不否定任何人的前提下，把定義權接過來。a Rorschach test 是關鍵——它委婉地說「這個詞現在是空的，投射什麼進去都可以」，然後你才填自己的內容。
swaps: That term means different things to different people — the way I use it is...
Let me say what I mean by that, because it's used pretty loosely.
cards.pmNote: 跨團隊對齊的第一步永遠是把共用名詞定義下來，否則所有共識都是假的。
cards.episode: Behind the founder: Drew Houston (Dropbox)

alts.quote: A lot of people see product market fit as this binary, "I have it or I don't." What you're describing is what I often hear, it's more of this spectrum of more and more confidence.
alts.zh: 很多人把 PMF 看成二元的：不是有就是沒有。而你在描述的，是我常聽到的另一種——它比較像一條逐漸累積信心的光譜。

alts.quote: Let me refine that a little bit more. It's more about giving people the information that they can use for decisions that they alone are good at...
alts.zh: 我把那個講法再修得精準一點。重點比較是：給人們他們才擅長的那類決策所需要的資訊。

alts.quote: And if it's helpful, let me break down the question a little bit.
alts.zh: 如果有幫助的話，我把這個問題拆開來講一下。

cards.quote: And then you flip to your development areas because no one calls them weaknesses.
cards.zh: 然後你翻到「待發展面向」那一頁——因為沒人會直接叫它「缺點」。
cards.why: 用一句自嘲式的旁白拆穿職場委婉語，既表示你懂遊戲規則，又不刻薄。實用價值很直接：英文職場一律講 development areas / growth areas，台灣人常照字面說 weaknesses，在 360 或 1:1 裡聽起來會過重。
swaps: your growth areas — nobody says weaknesses out loud
the development section, as it's politely called
cards.pmNote: 回饋要能被接住，用詞的溫度跟內容一樣重要；先降溫再給料。
cards.episode: Behind the founder: Drew Houston (Dropbox)

alts.quote: I care so much about you and I'm giving you this feedback because I want you to be successful and I want you to be able to reach the pinnacle of what I know you can accomplish.
alts.zh: 我非常在乎你，我給你這個回饋是因為我希望你成功、希望你能走到我知道你能到的高度。

alts.quote: To suggest an idea, use language with your manager like, “I noticed that we are often late on projects because we forget to account for vacation schedules and then someone critical is out.
alts.zh: 我注意到我們專案常常延遲，因為我們排程時忘了把休假算進去，然後關鍵的人剛好就不在。

alts.quote: At one point I noticed I was spending six to 7% of my week on these areas, these areas where I can truly be world-class at.
alts.zh: 有一陣子我注意到，我一週只花百分之六到七的時間在這些領域上——那些我真的能做到世界頂尖的領域。

cards.pattern: [聰明人] have a really fast rationalization hamster — they can convince themselves that here's how they were technically right even though clearly they were wrong.
cards.quote: smart people have a really fast rationalization hamster. They can convince themselves that, well, here's how they were technically right even though clearly they were wrong
cards.zh: 聰明人腦裡那隻「合理化的倉鼠」跑得特別快，他們有辦法說服自己「技術上我其實是對的」，即使明明就錯了。
cards.why: rationalization hamster 是自創的具象化說法，把抽象的認知偏誤變成一隻在跑滾輪的動物，聽一次就忘不掉。而且 technically right 這個搭配本身就是英文職場的暗語——說某人 technically right 幾乎等於說他錯了。
swaps: Smart people are unusually good at explaining away their own misses.
The smarter the person, the faster the rationalization.
cards.pmNote: 面試資深職位時，比起「知道什麼」更該測「能不能承認自己判斷錯過」。
cards.episode: Behind the founder: Drew Houston (Dropbox)

alts.quote: Your belief is that if we add buy now pay later, a lot more people will be able to buy and transact, and so it's going to pay off. Do I have that right?
alts.zh: 你的認定是：只要我們加了先買後付，會有更多人買得下去、成交量會上來，所以這筆投資划得來。我這樣理解對嗎？

alts.quote: I think sometimes people use data a lot or too much because they're worrying or they're afraid that, will I make the wrong choice? And I'm using data to make the choice for me.
alts.zh: 我覺得有時候大家用數據用得太兇，是因為他們在怕：萬一我選錯了怎麼辦？於是就讓數據替他們做決定。

alts.quote: Well, I mean this is the irony of growth, is people think growth is overnight success and it's not. It is a lot of short wins and short-term execution for a longer-term gain.
alts.zh: 成長最諷刺的地方就在這：大家以為成長是一夜爆紅，其實不是。它是一堆短期的小勝仗，堆出長期的結果。

cards.quote: So I think finding ways to take responsibility or always have a mindset of what if I were a hundred percent responsible for this? What if it was no one else's fault?
cards.zh: 我覺得要一直找辦法把責任接下來，常常問自己：如果這件事百分之百是我的責任呢？如果完全不是別人的錯呢？
cards.why: 用假設語氣（What if）而不是斷言（It was my fault），所以不必真的相信這是事實也能用——他後面也承認 those things are never true。這讓「扛責任」變成一種思考工具而不是自虐，開檢討會時特別好用。
swaps: Let's assume for a minute this was entirely on us — what would we change?
If none of the external stuff existed, what's still our problem?
cards.pmNote: postmortem 的高產出設定：先假設 100% 內部歸因，把可控項全撈出來再談外部因素。
cards.episode: Behind the founder: Drew Houston (Dropbox)

alts.quote: I don't want them to leave it at, "It was a big loss." You want to say, "What I learned from that is now I always run a load test, and I've had many successful launches since then."
alts.zh: 我不希望他只停在「那是一次很大的損失」。你應該說：我從那件事學到，現在我一定會先跑壓力測試，後來的好幾次上線都沒再出過同樣的問題。

alts.quote: And then the second piece of advice I would give I think we should have been talking to potential acquirers from the beginning and sharing our vision and what we were trying to accomplish because we started those quite late in our journey as a company.
alts.zh: 我要給的第二個建議是：我覺得我們一開始就該去跟潛在的收購方聊，分享我們的願景跟想達成的事。我們啟動得太晚了。

alts.quote: Probably for me, I think my time at Instacart was probably not my best time. I think I went to Instacart with a vision of what I felt the product could be, but I was not aware or in tune with what the DNA of the company was.
alts.zh: 對我來說，Instacart 那段大概是我狀態最不好的時候。我帶著一套「產品應該長成什麼樣」的想像進去，卻沒真的看懂那家公司的 DNA 是什麼。

cards.pattern: The only thing our customers have really meaningfully seen from us in [三年] is [a price increase]. What are we doing?
cards.quote: Look, we haven't shipped any. Last three years, the only thing our customers have really meaningfully seen from our product is a price increase. What the hell are we doing?
cards.zh: 你看，我們什麼都沒出。過去三年，客戶從我們產品上真正感受到的只有一件事：漲價。我們到底在幹嘛？
cards.why: 把難聽的話換算成「客戶視角的唯一事實」，就沒人能辯——不是我覺得你們不夠好，是客戶三年只收到一次漲價。最後那個問句不是要答案，是把不舒服留在房間裡。內部要打破自我感覺良好時，這是最短路徑。
swaps: From the customer's side, the only change in two years was the price.
Let's be honest about what shipped and what didn't.
cards.pmNote: 組織自嗨的解毒劑：把內部成果單換算成「使用者實際感受到的變化」。
cards.episode: Behind the founder: Drew Houston (Dropbox)

alts.quote: It was pretty obvious after six months this thing was a bit of a zombie product walking, and the least I could have done is said, "This thing is dead." We could have called it dead way earlier.
alts.zh: 半年後就很明顯這是個活死人產品了，我至少可以做的，就是講一句：這個東西已經死了。我們早就該宣布它死亡。

alts.quote: And at Uber, I learned this because, it pains me to say this, but really the price and the ETA at Uber was the product.
alts.zh: 我在 Uber 學到這件事——講出來我自己都有點痛——但價格跟預估時間，那才是 Uber 真正的產品。

alts.quote: The last handoff meeting we had, you didn’t share any background customer research, which I failed to flag at the time.
alts.zh: 上次交接會議你沒有分享任何背景使用者研究，而我當下也沒有把這件事提出來。

cards.quote: So first of all, when you're in the early innings, you'll actually get more useful advice often from your peers because they're going through the same thing.
cards.zh: 首先，在很前期的階段，你從同輩那裡拿到的建議其實比較有用，因為他們正在經歷一模一樣的事。
cards.why: in the early innings（棒球用語＝比賽還很前面）是矽谷高頻慣用語，台灣人幾乎不會用但一講就很到位。這句的實用性在於它給了一個選 mentor 的判準：不是找最資深的，是找階段最貼近的。
swaps: Early on, peers give better advice than veterans.
For this stage, I'd rather ask someone who did it last year.
cards.pmNote: 建人脈梯隊：同階段 1-2 人、領先 2 年、領先 5 年、領先 20 年，各問不同層級的問題。
cards.episode: Behind the founder: Drew Houston (Dropbox)

alts.quote: So especially when you're meeting with a new engineering team for the first time, actually ask them, what is one thing I can do to help you this week?
alts.zh: 尤其是第一次跟新的工程團隊碰面時，真的去問他們：這禮拜我可以幫上哪一件事？

alts.quote: My uncle and aunt were coming in, and they're encouraging me, "This is all up to you, but try not to lose it all on night number one," which was good advice to give me.
alts.zh: 我叔叔阿姨要來，他們鼓勵我說：「這都是你自己決定，不過盡量不要第一晚就全輸光。」後來覺得這建議給得很好。

alts.quote: I picked you because I really trust you to be a sound source of truthful advice and give me some feedback. So I really value that. Do you mind spending a couple of minutes and just giving me some thoughts on this?
alts.zh: 我會找你，是因為我真的很信任你會給我誠實的建議跟回饋，這對我很有價值。可以請你花個幾分鐘，給我一點想法嗎？

cards.pattern: A year from now, what will I wish I had been learning today? Two years? Five years?
cards.quote: always be working back from, in one year from now, what will I wish I had been learning today? Two years, five years?
cards.zh: 永遠從未來往回推：一年後的我，會希望今天的我在學什麼？兩年後呢？五年後呢？
cards.why: working back from 是這句的骨架，把提問的時間原點從現在搬到未來，答案就會完全不同。後面只丟兩個名詞（Two years, five years?）當追問，是很自然的口語省略——不必重複整句問句。
swaps: What will next year's version of me wish I'd started today?
Working back from a year out, what's missing now?
cards.pmNote: 個人成長曲線要跑在公司成長曲線前面，這個問句是它的操作版本。
cards.episode: Behind the founder: Drew Houston (Dropbox)

alts.quote: And it's the short, medium, lon-term in product, but it's what are you optimizing for today, this quarter, this year?
alts.zh: 產品上分短中長期，但問題就是：你今天、這一季、今年，到底在最佳化什麼？

alts.quote: Walk me through what's living in your head right now.
alts.zh: 帶我走一遍你現在腦子裡裝的東西。

alts.quote: If you can tell me what you're working on and ask me at the end of a meeting specifically what I noticed then that is much better."
alts.zh: 如果你可以先跟我說你在忙什麼，然後在會議結束時具體問我注意到了什麼，那效果好得多。

cards.pattern: Hopefully I don't come off as [對方可能的誤解]. I'm not saying that at all. What I'm saying is [你真正的意思].
cards.quote: Hopefully, I don't come off as encouraging everyone to be like me. I'm not saying that at all. What I'm saying is, this is a way to be.
cards.zh: 希望我聽起來不是在鼓吹大家都要跟我一樣。我完全不是那個意思。我要說的是：這是一種活法。
cards.why: 三拍拆誤會：先點名可能的誤讀（come off as）、再切斷（I'm not saying that at all）、最後才給正確版本（What I'm saying is）。整段最重的字是 a way——不是 the way，一個冠詞就把主張從教條降成選項。
swaps: I don't want this to come across as X. What I mean is Y.
To be clear, I'm not arguing for X — I'm saying X is one option.
cards.pmNote: 提出非主流做法時先自曝可能的誤讀，可以擋掉一半的反對意見。
cards.episode: Jason Fried challenges your thinking on fundraising, goals, growth, and more

alts.quote: I'm not saying that having a large market someday doesn't matter, of course it does eventually. But trying to be super pedantic about market size when it's a pre-seed company, it's just not something I'd put a lot of thought.
alts.zh: 我不是說市場總有一天要夠大這件事不重要，當然重要。但在一家 pre-seed 公司還在糾結市場規模算得多精確，我不會花太多心思在上面。

alts.quote: It's like, "well, I'm not telling you that you should pivot. I'm just saying that is what it's called when you change the strategy, but try to have fidelity to the vision."
alts.zh: 我不是在叫你去 pivot。我只是說，當你改策略但盡量守住願景的時候，那件事就叫這個名字。

alts.quote: By the way, I'm being very mean to Figma so far in this conversation. There is a time when it's the right time for the Figma file.
alts.zh: 順帶一提，我到目前為止對 Figma 有點太兇了。Figma 檔是有它對的時機的。

cards.pattern: What's interesting is that [某群人] has found a way to make the most [adj] [X] the least [adj].
cards.quote: What's interesting is that Silicon Valley has found a way to make the most profitable style of business the least profitable.
cards.zh: 有趣的是，矽谷居然有辦法把全世界最好賺的生意做成最不賺錢的生意。
cards.why: 同一個形容詞的最高級正反並排（the most profitable / the least profitable），矛盾自己會跳出來，不必加任何評論。開頭 What's interesting is 又把一句很嗆的批評包成觀察，語氣立刻降溫——這是英文裡最好用的「毒藥包糖衣」。
swaps: We've somehow turned the cheapest thing to build into the most expensive.
It's impressive how the easiest market to win became the hardest.
cards.pmNote: 軟體毛利本來就高，燒錢燒到不賺錢是選擇問題，不是產業結構問題。
cards.episode: Jason Fried challenges your thinking on fundraising, goals, growth, and more

alts.quote: What I've found is that once you commit to a decision, you actually learn more post committing to that decision about what's going to work and not going to work, and you move out of the hypothetical.
alts.zh: 我發現的是，一旦你對一個決定拍板，你在拍板之後反而會學到更多——什麼會成、什麼不會成——而且你會離開純假設的狀態。

alts.quote: In a world where it's easier to build things, it's more important to make sure that your time is spent figuring out what you should be building in the first place.
alts.zh: 在一個「東西越來越好做」的世界裡，更重要的是先確保你把時間花在想清楚「到底該做什麼」。

alts.quote: And again, everything I've just described, by the way, is just a very straightforward extrapolation of very basic economics. I'm not making any bold predictions of what I just said.
alts.zh: 我剛剛講的這一整串，其實只是最基本的經濟學往下推而已。我沒有在做什麼大膽預測。

cards.pattern: [X] is not just a stepping stone — [X] is a great destination itself.
cards.quote: Small is not just a stepping stone, small is a great destination itself.
cards.zh: 「小」不只是通往別處的墊腳石，「小」本身就是一個很好的終點。
cards.why: not just a stepping stone / a great destination 是一組現成的空間隱喻，用來替任何「被當成過渡狀態」的東西平反：小團隊、資深工程師不轉管理、產品不擴張都能套。重點在 itself——沒有它，這句就只是說小也不錯。
swaps: This isn't a phase we're trying to get out of.
Staying at this size is the plan, not a stage.
cards.pmNote: 不是每個產品線都要規劃成長路徑；有些的正確目標就是穩定與高毛利。
cards.episode: Jason Fried challenges your thinking on fundraising, goals, growth, and more

alts.quote: So having a shit draft is a million times more valuable than having all these great ideas. But it's also really painful.
alts.zh: 有一份爛草稿，比手上一堆很棒的點子有價值一百萬倍。但那個過程真的很痛。

alts.quote: I would underline it even, which is that we get excited about the markets, the opportunities, that might seem small from the outside.
alts.zh: 我甚至要再加重語氣：那些從外面看起來很小的市場、很小的機會，我們反而會興奮。

alts.quote: In a world where it's easier to build things, it's more important to make sure that your time is spent figuring out what you should be building in the first place.
alts.zh: 在一個「東西越來越好做」的世界裡，更重要的是先確保你把時間花在想清楚「到底該做什麼」。

cards.pattern: This is not an estimate of time, it's an appetite. It doesn't sound like that much of a different word, but it really is.
cards.quote: So this is not an estimate of time, it's an appetite, which is a radically different approach. It doesn't sound like that much of a different word, but it really is.
cards.zh: 這不是「時間估算」，這是「胃口」——做法完全不一樣。聽起來只是換個字，但差別真的很大。
cards.why: 換掉一個名詞就換掉整套邏輯：estimate 是「這要多久」，appetite 是「我願意花多久」，因果方向相反。第二句先替聽眾說出他的懷疑（聽起來只是換字），再堅持（but it really is），比直接解釋更有說服力。
swaps: We're not estimating this, we're budgeting it.
The question isn't how long it takes — it's how long it's worth.
cards.pmNote: fixed time, variable scope：時間先鎖死，範圍才是變數，這是 Shape Up 的核心。
cards.episode: Jason Fried challenges your thinking on fundraising, goals, growth, and more

alts.quote: Strategy should hurt is a much better way to explain it to people which is, if you're not making trade-offs that are painful, you are not actually helping people prioritize their time.
alts.zh: 「策略應該要會痛」是更好的說法：如果你做的取捨一點都不痛，那你根本沒在幫大家決定時間該花在哪。

alts.quote: The number one thing to figure out when you're thinking about the different pricing pieces, pound for pound, it's the pricing metric or the value metric.
alts.zh: 定價的各個環節裡，論投入產出比，最該先搞定的就是計價單位（價值指標）。

alts.quote: So yeah, no hard and fast rule, but I think it's always you need to have this matrix of options in your mind and be very deliberate about which one you are going with and why.
alts.zh: 沒有什麼鐵則，但你腦中要有一張選項矩陣，而且要很清楚自己選了哪一格、為什麼。

cards.pattern: There's nothing easier than promising [work] later — and the further away it is, the easier it is to promise.
cards.quote: There's nothing easier than promising work later.
cards.zh: 沒有什麼比「答應以後再做」更容易的事了。
cards.why: 八個字擋掉「那放到 Q4 好不好」。它攻擊的是「承諾」這個行為本身而不是對方的需求，所以不會撕破臉；接下來那句 the further away it is, the easier it is to promise 用比較級連動，把心理機制講成公式，聽者會自動想到自己剛才差點答應的事。
swaps: Committing to something six months out costs nothing today — that's the problem.
The easiest promise to make is the one that's furthest away.
cards.pmNote: 「by the end of the year」是最危險的承諾句型，成本為零、代價全在未來。
cards.episode: Jason Fried challenges your thinking on fundraising, goals, growth, and more

alts.quote: if you want to change during the course of the quarter, if you want to disrupt our whole engineering product team, you can do it, but understand there's a high cost, and the later you do it in the quarter, the less successful it's going to be
alts.zh: 你想在季中改、想打亂整個工程團隊，可以啊，但你要知道代價很高——而且愈晚改，效果只會愈差。

alts.quote: that's too easy to come to me and be like, "Oh, here's A and B. You do the work and tell me which you one to pick." No way.
alts.zh: 「這裡有 A 案和 B 案，你來想、你來選」——這太輕鬆了。不行。

alts.quote: And so even though I really like a lot about this, I'm going to say no." And I often think that founders think that there's some secret truth that's being held from them on why someone says no or they want more feedback.
alts.zh: 「就算我真的很喜歡這個東西的很多地方，我還是要說不。」我也常覺得，創辦人以為別人說不的背後藏著什麼沒告訴他的秘密，或想再要更多回饋。

cards.pattern: Keep working the way you're working, but on some low-criticality project, try this new method on that.
cards.quote: So what we often encourage people to do is keep working the way you're working, but some future project, some low criticality project, try this new method on that.
cards.zh: 我們常建議的是：現在的做法照舊，但挑一個之後的、沒那麼要緊的專案，在那上面試新方法。
cards.why: 推新做法時最大的阻力是風險，這句直接把風險拿掉：不動現況、只在低風險的地方試。keep... but... 的結構讓對方不必先否定自己現在的做法就能點頭，成功率比「我們改用 X 吧」高很多。
swaps: Let's not change anything critical — let's try it on the next low-stakes project.
Same process for now; I'd just like one small project to pilot this.
cards.pmNote: 流程變革要先降低 criticality；在關鍵專案上試新方法失敗一次，就再也不會有第二次機會。
cards.episode: Jason Fried challenges your thinking on fundraising, goals, growth, and more

alts.quote: the best way to get feedback from people is not by asking what they think, but to put something concrete in front of them and then have them react to it, right?
alts.zh: 要拿到回饋，最好的方式不是問人家怎麼想，而是先擺一個具體的東西在他面前，讓他反應，對吧？

alts.quote: None of this is going to blow anyone's minds, I think, because it's very best practices. But it's easy to overlook when you're so focused on so many different steps of a process.
alts.zh: 這些應該不會讓誰驚呆，因為都是很基本的最佳實務。但當你同時盯著流程裡一大堆步驟時，就是很容易漏掉。

alts.quote: I want you to pull the hiring manager aside and say, "Hey, Lenny, you're the hiring manager. I've thought about what the role is. I want to make sure I'm understanding it correctly.
alts.zh: 我要你把用人主管拉到一旁說：「我想過這個職位到底是什麼，我想確認我理解得對不對。我可以跟你分享一下嗎？」

cards.pattern: I don't like the word [X] — how do you feel after a [X]?
cards.quote: I don't like the word sprint because how do you feel after a sprint? Exhausted.
cards.zh: 我不喜歡「衝刺」這個詞——你衝刺完是什麼感覺？累爆。
cards.why: 拆一個用久到沒人再想的詞：不吵它的定義，而是問它的字面經驗，然後自己答一個字（Exhausted.）。這種一字回答是英文口語的重錘，比講一整句解釋更有停頓感，也留給對方反駁的空間。
swaps: I'd avoid that word — think about what it literally describes.
What does that word actually imply about how we work?
cards.pmNote: 團隊語彙會塑造行為：叫 sprint 就會一直衝，叫 cycle 才會有節奏與冷卻期。
cards.episode: Jason Fried challenges your thinking on fundraising, goals, growth, and more

alts.quote: So, I don't really care how high quality the initial MVP is because quality is defined by the customer. And if we don't know who our customer is, we literally don't know what the word quality means.
alts.zh: 所以第一版的 MVP 品質多高，我其實沒那麼在意，因為品質是由客戶定義的。如果我們連客戶是誰都不知道，我們根本不知道「品質」這兩個字是什麼意思。

alts.quote: And so I'm going to kind of reject that premise, because I don't think design takes more time.
alts.zh: 所以我要說，我不太接受那個前提，因為我不認為設計會花比較多時間。

alts.quote: Just because AI is all the rage and investors really like AI doesn't necessarily mean it should be front and center
alts.zh: AI 現在很紅、投資人也很愛，但這不代表它就該擺在最前面。

cards.pattern: We ask people "What do you think?" We don't say "What do you know?"
cards.quote: What we ask people in general is we say, what do you think? We don't say, what do you know? We often say, what do you think?
cards.zh: 我們一般會問人「你怎麼想？」我們不會問「你知道什麼？」我們最常問的就是「你怎麼想？」
cards.why: 把兩個看起來差不多的問句擺在一起比，差別就出來了：know 要求證據、think 要求判斷。而且他刻意重複第一句收尾，是很自然的口語強調法（A → not B → A）。要讓資淺同事願意開口，換這個動詞就夠了。
swaps: I'm not asking what the data says — what do you think?
What's your read on this?
cards.pmNote: 1:1 裡問 what do you know 會得到報告，問 what do you think 才會得到判斷。
cards.episode: Jason Fried challenges your thinking on fundraising, goals, growth, and more

alts.quote: I often think about this phrase, which is people don't care what you know until they know that you care.
alts.zh: 我常想到這句話：在別人知道你在乎之前，他們不會在乎你懂什麼。

alts.quote: You ask questions like, what's the hardest you've ever worked to get something done and why? And that does differentiate a lot of people, a lot of people don't actually have a great answer to that.
alts.zh: 你可以問這種問題：你這輩子為了完成某件事最拚的一次是什麼？為什麼？這題真的很能分辨人，很多人其實答不太出來。

alts.quote: People call me sometimes they're like "I want to know if I have product market fit." Well, the fact that you have time to call me and ask me this question already tells me the answer.
alts.zh: 有人打給我說：「我想知道我們有沒有 PMF。」嗯，你有空打這通電話問我，這件事本身就給了答案。

cards.quote: And one of the things I'll often ask is, if you had another couple days, what would you do with this?
cards.zh: 我很常問的一個問題是：如果再多給你幾天，你會拿這個東西做什麼？
cards.why: 假設性問句把人從「辯護已交付的東西」切換成「想下一步」，答案會露出他真正的品味和存貨。面試、design review、1:1 都能用，而且因為是假設，對方不會覺得是在被挑毛病。
swaps: If we gave this another week, where would it go?
What's the version of this you didn't have time to build?
cards.pmNote: 評估設計師／PM 的深度，看他手上還有沒有「沒放進去的下一層想法」。
cards.episode: Jason Fried challenges your thinking on fundraising, goals, growth, and more

alts.quote: One of the things I ask a lot in product review when someone says, "Hey, we want to run an experiment," is, "Okay, what do we do if it's green? What do we do if it's red?"
alts.zh: 有人說「我們想跑個實驗」，我在產品評審上最常問的就是：「如果結果是綠的我們做什麼？紅的又做什麼？」

alts.quote: One of the things to ask oneself is what draws me to this position in the first place?
alts.zh: 有個可以問自己的問題是：當初到底是什麼把我吸引到這個位置的？

alts.quote: I always ask, "What worked? What didn't work?"
alts.zh: 我每次都會問：哪裡有用？哪裡沒用？

cards.pattern: The more massive an object, the more energy it takes to change its direction. This is why [大公司] move slowly.
cards.quote: The more massive an object, the more energy it takes to change its direction. This is why big companies move slowly.
cards.zh: 物體越重，要改變它的方向就要越多能量。這就是為什麼大公司動得慢。
cards.why: 借一條沒人會反駁的物理定律，再用 This is why 一句話落到組織上。這種「定律＋落地」的兩句組合，能讓一個主觀判斷聽起來像推論結果；而且對方要反駁，得先反駁牛頓。
swaps: Momentum is real — the bigger the team, the more energy a turn costs.
You can't turn a big ship on a dime.
cards.pmNote: 組織轉向的成本跟規模成正比，改流程要估的是能量不是時間。
cards.episode: Jason Fried challenges your thinking on fundraising, goals, growth, and more

alts.quote: I'd say that was the beginning of chapter two where it was we went from the company that could do no wrong to the company that could do no right, which was a big flip.
alts.zh: 我會說那就是第二章的開始——我們從「怎麼做都對」的公司，變成「怎麼做都錯」的公司，整個翻過來。

alts.quote: I often use this analogy of if you're doing a home renovation, you can have the most beautiful rendering of the new bedroom. But if you haven't checked if there's electricity in that wall there or not, it's going to drastically change the cost and the time and everything.
alts.zh: 我常用一個比喻：你在裝修房子，臥室的效果圖可以做得美到不行。但如果你沒去確認那面牆裡到底有沒有電線，成本跟時間都會整個變樣。

alts.quote: I always say you should have, what I call an elephant at the beginning of the story, which is actually a big spaceship shooting at a little spaceship or a police officer chasing a guy across a roof.
alts.zh: 我一直說你應該在故事開頭放一隻我稱為「大象」的東西——實際上就是一艘大太空船在射一艘小太空船，或是警察在屋頂上追一個人。

cards.quote: I'm like, "I'm not surprised to hear that. Tell me how you did it."
cards.zh: 我就說：「我一點都不意外。你跟我說說你們是怎麼做的。」
cards.why: 對方抱怨「你的方法沒用」，這兩句既不辯護也不道歉：I'm not surprised 穩住場面又暗示問題可能在執行，Tell me how you did it 直接把對話推進到事實層。台灣人在這種場合最常見的反應是先道歉或先解釋，兩者都會失去診斷的機會。
swaps: That doesn't surprise me — walk me through what you actually did.
Makes sense. How did you run it?
cards.pmNote: 有人說某個做法失敗時，先問執行細節再談方法論，八成問題出在前者。
cards.episode: Jason Fried challenges your thinking on fundraising, goals, growth, and more

alts.quote: You could tell, he's like, "Help me understand this part of your thinking."
alts.zh: 你看得出來，他就會說：「幫我理解你這一段的思路。」

alts.quote: Great. Tell me a situation where that best practice would not be applicable.
alts.zh: 很好。那你跟我說一個「這個最佳實務不適用」的情境。

alts.quote: In six months, if I'm telling you what to do, I've hired the wrong person.
alts.zh: 半年後如果還是我在告訴你要做什麼，那就是我當初找錯人了。

cards.pattern: What's the worst that can happen? You've got to be at peace with the worst that can happen.
cards.quote: which is just the idea of negative visualization. What's the worst that can happen? You got to be at peace with the worst that can happen.
cards.zh: 這就是「負面預想」：最糟會發生什麼事？你必須跟那個最糟的結果和平共處。
cards.why: 把風險提問跟心理準備綁成一組（問完還要 be at peace with），所以不會停在嚇人。at peace with 是關鍵搭配——不是 accept、不是 prepare for，而是「不再抗拒」，語氣冷靜很多。提案被質疑風險時用這句可以把對話從恐懼轉成盤點。
swaps: Let's name the worst case and decide if we can live with it.
If this fails completely, what have we actually lost?
cards.pmNote: pre-mortem 的私人版；能接受最壞情況，決策速度會快很多。
cards.episode: Jason Fried challenges your thinking on fundraising, goals, growth, and more

alts.quote: But, and this is the big but, no one has this at the early stages when they don't have a good idea and they don't have customers and it's objectively not working.
alts.zh: 但是——而且這是很大的一個「但是」——在最早期、還沒有好點子、沒有客戶、客觀上根本不 work 的時候，沒有人會有那種信念。

alts.quote: And I always write them back and say like, "Please tell me the better term and popularize it and I'll use it. It's a great idea."
alts.zh: 我都回信說：「請你告訴我更好的講法，然後把它推廣開，我就會改用。這主意很好。」

alts.quote: That's a good idea, but we don't actually understand these three things before we start working on that. So maybe we should do understand work to make sure that that is actually the right idea.
alts.zh: 這個想法不錯，但在動手之前有三件事我們其實還沒搞懂。也許先做點「理解型的工作」，確認這真的是對的方向。

cards.pattern: We use words to establish a perspective. And if those are the words that are in your head, then you feel like [結果].
cards.quote: We use words to establish a perspective in a way of thinking about the world. And if those are the words that are in your head, then you feel like it's this war.
cards.zh: 我們用字詞來建立一種看世界的角度。如果你腦袋裡裝的是那些字，你就會覺得這是一場戰爭。
cards.why: 要改團隊文化卻不想講大道理時，從用詞下手：先給機制（字詞建立視角），再給後果（你會覺得這是戰爭）。整段沒有一句是罵人的，但把「攻佔市場、殲滅對手」這類講法的代價說清楚了。
swaps: The words we pick shape how we see the work.
If that's the vocabulary, that's the mindset we'll end up with.
cards.pmNote: 團隊慣用語是文化的先行指標；改語言比改流程便宜。
cards.episode: Jason Fried challenges your thinking on fundraising, goals, growth, and more

alts.quote: It's not that you actually are going to watch it the whole time, but it gives you a mental model and makes you feel in control.
alts.zh: 並不是說你真的會全程盯著看，而是它讓你有一個心智模型，讓你覺得自己掌握著方向盤。

alts.quote: You feel like a broken record, right? You're like, "I've said this 45 times." Turns out no one heard you the first 43.
alts.zh: 你會覺得自己像跳針的唱片：「這件事我講過四十五次了。」結果是前四十三次根本沒人聽進去。

alts.quote: So we try to build a team based on the needs of the work a bit, but then end up with a much smaller core.
alts.zh: 所以我們會盡量照工作本身的需求去組團隊，最後就會收斂成一個小很多的核心。

cards.pattern: Why are we always looking to [極端的對照組] to tell us how to run our business?
cards.quote: Why are we always looking to Navy SEALs to tell us how to run our business?
cards.zh: 我們為什麼老是要去看海豹部隊怎麼做，來決定自己公司該怎麼經營？
cards.why: 用一個誇張但真實存在的類比對象（海豹部隊）逼出情境落差——他後面那句 what you're doing is you're making B2B accounting software 才是真正的重擊。要拆掉「某某大廠都這樣做」的論點，先把那個對象的情境放大到荒謬即可。
swaps: Why do we keep borrowing playbooks from a completely different context?
That works for them because their stakes are nothing like ours.
cards.pmNote: 抄大公司做法前先問：他們的限制條件跟我們一樣嗎？
cards.episode: Jason Fried challenges your thinking on fundraising, goals, growth, and more

alts.quote: We're going to get to work on that, but can you tell me how are you measuring success? We want to make sure that what we do, you consider it successful.
alts.zh: 這件事我們會開始動工，不過可以先跟我說你是怎麼衡量成功的嗎？我們想確保做出來的東西，在你眼中算是成功。

alts.quote: It's one thing to say you're spending a lot of time looking outside the building. It's a whole other thing to hear from the places you don't normally hear from.
alts.zh: 說自己花很多時間在公司外面看，是一回事；真的去聽那些你平常聽不到的聲音，完全是另一回事。

alts.quote: They would write principles such as move fast and I would always be, "Everyone likes to move fast." It is not a good principle actually because nobody can really disagree with this reasonably.
alts.zh: 他們會寫「快速行動」這種原則，我都會回：誰不喜歡快速行動？那其實不是好的原則，因為沒有人會合理地反對它。

cards.pattern: I want to provide an alternative, not a competitor. If it's not an alternative, it doesn't need to exist.
cards.quote: If it's not an alternative, it doesn't need to exist.
cards.zh: 如果它不是一個「另一種選擇」，那它根本沒必要存在。
cards.why: 十個字的判準句，可以直接拿去砍需求：這個功能只是把別人做過的再做一次嗎？If it's not X, it doesn't need to exist 這個框架很萬用，換掉 X 就能定義任何團隊的存在門檻。
swaps: If it's the same thing again, why build it?
Unless it offers a genuinely different approach, it shouldn't ship.
cards.pmNote: differentiation 不是功能多寡，而是「是否提供一種不同的做法」。
cards.episode: Jason Fried challenges your thinking on fundraising, goals, growth, and more

alts.quote: When we talk about pricing strategies, we hear many buzzwords, and it's irrelevant. So when we take a step back and look at it, there's literally only three types of pricing strategies.
alts.zh: 談定價策略的時候會聽到一堆流行詞，那些都不重要。退一步看，定價策略其實就只有三種。

alts.quote: And then just the nature of the future is like we just don't know all the answers and that's okay. And then the right way to deal with that is to run as many experiments as possible.
alts.zh: 未來的本質就是我們不會知道所有答案，這沒關係。面對這件事正確的做法，是盡可能多跑一些實驗。

alts.quote: And then the third one's around really designing for clarity instead of cleverness.
alts.zh: 第三點是：為了「清楚」而設計，不是為了「聰明」而設計。

cards.pattern: People act like [X] is the worst thing that can happen to you. That's not even in the top 10.
cards.quote: People act like having a startup fail is the worst thing that can happen to you. And man, that's not even in the top 10.
cards.zh: 大家都把「創業失敗」講得像是人生最慘的事。老實說，那連前十名都排不進去。
cards.why: 先精準複述大家的預設（People act like...），再用一個帶數字的說法一口氣打掉（not even in the top 10）。not even in the top 10 比 that's not true 有力太多，因為它暗示你手上有一份更慘的清單——聽眾會等著你講下去。
swaps: Everyone treats that as the disaster scenario. It isn't even close.
That's not the worst outcome here — not by a long way.
cards.pmNote: 風險排序要重排：比「這個專案失敗」更糟的通常是「這個專案不死不活拖兩年」。
cards.episode: Reflections on a movement | Eric Ries (creator of the Lean Startup methodology)

alts.quote: So I have my definition of success I came up with years ago. Success is making the people who believed in you look brilliant. That's it.
alts.zh: 我幾年前想出了自己對成功的定義。成功就是：讓當初相信你的人看起來很有眼光。就這樣。

alts.quote: And one thing people make fun of me a lot for that I think is just a great example of extreme clarity is I never use bulleted lists because you can never refer to a bullet.
alts.zh: 有件事大家常笑我，但我覺得那正是「極度清楚」的最佳示範：我從來不用項目符號，因為你沒辦法指名某一個點。

alts.quote: I think the hardest thing for a founder, challenge is not optional. You're going to be challenged, but the suffering is optional.
alts.zh: 對創辦人來說最難的是：挑戰不是選項，你一定會被挑戰；但要不要痛苦，是選項。

cards.quote: Well, first of all, thank you for saying all that. That's giving me too much credit, but I like the idea that it's going to balance out the too little credit I ostensibly get somewhere else, that's great.
cards.zh: 首先謝謝你這樣說。你太抬舉我了——不過我喜歡這個說法，就當作是補回我在別的地方被低估的部分吧。
cards.why: 被公開稱讚時最難的是既不推掉也不照單全收。這裡的解法是先謙虛（too much credit），再用一個俏皮的會計比喻（跟別處被低估的互相抵銷）把讚美收下來。台灣人多半只做前半段，結果整段對話停在尷尬的推辭。
swaps: That's very generous — I'll take it to offset the times nobody noticed.
Too kind, but I'll happily bank that one.
cards.pmNote: 績效面談收到讚美時，接住它並接一句事實，比一直說 no no no 更有利。
cards.episode: Reflections on a movement | Eric Ries (creator of the Lean Startup methodology)

alts.quote: And I'm not saying that's the thing that made it happen, but I will say very quickly after that, we became very close partners and ultimately they acquired me.
alts.zh: 我不是說就是因為這件事才成的，但我可以說，那之後我們很快就變成很緊密的夥伴，最後他們把我們買下來了。

alts.quote: I was going to start by saying, I've been wrong about tons of things, but I buried those out back behind the shed.
alts.zh: 我本來想說，我看走眼的次數多到數不清啦，只是那些我都埋在後院工具間後面了。

alts.quote: Footnote, correlation versus causation. It's all put out there.
alts.zh: 附註一下：相關不等於因果。我先把話擺在這裡。

cards.pattern: Did they succeed because of [那個做法], or in spite of it?
cards.quote: Exactly. Did they succeed because of that or in spite of that?
cards.zh: 沒錯。他們成功是「因為」那個做法，還是「儘管」有那個做法？
cards.why: 十二個字拆掉所有的成功學案例。because of / in spite of 是一組現成的反義介系詞，擺在同一個問句裡就形成完整的二分——對方必須提出證據才能回答，而通常他沒有。會議上有人搬出大公司案例時的萬用回應。
swaps: Was that the cause, or did it work despite that?
How do we know that's what made the difference?
cards.pmNote: benchmark 的最大陷阱：把倖存者的所有行為都當成成功原因。
cards.episode: Reflections on a movement | Eric Ries (creator of the Lean Startup methodology)

alts.quote: Just because AI is all the rage and investors really like AI doesn't necessarily mean it should be front and center
alts.zh: AI 現在很紅、投資人也很愛，但這不代表它就該擺在最前面。

alts.quote: I don't like the word sprint because how do you feel after a sprint? Exhausted.
alts.zh: 我不喜歡「衝刺」這個詞——你衝刺完是什麼感覺？累爆。

alts.quote: I really try and stay away from better, because that's really hard to define, and better means something different to everyone.
alts.zh: 我盡量不用「比較好」這個字，因為它很難定義，而且每個人心中的「比較好」都不一樣。

cards.pattern: All the advice used to be of the form, "[名人] once did this thing, so if you do it too, you'll be like [名人]." Well, he also [一個明顯無關的細節].
cards.quote: All the advice used to be of the form, "Steve Jobs once did this thing, so if you do it too, you'll be like Steve Jobs." And it's like, well, he also wore the black turtleneck.
cards.zh: 以前的建議都是這個格式：「賈伯斯做過這件事，所以你也做，你就會變成賈伯斯。」我就想說，那他還穿黑色高領毛衣呢。
cards.why: 歸謬法的教科書範例：不否定前提，只是照著同一套邏輯再推一個明顯荒謬的結論。of the form 這個說法把對方的論點抽象成一個公式，等於先聲明「我要拆的是結構不是你這個人」，殺傷力大但衝突感低。
swaps: By that logic we should also copy their office layout.
That argument proves too much.
cards.pmNote: 案例式建議要先問：這個做法在他們身上生效的前提條件，我們有嗎？
cards.episode: Reflections on a movement | Eric Ries (creator of the Lean Startup methodology)

alts.quote: We all have heard the phrase, "If you're not growing, you're dying." Is that true or is that the kind of thing that investors use to make founders grow even when they shouldn't?
alts.zh: 我們都聽過那句「不成長就是等死」。那到底是真的，還是投資人拿來逼創辦人在不該成長的時候硬成長的說法？

alts.quote: It's funny that everyone complained about Google as this really, really smart, all-knowing LLM, and at the same time, they think they're dumb enough to fall for these guest posts.
alts.zh: 很好笑的是，大家一邊抱怨 Google 是那種超級聰明、什麼都知道的 LLM，一邊又覺得它笨到會被這些客座文章騙過去。

alts.quote: I think there's this cult of lean, scrappy, fast, throw away your product quickly, keep moving. And I think at some level it's true, but a lot of times I see teams give up too early.
alts.zh: 現在有一種「精實、克難、快、東西不行就丟、繼續往前」的教派。某種程度上它是對的，但我常看到團隊太早就放棄了。

cards.pattern: I'm not telling you that you should [做 X]. I'm just saying that is what it's called when [情況].
cards.quote: It's like, "well, I'm not telling you that you should pivot. I'm just saying that is what it's called when you change the strategy, but try to have fidelity to the vision."
cards.zh: 我不是在叫你去 pivot。我只是說，當你改策略但盡量守住願景的時候，那件事就叫這個名字。
cards.why: 把「描述」和「主張」明確切開，是化解無謂爭執最快的一招——對方以為你在逼他做某事，你只是在替一個現象命名。I'm not telling you... I'm just saying... 這組句型在任何被誤會成施壓的場合都能用。
swaps: I'm not recommending it — I'm just naming what's happening.
That's a description, not a proposal.
cards.pmNote: 團隊反彈某個名詞時，先確認他們反對的是名字還是那件事本身。
cards.episode: Reflections on a movement | Eric Ries (creator of the Lean Startup methodology)

alts.quote: I'm not saying that having a large market someday doesn't matter, of course it does eventually. But trying to be super pedantic about market size when it's a pre-seed company, it's just not something I'd put a lot of thought.
alts.zh: 我不是說市場總有一天要夠大這件事不重要，當然重要。但在一家 pre-seed 公司還在糾結市場規模算得多精確，我不會花太多心思在上面。

alts.quote: So I think it's an unnecessary addition, but maybe I'm just being protective of my original idea.
alts.zh: 我覺得那是多此一舉的補充，不過也可能只是我在護著自己原本的想法啦。

alts.quote: And it's kind of building a house that you want every brick in the house to match. And if you go and try and take some bricks from someone else's house and stick it in your house, it's probably going to not look very matched.
alts.zh: 這有點像蓋房子，你會希望每一塊磚都是搭的。如果你跑去人家家裡搬幾塊磚塞進自己家，看起來大概就是不搭。

cards.pattern: Please tell me the better [說法／做法] and popularize it and I'll use it. It's a great idea.
cards.quote: And I always write them back and say like, "Please tell me the better term and popularize it and I'll use it. It's a great idea."
cards.zh: 我都回信說：「請你告訴我更好的講法，然後把它推廣開，我就會改用。這主意很好。」
cards.why: 被批評時不辯護、直接把球丟回去，而且丟得很誠懇（It's a great idea 不是諷刺）。這招的實際效果是把「抱怨者」變成「要負責提案的人」，八成的人就此收手；真的提案的那兩成，你也真的得到了東西。
swaps: If you've got a better framing, I'll switch to it — genuinely.
Send me the better version and I'll use it.
cards.pmNote: 接住反對意見的高效版：把否定轉成一個具體的交付要求。
cards.episode: Reflections on a movement | Eric Ries (creator of the Lean Startup methodology)

alts.quote: Not to say it's not better, but just this is the structure of it, and it kind of sets you up for bragging.
alts.zh: 我不是說它不好，我只是在講它的結構——這個結構會把你逼到一直自誇。

alts.quote: On Twitter, you'll see people say, "Oh, it's the most expensive use of everyone's time," but it's like, "Yep. But there's 0% fidelity loss in that.
alts.zh: 推特上會有人說：「那是最貴的一種時間使用方式。」但我的回答是：「對啊。可是這樣資訊零失真。」

alts.quote: But, and this is the big but, no one has this at the early stages when they don't have a good idea and they don't have customers and it's objectively not working.
alts.zh: 但是——而且這是很大的一個「但是」——在最早期、還沒有好點子、沒有客戶、客觀上根本不 work 的時候，沒有人會有那種信念。

cards.quote: That's the whole ball game. No one had to lose in order for us to win.
cards.zh: 這才是重點。我們要贏，不需要有人輸。
cards.why: 十個字解散一場零和框架。當兩個團隊互相指責、或有人硬要把討論變成路線之爭時，這句話把賽局重新定義；前面加一句 That's the whole ball game（這才是關鍵）先立場再落句，節奏很穩。
swaps: This doesn't have to be zero-sum.
Our win doesn't require their loss.
cards.pmNote: 跨團隊卡住時先檢查是不是被架成零和；多數資源衝突其實有第三解。
cards.episode: Reflections on a movement | Eric Ries (creator of the Lean Startup methodology)

alts.quote: Anytime you have these disagreements that feel really thorny or they feel like a disagreement in values, that's a sign that you really have a disagreement in strategy.
alts.zh: 每當某個爭執特別棘手、感覺像是價值觀的衝突，那通常是個訊號：你們真正在吵的是策略。

alts.quote: Okay, guys, I'm seeing something happen here. Every time we get close to talking about something that's really painful, somebody makes a joke and all the energy disappears.
alts.zh: 好，我看到一個現象。每次我們快要談到真正痛的事情，就會有人開個玩笑，然後所有能量就消失了。

alts.quote: So how are you doing? I bet it's been a hard week.
alts.zh: 所以你還好嗎？我猜這禮拜很難熬吧。

cards.pattern: "[對方指控你漏掉的東西], you say?" — and you take notes — "Oh, interesting."
cards.quote: I'd be like, "X, Y, Z, you say?" And I'd be like taking notes, "Oh, interesting."
cards.zh: 我會說：「X、Y、Z 是嗎？」然後一邊做筆記，一邊說：「喔，有意思。」
cards.why: 「名詞＋you say?」是把對方的指控原封不動複誦回去的懶人句型，效果是降速＋表示你聽進去了。搭配動作（做筆記）跟一個不表態的評語（Oh, interesting），整段完全沒有防衛姿態，但也沒有答應任何事。
swaps: X and Y, you say? Let me write that down.
Interesting — say more about Z.
cards.pmNote: 使用者罵你少了什麼功能時，那份清單本身就是最便宜的 roadmap 訊號。
cards.episode: Reflections on a movement | Eric Ries (creator of the Lean Startup methodology)

alts.quote: So they would say, "Oh, your market's not big enough." And I would say, "It's going to be huge." And I'd add a new page in my pitch deck that said how big the market I believe was.
alts.zh: 他們會說：「你的市場不夠大。」我就說：「它會變超大。」然後我就在簡報裡加一頁，講我認為這市場有多大。

alts.quote: And I'd say it's not just that the budget's too small, it would be that they put all their eggs in one basket.
alts.zh: 我會說，問題不只是預算太小，而是他們把所有雞蛋放在同一個籃子裡。

alts.quote: Not to say it's not better, but just this is the structure of it, and it kind of sets you up for bragging.
alts.zh: 我不是說它不好，我只是在講它的結構——這個結構會把你逼到一直自誇。

cards.quote: So, I don't really care how high quality the initial MVP is because quality is defined by the customer. And if we don't know who our customer is, we literally don't know what the word quality means.
cards.zh: 所以第一版的 MVP 品質多高，我其實沒那麼在意，因為品質是由客戶定義的。如果我們連客戶是誰都不知道，我們根本不知道「品質」這兩個字是什麼意思。
cards.why: 把爭執從形容詞（夠不夠好）拉到定義層（誰有資格定義「好」），對方就沒得吵了。literally 在這裡不是口頭禪，是強調「這不是修辭，是字面意思」——用對的話很有力，用錯就變油。
swaps: Good is relative to a user. Which user?
We can't judge quality until we know who it's for.
cards.pmNote: craft 之爭多半是 target user 沒對齊之爭；先定義使用者再談品質標準。
cards.episode: Reflections on a movement | Eric Ries (creator of the Lean Startup methodology)

alts.quote: I don't like the word sprint because how do you feel after a sprint? Exhausted.
alts.zh: 我不喜歡「衝刺」這個詞——你衝刺完是什麼感覺？累爆。

alts.quote: I really try and stay away from better, because that's really hard to define, and better means something different to everyone.
alts.zh: 我盡量不用「比較好」這個字，因為它很難定義，而且每個人心中的「比較好」都不一樣。

alts.quote: You write this document and I'm sorry, who actually reads it? You know what I mean? I know it's painful, but it's like that.
alts.zh: 你寫了那份文件——不好意思，但到底有誰真的會讀？你懂我意思吧？我知道這很刺耳，但事實就是這樣。

cards.pattern: If you're asking whether you should [做重大決定], you probably know the answer already.
cards.quote: So first of all, if you're asking whether you should pivot or not you probably know the answer already.
cards.zh: 首先，如果你在問「該不該轉向」，你八成心裡已經有答案了。
cards.why: 不回答問題，改回答「你會問這個問題」這件事本身——這是教練式對話最高階的一手。probably 跟 already 都是緩衝，讓這句不至於太篤定；拿掉它們就會變成不禮貌的斷言。
swaps: The fact that it's a question probably answers it.
If you have to ask, you've mostly decided.
cards.pmNote: 評估 product-market fit 時，「有沒有餘裕開會討論這件事」本身就是訊號。
cards.episode: Reflections on a movement | Eric Ries (creator of the Lean Startup methodology)

alts.quote: And then I would say, what are you world-class at and how do you know that you're at that? And the second part is almost more important.
alts.zh: 然後我會問：你在什麼事情上是世界級的？你怎麼知道自己是？第二個問題其實更重要。

alts.quote: One of the things to ask oneself is what draws me to this position in the first place?
alts.zh: 有個可以問自己的問題是：當初到底是什麼把我吸引到這個位置的？

alts.quote: I'm asking them, "What do you do for joy? Are you doing something every single day that's bringing you joy in your life?" And if they say no, I'm like, "That's a problem."
alts.zh: 我會問他們：「你都做什麼讓自己開心？你每天有沒有一件事是讓你有樂趣的？」如果回答沒有，我就會說：「那這是個問題。」

cards.pattern: The fact that you have time to ask me this question already tells me the answer.
cards.quote: People call me sometimes they're like "I want to know if I have product market fit." Well, the fact that you have time to call me and ask me this question already tells me the answer.
cards.zh: 有人打給我說：「我想知道我們有沒有 PMF。」嗯，你有空打這通電話問我，這件事本身就給了答案。
cards.why: 把「行為」當證據，而不是把「說法」當證據——他沒聽你的數據，只看你有沒有空。這種以行為推論狀態的句型（the fact that you... already tells me...）在英文裡非常有份量，因為它不可反駁。
swaps: The fact that we're debating this tells me where we are.
If it were working, you wouldn't have time for this call.
cards.pmNote: PMF 的體感判準：真的抓到的時候，忙到沒空自我懷疑。
cards.episode: Reflections on a movement | Eric Ries (creator of the Lean Startup methodology)

alts.quote: What else can people do to become better storytellers in business? I know this is a big question, but let's see where it goes.
alts.zh: 在商業場合還可以怎麼把故事講得更好？我知道這題很大，但我們就看看會聊到哪。

alts.quote: What we ask people in general is we say, what do you think? We don't say, what do you know? We often say, what do you think?
alts.zh: 我們一般會問人「你怎麼想？」我們不會問「你知道什麼？」我們最常問的就是「你怎麼想？」

alts.quote: You ask questions like, what's the hardest you've ever worked to get something done and why? And that does differentiate a lot of people, a lot of people don't actually have a great answer to that.
alts.zh: 你可以問這種問題：你這輩子為了完成某件事最拚的一次是什麼？為什麼？這題真的很能分辨人，很多人其實答不太出來。

cards.pattern: Everyone go around the room and say: "If I could start this over again, the thing I wish we were doing was ___."
cards.quote: Now that you've agreed among yourselves that you're going to do that for a fixed period of time, everyone go around the room and say, "If I could start this company over again the thing I wish we were doing was."
cards.zh: 既然大家已經同意用一段固定的時間來試，那就一個一個講：「如果能重來一次，我希望我們在做的是＿＿＿。」
cards.why: 會議設計的兩個關鍵都在這句：go around the room（每個人都要講，不能躲）＋一個未完成的句子（不必自己組織語言，填空就好）。而且用假設語氣包裝，講出「我早就想換方向」不會像背叛。
swaps: Let's go around: if we were starting today, what would we be building?
Everyone finish this sentence — the thing I'd rather we were doing is...
cards.pmNote: 重大轉向前先做一輪匿名或輪流表態，常會發現大家早就想同一件事但都不敢先開口。
cards.episode: Reflections on a movement | Eric Ries (creator of the Lean Startup methodology)

alts.quote: "I need 20 minutes of focused time to interrogate something that I've done. We're not going to talk. I'm literally going to force us into a room or Zoom.
alts.zh: 「我需要二十分鐘的專注時間來拷問我做的東西。我們不用講話。我就是要把大家關進一個會議室或 Zoom。」

alts.quote: We start all of our meetings with what are you scared to say in our business?
alts.zh: 我們每場會議都從這個問題開始：在這家公司裡，你不敢講的是什麼？

alts.quote: I'm going to come back to what you've learned about what makes super successful PMs, what makes you really successful. I want to take a tangent to Zuck.
alts.zh: 成功 PM 的特質這題我等一下會繞回來。我想先岔題聊一下 Zuck。

cards.quote: And one of my main takeaways of that entire process is that it's always too early until it's too late.
cards.zh: 我從那整段過程裡學到最重要的一件事是：這種事永遠都「太早」，直到它「太遲」。
cards.why: 七個字裝下一個完整的機制：每一次單獨看都太早，加總起來就變成太遲。too early / too late 的對仗讓它像諺語一樣好記，要推動任何「現在做沒感覺、以後做來不及」的事（技術債、治理、文件化）都可以直接引用。
swaps: Every single time it's premature — right up until it's impossible.
There's never a good moment, and then the moment's gone.
cards.pmNote: 架構債、資安、治理這類事沒有「剛剛好的時機」，要用日曆而不是用時機來排。
cards.episode: Reflections on a movement | Eric Ries (creator of the Lean Startup methodology)

alts.quote: I'm just trying to argue this advice applied to a startup that's too early is actively not helpful.
alts.zh: 我只是想主張：把這套建議套在太早期的新創身上，是「主動有害」而不只是沒用。

alts.quote: In a world where it's easier to build things, it's more important to make sure that your time is spent figuring out what you should be building in the first place.
alts.zh: 在一個「東西越來越好做」的世界裡，更重要的是先確保你把時間花在想清楚「到底該做什麼」。

alts.quote: And so ever since then, we've been automating jobs and creating new jobs, and you can always see the job that's going to go away, and you don't know the new job because it doesn't exist yet.
alts.zh: 從那時候到現在，我們一直在自動化舊工作、也一直在長出新工作；而你永遠看得到那個要消失的工作，看不到新的，因為它還不存在。

cards.pattern: Don't ask them "Should I do it?" Ask them "Can you give me the pros and cons of doing it?"
cards.quote: And don't ask them, "Should I do it?" Ask them, "Tell me for each thing, can you give me the pros and cons of doing it?"
cards.zh: 不要問他們「我該不該做？」要問他們「每一個做法的利弊分別是什麼？」
cards.why: 同一件事、兩種問法，收到的東西完全不同：問「該不該」拿到的是對方的偏好（而且通常是最保守那個），問「利弊」拿到的是你自己判斷所需的材料。Don't ask X, ask Y 的對照結構讓建議很好記也很好轉述。
swaps: I'm not asking for a recommendation — I want the trade-offs.
Walk me through the upside and downside of each option.
cards.pmNote: 找專家要的是選項的成本結構，決策權留在自己身上。
cards.episode: Reflections on a movement | Eric Ries (creator of the Lean Startup methodology)

alts.quote: So especially when you're meeting with a new engineering team for the first time, actually ask them, what is one thing I can do to help you this week?
alts.zh: 尤其是第一次跟新的工程團隊碰面時，真的去問他們：這禮拜我可以幫上哪一件事？

alts.quote: I picked you because I really trust you to be a sound source of truthful advice and give me some feedback. So I really value that. Do you mind spending a couple of minutes and just giving me some thoughts on this?
alts.zh: 我會找你，是因為我真的很信任你會給我誠實的建議跟回饋，這對我很有價值。可以請你花個幾分鐘，給我一點想法嗎？

alts.quote: go reach out to a PM and ask how you can make their day easier
alts.zh: 直接去找一個 PM，問他你可以幫他分擔什麼、讓他今天輕鬆一點。

cards.quote: Thank you for advising me on the pros and cons. You work for me, you're my lawyer. I'd like to implement this thing.
cards.zh: 謝謝你把利弊分析給我。你是替我工作的、你是我的律師。我決定要做這件事。
cards.why: 聽完專業建議之後仍然拍板的標準三步：先謝（承認對方的專業）、再定位（誰對誰負責）、最後宣布（I'd like to，不是 I want）。台灣人最常卡在第二步，結果被顧問或資深同事的偏好牽著走。
swaps: I appreciate the analysis. I've made the call — let's go with this.
Noted, and I'd still like to move forward with it.
cards.pmNote: 顧問／專家給的是選項與風險，決策責任仍在 DRI 身上，這個界線要講出來。
cards.episode: Reflections on a movement | Eric Ries (creator of the Lean Startup methodology)

alts.quote: This is a tricky one. So, you're right that it's implied, but the thing is, in real life, if you make a commitment and you get alignment that we are going to spend six weeks of engineering time building this thing…
alts.zh: 這題很麻煩。你說得沒錯，那個確實是言下之意，但問題是，現實裡如果你已經做出承諾、也拿到共識要花六週工程時間……

alts.quote: So much so that the company was number one on Glassdoor's best place to work, I was the number one CEO on Glassdoor, and as I look back at that, I'm not sure that's a good thing.
alts.zh: 誇張到公司在 Glassdoor 拿最佳職場第一名、我自己是第一名的 CEO，可是現在回頭看，我不確定那是件好事。

alts.quote: That one always makes me laugh because I was thinking, "Do you know how many hours a week I'd need to work if that was my only job?"
alts.zh: 這種說法每次都讓我笑出來，因為我心想：如果那真的是我唯一的工作，你知道我一週只需要上多少小時的班嗎？

cards.pattern: You can't have it both ways. Are you [自己吹的那個大話]? Well, then you have [對應的責任].
cards.quote: It's like you can't have it both ways, buddy. Are you the Superman who's reordering the whole world to your whim? Well, then you have moral responsibility for the outcomes.
cards.zh: 你不能兩邊都要。你到底是不是那個要照自己意思重排整個世界的超人？是的話，結果的道德責任你就得扛。
cards.why: 抓住對方前後不一致（募資時說要改變世界、被追責時說只是個小廠商），用 You can't have it both ways 一句封住，再用一個 Are you...? 問句逼他選邊。這是英文裡處理雙重標準最直接的句型，語氣重，用在有把握的場合。
swaps: You can't claim both of those at once.
Pick one — either it's transformative or it's just a tool.
cards.pmNote: 對外宣稱的野心大小，會決定外界對你的責任標準，兩者要同時規劃。
cards.episode: Reflections on a movement | Eric Ries (creator of the Lean Startup methodology)

alts.quote: To me, I think it's a great accelerant when it's already working, but it can't fix it if people don't want to talk about your product.
alts.zh: 對我來說，那在本來就跑得動的時候是很好的加速器，但如果根本沒人想談論你的產品，它救不了你。

alts.quote: It's not LLMs to be clear, but there's engines like Stockfish these days that are just dramatically better than the top grand masters in the world.
alts.zh: 講清楚，那不是 LLM，但現在有像 Stockfish 那種引擎，已經遠遠強過世界頂尖大師。

alts.quote: First let's examine the counterfactual, right? So let's start with the opposite of your question and say, "How would the world be sadder if we all just gave up on this?"
alts.zh: 我們先看反面情況吧。從你問題的相反面開始想：如果大家乾脆全都放棄這件事，世界會變得多糟？

cards.pattern: Given that it's not knowable what's going to happen, the thing that makes sense is to pick actions today that make sense in a wide variety of future scenarios.
cards.quote: The thing that makes sense is to pick actions today that make ethical sense in a wide variety of future scenarios and do those.
cards.zh: 比較合理的做法是：挑那些在很多種未來版本裡都說得通的行動，今天就去做。
cards.why: 承認不確定卻不癱瘓的標準解法——不是預測未來，而是找「哪個未來成立都不會後悔」的動作。a wide variety of future scenarios 這個說法很好用，因為它把「我不知道」轉成一個具體的篩選條件。
swaps: Let's do the things that hold up whichever way this goes.
We can't predict it, so let's pick no-regret moves.
cards.pmNote: 高度不確定時的決策原則：no-regret moves 優先，可逆決策快做、不可逆決策慢做。
cards.episode: Reflections on a movement | Eric Ries (creator of the Lean Startup methodology)

alts.quote: I do want to apply a pretty severe caveat here though, which is, a decision log is not a replacement for building products. It's a additional complimentary thing that you can be doing on your own.
alts.zh: 不過我要加一個很重的但書：決策日誌不能取代真的去做產品。它只是你自己可以額外做的補充。

alts.quote: And I guess it's kind of an embarrassing thing to say because everyone who's a startup founder thinks, my startup moves super fast and the talent bar is super high.
alts.zh: 說這話其實有點難為情，因為每個新創創辦人都覺得「我們超快、人才標準超高」。

alts.quote: And I don't know how much this matters in the future now, but there's this just elegance to functional programming and thinking in types, and this is just the way that I code, and the way that I can't stop thinking about coding.
alts.zh: 我不知道這件事在未來還有多重要，但函數式程式設計跟用型別思考就是有一種優雅，這就是我寫程式的方式，我沒辦法不這樣想。

cards.quote: Great. Tell me a situation where that best practice would not be applicable.
cards.zh: 很好。那你跟我說一個「這個最佳實務不適用」的情境。
cards.why: 先給一個廉價的肯定（Great.）再丟出真正的問題，落差本身就是壓力測試。這題測的不是知識而是理解深度——真的會用的人講得出邊界，只背過的人講不出來（他說大部分人答不出來）。面試、招募、找顧問都適用。
swaps: When would you not do it that way?
Where does that framework break down?
cards.pmNote: 面試判斷「真懂 vs 背過」的通用題：請對方講出方法論的失效條件。
cards.episode: Reflections on a movement | Eric Ries (creator of the Lean Startup methodology)

alts.quote: I asked them, think about one of the biggest mistakes you've made, truly, the more painful the better. And tell me what the mistake was.
