alts.zh: 我會請對方想一個自己犯過最大的錯——說真的，越痛越好——然後告訴我那個錯是什麼。

alts.quote: If you can tell me what you're working on and ask me at the end of a meeting specifically what I noticed then that is much better."
alts.zh: 如果你可以先跟我說你在忙什麼，然後在會議結束時具體問我注意到了什麼，那效果好得多。

alts.quote: What else can people do to become better storytellers in business? I know this is a big question, but let's see where it goes.
alts.zh: 在商業場合還可以怎麼把故事講得更好？我知道這題很大，但我們就看看會聊到哪。

cards.pattern: Not to be too [哲學／戲劇化／悲觀] about this, but it really goes right to the issue of [一個很大的主題].
cards.quote: and not to be too spiritual about this, but it really goes right to the issue of ego identification
cards.zh: 不是想把這件事講得太玄，但它真的直接踩到「自我認同」這個問題。
cards.why: 在商業場合要拋出一個偏哲學／情緒／價值觀的主張時，這個前綴先替聽眾說出他們的顧慮（你是不是要開始講心靈雞湯了），拿到許可後再講。not to be too X about this, but... 可以換成 not to get too philosophical / not to be dramatic，是英文會議裡極高頻的軟化裝置。
swaps: Not to get too philosophical, but this is really about identity.
At the risk of sounding dramatic, this goes deeper than process.
cards.pmNote: 把「情感／認同」議題帶進工作討論前先加一層 hedge，接受度會高很多。
cards.episode: Reflections on a movement | Eric Ries (creator of the Lean Startup methodology)

alts.quote: Most writers, most course instructors spend too much time on the what and the why and not enough time on how.
alts.zh: 大部分寫作者、大部分課程講師，都花太多時間在「是什麼」跟「為什麼」，花太少時間在「怎麼做」。

alts.quote: So here's the really wonderful thing about moving from a coercive model to really, I guess you could say a model of curiosity, right? You want to be curious, not coercive.
alts.zh: 從一個高壓的模式，換成一個好奇的模式——你要的是好奇，不是強迫。

alts.quote: the best way to get feedback from people is not by asking what they think, but to put something concrete in front of them and then have them react to it, right?
alts.zh: 要拿到回饋，最好的方式不是問人家怎麼想，而是先擺一個具體的東西在他面前，讓他反應，對吧？

cards.pattern: It's felt like [大家的直覺]. But actually, if you look for evidence of that, you basically can't find it.
cards.quote: It's felt like we've been in a time of great technological change. But actually, if you look for actually evidence of that, in statistical evidence of that, analytical evidence of that, you basically can't find it.
cards.zh: 大家都覺得這幾十年科技變化很快。但你真的去找證據——統計上的、分析上的——其實根本找不到。
cards.why: 先用 it's felt like 把對方的直覺說出來（而且說得很同情），再用 but actually + if you look for evidence 把戰場從「感覺」換到「證據」。攻擊的是資料不是人，所以對方不會防衛。
swaps: The perception is that X. The data tells a different story
It feels true, but I couldn't find anything that backs it up
cards.pmNote: 推翻團隊共識前，先把共識講得比對方還準，接受度會高很多。
cards.episode: Marc Andreessen: The real AI boom hasn’t even started yet

alts.quote: It's one thing to say you're spending a lot of time looking outside the building. It's a whole other thing to hear from the places you don't normally hear from.
alts.zh: 說自己花很多時間在公司外面看，是一回事；真的去聽那些你平常聽不到的聲音，完全是另一回事。

alts.quote: We're all sitting talking about it, and Tate says, "It's a low margin reseller, one time sells." "You can say dotcom all you like, it's a low margin reseller."
alts.zh: 大家在車上討論，Tate 說：「它就是個低毛利的經銷商，一次性買賣。你要講幾次『.com』都可以，它還是個低毛利經銷商。」

alts.quote: You write this document and I'm sorry, who actually reads it? You know what I mean? I know it's painful, but it's like that.
alts.zh: 你寫了那份文件——不好意思，但到底有誰真的會讀？你懂我意思吧？我知道這很刺耳，但事實就是這樣。

cards.pattern: Everything I've just described is just a straightforward extrapolation of [基本原理]. I'm not making any bold predictions.
cards.quote: And again, everything I've just described, by the way, is just a very straightforward extrapolation of very basic economics. I'm not making any bold predictions of what I just said.
cards.zh: 我剛剛講的這一整串，其實只是最基本的經濟學往下推而已。我沒有在做什麼大膽預測。
cards.why: 講完一個聽起來很狂的結論後，馬上把它降級成「這只是常識往下推」。先自己拆掉「你太樂觀／你在唬爛」這顆炸彈，對方就很難用「這只是你的猜測」來反駁。
swaps: None of this requires a leap—it's just following the numbers
I'm not predicting anything exotic here, just applying the basics
cards.pmNote: 提大膽提案時，把推論鏈拆成「每一步都很無聊」，比把結論講得很興奮更有說服力。
cards.episode: Marc Andreessen: The real AI boom hasn’t even started yet

alts.quote: The way I think about this that I've heard well described is just there's no silver bullets, just many lead bullets.
alts.zh: 我對這件事的想法——我聽過一個說得很好的講法——就是沒有銀色子彈，只有很多顆鉛彈。

alts.quote: If I told you, I'm going to build an autonomous vehicle, and I said our team is 10 people, you should rightfully say, Varun, you're not serious. And you'd be right.
alts.zh: 如果我跟你說我要做自駕車，然後說團隊只有 10 個人，你完全應該回我：Varun，你不是認真的吧。而且你會是對的。

alts.quote: I've learned that some of the companies we admire are not working the way we are, and maybe we should try this.
alts.zh: 我發現我們很欣賞的那幾家公司，做事方式跟我們並不一樣，也許我們可以試試看他們的做法。

cards.pattern: I've been wrong about tons of things, but I [幽默地說自己把證據藏起來了].
cards.quote: I was going to start by saying, I've been wrong about tons of things, but I buried those out back behind the shed.
cards.zh: 我本來想說，我看走眼的次數多到數不清啦，只是那些我都埋在後院工具間後面了。
cards.why: 被大力稱讚時，母語者不會謙虛地否認，而是用一個誇張的玩笑承認自己也有很多失敗——既接住讚美又不顯得自滿。台灣人習慣講「沒有啦哪有」，在英語職場會顯得沒自信。
swaps: I've been wrong plenty of times too—those just don't make the highlight reel
For every one of those there are five you haven't heard about
cards.episode: Marc Andreessen: The real AI boom hasn’t even started yet

alts.quote: Well, first of all, thank you for saying all that. That's giving me too much credit, but I like the idea that it's going to balance out the too little credit I ostensibly get somewhere else, that's great.
alts.zh: 首先謝謝你這樣說。你太抬舉我了——不過我喜歡這個說法，就當作是補回我在別的地方被低估的部分吧。

alts.quote: Looking back, my career has been a little bit like a bingo card. I've always been looking to fill in boxes I didn't have filled because I felt like that would make me a better professional.
alts.zh: 回頭看，我的職涯有點像一張賓果卡。我一直在補那些還沒被填滿的格子，因為我覺得那會讓我變成更好的專業工作者。

alts.quote: What I didn't tell is that there was at least six years of accidental work behind this. I started a blog six years before... Actually, I've always been blogging since I graduated.
alts.zh: 我沒講的是，這背後至少有六年、不是刻意規劃的累積。我在那之前六年就開始寫部落格了——其實我從畢業就一直在寫。

cards.pattern: I've come much more around to [某人]'s point of view. I would argue that quite a bit differently today than I did.
cards.quote: By the way, I will say on the Peter one, I've come much more around to Peter's point of view. I would probably argue that one quite a bit differently today than I did, and I would give his view, I think, a lot more credit.
cards.zh: 順帶一提，Peter 那場辯論，我現在比較站到他那邊了。同樣的題目今天要我講，我會講得很不一樣，也會給他的看法多很多分數。
cards.why: 改變立場的三段式：come around to someone's view（承認位移）→ argue it differently today（把改變歸給時間而不是自己蠢）→ give his view more credit（給對方加分）。全程沒有一句「我錯了」，但誠意十足。
swaps: I've moved a long way toward his position on that
If I were making that argument today, I'd frame it very differently
cards.pmNote: 公開改變立場是資深訊號；重點是把新資訊當主詞，而不是把自己當被告。
cards.episode: Marc Andreessen: The real AI boom hasn’t even started yet

alts.quote: I think that's the biggest major fundamental 180 degree change that I've changed my mind on, but I changed my mind all the time.
alts.zh: 那大概是我立場整個一百八十度翻過來、最大的一次改變，不過我本來就一天到晚在改想法。

alts.quote: No, I mean I've shared that enough, but I used to not talk about it before because I used to think that I would get some sympathy for that.
alts.zh: 不會，這件事我講得夠多了。不過我以前不太提，因為我當時覺得講了會被同情。

alts.quote: I agree, I've changed my mind. You're right. You just saw it in a way that I hadn't seen.
alts.zh: 我同意，我改變想法了。你是對的，你看到的角度是我原本沒看到的。

cards.pattern: Everybody wants to talk about [表層現象], but really, what you want to look at is [底層單位].
cards.quote: Everybody wants to talk about job loss, but really, what you want to look at is task loss, the tasks changing.
cards.zh: 大家都在談工作被取代，但真正該看的是「任務」被取代——是任務在變。
cards.why: 一句話把討論的分析單位換掉，這是資深的人最常用的一招。Everybody wants to talk about X 不否定對方，只說那不是最有用的切面；whatt you want to look at 又把建議包成中性的「該看的」而不是「你錯了」。
swaps: The conversation is about X, but the unit that actually moves is Y
I'd reframe it: it's less about X, more about Y
cards.pmNote: framing 決定討論走向——換掉分析單位，比在原本的單位上贏辯論有效十倍。
cards.episode: Marc Andreessen: The real AI boom hasn’t even started yet

alts.quote: We call this the champion in the account because this person, their job is to get consensus and champion the deal across everybody, including their boss, who's the actual economic buyer, the person that writes the check.
alts.zh: 我們把這個人叫做「客戶內部的擁護者」，因為他的工作就是在所有人之間建立共識、替這筆案子背書，包括他的老闆——那個真正掏錢的經濟決策者。

alts.quote: Most people don't forget their talk. They forget the transitions in their talk.
alts.zh: 大部分人不是忘記整場講稿，是忘記段落之間怎麼接。

alts.quote: One is people set this goal, I want to be promoted the next thing, or I want to lead this big project. And those are bad goals, because it's not in your control. A good goal is what you can do.
alts.zh: 有一種是設「我要升到下一級」或「我要主導那個大專案」。這些是壞目標，因為不在你的掌控裡。好目標是你自己做得到的事。

cards.pattern: I could have been pretty good at [A], or pretty good at [B], but being [A] who understood [B] made me spectacularly great at [成果].
cards.quote: He said, "I could have been a pretty good cartoonist or I could have been pretty good at business, but the fact that I was a cartoonist who understood business made me spectacularly great at making Dilbert."
cards.zh: 他說：「我可以當個還不錯的漫畫家，也可以當個還不錯的商業人，但因為我是一個懂商業的漫畫家，才讓我把呆伯特做到無人能及。」
cards.why: pretty good at A / pretty good at B / spectacularly great at 的三拍節奏，把「跨界」這個抽象概念變成可以量的落差。母語者很愛用 the fact that I was X who understood Y 這個結構來描述自己的獨特定位。
swaps: Either alone would have been fine; the combination is what made it work
It took someone with both skills to pull that off
cards.pmNote: 談職涯定位時，講「兩個領域的交集」比講「我很強」更難被反駁。
cards.episode: Marc Andreessen: The real AI boom hasn’t even started yet

alts.quote: So I have my definition of success I came up with years ago. Success is making the people who believed in you look brilliant. That's it.
alts.zh: 我幾年前想出了自己對成功的定義。成功就是：讓當初相信你的人看起來很有眼光。就這樣。

alts.quote: It doesn't matter if you think Bloomberg or Trump should be president. Do you think everyone should have access to great education? Most people would say yes.
alts.zh: 你覺得該讓 Bloomberg 還是 Trump 當總統，都無所謂。你覺得每個人都該有機會受好的教育嗎？大多數人會說會。

alts.quote: And I'm looking at this, and suddenly I realized, 'Oh, this speech, nobody cares about this. This is not a good speech. This is terrible.'
alts.zh: 我看著畫面，突然意識到：「喔，這篇講稿根本沒人在乎。這不是一篇好講稿。這爛透了。」

cards.pattern: He used to tell people, "[一句格言]". What that means essentially is [白話翻譯].
cards.quote: He used to tell people, he said, "The key for career planning is," he said, "don't be fungible." He's an economist and so that was economic speaking. What that means essentially is don't be replaceable.
cards.zh: 他都跟人說：「職涯規劃的關鍵就是，別讓自己可被替換。」他是經濟學家，所以講得比較術語。白話講就是：別讓自己是可以隨便換掉的那個人。
cards.why: 先丟術語再自己翻譯，是英語會議裡最實用的一組動作：術語讓你顯得懂行，緊接著的 what that means essentially is 讓沒跟上的人不必舉手發問，等於幫全場保住面子。
swaps: In plain English, that just means...
The non-jargon version of that is...
cards.pmNote: 用了任何專有名詞，下一句就要自己翻譯——這是主持會議的基本禮貌。
cards.episode: Marc Andreessen: The real AI boom hasn’t even started yet

alts.quote: He said that, "Hey, CJ, I'm hearing that a lot of people don't really understand why we are working on what we are working on," and that was it.
alts.zh: 他說：「欸 CJ，我聽到不少人其實不太明白，我們為什麼在做我們正在做的事。」就這樣，講完了。

alts.quote: And I would just say generally, until you see pull, just people pulling the product out of your hands, you don't want to be spending money.
alts.zh: 我會說一個通則：在你看到「拉力」之前——就是人家把產品從你手上搶走那種——你都不該開始花錢。

alts.quote: People often think that I get hired into later stage companies because I'm supposed to teach them how to operate like a big company, and in fact, I say I'm hired to remind them they can operate like a startup.
alts.zh: 大家常以為，公司找我去後期階段是要我教他們怎麼像大公司一樣運作；但其實我都說，我是被找去提醒他們，他們還可以像新創一樣運作。

cards.pattern: There's this rush to judgment upfront where people say, "It's therefore obvious that [X]."
cards.quote: There's this rush to judgment upfront where people say, "Oh, it's therefore obvious that X, Y, Z. It's obvious that the moats are going to be in this area of the technology, but not in this other area."
cards.zh: 一開始大家都會急著下判斷，說「所以顯然就是 X、Y、Z」、「顯然護城河一定在這一塊，不會在那一塊」。
cards.why: 不點名任何人，而是把對手的立場模仿出來（用 people say + 引號），再讓那個語氣自己聽起來太滿。這比直接說「你太武斷」安全得多，是英語裡最常見的軟性反駁。
swaps: There's a lot of premature certainty around this
People jump straight to "and therefore obviously..."
cards.pmNote: pre-mortem 時先蒐集大家的「顯然」，那通常就是最大的風險清單。
cards.episode: Marc Andreessen: The real AI boom hasn’t even started yet

alts.quote: On Twitter, you'll see people say, "Oh, it's the most expensive use of everyone's time," but it's like, "Yep. But there's 0% fidelity loss in that.
alts.zh: 推特上會有人說：「那是最貴的一種時間使用方式。」但我的回答是：「對啊。可是這樣資訊零失真。」

alts.quote: So they would say, "Oh, your market's not big enough." And I would say, "It's going to be huge." And I'd add a new page in my pitch deck that said how big the market I believe was.
alts.zh: 他們會說：「你的市場不夠大。」我就說：「它會變超大。」然後我就在簡報裡加一頁，講我認為這市場有多大。

alts.quote: But before that, I think getting to product-market fit, obviously there's a lot of methodology for doing it today that might make it a bit easier for people, but I still think it's fairly random and pretty dang hard.
alts.zh: 在那之前——我覺得要走到 PMF，現在當然有很多方法論可能讓大家輕鬆一點，但我還是認為它相當隨機，而且真的很難。

cards.pattern: I'll just run this as a thought experiment and you can see what you think, but [問題].
cards.quote: I'll just run this as a thought experiment and you can see what you think on this, but it's like, are AI models themselves defensible?
cards.zh: 我把它當成一個思想實驗丟出來，你自己判斷——AI 模型本身到底有沒有護城河？
cards.why: 先把提案降級成「思想實驗」，等於預先聲明「我還沒押注在這上面」，別人反駁時就不是在打你的臉。you can see what you think 又把決定權交還給對方，開會拋新方向時最安全的開場。
swaps: Let me float something and you tell me if it holds up
Purely as a hypothetical—what if...
cards.pmNote: roadmap 會議第一次拋新方向，用「思想實驗」包裝可以避免太早被逼表態。
cards.episode: Marc Andreessen: The real AI boom hasn’t even started yet

alts.quote: I actually think it's easier. Spicy take.
alts.zh: 我其實覺得更容易。這個看法比較嗆。

alts.quote: The old way I think is shitty. I think it's broken, and I haven't found anything out there that is innovating on this.
alts.zh: 舊的做法我覺得很爛。我覺得它是壞的，而且我沒看到市面上有任何人在改良它。

alts.quote: I sat for about a half a day and I thought, I think I can help here, drew out an org chart, put my name on the top, walked into my boss's office and said, "This is one potential solve of your marketing organization question."
alts.zh: 我想了大概半天，覺得我應該幫得上忙，就畫了一張組織圖，把自己放在最上面，走進我主管辦公室說：「這是你那個行銷組織問題的其中一個解法。」

cards.quote: And so again, it's just like, I don't know, my view is I need to put a big discount on my forecasting ability on this one.
cards.zh: 所以這一題，我的看法是：我得把自己的預測能力先打一個大折扣。
cards.why: 用金融語彙 put a discount on 講自謙，聽起來像在做風險定價而不是在示弱。這種「用專業框架講自己的限制」是英語職場承認不確定最漂亮的方式。
swaps: I'd weight my own prediction pretty lightly here
My track record doesn't buy me much confidence on this one
cards.pmNote: 對外給預估時主動標示信心水準，比事後解釋為什麼估錯便宜得多。
cards.episode: Marc Andreessen: The real AI boom hasn’t even started yet

alts.quote: I don't know how many customer support folks we have, but it's not very many, 30, 40, I'm not sure, way smaller than you would have at any comparable company, and it's because we've automated a lot of our flows.
alts.zh: 我不知道我們有多少客服人力，但沒有很多，三十、四十吧，我不確定，總之比任何同等規模的公司都少很多，因為我們把很多流程自動化了。

alts.quote: And I don't know when it's going to saturate and nobody else knows either, but when that happens, the next frontier is the physical world.
alts.zh: 我不知道它什麼時候會飽和，別人也都不知道，但等它飽和的那天，下一個戰場就是實體世界。

alts.quote: So I think it has to come with a place of knowing that you don't know everything and humility to say, "Hey, I need help." And it actually earns you a lot more credit than you think.
alts.zh: 我覺得這要來自一個認知：你不可能什麼都懂，還要有那個謙虛去說「嘿，我需要幫忙」。而且這其實比你想像的更會替你加分。

cards.pattern: I don't think I can predict that. I think a much better use of my time is [替代做法].
cards.quote: It's like, I don't think I can predict that. I think a much better use of my time is being very flexible and adaptable at a time like this.
cards.zh: 我不覺得我預測得了那個。我覺得我的時間花在保持彈性、快速調整上，回報高得多。
cards.why: 拒絕回答一個問題時，不要只說做不到，要立刻交出你打算改做什麼。a much better use of my time 把「我不做」翻譯成「我在做更有價值的事」，主導權還在自己手上。
swaps: That's not a call I can make—what I can control is...
Rather than guess at that, I'd rather spend the time on...
cards.pmNote: 擋需求的標準句型：先說做不到什麼，再說改做什麼，永遠不要只留前半段。
cards.episode: Marc Andreessen: The real AI boom hasn’t even started yet

alts.quote: I don't think it's particularly productive to say, "Well, is it 20% bigger than the internet or 100%?" Those aren't productive conversations.
alts.zh: 去爭「它比網路大 20% 還是 100%」我覺得沒什麼意義，那種對話不會有產出。

alts.quote: But if we're not going to be good at a task and we think the open source is better or Anthropic's better, we'll go and just use the open source or Anthropic.
alts.zh: 但如果我們在某件事上就是做不好，而我們認為開源或 Anthropic 更好，那我們就直接去用開源或 Anthropic。

alts.quote: For what it's worth, we're not really motivated to try to create a self-improvement empire. This is not our full-time job. We just hope it works for you and is useful.
alts.zh: 順帶一提，我們並不是想搞一個自我成長帝國。這不是我們的正職。我們只是希望這對你有用。

cards.pattern: The nature of [X] is we just don't know all the answers, and that's okay. The right way to deal with that is [做法].
cards.quote: And then just the nature of the future is like we just don't know all the answers and that's okay. And then the right way to deal with that is to run as many experiments as possible.
cards.zh: 未來的本質就是我們不會知道所有答案，這沒關係。面對這件事正確的做法，是盡可能多跑一些實驗。
cards.why: and that's okay 這三個字是整句的關鍵——它把不確定從問題變成前提，後面的策略才站得住。少了它，「我們不知道」只會讓人焦慮。
swaps: We're not going to have certainty here, and that's fine—so we optimize for learning speed
Given we can't know, the strategy is to buy information cheaply
cards.pmNote: 策略就是取捨：不確定性高的時候，選項價值大於準確度。
cards.episode: Marc Andreessen: The real AI boom hasn’t even started yet

alts.quote: I think so many folks don't know where to begin on starting a startup, and my tactical advice is start doing customer validation first versus building a PowerPoint deck.
alts.zh: 很多人根本不知道創業要從哪裡開始，我很具體的建議是：先去做客戶驗證，而不是先做一份簡報。

alts.quote: Often people have a mission that's kind of on the wall somewhere and then what they're actually doing and the way they actually make money and the way people actually spend their time is in a very, very different direction from that original mission.
alts.zh: 很多公司的使命就掛在牆上某個地方，可是他們真正在做的事、真正賺錢的方式、大家真正把時間花在哪，跟那個使命的方向差超多。

alts.quote: We usually say how you charge is way more important than how much you charge.
alts.zh: 我們常說：「怎麼收費」比「收多少」重要得多。

cards.pattern: I don't think there's any reason to assume that [大家默認的上限] is the cap on anything.
cards.quote: And the reason for that is, I don't think there's any reason to assume that human skill level is the cap on anything.
cards.zh: 原因是：我不覺得有任何理由要假設「人類的能力水準」就是天花板。
cards.why: I don't think there's any reason to assume 把舉證責任推回給對方——不是我要證明可以更高，是你要證明為什麼不行。這是拆隱含假設最省力的一句。
swaps: Who says that's the ceiling?
Nothing forces that number to be the limit
cards.pmNote: first principles 的入口通常是一句「這個上限是誰定的？」
cards.episode: Marc Andreessen: The real AI boom hasn’t even started yet

alts.quote: I don't think there's any one thing that has happened. I think that a lot of times people ascribe a lot of momentum to a one time change or a single person.
alts.zh: 我不覺得有哪一件事是關鍵。很多時候大家會把一整段動能歸給某一次改動、或某一個人。

alts.quote: I think people assume that there's a much more detailed semantic understanding of everybody's interests and preferences in the algorithm than there is.
alts.zh: 我覺得大家會以為演算法對每個人的興趣和偏好，有一套比實際上細膩得多的語意理解。

alts.quote: I challenge it and I say, "First of all, I don't think there's evidence for that. Is there evidence for that? And even if there is, it doesn't really matter."
alts.zh: 我會直接反問：「首先，我不覺得這件事有任何證據。你有證據嗎？就算有好了，其實也不重要。」

cards.pattern: I love this answer. So what I'm hearing is, essentially, [一句話重述].
cards.quote: I love this answer. So what I'm hearing is, essentially, if you're amazing at any of these three roles, you will do well.
cards.zh: 我很喜歡這個回答。所以我聽到的意思，簡單講就是：這三個角色你任何一個做到頂尖，都會過得很好。
cards.why: so what I'm hearing is 是英語會議裡的萬用安全帶：既確認理解、又不必承認自己剛剛沒聽懂。前面加一句 I love this answer 讓重述不像考試，而像接話。
swaps: Let me play that back—you're saying...
If I'm following you, the takeaway is...
cards.pmNote: 對齊（alignment）不是問「你懂嗎」，是自己重述一遍讓對方修正。
cards.episode: Marc Andreessen: The real AI boom hasn’t even started yet

alts.quote: I say something to you like, "Lenny, I think what I'm hearing you say is you're off and you're thinking, screw you, Matt.
alts.zh: 我會對你說：「Lenny，我想我聽到你在說的是——你火了，你心裡在想：去你的，Matt。」

alts.quote: You're sitting in the meeting and you're like, "This is a dumb question. Everyone's going to think I'm an idiot." But then you get brave and you ask it and it turns out it wasn't a dumb question.
alts.zh: 你坐在會議裡想：「這問題也太蠢，問了大家會覺得我是白痴。」結果你鼓起勇氣問了，才發現根本不是蠢問題。

alts.quote: The reason I'm a little confused, just because I want to get it right, is what I'm hearing, which maybe isn't what you said
alts.zh: 我有點不確定，純粹是想弄清楚——我聽到的（可能不是你講的意思）是……

cards.pattern: My most controversial opinion is that [X] is as big a deal as [Y]. And only as big a deal as [Y].
cards.quote: My most controversial opinion is that I think that AI is as big a deal as the internet or mobile. And only as big a deal as the internet or mobile.
cards.zh: 我最有爭議的一個看法是：AI 跟網路、行動裝置一樣重大——而且也「只」跟它們一樣重大而已。
cards.why: 同一句話重複一次、只換一個字（and only），前半段拉攏樂觀派、後半段一秒打臉狂熱派。這種「重複＋一字反轉」是英語裡最漂亮的立場宣告技巧。
swaps: It's a huge deal—and no bigger than the last huge deal
As big as X. Exactly as big as X, and no bigger
cards.pmNote: 先給對方一半的認同再收回另一半，比一開始就唱反調更容易被聽完。
cards.episode: A rational conversation on where AI is actually going | Benedict Evans

alts.quote: We use our gut instinct on like, "Hey, no one's asking for this, in meaningful numbers at least. But we think this is going to be a big deal."
alts.zh: 我們就靠直覺判斷：「這件事沒什麼人在要求——至少沒有多到有意義。但我們覺得它會是個大事。」

alts.quote: Here's the thing that I think is the easiest to change, is to realize the only thing that's ever supposed to happen in a meeting is the discussion part.
alts.zh: 我覺得最容易改的是這件事：認清一場會議裡唯一該發生的，只有「討論」。

alts.quote: I think a lot of people think about markets almost like these bodies of water. And it's like, "Oh, it's this big body of water that we're going after." And I actually think that the most interesting markets, you have to think of them like currents.
alts.zh: 很多人把市場想成一片水域，覺得「喔，我們要去攻的是這一大片水」。但我覺得最有意思的市場，你得把它想成水流。

cards.pattern: I don't think it's particularly productive to argue whether [A or B]. Those aren't productive conversations.
cards.quote: I don't think it's particularly productive to say, "Well, is it 20% bigger than the internet or 100%?" Those aren't productive conversations.
cards.zh: 去爭「它比網路大 20% 還是 100%」我覺得沒什麼意義，那種對話不會有產出。
cards.why: 不說對方講錯，而說這個「對話」沒有生產力——把否定對準議題而不是人。particularly 這個副詞讓語氣軟一級，是英語裡標準的緩衝副詞。
swaps: I'm not sure that debate takes us anywhere useful
That's an argument we can't settle and don't need to
cards.pmNote: 會議上最貴的成本是辯論一個無論結果如何都不改行動的問題。
cards.episode: A rational conversation on where AI is actually going | Benedict Evans

alts.quote: It's like, I don't think I can predict that. I think a much better use of my time is being very flexible and adaptable at a time like this.
alts.zh: 我不覺得我預測得了那個。我覺得我的時間花在保持彈性、快速調整上，回報高得多。

alts.quote: If none of those companies are using it, I'm like, "Don't bother me. It's either snake oil or it's not proven yet."
alts.zh: 如果那些公司一家都沒在用，那我的反應就是：別來煩我，這東西不是江湖偏方，就是還沒被驗證。

alts.quote: I always say to people don't come to me for management 101, I'm not the person to ask on how to run the most effective one-on-one with your people.
alts.zh: 我常跟人講：管理入門的東西不要來問我，怎麼把一對一開得最有效率，我不是那個該問的人。

cards.pattern: One of the comments was "[別人的酸言]", which is slightly facetious, but also kind of true.
cards.quote: One of the comments was, "Benedict, this is 80 slides of saying we don't know," which is slightly facetious, but also kind of true.
cards.zh: 有人留言說：「Benedict，你這 80 張投影片就是在講『我們不知道』。」講得有點壞，但也算是實話。
cards.why: 自己把最刺的批評唸出來，再用 slightly facetious, but also kind of true 半接下來。這招同時做到三件事：顯得有幽默感、拆掉對方的火力、還讓「我們不知道」變成刻意的結論。
swaps: Someone called it X—unfair, but not entirely wrong
That's a cheap shot, and it's also basically accurate
cards.pmNote: 預先講出對你最不利的一句話，會場上就沒人需要幫你講了。
cards.episode: A rational conversation on where AI is actually going | Benedict Evans

alts.quote: If you don't say yes, what you're essentially saying is, I am so presumptuous that I understand what's on the other side of that door already.
alts.zh: 你如果不答應，你其實等於在說：我狂妄到已經知道那扇門後面是什麼了。

alts.quote: So this kind of behavioral framing and nudging becomes important, it's not about deceiving your customers, but it's just about framing the products in such a way that it also appeals to the irrational side of the brain.
alts.zh: 這種行為框架跟推力很重要——它不是要騙客戶，而是把產品呈現得也能打到大腦不理性的那一面。

alts.quote: I've also found that its biggest strength is also somewhat its weakness, which is these mock strategies tend to be pretty comprehensive and extensive.
alts.zh: 我也發現它最大的優點同時是它的缺點：這些模擬策略往往非常全面、非常詳盡。

cards.pattern: What's the hard part of the job? Is it [表面工作]? Or is it something else?
cards.quote: What's the hard part of the job? Is the hard part of the job writing the code line by line? Is the hard part of the job giving you the SKU, or making the PowerPoint?
cards.zh: 這份工作真正難的部分是什麼？是一行一行寫程式嗎？是把貨號調出來、把投影片做出來嗎？
cards.why: 連續三個同構的問句（都以 Is the hard part of the job 開頭），節奏本身就在暗示答案是「都不是」。用問句串起來的論證，聽眾會覺得結論是自己推出來的。
swaps: Where does the difficulty actually live in this job?
Which part of this is the part you're really paid for?
cards.pmNote: 拆自動化風險前先問「難的部分在哪」，答案通常不在被自動化的那一段。
cards.episode: A rational conversation on where AI is actually going | Benedict Evans

alts.quote: Everybody wants to talk about job loss, but really, what you want to look at is task loss, the tasks changing.
alts.zh: 大家都在談工作被取代，但真正該看的是「任務」被取代——是任務在變。

alts.quote: Communication isn't about being able to convey a message. It's about being able to convey a message in a way that the listener receives it and understands it and remembers it. And that's really hard to do.
alts.zh: 溝通不是把訊息送出去。溝通是用一種方式送出去，讓聽的人接收到、聽懂、而且記得住。這超級難。

alts.quote: The problem is not like what should my goal be or how should I figure out what to do with my life? They usually know, but it's very hard to actually make time for those things.
alts.zh: 問題不在於「我的目標該是什麼」或「我這輩子要幹嘛」。這個大家其實都知道。問題是很難真的挪出時間去做那些事。

cards.pattern: Young people won't believe this, but before [X], [誇張的舊苦日子]. And now thanks to [X], [反諷的結果].
cards.quote: Young people won't believe this, but before Excel, junior investment bankers worked really long hours. And now thanks to Excel, Goldman's associates will work at lunchtime on Fridays.
cards.zh: 年輕人可能不信，Excel 出現以前，投行的菜鳥可是要加班到很晚的。現在多虧有了 Excel，高盛的 associate 禮拜五中午就能下班了。
cards.why: 整句是反話：大家都知道投行現在更操。用一個假裝正經的歷史敘述把「效率提升＝工時減少」這個假設笑掉，比直接反駁有力十倍。young people won't believe this 是講反話的招牌開場。
swaps: Remember how X was supposed to give us all more free time?
Funny how that efficiency never showed up in anyone's calendar
cards.pmNote: 效率工具通常提高產出而不是減少工時（Jevons paradox）——排期時別把節省的時間當成可回收。
cards.episode: A rational conversation on where AI is actually going | Benedict Evans

alts.quote: That's a good idea, but we don't actually understand these three things before we start working on that. So maybe we should do understand work to make sure that that is actually the right idea.
alts.zh: 這個想法不錯，但在動手之前有三件事我們其實還沒搞懂。也許先做點「理解型的工作」，確認這真的是對的方向。

alts.quote: But before that, I think getting to product-market fit, obviously there's a lot of methodology for doing it today that might make it a bit easier for people, but I still think it's fairly random and pretty dang hard.
alts.zh: 在那之前——我覺得要走到 PMF，現在當然有很多方法論可能讓大家輕鬆一點，但我還是認為它相當隨機，而且真的很難。

alts.quote: I often tell people that I hate the word 'favorite' because it tells me to become limited in my mind. So I stay away from 'favorite', but I learn all the time from everybody.
alts.zh: 我常跟人說我討厭「最喜歡的」這個詞，因為它會逼我的腦袋變窄。所以我不用這個詞，但我隨時都在跟每個人學東西。

cards.pattern: It's all the other stuff. [顯眼的產出] is just the task, but that's not what you hired them for.
cards.quote: It's all the other stuff. And the PowerPoint is just like the task, but that's not what you hired them for.
cards.zh: 價值在其他所有事情上。投影片只是那個「任務」，但那不是你花錢請他們來做的事。
cards.why: 把對方看得見的產出降格成 the task，再用 that's not what you hired them for 把價值移到看不見的地方。這句可以原封不動搬去回應「這功能 AI 一天就做得出來」。
swaps: The deliverable isn't the value—it's the residue of the value
You're not paying for the artifact, you're paying for the judgment
cards.pmNote: 被質疑「這個外包／AI 也能做」時，先分清楚 task 跟 job 的界線。
cards.episode: A rational conversation on where AI is actually going | Benedict Evans

alts.quote: Yeah, I think that's an important question, and it's a question I hear a lot because we all know a bullshitter.
alts.zh: 我覺得那是一個重要的問題，而且我常常被問到——因為我們每個人都認識一個唬爛的人。

alts.quote: Sometimes I feel the need to defend that the process is not for process' sake, it's ultimately to help us all move faster and work better.
alts.zh: 有時候我得替流程辯護一下：流程不是為了流程而存在，它最終是要讓大家跑得更快、做得更好。

alts.quote: There's this rush to judgment upfront where people say, "Oh, it's therefore obvious that X, Y, Z. It's obvious that the moats are going to be in this area of the technology, but not in this other area."
alts.zh: 一開始大家都會急著下判斷，說「所以顯然就是 X、Y、Z」、「顯然護城河一定在這一塊，不會在那一塊」。

cards.pattern: [某產業] do not think of themselves as being in the business of [不起眼的實際工作], but that was what they actually did.
cards.quote: Record companies do not think of themselves as being in the business of manufacturing small pieces of plastic, but that was what they actually did.
cards.zh: 唱片公司從來不覺得自己是在做小塑膠片的生意，但他們實際上做的就是這個。
cards.why: in the business of 是英語商業裡定義「你到底在賣什麼」的固定說法。前後兩句刻意矛盾（他們以為 vs 實際上），把一個公司的自我認知與現金流來源拆開，是最狠也最有禮貌的一種質疑。
swaps: They thought they were selling X; they were actually selling Y
Nobody there would say they were in the Y business, but that's what the P&L says
cards.pmNote: 問「我們實際上在賣什麼」比問「我們的願景是什麼」更能預測誰會被顛覆。
cards.episode: A rational conversation on where AI is actually going | Benedict Evans

alts.quote: The way I learned how to pitch in business school, and I think the way most people did, is what I call the arrogant doctor.
alts.zh: 我在商學院學到的提案方式——我想大部分人學的也是——就是我說的「傲慢醫生」那一套。

alts.quote: The way that I think of Entrepreneur is that it's not even a magazine about business. It's a magazine about thinking.
alts.zh: 我自己是這樣看《Entrepreneur》的：它根本不是一本講商業的雜誌，而是一本講「怎麼想事情」的雜誌。

alts.quote: That was one of the big motivations, actually identifying that user problem, being very disgruntled on behalf of the user. We're just failing the user every day.
alts.zh: 那就是最大的動力之一：真的把使用者的問題認出來，然後代替使用者生氣。我們每天都在辜負他們。

cards.pattern: I think one needs to be a little bit cautious on what [人] says. And that's setting aside the cynical view that [難聽的解讀], which I don't believe at all.
cards.quote: So, I think one needs to be a little bit cautious on what Dario says. And that's setting aside the cynical view that he's just doing that department stock, which I don't believe at all.
cards.zh: 我覺得對 Dario 講的話要保留一點。而且我這裡還先撇開那種比較酸的解讀——說他只是在替自家股價講話——那我完全不相信。
cards.why: one needs to be cautious 用非人稱主詞把批評講得像通則。真正高明的是後半句：主動把更難聽的攻擊講出來，同時聲明自己不採用——既讓聽眾想到那個可能，又保住了風度。
swaps: I'd take that with a pinch of salt—and I'm not even going down the cynical route
There's an unkind reading of this that I don't buy, so let's set it aside
cards.pmNote: 反對高層意見時，把「立場利益」講出來但明說自己不採信，殺傷力與安全性兼具。
cards.episode: A rational conversation on where AI is actually going | Benedict Evans

alts.quote: And the way Reid records, which I'm not sure I would recommend this, but he does it a little bit differently than you do.
alts.zh: Reid 錄音的方式——我不確定我會推薦這樣做——跟你的做法有點不一樣。

alts.quote: The other thing that's a little bit different about what you said is that emotions do need to be felt.
alts.zh: 還有一點跟你剛剛講的稍微不一樣，就是情緒是真的需要被感受到的。

alts.quote: I think that as a smaller company, I don't know that that's the case.
alts.zh: 我覺得如果是規模比較小的公司，我不確定情況會是這樣。

cards.quote: And so ever since then, we've been automating jobs and creating new jobs, and you can always see the job that's going to go away, and you don't know the new job because it doesn't exist yet.
cards.zh: 從那時候到現在，我們一直在自動化舊工作、也一直在長出新工作；而你永遠看得到那個要消失的工作，看不到新的，因為它還不存在。
cards.why: 用一個對稱句解釋為什麼恐慌是結構性的：看得見的一定是損失。這種「不對稱可見性」的論證，換掉主詞就能用在裁員、砍功能、換技術棧任何場合。
swaps: The losses are visible on day one; the gains only show up later
We can name what goes away; we can't name what replaces it yet
cards.pmNote: 報壞消息時主動說明「新機會現在講不出具體名字」，比硬編一個更可信。
cards.episode: A rational conversation on where AI is actually going | Benedict Evans

alts.quote: And if you don't have them on your growth roadmap, you are going to be in some really big trouble over the next year to two years because your cost of acquisition is only going to go up.
alts.zh: 如果你的成長路線圖上沒有這些東西，未來一到兩年你會陷入大麻煩，因為你的獲客成本只會一路往上。

alts.quote: So we can think there's people who don't know about it, there's people who do know about it but don't do it, and then there's people who do know about it, but do do it. And it's that last group that's so tiny.
alts.zh: 可以分成三種人：不知道這件事的、知道但不做的、知道又真的去做的。而最後那一群小得可憐。

alts.quote: My sense is if you want work-life balance, don't join one of these companies, because that's just not the way they work.
alts.zh: 我的感覺是，如果你想要工作生活平衡，就別加入這種公司，因為它們就不是那樣運作的。

cards.pattern: You don't have to believe [激進前提] to believe that [結論].
cards.quote: So you don't have to believe in any of that stuff to believe that this is a giant deal.
cards.zh: 你完全不用相信那一整套說法，也可以相信這件事非常重大。
cards.why: 把結論跟最容易被攻擊的前提脫鉤，讓懷疑派也能點頭。這是說服光譜上最有效的一句話：降低對方買單所需要的信仰量。
swaps: You can reject the whole thesis and still land in the same place
None of that has to be true for this to matter
cards.pmNote: 提案時把「必須先同意的前提」壓到最少，過關率最高。
cards.episode: A rational conversation on where AI is actually going | Benedict Evans

alts.quote: And the third thing is that I really believe that... I don't believe. I think we all know at this point that the most important thing for the growth of anything tech is retention.
alts.zh: 第三件事是我真的相信——不，不是相信。我覺得到這個時間點大家都已經知道了：科技產品成長最重要的就是留存。

alts.quote: I don't want to spend any years of my life becoming passively okay at something.
alts.zh: 我不想花人生的任何幾年，只為了在某件事上變得「勉強還行」。

alts.quote: I genuinely believe that every idea is awesome, but that doesn't mean I can do every idea.
alts.zh: 我真心覺得每個點子都很棒——但那不代表我每個都能做。

cards.pattern: Obviously if [極端個案], then you're really pissed off. But that's a [別的問題]. That's not a [我的問題].
cards.quote: Now, obviously if you live in a small town and they capped the well and gave all the water to the data center, then you're really pissed off. But that's a planning problem. That's not a data center problem.
cards.zh: 當然，如果你住在小鎮上，井被封了、水全給了資料中心，那你當然火大。但那是都市規劃的問題，不是資料中心的問題。
cards.why: 先把對方的情緒完整承認（you're really pissed off，用他的語氣講），再用兩個短句把問題重新歸類。承認情緒但不承認歸因——這是接住反對意見最乾淨的一組動作。
swaps: That's a real complaint, but it's a policy issue, not a product issue
Totally fair to be angry about that—it's just a different root cause
cards.pmNote: 接住反對時，先驗證感受、再爭論歸因，順序反了就會被當成迴避。
cards.episode: A rational conversation on where AI is actually going | Benedict Evans

alts.quote: I will say if you're like, the hardest problem I have is that I need to build a new unicorn business, obviously that's not going to work. Not yet.
alts.zh: 當然啦，如果你說「我最難的問題是要生出一家獨角獸」，那顯然行不通。目前還不行。

alts.quote: Here's what I have a problem with. First of all, having a growth mindset is a very, very helpful thing.
alts.zh: 我要說的是我對它的哪一點有意見。首先，擁有成長心態本身是非常非常有幫助的事。

alts.quote: But if they come in on day one saying your strategy is all wrong, raises the question of, "Well then why did you join my team if you didn't believe in my strategy?"
alts.zh: 但如果他第一天就說你的策略整個都錯了，那就會讓人想問：既然你不相信這個策略，當初為什麼要加入我的團隊？

cards.pattern: Now that may be completely wrong. Imagine having this conversation about [X] in [年份]—what would you have got right?
cards.quote: Now that may be completely wrong, and one of the points I make in the presentation is like, imagine having this conversation about the internet in 1997, what would you have got right?
cards.zh: 當然，這可能完全錯。我在簡報裡就有提到：想像我們在 1997 年談網路，你當時猜對過幾題？
cards.why: 剛講完一個很篤定的推論就自己補一句 that may be completely wrong，是英語論述型講者的紀律：立場要硬，信心要標示。後面的歷史類比讓自謙有依據，不是客套。
swaps: I could be completely wrong about this
Ask me again in five years and I'll probably wince
cards.episode: A rational conversation on where AI is actually going | Benedict Evans

alts.quote: Now, what I come back to, and I could be wrong, but what I come back to is we're talking through a medium, a mediated experience.
alts.zh: 我一直會回到的一點——我也可能是錯的——就是：我們是透過一個媒介在對話，一種被中介過的經驗。

alts.quote: We're going to go off and make this two-year, five-year, whatever, 10-year vision even, and we're going to point us towards something." But the way that the technology is changing now, we don't know what's going to happen in two years.
alts.zh: 我們本來會去做那種兩年、五年甚至十年的願景，把大家指向某個方向，但以現在技術變化的速度，我們根本不知道兩年後會發生什麼事。

alts.quote: So assume that at least half of what I've said is wrong in the same basis that half of the things I've probably ever shipped are not correct.
alts.zh: 所以你就當我講的至少有一半是錯的——就像我這輩子出過的東西大概也有一半是錯的一樣。

cards.pattern: You can say [時髦標籤] all you like—it's [本質].
cards.quote: We're all sitting talking about it, and Tate says, "It's a low margin reseller, one time sells." "You can say dotcom all you like, it's a low margin reseller."
cards.zh: 大家在車上討論，Tate 說：「它就是個低毛利的經銷商，一次性買賣。你要講幾次『.com』都可以，它還是個低毛利經銷商。」
cards.why: You can say X all you like 是英語裡專門用來剝掉包裝的句型：不否認標籤，只是宣告標籤不改變經濟結構。重複同一個判斷兩次，讓它變成定論。
swaps: Call it AI-native if you want—the unit economics are the same
The label changes; the margin structure doesn't
cards.pmNote: 評估新商業模式，先把行銷詞拿掉看毛利結構。
cards.episode: A rational conversation on where AI is actually going | Benedict Evans

alts.quote: It's one thing to say you're spending a lot of time looking outside the building. It's a whole other thing to hear from the places you don't normally hear from.
alts.zh: 說自己花很多時間在公司外面看，是一回事；真的去聽那些你平常聽不到的聲音，完全是另一回事。

alts.quote: It's funny that everyone complained about Google as this really, really smart, all-knowing LLM, and at the same time, they think they're dumb enough to fall for these guest posts.
alts.zh: 很好笑的是，大家一邊抱怨 Google 是那種超級聰明、什麼都知道的 LLM，一邊又覺得它笨到會被這些客座文章騙過去。

alts.quote: People say that time flies and it doesn't. What happens is it goes by unaccounted.
alts.zh: 大家都說時間過得很快，其實不是。真正發生的是：那些日子根本沒被記下來。

cards.pattern: Somebody said the problem with me is my answer to everything is "it depends". Yeah, it does. It depends.
cards.quote: I remember somebody on social media said the problem with Benedict is his answer to everything is it depends. It's like, yeah, it does. It depends.
cards.zh: 我記得有人在社群上說：Benedict 的問題就是他對什麼都回答「看情況」。呃，本來就是啊。就是看情況。
cards.why: 面對嘲諷最強的回應不是辯解，是完全同意再重複一次。Yeah, it does. It depends. 兩個短句把批評變成立場宣告，對方的攻擊反而幫你打了廣告。
swaps: Guilty. It really does depend
That's the criticism, and I'll own it
cards.episode: A rational conversation on where AI is actually going | Benedict Evans

alts.quote: Now even if they had the best of experiences with your answer, now they're looking at everything you said through the lens of, oh, this person was kind of uncertain.
alts.zh: 就算他們原本對你的回答感受很好，現在他們也會透過「這個人好像沒把握」這個濾鏡，重新看你剛剛講的每一句話。

alts.quote: So they would say, "Oh, your market's not big enough." And I would say, "It's going to be huge." And I'd add a new page in my pitch deck that said how big the market I believe was.
alts.zh: 他們會說：「你的市場不夠大。」我就說：「它會變超大。」然後我就在簡報裡加一頁，講我認為這市場有多大。

alts.quote: And by the way, everything I say here, I have been that person. So I have been that person who's procrastinated on an L task, whether it's the strategy or whether it's writing the PRD.
alts.zh: 順帶一提，我講的這些我自己都幹過。我就是那個會拖著高槓桿任務不做的人，不管是策略還是那份 PRD。

cards.pattern: I should just wind back on what you just said—[修正對方的前提].
cards.quote: Well, I should just wind back on what you just said. So on average, nobody died in World War I. Great.
cards.zh: 我得先把你剛剛那句話往回拉一點。用平均來看，一次大戰沒有人死掉嘛，很好。但你如果是 1914 年的十九歲男生，有三分之一機率回不來。
cards.why: wind back on what you just said 是一個很有禮貌的煞車片語：不說你錯，只說「我們倒回去一點」。接著他用「平均來說一戰沒人死掉」這種荒謬的算法，再補上「但你如果是 1914 年的十九歲男生，有三分之一機率回不來」——一句話拆掉「整體來看沒事」這種安慰式論述。
swaps: Let me push back on the framing there for a second
Before we move on—averages hide the thing that matters here
cards.pmNote: 看到「平均沒問題」的指標，先問分佈：受害最深的那一群是誰。
cards.episode: A rational conversation on where AI is actually going | Benedict Evans

alts.quote: Instead, it's my instinct to go the wrong way on challenge directly and to pretend that I agree when I disagree, and then I wind up in the worst place of all, manipulative insincerity.
alts.zh: 我的本能反而是在「直接挑戰」這件事上走錯邊——明明不同意卻裝作同意，最後掉進最糟的那一格：虛偽的操弄。

alts.quote: I'm not sure we're solving the right problem, but boy, we run a great meeting." And it's not meant to diminish any of that.
alts.zh: 「我不確定我們解的是不是對的問題，但天啊，我們的會開得可真好。」而且這不是要否定那些努力。

alts.quote: So much so that the company was number one on Glassdoor's best place to work, I was the number one CEO on Glassdoor, and as I look back at that, I'm not sure that's a good thing.
alts.zh: 誇張到公司在 Glassdoor 拿最佳職場第一名、我自己是第一名的 CEO，可是現在回頭看，我不確定那是件好事。

cards.pattern: Don't [自我感覺良好的迴避]—that gives you a great feeling of moral superiority, but it's not going to help.
cards.quote: The only answer I think one can have is, don't stick your head in the sand and say, "I hate all of this stuff," because that gives you a great feeling of moral superiority.
cards.zh: 我覺得唯一的答案是：別把頭埋進沙子裡說「我討厭這些東西」，因為那只會讓你很有道德優越感。
cards.why: 不罵對方逃避，而是精準說出逃避帶來的好處（道德優越感）——把對方的心理動機講穿，比指責更難反駁。這是給難聽回饋時最鋒利也最不失禮的角度。
swaps: Refusing to engage feels principled, but it doesn't move you forward
That position is comfortable, and it costs you
cards.episode: A rational conversation on where AI is actually going | Benedict Evans

alts.quote: I think we do a disservice when we say we're not good at speaking up because it's a skill like any other.
alts.zh: 我覺得我們說自己「不擅長發言」是在害自己，因為那跟其他技能沒有兩樣。

alts.quote: Of course, I don't want to be cruel to the people who are putting their hearts into that work, because the Figma file is beautiful. It's just coming a little early.
alts.zh: 當然，我不想對那些真心投入的人太苛刻——那些 Figma 檔真的很漂亮。只是它來得太早了一點。

alts.quote: And it's not because people are bad people. I think most people are really well-intentioned. But what happens when you have people that join and you didn't really need them?
alts.zh: 這不是因為誰是壞人，我覺得大多數人動機都很好。但問題是：當你招了一批其實不需要的人，會發生什麼事？

cards.pattern: A really interesting takeaway here is that your sense is [重述對方的預測].
cards.quote: A really interesting takeaway here is that your sense is over time the foundational model companies, their margins will get squeezed, and the bigger opportunities in the application layer.
cards.zh: 所以一個很有意思的結論是：你的判斷是，長期來看基礎模型公司的毛利會被壓縮，比較大的機會在應用層。
cards.why: 用 your sense is 而不是 you said，把重述框成「我理解的你的判斷」——留了修正空間，也避免把對方的推測講成斷言。這是複述別人立場時最安全的動詞。
swaps: So your read is that...
If I'm capturing it right, your expectation is...
cards.pmNote: 會議紀錄裡把「判斷」跟「事實」用不同動詞標開，後面追責才不會失真。
cards.episode: A rational conversation on where AI is actually going | Benedict Evans

alts.quote: So to replay the system overall highlight is about the thing you want to make time for today. The most important thing today, laser is about creating barriers to distraction.
alts.zh: 把整套系統再跑一遍：highlight 是你今天最想騰出時間做的那件事；laser 是替干擾設路障。

alts.quote: Just to summarize in case people didn't totally catch it, basically, layer one is focus, layer two, tip the market, layer three, dominate the market.
alts.zh: 總結一下，怕大家沒完全抓到——基本上第一層是聚焦，第二層是把市場推倒，第三層是主宰市場。

alts.quote: Literally, for your product folks, the number one lesson, and I hope this is the biggest takeaway for your audience, you cannot prioritize a product roadmap without having a willingness to pay conversation.
alts.zh: 對做產品的人來說，第一號的教訓——我希望這是聽眾最大的收穫——就是：沒有做過付費意願對話，你根本沒辦法排產品路線圖的優先順序。

cards.quote: And that's the classic explanation of what they do. So, they sell a data platform. So, that's the capsule answer, but there's lots to unpack in there.
cards.zh: 這是最制式的講法：他們賣的是一個資料平台。這是濃縮版的答案，但底下還有很多可以拆。
cards.why: 先給一個 30 秒版本，再宣告「還有很多可以拆」，等於把節奏交還給對方決定要不要深入。台灣人回答大問題常一路講到底，用 capsule answer 這個標記會顯得結構清楚很多。
swaps: That's the short version—happy to go deeper on any part
That's the elevator answer; there's a lot underneath it
cards.pmNote: 面對高層先給壓縮版答案，再問要不要展開，是最省時間的匯報結構。
cards.episode: How Palantir built the ultimate founder factory | Nabeel S. Qureshi (founder, writer, ex-Palantir)

alts.quote: For folks that haven't worked at a company with this kind of on the ground ops team, can you just unpack what that is?
alts.zh: 對於沒待過有這種第一線營運團隊的人來說，你可以幫忙拆解一下那是什麼嗎？

alts.quote: At the top of the interview, Lenny, you asked, "What do most people get wrong when they think about this productivity, time management, whatever?" And I'll frame my answer in those terms.
alts.zh: Lenny，你一開始問過：「大家在生產力、時間管理這些事情上最常搞錯什麼？」我就用那個框架來回答。

alts.quote: The support's not going to be good enough. They probably don't have good governance policies or other things that we need. Whether that's true or not, this is what it looks like.
alts.zh: 他們的客服大概不夠好、治理政策大概也不合我們要求。這是不是事實不重要——重點是看起來就是這樣。

cards.pattern: The companies that attract talent put out a distinctive bad signal—it has to turn some people off. That's the key of a good bad signal.
cards.quote: He thinks that a lot of the best recruiters in the world or the companies that attract talent, they put out this distinctive bad signal and it has to turn some people off. That's the key of a good, bad signal.
cards.zh: 他認為最會吸引人才的公司，都會刻意放出一個「不討喜的訊號」，而且一定要有人被勸退。這才是好的壞訊號的重點。
cards.why: good, bad signal 這種故意的矛盾詞組，逼聽眾停下來重新解讀，正是它值錢的地方。用 it has to turn some people off 把「勸退」講成功能而不是副作用，一句話就把價值觀定位講完了。
swaps: If nobody's put off by it, it isn't doing its job
The filter only works if it actually filters
cards.pmNote: 定義團隊價值觀時，最重要的一句是「這裡不適合誰」。
cards.episode: How Palantir built the ultimate founder factory | Nabeel S. Qureshi (founder, writer, ex-Palantir)

alts.quote: But human beings are notoriously good at trading off the long run just to feel good in the short run. That's why we're all eating chocolate and cupcakes and stuff that we know is bad for us because it feels good.
alts.zh: 人類非常擅長犧牲長期，只為了短期舒服。所以我們才都在吃明知不好的巧克力跟杯子蛋糕。

alts.quote: And I think craft is a dessert that you get after the meal of does your thing solve a real problem in the world and are people clamoring, needing it badly?
alts.zh: 我覺得「做工精緻」是甜點，前面那頓正餐是：你的東西有沒有解決世界上真實的問題、有沒有人急著要它。

alts.quote: The good news is, you're just like everybody else. The bad news is, you're mediocre just like everybody else.
alts.zh: 好消息是，你跟大家一樣；壞消息是，你跟大家一樣平庸。

cards.quote: So the idea is, basically, you write up a two-page plan for the project. You invite three or four smart folks who don't know anything about the project and their job is just to tear apart your plan.
cards.zh: 做法是：你先寫一份兩頁的專案計畫，然後找三四個完全不懂這個專案的聰明人來，他們的任務就是把你的計畫拆爛。
cards.why: their job is just to tear apart 把「被批評」制度化成一個有職稱的角色，所以沒有人是在針對你。要在英語團隊裡導入任何批評機制，這個「指派任務」的講法最好用。
swaps: Their only job in the room is to find the holes
We assign people to argue against it on purpose
cards.pmNote: murder board／pre-mortem：找不懂脈絡的人來拆，比找懂的人來背書有價值。
cards.episode: How Palantir built the ultimate founder factory | Nabeel S. Qureshi (founder, writer, ex-Palantir)

alts.quote: That's a good idea, but we don't actually understand these three things before we start working on that. So maybe we should do understand work to make sure that that is actually the right idea.
alts.zh: 這個想法不錯，但在動手之前有三件事我們其實還沒搞懂。也許先做點「理解型的工作」，確認這真的是對的方向。

alts.quote: Now, don't get me wrong, I've built the experimentation platform at Lyft. I'm a guy who loves data and loves using it and looking at experiments.
alts.zh: 先別誤會我的意思——Lyft 的實驗平台就是我建的。我是個超愛用數據、愛看實驗的人。

alts.quote: And that is never, ever, ever the reason. How do I know? Because they already looked at your homepage, read all the stuff, saw what you promised, looked at the pricing page and decided to buy it.
alts.zh: 那絕對、絕對不會是真正的原因。我怎麼知道？因為他們早就看過你的首頁、讀完那些內容、看過你承諾了什麼、也看過定價頁，然後決定買了。

cards.pattern: "[人人都同意的原則]" is not a good principle, because nobody can reasonably disagree with it.
cards.quote: They would write principles such as move fast and I would always be, "Everyone likes to move fast." It is not a good principle actually because nobody can really disagree with this reasonably.
cards.zh: 他們會寫「快速行動」這種原則，我都會回：誰不喜歡快速行動？那其實不是好的原則，因為沒有人會合理地反對它。
cards.why: 用一個測試取代爭論：「有沒有人會合理地反對？」沒有的話它就不是原則、只是廢話。給對方一把尺，比直接說「你寫得很空」有建設性得多。
swaps: If the opposite sounds insane, it's not a real principle
A principle only counts if someone could sensibly argue the other side
cards.pmNote: 寫 principles 或 tenets 時，每一條都要能寫出一個合理的反面版本。
cards.episode: How Palantir built the ultimate founder factory | Nabeel S. Qureshi (founder, writer, ex-Palantir)

alts.quote: I really try and stay away from better, because that's really hard to define, and better means something different to everyone.
alts.zh: 我盡量不用「比較好」這個字，因為它很難定義，而且每個人心中的「比較好」都不一樣。

alts.quote: They're not useful as decision-making tools because nobody would ever argue the opposite. Nobody ever sat in a meeting and said, "Oh, forget clear. Let's try to make it as confusing as possible."
alts.zh: 這些東西沒辦法拿來做決策，因為根本不會有人主張反面。從來沒有人在會議上說：「別管清楚了，我們把它做得越難懂越好。」

alts.quote: You write this document and I'm sorry, who actually reads it? You know what I mean? I know it's painful, but it's like that.
alts.zh: 你寫了那份文件——不好意思，但到底有誰真的會讀？你懂我意思吧？我知道這很刺耳，但事實就是這樣。

cards.pattern: They've accomplished very difficult goals in very hostile environments. And it turns out that [對照場景], that's actually a very useful skill.
cards.quote: They tend to have accomplished very difficult goals in very hostile environments. And it turns out that when you're starting a somewhat chaotic tech company, that's actually a very useful skill to have.
cards.zh: 這些人習慣在極度不友善的環境裡把很難的目標做出來。結果發現，開一家有點混亂的科技公司，這剛好是非常有用的能力。
cards.why: and it turns out that 是英語裡「意外發現」的標準連接詞，讓一個非直覺的招聘決定聽起來像被資料驗證過，而不是老闆的偏好。
swaps: As it happens, that maps almost perfectly onto...
Turns out that's exactly the muscle you need when...
cards.pmNote: 招募差異化人才時，要講清楚「他們原本的環境」跟「我們的環境」哪裡同構。
cards.episode: How Palantir built the ultimate founder factory | Nabeel S. Qureshi (founder, writer, ex-Palantir)

alts.quote: You could have all the usage data in the world, that's going to tell you what's actually happening in your product, but it doesn't tell you why.
alts.zh: 就算你握有全世界的使用數據，它只會告訴你產品裡實際發生了什麼，不會告訴你為什麼。

alts.quote: Number one is actually measuring it. I can't tell you how many times I suggest to a founder to track cohorts and that's a new thing.
alts.zh: 第一件事其實是去量它。我真的數不清有多少次我建議創辦人追蹤 cohort，結果那對他們是全新的東西。

alts.quote: I have custom software that I've written that will say, 'Okay, here are the points at which the audience laughed.' Actually audibly laughed. That's the only way it counts.
alts.zh: 我自己寫了一套軟體，會告訴我「聽眾在哪些點笑了」。是真的出聲笑。只有出聲才算。

cards.pattern: The job is not just to [X]. It is not just to [Y]. It is to actually [真正的目標].
cards.quote: But then the job of the forward deployed engineer is not just to deploy software. It is not just to sell software. It is to actually solve the problem.
cards.zh: 前線工程師的工作不只是把軟體部署上去，也不只是把軟體賣出去，而是真的把問題解決掉。
cards.why: 兩個 not just 疊出節奏，最後一個 It is to actually 落地。三段式否定＋肯定是英語裡定義角色最有力的結構，用來回答「這個職位到底在幹嘛」百試百靈。
swaps: The deliverable isn't the software, it's the outcome
We're not measured on shipping it—we're measured on it working
cards.pmNote: 定義角色時用「不是什麼」開頭，比列職責清單更能對齊期待。
cards.episode: How Palantir built the ultimate founder factory | Nabeel S. Qureshi (founder, writer, ex-Palantir)

alts.quote: But before you do that, you should think about, "Is this a problem I can invest five to 10 years into actually solving? Do I care deeply enough about it?"
alts.zh: 但在那之前你該先想：這是不是一個我願意投入五到十年去真正解決的問題？我對它在乎得夠深嗎？

alts.quote: It's not that you actually are going to watch it the whole time, but it gives you a mental model and makes you feel in control.
alts.zh: 並不是說你真的會全程盯著看，而是它讓你有一個心智模型，讓你覺得自己掌握著方向盤。

alts.quote: Software is deterministic. When you write code and you hit run, it either runs or it doesn't.
alts.zh: 軟體是確定性的。你寫完程式按下執行，它要嘛跑起來、要嘛跑不起來。

cards.pattern: The error people make more often than not is [X]. That's the mistake I've seen more than the other way around.
cards.quote: And I think the error that people make more often than not is they are actually too stuck on their own product vision. That's the mistake I've seen a little bit more actually than the other way around.
cards.zh: 我覺得大家最常犯的錯，是太黏著自己原本的產品願景。這個錯我看到的，其實比反過來的那種多一點。
cards.why: 把批評講成一個群體現象（the error people make），對方就不必對號入座。再用 more than the other way around 承認兩種錯都存在，只是比例不同——這種比例式判斷比絕對判斷容易被接受。
swaps: The more common failure mode is the opposite of what people expect
In my experience people over-index on their original thesis
cards.pmNote: 客戶說的痛點跟你的產品願景衝突時，先假設客戶是對的。
cards.episode: How Palantir built the ultimate founder factory | Nabeel S. Qureshi (founder, writer, ex-Palantir)

alts.quote: I just think every time we make a demand on the audience, that's a failure on our part.
alts.zh: 我就是覺得，每次我們對觀眾提出一個要求，那都是我們自己的失敗。

alts.quote: The only thing that's different is the insight that the founder has on the market, which is a hard pill to swallow. And I know that's hard to hear too.
alts.zh: 唯一的差別是創辦人對市場的洞察——這顆藥很難吞。我也知道這話很難聽。

alts.quote: Hey, well this is how other people perceive you including me, but maybe this is not what you are intending...
alts.zh: 其他人——包括我——是這樣看你的，但這可能不是你原本想呈現的樣子。

cards.pattern: There's no hard and fast rule, but you need to have this matrix of options in your mind and be very deliberate about which one you're going with and why.
cards.quote: So yeah, no hard and fast rule, but I think it's always you need to have this matrix of options in your mind and be very deliberate about which one you are going with and why.
cards.zh: 沒有什麼鐵則，但你腦中要有一張選項矩陣，而且要很清楚自己選了哪一格、為什麼。
cards.why: 被問到「有沒有標準答案」時最好的回法：先承認沒有（no hard and fast rule），再把價值放在「有意識地選」。deliberate about which one and why 把要求從答案轉成流程，聽起來專業又不敷衍。
swaps: There's no formula—what matters is knowing which trade-off you took
It's situational, but the choice should never be accidental
cards.pmNote: 沒有最佳解時，決策品質等於「你有沒有明確知道自己放棄了什麼」。
cards.episode: How Palantir built the ultimate founder factory | Nabeel S. Qureshi (founder, writer, ex-Palantir)

alts.quote: I think it's the difference between oversimplification and focusing. You can have a complex problem and be like, "You know what? I need to hold some things constant."
alts.zh: 我覺得差別在於「過度簡化」和「聚焦」。面對複雜問題你可以說：好，我需要先把某些變數固定住。

alts.quote: And it's hard because in making it compact you're losing completeness.
alts.zh: 這很難，因為你把它壓得越精簡，就越不完整。

alts.quote: I communicate to my leaders that my expectation is they bring in the clock speed one click faster, which means if you think something needs to be done this year, it needs to be done this half.
alts.zh: 我會跟我的主管們講，我的期待是把時鐘往前撥一格：如果你覺得某件事今年要做完，那就是這半年要做完。

cards.pattern: Sorry, this is a little bit dark, but [不舒服的類比].
cards.quote: As a very simple example, sorry, this is a little bit dark, but how restaurants want to turn over tables as fast as possible in order to maximize for the day? Hospitals actually want to do the same with patients.
cards.zh: 舉個很簡單的例子——抱歉這個講法有點黑暗——餐廳希望翻桌越快越好，好把一天的收益拉高。醫院對病床其實也是同一件事。
cards.why: sorry, this is a little bit dark 是一個預警標籤：先幫聽眾準備好情緒，他們就不會把你的冷血歸咎到人格上。要講不討喜但真實的商業邏輯時，這個緩衝幾乎是必備的。
swaps: This is going to sound cynical, but...
Forgive the blunt framing, but the economics work like this
cards.pmNote: 理解客戶產業，要從「他們怎麼算錢」而不是「他們怎麼自我介紹」開始。
cards.episode: How Palantir built the ultimate founder factory | Nabeel S. Qureshi (founder, writer, ex-Palantir)

alts.quote: Over the course of our life, because of all these little situations that happen, we start getting bugs in the software and we're not really upgrading our software.
alts.zh: 在人生的過程裡，因為發生了各種小事，我們的軟體開始長 bug，而我們也沒有真的在更新它。

alts.quote: I always say you should have, what I call an elephant at the beginning of the story, which is actually a big spaceship shooting at a little spaceship or a police officer chasing a guy across a roof.
alts.zh: 我一直說你應該在故事開頭放一隻我稱為「大象」的東西——實際上就是一艘大太空船在射一艘小太空船，或是警察在屋頂上追一個人。

alts.quote: I call this habit “gossiping” to AI, because I fill in my copilot the same way I’d lean over and vent to a colleague sitting next to me.
alts.zh: 我把這個習慣叫做對 AI「講八卦」，因為我更新我的副駕的方式，就跟我側身跟隔壁同事抱怨一樣。

cards.pattern: There's so much advice on this and you read it and think "this is super obvious". Then when you live it, you're like, "this is why people say this".
cards.quote: I think with hiring, it's funny, man, there's so much hiring advice online and you read it and you're like, "Yeah, this is super obvious." And then when you live it, you're suddenly like, "Aah, this is why people say this."
cards.zh: 招人這件事很好笑，網路上一堆建議，你看的時候都覺得「這不是廢話嗎」。等你真的經歷過，才會突然懂「喔，原來大家是這個意思」。
cards.why: 自己先講出「這聽起來很廢」，讀者／聽者就不會替你講。用 read it vs live it 的對比把老生常談重新充電，是分享常識型結論時最重要的一道手續。
swaps: It sounds obvious until it happens to you
Everyone knows this; almost nobody has felt it
cards.episode: How Palantir built the ultimate founder factory | Nabeel S. Qureshi (founder, writer, ex-Palantir)

alts.quote: So we can think there's people who don't know about it, there's people who do know about it but don't do it, and then there's people who do know about it, but do do it. And it's that last group that's so tiny.
alts.zh: 可以分成三種人：不知道這件事的、知道但不做的、知道又真的去做的。而最後那一群小得可憐。

alts.quote: If I told you, I'm going to build an autonomous vehicle, and I said our team is 10 people, you should rightfully say, Varun, you're not serious. And you'd be right.
alts.zh: 如果我跟你說我要做自駕車，然後說團隊只有 10 個人，你完全應該回我：Varun，你不是認真的吧。而且你會是對的。

alts.quote: That sounds cliche. I think a lot of founders and startup people like to talk about the mission, and I get it, and I think it's real. But I really mean it.
alts.zh: 我知道這聽起來很老套。很多創辦人都愛談使命，我懂，我也覺得那是真的。但我是真心這樣講。

cards.quote: You ask questions like, what's the hardest you've ever worked to get something done and why? And that does differentiate a lot of people, a lot of people don't actually have a great answer to that.
cards.zh: 你可以問這種問題：你這輩子為了完成某件事最拚的一次是什麼？為什麼？這題真的很能分辨人，很多人其實答不太出來。
cards.why: 先給問題、再給這題的診斷價值（能分辨什麼、大部分人會怎麼卡住）。介紹面試題時附上「答不出來代表什麼」，聽眾才知道怎麼用，而不是只抄一個題目。
swaps: Tell me about a time you went well past what was asked
What's the most effort you've ever put into something nobody made you do?
cards.pmNote: 行為面試題的重點不是答案內容，是對方有沒有具體到細節。
cards.episode: How Palantir built the ultimate founder factory | Nabeel S. Qureshi (founder, writer, ex-Palantir)

alts.quote: What we ask people in general is we say, what do you think? We don't say, what do you know? We often say, what do you think?
alts.zh: 我們一般會問人「你怎麼想？」我們不會問「你知道什麼？」我們最常問的就是「你怎麼想？」

alts.quote: People call me sometimes they're like "I want to know if I have product market fit." Well, the fact that you have time to call me and ask me this question already tells me the answer.
alts.zh: 有人打給我說：「我想知道我們有沒有 PMF。」嗯，你有空打這通電話問我，這件事本身就給了答案。

alts.quote: I always ask, "What worked? What didn't work?"
alts.zh: 我每次都會問：哪裡有用？哪裡沒用？

cards.pattern: And then there's this question of: would you rather be in the room making this better, or not?
cards.quote: And then there's this question of, well, would you rather be in the room and making this better or not?
cards.zh: 然後就有一個問題：你是寧願待在那個房間裡把它變好，還是乾脆不在？
cards.why: 把道德爭議轉成一個只有兩個選項的選擇題，而且兩個選項都由對方承擔後果。用問句而不是主張，讓聽眾自己走到你要的位置，反彈最小。
swaps: Is walking away actually the higher-impact choice here?
Does opting out make the outcome better or just make you cleaner?
cards.pmNote: 遇到「該不該參與」的爭議，先問「不參與的話結果會變好嗎」。
cards.episode: How Palantir built the ultimate founder factory | Nabeel S. Qureshi (founder, writer, ex-Palantir)

alts.quote: But if they come in on day one saying your strategy is all wrong, raises the question of, "Well then why did you join my team if you didn't believe in my strategy?"
alts.zh: 但如果他第一天就說你的策略整個都錯了，那就會讓人想問：既然你不相信這個策略，當初為什麼要加入我的團隊？

alts.quote: It's not LLMs to be clear, but there's engines like Stockfish these days that are just dramatically better than the top grand masters in the world.
alts.zh: 講清楚，那不是 LLM，但現在有像 Stockfish 那種引擎，已經遠遠強過世界頂尖大師。

alts.quote: Not to say it's not better, but just this is the structure of it, and it kind of sets you up for bragging.
alts.zh: 我不是說它不好，我只是在講它的結構——這個結構會把你逼到一直自誇。

cards.pattern: You sort of want to say to them, "Hey, are you thinking about [他們在迴避的後果]?"
cards.quote: So you have engineers now who are working on optimizing short form videos for higher engagement, and you sort of want to say to them like, "Hey, are you thinking about what this is doing to the brains of young children?"
cards.zh: 現在有一群工程師在優化短影音的互動率，你會有點想跟他們說：「欸，你有想過這對小朋友的腦袋在做什麼嗎？」
cards.why: you sort of want to say to them 是一層很好用的緩衝：把尖銳的話講出來，但框成「我有點想說」而不是「我現在正在對你說」。sort of 再降一級語氣，整句就從指控變成感嘆。
swaps: Part of me wants to ask them whether...
You almost want to stop them and say...
cards.episode: How Palantir built the ultimate founder factory | Nabeel S. Qureshi (founder, writer, ex-Palantir)

alts.quote: Of course, I don't want to be cruel to the people who are putting their hearts into that work, because the Figma file is beautiful. It's just coming a little early.
alts.zh: 當然，我不想對那些真心投入的人太苛刻——那些 Figma 檔真的很漂亮。只是它來得太早了一點。

alts.quote: I do want to be clear, it's one leader and their team who are accountable and responsible.
alts.zh: 我想把話講清楚：負責的就是一位負責人跟他的團隊。

alts.quote: I would say there are a few things that PMs do that annoy engineers and to be clear, I am sure that engineers annoy PMs, just as much.
alts.zh: 我會說有幾件事是 PM 做了會惹惱工程師的——先講清楚，我相信工程師惹惱 PM 的程度也不遑多讓。

cards.pattern: It turned out my comparative advantage in a lot of ways was [別人不想碰的那塊].
cards.quote: But it turned out, look, my comparative advantage in a lot of ways was the networks I'd built and the experience I'd had in engaging with the messy parts of the world.
cards.zh: 但後來發現，我真正的比較利益，其實是那些人脈，還有跟這個世界最麻煩的那些地方打交道的經驗。
cards.why: comparative advantage 是經濟學詞，用來講自己的強項時特別好：它承認「我不是每件事都比別人強」，只是說「相對來說我在這塊最划算」。談成績時最不招人反感的措辭。
swaps: Where I'm actually differentiated is...
My edge isn't raw skill, it's the terrain I know
cards.pmNote: 談自己的價值時用「相對優勢」而不是「我最強」，可信度高很多。
cards.episode: How Palantir built the ultimate founder factory | Nabeel S. Qureshi (founder, writer, ex-Palantir)

alts.quote: But where I started understanding deeply the dynamics of the marketplace was actually my experience and the one job I've had that not been in the creator or art or these big consumer platforms.
alts.zh: 但我真正開始深入理解市集的運作機制，其實是在那份唯一不屬於創作者、藝術或大型消費平台的工作裡。

alts.quote: Well, it's very generous of you. I wouldn't say... look, we've done some really good work, some good work so far at YouTube, and it's been a journey.
alts.zh: 你太抬舉我了。我不會這樣講啦——我們在 YouTube 是做了一些不錯的成績，過程也蠻曲折的。

alts.quote: I don't want to make it seem like it was me against everyone because that was definitely not the case. I think the starting engineers and designers on that team really cared about the quality of what they built too.
alts.zh: 我不想講得好像是我一個人對抗全世界，完全不是那樣。那個團隊的工程師跟設計師本來就很在乎品質。

cards.pattern: You have to aim for [最高標準]. You have to make something better than that. That should be your goal—not something you feel is good enough.
cards.quote: And he would say, you have to aim for Chartres. You have to make something that is better than that. That should be your goal, not to just turn in something that's what you feel is good enough.
cards.zh: 他會說：你要對準夏特大教堂。你要做出比它更好的東西。那才是你的目標，而不是交出一個你自己覺得「還可以」的作品。
cards.why: 用一個具體到不能再具體的標的（那座教堂）取代抽象的「追求卓越」，三個短句層層加碼，最後用 good enough 當反例收尾。設定標準時，指著一個實體遠比形容詞有效。
swaps: Benchmark against the best thing ever made in this category, not against last quarter
Don't aim for shippable, aim for the thing people still study in twenty years
cards.pmNote: 把品質標準綁在一個具體的參照物上，團隊才不會各自解讀「夠好」。
cards.episode: How Palantir built the ultimate founder factory | Nabeel S. Qureshi (founder, writer, ex-Palantir)

alts.quote: And I think the thing that I love about a crazy big goal is that you feel completely inadequate before it.
alts.zh: 我最喜歡「瘋狂大目標」的一點，就是站在它面前你會覺得自己完全不夠格。

alts.quote: So since June, this is the worst it will ever be, the state of AI coding. And it's already this good.
alts.zh: 所以從六月到現在，AI 寫程式的水準就是它「最差」的時候了。而它已經這麼好了。

alts.quote: And so we felt like that was the wrong, that didn't feel right, and so could we help democratize visual storytelling, visual communication? That was sort of our north star.
alts.zh: 我們覺得這件事不對勁，所以問：我們有沒有辦法讓視覺敘事、視覺溝通變得人人可用？那就是我們的北極星。

cards.pattern: I think [不流行的主張]. I think this is a somewhat contrarian view within [某圈子], maybe not outside it.
cards.quote: I think going to college is great. I think this is a somewhat contrarian view within tech, maybe not in the broader economy.
cards.zh: 我覺得念大學很棒。我知道這在科技圈算是個有點逆風的看法，在一般社會可能就還好。
cards.why: 先講立場，再標示「這在哪個圈子算逆風」。這個座標定位讓聽眾知道你不是狀況外，而是明知故犯——講不受歡迎的意見時，這一句能省下一半的辯護。
swaps: I know this isn't the popular take in this room
This puts me in the minority here, and I'll stand by it
cards.episode: How Palantir built the ultimate founder factory | Nabeel S. Qureshi (founder, writer, ex-Palantir)

alts.quote: So for positioning work, I'm going to say something that is contentious, but I don't think it is at all.
alts.zh: 講到定位這件事，我要說一句大家可能覺得很有爭議的話——但我完全不覺得有爭議。

alts.quote: None of this is going to blow anyone's minds, I think, because it's very best practices. But it's easy to overlook when you're so focused on so many different steps of a process.
alts.zh: 這些應該不會讓誰驚呆，因為都是很基本的最佳實務。但當你同時盯著流程裡一大堆步驟時，就是很容易漏掉。

alts.quote: Now, I'm biased when I'm going to say this, so take this with a pinch of salt, but I think the Accordion Method might be one of the things I'm the most proud of in my entire life.
alts.zh: 我要講的這件事我是有偏見的，所以你打個折聽——但我覺得手風琴法可能是我這輩子最引以為傲的東西之一。

cards.quote: I'm going to mirror back the tips you just shared, and there's actually a secondary tip that I think is the more interesting piece.
cards.zh: 我把你剛剛給的建議重述一遍——而且我覺得裡面藏了一個更有意思的第二層建議。
cards.why: mirror back 是「原樣反射回去」的說法，比 summarize 更強調忠實。加上 the more interesting piece，你在複述的同時也加了值，這是會議裡把角色從記錄者變成參與者的關鍵一句。
swaps: Let me reflect that back—and add what I think the real insight is
Playing that back to you, plus the part I think you buried
cards.pmNote: 總結別人的話時順手指出「最有價值的其實是第二點」，比純複述有影響力。
cards.episode: How Palantir built the ultimate founder factory | Nabeel S. Qureshi (founder, writer, ex-Palantir)

alts.quote: Sometimes I'm like, "Who's owning this?" And it's like people don't know. That's why I think it's very important to have a single-threaded owner.
alts.zh: 有時候我問「這件事誰在 own？」結果大家都不知道。這就是為什麼一定要有一個單一負責人。

alts.quote: So basically my long answer to your question, maybe boring answer is that I think starting next year, we're going to see early adopters starting to hockey stick their productivity.
alts.zh: 所以我這個落落長、可能還有點無聊的答案就是：我覺得從明年開始，早期採用者的生產力會開始往上翹。

alts.quote: So let's take a step back. The fear is, if I can reflect back to your original question, the fear is if I go there, I don't know what's going to happen as a consequence of that.
alts.zh: 我們退一步看。如果我把你原本的問題回映給你，那個恐懼是：如果我真的往下探，我不知道會發生什麼後果。

cards.pattern: I'll just say it as plainly as possible: they don't care about you. They care about [他們真正在服務的對象].
cards.quote: The editor, the writer, I'll just say it as plainly as possible, they don't care about you. They don't care about you. They care about their reader, or their listener, or their viewer.
cards.zh: 編輯也好、記者也好，我把話講到最白：他們不在乎你。他們真的不在乎你。他們在乎的是他們的讀者、聽眾、觀眾。
cards.why: I'll just say it as plainly as possible 是講重話前的許可證，先宣告「接下來會很直接」，聽者就會把它當事實而不是攻擊。緊接著把同一句重複一次，是英語口語裡最強的加粗方式。
swaps: Let me put this bluntly
I'll be as direct as I can about this
cards.pmNote: 跨部門協作時先搞清楚對方真正被誰考核，需求才推得動。
cards.episode: How to get press for your product | Jason Feifer (editor in chief of Entrepreneur magazine)

alts.quote: Let's just say there's a product manager and nobody's ever coached this poor person, and so they really don't know much.
alts.zh: 我們就假設有一個產品經理，從來沒有人帶過他，所以他其實懂得不多。

alts.quote: And so then the first few pages became very much more problem-based because if people don't understand the problem then they can't understand or care about your solution.
alts.zh: 所以前面幾頁後來就大改成以「問題」為主，因為人如果不懂那個問題，就不可能懂、也不可能在乎你的解法。

alts.quote: So there's, I wouldn't say a checklist, but there's a series of questions that I asked to diagnose why is growth slowing in this order, because it's one of these things where the first one that's a problem, if you don't fix that, it doesn't matter if you fix one of the ones below.
alts.zh: 我不會說那是一張檢查清單，但我確實有一組問題，會照順序問下去診斷成長為什麼變慢——因為只要最前面那個沒修，後面修再多都沒用。

cards.pattern: Think about [X] the same way you think about [Y]: you do it when you know what it's for.
cards.quote: Think about press the same way that you think about raising money, which is to say you do it when you know what the money is for, and you should do it when you know what the press is for.
cards.zh: 把「找媒體報導」想成「募資」：你會在知道這筆錢要幹嘛的時候才去募，那你也該在知道這次曝光要幹嘛的時候才去找。
cards.why: 借用對方已經有紀律的領域（募資）來規範他還沒有紀律的領域（公關），一句話就把標準搬過去。which is to say 是把類比講成明確規則的橋接詞。
swaps: Treat it like hiring—you don't open a req until you know the gap
Same rule as fundraising: know the use of funds first
cards.pmNote: 任何資源投入前先寫下「這一輪要換到什麼」，否則無法判斷成敗。
cards.episode: How to get press for your product | Jason Feifer (editor in chief of Entrepreneur magazine)

alts.quote: The way I think about this is that emotions are like a tube, let's say, and there's water moving through the tube.
alts.zh: 我自己是這樣想這件事的：情緒像一根管子，裡面有水在流。

alts.quote: Let's just say there's a product manager and nobody's ever coached this poor person, and so they really don't know much.
alts.zh: 我們就假設有一個產品經理，從來沒有人帶過他，所以他其實懂得不多。

alts.quote: And that's the thing they used to say, "Hey, leadership, this is the problem statement. Here's what we think how might we solve this big problem and here's what we think it looks like when we ship it." That's a mini-vision.
alts.zh: 「各位主管，這是問題陳述。我們認為可以怎麼解這個大問題，還有我們認為做出來會長什麼樣。」這就是一個小型願景。

cards.pattern: I respect that, and I relate to it. But "[對方的理由]" is not a good tactical decision for your business.
cards.quote: I respect that, and I relate to it in some ways with my own trying to get attention for my own work. But, "I deserve this" that's not a good tactical decision for your business.
cards.zh: 我尊重這種心情，我自己在推廣作品時也有過。但「我值得」不是一個好的商業決策理由。
cards.why: 先承認情緒（respect / relate to），再把它從決策依據裡剔除。關鍵在 not a good tactical decision——不否定感受本身，只否定它作為決策輸入的資格。這是給難聽回饋時最乾淨的切法。
swaps: I get the feeling, but it isn't a business reason
That's completely understandable—it's just not a criterion
cards.pmNote: 擋需求時把「情緒是真的」跟「情緒不能當排序依據」分兩句講。
cards.episode: How to get press for your product | Jason Feifer (editor in chief of Entrepreneur magazine)

alts.quote: And I think the error that people make more often than not is they are actually too stuck on their own product vision. That's the mistake I've seen a little bit more actually than the other way around.
alts.zh: 我覺得大家最常犯的錯，是太黏著自己原本的產品願景。這個錯我看到的，其實比反過來的那種多一點。

alts.quote: The only thing that's different is the insight that the founder has on the market, which is a hard pill to swallow. And I know that's hard to hear too.
alts.zh: 唯一的差別是創辦人對市場的洞察——這顆藥很難吞。我也知道這話很難聽。

alts.quote: That person needs to step up more, to be somebody who's really contributing and adding and being a multiplier on the work of everybody else on their team.
alts.zh: 那個人需要更站出來一點，成為真正有貢獻、有加分，能把團隊其他人的產出放大的角色。

cards.pattern: Was it that hard to [做那件小事]? No. But scale that out.
cards.quote: Was it that hard to come up and talk to me at the conference? No. But scale that out.
cards.zh: 好，那走過來跟我講兩句話有多難？不難。但你把這件事乘上去看——像這樣的信他到底寄了幾封？
cards.why: 對方一定會回「這又沒花多少力氣」，所以先自己承認（No），再用 scale that out 把單次成本乘上頻率。這是拆「反正很便宜」型反對意見的萬用招。
swaps: Individually it's cheap. Multiply it by fifty and it isn't
One of these costs nothing. That's not the number that matters
cards.pmNote: 評估瑣事成本要看總量，不看單次——這也是技術債累積的主因。
cards.episode: How to get press for your product | Jason Feifer (editor in chief of Entrepreneur magazine)

alts.quote: But if they come in on day one saying your strategy is all wrong, raises the question of, "Well then why did you join my team if you didn't believe in my strategy?"
alts.zh: 但如果他第一天就說你的策略整個都錯了，那就會讓人想問：既然你不相信這個策略，當初為什麼要加入我的團隊？

alts.quote: And I think one of the monikers we use internally is no, then go. As in just think through all the things that could go wrong, understand where scale will break, understand the things that might happen, and then move on anyway.
alts.zh: 我們內部有個口號叫「先說不，然後走」。把所有可能出錯的地方都想過一輪，知道規模在哪裡會斷，然後照樣往前。

alts.quote: The theory is that if you perfect yourself and somehow rays come out of your head and people will follow you, because you're so magnetic, and you're so perfect.
alts.zh: 那套理論是說：只要你把自己修煉到完美，頭上就會發出光芒，大家自然會跟隨你，因為你太有魅力、太完美了。

cards.pattern: The way I think of [我們] is that it's not even a [類別]. It's a [重新定義].
cards.quote: The way that I think of Entrepreneur is that it's not even a magazine about business. It's a magazine about thinking.
cards.zh: 我自己是這樣看《Entrepreneur》的：它根本不是一本講商業的雜誌，而是一本講「怎麼想事情」的雜誌。
cards.why: not even a X 的 even 是關鍵，它預設對方本來就會把你歸到 X 類，然後直接跳過那個層級。用兩句話重新定義自己的產品類別，是產品定位最短的講法。
swaps: We're not really a project management tool—we're a decision log
Think of it less as a product and more as a habit
cards.pmNote: 產品定位講「我們不是什麼」通常比「我們是什麼」更快讓對方抓到差異。
cards.episode: How to get press for your product | Jason Feifer (editor in chief of Entrepreneur magazine)

alts.quote: The way I learned how to pitch in business school, and I think the way most people did, is what I call the arrogant doctor.
alts.zh: 我在商學院學到的提案方式——我想大部分人學的也是——就是我說的「傲慢醫生」那一套。

alts.quote: The way I think about this is that emotions are like a tube, let's say, and there's water moving through the tube.
alts.zh: 我自己是這樣想這件事的：情緒像一根管子，裡面有水在流。

alts.quote: Communication isn't about being able to convey a message. It's about being able to convey a message in a way that the listener receives it and understands it and remembers it. And that's really hard to do.
alts.zh: 溝通不是把訊息送出去。溝通是用一種方式送出去，讓聽的人接收到、聽懂、而且記得住。這超級難。

cards.quote: And so what I'm looking for when somebody reaches out is did they make some interesting counterintuitive decision that solved a problem in their business, and I'll emphasize in.
cards.zh: 所以我在找的是：他有沒有做過什麼有趣、反直覺的決定，解決了他公司「內部」的問題——我要特別強調是「內部」。
cards.why: I'll emphasize in 這種「我要特別強調這個介係詞」的講法，是英語裡處理最容易被誤解的一個字的標準動作。台灣人講英文很少停下來標記單字，但這一秒往往省掉整輪來回。
swaps: —and the word doing the work there is "internal"
I want to underline that one word
cards.pmNote: 寫需求規格時，最容易出事的通常是一個介係詞或量詞，值得單獨標註。
cards.episode: How to get press for your product | Jason Feifer (editor in chief of Entrepreneur magazine)

alts.quote: To set the answer up, I'll give you a super brief history of Make Time.
alts.zh: 為了鋪陳我的答案，我先講一段 Make Time 的超簡短來歷。

alts.quote: I read the email, I'm like, "What do you want me to do? Is this an FYI? Are you saying there's a problem? Do you want me to help?"
alts.zh: 我讀完信心想：「你到底要我做什麼？這是知會嗎？你是在說有問題嗎？還是你要我幫忙？」

alts.quote: Just to close the loop on this advice around getting better at vision and strategy, if I were to reflect back what I'm hearing its be very self-aware about what you are not strong at, say openness.
alts.zh: 就把「怎麼變得更擅長願景與策略」這段收掉——如果讓我把聽到的反映回去，就是：對自己不擅長的地方要非常自覺，比如開放性。

cards.pattern: Don't confuse [表面指標] with actual success.
cards.quote: So don't confuse posting press releases even on very big websites with actual success.
cards.zh: 所以不要把「新聞稿被大網站登出來」跟真正的成功搞混。
cards.why: don't confuse A with B 是英語裡拆虛榮指標最短的句型，一句話就能在會議上把 vanity metric 擋掉。重點在於它不指責任何人，只指出兩件事被混為一談。
swaps: Let's not mistake activity for impact
Coverage isn't the same as being read
cards.pmNote: 定義成功指標時，先列出三個最容易被誤當成功的虛榮指標。
cards.episode: How to get press for your product | Jason Feifer (editor in chief of Entrepreneur magazine)

alts.quote: I think people don't realize that there's a big difference between moving from 80% performance to 90% performance to 99% performance to 99.9% performance, and so on, and so on.
alts.zh: 我覺得大家沒意識到，從 80% 做到 90%、再到 99%、再到 99.9%，這幾段之間的差距有多大。

alts.quote: If we just acknowledge reality and this person looks bored, they look bored, that is data. Don't ignore that data.
alts.zh: 如果我們願意面對現實——這個人看起來很無聊，那他就是很無聊。那是資料。別忽略那筆資料。

alts.quote: And in that case, it was from about a 50% hit rate to 65. So that's pretty huge, so that's a really big difference.
alts.zh: 那個案例是命中率從大約 50% 提到 65%。這個差距其實非常大。

cards.pattern: What you want in [某個角色] is someone who traffics in one thing, and that is [核心資產].
cards.quote: What you want in an actual PR person is someone who traffics in one thing, and that is relationships.
cards.zh: 你要找的公關，是那種只靠一件事吃飯的人——關係。
cards.why: traffics in 是很精準的動詞（以某物為交易標的），用它把一個職位的核心價值壓成一個名詞。要人要預算時，先把「這個角色唯一不可取代的東西」講出來，說服力最強。
swaps: The one thing that role has to bring is X
You're not buying hours, you're buying access
cards.pmNote: 要 headcount 時，論證要落在「這個角色唯一提供的東西」，不是工作量。
cards.episode: How to get press for your product | Jason Feifer (editor in chief of Entrepreneur magazine)

alts.quote: I want to make sure I've got air cover from the highest people in the company setting the culture.
alts.zh: 我要確定最高層那些定文化的人會幫我掩護。

alts.quote: And I want you to say, "This is great. I want to talk about money, but before we do, I want to think about some of the things that will set me up to see succeed in this role.
alts.zh: 我要你這樣說：「這很好。我想談薪水，但在那之前，我想先談談有哪些東西能讓我在這個角色上成功。」

alts.quote: I say to the person, “Let’s come up with an arbitrary deadline!” We both know it’s made up, but there’s a weird gravitational pull once you’ve put a date out there.
alts.zh: 我會跟對方說：「我們來訂一個隨便的死線吧！」我們都知道那是編的，但日期一旦放上去，就會有一種奇怪的引力。

cards.pattern: You should like it when [對方] pushes back and says "[反對意見]". That's someone you should hire.
cards.quote: You should like when a PR person pushes back on you and says, "You know what? I don't think that your story is right for that publication. Here's why." That's someone you should hire.
cards.zh: 當一個公關回你「老實說，我覺得你的故事不適合那家媒體，原因是這樣」，你應該要高興。這種人才值得聘。
cards.why: 把「被拒絕」重新標記成「值得付錢的訊號」，用 that's someone you should hire 一句收尾。要在團隊裡鼓勵反對意見，最有效的不是說「歡迎批評」，而是明確說出「會這樣做的人我們會留下來」。
swaps: The ones who tell you no are the ones worth keeping
Pushback is the service, not a failure to deliver it
cards.pmNote: 想要團隊敢講真話，就要公開獎勵第一個說「這個方向不對」的人。
cards.episode: How to get press for your product | Jason Feifer (editor in chief of Entrepreneur magazine)

alts.quote: Look, I haven't met the person who does a TikTok and they're fantastic. I definitely don't want to demerit their work. It's awesome, I don't think it's easy to do.
alts.zh: 老實說我沒見過負責 TikTok 的那個人，但他們超強。我完全不想貶低他們的工作，那真的很厲害，也一點都不好做。

alts.quote: Well, thank you for sharing the real talk. I think you made the right choice.
alts.zh: 謝謝你講了實話。我覺得你那個選擇是對的。

alts.quote: I do not believe in being liked. I believe in being loved, right? And that's a very, very different thing.
alts.zh: 我不追求被喜歡。我追求被愛。這是兩件非常、非常不一樣的事。

cards.pattern: So I would expect that it would be possibly very reasonable that [結論] might not be [X] right now.
cards.quote: So I would expect that if you have a startup and that startup is not B2B in some way, that it would be possibly very reasonable that business publications might not be your target right now.
cards.zh: 所以我會預期，如果你的新創不算 B2B，那商業媒體現在可能不是你該鎖定的對象——這樣想其實滿合理的。
cards.why: 一句話裡疊了四層緩衝（would expect / possibly / very reasonable / might not），語意其實是「不要去」。這是英語顧問式建議的極端示範：越是要否定對方的計畫，緩衝疊得越厚。台灣人常直接說 you shouldn't，語氣會硬三級。
swaps: It might well be that this isn't the right channel for you yet
I'd probably question whether that's where your audience is
cards.episode: How to get press for your product | Jason Feifer (editor in chief of Entrepreneur magazine)

alts.quote: I think if you're building a product where it's not necessarily an AI- first product and you have some AI features that are on the side, but it's not the core of your value, I don't know that I would operate this way.
alts.zh: 如果你做的不是 AI 優先的產品，只是旁邊掛幾個 AI 功能、AI 不是核心價值，那我不確定我會這樣做。

alts.quote: I agree with you. I totally agree with you. Now, I think it's the human aspect though of boldness, seeing the future in a way that a thing trained on priors cannot.
alts.zh: 我同意你，完全同意。不過我覺得，人的那一塊——那種膽識、那種能看見未來的能力，是只學過去資料的東西做不到的。

alts.quote: By the way, I'm being very mean to Figma so far in this conversation. There is a time when it's the right time for the Figma file.
