alts.zh: 順帶一提，我到目前為止對 Figma 有點太兇了。Figma 檔是有它對的時機的。

cards.pattern: These reach millions of people. That does not mean your [X] is going to be read by millions of people.
cards.quote: These are reaching millions of people, their websites get many, many, many millions of unique visitors each month. That does not mean that your story is going to be read by millions of people.
cards.zh: 這些媒體確實觸及上百萬人，網站每個月幾百萬不重複訪客。但這不代表你那篇報導會被上百萬人看到。
cards.why: 先把對方期待的數字完整講一遍（甚至幫他放大），再用 that does not mean 把它跟他真正在意的結果切開。管理期待時，最有效的做法是承認大數字為真、只否定它的推論。
swaps: The reach is real. Your share of it won't be
Big audience, small slice—those are different numbers
cards.pmNote: 期望管理：讓對方保有大數字，只把「這跟你有關的部分」拆出來講。
cards.episode: How to get press for your product | Jason Feifer (editor in chief of Entrepreneur magazine)

alts.quote: We are a series A startup. We are pushing really hard at product-market fit. The expectation here is going to be that you're online at 10:00, that you can occasionally hop on a meeting on a Saturday or Sunday."
alts.zh: 「我們是 A 輪新創。我們正在拚產品市場契合。這裡的預期是你晚上十點還在線上，週六日偶爾也要開會。」

alts.quote: People loved it, but it was too ambitious and so we failed.
alts.zh: 大家很喜歡它，但我們做得太貪心了，所以失敗了。

alts.quote: By the way, a very, very successful company for a new set of products has a 50% hit rate. So half of you are going to come back in a year and have a different job. Do you have the resilience to do that?
alts.zh: 順帶一提，一家非常成功的公司做新產品的成功率大概是五成。所以你們有一半的人一年後會換一份工作。你們有那個韌性嗎？

cards.pattern: Did we get anything from that? The answer is no, like nothing. But you better believe that every [場合] includes the link.
cards.quote: Did we get anything from that story in Variety? The answer is no, like nothing. But you better believe that every email we send out to every potential advertiser, to every partner, includes the link.
cards.zh: 那篇 Variety 的報導有帶來什麼嗎？完全沒有。但你可以放心，我們寄給每個潛在廣告主、每個合作方的信裡，一定都附上那個連結。
cards.why: 先誠實承認直接成效是零，再把價值移到第二層用途。you better believe that 是很有畫面的口語強調（你最好相信＝我當然有做）。承認失敗再翻盤，比一開始就吹更可信。
swaps: Direct impact? Zero. Second-order value? Enormous
It moved no numbers. It opens every door
cards.pmNote: 談成效時把「直接指標」跟「第二層用途」分開講，避免被單一數字定生死。
cards.episode: How to get press for your product | Jason Feifer (editor in chief of Entrepreneur magazine)

alts.quote: Looking back, my career has been a little bit like a bingo card. I've always been looking to fill in boxes I didn't have filled because I felt like that would make me a better professional.
alts.zh: 回頭看，我的職涯有點像一張賓果卡。我一直在補那些還沒被填滿的格子，因為我覺得那會讓我變成更好的專業工作者。

alts.quote: And I'm now doing stuff that I love, and in some strange way, I guess it even pays better.
alts.zh: 我現在在做我喜歡的事，而且莫名其妙地，好像還賺得更多。

alts.quote: My one learning there that has stuck with me, and I think can work for other people too, is that it's not just about doing things that actually matter, and learning. It's about being able to tell the story.
alts.zh: 那段經驗裡有一個一直留在我身上的體悟，我覺得對別人也適用：重點不只是去做真正重要的事、去學東西，還要能把這件事講成一個故事。

cards.pattern: There is literally no magic answer to that. I wish that there was, but there is not. The closest I can give you is [替代答案].
cards.quote: I mean, look, there is literally no magic answer to that. I wish that there was, but there is not. There's no format.
cards.zh: 老實說，這題沒有什麼神奇答案。我也希望有，但就是沒有。也沒有什麼固定格式。
cards.why: I wish that there was, but there is not 這句多餘的重複，作用是表達「我知道你想要答案，我也很遺憾」——先處理失望，再處理資訊。之後接 the closest I can give you 交出次佳解，整段就不會空手。
swaps: There's no formula here—I wish I had one for you
No silver bullet. The nearest thing I can offer is...
cards.pmNote: 說「不知道」之後一定要接「我能給的最接近的東西是」，否則等於沒回答。
cards.episode: How to get press for your product | Jason Feifer (editor in chief of Entrepreneur magazine)

alts.quote: I mean, look, I don't know that it's a perfect answer, but I think the reality is just that what kills most projects most early companies is stamina.
alts.zh: 我是說，我不確定這是不是完美的答案，但我覺得現實就是：殺死大多數專案、大多數早期公司的，是續航力。

alts.quote: That's the problem. I mean, that is the trillion dollar question so I don't really have an answer. I have a couple thoughts on it.
alts.zh: 問題就在這。這是那種價值一兆美元的問題，所以我其實沒有答案，但我有幾點想法。

alts.quote: So again, I don't mean to overstate this, and I certainly don't mean to claim that there's some answer that's right for everybody, of course, but surely this is the right kind of question.
alts.zh: 我不想把這件事講得太滿，也絕對不是說有一個答案適用所有人——但這絕對是該問的那類問題。

cards.pattern: I hate [大家以為你要的東西]. I love [你真正要的東西].
cards.quote: I hate success stories. I love problem solving stories. And that's why when I talk to an entrepreneur, I expect them to be really open about that stuff.
cards.zh: 我討厭成功故事。我喜歡解決問題的故事。所以我跟創業者聊的時候，會期待他們願意把難的部分講出來。
cards.why: 兩個四個字的對句，把一整套編輯標準壓縮成八個字，對方聽完立刻知道該給你什麼。要傳達偏好時，「我討厭 A、我喜歡 B」的極簡對比比任何說明段落都有效。
swaps: Spare me the highlight reel—show me the mess
Wins bore me. Recoveries don't
cards.pmNote: review 或 postmortem 邀請別人講真話時，先明說你想聽的是問題不是成果。
cards.episode: How to get press for your product | Jason Feifer (editor in chief of Entrepreneur magazine)

alts.quote: And that's the thing they used to say, "Hey, leadership, this is the problem statement. Here's what we think how might we solve this big problem and here's what we think it looks like when we ship it." That's a mini-vision.
alts.zh: 「各位主管，這是問題陳述。我們認為可以怎麼解這個大問題，還有我們認為做出來會長什麼樣。」這就是一個小型願景。

alts.quote: That's not a data center problem.
alts.zh: 那不是資料中心的問題。

alts.quote: And so in that case, someone like me who's an advisor comes in and is like, "That's right, it's not a marketing problem, it's company strategy problem.
alts.zh: 所以那種情況下，像我這種顧問進去就會說：「沒錯，這不是行銷的問題，這是公司策略的問題。」

cards.quote: But Fred got his press because sometimes, and here's the lesson, sometimes you are not the story, but you can be part of the story.
cards.zh: Fred 之所以拿到報導，是因為——這就是重點——有時候你本身不是那個故事，但你可以是故事的一部分。
cards.why: and here's the lesson 是插在句子中間的標記，等於在說「接下來這句要抄下來」。後半句的 not the story / part of the story 只換一個介係詞，就把一個策略講完了。
swaps: You don't have to be the headline to be in the piece
Aim to be the example, not the subject
cards.pmNote: 打不進主場的時候，先找一個正在被討論的趨勢，把自己放進去當案例。
cards.episode: How to get press for your product | Jason Feifer (editor in chief of Entrepreneur magazine)

alts.quote: I fundamentally do not believe in outsourcing the heartbeat of the organization, which is sales.
alts.zh: 我從根本上不相信可以把一家公司的心跳外包出去——而銷售就是心跳。

alts.quote: I think so many folks don't know where to begin on starting a startup, and my tactical advice is start doing customer validation first versus building a PowerPoint deck.
alts.zh: 很多人根本不知道創業要從哪裡開始，我很具體的建議是：先去做客戶驗證，而不是先做一份簡報。

alts.quote: When we talk about pricing strategies, we hear many buzzwords, and it's irrelevant. So when we take a step back and look at it, there's literally only three types of pricing strategies.
alts.zh: 談定價策略的時候會聽到一堆流行詞，那些都不重要。退一步看，定價策略其實就只有三種。

cards.pattern: You have to know that there's a chance it could blow up in your face. That's the price you're paying for [好處].
cards.quote: You have to go into this being vulnerable and you have to know that there's a chance that it could blow up in your face. That's the price that you're paying for reaching their audience.
cards.zh: 你得帶著會受傷的心理準備進來，而且要知道這件事有可能整個炸在你臉上。這就是你為了觸及他們的受眾所付的代價。
cards.why: That's the price you're paying for X 把風險明確標價，讓對方自己決定要不要買。談取捨時最強的一句話，因為它不勸阻也不鼓勵，只是把帳算清楚。
swaps: That's the cost of admission for this channel
That downside is baked into the upside—you can't buy one without the other
cards.pmNote: 講取捨時把代價講成價格（price of X），比講成風險更容易讓對方做決定。
cards.episode: How to get press for your product | Jason Feifer (editor in chief of Entrepreneur magazine)

alts.quote: In product, I like to joke, there's no right answers. There's only wrong answers, and you're just trying to execute well on the least wrong answer that's available to you.
alts.zh: 做產品這行我常開玩笑說：沒有對的答案，只有錯的答案；你能做的就是把眼前「最不錯」的那個做好。

alts.quote: And then the last thing I would say about this detection is if you don't know what to do, or all else being equal, then focus on onboarding.
alts.zh: 關於怎麼提早偵測，我最後想講的是：如果你不知道該做什麼，或其他條件都差不多，那就去弄 onboarding。

alts.quote: I think that becomes a bit of a strategic conversation of do we want to have a better chance of surviving, going after a niche that we know we can serve well?
alts.zh: 我覺得這時候就變成一個策略層級的討論了：我們是要提高存活機率、去打一個我們服務得很好的利基市場嗎？

cards.pattern: I want to run a theory by you. Do you think the reason you [做了X] is actually because of [Y]?
cards.quote: I'll say, "I want to run a theory by you. Do you think that the reason why you are really interested in this or you made that decision is actually because of this other thing that you told me a little bit about?"
cards.zh: 我會說：「我想跟你對一個猜測。你會這麼在意這件事、或做了那個決定，會不會其實是因為你剛剛提到的另一件事？」
cards.why: run a theory by you 把一個很私人的推測包成待驗證的假設，對方可以否認而不必尷尬。這招在 1:1 帶人時特別好用：你證明自己有在聽，又不強加詮釋。
swaps: Can I test a hunch on you?
Tell me if this is off—I wonder whether the real driver here is...
cards.pmNote: 1:1 帶人不給答案，但可以給一個「假設」讓對方自己驗證或推翻。
cards.episode: How to get press for your product | Jason Feifer (editor in chief of Entrepreneur magazine)

alts.quote: It's like why was this decision made? Why do you think the decision was made? And I might ask, "Do you think it was the right decision or did you agree on it?"
alts.zh: 像是：這個決定為什麼會做？你覺得為什麼會這樣決定？然後我可能會問：你覺得那是對的決定嗎？你當時同意嗎？

alts.quote: And then there'll be some other thing that happens that causes you to reinstall it, and that's totally fine, because you're being deliberate about it and you're paying attention.
alts.zh: 然後某天會發生某件事讓你又把它裝回來——那完全沒問題，因為你是刻意這樣做的，你有在注意。

alts.quote: And when you do this, the wrong way is to ask, why did you cancel? What you want to do is say, "What made you cancel?"
alts.zh: 問的時候，錯誤版本是「你為什麼取消？」你要問的是：「是什麼讓你取消的？」

cards.pattern: Okay, so let me summarize things that you've taught us so far. One is [X]. Two is [Y].
cards.quote: Okay, so let me summarize things that you've taught us so far. One is think about publications that go to people that will buy your thing. Two is don't think of it broad thing.
cards.zh: 好，我來把你目前教我們的整理一下。第一，挑那些會接觸到你買家的媒體。第二，不要只想到媒體這個層級。
cards.why: let me summarize things that you've taught us 這個措辭把總結變成致謝，對方不會覺得你在搶話。編號（One is / Two is）讓聽眾知道還有幾點，也逼自己收斂。
swaps: Let me recap where we've landed so far
So far I've got three things—stop me if I've missed one
cards.pmNote: 長會議每 20 分鐘做一次編號小結，決議品質會明顯提升。
cards.episode: How to get press for your product | Jason Feifer (editor in chief of Entrepreneur magazine)

alts.quote: Sometimes I'm like, "Who's owning this?" And it's like people don't know. That's why I think it's very important to have a single-threaded owner.
alts.zh: 有時候我問「這件事誰在 own？」結果大家都不知道。這就是為什麼一定要有一個單一負責人。

alts.quote: Let me just try to summarize what you shared, this five step framework.
alts.zh: 我試著把你剛剛講的整理一下，這個五步驟的框架。

alts.quote: So just to summarize so people can have just a very short definition of this framework.
alts.zh: 所以快速總結一下，讓大家可以有一個很短的定義知道這個框架是什麼。

cards.pattern: Inherent in your question is this assumption that [對方沒說出口的前提]. And so I'm going to reject that premise, because [你的理由].
cards.quote: Well, inherent in your question is this assumption that design takes more time. And so I'm going to kind of reject that premise, because I don't think design takes more time.
cards.zh: 你這個問題裡本身就藏了一個假設：做設計會比較花時間。我要先否掉這個前提，因為我不覺得設計比較花時間。
cards.why: 不去回答問題，而是先把問題底下的假設挖出來擺上桌，再明講「我要拒絕這個前提」。這是英語會議裡最高階的反駁：你沒有反對任何人的立場，你只是指出大家都沒察覺的預設。kind of 是關鍵緩衝，把「拒絕」變成半步後退。
swaps: There's an assumption baked into that question that I'd want to challenge
Before I answer, can I push on the premise a bit?
cards.pmNote: 被問「這要花多久」時，先確認問題本身有沒有錯誤前提——很多 roadmap 爭論其實是前提之爭，不是估時之爭。
cards.episode: 35 years of product design wisdom from Apple, Disney, Pinterest, and beyond | Bob Baxley

alts.quote: I don't think there's any one thing that has happened. I think that a lot of times people ascribe a lot of momentum to a one time change or a single person.
alts.zh: 我不覺得有哪一件事是關鍵。很多時候大家會把一整段動能歸給某一次改動、或某一個人。

alts.quote: I think sometimes people use data a lot or too much because they're worrying or they're afraid that, will I make the wrong choice? And I'm using data to make the choice for me.
alts.zh: 我覺得有時候大家用數據用得太兇，是因為他們在怕：萬一我選錯了怎麼辦？於是就讓數據替他們做決定。

alts.quote: Our loops are less tactical. In fact, if I'm being brutally honest, I think loops are kind of hard to achieve in B2B SaaS.
alts.zh: 我們的成長迴圈比較不那麼戰術。老實說，我覺得在 B2B SaaS 裡要做出真正的迴圈其實蠻難的。

cards.pattern: [X] isn't useful as a decision-making tool, because nobody would ever argue the opposite.
cards.quote: They're not useful as decision-making tools because nobody would ever argue the opposite. Nobody ever sat in a meeting and said, "Oh, forget clear. Let's try to make it as confusing as possible."
cards.zh: 這些東西沒辦法拿來做決策，因為根本不會有人主張反面。從來沒有人在會議上說：「別管清楚了，我們把它做得越難懂越好。」
cards.why: 拆穿廢話的通用檢驗法：能不能想像有人主張反面？不能，就代表這句話沒有決策力。第二句用一個荒謬的假想台詞把論證演出來，比抽象講理有力十倍。
swaps: That's not a real criterion—nobody's going to argue for the opposite
If the opposite of your principle sounds insane, it isn't a principle
cards.pmNote: 設計原則要能砍掉選項才有用；「簡單、清楚、快」這種沒人反對的詞，只是標語不是準則。
cards.episode: 35 years of product design wisdom from Apple, Disney, Pinterest, and beyond | Bob Baxley

alts.quote: I think sometimes people use data a lot or too much because they're worrying or they're afraid that, will I make the wrong choice? And I'm using data to make the choice for me.
alts.zh: 我覺得有時候大家用數據用得太兇，是因為他們在怕：萬一我選錯了怎麼辦？於是就讓數據替他們做決定。

alts.quote: How can you hire people whom you expect to make decisions without running them through you if you can't tolerate them making a decision that you disagree with?
alts.zh: 如果你受不了他們做出你不同意的決定，你怎麼可能招到那種不需要事事回報你就能決策的人？

alts.quote: I really try and stay away from better, because that's really hard to define, and better means something different to everyone.
alts.zh: 我盡量不用「比較好」這個字，因為它很難定義，而且每個人心中的「比較好」都不一樣。

cards.pattern: You're focused on [對方的框架] and I'm just going to push back.
cards.quote: You're focused on recent and I'm just going to push back. No, there's nothing terribly recent.
cards.zh: 你一直扣在「最近」這個點上，我要反過來擋一下——沒有，最近沒什麼特別的。
cards.why: 先把對方問題裡的限制條件講出來（You're focused on X），再宣告自己要反駁。先命名再反對，對方不會覺得被突襲；push back 是英語職場最安全的「我不同意」動詞，比 disagree 輕、比 I think 有力。
swaps: You're framing this as X—let me push back on that
I'm going to push back on the question itself
cards.episode: 35 years of product design wisdom from Apple, Disney, Pinterest, and beyond | Bob Baxley

alts.quote: So I'm going to disagree with Sedaris a little bit.
alts.zh: 這點我要跟 Sedaris 有一點不一樣的看法。

alts.quote: Both things can be true. It's like, yeah, there's nothing perfect in product. However, it is true that some companies are healthier than others.
alts.zh: 這兩件事可以同時成立。對，產品這行沒有什麼是完美的；但同樣真實的是，有些公司確實比其他公司健康得多。

alts.quote: And don't get me wrong, I think there's a lot of product folks out there who enjoy that modality of work, I'm not one of them.
alts.zh: 別誤會，我知道有很多產品人是真的喜歡那種工作方式的——我不是。

cards.pattern: [對方用的那個詞] doesn't feel quite right to me, because [那個詞] feels like [A]. And that's different from [B].
cards.quote: Yeah, sorry. Buy-in doesn't feel quite right to me, because buy-in feels like, oh, I've come to agree with you. And that's different from it's a part of me.
cards.zh: 抱歉，我覺得「buy-in（買單）」這個詞不太對。buy-in 聽起來像「我最後被你說服了」，那跟「這東西本來就是我的一部分」是兩回事。
cards.why: 不反對想法，只反對用詞——這是最低風險的異議。doesn't feel quite right to me 把客觀爭論降級成主觀語感，對方幾乎不可能生氣；接著用 A feels like…that's different from… 把兩個概念的差距拉開。
swaps: I'd use a different word there—X suggests Y, and that's not quite it
"Alignment" doesn't feel like the right word to me
cards.pmNote: buy-in（事後被說服）和 ownership（一開始就在場）是兩種團隊狀態，交付品質差很多。
cards.episode: 35 years of product design wisdom from Apple, Disney, Pinterest, and beyond | Bob Baxley

alts.quote: Yeah, it's definitely a huge part of it. There's a couple of things that I noticed get in the way.
alts.zh: 對，那絕對是很大一塊。不過我有注意到幾件事會卡住。

alts.quote: it's okay to have a culture that doesn't believe that, it's not a culture for me, and that's okay, that's the entire point
alts.zh: 你們公司文化不信這一套也沒關係，那只是不適合我，這樣就好——這本來就是重點。

alts.quote: I don't buy that, because I've met most people and most people are like, "Hell no," when they hear about my life.
alts.zh: 我不買單，因為我見過的大多數人，聽到我的生活方式時的反應都是「才不要」。

cards.pattern: Many of my [同行] will push back on this and they'll say [對方論點], and that's a solid argument as well.
cards.quote: And many of my design friends will push back on this and they'll say design should be its own thing and it should be an independent group and we should have three co-equal branches of government, and that's a solid argument as well
cards.zh: 我很多設計圈的朋友會反對，他們會說設計應該獨立成一個部門，跟產品、工程三權分立——那也是很有道理的論點。
cards.why: 自己先把最強的反方論點講出來，而且承認它成立（that's a solid argument as well）。搶先講反對意見會讓聽者覺得你思考過全局，後面你講自己的立場時可信度直接翻倍。台灣人習慣藏起反例，反而顯得沒想清楚。
swaps: A lot of people will disagree with me here, and honestly they've got a point
The counterargument is X—and it's a good one
cards.pmNote: pre-mortem 的口語版：把反對意見先講掉，比等對方講出來再接招容易十倍。
cards.episode: 35 years of product design wisdom from Apple, Disney, Pinterest, and beyond | Bob Baxley

alts.quote: And I always write them back and say like, "Please tell me the better term and popularize it and I'll use it. It's a great idea."
alts.zh: 我都回信說：「請你告訴我更好的講法，然後把它推廣開，我就會改用。這主意很好。」

alts.quote: Now, obviously if you live in a small town and they capped the well and gave all the water to the data center, then you're really pissed off. But that's a planning problem. That's not a data center problem.
alts.zh: 當然，如果你住在小鎮上，井被封了、水全給了資料中心，那你當然火大。但那是都市規劃的問題，不是資料中心的問題。

alts.quote: That's a good idea, but we don't actually understand these three things before we start working on that. So maybe we should do understand work to make sure that that is actually the right idea.
alts.zh: 這個想法不錯，但在動手之前有三件事我們其實還沒搞懂。也許先做點「理解型的工作」，確認這真的是對的方向。

cards.pattern: Although I know this will frustrate [某群人], I just haven't been able to figure out how [X] works.
cards.quote: And although I know this will frustrate some of my friends, I just haven't been able to figure out how that works for design.
cards.zh: 我知道這樣講會讓一些朋友不爽，但我真的還沒想通這件事在設計上要怎麼運作。
cards.why: 承認不知道 + 承認會惹到人，兩個示弱疊在一起，反而變成資深訊號。I just haven't been able to figure out 的重點在 been able to——它把「我不懂」講成「我努力過但還沒解」。
swaps: I know this isn't a popular view, but I haven't cracked it
This will annoy some people, but I don't have a good answer here
cards.pmNote: 設計團隊該不該背數字，業界至今沒有共識；不要假裝有標準答案。
cards.episode: 35 years of product design wisdom from Apple, Disney, Pinterest, and beyond | Bob Baxley

alts.quote: I don't know enough about it, I don't know what it is, but it wouldn't surprise me if they harnessed inflections in some way that was disorienting to the incumbent.
alts.zh: 這件事我了解得不夠、我也不知道它到底是什麼，但如果他們用某種方式抓住了轉折點、把在位者打亂了，我不會意外。

alts.quote: I don't know if I want to highlight any specific categories, but I can talk about some of the things that we've funded in the past that has real legs.
alts.zh: 我不確定我想特別點名哪些類別，但我可以聊聊我們過去投過、確實有搞頭的一些東西。

alts.quote: I haven't seen their CAD, so I don't know what it's like inside their device, but they do have a lot of things going on.
alts.zh: 我沒看過他們的 CAD 圖，所以我不知道他們裝置裡面長怎樣，但他們確實塞了很多東西進去。

cards.pattern: I would kind of defer to you on that, honestly. You've [對方的優勢], so you have a much broader set of information you're working with.
cards.quote: Yeah, look, I would kind of defer to you on that, honestly. You've talked to a lot more people across a lot more companies, so you have a much broader set of information you're working with.
cards.zh: 老實說這題我聽你的。你跟更多公司、更多人聊過，你手上的資訊面比我廣太多。
cards.why: defer to you 不是投降，是「在這個題目上我把發言權讓給你」，而且立刻給出讓權的具體理由。這招讓你在不知道答案時仍然顯得判斷力清楚——你知道誰該回答這題。
swaps: I'd defer to you here—you've got far more data points than I do
You're closer to this than I am, so I'll take your read on it
cards.pmNote: 跨部門會議中主動 defer 一次，往往換來對方下次在你的地盤 defer 給你。
cards.episode: 35 years of product design wisdom from Apple, Disney, Pinterest, and beyond | Bob Baxley

alts.quote: Look, I won't claim to be an expert on this at all, but I think that with every technology that's come out, we've been able to harness it and it takes a lot of harnessing.
alts.zh: 我先講，我完全不敢說自己是這方面的專家，但我覺得每一種新技術出來，我們最後都有辦法駕馭它，只是那個駕馭要花很多力氣。

alts.quote: I mean, look, I don't know that it's a perfect answer, but I think the reality is just that what kills most projects most early companies is stamina.
alts.zh: 我是說，我不確定這是不是完美的答案，但我覺得現實就是：殺死大多數專案、大多數早期公司的，是續航力。

alts.quote: If you're traditionally trained in product management, this is what you'll do, which is, look, I don't know how to build this in 120 countries.
alts.zh: 如果你是傳統產品管理訓練出來的，你會這樣做：欸，我不知道怎麼在一百二十個國家做這件事。

cards.quote: But if a PM came to me with something that was drawn and kind of fully baked, my response was like, thanks for giving me that. Now I know exactly what we're not going to do.
cards.zh: 如果 PM 拿一張畫得很完整的圖來找我，我的回應是：謝謝你給我這個，現在我很清楚我們「不會」做成這樣。
cards.why: 用感謝當包裝，把拒絕塞在第二句。fully baked（做到全熟）是很有畫面的行話，指「別人已經幫你決定完的方案」。這句的殺傷力來自反差，但也因為有 thanks 開頭而不至於變成人身攻擊。
swaps: That's helpful—now I know one direction we won't take
Appreciate the sketch. I'll treat it as one option to rule out
cards.pmNote: PM 給 designer 的應該是問題與限制，不是解法；給了解法等於把對方降級成畫圖的人。
cards.episode: 35 years of product design wisdom from Apple, Disney, Pinterest, and beyond | Bob Baxley

alts.quote: We're not going to interrupt you with a popup that says like, "Do you want to save your changes," or any of that kind of stuff.
alts.zh: 我們不會用那種「你要儲存變更嗎？」的彈窗打斷你，那類東西都不會有。

alts.quote: Or we're not going to do something unnatural or something that doesn't align with the business goals in order to gain any short term brownie points with investors.
alts.zh: 我們也不會為了在投資人面前拿一點短期的印象分，就去做不自然、或跟商業目標不一致的事。

alts.quote: And so we had this idea that we came up with that would do it. I'm not going to let that one out.
alts.zh: 我們後來想到一個做得到的點子。那個我就不外流了。

cards.pattern: You don't give them [太大的範圍] and you don't even give them [中等範圍]. You give them something more like [剛好的範圍].
cards.quote: You don't give them an airport tarmac and you don't even give them a football field. You give them something more like a basketball court, a sort of scale at which they can do their design thing.
cards.zh: 你不會給他們一整條機場跑道，連足球場都不該給。要給的是差不多籃球場那種大小——大到能發揮，小到能收斂。
cards.why: 把抽象的「範圍要多大」換成三個一路縮小的具體場地，聽的人不用思考就能感覺到尺度差。談 scope 時最難的就是量化，這種遞減式比喻是母語者的標準解法。
swaps: Not a blank cheque, not a straitjacket—somewhere in between
Give them guardrails, not a tiny box
cards.pmNote: 設計需要限制才跑得快；限制不足和限制過度一樣傷產出。
cards.episode: 35 years of product design wisdom from Apple, Disney, Pinterest, and beyond | Bob Baxley

alts.quote: I communicate to my leaders that my expectation is they bring in the clock speed one click faster, which means if you think something needs to be done this year, it needs to be done this half.
alts.zh: 我會跟我的主管們講，我的期待是把時鐘往前撥一格：如果你覺得某件事今年要做完，那就是這半年要做完。

alts.quote: It's important to obsess about the details of craft, while simultaneously having the perspective and wisdom of which details don't actually matter.
alts.zh: 你要對細節的講究到近乎偏執，同時又要有那個判斷力，知道哪些細節其實根本不重要。

alts.quote: And then the last thing I would say about this detection is if you don't know what to do, or all else being equal, then focus on onboarding.
alts.zh: 關於怎麼提早偵測，我最後想講的是：如果你不知道該做什麼，或其他條件都差不多，那就去弄 onboarding。

cards.pattern: If you give [對象] a lot of [問題], they're going to [後果], and honestly, that's your fault as the [對方的角色].
cards.quote: And if you give designers a lot of ambiguity, they're going to spend a lot of time spinning around, and honestly, that's your fault as the client.
cards.zh: 你丟一堆模糊的東西給設計師，他們就會一直空轉——老實說，那是你這個「業主」的問題。
cards.why: 把責任歸屬藏在因果句尾，而不是開頭指著人罵。honestly 在這裡是「我要說重話了」的訊號燈，而 as the client 給了對方一個角色而不是罪名——你批評的是他的職責履行，不是他的人格。
swaps: That's on us as the people writing the brief
Honestly, that one's on the requester, not the team
cards.pmNote: 設計拿到模糊的 input，卻被要求交出精確的 output——這種不對稱是多數 design churn 的根源。
cards.episode: 35 years of product design wisdom from Apple, Disney, Pinterest, and beyond | Bob Baxley

alts.quote: And I think the error that people make more often than not is they are actually too stuck on their own product vision. That's the mistake I've seen a little bit more actually than the other way around.
alts.zh: 我覺得大家最常犯的錯，是太黏著自己原本的產品願景。這個錯我看到的，其實比反過來的那種多一點。

alts.quote: Direct is kind. And it feels kind or, really, honestly, easy to avoid these things or to work around them.
alts.zh: 直說才是善意。避開不談、繞過去，感覺很體貼，其實只是比較輕鬆而已。

alts.quote: The only thing that's different is the insight that the founder has on the market, which is a hard pill to swallow. And I know that's hard to hear too.
alts.zh: 唯一的差別是創辦人對市場的洞察——這顆藥很難吞。我也知道這話很難聽。

cards.pattern: It's not that [對方] couldn't [做那件事], it's just I need you to play that position.
cards.quote: It's not that one of my PM counterparts couldn't bring a lot to the design table, it's just I need you to play that position.
cards.zh: 不是說 PM 對設計沒有貢獻——他們當然有；只是我需要你守住你的位置。
cards.why: It's not that X, it's just Y 是英語裡「擋人但不貶低人」的專用句型：前半句先確認對方有能力，後半句把拒絕轉成分工需求。台灣人常直接講「這不是你的守備範圍」，殺傷力大很多。
swaps: It's not that you can't—it's that I need you covering your own base
Not a capability question, a role question
cards.pmNote: Bob 的棒球比喻：二壘手不會去補一壘；每個人守好自己的位置，整個場才守得住。
cards.episode: 35 years of product design wisdom from Apple, Disney, Pinterest, and beyond | Bob Baxley

alts.quote: It's really important to give two people on your team different charges. One is like go grow the product and the other one is maintain that design, that craft. That tension is extremely healthy.
alts.zh: 團隊裡要刻意讓兩個人扛不同的任務：一個負責把產品做大，另一個負責守住設計跟質感。這種張力其實非常健康。

alts.quote: We've all been under Jeff's Eye of Sauron, we know it's miserable. What can we do to help?
alts.zh: 我們都被那道索倫之眼盯過，知道那有多難受。我們能幫上什麼？

alts.quote: I was like, "First of all, I don't even think I can work with you anymore given this environment you're creating, but I need to understand why you are talking to your team like that."
alts.zh: 我就說：「老實講，看到你製造出來的這種氣氛，我覺得我沒辦法再跟你合作下去了。但我還是想先搞懂，你為什麼會這樣跟你的團隊講話。」

cards.pattern: Let me back up and just dissect a little bit the way you described [X]—you described it in [某種] terms.
cards.quote: Let me back up and just dissect a little bit the way you described design, you described it in really tactical terms.
cards.zh: 先讓我退一步，拆解一下你剛剛描述設計的方式——你講的是很戰術層次的東西。
cards.why: 回答之前先動手拆對方的用詞，等於重新定義整場對話的地基。Let me back up 是英語會議裡最有用的一句話：它買到時間、拿回主導權，而且聽起來像謹慎不像抗拒。
swaps: Can I back up for a second and unpack how you framed that?
Before I answer, let me pull apart the way you're defining it
cards.episode: 35 years of product design wisdom from Apple, Disney, Pinterest, and beyond | Bob Baxley

alts.quote: Let me refine that a little bit more. It's more about giving people the information that they can use for decisions that they alone are good at...
alts.zh: 我把那個講法再修得精準一點。重點比較是：給人們他們才擅長的那類決策所需要的資訊。

alts.quote: And if it's helpful, let me break down the question a little bit.
alts.zh: 如果有幫助的話，我把這個問題拆開來講一下。

alts.quote: Just to pull on this thread a little bit more, what is the general advice you share there for people that also don't want to die?
alts.zh: 順著這條線再拉一下：對那些也不想死掉的人，你通常會給什麼建議？

cards.pattern: Look for places where the team keeps having the same debate over and over, and have it once, get it done, and put it behind you.
cards.quote: So I'd say practically just try to look for places where it seems the team's having the same debate over and over and have it once, get it done, and put it behind you.
cards.zh: 很實際的做法是：找出團隊一再重複爭論的那幾件事，把那場辯論一次辯完、定案、然後永遠翻過去。
cards.why: 三個祈使短句連發（have it once / get it done / put it behind you），節奏本身就是說服力。這是英語裡把「制度化」講得有畫面的標準做法：不是 let's document it，而是把它「放到身後」。
swaps: Let's settle this once so we never have to relitigate it
We keep relitigating this—can we decide it for good today?
cards.pmNote: 重複出現的辯論＝缺一條 tenet；Bob 說 tenet 是決策工具，principle 只是標語。
cards.episode: 35 years of product design wisdom from Apple, Disney, Pinterest, and beyond | Bob Baxley

alts.quote: Now that you've agreed among yourselves that you're going to do that for a fixed period of time, everyone go around the room and say, "If I could start this company over again the thing I wish we were doing was."
alts.zh: 既然大家已經同意用一段固定的時間來試，那就一個一個講：「如果能重來一次，我希望我們在做的是＿＿＿。」

alts.quote: I always say that my superpower is being a professional moron. Because I'm the one that shows up in a room and is like, “Do we have goals? Why are we having this meeting?”
alts.zh: 我常說我的超能力就是當一個專業級的蠢蛋。我就是那種進到會議室會問：「我們有目標嗎？我們現在在幹嘛？這個會到底為什麼要開？」

alts.quote: We start all of our meetings with what are you scared to say in our business?
alts.zh: 我們每場會議都從這個問題開始：在這家公司裡，你不敢講的是什麼？

cards.pattern: It's not about me, it's about the idea. And don't be afraid to stand behind [那個想法].
cards.quote: It's not about you, it's about the idea. And don't be afraid to stand behind the idea.
cards.zh: 重點不是你，是那個想法。而且不要怕站在那個想法後面。
cards.why: 專治華人的「自我推銷罪惡感」：把發聲的主體從自己轉到 idea 上，你就不是在自誇，而是在替一個想法出頭。這一句在 LinkedIn 貼文、公開簡報、爭取資源時都能當開場的心理許可。
swaps: I'm not promoting myself, I'm advocating for this idea
Put the idea forward, not yourself
cards.pmNote: Bob 引 NASA 的 John Hobolt：好想法需要有人賭上職涯去當 champion，否則會躺在那裡幾十年。
cards.episode: 35 years of product design wisdom from Apple, Disney, Pinterest, and beyond | Bob Baxley

alts.quote: Well, first of all, thank you for saying all that. That's giving me too much credit, but I like the idea that it's going to balance out the too little credit I ostensibly get somewhere else, that's great.
alts.zh: 首先謝謝你這樣說。你太抬舉我了——不過我喜歡這個說法，就當作是補回我在別的地方被低估的部分吧。

alts.quote: So at any given point in time, I probably give myself a B to B-, and sometimes it's a C and sometimes it's a D, and sometimes it's an A, and I'm really plugging away, but it's totally an ongoing challenge.
alts.zh: 任何時間點上，我大概給自己 B 到 B-，有時候 C、有時候 D，偶爾也有 A，我真的一直在努力，但這就是個持續的挑戰。

alts.quote: I just want to say, I'm this Nigerian girl. I don't have an MBA, I didn't work in consulting, and I'm here, right?
alts.zh: 我只想說：我就是個奈及利亞女生。我沒有 MBA，也沒做過顧問業，但我人就在這裡。

cards.pattern: What I'm usually looking for is do they have a story as to why [他們相信某件事]?
cards.quote: What I'm usually looking for is do they have a story as to why they believe in design?
cards.zh: 我通常在找的是：他們講不講得出一個故事，說明自己為什麼相信設計？
cards.why: 把抽象的評估標準壓成一個可驗證的動作：不是問「你重不重視設計」，而是看對方有沒有「故事」。另外注意 What I'm looking for is do they…——口語裡嵌入問句不做倒裝，是母語者的自然講法，台灣人常錯寫成 whether they have。
swaps: What I want to hear is whether they can tell me a story about why
The test for me is: is there a story behind the belief?
cards.pmNote: 面試公司時問「你們為什麼相信設計」，答不出故事的公司多半是事後才把設計嫁接上去。
cards.episode: 35 years of product design wisdom from Apple, Disney, Pinterest, and beyond | Bob Baxley

alts.quote: The problem is not like what should my goal be or how should I figure out what to do with my life? They usually know, but it's very hard to actually make time for those things.
alts.zh: 問題不在於「我的目標該是什麼」或「我這輩子要幹嘛」。這個大家其實都知道。問題是很難真的挪出時間去做那些事。

alts.quote: To me, I call it candor and not truth because if I march into a room and I say, "Lenny, I'm going to tell you the truth." I'm kind of implying I've got a pipeline to God and you don't know anything.
alts.zh: 對我來說，我叫它「坦率」而不是「真相」，因為如果我走進一個房間說：「Lenny，我要告訴你真相。」我等於在暗示我有一條直通上帝的專線，而你什麼都不懂。

alts.quote: So Google missed the opportunity of social mobile apps like WhatsApp, like Snapchat, etc and for me this story kind of was the epitome of what I call today, opinion-based development.
alts.zh: Google 錯過了 WhatsApp、Snapchat 這類社交手機 app 的機會，對我來說這個故事就是我今天所說的「意見驅動開發」的極致代表。

cards.pattern: I want to make sure I've got air cover from [最高層], because [沒有的話會怎樣].
cards.quote: I want to make sure I've got air cover from the highest people in the company setting the culture.
cards.zh: 我要確定最高層那些定文化的人會幫我掩護。
cards.why: air cover（空中掩護）是英語職場核心行話：不是要預算、要人，而是要「上面挺你」這種看不見的資源。台灣人談判時常只敢要具體資源，忘了政治掩護本身就能開口要。
swaps: I need top-level cover on this one
I want to know leadership will back this when it gets hard
cards.pmNote: 接高風險專案前先確認 air cover 來源，比談 headcount 更決定成敗。
cards.episode: 35 years of product design wisdom from Apple, Disney, Pinterest, and beyond | Bob Baxley

alts.quote: I love setting a fast pace at the company, but in order to do that with confidence, I need at least one day every week that I'm entirely unplugged.
alts.zh: 我很喜歡替公司設一個快節奏，但要有信心這樣衝，我每週至少需要一天完全斷線。

alts.quote: We always keep this kind of mentality internal is that we're still a young company, we want to grow and you can feel free to talk to anyone.
alts.zh: 我們內部一直維持這種心態：我們還是家年輕公司、我們想長大，所以你要找誰談都可以。

alts.quote: And I want you to say, "This is great. I want to talk about money, but before we do, I want to think about some of the things that will set me up to see succeed in this role.
alts.zh: 我要你這樣說：「這很好。我想談薪水，但在那之前，我想先談談有哪些東西能讓我在這個角色上成功。」

cards.pattern: I came in thinking I was supposed to [做法], which is [那個做法的特徵].
cards.quote: I came in thinking I was supposed to behave the way I behaved at Apple, which is very direct, fighting hard.
cards.zh: 我進去的時候以為我該照在 Apple 的那一套來——非常直接、硬碰硬地爭。
cards.why: I came in thinking… 把錯誤定位成「當時的認知」，而不是「我這個人有問題」。承認失誤而不自我否定，是英語裡談失敗經驗最安全的框架，面試講 failure 時直接可用。
swaps: I walked in assuming the same rules applied, and they didn't
My mistake was importing the old playbook wholesale
cards.pmNote: 換公司時要帶走的是價值觀，不是行為模式——同一種強度在 A 公司叫投入，在 B 公司叫攻擊性。
cards.episode: 35 years of product design wisdom from Apple, Disney, Pinterest, and beyond | Bob Baxley

alts.quote: Here's the way in which I was wrong.
alts.zh: 我來說一下我是哪裡錯了。

alts.quote: And so maybe I picked the wrong term in calling it growth hacking, but I think it at least opened the conversation to getting more people thinking about growth in a different way.
alts.zh: 所以也許我當初取 growth hacking 這個名字是取錯了，但至少它打開了對話，讓更多人開始用不同的方式想成長這件事。

alts.quote: And I was wrong by the way.
alts.zh: 順帶一提，我那時是錯的。

cards.pattern: I agree—[重述對方的顧慮] sounds like a high bar, and in some ways it is. [然後轉折].
cards.quote: I agree, look, having your soul at every little checkbox sounds like a high bar and in some ways it is.
cards.zh: 我同意，聽著，要求每一個小勾選框都灌注靈魂，聽起來標準很高，某種程度上也確實是。
cards.why: 先說 I agree，再把對方的話原封不動重述一次，最後承認 in some ways it is——三層讓步之後才轉折，對方已經沒有防衛的理由。台灣人反駁常跳過重述，對方會覺得沒被聽懂。
swaps: Fair—that does sound like a lot, and in some ways it is
You're right that it's a high bar. Here's why I'd still hold it
cards.episode: 35 years of product design wisdom from Apple, Disney, Pinterest, and beyond | Bob Baxley

alts.quote: In some ways, this sounds very puritanical, I don't mean it to sound this way, but there were lines that we didn't want to cross that just felt ethically not us, that I've seen other news players do more of.
alts.zh: 某種程度上這聽起來很清教徒，我不是要講成那樣，但確實有些線我們不想跨過去，那些做法感覺就不像我們——而我看到別的新聞產品做得更多。

alts.quote: Granted this looks hideous, but in some ways if I wanted to, I could go out and do that, right?
alts.zh: 當然啦，這看起來很醜，但重點是我如果想，我確實可以直接這樣改，對吧。

alts.quote: Here's what I have a problem with. First of all, having a growth mindset is a very, very helpful thing.
alts.zh: 我要說的是我對它的哪一點有意見。首先，擁有成長心態本身是非常非常有幫助的事。

cards.quote: We are about to launch something and then for example I or someone else goes to look at it and sees, "Oh, this doesn't feel right and we should fix it so I don't think we should launch this now."
cards.zh: 我們正要上線，然後我或別人去看了一眼，就會說：「這感覺不對，應該修一下，我覺得現在還不能上。」
cards.why: 喊卡的三段式：感覺判斷（doesn't feel right）→ 行動（we should fix it）→ 結論（I don't think we should launch）。關鍵在把主觀感受先講出來當理由，而不是硬找數據——在品質議題上，這反而更有說服力。
swaps: Something's off here—I'd rather hold the release
This isn't ready. Let's fix it before it goes out
cards.pmNote: Linear 沒有 A/B test 也不設功能指標，上不上線靠團隊試用後的直覺判斷。
cards.episode: Inside Linear: Building with taste, craft, and focus | Karri Saarinen (co-founder, designer, CEO)

alts.quote: So yeah, I think the only way you build something that matters that's going to change the world is if you find a big idea you believe in and you say no to everything else.
alts.zh: 我覺得要做出真正有份量、能改變世界的東西，唯一的路就是找到一個你相信的大想法，然後對其他所有東西說不。

alts.quote: The thing that I think a lot of large companies don't realize is that you can love something to death.
alts.zh: 很多大公司沒意識到的一件事是：你可以把一個東西「愛到死」。

alts.quote: It's like, I don't think I can predict that. I think a much better use of my time is being very flexible and adaptable at a time like this.
alts.zh: 我不覺得我預測得了那個。我覺得我的時間花在保持彈性、快速調整上，回報高得多。

cards.quote: In those stages, the experience can be a little janky or it's not that polished, but we're okay with it because we are saying, "It's not finished. We just want to get your feedback early so we can make it better."
cards.zh: 那個階段體驗可能有點卡、不太精緻，但我們可以接受，因為我們有先講清楚：「這還沒完成，我們只是想早點拿到你的回饋，好把它做得更好。」
cards.why: janky 是矽谷高頻口語（能動但粗糙），台灣人幾乎不會用。整句的語用價值在「先降期待、再要回饋」——把未完成品講成刻意的邀請，客戶的不滿就變成參與感。
swaps: Heads up, it's rough around the edges—that's on purpose
This is an early cut; we want your reaction before we polish it
cards.pmNote: beta 邀請信的標準框架：先聲明未完成、再說明為什麼現在給你看、最後只要一件事（回饋）。
cards.episode: Inside Linear: Building with taste, craft, and focus | Karri Saarinen (co-founder, designer, CEO)

alts.quote: It's so hard to give a founder hard feedback. Who wants to be the bearer of bad news?
alts.zh: 要給創辦人難聽的回饋真的很難。誰想當那個報壞消息的人？

alts.quote: And maybe this is a... I don't want to be very negative, but it's very hard inside a company like ours to task our best engineers to build a best in class sales product.
alts.zh: 我不想講得太負面，但在我們這種公司裡，要把最好的工程師派去做一個頂尖的業務工具，是非常困難的。

alts.quote: You know what? We should ship. It's embarrassing, but that's strictly less bad than not getting the feedback you wanted.
alts.zh: 我覺得就出吧。是很難看沒錯，但這比拿不到你要的回饋還是好一點。

cards.pattern: People think [X] is about [Y]. The downside with that mindset is that [代價].
cards.quote: I think sometimes people think that craft is about perfecting things and perfecting them in a very organized way or very early on. The downside with this perfection mindset is that it can be sometimes hard to put anything out because nothing is ever fully perfect.
cards.zh: 大家常以為所謂「工藝」就是把東西做到完美，而且要很有條理、很早就開始做。這種完美心態的代價是：你可能什麼都出不了貨，因為沒有東西是真正完美的。
cards.why: 不否定對方的價值觀，只指出它的副作用。The downside with this mindset is… 讓你可以反對一個「政治正確」的信念（追求品質）而不被貼上「不重視品質」的標籤。
swaps: The failure mode of that mindset is...
I get why people believe that. The cost is...
cards.pmNote: Linear 的做法是又快又修：第一週就把粗版推到 production，只給內部看。
cards.episode: Inside Linear: Building with taste, craft, and focus | Karri Saarinen (co-founder, designer, CEO)

alts.quote: One thing I've learned is that I think people are really good at coming up with very rational sounding reasons to not do things that just make them uncomfortable.
alts.zh: 我學到一件事：人非常擅長替「其實只是讓自己不舒服的事」找出聽起來很有道理的理由。

alts.quote: I think people assume that there's a much more detailed semantic understanding of everybody's interests and preferences in the algorithm than there is.
alts.zh: 我覺得大家會以為演算法對每個人的興趣和偏好，有一套比實際上細膩得多的語意理解。

alts.quote: So I think it is an utter waste of time for marketing to build these stupid little one pager persona things.
alts.zh: 所以我覺得行銷花時間做那些一頁式的 persona 小卡，根本是浪費時間。

cards.pattern: There's definitely a trade-off. [對方的做法] is more efficient—[但我們選另一邊的理由].
cards.quote: There's definitely a trade-off. I think sometimes when companies specialize roles a lot it's because it's more efficient.
cards.zh: 這確實有取捨。公司把角色切得很細，通常是因為那樣比較有效率。
cards.why: 先承認 trade-off 存在，再主動把對手選項的優點講清楚。這是談優先順序時的信任開關：你證明自己知道放棄了什麼，接下來的選擇才會被當成判斷而不是偏好。
swaps: There's a real trade-off here, and I want to name it
The other approach is genuinely more efficient—we're choosing something else
cards.pmNote: 角色切太細會讓每個人只執行不思考；Linear 刻意讓工程師與設計師承擔部分 PM 職責。
cards.episode: Inside Linear: Building with taste, craft, and focus | Karri Saarinen (co-founder, designer, CEO)

alts.quote: values aren't values unless there's an actual trade-off
alts.zh: 沒有真的要付出代價的價值觀，就不叫價值觀。

alts.quote: And it's hard because in making it compact you're losing completeness.
alts.zh: 這很難，因為你把它壓得越精簡，就越不完整。

alts.quote: Be careful. If you need to spend a little time on the problem, fine, but don't spend a lot of time because you need to save as much time as possible to come up with the winning solution.
alts.zh: 小心一點。你要花一點時間在問題上沒問題，但別花太多，因為你得盡量把時間留給「想出會贏的解法」。

cards.pattern: This is the scope of it for now and we're okay launching this. But we know that this is not the fully figured out version.
cards.quote: So I think a lot of times we just think, okay, this is the scope of it for now and we are okay launching this and the execution is good. But we know that this is not the fully figured out version.
cards.zh: 很多時候我們就是這樣想：現階段範圍就到這裡，執行品質夠好，可以上。但我們知道這還不是完整想通的版本。
cards.why: 把「已完成」和「已想通」拆開來各自宣告，是資深 PM 的招牌動作。for now 與 not the fully figured out version 一前一後，讓上線這件事不必等於承諾終局，也堵住了「所以這樣就好了嗎」的追問。
swaps: This is v1 scope; we're deliberately not solving the rest yet
Good enough to ship, not the end state
cards.episode: Inside Linear: Building with taste, craft, and focus | Karri Saarinen (co-founder, designer, CEO)

alts.quote: And I think people don't understand that in a competitive environment, being right is good, but being quick is necessary.
alts.zh: 我覺得大家沒搞懂：在競爭環境裡，做對是加分，做得快是必要條件。

alts.quote: And now, it's not like, "Okay, now, we're screwed and the project is going to be bigger." Now, we can have a really cool conversation about trade-offs.
alts.zh: 所以現在不是「完了，這專案要爆了」。現在我們可以來一場很棒的取捨對話。

alts.quote: But now I think we're getting to this point where actually if I could only choose one thing to understand, it would be really meaningful understanding of the problems that a certain customer has.
alts.zh: 但我覺得我們現在走到一個階段：如果只能挑一件事搞懂，那就是真正深刻地了解某一群客戶的問題。

cards.pattern: People use [X] too much because they're afraid: will I make the wrong choice? They're using [X] to make the choice for them.
cards.quote: I think sometimes people use data a lot or too much because they're worrying or they're afraid that, will I make the wrong choice? And I'm using data to make the choice for me.
cards.zh: 我覺得有時候大家用數據用得太兇，是因為他們在怕：萬一我選錯了怎麼辦？於是就讓數據替他們做決定。
cards.why: 把對方的行為重新歸因到情緒（fear）而不是理性，是拆假設最有效的一刀。注意他沒說「數據沒用」，只說「你在用它逃避決定」——攻擊動機而不是攻擊工具，對方很難反駁。
swaps: I wonder if we're reaching for data because we don't want to own the call
Are we measuring this, or are we hiding behind the measurement?
cards.pmNote: Karri：「至少那個決定是我們做的，不是數據幫我們做的。」錯了可以改，但決策權要留在人手上。
cards.episode: Inside Linear: Building with taste, craft, and focus | Karri Saarinen (co-founder, designer, CEO)

alts.quote: They're not useful as decision-making tools because nobody would ever argue the opposite. Nobody ever sat in a meeting and said, "Oh, forget clear. Let's try to make it as confusing as possible."
alts.zh: 這些東西沒辦法拿來做決策，因為根本不會有人主張反面。從來沒有人在會議上說：「別管清楚了，我們把它做得越難懂越好。」

alts.quote: More people does not actually make you faster. We think it does. It does not.
alts.zh: 人多不會讓你變快。我們都以為會，但真的不會。

alts.quote: Well, I mean this is the irony of growth, is people think growth is overnight success and it's not. It is a lot of short wins and short-term execution for a longer-term gain.
alts.zh: 成長最諷刺的地方就在這：大家以為成長是一夜爆紅，其實不是。它是一堆短期的小勝仗，堆出長期的結果。

cards.quote: And then we're like, "Well, does it help the customers? Does it help the product?" This sounds like a side quest to me, and basically means we shouldn't do it.
cards.zh: 然後我們就會問：「這對客戶有幫助嗎？對產品有幫助嗎？」這聽起來像支線任務，那基本上就是不該做。
cards.why: 用一個電玩比喻（主線 vs 支線）建立團隊共用的擋需求語彙——一旦大家接受這個詞，拒絕就不再是人跟人的衝突，而是分類問題。This sounds like X to me 也把判斷降級成個人觀感，留了台階。
swaps: Feels like a side quest—fun, but not the main line
Is this on the critical path, or is it a nice-to-have?
cards.pmNote: 在團隊裡建立一個共用的拒絕詞彙（side quest / main quest），比每次重新辯論省 90% 的力氣。
cards.episode: Inside Linear: Building with taste, craft, and focus | Karri Saarinen (co-founder, designer, CEO)

alts.quote: If you need this feature, if you need this integration, I want you back in six months when you use this big product that isn't that great. But today, we're not the right solution for you.
alts.zh: 如果你需要這個功能、需要這個串接，那你先去用那個大廠的爛產品，六個月後再回來找我。今天我們不是適合你的解法。

alts.quote: We're not going to write out long-form content around everything related to dating because that's not the Tinder product.
alts.zh: 我們不會針對所有跟約會有關的東西寫長文，因為那不是 Tinder 這個產品。

alts.quote: The point is growth can amplify great product market fit and growth can help you grow faster once you are already growing. But if you are slowing down, growth is going to be absolutely helpless to do anything.
alts.zh: 重點是：成長團隊可以放大本來就好的 PMF，可以讓已經在成長的東西長更快。但如果你正在衰退，成長團隊完全無能為力。

cards.quote: Or I always have this question, is this important to do now or is it important to maybe do later?
cards.zh: 我一直用的一個問題是：這件事是「現在」重要，還是「以後」才重要？
cards.why: 把 yes/no 的爭論偷換成 now/later 的爭論。對方要的東西你沒有否定它的價值，只重新談時間——這是英語擋需求最不傷感情的一招，也讓你保留了之後真的要做的餘地。
swaps: Not whether, but when
Is this a now problem or a later problem?
cards.pmNote: 把優先順序爭議從價值判斷轉成時序判斷，對方比較不會覺得自己的需求被否定。
cards.episode: Inside Linear: Building with taste, craft, and focus | Karri Saarinen (co-founder, designer, CEO)

alts.quote: Is the juice worth the squeeze? And now I would say that it's pretty clear that the juice is worth the squeeze.
alts.zh: 這個果汁值得你這樣擠嗎？以現在來看，我會說很明顯是值得的。

alts.quote: So yeah, no hard and fast rule, but I think it's always you need to have this matrix of options in your mind and be very deliberate about which one you are going with and why.
alts.zh: 沒有什麼鐵則，但你腦中要有一張選項矩陣，而且要很清楚自己選了哪一格、為什麼。

alts.quote: And now, it's not like, "Okay, now, we're screwed and the project is going to be bigger." Now, we can have a really cool conversation about trade-offs.
alts.zh: 所以現在不是「完了，這專案要爆了」。現在我們可以來一場很棒的取捨對話。

cards.pattern: We know that eventually we need [X], but we don't need it today. So we just say no to that.
cards.quote: And we know that eventually we need to get it, but we don't need it today. So we just say no to that.
cards.zh: 我們知道遲早得弄那個，但今天不需要。所以我們就直接說不。
cards.why: 先承認需求的正當性（eventually we need it），再用時間切割拒絕當下。第三句刻意講得極短乾脆——前面鋪墊夠了，拒絕就不必再解釋。長篇解釋反而會讓對方覺得有討價空間。
swaps: We'll need it one day, just not this quarter
Yes eventually, no now
cards.pmNote: Linear 早期直接跟客戶說「我們還沒有 SOC 2，之後會有」，多數客戶回答 that's fine。
cards.episode: Inside Linear: Building with taste, craft, and focus | Karri Saarinen (co-founder, designer, CEO)

alts.quote: We need to say no to a lot more of this optional work.
alts.zh: 這種「可做可不做」的工作，我們得再多拒絕一些。

alts.quote: I don't think it's particularly productive to say, "Well, is it 20% bigger than the internet or 100%?" Those aren't productive conversations.
alts.zh: 去爭「它比網路大 20% 還是 100%」我覺得沒什麼意義，那種對話不會有產出。

alts.quote: I always say to people don't come to me for management 101, I'm not the person to ask on how to run the most effective one-on-one with your people.
alts.zh: 我常跟人講：管理入門的東西不要來問我，怎麼把一對一開得最有效率，我不是那個該問的人。

cards.pattern: Why was this decision made? Why do you think it was made? Do you think it was the right decision, or did you agree with it?
cards.quote: It's like why was this decision made? Why do you think the decision was made? And I might ask, "Do you think it was the right decision or did you agree on it?"
cards.zh: 像是：這個決定為什麼會做？你覺得為什麼會這樣決定？然後我可能會問：你覺得那是對的決定嗎？你當時同意嗎？
cards.why: 三連問一路往內收：事實 → 對方的推測 → 對方的立場。最後一問把人逼到必須表態，但因為前面兩問已經暖過場，感覺是好奇不是逼問。面試與 1:1 通用。
swaps: What was the thinking behind that? Would you have done it differently?
Why do you think they went that way—and did you buy it?
cards.pmNote: Linear 用這組問題測「產品感」：有沒有觀點、能不能講出理由，比技能本身重要。
cards.episode: Inside Linear: Building with taste, craft, and focus | Karri Saarinen (co-founder, designer, CEO)

alts.quote: I'll say, "I want to run a theory by you. Do you think that the reason why you are really interested in this or you made that decision is actually because of this other thing that you told me a little bit about?"
alts.zh: 我會說：「我想跟你對一個猜測。你會這麼在意這件事、或做了那個決定，會不會其實是因為你剛剛提到的另一件事？」

alts.quote: What we ask people in general is we say, what do you think? We don't say, what do you know? We often say, what do you think?
alts.zh: 我們一般會問人「你怎麼想？」我們不會問「你知道什麼？」我們最常問的就是「你怎麼想？」

alts.quote: And when you do this, the wrong way is to ask, why did you cancel? What you want to do is say, "What made you cancel?"
alts.zh: 問的時候，錯誤版本是「你為什麼取消？」你要問的是：「是什麼讓你取消的？」

cards.pattern: Go slow to go fast. Urgency is important, but too much urgency means [代價].
cards.quote: Go slow to go fast. I think urgency is important, but then sometimes you have too much urgency and you are rushing things.
cards.zh: 先慢才會快。急迫感很重要，但有時候急過頭，你就開始趕，結果反而要回頭重修。
cards.why: 四個字的矛盾句當標題，後面立刻補一句承認對立面的價值（urgency is important）。英語職場很吃這種「口號 + 立刻自我平衡」的結構：口號負責被記住，平衡句負責不被當成偏執。
swaps: Slow is smooth, smooth is fast
Measure twice, cut once
cards.episode: Inside Linear: Building with taste, craft, and focus | Karri Saarinen (co-founder, designer, CEO)

alts.quote: So yeah, no hard and fast rule, but I think it's always you need to have this matrix of options in your mind and be very deliberate about which one you are going with and why.
alts.zh: 沒有什麼鐵則，但你腦中要有一張選項矩陣，而且要很清楚自己選了哪一格、為什麼。

alts.quote: I think it's the difference between oversimplification and focusing. You can have a complex problem and be like, "You know what? I need to hold some things constant."
alts.zh: 我覺得差別在於「過度簡化」和「聚焦」。面對複雜問題你可以說：好，我需要先把某些變數固定住。

alts.quote: A decision with too little data is fatal. A decision that takes too long and collects too much data is also fatal. So it's about trying to find the balance.
alts.zh: 資料太少就下決策，是致命的；拖太久、蒐集太多資料才決策，一樣致命。所以重點是抓到那個平衡。

cards.pattern: What I'm hearing is basically [你的理解]. Is that right?
cards.quote: What I'm hearing is basically you give those responsibilities to the engineers, designer, and maybe other functions within the team. Is that right?
cards.zh: 我聽到的意思基本上是：你們把那些責任分給工程師、設計師，可能還有團隊裡其他角色。我理解對嗎？
cards.why: 英文會議裡沒聽懂卻不想顯得跟不上，這句是最安全的解法：你不是在問「你剛剛說什麼」，而是在展示你的理解版本。basically 讓你的複述不必精準，Is that right? 把驗證的責任交回對方。
swaps: So if I'm following, you're saying X—is that fair?
Let me play that back: X. Did I get that right?
cards.pmNote: 會議中每 10 分鐘做一次 playback，是最便宜的對齊機制。
cards.episode: Inside Linear: Building with taste, craft, and focus | Karri Saarinen (co-founder, designer, CEO)

alts.quote: The reason I'm a little confused, just because I want to get it right, is what I'm hearing, which maybe isn't what you said
alts.zh: 我有點不確定，純粹是想弄清楚——我聽到的（可能不是你講的意思）是……

alts.quote: What I'm hearing is step one is just get your kind of peer leaders aligned behind something that may not obviously be something your leaders want you to do, is that right?
alts.zh: 我聽到的是：第一步就是先把同層的主管拉到同一邊，就算那件事你的上面不見得想要你做——是這樣嗎？

alts.quote: Backing up a little bit, we jumped right in. I'm curious how you even describe positioning, what the heck is positioning?
alts.zh: 稍微倒回去一下——我們一開始就直接跳進來了。我很好奇你會怎麼定義「定位」這件事？

cards.pattern: So just to summarize so far, you have no [A], you have no [B], you have essentially no [C].
cards.quote: So just to summarize so far, you have no metrics, you have no experiments, you have essentially no PMs, just one product leader.
cards.zh: 所以先總結一下：你們沒有指標、沒有實驗、基本上也沒有 PM，只有一個產品負責人。
cards.why: 三個平行的 you have no… 排比，把一堆零散資訊壓成一個有衝擊力的畫面。essentially 是關鍵保險絲——第三項並非完全成立，用一個副詞就避免了被更正。
swaps: So to recap where we are: no A, no B, essentially no C
Let me pull the threads together—here's what I'm taking away
cards.episode: Inside Linear: Building with taste, craft, and focus | Karri Saarinen (co-founder, designer, CEO)

alts.quote: So just to summarize what you shared, which I was just writing as you were talking about the things that essentially help Stripe build this incredible team.
alts.zh: 所以總結一下你分享的——你講的時候我就在寫——那些讓 Stripe 能建出這支超強團隊的東西。

alts.quote: Let me just try to summarize what you shared, this five step framework.
alts.zh: 我試著把你剛剛講的整理一下，這個五步驟的框架。

alts.quote: So to your question, you're a feature team. You want to give it a shot, be in a real product team. These are the four things you need to go out and do.
alts.zh: 回到你的問題：你在一支功能團隊，想試試看真正的產品團隊怎麼運作——那你要去做的就是這四件事。

cards.pattern: That was a tangent, but I want to come back to [原本的主題].
cards.quote: Awesome, that was a tangent because I could not go in that direction, but I want to come back to design again and craft.
cards.zh: 很棒，剛剛那段是離題——我實在忍不住問——但我想拉回設計跟工藝這條線。
cards.why: 主動把自己剛剛的離題命名為 tangent，等於向全場宣告「我知道我們跑掉了，現在收回來」。控場的權力來自命名：你講出偏離，就重新拿回議程。
swaps: Sorry, that was a bit of a detour—back to the main thread
Parking that one. Where we were is...
cards.episode: Inside Linear: Building with taste, craft, and focus | Karri Saarinen (co-founder, designer, CEO)

alts.quote: So let me take us back on track and let's talk about just the high level framework here.
alts.zh: 我們把話題拉回來，來談一下這個框架的高層次架構。

alts.quote: Now that you've agreed among yourselves that you're going to do that for a fixed period of time, everyone go around the room and say, "If I could start this company over again the thing I wish we were doing was."
alts.zh: 既然大家已經同意用一段固定的時間來試，那就一個一個講：「如果能重來一次，我希望我們在做的是＿＿＿。」

alts.quote: Yeah, we can go deep into this and you can pull me back or ask me to go deeper, whatever. It doesn't matter.
alts.zh: 這題我們可以講得很深，你隨時可以把我拉回來，或叫我再講細一點，都行。

cards.pattern: A lot of people see [X] as [簡化的看法]. What you're describing is more of [更細緻的看法].
cards.quote: A lot of people see product market fit as this binary, "I have it or I don't." What you're describing is what I often hear, it's more of this spectrum of more and more confidence.
cards.zh: 很多人把 PMF 看成二元的：不是有就是沒有。而你在描述的，是我常聽到的另一種——它比較像一條逐漸累積信心的光譜。
cards.why: 把對方沒說清楚的話升級成一個對比架構（binary vs spectrum），再掛回對方名下。這是會議裡最高價值的貢獻：你沒有新資訊，但你讓對方的模糊直覺變成一個團隊可以引用的概念。
swaps: Most people treat this as either/or; you're framing it as a spectrum
So it's less a yes/no and more a matter of degree
cards.pmNote: PMF 要按分眾談：對早期新創有、對 Fortune 500 沒有，是完全正常的狀態。
cards.episode: Inside Linear: Building with taste, craft, and focus | Karri Saarinen (co-founder, designer, CEO)

alts.quote: So founder mode means a lot of things to a lot of people. So it's a bit of a Rorschach test
alts.zh: 「founder mode」這個詞，每個人講的都不太一樣，有點像羅夏克墨漬測驗——但真正打到我的部分是⋯⋯

alts.quote: I think they're very related concepts that people sometimes conflate, but I see them as being different. So related, but different.
alts.zh: 我覺得這是常被混用的相關概念，但我把它們看成不同的東西。所以是——相關，但不同。

alts.quote: Let me refine that a little bit more. It's more about giving people the information that they can use for decisions that they alone are good at...
alts.zh: 我把那個講法再修得精準一點。重點比較是：給人們他們才擅長的那類決策所需要的資訊。

cards.quote: It's actually not. It's not. So many people are used to it and they think that it's just how it is, but it's actually not.
cards.zh: 其實不是。真的不是。太多人習慣了，就以為事情本來就是這樣——但其實不是。
cards.why: 重複三次 it's actually not，中間夾一句解釋為什麼大家會誤會（they're used to it）。英語裡拆「這是常態」型假設的標準節奏：先否定、給同理、再否定一次。重複本身就是強調手段，台灣人常改用更長的句子，反而弱。
swaps: Everyone assumes that's just how it works. It isn't
That feels like a law of nature. It's actually a choice someone made
cards.pmNote: 系統之間的依賴多半是可以拆的；好的工程領導的價值就是讓一塊系統能獨立被改。
cards.episode: A better way to plan, build, and ship products | Ryan Singer (creator of “Shape Up,” early employee at 37signals)

alts.quote: More people does not actually make you faster. We think it does. It does not.
alts.zh: 人多不會讓你變快。我們都以為會，但真的不會。

alts.quote: Well, I mean this is the irony of growth, is people think growth is overnight success and it's not. It is a lot of short wins and short-term execution for a longer-term gain.
alts.zh: 成長最諷刺的地方就在這：大家以為成長是一夜爆紅，其實不是。它是一堆短期的小勝仗，堆出長期的結果。

alts.quote: It's actually one of the things I see people fail on the most is they assume something working for one system will work in your world.
alts.zh: 我看到最多人栽的地方就是：他們假設在別的系統上行得通的東西，在你這邊也會行得通。

cards.pattern: I'll quote [某人]: "[一句畫面感強的俗諺]"
cards.quote: So, I think I'll quote Bob Moesta, who's been on your show a couple times, "You can't put 10 pounds of crap in a five pound bag."
cards.zh: 我引 Bob Moesta 一句話：「你沒辦法把十磅的東西塞進五磅的袋子。」
cards.why: 借別人的嘴講難聽話，是英語職場的標準避雷做法：話的粗俗歸原作者，判斷歸你。畫面感越強的俗諺越好用——它會被會議室其他人重複引用，你的立場就自動擴散了。
swaps: As someone once put it, you can't fit a quart into a pint pot
There's a saying I like here:
cards.pmNote: 把巨大專案丟給團隊說「六週內自己砍 scope」不是授權，是推責。
cards.episode: A better way to plan, build, and ship products | Ryan Singer (creator of “Shape Up,” early employee at 37signals)

alts.quote: It's like, I don't think I can predict that. I think a much better use of my time is being very flexible and adaptable at a time like this.
alts.zh: 我不覺得我預測得了那個。我覺得我的時間花在保持彈性、快速調整上，回報高得多。

alts.quote: I don't think it's particularly productive to say, "Well, is it 20% bigger than the internet or 100%?" Those aren't productive conversations.
alts.zh: 去爭「它比網路大 20% 還是 100%」我覺得沒什麼意義，那種對話不會有產出。

alts.quote: If you really need us to put us on the shelf and drop everything for a million dollar deal, we're a startup, we'll do it. But understand, just, is this really really what you want?
alts.zh: 如果你真的要我們把手上的東西全放下、為了這筆一百萬的案子全部重來，我們是新創，我們會做。但你想清楚——這真的是你要的嗎？

cards.pattern: This is a tricky one. So, you're right that [對方說對的部分], but the thing is, in real life, [現實].
cards.quote: This is a tricky one. So, you're right that it's implied, but the thing is, in real life, if you make a commitment and you get alignment that we are going to spend six weeks of engineering time building this thing…
cards.zh: 這題很麻煩。你說得沒錯，那個確實是言下之意，但問題是，現實裡如果你已經做出承諾、也拿到共識要花六週工程時間……
cards.why: 三層緩衝之後才反對：先標記難度（This is a tricky one）、再確認對方哪裡對（you're right that）、最後用 but the thing is, in real life 把戰場從理論拉到現場。台灣人想反駁權威時，這是最完整的安全句型。
swaps: That's the theory, and it's right—in practice it breaks down because...
Yes and no. On paper that's true; in real life...
cards.episode: A better way to plan, build, and ship products | Ryan Singer (creator of “Shape Up,” early employee at 37signals)

alts.quote: I think if you're building a product where it's not necessarily an AI- first product and you have some AI features that are on the side, but it's not the core of your value, I don't know that I would operate this way.
alts.zh: 如果你做的不是 AI 優先的產品，只是旁邊掛幾個 AI 功能、AI 不是核心價值，那我不確定我會這樣做。

alts.quote: And it's kind of building a house that you want every brick in the house to match. And if you go and try and take some bricks from someone else's house and stick it in your house, it's probably going to not look very matched.
alts.zh: 這有點像蓋房子，你會希望每一塊磚都是搭的。如果你跑去人家家裡搬幾塊磚塞進自己家，看起來大概就是不搭。

alts.quote: That's fine, but you're going to need me the next time too. You're going to keep needing me because you're not really becoming a storyteller.
alts.zh: 這樣也行，但下次你還是得找我。你會一直需要我，因為你並沒有真的變成一個會說故事的人。

cards.pattern: We can't just cut [已承諾的核心] and say we shipped on time. That's going to kill everybody's morale.
cards.quote: We can't just cut the scope and say, "Oh, well now, we managed to ship inside of six weeks." That's going to kill everybody's morale.
cards.zh: 我們不能就這樣砍掉範圍，然後說「你看，我們六週內出貨了」。那會把所有人的士氣打死。
cards.why: 反對一個「表面上達標」的解法時，最有力的理由不是邏輯而是後果，而且是人的後果。kill everybody's morale 是英語裡少數可以在會議上直接拿來當否決理由的情緒詞。
swaps: Shipping on time by gutting it isn't a win
That's a technically-on-time, actually-demoralising outcome
cards.episode: A better way to plan, build, and ship products | Ryan Singer (creator of “Shape Up,” early employee at 37signals)

alts.quote: You know what? We should ship. It's embarrassing, but that's strictly less bad than not getting the feedback you wanted.
alts.zh: 我覺得就出吧。是很難看沒錯，但這比拿不到你要的回饋還是好一點。

alts.quote: And the good news bad news is that's true. That is absolutely true.
alts.zh: 好消息也是壞消息：那是真的。千真萬確。

alts.quote: By the way, a very, very successful company for a new set of products has a 50% hit rate. So half of you are going to come back in a year and have a different job. Do you have the resilience to do that?
alts.zh: 順帶一提，一家非常成功的公司做新產品的成功率大概是五成。所以你們有一半的人一年後會換一份工作。你們有那個韌性嗎？

cards.pattern: You probably know what happens when [產物] makes first contact with [另一個團隊]. There's a reality check that happens there.
cards.quote: So you probably know about what happens when the Figma file makes first contact with the engineering team. There's a reality check that happens there and very often, there's a back to the drawing board.
cards.zh: 你大概知道 Figma 檔第一次「接觸」到工程團隊時會發生什麼事。那裡會有一次現實檢驗，而且常常整個打掉重來。
cards.why: makes first contact 借自軍事／科幻，把交付講成一次會出事的遭遇戰。前面加 you probably know，讓聽者站在「我們都懂」的同一邊——描述共同痛點時，先建立同盟再描述傷口。
swaps: You know what happens when the design finally hits engineering
That's where it collides with reality
cards.pmNote: back to the drawing board（打掉重來）是英語職場高頻片語，值得整組背下來。
cards.episode: A better way to plan, build, and ship products | Ryan Singer (creator of “Shape Up,” early employee at 37signals)

alts.quote: So there's, I wouldn't say a checklist, but there's a series of questions that I asked to diagnose why is growth slowing in this order, because it's one of these things where the first one that's a problem, if you don't fix that, it doesn't matter if you fix one of the ones below.
alts.zh: 我不會說那是一張檢查清單，但我確實有一組問題，會照順序問下去診斷成長為什麼變慢——因為只要最前面那個沒修，後面修再多都沒用。

alts.quote: I often say most communication in business is round white and flavorless, intentionally so, because a lot of people are afraid to stand out.
alts.zh: 我常說，商業場合的溝通大多是圓的、白的、沒有味道的——而且是故意的，因為大家都怕突出。

alts.quote: Let's just say there's a product manager and nobody's ever coached this poor person, and so they really don't know much.
alts.zh: 我們就假設有一個產品經理，從來沒有人帶過他，所以他其實懂得不多。

cards.pattern: I often use this analogy: [日常場景]. You can have [表面完美的東西], but if you haven't checked [底層的隱藏條件], it's going to drastically change the cost.
cards.quote: I often use this analogy of if you're doing a home renovation, you can have the most beautiful rendering of the new bedroom. But if you haven't checked if there's electricity in that wall there or not, it's going to drastically change the cost and the time and everything.
cards.zh: 我常用一個比喻：你在裝修房子，臥室的效果圖可以做得美到不行。但如果你沒去確認那面牆裡到底有沒有電線，成本跟時間都會整個變樣。
cards.why: I often use this analogy of… 直接宣告接下來是比喻，聽者立刻切換到「聽故事」模式。比喻本身選了一個對方一定有經驗的場景（裝修），而且精準對應到技術債：漂亮的表面 vs 牆裡看不見的東西。
swaps: The analogy I keep coming back to is...
Think of it like renovating a house you haven't opened the walls on
cards.pmNote: shaping 的核心就是「先開牆看管線」——在承諾時間之前把未知拆出來。
cards.episode: A better way to plan, build, and ship products | Ryan Singer (creator of “Shape Up,” early employee at 37signals)

alts.quote: It's like you had a very smooth flight across the Atlantic and your landing was absolutely horrible. You're not going to remember the smooth flight, you're going to remember the ending.
alts.zh: 就像你飛越大西洋一路很平穩，結果降落爛透了。你不會記得那段平穩的飛行，你只會記得結尾。

alts.quote: I think the hardest thing for a founder, challenge is not optional. You're going to be challenged, but the suffering is optional.
alts.zh: 對創辦人來說最難的是：挑戰不是選項，你一定會被挑戰；但要不要痛苦，是選項。

alts.quote: In lay person's terms, the second law of thermodynamics, I'm paraphrasing here, is that, 'Over time, unless you intervene, everything goes to crap.'
alts.zh: 用白話講，熱力學第二定律——我這是意譯——就是：隨著時間過去，除非你出手干預，不然一切都會爛掉。

cards.pattern: It's not [大而模糊的名詞]. It's [具體到可執行的描述].
cards.quote: So, what you can see here is it's not like, what is a calendar? It's not a calendar. It's a two-month dot grid with scrolling agenda view underneath.
cards.zh: 所以你看，重點不是「什麼叫行事曆」。它不是一個行事曆，它是「兩個月的圓點格線，下面搭一個可捲動的議程檢視」。
cards.why: 先否定那個大詞，再用一句精準到可以動手的描述取代它。這一招同時完成兩件事：擋掉無限膨脹的期待，並讓工程師當場知道要蓋什麼。名詞越大越危險，是英語產品討論的共識。
swaps: We're not building "search"—we're building X, Y and Z
Let's stop saying dashboard and say what it actually is
cards.pmNote: 專案名稱如果是一個名詞（calendar / dashboard），就代表還沒 framing 完。
cards.episode: A better way to plan, build, and ship products | Ryan Singer (creator of “Shape Up,” early employee at 37signals)

alts.quote: And so the anti-pattern I see is there are lots of founders that are very familiar with your awesome work.
alts.zh: 所以我常看到的反模式是：很多創辦人非常熟你那些很棒的內容（然後在錯的階段照做）。

alts.quote: I think that the issue is, it's not just about product market fit, it is about achieving a product market pricing fit.
alts.zh: 我覺得問題在於：重點不只是 product-market fit，而是要做到 product-market-pricing fit。

alts.quote: The problem is not like what should my goal be or how should I figure out what to do with my life? They usually know, but it's very hard to actually make time for those things.
alts.zh: 問題不在於「我的目標該是什麼」或「我這輩子要幹嘛」。這個大家其實都知道。問題是很難真的挪出時間去做那些事。

cards.pattern: I've got to tell you, the dominant failure case that I see in the real world is always, again and again, [根因].
cards.quote: I got to tell you, the dominant failure case that I see in the real world is always, again and again, not enough detail.
cards.zh: 我得說，我在現實世界裡看到的主要失敗模式，一次又一次都是同一件事：細節給得不夠。
cards.why: I got to tell you 是「我要講一句你可能不愛聽的話」的訊號。in the real world 與 again and again 把個人意見升級成觀察樣本——沒有數字，卻建立了經驗權威。
swaps: Honestly, the most common failure mode I see is...
Nine times out of ten, the root cause is the same thing
cards.episode: A better way to plan, build, and ship products | Ryan Singer (creator of “Shape Up,” early employee at 37signals)

alts.quote: And again, I'm not saying always, but sometimes it can happen that the thing that ends up shipping is the least common denominator that annoyed everybody the least amount, right?
alts.zh: 我不是說每次都這樣，但有時候最後出貨的東西，就是那個讓所有人都最不生氣的最小公約數。

alts.quote: Hey, here's what I'm seeing and tell me what's going on for you.
alts.zh: 我先講我這邊看到的狀況，然後換你講講你那邊發生了什麼事。

alts.quote: Now, to be clear, most of that is garbage in the real garbagey sense, right.
alts.zh: 先把話講清楚，那裡面大部分都是垃圾，字面意義上的垃圾。

cards.pattern: I can understand why the hair stands up on the back of your neck thinking about that.
cards.quote: But I can understand why the hair stands up on the back of the neck a little bit thinking about it because, of course, if you give a senior engineer like, "Here's how I want you to go implement the schema"…
cards.zh: 但我理解為什麼你一想到這個就會汗毛豎起來——畢竟你如果去跟資深工程師說「這個 schema 我要你這樣實作」……
cards.why: 先替對方把還沒說出口的生理反應講出來。用身體感覺（hair stands up）而不是抽象的 concern，對方會覺得「他真的懂我在怕什麼」，接下來的反駁就進得去。
swaps: I get why that makes people bristle
I know that sets off alarm bells—let me explain
cards.episode: A better way to plan, build, and ship products | Ryan Singer (creator of “Shape Up,” early employee at 37signals)

alts.quote: But the only way to build long-term enduring value with a marketplace is to corner the demand side. And so it's kind of a little bit that evolution of a marketplace that ends up changing who you focus on.
alts.zh: 但要做出長期能留住價值的市集，唯一的路是掌握需求端。所以那有點像是市集的演化，會慢慢改變你該把重心放在誰身上。

alts.quote: If someone else has a strategy for moving revenue that isn't getting it from customers, I want to know about it because it's so hard to get it from customers.
alts.zh: 如果有人有辦法在不靠客戶的情況下推動營收，我很想知道，因為從客戶身上拿到營收真的太難了。

alts.quote: You have to really understand why someone uses your product, because not every great thing is going to be invented by you.
alts.zh: 你得真的搞懂別人為什麼用你的產品，因為不是每一個好東西都會由你發明出來。

cards.pattern: It's not a universal thing. [X] is a dial that we can turn, and it depends on [變數].
cards.quote: But what's really interesting is it's not a universal thing. The amount of detail that the team is going to feel helps them is a dial that we can turn that depends on who's on the team.
cards.zh: 但有趣的是，這件事沒有通則。要給多少細節其實是一個可以轉的旋鈕，看團隊裡是誰。
cards.why: a dial we can turn 把 A/B 二選一的爭論轉成連續刻度，爭論立刻消失——大家不再爭立場，而是一起找刻度。這是英語裡化解「該多還是該少」型爭執最漂亮的一個比喻。
swaps: It's a dial, not a switch
There's no universal answer—it slides depending on the team
cards.pmNote: 資淺工程師需要更多細節才敢動手，資深的則相反；細節量該按人調，不是按流程調。
cards.episode: A better way to plan, build, and ship products | Ryan Singer (creator of “Shape Up,” early employee at 37signals)

alts.quote: What's the hill that I'm going to die on and is this something that I can shift or is this something that is not worth shifting?
alts.zh: 哪座山是我願意死守的？這件事我推得動嗎？還是根本不值得去推？

alts.quote: So yeah, no hard and fast rule, but I think it's always you need to have this matrix of options in your mind and be very deliberate about which one you are going with and why.
alts.zh: 沒有什麼鐵則，但你腦中要有一張選項矩陣，而且要很清楚自己選了哪一格、為什麼。

alts.quote: Not all of these variables is created equal and the manager is the most important variable in the environment, because a great manager who is empathetic, who is aware of what's going on, has the ability to move the chess pieces around.
alts.zh: 這幾個變數的份量不一樣，主管是環境裡最關鍵的那一個——因為一個有同理心、狀況清楚的好主管，是有能力幫你把棋子移一移的。

cards.pattern: It's not like now we're screwed. Now we can have a really cool conversation about trade-offs.
cards.quote: And now, it's not like, "Okay, now, we're screwed and the project is going to be bigger." Now, we can have a really cool conversation about trade-offs.
cards.zh: 所以現在不是「完了，這專案要爆了」。現在我們可以來一場很棒的取捨對話。
cards.why: 壞消息出現時把它重新標籤成機會。先把大家腦中最糟的解讀原句念出來（now we're screwed），再直接否定並替換——因為對方那句話已經被說出口，反駁才有著力點。
swaps: This isn't a disaster—it's the conversation we needed to have
Good news: we found it now, not in week four
cards.pmNote: 早期發現複雜度是好事；同一個發現出現在 build 第四週就是災難。
cards.episode: A better way to plan, build, and ship products | Ryan Singer (creator of “Shape Up,” early employee at 37signals)

alts.quote: Now, again, don't hear this as antagonistic. We're not antagonistic here. We're trying to say, "What's going to help me succeed?"
alts.zh: 再說一次，不要把這聽成對立。我們不是在對抗。我們是在問：什麼能幫我把這件事做成？

alts.quote: It's like a stepping stone back, but there is a much bigger room for upside that you can get to, but you are going to have to work to get to that upside.
alts.zh: 它其實是往後退一步，但後面有大得多的上升空間可以拿——只是你得努力才走得到。

alts.quote: You get to these points of just diminishing marginal return in every system where it feels like you could put 50 people on this project, it's just not going to dramatically move the needle.
alts.zh: 每個系統都會走到邊際效益遞減的那個點——你感覺得出來，就算再丟 50 個人下去，也不會讓數字有什麼大變化。

cards.pattern: By the way, I'm being very mean to [X] so far in this conversation. There is a time when it's the right time for [X].
cards.quote: By the way, I'm being very mean to Figma so far in this conversation. There is a time when it's the right time for the Figma file.
cards.zh: 順帶一提，我到目前為止對 Figma 有點太兇了。Figma 檔是有它對的時機的。
cards.why: 自己承認立場偏頗，等於預先拆掉對方「你就是討厭 X」的反擊。being mean to 是很輕鬆的自嘲用詞，把一場可能變成派系之爭的討論拉回技術層面。
swaps: I've been unfair to X here—it does have its place
To be clear, I'm not anti-X; I'm anti-X-too-early
cards.episode: A better way to plan, build, and ship products | Ryan Singer (creator of “Shape Up,” early employee at 37signals)

alts.quote: So I think it's an unnecessary addition, but maybe I'm just being protective of my original idea.
alts.zh: 我覺得那是多此一舉的補充，不過也可能只是我在護著自己原本的想法啦。

alts.quote: But as an overall missive, don't focus on your competitors is terrible advice. And if I'm being charitable, it's just outdated
alts.zh: 但當成通則來講，「不要管競爭對手」是很爛的建議。往好處說的話，它只是過時了。

alts.quote: I'm not sure we're solving the right problem, but boy, we run a great meeting." And it's not meant to diminish any of that.
alts.zh: 「我不確定我們解的是不是對的問題，但天啊，我們的會開得可真好。」而且這不是要否定那些努力。

cards.pattern: It's [完成的定義] if we can give this to [某人] and they say, "Yeah, I know what to go do now."
cards.quote: So maybe this is a way to come back to your question about what's the output of the shaping session, it's like it's shaped if we can give this to a technical person and they say, "Yeah, I know what to go build now."
cards.zh: 所以回到你剛剛問的「shaping session 的產出是什麼」：判準是——把它交給一個技術的人，他會說「好，我知道要蓋什麼了」。
cards.why: 先明講「這是在回你剛剛的問題」（長篇回答後的必要收線），再用一句對方會講的台詞當驗收標準。把抽象的完成定義換成一個可觀察的行為，是英語裡定義 done 的最佳實務。
swaps: The test is whether the builder says "I know what to do now"
Coming back to your question—here's the acceptance criterion
cards.pmNote: 定義 done 時用「誰會說出什麼話」，比用文件清單更難鑽漏洞。
cards.episode: A better way to plan, build, and ship products | Ryan Singer (creator of “Shape Up,” early employee at 37signals)

alts.quote: So let's take a step back. The fear is, if I can reflect back to your original question, the fear is if I go there, I don't know what's going to happen as a consequence of that.
alts.zh: 我們退一步看。如果我把你原本的問題回映給你，那個恐懼是：如果我真的往下探，我不知道會發生什麼後果。

alts.quote: Sometimes I'm like, "Who's owning this?" And it's like people don't know. That's why I think it's very important to have a single-threaded owner.
alts.zh: 有時候我問「這件事誰在 own？」結果大家都不知道。這就是為什麼一定要有一個單一負責人。

alts.quote: I'm in too many conversations where I'm like, "Who is on the hook for this decision? Who cares if this decision is made?" It's not like six people with consensus. Who is the person?
alts.zh: 我參加過太多會議，我會問：「這個決定是誰扛？誰真的在乎它有沒有被做出來？」不是六個人共識，是哪一個人？

cards.pattern: I would say wait until it hurts more. If [不熟悉] is the big problem, then maybe things are fine.
cards.quote: I would say wait until it hurts more. If the unfamiliarity is the big problem with it, then maybe the things are fine.
cards.zh: 我會說：等到更痛再來。如果你最大的問題只是「不熟悉」，那可能表示現在其實還好。
cards.why: 把自己的方法論往外推。勸人不要買你在賣的東西，是最強的可信度動作；語言上的關鍵是給出一個判準（痛感 vs 陌生感），讓拒絕聽起來像診斷而不是謙虛。
swaps: Honestly, don't change until the pain is real
If it's just unfamiliar rather than painful, leave it alone
cards.episode: A better way to plan, build, and ship products | Ryan Singer (creator of “Shape Up,” early employee at 37signals)

alts.quote: Pulling off other responsibilities is no problem. It's a good thing to do, especially as you grow, but never when you touch those three sacred things.
alts.zh: 把其他職責分出去完全沒問題，隨著規模變大這反而是好事——但前提是不能碰到那三件神聖不可讓的事。

alts.quote: When I first started out in PM somebody, it's obviously a chestnut, but he pointed out that realistically when you're a product manager, your job is to say no to 90% of things that get brought your way.
alts.zh: 我剛入行做 PM 的時候，有人跟我說——雖然是老生常談——現實是，PM 的工作就是把送到你面前的事拒絕掉九成。

alts.quote: You can say, "Yes, I agree. That is a real problem. Yes, I think we could test this design with users."
alts.zh: 你可以說：「對，我同意，那確實是個真的問題。對，我覺得這個設計我們可以拿去跟使用者測。」

cards.quote: Of course, I don't want to be cruel to the people who are putting their hearts into that work, because the Figma file is beautiful. It's just coming a little early.
cards.zh: 當然，我不想對那些真心投入的人太苛刻——那些 Figma 檔真的很漂亮。只是它來得太早了一點。
cards.why: 把批評從「品質不好」改成「時機不對」，是保住對方尊嚴的最短路徑。三段結構：宣告不想傷人 → 具體稱讚 → 用一句極輕的話點出問題（just / a little 兩個減壓詞疊用）。
swaps: The work is good—it's just landing at the wrong point in the process
Nothing wrong with it. It's premature, not bad
cards.episode: A better way to plan, build, and ship products | Ryan Singer (creator of “Shape Up,” early employee at 37signals)

alts.quote: Look, I don't have time to sugarcoat any feedback, and frankly, the best people I've worked with are the people who come into one-on-ones with me and yell at me and tell me I'm messing up.
alts.zh: 老實說，我沒空把回饋包糖衣；而且說真的，我合作過最好的人，都是會在一對一裡對我吼、直接說我哪裡搞砸了的人。

alts.quote: So when the feedback is coming like raw, they know that it's in their best interest because I've shown them enough times that I genuinely care about the person behind the role.
alts.zh: 所以當回饋很生硬地丟過來，他們知道那是為他們好——因為我已經用夠多次證明，我在乎的是角色背後那個人。

alts.quote: And it's not because people are bad people. I think most people are really well-intentioned. But what happens when you have people that join and you didn't really need them?
alts.zh: 這不是因為誰是壞人，我覺得大多數人動機都很好。但問題是：當你招了一批其實不需要的人，會發生什麼事？

cards.quote: You write this document and I'm sorry, who actually reads it? You know what I mean? I know it's painful, but it's like that.
cards.zh: 你寫了那份文件——不好意思，但到底有誰真的會讀？你懂我意思吧？我知道這很刺耳，但事實就是這樣。
cards.why: I'm sorry 插在句中，不是道歉而是「我要說實話了」的減震器。結尾 I know it's painful, but it's like that 承認對方會不舒服卻不收回主張——承認情緒、不撤回內容，是英語說重話的標準收尾。
swaps: Sorry to be blunt, but does anyone actually read these?
I know that stings, but that's the reality
cards.episode: A better way to plan, build, and ship products | Ryan Singer (creator of “Shape Up,” early employee at 37signals)

alts.quote: Go and talk to that executive and say, "Look, I know you've told me to do this, but what would we observe if this was working versus not working? I'm here to help you with that."
alts.zh: 你可以去找那位主管說：「我知道你已經指定要做這個了，但如果它有效跟沒效，我們會分別看到什麼？這部分我可以幫你。」

alts.quote: So, I don't really care how high quality the initial MVP is because quality is defined by the customer. And if we don't know who our customer is, we literally don't know what the word quality means.
alts.zh: 所以第一版的 MVP 品質多高，我其實沒那麼在意，因為品質是由客戶定義的。如果我們連客戶是誰都不知道，我們根本不知道「品質」這兩個字是什麼意思。

alts.quote: It's felt like we've been in a time of great technological change. But actually, if you look for actually evidence of that, in statistical evidence of that, analytical evidence of that, you basically can't find it.
alts.zh: 大家都覺得這幾十年科技變化很快。但你真的去找證據——統計上的、分析上的——其實根本找不到。

cards.pattern: Well, I understand what the [某某] critique is supposed to be. The thing is, [你的反轉].
cards.quote: Yeah. Well, I understand what the feature factory critique is supposed to be.
cards.zh: 嗯，我理解「功能工廠」這個批評原本想講的是什麼。
cards.why: is supposed to be 這三個字很毒：它同時表示「我懂這個說法的原意」和「但它沒有真的成立」。想質疑一個流行術語又不想顯得沒讀書時，這是最省力的開場。
swaps: I know what that critique is meant to capture
I take the point behind the term, but
cards.episode: A better way to plan, build, and ship products | Ryan Singer (creator of “Shape Up,” early employee at 37signals)

alts.quote: If you don't say yes, what you're essentially saying is, I am so presumptuous that I understand what's on the other side of that door already.
alts.zh: 你如果不答應，你其實等於在說：我狂妄到已經知道那扇門後面是什麼了。

alts.quote: It's like you can't have it both ways, buddy. Are you the Superman who's reordering the whole world to your whim? Well, then you have moral responsibility for the outcomes.
alts.zh: 你不能兩邊都要。你到底是不是那個要照自己意思重排整個世界的超人？是的話，結果的道德責任你就得扛。

alts.quote: I still think that things that we interviewed for in the past, a critical mindset, the ability to really understand deeply the technical nature of a problem is still much more important than whether you're a fully AI native programmer or not.
alts.zh: 我還是認為我們過去在面試裡看的那些東西——批判性的思維、能真正深入理解問題技術本質的能力——遠比你是不是一個完全 AI 原生的工程師重要得多。

cards.pattern: Imagine: [極端的對照場景]. No such thing as [你們每天在忍的事]. Never.
cards.quote: Yeah. Imagine, no such thing as a request from sales, yeah? No such thing as pressure of like, "We need this thing in order to upsell or to close this deal." Never.
cards.zh: 你想像一下：完全沒有業務來提需求，好嗎？也完全沒有那種「我們需要這個功能才能升級方案、才能成交」的壓力。從來沒有。
cards.why: 用 Imagine 開頭把聽者拉進一個他沒經歷過的世界，再用 No such thing as… 連續否定他每天在忍的事，最後單字成句的 Never 收尾。解釋「為什麼別人的做法在你這裡行不通」時，這比列差異清單有效太多。
swaps: Picture a world where nobody's asking you for a deal-blocker feature
Now imagine none of that pressure exists. That was their setup
cards.pmNote: 抄別人的流程前先看他們的前提：Basecamp 沒有業務團隊，所以工程時間從不被搶。
cards.episode: A better way to plan, build, and ship products | Ryan Singer (creator of “Shape Up,” early employee at 37signals)

alts.quote: I think the thing you really need to know is that for under 16-year-olds, if they want to change any of these defaults, they're going to have to get their parents' permission.
alts.zh: 我覺得你真正需要知道的是：未滿 16 歲的用戶如果想改這些預設值，必須先拿到父母同意。

alts.quote: Maybe my best advice here is for founders to put themselves in the shoes of investors and just imagine what their life is like and how if you are in their shoes you would make decisions.
alts.zh: 我最好的建議大概是：創辦人去站在投資人的位置上，想像他們的日子長什麼樣、如果換成你會怎麼做決定。

alts.quote: Virtual office could get pretty good, but we would never beat that. And so we were almost limited in our own imagination about how good could this product be.
alts.zh: 虛擬辦公室可以做到不錯，但我們永遠贏不過真實見面。所以我們等於是被自己的想像力上限卡住了——這個產品最好能到哪裡。

cards.pattern: I've got to tell you, I had no idea how unique we were until I was outside.
cards.quote: I got to tell you, I had no idea how unique we were until I was outside and there are so many things.
cards.zh: 我得說，直到我離開之後，我才知道我們當時有多特殊——太多事情都是。
cards.why: 承認自己曾經把特例當通則，是寫過書、給過建議的人最需要的一句話。until I was outside 把認錯講成視角變化，而不是能力不足——既保住權威，又贏得信任。
swaps: I didn't realise how unusual our setup was until I left
I was taking a lot of things for granted that turned out to be rare
cards.episode: A better way to plan, build, and ship products | Ryan Singer (creator of “Shape Up,” early employee at 37signals)

alts.quote: But basically what happened is that we pushed out an update that made the model more likely to tell you things that sound good in the moment.
alts.zh: 簡單講就是，我們推了一個更新，結果讓模型更容易講出那種當下聽起來很順耳的話。

alts.quote: I don't want them to leave it at, "It was a big loss." You want to say, "What I learned from that is now I always run a load test, and I've had many successful launches since then."
alts.zh: 我不希望他只停在「那是一次很大的損失」。你應該說：我從那件事學到，現在我一定會先跑壓力測試，後來的好幾次上線都沒再出過同樣的問題。
