alts.quote: So it's someone that as a leader, you are in the hot seat and you can take accountability. So if some of these things don't pan out, it's on you and not on your team, and give your team permission to fail.
alts.zh: 身為領導者，你就是坐在火線上、要負起責任的人。如果這些事沒成，那是你的責任，不是團隊的責任——同時給團隊失敗的許可。

cards.pattern: To set the answer up, I'll give you a super brief history of [背景].
cards.quote: To set the answer up, I'll give you a super brief history of Make Time.
cards.zh: 為了鋪陳我的答案，我先講一段 Make Time 的超簡短來歷。
cards.why: 先宣告「我要繞路，但這是為了回答你」。台灣人在英文會議裡最怕的就是講一長串背景卻讓人以為離題；一句 to set the answer up 就買到了一段合法的鋪陳時間，super brief 又預告了長度。
swaps: Quick bit of context before I answer
Let me set that up with 30 seconds of background
cards.episode: Making time for what matters | Jake Knapp and John Zeratsky (authors of Sprint and Make Time, co-founders of Character Capital)

alts.quote: Just to make sure I understand what you're saying there, you're saying generally maybe third party tools limit what you can do, which set you up for hardship later.
alts.zh: 我確認一下我有聽懂你的意思：你是說一般來說第三方工具會限制你能做的事，之後會讓你很痛苦。

alts.quote: To make this even more concrete for people that are starting to like, oh, shit I got to do this. Can you just give us a list that doesn't have to be exhaustive?
alts.zh: 為了讓大家更具體一點——那些正在想「糟糕我得開始做了」的人——你可以給我們一個清單嗎？不用列很完整沒關係。

alts.quote: So I think about it as designing an interface and make it an extension of yourself rather than a black box on its own that you just need more information to. Is that helpful?
alts.zh: 所以我把它想成在設計一個介面，讓它成為你的延伸，而不是一個你只能不斷餵資料的黑盒子。這樣講有幫到你嗎？

cards.pattern: The problem is not [大家以為的問題]. They usually know that. The problem is [真正的問題].
cards.quote: The problem is not like what should my goal be or how should I figure out what to do with my life? They usually know, but it's very hard to actually make time for those things.
cards.zh: 問題不在於「我的目標該是什麼」或「我這輩子要幹嘛」。這個大家其實都知道。問題是很難真的挪出時間去做那些事。
cards.why: 定義問題的標準動作：先否定一個大家預設的問題，再指出真正的痛點。中間插一句 they usually know 是關鍵——它證明你調查過，不是在憑空重新定義。
swaps: It's not a clarity problem, it's an allocation problem
People know what matters. What they can't do is protect the time for it
cards.pmNote: problem statement 寫壞的第一名死法：解決一個大家早就解決了的問題。
cards.episode: Making time for what matters | Jake Knapp and John Zeratsky (authors of Sprint and Make Time, co-founders of Character Capital)

alts.quote: So there's, I wouldn't say a checklist, but there's a series of questions that I asked to diagnose why is growth slowing in this order, because it's one of these things where the first one that's a problem, if you don't fix that, it doesn't matter if you fix one of the ones below.
alts.zh: 我不會說那是一張檢查清單，但我確實有一組問題，會照順序問下去診斷成長為什麼變慢——因為只要最前面那個沒修，後面修再多都沒用。

alts.quote: Everyone that I know says they have a bottom of funnel problem. It's never a bottom of funnel problem. It's a top of funnel problem.
alts.zh: 我認識的每個人都說自己是漏斗底部有問題。從來都不是漏斗底部的問題，是漏斗頂端的問題。

alts.quote: One is people set this goal, I want to be promoted the next thing, or I want to lead this big project. And those are bad goals, because it's not in your control. A good goal is what you can do.
alts.zh: 有一種是設「我要升到下一級」或「我要主導那個大專案」。這些是壞目標，因為不在你的掌控裡。好目標是你自己做得到的事。

cards.pattern: And I don't mean to sound like I'm above it all and have figured it all out. It still [你也還在犯的事].
cards.quote: And I don't mean to sound like I'm above it all and have figured it all out. It still drives my stress
cards.zh: 我不是想擺出一副「我早就超脫了、全都想通了」的樣子。那件事到現在還是讓我很焦慮。
cards.why: 教別人做某件事時最容易失去的就是可信度。這句先否認自己站在制高點，再承認自己仍受同樣困擾——聽眾從「被說教」切換成「同一條船」。給建議、做內部分享、寫文件開頭都能用。
swaps: I'm not saying I've cracked this—I still fall into it
Not preaching from the mountain here; I struggle with it too
cards.episode: Making time for what matters | Jake Knapp and John Zeratsky (authors of Sprint and Make Time, co-founders of Character Capital)

alts.quote: I mean, I think Things probably, I'm just guessing, I don't know any of the numbers or whatever, but I would assume it makes between five and $25 million of revenue, which to a VC is not even worth considering a VC.
alts.zh: 我是說，Things 這款——我純粹在猜，數字我完全不知道——但我猜它一年營收大概在五百萬到兩千五百萬美金之間，這種規模對創投來說根本不值得看。

alts.quote: I mean, look, I don't know that it's a perfect answer, but I think the reality is just that what kills most projects most early companies is stamina.
alts.zh: 我是說，我不確定這是不是完美的答案，但我覺得現實就是：殺死大多數專案、大多數早期公司的，是續航力。

alts.quote: I don't know that I'm perfect at it, but I've learned to balance those things quite a bit more than I did in the past when I would just purely read from my questions and my rubric and not care about anything else.
alts.zh: 我不敢說我做得多完美，但我已經學會比以前平衡得多了——以前我只會照著自己的問題清單和評分表念，其他一概不管。

cards.pattern: At the top of the interview you asked, "[原問題]" And I'll frame my answer in those terms.
cards.quote: At the top of the interview, Lenny, you asked, "What do most people get wrong when they think about this productivity, time management, whatever?" And I'll frame my answer in those terms.
cards.zh: Lenny，你一開始問過：「大家在生產力、時間管理這些事情上最常搞錯什麼？」我就用那個框架來回答。
cards.why: 回頭引用對方半小時前的問題，等於證明你一直在聽，也讓長回答有了正當理由。I'll frame my answer in those terms 更是控場：接下來用「我的框架」講，但功勞掛在對方問題上。
swaps: Going back to what you asked at the start—let me answer it in those terms
You asked earlier about X; I'll use that frame
cards.episode: Making time for what matters | Jake Knapp and John Zeratsky (authors of Sprint and Make Time, co-founders of Character Capital)

alts.quote: I think they're very related concepts that people sometimes conflate, but I see them as being different. So related, but different.
alts.zh: 我覺得這是常被混用的相關概念，但我把它們看成不同的東西。所以是——相關，但不同。

alts.quote: I say something to you like, "Lenny, I think what I'm hearing you say is you're off and you're thinking, screw you, Matt.
alts.zh: 我會對你說：「Lenny，我想我聽到你在說的是——你火了，你心裡在想：去你的，Matt。」

alts.quote: Just to pull on this thread a little bit more, what is the general advice you share there for people that also don't want to die?
alts.zh: 順著這條線再拉一下：對那些也不想死掉的人，你通常會給什麼建議？

cards.pattern: At any given point in time, I probably give myself a [等第], and sometimes it's a [更低的], and sometimes it's an A.
cards.quote: So at any given point in time, I probably give myself a B to B-, and sometimes it's a C and sometimes it's a D, and sometimes it's an A, and I'm really plugging away, but it's totally an ongoing challenge.
cards.zh: 任何時間點上，我大概給自己 B 到 B-，有時候 C、有時候 D，偶爾也有 A，我真的一直在努力，但這就是個持續的挑戰。
cards.why: 用學校成績當自評尺度，讓誠實變得輕鬆且具體。給一個區間而不是單點（B to B-），再列出高低兩端，聽起來是誠實而不是自貶。績效面談被問「你覺得自己做得如何」時很好用。
swaps: On a good week it's a B; on a bad week, honestly a D
I'd give myself a solid B-minus and I'm still working at it
cards.episode: Making time for what matters | Jake Knapp and John Zeratsky (authors of Sprint and Make Time, co-founders of Character Capital)

alts.quote: Yeah, this is not something I'd ever say about myself. It's nice that someone else would say it, but it's a mysterious thing.
alts.zh: 這種話我自己絕對講不出口。有別人這樣說當然開心，不過這東西其實挺玄的。

alts.quote: But probably the stat I'm most proud of, and the hardest thing to make happen out of all of that was we acquired 70% of the users that found out about Wise last month through word of mouth.
alts.zh: 大概是我最自豪、也最難做到的一個數字：上個月知道 Wise 的使用者裡，有 70% 是靠口碑來的。

alts.quote: It's not about you, it's about the idea. And don't be afraid to stand behind the idea.
alts.zh: 重點不是你，是那個想法。而且不要怕站在那個想法後面。

cards.pattern: And one core idea I don't think we've mentioned yet is that [你的重點].
cards.quote: And one core idea I don't think we've mentioned yet is that we strongly believe in people's intuition about how they should spend their time if they have the chance.
cards.zh: 還有一個核心想法我覺得我們還沒提到：我們非常相信一個人只要有機會，他自己知道時間該花在哪。
cards.why: 母語者講不停時要切進去，最安全的入口不是「我可以說一下嗎」，而是宣稱有一個「還沒被提到」的東西。I don't think we've mentioned yet 把插話轉成補漏，沒有人會拒絕補漏。
swaps: One thing we haven't touched on yet is...
Can I add one piece that hasn't come up?
cards.episode: Making time for what matters | Jake Knapp and John Zeratsky (authors of Sprint and Make Time, co-founders of Character Capital)

alts.quote: Before you actually move on to the next one, I want to spend a little time on this one
alts.zh: 在你跳到下一點之前，我想在這一點上多待一下。

alts.quote: I'm not going to interrupt the flow conversation. I'm just going to summarize in Zoom chat this is what I've heard, and this is what I think we're saying in this conversation.
alts.zh: 我不打斷大家的討論節奏，我直接在 Zoom 聊天室整理一下我聽到的、以及我認為我們在談的東西。

alts.quote: And I'm like, "Time out. What you're going to do is raise prices again. You just told me you 12x-ed the price and nothing observable changed."
alts.zh: 我就說：「等一下。你接下來要做的是再漲一次價。你剛剛才跟我說你把價格拉了十二倍，結果什麼都沒變。」

cards.pattern: [A] could be like [情境A]. [B] could be like [情境B]. They're in the same family, but they're cousins.
cards.quote: Satisfaction could be like, "I know this thing has to get done, and I got it done." Joy could be like, "Man, that was great." And they're in the same family, but they're cousins.
cards.zh: 「滿足」比較像：我知道這件事非做不可，而我做完了。「喜悅」比較像：哇，那真的太棒了。它們算同一家族，但只是表親。
cards.why: 分辨近義詞的最佳範本：不查字典，而是各給一句情境台詞，再用一個親屬比喻定位距離（same family, but cousins）。要向老外解釋兩個中文近義詞、或聽懂他們在細分什麼時，這句可以直接搬。
swaps: They're related, but they're not the same thing
Same neighbourhood, different houses
cards.episode: Making time for what matters | Jake Knapp and John Zeratsky (authors of Sprint and Make Time, co-founders of Character Capital)

alts.quote: I talk about what I like to call the magic questions, but the thing about magic questions is they're not actually questions, they're statements and they end with, "Do you agree?" Or "Is that right?"
alts.zh: 我把它叫做「魔法問句」，但重點是它們根本不是問句——它們是敘述句，結尾加上「你同意嗎？」或「我理解得對嗎？」

alts.quote: And then just to make sure I heard you right, these five stages are roughly the same across role, so designers have the same five and they're described similarly.
alts.zh: 然後確認一下我有沒有聽對：這五個階段跨角色大致相同，設計師也是同樣五個、描述也差不多？

alts.quote: I guess just to be clear, are these the same thing in your mind with different words?
alts.zh: 我想確認一下：在你心裡，這兩個是同一件事、只是換個詞嗎？

cards.quote: Well, thank you for sharing the real talk. I think you made the right choice.
cards.zh: 謝謝你講了實話。我覺得你那個選擇是對的。
cards.why: real talk 是英語裡對「坦白講不好聽／不好意思的事」的專門讚美，比 thank you for sharing 精準得多。有人在會議上自曝失敗時，這一句能確保下次還有人願意講真話。
swaps: Appreciate the honesty—that's not easy to say out loud
Thanks for the candour
cards.episode: Making time for what matters | Jake Knapp and John Zeratsky (authors of Sprint and Make Time, co-founders of Character Capital)

alts.quote: You should like when a PR person pushes back on you and says, "You know what? I don't think that your story is right for that publication. Here's why." That's someone you should hire.
alts.zh: 當一個公關回你「老實說，我覺得你的故事不適合那家媒體，原因是這樣」，你應該要高興。這種人才值得聘。

alts.quote: I said, "Hi, my name's Camille. I'm interning here this summer. It's my first day. I just wanted to say thank you for spending your time doing that speech for us on Saturday."
alts.zh: 我說：「嗨，我叫 Camille，今年夏天在這裡實習，今天是我第一天。我只是想跟你說謝謝，謝謝你週六花時間為我們做那場演講。」

alts.quote: So we deployed historic amounts of money in the campaign. It wasn't me, Gina, personally. I think that's important to share.
alts.zh: 我們在那場競選裡砸下的錢是歷史級的。不是我 Gina 個人在砸。我覺得這點必須講清楚。

cards.pattern: There's great research on this, but for now just trust me: [你的主張].
cards.quote: The basic principle with laser is that willpower is never going to win, and there's great research on this, but for now just trust me, you're not going to white-knuckle your way through not looking at Twitter when you're trying to work.
cards.zh: laser 的基本原理是：意志力永遠贏不了。這方面有很多很好的研究，但現在你先信我——你不可能靠硬撐來讓自己工作時不看 Twitter。
cards.why: 手上沒有引用來源、又不想顯得心虛時的標準做法：宣告證據存在、承認現在不展開、請對方暫時信任。for now 是關鍵——它把「不提供證據」框成時間安排，而不是心虛。white-knuckle（握到指節發白地硬撐）也是很值得學的動詞。
swaps: There's solid research behind this—happy to send it after
I'll spare you the citations for now, but the evidence is there
cards.episode: Making time for what matters | Jake Knapp and John Zeratsky (authors of Sprint and Make Time, co-founders of Character Capital)

alts.quote: If you say, 'I think this is going to take three months to launch' and I was thinking four weeks, you're never going to hear four weeks from me, ever.
alts.zh: 如果你說「我覺得要三個月」，而我原本想的是四週，那你永遠不會從我嘴裡聽到四週。永遠不會。

alts.quote: Wait, reduction of cognitive load." Maybe even if 10% of people get confused to get 90% of people far faster through this process is a big win and a great opportunity cost trade off.
alts.zh: 就算有 10% 的人會被搞混，只要能讓 90% 的人快很多地走完這個流程，那還是大勝，機會成本上很划算。

alts.quote: Data is more like a compass than a GPS. If you look at data as a way of giving you the answer, you're always wrong. Wrong or slow, or sometimes both.
alts.zh: 數據比較像指南針，不是導航。如果你把數據當成會給你答案的東西，你不是錯就是慢，有時候兩者都有。

cards.pattern: And that's totally fine, because you're being deliberate about it, rather than [僵化的做法].
cards.quote: And then there'll be some other thing that happens that causes you to reinstall it, and that's totally fine, because you're being deliberate about it and you're paying attention.
cards.zh: 然後某天會發生某件事讓你又把它裝回來——那完全沒問題，因為你是刻意這樣做的，你有在注意。
cards.why: 帶人時最有用的一句：先預告對方會退步，再預先赦免。that's totally fine, because… 把判準從「有沒有做到」換成「有沒有意識」，讓對方不會因為一次失敗就整套放棄。
swaps: That's fine—as long as it's a decision and not a drift
Falling off is fine; noticing is the whole skill
cards.episode: Making time for what matters | Jake Knapp and John Zeratsky (authors of Sprint and Make Time, co-founders of Character Capital)

alts.quote: I'll say, "I want to run a theory by you. Do you think that the reason why you are really interested in this or you made that decision is actually because of this other thing that you told me a little bit about?"
alts.zh: 我會說：「我想跟你對一個猜測。你會這麼在意這件事、或做了那個決定，會不會其實是因為你剛剛提到的另一件事？」

alts.quote: What does success look like for the thing you're trying to do here?
alts.zh: 你想在這裡做成的那件事，成功長什麼樣子？

alts.quote: Okay, so I noticed that I needed to change that at some point, and actually found a solution, again, late in my career, but I found a solution, because I asked myself this question, which is, "Why am I so busy?
alts.zh: 我注意到我某個時間點需要改掉這個，後來真的找到解法——雖然是職涯很後期才找到——因為我問了自己一個問題：「我為什麼這麼忙？」

cards.pattern: So yeah, anyway, sorry, that's just a rant, but [收回重點].
cards.quote: So yeah, anyway, sorry, that's just a rant, but you should try it.
cards.zh: 總之，抱歉，剛剛那段只是我在碎念——但你真的該試試看。
cards.why: 自己講太久之後的標準煞車：把剛剛那段命名為 rant（一時激動的長篇），道歉，然後用一句話把重點壓回去。台灣人講太久常直接停住讓場面尷尬；這句能把失控轉成有意識的收尾。
swaps: Anyway—rant over. The point is X
Sorry, I got on a soapbox there. Short version:
cards.episode: Making time for what matters | Jake Knapp and John Zeratsky (authors of Sprint and Make Time, co-founders of Character Capital)

alts.quote: Yeah. I actually have a better one for you.
alts.zh: 對。不過我有一個更好的例子可以給你。

alts.quote: Let me follow that thread real quickly because that's really interesting.
alts.zh: 我快速追一下那條線，因為那真的很有意思。

alts.quote: So is that my legacy? Yeah, and maybe there's some ego implicit in that, but can I go on for just a bit on this?
alts.zh: 所以那算是我的 legacy 嗎？算吧，裡面可能也有一點自我——不過我可以再多講一下嗎？

cards.pattern: Well, first a pairing, and then one more. The pairing is [A] and [B].
cards.quote: Well, first a pairing, and then one more. The pairing is reset expectations and slow your inbox.
cards.zh: 好，先講一組配套的，再講一個。配套的是：重設期待，還有讓你的收件匣慢下來。
cards.why: 開口前先報數量與結構，聽者就知道要等多久、怎麼記。first…and then one more 是最輕量的路標，比 firstly/secondly 自然，適合口語會議。
swaps: Two that go together, then a bonus one
I've got a pair here, plus one extra
cards.episode: Making time for what matters | Jake Knapp and John Zeratsky (authors of Sprint and Make Time, co-founders of Character Capital)

alts.quote: So I think we talked about how to decide whether to resource SEO, but we didn't talk about how to understand what the expectations are from SEO.
alts.zh: 我覺得我們談了「要不要投資源做 SEO」，但還沒談「對 SEO 的期待該怎麼設定」。

alts.quote: So let me take us back on track and let's talk about just the high level framework here.
alts.zh: 我們把話題拉回來，來談一下這個框架的高層次架構。

alts.quote: I took us off track a little bit. I think you were going to go onto a second piece of advice.
alts.zh: 我剛剛好像把話題帶偏了一點。你原本要講的第二個建議是什麼？

cards.pattern: Just saying "because" dramatically boosted [結果]. We're suckers for explanations, all of us.
cards.quote: And just saying because dramatically boosted the percentage of the time that a person would let them cut the line. We're suckers for explanations, all of us.
cards.zh: 光是講出「因為」，別人讓他插隊的比例就大幅上升。我們每個人都吃「解釋」這一套。
cards.why: 先給實驗結果，再用一句自嘲式通則收尾（把自己也算進去：all of us）。be a sucker for X（對 X 沒抵抗力）是高頻口語。實務含意也很重要：擋需求時記得補一個 because，理由本身合不合理反而次要。
swaps: People will accept almost anything with a "because" attached
We're all wired to accept a reason, even a weak one
cards.pmNote: 拒絕或延後需求時一律附理由；有 because 的拒絕接受度遠高於同樣內容的無理由拒絕。
cards.episode: Making time for what matters | Jake Knapp and John Zeratsky (authors of Sprint and Make Time, co-founders of Character Capital)

alts.quote: If we go up to the 30,000-foot level, what are we doing here? What's our mission? We're building a private safety net for all those who've been laid off or let go.
alts.zh: 如果拉到三萬英尺的高度看，我們到底在做什麼？我們的使命是什麼？我們在為所有被裁員的人建一張民間的安全網。

alts.quote: But human beings are notoriously good at trading off the long run just to feel good in the short run. That's why we're all eating chocolate and cupcakes and stuff that we know is bad for us because it feels good.
alts.zh: 人類非常擅長犧牲長期，只為了短期舒服。所以我們才都在吃明知不好的巧克力跟杯子蛋糕。

alts.quote: Every time that you hire someone new, mark your calendars for 30 days down the road and ask yourself one question: knowing what I know today, would I hire this person?
alts.zh: 每次你雇了新人，就在行事曆上標記三十天後，然後問自己一個問題：以我今天知道的事情，我還會雇這個人嗎？

cards.pattern: It seems like it would be a big deal because [表面理由], and that is true. But the real power of it is [更深的理由].
cards.quote: And it seems like it would be a huge deal because it changes others expectations, and that is true. But the real power of it is in changing our own expectations about what we are going to do.
cards.zh: 看起來它之所以有用，是因為它改變了別人的期待——這也沒錯。但它真正的威力，在於改變我們自己對自己的期待。
cards.why: 先確認那個顯而易見的理由成立（and that is true），再說「但真正的力量在別的地方」。這個兩段式讓你不必否定任何人，就把討論拉到更深一層——說服資深聽眾時特別有效。
swaps: That's the obvious benefit, and it's real. The bigger one is...
Everyone sees the first-order effect; the second-order effect is where it pays
cards.episode: Making time for what matters | Jake Knapp and John Zeratsky (authors of Sprint and Make Time, co-founders of Character Capital)

alts.quote: And if you don't have them on your growth roadmap, you are going to be in some really big trouble over the next year to two years because your cost of acquisition is only going to go up.
alts.zh: 如果你的成長路線圖上沒有這些東西，未來一到兩年你會陷入大麻煩，因為你的獲客成本只會一路往上。

alts.quote: And so ever since then, we've been automating jobs and creating new jobs, and you can always see the job that's going to go away, and you don't know the new job because it doesn't exist yet.
alts.zh: 從那時候到現在，我們一直在自動化舊工作、也一直在長出新工作；而你永遠看得到那個要消失的工作，看不到新的，因為它還不存在。

alts.quote: Okay, correct statement, we're falling behind. A real diagnosis would say, because. We jumped immediately to therefore.
alts.zh: 這句話沒錯，我們的確落後了。但真正的診斷會說「因為」。我們卻直接跳到「所以」。

cards.pattern: So to replay the system overall: [A] is about [X], [B] is about [Y].
cards.quote: So to replay the system overall highlight is about the thing you want to make time for today. The most important thing today, laser is about creating barriers to distraction.
cards.zh: 把整套系統再跑一遍：highlight 是你今天最想騰出時間做的那件事；laser 是替干擾設路障。
cards.why: replay 這個動詞比 summarize 更口語、也更精準——它暗示「照原樣再放一次」而不是加入你的詮釋。長會議尾聲重述架構時，用「一個詞 + is about + 一句話」的模組，聽者最容易記住。
swaps: Let me replay the whole thing quickly
To put the pieces back together: A does X, B does Y
cards.episode: Making time for what matters | Jake Knapp and John Zeratsky (authors of Sprint and Make Time, co-founders of Character Capital)

alts.quote: And one last thing to touch on, you said something really important about pull, and I want to double down on that.
alts.zh: 還有最後一件事，你剛剛講到「拉力」那個點很重要，我想把它再放大講。

alts.quote: Sometimes I'm like, "Who's owning this?" And it's like people don't know. That's why I think it's very important to have a single-threaded owner.
alts.zh: 有時候我問「這件事誰在 own？」結果大家都不知道。這就是為什麼一定要有一個單一負責人。

alts.quote: A really interesting takeaway here is that your sense is over time the foundational model companies, their margins will get squeezed, and the bigger opportunities in the application layer.
alts.zh: 所以一個很有意思的結論是：你的判斷是，長期來看基礎模型公司的毛利會被壓縮，比較大的機會在應用層。

cards.pattern: For what it's worth, we're not really motivated to [對方以為你的動機]. We just hope it works for you.
cards.quote: For what it's worth, we're not really motivated to try to create a self-improvement empire. This is not our full-time job. We just hope it works for you and is useful.
cards.zh: 順帶一提，我們並不是想搞一個自我成長帝國。這不是我們的正職。我們只是希望這對你有用。
cards.why: For what it's worth 是英語裡「這句話你可以不採納」的最輕開場，用來降低推銷嫌疑剛好。主動否認自己的商業動機、並補一句「不想買書我們懂」，反而讓推薦更容易被接受。
swaps: For what it's worth, we're not trying to sell you anything here
If you don't want to buy the book, we get it
cards.episode: Making time for what matters | Jake Knapp and John Zeratsky (authors of Sprint and Make Time, co-founders of Character Capital)

alts.quote: We're not going to create new changes to the product or create one time buys or reactivation emails.
alts.zh: 我們不會去動產品做新的改動，也不會做一次性購買或喚回信。

alts.quote: It's like, I don't think I can predict that. I think a much better use of my time is being very flexible and adaptable at a time like this.
alts.zh: 我不覺得我預測得了那個。我覺得我的時間花在保持彈性、快速調整上，回報高得多。

alts.quote: I'm like, "You have not earned that yet. That's not a statement about your worth. It's just you're not ready for that conversation."
alts.zh: 我會說：「這個你還沒掙到。這不是在評斷你的價值，只是你還沒到可以進行那場對話的階段。」

cards.pattern: So I've used up basically all our time on [A]. What I think we do is [調整方案].
cards.quote: So I've used up basically all our time talking about Make Time. I think we should have a follow-up episode just to talk about Sprint. What I think we do is let's cut off the lightning round.
cards.zh: 我基本上把時間都花在 Make Time 上了。我覺得我們該再錄一集專門講 Sprint。現在我的想法是：閃電問答就先砍掉。
cards.why: 會議超時的完整處理三步：承認是自己造成的（I've used up）、給議題一個未來的家（follow-up）、當場提出砍哪一段。台灣人常只做第一步一直道歉，母語者的重點在第三步：立刻提出取捨方案。
swaps: We're out of time on this—here's what I suggest we drop
I've eaten the clock. Let's park X and take Y offline
cards.episode: Making time for what matters | Jake Knapp and John Zeratsky (authors of Sprint and Make Time, co-founders of Character Capital)

alts.quote: "I need 20 minutes of focused time to interrogate something that I've done. We're not going to talk. I'm literally going to force us into a room or Zoom.
alts.zh: 「我需要二十分鐘的專注時間來拷問我做的東西。我們不用講話。我就是要把大家關進一個會議室或 Zoom。」

alts.quote: But I think it's really important for it to be a time capped group conversation. And if you give a team 30 days, they'll take 30 days. If you give them six months, they'll take six months.
alts.zh: 我覺得這一定要是一場有時間上限的團體討論。你給團隊 30 天，他們就會用滿 30 天；你給六個月，他們就會用滿六個月。

alts.quote: he'll sit in a review and be like, "I don't think this is right." And then he'll pause and say, "I'm going to clear the rest of my day. Let's sit and figure it out."
alts.zh: 他會在評審會上說：「我覺得這不對。」然後停一下說：「我把今天剩下的行程清掉，我們一起坐下來把它弄清楚。」

cards.quote: Hey, here's what I'm seeing and tell me what's going on for you.
cards.zh: 我先講我這邊看到的狀況，然後換你講講你那邊發生了什麼事。
cards.why: 用 what I'm seeing 把「觀察」跟「評價」切開——不是你有問題，是我看到一個現象；後半句立刻把發言權交還對方，讓他不必先防衛。台灣人常一開口就是「你是不是哪裡沒做好」，對方馬上關門。
swaps: Here's what I'm noticing — what's your read on it?
Let me share what I'm observing, and then I want your side.
cards.pmNote: 難談的 1:1 一律用雙向開場：先講觀察，再問對方版本，通常會發現你們對「他的職責」根本認知不同。
cards.episode: The high-growth handbook: Molly Graham’s frameworks for leading through chaos, change, and scale

alts.quote: I'm like, "Oh, cool. Tell me what I'm missing."
alts.zh: 我會說：「好啊，跟我說我漏掉了什麼。」

alts.quote: Look, I don't have time to sugarcoat any feedback, and frankly, the best people I've worked with are the people who come into one-on-ones with me and yell at me and tell me I'm messing up.
alts.zh: 老實說，我沒空把回饋包糖衣；而且說真的，我合作過最好的人，都是會在一對一裡對我吼、直接說我哪裡搞砸了的人。

alts.quote: And so here's where I think we go off the rails in marketing.
alts.zh: 而我覺得行銷就是在這一步脫軌的。

cards.quote: I always start with, "Does this person actually know what you expect of them?" If not, go back to step one.
cards.zh: 我一定先問一句：這個人到底知不知道你對他的期待是什麼？如果不知道，那就回到第一步。
cards.why: 把「人的問題」硬轉成「期待有沒有講清楚」，等於幫對方保留面子的同時把責任拉回管理者身上。go back to step one 是英語職場很好用的收尾——不指責，直接指出下一步。
swaps: First question I ask is whether expectations were ever made explicit.
Before we call it a performance issue — has anyone actually told them what good looks like?
cards.pmNote: 80% 的「績效問題」其實是角色與成功定義沒講清楚，先修結構再檢討人。
cards.episode: The high-growth handbook: Molly Graham’s frameworks for leading through chaos, change, and scale

alts.quote: That person needs to step up more, to be somebody who's really contributing and adding and being a multiplier on the work of everybody else on their team.
alts.zh: 那個人需要更站出來一點，成為真正有貢獻、有加分，能把團隊其他人的產出放大的角色。

alts.quote: It's like they know what to do, but they don't understand how to tie it back to the business context and the overall strategy needs and so where to prioritize.
alts.zh: 他們知道該做什麼，只是不知道怎麼把這件事接回商業脈絡跟整體策略，所以也就排不出優先順序。

alts.quote: So when the feedback is coming like raw, they know that it's in their best interest because I've shown them enough times that I genuinely care about the person behind the role.
alts.zh: 所以當回饋很生硬地丟過來，他們知道那是為他們好——因為我已經用夠多次證明，我在乎的是角色背後那個人。

cards.pattern: The rule is you snorkel before you scuba — [X]% of problems come from [結構層], not from the people.
cards.quote: The rule with the Waterline Model, which is very memorable, is you snorkel before you scuba. So, 80% of problems on teams actually happen because of structural issues or dynamics issues.
cards.zh: 這個模型的規則很好記：先浮潛，再深潛。團隊上八成的問題其實出在結構或運作方式，不是出在人。
cards.why: 一句口訣（snorkel before you scuba）把抽象的診斷順序變成畫面，開會時丟出來所有人立刻懂。母語者很愛用這種押韻／對比型 rule of thumb 來擋掉「先怪人」的直覺。
swaps: Let's check the shallow stuff before we go deep on personalities.
Start at the surface: goals, roles, expectations — then look at people.
cards.pmNote: 團隊卡住的排查順序：結構（目標／角色／期待）→ 運作（決策／衝突）→ 人際 → 個人。
cards.episode: The high-growth handbook: Molly Graham’s frameworks for leading through chaos, change, and scale

alts.quote: Okay, guys, I'm seeing something happen here. Every time we get close to talking about something that's really painful, somebody makes a joke and all the energy disappears.
alts.zh: 好，我看到一個現象。每次我們快要談到真正痛的事情，就會有人開個玩笑，然後所有能量就消失了。

alts.quote: Instead of getting mad at Lenny for his really stupid idea or getting mad at Nicole because this was a really bad idea, we can say, "This was problematic. What's wrong here?"
alts.zh: 與其去氣 Lenny 出了個爛點子、或氣 Nicole 這主意很糟，我們可以說：「這裡有問題。是哪裡出錯了？」

alts.quote: It's really important to give two people on your team different charges. One is like go grow the product and the other one is maintain that design, that craft. That tension is extremely healthy.
alts.zh: 團隊裡要刻意讓兩個人扛不同的任務：一個負責把產品做大，另一個負責守住設計跟質感。這種張力其實非常健康。

cards.pattern: You feel like a broken record — "I've said this [45] times." Turns out no one heard you the first [43].
cards.quote: You feel like a broken record, right? You're like, "I've said this 45 times." Turns out no one heard you the first 43.
cards.zh: 你會覺得自己像跳針的唱片：「這件事我講過四十五次了。」結果是前四十三次根本沒人聽進去。
cards.why: 用「45 次 / 43 次」這種具體假數字製造幽默，把「重複講很煩」正常化成領導者的本分。broken record 是母語者抱怨自己重複時的固定說法，台灣人多半只會說 I said it many times。
swaps: I know I sound like a broken record, but let me say it one more time.
At the risk of repeating myself for the tenth time —
cards.pmNote: 策略與角色定義要一講再講；你覺得囉唆的那一刻，通常才剛開始被聽見。
cards.episode: The high-growth handbook: Molly Graham’s frameworks for leading through chaos, change, and scale

alts.quote: We use words to establish a perspective in a way of thinking about the world. And if those are the words that are in your head, then you feel like it's this war.
alts.zh: 我們用字詞來建立一種看世界的角度。如果你腦袋裡裝的是那些字，你就會覺得這是一場戰爭。

alts.quote: He used to tell people, he said, "The key for career planning is," he said, "don't be fungible." He's an economist and so that was economic speaking. What that means essentially is don't be replaceable.
alts.zh: 他都跟人說：「職涯規劃的關鍵就是，別讓自己可被替換。」他是經濟學家，所以講得比較術語。白話講就是：別讓自己是可以隨便換掉的那個人。

alts.quote: It's not that you actually are going to watch it the whole time, but it gives you a mental model and makes you feel in control.
alts.zh: 並不是說你真的會全程盯著看，而是它讓你有一個心智模型，讓你覺得自己掌握著方向盤。

cards.pattern: Strategy should hurt — if you're not making trade-offs that are painful, you're not actually helping people prioritize.
cards.quote: Strategy should hurt is a much better way to explain it to people which is, if you're not making trade-offs that are painful, you are not actually helping people prioritize their time.
cards.zh: 「策略應該要會痛」是更好的說法：如果你做的取捨一點都不痛，那你根本沒在幫大家決定時間該花在哪。
cards.why: 把抽象的「策略」綁到一個身體感受（hurt），一秒讓人判斷自己有沒有真的在做策略。if you're not... you are not actually... 是英語裡很兇但不針對人的反證句型。
swaps: If the roadmap didn't hurt to write, it isn't a roadmap.
A strategy that costs you nothing isn't a strategy.
cards.pmNote: 設目標時「不做什麼」要跟「要做什麼」一樣明確，否則團隊會自己幫你排優先順序。
cards.episode: The high-growth handbook: Molly Graham’s frameworks for leading through chaos, change, and scale

alts.quote: Is it a better outcome to just ship more faster now, but most of the things aren't impactful? Or is it a better outcome to ship fewer things but really work on making sure that you're shipping them in the best way?
alts.zh: 到底哪個結果比較好：現在拚命多出貨，但大部分都沒什麼影響力？還是少做幾件，但每一件都確保做到最好？

alts.quote: So this is not an estimate of time, it's an appetite, which is a radically different approach. It doesn't sound like that much of a different word, but it really is.
alts.zh: 這不是「時間估算」，這是「胃口」——做法完全不一樣。聽起來只是換個字，但差別真的很大。

alts.quote: And it's hard because in making it compact you're losing completeness.
alts.zh: 這很難，因為你把它壓得越精簡，就越不完整。

cards.pattern: Two people owning [X] is no one owning [X]. One person owns it — who is it?
cards.quote: Two people owning a goal is no one owning a goal. One person owns the goal, who is it?
cards.zh: 兩個人一起扛一個目標，等於沒人在扛。這個目標只能有一個人負責——是誰？
cards.why: 先用「A=B」的悖論句把模糊狀態講死，再用一個五個字的問句逼出名字。會議收尾要定 owner 時，這比 "who wants to take this?" 有力十倍。
swaps: Shared ownership is no ownership. Whose name goes next to this?
Let's put one name on it — who's the DRI?
cards.pmNote: 一個目標一個 owner，而且不能是 CEO 自己；沒有名字的目標等於沒設。
cards.episode: The high-growth handbook: Molly Graham’s frameworks for leading through chaos, change, and scale

alts.quote: I'm in too many conversations where I'm like, "Who is on the hook for this decision? Who cares if this decision is made?" It's not like six people with consensus. Who is the person?
alts.zh: 我參加過太多會議，我會問：「這個決定是誰扛？誰真的在乎它有沒有被做出來？」不是六個人共識，是哪一個人？

alts.quote: Sometimes I'm like, "Who's owning this?" And it's like people don't know. That's why I think it's very important to have a single-threaded owner.
alts.zh: 有時候我問「這件事誰在 own？」結果大家都不知道。這就是為什麼一定要有一個單一負責人。

alts.quote: But really, we want to help people answer the question at work, "Who is doing what by when, and why?" So that notion of clarity of purpose, clarity of plan, progress, and responsibility are often so painful in people's work lives.
alts.zh: 我們真正想幫人在工作上回答的問題是：誰、在什麼時候之前、要做什麼、為什麼？所以目的清楚、計畫清楚、進度與責任清楚，這些在多數人的工作裡都非常痛苦。

cards.pattern: I have a bone to pick with [X]. It's obviously been really helpful for [A and B], but...
cards.quote: I definitely have a bone to pick with OKRs. I feel like it's obviously been a really helpful framework for Google and others.
cards.zh: 我對 OKR 是真的有意見。當然啦，它對 Google 那些公司顯然是很有用的框架——
cards.why: have a bone to pick with 是「我有帳要算」的口語說法，先亮出立場再馬上讓一步（obviously been really helpful），讓後面的批評聽起來像持平判斷而不是唱反調。
swaps: I've got some issues with how we use OKRs — useful framework, wrong application.
I'll push back on OKRs a bit, with all due respect to the framework.
cards.pmNote: 目標的本質是溝通工具；一百行的 OKR 試算表對誰都沒有製造清晰。
cards.episode: The high-growth handbook: Molly Graham’s frameworks for leading through chaos, change, and scale

alts.quote: Yeah, it's definitely a huge part of it. There's a couple of things that I noticed get in the way.
alts.zh: 對，那絕對是很大一塊。不過我有注意到幾件事會卡住。

alts.quote: Yeah, sorry. Buy-in doesn't feel quite right to me, because buy-in feels like, oh, I've come to agree with you. And that's different from it's a part of me.
alts.zh: 抱歉，我覺得「buy-in（買單）」這個詞不太對。buy-in 聽起來像「我最後被你說服了」，那跟「這東西本來就是我的一部分」是兩回事。

alts.quote: Both things can be true. It's like, yeah, there's nothing perfect in product. However, it is true that some companies are healthier than others.
alts.zh: 這兩件事可以同時成立。對，產品這行沒有什麼是完美的；但同樣真實的是，有些公司確實比其他公司健康得多。

cards.pattern: Don't come to me for [X] — I'm not the person to ask about [Y].
cards.quote: I always say to people don't come to me for management 101, I'm not the person to ask on how to run the most effective one-on-one with your people.
cards.zh: 我常跟人講：管理入門的東西不要來問我，怎麼把一對一開得最有效率，我不是那個該問的人。
cards.why: 把「拒絕」講成「界定專業範圍」，完全不帶歉意也不失禮。台灣人拒絕時容易繞一大圈道歉，母語者直接說 I'm not the person to ask，反而顯得有自知之明。
swaps: That's outside my wheelhouse — you'd want to ask someone else.
I'm the wrong person for that one, but I can point you to who isn't.
cards.pmNote: 把自己的守備範圍講清楚，比什麼都接下來再做不好有用。
cards.episode: The high-growth handbook: Molly Graham’s frameworks for leading through chaos, change, and scale

alts.quote: I don't think it's particularly productive to say, "Well, is it 20% bigger than the internet or 100%?" Those aren't productive conversations.
alts.zh: 去爭「它比網路大 20% 還是 100%」我覺得沒什麼意義，那種對話不會有產出。

alts.quote: And so even though I really like a lot about this, I'm going to say no." And I often think that founders think that there's some secret truth that's being held from them on why someone says no or they want more feedback.
alts.zh: 「就算我真的很喜歡這個東西的很多地方，我還是要說不。」我也常覺得，創辦人以為別人說不的背後藏著什麼沒告訴他的秘密，或想再要更多回饋。

alts.quote: Say no to stuff you’ve said yes to In the previous post, I shared a tactic for knowing when to say no: ask yourself, would I say yes if it were tomorrow?
alts.zh: 對那些你已經答應的事說不。上一篇我分享過一個判斷該不該拒絕的方法：問自己，如果這件事是明天，我還會答應嗎？

cards.pattern: Your job is not to have all the answers — it's to get good at finding them.
cards.quote: Your job as manager and a leader is not to have all the answers. It is not to have all the answers, it is to get good at finding them.
cards.zh: 你當主管、當領導者的工作不是要有全部的答案。真的不是——是要變得很會把答案找出來。
cards.why: 重複同一句（It is not to have all the answers）製造強調，是英語口說裡的 anaphora；再用 not X, it is Y 把職責重新定義。承認不知道的時候，這句可以先鋪路。
swaps: My job isn't to know — it's to make sure we find out fast.
Leadership isn't having answers, it's building the path to them.
cards.pmNote: 變動越快的公司，越是「會探索的人」贏，不是「已經知道的人」贏。
cards.episode: The high-growth handbook: Molly Graham’s frameworks for leading through chaos, change, and scale

alts.quote: And that requires analysis as much as analogy, and we are very much in the middle of that process and we don't know all of the answers.
alts.zh: 那需要的分析跟類比一樣多，而我們正在這個過程的中間，我們沒有掌握全部的答案。

alts.quote: My purely anecdotal guess is maybe 10 to 15% are good product companies, something like that.
alts.zh: 我純粹憑印象猜，大概一成到一成五算是好的產品公司吧，差不多這個量級。

alts.quote: Is it going to eliminate PMs next year? Probably not. Are the ratios between PMs and other teams going to shift over time? Yes. Are the skills required going to shift? Yes. Could they shift much faster than we all anticipate? Probably.
alts.zh: 明年就會取代 PM 嗎？大概不會。PM 跟其他團隊的比例會不會變？會。需要的技能會不會變？會。會不會變得比我們預期的快很多？很可能。

cards.pattern: There is literally no faster way to [demoralize X] than [Y].
cards.quote: There is literally no faster way to demoralize high performers than going back on a promise.
cards.zh: 要讓高績效的人瞬間心死，沒有比毀約更快的方法了。
cards.why: no faster way to X than Y 是英語裡最有力的警告句型之一，用最高級把後果講到底，卻不需要指名道姓。literally 在口語裡是強調詞，不是「字面上」。
swaps: Nothing kills trust faster than walking back a commitment.
The quickest way to lose your best people is to promise what you can't control.
cards.pmNote: 招人時不要承諾你控制不了的事（title、穩定、永遠不會有人壓在你上面）——那是寄給未來自己的炸彈。
cards.episode: The high-growth handbook: Molly Graham’s frameworks for leading through chaos, change, and scale

alts.quote: By the way, a very, very successful company for a new set of products has a 50% hit rate. So half of you are going to come back in a year and have a different job. Do you have the resilience to do that?
alts.zh: 順帶一提，一家非常成功的公司做新產品的成功率大概是五成。所以你們有一半的人一年後會換一份工作。你們有那個韌性嗎？

alts.quote: This is exactly where we are. This is what we're going to do and the next hour, and this is when you'll get your next update. I will update you again at 9:00 AM.
alts.zh: 目前的狀況就是這樣。接下來一小時我們要做的是這些，下一次更新會在什麼時候。我九點會再跟你更新一次。

alts.quote: It was pretty obvious after six months this thing was a bit of a zombie product walking, and the least I could have done is said, "This thing is dead." We could have called it dead way earlier.
alts.zh: 半年後就很明顯這是個活死人產品了，我至少可以做的，就是講一句：這個東西已經死了。我們早就該宣布它死亡。

cards.pattern: My mantra that almost always leads in the best direction is [A], not [B].
cards.quote: My mantra that almost always leads in the best direction is serve the business, not the people.
cards.zh: 我幾乎每次靠它都能做出對的決定，那句口訣是：服務這門生意，不是服務個別的人。
cards.why: 先幫這句話上一層保險（almost always leads in the best direction），再丟出可能刺耳的 A not B。政治角力時，把判準拉到「對公司最好」這個大家都同意的層次，等於抽掉個人恩怨。
swaps: The question I fall back on is what's right for the business.
Let's optimize for the company here, not for anyone's comfort.
cards.pmNote: 跨團隊卡住時，把爭執升級到「對公司最好的做法是什麼」，人的問題常常就自己散了。
cards.episode: The high-growth handbook: Molly Graham’s frameworks for leading through chaos, change, and scale

alts.quote: So the ability to be really truth seeking and take the most respectful interpretation when you're giving feedback to focus on trying to get to a smart good outcome that benefits the business.
alts.zh: 所以那種追求真相、並且在給回饋時採取「最善意的解讀」的能力，目標是導向對生意有利的好結果。

alts.quote: It's really important to give two people on your team different charges. One is like go grow the product and the other one is maintain that design, that craft. That tension is extremely healthy.
alts.zh: 團隊裡要刻意讓兩個人扛不同的任務：一個負責把產品做大，另一個負責守住設計跟質感。這種張力其實非常健康。

alts.quote: We've all been under Jeff's Eye of Sauron, we know it's miserable. What can we do to help?
alts.zh: 我們都被那道索倫之眼盯過，知道那有多難受。我們能幫上什麼？

cards.pattern: Direct is kind. It feels easier to avoid it, but [代價].
cards.quote: Direct is kind. And it feels kind or, really, honestly, easy to avoid these things or to work around them.
cards.zh: 直說才是善意。避開不談、繞過去，感覺很體貼，其實只是比較輕鬆而已。
cards.why: 三個字的口號式句子（Direct is kind）在英語職場是給難聽話撐腰的萬用開場；後半句用 it feels kind... easy 拆穿「體貼」其實是「怕麻煩」。
swaps: Being clear is being kind.
I'd rather be direct with you than let this drag on.
cards.pmNote: 不處理的人會變成船底的藤壺——拖慢整艘船，而且拖越久越難拔。
cards.episode: The high-growth handbook: Molly Graham’s frameworks for leading through chaos, change, and scale

alts.quote: And if you give designers a lot of ambiguity, they're going to spend a lot of time spinning around, and honestly, that's your fault as the client.
alts.zh: 你丟一堆模糊的東西給設計師，他們就會一直空轉——老實說，那是你這個「業主」的問題。

alts.quote: I asked her once, I said, "I noticed that you never answer questions when we do these presentations."
alts.zh: 我有一次問她：「我注意到，我們在做這些簡報的時候，你從來不回答問題。」

alts.quote: He said, "Well, two things. First, you were wrong. You were wrong to prioritize date over our reputation."
alts.zh: 他說：「兩件事。第一，你錯了。你不該把時程放在我們的商譽前面。」

cards.quote: What escalation is, "We disagree. Neither one of us has enough power to make this decision. Let's go to someone who does."
cards.zh: 所謂升級是這樣講的：「我們兩個看法不同，而且我們誰都沒有權限拍板，那就找有權限的人。」
cards.why: 三句話拆成「事實／限制／提議」，完全不談對錯也不帶情緒，所以對方不會覺得你要去告狀。台灣人怕 escalate 被當成打小報告，關鍵就在有沒有這句 neither one of us has enough power。
swaps: This one's above both our pay grades — let's take it up together.
We're deadlocked and neither of us owns this call. Who does?
cards.pmNote: escalation 是工具不是失敗；卡在同層級互推時，主管的存在就是為了解鎖。
cards.episode: The high-growth handbook: Molly Graham’s frameworks for leading through chaos, change, and scale

alts.quote: Okay, guys, I'm seeing something happen here. Every time we get close to talking about something that's really painful, somebody makes a joke and all the energy disappears.
alts.zh: 好，我看到一個現象。每次我們快要談到真正痛的事情，就會有人開個玩笑，然後所有能量就消失了。

alts.quote: It's really important to give two people on your team different charges. One is like go grow the product and the other one is maintain that design, that craft. That tension is extremely healthy.
alts.zh: 團隊裡要刻意讓兩個人扛不同的任務：一個負責把產品做大，另一個負責守住設計跟質感。這種張力其實非常健康。

alts.quote: I'm not interested in litigating the things that happened already when we can move forward.
alts.zh: 已經發生的事我沒興趣再打官司，我們可以往前走。

cards.pattern: And I'm like, "Could you possibly do that with [更小的數字]?"
cards.quote: And I'm like, "Could you possibly do that with 100 people?"
cards.zh: 我就會問一句：「這件事有沒有可能用一百個人就做完？」
cards.why: 不否定對方的計畫，只把數字換小然後丟回去。Could you possibly...? 表面是禮貌的可能性提問，實際上是逼對方自己去證明那個數字的必要性。
swaps: Is there a version of this that works with half the headcount?
What would it take to do this with the team we already have?
cards.pmNote: 人數成長超過一倍，你就快到來不及去重複的職缺與重疊的職責。
cards.episode: The high-growth handbook: Molly Graham’s frameworks for leading through chaos, change, and scale

alts.quote: I think sometimes people use data a lot or too much because they're worrying or they're afraid that, will I make the wrong choice? And I'm using data to make the choice for me.
alts.zh: 我覺得有時候大家用數據用得太兇，是因為他們在怕：萬一我選錯了怎麼辦？於是就讓數據替他們做決定。

alts.quote: I think people assume that there's a much more detailed semantic understanding of everybody's interests and preferences in the algorithm than there is.
alts.zh: 我覺得大家會以為演算法對每個人的興趣和偏好，有一套比實際上細膩得多的語意理解。

alts.quote: People say that time flies and it doesn't. What happens is it goes by unaccounted.
alts.zh: 大家都說時間過得很快，其實不是。真正發生的是：那些日子根本沒被記下來。

cards.pattern: [X] does not actually make you [Y]. We think it does. It does not.
cards.quote: More people does not actually make you faster. We think it does. It does not.
cards.zh: 人多不會讓你變快。我們都以為會，但真的不會。
cards.why: 三段式節奏：主張、承認共同直覺、再否定一次。第三句只有三個字，等於用停頓當鎚子。母語者在打破常識時很愛這種短句重擊。
swaps: Adding headcount doesn't buy speed. It feels like it should. It doesn't.
More resources won't fix this — we assume they will, and they won't.
cards.pmNote: 資源不足反而讓團隊只做高優先的事；先問「有沒有可能不加人」。
cards.episode: The high-growth handbook: Molly Graham’s frameworks for leading through chaos, change, and scale

alts.quote: I think sometimes people use data a lot or too much because they're worrying or they're afraid that, will I make the wrong choice? And I'm using data to make the choice for me.
alts.zh: 我覺得有時候大家用數據用得太兇，是因為他們在怕：萬一我選錯了怎麼辦？於是就讓數據替他們做決定。

alts.quote: It's actually not. It's not. So many people are used to it and they think that it's just how it is, but it's actually not.
alts.zh: 其實不是。真的不是。太多人習慣了，就以為事情本來就是這樣——但其實不是。

alts.quote: One thing I've learned is that I think people are really good at coming up with very rational sounding reasons to not do things that just make them uncomfortable.
alts.zh: 我學到一件事：人非常擅長替「其實只是讓自己不舒服的事」找出聽起來很有道理的理由。

cards.pattern: You're sitting there thinking "this is a dumb question" — then you ask it and it turns out it wasn't.
cards.quote: You're sitting in the meeting and you're like, "This is a dumb question. Everyone's going to think I'm an idiot." But then you get brave and you ask it and it turns out it wasn't a dumb question.
cards.zh: 你坐在會議裡想：「這問題也太蠢，問了大家會覺得我是白痴。」結果你鼓起勇氣問了，才發現根本不是蠢問題。
cards.why: 用引號直接把腦內小劇場演出來（英語口說的 quotative like），聽眾馬上有共感。這段話本身也是一個社交許可：講完就可以接著問那個問題。
swaps: This might be a basic question, but I'd rather ask it than guess.
Probably a dumb question — what does that acronym actually mean?
cards.pmNote: 會議裡沒人敢問的問題，通常是所有人都想問的；問它就是在製造清晰。
cards.episode: The high-growth handbook: Molly Graham’s frameworks for leading through chaos, change, and scale

alts.quote: I say something to you like, "Lenny, I think what I'm hearing you say is you're off and you're thinking, screw you, Matt.
alts.zh: 我會對你說：「Lenny，我想我聽到你在說的是——你火了，你心裡在想：去你的，Matt。」

alts.quote: I often go into a project, everyone's operating at a PhD level, I'm coming in at a kindergarten level...
alts.zh: 我常常進到一個專案時，大家都在博士班的水準討論，而我是幼稚園程度進來的。

alts.quote: I explicitly do not mean read a bunch of other PM artifacts. You're not going to become a better writer by reading PRDs or whatever it is or support articles. It needs to be writing that compels.
alts.zh: 我明確講：我不是叫你去讀一堆 PM 文件。讀 PRD 不會讓你變成更好的作者。你要讀的是那種會推著你行動的文字。

cards.pattern: My superpower is being a professional [moron]: "Do we have goals? Why are we having this meeting?"
cards.quote: I always say that my superpower is being a professional moron. Because I'm the one that shows up in a room and is like, “Do we have goals? Why are we having this meeting?”
cards.zh: 我常說我的超能力就是當一個專業級的蠢蛋。我就是那種進到會議室會問：「我們有目標嗎？我們現在在幹嘛？這個會到底為什麼要開？」
cards.why: 先自嘲（professional moron）取得社交許可，才敢連丟三個直球問題。這是非母語者最該偷學的招：用降低自己的姿態，換取問最基本問題的權利。
swaps: Let me play dumb for a second — what's the goal of this meeting?
At the risk of asking the obvious: what are we actually deciding today?
cards.pmNote: 會議發散時，把大家拉回「我們今天要決定什麼」通常比任何議程都有效。
cards.episode: The high-growth handbook: Molly Graham’s frameworks for leading through chaos, change, and scale

alts.quote: Every additional person in a meeting has a cost, because every additional person in a meeting makes the people in that meeting less candid than they would have been if there were fewer people in that meeting.
alts.zh: 會議每多一個人都是有代價的，因為人越多，在場的人講話就越保留。

alts.quote: Now that you've agreed among yourselves that you're going to do that for a fixed period of time, everyone go around the room and say, "If I could start this company over again the thing I wish we were doing was."
alts.zh: 既然大家已經同意用一段固定的時間來試，那就一個一個講：「如果能重來一次，我希望我們在做的是＿＿＿。」

alts.quote: So I'd say practically just try to look for places where it seems the team's having the same debate over and over and have it once, get it done, and put it behind you.
alts.zh: 很實際的做法是：找出團隊一再重複爭論的那幾件事，把那場辯論一次辯完、定案、然後永遠翻過去。

cards.pattern: In [six months], if I'm telling you what to do, I've hired the wrong person.
cards.quote: In six months, if I'm telling you what to do, I've hired the wrong person.
cards.zh: 半年後如果還是我在告訴你要做什麼，那就是我當初找錯人了。
cards.why: 把標準講成「我的失敗」而不是「你的失敗」，壓力同時落在雙方身上，卻沒有一句話在威脅對方。這是英語管理語言裡很高竿的一種責任互換。
swaps: A year from now you should be setting the agenda, not me.
If I'm still unblocking you every week in six months, I've done this wrong.
cards.pmNote: 用這條標準面試，你會自動去找有 judgment 跟自主性的人，而不是找執行者。
cards.episode: From ChatGPT to Instagram to Uber: The quiet architect behind the world’s most popular products | Peter Deng

alts.quote: I ask them, "What are your goals when it comes to coaching? Roll it forward six months, what have you gotten done in your coaching experience."
alts.zh: 我會問他們：「你找教練的目標是什麼？把時間快轉六個月，那時候你在教練這件事上完成了什麼？」

alts.quote: put a calendar invite, let it renew every three months. You're going to snooze it a couple of times, I get it, I've seen this many, many times before. But just do something, even if it's super small.
alts.zh: 開一個行事曆邀請，每三個月自動重複。你一定會按掉個幾次，我懂，我看過太多次了。但就是做點什麼，再小都好。

alts.quote: I try to focus them less around whatever happened and more on what is the action that you can take next to counter program the narrative that you are afraid that this other person has of you.
alts.zh: 我會把他的注意力從「已經發生的事」拉開，改放到：你接下來可以做什麼動作，去反寫你擔心對方對你形成的那個印象。

cards.pattern: Look, I don't have time to sugarcoat any feedback — the best people I work with are the ones who tell me I'm messing up.
cards.quote: Look, I don't have time to sugarcoat any feedback, and frankly, the best people I've worked with are the people who come into one-on-ones with me and yell at me and tell me I'm messing up.
cards.zh: 老實說，我沒空把回饋包糖衣；而且說真的，我合作過最好的人，都是會在一對一裡對我吼、直接說我哪裡搞砸了的人。
cards.why: sugarcoat（裹糖衣）是給難聽話開場的關鍵字；後半句立刻把「直說」跟「我最欣賞的人」綁在一起，等於預先授權對方也可以這樣對你。
swaps: I'm not going to sugarcoat this — here's what I saw.
I'd rather be blunt than polite here, and I want the same from you.
cards.pmNote: 先建立雙向可以直說的關係，之後給難聽回饋才不會被當成人身攻擊。
cards.episode: From ChatGPT to Instagram to Uber: The quiet architect behind the world’s most popular products | Peter Deng

alts.quote: Of course, I don't want to be cruel to the people who are putting their hearts into that work, because the Figma file is beautiful. It's just coming a little early.
alts.zh: 當然，我不想對那些真心投入的人太苛刻——那些 Figma 檔真的很漂亮。只是它來得太早了一點。

alts.quote: So when the feedback is coming like raw, they know that it's in their best interest because I've shown them enough times that I genuinely care about the person behind the role.
alts.zh: 所以當回饋很生硬地丟過來，他們知道那是為他們好——因為我已經用夠多次證明，我在乎的是角色背後那個人。

alts.quote: I'm not saying I know the answer, but there was almost this refusal to look at what tech was doing from a political lens for a very long time.
alts.zh: 我不是說我知道答案，但有很長一段時間，大家幾乎是拒絕從政治的角度去看科技業在做什麼。

cards.pattern: Tell me about one of the biggest mistakes you've made — truly, the more painful the better — and how you work differently now.
cards.quote: I asked them, think about one of the biggest mistakes you've made, truly, the more painful the better. And tell me what the mistake was.
cards.zh: 我會請對方想一個自己犯過最大的錯——說真的，越痛越好——然後告訴我那個錯是什麼。
cards.why: the more painful the better 這個插入語直接把「可以講真的」寫進題目裡，破解制式的假答案。英語裡 the more X the better 是很順的邀請結構，中文直譯反而會像在為難人。
swaps: Walk me through a decision you got badly wrong — the more painful the better.
What's a mistake that actually changed how you work?
cards.pmNote: 面試只考一件事的話，考 growth mindset：他能不能反省、接受回饋、把錯變成原則。
cards.episode: From ChatGPT to Instagram to Uber: The quiet architect behind the world’s most popular products | Peter Deng

alts.quote: I'll say, "I want to run a theory by you. Do you think that the reason why you are really interested in this or you made that decision is actually because of this other thing that you told me a little bit about?"
alts.zh: 我會說：「我想跟你對一個猜測。你會這麼在意這件事、或做了那個決定，會不會其實是因為你剛剛提到的另一件事？」

alts.quote: If you can tell me what you're working on and ask me at the end of a meeting specifically what I noticed then that is much better."
alts.zh: 如果你可以先跟我說你在忙什麼，然後在會議結束時具體問我注意到了什麼，那效果好得多。

alts.quote: It's like why was this decision made? Why do you think the decision was made? And I might ask, "Do you think it was the right decision or did you agree on it?"
alts.zh: 像是：這個決定為什麼會做？你覺得為什麼會這樣決定？然後我可能會問：你覺得那是對的決定嗎？你當時同意嗎？

cards.quote: And guess what? It's all okay. It's not a loss, it's a lesson.
cards.zh: 然後你知道嗎？那都沒關係。那不是損失，那是一課。
cards.why: not a X, it's a Y 的押韻對句（loss / lesson）讓認錯不變成自責。承認失敗後補這一句，可以把場面從尷尬拉回可以往前走的狀態。
swaps: We didn't lose the quarter, we bought information.
Call it tuition, not failure.
cards.pmNote: 事後檢討的語氣決定下次還有沒有人願意冒險；把失敗定義成學費是最低成本的做法。
cards.episode: From ChatGPT to Instagram to Uber: The quiet architect behind the world’s most popular products | Peter Deng

alts.quote: Yes, it's not working. It's my fault. I will deal with it.
alts.zh: 我做的第一件事就是認下來。我說：「對，它現在是壞的。是我的錯。我會處理。」

alts.quote: Then just to admit, "Okay, I was wrong.
alts.zh: 然後就是承認一句：好吧，我錯了。

alts.quote: I don't want them to leave it at, "It was a big loss." You want to say, "What I learned from that is now I always run a load test, and I've had many successful launches since then."
alts.zh: 我不希望他只停在「那是一次很大的損失」。你應該說：我從那件事學到，現在我一定會先跑壓力測試，後來的好幾次上線都沒再出過同樣的問題。

cards.quote: She used to have this saying, which is like, "Repetition doesn't spoil the prayer."
cards.zh: 她有一句話我一直記著：「重複並不會壞了那句禱告。」
cards.why: 用一句諺語替「一直重複講」正名，講完就不必再為囉唆道歉。引用別人的話（She used to have this saying）也讓你不必自己扛這個主張。
swaps: I'll say it again — repetition is the job.
You can't over-communicate a priority.
cards.pmNote: 願景與目標要對上、對下、對外一直重複；你講到膩的時候，組織才剛聽到第一次。
cards.episode: From ChatGPT to Instagram to Uber: The quiet architect behind the world’s most popular products | Peter Deng

alts.quote: Extreme clarity means everyone's on the same page. It definitely doesn't mean that they all agree with each other, but they just have the same understanding of the facts.
alts.zh: 極度清晰的意思是大家在同一頁上。它絕對不是說大家都同意彼此，而是大家對事實的理解是一致的。

alts.quote: What does the CEO want to hear more? Growth or saves money? Both are good, but I know which one is healthier for the company, increases market share, is better competitively.
alts.zh: CEO 比較想聽哪一個：成長，還是省錢？兩個都好，但我知道哪一個對公司比較健康、比較能拉市佔、比較有競爭力。

alts.quote: Look, I just hired Lenny. Super rockstar. But he knows nothing about that business, nothing about how we work — I will love for you to teach him some things.
alts.zh: 我會說：「這是我剛找進來的 Lenny，超強，做過這些那些。可是我們這門生意他一無所知，公司怎麼運作也不懂，很希望你能教他一些東西。」

cards.quote: The way I would say it is, say you're going to do the thing, say that you're doing the thing, and then say that you did it.
cards.zh: 我的講法是：先說你要做這件事，做的過程中說你在做，做完再說你做完了。
cards.why: 三拍節奏加上刻意重複 the thing，讓一個管理原則變得像口訣一樣記得住。中間那步最值錢——它給主管一個「其實不用做了」的插話點。
swaps: Flag it, work it, close the loop.
Tell them what you'll do, tell them you're doing it, tell them it's done.
cards.pmNote: 向上管理不是拍馬屁，是讓對方有機會在你做錯方向前喊停。
cards.episode: From ChatGPT to Instagram to Uber: The quiet architect behind the world’s most popular products | Peter Deng

alts.quote: Or if the meeting is not under the context of buying it all, it's like, "We're working on something cool. We have a great vision. It aligns with what you're doing. Maybe there's a partnership here."
alts.zh: 或者那場會根本不是在談收購，而是：「我們在做一件很酷的事，我們有很好的願景，跟你們在做的方向對得上。也許這裡有合作的空間。」

alts.quote: You earn their trust by asking them to do two things. One, you're either going to teach me or I'm going to help you.
alts.zh: 取得信任的方法就是給對方兩個選項：要嘛你教我，要嘛我來幫你。

alts.quote: I very quickly just sent her a note that said, "Wanted to build on this idea you had today. I really liked that idea, by the way. I saw this article, I saw this research about this other emerging thing."
alts.zh: 我很快就傳了一則訊息給她：「想接著你今天那個想法往下延伸。順帶一提，我真的很喜歡那個點子。我看到一篇研究提到另一個正在浮現的現象……」

cards.pattern: People who don't want to draw attention tend to get lost in organizations — so if that describes you, just remember to say what you did.
cards.quote: I think those people tend to get lost in organizations. So if that describes you, just remember to say what you did.
cards.zh: 這種人在組織裡很容易被淹沒。所以如果你就是這種人，記得一定要把你做過的事講出來。
cards.why: if that describes you 是一個很體貼的點名方式——不指著誰，但被說中的人自己會對號入座。內向者要學會的不是變外向，只是「把做完的事說出口」。
swaps: Quick recap of what shipped this week, in case it got lost in the noise.
I don't love self-promotion, but I want to make sure this lands: we shipped X.
cards.pmNote: 績效面談前先累積一份「說過會做／做了／做完」的紀錄，成績就不用臨時掰。
cards.episode: From ChatGPT to Instagram to Uber: The quiet architect behind the world’s most popular products | Peter Deng

alts.quote: Beyond those cosmetics, the biggest thing I see particularly at higher levels is people talk about what they have done but not why it mattered.
alts.zh: 撇開那些表面功夫，我在比較資深的層級看到最大的問題是：大家只講自己做了什麼，不講那件事為什麼重要。

alts.quote: My one learning there that has stuck with me, and I think can work for other people too, is that it's not just about doing things that actually matter, and learning. It's about being able to tell the story.
alts.zh: 那段經驗裡有一個一直留在我身上的體悟，我覺得對別人也適用：重點不只是去做真正重要的事、去學東西，還要能把這件事講成一個故事。

alts.quote: I think the other thing is really asking yourself, "What do I do that no one else in this organization can do?" There are lots of things that I do that other people in the organization can do.
alts.zh: 另外一件事是問自己：「我做的哪些事，是這個組織裡其他人做不到的？」我做的很多事，其實別人也能做。

cards.pattern: Give two people different charges — [grow it] and [protect the craft]. That tension is extremely healthy.
cards.quote: It's really important to give two people on your team different charges. One is like go grow the product and the other one is maintain that design, that craft. That tension is extremely healthy.
cards.zh: 團隊裡要刻意讓兩個人扛不同的任務：一個負責把產品做大，另一個負責守住設計跟質感。這種張力其實非常健康。
cards.why: healthy tension 是英語職場把「衝突」正名的關鍵詞——衝突不是壞事，是刻意設計出來的制衡。主持會議時可以用它讓兩邊安心繼續吵。
swaps: This disagreement is by design — that's a healthy tension, not a problem.
I want someone in the room whose job is to argue the other side.
cards.pmNote: 團隊也是產品：刻意配置互補（甚至互斥）的角色，決策品質才會拉開。
cards.episode: From ChatGPT to Instagram to Uber: The quiet architect behind the world’s most popular products | Peter Deng

alts.quote: It's not that one of my PM counterparts couldn't bring a lot to the design table, it's just I need you to play that position.
alts.zh: 不是說 PM 對設計沒有貢獻——他們當然有；只是我需要你守住你的位置。

alts.quote: This stress between product and sales is a good thing. It's a sign of a well-run B2B company when there is stress between product and sales.
alts.zh: 產品跟業務之間的緊張是好事。B2B 公司如果產品跟業務之間有張力，那才叫營運健康。

alts.quote: We've all been under Jeff's Eye of Sauron, we know it's miserable. What can we do to help?
alts.zh: 我們都被那道索倫之眼盯過，知道那有多難受。我們能幫上什麼？

cards.pattern: Just like you wouldn't [fly a plane without instruments], why would you [run a product without instrumentation]?
cards.quote: This sounds, again, very simple but just like how you wouldn't fly a plane without instruments, why would you run your products without understanding the instrumentation and how it's doing.
cards.zh: 這聽起來很簡單，但就像你不會沒有儀表就開飛機一樣，為什麼你會在完全不看數據的情況下經營產品？
cards.why: 先自己承認 sounds very simple 卸掉對方的防備，再用一個沒人會反對的類比把結論逼出來。反問句（why would you...）讓對方自己說出答案，比直接主張更難反駁。
swaps: You wouldn't drive at night without headlights — same logic here.
We'd never ship code without tests; why do we ship features without metrics?
cards.pmNote: 從 1 到 10 的階段最該做的事：把所有東西量起來，通常會發現一半的行為根本沒 log。
cards.episode: From ChatGPT to Instagram to Uber: The quiet architect behind the world’s most popular products | Peter Deng

alts.quote: So it sounds like that's necessary. Might not be sufficient, but it's necessary.
alts.zh: 聽起來這是必要條件。不一定充分，但一定必要。

alts.quote: That is not a tier three issue. I am not able to run my business without getting on an airplane should be sending alerts off in your whole psyche.
alts.zh: 那不是什麼三級小事。「我不搭飛機就沒辦法開公司」這句話，應該讓你整個腦袋警鈴大作。

alts.quote: That sounds cliche. I think a lot of founders and startup people like to talk about the mission, and I get it, and I think it's real. But I really mean it.
alts.zh: 我知道這聽起來很老套。很多創辦人都愛談使命，我懂，我也覺得那是真的。但我是真心這樣講。

cards.pattern: [Name]'s really special. I've got to just take a moment to give her a giant shout out — she is the only person I've worked with who [X].
cards.quote: Joanne's really special. I got to just take a moment to give her a giant shout out. She is the only person that I've worked with that has as much technical depth as she does have product taste.
cards.zh: Joanne 真的很特別。我一定要停下來大聲說一下她有多厲害——她是我合作過唯一一個技術深度跟產品品味一樣強的人。
cards.why: take a moment to give a shout out 是英語公開稱讚的標準動作：先宣告要停下來讚美（製造焦點），再給一個具體到不能複製的理由。台灣人稱讚常停在 she's great，沒有那個「唯一」的比較級。
swaps: Quick shout out to Ray — he's the reason this shipped on time.
I want to call this out publicly: nobody else on the team could have done that.
cards.pmNote: 公開稱讚要具體到「別人做不到的那一點」，否則只是客套，起不了帶動士氣的作用。
cards.episode: From ChatGPT to Instagram to Uber: The quiet architect behind the world’s most popular products | Peter Deng

alts.quote: When somebody is using AI to solve a problem that they wouldn't have used AI before, give them a shout-out in the team meeting, let them demo that. Again, make them feel like a million bucks for doing the thing.
alts.zh: 只要有人用 AI 解掉一個他以前不會這樣解的問題，就在團隊會議上點名讚美他，讓他 demo 一次。就是要讓他爽到不行。

alts.quote: And to her credit, she didn't put it in, and it still worked brilliantly.
alts.zh: 而且說句公道話，她確實沒放進去，結果一樣做得很漂亮。

alts.quote: Credit our CEO with this, that I shared the data with him and he basically told the product team, "We are putting a complete freeze on the product development roadmap."
alts.zh: 這件事要歸功給我們執行長：我把數據給他看，他就直接跟產品團隊說「產品路線圖全面凍結」。

cards.pattern: Honestly, I'm more proud of [the team I built] than [the products].
cards.quote: I'm so proud of, honestly, the team that I built there more than the products.
cards.zh: 老實講，比起那些產品，我更以我在那裡帶出來的團隊為榮。
cards.why: 把 honestly 插在句中而不是句首，是母語者強調真心的節奏；more than 的比較讓稱讚有份量——你放棄了更亮眼的功績來讚美人。
swaps: The thing I'm proudest of isn't the launch, it's the people.
Ask me what I'd put on my resume — it's this team.
cards.pmNote: 領導者的長期成績是「離開後那些人去了哪」，不是當時 ship 了什麼。
cards.episode: From ChatGPT to Instagram to Uber: The quiet architect behind the world’s most popular products | Peter Deng

alts.quote: What if I called it educating your manager about all the great work your team has been doing? What if I called it helping people see why your team should get more resources?
alts.zh: 如果我把它叫做「讓主管了解你的團隊做了哪些很棒的事」呢？如果我把它叫做「幫大家看見為什麼你的團隊該拿到更多資源」呢？

alts.quote: Credit our CEO with this, that I shared the data with him and he basically told the product team, "We are putting a complete freeze on the product development roadmap."
alts.zh: 這件事要歸功給我們執行長：我把數據給他看，他就直接跟產品團隊說「產品路線圖全面凍結」。

alts.quote: When somebody is using AI to solve a problem that they wouldn't have used AI before, give them a shout-out in the team meeting, let them demo that. Again, make them feel like a million bucks for doing the thing.
alts.zh: 只要有人用 AI 解掉一個他以前不會這樣解的問題，就在團隊會議上點名讚美他，讓他 demo 一次。就是要讓他爽到不行。

cards.quote: Look, I won't claim to be an expert on this at all, but I think that with every technology that's come out, we've been able to harness it and it takes a lot of harnessing.
cards.zh: 我先講，我完全不敢說自己是這方面的專家，但我覺得每一種新技術出來，我們最後都有辦法駕馭它，只是那個駕馭要花很多力氣。
cards.why: I won't claim to be an expert 不是示弱，是先把自己的可信度範圍畫好，之後的意見就變成「一個有經驗的人的判斷」而不是「專家宣稱」。台灣人常用 I'm not sure，語感上弱很多。
swaps: I'm no expert here, but my read is —
Take this with a grain of salt since it's outside my area, but...
cards.pmNote: 承認知識邊界是資深訊號；重點是承認完之後仍然給出明確判斷。
cards.episode: From ChatGPT to Instagram to Uber: The quiet architect behind the world’s most popular products | Peter Deng

alts.quote: So I think it has to come with a place of knowing that you don't know everything and humility to say, "Hey, I need help." And it actually earns you a lot more credit than you think.
alts.zh: 我覺得這要來自一個認知：你不可能什麼都懂，還要有那個謙虛去說「嘿，我需要幫忙」。而且這其實比你想像的更會替你加分。

alts.quote: I don't think we should filter out AI content. I think we should let you know if content is AI content or not. That's hard, by the way.
alts.zh: 我不認為我們該把 AI 內容濾掉。我認為該做的是讓你知道這則內容是不是 AI 產的。順帶一提，這很難。

alts.quote: Yeah, look, I would kind of defer to you on that, honestly. You've talked to a lot more people across a lot more companies, so you have a much broader set of information you're working with.
alts.zh: 老實說這題我聽你的。你跟更多公司、更多人聊過，你手上的資訊面比我廣太多。

cards.pattern: I love that you're starting with a spicy question — let me share some more context behind it.
cards.quote: I love it that you're starting with a spicy question here and let me share some more context behind it.
cards.zh: 我很喜歡你一開始就丟這麼辣的問題，讓我先把背後的脈絡補一下。
cards.why: 被問到尖銳問題時，先誇問題（spicy question）再爭取鋪陳空間，等於用一句話同時降溫、拖秒數、掌控框架。這比 that's a good question 高明，因為它承認了問題的攻擊性。
swaps: That's a spicy one — let me give you the context first.
Fair challenge. Before I answer, let me set some background.
cards.pmNote: 被 exec 當場質疑時，先給脈絡再給答案，可以避免答案被斷章取義。
cards.episode: From ChatGPT to Instagram to Uber: The quiet architect behind the world’s most popular products | Peter Deng

alts.quote: How do I share enough context about my thought process and rationale so that my boss has enough information to be able to push back if needed or to be able to approve?
alts.zh: 我要怎麼把我的思路跟理由講到足夠，讓我主管有足夠資訊可以在需要時反對我、或是直接批准？

alts.quote: If you don't say yes, what you're essentially saying is, I am so presumptuous that I understand what's on the other side of that door already.
alts.zh: 你如果不答應，你其實等於在說：我狂妄到已經知道那扇門後面是什麼了。

alts.quote: First let's examine the counterfactual, right? So let's start with the opposite of your question and say, "How would the world be sadder if we all just gave up on this?"
alts.zh: 我們先看反面情況吧。從你問題的相反面開始想：如果大家乾脆全都放棄這件事，世界會變得多糟？

cards.pattern: If you're [doing the shortcut], you're missing the point. You can't [empathize] with a summary.
cards.quote: I think that to anyone out there who's doing user interviews and then saying, hey ChatGPT, summarize the takeaways, you're missing the point. You can't empathize with the summary.
cards.zh: 如果你做完使用者訪談，轉頭就叫 ChatGPT 幫你摘要重點，那你就搞錯重點了。你沒辦法對一份摘要產生同理心。
cards.why: you're missing the point 是英語裡最直接但仍可接受的糾正；後面那句短短六個字（can't empathize with the summary）把抽象的損失講成一個具體不可能的動作，殺傷力很大。
swaps: Reading the transcript isn't the same as sitting in the room.
You can automate the notes, you can't automate the empathy.
cards.pmNote: 使用者研究的價值在「你自己感受到那個痛」，不在那份重點整理。
cards.episode: From ChatGPT to Instagram to Uber: The quiet architect behind the world’s most popular products | Peter Deng

alts.quote: I think I made the product better, but is anyone using it? Does anyone care? Or are we just congratulating ourselves?
alts.zh: 我覺得我把產品做得更好了——可是有人在用嗎？有人在乎嗎？還是我們只是在自我感覺良好？

alts.quote: How can you hire people whom you expect to make decisions without running them through you if you can't tolerate them making a decision that you disagree with?
alts.zh: 如果你受不了他們做出你不同意的決定，你怎麼可能招到那種不需要事事回報你就能決策的人？

alts.quote: Well, inherent in your question is this assumption that design takes more time. And so I'm going to kind of reject that premise, because I don't think design takes more time.
alts.zh: 你這個問題裡本身就藏了一個假設：做設計會比較花時間。我要先否掉這個前提，因為我不覺得設計比較花時間。

cards.pattern: It pains me to say this, but really [the uncomfortable truth].
cards.quote: And at Uber, I learned this because, it pains me to say this, but really the price and the ETA at Uber was the product.
cards.zh: 我在 Uber 學到這件事——講出來我自己都有點痛——但價格跟預估時間，那才是 Uber 真正的產品。
cards.why: it pains me to say this 事先承認「這句話對我也不好受」，讓聽者把注意力放在事實而不是說話者的立場。要講一個大家不想聽的結論時，這是很好的緩衝。
swaps: I hate to say it, but the data doesn't support our theory.
This one hurts to admit — the feature isn't what moved the number.
cards.pmNote: 有時候你精雕細琢的介面根本不是產品；先確認什麼才是使用者真正在消費的東西。
cards.episode: From ChatGPT to Instagram to Uber: The quiet architect behind the world’s most popular products | Peter Deng

alts.quote: Look, we haven't shipped any. Last three years, the only thing our customers have really meaningfully seen from our product is a price increase. What the hell are we doing?
alts.zh: 你看，我們什麼都沒出。過去三年，客戶從我們產品上真正感受到的只有一件事：漲價。我們到底在幹嘛？

alts.quote: I definitely don't think it was obvious to everyone, and I can definitely say that because we were given a pretty strict deadline that we needed to launch by and I pushed it out three times.
alts.zh: 我完全不覺得這對所有人來說是顯而易見的，我敢這樣說是因為我們當初拿到一個很硬的上線死線，而我把它往後推了三次。

alts.quote: I would be honest with people and say some patience is required. However, there is a lot you can do. A lot is in your control.
alts.zh: 我會誠實地說：這需要一點耐心。不過，你能做的事很多，很多都在你的掌控裡。

cards.quote: There's a saying that Mike and Kevin had at Instagram which is we may not be right, but at least we're not confused.
cards.zh: Instagram 的 Mike 跟 Kevin 有一句話：我們不見得是對的，但至少我們不是一團混亂。
cards.why: we may not be right, but at least... 用讓步句把「決策不確定」跟「方向清楚」分開處理，是在不確定中仍然要求執行力時最好用的一句。
swaps: We might be wrong, but we won't be vague.
I'd rather be clearly wrong than fuzzily right.
cards.pmNote: 猶豫不決的代價通常高於選錯；先定一個方向，再用數據修正。
cards.episode: From ChatGPT to Instagram to Uber: The quiet architect behind the world’s most popular products | Peter Deng

alts.quote: I fundamentally do not believe in outsourcing the heartbeat of the organization, which is sales.
alts.zh: 我從根本上不相信可以把一家公司的心跳外包出去——而銷售就是心跳。

alts.quote: When we talk about pricing strategies, we hear many buzzwords, and it's irrelevant. So when we take a step back and look at it, there's literally only three types of pricing strategies.
alts.zh: 談定價策略的時候會聽到一堆流行詞，那些都不重要。退一步看，定價策略其實就只有三種。

alts.quote: And what Canva really does is we're literally smack bang in the middle of that Venn diagram of creativity and productivity, rather than making our customers have to make a choice between those two suites.
alts.zh: Canva 真正在做的事，就是不偏不倚站在「創意」跟「生產力」這兩個圈的交集正中央，而不是逼客戶在兩邊二選一。

cards.pattern: You have to obsess over [the details of craft] while simultaneously having the wisdom of which details don't actually matter.
cards.quote: It's important to obsess about the details of craft, while simultaneously having the perspective and wisdom of which details don't actually matter.
cards.zh: 你要對細節的講究到近乎偏執，同時又要有那個判斷力，知道哪些細節其實根本不重要。
cards.why: while simultaneously 把兩個看似矛盾的要求綁成同一個能力，是英語裡描述「資深」的常用結構。台灣人容易講成 but also，力道弱一半。
swaps: Care about everything, and know what to let go of.
Sweat the details that matter — and be ruthless about which ones don't.
cards.pmNote: 資淺 PM 卡在「什麼都想做好」，資深 PM 的差別在知道哪些地方可以不做好。
cards.episode: From ChatGPT to Instagram to Uber: The quiet architect behind the world’s most popular products | Peter Deng

alts.quote: And as long as your decision is like 70% right, you can iterate on that 20, 30% in either direction, but if you don't commit, then you don't actually get any new information that is high fidelity and high quality.
alts.zh: 只要決策有七成對，剩下的兩三成你都可以往任一邊修；但你不下注，就拿不到任何高品質的新資訊。

alts.quote: So yeah, no hard and fast rule, but I think it's always you need to have this matrix of options in your mind and be very deliberate about which one you are going with and why.
alts.zh: 沒有什麼鐵則，但你腦中要有一張選項矩陣，而且要很清楚自己選了哪一格、為什麼。

alts.quote: You don't give them an airport tarmac and you don't even give them a football field. You give them something more like a basketball court, a sort of scale at which they can do their design thing.
alts.zh: 你不會給他們一整條機場跑道，連足球場都不該給。要給的是差不多籃球場那種大小——大到能發揮，小到能收斂。

cards.pattern: You earn their trust by asking them to do one of two things: either you teach me, or I help you.
cards.quote: You earn their trust by asking them to do two things. One, you're either going to teach me or I'm going to help you.
cards.zh: 取得信任的方法就是給對方兩個選項：要嘛你教我，要嘛我來幫你。
cards.why: 把「我想跟你搞好關係」轉譯成兩個對方都不吃虧的具體請求，任何一邊他都不好拒絕。teach me / help you 這組對仗把「主動示弱」變成一個交易。
swaps: Either I learn from you or I take work off your plate — your call.
I'd love an hour of your time; if you don't have it, put me to work instead.
cards.pmNote: 新進公司先去找那個最有影響力、最吵的人，把他的信任借到自己身上。
cards.episode: The essence of product management | Christian Idiodi (SVPG)

alts.quote: The way I would say it is, say you're going to do the thing, say that you're doing the thing, and then say that you did it.
alts.zh: 我的講法是：先說你要做這件事，做的過程中說你在做，做完再說你做完了。

alts.quote: Or if the meeting is not under the context of buying it all, it's like, "We're working on something cool. We have a great vision. It aligns with what you're doing. Maybe there's a partnership here."
alts.zh: 或者那場會根本不是在談收購，而是：「我們在做一件很酷的事，我們有很好的願景，跟你們在做的方向對得上。也許這裡有合作的空間。」

alts.quote: And then once the team has kind of gotten to a place, I'm not trying to get anyone to a hundred percent certainty, I'm trying to get you just on the ride. They will come, right?
alts.zh: 團隊到了某個程度就好——我不是要每個人百分之百確定，我只是要你先上車。剩下的他們自己會跟上。

cards.pattern: Look, I just hired [X]. Super rockstar. But he knows nothing about [our business] — I'd love for you to teach him some things.
cards.quote: Look, I just hired Lenny. Super rockstar. But he knows nothing about that business, nothing about how we work — I will love for you to teach him some things.
cards.zh: 我會說：「這是我剛找進來的 Lenny，超強，做過這些那些。可是我們這門生意他一無所知，公司怎麼運作也不懂，很希望你能教他一些東西。」
cards.why: 先抬（super rockstar）再壓（knows nothing），對方就不會覺得你在推一個麻煩給他，而是被邀請去塑造一個高潛力的人。這是替下屬引薦的標準句法。
swaps: She's excellent, but brand new to how we operate — could she learn from you?
I'd love for you to shape how he thinks about this space.
cards.pmNote: 讓有影響力的人「共同持有」新人的成長，之後他就很難公開說這個新人不行。
cards.episode: The essence of product management | Christian Idiodi (SVPG)

alts.quote: She used to have this saying, which is like, "Repetition doesn't spoil the prayer."
alts.zh: 她有一句話我一直記著：「重複並不會壞了那句禱告。」

alts.quote: We can't just have the marketing department sit down and cook up new positioning and then heave it over the wall to everybody else. It's a team sport.
alts.zh: 不能讓行銷部門自己關起門想一套新定位，然後往牆外一丟就沒事了。這是團隊運動。

alts.quote: Hey, you have your planning committee today. Here are the three questions I want you to go in and get answered at that committee.
alts.zh: 你今天有規劃委員會對吧？這是我希望你進去幫我問到答案的三個問題。

cards.pattern: He's just got to sit in the meetings you're in, quiet, observe. No stress, nothing to give.
cards.quote: He's just got to sit in meetings you are, quiet, observe, just by observing you, he will be a rockstar. No stress, nothing to give.
cards.zh: 他只要坐在你會出席的會議裡，安靜、看就好，光是看你怎麼做他就會變很強。你完全不用出力，也不用有壓力。
cards.why: No stress, nothing to give 這六個字把對方的成本降到零，是說服忙人答應最關鍵的一句。台灣人請人幫忙時常反而強調「不會耽誤你太多時間」，遠不如直接說「你什麼都不用做」。
swaps: Zero prep needed on your side — she'll just be a fly on the wall.
You don't have to do anything differently; he'll just shadow you.
cards.pmNote: 跟忙碌的 stakeholder 建關係，先設計一個他成本為零的接觸方式。
cards.episode: The essence of product management | Christian Idiodi (SVPG)

alts.quote: We can't just have the marketing department sit down and cook up new positioning and then heave it over the wall to everybody else. It's a team sport.
alts.zh: 不能讓行銷部門自己關起門想一套新定位，然後往牆外一丟就沒事了。這是團隊運動。

alts.quote: Hey, you have your planning committee today. Here are the three questions I want you to go in and get answered at that committee.
alts.zh: 你今天有規劃委員會對吧？這是我希望你進去幫我問到答案的三個問題。

alts.quote: Extreme clarity means everyone's on the same page. It definitely doesn't mean that they all agree with each other, but they just have the same understanding of the facts.
alts.zh: 極度清晰的意思是大家在同一頁上。它絕對不是說大家都同意彼此，而是大家對事實的理解是一致的。

cards.pattern: Is it okay if I show you an alternative way of doing that?
cards.quote: And I said, "Is it okay if I show you an alternative way of communicating that?"
cards.zh: 我就說：「我可以示範一種不一樣的講法給你看嗎？」
cards.why: 先要許可再示範，把糾正變成一份禮物而不是評判；alternative way 也刻意避開「你錯了」的預設。對上位者給回饋，這句幾乎是萬用鑰匙。
swaps: Would it be useful if I showed you another way to frame that?
Mind if I try saying the same thing differently?
cards.pmNote: 多數人不是不想改，是沒看過別的做法有效；示範比說教有用。
cards.episode: The essence of product management | Christian Idiodi (SVPG)

alts.quote: I said, "The way you are operating is not meeting our leadership expectations. If you do not change, you cannot be part of this organization anymore. I believe you can operate differently."
alts.zh: 我跟他們說：「你們現在的做事方式沒有達到我們對領導者的期待。如果不改變，你們就不能繼續留在這個組織。我相信你們有能力用不同的方式做事。」

alts.quote: He said, "Well, two things. First, you were wrong. You were wrong to prioritize date over our reputation."
alts.zh: 他說：「兩件事。第一，你錯了。你不該把時程放在我們的商譽前面。」

alts.quote: And I think the error that people make more often than not is they are actually too stuck on their own product vision. That's the mistake I've seen a little bit more actually than the other way around.
alts.zh: 我覺得大家最常犯的錯，是太黏著自己原本的產品願景。這個錯我看到的，其實比反過來的那種多一點。

cards.pattern: First of all, I don't think I can [keep working with you] given [this]. But I need to understand why you [do X].
cards.quote: I was like, "First of all, I don't even think I can work with you anymore given this environment you're creating, but I need to understand why you are talking to your team like that."
cards.zh: 我就說：「老實講，看到你製造出來的這種氣氛，我覺得我沒辦法再跟你合作下去了。但我還是想先搞懂，你為什麼會這樣跟你的團隊講話。」
cards.why: 先亮出最重的底牌（我可能不做了），再馬上轉成一個真誠的提問，讓對方在震撼中還有台階可下。but I need to understand why 是把對峙轉成對話的樞紐。
swaps: I'm not sure I can be part of this, but help me understand where it's coming from.
This is a line for me — and I still want to hear your reasoning.
cards.pmNote: 要求對方改變前，先確認你有沒有理解他為什麼一直這樣做。
cards.episode: The essence of product management | Christian Idiodi (SVPG)

alts.quote: Okay, guys, I'm seeing something happen here. Every time we get close to talking about something that's really painful, somebody makes a joke and all the energy disappears.
alts.zh: 好，我看到一個現象。每次我們快要談到真正痛的事情，就會有人開個玩笑，然後所有能量就消失了。

alts.quote: We've all been under Jeff's Eye of Sauron, we know it's miserable. What can we do to help?
alts.zh: 我們都被那道索倫之眼盯過，知道那有多難受。我們能幫上什麼？

alts.quote: So the ability to be really truth seeking and take the most respectful interpretation when you're giving feedback to focus on trying to get to a smart good outcome that benefits the business.
alts.zh: 所以那種追求真相、並且在給回饋時採取「最善意的解讀」的能力，目標是導向對生意有利的好結果。

cards.pattern: Doing [X] is the [報告者]'s job, but getting better at [X] is the manager's job.
cards.quote: Doing product management is a product manager's job, but getting better at product management is the manager's job, is the coach's job.
cards.zh: 把產品管理做出來，是 PM 的工作；讓 PM 在產品管理上變得更強，那是主管的工作、教練的工作。
cards.why: 同一個名詞（product management）配上 doing / getting better at 的對比，一句話重新劃分責任。這種「做 vs. 變強」的對仗在英語管理場合非常好記也很難反駁。
swaps: Shipping is their job; growing them is mine.
They own the work — I own whether they get better at the work.
cards.pmNote: 主管的日常工作是 coaching，不是自己下去解題；解題的人只會養出微管理。
cards.episode: The essence of product management | Christian Idiodi (SVPG)

alts.quote: So if your partner comes to you and says that marketing plan or that product roadmap that you put together, not good, do you take it as the plan is not good and let's talk about what we can actually do to fix it?
alts.zh: 如果你的夥伴跟你說，你做的行銷計畫或產品路線圖不好，你會理解成「這份計畫不好，我們來談怎麼修」嗎？

alts.quote: People call me sometimes they're like "I want to know if I have product market fit." Well, the fact that you have time to call me and ask me this question already tells me the answer.
alts.zh: 有人打給我說：「我想知道我們有沒有 PMF。」嗯，你有空打這通電話問我，這件事本身就給了答案。

alts.quote: I asked them, think about one of the biggest mistakes you've made, truly, the more painful the better. And tell me what the mistake was.
alts.zh: 我會請對方想一個自己犯過最大的錯——說真的，越痛越好——然後告訴我那個錯是什麼。

cards.pattern: Let me tell you what a [director] does — because I'm promoting you to do the job, not to learn the job.
cards.quote: Let me tell you what a director does. And you're going to work with me over the next couple of months to do those things because I am promoting you to do the job, not to learn the job.
cards.zh: 我先跟你講總監到底在做什麼。接下來這幾個月你要跟我一起把那些事做一遍——因為我升你是要你來做這個職位，不是來學這個職位。
cards.why: to do the job, not to learn the job 用同一個動詞結構做對比，把升遷的門檻講得極清楚卻不帶羞辱。想爭取升遷時反過來用也成立：我想先做，再談 title。
swaps: Start doing the role now; the title follows the evidence.
I'd rather you practise the job before you have to survive it.
cards.pmNote: 最適合學當 VP 的時機，是你還不是 VP 的時候——犯錯成本最低。
cards.episode: The essence of product management | Christian Idiodi (SVPG)

alts.quote: put a calendar invite, let it renew every three months. You're going to snooze it a couple of times, I get it, I've seen this many, many times before. But just do something, even if it's super small.
alts.zh: 開一個行事曆邀請，每三個月自動重複。你一定會按掉個幾次，我懂，我看過太多次了。但就是做點什麼，再小都好。

alts.quote: "Hey, help me understand how you came to that conclusion because here's my reaction to that." So, you're honest, but you're also curious.
alts.zh: 「嘿，幫我理解你是怎麼得出這個結論的，因為我的反應是這樣。」——你既誠實，也保持好奇。

alts.quote: If you can tell me what you're working on and ask me at the end of a meeting specifically what I noticed then that is much better."
alts.zh: 如果你可以先跟我說你在忙什麼，然後在會議結束時具體問我注意到了什麼，那效果好得多。

cards.pattern: I can teach most things, I can coach a lot of things — but [arrogance] is very, very challenging.
cards.quote: Most of I can teach, I can coach a lot of things, but that arrogance, that ego, those "I walk alone" kinds of things, those are very, very challenging and disruptive to a team culture.
cards.zh: 大部分東西我都能教、都能帶，但那種傲慢、那種自我、那種「我一個人走」的姿態，非常難處理，而且會傷到團隊文化。
cards.why: 先大方承認「絕大多數我都能教」，再把唯一的例外點出來，讓這個否定顯得客觀。those "I walk alone" kinds of things 用引號把一種態度具象化，比 arrogant 更有畫面。
swaps: Skills I can teach. The attitude I can't.
Everything else is coachable — this part isn't.
cards.pmNote: 面試可以放過技能缺口，不能放過拒絕協作的傾向。
cards.episode: The essence of product management | Christian Idiodi (SVPG)

alts.quote: I shared a lot of my impressions with her and I told her, "I respect you so much as an operator. I want to tell you that in the physical meeting that we had together, there was this disparity on how I would've potentially perceived you."
alts.zh: 我把我的印象跟她說了：「我非常尊敬你作為一個經營者的能力。我想跟你講，我們那次實體見面時，我對你的印象跟我原本認識的你有落差。」

alts.quote: This isn't funny, Hilary. This is a serious issue for a lot of people, and it's an emerging problem in some cases. And I think we should take it seriously.
alts.zh: 這不好笑。這對很多人來說是很嚴重的問題，而且在某些地方正在惡化。我覺得我們應該認真看待。

alts.quote: This is how we think about things. This is how we handle this type of behavior here. If that's hard for you, let's find you another job.
alts.zh: 我們就是這樣想事情的。這種狀況我們在這裡就是這樣處理的。如果你覺得很難接受，那我們一起幫你找個別的工作。
