cards.quote: My one learning there that has stuck with me, and I think can work for other people too, is that it's not just about doing things that actually matter, and learning. It's about being able to tell the story.
cards.zh: 那段經驗裡有一個一直留在我身上的體悟，我覺得對別人也適用：重點不只是去做真正重要的事、去學東西，還要能把這件事講成一個故事。
cards.why: my one learning 用單數，等於承諾只講一件事，聽者立刻放心。中間插一句 and I think can work for other people too，把個人經驗擴權成通則，卻用 I think 保留退路——這個組合在分享心得時非常安全。
swaps: The one thing I took from that — and I think it generalizes — is...
If I kept one lesson from it, it's this.
This might just be me, but it's held up.
cards.pmNote: 績效面談的兩個環節：做出成果，以及讓成果被理解成成果。
cards.episode: Scaling Duolingo, embracing failure, and insight into Latin America’s tech scene | Gina Gotthilf (Latitud, Duolingo)

alts.quote: I think the other thing is really asking yourself, "What do I do that no one else in this organization can do?" There are lots of things that I do that other people in the organization can do.
alts.zh: 另外一件事是問自己：「我做的哪些事，是這個組織裡其他人做不到的？」我做的很多事，其實別人也能做。

alts.quote: What I didn't tell is that there was at least six years of accidental work behind this. I started a blog six years before... Actually, I've always been blogging since I graduated.
alts.zh: 我沒講的是，這背後至少有六年、不是刻意規劃的累積。我在那之前六年就開始寫部落格了——其實我從畢業就一直在寫。

alts.quote: I think those people tend to get lost in organizations. So if that describes you, just remember to say what you did.
alts.zh: 這種人在組織裡很容易被淹沒。所以如果你就是這種人，記得一定要把你做過的事講出來。

cards.pattern: We did [大成績]. It wasn't me personally. I think that's important to share.
cards.quote: So we deployed historic amounts of money in the campaign. It wasn't me, Gina, personally. I think that's important to share.
cards.zh: 我們在那場競選裡砸下的錢是歷史級的。不是我 Gina 個人在砸。我覺得這點必須講清楚。
cards.why: 主持人把功勞放大時，最俐落的處理是先接住成績（we did）再切割個人（not me personally），最後用 I think that's important to share 說明你為什麼要糾正——把謙虛升級成誠信。
swaps: That was the team, not me.
I want to be accurate about my part in that.
Credit where it's due — I owned a slice of it.
cards.pmNote: 誇大自己的貢獻範圍是信譽最快折損的方式，主動校正反而加分。
cards.episode: Scaling Duolingo, embracing failure, and insight into Latin America’s tech scene | Gina Gotthilf (Latitud, Duolingo)

alts.quote: You should like when a PR person pushes back on you and says, "You know what? I don't think that your story is right for that publication. Here's why." That's someone you should hire.
alts.zh: 當一個公關回你「老實說，我覺得你的故事不適合那家媒體，原因是這樣」，你應該要高興。這種人才值得聘。

alts.quote: It's not often I use a product and I'm like, "This thing is 10 times better than anything that's come before it." It's one of those for me.
alts.zh: 我很少用到一個產品會覺得「這東西比之前所有的東西好上十倍」。這個對我來說就是其中之一。

alts.quote: Well, thank you for sharing the real talk. I think you made the right choice.
alts.zh: 謝謝你講了實話。我覺得你那個選擇是對的。

cards.pattern: My best bet for adding value was not to be another cook in the kitchen, but to move to [沒人在管的那一步].
cards.quote: I realized that my best bet in terms of actually adding value was not to be another cook in the kitchen trying to figure that out, but to move into the next step of the journey, which nobody was paying attention to.
cards.zh: 我意識到，我真正能加值的方式，不是再擠進廚房當第 N 個廚師，而是往旅程的下一步走——那一步根本沒人在顧。
cards.why: another cook in the kitchen 借自 too many cooks 的諺語，用來自嘲「我加進去只是添亂」，比 I wasn't needed there 有風度。which nobody was paying attention to 則是機會論證：不是我厲害，是那裡空著。
swaps: There were already enough people on that. I went where nobody was.
My leverage wasn't there — it was one step downstream.
I looked for the unowned part of the funnel.
cards.pmNote: 找影響力先找「沒有 owner 的那一步」，通常就在大家搶的那一步後面。
cards.episode: Scaling Duolingo, embracing failure, and insight into Latin America’s tech scene | Gina Gotthilf (Latitud, Duolingo)

alts.quote: So by improving a creator's first and second month revenue by 25%, we were then able to improve their overall value on Patreon by an equivalent amount, which is pretty massive.
alts.zh: 所以把創作者第一、第二個月的收入提升 25% 之後，我們就能把他們在 Patreon 的整體價值也拉高差不多的幅度。

alts.quote: What I didn't tell is that there was at least six years of accidental work behind this. I started a blog six years before... Actually, I've always been blogging since I graduated.
alts.zh: 我沒講的是，這背後至少有六年、不是刻意規劃的累積。我在那之前六年就開始寫部落格了——其實我從畢業就一直在寫。

alts.quote: But where I started understanding deeply the dynamics of the marketplace was actually my experience and the one job I've had that not been in the creator or art or these big consumer platforms.
alts.zh: 但我真正開始深入理解市集的運作機制，其實是在那份唯一不屬於創作者、藝術或大型消費平台的工作裡。

cards.pattern: None of this is going to blow anyone's minds — it's just best practices. But it's easy to overlook when [你正忙著別的].
cards.quote: None of this is going to blow anyone's minds, I think, because it's very best practices. But it's easy to overlook when you're so focused on so many different steps of a process.
cards.zh: 這些應該不會讓誰驚呆，因為都是很基本的最佳實務。但當你同時盯著流程裡一大堆步驟時，就是很容易漏掉。
cards.why: 先自貶（不會讓你驚呆）再解釋為什麼還是值得聽（因為你會漏掉），這個順序讓平凡的建議不會被當成廢話。blow anyone's minds 這種誇張說法用在否定句裡，是很典型的英文自我調降。
swaps: This is basic, and that's exactly why it gets skipped.
Nothing clever here — just the part everyone forgets.
Obvious in hindsight, invisible in the moment.
cards.pmNote: 轉換率的大幅提升常來自基本功（行動裝置優化、按鈕在首屏），不是新點子。
cards.episode: Scaling Duolingo, embracing failure, and insight into Latin America’s tech scene | Gina Gotthilf (Latitud, Duolingo)

alts.quote: Is that your recommendation? Because if it is then great, because you're leading the reader to that conclusion. But if it's not, you're asking a leading question that is skewing the results.
alts.zh: 那是你的建議嗎？如果是，那很好，因為你正在把讀者帶往那個結論。但如果不是，那你就是在問一個誘導性的問題，會扭曲你收到的答案。

alts.quote: I think a lot of people think about markets almost like these bodies of water. And it's like, "Oh, it's this big body of water that we're going after." And I actually think that the most interesting markets, you have to think of them like currents.
alts.zh: 很多人把市場想成一片水域，覺得「喔，我們要去攻的是這一大片水」。但我覺得最有意思的市場，你得把它想成水流。

alts.quote: So for positioning work, I'm going to say something that is contentious, but I don't think it is at all.
alts.zh: 講到定位這件事，我要說一句大家可能覺得很有爭議的話——但我完全不覺得有爭議。

cards.pattern: That sounds cliché. I get it. But I really mean it, because [具體理由].
cards.quote: That sounds cliche. I think a lot of founders and startup people like to talk about the mission, and I get it, and I think it's real. But I really mean it.
cards.zh: 我知道這聽起來很老套。很多創辦人都愛談使命，我懂，我也覺得那是真的。但我是真心這樣講。
cards.why: 要講一個已經被講爛的主張時，先自己說它老套、再說 I get it（我懂你為什麼翻白眼），最後用 But I really mean it 重新申請信任。這一套三步在英文裡幾乎是固定程序。
swaps: I know how this sounds.
Everyone says this. I'm going to say it anyway.
Cliché, yes — and still true here.
cards.pmNote: 使命不是文宣，它是決策時的排除條件——會擋掉哪些短期賺錢的選項。
cards.episode: Scaling Duolingo, embracing failure, and insight into Latin America’s tech scene | Gina Gotthilf (Latitud, Duolingo)

alts.quote: I think with hiring, it's funny, man, there's so much hiring advice online and you read it and you're like, "Yeah, this is super obvious." And then when you live it, you're suddenly like, "Aah, this is why people say this."
alts.zh: 招人這件事很好笑，網路上一堆建議，你看的時候都覺得「這不是廢話嗎」。等你真的經歷過，才會突然懂「喔，原來大家是這個意思」。

alts.quote: So I think the answer is a lot with a big if, with an if you can get people to do it.
alts.zh: 我覺得答案是「效果很大」，但有一個很大的 if：前提是你真的能讓人去做。

alts.quote: A lot of founders think about not wanting to have a leaky bucket on the product side, but the same thing applies on the team side.
alts.zh: 很多創辦人都很在意產品端不要有「破桶子」，但同樣的道理在團隊這一端也成立。

cards.pattern: I have survivorship bias, but I really believe in this.
cards.quote: So I got to ride in a plane that survived. So I have, oh, it's called survivor bias. I have survivor bias, but I really believe in this.
cards.zh: 我坐的是那架平安飛回來的飛機。所以我有——對，叫倖存者偏誤。我有倖存者偏誤，但我還是真的相信這件事。
cards.why: 自己先把可能被拿來攻擊你的偏誤講出來，對方就沒有那張牌可以打了。but I really believe in this 表示你知道風險仍然選擇這個立場——承認偏誤不等於撤回主張，這一點很多人搞混。
swaps: Caveat: I only saw the winners.
I'm biased by my own sample, and I still hold this.
Take this with the survivorship discount.
cards.pmNote: 引用自家成功案例時主動標記倖存者偏誤，論點反而更耐打。
cards.episode: Scaling Duolingo, embracing failure, and insight into Latin America’s tech scene | Gina Gotthilf (Latitud, Duolingo)

alts.quote: At that stage, what I think you've got is a positioning thesis... But it's just a thesis.
alts.zh: 在那個階段，你手上有的其實是一個「定位假設」……但它就只是個假設。

alts.quote: I think this is a nuanced question and it's hard for me to say something on a podcast that'll actually be useful to people, but here's a couple of thoughts.
alts.zh: 我覺得這是個很有層次的問題，要在 podcast 上講出真的對別人有用的東西很難，不過我有幾個想法。

alts.quote: Those are just numbers I'm putting out there. It's always going to be a gut call based on where you are.
alts.zh: 那些數字只是我隨口丟出來的。這終究是看你所在的位置做的直覺判斷。

cards.quote: I was just talking to an entrepreneur this morning, he was like, "Oh, we were able to hit a 10-cent CAC." And I'm like, "Yeah, but that grows."
cards.zh: 我今天早上才跟一個創業者聊，他說「我們把 CAC 壓到十美分欸」。我就說：「對啊，但那個數字會漲。」
cards.why: Yeah, but 是英文裡最短的反駁：先給一個字的同意權，再馬上加限定。這裡搭配 that grows 三個字就把對方的好消息重新定義成暫時現象，經濟到極點。
swaps: Sure — for now.
True today. Won't be true at 10x.
That's the early-adopter price.
cards.pmNote: 低 CAC 通常是低垂果實的價格；規模一擴大，邊際獲客成本一定往上。
cards.episode: Scaling Duolingo, embracing failure, and insight into Latin America’s tech scene | Gina Gotthilf (Latitud, Duolingo)

alts.quote: Now, don't get me wrong, I've built the experimentation platform at Lyft. I'm a guy who loves data and loves using it and looking at experiments.
alts.zh: 先別誤會我的意思——Lyft 的實驗平台就是我建的。我是個超愛用數據、愛看實驗的人。

alts.quote: I'm not saying we should go back to the early 90's, but I'm saying it wasn't always like this.
alts.zh: 我不是說我們該回到九零年代初，我是說事情不是一直都長這樣。

alts.quote: I remember somebody on social media said the problem with Benedict is his answer to everything is it depends. It's like, yeah, it does. It depends.
alts.zh: 我記得有人在社群上說：Benedict 的問題就是他對什麼都回答「看情況」。呃，本來就是啊。就是看情況。

cards.pattern: I really believe that — I don't believe. I think we all know at this point that [X].
cards.quote: And the third thing is that I really believe that... I don't believe. I think we all know at this point that the most important thing for the growth of anything tech is retention.
cards.zh: 第三件事是我真的相信——不，不是相信。我覺得到這個時間點大家都已經知道了：科技產品成長最重要的就是留存。
cards.why: 當場把 I believe 收回改成 we all know，是把一個私人意見升格成共識的即時操作。這種自我修正在英文裡不但不減分，反而顯得誠實又有份量——因為修正的方向是往上，不是往下。
swaps: This isn't a belief at this point — it's settled.
Let me put that more strongly.
Actually, that's not an opinion.
cards.pmNote: 留存不是「留住用戶」的技巧問題，是「這東西到底有沒有價值」的證據。
cards.episode: Scaling Duolingo, embracing failure, and insight into Latin America’s tech scene | Gina Gotthilf (Latitud, Duolingo)

alts.quote: So we can think there's people who don't know about it, there's people who do know about it but don't do it, and then there's people who do know about it, but do do it. And it's that last group that's so tiny.
alts.zh: 可以分成三種人：不知道這件事的、知道但不做的、知道又真的去做的。而最後那一群小得可憐。

alts.quote: Not having things be your idea I think is really powerful. I just talked to 50 customers who all yelled the same thing.
alts.zh: 讓這件事「不是你的點子」其實非常有力。我剛跟五十個客戶談過，他們全都在吼同一件事。

alts.quote: And if you don't have them on your growth roadmap, you are going to be in some really big trouble over the next year to two years because your cost of acquisition is only going to go up.
alts.zh: 如果你的成長路線圖上沒有這些東西，未來一到兩年你會陷入大麻煩，因為你的獲客成本只會一路往上。

cards.pattern: An obsession for [X]. Again, sounds obvious but isn't.
cards.quote: An obsession for the product. Again, sounds obvious but isn't.
cards.zh: 對產品的偏執。一樣，聽起來理所當然，其實不是。
cards.why: sounds obvious but isn't 五個字就完成了「我知道你想跳過這段，別跳」的攔截，是英文簡報裡效率最高的一個小句。省略主詞（It sounds...）讓它更像口語重音。
swaps: Obvious on paper, rare in practice.
Sounds basic. Almost nobody does it.
Everyone agrees with this and few live it.
cards.pmNote: 抄競品的介面等於抄答案，抄不到的是背後每天看數據、提假設的過程。
cards.episode: Scaling Duolingo, embracing failure, and insight into Latin America’s tech scene | Gina Gotthilf (Latitud, Duolingo)

alts.quote: And a tiger is a threat that will actually kill us, just like a tiger would. So these are actual problematic things that could be really harmful to the product or the project.
alts.zh: 老虎是那種真的會弄死我們的威脅，就像真的老虎一樣。也就是真的會嚴重傷害產品或專案的問題。

alts.quote: One of them is this thing that culture is a product, period. Every company builds two products: one is the product they build for their customers, and the other is a product they build for their team.
alts.zh: 其中一個想法是：文化就是一個產品，就這樣。每家公司都在做兩個產品——一個給客戶，一個給團隊。

alts.quote: There's this thing in my head and I haven't fully validated it but I'm going to share it with you.
alts.zh: 我腦中有個想法，還沒完全驗證過，但我還是講給你聽。

cards.quote: So I actually ended up not letting the team run this experiment for six months so that we focus on lower hanging fruit. So that's a mistake on my end.
cards.zh: 所以我其實壓著這個實驗六個月沒讓團隊做，因為想先撿低垂的果實。這是我的錯。
cards.why: on my end 是把責任精確劃到自己那一端，比 my fault 冷靜、比 we made a mistake 誠實。先講完整決策脈絡再認錯，聽起來是判斷失誤而不是能力不足。
swaps: That call was mine, and it was wrong.
I got that one wrong.
That delay is on me.
cards.pmNote: 用 ROI 排序實驗會系統性地低估「要先建基礎設施」的那一類機會。
cards.episode: Scaling Duolingo, embracing failure, and insight into Latin America’s tech scene | Gina Gotthilf (Latitud, Duolingo)

alts.quote: We would remind ourselves of this motto and then we would become more candid. And then six months later, we would realize that we were in fact not candid six months ago.
alts.zh: 我們會提醒自己這句座右銘，然後變得更坦白一點。結果半年後又發現，半年前的我們其實一點也不坦白。

alts.quote: I failed year after year trying to make the team, trying to make the boat.
alts.zh: 我年復一年地失敗，一直想擠進校隊、想上那條船。

alts.quote: Yeah, I messed up. But I know I'm still a good person and a good worker. Yes, I made a mistake, but I'm going to move on.
alts.zh: 對，我搞砸了。但我知道我還是個好人、也還是個好的工作者。對，我犯了錯，但我要往前走。

cards.pattern: If we had just [做了那件小事], we would have all known [結果].
cards.quote: We were like, "You know what? If we had just tested that, we would have all known that this was a super lame badge." And I was like, "Why are we not testing our experiments?"
cards.zh: 我們就說：「欸，我們如果當初有自己測一下，早就知道這個徽章有夠遜。」我就問：「所以我們為什麼沒有在測自己的實驗？」
cards.why: 第三條件句（If we had...we would have）是英文檢討會的預設時態，用它把「早就知道」講出來，語氣是遺憾不是指責。結尾把個案問題升級成制度問題（Why are we not...），這一跳才是重點。
swaps: One dogfood session would have caught this.
We'd have known in five minutes.
The cheapest test we didn't run.
cards.pmNote: 檢討要問「這是個案還是一類」——一類就要改流程，不是改這一次。
cards.episode: Scaling Duolingo, embracing failure, and insight into Latin America’s tech scene | Gina Gotthilf (Latitud, Duolingo)

alts.quote: Yeah, I messed up. But I know I'm still a good person and a good worker. Yes, I made a mistake, but I'm going to move on.
alts.zh: 對，我搞砸了。但我知道我還是個好人、也還是個好的工作者。對，我犯了錯，但我要往前走。

alts.quote: I wrote down, I have a note on my phone called Failure Resume, and I wrote down all the times I failed and it is depressing.
alts.zh: 我手機裡有一則筆記叫「失敗履歷」，我把每次失敗都記下來——看了很沮喪。

alts.quote: I failed for, I don't know, somewhere between 10 and 15 years before getting to this point.
alts.zh: 我大概失敗了……我也不確定，十到十五年吧，才走到現在這一步。

cards.pattern: It doesn't matter if you think [爭議立場]. Do you think [沒人會反對的事]? Most people would say yes.
cards.quote: It doesn't matter if you think Bloomberg or Trump should be president. Do you think everyone should have access to great education? Most people would say yes.
cards.zh: 你覺得該讓 Bloomberg 還是 Trump 當總統，都無所謂。你覺得每個人都該有機會受好的教育嗎？大多數人會說會。
cards.why: 先主動作廢一個會讓人分裂的爭議，再問一個幾乎人人會點頭的問題，等於替敘事清出一塊公共地。這是找共同立足點（common ground）的標準操作，跨部門說服時特別好用。
swaps: Set aside where you land on X. Can we agree on Y?
Whatever your view on that, this part is uncontroversial.
Different politics, same answer here.
cards.pmNote: 使命敘事要選一個「幾乎沒人反對」的層級，才會被引用、被轉述。
cards.episode: Scaling Duolingo, embracing failure, and insight into Latin America’s tech scene | Gina Gotthilf (Latitud, Duolingo)

alts.quote: And one thing people make fun of me a lot for that I think is just a great example of extreme clarity is I never use bulleted lists because you can never refer to a bullet.
alts.zh: 有件事大家常笑我，但我覺得那正是「極度清楚」的最佳示範：我從來不用項目符號，因為你沒辦法指名某一個點。

alts.quote: You really cut out all the parts that make people go dead in the eyes and just say the parts that make their eyes light up.
alts.zh: 你要做的就是把那些讓人眼神死掉的段落全砍掉，只留下讓人眼睛發亮的部分。

alts.quote: Which is you bring a fruit to the reviewer and say, "Hey, here's a mango, what do you think?" And the reviewer says, "I actually don't like mangoes."
alts.zh: 你拿一個水果去給主管看：「欸，這是芒果，你覺得怎樣？」主管說：「我其實不喜歡芒果。」

cards.pattern: We asked of every piece of copy: could this have been written by any other company?
cards.quote: We constantly looked at every copy we wrote and asked, "Could this have been written by other companies? Could this have been any other company or is it Duolingo? What makes this Duolingo?"
cards.zh: 我們每寫一段文案都會回頭問：「這段別家公司寫得出來嗎？這可以是任何一家公司，還是它就是 Duolingo？哪裡讓它是 Duolingo？」
cards.why: 把抽象的「品牌調性」變成一個可以當場判定的是非題，是這句最強的地方。三個問句層層收窄（別家能寫嗎 → 是誰 → 哪裡是），示範了怎麼把模糊標準拆成可執行的檢查。
swaps: Would this pass as anyone else's?
Swap our logo out — does it still work? Then it's not ours.
What in this sentence is only us?
cards.pmNote: 品牌一致性的可操作檢查：任何一句對外文案，換掉 logo 後還成立就代表沒差異化。
cards.episode: Scaling Duolingo, embracing failure, and insight into Latin America’s tech scene | Gina Gotthilf (Latitud, Duolingo)

alts.quote: And then there'll be some other thing that happens that causes you to reinstall it, and that's totally fine, because you're being deliberate about it and you're paying attention.
alts.zh: 然後某天會發生某件事讓你又把它裝回來——那完全沒問題，因為你是刻意這樣做的，你有在注意。

alts.quote: I was looking at your LinkedIn and your career history, and I noticed that you've worked for a different billionaire every decade of your life.
alts.zh: 我看了你的 LinkedIn 跟你的職涯，我注意到你人生每十年都在幫一個不同的億萬富翁工作。

alts.quote: When I joined Microsoft many years ago, the first thing I noticed was that Outlook was very buggy and I asked people what's going on?
alts.zh: 我很多年前剛進微軟的時候，第一件注意到的事就是 Outlook 超多 bug，我就去問大家：這是怎麼回事？

cards.pattern: I haven't met the person who does [X] and they're fantastic. I definitely don't want to take anything away from their work.
cards.quote: Look, I haven't met the person who does a TikTok and they're fantastic. I definitely don't want to demerit their work. It's awesome, I don't think it's easy to do.
cards.zh: 老實說我沒見過負責 TikTok 的那個人，但他們超強。我完全不想貶低他們的工作，那真的很厲害，也一點都不好做。
cards.why: 在你要說「其實不只是靠那個人」之前，先花兩句把那個人捧好——這樣後面的論點才不會被聽成搶功。Look, 開頭是英文口語裡「我要講實話了」的信號詞，語氣親近而不失禮。
swaps: Full credit to them — and there's more to it.
That's genuinely hard, and it's not the whole story.
Not taking anything away from them, but...
cards.pmNote: 拆解別家的成功時先給執行者應得的肯定，你的結構性分析才聽得進去。
cards.episode: Scaling Duolingo, embracing failure, and insight into Latin America’s tech scene | Gina Gotthilf (Latitud, Duolingo)

alts.quote: You should like when a PR person pushes back on you and says, "You know what? I don't think that your story is right for that publication. Here's why." That's someone you should hire.
alts.zh: 當一個公關回你「老實說，我覺得你的故事不適合那家媒體，原因是這樣」，你應該要高興。這種人才值得聘。

alts.quote: What if I called it educating your manager about all the great work your team has been doing? What if I called it helping people see why your team should get more resources?
alts.zh: 如果我把它叫做「讓主管了解你的團隊做了哪些很棒的事」呢？如果我把它叫做「幫大家看見為什麼你的團隊該拿到更多資源」呢？

alts.quote: Joanne's really special. I got to just take a moment to give her a giant shout out. She is the only person that I've worked with that has as much technical depth as she does have product taste.
alts.zh: Joanne 真的很特別。我一定要停下來大聲說一下她有多厲害——她是我合作過唯一一個技術深度跟產品品味一樣強的人。

cards.pattern: So [名字], I don't see it as a [他用的詞], because [你的版本].
cards.quote: So Lenny, I don't see it as a pivot because as we were joking in the beginning, I've been an employee, I was an operator there at early stage startups and now I'm a founder and I'm a VC.
cards.zh: Lenny，我不覺得那是轉彎——就像我們一開始開玩笑講的，我當過員工、在早期新創當過操盤手，現在是創辦人，也是投資人。
cards.why: 反對別人的用字（而不是內容）時，先喊對方名字會讓語氣從對立變成對話。I don't see it as X 是把分歧定位成視角差異，比 that's not a pivot 少了糾正的意味。
swaps: I'd frame it differently.
I wouldn't call it that, actually.
That's not how it felt from the inside.
cards.pmNote: 別人替你的職涯或專案下標籤時，當場換一個字，敘事的所有權就回到你身上。
cards.episode: Scaling Duolingo, embracing failure, and insight into Latin America’s tech scene | Gina Gotthilf (Latitud, Duolingo)

alts.quote: I'm not trying to diss anyone, but you'll see things that become fashionable really quickly because someone found success in this unfashionable space and then it becomes fashionable.
alts.zh: 我不是要酸誰，但你會看到有些東西紅得很快——因為有人在一個沒人做的領域做成了，然後它就變成流行。

alts.quote: I don't buy that, because I've met most people and most people are like, "Hell no," when they hear about my life.
alts.zh: 我不買單，因為我見過的大多數人，聽到我的生活方式時的反應都是「才不要」。

alts.quote: Again, don't get me wrong, I'm not trying to talk people out of doing it. But for me, a lot of this was luck.
alts.zh: 先說清楚，我不是想勸大家不要做。但對我來說，這裡面有很大一部分是運氣。

cards.pattern: What are you world-class at, and how do you know? The second part is almost more important.
cards.quote: And then I would say, what are you world-class at and how do you know that you're at that? And the second part is almost more important.
cards.zh: 然後我會問：你在什麼事情上是世界級的？你怎麼知道自己是？第二個問題其實更重要。
cards.why: 問完之後自己標記哪一半才是重點（The second part is almost more important），是面試官/教練把注意力導到證據上的技巧。almost 這個副詞讓判斷留了餘地，聽起來像思考不像評分。
swaps: What's your edge, and what's the evidence?
How would you prove that to a stranger?
The 'how do you know' is the real question.
cards.pmNote: 面試看的不是自評高低，是對方有沒有用可驗證的方式評估自己。
cards.episode: Scaling Duolingo, embracing failure, and insight into Latin America’s tech scene | Gina Gotthilf (Latitud, Duolingo)

alts.quote: So first of all, if you're asking whether you should pivot or not you probably know the answer already.
alts.zh: 首先，如果你在問「該不該轉向」，你八成心裡已經有答案了。

alts.quote: What we ask people in general is we say, what do you think? We don't say, what do you know? We often say, what do you think?
alts.zh: 我們一般會問人「你怎麼想？」我們不會問「你知道什麼？」我們最常問的就是「你怎麼想？」

alts.quote: I'll say, "I want to run a theory by you. Do you think that the reason why you are really interested in this or you made that decision is actually because of this other thing that you told me a little bit about?"
alts.zh: 我會說：「我想跟你對一個猜測。你會這麼在意這件事、或做了那個決定，會不會其實是因為你剛剛提到的另一件事？」

cards.pattern: And it stunned me into silence, because essentially that is and was [X] — and that forced me to pivot my thinking.
cards.quote: And it stunned me into silence because essentially that is and was SEO, and then that forced me to really pivot my thinking around what SEO might be.
cards.zh: 那句話讓我當場說不出話，因為 SEO 本來、現在也確實就是那樣。也就是那一刻逼我重新想：SEO 到底可以是什麼。
cards.why: 承認被外行問倒，卻把它講成自己思考升級的起點——這是把丟臉的事變成資歷的標準敘事。that is and was 用現在式加過去式並排，強調「不是他誤解，是真的一直如此」。
swaps: I didn't have an answer, and that was the point.
That question rearranged how I think about this.
He was right, and it changed my whole approach.
cards.pmNote: 客戶問「那我為什麼要付你錢」，通常是你的價值主張還停在交付項目層級。
cards.episode: Rethinking SEO in the age of AI | Eli Schwartz (SEO advisor, author)

alts.quote: By the way, I will say on the Peter one, I've come much more around to Peter's point of view. I would probably argue that one quite a bit differently today than I did, and I would give his view, I think, a lot more credit.
alts.zh: 順帶一提，Peter 那場辯論，我現在比較站到他那邊了。同樣的題目今天要我講，我會講得很不一樣，也會給他的看法多很多分數。

alts.quote: No, I mean I've shared that enough, but I used to not talk about it before because I used to think that I would get some sympathy for that.
alts.zh: 不會，這件事我講得夠多了。不過我以前不太提，因為我當時覺得講了會被同情。

alts.quote: But I no longer have to provide the first-round feedback I once did, since the draft has already undergone several rounds of what are essentially my suggestions before I even touch it.
alts.zh: 但我已經不必再給以前那種第一輪回饋了，因為草稿在我碰到之前，已經跑過好幾輪等同我意見的修改。

cards.pattern: Actually, it's not that [他的說法] — it's that [你的說法].
cards.quote: Actually, it's not that it's harder to find, your stuff becomes less relevant. And that's the part about SEO that I'm excited about.
cards.zh: 其實不是變得比較難被找到，是你的東西變得沒那麼相關了。而這正是 SEO 讓我興奮的地方。
cards.why: It's not that A, it's that B 是最乾淨的修正句型：不否定對方觀察到的現象，只換掉他的因果解釋。後面立刻補一句自己為什麼興奮，讓糾正的落點是正面的，不會冷場。
swaps: The problem isn't visibility — it's relevance.
I'd put it slightly differently.
Close, but the mechanism is different.
cards.pmNote: AI 摘要吃掉的是 top-of-funnel 的資訊型查詢，不是有購買意圖的中段查詢。
cards.episode: Rethinking SEO in the age of AI | Eli Schwartz (SEO advisor, author)

alts.quote: Yeah, sorry. Buy-in doesn't feel quite right to me, because buy-in feels like, oh, I've come to agree with you. And that's different from it's a part of me.
alts.zh: 抱歉，我覺得「buy-in（買單）」這個詞不太對。buy-in 聽起來像「我最後被你說服了」，那跟「這東西本來就是我的一部分」是兩回事。

alts.quote: I actually say I disagree with Naval on this because often, when you're part of a large organization, it's really hard to do great work and get recognized for it.
alts.zh: 我其實在這件事上跟 Naval 意見不同，因為在大組織裡，你常常很難既做出好成果又被看見。

alts.quote: I think this is an interesting thing that technical founders sometimes don't really like. They think sales is a very negative part of the process. I think it's not that black and white.
alts.zh: 技術背景的創辦人常常不太喜歡這件事，他們覺得業務是整個過程裡很負面的一塊。我覺得沒那麼非黑即白。

cards.pattern: Transparently, I thought this was going to be [誇張的預測]. We have not seen it yet.
cards.quote: Transparently, I thought this was going to be an apocalypse. So I shared about a year ago that it's going to be an apocalypse. We have not seen it yet.
cards.zh: 老實說，我本來以為這會是世界末日。我一年前也是這樣公開講的。到目前為止並沒有發生。
cards.why: Transparently 當句首副詞是近年英文職場很流行的誠實信號（比 honestly 更正式一點）。主動翻出自己講錯的舊預測，是建立可信度最貴也最有效的方式——因為多數人不會這樣做。
swaps: To be straight with you, I called this wrong.
I predicted X publicly. It hasn't happened.
Full disclosure: my earlier take was too extreme.
cards.pmNote: 公開修正自己的舊預測，是預測型工作（策略、成長）唯一能累積信譽的方式。
cards.episode: Rethinking SEO in the age of AI | Eli Schwartz (SEO advisor, author)

alts.quote: A year ago, I thought we were going through a similar kind of transition. We're clearly not. This is different.
alts.zh: 一年前我以為我們正在經歷類似的轉型。顯然不是。這次不一樣。

alts.quote: Fast-forward to the middle of 2023, everything looks like it's going to be a transformer. So now our hypotheses are just wrong.
alts.zh: 快轉到 2023 年中，看起來全部都會走向 transformer。所以我們原本的假設就是錯的。

alts.quote: Four or five years ago, I would've said, well, personal skills, nothing. It's all the environment. I used to be one of those particular people.
alts.zh: 四五年前我會說：個人能力根本不重要，全都是環境造成的。我以前就是那一派的人。

cards.pattern: If you take all those steps back and look at it from [X] perspective, there's no way that it won't [結果].
cards.quote: So I think if you take all those steps back and you look at this from a journey perspective, there's no way that it won't be impacting search. It's just going to be hard to find.
cards.zh: 所以我覺得，只要你退開幾步、用「使用者旅程」的角度看，它不可能不影響搜尋。只是那個影響很難被指認出來。
cards.why: there's no way that it won't 是雙重否定的強調法，比 it will definitely 更有推理感——像是排除所有其他可能之後剩下的結論。後面立刻自己加上限制（很難被指認），讓強斷言不失分寸。
swaps: I don't see how it doesn't affect search.
Structurally, this has to show up somewhere.
The effect is certain; the measurement isn't.
cards.pmNote: 指標沒動不等於沒影響——同時期的其他變動可能把訊號蓋掉了。
cards.episode: Rethinking SEO in the age of AI | Eli Schwartz (SEO advisor, author)

alts.quote: There's no way that you can lower the cost of content creation and increase the scale of distribution and not see this emerge, this creator economy I think emerge.
alts.zh: 你不可能同時把內容製作成本壓低、又把發行規模放大，然後這個東西——創作者經濟——不出現。

alts.quote: I think with hiring, it's funny, man, there's so much hiring advice online and you read it and you're like, "Yeah, this is super obvious." And then when you live it, you're suddenly like, "Aah, this is why people say this."
alts.zh: 招人這件事很好笑，網路上一堆建議，你看的時候都覺得「這不是廢話嗎」。等你真的經歷過，才會突然懂「喔，原來大家是這個意思」。

alts.quote: So we can think there's people who don't know about it, there's people who do know about it but don't do it, and then there's people who do know about it, but do do it. And it's that last group that's so tiny.
alts.zh: 可以分成三種人：不知道這件事的、知道但不做的、知道又真的去做的。而最後那一群小得可憐。

cards.quote: Yeah. I actually have a better one for you.
cards.zh: 對。不過我有一個更好的例子可以給你。
cards.why: 先用 Yeah 接住對方的總結，再用 I actually have a better one 把發言權要回來——不是打斷，是加碼。for you 讓這個動作變成給予而不是搶話，是英文口語裡很小但很好用的軟化。
swaps: Can I give you a sharper example?
There's a cleaner case I'd rather use.
Actually, let me swap in a better one.
cards.pmNote: 會議裡要把討論拉回你想講的案例，用「我有一個更好的例子」比反駁對方的例子有效。
cards.episode: Rethinking SEO in the age of AI | Eli Schwartz (SEO advisor, author)

alts.quote: So yeah, anyway, sorry, that's just a rant, but you should try it.
alts.zh: 總之，抱歉，剛剛那段只是我在碎念——但你真的該試試看。

alts.quote: Before you actually move on to the next one, I want to spend a little time on this one
alts.zh: 在你跳到下一點之前，我想在這一點上多待一下。

alts.quote: So is that my legacy? Yeah, and maybe there's some ego implicit in that, but can I go on for just a bit on this?
alts.zh: 所以那算是我的 legacy 嗎？算吧，裡面可能也有一點自我——不過我可以再多講一下嗎？

cards.pattern: Step one is the step that almost everyone misses, which is [X].
cards.quote: I think step one is the step that almost everyone misses on SEO, which is be the user. Try to understand who your user is.
cards.zh: 我覺得第一步就是幾乎每個人都跳過的那一步：去當那個使用者。先弄懂你的使用者是誰。
cards.why: 宣告「這是大家都漏掉的第一步」會讓一個很基本的建議聽起來像內幕。which is 後面接一個超短的祈使句（be the user），長句鋪陳、短句落地，是英文口語製造份量的標準節奏。
swaps: The part everyone skips is step one.
Before any of that: be the user.
Nobody starts here, and everybody should.
cards.pmNote: 做 SEO 前先問「使用者會搜什麼字」，答不出來就代表這個渠道不成立。
cards.episode: Rethinking SEO in the age of AI | Eli Schwartz (SEO advisor, author)

alts.quote: I think a lot of people think about markets almost like these bodies of water. And it's like, "Oh, it's this big body of water that we're going after." And I actually think that the most interesting markets, you have to think of them like currents.
alts.zh: 很多人把市場想成一片水域，覺得「喔，我們要去攻的是這一大片水」。但我覺得最有意思的市場，你得把它想成水流。

alts.quote: I'll just run this as a thought experiment and you can see what you think on this, but it's like, are AI models themselves defensible?
alts.zh: 我把它當成一個思想實驗丟出來，你自己判斷——AI 模型本身到底有沒有護城河？

alts.quote: the best way to get feedback from people is not by asking what they think, but to put something concrete in front of them and then have them react to it, right?
alts.zh: 要拿到回饋，最好的方式不是問人家怎麼想，而是先擺一個具體的東西在他面前，讓他反應，對吧？

cards.pattern: If you can't answer the question about [X], then don't do [Y].
cards.quote: So if you can't answer the question about what is it that someone's going to do a search on, then don't do SEO, because SEO is about appealing to that user.
cards.zh: 所以如果你答不出「別人會搜什麼」這個問題，那就不要做 SEO——因為 SEO 就是在對那個使用者說話。
cards.why: 把「不要做」綁在一個可檢驗的前置條件上，讓拒絕變成規則而不是意見——對方不是被你否決，是沒通過門檻。這種條件式的 no 在跨部門擋需求時特別安全。
swaps: No answer to that question, no channel.
If we can't name the query, we shouldn't fund this.
That's the entry test. We don't pass it.
cards.pmNote: 每個獲客渠道都該有一個 go/no-go 的前置問題，答不出來就先不投資源。
cards.episode: Rethinking SEO in the age of AI | Eli Schwartz (SEO advisor, author)

alts.quote: You can't fund everything. You don't get to pick everything.
alts.zh: 你沒辦法什麼都投資。你也沒有權利什麼都選。

alts.quote: Because if I'm not excited about what you you're doing, we're not going to work together.
alts.zh: 因為如果我對你在做的事沒有興奮感，我們就不會合作。

alts.quote: And if with all of that it didn't work, then you can say, "Hey, we're not going to try this again because we literally did try everything that we could to test this hypothesis.
alts.zh: 如果做到那樣還是沒用，你就可以說：「我們不會再試一次了，因為我們真的已經把能測的都測過了。」

cards.pattern: We have to really put away the myth that [X], because it's absolutely not.
cards.quote: So we have to really put away the myth that SEO is free because it's absolutely not free. There's a cost in time. There's a cost in resources.
cards.zh: 我們得先把「SEO 是免費的」這個迷思收起來，因為它絕對不免費。有時間成本，也有資源成本。
cards.why: put away the myth 把一個信念講成可以收進抽屜的東西，動作感很強，比 debunk 口語。接著用兩個對稱短句列成本，讓「不免費」不只是口號而有清單。
swaps: Let's retire the idea that this is free.
There's no such thing as a free channel.
It's not free — it's just not invoiced.
cards.pmNote: 「免費渠道」的成本藏在人力與機會成本裡，評估時要跟付費渠道用同一把尺。
cards.episode: Rethinking SEO in the age of AI | Eli Schwartz (SEO advisor, author)

alts.quote: I think there's this cult of lean, scrappy, fast, throw away your product quickly, keep moving. And I think at some level it's true, but a lot of times I see teams give up too early.
alts.zh: 現在有一種「精實、克難、快、東西不行就丟、繼續往前」的教派。某種程度上它是對的，但我常看到團隊太早就放棄了。

alts.quote: I really try and stay away from better, because that's really hard to define, and better means something different to everyone.
alts.zh: 我盡量不用「比較好」這個字，因為它很難定義，而且每個人心中的「比較好」都不一樣。

alts.quote: It's one thing to say you're spending a lot of time looking outside the building. It's a whole other thing to hear from the places you don't normally hear from.
alts.zh: 說自己花很多時間在公司外面看，是一回事；真的去聽那些你平常聽不到的聲音，完全是另一回事。

cards.pattern: I hate to use the words "it depends," because when consultants say it depends, they're throwing their hands up.
cards.quote: So those will be custom for anything. And I hate to use the word, it depends because I think whenever consultants say it depends, they're just throwing their hands up and saying, "I don't really know."
cards.zh: 這些每家都不一樣。我很不想講「看情況」，因為顧問一講「看情況」，通常就是兩手一攤說「我其實不知道」。
cards.why: 先自我批評你即將要用的說法，再用它——這樣聽眾就不會覺得你在敷衍。throwing their hands up 是「投降式攤手」的動作意象，比 avoiding the question 生動且不點名任何人。
swaps: I know how 'it depends' sounds, so let me give you the variables.
That answer is a cop-out unless I tell you on what.
It depends — and here's exactly on what.
cards.pmNote: 回答「看情況」時一定要接著列出決定因素，否則就是沒回答。
cards.episode: Rethinking SEO in the age of AI | Eli Schwartz (SEO advisor, author)

alts.quote: So I think it has to come with a place of knowing that you don't know everything and humility to say, "Hey, I need help." And it actually earns you a lot more credit than you think.
alts.zh: 我覺得這要來自一個認知：你不可能什麼都懂，還要有那個謙虛去說「嘿，我需要幫忙」。而且這其實比你想像的更會替你加分。

alts.quote: I don't know that I'm perfect at it, but I've learned to balance those things quite a bit more than I did in the past when I would just purely read from my questions and my rubric and not care about anything else.
alts.zh: 我不敢說我做得多完美，但我已經學會比以前平衡得多了——以前我只會照著自己的問題清單和評分表念，其他一概不管。

alts.quote: And again, I'm not an expert in this and I think Erin Meyer wrote that book, The Culture Map. So you should just find what those people wrote because they're much smarter than I am about this.
alts.zh: 再說一次，我不是這方面的專家。Erin Meyer 寫過《文化地圖》那本書，你們應該直接去看他們寫的，他們比我懂太多了。

cards.pattern: Total waste of time. I mean, unless there's a reason for it.
cards.quote: Yeah, total waste of time. Yeah, I mean, unless there's a reason for it. So if you're a media company and traffic means that that number keeps going up, then yes, it matters.
cards.zh: 對，純粹浪費時間。嗯，除非真的有理由啦。如果你是媒體公司、流量就是那個一路往上的數字，那當然有意義。
cards.why: 先給一句極短的重判（total waste of time），再用 unless 開一扇小門——這個先重後鬆的順序，讓立場清楚但不絕對。台灣人通常會反過來先鋪一堆條件，結果沒人記得結論。
swaps: Not worth doing — unless you're in this one case.
I'd cut it. The exception is...
Waste of effort, with one caveat.
cards.pmNote: 流量只有在它就是商業模式（媒體）時才是目標指標，其他情況都要換成轉換。
cards.episode: Rethinking SEO in the age of AI | Eli Schwartz (SEO advisor, author)

alts.quote: So yeah, I think the only way you build something that matters that's going to change the world is if you find a big idea you believe in and you say no to everything else.
alts.zh: 我覺得要做出真正有份量、能改變世界的東西，唯一的路就是找到一個你相信的大想法，然後對其他所有東西說不。

alts.quote: Realistically when you're a product manager, your job is to say no to 90% of things that get brought your way. And so you're saying no to 90%, so you can say yes to 10%.
alts.zh: 說穿了，當產品經理的工作就是把送到你面前的九成東西拒絕掉——你拒絕九成，才有辦法對那一成說好。

alts.quote: We're not going to create new changes to the product or create one time buys or reactivation emails.
alts.zh: 我們不會去動產品做新的改動，也不會做一次性購買或喚回信。

cards.pattern: It's not a statistically significant survey, but [結果] is fairly indicative — which surprises me.
cards.quote: It's not a statistically significant survey in general, but it will never go to 99% and one. That's fairly indicative that people are clicking the links, which surprises me.
cards.zh: 這份調查在統計上不算顯著，但它也不可能是 99 比 1。這蠻能說明大家真的有在點那些連結——這讓我有點意外。
cards.why: 承認樣本不夠好，卻指出「再不準也不會差到反轉結論」，是弱數據的正確用法。fairly indicative 這種降級的形容詞（不是 proves），加上結尾坦承結果跟自己預期相反，讓可信度反而更高。
swaps: Not rigorous, but directionally hard to ignore.
The sample's weak; the gap isn't.
I wouldn't publish this, but I'd act on it.
cards.pmNote: 小樣本可以推翻極端假設，不能拿來做精確估計——講清楚它能做什麼就不算誤用。
cards.episode: Rethinking SEO in the age of AI | Eli Schwartz (SEO advisor, author)

alts.quote: Whenever you talk to people who are at the company, they're always try to tell you the best version of the company. It's on you to triangulate that information, but you need both sides.
alts.zh: 你去問還在公司裡的人，他們永遠給你公司最好的那個版本。要交叉比對是你自己的責任，但兩邊的說法你都得聽到。

alts.quote: So there's a different metric that I like to use, which keys off of this idea that I think, again, people don't appreciate, which is cancellations grow faster than marketing.
alts.zh: 我比較喜歡用另一個指標，它是從一個大家常常沒放在心上的觀念推出來的：取消的成長速度比行銷快。

alts.quote: I have custom software that I've written that will say, 'Okay, here are the points at which the audience laughed.' Actually audibly laughed. That's the only way it counts.
alts.zh: 我自己寫了一套軟體，會告訴我「聽眾在哪些點笑了」。是真的出聲笑。只有出聲才算。

cards.pattern: It's funny that everyone says [A] and at the same time thinks [與 A 矛盾的 B].
cards.quote: It's funny that everyone complained about Google as this really, really smart, all-knowing LLM, and at the same time, they think they're dumb enough to fall for these guest posts.
cards.zh: 很好笑的是，大家一邊抱怨 Google 是那種超級聰明、什麼都知道的 LLM，一邊又覺得它笨到會被這些客座文章騙過去。
cards.why: 指出對方兩個信念互相打架，是最難反駁的一種反駁——因為攻擊的不是事實而是一致性。用 It's funny that 開頭，把嘲諷包在幽默裡，不會直接變成人身攻擊。
swaps: We can't have it both ways.
Those two beliefs can't both be true.
Pick one: they're smart, or they're fooled by this.
cards.pmNote: 碰到互相矛盾的團隊共識，先把兩句話並排唸出來，通常不需要再多論證。
cards.episode: Rethinking SEO in the age of AI | Eli Schwartz (SEO advisor, author)

alts.quote: So I think it is an utter waste of time for marketing to build these stupid little one pager persona things.
alts.zh: 所以我覺得行銷花時間做那些一頁式的 persona 小卡，根本是浪費時間。

alts.quote: We're all sitting talking about it, and Tate says, "It's a low margin reseller, one time sells." "You can say dotcom all you like, it's a low margin reseller."
alts.zh: 大家在車上討論，Tate 說：「它就是個低毛利的經銷商，一次性買賣。你要講幾次『.com』都可以，它還是個低毛利經銷商。」

alts.quote: I think maybe on the flip side of less positive is what it definitely learned is most of the time you hear it's really complex, it isn't. Leadership's just weak.
alts.zh: 我確實學到的是：多數時候你聽到「這件事很複雜」，其實它不複雜。只是領導層軟弱而已。

cards.quote: Yes, there are nuances. But for the most part, you get from most... Zero to 10, you can get to step eight by just doing the best practices.
cards.zh: 對，是有很多細節。但大多數情況下，從 0 到 10，你光靠基本功就能走到第 8。
cards.why: Yes, there are nuances. But for the most part... 是應付「你講得太簡化了」這種質疑的萬用組合：一句話承認複雜度，再用比例（for the most part）把主導權拿回來。搭配 0 到 10 的量化說法特別有說服力。
swaps: Sure, edge cases exist. The 80% is straightforward.
Granted, it's more complex. It's not that much more complex.
Yes — and the basics still get you most of the way.
cards.pmNote: 把一個領域講得神秘會阻礙團隊自己動手；先給 80% 的簡化版比較實際。
cards.episode: Rethinking SEO in the age of AI | Eli Schwartz (SEO advisor, author)

alts.quote: Yes and no. It depends on how you define that really.
alts.zh: 算是，也不算。要看你怎麼定義。

alts.quote: It's like these things that seem so common sense are actually hard with what they're doing… a lot of the advice is common sense. That doesn't mean it's easy to put in motion.
alts.zh: 這些看起來根本是常識的東西，真的做起來很難……很多建議都是常識，但常識不代表容易落地。

alts.quote: I acknowledge that that's a reaction that some people have. That's totally valid. This is unusual, what we're doing here.
alts.zh: 我承認有些人確實會有這種反應，這完全合理。我們在做的事本來就不太尋常。

cards.pattern: Yes, so I am biased. I think [立場].
cards.quote: Yes, so I am biased. I think they should have the right people give them advice on SEO.
cards.zh: 對，我確實有利益關係。但我還是覺得他們應該找對的人來給 SEO 建議。
cards.why: 主持人先說「你當然會偏向這個答案」，最俐落的回應是直接認下來（Yes, so I am biased），不辯解。認完之後照樣講立場，聽眾反而會自己替你的話打折而不是全盤否定。
swaps: Conflict of interest noted — here's my view anyway.
I have skin in this, so discount accordingly.
Fair, I'm not neutral on this one.
cards.pmNote: 有利益衝突時主動揭露，比等別人指出來便宜太多。
cards.episode: Rethinking SEO in the age of AI | Eli Schwartz (SEO advisor, author)

alts.quote: So, I don't know if supersystem is still the right exact analogy, but I think people just think of it as their AI.
alts.zh: 我不確定「超級系統」現在還是不是最精確的類比，但我覺得大家就是把它當成自己的 AI。

alts.quote: And again, I'm not an expert in this and I think Erin Meyer wrote that book, The Culture Map. So you should just find what those people wrote because they're much smarter than I am about this.
alts.zh: 再說一次，我不是這方面的專家。Erin Meyer 寫過《文化地圖》那本書，你們應該直接去看他們寫的，他們比我懂太多了。

alts.quote: I think this is a nuanced question and it's hard for me to say something on a podcast that'll actually be useful to people, but here's a couple of thoughts.
alts.zh: 我覺得這是個很有層次的問題，要在 podcast 上講出真的對別人有用的東西很難，不過我有幾個想法。

cards.pattern: We talked about [A], but we didn't talk about [B].
cards.quote: So I think we talked about how to decide whether to resource SEO, but we didn't talk about how to understand what the expectations are from SEO.
cards.zh: 我覺得我們談了「要不要投資源做 SEO」，但還沒談「對 SEO 的期待該怎麼設定」。
cards.why: 在會議快結束時盤點「講過什麼／沒講什麼」，是把議程主導權拿回來最自然的方式——你不是要求加時間，你只是指出缺口。這個句型也很適合會議紀錄的開頭。
swaps: One thing we haven't covered is...
We've done the whether. We haven't done the how much.
There's a gap I want to close before we wrap.
cards.pmNote: 會議收尾前主動點名沒被討論到的題目，能避免決策帶著隱形缺口離場。
cards.episode: Rethinking SEO in the age of AI | Eli Schwartz (SEO advisor, author)

alts.quote: So I've used up basically all our time talking about Make Time. I think we should have a follow-up episode just to talk about Sprint. What I think we do is let's cut off the lightning round.
alts.zh: 我基本上把時間都花在 Make Time 上了。我覺得我們該再錄一集專門講 Sprint。現在我的想法是：閃電問答就先砍掉。

alts.quote: So let me take us back on track and let's talk about just the high level framework here.
alts.zh: 我們把話題拉回來，來談一下這個框架的高層次架構。

alts.quote: Well, first a pairing, and then one more. The pairing is reset expectations and slow your inbox.
alts.zh: 好，先講一組配套的，再講一個。配套的是：重設期待，還有讓你的收件匣慢下來。

cards.pattern: I've never seen [X] get to the truth, but it will help you make a better decision than if you just guess.
cards.quote: I've never seen a product plan get to the truth of what it could do, but it will help you make a better decision than if you just guess.
cards.zh: 我沒看過哪份產品計畫真的算準過它能做到什麼，但它還是會讓你的決定比純用猜的好。
cards.why: 先承認方法不準，再把標準從「準確」換成「比不做好」——這是替一切估算辯護的最強姿勢。better than if you just guess 給了一個誰都同意的比較基準，反對者很難再要求你精準。
swaps: It won't be right. It'll be less wrong than guessing.
The number is fiction; the reasoning isn't.
Directionally useful, precisely wrong.
cards.pmNote: 預測的價值在於逼你把假設寫下來，之後才有東西可以被推翻。
cards.episode: Rethinking SEO in the age of AI | Eli Schwartz (SEO advisor, author)

alts.quote: What I've found is that once you commit to a decision, you actually learn more post committing to that decision about what's going to work and not going to work, and you move out of the hypothetical.
alts.zh: 我發現的是，一旦你對一個決定拍板，你在拍板之後反而會學到更多——什麼會成、什麼不會成——而且你會離開純假設的狀態。

alts.quote: But, what I've found is when you build a product, most founders, and most teams kind of stop when it works.
alts.zh: 但我發現的是，做產品的時候，大部分創辦人跟團隊在「能用了」的那一刻就停了。

alts.quote: And that what I've found over the years with founders is that they start to use Proven, Better, New to justify a wrong idea.
alts.zh: 我這些年在創辦人身上發現的是，他們會開始拿「已驗證、更好、全新」這套框架去合理化一個錯的點子。

cards.pattern: I'm not saying [窄的說法]. I'm saying [寬的說法].
cards.quote: So I'm not saying they didn't get the exact monthly number wrong. I'm saying they got it wrong by many factors.
cards.zh: 我不是在說他們只是月份的確切數字抓錯。我是說他們錯了好幾個量級。
cards.why: I'm not saying X, I'm saying Y 是被誤解時最快的校正器：先刪掉對方的版本，再放上自己的。這裡還順手把主張放大了（不是小誤差，是量級誤差），示範了澄清也可以是加強。
swaps: To be precise: it's not off by a bit, it's off by an order of magnitude.
Let me sharpen that.
Not slightly wrong — structurally wrong.
cards.pmNote: 指出估算有誤時要講清楚是「誤差」還是「量級錯誤」，處置方式完全不同。
cards.episode: Rethinking SEO in the age of AI | Eli Schwartz (SEO advisor, author)

alts.quote: I'm not saying that we should not take customer feedback, that's very different.
alts.zh: 我不是說不要聽客戶回饋——那是完全不同的兩件事。

alts.quote: I read the email, I'm like, "What do you want me to do? Is this an FYI? Are you saying there's a problem? Do you want me to help?"
alts.zh: 我讀完信心想：「你到底要我做什麼？這是知會嗎？你是在說有問題嗎？還是你要我幫忙？」

alts.quote: And correct me if I'm wrong.
alts.zh: 講錯的話你糾正我。

cards.pattern: They're helpful. But I don't think they're a source of actual truth.
cards.quote: So they're helpful. Tools are helpful. But I don't think they are a source of actual truth.
cards.zh: 所以它們是有幫助的。工具是有幫助的。但我不覺得它們是真相的來源。
cards.why: 重複一次 helpful（they're / tools are）是刻意把肯定講滿，這樣後面的 But 才不會被聽成全盤否定。a source of actual truth 這個名詞化的說法，把爭論從「好不好用」精準地移到「能不能當依據」。
swaps: Useful, not authoritative.
Good for direction, bad for decisions.
I'd use them to compare, not to conclude.
cards.pmNote: 第三方數據工具適合做相對比較與正規化，不適合當絕對值進財測。
cards.episode: Rethinking SEO in the age of AI | Eli Schwartz (SEO advisor, author)

alts.quote: And I think people don't understand that in a competitive environment, being right is good, but being quick is necessary.
alts.zh: 我覺得大家沒搞懂：在競爭環境裡，做對是加分，做得快是必要條件。

alts.quote: Be careful. If you need to spend a little time on the problem, fine, but don't spend a lot of time because you need to save as much time as possible to come up with the winning solution.
alts.zh: 小心一點。你要花一點時間在問題上沒問題，但別花太多，因為你得盡量把時間留給「想出會贏的解法」。

alts.quote: And as long as your decision is like 70% right, you can iterate on that 20, 30% in either direction, but if you don't commit, then you don't actually get any new information that is high fidelity and high quality.
alts.zh: 只要決策有七成對，剩下的兩三成你都可以往任一邊修；但你不下注，就拿不到任何高品質的新資訊。

cards.pattern: You can do it, but understand there's a high cost — and the later you [做這件事的時機], the less successful it's going to be
cards.quote: if you want to change during the course of the quarter, if you want to disrupt our whole engineering product team, you can do it, but understand there's a high cost, and the later you do it in the quarter, the less successful it's going to be
cards.zh: 你想在季中改、想打亂整個工程團隊，可以啊，但你要知道代價很高——而且愈晚改，效果只會愈差。
cards.why: 不說 no，改成把 yes 的價碼標出來：you can do it 先把權力交回對方，but understand 再把後果掛在對方帳上。台灣人擋需求常只會說「這個有困難」，母語者的做法是「可以，但這是代價，你自己決定」。
swaps: We can absolutely do that — it just means X slips
That's doable. I just want you to see what it displaces first.
cards.pmNote: 擋需求最有效的不是拒絕，是把 opportunity cost 明碼標價後讓對方自己收手。
cards.episode: We replaced our sales team with 20 AI agents—here’s what happened | Jason Lemkin (SaaStr)

alts.quote: And so even though I really like a lot about this, I'm going to say no." And I often think that founders think that there's some secret truth that's being held from them on why someone says no or they want more feedback.
alts.zh: 「就算我真的很喜歡這個東西的很多地方，我還是要說不。」我也常覺得，創辦人以為別人說不的背後藏著什麼沒告訴他的秘密，或想再要更多回饋。

alts.quote: And when we got acquired, we had a conversation with our team where we said, we're going to of course embrace Spotify's culture and Spotify's core values, but we're not going to forget who we are as a team.
alts.zh: 被併購之後我們跟團隊談，說我們當然會擁抱 Spotify 的文化和核心價值，但我們不會忘記自己這個團隊是誰。

alts.quote: There's nothing easier than promising work later.
alts.zh: 沒有什麼比「答應以後再做」更容易的事了。

cards.pattern: [A], [B], whatever you want — you've got [固定額度]. But you've got to decide now.
cards.quote: HubSpot, SAP, whatever you want, you've got 10% of the budget, you've got a hundred story points, whatever metric or heuristic you use, but you've got to decide now each quarter
cards.zh: HubSpot、SAP，你要哪個都行，你有 10% 的額度、一百個 story point，隨你怎麼算——但你這一季現在就得決定。
cards.why: whatever you want 聽起來像全面讓步，其實是先把「總量」框死，再把選擇權（和排序的痛苦）丟回對方。談優先順序時，給額度比給答案有效得多。
swaps: Pick any two — you've got one sprint's worth of capacity
It's your call what goes in, but the envelope is fixed
cards.pmNote: 給 sales 固定 % 的 roadmap 額度，是把跨部門角力變成他們內部的自我排序。
cards.episode: We replaced our sales team with 20 AI agents—here’s what happened | Jason Lemkin (SaaStr)

alts.quote: Is the juice worth the squeeze? And now I would say that it's pretty clear that the juice is worth the squeeze.
alts.zh: 這個果汁值得你這樣擠嗎？以現在來看，我會說很明顯是值得的。

alts.quote: So I think a lot of times we just think, okay, this is the scope of it for now and we are okay launching this and the execution is good. But we know that this is not the fully figured out version.
alts.zh: 很多時候我們就是這樣想：現階段範圍就到這裡，執行品質夠好，可以上。但我們知道這還不是完整想通的版本。

alts.quote: And now, it's not like, "Okay, now, we're screwed and the project is going to be bigger." Now, we can have a really cool conversation about trade-offs.
alts.zh: 所以現在不是「完了，這專案要爆了」。現在我們可以來一場很棒的取捨對話。

cards.pattern: If you really need us to [激烈的要求], we'll do it. But understand — is this really what you want?
cards.quote: If you really need us to put us on the shelf and drop everything for a million dollar deal, we're a startup, we'll do it. But understand, just, is this really really what you want?
cards.zh: 如果你真的要我們把手上的東西全放下、為了這筆一百萬的案子全部重來，我們是新創，我們會做。但你想清楚——這真的是你要的嗎？
cards.why: 先答應到底（we'll do it），再用一個問句把責任整包退還。這比「不行」殺傷力更大，因為對方沒有可以吵的對象，只剩自己的判斷。
swaps: If that's the call, we'll make it. Just confirm that's the trade you want.
Say the word and we'll drop everything — but is that where you want the team?
cards.pmNote: 把不合理的需求「照單全收＋回問一次」，多數時候對方自己會撤回。
cards.episode: We replaced our sales team with 20 AI agents—here’s what happened | Jason Lemkin (SaaStr)

alts.quote: let's say somebody commenting about your business, who does not understand the nuance of it, you can't be reacting to everything.
alts.zh: 假設有人在評論你的生意，但他根本不懂裡面的細節——你不可能每件事都去回應。

alts.quote: And if with all of that it didn't work, then you can say, "Hey, we're not going to try this again because we literally did try everything that we could to test this hypothesis.
alts.zh: 如果做到那樣還是沒用，你就可以說：「我們不會再試一次了，因為我們真的已經把能測的都測過了。」

alts.quote: We're not going to write out long-form content around everything related to dating because that's not the Tinder product.
alts.zh: 我們不會針對所有跟約會有關的東西寫長文，因為那不是 Tinder 這個產品。

cards.pattern: If you need [X], if you need [Y], I want you back in six months. But today, we're not the right solution for you.
cards.quote: If you need this feature, if you need this integration, I want you back in six months when you use this big product that isn't that great. But today, we're not the right solution for you.
cards.zh: 如果你需要這個功能、需要這個串接，那你先去用那個大廠的爛產品，六個月後再回來找我。今天我們不是適合你的解法。
cards.why: 主動把自己判出局，反而建立可信度。關鍵是 I want you back in six months——拒絕的同時給了一個回來的時間點，關係沒斷。台灣人怕失去機會，往往硬撐，結果第二次連門都進不去。
swaps: Honestly, we're not the right fit for that today — come back when X
I'd rather you not buy this now and stay a fan
cards.pmNote: 頂尖 sales 敢說「現在不要買」；這叫 honest disqualification，長期 NPS 與轉介率都更高。
cards.episode: We replaced our sales team with 20 AI agents—here’s what happened | Jason Lemkin (SaaStr)

alts.quote: We're not going to settle for all the annoying bad technology that we use today.
alts.zh: 我們不會將就現在用的那些又爛又煩人的技術。

alts.quote: And then we're like, "Well, does it help the customers? Does it help the product?" This sounds like a side quest to me, and basically means we shouldn't do it.
alts.zh: 然後我們就會問：「這對客戶有幫助嗎？對產品有幫助嗎？」這聽起來像支線任務，那基本上就是不該做。

alts.quote: We're not going to write out long-form content around everything related to dating because that's not the Tinder product.
alts.zh: 我們不會針對所有跟約會有關的東西寫長文，因為那不是 Tinder 這個產品。

cards.pattern: I know we all [大家嘴上都這麼說], but the reality is [實況], no matter what we say
cards.quote: I know we all release 28 times a day, but the reality is, software still goes on quarterly release cycles no matter what we say
cards.zh: 我知道我們嘴上都說一天出 28 版，但現實是，不管我們怎麼講，軟體對客戶來說還是季度發版。
cards.why: 先用 I know we all… 把自己也算進那個「大家」，反對就不再是你 vs 我，而是我們 vs 現實。no matter what we say 是收尾的鎚子，堵掉「可是我們流程不是這樣」的回嘴。
swaps: I know that's what we all say, but in practice…
On paper, yes. In reality, no matter how we frame it…
cards.pmNote: 內部 release 節奏 ≠ 客戶感知節奏；客戶一年最多消化兩次大改版。
cards.episode: We replaced our sales team with 20 AI agents—here’s what happened | Jason Lemkin (SaaStr)

alts.quote: You know what, I'll say yes and, right.
alts.zh: 這樣說吧，我要用「是，而且」來回答。

alts.quote: I don't know that I would look back at what I shipped back then or what we shipped back then, and say they were the best possible solutions or best possible product.
alts.zh: 我不確定我會回頭看當年出的東西，然後說那是最好的解法、最好的產品。

alts.quote: It sounds wonderful, having one person to deal with across all these functions. — It is and isn't. I'll just say, I've done both.
alts.zh: 「有一個人統管這些功能聽起來很棒。」——是也不是。我只能說，兩種我都做過。

cards.pattern: Everyone [做了某件事]. The question I ask folks is, "Did you earn it?"
cards.quote: Everyone raised prices. The question I ask folks is, "Did you earn it?"
cards.zh: 大家都漲價了。但我會問一句：你憑什麼漲？（你賺到這個漲價了嗎？）
cards.why: 不否定行為，只加一個評分標準。earn it 把「我們可以做」偷偷換成「我們配不配」，一句話就把討論從執行層拉回價值層——而且短到沒人能迴避。
swaps: Sure, but did we earn that?
The question I'd ask is whether we've earned the right to do that yet
cards.pmNote: 漲價要先加值：漲 8% 前先問這一年是否多給了 30% 的價值。
cards.episode: We replaced our sales team with 20 AI agents—here’s what happened | Jason Lemkin (SaaStr)

alts.quote: Ask if they understand your options, why you made your specific decision, and what would change your mind.
alts.zh: 問問他們懂不懂你有哪些選項、為什麼你做了那個決定，以及什麼會讓你改變想法。

alts.quote: I really try and stay away from better, because that's really hard to define, and better means something different to everyone.
alts.zh: 我盡量不用「比較好」這個字，因為它很難定義，而且每個人心中的「比較好」都不一樣。

alts.quote: They would write principles such as move fast and I would always be, "Everyone likes to move fast." It is not a good principle actually because nobody can really disagree with this reasonably.
alts.zh: 他們會寫「快速行動」這種原則，我都會回：誰不喜歡快速行動？那其實不是好的原則，因為沒有人會合理地反對它。

cards.pattern: I'd much rather have [少而強] than [多而弱]
cards.quote: I'd much rather have two reps, each closing a million than 20 reps struggling to close 100k each.
cards.zh: 我寧可要兩個各成交一百萬的業務，也不要二十個each 苦哈哈只做十萬的。
cards.why: I'd much rather have A than B 是英文講優先順序最乾淨的骨架：不解釋、不辯論，直接把兩個具體畫面並排，讓對方自己選。台灣人常用「我覺得應該要……比較好」，力度差很多。
swaps: I'd take one great X over five okay ones any day
Given the choice, fewer and better wins
cards.pmNote: 早期把 leads 集中給最強的人，比雨露均霑更快找到可複製的打法。
cards.episode: We replaced our sales team with 20 AI agents—here’s what happened | Jason Lemkin (SaaStr)

alts.quote: Yes, such a great point, Lenny. You absolutely need to time box this.
alts.zh: 對，這點問得很好。這件事你一定要設一個時間框。

alts.quote: A decision with too little data is fatal. A decision that takes too long and collects too much data is also fatal. So it's about trying to find the balance.
alts.zh: 資料太少就下決策，是致命的；拖太久、蒐集太多資料才決策，一樣致命。所以重點是抓到那個平衡。

alts.quote: I had this reputation that's, like I randomly pulled the number and said, my reputation worth $5 million. Why would I possibly mortgage that reputation for $20,000?
alts.zh: 我隨便抓個數字，說我的名聲值五百萬美金。那我幹嘛為了兩萬塊去把這個名聲抵押掉？

cards.pattern: The reason I'm a little confused, just because I want to get it right, is what I'm hearing — which maybe isn't what you said — is [複述]
cards.quote: The reason I'm a little confused, just because I want to get it right, is what I'm hearing, which maybe isn't what you said
cards.zh: 我有點不確定，純粹是想弄清楚——我聽到的（可能不是你講的意思）是……
cards.why: 三層保險：先認領困惑（我 confused，不是你講不清）、再說明動機（I want to get it right）、最後預留誤聽的退路（which maybe isn't what you said）。這是英文會議裡最安全的追問法，不會讓對方覺得被質疑。
swaps: Just so I get this right — what I'm hearing is…
Let me play that back, and tell me where I've got it wrong
cards.pmNote: 聽不懂時說「我 confused」而不是「你沒講清楚」，是跨部門對齊的基本禮貌。
cards.episode: We replaced our sales team with 20 AI agents—here’s what happened | Jason Lemkin (SaaStr)

alts.quote: What I'm hearing is step one is just get your kind of peer leaders aligned behind something that may not obviously be something your leaders want you to do, is that right?
alts.zh: 我聽到的是：第一步就是先把同層的主管拉到同一邊，就算那件事你的上面不見得想要你做——是這樣嗎？

alts.quote: What I'm hearing is basically you give those responsibilities to the engineers, designer, and maybe other functions within the team. Is that right?
alts.zh: 我聽到的意思基本上是：你們把那些責任分給工程師、設計師，可能還有團隊裡其他角色。我理解對嗎？

alts.quote: Backing up a little bit, we jumped right in. I'm curious how you even describe positioning, what the heck is positioning?
alts.zh: 稍微倒回去一下——我們一開始就直接跳進來了。我很好奇你會怎麼定義「定位」這件事？

cards.pattern: I have a lot of opinions here that are data-driven. This one, I need another year in the oven, and I'll tell you why.
cards.quote: As you can see, I have a lot of opinions on things here that are data-driven and they're live experience. This one, I need another year in the oven, and I'll tell you why.
cards.zh: 你也看得出來，我很多看法都是有數據、有實戰的。但這一題我還需要再放一年才熟，我跟你說為什麼。
cards.why: 承認不知道之前，先把自己的可信度墊高（其他題我都很有把握）——這樣「我還沒想清楚」就變成專業的訊號而不是弱點。need another year in the oven（還要再烤一年）是母語者常用、台灣人幾乎想不到的比喻。
swaps: I've got strong views on most of this — this one needs more time in the oven
Ask me again in a year; I don't have enough reps on this one yet
cards.pmNote: 資深的訊號不是每題都有答案，而是能明確標出哪一題自己還沒資格下判斷。
cards.episode: We replaced our sales team with 20 AI agents—here’s what happened | Jason Lemkin (SaaStr)

alts.quote: So I think it has to come with a place of knowing that you don't know everything and humility to say, "Hey, I need help." And it actually earns you a lot more credit than you think.
alts.zh: 我覺得這要來自一個認知：你不可能什麼都懂，還要有那個謙虛去說「嘿，我需要幫忙」。而且這其實比你想像的更會替你加分。

alts.quote: I'm not sure that it matches exactly to functions, but I can tell you what we're seeing more of, we need more of.
alts.zh: 我不確定這能不能剛好對到各個職能，但我可以告訴你我們看到什麼在變多、我們需要什麼變多。

alts.quote: I haven't seen their CAD, so I don't know what it's like inside their device, but they do have a lot of things going on.
alts.zh: 我沒看過他們的 CAD 圖，所以我不知道他們裝置裡面長怎樣，但他們確實塞了很多東西進去。

cards.pattern: It shouldn't have taken me this long to realize that [結論]
cards.quote: And the big epiphany, we already talked about it, it shouldn't have taken me this long to realize that anytime an employee fails, it's your fault.
cards.zh: 我最大的頓悟——其實前面也提過——是我不該這麼晚才明白：只要有員工陣亡，那都是你的錯。
cards.why: 把「我錯了」升級成「我太晚才懂」：承認的不是單一決策，而是自己的學習速度，聽起來更誠實也更有份量。台灣人講反省常停在「當時沒考慮到」，少了這層時間維度。
swaps: It took me way too long to see that…
I wish I'd understood this five years earlier
cards.pmNote: 招錯人是主管的責任，不是被招者的責任——這個歸因方向決定 postmortem 的品質。
cards.episode: We replaced our sales team with 20 AI agents—here’s what happened | Jason Lemkin (SaaStr)

alts.quote: And I'll tell you, ProfitWell, this was a big mistake. Yes, it was a great exit, we sold for over $200 million, et cetera, but we probably, if we had taken money, we could have had a billion-dollar exit
alts.zh: 老實說 ProfitWell 這件事是個大失誤。是啦，出場很漂亮，賣了兩億多美元，但如果我們當初有拿錢，可能會是十億等級的出場。

alts.quote: Yes, it's not working. It's my fault. I will deal with it.
alts.zh: 我做的第一件事就是認下來。我說：「對，它現在是壞的。是我的錯。我會處理。」

alts.quote: I don't want them to leave it at, "It was a big loss." You want to say, "What I learned from that is now I always run a load test, and I've had many successful launches since then."
alts.zh: 我不希望他只停在「那是一次很大的損失」。你應該說：我從那件事學到，現在我一定會先跑壓力測試，後來的好幾次上線都沒再出過同樣的問題。

cards.pattern: If you just want [高成本的請求], I'm sorry, honestly, I'm sorry, I don't have that. But if you want [低成本的替代]…
cards.quote: if you just want an hour of my time randomly, I'm sorry, honestly, I'm sorry, I don't have that hour of time
cards.zh: 如果你只是想隨機約我一小時，抱歉，真的很抱歉，我沒有那一小時。
cards.why: 重複的 I'm sorry, honestly, I'm sorry 不是囉唆，是把「拒絕」的情緒成本先付掉；接著馬上給替代管道，讓拒絕變成分流而不是關門。
swaps: I'm sorry — genuinely — I can't do calls. Email me the question though.
I don't have that hour, but I do read everything you send.
cards.pmNote: 拒絕請求時一定要附替代路徑，否則對方只記得被拒。
cards.episode: We replaced our sales team with 20 AI agents—here’s what happened | Jason Lemkin (SaaStr)

alts.quote: It's like, I don't think I can predict that. I think a much better use of my time is being very flexible and adaptable at a time like this.
alts.zh: 我不覺得我預測得了那個。我覺得我的時間花在保持彈性、快速調整上，回報高得多。

alts.quote: I always say to people don't come to me for management 101, I'm not the person to ask on how to run the most effective one-on-one with your people.
alts.zh: 我常跟人講：管理入門的東西不要來問我，怎麼把一對一開得最有效率，我不是那個該問的人。

alts.quote: All 25 have to want the same thing. If one person's out, you just don't do it at all.
alts.zh: 二十五個人得要的是同一件事。只要有一個人不要，那這個東西就整個不做。

cards.pattern: Here's the mistake that 99% of [某群人] make. We're not really [表面在做的事], we're [真正在做的事].
cards.quote: Here's the mistake that 99% of founders and sales reps make. We're not really selling in B2B, we're solving problems.
cards.zh: 99% 的創辦人跟業務都犯同一個錯。B2B 我們其實不是在賣東西，是在解問題。
cards.why: 先丟一個「你大概也在犯」的鉤子，再用 not X, we're Y 一句話換掉整個問題框架。這個 not A, but B 的重新命名句型，是英文簡報最省力的開場武器。
swaps: Most teams get this backwards. We're not shipping features, we're removing work.
The mistake almost everyone makes is thinking this is X. It isn't — it's Y.
cards.pmNote: 問題框架（framing）一改，整場討論的評估標準跟著改。
cards.episode: We replaced our sales team with 20 AI agents—here’s what happened | Jason Lemkin (SaaStr)

alts.quote: A lot of early stage founders get tripped up as they're taking late stage sales advice.
alts.zh: 很多早期創辦人會踩坑，是因為他們套用了後期階段的銷售建議。

alts.quote: I hate success stories. I love problem solving stories. And that's why when I talk to an entrepreneur, I expect them to be really open about that stuff.
alts.zh: 我討厭成功故事。我喜歡解決問題的故事。所以我跟創業者聊的時候，會期待他們願意把難的部分講出來。

alts.quote: And that's the thing they used to say, "Hey, leadership, this is the problem statement. Here's what we think how might we solve this big problem and here's what we think it looks like when we ship it." That's a mini-vision.
alts.zh: 「各位主管，這是問題陳述。我們認為可以怎麼解這個大問題，還有我們認為做出來會長什麼樣。」這就是一個小型願景。

cards.pattern: The best [人] never leave a meeting without a next step. The next step does not have to be [最終目標].
cards.quote: The best salespeople never leave a meeting without a next step. The next step does not have to be a check.
cards.zh: 最好的業務絕不會沒有下一步就散會。而下一步不一定要是簽約。
cards.why: 第二句是關鍵：先把「下一步」的門檻降到誰都能答應，會議才收得起來。台灣人在英文會議最常見的失敗就是收尾只說 thank you，然後在信箱裡等一個永遠不會來的回信。
swaps: Before we drop off — what's the next step?
Let's not end without something on the calendar
cards.pmNote: 每場會結束都要留下 owner + 下一個時間點，這是 DRI 制度的最小單位。
cards.episode: We replaced our sales team with 20 AI agents—here’s what happened | Jason Lemkin (SaaStr)

alts.quote: Let me just try to summarize what you shared, this five step framework.
alts.zh: 我試著把你剛剛講的整理一下，這個五步驟的框架。

alts.quote: So basically my long answer to your question, maybe boring answer is that I think starting next year, we're going to see early adopters starting to hockey stick their productivity.
alts.zh: 所以我這個落落長、可能還有點無聊的答案就是：我覺得從明年開始，早期採用者的生產力會開始往上翹。

alts.quote: So just to wrap things up, is there anything else that you thought would be fun to share or maybe a piece of wisdom you want to leave listeners with before we get to a very exciting lightning round?
alts.zh: 那就準備收尾了——還有什麼你覺得好玩、想分享的，或想留給大家的一句話，然後我們才進快問快答？

cards.pattern: What would it take, [名字]? How can we get going on [事情]? What would it take?
cards.quote: What would it take, Lenny? How can we get going on Riverside? What would it take?
cards.zh: 那要怎樣才成呢，Lenny？我們要怎麼把 Riverside 這件事推動起來？要什麼條件你才點頭？
cards.why: What would it take? 把「你要不要」換成「要什麼條件」——對方不用拒絕你，只需要開條件，談判就從 yes/no 變成填空題。這是英文要資源、要預算最高 CP 值的一句話。
swaps: What would need to be true for this to happen?
What would it take to get a yes from your side?
cards.pmNote: 要人要預算時，先問對方的條件式，比直接提數字更容易拿到東西。
cards.episode: We replaced our sales team with 20 AI agents—here’s what happened | Jason Lemkin (SaaStr)

alts.quote: Lenny, you can say, "Hey, are you open to 450? That was really what I was hoping for.
alts.zh: 你可以說：「你們可以接受 450 嗎？這其實是我原本期待的數字。這件事我們可以談嗎？」

alts.quote: And then I propose a little contingency plan, like hey, if that doesn't work out, here's the rollback plan, here's the maximum impact it will have done in a negative way, which is not going to be too much.
alts.zh: 然後我會提一個小小的備案：如果沒成，這是回滾計畫，這是最壞情況下的負面影響——而且不會太大。

alts.quote: We always keep this kind of mentality internal is that we're still a young company, we want to grow and you can feel free to talk to anyone.
alts.zh: 我們內部一直維持這種心態：我們還是家年輕公司、我們想長大，所以你要找誰談都可以。

cards.pattern: I know you're mad at me today, but it is your fault. A hundred percent your fault if [結果]. Don't blame them.
cards.quote: I know you're mad at me today, but it is your fault. A hundred percent your fault if any of your hires fail. Don't blame them.
cards.zh: 我知道你今天會氣我，但這是你的錯。招進來的人陣亡，百分之百是你的錯。別怪他們。
cards.why: 先替對方說出他的情緒（I know you're mad at me today），對方就沒有情緒可以再爆；接著才下重話。承認代價在先、指控在後，是英文給重話的標準順序。
swaps: You're not going to like this, but this one's on us
I know this lands badly — and it's still our call that failed
cards.pmNote: mishire 的檢討要往上歸因到招募流程，不然同一個坑會一直踩。
cards.episode: We replaced our sales team with 20 AI agents—here’s what happened | Jason Lemkin (SaaStr)

alts.quote: Clearly, you're not so scared that you can't do anything, so I'm not buying it. I don't do it quite like that, I do it with a lot more love than that.
alts.zh: 很明顯你沒有害怕到什麼都做不了，所以這個說法我不買單。我實際上不會講得這麼硬，我會帶更多善意。

alts.quote: It's like they know what to do, but they don't understand how to tie it back to the business context and the overall strategy needs and so where to prioritize.
alts.zh: 他們知道該做什麼，只是不知道怎麼把這件事接回商業脈絡跟整體策略，所以也就排不出優先順序。

alts.quote: Look, I don't have time to sugarcoat any feedback, and frankly, the best people I've worked with are the people who come into one-on-ones with me and yell at me and tell me I'm messing up.
alts.zh: 老實說，我沒空把回饋包糖衣；而且說真的，我合作過最好的人，都是會在一對一裡對我吼、直接說我哪裡搞砸了的人。

cards.pattern: And I know this is going to trigger some people, but the truth is [不受歡迎的事實]
cards.quote: And I know this is going to trigger some people, but the truth is they don't want to work.
cards.zh: 我知道這句會讓一些人不爽，但事實就是——他們不想做事。
cards.why: 先自報「這句會踩到人」，等於把反彈先繳械：聽者的力氣被用在「他知道自己在講什麼」上，而不是「他怎麼可以這樣講」。台灣人講重話常直接上，或乾脆不講。
swaps: This is going to be unpopular, but…
I'll probably catch heat for this, and I still think it's true
cards.pmNote: 在會議裡丟不受歡迎的判斷前，先標記它不受歡迎，可大幅降低防衛反應。
cards.episode: We replaced our sales team with 20 AI agents—here’s what happened | Jason Lemkin (SaaStr)

alts.quote: We're very interested in folks who have already been thinking about what the future should look like with agents. And we don't have to agree on where we're going, but we want people who are very passionate.
alts.zh: 我們很想找那種已經在思考「agent 的未來該長什麼樣」的人。方向上我們不一定要有共識，但我們要真的在乎這件事的人。

alts.quote: And it's kind of building a house that you want every brick in the house to match. And if you go and try and take some bricks from someone else's house and stick it in your house, it's probably going to not look very matched.
alts.zh: 這有點像蓋房子，你會希望每一塊磚都是搭的。如果你跑去人家家裡搬幾塊磚塞進自己家，看起來大概就是不搭。

alts.quote: I think if you're building a product where it's not necessarily an AI- first product and you have some AI features that are on the side, but it's not the core of your value, I don't know that I would operate this way.
alts.zh: 如果你做的不是 AI 優先的產品，只是旁邊掛幾個 AI 功能、AI 不是核心價值，那我不確定我會這樣做。

cards.pattern: [某種摩擦] is a good thing. It's a sign of [健康的組織] when there is [那個摩擦].
cards.quote: This stress between product and sales is a good thing. It's a sign of a well-run B2B company when there is stress between product and sales.
cards.zh: 產品跟業務之間的緊張是好事。B2B 公司如果產品跟業務之間有張力，那才叫營運健康。
cards.why: 把衝突重新命名為健康指標，兩邊都下得了台，接著才有空間談「怎麼管理張力」而不是「誰該讓步」。處理跨團隊卡關時，先改標籤再談方法。
swaps: The friction here isn't the problem — the lack of a process for it is
If there were no tension, I'd be more worried
cards.pmNote: 產品與業務零摩擦，通常代表產品沒進到夠多真實案子裡。
cards.episode: We replaced our sales team with 20 AI agents—here’s what happened | Jason Lemkin (SaaStr)

alts.quote: It's really important to give two people on your team different charges. One is like go grow the product and the other one is maintain that design, that craft. That tension is extremely healthy.
alts.zh: 團隊裡要刻意讓兩個人扛不同的任務：一個負責把產品做大，另一個負責守住設計跟質感。這種張力其實非常健康。

alts.quote: We've all been under Jeff's Eye of Sauron, we know it's miserable. What can we do to help?
alts.zh: 我們都被那道索倫之眼盯過，知道那有多難受。我們能幫上什麼？

alts.quote: Anytime you have these disagreements that feel really thorny or they feel like a disagreement in values, that's a sign that you really have a disagreement in strategy.
alts.zh: 每當某個爭執特別棘手、感覺像是價值觀的衝突，那通常是個訊號：你們真正在吵的是策略。

cards.pattern: I'm going to tell my boss that I think we should do that. I'm going to use a little social capital and say we should do this.
cards.quote: I'm going to tell my boss, on Monday, that I think we should do that. I'm going to use a little social capital and say we should do this.
cards.zh: 我禮拜一會跟我主管講，我覺得這個該做。我會動用一點我的政治額度，去替它說話。
cards.why: use a little social capital 是英文職場的高階說法：明講「我要為你花掉我的一點信用額度」，既表態支持又暗示這件事不是免費的。台灣人多半只會說「我幫你反映」，力度和誠意都輸一截。
swaps: I'll spend some capital on this one
I'll put my name on it when I raise it upstairs
cards.pmNote: IC 不該當場答應 roadmap，該做的是把訴求往上帶並標明自己願意背書多少。
cards.episode: We replaced our sales team with 20 AI agents—here’s what happened | Jason Lemkin (SaaStr)

alts.quote: So for positioning work, I'm going to say something that is contentious, but I don't think it is at all.
alts.zh: 講到定位這件事，我要說一句大家可能覺得很有爭議的話——但我完全不覺得有爭議。

alts.quote: Now, I'm biased when I'm going to say this, so take this with a pinch of salt, but I think the Accordion Method might be one of the things I'm the most proud of in my entire life.
alts.zh: 我要講的這件事我是有偏見的，所以你打個折聽——但我覺得手風琴法可能是我這輩子最引以為傲的東西之一。

alts.quote: We use our gut instinct on like, "Hey, no one's asking for this, in meaningful numbers at least. But we think this is going to be a big deal."
alts.zh: 我們就靠直覺判斷：「這件事沒什麼人在要求——至少沒有多到有意義。但我們覺得它會是個大事。」

cards.pattern: [某種價值/原則] aren't [價值/原則] unless there's an actual trade-off
cards.quote: values aren't values unless there's an actual trade-off
cards.zh: 沒有真的要付出代價的價值觀，就不叫價值觀。
cards.why: X aren't X unless… 是英文最俐落的重新定義句型：不否定對方，只加一個門檻，讓對方原本的東西自動不合格。八個字就能終結一場關於「我們的價值觀是什麼」的空轉會議。
swaps: It's not a priority unless something else drops
A strategy isn't a strategy until it says no to something
cards.pmNote: 策略即取捨：任何沒有排除項的優先順序都是願望清單。
cards.episode: 10 lessons on bootstrapping a $200m business | Patrick Campbell (ProfitWell)

alts.quote: There's definitely a trade-off. I think sometimes when companies specialize roles a lot it's because it's more efficient.
alts.zh: 這確實有取捨。公司把角色切得很細，通常是因為那樣比較有效率。

alts.quote: And now, it's not like, "Okay, now, we're screwed and the project is going to be bigger." Now, we can have a really cool conversation about trade-offs.
alts.zh: 所以現在不是「完了，這專案要爆了」。現在我們可以來一場很棒的取捨對話。

alts.quote: Is it a better outcome to just ship more faster now, but most of the things aren't impactful? Or is it a better outcome to ship fewer things but really work on making sure that you're shipping them in the best way?
alts.zh: 到底哪個結果比較好：現在拚命多出貨，但大部分都沒什麼影響力？還是少做幾件，但每一件都確保做到最好？

cards.pattern: It's okay to [別的做法]; it's not [適合我的], and that's okay — that's the entire point
cards.quote: it's okay to have a culture that doesn't believe that, it's not a culture for me, and that's okay, that's the entire point
cards.zh: 你們公司文化不信這一套也沒關係，那只是不適合我，這樣就好——這本來就是重點。
cards.why: 把分歧降級成「適配問題」而不是「對錯問題」：三次 okay 讓對方完全沒有被否定的感覺，但你的立場一步都沒退。這是英文表達不同意最不傷人的一招。
swaps: That works for plenty of teams — it just isn't how I'd run mine
Totally valid approach. Not mine, and that's fine.
cards.pmNote: 文化價值觀的功能是篩人，不是分對錯；能講清楚「誰不適合」的價值觀才有用。
cards.episode: 10 lessons on bootstrapping a $200m business | Patrick Campbell (ProfitWell)

alts.quote: Yeah, sorry. Buy-in doesn't feel quite right to me, because buy-in feels like, oh, I've come to agree with you. And that's different from it's a part of me.
alts.zh: 抱歉，我覺得「buy-in（買單）」這個詞不太對。buy-in 聽起來像「我最後被你說服了」，那跟「這東西本來就是我的一部分」是兩回事。

alts.quote: I'm not saying that having a large market someday doesn't matter, of course it does eventually. But trying to be super pedantic about market size when it's a pre-seed company, it's just not something I'd put a lot of thought.
alts.zh: 我不是說市場總有一天要夠大這件事不重要，當然重要。但在一家 pre-seed 公司還在糾結市場規模算得多精確，我不會花太多心思在上面。

alts.quote: So, I think one needs to be a little bit cautious on what Dario says. And that's setting aside the cynical view that he's just doing that department stock, which I don't believe at all.
alts.zh: 我覺得對 Dario 講的話要保留一點。而且我這裡還先撇開那種比較酸的解讀——說他只是在替自家股價講話——那我完全不相信。

cards.pattern: This is how we think about things. This is how we handle [這類狀況] here. If that's hard for you, let's find you another job.
cards.quote: This is how we think about things. This is how we handle this type of behavior here. If that's hard for you, let's find you another job.
cards.zh: 我們就是這樣想事情的。這種狀況我們在這裡就是這樣處理的。如果你覺得很難接受，那我們一起幫你找個別的工作。
cards.why: 前兩句只陳述事實、不評價人；第三句 let's find you another job 用 let's（我們一起）把開除包裝成合作。冷、清楚、但不侮辱——這是英文最難學會的重話語氣。
swaps: If that's a dealbreaker, let's help you land somewhere better
This is the deal here. If it doesn't fit, we'll help you find one that does.
cards.pmNote: 價值觀衝突要在試用期內處理完，拖越久對雙方成本越高。
cards.episode: 10 lessons on bootstrapping a $200m business | Patrick Campbell (ProfitWell)

alts.quote: So then the question is, how should we be candid? Okay, well, let's think of being candid as an act of kindness.
alts.zh: 所以問題變成：我們該怎麼坦白？後來想通了——把「坦白」當成一種善意的行為。

alts.quote: The only thing that's different is the insight that the founder has on the market, which is a hard pill to swallow. And I know that's hard to hear too.
alts.zh: 唯一的差別是創辦人對市場的洞察——這顆藥很難吞。我也知道這話很難聽。

alts.quote: And I honestly think saying, "You are not doing a good job," is much kinder than, "I think you can improve on this aspect or that aspect."
alts.zh: 老實說我覺得直接講「你做得不夠好」，其實比「我覺得你在某某方面可以再進步」還要仁慈。

cards.quote: We're not better than you, you're not better than us, it's just this is how we do things here.
cards.zh: 我們沒有比你好，你也沒有比我們好，就只是我們這裡是這樣做事的。
cards.why: 對稱句（不是你錯也不是我對）把價值判斷整個拿掉，只留下差異本身。處理立場衝突時，先把「誰高誰低」這個軸拔掉，剩下的就只是要不要合作。
swaps: Neither of us is wrong here — we just work differently
This isn't better or worse, it's just different
cards.pmNote: 跨團隊卡住時先確認是「標準不同」還是「利益不同」，處方完全不一樣。
cards.episode: 10 lessons on bootstrapping a $200m business | Patrick Campbell (ProfitWell)

alts.quote: So how are you doing? I bet it's been a hard week.
alts.zh: 所以你還好嗎？我猜這禮拜很難熬吧。

alts.quote: So the ability to be really truth seeking and take the most respectful interpretation when you're giving feedback to focus on trying to get to a smart good outcome that benefits the business.
alts.zh: 所以那種追求真相、並且在給回饋時採取「最善意的解讀」的能力，目標是導向對生意有利的好結果。

alts.quote: It's not that one of my PM counterparts couldn't bring a lot to the design table, it's just I need you to play that position.
alts.zh: 不是說 PM 對設計沒有貢獻——他們當然有；只是我需要你守住你的位置。

cards.pattern: You probably didn't know, but I don't really like when [具體行為]
cards.quote: Hey, Lenny. You probably didn't know, but I don't really like when people comment on my shirt.
cards.zh: 嘿 Lenny，你可能不知道，我其實不太喜歡別人評論我的衣服。
cards.why: You probably didn't know 一句話就替對方脫罪，把「你冒犯我」變成「你少了一則資訊」。這是英文日常給微型回饋的黃金開場，台灣人不是忍著就是憋到爆炸。
swaps: You had no way of knowing this, but…
Small thing, and you couldn't have known — I'd rather we didn't…
cards.pmNote: 把最寬容的解讀（most charitable interpretation）當預設，是低內耗團隊的基本設定。
cards.episode: 10 lessons on bootstrapping a $200m business | Patrick Campbell (ProfitWell)

alts.quote: And one thing that I noticed, a lot of people just don't know what you built.
alts.zh: 我注意到一件事：很多人根本不知道你做了什麼。

alts.quote: Hey, well this is how other people perceive you including me, but maybe this is not what you are intending...
alts.zh: 其他人——包括我——是這樣看你的，但這可能不是你原本想呈現的樣子。

alts.quote: It's like they know what to do, but they don't understand how to tie it back to the business context and the overall strategy needs and so where to prioritize.
alts.zh: 他們知道該做什麼，只是不知道怎麼把這件事接回商業脈絡跟整體策略，所以也就排不出優先順序。

cards.pattern: [某個廣被接受的建議] is terrible advice. And if I'm being charitable, it's just outdated.
cards.quote: But as an overall missive, don't focus on your competitors is terrible advice. And if I'm being charitable, it's just outdated
cards.zh: 但當成通則來講，「不要管競爭對手」是很爛的建議。往好處說的話，它只是過時了。
cards.why: if I'm being charitable（往好處說的話）是英文反對時的高段緩衝：先重話、再自願讓一步，顯得你是就事論事而不是在鬥人。台灣人通常反過來——先客氣半天，重點卻沒說出口。
swaps: Being generous, it's just out of date
At best, that advice hasn't aged well
cards.pmNote: 老建議要檢查它成立時的市場條件是否還在（CAC、競品密度）。
cards.episode: 10 lessons on bootstrapping a $200m business | Patrick Campbell (ProfitWell)

alts.quote: So I think it's an unnecessary addition, but maybe I'm just being protective of my original idea.
alts.zh: 我覺得那是多此一舉的補充，不過也可能只是我在護著自己原本的想法啦。

alts.quote: By the way, I'm being very mean to Figma so far in this conversation. There is a time when it's the right time for the Figma file.
alts.zh: 順帶一提，我到目前為止對 Figma 有點太兇了。Figma 檔是有它對的時機的。

alts.quote: Oh, I think this is my hot take. You hear people talking about craft and taste and product management, and it's all very wonderful. And I'm totally on board.
alts.zh: 喔，這大概是我的爭議發言了。大家都在談 craft、談品味、談產品管理，聽起來都很美好，我也完全買單——

cards.pattern: The biggest misconception about [X] is [誤解]. You don't have to [誤解] at all — you just have to [真正該做的].
cards.quote: the biggest misconception about customer research is I have to listen to them. You don't have to listen to them at all, you just have to understand where they are
cards.zh: 對客戶研究最大的誤解，是以為做了就得照客戶說的做。你完全不必照做，你只需要搞清楚他們現在站在哪裡。
cards.why: 接住反對時最有效的不是辯論，是指認出對方腦中那個沒說出口的假設，然後只拆掉那一塊。you don't have to X at all, you just have to Y 是這個動作的標準骨架。
swaps: You're not obligated to act on it — you just need to know it
Listening isn't obeying
cards.pmNote: 使用者研究的產出是理解，不是需求清單；判斷仍然是 PM 的工作。
cards.episode: 10 lessons on bootstrapping a $200m business | Patrick Campbell (ProfitWell)

alts.quote: And I think one of the monikers we use internally is no, then go. As in just think through all the things that could go wrong, understand where scale will break, understand the things that might happen, and then move on anyway.
alts.zh: 我們內部有個口號叫「先說不，然後走」。把所有可能出錯的地方都想過一輪，知道規模在哪裡會斷，然後照樣往前。

alts.quote: That's a good idea, but we don't actually understand these three things before we start working on that. So maybe we should do understand work to make sure that that is actually the right idea.
alts.zh: 這個想法不錯，但在動手之前有三件事我們其實還沒搞懂。也許先做點「理解型的工作」，確認這真的是對的方向。

alts.quote: One, what a problem to have. Of all the problems in the world, "I'm overwhelmed by customer interest," is on the top list of problems I want to have.
alts.zh: 第一，這是多好的問題啊。世界上這麼多問題，「客戶熱情多到我應付不來」是我最想要的那幾個之一。

cards.pattern: I'm giving you some heuristics, I'm giving you some benchmarks — but your mileage is going to vary.
cards.quote: So I'm giving some heuristics, I'm giving some benchmarks, but your mileage is going to vary.
cards.zh: 我給的是一些經驗法則、一些對照基準，但你們的狀況一定會不一樣。
cards.why: your mileage may vary（原本是汽車油耗廣告的免責話）已經是英語職場標配的免責句。在一長串斷言之後補這一句，等於幫自己的建議加上有效範圍，聽起來更可信不是更弱。
swaps: These are benchmarks, not laws
Treat these as starting points — your context will move the numbers
cards.pmNote: 引用 benchmark 時一定要標明樣本與情境，否則會被當成保證值。
cards.episode: 10 lessons on bootstrapping a $200m business | Patrick Campbell (ProfitWell)

alts.quote: Those are just numbers I'm putting out there. It's always going to be a gut call based on where you are.
alts.zh: 那些數字只是我隨口丟出來的。這終究是看你所在的位置做的直覺判斷。

alts.quote: I'll admit I'm definitely not an SEO expert. I've been fortunate to work with some of the best marketers in the world who I think are bonafide legends at this point
alts.zh: 我坦白說我絕對不是 SEO 專家。我只是很幸運跟一些世界頂尖的行銷人共事過，那些人到今天都算是真正的傳奇。

alts.quote: I'm not an expert on MMM, so I'm not going to be able to comment to quite the degree that they have.
alts.zh: MMM 我不是專家，所以我沒辦法講到他們那個深度。

cards.quote: So I don't know if I answered your question, but that's the scope of that problem I think
cards.zh: 我不確定有沒有回答到你的問題，但這大概就是這個問題的範圍。
cards.why: 講完一大段之後主動交回主控權：既承認可能離題，又順手替自己的長答案下了一個標籤（我在描述問題的範圍）。台灣人講完長答案通常就停住，讓對方尷尬地判斷要不要追問。
swaps: Not sure that's what you were asking — happy to take it from another angle
That may have been more than you wanted. Did that get at it?
cards.pmNote: 長答案結束時自評一句，是主持會議與被訪談時都通用的收尾。
cards.episode: 10 lessons on bootstrapping a $200m business | Patrick Campbell (ProfitWell)
