alts.quote: You're sitting in the meeting and you're like, "This is a dumb question. Everyone's going to think I'm an idiot." But then you get brave and you ask it and it turns out it wasn't a dumb question.
alts.zh: 你坐在會議裡想：「這問題也太蠢，問了大家會覺得我是白痴。」結果你鼓起勇氣問了，才發現根本不是蠢問題。

alts.quote: The support's not going to be good enough. They probably don't have good governance policies or other things that we need. Whether that's true or not, this is what it looks like.
alts.zh: 他們的客服大概不夠好、治理政策大概也不合我們要求。這是不是事實不重要——重點是看起來就是這樣。

alts.quote: So just to mirror back what I'm hearing, there's this, if you visualize this curve at the bottom, it's like I don't even know what this is.
alts.zh: 所以把我聽到的鏡射回去：如果你把那條曲線想像出來，最底下那段就是——我根本不知道這是什麼。

cards.pattern: [明確立場]. And that answer offends everybody.
cards.quote: The basic idea is bootstrapping is for lifestyle businesses that want to cash flow. Funding is for companies trying to create a billion dollars in annual revenue. And that answer offends everybody.
cards.zh: 基本想法是：自力經營是給想要現金流的生活型事業，募資是給要做到年營收十億美元的公司。而這個答案會得罪所有人。
cards.why: 先把立場講死，再自己宣布「這會得罪大家」——反對的話被你先講掉，聽眾反而會想聽你怎麼撐住。這是英文丟爭議觀點的標準保護罩。
swaps: I know this annoys both camps, and here it is anyway
This take has no friends, but…
cards.pmNote: 募資與否要回推目標規模，不是回推當下現金水位。
cards.episode: 10 lessons on bootstrapping a $200m business | Patrick Campbell (ProfitWell)

alts.quote: And he asked me, 'Do you want the right answer or the real answer?' Say, 'You know, I heard the right answer so many times, give me the real answer.'
alts.zh: 他問我：「你要聽正確答案，還是真實答案？」我說：「正確答案我聽過太多次了，給我真實的那個。」

alts.quote: If someone else has a strategy for moving revenue that isn't getting it from customers, I want to know about it because it's so hard to get it from customers.
alts.zh: 如果有人有辦法在不靠客戶的情況下推動營收，我很想知道，因為從客戶身上拿到營收真的太難了。

alts.quote: But, and this is the big but, no one has this at the early stages when they don't have a good idea and they don't have customers and it's objectively not working.
alts.zh: 但是——而且這是很大的一個「但是」——在最早期、還沒有好點子、沒有客戶、客觀上根本不 work 的時候，沒有人會有那種信念。

cards.pattern: This was a big mistake. Yes, [好結果], but [其實可以更好的版本].
cards.quote: And I'll tell you, ProfitWell, this was a big mistake. Yes, it was a great exit, we sold for over $200 million, et cetera, but we probably, if we had taken money, we could have had a billion-dollar exit
cards.zh: 老實說 ProfitWell 這件事是個大失誤。是啦，出場很漂亮，賣了兩億多美元，但如果我們當初有拿錢，可能會是十億等級的出場。
cards.why: 承認錯誤最難的情況是「結果其實不差」。Yes, [成績], but [更高的參照點] 這個結構讓你在有成績時仍然檢討得下去——用更高的標準，而不是用失敗來自責。
swaps: It worked, and it was still the wrong call
Good outcome, wrong decision — those aren't the same thing
cards.pmNote: 檢討決策要看決策當下的資訊與可選項，不要用結果好壞倒推對錯。
cards.episode: 10 lessons on bootstrapping a $200m business | Patrick Campbell (ProfitWell)

alts.quote: Yeah, I messed up. But I know I'm still a good person and a good worker. Yes, I made a mistake, but I'm going to move on.
alts.zh: 對，我搞砸了。但我知道我還是個好人、也還是個好的工作者。對，我犯了錯，但我要往前走。

alts.quote: And the big epiphany, we already talked about it, it shouldn't have taken me this long to realize that anytime an employee fails, it's your fault.
alts.zh: 我最大的頓悟——其實前面也提過——是我不該這麼晚才明白：只要有員工陣亡，那都是你的錯。

alts.quote: I don't want them to leave it at, "It was a big loss." You want to say, "What I learned from that is now I always run a load test, and I've had many successful launches since then."
alts.zh: 我不希望他只停在「那是一次很大的損失」。你應該說：我從那件事學到，現在我一定會先跑壓力測試，後來的好幾次上線都沒再出過同樣的問題。

cards.pattern: You're going to snooze it a couple of times, I get it. But just do something, even if it's super small.
cards.quote: put a calendar invite, let it renew every three months. You're going to snooze it a couple of times, I get it, I've seen this many, many times before. But just do something, even if it's super small.
cards.zh: 開一個行事曆邀請，每三個月自動重複。你一定會按掉個幾次，我懂，我看過太多次了。但就是做點什麼，再小都好。
cards.why: 先幫對方把藉口講完（你會按掉，我懂），對方就沒有藉口可以拿出來用；然後把門檻降到最低（even if it's super small）。這是英文推動別人行動最好用的兩段式。
swaps: You'll skip it a few times — that's fine. Just don't skip it forever.
I know it'll slip. Do the smallest version anyway.
cards.pmNote: 定價每季至少動一件事，比一年做一次大改版更容易累積。
cards.episode: 10 lessons on bootstrapping a $200m business | Patrick Campbell (ProfitWell)

alts.quote: Let me tell you what a director does. And you're going to work with me over the next couple of months to do those things because I am promoting you to do the job, not to learn the job.
alts.zh: 我先跟你講總監到底在做什麼。接下來這幾個月你要跟我一起把那些事做一遍——因為我升你是要你來做這個職位，不是來學這個職位。

alts.quote: In six months, if I'm telling you what to do, I've hired the wrong person.
alts.zh: 半年後如果還是我在告訴你要做什麼，那就是我當初找錯人了。

alts.quote: I'm asking them, "What do you do for joy? Are you doing something every single day that's bringing you joy in your life?" And if they say no, I'm like, "That's a problem."
alts.zh: 我會問他們：「你都做什麼讓自己開心？你每天有沒有一件事是讓你有樂趣的？」如果回答沒有，我就會說：「那這是個問題。」

cards.pattern: Pound for pound, it's [最關鍵的那一項]
cards.quote: The number one thing to figure out when you're thinking about the different pricing pieces, pound for pound, it's the pricing metric or the value metric.
cards.zh: 定價的各個環節裡，論投入產出比，最該先搞定的就是計價單位（價值指標）。
cards.why: pound for pound 原是拳擊術語（同量級比較），母語者拿來表示「以投入產出比來說最強的」。這是台灣人幾乎想不到、但一講出來就顯得很在地的排序用語。
swaps: Dollar for dollar, this is the highest-leverage one
If you only fix one thing, fix this
cards.pmNote: 價值指標（per seat / per 1,000 visits）決定 churn 與 expansion，比價格數字本身重要。
cards.episode: 10 lessons on bootstrapping a $200m business | Patrick Campbell (ProfitWell)

alts.quote: So this is not an estimate of time, it's an appetite, which is a radically different approach. It doesn't sound like that much of a different word, but it really is.
alts.zh: 這不是「時間估算」，這是「胃口」——做法完全不一樣。聽起來只是換個字，但差別真的很大。

alts.quote: And it's hard because in making it compact you're losing completeness.
alts.zh: 這很難，因為你把它壓得越精簡，就越不完整。

alts.quote: But what's really interesting is it's not a universal thing. The amount of detail that the team is going to feel helps them is a dial that we can turn that depends on who's on the team.
alts.zh: 但有趣的是，這件事沒有通則。要給多少細節其實是一個可以轉的旋鈕，看團隊裡是誰。

cards.pattern: I'm just going to bump you up to [新方案]. Let me know if you have any questions.
cards.quote: I'm just going to bump you up to the 100-video plan. Let me know if you have any questions.
cards.zh: 我就直接幫你升到 100 支影片的方案囉。有問題再跟我說。
cards.why: 漲價講成「已完成的服務動作」：I'm just going to… 是既成事實式語氣，Let me know if you have any questions 把異議管道留著卻不主動邀請。比「請問您願意升級嗎」成功率高得多。
swaps: I'll go ahead and move you to the next tier — shout if that's a problem
We're moving you up to X from next cycle; let me know if you'd rather not
cards.pmNote: 用量型定價的升級應該是自動發生的通知，不是一次重新銷售。
cards.episode: 10 lessons on bootstrapping a $200m business | Patrick Campbell (ProfitWell)

alts.quote: So what I'm hearing from them is that you're missing deadlines on a regular basis and not letting them know you're missing the deadlines, and that also you're not fully keeping your team up to speed.
alts.zh: 所以我從他們那邊聽到的是：你經常錯過死線，而且錯過的時候沒有讓他們知道，另外你也沒有讓你的團隊完全掌握狀況。

alts.quote: Hopefully I'm not making this sound too daunting. I'm just really trying to lay out all the mistakes I've made.
alts.zh: 希望我沒有把這件事講得太嚇人。我只是想把我自己踩過的坑全部攤出來。

alts.quote: By the way, a very, very successful company for a new set of products has a 50% hit rate. So half of you are going to come back in a year and have a different job. Do you have the resilience to do that?
alts.zh: 順帶一提，一家非常成功的公司做新產品的成功率大概是五成。所以你們有一半的人一年後會換一份工作。你們有那個韌性嗎？

cards.quote: Okay, let me not overreact here. Let me seek to understand and then react or respond, versus react.
cards.zh: 好，我先別反應過度。我先搞懂發生什麼事，再回應，而不是直接反射。
cards.why: respond vs react 這組對比是英語職場處理衝突的核心詞：react 是被觸發，respond 是選擇過的。把它講出聲（let me…）等於當著對方的面按下暫停鍵，也在示範你要的團隊文化。
swaps: Let me sit with this before I answer
I want to respond to this, not react to it
cards.pmNote: 第一反應通常是資訊不足下的猜測；先問三個問題再表態。
cards.episode: 10 lessons on bootstrapping a $200m business | Patrick Campbell (ProfitWell)

alts.quote: I was like, "First of all, I don't even think I can work with you anymore given this environment you're creating, but I need to understand why you are talking to your team like that."
alts.zh: 我就說：「老實講，看到你製造出來的這種氣氛，我覺得我沒辦法再跟你合作下去了。但我還是想先搞懂，你為什麼會這樣跟你的團隊講話。」

alts.quote: Okay, guys, I'm seeing something happen here. Every time we get close to talking about something that's really painful, somebody makes a joke and all the energy disappears.
alts.zh: 好，我看到一個現象。每次我們快要談到真正痛的事情，就會有人開個玩笑，然後所有能量就消失了。

alts.quote: We've all been under Jeff's Eye of Sauron, we know it's miserable. What can we do to help?
alts.zh: 我們都被那道索倫之眼盯過，知道那有多難受。我們能幫上什麼？

cards.pattern: [某群人] who [做了 X] have [10 到 30%] higher [指標] than those who didn't
cards.quote: prospects who meet you in person have 10 to 30% higher willingness to pay than those who didn't. Churn for those folks who you meet in person is typically 20% lower than those folks who have never met you.
cards.zh: 跟你當面見過的潛在客戶，付費意願會高出 10 到 30%；見過面的客戶流失率通常比沒見過的低 20%。
cards.why: 用數據撐主張的標準句型：A 組 vs 對照組 + 區間值（10 to 30%）+ typically。給區間而不是單一數字，反而讓人更信——因為它承認了變異。
swaps: Teams that do X see roughly a 20% lift versus those that don't
Directionally, it's a 10–30% difference — not a rounding error
cards.pmNote: 引用內部數據時給區間＋樣本量，比給一個漂亮的整數更有說服力。
cards.episode: 10 lessons on bootstrapping a $200m business | Patrick Campbell (ProfitWell)

alts.quote: And for people who completed a quiz, 53% of them went on to purchase versus 37% who didn't complete.
alts.zh: 有做完測驗的人，後來有 53% 去購買；沒做完的只有 37%。

alts.quote: Never ever once have I seen a rebrand or redesign, especially of a marketing site, produce good performance results.
alts.zh: 我從來、一次都沒看過品牌重塑或改版——尤其是行銷官網——帶來好的成效數字。

alts.quote: The basic principle with laser is that willpower is never going to win, and there's great research on this, but for now just trust me, you're not going to white-knuckle your way through not looking at Twitter when you're trying to work.
alts.zh: laser 的基本原理是：意志力永遠贏不了。這方面有很多很好的研究，但現在你先信我——你不可能靠硬撐來讓自己工作時不看 Twitter。

cards.quote: you can't be everything to all people, so who are you for? Who are you for and who are you not for?
cards.zh: 你不可能討好所有人，所以你到底是為誰做的？你是為誰做的、又不是為誰做的？
cards.why: 把模糊的「我們要做好」轉成一個必須排除的問題：who are you not for 這半句才是重點。定義問題時強迫對方講出排除項，是最快讓討論落地的方式。
swaps: Who is this explicitly not for?
Let's name who we're happy to lose
cards.pmNote: problem statement 要含 non-goals，否則範疇會無限擴張。
cards.episode: 10 lessons on bootstrapping a $200m business | Patrick Campbell (ProfitWell)

alts.quote: And so then the first few pages became very much more problem-based because if people don't understand the problem then they can't understand or care about your solution.
alts.zh: 所以前面幾頁後來就大改成以「問題」為主，因為人如果不懂那個問題，就不可能懂、也不可能在乎你的解法。

alts.quote: Most people don't forget their talk. They forget the transitions in their talk.
alts.zh: 大部分人不是忘記整場講稿，是忘記段落之間怎麼接。

alts.quote: One is people set this goal, I want to be promoted the next thing, or I want to lead this big project. And those are bad goals, because it's not in your control. A good goal is what you can do.
alts.zh: 有一種是設「我要升到下一級」或「我要主導那個大專案」。這些是壞目標，因為不在你的掌控裡。好目標是你自己做得到的事。

cards.quote: One, I think that's a really fantastic, maybe not counterpoint, but thing to call out.
cards.zh: 第一，我覺得你這個提得非常好——也不算是反駁啦，但確實是該點出來的一件事。
cards.why: 被當場質疑時，先幫對方的質疑「降級命名」：不是 counterpoint（反駁），而是 thing to call out（值得點出的事）。既接住了對方，也悄悄把對立關係拆掉——你們變成同一邊在補洞。
swaps: That's a fair thing to flag — I wouldn't even call it a rebuttal
Good call-out. Let me take it head on.
cards.pmNote: pre-mortem 的精神：把反對意見當成幫你補洞的人，而不是敵人。
cards.episode: Relentless curiosity, radical accountability, and HubSpot’s winning growth formula | Christopher Miller (VP of Product, Growth and AI)

alts.quote: And to be clear, I think we're looking at a world that's not radically transformed the way that, maybe, the utopians think that it will be or the dystopians think it will be.
alts.zh: 先講清楚，我認為我們面對的世界，不會像烏托邦派想的那樣被徹底改造，也不會像反烏托邦派想的那樣。

alts.quote: I was like, "That's the product. The thing you're talking about is the product."
alts.zh: 我就說：「那就是產品啊。你正在講的那個東西，就是產品本身。」

alts.quote: I don't really agree and I still think it's wrong, but I'm committed to it." That's not actually commitment.
alts.zh: 「我其實不同意，我還是覺得這是錯的，但我會照做。」那並不是真正的承諾。

cards.pattern: When you're making decisions that could be described as [對某方有害] but a net positive for [另一方], you're probably not thinking long-term enough
cards.quote: when you're making decisions that could be described as hostile towards your customers, but a net positive for the business, you're probably not thinking long-term enough
cards.zh: 當你在做的決定可以被形容為「對客戶不友善、但對公司淨正面」時，多半代表你想得還不夠長。
cards.why: 不說對方錯，只說對方的時間軸太短——把價值爭論換成參數爭論。could be described as 又是一層緩衝（不是我說的，是這件事看起來像）。這兩層加起來，反對變得幾乎無法反彈。
swaps: That only pencils out if we're optimizing for this quarter
If it looks good for us and bad for them, the time horizon is probably too short
cards.pmNote: 「對客戶不利但對公司有利」的決策幾乎都是把未來的錢挪到現在。
cards.episode: Relentless curiosity, radical accountability, and HubSpot’s winning growth formula | Christopher Miller (VP of Product, Growth and AI)

alts.quote: How can you hire people whom you expect to make decisions without running them through you if you can't tolerate them making a decision that you disagree with?
alts.zh: 如果你受不了他們做出你不同意的決定，你怎麼可能招到那種不需要事事回報你就能決策的人？

alts.quote: 90% of customers or people who we meet who claim to have a land and expand strategy are only landing. They're not expanding because they gave their farm away in the land.
alts.zh: 我們遇到宣稱自己有 land and expand 策略的人，九成其實只有 land。他們沒辦法 expand，因為一開始就把家當全給出去了。

alts.quote: I think that to anyone out there who's doing user interviews and then saying, hey ChatGPT, summarize the takeaways, you're missing the point. You can't empathize with the summary.
alts.zh: 如果你做完使用者訪談，轉頭就叫 ChatGPT 幫你摘要重點，那你就搞錯重點了。你沒辦法對一份摘要產生同理心。

cards.pattern: I don't know that we even talk about problems without a qualifier. Are we talking about a [商業] problem? Are we talking about a [客戶] problem?
cards.quote: I don't know that we even talk about problems without a qualifier. Are we talking about a business problem? Are we talking about a customer problem?
cards.zh: 我們大概不會不加限定詞就講「問題」這兩個字。我們現在講的是商業問題？還是客戶問題？
cards.why: 用一個「我們公司習慣」的說法（we don't talk about problems without a qualifier）把追問變成規範而不是質疑，接著用兩個並列問句逼出分類。這是把模糊抱怨變成可解問題最快的兩句話。
swaps: Before we solve it — whose problem is this?
Is that a customer problem or a metric problem?
cards.pmNote: 商業問題若不先翻譯成客戶問題，做出來的解法通常對客戶有害。
cards.episode: Relentless curiosity, radical accountability, and HubSpot’s winning growth formula | Christopher Miller (VP of Product, Growth and AI)

alts.quote: And so then the first few pages became very much more problem-based because if people don't understand the problem then they can't understand or care about your solution.
alts.zh: 所以前面幾頁後來就大改成以「問題」為主，因為人如果不懂那個問題，就不可能懂、也不可能在乎你的解法。

alts.quote: The problem is not like what should my goal be or how should I figure out what to do with my life? They usually know, but it's very hard to actually make time for those things.
alts.zh: 問題不在於「我的目標該是什麼」或「我這輩子要幹嘛」。這個大家其實都知道。問題是很難真的挪出時間去做那些事。

alts.quote: So there's, I wouldn't say a checklist, but there's a series of questions that I asked to diagnose why is growth slowing in this order, because it's one of these things where the first one that's a problem, if you don't fix that, it doesn't matter if you fix one of the ones below.
alts.zh: 我不會說那是一張檢查清單，但我確實有一組問題，會照順序問下去診斷成長為什麼變慢——因為只要最前面那個沒修，後面修再多都沒用。

cards.pattern: I'll admit I'm definitely not a [領域] expert. I've been fortunate to work with [真正的專家]…
cards.quote: I'll admit I'm definitely not an SEO expert. I've been fortunate to work with some of the best marketers in the world who I think are bonafide legends at this point
cards.zh: 我坦白說我絕對不是 SEO 專家。我只是很幸運跟一些世界頂尖的行銷人共事過，那些人到今天都算是真正的傳奇。
cards.why: 承認不懂的正確順序：先劃清界線（我不是專家），再交代自己的資訊來源（我跟誰共事過）。這樣接下來講的內容仍然可信，但你不必為它背專家責任。台灣人常只做前半段，結果整段話被忽略。
swaps: I'm not the expert here — what I've picked up from the people who are is…
Caveat: this is secondhand from folks who do this for a living
cards.pmNote: 知識誠實：講出資訊來源的層級（第一手／二手），讓聽者自己調整信心權重。
cards.episode: Relentless curiosity, radical accountability, and HubSpot’s winning growth formula | Christopher Miller (VP of Product, Growth and AI)

alts.quote: Definitely don't bring me on here as a pricing expert, I think you have got better people for that.
alts.zh: 千萬別把我當定價專家找來，這題你應該去找更懂的人。

alts.quote: And I'll be very honest, I'm not an expert in education, but I just thought a lot about it.
alts.zh: 老實說，教育我不是專家，但我想過很多。

alts.quote: There are plenty of agencies that go into the 50s and 60s a month, but that's just a whole nother world, and I'm not an expert on that part.
alts.zh: 也有很多代理商月費開到五、六萬美金，但那完全是另一個世界了，那一塊我不是專家。

cards.pattern: I can't give a specific number, but [仍然回答問題的定性版本]
cards.quote: I can't give a specific number, but a large percentage of our revenue flows through the product.
cards.zh: 具體數字我不能講，但我們相當高比例的營收是走產品這條路進來的。
cards.why: 拒絕透露不等於不回答。先關門（I can't give a specific number），立刻開一扇小窗（a large percentage）——對方拿到了方向感，你什麼都沒洩漏。這句在面試、對外訪談、跨公司會議都極度實用。
swaps: I can't share the exact figure — directionally it's the majority
Not something I can put a number on, but it's material
cards.pmNote: 被問敏感數字時給量級或方向，比冷冰冰的「不方便透露」保住更多關係。
cards.episode: Relentless curiosity, radical accountability, and HubSpot’s winning growth formula | Christopher Miller (VP of Product, Growth and AI)

alts.quote: If the product manager and the designer are not available to be there during their product test, cancel the test. They need to be there.
alts.zh: 如果產品經理和設計師沒辦法到場，那這場使用者測試就取消。他們一定要在現場。

alts.quote: Realistically when you're a product manager, your job is to say no to 90% of things that get brought your way. And so you're saying no to 90%, so you can say yes to 10%.
alts.zh: 說穿了，當產品經理的工作就是把送到你面前的九成東西拒絕掉——你拒絕九成，才有辦法對那一成說好。

alts.quote: You can't fund everything. You don't get to pick everything.
alts.zh: 你沒辦法什麼都投資。你也沒有權利什麼都選。

cards.pattern: Truth be told, I think I bombed it. I actually don't think I would've hired me back then.
cards.quote: truth be told, when I interviewed with Fareed that first time, I think back to the interview and I think I bombed it. I actually don't think I would've hired me back then.
cards.zh: 老實講，我第一次跟 Fareed 面試的時候，現在回想起來我覺得我搞砸了。換成是我，當時我大概也不會錄取我自己。
cards.why: I wouldn't have hired me（我不會錄取我自己）是英文自嘲的高階用法：把自己同時放在評審與被評審的位置，顯示你有能力用客觀標準看自己。承認失手卻讓人覺得你更可靠。
swaps: Looking back, I wouldn't have hired me either
I didn't earn that offer — someone took a bet on me
cards.pmNote: 把貴人講成「押注在你身上的人（sponsor）」而不是 mentor，更準確也更有份量。
cards.episode: Relentless curiosity, radical accountability, and HubSpot’s winning growth formula | Christopher Miller (VP of Product, Growth and AI)

alts.quote: Probably for me, I think my time at Instacart was probably not my best time. I think I went to Instacart with a vision of what I felt the product could be, but I was not aware or in tune with what the DNA of the company was.
alts.zh: 對我來說，Instacart 那段大概是我狀態最不好的時候。我帶著一套「產品應該長成什麼樣」的想像進去，卻沒真的看懂那家公司的 DNA 是什麼。

alts.quote: I feel really bad because I'm like, it should have been obvious. We should have been able to call a spade a spade and I guess speak truth to power.
alts.zh: 我到現在還是很懊惱，因為這件事本來就該一眼看穿。我們應該有辦法直話直說，向上把真話講出來。

alts.quote: And so maybe I picked the wrong term in calling it growth hacking, but I think it at least opened the conversation to getting more people thinking about growth in a different way.
alts.zh: 所以也許我當初取 growth hacking 這個名字是取錯了，但至少它打開了對話，讓更多人開始用不同的方式想成長這件事。

cards.pattern: I have a lot of rough edges that people have learned to deal with over the years, but I try to be self-aware about them
cards.quote: I have a lot of rough edges to my personality that I think people have just learned to deal with over the years, but I try to be self-aware about them
cards.zh: 我個性上有很多稜角，同事這些年大概是習慣了，但我至少努力對它們保持自覺。
cards.why: 回答缺點題的成熟版：不假謙虛、不列一個假缺點，而是承認稜角存在＋承諾自覺。rough edges 這個詞比 weakness 更中性，不會把自己講成有缺陷的產品。
swaps: I've got sharp edges; what I owe people is being aware of them
I'm not going to pretend those go away — I just try to flag them early
cards.pmNote: 面試自我覺察題的評分點是「你知不知道別人怎麼形容你」，不是缺點本身。
cards.episode: Relentless curiosity, radical accountability, and HubSpot’s winning growth formula | Christopher Miller (VP of Product, Growth and AI)

alts.quote: I'll tell the story that is kind of true, and people will think it's amazing, and also the real deal behind it.
alts.zh: 我先講那個「差不多是真的」的版本，大家會覺得很厲害；然後再講背後真正的狀況。

alts.quote: I genuinely think that some of the best product managers come from something else because you have empathy for being on the other side.
alts.zh: 我真心覺得最好的產品經理很多都是從別的領域轉過來的，因為你真的體會過站在另一邊是什麼感覺。

alts.quote: And I tried through that to be my most ordinary self as opposed to interview self, if that makes sense. Because you got to ask yourself, do I really want to spend my whole time having this discussion and this debate?
alts.zh: 整個過程我盡量拿出最平常的自己，而不是「面試版的自己」。因為你得問自己：我真的想每天都花時間在這種討論上嗎？

cards.pattern: If the people you most recently worked with were in a room and you weren't there, how would they talk about you?
cards.quote: if the people that you most recently worked with were in a room and you weren't there, how would they talk about you?
cards.zh: 如果你最近一起共事的那些人聚在一個房間裡、而你不在場，他們會怎麼講你？
cards.why: 把「請你自評」改成「請你模擬別人的評價」，對方無法只講漂亮話（因為他知道你可能真的會去問）。教練式提問的精髓：換一個觀察位置，答案就誠實了。
swaps: What would your last team say about you when you're not in the room?
How do you think you're described by people who've worked with you?
cards.pmNote: 這題同時是 reference check 的預告，能大幅提高回答的誠實度。
cards.episode: Relentless curiosity, radical accountability, and HubSpot’s winning growth formula | Christopher Miller (VP of Product, Growth and AI)

alts.quote: I'm like, "Let's say we weren't in the room as the leadership team," which is the one the team wants to get behind. Then you'll sometimes see the team hasn't even done the work between themselves talking.
alts.zh: 我會問：「假設我們這些主管不在這個房間，你們團隊自己最想投哪一個？」有時候你會發現他們彼此之間根本還沒討論過。

alts.quote: You ask questions like, what's the hardest you've ever worked to get something done and why? And that does differentiate a lot of people, a lot of people don't actually have a great answer to that.
alts.zh: 你可以問這種問題：你這輩子為了完成某件事最拚的一次是什麼？為什麼？這題真的很能分辨人，很多人其實答不太出來。

alts.quote: So if your partner comes to you and says that marketing plan or that product roadmap that you put together, not good, do you take it as the plan is not good and let's talk about what we can actually do to fix it?
alts.zh: 如果你的夥伴跟你說，你做的行銷計畫或產品路線圖不好，你會理解成「這份計畫不好，我們來談怎麼修」嗎？

cards.pattern: I might even ask them to define what [關鍵詞] means to them, so we can get on the same page of what we're even talking about
cards.quote: And I might even ask them to define what product-led means to them that we can get on the same page of what we're even talking about.
cards.zh: 我甚至會請他們先定義一下「產品驅動成長」對他們來說是什麼意思，這樣我們才知道彼此在講的是不是同一件事。
cards.why: what we're even talking about 裡的 even 是關鍵語氣：暗示「我們可能連題目都不同」，但因為包在一個提議裡（I might even ask），聽起來像謹慎而不是刁難。專治大家用同一個詞、想著不同東西的會議。
swaps: Before we go further — what does X mean in your head?
Let's align on the definition, otherwise we'll argue past each other
cards.pmNote: 對齊（alignment）的第一步永遠是名詞定義，不是目標設定。
cards.episode: Relentless curiosity, radical accountability, and HubSpot’s winning growth formula | Christopher Miller (VP of Product, Growth and AI)

alts.quote: Just for folks that are listening, just to calibrate what size of company you're talking about selling to here.
alts.zh: 為了讓聽的人有個基準——你剛剛講的是賣給多大規模的公司？

alts.quote: To make this even more concrete for people that are starting to like, oh, shit I got to do this. Can you just give us a list that doesn't have to be exhaustive?
alts.zh: 為了讓大家更具體一點——那些正在想「糟糕我得開始做了」的人——你可以給我們一個清單嗎？不用列很完整沒關係。

alts.quote: Okay, what do you mean by this? Are you talking about inner and outer loop? Are you talking about friction?
alts.zh: 好，你指的是什麼意思？你講的是內外迴圈嗎？還是講摩擦成本？

cards.pattern: Don't get me wrong, [承認對方那一派的正當性] — I'm not one of them.
cards.quote: And don't get me wrong, I think there's a lot of product folks out there who enjoy that modality of work, I'm not one of them.
cards.zh: 別誤會，我知道有很多產品人是真的喜歡那種工作方式的——我不是。
cards.why: Don't get me wrong 先擋掉「你在貶低別人」的解讀，把否定收斂成個人偏好（I'm not one of them）。四個字的免責聲明，換來一句可以直說的真心話。
swaps: No shade — it's just not how I like to work
Plenty of people thrive on that. I don't.
cards.pmNote: 表達偏好而非優劣，能保留跟不同工作風格的人合作的空間。
cards.episode: Relentless curiosity, radical accountability, and HubSpot’s winning growth formula | Christopher Miller (VP of Product, Growth and AI)

alts.quote: Again, don't get me wrong, I'm not trying to talk people out of doing it. But for me, a lot of this was luck.
alts.zh: 先說清楚，我不是想勸大家不要做。但對我來說，這裡面有很大一部分是運氣。

alts.quote: I'm curious what you think. I still don't think ideas are worth as much as maybe a lot of people think. I still think execution is really hard.
alts.zh: 我反而想聽你怎麼看。我還是不覺得點子有大家講的那麼值錢，我還是覺得執行才難。

alts.quote: Yeah, and don't get me wrong, there's obviously a ton of value in prototyping.
alts.zh: 嗯，別誤會，做原型當然有非常大的價值。

cards.pattern: In fact, if I'm being brutally honest, I think [大家都默認的東西] is kind of hard to achieve in [情境]
cards.quote: Our loops are less tactical. In fact, if I'm being brutally honest, I think loops are kind of hard to achieve in B2B SaaS.
cards.zh: 我們的成長迴圈比較不那麼戰術。老實說，我覺得在 B2B SaaS 裡要做出真正的迴圈其實蠻難的。
cards.why: if I'm being brutally honest 是英文的「授權自己講真話」開關，通常用在要推翻業界共識時。搭配 kind of（有點）當減壓閥，讓一句踩到整個社群的話聽起來仍然可討論。
swaps: Honestly? I don't think that model holds here.
Being blunt — I've never seen that work in this context
cards.pmNote: B2B SaaS 難有真正的成長迴圈，多半是漏斗＋口碑的宏觀飛輪。
cards.episode: Relentless curiosity, radical accountability, and HubSpot’s winning growth formula | Christopher Miller (VP of Product, Growth and AI)

alts.quote: And so I'm going to kind of reject that premise, because I don't think design takes more time.
alts.zh: 所以我要說，我不太接受那個前提，因為我不認為設計會花比較多時間。

alts.quote: I think sometimes people think that craft is about perfecting things and perfecting them in a very organized way or very early on. The downside with this perfection mindset is that it can be sometimes hard to put anything out because nothing is ever fully perfect.
alts.zh: 大家常以為所謂「工藝」就是把東西做到完美，而且要很有條理、很早就開始做。這種完美心態的代價是：你可能什麼都出不了貨，因為沒有東西是真正完美的。

alts.quote: I think people assume that there's a much more detailed semantic understanding of everybody's interests and preferences in the algorithm than there is.
alts.zh: 我覺得大家會以為演算法對每個人的興趣和偏好，有一套比實際上細膩得多的語意理解。

cards.quote: Does this continue to serve us today? And if not, we should be really comfortable of letting it go.
cards.zh: 這件事到今天還對我們有用嗎？如果沒有，我們應該要能很坦然地把它放掉。
cards.why: serve us（為我們服務）把制度、文化、做法都降格成工具——工具過期就丟，不涉及誰對誰錯。要收回既有立場時，先把它重新定義成「當時有用的東西」。
swaps: Is this still earning its place?
That made sense then. Does it make sense now?
cards.pmNote: 定期壓力測試自家文化與流程，是規模化時的必要動作。
cards.episode: Relentless curiosity, radical accountability, and HubSpot’s winning growth formula | Christopher Miller (VP of Product, Growth and AI)

alts.quote: By the way, I will say on the Peter one, I've come much more around to Peter's point of view. I would probably argue that one quite a bit differently today than I did, and I would give his view, I think, a lot more credit.
alts.zh: 順帶一提，Peter 那場辯論，我現在比較站到他那邊了。同樣的題目今天要我講，我會講得很不一樣，也會給他的看法多很多分數。

alts.quote: A year ago, I thought we were going through a similar kind of transition. We're clearly not. This is different.
alts.zh: 一年前我以為我們正在經歷類似的轉型。顯然不是。這次不一樣。

alts.quote: If you had asked me when I first started the company, it would've been an enthusiastic hell yes. I totally recommend. Now, I have a couple asterisks on top of it.
alts.zh: 如果你在我剛創業的時候問我，答案會是超級肯定的「絕對推薦」。現在的話，我會加上幾個但書。

cards.quote: if I had to guess how people might talk about that, if I wasn't in the room, maybe they would cite that, but it's tough to say.
cards.zh: 如果要我猜、我不在場的時候別人會怎麼講這件事，他們可能會提到那個吧——但很難說。
cards.why: 談自己的功勞最尷尬，這句把主語換成「別人在我不在時的說法」，等於借別人的嘴講自己的成績，再用 it's tough to say 收尾保持謙遜。不吹牛也不縮小，正是升遷簡報最難拿捏的那個位置。
swaps: I'd guess that's what people would point to, though I'm not the one to say
If you asked my team, I think they'd say X — but that's their call, not mine
cards.pmNote: 談影響力時把判斷權交給第三方，可信度比自我宣告高。
cards.episode: Relentless curiosity, radical accountability, and HubSpot’s winning growth formula | Christopher Miller (VP of Product, Growth and AI)

alts.quote: Beyond those cosmetics, the biggest thing I see particularly at higher levels is people talk about what they have done but not why it mattered.
alts.zh: 撇開那些表面功夫，我在比較資深的層級看到最大的問題是：大家只講自己做了什麼，不講那件事為什麼重要。

alts.quote: I think those people tend to get lost in organizations. So if that describes you, just remember to say what you did.
alts.zh: 這種人在組織裡很容易被淹沒。所以如果你就是這種人，記得一定要把你做過的事講出來。

alts.quote: Well, it's very generous of you. I wouldn't say... look, we've done some really good work, some good work so far at YouTube, and it's been a journey.
alts.zh: 你太抬舉我了。我不會這樣講啦——我們在 YouTube 是做了一些不錯的成績，過程也蠻曲折的。

cards.pattern: You could have all the [某種數據] in the world — it tells you what's happening, but it doesn't tell you why
cards.quote: You could have all the usage data in the world, that's going to tell you what's actually happening in your product, but it doesn't tell you why.
cards.zh: 就算你握有全世界的使用數據，它只會告訴你產品裡實際發生了什麼，不會告訴你為什麼。
cards.why: 用數據撐主張的反面技巧：主動指出自家數據的極限，反而讓你接下來要引用的質性資料變得必要。what vs why 這組對比是英文談研究方法時的固定句式。
swaps: The numbers tell us what, not why
Quant gets us to the question; qual gets us to the answer
cards.pmNote: 量化找出異常，質性解釋成因；兩者缺一，決策就會賭運氣。
cards.episode: Relentless curiosity, radical accountability, and HubSpot’s winning growth formula | Christopher Miller (VP of Product, Growth and AI)

alts.quote: Number one is actually measuring it. I can't tell you how many times I suggest to a founder to track cohorts and that's a new thing.
alts.zh: 第一件事其實是去量它。我真的數不清有多少次我建議創辦人追蹤 cohort，結果那對他們是全新的東西。

alts.quote: That often comes in the form of an interesting anecdote or a data point that's going to support that, or a story that's going to add emotion or illustrate it.
alts.zh: 那通常會以一個有趣的軼事、一個支撐它的數據點、或一個能加上情緒或具體說明的故事的形式出現。

alts.quote: They tend to have accomplished very difficult goals in very hostile environments. And it turns out that when you're starting a somewhat chaotic tech company, that's actually a very useful skill to have.
alts.zh: 這些人習慣在極度不友善的環境裡把很難的目標做出來。結果發現，開一家有點混亂的科技公司，這剛好是非常有用的能力。

cards.pattern: The number one mistake is hiring [某角色], giving them no resources, and expecting them to pull a rabbit out of their hat
cards.quote: the number one mistake is hiring a head of growth, giving them no resources and expecting them to pull rabbit out of their hat.
cards.zh: 最常見的錯誤，就是找了一個成長負責人來，什麼資源都不給，然後期待他變魔術。
cards.why: 要資源時最有效的說法不是「我需要 X」，而是把「沒有 X」講成一個大家都認得的失敗模式。pull a rabbit out of a hat（變兔子）讓不合理的期待聽起來荒謬，你就不必自己抱怨。
swaps: Hiring the role without the budget is how this usually fails
You can't hand someone a number and no levers
cards.pmNote: 談資源時先講失敗模式，再談需求，比直接開清單容易過關。
cards.episode: Relentless curiosity, radical accountability, and HubSpot’s winning growth formula | Christopher Miller (VP of Product, Growth and AI)

alts.quote: I say to the person, “Let’s come up with an arbitrary deadline!” We both know it’s made up, but there’s a weird gravitational pull once you’ve put a date out there.
alts.zh: 我會跟對方說：「我們來訂一個隨便的死線吧！」我們都知道那是編的，但日期一旦放上去，就會有一種奇怪的引力。

alts.quote: So discounting just to get the deal over the line, you're negotiating with yourself.
alts.zh: 為了把案子推過線就先給折扣，那你是在跟自己談判。

alts.quote: Okay. I would like to carve 20% of my time listening and I'm happy to do this work 80% of the time.
alts.zh: 好，我想切出兩成的時間去聽，另外八成的時間我很樂意投入手上的工作。

cards.pattern: Go reach out to [某人] and ask how you can make their day easier
cards.quote: go reach out to a PM and ask how you can make their day easier
cards.zh: 直接去找一個 PM，問他你可以幫他分擔什麼、讓他今天輕鬆一點。
cards.why: 把「請教／討教」翻轉成「我能替你做什麼」，對方沒有拒絕的理由，你也不欠人情。想跨進一個新領域時，這句比 can I pick your brain 好用十倍。
swaps: What could I take off your plate this week?
Is there a piece of this I could own for you?
cards.pmNote: 建立人脈的最短路徑是先提供勞力，再要資訊。
cards.episode: Relentless curiosity, radical accountability, and HubSpot’s winning growth formula | Christopher Miller (VP of Product, Growth and AI)

alts.quote: So especially when you're meeting with a new engineering team for the first time, actually ask them, what is one thing I can do to help you this week?
alts.zh: 尤其是第一次跟新的工程團隊碰面時，真的去問他們：這禮拜我可以幫上哪一件事？

alts.quote: And don't ask them, "Should I do it?" Ask them, "Tell me for each thing, can you give me the pros and cons of doing it?"
alts.zh: 不要問他們「我該不該做？」要問他們「每一個做法的利弊分別是什麼？」

alts.quote: Because I asked them to ask a golden question, if you were in my shoes, how would you approach this? I call that the golden question. It's such a creative question.
alts.zh: 我請他們問一個「黃金問題」：如果你是我，你會怎麼處理？我把它叫做黃金問題，這問題非常有創造性。

cards.quote: And again, these are all conjectures, which I can't prove in any way, but it's a thought experiment to talk about these things.
cards.zh: 再說一次，這些都只是我的推測，我完全沒辦法證明，但當成思想實驗來聊是有意思的。
cards.why: 先幫自己的整段論述標上「推測」標籤，再用 thought experiment 把它從「主張」降級成「一起玩的東西」。這樣講完後即使被推翻，你也沒有輸——因為你從沒宣稱它是真的。
swaps: Strictly a hypothesis — I can't back this with data
Treat this as a thought experiment, not a claim
cards.pmNote: 把假設明確標為假設，是團隊敢挑戰你的前提。
cards.episode: Kunal Shah on winning in India, second-order thinking, the philosophy of startups, and more

alts.quote: I don't know if I want to highlight any specific categories, but I can talk about some of the things that we've funded in the past that has real legs.
alts.zh: 我不確定我想特別點名哪些類別，但我可以聊聊我們過去投過、確實有搞頭的一些東西。

alts.quote: I don't know how many customer support folks we have, but it's not very many, 30, 40, I'm not sure, way smaller than you would have at any comparable company, and it's because we've automated a lot of our flows.
alts.zh: 我不知道我們有多少客服人力，但沒有很多，三十、四十吧，我不確定，總之比任何同等規模的公司都少很多，因為我們把很多流程自動化了。

alts.quote: I mean, I think Things probably, I'm just guessing, I don't know any of the numbers or whatever, but I would assume it makes between five and $25 million of revenue, which to a VC is not even worth considering a VC.
alts.zh: 我是說，Things 這款——我純粹在猜，數字我完全不知道——但我猜它一年營收大概在五百萬到兩千五百萬美金之間，這種規模對創投來說根本不值得看。

cards.pattern: I hate the word "[某個詞]" because [理由]. So I stay away from "[那個詞]", but [你真正的回答]
cards.quote: I often tell people that I hate the word 'favorite' because it tells me to become limited in my mind. So I stay away from 'favorite', but I learn all the time from everybody.
cards.zh: 我常跟人說我討厭「最喜歡的」這個詞，因為它會逼我的腦袋變窄。所以我不用這個詞，但我隨時都在跟每個人學東西。
cards.why: 不回答問題、但也不逃避：先拒絕題目裡的那個詞（並給理由），再用自己的框架回答。這是被問到不想回答的問題時，母語者最優雅的一招——換題目，不換態度。
swaps: I'd push back on the word 'best' here — what I'd say instead is…
I try not to think in terms of favorites, but here's what I keep coming back to
cards.pmNote: 被問到框架本身有問題的問題時，先重構問題再作答。
cards.episode: Kunal Shah on winning in India, second-order thinking, the philosophy of startups, and more

alts.quote: And I still think it is still cheaper than sending everybody to trainings and conferences all the time, and it has a lot of, yeah, ripple effects and network effects.
alts.zh: 而且我還是覺得，這比一天到晚把所有人送去上課、跑研討會便宜，而且它還有很多連鎖效應和網絡效應。

alts.quote: Yeah, I think that's an important question, and it's a question I hear a lot because we all know a bullshitter.
alts.zh: 我覺得那是一個重要的問題，而且我常常被問到——因為我們每個人都認識一個唬爛的人。

alts.quote: The theory is that if you perfect yourself and somehow rays come out of your head and people will follow you, because you're so magnetic, and you're so perfect.
alts.zh: 那套理論是說：只要你把自己修煉到完美，頭上就會發出光芒，大家自然會跟隨你，因為你太有魅力、太完美了。

cards.pattern: It's a day long [主題] on its own. So some other time.
cards.quote: It's a day long podcast on its own. So some other time.
cards.zh: 那個講一整天都講不完，改天再說吧。
cards.why: 把離題的支線先讚美（值得講一整天），再乾脆地推遲（some other time）。11 個字就把會議拉回正軌，而且對方不會覺得他的話題被否定。台灣人通常是硬聽完，或直接打斷。
swaps: That's a whole meeting on its own — let's park it
Big topic. Let's take that offline.
cards.pmNote: 會議設計的基本功：離題的東西要「放進停車場」而不是砍掉。
cards.episode: Kunal Shah on winning in India, second-order thinking, the philosophy of startups, and more

alts.quote: Maybe that's another podcast for another day, but I fundamentally believe in when products take on some kind of persona.
alts.zh: 這可能要另開一集才講得完，但我真的相信產品應該要有某種人格。

alts.quote: But I think it's really important for it to be a time capped group conversation. And if you give a team 30 days, they'll take 30 days. If you give them six months, they'll take six months.
alts.zh: 我覺得這一定要是一場有時間上限的團體討論。你給團隊 30 天，他們就會用滿 30 天；你給六個月，他們就會用滿六個月。

alts.quote: Now that you've agreed among yourselves that you're going to do that for a fixed period of time, everyone go around the room and say, "If I could start this company over again the thing I wish we were doing was."
alts.zh: 既然大家已經同意用一段固定的時間來試，那就一個一個講：「如果能重來一次，我希望我們在做的是＿＿＿。」

cards.pattern: [某個雜訊來源] is designed for [它的真實動機]. So I wouldn't read too much into it.
cards.quote: And Twitter is designed for outrage getting likes. So I wouldn't read too much into it.
cards.zh: Twitter 這個場子本來就是設計來讓憤怒獲得按讚的。所以我不會太當一回事。
cards.why: 先解釋雜訊的生成機制，再說「我不會太放在心上」——因為有了機制解釋，這句話就不是逃避批評，而是校準訊號。面對負評、酸言、非代表性回饋時最好用。
swaps: That channel selects for the loudest, not the typical — I'd weight it accordingly
I wouldn't over-index on that feedback
cards.pmNote: 回饋要先看來源的選擇偏誤，再決定要不要進 backlog。
cards.episode: Kunal Shah on winning in India, second-order thinking, the philosophy of startups, and more

alts.quote: On Twitter, you'll see people say, "Oh, it's the most expensive use of everyone's time," but it's like, "Yep. But there's 0% fidelity loss in that.
alts.zh: 推特上會有人說：「那是最貴的一種時間使用方式。」但我的回答是：「對啊。可是這樣資訊零失真。」

alts.quote: And I'd say it's not just that the budget's too small, it would be that they put all their eggs in one basket.
alts.zh: 我會說，問題不只是預算太小，而是他們把所有雞蛋放在同一個籃子裡。

alts.quote: But before that, I think getting to product-market fit, obviously there's a lot of methodology for doing it today that might make it a bit easier for people, but I still think it's fairly random and pretty dang hard.
alts.zh: 在那之前——我覺得要走到 PMF，現在當然有很多方法論可能讓大家輕鬆一點，但我還是認為它相當隨機，而且真的很難。

cards.pattern: I'm not saying that we should not [對方可能誤會的事] — that's very different.
cards.quote: I'm not saying that we should not take customer feedback, that's very different.
cards.zh: 我不是說不要聽客戶回饋——那是完全不同的兩件事。
cards.why: 講完一個激烈主張後，立刻把「可能被誤讀的版本」切掉。that's very different 是英文劃清界線最短的一句，比長篇補充有效得多。台灣人常等到被誤解之後才澄清，那時已經來不及。
swaps: To be clear, I'm not saying X — different thing entirely
Let me not be misheard: this isn't about X
cards.pmNote: 拋出強烈立場後，主動列出「這句話不包含什麼」，可省下大量後續解釋。
cards.episode: Kunal Shah on winning in India, second-order thinking, the philosophy of startups, and more

alts.quote: So I'm not saying they didn't get the exact monthly number wrong. I'm saying they got it wrong by many factors.
alts.zh: 我不是在說他們只是月份的確切數字抓錯。我是說他們錯了好幾個量級。

alts.quote: I read the email, I'm like, "What do you want me to do? Is this an FYI? Are you saying there's a problem? Do you want me to help?"
alts.zh: 我讀完信心想：「你到底要我做什麼？這是知會嗎？你是在說有問題嗎？還是你要我幫忙？」

alts.quote: So put another way, it defines what are the alternatives to what you do? How are you different?
alts.zh: 換個講法：它定義的是——你的替代方案有哪些？你跟它們差在哪？

cards.pattern: Somebody commenting about [你的事] who does not understand the nuance of it — you can't be reacting to everything.
cards.quote: let's say somebody commenting about your business, who does not understand the nuance of it, you can't be reacting to everything.
cards.zh: 假設有人在評論你的生意，但他根本不懂裡面的細節——你不可能每件事都去回應。
cards.why: 拒絕的理由放在「對方的資訊不足」而不是「你不重要」，語氣就不會刻薄。you can't be reacting to everything 用進行式表達一種持續消耗的狀態，比 I won't respond 更委婉也更真實。
swaps: We can't chase every piece of feedback
Not every comment deserves a response from us
cards.pmNote: 把回饋分成「懂脈絡的」與「不懂脈絡的」，只對前者投入回應成本。
cards.episode: Kunal Shah on winning in India, second-order thinking, the philosophy of startups, and more

alts.quote: If you really need us to put us on the shelf and drop everything for a million dollar deal, we're a startup, we'll do it. But understand, just, is this really really what you want?
alts.zh: 如果你真的要我們把手上的東西全放下、為了這筆一百萬的案子全部重來，我們是新創，我們會做。但你想清楚——這真的是你要的嗎？

alts.quote: And if with all of that it didn't work, then you can say, "Hey, we're not going to try this again because we literally did try everything that we could to test this hypothesis.
alts.zh: 如果做到那樣還是沒用，你就可以說：「我們不會再試一次了，因為我們真的已經把能測的都測過了。」

alts.quote: When I first started out in PM somebody, it's obviously a chestnut, but he pointed out that realistically when you're a product manager, your job is to say no to 90% of things that get brought your way.
alts.zh: 我剛入行做 PM 的時候，有人跟我說——雖然是老生常談——現實是，PM 的工作就是把送到你面前的事拒絕掉九成。

cards.quote: Sometimes I wonder if the challenges and the opportunities are exactly the same.
cards.zh: 我有時候會想，所謂的挑戰跟機會，會不會根本是同一件事。
cards.why: 被問「最大的挑戰是什麼」時，用一句話把二分法折起來，接下來的內容自動變得有洞見。Sometimes I wonder if… 又讓這個大膽命題保持在思考狀態，聽者容易跟著一起想。
swaps: I'm not sure those are two different lists
The risk and the opportunity might be the same thing here
cards.pmNote: 重新定義問題時，先檢查兩個相對的清單是不是同一份。
cards.episode: Kunal Shah on winning in India, second-order thinking, the philosophy of startups, and more

alts.quote: Same person, wrong question, wrong result.
alts.zh: 同一個人，問錯問題，得到錯的結論。

alts.quote: Finding a new manager is always an option, but I guess sometimes the real question is, is actually spending time to try to understand what is your manager optimizing?
alts.zh: 換一個主管永遠是個選項，但我想有時候真正的問題是：要不要花時間去搞懂你的主管到底在最佳化什麼？

alts.quote: Think about press the same way that you think about raising money, which is to say you do it when you know what the money is for, and you should do it when you know what the press is for.
alts.zh: 把「找媒體報導」想成「募資」：你會在知道這筆錢要幹嘛的時候才去募，那你也該在知道這次曝光要幹嘛的時候才去找。

cards.pattern: I have a strong view that [立場]. In fact, [更進一步的推論].
cards.quote: So I have a strong view that we will never, never have equality of wealth. In fact, chasing that is actually a bad idea.
cards.zh: 我有個很強的看法：我們永遠、永遠不會有財富平等。事實上，去追求那個本身就是個壞主意。
cards.why: I have a strong view that… 是英文宣告立場強度的標準頭銜（比 I think 重、比 I know 安全）；接著 In fact 不是舉證，而是把立場再推一級。先標強度、再加碼，是英文建立論點的常見節奏。
swaps: I hold this one strongly: …
I'd go further than that, actually
cards.pmNote: 表態時先講強度（strong view / loose hunch），聽者才知道要不要花力氣挑戰你。
cards.episode: Kunal Shah on winning in India, second-order thinking, the philosophy of startups, and more

alts.quote: The good news is, you're just like everybody else. The bad news is, you're mediocre just like everybody else.
alts.zh: 好消息是，你跟大家一樣；壞消息是，你跟大家一樣平庸。

alts.quote: I would argue that the more power you have, the more moral responsibility you have to actually pause and figure out what it is that you're doing.
alts.zh: 我會主張：你握有的權力越大，你就越有道德責任停下來，搞清楚自己在做什麼。

alts.quote: I've never seen a product plan get to the truth of what it could do, but it will help you make a better decision than if you just guess.
alts.zh: 我沒看過哪份產品計畫真的算準過它能做到什麼，但它還是會讓你的決定比純用猜的好。

cards.pattern: No, but the nuance that is important is [你要補的那一層]
cards.quote: No, but the nuance that is important is that you can actually increase the database size infinitely.
cards.zh: 不對，但這裡有個很重要的細節：那個資料庫的大小其實是可以無限擴張的。
cards.why: 英文裡直接的 No 很傷人，但後面接 but the nuance that is important is… 就會把反對重新包裝成「補一層你漏掉的細節」。對方保留了面子，你的修正也完整送達。
swaps: Close — the nuance I'd add is…
Almost, but there's a wrinkle that changes the conclusion
cards.pmNote: 修正別人的模型時，補細節比推翻整體更容易被接受。
cards.episode: Kunal Shah on winning in India, second-order thinking, the philosophy of startups, and more

alts.quote: I'm not saying that having a large market someday doesn't matter, of course it does eventually. But trying to be super pedantic about market size when it's a pre-seed company, it's just not something I'd put a lot of thought.
alts.zh: 我不是說市場總有一天要夠大這件事不重要，當然重要。但在一家 pre-seed 公司還在糾結市場規模算得多精確，我不會花太多心思在上面。

alts.quote: I actually say I disagree with Naval on this because often, when you're part of a large organization, it's really hard to do great work and get recognized for it.
alts.zh: 我其實在這件事上跟 Naval 意見不同，因為在大組織裡，你常常很難既做出好成果又被看見。

alts.quote: Right. Except the leaks automatically increase and that's what people don't appreciate.
alts.zh: 對——只是那個破洞會自己愈破愈大，這就是大家沒意識到的地方。

cards.pattern: And therefore [抽象概念] is like [日常事物]. It's like a [屬性] service.
cards.quote: And therefore envy is like wifi. It's like a hyperlocal service.
cards.zh: 所以說，嫉妒就像 wifi，是一種超在地的服務——只在很近的範圍內有訊號。
cards.why: 用一個大家每天都在用的東西當喻體，抽象概念立刻有形狀且可傳播。母語者說服人時很少堆形容詞，而是丟一個能被複述的比喻——因為聽眾轉述得出去，你的論點才會走遠。
swaps: Think of it like wifi — the signal only reaches so far
It behaves like a local network, not a broadcast
cards.pmNote: 策略敘事的可傳播性取決於比喻，不取決於資料量。
cards.episode: Kunal Shah on winning in India, second-order thinking, the philosophy of startups, and more

alts.quote: I often use this analogy of if you're doing a home renovation, you can have the most beautiful rendering of the new bedroom. But if you haven't checked if there's electricity in that wall there or not, it's going to drastically change the cost and the time and everything.
alts.zh: 我常用一個比喻：你在裝修房子，臥室的效果圖可以做得美到不行。但如果你沒去確認那面牆裡到底有沒有電線，成本跟時間都會整個變樣。

alts.quote: It's a statement of value, you would like to grow faster than you are. I'd like to be taller than I am. I'd like to have more hair.
alts.zh: 那是一句願望：你希望公司長得比現在快。我也希望自己長得比現在高。我也希望自己頭髮多一點。

alts.quote: So time becomes a convenient excuse for us where we say, 'Well, it's not me. It's just, I don't have time to work on it.'
alts.zh: 時間就變成一個很方便的藉口，我們會說：「不是我的問題，我只是沒時間做這件事。」

cards.quote: I ask myself and my key reportees every month, we go around the table and ask ourselves, "What are the hardest problems we solved last month?"
cards.zh: 我每個月都會跟直屬主管們繞著桌子問一輪：我們上個月解掉的最難的問題是什麼？
cards.why: 問題本身就是標準：不問「你做了什麼」（會得到一堆忙碌），而問「最難的是什麼」（逼出位移量）。教練式提問的核心不是引導，是換一個讓人無法用忙碌搪塞的量尺。
swaps: What's the hardest thing you unblocked this month?
What did you move that wouldn't have moved without you?
cards.pmNote: 資深者的產出應以「解掉的難題」計，不以工時或票數計。
cards.episode: Kunal Shah on winning in India, second-order thinking, the philosophy of startups, and more

alts.quote: You ask questions like, what's the hardest you've ever worked to get something done and why? And that does differentiate a lot of people, a lot of people don't actually have a great answer to that.
alts.zh: 你可以問這種問題：你這輩子為了完成某件事最拚的一次是什麼？為什麼？這題真的很能分辨人，很多人其實答不太出來。

alts.quote: One of the things to ask oneself is what draws me to this position in the first place?
alts.zh: 有個可以問自己的問題是：當初到底是什麼把我吸引到這個位置的？

alts.quote: I ask them, "What are your goals when it comes to coaching? Roll it forward six months, what have you gotten done in your coaching experience."
alts.zh: 我會問他們：「你找教練的目標是什麼？把時間快轉六個月，那時候你在教練這件事上完成了什麼？」

cards.pattern: You do a fabulous job of [具體的動作], and making it [具體的效果] for many of us
cards.quote: you do a fabulous job of taking the information asymmetry of the art of product and making it accessible to many of us across the world
cards.zh: 你把產品這門手藝裡的資訊落差拿出來，讓全世界很多人都能取得——這件事你做得非常出色。
cards.why: 稱讚時不用形容詞（you're amazing），而是描述對方做的那個「動作」與造成的「效果」。具體到能被複述的讚美才有份量，也才不會像客套。
swaps: What you do really well is taking X and making it usable for people like us
You've closed a gap that most people don't even notice exists
cards.pmNote: 公開肯定要指名具體行為與受益者，團隊才知道什麼行為值得複製。
cards.episode: Kunal Shah on winning in India, second-order thinking, the philosophy of startups, and more

alts.quote: Credit our CEO with this, that I shared the data with him and he basically told the product team, "We are putting a complete freeze on the product development roadmap."
alts.zh: 這件事要歸功給我們執行長：我把數據給他看，他就直接跟產品團隊說「產品路線圖全面凍結」。

alts.quote: And that means being very clear when people are not meeting expectations, making it very clear that questioning ideas is not questioning innate talent.
alts.zh: 這代表在別人沒達到期待時要講得很清楚，同時也要講清楚：質疑一個想法，不等於質疑一個人的天賦。

alts.quote: Joanne's really special. I got to just take a moment to give her a giant shout out. She is the only person that I've worked with that has as much technical depth as she does have product taste.
alts.zh: Joanne 真的很特別。我一定要停下來大聲說一下她有多厲害——她是我合作過唯一一個技術深度跟產品品味一樣強的人。

cards.pattern: Before you move on to the next one, I want to spend a little time on this one
cards.quote: Before you actually move on to the next one, I want to spend a little time on this one
cards.zh: 在你跳到下一點之前，我想在這一點上多待一下。
cards.why: 插話而不打斷：Before you move on 承認對方正在推進、也承認他有下一步，只請求延後。這是英文會議中最安全的切入點——比 Sorry to interrupt 更主動也更專業。
swaps: Can we stay on that one a beat longer?
Before we leave this point — one thing
cards.pmNote: 在英文會議建立存在感的關鍵是「切入的時機點」而不是講話總量。
cards.episode: Relentless curiosity, radical accountability, and HubSpot’s winning growth formula | Christopher Miller (VP of Product, Growth and AI)

alts.quote: I'm taking us off track, but I want to go a little deeper with this.
alts.zh: 我知道這樣會離題，但我想在這裡多挖一點。

alts.quote: And one core idea I don't think we've mentioned yet is that we strongly believe in people's intuition about how they should spend their time if they have the chance.
alts.zh: 還有一個核心想法我覺得我們還沒提到：我們非常相信一個人只要有機會，他自己知道時間該花在哪。

alts.quote: Can I actually jump in real quick because that's a really cool framework that I haven't heard before, this idea of fuel and engine from a marketing perspective.
alts.zh: 我可以插一下嗎？因為這個框架真的很酷，我以前沒聽過——就是行銷上「燃料 vs 引擎」這個想法。

cards.pattern: So I cut you off on this one. So let's keep going.
cards.quote: Okay. So, I cut you off in this one bullet point so far. So, let's keep going.
cards.zh: 好，我剛剛在這一點把你打斷了。我們繼續吧。
cards.why: 把話語權還回去的標準動作：先承認自己打斷（I cut you off），再明確交棒（let's keep going）。承認打斷這一步台灣人幾乎都省略，結果對方不確定要不要接回原本的主題。
swaps: Sorry, I derailed you — you were on point three
I jumped in there. Please carry on.
cards.pmNote: 主持會議時記得把被打斷的人送回原位，議程才不會斷線。
cards.episode: Relentless curiosity, radical accountability, and HubSpot’s winning growth formula | Christopher Miller (VP of Product, Growth and AI)

alts.quote: he'll sit in a review and be like, "I don't think this is right." And then he'll pause and say, "I'm going to clear the rest of my day. Let's sit and figure it out."
alts.zh: 他會在評審會上說：「我覺得這不對。」然後停一下說：「我把今天剩下的行程清掉，我們一起坐下來把它弄清楚。」

alts.quote: So let me take us back on track and let's talk about just the high level framework here.
alts.zh: 我們把話題拉回來，來談一下這個框架的高層次架構。

alts.quote: Now that you've agreed among yourselves that you're going to do that for a fixed period of time, everyone go around the room and say, "If I could start this company over again the thing I wish we were doing was."
alts.zh: 既然大家已經同意用一段固定的時間來試，那就一個一個講：「如果能重來一次，我希望我們在做的是＿＿＿。」

cards.quote: That's over my head, but I love it anyway.
cards.zh: 這超出我的理解範圍了，但我還是很喜歡。
cards.why: 承認聽不懂卻不掉價：over my head 是輕鬆的自嘲（不是 I don't understand 那種硬碰硬），加上 but I love it anyway 保住了對談的溫度。對非母語者來說，這比假裝跟得上安全太多。
swaps: That one went over my head — say more?
You lost me there, and I'm into it
cards.pmNote: 承認沒跟上，是把對方拉回共同語言的最快方式。
cards.episode: Kunal Shah on winning in India, second-order thinking, the philosophy of startups, and more

alts.quote: That's the problem. I mean, that is the trillion dollar question so I don't really have an answer. I have a couple thoughts on it.
alts.zh: 問題就在這。這是那種價值一兆美元的問題，所以我其實沒有答案，但我有幾點想法。

alts.quote: Okay, that's a difficult and different question.
alts.zh: 好，這是個困難、而且性質不太一樣的問題。

alts.quote: I don't think we should filter out AI content. I think we should let you know if content is AI content or not. That's hard, by the way.
alts.zh: 我不認為我們該把 AI 內容濾掉。我認為該做的是讓你知道這則內容是不是 AI 產的。順帶一提，這很難。

cards.quote: I want to zoom out a little bit before we go in a different direction.
cards.zh: 在我們轉去別的方向之前，我想先拉高一點來看。
cards.why: 轉場的雙動作句：zoom out（先升高視角收尾目前的主題）＋ before we go in a different direction（預告要換題）。聽者知道現在在哪、接下來去哪，會議節奏就不會亂。
swaps: Let me pull up a level before we switch topics
One big-picture question, then I'll move us on
cards.pmNote: 換題前先做一次拉高總結，是主持人維持議程感的基本動作。
cards.episode: Kunal Shah on winning in India, second-order thinking, the philosophy of startups, and more

alts.quote: I want to talk about public speaking skills, but just to close the loop on that.
alts.zh: 我想聊聊公開演講的技巧，不過在那之前先把剛剛那題收尾。

alts.quote: "I need 20 minutes of focused time to interrogate something that I've done. We're not going to talk. I'm literally going to force us into a room or Zoom.
alts.zh: 「我需要二十分鐘的專注時間來拷問我做的東西。我們不用講話。我就是要把大家關進一個會議室或 Zoom。」

alts.quote: Well, first a pairing, and then one more. The pairing is reset expectations and slow your inbox.
alts.zh: 好，先講一組配套的，再講一個。配套的是：重設期待，還有讓你的收件匣慢下來。

cards.pattern: If you were in my shoes, how would you approach [X]?
cards.quote: Because I asked them to ask a golden question, if you were in my shoes, how would you approach this? I call that the golden question. It's such a creative question.
cards.zh: 我請他們問一個「黃金問題」：如果你是我，你會怎麼處理？我把它叫做黃金問題，這問題非常有創造性。
cards.why: 把對方放進你的位置，他就不必評價你、也不必負責，只要「代入」就好——心理成本瞬間降到最低。台灣人請教常問「你覺得我這樣可以嗎？」逼對方當評審，對方反而不敢說真話。
swaps: If you were me, what would you do here?
How would you play this if you were in my position?
cards.pmNote: Phyl 把找工作當產品做：Mnookin 兩頁紙（要什麼／不要什麼）→ listening tour →收斂出 candidate market fit。
cards.episode: Land your dream job in today’s market: negotiation tactics, job search councils, and more | Phyl Terry (Author, “Never Search Alone”)

alts.quote: So especially when you're meeting with a new engineering team for the first time, actually ask them, what is one thing I can do to help you this week?
alts.zh: 尤其是第一次跟新的工程團隊碰面時，真的去問他們：這禮拜我可以幫上哪一件事？

alts.quote: I picked you because I really trust you to be a sound source of truthful advice and give me some feedback. So I really value that. Do you mind spending a couple of minutes and just giving me some thoughts on this?
alts.zh: 我會找你，是因為我真的很信任你會給我誠實的建議跟回饋，這對我很有價值。可以請你花個幾分鐘，給我一點想法嗎？

alts.quote: And don't ask them, "Should I do it?" Ask them, "Tell me for each thing, can you give me the pros and cons of doing it?"
alts.zh: 不要問他們「我該不該做？」要問他們「每一個做法的利弊分別是什麼？」

cards.pattern: What did I do well? What do you think my strengths are? Do you think I'm accurately projecting myself?
cards.quote: This is people you used to work with before, go ask them, "Hey, what did I do well, what do you think my strengths are? What do you think I'm a fit for?
cards.zh: 去問以前的同事：「我哪裡做得好？你覺得我的強項是什麼？我是這樣想的——你覺得我對自己的認知準確嗎？」
cards.why: 最後那句 Do you think I accurately am projecting myself? 是關鍵：不是問「我好不好」，而是問「我對自己的描述準不準」。把問題從價值判斷改成事實校準，對方就敢講真話了。
swaps: Does how I describe myself match how you actually experienced working with me?
Is there a gap between how I see myself and how you see me?
cards.pmNote: Phyl 稱這叫 reverse exit interview：離職面談通常公司問你，這次換你問前同事。
cards.episode: Land your dream job in today’s market: negotiation tactics, job search councils, and more | Phyl Terry (Author, “Never Search Alone”)

alts.quote: Hey, I'm an early stage startup. We have a lot to learn. Can we kind of gain your insight into how this problem is manifesting on your side?
alts.zh: 嗨，我們是很早期的新創，還有很多要學。能不能請教你，這個問題在你們那邊是怎麼呈現的？

alts.quote: Hey, I'm really enjoying working with you. I'm wondering is there some way I could help you that would also help me reach my goal?
alts.zh: 嘿，跟你合作我覺得很愉快。我在想，有沒有什麼事我可以幫你、同時也能幫我朝目標前進的？

alts.quote: I would really love to become a people manager someday. What do you suggest that I work on now so that I'll be ready when the opportunity comes up?
alts.zh: 我以後很想帶人。你建議我現在可以先練哪些東西，等機會來的時候我已經準備好了？

cards.pattern: I know you don't know me, but I would love your advice on [具體的事] and what you would do if you were in my shoes.
cards.quote: If they had reached out to me and said, "I know you don't know me. I have this small software company. I'm not well-connected, but I would love your advice on how to grow this business and what you would do if you were in my shoes,"
cards.zh: 如果他們寫信說：「我知道你不認識我。我有間小軟體公司，我人脈也不廣，但我很想聽聽你對怎麼把它做大的建議——如果你是我會怎麼做？」
cards.why: 冷開發信的完整結構：先主動承認關係為零（I know you don't know me），再給一句最小的背景，最後 ask 只要「建議」不要「資源」。台灣人寫冷信最常見的死法是直接跳到「可以幫我介紹某某人嗎」。
swaps: We haven't met, but I'd really value your perspective on...
This is out of the blue, but I'd love your take on...
cards.pmNote: Phyl 的判準：求「觀點」幾乎都會被接受，求「引薦」在關係建立前幾乎都會被忽略。
cards.episode: Land your dream job in today’s market: negotiation tactics, job search councils, and more | Phyl Terry (Author, “Never Search Alone”)

alts.quote: It might actually mean a proactive conversation with your manager or the leadership to say, "I love what I'm doing here, and I would also like to learn a little bit more. And here's what I'm interested in."
alts.zh: 這可能只是主動找主管或高層談一次，跟他說：「我很喜歡現在做的事，同時我也想再多學一些，這是我有興趣的方向。」

alts.quote: Hey, I'm an early stage startup. We have a lot to learn. Can we kind of gain your insight into how this problem is manifesting on your side?
alts.zh: 嗨，我們是很早期的新創，還有很多要學。能不能請教你，這個問題在你們那邊是怎麼呈現的？

alts.quote: Hey, I'm really enjoying working with you. I'm wondering is there some way I could help you that would also help me reach my goal?
alts.zh: 嘿，跟你合作我覺得很愉快。我在想，有沒有什麼事我可以幫你、同時也能幫我朝目標前進的？

cards.pattern: I have a favor to ask. Would you be willing to [具體的事]?
cards.quote: Whereas I should said, "Lenny, I have a favor to ask. Would you be willing to do this?" You just say yes or no.
cards.zh: 我應該直接說：「我有件事想拜託你，你願意幫這個忙嗎？」你回是或不是就好。
cards.why: hide the ask（把請求包裝成「這對你也有好處喔」）是英語職場很容易被識破的失禮。先自報「這是一個 favor」，等於預先給對方拒絕的權利，反而更容易被答應。
swaps: Quick favor to ask — feel free to say no.
This is purely a favor, no strings: would you be up for...?
cards.pmNote: 同理適用於 cold intro：沒先問就把兩個人湊在一起，通常是幫了 A、卻在跟 B 收人情。
cards.episode: Land your dream job in today’s market: negotiation tactics, job search councils, and more | Phyl Terry (Author, “Never Search Alone”)

alts.quote: So especially when you're meeting with a new engineering team for the first time, actually ask them, what is one thing I can do to help you this week?
alts.zh: 尤其是第一次跟新的工程團隊碰面時，真的去問他們：這禮拜我可以幫上哪一件事？

alts.quote: Say, "Hey, let's have a workshop first. I have this problem. I think that you can help me fix it."
alts.zh: 你就說：「嘿，我們先辦一場工作坊吧。我手上有這個問題，我覺得你可以幫我解。」

alts.quote: So in your case, I said, "Here are nine topics. Can you pick your top two and tell me why you like them?"
alts.zh: 以你這次來說，我就是問：「這裡有九個主題，可以請你挑出你最喜歡的兩個，然後告訴我為什麼嗎？」

cards.pattern: Is it just me, or is [X]?
cards.quote: And he says, first question he has is, "Is this meeting, is it just me or is this meeting intense?"
cards.zh: 他說，他問的第一個問題是：「這個會議……是只有我這樣覺得，還是它真的很緊繃？」
cards.why: Is it just me, or...? 是英語職場最好用的一句社交校準：既承認了自己的困惑，又把它降級成「可能只是我」，對方不但不會看輕你，還多半會鬆一口氣說「我也是」。非母語者在陌生會議上最需要這一句。
swaps: Am I the only one finding this hard to follow?
Is this normally this fast, or am I just new?
cards.pmNote: Bradley Horowitz 就是用這句跟當時同為 director 的 Sundar Pichai 建立信任，後來一路做到 VP of Product。
cards.episode: Land your dream job in today’s market: negotiation tactics, job search councils, and more | Phyl Terry (Author, “Never Search Alone”)

alts.quote: That's the problem. I mean, that is the trillion dollar question so I don't really have an answer. I have a couple thoughts on it.
alts.zh: 問題就在這。這是那種價值一兆美元的問題，所以我其實沒有答案，但我有幾點想法。

alts.quote: And this may not be a direct answer to the question, but it didn't really necessarily come from Mark.
alts.zh: 這可能不算直接回答你的問題，不過這件事其實不見得是 Mark 起頭的。

alts.quote: Okay, that's a difficult and different question.
alts.zh: 好，這是個困難、而且性質不太一樣的問題。

cards.pattern: You strike me as [正面評價]. Why [看似矛盾的事實]?
cards.quote: "I haven't been here very long, but you, Sundar, you strike me as a really thoughtful person and great leader. Why is your remit just working on a toolbar for Marissa?" Whoa.
cards.zh: 「我來這裡沒多久，但 Sundar，我覺得你是個非常有想法的人、很好的領導者。那為什麼你負責的範圍只是一個工具列？」
cards.why: you strike me as X 是「我的主觀印象」而非「事實斷言」，所以後面接一個尖銳問題也不會變成冒犯。前面再加 I haven't been here very long 當免責聲明，把可能的無禮預先報備掉。
swaps: You come across as someone who...
My read on you is that..., so I'm curious why...
cards.pmNote: 問前先確認關係存量：同一句話對信任你的人是好奇，對不熟的人是侮辱。
cards.episode: Land your dream job in today’s market: negotiation tactics, job search councils, and more | Phyl Terry (Author, “Never Search Alone”)

alts.quote: Hey, I'm really enjoying working with you. I'm wondering is there some way I could help you that would also help me reach my goal?
alts.zh: 嘿，跟你合作我覺得很愉快。我在想，有沒有什麼事我可以幫你、同時也能幫我朝目標前進的？

alts.quote: So first of all, when you're in the early innings, you'll actually get more useful advice often from your peers because they're going through the same thing.
alts.zh: 首先，在很前期的階段，你從同輩那裡拿到的建議其實比較有用，因為他們正在經歷一模一樣的事。

alts.quote: Hey, I'm an early stage startup. We have a lot to learn. Can we kind of gain your insight into how this problem is manifesting on your side?
alts.zh: 嗨，我們是很早期的新創，還有很多要學。能不能請教你，這個問題在你們那邊是怎麼呈現的？

cards.pattern: You have not earned that yet. That's not a statement about your worth. It's just [事實].
cards.quote: I'm like, "You have not earned that yet. That's not a statement about your worth. It's just you're not ready for that conversation."
cards.zh: 我會說：「這個你還沒掙到。這不是在評斷你的價值，只是你還沒到可以進行那場對話的階段。」
cards.why: 拒絕的同時明講「這不是在評價你這個人」，把 rejection 從人格層拉回事實層。That's not a statement about your worth 這句是整段的緩衝墊，沒有它，前一句就是羞辱。
swaps: That's not a judgment on you — it's just timing.
Nothing to do with your ability; the relationship just isn't there yet.
cards.pmNote: 擋需求也適用：把「不做」歸因於順位與時機，而不是提案人的能力。
cards.episode: Land your dream job in today’s market: negotiation tactics, job search councils, and more | Phyl Terry (Author, “Never Search Alone”)

alts.quote: If none of those companies are using it, I'm like, "Don't bother me. It's either snake oil or it's not proven yet."
alts.zh: 如果那些公司一家都沒在用，那我的反應就是：別來煩我，這東西不是江湖偏方，就是還沒被驗證。

alts.quote: For what it's worth, we're not really motivated to try to create a self-improvement empire. This is not our full-time job. We just hope it works for you and is useful.
alts.zh: 順帶一提，我們並不是想搞一個自我成長帝國。這不是我們的正職。我們只是希望這對你有用。

alts.quote: And so even though I really like a lot about this, I'm going to say no." And I often think that founders think that there's some secret truth that's being held from them on why someone says no or they want more feedback.
alts.zh: 「就算我真的很喜歡這個東西的很多地方，我還是要說不。」我也常覺得，創辦人以為別人說不的背後藏著什麼沒告訴他的秘密，或想再要更多回饋。

cards.pattern: I acknowledge that that's a reaction some people have. That's totally valid. [然後才反駁]
cards.quote: I acknowledge that that's a reaction that some people have. That's totally valid. This is unusual, what we're doing here.
cards.zh: 我承認有些人確實會有這種反應，這完全合理。我們在做的事本來就不太尋常。
cards.why: 先幫反對者把反對意見說出來、蓋章認證「合理」，對方的防衛就卸掉一半。最狠的是第三句主動承認自己的方案很怪——搶在對方之前講缺點，反而增加可信度。
swaps: That's a fair reaction, and honestly a common one.
I'd probably feel the same way in your position.
cards.pmNote: pre-mortem 的口語版：把最可能的反對先講完，會議剩下的時間才有機會談實質。
cards.episode: Land your dream job in today’s market: negotiation tactics, job search councils, and more | Phyl Terry (Author, “Never Search Alone”)

alts.quote: But before that, I think getting to product-market fit, obviously there's a lot of methodology for doing it today that might make it a bit easier for people, but I still think it's fairly random and pretty dang hard.
alts.zh: 在那之前——我覺得要走到 PMF，現在當然有很多方法論可能讓大家輕鬆一點，但我還是認為它相當隨機，而且真的很難。

alts.quote: It's like these things that seem so common sense are actually hard with what they're doing… a lot of the advice is common sense. That doesn't mean it's easy to put in motion.
alts.zh: 這些看起來根本是常識的東西，真的做起來很難……很多建議都是常識，但常識不代表容易落地。

alts.quote: Yes, there are nuances. But for the most part, you get from most... Zero to 10, you can get to step eight by just doing the best practices.
alts.zh: 對，是有很多細節。但大多數情況下，從 0 到 10，你光靠基本功就能走到第 8。

cards.pattern: Every bone in your body is going to want to [直覺反應]. Just know that's what everyone feels.
cards.quote: That's why you need your job search council. This is when you really need to ask for help because every bone in your body is going to say, "I'm not going to negotiate. That's going to make it worse," and it almost never does.
cards.zh: 這就是為什麼你需要求職小組。你全身上下每根骨頭都會喊：「我不要談判，談了只會更糟。」但幾乎從來不會更糟。
cards.why: every bone in your body 這個誇張慣用語，把「我知道你會抗拒」講得有畫面又不說教。先描述對方的內心戲，再用資料打臉——比直接說「你錯了」有效太多。
swaps: Everything in you is going to want to...
Your gut is going to scream at you to...
cards.pmNote: Phyl 的數據：長期來看，開口要更高薪水有 87% 的機率會拿到（市場差時較低，但仍值得問）。
cards.episode: Land your dream job in today’s market: negotiation tactics, job search councils, and more | Phyl Terry (Author, “Never Search Alone”)

alts.quote: I will say if you're like, the hardest problem I have is that I need to build a new unicorn business, obviously that's not going to work. Not yet.
alts.zh: 當然啦，如果你說「我最難的問題是要生出一家獨角獸」，那顯然行不通。目前還不行。

alts.quote: You have to really understand why someone uses your product, because not every great thing is going to be invented by you.
alts.zh: 你得真的搞懂別人為什麼用你的產品，因為不是每一個好東西都會由你發明出來。

alts.quote: This is baby talk, but CEO after CEO will stand up and say, 'Well, we're going to grow and we're going to make a profit.'
alts.zh: 這根本是幼稚園程度，但一個又一個執行長還是會站上台說：「我們要成長，我們也要賺錢。」

cards.pattern: Can I share one story about [主題]?
cards.quote: Can I share one story about candidate market fit-
cards.zh: 我可以分享一個關於「候選人市場適配」的故事嗎？
cards.why: 插話的最短完整結構：請求許可＋預告內容＋限定份量（one story）。加了 one 之後對方知道你只會佔用一小段時間，答應的成本就低了。母語者在會議上搶麥克風幾乎都用這種包裝。
swaps: Can I jump in with a quick example?
Mind if I add one data point here?
cards.pmNote: 會議上的存在感不是講得多，而是每次開口都先讓人知道你要花掉多少時間、換來什麼。
cards.episode: Land your dream job in today’s market: negotiation tactics, job search councils, and more | Phyl Terry (Author, “Never Search Alone”)

alts.quote: That's an awesome story, just to comment in that real quick.
alts.zh: 那故事太棒了，我快速針對它講一句。

alts.quote: I'm taking us off track, but I want to go a little deeper with this.
alts.zh: 我知道這樣會離題，但我想在這裡多挖一點。

alts.quote: So let's just pause, Lenny.
alts.zh: 我們先暫停一下。

cards.quote: If we go up to the 30,000-foot level, what are we doing here? What's our mission? We're building a private safety net for all those who've been laid off or let go.
cards.zh: 如果拉到三萬英尺的高度看，我們到底在做什麼？我們的使命是什麼？我們在為所有被裁員的人建一張民間的安全網。
cards.why: go up to the 30,000-foot level 是英語職場最常用的「切換視角」訊號詞，宣告接下來要離開細節。後面接自問自答（what are we doing here? what's our mission?）製造節奏，讓聽眾準備好接一句大的。
swaps: Let's zoom out for a second.
If we pull all the way back, the question is...
cards.pmNote: 細節會議陷入僵局時，先拉到 30,000 呎重述目標，往往比繼續辯細節快。
cards.episode: Land your dream job in today’s market: negotiation tactics, job search councils, and more | Phyl Terry (Author, “Never Search Alone”)

alts.quote: And just saying because dramatically boosted the percentage of the time that a person would let them cut the line. We're suckers for explanations, all of us.
alts.zh: 光是講出「因為」，別人讓他插隊的比例就大幅上升。我們每個人都吃「解釋」這一套。

alts.quote: But human beings are notoriously good at trading off the long run just to feel good in the short run. That's why we're all eating chocolate and cupcakes and stuff that we know is bad for us because it feels good.
alts.zh: 人類非常擅長犧牲長期，只為了短期舒服。所以我們才都在吃明知不好的巧克力跟杯子蛋糕。

alts.quote: And getting to $1,000,000 of GMV in a constrained market is a lot harder, takes longer, but it's actually the path to building something that endures.
alts.zh: 在一個受限的市場裡做到一百萬 GMV 難很多、也慢很多，但那才是真正做出能長久的東西的路。

cards.quote: And it will still be hard. It will still be hard. I wish that weren't true, Lenny.
cards.zh: 而且還是會很辛苦。真的還是會很辛苦。我也希望不是這樣。
cards.why: I wish that weren't true 是一句成本極低、效果極高的同理：你沒有假裝能解決，但你站在對方那一邊。虛擬語氣（weren't）在這裡是必須的，用 isn't 就變成單純陳述、失去情感。
swaps: I wish I had better news.
I hate that this is the answer, but it is the answer.
cards.pmNote: 報延期／砍功能時，講一句 I wish that weren't true 比多解釋三分鐘理由更有效。
cards.episode: Land your dream job in today’s market: negotiation tactics, job search councils, and more | Phyl Terry (Author, “Never Search Alone”)

alts.quote: It's so hard to give a founder hard feedback. Who wants to be the bearer of bad news?
alts.zh: 要給創辦人難聽的回饋真的很難。誰想當那個報壞消息的人？

alts.quote: And the good news bad news is that's true. That is absolutely true.
alts.zh: 好消息也是壞消息：那是真的。千真萬確。

alts.quote: Nobody wants to hear it. Everybody wants to just think about these really cool models and how smart they are. But really it's just the hard work of getting really good data to the LLMs.
alts.zh: 沒有人想聽這個。大家都只想談那些很酷的模型有多聰明。但說到底，這就是把好資料餵給 LLM 的苦工。

cards.quote: And I want you to say, "This is great. I want to talk about money, but before we do, I want to think about some of the things that will set me up to see succeed in this role.
cards.zh: 我要你這樣說：「這很好。我想談薪水，但在那之前，我想先談談有哪些東西能讓我在這個角色上成功。」
cards.why: 談判的順序設計：先確認雙方都想要「你成功」，再談錢。set me up to succeed 這個片語把所有要求（預算、人力、訓練）都包裝成公司的利益，不是你的索取。這是整集最值錢的一句。
swaps: Before we land on numbers, can we talk about what I'd need to deliver on this?
I'd love to align on what success requires first, then comp.
cards.pmNote: Phyl 的四腳談判：預算、人力、訓練、決策權——全部綁回已經談定的 job mission OKRs。
cards.episode: Land your dream job in today’s market: negotiation tactics, job search councils, and more | Phyl Terry (Author, “Never Search Alone”)

alts.quote: What do you think about us doing an experiment? For the next quarter or two, why don't you let us try running like this? If it goes well, great; if it doesn't, no harm.
alts.zh: 我們來做個實驗你覺得如何？接下來一兩季，讓我們試著用這種方式跑跑看。順利的話很好，不順利也沒損失，我們就退回原本的做法。

alts.quote: We always keep this kind of mentality internal is that we're still a young company, we want to grow and you can feel free to talk to anyone.
alts.zh: 我們內部一直維持這種心態：我們還是家年輕公司、我們想長大，所以你要找誰談都可以。

alts.quote: It might be easier if I just go, I might be able to save you some time and some energy if I just joined you.
alts.zh: 也許我直接去比較快，我一起進去的話，說不定可以幫你省下一些時間跟力氣。

cards.pattern: Are you open to [數字]? That was really what I was hoping for. Is that something we can talk about?
cards.quote: Lenny, you can say, "Hey, are you open to 450? That was really what I was hoping for.
cards.zh: 你可以說：「你們可以接受 450 嗎？這其實是我原本期待的數字。這件事我們可以談嗎？」
cards.why: Are you open to X? 把要求改寫成一個「是非題」，對方回 no 也不傷關係。再加 Is that something we can talk about? 等於連被拒絕之後的下一步都先鋪好。這是全英語談判裡風險最低的開價句。
swaps: Is there any flexibility on the base?
Would you be open to revisiting the number?
cards.pmNote: 盡量跟 hiring manager 談而不是 recruiter——hiring manager 通常沒有明確預算上限，也更願意替你去爭取。
cards.episode: Land your dream job in today’s market: negotiation tactics, job search councils, and more | Phyl Terry (Author, “Never Search Alone”)

alts.quote: What would it take, Lenny? How can we get going on Riverside? What would it take?
alts.zh: 那要怎樣才成呢，Lenny？我們要怎麼把 Riverside 這件事推動起來？要什麼條件你才點頭？

alts.quote: And then I propose a little contingency plan, like hey, if that doesn't work out, here's the rollback plan, here's the maximum impact it will have done in a negative way, which is not going to be too much.
alts.zh: 然後我會提一個小小的備案：如果沒成，這是回滾計畫，這是最壞情況下的負面影響——而且不會太大。

alts.quote: I say to the person, “Let’s come up with an arbitrary deadline!” We both know it’s made up, but there’s a weird gravitational pull once you’ve put a date out there.
alts.zh: 我會跟對方說：「我們來訂一個隨便的死線吧！」我們都知道那是編的，但日期一旦放上去，就會有一種奇怪的引力。

cards.pattern: Don't hear this as [誤解]. We're trying to figure out [真正目的].
cards.quote: Now, again, don't hear this as antagonistic. We're not antagonistic here. We're trying to say, "What's going to help me succeed?"
cards.zh: 再說一次，不要把這聽成對立。我們不是在對抗。我們是在問：什麼能幫我把這件事做成？
cards.why: Don't hear this as X 是預先攔截誤解的專用句型——不是解釋你講了什麼，是規定對方該怎麼接收。在跨文化溝通裡特別有用，因為你無法確定對方會不會把直接當成冒犯。
swaps: I don't want this to land as pushback.
Read this as curiosity, not criticism.
cards.pmNote: 談判姿態決定結果：同樣的要求，用 collaborative 框架講，公司通常會加碼而不是縮手。
cards.episode: Land your dream job in today’s market: negotiation tactics, job search councils, and more | Phyl Terry (Author, “Never Search Alone”)

alts.quote: And now, it's not like, "Okay, now, we're screwed and the project is going to be bigger." Now, we can have a really cool conversation about trade-offs.
alts.zh: 所以現在不是「完了，這專案要爆了」。現在我們可以來一場很棒的取捨對話。

alts.quote: Is the juice worth the squeeze? And now I would say that it's pretty clear that the juice is worth the squeeze.
alts.zh: 這個果汁值得你這樣擠嗎？以現在來看，我會說很明顯是值得的。

alts.quote: What's the hill that I'm going to die on and is this something that I can shift or is this something that is not worth shifting?
alts.zh: 哪座山是我願意死守的？這件事我推得動嗎？還是根本不值得去推？

cards.pattern: I've thought about what [X] is. I want to make sure I'm understanding it correctly. Can I share something with you?
cards.quote: I want you to pull the hiring manager aside and say, "Hey, Lenny, you're the hiring manager. I've thought about what the role is. I want to make sure I'm understanding it correctly.
cards.zh: 我要你把用人主管拉到一旁說：「我想過這個職位到底是什麼，我想確認我理解得對不對。我可以跟你分享一下嗎？」
cards.why: 把「我幫你重寫了職位描述」這種可能顯得自大的動作，包裝成「我想確認我理解對不對」。三段式：宣告我做了功課→降級成求證→請求許可。整個攻擊性歸零，但東西照樣送到對方桌上。
swaps: I put some thinking down on this — can I walk you through it and you tell me where I'm off?
I drafted my understanding of the role. Mind sanity-checking it?
cards.pmNote: Phyl 的 job mission with OKRs：面試中期私下給用人主管看你自訂的職責與成果指標，是他書裡拿到 offer 最有效的單一戰術。
cards.episode: Land your dream job in today’s market: negotiation tactics, job search councils, and more | Phyl Terry (Author, “Never Search Alone”)

alts.quote: If you are bored one day and you're not sure what to measure, just make a user having a bad day chart, emit a log line and count it as a bar chart.
alts.zh: 哪天你閒著、又不知道該量什麼，就做一張「使用者今天很衰」的圖表——打一行 log，堆成長條圖就好。

alts.quote: So for positioning work, I'm going to say something that is contentious, but I don't think it is at all.
alts.zh: 講到定位這件事，我要說一句大家可能覺得很有爭議的話——但我完全不覺得有爭議。

alts.quote: Now, I'm biased when I'm going to say this, so take this with a pinch of salt, but I think the Accordion Method might be one of the things I'm the most proud of in my entire life.
alts.zh: 我要講的這件事我是有偏見的，所以你打個折聽——但我覺得手風琴法可能是我這輩子最引以為傲的東西之一。

cards.pattern: Once upon a time [現狀]. And then one day [轉折]. And because of that [連鎖]. And finally [留給世界的東西].
cards.quote: And because of that and because of that... And I usually like to end it with, and finally, this was the last thing you left the world with.
cards.zh: 「很久以前……然後有一天……因為這樣、又因為這樣……最後，這就是你留給世界的東西。」
cards.why: 把童話的骨架直接搬進商業簡報。because of that 的重複是引擎，逼你把因果一節一節扣起來，不能跳步。台灣人做願景常直接跳到結論畫面，中間的因果鏈缺了，聽眾就不會相信。
swaps: Today...; then...; which means...; and ultimately...
Here's where we are. Here's what changes. Here's what that unlocks.
cards.pmNote: Ebi 的三種願景載體：Mad Libs 故事、未來的 TechCrunch 標題、App Store 截圖草稿——都比 PRD 快。
cards.episode: Crafting a compelling product vision | Ebi Atawodi (YouTube, Netflix, Uber)

alts.quote: An RFP is a great example of overfitting in the world of procurement because it tells you nothing about the quality of software behind it.
alts.zh: RFP 就是採購世界裡「過度擬合」的最佳例子，因為它完全講不出背後那套軟體的品質好不好。

alts.quote: Yeah, so follow me on the detour to science world temporarily. If we all remember high school science classes, there was this concept of potential and kinetic energy.
alts.zh: 先跟我繞去科學世界一下。如果大家還記得高中物理，有個概念叫位能跟動能。

alts.quote: There's this thing from consumer advertising, which is you throw a consumer one egg, they can probably catch it. You throw them four or five eggs, they're probably going to drop all of them.
alts.zh: 廣告圈有個說法：你丟一顆蛋給消費者，他大概接得住；你一次丟四五顆，他大概會全部摔在地上。

cards.pattern: Here's the problem statement. How might we [解決]? And here's what we think it looks like when we ship it.
cards.quote: And that's the thing they used to say, "Hey, leadership, this is the problem statement. Here's what we think how might we solve this big problem and here's what we think it looks like when we ship it." That's a mini-vision.
cards.zh: 「各位主管，這是問題陳述。我們認為可以怎麼解這個大問題，還有我們認為做出來會長什麼樣。」這就是一個小型願景。
cards.why: how might we 是設計思考留下的最好用句型：might 保留了「還沒定案」的空間，we 把提問者也綁進解法裡，所以不會變成質問。三段（問題→怎麼解→長什麼樣）是向上報告的最小完整單位。
swaps: The problem is X. How might we...? And here's the rough shape of the answer.
Problem, hypothesis, and what shipped looks like.
cards.pmNote: Lenny 稱之為 fertile question：好的問題會長出討論，壞的問題只會長出沉默。
cards.episode: Crafting a compelling product vision | Ebi Atawodi (YouTube, Netflix, Uber)

alts.quote: And so I think a lot of it comes down to not the things you try, but how you deeply understand the problem that's preventing someone from using your product effectively.
alts.zh: 所以我覺得關鍵不在你試了哪些招，而在你有多深地搞懂「是什麼擋住使用者用好你的產品」。

alts.quote: So there's, I wouldn't say a checklist, but there's a series of questions that I asked to diagnose why is growth slowing in this order, because it's one of these things where the first one that's a problem, if you don't fix that, it doesn't matter if you fix one of the ones below.
alts.zh: 我不會說那是一張檢查清單，但我確實有一組問題，會照順序問下去診斷成長為什麼變慢——因為只要最前面那個沒修，後面修再多都沒用。

alts.quote: The way I think about this is that emotions are like a tube, let's say, and there's water moving through the tube.
alts.zh: 我自己是這樣想這件事的：情緒像一根管子，裡面有水在流。

cards.pattern: Do not use [藉口] as the excuse for why you don't [該做的事].
cards.quote: Do not use, I don't have a designer, to be the excuse for why you don't bring it to life.
cards.zh: 不要拿「我沒有設計師」當作你不把它具象化的藉口。
cards.why: 直接把對方預備好的藉口點名封殺。命令句＋Do not use X as the excuse 的結構很強硬，但因為它針對的是「藉口」不是「人」，在英語職場不會被當成人身攻擊。
swaps: "No resources" isn't a reason not to sketch it.
Let's not let tooling be the blocker here.
cards.pmNote: 低擬真度的手繪也有用——設計師看到醜的版本，反而更容易被激起來把它做好。
cards.episode: Crafting a compelling product vision | Ebi Atawodi (YouTube, Netflix, Uber)

alts.quote: I also think it would be easy to use all what I just said as an excuse not to eventually build a great product.
alts.zh: 我也覺得，我剛剛講的那些很容易被拿來當藉口，變成「反正最後也不用做出好產品」。

alts.quote: Now, don't get me wrong, I've built the experimentation platform at Lyft. I'm a guy who loves data and loves using it and looking at experiments.
alts.zh: 先別誤會我的意思——Lyft 的實驗平台就是我建的。我是個超愛用數據、愛看實驗的人。

alts.quote: So the idea is, basically, you write up a two-page plan for the project. You invite three or four smart folks who don't know anything about the project and their job is just to tear apart your plan.
alts.zh: 做法是：你先寫一份兩頁的專案計畫，然後找三四個完全不懂這個專案的聰明人來，他們的任務就是把你的計畫拆爛。

cards.pattern: We heard you, we parsed everything into these [N], and that's why we came to [結論].
cards.quote: It's like we heard you and then we parse them into these 10 and everybody agreed with these 10 and therefore that's why we came up with this solution.
cards.zh: 人最在意的是知道你有聽進去。「你這個願景是怎麼來的？」這種質疑就消失了——我們聽了大家的意見，收斂成這 10 條，而且大家都同意。
cards.why: 把「我聽了你的意見」變成可驗證的流程證據（你給了 10 條、被收進來、你也點頭過）。英語職場的 alignment 不是說服，是讓對方在最終結論裡找得到自己的指紋。
swaps: This came directly from what you all put in — here's the trace.
Everything on this list came from one of your teams.
cards.pmNote: 會前先收集每個利害關係人的「你該知道的 10 件事」，evangelize 階段的阻力會少一半。
cards.episode: Crafting a compelling product vision | Ebi Atawodi (YouTube, Netflix, Uber)

alts.quote: We can't just have the marketing department sit down and cook up new positioning and then heave it over the wall to everybody else. It's a team sport.
alts.zh: 不能讓行銷部門自己關起門想一套新定位，然後往牆外一丟就沒事了。這是團隊運動。

alts.quote: Or if the meeting is not under the context of buying it all, it's like, "We're working on something cool. We have a great vision. It aligns with what you're doing. Maybe there's a partnership here."
alts.zh: 或者那場會根本不是在談收購，而是：「我們在做一件很酷的事，我們有很好的願景，跟你們在做的方向對得上。也許這裡有合作的空間。」

alts.quote: Hey, you have your planning committee today. Here are the three questions I want you to go in and get answered at that committee.
alts.zh: 你今天有規劃委員會對吧？這是我希望你進去幫我問到答案的三個問題。

cards.pattern: I'm not trying to get you to 100% certainty. I'm just trying to get you on the ride.
cards.quote: And then once the team has kind of gotten to a place, I'm not trying to get anyone to a hundred percent certainty, I'm trying to get you just on the ride. They will come, right?
cards.zh: 團隊到了某個程度就好——我不是要每個人百分之百確定，我只是要你先上車。剩下的他們自己會跟上。
cards.why: 主動把「成功標準」講低。一旦你宣告不需要對方 100% 同意，對方的抵抗就沒有對象了。get you on the ride 這個比喻也很關鍵：上車是可逆的，簽字不是。
swaps: I don't need you convinced, I need you curious.
You don't have to buy it — just don't get off the bus yet.
cards.pmNote: 願景文件開「留言權限」而不是「檢視權限」：讓人留得下指紋，就留得住人。
cards.episode: Crafting a compelling product vision | Ebi Atawodi (YouTube, Netflix, Uber)

alts.quote: We can't just have the marketing department sit down and cook up new positioning and then heave it over the wall to everybody else. It's a team sport.
