alts.zh: 不能讓行銷部門自己關起門想一套新定位，然後往牆外一丟就沒事了。這是團隊運動。

alts.quote: You earn their trust by asking them to do two things. One, you're either going to teach me or I'm going to help you.
alts.zh: 取得信任的方法就是給對方兩個選項：要嘛你教我，要嘛我來幫你。

alts.quote: Hey, you have your planning committee today. Here are the three questions I want you to go in and get answered at that committee.
alts.zh: 你今天有規劃委員會對吧？這是我希望你進去幫我問到答案的三個問題。

cards.pattern: Go as big as possible. Let people tell you to pull back.
cards.quote: Go big. Let people tell you to pull back. Let your manager use lasso and pull you back.
cards.zh: 就是要大。讓別人來叫你收，讓你的主管拿套索把你拉回來。
cards.why: Let people tell you to pull back 是很反台灣直覺的一句：預設值不是自我審查，而是先過頭、等人喊停。對習慣先自我打折的人來說，這句話等於一張授權書。
swaps: Aim past the target and let someone dial it back.
Better to be reined in than to have pre-shrunk it yourself.
cards.pmNote: Ebi 第一次做願景練習時只是 L4 PM——職級不是做願景的門檻。
cards.episode: Crafting a compelling product vision | Ebi Atawodi (YouTube, Netflix, Uber)

alts.quote: And I think the thing that I love about a crazy big goal is that you feel completely inadequate before it.
alts.zh: 我最喜歡「瘋狂大目標」的一點，就是站在它面前你會覺得自己完全不夠格。

alts.quote: In deciding to turn Dropbox into this lab for distributed work, we're like, "Okay, when you open up your laptop in 2025, 2030, what do you see?"
alts.zh: 我們決定把 Dropbox 變成遠距工作的實驗室時，問的是：「二〇二五、二〇三〇年，你打開筆電的那一刻，看到的是什麼？」

alts.quote: This is kind of the first time that, you don't have to be technical to make production grade web, full-stack web and mobile apps.
alts.zh: 這大概是史上第一次，你不需要是工程背景，也能做出可上線等級的全端網頁和行動 App。

cards.pattern: Let's say we weren't in the room — which one does the team want to get behind?
cards.quote: I'm like, "Let's say we weren't in the room as the leadership team," which is the one the team wants to get behind. Then you'll sometimes see the team hasn't even done the work between themselves talking.
cards.zh: 我會問：「假設我們這些主管不在這個房間，你們團隊自己最想投哪一個？」有時候你會發現他們彼此之間根本還沒討論過。
cards.why: 把自己的權力暫時從房間裡拿掉，讓對方能講真話。這是資深主管必備的一句——因為只要你在場，多數答案都是說給你聽的。
swaps: Forget what you think I want to hear — what's your call?
If this were entirely your decision, which way?
cards.pmNote: 團隊丟 A/B 兩案給主管選，通常代表他們還沒做完自己的功課。
cards.episode: Crafting a compelling product vision | Ebi Atawodi (YouTube, Netflix, Uber)

alts.quote: I'm asking them, "What do you do for joy? Are you doing something every single day that's bringing you joy in your life?" And if they say no, I'm like, "That's a problem."
alts.zh: 我會問他們：「你都做什麼讓自己開心？你每天有沒有一件事是讓你有樂趣的？」如果回答沒有，我就會說：「那這是個問題。」

alts.quote: if the people that you most recently worked with were in a room and you weren't there, how would they talk about you?
alts.zh: 如果你最近一起共事的那些人聚在一個房間裡、而你不在場，他們會怎麼講你？

alts.quote: So which game do you want to play? Let's just start there.
alts.zh: 所以你想玩哪一種賽局？我們就從這裡開始。

cards.pattern: That's too easy — to come to me with A and B and have me do the work. Go figure out why you can't stand by A.
cards.quote: that's too easy to come to me and be like, "Oh, here's A and B. You do the work and tell me which you one to pick." No way.
cards.zh: 「這裡有 A 案和 B 案，你來想、你來選」——這太輕鬆了。不行。
cards.why: 退件的同時給出明確的下一步動作（go figure out why…）。英語職場的「打回去」如果只有 No way 會顯得暴躁，加上一個具體任務就變成教練。
swaps: Come back with a recommendation, not a menu.
I'll take the risk conversation, not the choice.
cards.pmNote: 有把握就給建議＋風險清單；沒把握就講清楚你卡在哪一個未知，不要把選擇題丟給主管。
cards.episode: Crafting a compelling product vision | Ebi Atawodi (YouTube, Netflix, Uber)

alts.quote: So yeah, I think the only way you build something that matters that's going to change the world is if you find a big idea you believe in and you say no to everything else.
alts.zh: 我覺得要做出真正有份量、能改變世界的東西，唯一的路就是找到一個你相信的大想法，然後對其他所有東西說不。

alts.quote: There's nothing easier than promising work later.
alts.zh: 沒有什麼比「答應以後再做」更容易的事了。

alts.quote: I always say to people don't come to me for management 101, I'm not the person to ask on how to run the most effective one-on-one with your people.
alts.zh: 我常跟人講：管理入門的東西不要來問我，怎麼把一對一開得最有效率，我不是那個該問的人。

cards.quote: I'm in too many conversations where I'm like, "Who is on the hook for this decision? Who cares if this decision is made?" It's not like six people with consensus. Who is the person?
cards.zh: 我參加過太多會議，我會問：「這個決定是誰扛？誰真的在乎它有沒有被做出來？」不是六個人共識，是哪一個人？
cards.why: on the hook for 是英語職場講「責任歸屬」最口語也最不傷人的說法（比 responsible for 更有「掛在那裡」的重量感）。連問兩個問題把「大家一起負責＝沒人負責」直接戳破。
swaps: Who's the DRI here?
Whose name goes next to this one?
cards.pmNote: informed captain：一個人做決定，但他有義務把所有 context 收齊。
cards.episode: Crafting a compelling product vision | Ebi Atawodi (YouTube, Netflix, Uber)

alts.quote: Sometimes I'm like, "Who's owning this?" And it's like people don't know. That's why I think it's very important to have a single-threaded owner.
alts.zh: 有時候我問「這件事誰在 own？」結果大家都不知道。這就是為什麼一定要有一個單一負責人。

alts.quote: Two people owning a goal is no one owning a goal. One person owns the goal, who is it?
alts.zh: 兩個人一起扛一個目標，等於沒人在扛。這個目標只能有一個人負責——是誰？

alts.quote: So, my feeling on deadlines is don't have too many of them, and when you do, it's a P0.
alts.zh: 我對死線的看法是：不要訂太多，但一旦訂了，那就是 P0。

cards.pattern: I don't believe in being [表淺的]. I believe in being [有深度的]. And that's a very different thing.
cards.quote: I do not believe in being liked. I believe in being loved, right? And that's a very, very different thing.
cards.zh: 我不追求被喜歡。我追求被愛。這是兩件非常、非常不一樣的事。
cards.why: I don't believe in X, I believe in Y 是英語裡宣告價值觀最有力的骨架：不解釋、不鋪陳，靠一組近義詞的對比製造張力。第三句 And that's a very different thing 是刻意留白，逼聽者自己去想差在哪。
swaps: I'm not optimizing for consensus, I'm optimizing for clarity.
It's not about being nice; it's about being useful.
cards.pmNote: Ebi 的定義：愛＝為了另一個人的成長而延伸自己。所以愛有時候長得像難聽的回饋。
cards.episode: Crafting a compelling product vision | Ebi Atawodi (YouTube, Netflix, Uber)

alts.quote: It's not often I use a product and I'm like, "This thing is 10 times better than anything that's come before it." It's one of those for me.
alts.zh: 我很少用到一個產品會覺得「這東西比之前所有的東西好上十倍」。這個對我來說就是其中之一。

alts.quote: You should like when a PR person pushes back on you and says, "You know what? I don't think that your story is right for that publication. Here's why." That's someone you should hire.
alts.zh: 當一個公關回你「老實說，我覺得你的故事不適合那家媒體，原因是這樣」，你應該要高興。這種人才值得聘。

alts.quote: Well, thank you for sharing the real talk. I think you made the right choice.
alts.zh: 謝謝你講了實話。我覺得你那個選擇是對的。

cards.pattern: When the feedback comes in raw, they know it's in their best interest — because I've shown enough times that I care.
cards.quote: So when the feedback is coming like raw, they know that it's in their best interest because I've shown them enough times that I genuinely care about the person behind the role.
cards.zh: 所以當回饋很生硬地丟過來，他們知道那是為他們好——因為我已經用夠多次證明，我在乎的是角色背後那個人。
cards.why: the person behind the role（角色背後的那個人）是一個很好用的說法，把「我關心你」講得具體而不油膩。整句也點出關鍵機制：坦率的額度是靠平時累積的，不是講的時候臨時借的。
swaps: I've earned the right to be blunt with them.
The candor works because the care came first.
cards.pmNote: radical candor 的前置條件是 care personally——只有 challenge 沒有 care，就只是刻薄。
cards.episode: Crafting a compelling product vision | Ebi Atawodi (YouTube, Netflix, Uber)

alts.quote: I care so much about you and I'm giving you this feedback because I want you to be successful and I want you to be able to reach the pinnacle of what I know you can accomplish.
alts.zh: 我非常在乎你，我給你這個回饋是因為我希望你成功、希望你能走到我知道你能到的高度。

alts.quote: Of course, I don't want to be cruel to the people who are putting their hearts into that work, because the Figma file is beautiful. It's just coming a little early.
alts.zh: 當然，我不想對那些真心投入的人太苛刻——那些 Figma 檔真的很漂亮。只是它來得太早了一點。

alts.quote: Look, I don't have time to sugarcoat any feedback, and frankly, the best people I've worked with are the people who come into one-on-ones with me and yell at me and tell me I'm messing up.
alts.zh: 老實說，我沒空把回饋包糖衣；而且說真的，我合作過最好的人，都是會在一對一裡對我吼、直接說我哪裡搞砸了的人。

cards.pattern: Maybe that's another conversation for another day, but [先給一句版本].
cards.quote: Maybe that's another podcast for another day, but I fundamentally believe in when products take on some kind of persona.
cards.zh: 這可能要另開一集才講得完，但我真的相信產品應該要有某種人格。
cards.why: 把離題的東西「掛起來」而不是丟掉：先宣告這裡不展開，再給一句最短版本。這讓你既守住了會議節奏，又沒有把自己的洞見吞回去——台灣人多半直接吞回去。
swaps: That's a whole other thread — parking it for now.
Happy to go deeper offline; the short version is...
cards.pmNote: 會議上有價值的離題要放進 parking lot，不要當場辯完也不要當場消失。
cards.episode: Crafting a compelling product vision | Ebi Atawodi (YouTube, Netflix, Uber)

alts.quote: It's a day long podcast on its own. So some other time.
alts.zh: 那個講一整天都講不完，改天再說吧。

alts.quote: So let me take us back on track and let's talk about just the high level framework here.
alts.zh: 我們把話題拉回來，來談一下這個框架的高層次架構。

alts.quote: But I think it's really important for it to be a time capped group conversation. And if you give a team 30 days, they'll take 30 days. If you give them six months, they'll take six months.
alts.zh: 我覺得這一定要是一場有時間上限的團體討論。你給團隊 30 天，他們就會用滿 30 天；你給六個月，他們就會用滿六個月。

cards.pattern: I'm [非典型背景]. I don't have [別人有的資歷], I didn't [別人走的路]. And I'm here.
cards.quote: I just want to say, I'm this Nigerian girl. I don't have an MBA, I didn't work in consulting, and I'm here, right?
cards.zh: 我只想說：我就是個奈及利亞女生。我沒有 MBA，也沒做過顧問業，但我人就在這裡。
cards.why: 非典型背景者講自己成績的教科書句型：把三個「缺的」快速列完，最後用一句 And I'm here 收——不辯解、不悲情，讓事實自己說話。對台灣讀者價值極高，因為華人習慣先道歉自己不夠格。
swaps: No CS degree, no big-tech pedigree — and I still shipped this.
I came in through the side door, and the work speaks for itself.
cards.pmNote: Ebi 認為最好的 PM 常常是從別的職能轉過來的——因為你對「另一邊」有真的同理心。
cards.episode: Crafting a compelling product vision | Ebi Atawodi (YouTube, Netflix, Uber)

alts.quote: Yeah, I mean, I don't want to overstate it, but they basically said all the early stuff we did to grow TikTok was based on your writing.
alts.zh: 我不想講得太誇張，不過他們基本上是說：TikTok 早期做的成長工作，都是照你寫的東西做的。

alts.quote: What I didn't tell is that there was at least six years of accidental work behind this. I started a blog six years before... Actually, I've always been blogging since I graduated.
alts.zh: 我沒講的是，這背後至少有六年、不是刻意規劃的累積。我在那之前六年就開始寫部落格了——其實我從畢業就一直在寫。

alts.quote: Well, it's very generous of you. I wouldn't say... look, we've done some really good work, some good work so far at YouTube, and it's been a journey.
alts.zh: 你太抬舉我了。我不會這樣講啦——我們在 YouTube 是做了一些不錯的成績，過程也蠻曲折的。

cards.pattern: Some of the best [職位] come from somewhere else, because you have empathy for being on the other side.
cards.quote: I genuinely think that some of the best product managers come from something else because you have empathy for being on the other side.
cards.zh: 我真心覺得最好的產品經理很多都是從別的領域轉過來的，因為你真的體會過站在另一邊是什麼感覺。
cards.why: 把「我不是本科出身」這個弱點，改寫成一個結構性優勢，而且理由具體（你當過對面那個人）。轉職者面試被問「你為什麼沒相關經驗」時，這是最漂亮的回法。
swaps: Coming from support means I've been on the receiving end of every bad decision.
My detour is the reason I catch things others don't.
cards.pmNote: 10,000 小時不必等到有職稱才開始累積：先用你自己愛用的 app 練「找出前 10 個問題」。
cards.episode: Crafting a compelling product vision | Ebi Atawodi (YouTube, Netflix, Uber)

alts.quote: I'll be honest, I didn't really enjoy being a manager of managers. It felt a bit too abstract. I didn't like being in the meetings, not doing the work.
alts.zh: 老實說，我沒有很喜歡當「管理主管的主管」。感覺有點太抽象了。我不喜歡一直在開會、卻沒有真的在做事。

alts.quote: What drew me to that side of the business probably was maybe accidental at the beginning. Just again, coming from this musical family and background, I always had a natural interest in helping artists make a living.
alts.zh: 會被那一塊業務吸引，一開始大概、應該說算是偶然吧。不過我出身音樂家庭，本來就對「幫藝術家養活自己」這件事有興趣。

alts.quote: I have a lot of rough edges to my personality that I think people have just learned to deal with over the years, but I try to be self-aware about them
alts.zh: 我個性上有很多稜角，同事這些年大概是習慣了，但我至少努力對它們保持自覺。

cards.quote: I read the email, I'm like, "What do you want me to do? Is this an FYI? Are you saying there's a problem? Do you want me to help?"
cards.zh: 我讀完信心想：「你到底要我做什麼？這是知會嗎？你是在說有問題嗎？還是你要我幫忙？」
cards.why: 三個選項一次攤開，讓對方只要選一個。用在你收到不知所云的訊息時很有效；反過來也是提醒：你自己寫信時，開頭就該標明是 FYI、求助、還是要決策。
swaps: Just to check — is this FYI, a decision request, or a help request?
What do you need from me on this one?
cards.pmNote: PM 的工作是製造清晰度；連自己的信都要讓人一秒知道該做什麼。
cards.episode: Crafting a compelling product vision | Ebi Atawodi (YouTube, Netflix, Uber)

alts.quote: So I'm not saying they didn't get the exact monthly number wrong. I'm saying they got it wrong by many factors.
alts.zh: 我不是在說他們只是月份的確切數字抓錯。我是說他們錯了好幾個量級。

alts.quote: I'm not saying that we should not take customer feedback, that's very different.
alts.zh: 我不是說不要聽客戶回饋——那是完全不同的兩件事。

alts.quote: The reason I'm a little confused, just because I want to get it right, is what I'm hearing, which maybe isn't what you said
alts.zh: 我有點不確定，純粹是想弄清楚——我聽到的（可能不是你講的意思）是……

cards.pattern: If I could put all of this into an AI and it would spit out [你的產出], then you haven't done your job.
cards.quote: If I could put all the research into Bard or ChatGPT and it could spit out a PRD, then you haven't done your job.
cards.zh: 如果我把所有研究丟進 ChatGPT，它就能吐出一份 PRD，那代表你根本沒做到你的工作。
cards.why: 用一個條件句設下標準，而不是直接罵人。If [AI 就能做到], then [你沒做到你的工作] 這個結構現在極度好用，可以套在任何職能上，逼團隊去想自己的不可替代處在哪。
swaps: If a model can produce it from the same inputs, what did you add?
Where's the judgment that isn't in the prompt?
cards.pmNote: AI 時代 PM 的差異化在 product sense——一種靠大量接觸好產品養出來的「感覺」，不是邏輯推導。
cards.episode: Crafting a compelling product vision | Ebi Atawodi (YouTube, Netflix, Uber)

alts.quote: That is an artificial timeline introduced by Google Calendar or whatever calendar you use. It's not a real thing, and so I want to put us on real timelines.
alts.zh: 那只是 Google 日曆——或你們用的任何行事曆——生出來的假期限，它不是真的。所以我希望我們回到真正的時間軸上。

alts.quote: We're all sitting talking about it, and Tate says, "It's a low margin reseller, one time sells." "You can say dotcom all you like, it's a low margin reseller."
alts.zh: 大家在車上討論，Tate 說：「它就是個低毛利的經銷商，一次性買賣。你要講幾次『.com』都可以，它還是個低毛利經銷商。」

alts.quote: I think sometimes people think that craft is about perfecting things and perfecting them in a very organized way or very early on. The downside with this perfection mindset is that it can be sometimes hard to put anything out because nothing is ever fully perfect.
alts.zh: 大家常以為所謂「工藝」就是把東西做到完美，而且要很有條理、很早就開始做。這種完美心態的代價是：你可能什麼都出不了貨，因為沒有東西是真正完美的。

cards.pattern: [被輕視的東西] is the product. Period.
cards.quote: By the way, the infrastructure piece, I know it's a nugget on the side but infrastructure is the product. Period.
cards.zh: 順帶一提，基礎建設這塊——我知道這是題外話——但基礎建設就是產品。就這樣。
cards.why: Period. 是英語裡的句點宣告，等於「這件事我不打算辯論」。再用一次改名（tech debt → product debt）把責任從工程搬到自己頭上——重新命名是 PM 最省力的一種奪權。
swaps: Reliability is a feature. Full stop.
That's not eng debt, that's roadmap debt.
cards.pmNote: 把「技術債」改叫「產品債」，這筆帳就進了你的 roadmap，而不是永遠等工程自己找時間。
cards.episode: Crafting a compelling product vision | Ebi Atawodi (YouTube, Netflix, Uber)

alts.quote: Know that it's coming and make sure you land the plane.
alts.zh: 先知道它一定會來，然後確保你把飛機落好。

alts.quote: Even if we had no more progress today with models, which is absolutely not the case, but even if we had no more progress, we are way behind on product.
alts.zh: 就算模型從今天起完全不再進步——當然實際上完全不是這樣——就算真的不再進步，我們在產品上還是落後一大截。

alts.quote: So we can think there's people who don't know about it, there's people who do know about it but don't do it, and then there's people who do know about it, but do do it. And it's that last group that's so tiny.
alts.zh: 可以分成三種人：不知道這件事的、知道但不做的、知道又真的去做的。而最後那一群小得可憐。

cards.pattern: I'm okay at those things. I'm potentially world-class at this other thing. Let me double down there.
cards.quote: I'm potentially world-class at this other thing. Let me see what it feels like to double down on this area."
cards.zh: 比較好的說法是：「那些事我做得還行。但這件事我可能可以做到世界級。那就往這邊押吧。」
cards.why: 解釋轉職的黃金公式：不是「我當不成工程師只好當 PM」（settle for），而是「我把賭注押在我最強的地方」（double down）。同一段人生履歷，動詞一換，聽起來就從退而求其次變成主動選擇。
swaps: I was competent there; I think I can be exceptional here.
It wasn't a step down, it was a bet on my sharpest edge.
cards.pmNote: Kevin 建議想當 PM 的人先做工程、設計或業務——你要接手誰的責任，就先去做那份工作。
cards.episode: Unorthodox PM wisdom: Automating user insights, unselling job candidates, logging every decision, more | Kevin Yien (Stripe, Square, Mutiny)

alts.quote: I even told my manager this when I first came in, "I'm here to learn to be a better founder." So if I can make my LinkedIn experiences match to that, that would be a huge win for me independent of promotion, or compensation.
alts.zh: 我一進去就跟我主管講了：「我來這裡是為了學會怎麼當一個更好的創辦人。」所以只要 LinkedIn 的經歷能配上這個目標，對我就是大勝利，跟升職或薪水無關。

alts.quote: I genuinely think that some of the best product managers come from something else because you have empathy for being on the other side.
alts.zh: 我真心覺得最好的產品經理很多都是從別的領域轉過來的，因為你真的體會過站在另一邊是什麼感覺。

alts.quote: I'll tell the story that is kind of true, and people will think it's amazing, and also the real deal behind it.
alts.zh: 我先講那個「差不多是真的」的版本，大家會覺得很厲害；然後再講背後真正的狀況。

cards.quote: I don't want to make it seem like it was me against everyone because that was definitely not the case. I think the starting engineers and designers on that team really cared about the quality of what they built too.
cards.zh: 我不想講得好像是我一個人對抗全世界，完全不是那樣。那個團隊的工程師跟設計師本來就很在乎品質。
cards.why: 講完自己的功勞後主動拆掉英雄敘事。I don't want to make it seem like… 是英語職場最實用的自我修正詞——它讓你可以先把故事講精彩，再把功勞分回去，兩邊都不虧。
swaps: To be clear, this wasn't me pushing a rock uphill alone.
I don't want to overstate my role here.
cards.pmNote: 績效面談講成績時，把團隊的貢獻主動說出來，反而讓你的判斷力顯得更可信。
cards.episode: Unorthodox PM wisdom: Automating user insights, unselling job candidates, logging every decision, more | Kevin Yien (Stripe, Square, Mutiny)

alts.quote: Looking back, my career has been a little bit like a bingo card. I've always been looking to fill in boxes I didn't have filled because I felt like that would make me a better professional.
alts.zh: 回頭看，我的職涯有點像一張賓果卡。我一直在補那些還沒被填滿的格子，因為我覺得那會讓我變成更好的專業工作者。

alts.quote: Yeah, I mean, I don't want to overstate it, but they basically said all the early stuff we did to grow TikTok was based on your writing.
alts.zh: 我不想講得太誇張，不過他們基本上是說：TikTok 早期做的成長工作，都是照你寫的東西做的。

alts.quote: My one learning there that has stuck with me, and I think can work for other people too, is that it's not just about doing things that actually matter, and learning. It's about being able to tell the story.
alts.zh: 那段經驗裡有一個一直留在我身上的體悟，我覺得對別人也適用：重點不只是去做真正重要的事、去學東西，還要能把這件事講成一個故事。

cards.quote: Footnote, correlation versus causation. It's all put out there.
cards.zh: 附註一下：相關不等於因果。我先把話擺在這裡。
cards.why: 被誇獎時的高階回法：不否認、不謙讓，改成給一個技術性的免責聲明。Footnote 這個用法（把整句話當成註腳）很輕巧，既幽默又表現出你自己在檢查因果——反而讓人更信你。
swaps: Caveat: I can't prove those two are connected.
Survivorship bias, probably — worth saying out loud.
cards.pmNote: Kevin 的 decision log：記下判斷與理由，設好日曆提醒回頭對答案——這是練 product sense 最便宜的方式。
cards.episode: Unorthodox PM wisdom: Automating user insights, unselling job candidates, logging every decision, more | Kevin Yien (Stripe, Square, Mutiny)

alts.quote: Well, first of all, thank you for saying all that. That's giving me too much credit, but I like the idea that it's going to balance out the too little credit I ostensibly get somewhere else, that's great.
alts.zh: 首先謝謝你這樣說。你太抬舉我了——不過我喜歡這個說法，就當作是補回我在別的地方被低估的部分吧。

alts.quote: if I had to guess how people might talk about that, if I wasn't in the room, maybe they would cite that, but it's tough to say.
alts.zh: 如果要我猜、我不在場的時候別人會怎麼講這件事，他們可能會提到那個吧——但很難說。

alts.quote: Yeah, I mean, I don't want to overstate it, but they basically said all the early stuff we did to grow TikTok was based on your writing.
alts.zh: 我不想講得太誇張，不過他們基本上是說：TikTok 早期做的成長工作，都是照你寫的東西做的。

cards.pattern: I do want to apply a pretty severe caveat here though, which is [限制].
cards.quote: I do want to apply a pretty severe caveat here though, which is, a decision log is not a replacement for building products. It's a additional complimentary thing that you can be doing on your own.
cards.zh: 不過我要加一個很重的但書：決策日誌不能取代真的去做產品。它只是你自己可以額外做的補充。
cards.why: apply a caveat（加但書）是把自己剛講的東西「限定射程」的專業說法。加上 severe 這個形容詞，等於告訴聽眾這句但書比前面的建議還重要——一種先發制人的防誤用。
swaps: Big asterisk on all of that:
One important boundary on this advice:
cards.pmNote: 光坐著看市場評論不會讓你變強；決策日誌是輔助動作，不是主訓練。
cards.episode: Unorthodox PM wisdom: Automating user insights, unselling job candidates, logging every decision, more | Kevin Yien (Stripe, Square, Mutiny)

alts.quote: And I guess it's kind of an embarrassing thing to say because everyone who's a startup founder thinks, my startup moves super fast and the talent bar is super high.
alts.zh: 說這話其實有點難為情，因為每個新創創辦人都覺得「我們超快、人才標準超高」。

alts.quote: And again, these are all conjectures, which I can't prove in any way, but it's a thought experiment to talk about these things.
alts.zh: 再說一次，這些都只是我的推測，我完全沒辦法證明，但當成思想實驗來聊是有意思的。

alts.quote: My guess is what you want to be doing is learning and creating and not spending a lot of time managing.
alts.zh: 我猜你真正想做的是學習跟創造，而不是花一堆時間在管理上。

cards.pattern: I explicitly do not mean [容易被誤解的版本].
cards.quote: I explicitly do not mean read a bunch of other PM artifacts. You're not going to become a better writer by reading PRDs or whatever it is or support articles. It needs to be writing that compels.
cards.zh: 我明確講：我不是叫你去讀一堆 PM 文件。讀 PRD 不會讓你變成更好的作者。你要讀的是那種會推著你行動的文字。
cards.why: explicitly do not mean 是精準度極高的一句：先封死最可能的誤讀，再給正解。給建議時最怕對方照字面執行到錯的地方，這句話就是那道防呆。
swaps: To be very clear, that's not what I'm suggesting.
I want to rule out one reading of this:
cards.pmNote: Kevin 的判準：好文字要 compel（推動行動），不是讓人覺得 interesting 就好。
cards.episode: Unorthodox PM wisdom: Automating user insights, unselling job candidates, logging every decision, more | Kevin Yien (Stripe, Square, Mutiny)

alts.quote: You're sitting in the meeting and you're like, "This is a dumb question. Everyone's going to think I'm an idiot." But then you get brave and you ask it and it turns out it wasn't a dumb question.
alts.zh: 你坐在會議裡想：「這問題也太蠢，問了大家會覺得我是白痴。」結果你鼓起勇氣問了，才發現根本不是蠢問題。

alts.quote: The support's not going to be good enough. They probably don't have good governance policies or other things that we need. Whether that's true or not, this is what it looks like.
alts.zh: 他們的客服大概不夠好、治理政策大概也不合我們要求。這是不是事實不重要——重點是看起來就是這樣。

alts.quote: Just for folks that are listening, just to calibrate what size of company you're talking about selling to here.
alts.zh: 為了讓聽的人有個基準——你剛剛講的是賣給多大規模的公司？

cards.pattern: This is maybe going to come across a little bit flippant, but [直白的話].
cards.quote: This is maybe going to come across a little bit flippant, but they can't stop you from sending an email technically. So I'm just going to send the email.
cards.zh: 這樣講可能有點輕佻，但嚴格來說他們也不能阻止我寄信。所以我就照寄。
cards.why: come across as 是「給人的感覺是」——用它預告自己接下來的話可能不中聽，等於先幫對方消化。台灣人要嘛不敢講，要嘛講完才補「我不是那個意思」，這句是把補救提前。
swaps: This might sound harsh, but...
At the risk of sounding glib —
cards.pmNote: Kevin 的 unsell email 讓 offer 階段流失 30% 候選人，招募同事很不爽——但六個月後的留任率救回來了。
cards.episode: Unorthodox PM wisdom: Automating user insights, unselling job candidates, logging every decision, more | Kevin Yien (Stripe, Square, Mutiny)

alts.quote: So I'm going to disagree with Sedaris a little bit.
alts.zh: 這點我要跟 Sedaris 有一點不一樣的看法。

alts.quote: I would soften it a little bit... I wouldn't say I'm not a fan of creating category.
alts.zh: 我會講得軟一點——我不會說我不喜歡做品類（category）這件事。

alts.quote: I'd maybe put it a little bit differently.
alts.zh: 我可能會換一個講法。

cards.pattern: I'm cool with six of these. This one freaks me out. Can we talk more?
cards.quote: Most of the time they will say, "Thank you. I am cool with six of these. This one freaks me out.
cards.zh: 多數人會回：「這裡面有六點我可以接受。但這一點讓我很不安，可以再聊聊嗎？」
cards.why: 回應一份混合好壞的提案時最好用的三段：先劃出可接受的範圍→只標出一個真正的痛點→提出下一步。比「我有一些疑慮」精準太多，對方馬上知道要處理什麼。
swaps: Most of this works for me; number three is the sticking point.
I'm fine with the scope. The timeline is what worries me.
cards.pmNote: unsell email：offer 階段主動把最糟的八件事寫給候選人——看完還一樣興奮的，就是 A+ 人選。
cards.episode: Unorthodox PM wisdom: Automating user insights, unselling job candidates, logging every decision, more | Kevin Yien (Stripe, Square, Mutiny)

alts.quote: On Twitter, you'll see people say, "Oh, it's the most expensive use of everyone's time," but it's like, "Yep. But there's 0% fidelity loss in that.
alts.zh: 推特上會有人說：「那是最貴的一種時間使用方式。」但我的回答是：「對啊。可是這樣資訊零失真。」

alts.quote: Another one, love him or hate him, one of the things that Elon Musk has said that I found it very valuable in my time.
alts.zh: 還有一個，不管你喜不喜歡他啦——馬斯克講過一句話，我覺得對我很受用。

alts.quote: It's like these things that seem so common sense are actually hard with what they're doing… a lot of the advice is common sense. That doesn't mean it's easy to put in motion.
alts.zh: 這些看起來根本是常識的東西，真的做起來很難……很多建議都是常識，但常識不代表容易落地。

cards.pattern: I'll be really clear: the expectation here is going to be [不好聽的現實].
cards.quote: We are a series A startup. We are pushing really hard at product-market fit. The expectation here is going to be that you're online at 10:00, that you can occasionally hop on a meeting on a Saturday or Sunday."
cards.zh: 「我們是 A 輪新創。我們正在拚產品市場契合。這裡的預期是你晚上十點還在線上，週六日偶爾也要開會。」
cards.why: I'll be really clear 之後接一句具體到時間點的現實。壞消息要用具體數字講，不能用形容詞（"it can get busy"）——含糊的預告等於沒預告，六個月後對方一樣覺得被騙。
swaps: Let me be upfront about the parts people struggle with here.
Here's the version I'd want to know before saying yes.
cards.pmNote: 壞消息前置的成本是 offer 流失率，回報是六個月後的留任率——這筆帳要跟老闆講清楚。
cards.episode: Unorthodox PM wisdom: Automating user insights, unselling job candidates, logging every decision, more | Kevin Yien (Stripe, Square, Mutiny)

alts.quote: And maybe this is a... I don't want to be very negative, but it's very hard inside a company like ours to task our best engineers to build a best in class sales product.
alts.zh: 我不想講得太負面，但在我們這種公司裡，要把最好的工程師派去做一個頂尖的業務工具，是非常困難的。

alts.quote: Then you're pushing deadlines out, and you're making your marketing team very sad.
alts.zh: 然後你就開始一直往後延，把行銷團隊搞得很難過。

alts.quote: These are reaching millions of people, their websites get many, many, many millions of unique visitors each month. That does not mean that your story is going to be read by millions of people.
alts.zh: 這些媒體確實觸及上百萬人，網站每個月幾百萬不重複訪客。但這不代表你那篇報導會被上百萬人看到。

cards.pattern: I need 20 minutes of focused time to interrogate this. We're not going to talk — you read, I respond in real time.
cards.quote: "I need 20 minutes of focused time to interrogate something that I've done. We're not going to talk. I'm literally going to force us into a room or Zoom.
cards.zh: 「我需要二十分鐘的專注時間來拷問我做的東西。我們不用講話。我就是要把大家關進一個會議室或 Zoom。」
cards.why: 開會前先宣告「這場會不講話」，把大家對會議的預期整個換掉。interrogate（拷問）用在自己的文件上很有意思：你不是在求贊同，你是在請人來拆。
swaps: This is a working session, not a presentation.
Twenty minutes, cameras off, comment as you read.
cards.pmNote: silent read（Amazon／Square 傳統）：非同步收不到回饋時，把「讀文件」本身變成一場會。
cards.episode: Unorthodox PM wisdom: Automating user insights, unselling job candidates, logging every decision, more | Kevin Yien (Stripe, Square, Mutiny)

alts.quote: Now that you've agreed among yourselves that you're going to do that for a fixed period of time, everyone go around the room and say, "If I could start this company over again the thing I wish we were doing was."
alts.zh: 既然大家已經同意用一段固定的時間來試，那就一個一個講：「如果能重來一次，我希望我們在做的是＿＿＿。」

alts.quote: So I've used up basically all our time talking about Make Time. I think we should have a follow-up episode just to talk about Sprint. What I think we do is let's cut off the lightning round.
alts.zh: 我基本上把時間都花在 Make Time 上了。我覺得我們該再錄一集專門講 Sprint。現在我的想法是：閃電問答就先砍掉。

alts.quote: he'll sit in a review and be like, "I don't think this is right." And then he'll pause and say, "I'm going to clear the rest of my day. Let's sit and figure it out."
alts.zh: 他會在評審會上說：「我覺得這不對。」然後停一下說：「我把今天剩下的行程清掉，我們一起坐下來把它弄清楚。」

cards.pattern: There is a world of difference between reading a report about [X] and standing with [X].
cards.quote: The best comparison I can give is, there is a world of difference between reading a report about a lime cook and then standing with a lime cook.
cards.zh: 我能給的最好對照是：讀一份關於廚房廚師的報告，跟真的站在他旁邊，是天差地遠的兩件事。
cards.why: a world of difference between A and B 是英語裡最有力的對比句型之一。這裡的技巧是兩邊都用具體動作（reading a report / standing with），而不是抽象概念——畫面出來了，論點就成立了。
swaps: Reading the summary and sitting in the room are not the same job.
Second-hand data and first-hand exposure aren't interchangeable.
cards.pmNote: Kevin 的原則：PM 不該只透過「磨砂玻璃」看使用者——研究報告、業務轉述都已經被別人處理過。
cards.episode: Unorthodox PM wisdom: Automating user insights, unselling job candidates, logging every decision, more | Kevin Yien (Stripe, Square, Mutiny)

alts.quote: I think people don't realize that there's a big difference between moving from 80% performance to 90% performance to 99% performance to 99.9% performance, and so on, and so on.
alts.zh: 我覺得大家沒意識到，從 80% 做到 90%、再到 99%、再到 99.9%，這幾段之間的差距有多大。

alts.quote: And my first question to him as a product guy is like, "Wow, would you give me a million dollars to solve this problem?"
alts.zh: 身為做產品的人，我第一個問題是：「哇，那你願意花一百萬美元讓我解掉這個問題嗎？」

alts.quote: If you're solving literally for that ratio of laughs per minute, there are two ways to improve it. One is to add more laughs. Two is to decrease the number of words between laughs.
alts.zh: 如果你真的在解「每分鐘笑聲數」這個比值，只有兩種改法。一是增加笑點，二是減少笑點之間的字數。

cards.pattern: That is a very tempting lie to tell yourself.
cards.quote: I can use my intuition from the hundred interviews I've already done. I don't need to do one more interview."
cards.zh: 「我已經訪過一百個使用者了，靠直覺就夠。我不需要再訪一個。」
cards.why: a tempting lie to tell yourself 精準命中一種特定的自欺：不是不知道，是知道了卻選擇相信方便的版本。用 tempting 而不是 stupid，讓被說的人不必防衛，就能承認。
swaps: That's the comfortable story, not the true one.
It's an easy thing to convince yourself of.
cards.pmNote: 使用者的生活一直在變；你腦中的模型會過期，而且不會發出過期通知。
cards.episode: Unorthodox PM wisdom: Automating user insights, unselling job candidates, logging every decision, more | Kevin Yien (Stripe, Square, Mutiny)

alts.quote: It's one thing to say you're spending a lot of time looking outside the building. It's a whole other thing to hear from the places you don't normally hear from.
alts.zh: 說自己花很多時間在公司外面看，是一回事；真的去聽那些你平常聽不到的聲音，完全是另一回事。

alts.quote: Obviously never say never. Sometimes it might work, and if it worked for you, I am so glad. But that's an outlier and don't treat it as a pattern.
alts.zh: 當然，凡事沒有絕對。有時候真的會成功，如果你成功了我真的替你高興。但那是特例，不要把它當成通則。

alts.quote: Where I've seen people get lost is they assume that if you do that alone, it will work.
alts.zh: 我看過很多人卡住的地方是：他們假設光做這件事就會成功。

cards.quote: you eventually need to convince yourself that there is a difference between you not being good at something and a business or company not needing that thing at a particular moment in time
cards.zh: 你終究得說服自己：「你不擅長某件事」跟「公司此刻不需要那件事」，是兩回事。
cards.why: 被裁員、被拒絕之後最需要的一句切割。英語職場很習慣把「人」和「當下的需求」分開講，因為這樣才可能在下一場面試裡不帶怨氣地敘述同一段經歷。
swaps: That was a fit problem, not a capability problem.
The company's needs changed; my skills didn't disappear.
cards.pmNote: Kevin 被裁時太太懷孕九個月——他說最痛的不是失業，是「我以為我是 PM，這證明我不是」。
cards.episode: Unorthodox PM wisdom: Automating user insights, unselling job candidates, logging every decision, more | Kevin Yien (Stripe, Square, Mutiny)

alts.quote: Probably for me, I think my time at Instacart was probably not my best time. I think I went to Instacart with a vision of what I felt the product could be, but I was not aware or in tune with what the DNA of the company was.
alts.zh: 對我來說，Instacart 那段大概是我狀態最不好的時候。我帶著一套「產品應該長成什麼樣」的想像進去，卻沒真的看懂那家公司的 DNA 是什麼。

alts.quote: But basically what happened is that we pushed out an update that made the model more likely to tell you things that sound good in the moment.
alts.zh: 簡單講就是，我們推了一個更新，結果讓模型更容易講出那種當下聽起來很順耳的話。

alts.quote: Yeah, I messed up. But I know I'm still a good person and a good worker. Yes, I made a mistake, but I'm going to move on.
alts.zh: 對，我搞砸了。但我知道我還是個好人、也還是個好的工作者。對，我犯了錯，但我要往前走。

cards.pattern: My skills and the way that company operates were not compatible.
cards.quote: The second one though is my skills and the way that company operates are not compatible.
cards.zh: 第二種是：我的能力跟那家公司的運作方式不相容。
cards.why: 面試被問「上一份為什麼結束」的最佳骨架：用 compatible 這個中性詞（像插頭與插座），不指責公司也不貶低自己，再補一個「這很常見」的觀察把它常態化。
swaps: The operating style there and the way I work didn't line up.
It was an environment mismatch more than anything else.
cards.pmNote: 同一個人換環境就起飛，多半不是能力變了，是棲地變了。
cards.episode: Unorthodox PM wisdom: Automating user insights, unselling job candidates, logging every decision, more | Kevin Yien (Stripe, Square, Mutiny)

alts.quote: I even told my manager this when I first came in, "I'm here to learn to be a better founder." So if I can make my LinkedIn experiences match to that, that would be a huge win for me independent of promotion, or compensation.
alts.zh: 我一進去就跟我主管講了：「我來這裡是為了學會怎麼當一個更好的創辦人。」所以只要 LinkedIn 的經歷能配上這個目標，對我就是大勝利，跟升職或薪水無關。

alts.quote: I'll tell the story that is kind of true, and people will think it's amazing, and also the real deal behind it.
alts.zh: 我先講那個「差不多是真的」的版本，大家會覺得很厲害；然後再講背後真正的狀況。

alts.quote: As head of fan monetization, I have a team of folks who are really passionate about figuring out new ways to help artists and fans connect and also figure out ways to make those connections result in new monetization opportunities for the artists.
alts.zh: 我的職稱是 head of fan monetization，我帶一群很熱衷於「幫藝人跟粉絲建立連結」的人，同時想辦法把這些連結變成藝人新的收入來源。

cards.pattern: You are not bad. It's that the machine you're a part of isn't the kind you thrive in.
cards.quote: But the reality is, you are not bad. It is that maybe the way that your environment is working, the machine that you exist as a part of, is not the kind that you thrive in.
cards.zh: 但事實是：你不是不好。而是你所處的環境、你身在其中的那台機器，不是能讓你發揮的那種。這其實是很有力量的認知。
cards.why: 績效對話最難的一刻——對方聽到的是「我很爛」。這句把焦點從「人」移到「機器」，然後用 And that's empowering 把結論翻正：因為機器可以換，人格不能。
swaps: This isn't a verdict on you; it's a read on the fit.
The system isn't set up for how you do your best work.
cards.pmNote: 績效談話後給對方兩條路：改變自己的工作方式以適配環境，或去找適配的環境——兩條都在他控制範圍內。
cards.episode: Unorthodox PM wisdom: Automating user insights, unselling job candidates, logging every decision, more | Kevin Yien (Stripe, Square, Mutiny)

alts.quote: I said, "The way you are operating is not meeting our leadership expectations. If you do not change, you cannot be part of this organization anymore. I believe you can operate differently."
alts.zh: 我跟他們說：「你們現在的做事方式沒有達到我們對領導者的期待。如果不改變，你們就不能繼續留在這個組織。我相信你們有能力用不同的方式做事。」

alts.quote: So you have engineers now who are working on optimizing short form videos for higher engagement, and you sort of want to say to them like, "Hey, are you thinking about what this is doing to the brains of young children?"
alts.zh: 現在有一群工程師在優化短影音的互動率，你會有點想跟他們說：「欸，你有想過這對小朋友的腦袋在做什麼嗎？」

alts.quote: And it's not because people are bad people. I think most people are really well-intentioned. But what happens when you have people that join and you didn't really need them?
alts.zh: 這不是因為誰是壞人，我覺得大多數人動機都很好。但問題是：當你招了一批其實不需要的人，會發生什麼事？

cards.quote: writing is clarity at scale, and a key component to a PM's job is creating clarity both internally and externally
cards.zh: 寫作就是「規模化的清晰」，而 PM 工作的核心之一，就是對內對外製造清晰。
cards.why: X is Y at scale 是矽谷極常見的定義句型（clarity at scale / trust at scale / taste at scale）。一句話同時給出定義和價值主張，開會時拿來當論點的開頭非常好用。
swaps: Documentation is judgment at scale.
A good spec is alignment at scale.
cards.pmNote: Kevin 的判準：如果你沒辦法賣自己的產品、也沒辦法支援它，我不相信你能做出它。
cards.episode: Unorthodox PM wisdom: Automating user insights, unselling job candidates, logging every decision, more | Kevin Yien (Stripe, Square, Mutiny)

alts.quote: And so ever since then, we've been automating jobs and creating new jobs, and you can always see the job that's going to go away, and you don't know the new job because it doesn't exist yet.
alts.zh: 從那時候到現在，我們一直在自動化舊工作、也一直在長出新工作；而你永遠看得到那個要消失的工作，看不到新的，因為它還不存在。

alts.quote: So the risk you take if you're not telling stories is that you will be forgotten. 100%. You will be forgotten.
alts.zh: 所以你不講故事的風險就是：你會被忘記。百分之百，你一定會被忘記。

alts.quote: So having a shit draft is a million times more valuable than having all these great ideas. But it's also really painful.
alts.zh: 有一份爛草稿，比手上一堆很棒的點子有價值一百萬倍。但那個過程真的很痛。

cards.pattern: Follow me on a detour to [不相干的領域] for a second.
cards.quote: Yeah, so follow me on the detour to science world temporarily. If we all remember high school science classes, there was this concept of potential and kinetic energy.
cards.zh: 先跟我繞去科學世界一下。如果大家還記得高中物理，有個概念叫位能跟動能。
cards.why: 要講一個長類比之前先報備。follow me on a detour 讓聽眾知道「接下來這段看起來離題，但會繞回來」，於是他們願意等——沒有這句預告，長類比很容易被打斷。
swaps: Bear with me on a tangent for a second.
Let me take the long way round to answer that.
cards.pmNote: Kevin 的 PM 定義：把團隊的位能，用最小損耗轉成使用者拿到的動能。
cards.episode: Unorthodox PM wisdom: Automating user insights, unselling job candidates, logging every decision, more | Kevin Yien (Stripe, Square, Mutiny)

alts.quote: And because of that and because of that... And I usually like to end it with, and finally, this was the last thing you left the world with.
alts.zh: 「很久以前……然後有一天……因為這樣、又因為這樣……最後，這就是你留給世界的東西。」

alts.quote: It's like you had a very smooth flight across the Atlantic and your landing was absolutely horrible. You're not going to remember the smooth flight, you're going to remember the ending.
alts.zh: 就像你飛越大西洋一路很平穩，結果降落爛透了。你不會記得那段平穩的飛行，你只會記得結尾。

alts.quote: And so you go from this moment of the hard high cost of sales, pounding the pavement, to getting a list on a silver platter of restaurants to onboard. And that's that feeling of tipping, where all of a sudden something goes from being really freaking hard to so much easier.
alts.zh: 你會從那種一家一家敲門、成本超高的銷售，變成人家直接把一份餐廳名單端到你面前。那就是市場翻轉的感覺——某件事忽然從超級難變成輕鬆很多。

cards.pattern: The best way to get feedback is not to ask what people think, but to put something concrete in front of them.
cards.quote: the best way to get feedback from people is not by asking what they think, but to put something concrete in front of them and then have them react to it, right?
cards.zh: 要拿到回饋，最好的方式不是問人家怎麼想，而是先擺一個具體的東西在他面前，讓他反應，對吧？
cards.why: not by X, but by Y 的對比句型把方法論壓成一句。實務價值極高：開放式問句（你覺得呢）在英語會議上通常換來沉默，一份粗糙草稿卻能換來十條意見。
swaps: Don't ask for opinions, ask for reactions to a draft.
Put a strawman up and let people knock it down.
cards.pmNote: Kevin 稱之為 tuning fork（音叉）：先發出一個音，讓別人告訴你偏了多少。
cards.episode: Unorthodox PM wisdom: Automating user insights, unselling job candidates, logging every decision, more | Kevin Yien (Stripe, Square, Mutiny)

alts.quote: The old way I think is shitty. I think it's broken, and I haven't found anything out there that is innovating on this.
alts.zh: 舊的做法我覺得很爛。我覺得它是壞的，而且我沒看到市面上有任何人在改良它。

alts.quote: You don't have to do the thing I'm asking, but it is something that I would do if I were you, or at least I would consider if I were you.
alts.zh: 你不一定要照我說的做，但如果我是你，我會做這件事——至少會認真考慮。

alts.quote: So for positioning work, I'm going to say something that is contentious, but I don't think it is at all.
alts.zh: 講到定位這件事，我要說一句大家可能覺得很有爭議的話——但我完全不覺得有爭議。

cards.quote: And if you push a really experienced product director like that, they're going to go, "Good point, I don't. I'm going to go find out."
cards.zh: 你這樣逼一個真正資深的產品總監，他會說：「說得對，我確實不知道。我去查清楚。」
cards.why: 承認不知道的極簡三拍：認可提問（Good point）→承認（I don't）→承諾行動（I'm going to go find out）。九個字。台灣人常在第一拍就開始解釋，反而顯得心虛；資深的訊號是快、短、帶下一步。
swaps: Fair — I don't know. Let me get back to you with the answer.
You're right to push. I'll go check and come back.
cards.pmNote: Tom 的追問法：「你怎麼知道那是詐欺？」→「資料裡標的」→「你知道它怎麼被標的嗎？」→那你就不知道那是詐欺。
cards.episode: This CPO regrets that product management exists | Tom Verrilli (CPO of Whatnot)

alts.quote: And again, I'm not an expert in this and I think Erin Meyer wrote that book, The Culture Map. So you should just find what those people wrote because they're much smarter than I am about this.
alts.zh: 再說一次，我不是這方面的專家。Erin Meyer 寫過《文化地圖》那本書，你們應該直接去看他們寫的，他們比我懂太多了。

alts.quote: At that point, I was an interim CMO at Nero and I'm like, "I don't know how to do this." And it actually earns you a lot more credit than you think.
alts.zh: 那時候我在 Nero 當代理行銷長，我就說：「我不知道該怎麼做這件事。」結果這反而幫你賺到比你想像中多得多的信任。

alts.quote: I don't understand what this is, and I'm not the right person for this role," and it turned out, nobody understood exactly what was going on.
alts.zh: 「我看不懂這是什麼，我也不是這個職位該找的人」——結果發現，根本沒有人真的搞懂在發生什麼事。

cards.pattern: How do you know that? Do you know how it gets [產生的]? Okay, so you don't actually know.
cards.quote: Turn around and be like, "How do you know that was fraud?" "Oh, it's labeled in the dataset as fraud. "Okay. Do you know how it gets labeled?"
cards.zh: 你就回問：「你怎麼知道那是詐欺？」「喔，資料集裡標成詐欺。」「好，那你知道它是怎麼被標上去的嗎？」
cards.why: 三層追問的階梯，每一層都只用一個中性問句，不帶指控。厲害在最後結論不必由你講出口——對方自己走到「我其實不知道」。這是英語會議裡最有效的挑戰假設方式。
swaps: Where does that number come from? And who defines it?
Walk me back one step — how is that measured?
cards.pmNote: 資料標籤的定義往往藏在某個 ops SOP 裡；沒人看過，但整個決策都建在上面。
cards.episode: This CPO regrets that product management exists | Tom Verrilli (CPO of Whatnot)

alts.quote: You write this document and I'm sorry, who actually reads it? You know what I mean? I know it's painful, but it's like that.
alts.zh: 你寫了那份文件——不好意思，但到底有誰真的會讀？你懂我意思吧？我知道這很刺耳，但事實就是這樣。

alts.quote: Your belief is that if we add buy now pay later, a lot more people will be able to buy and transact, and so it's going to pay off. Do I have that right?
alts.zh: 你的認定是：只要我們加了先買後付，會有更多人買得下去、成交量會上來，所以這筆投資划得來。我這樣理解對嗎？

alts.quote: Go and talk to that executive and say, "Look, I know you've told me to do this, but what would we observe if this was working versus not working? I'm here to help you with that."
alts.zh: 你可以去找那位主管說：「我知道你已經指定要做這個了，但如果它有效跟沒效，我們會分別看到什麼？這部分我可以幫你。」

cards.quote: One of the things I ask a lot in product review when someone says, "Hey, we want to run an experiment," is, "Okay, what do we do if it's green? What do we do if it's red?"
cards.zh: 有人說「我們想跑個實驗」，我在產品評審上最常問的就是：「如果結果是綠的我們做什麼？紅的又做什麼？」
cards.why: 兩個對稱的問句，逼對方在拿到資料之前先承諾行動。如果兩個答案一樣，這個實驗就不用跑了——這是用問題（而非否決）殺掉一個爛提案的最優雅方式。
swaps: What changes if this wins? What changes if it doesn't?
What decision does this data actually unlock?
cards.pmNote: 高成長階段不該追求 5% 的統計顯著勝利，要找會改變業務曲線、而且會複利的東西。
cards.episode: This CPO regrets that product management exists | Tom Verrilli (CPO of Whatnot)

alts.quote: People call me sometimes they're like "I want to know if I have product market fit." Well, the fact that you have time to call me and ask me this question already tells me the answer.
alts.zh: 有人打給我說：「我想知道我們有沒有 PMF。」嗯，你有空打這通電話問我，這件事本身就給了答案。

alts.quote: And one of the things I'll often ask is, if you had another couple days, what would you do with this?
alts.zh: 我很常問的一個問題是：如果再多給你幾天，你會拿這個東西做什麼？

alts.quote: You ask questions like, what's the hardest you've ever worked to get something done and why? And that does differentiate a lot of people, a lot of people don't actually have a great answer to that.
alts.zh: 你可以問這種問題：你這輩子為了完成某件事最拚的一次是什麼？為什麼？這題真的很能分辨人，很多人其實答不太出來。

cards.quote: So I often try and start with like, am I hearing you right that this is your prior? Is there a piece of context or something that I don't have that helps inform that prior?
cards.zh: 我通常會先問：「我理解得對嗎，你的預設立場是這個？有沒有什麼我不知道的背景，讓你形成這個判斷？」
cards.why: 向上反對的最佳開場。先確認你聽懂了，再把「我不同意」改寫成「我可能缺資訊」。prior（先驗判斷）這個詞讓整段變成理性討論而非立場對抗，而且給了對方一個台階：他可以補資訊，也可以發現自己沒有。
swaps: Let me play that back — is that the assumption you're working from?
What are you seeing that I'm not?
cards.pmNote: 被主管從奇怪的角度質疑時，先停下來確認他為什麼那樣問，不要急著防守你的方案。
cards.episode: This CPO regrets that product management exists | Tom Verrilli (CPO of Whatnot)

alts.quote: Yeah, I don't think of them as an or. I think they have to be intersected because basically the way I think about it is you actually start with a problem.
alts.zh: 我不覺得這是二選一。我覺得這兩件事必須交集在一起，因為在我看來，你本來就是從一個問題開始。

alts.quote: Something I caution people against though is don't use the data alone to figure out who the marginal user is.
alts.zh: 不過有件事我會提醒大家小心：不要只靠數據去判斷誰是邊際使用者。

alts.quote: So this might mean that I think... I don't want to say that if you don't have experience, don't start one, but it's kind of true. So become an expert somewhere, somehow, before you start.
alts.zh: 我不想說「沒經驗就別開始」這種話……但其實有點是真的。所以動手前，先想辦法在某個地方變成專家。

cards.quote: Sometimes it can be as simple as like, is your mind made up on this or are you open to input? If the answer is like, "No, I'm pretty set that this is the answer," shut up.
cards.zh: 有時候簡單問一句就好：「這件事你已經決定了，還是還能聽意見？」如果對方說「我滿確定就是這個答案」，那就閉嘴。
cards.why: 在花力氣說服之前先問「這場辯論存不存在」。這一句省下的會議時間比任何技巧都多，而且它把主導權交給對方，所以問了不會冒犯。母語者用得很自然，台灣人幾乎不會想到可以直接問。
swaps: Is this decided, or still open?
Do you want pushback on this, or do you want execution?
cards.pmNote: Tom 的規矩：如果雙方都沒資料，那就是兩個意見，CEO 的意見會贏——這時候就把自尊放門口。
cards.episode: This CPO regrets that product management exists | Tom Verrilli (CPO of Whatnot)

alts.quote: I'm not saying that sales-led is not good, but sometimes there's a decision to be made.
alts.zh: 我不是說銷售驅動不好，但有時候就是得做出取捨。

alts.quote: I would soften it a little bit... I wouldn't say I'm not a fan of creating category.
alts.zh: 我會講得軟一點——我不會說我不喜歡做品類（category）這件事。

alts.quote: I'm not saying that having a large market someday doesn't matter, of course it does eventually. But trying to be super pedantic about market size when it's a pre-seed company, it's just not something I'd put a lot of thought.
alts.zh: 我不是說市場總有一天要夠大這件事不重要，當然重要。但在一家 pre-seed 公司還在糾結市場規模算得多精確，我不會花太多心思在上面。

cards.pattern: Definitely agree. My only build on that would be [補充／修正].
cards.quote: I think my only build on that would be to say I think those core PM skills aren't necessarily the things that we have rewarded PMs for over the last five years, versus storytelling, alignment, strategy.
cards.zh: 我唯一想補的是：那些核心 PM 能力，其實不是我們過去五年在獎勵的東西——我們獎勵的是說故事、跨部門對齊、講策略。
cards.why: build 當名詞用（my build on that）是矽谷會議室的高頻詞，意思是「我在你的基礎上加一層」。它讓一個實質上的修正聽起來像是合作蓋房子。加 only 又進一步縮小了異議的體積。
swaps: Yes, and — one build on that:
Agree with all of that; the one thing I'd layer on is...
cards.pmNote: PM 的核心能力（懂客戶、懂生意、懂技術，並把三者翻譯起來）沒變，變的是這五年獎勵了「說故事」而不是「做事」。
cards.episode: This CPO regrets that product management exists | Tom Verrilli (CPO of Whatnot)

alts.quote: I think if you're building a product where it's not necessarily an AI- first product and you have some AI features that are on the side, but it's not the core of your value, I don't know that I would operate this way.
alts.zh: 如果你做的不是 AI 優先的產品，只是旁邊掛幾個 AI 功能、AI 不是核心價值，那我不確定我會這樣做。

alts.quote: I will say that when you say things are going well, I think we don't know the counterfactual.
alts.zh: 我要說一句：當你說事情進展順利的時候，我覺得我們並不知道反事實會是什麼。

alts.quote: And then our CEO gets in, and he's like, "I think really number four is the only reasonable one for these reasons."
alts.zh: 然後我們執行長進來說：「我認為真正合理的其實只有第四個，理由如下。」

cards.pattern: No, then go — think through everything that could break, and then move anyway.
cards.quote: And I think one of the monikers we use internally is no, then go. As in just think through all the things that could go wrong, understand where scale will break, understand the things that might happen, and then move on anyway.
cards.zh: 我們內部有個口號叫「先說不，然後走」。把所有可能出錯的地方都想過一輪，知道規模在哪裡會斷，然後照樣往前。
cards.why: 把「想清楚風險」跟「因為風險而停下」拆成兩件事。and then move on anyway 是整句的關鍵——它預先回答了「你不是不知道風險，你是決定承擔」。這是被法務／財務嚇住時最好用的立場。
swaps: Pre-mortem it, then ship it anyway.
Name every failure mode, then decide to go.
cards.pmNote: 把可能出事的情況全想過一遍，你自然會順手擋掉一半——不必全部解決才動。
cards.episode: This CPO regrets that product management exists | Tom Verrilli (CPO of Whatnot)

alts.quote: Actually, all feedback I think is valid. People's feelings are valid, but it doesn't mean that you need to do something about all of those things.
alts.zh: 其實我覺得所有回饋都是有效的。別人的感受都是真的，但這不代表你每一項都得去處理。

alts.quote: the biggest misconception about customer research is I have to listen to them. You don't have to listen to them at all, you just have to understand where they are
alts.zh: 對客戶研究最大的誤解，是以為做了就得照客戶說的做。你完全不必照做，你只需要搞清楚他們現在站在哪裡。

alts.quote: I also think it would be easy to use all what I just said as an excuse not to eventually build a great product.
alts.zh: 我也覺得，我剛剛講的那些很容易被拿來當藉口，變成「反正最後也不用做出好產品」。

cards.quote: So assume that at least half of what I've said is wrong in the same basis that half of the things I've probably ever shipped are not correct.
cards.zh: 所以你就當我講的至少有一半是錯的——就像我這輩子出過的東西大概也有一半是錯的一樣。
cards.why: 三段收尾：宣告我確定什麼→劃清我不確定什麼→主動打折。這種主動打折在英語職場不會被讀成沒信心，反而是老手的訊號，因為只有真的做過的人才知道界線在哪。
swaps: Take what's useful, discard the rest.
This is one data point from one company, not a law.
cards.pmNote: Tom 的內部文件開宗明義：目標是打擊率五成——你期待自己錯的次數跟對的一樣多。
cards.episode: This CPO regrets that product management exists | Tom Verrilli (CPO of Whatnot)

alts.quote: I mean, I think Things probably, I'm just guessing, I don't know any of the numbers or whatever, but I would assume it makes between five and $25 million of revenue, which to a VC is not even worth considering a VC.
alts.zh: 我是說，Things 這款——我純粹在猜，數字我完全不知道——但我猜它一年營收大概在五百萬到兩千五百萬美金之間，這種規模對創投來說根本不值得看。

alts.quote: I don't know that I'm perfect at it, but I've learned to balance those things quite a bit more than I did in the past when I would just purely read from my questions and my rubric and not care about anything else.
alts.zh: 我不敢說我做得多完美，但我已經學會比以前平衡得多了——以前我只會照著自己的問題清單和評分表念，其他一概不管。

alts.quote: However, I've read a few articles that have said that Google no longer does prioritize press releases in SEO, so I don't know how much that holds up.
alts.zh: 不過我讀過幾篇文章說 Google 現在 SEO 已經不會優先給新聞稿了，所以我不知道這個說法現在還成不成立。

cards.pattern: There's a really common thread to it, which is [你反覆犯的那個錯].
cards.quote: So there's probably just too many specific examples of times I've screwed up in my career, but there probably is a really common thread to it. And I think it's probably an easy trap for any PM to fall into, which is averages mean nothing to the individual is probably the thing that I've really scarred by.
cards.zh: 我職涯搞砸的例子多到講不完，但它們有一條很明顯的共通線：平均值對個別使用者毫無意義——這是我被燙傷最深的一課。
cards.why: 面試被問失敗經驗的最高階答法：不是講一個故事，而是講一個「模式」。承認例子多到講不完（顯示誠實），再抽出一條可傳授的規律（顯示反省深度）。
swaps: The specific failures vary; the underlying mistake is always the same.
If I pattern-match my worst calls, they all share one thing.
cards.pmNote: 只有 3% 的人用某功能，不代表可以砍——那 3% 可能有一群人，那是他們 100% 的用途。
cards.episode: This CPO regrets that product management exists | Tom Verrilli (CPO of Whatnot)

alts.quote: I don't want them to leave it at, "It was a big loss." You want to say, "What I learned from that is now I always run a load test, and I've had many successful launches since then."
alts.zh: 我不希望他只停在「那是一次很大的損失」。你應該說：我從那件事學到，現在我一定會先跑壓力測試，後來的好幾次上線都沒再出過同樣的問題。

alts.quote: Probably for me, I think my time at Instacart was probably not my best time. I think I went to Instacart with a vision of what I felt the product could be, but I was not aware or in tune with what the DNA of the company was.
alts.zh: 對我來說，Instacart 那段大概是我狀態最不好的時候。我帶著一套「產品應該長成什麼樣」的想像進去，卻沒真的看懂那家公司的 DNA 是什麼。

alts.quote: And so maybe I picked the wrong term in calling it growth hacking, but I think it at least opened the conversation to getting more people thinking about growth in a different way.
alts.zh: 所以也許我當初取 growth hacking 這個名字是取錯了，但至少它打開了對話，讓更多人開始用不同的方式想成長這件事。

cards.pattern: I tried to be my most ordinary self, as opposed to my interview self.
cards.quote: And I tried through that to be my most ordinary self as opposed to interview self, if that makes sense. Because you got to ask yourself, do I really want to spend my whole time having this discussion and this debate?
cards.zh: 整個過程我盡量拿出最平常的自己，而不是「面試版的自己」。因為你得問自己：我真的想每天都花時間在這種討論上嗎？
cards.why: my ordinary self / my interview self 這組對比是英語裡很好用的自我描述法，一句就把「表演」跟「真實」拆開。用在面試回顧、談公司文化契合度時，比 authentic 這種空詞具體太多。
swaps: I deliberately didn't perform in that conversation.
I showed up as I'd actually be on a Tuesday, not as a candidate.
cards.pmNote: 面試資深職位是雙向的：你在測「我想不想每天跟這個人辯論這些事」。
cards.episode: This CPO regrets that product management exists | Tom Verrilli (CPO of Whatnot)

alts.quote: I like to ask people to tell me about something they're really proud of that they accomplished and take me through the process and talk to me about why they're proud of it.
alts.zh: 我喜歡請對方講一件他真的很自豪的成就，帶我走過整個過程，並告訴我為什麼他覺得自豪。

alts.quote: I have a lot of rough edges to my personality that I think people have just learned to deal with over the years, but I try to be self-aware about them
alts.zh: 我個性上有很多稜角，同事這些年大概是習慣了，但我至少努力對它們保持自覺。

alts.quote: I genuinely think that some of the best product managers come from something else because you have empathy for being on the other side.
alts.zh: 我真心覺得最好的產品經理很多都是從別的領域轉過來的，因為你真的體會過站在另一邊是什麼感覺。

cards.quote: And then there is an art to learning how to push somebody without competing with them. And I think a lot of the times I've seen the CPO CEO relationship go badly. It ends up with the CPO is competing with the CEO for vision and they end up at loggerheads.
cards.zh: 怎麼推對方一把、又不變成跟他競爭，這是一門功夫。我看過很多 CPO 跟 CEO 關係搞砸，都是因為 CPO 在跟 CEO 搶願景。
cards.why: push somebody vs compete with somebody 這組區別是向上管理的核心。there is an art to X 這個開場也很好用：它宣告接下來講的是難以言傳的手感，聽的人就會放下防衛、進入學習模式。
swaps: You can challenge the thinking without contesting the ownership.
Push on the logic, not on whose vision it is.
cards.pmNote: 在創辦人主導的公司，你的工作是把他的直覺翻譯成現實，不是替換掉他的直覺。
cards.episode: This CPO regrets that product management exists | Tom Verrilli (CPO of Whatnot)

alts.quote: And then our CEO gets in, and he's like, "I think really number four is the only reasonable one for these reasons."
alts.zh: 然後我們執行長進來說：「我認為真正合理的其實只有第四個，理由如下。」

alts.quote: I'm curious what you think. I still don't think ideas are worth as much as maybe a lot of people think. I still think execution is really hard.
alts.zh: 我反而想聽你怎麼看。我還是不覺得點子有大家講的那麼值錢，我還是覺得執行才難。

alts.quote: He just had an episode recently about a skeptical take on AI that I disagreed with a lot, but it was really interesting to think about it from a different perspective.
alts.zh: 他最近那集講了一個對 AI 很懷疑的觀點，我非常不同意，但從另一個角度想這件事真的很有意思。

cards.quote: I think maybe on the flip side of less positive is what it definitely learned is most of the time you hear it's really complex, it isn't. Leadership's just weak.
cards.zh: 我確實學到的是：多數時候你聽到「這件事很複雜」，其實它不複雜。只是領導層軟弱而已。
cards.why: Most of the time you hear X, it isn't 是一個很強的懷疑句型，把「複雜」當成一種需要被檢驗的說法而不是事實。中間插一句 nobody died 的黑色幽默，讓這種挑戰不至於太硬。
swaps: "It's complicated" is often code for "no one wants to decide."
Nine times out of ten, complexity is a stand-in for reluctance.
cards.pmNote: Twitter 花了三年多才把 140 字上限拿掉——所有人都知道該做，只是沒人願意拍板。
cards.episode: This CPO regrets that product management exists | Tom Verrilli (CPO of Whatnot)

alts.quote: It's one thing to say you're spending a lot of time looking outside the building. It's a whole other thing to hear from the places you don't normally hear from.
alts.zh: 說自己花很多時間在公司外面看，是一回事；真的去聽那些你平常聽不到的聲音，完全是另一回事。

alts.quote: It's funny that everyone complained about Google as this really, really smart, all-knowing LLM, and at the same time, they think they're dumb enough to fall for these guest posts.
alts.zh: 很好笑的是，大家一邊抱怨 Google 是那種超級聰明、什麼都知道的 LLM，一邊又覺得它笨到會被這些客座文章騙過去。

alts.quote: So I think it is an utter waste of time for marketing to build these stupid little one pager persona things.
alts.zh: 所以我覺得行銷花時間做那些一頁式的 persona 小卡，根本是浪費時間。

cards.pattern: I don't think this is right. I'm going to clear the rest of my day. Let's sit and figure it out.
cards.quote: he'll sit in a review and be like, "I don't think this is right." And then he'll pause and say, "I'm going to clear the rest of my day. Let's sit and figure it out."
cards.zh: 他會在評審會上說：「我覺得這不對。」然後停一下說：「我把今天剩下的行程清掉，我們一起坐下來把它弄清楚。」
cards.why: 否決之後立刻用自己的時間補上，把「我不同意」變成「我陪你解」。I'm going to clear the rest of my day 是英語職場最有份量的一句承諾——它花的是說話者的成本，不是聽者的。
swaps: I'm not convinced — let's block the afternoon and work it through.
Rather than send you away, let's solve it here.
cards.pmNote: 評審會不該是「求綠燈」；把它變成一起找答案，PM 就不必為了信用而護航爛方案。
cards.episode: This CPO regrets that product management exists | Tom Verrilli (CPO of Whatnot)

alts.quote: I'm going to come back to what you've learned about what makes super successful PMs, what makes you really successful. I want to take a tangent to Zuck.
alts.zh: 成功 PM 的特質這題我等一下會繞回來。我想先岔題聊一下 Zuck。

alts.quote: Now that you've agreed among yourselves that you're going to do that for a fixed period of time, everyone go around the room and say, "If I could start this company over again the thing I wish we were doing was."
alts.zh: 既然大家已經同意用一段固定的時間來試，那就一個一個講：「如果能重來一次，我希望我們在做的是＿＿＿。」

alts.quote: "I need 20 minutes of focused time to interrogate something that I've done. We're not going to talk. I'm literally going to force us into a room or Zoom.
alts.zh: 「我需要二十分鐘的專注時間來拷問我做的東西。我們不用講話。我就是要把大家關進一個會議室或 Zoom。」

cards.pattern: Whatever is required to most effectively [目標] is the short answer.
cards.quote: Whatever is required to most effectively ship is the short answer. Have I personally shipped some production code at Whatnot? Yes.
cards.zh: 簡短的答案是：出貨需要什麼我就做什麼。我自己在 Whatnot 有沒有推過正式環境的程式碼？有。
cards.why: 先給一句可以直接引用的短答（…is the short answer），再用自問自答補細節。這種「短答＋自問自答」是英語訪談與會議裡收放自如的節奏控制，聽者隨時可以喊停。
swaps: The short answer is whatever unblocks the ship date.
Short version: I do the work the outcome needs.
cards.pmNote: PM 寫程式的價值多半在「理解程式碼」而不是「提交程式碼」——後者你會踩光工程師 L4 就學會避開的坑。
cards.episode: This CPO regrets that product management exists | Tom Verrilli (CPO of Whatnot)

alts.quote: And the right answer to these narrowly scoped defined problems is not to invent a whole new print dialogue.
alts.zh: 面對這種範圍很窄、已經定義清楚的問題，正確答案並不是重新發明一整套列印對話框。

alts.quote: Is it a better outcome to just ship more faster now, but most of the things aren't impactful? Or is it a better outcome to ship fewer things but really work on making sure that you're shipping them in the best way?
alts.zh: 到底哪個結果比較好：現在拚命多出貨，但大部分都沒什麼影響力？還是少做幾件，但每一件都確保做到最好？

alts.quote: HubSpot, SAP, whatever you want, you've got 10% of the budget, you've got a hundred story points, whatever metric or heuristic you use, but you've got to decide now each quarter
alts.zh: HubSpot、SAP，你要哪個都行，你有 10% 的額度、一百個 story point，隨你怎麼算——但你這一季現在就得決定。

cards.quote: I actually think it's easier. Spicy take.
cards.zh: 我其實覺得更容易。這個看法比較嗆。
cards.why: Spicy take 是先幫自己的話貼標籤（＝我知道這不主流），聽眾就會用「聽個新鮮觀點」的心態接收，而不是「這人不懂行情」。兩個字，換掉整段的接收框架。
swaps: Hot take, but hear me out:
Contrarian view — and I might be wrong:
cards.pmNote: Tom 的算法：與其養一整層 PM 金字塔，不如用同樣的錢請三個能自己交付的資深 IC。
cards.episode: This CPO regrets that product management exists | Tom Verrilli (CPO of Whatnot)

alts.quote: I think a lot of people think about markets almost like these bodies of water. And it's like, "Oh, it's this big body of water that we're going after." And I actually think that the most interesting markets, you have to think of them like currents.
alts.zh: 很多人把市場想成一片水域，覺得「喔，我們要去攻的是這一大片水」。但我覺得最有意思的市場，你得把它想成水流。

alts.quote: I'll just run this as a thought experiment and you can see what you think on this, but it's like, are AI models themselves defensible?
alts.zh: 我把它當成一個思想實驗丟出來，你自己判斷——AI 模型本身到底有沒有護城河？

alts.quote: The old way I think is shitty. I think it's broken, and I haven't found anything out there that is innovating on this.
alts.zh: 舊的做法我覺得很爛。我覺得它是壞的，而且我沒看到市面上有任何人在改良它。

cards.pattern: [做法] would be my push.
cards.quote: Start doing IC work in the role you're in would be my push. Get back to the basics of make sure that you're taking on practical work.
cards.zh: 我會建議的是：在你現在這個職位上就開始做 IC 的工作。回到基本功，確保你手上有實作的事情。
cards.why: 把建議放在句尾用 would be my push 收，比開頭就下命令柔軟得多。push 這個名詞用法（我會推你往這邊）保留了「你可以不接受」的空間，是資深主管給建議的常見語氣。
swaps: My push would be to start before you switch jobs.
If I were advising you, I'd start there.
cards.pmNote: 在現職就把 IC 肌肉練回來——這件事對你現在的位置也有幫助，不只是為了下一份工作。
cards.episode: This CPO regrets that product management exists | Tom Verrilli (CPO of Whatnot)

alts.quote: It might actually mean a proactive conversation with your manager or the leadership to say, "I love what I'm doing here, and I would also like to learn a little bit more. And here's what I'm interested in."
alts.zh: 這可能只是主動找主管或高層談一次，跟他說：「我很喜歡現在做的事，同時我也想再多學一些，這是我有興趣的方向。」

alts.quote: This is people you used to work with before, go ask them, "Hey, what did I do well, what do you think my strengths are? What do you think I'm a fit for?
alts.zh: 去問以前的同事：「我哪裡做得好？你覺得我的強項是什麼？我是這樣想的——你覺得我對自己的認知準確嗎？」

alts.quote: So especially when you're meeting with a new engineering team for the first time, actually ask them, what is one thing I can do to help you this week?
alts.zh: 尤其是第一次跟新的工程團隊碰面時，真的去問他們：這禮拜我可以幫上哪一件事？

cards.pattern: I'm obviously limited on what exactly I can share, but it is true that [可以講的那一半]
cards.quote: I'm obviously limited on what exactly I can share, but it is true that our retention numbers are really exciting and that is actually the thing we look at.
cards.zh: 我能講的東西確實有限，不過可以說的是，我們的留存數字真的很好看，而且那正是我們在看的指標。
cards.why: 台灣人碰到「不能講」通常只會說 I can't say，對話就死了。母語者的做法是先承認限制（limited on what I can share），立刻用 but it is true that 交出一塊真的有資訊量的東西。你守住了保密，也沒讓對方空手而回。
swaps: There's only so much I can get into, but what I can say is...
I can't give you the exact number, but directionally...
cards.pmNote: 被問到不能揭露的指標時，給「方向」不給「數值」是業界慣例——講 trend 不講 absolute。
cards.episode: Inside ChatGPT: The fastest-growing product in history | Nick Turley (Head of ChatGPT at OpenAI)

alts.quote: Those are just numbers I'm putting out there. It's always going to be a gut call based on where you are.
alts.zh: 那些數字只是我隨口丟出來的。這終究是看你所在的位置做的直覺判斷。

alts.quote: I'm not sure that it matches exactly to functions, but I can tell you what we're seeing more of, we need more of.
alts.zh: 我不確定這能不能剛好對到各個職能，但我可以告訴你我們看到什麼在變多、我們需要什麼變多。

alts.quote: And it could be actually we don't know what moves retention.
alts.zh: 也有可能，其實我們根本不知道什麼會影響留存。

cards.quote: I'll let you know when we figure it out. We're hiring. I think there's so many interesting product problems here.
cards.zh: 等我們想通了再告訴你。我們還在徵人，這裡真的有一堆很有意思的產品問題。
cards.why: 把「我不知道」講成一個未來的承諾而不是現在的缺口——I'll let you know when 預設了「終究會知道」。後面立刻補一句有能量的話（we're hiring），整段從示弱翻轉成自信。這句短到可以背起來當萬用擋箭牌。
swaps: Ask me again in six months.
We're still working through that one—I'll circle back when we have a view.
cards.pmNote: 產品願景被追問細節時，坦承「還沒答案」比硬編一個 roadmap 安全得多——編出來的都會變成別人拿來考核你的承諾。
cards.episode: Inside ChatGPT: The fastest-growing product in history | Nick Turley (Head of ChatGPT at OpenAI)

alts.quote: And I don't know exactly when that will be, but I think we're pretty close.
alts.zh: 我不知道確切會是什麼時候，但我覺得已經很接近了。

alts.quote: I don't think we should filter out AI content. I think we should let you know if content is AI content or not. That's hard, by the way.
alts.zh: 我不認為我們該把 AI 內容濾掉。我認為該做的是讓你知道這則內容是不是 AI 產的。順帶一提，這很難。

alts.quote: I don't know about you, but literally every time I think to do this, there's a fight in my head of like, "Ah, do I really need to work out today?
alts.zh: 我不知道你怎麼樣，但我每次想到要做這件事，腦子裡都會吵一架：欸，我今天真的需要運動嗎？

cards.pattern: my advice is super lame, which is [建議], which is not as actionable as [對方] would ideally like
cards.quote: And for that reason, my advice is super lame, which is make really high quality content, which is not as actionable as I think people making content would ideally like.
cards.zh: 所以我的建議很沒創意，就是做出真正高品質的內容——我知道這對做內容的人來說不夠具體可執行。
cards.why: 他自己先替對方把吐槽講完（super lame、not as actionable as you'd like），對方就無話可說了。這叫「自嘲式先制」：先認領建議的弱點，聽起來反而像誠實而不是敷衍。台灣人常反過來——把弱建議包裝得很厲害，結果被戳破更難看。
swaps: I know this is a boring answer, but...
This is going to sound unsatisfying, and I'm aware of that:
cards.pmNote: 給不出戰術層建議時，明講「這只是原則不是 playbook」，可以避免對方照著做卻沒效果而回頭怪你。
cards.episode: Inside ChatGPT: The fastest-growing product in history | Nick Turley (Head of ChatGPT at OpenAI)

alts.quote: But before that, I think getting to product-market fit, obviously there's a lot of methodology for doing it today that might make it a bit easier for people, but I still think it's fairly random and pretty dang hard.
alts.zh: 在那之前——我覺得要走到 PMF，現在當然有很多方法論可能讓大家輕鬆一點，但我還是認為它相當隨機，而且真的很難。

alts.quote: But what I think that misses is, it assumes that you go and you do this analyst job for two years, and at the end of it you have a person who knows how to make models really well.
alts.zh: 但我覺得這個說法漏掉了一件事：它預設你得先當兩年分析師，兩年之後才會長出一個很會建模型的人。

alts.quote: One of the comments was, "Benedict, this is 80 slides of saying we don't know," which is slightly facetious, but also kind of true.
alts.zh: 有人留言說：「Benedict，你這 80 張投影片就是在講『我們不知道』。」講得有點壞，但也算是實話。

cards.pattern: Definitely don't bring me on here as a [領域] expert, I think you have got better people for that.
cards.quote: Definitely don't bring me on here as a pricing expert, I think you have got better people for that.
cards.zh: 千萬別把我當定價專家找來，這題你應該去找更懂的人。
cards.why: 剛講完一個很成功的定價故事，馬上主動卸下「專家」這個頭銜。母語者在職場上很會做這件事——你可以分享經驗，但不接受一個你撐不住的標籤。台灣人常見的失誤是默默接下標籤，之後被問到深處就崩。
swaps: Don't take this as expert advice—it's just what happened to work for us.
I'm a sample size of one on this.
cards.pmNote: 分享做法時要區分「我們的做法」與「最佳實務」，否則會被當成 benchmark 反過來要求你負責。
cards.episode: Inside ChatGPT: The fastest-growing product in history | Nick Turley (Head of ChatGPT at OpenAI)

alts.quote: I'll admit I'm definitely not an SEO expert. I've been fortunate to work with some of the best marketers in the world who I think are bonafide legends at this point
alts.zh: 我坦白說我絕對不是 SEO 專家。我只是很幸運跟一些世界頂尖的行銷人共事過，那些人到今天都算是真正的傳奇。

alts.quote: And again, I'm not an expert in this and I think Erin Meyer wrote that book, The Culture Map. So you should just find what those people wrote because they're much smarter than I am about this.
alts.zh: 再說一次，我不是這方面的專家。Erin Meyer 寫過《文化地圖》那本書，你們應該直接去看他們寫的，他們比我懂太多了。

alts.quote: I don't think we should filter out AI content. I think we should let you know if content is AI content or not. That's hard, by the way.
alts.zh: 我不認為我們該把 AI 內容濾掉。我認為該做的是讓你知道這則內容是不是 AI 產的。順帶一提，這很難。

cards.pattern: I'm baffled by [A]. Even more baffled by [更誇張的 B].
cards.quote: I'm baffled by how much it took off as a concept. Even more baffled by how many people have copied the paradigm rather than trying out a different way of interacting with AI.
cards.zh: 這個概念會紅成這樣，我到現在都想不通。更想不通的是，怎麼那麼多人直接照抄，而不是去試別的跟 AI 互動的方式。
cards.why: baffled 是「困惑到說不出話」，比 surprised 強、比 confused 有格調。重點在第二句只用 Even more baffled by 開頭、省略主詞動詞——這種省略是口語裡加強語氣的節奏技巧，寫下來反而不對。
swaps: It still puzzles me how... And what puzzles me more is...
I genuinely don't understand why... Even less why...
cards.pmNote: 自家產品爆紅卻說不出所以然，是誠實訊號；假裝一切都在計畫中的 PM，通常學不到下一次成功的原因。
cards.episode: Inside ChatGPT: The fastest-growing product in history | Nick Turley (Head of ChatGPT at OpenAI)

alts.quote: I don't know how many customer support folks we have, but it's not very many, 30, 40, I'm not sure, way smaller than you would have at any comparable company, and it's because we've automated a lot of our flows.
alts.zh: 我不知道我們有多少客服人力，但沒有很多，三十、四十吧，我不確定，總之比任何同等規模的公司都少很多，因為我們把很多流程自動化了。

alts.quote: We're going to go off and make this two-year, five-year, whatever, 10-year vision even, and we're going to point us towards something." But the way that the technology is changing now, we don't know what's going to happen in two years.
alts.zh: 我們本來會去做那種兩年、五年甚至十年的願景，把大家指向某個方向，但以現在技術變化的速度，我們根本不知道兩年後會發生什麼事。

alts.quote: I mean, I think Things probably, I'm just guessing, I don't know any of the numbers or whatever, but I would assume it makes between five and $25 million of revenue, which to a VC is not even worth considering a VC.
alts.zh: 我是說，Things 這款——我純粹在猜，數字我完全不知道——但我猜它一年營收大概在五百萬到兩千五百萬美金之間，這種規模對創投來說根本不值得看。

cards.pattern: We get a lot of crap for [某個爛設計], and I own it.
cards.quote: We get a lot of crap for the model chooser, and I own it. I've tried to say that to everyone who will listen.
cards.zh: 模型選單被罵翻，這我認。我逢人就講這件事是我的責任。
cards.why: I own it 是英語職場最短、最有份量的認錯句，三個字結案，不解釋不辯護。前面用 get a lot of crap for 把外界批評如實引述（不美化成 feedback），可信度立刻上來。台灣人習慣先解釋再認錯，順序顛倒就沒了力道。
swaps: That one's on me.
We've taken a lot of heat for that, and rightly so.
cards.pmNote: 公開認領一個已知爛設計，可以讓團隊不必再花力氣替它辯護，直接進到「怎麼修」。
cards.episode: Inside ChatGPT: The fastest-growing product in history | Nick Turley (Head of ChatGPT at OpenAI)

alts.quote: I don't want them to leave it at, "It was a big loss." You want to say, "What I learned from that is now I always run a load test, and I've had many successful launches since then."
alts.zh: 我不希望他只停在「那是一次很大的損失」。你應該說：我從那件事學到，現在我一定會先跑壓力測試，後來的好幾次上線都沒再出過同樣的問題。

alts.quote: The biggest mistakes I've made have been going into business models where other people have repeatedly failed and thinking, I can do this better.
alts.zh: 我犯過最大的錯，都是跳進那種別人一再失敗的商業模式，然後心想：我可以做得比他們好。

alts.quote: But what can you do, if not look back on it and say, "Yeah, I was wrong.
alts.zh: 那你還能怎麼辦呢？不就是回頭看著它說一句：對，我那時錯了。

cards.pattern: What happened is that we pushed out an update that made [產品] more likely to [壞行為]
cards.quote: But basically what happened is that we pushed out an update that made the model more likely to tell you things that sound good in the moment.
cards.zh: 簡單講就是，我們推了一個更新，結果讓模型更容易講出那種當下聽起來很順耳的話。
cards.why: 事故說明的黃金結構：主詞是 we（不是 the system / a bug），動詞是主動的 pushed out，然後平鋪直敘描述後果。全句沒有一個形容詞在替自己緩頰。what happened is that 這個開場也很好用——宣告接下來是事實敘述，不是立場。
swaps: What went wrong was that we shipped a change that...
The short version is: we rolled out an update that...
cards.pmNote: postmortem 的第一段一定要用主動語態指出「誰做了什麼」，被動語態（a change was made）是逃避責任的訊號。
cards.episode: Inside ChatGPT: The fastest-growing product in history | Nick Turley (Head of ChatGPT at OpenAI)

alts.quote: Yeah, I messed up. But I know I'm still a good person and a good worker. Yes, I made a mistake, but I'm going to move on.
alts.zh: 對，我搞砸了。但我知道我還是個好人、也還是個好的工作者。對，我犯了錯，但我要往前走。

alts.quote: I got to tell you, I had no idea how unique we were until I was outside and there are so many things.
alts.zh: 我得說，直到我離開之後，我才知道我們當時有多特殊——太多事情都是。

alts.quote: you eventually need to convince yourself that there is a difference between you not being good at something and a business or company not needing that thing at a particular moment in time
alts.zh: 你終究得說服自己：「你不擅長某件事」跟「公司此刻不需要那件事」，是兩回事。

cards.pattern: It's [負面形容], but that's strictly less bad than [替代方案的代價].
cards.quote: You know what? We should ship. It's embarrassing, but that's strictly less bad than not getting the feedback you wanted.
cards.zh: 我覺得就出吧。是很難看沒錯，但這比拿不到你要的回饋還是好一點。
cards.why: strictly less bad 是精算式的英文——不宣稱「這是好事」，只宣稱「在兩個壞選項裡它比較不壞」。這種「比爛」框架特別適合報壞消息：你沒有粉飾，也沒有讓對方覺得沒得選。embarrassing 先自認難看，也堵住了對方要講的第一句話。
swaps: It's not pretty, but it beats the alternative.
This is the least bad option on the table.
cards.pmNote: 決策不是在好與壞之間選，多數時候是在兩個壞之間選——把選項的代價攤開講，比推銷「這是好方案」更有說服力。
cards.episode: Inside ChatGPT: The fastest-growing product in history | Nick Turley (Head of ChatGPT at OpenAI)

alts.quote: It's so hard to give a founder hard feedback. Who wants to be the bearer of bad news?
alts.zh: 要給創辦人難聽的回饋真的很難。誰想當那個報壞消息的人？

alts.quote: And the good news bad news is that's true. That is absolutely true.
alts.zh: 好消息也是壞消息：那是真的。千真萬確。

alts.quote: Nobody wants to hear it. Everybody wants to just think about these really cool models and how smart they are. But really it's just the hard work of getting really good data to the LLMs.
alts.zh: 沒有人想聽這個。大家都只想談那些很酷的模型有多聰明。但說到底，這就是把好資料餵給 LLM 的苦工。

cards.pattern: The thing you can't really express in [常見的衡量方式] is [真正重要的東西]
cards.quote: But again, the thing you can't really express in use cases or data is the vibe of the model.
cards.zh: 但話說回來，用案例或數據講不出來的那個東西，才是這個模型的「感覺」。
cards.why: 用「現有工具測不到」來定義一個問題，是資深者的招式：先承認既有衡量方式（use cases、data）的邊界，再把注意力導到那個沒被測到的東西。這比直接說「vibe 很重要」有力太多，因為你已經解釋了為什麼大家沒注意到它。
swaps: What doesn't show up in the numbers is...
The part our metrics can't capture is...
cards.pmNote: 指標抓不到的東西不代表不存在——把「未被衡量」明講出來，才有機會爭取資源去建新的衡量方式。
cards.episode: Inside ChatGPT: The fastest-growing product in history | Nick Turley (Head of ChatGPT at OpenAI)

alts.quote: We call this Right for Wrong, doing the right thing for the wrong reason, where the right thing may be completing the flow, but the wrong reason is seeing that error message go away.
alts.zh: 我們把這個叫做「對事錯因」——用錯誤的理由做對的事。對的事可能是完成流程，錯的理由是想讓那個錯誤訊息消失。

alts.quote: And so then the first few pages became very much more problem-based because if people don't understand the problem then they can't understand or care about your solution.
alts.zh: 所以前面幾頁後來就大改成以「問題」為主，因為人如果不懂那個問題，就不可能懂、也不可能在乎你的解法。

alts.quote: But you take the thing you're responsible for and you just do one zoom out of the problem you're solving and question that.
alts.zh: 你就拿你負責的那件事，把你在解的問題往外拉一層，然後質疑那一層。

cards.pattern: [現況] feels a little bit like [舊時代的東西]. We haven't built [新時代的東西] yet, and it'll be obvious once we do.
cards.quote: I still feel like ChatGPT feels a little bit like MS-DOS, like we haven't built Windows yet. And it'll be obvious once we do.
cards.zh: 我還是覺得 ChatGPT 有點像 MS-DOS——我們的 Windows 還沒做出來。而且一旦做出來，大家馬上就會知道那就是了。
cards.why: 用歷史上「大家都知道結局」的類比講願景，聽者不必相信你的預測，只要相信歷史會重演。最狠的是最後那句 it'll be obvious once we do——把「我說不清楚那是什麼」轉成一種自信，而不是心虛。
swaps: We're still at the command-line stage of this.
Today's version is the flip phone; the smartphone hasn't shown up yet.
cards.pmNote: 願景講不清細節時，用「我們在哪個歷史階段」代替「產品長什麼樣」，可以對齊方向而不鎖死解法。
cards.episode: Inside ChatGPT: The fastest-growing product in history | Nick Turley (Head of ChatGPT at OpenAI)

alts.quote: Obviously, I skew very heavily towards earned channels just because once you stand that up, that's a gift that just keeps on giving and nobody can take that away from you.
alts.zh: 我明顯偏向自有通路，因為那個東西一旦架起來，就是一份會一直給你回報的禮物，而且沒有人拿得走。

alts.quote: And I think the thing that I love about a crazy big goal is that you feel completely inadequate before it.
alts.zh: 我最喜歡「瘋狂大目標」的一點，就是站在它面前你會覺得自己完全不夠格。

alts.quote: And he would say, you have to aim for Chartres. You have to make something that is better than that. That should be your goal, not to just turn in something that's what you feel is good enough.
alts.zh: 他會說：你要對準夏特大教堂。你要做出比它更好的東西。那才是你的目標，而不是交出一個你自己覺得「還可以」的作品。

cards.pattern: You absolutely should [做 X], but you won't know [關鍵資訊] until after you [動作].
cards.quote: You absolutely should polish things like the model output, but you won't know what to polish until after you ship.
cards.zh: 該打磨的東西當然要打磨，像是模型輸出；但你要磨哪裡，得等出貨之後才會知道。
cards.why: 先把對方的價值觀完整接住（You absolutely should polish），再指出一個「順序問題」而非「對錯問題」。這是說服品質派最有效的角度：我不是叫你別做，我是說你現在做的時間點不對。absolutely 這個副詞在這裡是真心的，不是諷刺。
swaps: It's not that quality doesn't matter—it's that you're guessing until you ship.
Craft matters, but you need real usage to know where to spend it.
cards.pmNote: 在需求不明的階段投入打磨，本質是在賭你猜對了使用場景——多數時候賭輸。
cards.episode: Inside ChatGPT: The fastest-growing product in history | Nick Turley (Head of ChatGPT at OpenAI)

alts.quote: We should probably not do things that would've been invented by everybody else 10 minutes later. Where are the problems that are not solving themselves?
alts.zh: 我們大概不該去做那些晚十分鐘別人也會做出來的東西。真正該問的是：哪些問題是不會自己被解決的？

alts.quote: I think so many folks don't know where to begin on starting a startup, and my tactical advice is start doing customer validation first versus building a PowerPoint deck.
alts.zh: 很多人根本不知道創業要從哪裡開始，我很具體的建議是：先去做客戶驗證，而不是先做一份簡報。

alts.quote: One of the most important things that we did was we didn't really worry about competitors at all. We actually just saw where is there a gap in the market that we can uniquely fill
alts.zh: 我們做過最重要的一件事，就是根本不太管競爭對手。我們只看市場上哪裡有一個缺口，是我們可以獨一無二補上的。

cards.pattern: I also think it would be easy to use all what I just said as an excuse not to [對方擔心的事].
cards.quote: I also think it would be easy to use all what I just said as an excuse not to eventually build a great product.
cards.zh: 我也覺得，我剛剛講的那些很容易被拿來當藉口，變成「反正最後也不用做出好產品」。
cards.why: 講完一套可能被濫用的主張後，自己先把濫用方式點名。這招在英語職場叫「封住後門」——你堵住了最惡意的解讀，聽者反而更願意接受你原本的主張。台灣人常等到被人濫用了才回頭澄清，那時已經來不及。
swaps: I can see how this gets misused as a licence to ship junk.
To be clear, this isn't permission to stop caring about quality.
cards.pmNote: 推「快速出貨」文化時務必配一句「這不等於降低標準」，否則三個月後你會收到一堆用你的話當擋箭牌的爛東西。
cards.episode: Inside ChatGPT: The fastest-growing product in history | Nick Turley (Head of ChatGPT at OpenAI)

alts.quote: And I think one of the monikers we use internally is no, then go. As in just think through all the things that could go wrong, understand where scale will break, understand the things that might happen, and then move on anyway.
alts.zh: 我們內部有個口號叫「先說不，然後走」。把所有可能出錯的地方都想過一輪，知道規模在哪裡會斷，然後照樣往前。

alts.quote: To me, I think it's a great accelerant when it's already working, but it can't fix it if people don't want to talk about your product.
alts.zh: 對我來說，那在本來就跑得動的時候是很好的加速器，但如果根本沒人想談論你的產品，它救不了你。

alts.quote: Actually, all feedback I think is valid. People's feelings are valid, but it doesn't mean that you need to do something about all of those things.
alts.zh: 其實我覺得所有回饋都是有效的。別人的感受都是真的，但這不代表你每一項都得去處理。

cards.pattern: So, yes on [X], but no on [Y], is where I would describe my point of view.
cards.quote: So, yes on natural language, but no on chat is where I would describe my point of view.
cards.zh: 所以自然語言我贊成，但聊天介面我不贊成——這大概是我的立場。
cards.why: 把一個被綁在一起的概念拆成兩半，一半贊成一半反對，再用 is where I would describe my point of view 把它降級成「我的看法」而非定論。整句只有十幾個字，卻同時完成了拆解、表態、留餘地三件事。這是會議收斂的高效句。
swaps: I'm with you on the first half, not the second.
Agree on the principle, disagree on the format.
cards.pmNote: 很多爭論其實是兩個議題被綁在一起——拆開之後常會發現雙方在一半的事上早就同意了。
cards.episode: Inside ChatGPT: The fastest-growing product in history | Nick Turley (Head of ChatGPT at OpenAI)

alts.quote: I think some controversy is necessary and so I may be at a different point on that one.
alts.zh: 我覺得某種程度的爭議是必要的，所以這一題我的位置可能跟大家不太一樣。

alts.quote: So, I think one needs to be a little bit cautious on what Dario says. And that's setting aside the cynical view that he's just doing that department stock, which I don't believe at all.
alts.zh: 我覺得對 Dario 講的話要保留一點。而且我這裡還先撇開那種比較酸的解讀——說他只是在替自家股價講話——那我完全不相信。

alts.quote: I think if you're building a product where it's not necessarily an AI- first product and you have some AI features that are on the side, but it's not the core of your value, I don't know that I would operate this way.
alts.zh: 如果你做的不是 AI 優先的產品，只是旁邊掛幾個 AI 功能、AI 不是核心價值，那我不確定我會這樣做。

cards.pattern: It's not that you actually [做 X], but it gives you [心理效果]
cards.quote: It's not that you actually are going to watch it the whole time, but it gives you a mental model and makes you feel in control.
cards.zh: 並不是說你真的會全程盯著看，而是它讓你有一個心智模型，讓你覺得自己掌握著方向盤。
cards.why: 解釋一個「看起來沒用」的設計時，先誠實承認它字面上的用途不成立（It's not that you actually...），再把真正的價值放到心理層。這個先自拆再重建的順序，讓對方沒機會先提出質疑。
swaps: Nobody actually reads it—but knowing it's there changes how you feel.
The point isn't the information, it's the sense of control.
cards.pmNote: 自動化產品的信任感常來自「可觀察性」而不是「可控性」——讓用戶看得到過程，比讓他真的介入更重要。
cards.episode: Inside ChatGPT: The fastest-growing product in history | Nick Turley (Head of ChatGPT at OpenAI)

alts.quote: We use words to establish a perspective in a way of thinking about the world. And if those are the words that are in your head, then you feel like it's this war.
alts.zh: 我們用字詞來建立一種看世界的角度。如果你腦袋裡裝的是那些字，你就會覺得這是一場戰爭。

alts.quote: You feel like a broken record, right? You're like, "I've said this 45 times." Turns out no one heard you the first 43.
alts.zh: 你會覺得自己像跳針的唱片：「這件事我講過四十五次了。」結果是前四十三次根本沒人聽進去。

alts.quote: But before you do that, you should think about, "Is this a problem I can invest five to 10 years into actually solving? Do I care deeply enough about it?"
alts.zh: 但在那之前你該先想：這是不是一個我願意投入五到十年去真正解決的問題？我對它在乎得夠深嗎？

cards.pattern: You've got to do [A], you've got to do [B], if you want to be a serious player. And those are just non-negotiable.
cards.quote: You've got to do HIPAA, you got to do SOC 2, you've got to do all those things if you want to be a serious player. And those are just non-negotiable.
cards.zh: HIPAA 要做、SOC 2 要做，這些全都得做，你才算是玩真的。這些就是沒得談。
cards.why: non-negotiable 是英語職場結束討論最乾淨的一個詞——不是「我不想談」，是「這件事本來就不在談判桌上」。前面先用 if you want to be a serious player 把標準外部化成行業門檻，讓你的堅持不像個人偏好。
swaps: That one's table stakes—it's not on the table.
There's no version of this where we skip that.
cards.pmNote: 把 compliance 類需求標成 non-negotiable 並放進基準線，可以省下每季重新爭辯一次的成本。
cards.episode: Inside ChatGPT: The fastest-growing product in history | Nick Turley (Head of ChatGPT at OpenAI)
