alts.quote: Pulling off other responsibilities is no problem. It's a good thing to do, especially as you grow, but never when you touch those three sacred things.
alts.zh: 把其他職責分出去完全沒問題，隨著規模變大這反而是好事——但前提是不能碰到那三件神聖不可讓的事。

alts.quote: All 25 have to want the same thing. If one person's out, you just don't do it at all.
alts.zh: 二十五個人得要的是同一件事。只要有一個人不要，那這個東西就整個不做。

alts.quote: I don't think it's particularly productive to say, "Well, is it 20% bigger than the internet or 100%?" Those aren't productive conversations.
alts.zh: 去爭「它比網路大 20% 還是 100%」我覺得沒什麼意義，那種對話不會有產出。

cards.pattern: This is not something I'd ever say about myself. It's nice that someone else would say it, but [降溫]
cards.quote: Yeah, this is not something I'd ever say about myself. It's nice that someone else would say it, but it's a mysterious thing.
cards.zh: 這種話我自己絕對講不出口。有別人這樣說當然開心，不過這東西其實挺玄的。
cards.why: 接住讚美的三步：拒絕自封（I'd never say that about myself）、感謝來源（it's nice that someone else would）、然後把話題轉回內容本身。整段沒有一句 no no no 的假謙虛，卻完全沒有自誇的姿態。這是英語職場處理稱讚最安全的公式。
swaps: That's generous of them—I wouldn't claim that myself.
I'll take the compliment, but I'm not sure I'd describe it that way.
cards.pmNote: 被公開稱讚時把功勞轉回具體做法而非個人特質，既謙虛又順便傳播了做法本身。
cards.episode: Inside ChatGPT: The fastest-growing product in history | Nick Turley (Head of ChatGPT at OpenAI)

alts.quote: It's making what I would consider real money. Is it a venture scale thing? No. Does it need to be? No. I have a ambitious but not audacious goal for ChatPRD.
alts.zh: 它有在賺我認為是真的錢。是那種創投等級的規模嗎？不是。需要是嗎？也不需要。我對 ChatPRD 的目標是有企圖心，但不到誇張。

alts.quote: Well, it's very generous of you. I wouldn't say... look, we've done some really good work, some good work so far at YouTube, and it's been a journey.
alts.zh: 你太抬舉我了。我不會這樣講啦——我們在 YouTube 是做了一些不錯的成績，過程也蠻曲折的。

alts.quote: Well, first of all, thank you for saying all that. That's giving me too much credit, but I like the idea that it's going to balance out the too little credit I ostensibly get somewhere else, that's great.
alts.zh: 首先謝謝你這樣說。你太抬舉我了——不過我喜歡這個說法，就當作是補回我在別的地方被低估的部分吧。

cards.pattern: I love [高強度的事], but in order to do that with confidence, I need [你要的資源]
cards.quote: I love setting a fast pace at the company, but in order to do that with confidence, I need at least one day every week that I'm entirely unplugged.
cards.zh: 我很喜歡替公司設一個快節奏，但要有信心這樣衝，我每週至少需要一天完全斷線。
cards.why: 要資源（這裡是時間）的最佳姿勢：先證明你認同組織的目標（I love setting a fast pace），再把需求包裝成「達成那個目標的必要條件」而不是個人福利。in order to do that with confidence 這半句是關鍵鉸鏈，缺了它就變成在討休假。
swaps: I'm all in on the timeline—to hit it I need one more engineer.
I can commit to that, provided I get X.
cards.pmNote: 爭取資源時把需求綁在對方在乎的目標上（而非你的負擔上），拒絕的成本就轉嫁到對方身上了。
cards.episode: Inside ChatGPT: The fastest-growing product in history | Nick Turley (Head of ChatGPT at OpenAI)

alts.quote: I want to make sure I've got air cover from the highest people in the company setting the culture.
alts.zh: 我要確定最高層那些定文化的人會幫我掩護。

alts.quote: Instead of saying, "Look, your span of control, you have nine direct reports, you need leverage here. I have a lot of credibility with this side of the product organization. I think we could be doing more if this position existed."
alts.zh: 換成這樣講：「你看你的管理幅度，你手下有九個直屬，你需要有人幫你分擔。我在產品組織這一邊累積了不少信任。我覺得如果有這個職位，我們可以做得更多。」

alts.quote: When you get the term sheet, you should establish clearly how much time you will need and understand that if you go beyond this deadline, the term sheet could be withdrawn.
alts.zh: 拿到 term sheet 的時候，你應該明確講好你需要多少時間，並且清楚知道超過這個期限，term sheet 是可能被收回的。

cards.pattern: I can't speak to [你沒經歷的部分]. But what I can tell you about [你經歷過的] is [具體感受]
cards.quote: I can't speak to that whole period. But what I can tell you about what I'm feeling now is just an incredible sense of focus and urgency to deliver great products quickly.
cards.zh: 那一整段期間我沒辦法評論。但我可以告訴你現在的感受——一種非常強烈的專注感和急迫感，就是要快點把好產品交出去。
cards.why: I can't speak to X / what I can tell you is Y 是英語職場最實用的一組配對句。前半劃出你沒有第一手資訊的範圍（不是拒答，是誠實），後半立刻交出你確實握有的東西。整個過程沒有任何防禦姿態，聽者反而更信你後半那段。
swaps: I wasn't there for that, so I can't comment—what I can speak to is...
That predates me. What I do know firsthand is...
cards.pmNote: 被問到自己接手前的歷史時，明說「我沒經歷過」比轉述二手版本安全——二手版本出錯時責任會算在你頭上。
cards.episode: Inside Google's AI turnaround: The rise of AI Mode, strategy behind AI Overviews, and their vision for AI-powered search | Robby Stein (VP of Product, Google Search)

alts.quote: So I can't speak to specific clients because I'm not allowed to talk about the work that we've done in large part, but that would be one example.
alts.zh: 我沒辦法談具體的客戶，因為我們做過的案子大部分不能講，但那會是一個例子。

alts.quote: So I worked on Atlas for a bit. I don't work on it now. But a bit of the narrative here for me just to tell my story a bit was...
alts.zh: 我做過 Atlas 一陣子，現在沒在做了。不過就我自己的角度、講一下我的版本的話……

alts.quote: I'm not sure that it matches exactly to functions, but I can tell you what we're seeing more of, we need more of.
alts.zh: 我不確定這能不能剛好對到各個職能，但我可以告訴你我們看到什麼在變多、我們需要什麼變多。

cards.pattern: I don't think there's any one thing. A lot of times people ascribe momentum to a one-time change or a single person.
cards.quote: I don't think there's any one thing that has happened. I think that a lot of times people ascribe a lot of momentum to a one time change or a single person.
cards.zh: 我不覺得有哪一件事是關鍵。很多時候大家會把一整段動能歸給某一次改動、或某一個人。
cards.why: 拒絕回答「關鍵是什麼」這種問題時，不要只說「沒有單一原因」，要順手指出提問背後的認知偏誤（ascribe momentum to a single person）。這樣你的拒答就升級成一個洞見，對方會覺得學到東西而不是被打槍。
swaps: There's rarely a single cause—we tend to over-attribute.
I'd push back on the premise that it was one decision.
cards.pmNote: 成長歸因給單一功能是常見錯誤，會讓團隊重複投資在其實只佔一小部分貢獻的東西上。
cards.episode: Inside Google's AI turnaround: The rise of AI Mode, strategy behind AI Overviews, and their vision for AI-powered search | Robby Stein (VP of Product, Google Search)

alts.quote: It's one thing to say you're spending a lot of time looking outside the building. It's a whole other thing to hear from the places you don't normally hear from.
alts.zh: 說自己花很多時間在公司外面看，是一回事；真的去聽那些你平常聽不到的聲音，完全是另一回事。

alts.quote: And the reason for that is, I don't think there's any reason to assume that human skill level is the cap on anything.
alts.zh: 原因是：我不覺得有任何理由要假設「人類的能力水準」就是天花板。

alts.quote: Well, inherent in your question is this assumption that design takes more time. And so I'm going to kind of reject that premise, because I don't think design takes more time.
alts.zh: 你這個問題裡本身就藏了一個假設：做設計會比較花時間。我要先否掉這個前提，因為我不覺得設計比較花時間。

cards.quote: People come to search for a ridiculously wide set of things. They want a phone number, a price, directions. I think the vastness of that is underappreciated by many people.
cards.zh: 大家來搜尋的東西範圍寬到誇張——找電話、查價格、要路線。我覺得這個「廣度」被太多人低估了。
cards.why: underappreciated 是英語職場講「大家沒看到重點」時最有禮貌的字，不像 people don't understand 那樣把對方講成笨蛋。先給三個具體例子再下這個判斷，順序很重要：證據在前，斷言在後，聽者會自己得出同樣結論。
swaps: I don't think people fully appreciate how broad that is.
This gets consistently underrated.
cards.pmNote: 為既有產品辯護時，用「使用情境的廣度」而非「功能的深度」來反駁「它要被取代了」的論述。
cards.episode: Inside Google's AI turnaround: The rise of AI Mode, strategy behind AI Overviews, and their vision for AI-powered search | Robby Stein (VP of Product, Google Search)

alts.quote: When we talk about pricing, many people quickly gravitate to dollar figures. That's just a price point. But when we think about price, we think about it as a measure.
alts.zh: 談定價的時候，大部分人馬上跳到金額。那只是一個價格點。但我們看「價格」是把它當成一種度量。

alts.quote: Also, price is not just the number on the webpage. It's easy to think that, but how it's structured is just as important, how the product's positioned is just as important.
alts.zh: 還有，價格不是只有網頁上那個數字。很容易這樣以為，但怎麼收費、產品怎麼定位，重要程度完全一樣。

alts.quote: One is people set this goal, I want to be promoted the next thing, or I want to lead this big project. And those are bad goals, because it's not in your control. A good goal is what you can do.
alts.zh: 有一種是設「我要升到下一級」或「我要主導那個大專案」。這些是壞目標，因為不在你的掌控裡。好目標是你自己做得到的事。

cards.pattern: You get to these points of diminishing marginal return where you could put 50 people on it and it's just not going to move the needle.
cards.quote: You get to these points of just diminishing marginal return in every system where it feels like you could put 50 people on this project, it's just not going to dramatically move the needle.
cards.zh: 每個系統都會走到邊際效益遞減的那個點——你感覺得出來，就算再丟 50 個人下去，也不會讓數字有什麼大變化。
cards.why: 講「這裡不值得再投資」時，用經濟學的 diminishing marginal return 而不是「這個沒救了」，指標從主觀判斷變成結構性事實。後半刻意給一個誇張的數字（50 people），讓對方自己去感受投入與產出的落差，比講一堆數據有效。
swaps: We've squeezed most of the juice out of this one.
More headcount here doesn't buy us much anymore.
cards.pmNote: 判斷該不該從成熟功能撤資，看的是「再投入一單位資源能換回多少」，不是這個功能現在的絕對規模。
cards.episode: Inside Google's AI turnaround: The rise of AI Mode, strategy behind AI Overviews, and their vision for AI-powered search | Robby Stein (VP of Product, Google Search)

alts.quote: And now, it's not like, "Okay, now, we're screwed and the project is going to be bigger." Now, we can have a really cool conversation about trade-offs.
alts.zh: 所以現在不是「完了，這專案要爆了」。現在我們可以來一場很棒的取捨對話。

alts.quote: Not all of these variables is created equal and the manager is the most important variable in the environment, because a great manager who is empathetic, who is aware of what's going on, has the ability to move the chess pieces around.
alts.zh: 這幾個變數的份量不一樣，主管是環境裡最關鍵的那一個——因為一個有同理心、狀況清楚的好主管，是有能力幫你把棋子移一移的。

alts.quote: It's like a stepping stone back, but there is a much bigger room for upside that you can get to, but you are going to have to work to get to that upside.
alts.zh: 它其實是往後退一步，但後面有大得多的上升空間可以拿——只是你得努力才走得到。

cards.quote: That was one of the big motivations, actually identifying that user problem, being very disgruntled on behalf of the user. We're just failing the user every day.
cards.zh: 那就是最大的動力之一：真的把使用者的問題認出來，然後代替使用者生氣。我們每天都在辜負他們。
cards.why: on behalf of the user 這個介系詞片語是整句的樞紐——它把「我不爽」正當化成「我替使用者不爽」，情緒立刻變成專業立場。後面短句 We're just failing the user every day 用現在進行式加 every day，製造持續中的急迫感。
swaps: I'm annoyed on the user's behalf here.
We're letting people down on this, every single day.
cards.pmNote: 在會議上替使用者發火，比替自己的 roadmap 發火有效——前者沒有人能反對，後者馬上變成部門角力。
cards.episode: Inside Google's AI turnaround: The rise of AI Mode, strategy behind AI Overviews, and their vision for AI-powered search | Robby Stein (VP of Product, Google Search)

alts.quote: Record companies do not think of themselves as being in the business of manufacturing small pieces of plastic, but that was what they actually did.
alts.zh: 唱片公司從來不覺得自己是在做小塑膠片的生意，但他們實際上做的就是這個。

alts.quote: The problem is not like what should my goal be or how should I figure out what to do with my life? They usually know, but it's very hard to actually make time for those things.
alts.zh: 問題不在於「我的目標該是什麼」或「我這輩子要幹嘛」。這個大家其實都知道。問題是很難真的挪出時間去做那些事。

alts.quote: You're never trying to solve a problem of simplifying. And simplifying might be a solution, but it can never be a problem on its own.
alts.zh: 你不會是在解決「簡化」這個問題。簡化可能是一種解法，但它本身永遠不會是問題。

cards.quote: Yeah, I don't think of them as an or. I think they have to be intersected because basically the way I think about it is you actually start with a problem.
cards.zh: 我不覺得這是二選一。我覺得這兩件事必須交集在一起，因為在我看來，你本來就是從一個問題開始。
cards.why: 拒絕一個假二分法的標準句。an or 把 or 當名詞用是很地道的口語（等於「一個二選一的題目」）。intersected 又給了正面替代方案——你不只否定了問題，還提供了新的框架。反對而不空手，是這句的精髓。
swaps: I don't see that as either/or.
That's a false choice—it's both, and they feed each other.
cards.pmNote: 「做好產品 vs. 衝指標」幾乎永遠是假對立——真正的問題是你有沒有把指標選對。
cards.episode: Inside Google's AI turnaround: The rise of AI Mode, strategy behind AI Overviews, and their vision for AI-powered search | Robby Stein (VP of Product, Google Search)

alts.quote: I think if you're building a product where it's not necessarily an AI- first product and you have some AI features that are on the side, but it's not the core of your value, I don't know that I would operate this way.
alts.zh: 如果你做的不是 AI 優先的產品，只是旁邊掛幾個 AI 功能、AI 不是核心價值，那我不確定我會這樣做。

alts.quote: So this might mean that I think... I don't want to say that if you don't have experience, don't start one, but it's kind of true. So become an expert somewhere, somehow, before you start.
alts.zh: 我不想說「沒經驗就別開始」這種話……但其實有點是真的。所以動手前，先想辦法在某個地方變成專家。

alts.quote: So, I think one needs to be a little bit cautious on what Dario says. And that's setting aside the cynical view that he's just doing that department stock, which I don't believe at all.
alts.zh: 我覺得對 Dario 講的話要保留一點。而且我這裡還先撇開那種比較酸的解讀——說他只是在替自家股價講話——那我完全不相信。

cards.quote: You have to really understand why someone uses your product, because not every great thing is going to be invented by you.
cards.zh: 你得真的搞懂別人為什麼用你的產品，因為不是每一個好東西都會由你發明出來。
cards.why: 面對「你們抄襲」這種指控，這句用一個近乎常識的普遍原則，把爭議降級成「這是產業常態」。句子沒有辯解、沒有情緒，只是陳述一個沒人能否認的事實——這正是它有效的原因。
swaps: Good ideas don't only come from inside your building.
You don't have a monopoly on good ideas, and that's fine.
cards.pmNote: 採用競品驗證過的形式（format）不等於抄產品——要看你有沒有針對自家用戶重做一次判斷。
cards.episode: Inside Google's AI turnaround: The rise of AI Mode, strategy behind AI Overviews, and their vision for AI-powered search | Robby Stein (VP of Product, Google Search)

alts.quote: That's why you need your job search council. This is when you really need to ask for help because every bone in your body is going to say, "I'm not going to negotiate. That's going to make it worse," and it almost never does.
alts.zh: 這就是為什麼你需要求職小組。你全身上下每根骨頭都會喊：「我不要談判，談了只會更糟。」但幾乎從來不會更糟。

alts.quote: I also think it would be easy to use all what I just said as an excuse not to eventually build a great product.
alts.zh: 我也覺得，我剛剛講的那些很容易被拿來當藉口，變成「反正最後也不用做出好產品」。

alts.quote: To me, I think it's a great accelerant when it's already working, but it can't fix it if people don't want to talk about your product.
alts.zh: 對我來說，那在本來就跑得動的時候是很好的加速器，但如果根本沒人想談論你的產品，它救不了你。

cards.quote: These things become core primitives and formats, and then at the end of the day, you're just robbing your user base of the opportunity to have a better product.
cards.zh: 這些東西很快就變成核心的基本元件跟格式了，說到底，你不做只是在剝奪你的用戶擁有更好產品的機會。
cards.why: 把「抄襲」這個指控整個翻面：不做才是加害者，被害者是用戶。robbing 這個動詞刻意用了道德重量很高的字，把道德高地從指控方手上搶過來。這是英語辯論裡典型的 reframe，適合在被質疑動機時使用。
swaps: Refusing to build it just punishes our users.
The purist position here costs the user, not us.
cards.pmNote: 產品倫理的爭論最後都會回到「誰的利益」——把用戶利益放到論述中心，通常是最站得住腳的位置。
cards.episode: Inside Google's AI turnaround: The rise of AI Mode, strategy behind AI Overviews, and their vision for AI-powered search | Robby Stein (VP of Product, Google Search)

alts.quote: That's a good idea, but we don't actually understand these three things before we start working on that. So maybe we should do understand work to make sure that that is actually the right idea.
alts.zh: 這個想法不錯，但在動手之前有三件事我們其實還沒搞懂。也許先做點「理解型的工作」，確認這真的是對的方向。

alts.quote: It's not LLMs to be clear, but there's engines like Stockfish these days that are just dramatically better than the top grand masters in the world.
alts.zh: 講清楚，那不是 LLM，但現在有像 Stockfish 那種引擎，已經遠遠強過世界頂尖大師。

alts.quote: It's like these things that seem so common sense are actually hard with what they're doing… a lot of the advice is common sense. That doesn't mean it's easy to put in motion.
alts.zh: 這些看起來根本是常識的東西，真的做起來很難……很多建議都是常識，但常識不代表容易落地。

cards.quote: And so you have to add product carefully, but it needs to feel coherent but different.
cards.zh: 所以加東西要很小心，它必須感覺上是一體的，但同時又是不一樣的。
cards.why: 用兩個相反的形容詞夾出一個設計準則（coherent but different），短到可以貼在牆上。英語職場很愛這種「張力式標準」——它不給答案，但給了一把尺，讓團隊自己判斷每個決定落在哪。
swaps: Familiar enough to trust, distinct enough to notice.
It should belong here, but not blend in.
cards.pmNote: 新功能放進成熟產品時，視覺與互動要繼承（coherent），但心智模型要明確分離（different），否則用戶會用舊規則去解讀新東西。
cards.episode: Inside Google's AI turnaround: The rise of AI Mode, strategy behind AI Overviews, and their vision for AI-powered search | Robby Stein (VP of Product, Google Search)

alts.quote: Often people have a mission that's kind of on the wall somewhere and then what they're actually doing and the way they actually make money and the way people actually spend their time is in a very, very different direction from that original mission.
alts.zh: 很多公司的使命就掛在牆上某個地方，可是他們真正在做的事、真正賺錢的方式、大家真正把時間花在哪，跟那個使命的方向差超多。

alts.quote: I fundamentally do not believe in outsourcing the heartbeat of the organization, which is sales.
alts.zh: 我從根本上不相信可以把一家公司的心跳外包出去——而銷售就是心跳。

alts.quote: I think so many folks don't know where to begin on starting a startup, and my tactical advice is start doing customer validation first versus building a PowerPoint deck.
alts.zh: 很多人根本不知道創業要從哪裡開始，我很具體的建議是：先去做客戶驗證，而不是先做一份簡報。

cards.pattern: One of the things I see people fail on the most is they assume [在別處有效的東西] will work in your world.
cards.quote: It's actually one of the things I see people fail on the most is they assume something working for one system will work in your world.
cards.zh: 我看到最多人栽的地方就是：他們假設在別的系統上行得通的東西，在你這邊也會行得通。
cards.why: 用「我看過最多人失敗的地方」開場，把批評包裝成經驗分享，聽者不會覺得被針對。I see people fail on the most 是很典型的資深者句式——不指名、不說教，但殺傷力十足。
swaps: The most common mistake I see is assuming it transfers.
What works there won't automatically work here.
cards.pmNote: 抄成功案例前先問「他們的用戶在那個時刻的期待是什麼」——形式可以借，情境不能借。
cards.episode: Inside Google's AI turnaround: The rise of AI Mode, strategy behind AI Overviews, and their vision for AI-powered search | Robby Stein (VP of Product, Google Search)

alts.quote: Where I've seen people get lost is they assume that if you do that alone, it will work.
alts.zh: 我看過很多人卡住的地方是：他們假設光做這件事就會成功。

alts.quote: It's actually not. It's not. So many people are used to it and they think that it's just how it is, but it's actually not.
alts.zh: 其實不是。真的不是。太多人習慣了，就以為事情本來就是這樣——但其實不是。

alts.quote: I think people assume that there's a much more detailed semantic understanding of everybody's interests and preferences in the algorithm than there is.
alts.zh: 我覺得大家會以為演算法對每個人的興趣和偏好，有一套比實際上細膩得多的語意理解。

cards.quote: I think I made the product better, but is anyone using it? Does anyone care? Or are we just congratulating ourselves?
cards.zh: 我覺得我把產品做得更好了——可是有人在用嗎？有人在乎嗎？還是我們只是在自我感覺良好？
cards.why: 三個連續反問，一個比一個尖，最後一句 congratulating ourselves 直接點名團隊的自我陶醉。用 we 而不是 you，讓這記重拳打在全體身上包含自己，因此在會議上說出來不會結仇。
swaps: Did that move anything, or did it just feel good?
Are we celebrating output instead of outcome?
cards.pmNote: review 會議固定問一句「這有人在用嗎」，可以擋掉大量只有內部覺得酷的功能。
cards.episode: Inside Google's AI turnaround: The rise of AI Mode, strategy behind AI Overviews, and their vision for AI-powered search | Robby Stein (VP of Product, Google Search)

alts.quote: I was talking to security leaders in our customer advisory board recently and I heard this piece of feedback and this is what it made me think about our strategy, what do you think about that?
alts.zh: 我最近跟客戶顧問委員會的資安主管聊，聽到一個回饋，這讓我重新想我們的策略——你怎麼看？

alts.quote: I think sometimes people use data a lot or too much because they're worrying or they're afraid that, will I make the wrong choice? And I'm using data to make the choice for me.
alts.zh: 我覺得有時候大家用數據用得太兇，是因為他們在怕：萬一我選錯了怎麼辦？於是就讓數據替他們做決定。

alts.quote: Often, a product that you and I use that we've been using for years isn't actually the product that we're building for other people.
alts.zh: 我們自己用了好幾年的那個產品，其實跟我們正在為別人打造的那個產品，根本不是同一個東西。

cards.pattern: It wasn't very good, but it had these moments of brilliance.
cards.quote: We were really plugging away on it, and then we saw this little version of it emerge that wasn't very good, but it had this moments of brilliance.
cards.zh: 我們一直死磕著做，後來看到一個很小的雛形跑出來，其實不怎麼樣，但偶爾會閃出一些很厲害的時刻。
cards.why: 報告一個還很爛的原型時的標準句：先誠實下判斷（wasn't very good），再指出訊號（moments of brilliance）。順序不能反——先講亮點會像在推銷，先講缺點才會讓亮點顯得可信。這是爭取繼續投資的最佳角度。
swaps: Mostly rough, but there were flashes of something.
It was bad on average and great in patches—that's the interesting part.
cards.pmNote: 早期原型不該用平均品質評估，要看「最好的那幾次」有多好——那才是天花板的訊號。
cards.episode: Inside Google's AI turnaround: The rise of AI Mode, strategy behind AI Overviews, and their vision for AI-powered search | Robby Stein (VP of Product, Google Search)

alts.quote: And the good news bad news is that's true. That is absolutely true.
alts.zh: 好消息也是壞消息：那是真的。千真萬確。

alts.quote: Nobody wants to hear it. Everybody wants to just think about these really cool models and how smart they are. But really it's just the hard work of getting really good data to the LLMs.
alts.zh: 沒有人想聽這個。大家都只想談那些很酷的模型有多聰明。但說到底，這就是把好資料餵給 LLM 的苦工。

alts.quote: In those stages, the experience can be a little janky or it's not that polished, but we're okay with it because we are saying, "It's not finished. We just want to get your feedback early so we can make it better."
alts.zh: 那個階段體驗可能有點卡、不太精緻，但我們可以接受，因為我們有先講清楚：「這還沒完成，我們只是想早點拿到你的回饋，好把它做得更好。」

cards.pattern: You've got to have people test it to tell you the truth, and tell you when it sucks, because it probably does.
cards.quote: We tried to treat it a little more like a startup, because we feel like you got to have people test it to tell you the truth, and tell you when it sucks, because it probably does.
cards.zh: 我們刻意把它當成一個新創在做，因為你需要有人真的告訴你實話、告訴你它哪裡爛——而它八成真的很爛。
cards.why: because it probably does 這五個字是全句靈魂：預先承認自家東西大概就是不好。用 sucks 這種直白的字（而不是 has room for improvement）也是刻意的——你用什麼語氣談自家產品，別人就用什麼語氣給你回饋。
swaps: We need testers who'll tell us it's bad—because it is.
Assume version one is broken and go find out how.
cards.pmNote: 找 trusted tester 時要明講「請告訴我們哪裡爛」，否則你會收到一堆客氣的正面回饋，等於沒測。
cards.episode: Inside Google's AI turnaround: The rise of AI Mode, strategy behind AI Overviews, and their vision for AI-powered search | Robby Stein (VP of Product, Google Search)

alts.quote: And again, I'm not an expert in this and I think Erin Meyer wrote that book, The Culture Map. So you should just find what those people wrote because they're much smarter than I am about this.
alts.zh: 再說一次，我不是這方面的專家。Erin Meyer 寫過《文化地圖》那本書，你們應該直接去看他們寫的，他們比我懂太多了。

alts.quote: In a research paper, we'd have a discussion section, and this is where you get to guess. I would surmise, and we do this in the report, that it's probably because retail went through the retail apocalypse, right.
alts.zh: 我沒辦法告訴你原因。在論文裡這叫討論章節，也就是可以猜的地方。我的推測是——報告裡也是這樣寫的——大概是因為零售業經歷了那場零售末日。

alts.quote: And I guess it's kind of an embarrassing thing to say because everyone who's a startup founder thinks, my startup moves super fast and the talent bar is super high.
alts.zh: 說這話其實有點難為情，因為每個新創創辦人都覺得「我們超快、人才標準超高」。

cards.quote: Don't think of users as using your product. Think of users as hiring you to do something for them.
cards.zh: 別把使用者想成「在用你的產品」。要想成他們是「雇用你」去替他們完成某件事。
cards.why: Don't think of X as A. Think of X as B. 是最乾淨的觀念置換句型，兩句對稱、只換一個動詞。hiring 這個動詞立刻帶進「可以被開除」「有職務說明」「有績效」三層意涵，一個字換掉整個心智模型。
swaps: They're not using the product, they're hiring it for a job.
Stop asking what they do in the app; ask what they hired it to fix.
cards.pmNote: Jobs to be Done 的核心不是框架本身，而是逼你去找「他上次決定開始用的那一刻發生了什麼」。
cards.episode: Inside Google's AI turnaround: The rise of AI Mode, strategy behind AI Overviews, and their vision for AI-powered search | Robby Stein (VP of Product, Google Search)

alts.quote: And so I think a lot of it comes down to not the things you try, but how you deeply understand the problem that's preventing someone from using your product effectively.
alts.zh: 所以我覺得關鍵不在你試了哪些招，而在你有多深地搞懂「是什麼擋住使用者用好你的產品」。

alts.quote: I think most people don't like product managers often because they haven't experienced good product managers.
alts.zh: 我覺得多數人不喜歡 PM，多半是因為他們沒遇過真正好的 PM。

alts.quote: I think that the issue is, it's not just about product market fit, it is about achieving a product market pricing fit.
alts.zh: 我覺得問題在於：重點不只是 product-market fit，而是要做到 product-market-pricing fit。

cards.quote: And then the third one's around really designing for clarity instead of cleverness.
cards.zh: 第三點是：為了「清楚」而設計，不是為了「聰明」而設計。
cards.why: clarity instead of cleverness 用頭韻（都是 cl-）讓一條原則好記到不行。英語職場很多能傳開的原則都靠這種聲音上的設計。X instead of Y 這個結構本身也值得學——不是「要 X」，而是「用 X 取代那個你本來會選的 Y」。
swaps: Obvious beats clever.
Optimise for being understood, not for being interesting.
cards.pmNote: 命名與圖示要用產業通用符號，自創符號的認知成本永遠由用戶付。
cards.episode: Inside Google's AI turnaround: The rise of AI Mode, strategy behind AI Overviews, and their vision for AI-powered search | Robby Stein (VP of Product, Google Search)

alts.quote: We usually say how you charge is way more important than how much you charge.
alts.zh: 我們常說：「怎麼收費」比「收多少」重要得多。

alts.quote: If it's not an alternative, it doesn't need to exist.
alts.zh: 如果它不是一個「另一種選擇」，那它根本沒必要存在。

alts.quote: And then just the nature of the future is like we just don't know all the answers and that's okay. And then the right way to deal with that is to run as many experiments as possible.
alts.zh: 未來的本質就是我們不會知道所有答案，這沒關係。面對這件事正確的做法，是盡可能多跑一些實驗。

cards.quote: So we shipped it, we thought it would be great. This is the be humble part, wasn't great, had a bunch of, it was just super confusing.
cards.zh: 我們就上線了，本來以為會很棒。這就是「要謙虛」的那段——並不棒，做得超級混亂。
cards.why: This is the be humble part 是把自己剛講過的原則當場拿來自嘲，一句話就把失敗故事講得輕鬆又誠實。後面 wasn't great 省略主詞，是口語裡收得很快的節奏——講失敗不要拖長，拖長就變自憐。
swaps: We were sure it would land. It didn't.
Spoiler: it flopped.
cards.pmNote: 把失敗案例當成方法論的示範材料，比單獨檢討更有教學效果，也讓團隊敢承認失敗。
cards.episode: Inside Google's AI turnaround: The rise of AI Mode, strategy behind AI Overviews, and their vision for AI-powered search | Robby Stein (VP of Product, Google Search)

alts.quote: We were like, "You know what? If we had just tested that, we would have all known that this was a super lame badge." And I was like, "Why are we not testing our experiments?"
alts.zh: 我們就說：「欸，我們如果當初有自己測一下，早就知道這個徽章有夠遜。」我就問：「所以我們為什麼沒有在測自己的實驗？」

alts.quote: And I'll tell you, ProfitWell, this was a big mistake. Yes, it was a great exit, we sold for over $200 million, et cetera, but we probably, if we had taken money, we could have had a billion-dollar exit
alts.zh: 老實說 ProfitWell 這件事是個大失誤。是啦，出場很漂亮，賣了兩億多美元，但如果我們當初有拿錢，可能會是十億等級的出場。

alts.quote: And of course at the time I thought this was one of the biggest mistakes in my whole career.
alts.zh: 當然，我當下覺得那是我整個職涯裡最大的錯誤之一。

cards.pattern: There's this cult of [流行做法]. At some level it's true, but [你的保留]
cards.quote: I think there's this cult of lean, scrappy, fast, throw away your product quickly, keep moving. And I think at some level it's true, but a lot of times I see teams give up too early.
cards.zh: 現在有一種「精實、克難、快、東西不行就丟、繼續往前」的教派。某種程度上它是對的，但我常看到團隊太早就放棄了。
cards.why: cult of 是給流行做法降溫最有效的一個詞——不是說它錯，是說信奉它的人已經不思考了。接著 at some level it's true 先讓步再轉折，讓你的反對聽起來是補充而不是叫板。這是反對主流意見最安全的走法。
swaps: There's a bit of dogma around this. It's directionally right, but...
This has become an article of faith, and I'd add a caveat:
cards.pmNote: 小團隊不是目的而是手段——要問的是「這個野心需要多少人才做得出來」，而不是「怎麼維持人數最少」。
cards.episode: Inside Google's AI turnaround: The rise of AI Mode, strategy behind AI Overviews, and their vision for AI-powered search | Robby Stein (VP of Product, Google Search)

alts.quote: And the reason for that is, I don't think there's any reason to assume that human skill level is the cap on anything.
alts.zh: 原因是：我不覺得有任何理由要假設「人類的能力水準」就是天花板。

alts.quote: I think sometimes people use data a lot or too much because they're worrying or they're afraid that, will I make the wrong choice? And I'm using data to make the choice for me.
alts.zh: 我覺得有時候大家用數據用得太兇，是因為他們在怕：萬一我選錯了怎麼辦？於是就讓數據替他們做決定。

alts.quote: Well, I mean this is the irony of growth, is people think growth is overnight success and it's not. It is a lot of short wins and short-term execution for a longer-term gain.
alts.zh: 成長最諷刺的地方就在這：大家以為成長是一夜爆紅，其實不是。它是一堆短期的小勝仗，堆出長期的結果。

cards.quote: Yeah, it's the other thing. No advice is right universally, right?
cards.zh: 對，這就是另一種情況了。沒有哪個建議是放諸四海皆準的嘛。
cards.why: 被指出「這跟你剛剛講的原則矛盾」時的最省力回應。不辯解、不修正原則，只承認原則有適用範圍。句尾的 right? 把裁決權交給對方，整句既坦然又不失立場。台灣人遇到這種當面矛盾常會慌，其實一句話就能過。
swaps: Every rule has exceptions, and that's one.
Fair—that one breaks the pattern.
cards.pmNote: 被抓到原則與案例不一致時，承認原則有邊界比修改原則更好——原則一改再改就沒人記得住了。
cards.episode: Inside Google's AI turnaround: The rise of AI Mode, strategy behind AI Overviews, and their vision for AI-powered search | Robby Stein (VP of Product, Google Search)

alts.quote: Yeah, sorry. Buy-in doesn't feel quite right to me, because buy-in feels like, oh, I've come to agree with you. And that's different from it's a part of me.
alts.zh: 抱歉，我覺得「buy-in（買單）」這個詞不太對。buy-in 聽起來像「我最後被你說服了」，那跟「這東西本來就是我的一部分」是兩回事。

alts.quote: Both things can be true. It's like, yeah, there's nothing perfect in product. However, it is true that some companies are healthier than others.
alts.zh: 這兩件事可以同時成立。對，產品這行沒有什麼是完美的；但同樣真實的是，有些公司確實比其他公司健康得多。

alts.quote: But the other thing is I don't really love some of that thinking process just in general.
alts.zh: 另外還有一點：那整套思考方式，我其實不是很喜歡，講一般情況啦。

cards.pattern: You're pushing for a future you believe is true, but all the while you're getting new information. You need to kill the beliefs that you had.
cards.quote: It's this weird tightrope where you're pushing for a future that you believe is true, but all the while you're getting new information. You need to kill the beliefs that you had.
cards.zh: 這是一條很怪的鋼索：你一邊在推動一個你相信會成真的未來，一邊又不斷收到新資訊。你得親手殺掉自己原本的信念。
cards.why: kill the beliefs that you had 這個動詞選得很重——不是 update 也不是 revise，是「殺掉」。英語職場在講改變立場時，用越強烈的動詞越顯得果斷而非動搖。tightrope（鋼索）也把矛盾狀態變成一個可以想像的畫面。
swaps: Hold the conviction, but be ruthless about updating it.
You have to be willing to shoot your own assumptions.
cards.pmNote: strong opinions, loosely held 的實作就是：每個假設都要事先寫下「什麼證據會讓我放棄它」。
cards.episode: Building a magical AI code editor used by over 1 million developers in four months: The untold story of Windsurf | Varun Mohan (co-founder and CEO)

alts.quote: But what I have come to believe and this differs from what I used to believe is especially if you're working in a big company, you are one of the many thousands of employees in there.
alts.zh: 但我後來相信的事——這跟我以前相信的不一樣——是：如果你在大公司，你就只是那幾千個員工裡的一個。

alts.quote: Four or five years ago, I would've said, well, personal skills, nothing. It's all the environment. I used to be one of those particular people.
alts.zh: 四五年前我會說：個人能力根本不重要，全都是環境造成的。我以前就是那一派的人。

alts.quote: When I was younger and I was starting off, I used to think it's all about the product.
alts.zh: 我年輕、剛入行的時候，以為一切就是產品而已。

cards.pattern: Fast-forward to [時間], [新事實]. So now our hypotheses are just wrong.
cards.quote: Fast-forward to the middle of 2023, everything looks like it's going to be a transformer. So now our hypotheses are just wrong.
cards.zh: 快轉到 2023 年中，看起來全部都會走向 transformer。所以我們原本的假設就是錯的。
cards.why: 承認錯誤時最漂亮的走法：先講外部事實變了（fast-forward to），再讓「我們錯了」變成事實的自然結論。just wrong 三個字乾脆到不留餘地，反而讓人覺得你有掌握狀況——拖泥帶水的認錯才顯得心虛。
swaps: By mid-2023 the picture had changed, and our thesis no longer held.
The world moved, and that assumption stopped being true.
cards.pmNote: 策略假設要標註「基於什麼外部條件」，條件變了才能乾淨地換策略，而不是變成有人判斷失誤。
cards.episode: Building a magical AI code editor used by over 1 million developers in four months: The untold story of Windsurf | Varun Mohan (co-founder and CEO)

alts.quote: Transparently, I thought this was going to be an apocalypse. So I shared about a year ago that it's going to be an apocalypse. We have not seen it yet.
alts.zh: 老實說，我本來以為這會是世界末日。我一年前也是這樣公開講的。到目前為止並沒有發生。

alts.quote: A year ago, I thought we were going through a similar kind of transition. We're clearly not. This is different.
alts.zh: 一年前我以為我們正在經歷類似的轉型。顯然不是。這次不一樣。

alts.quote: If you had asked me when I first started the company, it would've been an enthusiastic hell yes. I totally recommend. Now, I have a couple asterisks on top of it.
alts.zh: 如果你在我剛創業的時候問我，答案會是超級肯定的「絕對推薦」。現在的話，我會加上幾個但書。

cards.pattern: If I told you [荒謬版本], you should rightfully say [反駁]. And you'd be right.
cards.quote: If I told you, I'm going to build an autonomous vehicle, and I said our team is 10 people, you should rightfully say, Varun, you're not serious. And you'd be right.
cards.zh: 如果我跟你說我要做自駕車，然後說團隊只有 10 個人，你完全應該回我：Varun，你不是認真的吧。而且你會是對的。
cards.why: 自己扮演對方、自己講出對方的質疑、再自己認證那個質疑是對的。三步做完，你的主張就不必再證明了。you should rightfully say 裡的 rightfully 是關鍵——它預先授權對方懷疑你，反而讓你顯得極度有把握。
swaps: If I said that with a straight face, you'd rightly call it out.
You'd be entitled to laugh at me, and you should.
cards.pmNote: 論證資源需求時，用一個明顯過小的假設版本做對照，比直接喊數字更有說服力。
cards.episode: Building a magical AI code editor used by over 1 million developers in four months: The untold story of Windsurf | Varun Mohan (co-founder and CEO)

alts.quote: Now, the good news is that you can then reverse that and say if I'm willing to do it, think about what an edge I'm going to have over people who aren't willing to do it, right?
alts.zh: 好消息是這件事可以反過來看：如果我願意做，想想我對那些不願意做的人會有多大的優勢。

alts.quote: I think with hiring, it's funny, man, there's so much hiring advice online and you read it and you're like, "Yeah, this is super obvious." And then when you live it, you're suddenly like, "Aah, this is why people say this."
alts.zh: 招人這件事很好笑，網路上一堆建議，你看的時候都覺得「這不是廢話嗎」。等你真的經歷過，才會突然懂「喔，原來大家是這個意思」。

alts.quote: In economics, people only do what their incentives told them to do. Broadly speaking, that is what they do. You get what you set out to measure.
alts.zh: 在經濟學裡，人只會做他們的誘因叫他們做的事。大致上就是這樣。你量什麼，就會得到什麼。

cards.pattern: It's not because people are bad people—most people are well-intentioned. But what happens is [結構性後果]
cards.quote: And it's not because people are bad people. I think most people are really well-intentioned. But what happens when you have people that join and you didn't really need them?
cards.zh: 這不是因為誰是壞人，我覺得大多數人動機都很好。但問題是：當你招了一批其實不需要的人，會發生什麼事？
cards.why: 在批評一個現象前，先把「人品」這條路封死（not because people are bad people），剩下的就只能往結構去解釋。這是英語職場給難聽回饋時的必備前置——你不做這個切割，聽者一定會把批評接收成人身攻擊。
swaps: This isn't about anyone's intentions—it's about incentives.
Good people, bad structure.
cards.pmNote: 組織問題九成是結構問題——先檢查誘因與編制，再檢討個人表現。
cards.episode: Building a magical AI code editor used by over 1 million developers in four months: The untold story of Windsurf | Varun Mohan (co-founder and CEO)

alts.quote: I think we do a disservice when we say we're not good at speaking up because it's a skill like any other.
alts.zh: 我覺得我們說自己「不擅長發言」是在害自己，因為那跟其他技能沒有兩樣。

alts.quote: Of course, I don't want to be cruel to the people who are putting their hearts into that work, because the Figma file is beautiful. It's just coming a little early.
alts.zh: 當然，我不想對那些真心投入的人太苛刻——那些 Figma 檔真的很漂亮。只是它來得太早了一點。

alts.quote: This isn't funny, Hilary. This is a serious issue for a lot of people, and it's an emerging problem in some cases. And I think we should take it seriously.
alts.zh: 這不好笑。這對很多人來說是很嚴重的問題，而且在某些地方正在惡化。我覺得我們應該認真看待。

cards.quote: You don't win by doing 10 things well. You win by doing one thing really well and maybe you fail nine things.
cards.zh: 你不是靠十件事都做得不錯來贏。你是靠一件事做到非常好而贏，另外九件搞砸也沒關係。
cards.why: You don't win by X. You win by Y. 這組對仗句是英語裡宣告優先順序最有力的格式。關鍵在 maybe you fail nine things——他沒有假裝取捨沒有代價，而是明白把代價講出來。承認代價才讓主張可信。
swaps: Winning is one thing done exceptionally, not ten done adequately.
Breadth doesn't win. Depth on the right thing does.
cards.pmNote: 季度規劃時強迫排出「唯一的第一名」，其餘全部標成可犧牲——沒有可犧牲清單的優先順序等於沒排。
cards.episode: Building a magical AI code editor used by over 1 million developers in four months: The untold story of Windsurf | Varun Mohan (co-founder and CEO)

alts.quote: You don't give them an airport tarmac and you don't even give them a football field. You give them something more like a basketball court, a sort of scale at which they can do their design thing.
alts.zh: 你不會給他們一整條機場跑道，連足球場都不該給。要給的是差不多籃球場那種大小——大到能發揮，小到能收斂。

alts.quote: And then the last thing I would say about this detection is if you don't know what to do, or all else being equal, then focus on onboarding.
alts.zh: 關於怎麼提早偵測，我最後想講的是：如果你不知道該做什麼，或其他條件都差不多，那就去弄 onboarding。

alts.quote: And I think people don't understand that in a competitive environment, being right is good, but being quick is necessary.
alts.zh: 我覺得大家沒搞懂：在競爭環境裡，做對是加分，做得快是必要條件。

cards.quote: This is very different than school. In school you optimize for your total GPA. But for companies, I just need to get an A+ on the one class that matters.
cards.zh: 這跟學校完全不一樣。在學校你是在拚總平均，但在公司，我只需要在那門真正重要的課拿 A+。
cards.why: 用「學校 vs. 公司」這個所有人都經歷過的對照，一秒解釋清楚為什麼平均分很危險。台灣的教育經驗讓這句特別扎——很多人職場上的痛苦，就是還在用 GPA 的方式工作。這種取自共同經驗的類比，是說服力最高的一種。
swaps: Careers aren't graded on a curve across all subjects.
Nobody's averaging your scores—one result carries the whole term.
cards.pmNote: 績效敘事要挑一個代表作講深，不要把十件小事平均展示——評審記得住的只有一件。
cards.episode: Building a magical AI code editor used by over 1 million developers in four months: The untold story of Windsurf | Varun Mohan (co-founder and CEO)

alts.quote: Be careful. If you need to spend a little time on the problem, fine, but don't spend a lot of time because you need to save as much time as possible to come up with the winning solution.
alts.zh: 小心一點。你要花一點時間在問題上沒問題，但別花太多，因為你得盡量把時間留給「想出會贏的解法」。

alts.quote: So yeah, no hard and fast rule, but I think it's always you need to have this matrix of options in your mind and be very deliberate about which one you are going with and why.
alts.zh: 沒有什麼鐵則，但你腦中要有一張選項矩陣，而且要很清楚自己選了哪一格、為什麼。

alts.quote: Yes, such a great point, Lenny. You absolutely need to time box this.
alts.zh: 對，這點問得很好。這件事你一定要設一個時間框。

cards.quote: If a software project could get built in two to three weeks, what does that really mean about the true complexity of what you built? Unless you believe you are way smarter than everyone else, but I think that's hubris.
cards.zh: 如果一個軟體專案兩三週就能做出來，那它到底有多複雜、多難被取代？除非你相信自己比全世界聰明太多——但我覺得那叫自大。
cards.why: 先給出一個唯一能讓對方站得住的前提（unless you believe...），再自己把那個前提命名為 hubris。這是英語辯論裡把對手逼進死角最優雅的方式：你沒有直接反駁，只是讓那條唯一的退路聽起來很難堪。
swaps: The only way that's true is if we're smarter than everyone—which I doubt.
That argument requires believing we're exceptional. I wouldn't bet on it.
cards.pmNote: 估時過度樂觀時，反問「為什麼別人要六個月我們只要三週」，通常能逼出被忽略的隱藏工作量。
cards.episode: Building a magical AI code editor used by over 1 million developers in four months: The untold story of Windsurf | Varun Mohan (co-founder and CEO)

alts.quote: I really try and stay away from better, because that's really hard to define, and better means something different to everyone.
alts.zh: 我盡量不用「比較好」這個字，因為它很難定義，而且每個人心中的「比較好」都不一樣。

alts.quote: I think sometimes people think that craft is about perfecting things and perfecting them in a very organized way or very early on. The downside with this perfection mindset is that it can be sometimes hard to put anything out because nothing is ever fully perfect.
alts.zh: 大家常以為所謂「工藝」就是把東西做到完美，而且要很有條理、很早就開始做。這種完美心態的代價是：你可能什麼都出不了貨，因為沒有東西是真正完美的。

alts.quote: Well, I mean this is the irony of growth, is people think growth is overnight success and it's not. It is a lot of short wins and short-term execution for a longer-term gain.
alts.zh: 成長最諷刺的地方就在這：大家以為成長是一夜爆紅，其實不是。它是一堆短期的小勝仗，堆出長期的結果。

cards.quote: I think this is an interesting thing that technical founders sometimes don't really like. They think sales is a very negative part of the process. I think it's not that black and white.
cards.zh: 技術背景的創辦人常常不太喜歡這件事，他們覺得業務是整個過程裡很負面的一塊。我覺得沒那麼非黑即白。
cards.why: not that black and white 是英語職場最常用、也最安全的溫和反對句，它反對的是「立場的絕對性」而不是立場本身。前面先中性地描述對方的看法（不加貶義），再輕輕加上這一句，幾乎不會引起防衛。這句該背起來。
swaps: I'd say it's more nuanced than that.
It's less binary than people make it out to be.
cards.pmNote: PLG 與 enterprise sales 不是二選一——多數 B2B 成長曲線是兩者疊在一起的。
cards.episode: Building a magical AI code editor used by over 1 million developers in four months: The untold story of Windsurf | Varun Mohan (co-founder and CEO)

alts.quote: But the other thing is I don't really love some of that thinking process just in general.
alts.zh: 另外還有一點：那整套思考方式，我其實不是很喜歡，講一般情況啦。

alts.quote: I agree with you. I totally agree with you. Now, I think it's the human aspect though of boldness, seeing the future in a way that a thing trained on priors cannot.
alts.zh: 我同意你，完全同意。不過我覺得，人的那一塊——那種膽識、那種能看見未來的能力，是只學過去資料的東西做不到的。

alts.quote: So this might mean that I think... I don't want to say that if you don't have experience, don't start one, but it's kind of true. So become an expert somewhere, somehow, before you start.
alts.zh: 我不想說「沒經驗就別開始」這種話……但其實有點是真的。所以動手前，先想辦法在某個地方變成專家。

cards.pattern: Granted, [自認的缺點], but [仍然成立的重點]
cards.quote: Granted this looks hideous, but in some ways if I wanted to, I could go out and do that, right?
cards.zh: 當然啦，這看起來很醜，但重點是我如果想，我確實可以直接這樣改，對吧。
cards.why: Granted 是一個專門用來「認領缺點」的連接詞，比 I know 更利落、比 admittedly 更口語。Demo 出包時這句可以救場：先承認眼前的難看，再把注意力導回你真正要示範的能力。台灣人 demo 時常裝作沒看到，反而更尷尬。
swaps: Yes, it looks terrible—that's not the point here.
Ugly, I know. The point is that it worked at all.
cards.pmNote: Demo 前先講明「這一段只是為了示範 X，視覺不代表成品」，可以避免整場討論被無關的細節綁架。
cards.episode: Building a magical AI code editor used by over 1 million developers in four months: The untold story of Windsurf | Varun Mohan (co-founder and CEO)

alts.quote: I agree, look, having your soul at every little checkbox sounds like a high bar and in some ways it is.
alts.zh: 我同意，聽著，要求每一個小勾選框都灌注靈魂，聽起來標準很高，某種程度上也確實是。

alts.quote: In some ways, this sounds very puritanical, I don't mean it to sound this way, but there were lines that we didn't want to cross that just felt ethically not us, that I've seen other news players do more of.
alts.zh: 某種程度上這聽起來很清教徒，我不是要講成那樣，但確實有些線我們不想跨過去，那些做法感覺就不像我們——而我看到別的新聞產品做得更多。

alts.quote: That's a good idea, but we don't actually understand these three things before we start working on that. So maybe we should do understand work to make sure that that is actually the right idea.
alts.zh: 這個想法不錯，但在動手之前有三件事我們其實還沒搞懂。也許先做點「理解型的工作」，確認這真的是對的方向。

cards.pattern: I don't want to be very negative, but it's very hard [做某事]
cards.quote: And maybe this is a... I don't want to be very negative, but it's very hard inside a company like ours to task our best engineers to build a best in class sales product.
cards.zh: 我不想講得太負面，但在我們這種公司裡，要把最好的工程師派去做一個頂尖的業務工具，是非常困難的。
cards.why: I don't want to be negative, but... 是一個坦率的預告：接下來的話會不好聽，我知道，我還是要說。這比裝作中立更誠實，也讓聽者有心理準備。注意他講的是自家的限制（inside a company like ours），把批評落在自己身上而非對方，殺傷力就降到最低。
swaps: I don't mean to sound pessimistic, but...
This is the uncomfortable part:
cards.pmNote: 談自建 vs. 採購時，最誠實的判準是「我們願不願意派最強的人去做它」——答案是否，就該買。
cards.episode: Building a magical AI code editor used by over 1 million developers in four months: The untold story of Windsurf | Varun Mohan (co-founder and CEO)

alts.quote: It's so hard to give a founder hard feedback. Who wants to be the bearer of bad news?
alts.zh: 要給創辦人難聽的回饋真的很難。誰想當那個報壞消息的人？

alts.quote: Nobody wants to hear it. Everybody wants to just think about these really cool models and how smart they are. But really it's just the hard work of getting really good data to the LLMs.
alts.zh: 沒有人想聽這個。大家都只想談那些很酷的模型有多聰明。但說到底，這就是把好資料餵給 LLM 的苦工。

alts.quote: In those stages, the experience can be a little janky or it's not that polished, but we're okay with it because we are saying, "It's not finished. We just want to get your feedback early so we can make it better."
alts.zh: 那個階段體驗可能有點卡、不太精緻，但我們可以接受，因為我們有先講清楚：「這還沒完成，我們只是想早點拿到你的回饋，好把它做得更好。」

cards.quote: If something is just purely code planning, there's not a great reason why we would be the best at that. I can't come up with a coherent argument for that.
cards.zh: 如果只是純粹的程式規劃，我想不出我們憑什麼會是最強的。這個我實在提不出一個站得住腳的論證。
cards.why: 承認「我論證不出來」而不是「這不重要」——這是知識誠實的最高標準。coherent argument 這個詞組把標準拉得很高：不是沒有理由，是沒有一個前後一致的理由。對自家產品講這句話，可信度會爆表。
swaps: I don't have a good story for why we'd win there.
I can't defend that one on the merits.
cards.pmNote: 評估差異化時要能講出一條「為什麼是我們」的因果鏈——講不出來就代表那不是護城河。
cards.episode: Building a magical AI code editor used by over 1 million developers in four months: The untold story of Windsurf | Varun Mohan (co-founder and CEO)

alts.quote: And I don't know how much this matters in the future now, but there's this just elegance to functional programming and thinking in types, and this is just the way that I code, and the way that I can't stop thinking about coding.
alts.zh: 我不知道這件事在未來還有多重要，但函數式程式設計跟用型別思考就是有一種優雅，這就是我寫程式的方式，我沒辦法不這樣想。

alts.quote: My purely anecdotal guess is maybe 10 to 15% are good product companies, something like that.
alts.zh: 我純粹憑印象猜，大概一成到一成五算是好的產品公司吧，差不多這個量級。

alts.quote: I can't speak to that whole period. But what I can tell you about what I'm feeling now is just an incredible sense of focus and urgency to deliver great products quickly.
alts.zh: 那一整段期間我沒辦法評論。但我可以告訴你現在的感受——一種非常強烈的專注感和急迫感，就是要快點把好產品交出去。

cards.pattern: Maybe just to set the record straight, [X] doesn't mean [被推導出的錯誤結論]
cards.quote: First of all, maybe just to set the record straight, if AI is writing over 90% of the code, that doesn't mean engineers are 10X as productive.
cards.zh: 首先，我先把話講清楚：就算 AI 寫了九成以上的程式碼，也不代表工程師的產出就變成十倍。
cards.why: set the record straight 是在對方還沒說錯之前先澄清一個廣為流傳的誤推。這個片語帶有「我要修正公共認知」的份量，適合在你是該領域最有資格說話的人時使用。X doesn't mean Y 的結構則精準指出錯在推論那一步，不是事實那一步。
swaps: Let me correct a common misreading of that stat:
That number gets misused—it doesn't imply what people think.
cards.pmNote: 引用生產力數據時要一併說明「分母是什麼」，否則局部加速會被誤讀成整體加速。
cards.episode: Building a magical AI code editor used by over 1 million developers in four months: The untold story of Windsurf | Varun Mohan (co-founder and CEO)

alts.quote: Actually, all feedback I think is valid. People's feelings are valid, but it doesn't mean that you need to do something about all of those things.
alts.zh: 其實我覺得所有回饋都是有效的。別人的感受都是真的，但這不代表你每一項都得去處理。

alts.quote: First let's examine the counterfactual, right? So let's start with the opposite of your question and say, "How would the world be sadder if we all just gave up on this?"
alts.zh: 我們先看反面情況吧。從你問題的相反面開始想：如果大家乾脆全都放棄這件事，世界會變得多糟？

alts.quote: Here's what I have a problem with. First of all, having a growth mindset is a very, very helpful thing.
alts.zh: 我要說的是我對它的哪一點有意見。首先，擁有成長心態本身是非常非常有幫助的事。

cards.pattern: We should be cannibalizing our own product every [週期]. It should make our existing product look silly.
cards.quote: We should be cannibalizing the existing state of our product every six to 12 months. Every six to 12 months, it should make our existing product look silly.
cards.zh: 我們應該每六到十二個月就把自己現有的產品吃掉一次。每六到十二個月，新的東西就該讓舊的看起來很蠢。
cards.why: 願景不用形容詞、用一個可檢驗的標準：舊版本看起來蠢不蠢。make our existing product look silly 這種具體到近乎粗魯的說法，比 continuous innovation 這種抽象詞管用一百倍——它讓團隊每半年可以自己驗收一次。
swaps: If last year's version still looks good, we didn't move enough.
We should be obsoleting ourselves on a schedule.
cards.pmNote: 把「自我淘汰」設成節奏（每 6-12 個月）而非口號，才有辦法在漸進式優化的壓力下保留破壞式投資。
cards.episode: Building a magical AI code editor used by over 1 million developers in four months: The untold story of Windsurf | Varun Mohan (co-founder and CEO)

alts.quote: What does a day in the life of a user look like in five years? What does the product look like in five to 10 years? Why is the world better in 10 years?
alts.zh: 五年後，使用者的一天長什麼樣子？五到十年後，這個產品長什麼樣子？十年後，這個世界為什麼會更好？

alts.quote: And that ultimately, we understand what makes it a must-have product. And then what we're trying to do is build a flywheel around that must-have value.
alts.zh: 最終我們要弄清楚是什麼讓它變成「非有不可」的產品，然後圍繞那個非有不可的價值，去打造一個飛輪。

alts.quote: So I guess there's two ways of planning. The way that you can plan is you can dream of what is the perfect vision of the future, what future do you want to exist in, what would you like the world to look like?
alts.zh: 我覺得規劃大概分兩種。一種是你去夢想那個最完美的未來——你想活在什麼樣的未來裡？你希望這個世界長什麼樣子？

cards.quote: Incremental feels very safe. But that is not the reason why we're going to win. That's almost table stakes.
cards.zh: 有個很微妙的張力：漸進式改動感覺很安全，多加一顆按鈕嘛。但那不是我們會贏的原因，那幾乎只是入場資格。
cards.why: table stakes（賭桌上的最低下注額）是英語商務裡把某件事降級成「基本盤」的關鍵詞——不是不做，是做了也不加分。先承認漸進式的心理吸引力（feels very safe），再把它降級，比直接罵它保守有效得多。
swaps: Those are table stakes, not differentiation.
Necessary, but it's not where the win comes from.
cards.pmNote: roadmap 要分「維持入場資格」與「創造差異化」兩欄，兩者搶同一批人時要明確標出誰讓步。
cards.episode: Building a magical AI code editor used by over 1 million developers in four months: The untold story of Windsurf | Varun Mohan (co-founder and CEO)

alts.quote: And what Canva really does is we're literally smack bang in the middle of that Venn diagram of creativity and productivity, rather than making our customers have to make a choice between those two suites.
alts.zh: Canva 真正在做的事，就是不偏不倚站在「創意」跟「生產力」這兩個圈的交集正中央，而不是逼客戶在兩邊二選一。

alts.quote: There's a saying that Mike and Kevin had at Instagram which is we may not be right, but at least we're not confused.
alts.zh: Instagram 的 Mike 跟 Kevin 有一句話：我們不見得是對的，但至少我們不是一團混亂。

alts.quote: And so the prompt here is to try to go more off the beaten path either from your personal experience, like in the case of Brex and Retool or Whatnot.
alts.zh: 所以這裡給你的思考提示是：試著走出那條被踩爛的路，從你自己的經驗裡挖，像 Brex、Retool、Whatnot 那樣。

cards.pattern: Maybe [某個詞] is the wrong term, but this idea of just being okay with being wrong faster.
cards.quote: Maybe humility is the wrong term, but this idea of just being okay with being wrong faster. I always think about this when we make decisions.
cards.zh: 也許「謙虛」不是最準的詞，但就是那種「更快接受自己錯了」的心態。我們在做決策時我常想到這件事。
cards.why: Maybe X is the wrong term, but... 讓你可以用一個不夠精準的詞卻不被抓語病——你自己先承認了。這是英語口語裡處理「我知道我要講的東西還沒找到名字」的標準做法，比在腦中卡住找完美用詞流暢太多。
swaps: That's not quite the right word, but you know what I mean—
For lack of a better term,
cards.pmNote: 決策速度的真正瓶頸常常不是「多快做決定」，而是「多快承認決定錯了」。
cards.episode: Building a magical AI code editor used by over 1 million developers in four months: The untold story of Windsurf | Varun Mohan (co-founder and CEO)

alts.quote: By the way, I will say on the Peter one, I've come much more around to Peter's point of view. I would probably argue that one quite a bit differently today than I did, and I would give his view, I think, a lot more credit.
alts.zh: 順帶一提，Peter 那場辯論，我現在比較站到他那邊了。同樣的題目今天要我講，我會講得很不一樣，也會給他的看法多很多分數。

alts.quote: Even if I don't agree with the feedback, what is the insight that I'm missing? How am I wrong about this? What would be true for this other person to be right?
alts.zh: 就算我不同意那個回饋，我也會問：我漏掉了什麼洞見？我哪裡想錯了？要怎麼樣，對方才會是對的？

alts.quote: And I used to think leadership was the same, which is, well, it's not about you as a leader, it's about who are you bringing along on your journey?
alts.zh: 我以前也以為領導力是同一回事——就是說，重點不在你這個領導者身上，而在你把誰一起帶上路。

cards.pattern: I guess it's kind of an embarrassing thing to say, because everyone thinks [同樣的事], but [你的版本]
cards.quote: And I guess it's kind of an embarrassing thing to say because everyone who's a startup founder thinks, my startup moves super fast and the talent bar is super high.
cards.zh: 說這話其實有點難為情，因為每個新創創辦人都覺得「我們超快、人才標準超高」。
cards.why: 要講一句聽起來很老套的話之前，先承認它老套。it's kind of an embarrassing thing to say 把聽者心裡的白眼先講出來，之後你講什麼都會被當成真心話。這招在英語職場叫 disarming——先解除對方的武裝。
swaps: I know how this sounds—everyone says this—but...
This is a cliché and I'm about to say it anyway:
cards.pmNote: 講「我們很快」這種所有公司都會講的話時，一定要接一個可驗證的具體事例，否則等於沒講。
cards.episode: The power user’s guide to Codex: parallelizing workflows, planning techniques, advanced context engineering tips, automating code reviews, and more | Alexander Embiricos

alts.quote: In a research paper, we'd have a discussion section, and this is where you get to guess. I would surmise, and we do this in the report, that it's probably because retail went through the retail apocalypse, right.
alts.zh: 我沒辦法告訴你原因。在論文裡這叫討論章節，也就是可以猜的地方。我的推測是——報告裡也是這樣寫的——大概是因為零售業經歷了那場零售末日。

alts.quote: I do want to apply a pretty severe caveat here though, which is, a decision log is not a replacement for building products. It's a additional complimentary thing that you can be doing on your own.
alts.zh: 不過我要加一個很重的但書：決策日誌不能取代真的去做產品。它只是你自己可以額外做的補充。

alts.quote: I don't know how many customer support folks we have, but it's not very many, 30, 40, I'm not sure, way smaller than you would have at any comparable company, and it's because we've automated a lot of our flows.
alts.zh: 我不知道我們有多少客服人力，但沒有很多，三十、四十吧，我不確定，總之比任何同等規模的公司都少很多，因為我們把很多流程自動化了。

cards.pattern: Even if [極端讓步], which is absolutely not the case, we'd still [你的主張]
cards.quote: Even if we had no more progress today with models, which is absolutely not the case, but even if we had no more progress, we are way behind on product.
cards.zh: 就算模型從今天起完全不再進步——當然實際上完全不是這樣——就算真的不再進步，我們在產品上還是落後一大截。
cards.why: 先給對方一個最極端的讓步，讓你的結論在最不利的假設下也成立。which is absolutely not the case 這個插入語很關鍵：讓步只是修辭，不是真的認同。這是英語論證裡最強的一種結構，能一次擋掉所有「可是如果……」。
swaps: Even in the worst case—which I don't believe—the conclusion holds.
Assume none of that improves. We'd still have this problem.
cards.pmNote: 提案要能通過「最保守假設」的檢驗——只有在樂觀假設下才成立的提案，通常會在第一個季度死掉。
cards.episode: The power user’s guide to Codex: parallelizing workflows, planning techniques, advanced context engineering tips, automating code reviews, and more | Alexander Embiricos

alts.quote: By the way, the infrastructure piece, I know it's a nugget on the side but infrastructure is the product. Period.
alts.zh: 順帶一提，基礎建設這塊——我知道這是題外話——但基礎建設就是產品。就這樣。

alts.quote: I would underline it even, which is that we get excited about the markets, the opportunities, that might seem small from the outside.
alts.zh: 我甚至要再加重語氣：那些從外面看起來很小的市場、很小的機會，我們反而會興奮。

alts.quote: What's interesting is that Silicon Valley has found a way to make the most profitable style of business the least profitable.
alts.zh: 有趣的是，矽谷居然有辦法把全世界最好賺的生意做成最不賺錢的生意。

cards.pattern: Maybe this is a harsh thing to say, but [直白的判斷]
cards.quote: Maybe this is a harsh thing to say, but I think very few companies have the talent caliber to be able to do that. So it might need to be adjusted if you were going to implement this.
cards.zh: 這樣講可能有點刺耳，但我覺得能做到這件事的公司真的很少。所以你要照搬的話，大概得先調整過。
cards.why: harsh 這個字讓你在說出難聽話之前先自我標註，聽者就會把它接收成「誠實」而非「不客氣」。更精細的是後面補了一句實用的調整建議——講完狠話留一條路，是英語職場給難聽回饋的完整動作。
swaps: This might come across as blunt, but...
I'll say the unpopular thing:
cards.pmNote: 介紹別家公司的做法時要標明前提條件（人才密度、規模、資金），否則會被當成通用最佳實務照抄。
cards.episode: The power user’s guide to Codex: parallelizing workflows, planning techniques, advanced context engineering tips, automating code reviews, and more | Alexander Embiricos

alts.quote: I would say there are a few things that PMs do that annoy engineers and to be clear, I am sure that engineers annoy PMs, just as much.
alts.zh: 我會說有幾件事是 PM 做了會惹惱工程師的——先講清楚，我相信工程師惹惱 PM 的程度也不遑多讓。

alts.quote: I think we do a disservice when we say we're not good at speaking up because it's a skill like any other.
alts.zh: 我覺得我們說自己「不擅長發言」是在害自己，因為那跟其他技能沒有兩樣。

alts.quote: The only answer I think one can have is, don't stick your head in the sand and say, "I hate all of this stuff," because that gives you a great feeling of moral superiority.
alts.zh: 我覺得唯一的答案是：別把頭埋進沙子裡說「我討厭這些東西」，因為那只會讓你很有道德優越感。

cards.pattern: We can have good conversations about a year out and about weeks out. But there's this awkward middle ground.
cards.quote: We can have really good conversations about something that's a year plus from now. And we can have really good conversations about what's happening in weeks. But there's this awkward middle ground.
cards.zh: 我們可以很好地討論一年以後的事，也可以很好地討論接下來幾週的事。但中間那一段就很尷尬。
cards.why: 把一個大家都隱約感覺到卻沒名字的困難命名為 awkward middle ground。給問題命名是資深者最有價值的動作之一——一旦有了名字，團隊就可以討論它、承認它、繞過它，而不是每次都重新卡住。
swaps: The hard horizon is the one in between.
Long-range and short-range are both tractable; the middle isn't.
cards.pmNote: 規劃週期要對應可預測性：一年看方向、幾週看執行，中間那段（一季到半年）刻意留彈性，別假裝能規劃。
cards.episode: The power user’s guide to Codex: parallelizing workflows, planning techniques, advanced context engineering tips, automating code reviews, and more | Alexander Embiricos

alts.quote: What's clearly happening is all of the functions are starting to bleed into each other, and the whole industry's wrestling with what that means.
alts.zh: 很明顯正在發生的是，各個職能開始互相滲透，而整個產業還在摸索這代表什麼。

alts.quote: So there's, I wouldn't say a checklist, but there's a series of questions that I asked to diagnose why is growth slowing in this order, because it's one of these things where the first one that's a problem, if you don't fix that, it doesn't matter if you fix one of the ones below.
alts.zh: 我不會說那是一張檢查清單，但我確實有一組問題，會照順序問下去診斷成長為什麼變慢——因為只要最前面那個沒修，後面修再多都沒用。

alts.quote: So I purposely chose the word complicit because complicit does not mean responsible, and that's a really important distinction.
alts.zh: 我是刻意選「共謀」這個詞的，因為共謀不等於負責，這個區別非常重要。

cards.pattern: It's a bit like [具體角色] that refuses to [行為] and doesn't [行為] unless you ask it to.
cards.quote: It's a bit like this really smart intern that refuses to read Slack and doesn't check Datadog or Sentry unless you ask it to.
cards.zh: 它有點像一個超聰明、但死不看 Slack、你不叫他他就不會去看 Datadog 或 Sentry 的實習生。
cards.why: 解釋一個抽象技術限制時，用「一個有性格缺陷的人」來比喻。refuses to（拒絕）把工具擬人化成有脾氣的同事，比 lacks context 這種正確但無感的說法好記十倍。要能用的關鍵是：比喻裡的缺點必須精準對應真實限制。
swaps: Think of it as a brilliant new hire with no access to any of your tools.
It's like a contractor who's never read your docs.
cards.pmNote: 向非技術利害關係人解釋 AI 能力邊界時，用「同事的能力與盲點」比講模型參數有效得多。
cards.episode: The power user’s guide to Codex: parallelizing workflows, planning techniques, advanced context engineering tips, automating code reviews, and more | Alexander Embiricos

alts.quote: And as smart as Stewart Butterfield is, he couldn't see Slack until he quit Glitch. And that is a true cost that he would've born of continuing with Glitch.
alts.zh: 連 Stewart Butterfield 這麼聰明的人，都是先關掉 Glitch 才看得見 Slack。而那就是繼續做下去真正的代價。

alts.quote: When, later, I would learn it's more of a boa constrictor.
alts.zh: 後來我才學到，它比較像一條蟒蛇慢慢把你絞緊。

alts.quote: You want to be that tree in the storm that is not so rigid that if the wind is too strong it's going to break in half, but not so flexible that it's going to swing every which direction as soon as there's a gust.
alts.zh: 你要當風暴裡的那棵樹——不要硬到風一大就攔腰折斷，也不要軟到一陣風來就往每個方向亂晃。

cards.pattern: I'm not going to try to define [術語] exactly, but at least [你能給的操作型描述]
cards.quote: And I'm not going to try to define agent exactly, but at least the stack that we think of it as having is you have this model, really smart reasoning model.
cards.zh: 我不打算給 agent 一個精準的定義，但至少我們認為它的堆疊長這樣：底下有一個很會推理的模型。
cards.why: 拒絕定義，但給出操作型描述。這一招讓你完全避開「定義之爭」這種最浪費時間的討論，同時仍然把事情講清楚。at least 這個轉折詞是關鍵——它承認你給的不是完整答案，但也是有用的答案。
swaps: I won't attempt a definition, but here's how we use the word:
Rather than define it, let me describe what it does.
cards.pmNote: 討論新概念時先講「我們在這個 context 下怎麼用這個詞」，可以省下整場會議的名詞戰爭。
cards.episode: The power user’s guide to Codex: parallelizing workflows, planning techniques, advanced context engineering tips, automating code reviews, and more | Alexander Embiricos

alts.quote: I don't understand what this is, and I'm not the right person for this role," and it turned out, nobody understood exactly what was going on.
alts.zh: 「我看不懂這是什麼，我也不是這個職位該找的人」——結果發現，根本沒有人真的搞懂在發生什麼事。

alts.quote: I mean, I think Things probably, I'm just guessing, I don't know any of the numbers or whatever, but I would assume it makes between five and $25 million of revenue, which to a VC is not even worth considering a VC.
alts.zh: 我是說，Things 這款——我純粹在猜，數字我完全不知道——但我猜它一年營收大概在五百萬到兩千五百萬美金之間，這種規模對創投來說根本不值得看。

alts.quote: And there were some studies around this too, I think that there's, I think in, I'm not sure exactly, I just have to go check up on this.
alts.zh: 我不太確定，這個我得回去查一下。

cards.quote: So I'll give you a contention and a plausible way we get there, but as for how it happens, who knows?
cards.zh: 我可以給你一個主張，還有一條看起來說得通的路徑，但實際上會怎麼發生，誰知道。
cards.why: 把答案明確拆成三層：主張（我相信什麼）、路徑（一種可能的走法）、機制（我不知道）。這種分層讓你能大膽預測而不必為細節負責。who knows 這種近乎隨性的收尾，在英語裡是自信的表現，不是敷衍。
swaps: Here's the claim and one path to it—the actual route, no idea.
I'll give you the destination and a plausible route, not a schedule.
cards.pmNote: 談長期願景時要明確區分「我們相信的終局」與「我們規劃的路徑」，後者一定會改，前者不該常改。
cards.episode: The power user’s guide to Codex: parallelizing workflows, planning techniques, advanced context engineering tips, automating code reviews, and more | Alexander Embiricos

alts.quote: I'll admit I'm definitely not an SEO expert. I've been fortunate to work with some of the best marketers in the world who I think are bonafide legends at this point
alts.zh: 我坦白說我絕對不是 SEO 專家。我只是很幸運跟一些世界頂尖的行銷人共事過，那些人到今天都算是真正的傳奇。

alts.quote: I always assume that the buyer I'm speaking to is highly educated and knows way more than I do.
alts.zh: 我永遠假設坐在對面的買家很懂，而且懂的比我多很多。

alts.quote: And I don't know when it's going to saturate and nobody else knows either, but when that happens, the next frontier is the physical world.
alts.zh: 我不知道它什麼時候會飽和，別人也都不知道，但等它飽和的那天，下一個戰場就是實體世界。

cards.pattern: I'm coming up with this on the spot, so it's not a good name, but [新概念]
cards.quote: So almost that it's like, I'm coming up with this on the spot, so it's not a good name, but chatter-driven development.
cards.zh: 有點像是——這名字是我現場亂想的，取得不好——「閒聊驅動開發」。
cards.why: 即興提出新概念時，先替名字道歉，重點就會落在概念本身而不是命名。on the spot（當場）這個片語明確標記了「未經打磨」，讓你可以放心丟出半成品想法。腦力激盪時這句幾乎萬用。
swaps: Terrible name, I just made it up, but the idea is—
Working title, don't judge it:
cards.pmNote: 腦力激盪階段要刻意把想法標成粗胚，否則團隊會開始批評包裝而不是討論核心。
cards.episode: The power user’s guide to Codex: parallelizing workflows, planning techniques, advanced context engineering tips, automating code reviews, and more | Alexander Embiricos

alts.quote: I think a lot of people think about markets almost like these bodies of water. And it's like, "Oh, it's this big body of water that we're going after." And I actually think that the most interesting markets, you have to think of them like currents.
alts.zh: 很多人把市場想成一片水域，覺得「喔，我們要去攻的是這一大片水」。但我覺得最有意思的市場，你得把它想成水流。

alts.quote: So for positioning work, I'm going to say something that is contentious, but I don't think it is at all.
alts.zh: 講到定位這件事，我要說一句大家可能覺得很有爭議的話——但我完全不覺得有爭議。

alts.quote: I sat for about a half a day and I thought, I think I can help here, drew out an org chart, put my name on the top, walked into my boss's office and said, "This is one potential solve of your marketing organization question."
alts.zh: 我想了大概半天，覺得我應該幫得上忙，就畫了一張組織圖，把自己放在最上面，走進我主管辦公室說：「這是你那個行銷組織問題的其中一個解法。」

cards.quote: Yeah. To be clear, we're not building that, but it's a fun idea.
cards.zh: 喔對，先說清楚，我們沒有要做這個，只是覺得這想法很好玩。
cards.why: 剛剛講了一個生動的假設情境，馬上澄清那不是產品計畫。To be clear 是英語裡專門用來防止誤引的訊號詞——尤其在公開場合、錄音、對媒體時是必備動作。台灣人常忘記做這一步，結果一個玩笑被寫成新聞標題。
swaps: That's not a roadmap item, just a thought experiment.
Hypothetical only—don't put that in the notes.
cards.pmNote: 對外談假設情境前後都要標記「這不是承諾」，任何被聽成 roadmap 的東西之後都會有人來要交期。
cards.episode: The power user’s guide to Codex: parallelizing workflows, planning techniques, advanced context engineering tips, automating code reviews, and more | Alexander Embiricos

alts.quote: What I'm hearing is the core issues, we're not able to feel our emotion.
alts.zh: 我聽到的重點是：核心問題在於我們沒辦法真的感受到自己的情緒。

alts.quote: And if it's helpful, let me break down the question a little bit.
alts.zh: 如果有幫助的話，我把這個問題拆開來講一下。

alts.quote: Just to be clear, I love Claude.
alts.zh: 先說清楚，我很愛 Claude。

cards.pattern: I'm curious what you think. I still don't think [流行看法] as much as a lot of people think.
cards.quote: I'm curious what you think. I still don't think ideas are worth as much as maybe a lot of people think. I still think execution is really hard.
cards.zh: 我反而想聽你怎麼看。我還是不覺得點子有大家講的那麼值錢，我還是覺得執行才難。
cards.why: 先把發言權遞出去（I'm curious what you think），再講自己的反對意見——這個順序讓反對變成對話而不是宣告。still 這個副詞也很妙：暗示「我知道風向變了，但我沒被說服」，堅持得很有禮貌。
swaps: Curious how you see it—I'm not convinced that's true.
I might be in the minority here, but I still think...
cards.pmNote: 反駁流行論述時先問對方看法，可以在你不知道對方立場時避免正面衝撞。
cards.episode: The power user’s guide to Codex: parallelizing workflows, planning techniques, advanced context engineering tips, automating code reviews, and more | Alexander Embiricos

alts.quote: Again, don't get me wrong, I'm not trying to talk people out of doing it. But for me, a lot of this was luck.
alts.zh: 先說清楚，我不是想勸大家不要做。但對我來說，這裡面有很大一部分是運氣。

alts.quote: And don't get me wrong, I think there's a lot of product folks out there who enjoy that modality of work, I'm not one of them.
alts.zh: 別誤會，我知道有很多產品人是真的喜歡那種工作方式的——我不是。

alts.quote: So I think it's an unnecessary addition, but maybe I'm just being protective of my original idea.
alts.zh: 我覺得那是多此一舉的補充，不過也可能只是我在護著自己原本的想法啦。

cards.pattern: If I could only choose one thing to [做/懂], it would be [X].
cards.quote: But now I think we're getting to this point where actually if I could only choose one thing to understand, it would be really meaningful understanding of the problems that a certain customer has.
cards.zh: 但我覺得我們現在走到一個階段：如果只能挑一件事搞懂，那就是真正深刻地了解某一群客戶的問題。
cards.why: If I could only choose one thing 是強迫自己排序的句型，也逼聽者接受這是取捨而非清單。比起列出五個重點，這種「只准選一個」的假設能讓你的主張穿透力大得多，適合用在建議、面試、給後輩指路。
swaps: If you only invest in one thing, make it—
Forced to pick a single competency, I'd take...
cards.pmNote: 建構能力時要先問「哪一項最難被 AI 或工具取代」——多半是對特定客戶問題的深度理解。
cards.episode: The power user’s guide to Codex: parallelizing workflows, planning techniques, advanced context engineering tips, automating code reviews, and more | Alexander Embiricos

alts.quote: And I think people don't understand that in a competitive environment, being right is good, but being quick is necessary.
alts.zh: 我覺得大家沒搞懂：在競爭環境裡，做對是加分，做得快是必要條件。

alts.quote: So I think a lot of times we just think, okay, this is the scope of it for now and we are okay launching this and the execution is good. But we know that this is not the fully figured out version.
alts.zh: 很多時候我們就是這樣想：現階段範圍就到這裡，執行品質夠好，可以上。但我們知道這還不是完整想通的版本。

alts.quote: And now, it's not like, "Okay, now, we're screwed and the project is going to be bigger." Now, we can have a really cool conversation about trade-offs.
alts.zh: 所以現在不是「完了，這專案要爆了」。現在我們可以來一場很棒的取捨對話。

cards.pattern: We can accidentally spend a lot of time on [某類事], and so we can end up oversolving for that.
cards.quote: So we can accidentally spend a lot of our time thinking about features that are very deep in the user adoption journey. And so we can kind of end up oversolving for that.
cards.zh: 我們很容易不小心把時間都花在使用者旅程很後段的功能上，結果就在那一段過度投入了。
cards.why: accidentally 和 end up 這兩個詞把一個團隊層級的錯誤講成「沒人故意的漂移」，沒有人被指責，問題卻被講清楚了。oversolving 是很好用的自創複合詞——不是做錯，是做太多，這種區分在資源討論時特別重要。
swaps: We drift towards the problems we personally feel.
There's a gravitational pull towards power-user features.
cards.pmNote: 團隊都是重度使用者時，會系統性高估進階功能、低估新手體驗——固定回頭看 D7 retention 是最簡單的解藥。
cards.episode: The power user’s guide to Codex: parallelizing workflows, planning techniques, advanced context engineering tips, automating code reviews, and more | Alexander Embiricos

alts.quote: Success is an output of a lot of failures, but the question is, how much time do you have to fail?
alts.zh: 成功是一堆失敗的產物，但問題是：你有多少時間可以失敗？

alts.quote: I often say most communication in business is round white and flavorless, intentionally so, because a lot of people are afraid to stand out.
alts.zh: 我常說，商業場合的溝通大多是圓的、白的、沒有味道的——而且是故意的，因為大家都怕突出。

alts.quote: That was one of the big motivations, actually identifying that user problem, being very disgruntled on behalf of the user. We're just failing the user every day.
alts.zh: 那就是最大的動力之一：真的把使用者的問題認出來，然後代替使用者生氣。我們每天都在辜負他們。

cards.pattern: I worked on [X] for a bit. I don't work on it now. But [你能講的角度]
cards.quote: So I worked on Atlas for a bit. I don't work on it now. But a bit of the narrative here for me just to tell my story a bit was...
cards.zh: 我做過 Atlas 一陣子，現在沒在做了。不過就我自己的角度、講一下我的版本的話……
cards.why: 被問到你只沾過邊的專案時，兩句話劃清界線再開口。for a bit（一陣子）與 I don't work on it now 把你的發言權限講得很精準，後面 my story 又進一步限縮成個人視角。這樣講出來的內容，就算之後被證明不完整也傷不到你。
swaps: I was on that team early on, not anymore—so from my angle...
I've got partial context on that. Here's my slice of it.
cards.pmNote: 跨團隊回答問題時先聲明你的資訊新鮮度，避免過期資訊被當成現況傳出去。
cards.episode: The power user’s guide to Codex: parallelizing workflows, planning techniques, advanced context engineering tips, automating code reviews, and more | Alexander Embiricos

alts.quote: We have this name, but we don't know how to tell the story around it.
alts.zh: 我們有了這個名字，但我們不知道要怎麼把它的故事講出來。

alts.quote: I can't speak to that whole period. But what I can tell you about what I'm feeling now is just an incredible sense of focus and urgency to deliver great products quickly.
alts.zh: 那一整段期間我沒辦法評論。但我可以告訴你現在的感受——一種非常強烈的專注感和急迫感，就是要快點把好產品交出去。

alts.quote: Now, I don't know what Claude Code is doing, obviously, but I would be willing to bet money that they're doing something in the form of evals.
alts.zh: 我當然不知道 Claude Code 內部到底在幹嘛，但我敢拿錢賭他們一定有在做某種形式的 evals。

cards.quote: I will say if you're like, the hardest problem I have is that I need to build a new unicorn business, obviously that's not going to work. Not yet.
cards.zh: 當然啦，如果你說「我最難的問題是要生出一家獨角獸」，那顯然行不通。目前還不行。
cards.why: 剛給完一個很大方的建議（把最難的問題丟給它），立刻自己畫出上限，防止對方測試到荒謬的邊界然後說你唬爛。Not yet 這個獨立短句是精髓——同時承認現在的限制與未來的可能，兩個字做完兩件事。
swaps: There's obviously a ceiling—we're not there yet.
Within reason, of course.
cards.pmNote: 宣傳產品能力時主動標出「還做不到什麼」，可以擋掉大量因期待落差而流失的新用戶。
cards.episode: The power user’s guide to Codex: parallelizing workflows, planning techniques, advanced context engineering tips, automating code reviews, and more | Alexander Embiricos

alts.quote: Now, obviously if you live in a small town and they capped the well and gave all the water to the data center, then you're really pissed off. But that's a planning problem. That's not a data center problem.
alts.zh: 當然，如果你住在小鎮上，井被封了、水全給了資料中心，那你當然火大。但那是都市規劃的問題，不是資料中心的問題。

alts.quote: That's why you need your job search council. This is when you really need to ask for help because every bone in your body is going to say, "I'm not going to negotiate. That's going to make it worse," and it almost never does.
alts.zh: 這就是為什麼你需要求職小組。你全身上下每根骨頭都會喊：「我不要談判，談了只會更糟。」但幾乎從來不會更糟。

alts.quote: So they would say, "Oh, your market's not big enough." And I would say, "It's going to be huge." And I'd add a new page in my pitch deck that said how big the market I believe was.
alts.zh: 他們會說：「你的市場不夠大。」我就說：「它會變超大。」然後我就在簡報裡加一頁，講我認為這市場有多大。

cards.pattern: Unfortunately, I don't think that's going to be binary. It's going to be very dependent on [變數].
cards.quote: So if we can rebuild systems to let the agent be default useful, we'll start unlocking hockey sticks. Unfortunately, I don't think that's going to be binary.
cards.zh: 所以如果我們能把系統重建成讓 agent 預設就有用，成長曲線就會開始往上翹。可惜我不覺得這會是一刀切的事。
cards.why: Unfortunately 放在句首不是在道歉，而是在標記「接下來要講的事不符合大家的期待」。binary 這個字精準表達了「不會有一個明確的時間點」，比 gradual 有力——因為它直接否定了提問者心中的模型。
swaps: It won't be a switch that flips.
There's no single moment—it'll be uneven across companies.
cards.pmNote: 談技術轉型時間點時，用「不同族群何時跨過門檻」取代「哪一年會發生」，判斷才有實用價值。
cards.episode: The power user’s guide to Codex: parallelizing workflows, planning techniques, advanced context engineering tips, automating code reviews, and more | Alexander Embiricos

alts.quote: I don't think we should filter out AI content. I think we should let you know if content is AI content or not. That's hard, by the way.
alts.zh: 我不認為我們該把 AI 內容濾掉。我認為該做的是讓你知道這則內容是不是 AI 產的。順帶一提，這很難。

alts.quote: We don't know if we're going to actually end up going, and based on the results whether we're going to actually move forward with investing in that area, but that's a body of work we can commit to.
alts.zh: 我們不知道最後會不會真的往那邊走、也要看結果才知道要不要真的投資那個領域，但那是一塊我們可以承諾投入的工作量。

alts.quote: And I don't know how to vet companies, I don't know how to really logically think through what space is going to take off or something like that, but I just do feel like I have a sense on people.
alts.zh: 我不知道怎麼審公司、也不知道怎麼有邏輯地判斷哪個領域會起飛，但我就是覺得我對人有直覺。

cards.pattern: So my long answer to your question—maybe boring answer—is that [結論]
cards.quote: So basically my long answer to your question, maybe boring answer is that I think starting next year, we're going to see early adopters starting to hockey stick their productivity.
cards.zh: 所以我這個落落長、可能還有點無聊的答案就是：我覺得從明年開始，早期採用者的生產力會開始往上翹。
cards.why: 講了很長一段之後，用 So my long answer is that 把整段壓縮成一句。這是英語會議裡非常受歡迎的動作——聽者已經累了，你替他做總結。中間插入 maybe boring answer 又順手降低期待，讓結論即使平淡也不失望。
swaps: The short version of all that is—
To land the plane: my answer is...
cards.pmNote: 長篇回答一定要自己收尾成一句，否則聽者記走的會是他自己挑的那句，而不是你的結論。
cards.episode: The power user’s guide to Codex: parallelizing workflows, planning techniques, advanced context engineering tips, automating code reviews, and more | Alexander Embiricos

alts.quote: I know I keep saying we're going to wrap this up, but here's a question and if it doesn't work, we'll get rid of it.
alts.zh: 我知道我一直說要收尾了，但這裡有個問題——如果行不通，我們就把它砍掉。

alts.quote: I'm going to mirror back the tips you just shared, and there's actually a secondary tip that I think is the more interesting piece.
alts.zh: 我把你剛剛給的建議重述一遍——而且我覺得裡面藏了一個更有意思的第二層建議。

alts.quote: So maybe this is a way to come back to your question about what's the output of the shaping session, it's like it's shaped if we can give this to a technical person and they say, "Yeah, I know what to go build now."
alts.zh: 所以回到你剛剛問的「shaping session 的產出是什麼」：判準是——把它交給一個技術的人，他會說「好，我知道要蓋什麼了」。

cards.pattern: We would realize that we were in fact not [X] six months ago, and we needed to be even more [X].
cards.quote: We would remind ourselves of this motto and then we would become more candid. And then six months later, we would realize that we were in fact not candid six months ago.
cards.zh: 我們會提醒自己這句座右銘，然後變得更坦白一點。結果半年後又發現，半年前的我們其實一點也不坦白。
cards.why: 承認一個「反覆犯的錯」而不是一次性的錯，難度高很多。in fact 這個插入語在這裡帶著自嘲的重量——事實跟我們當時的自我認知不符。這種螺旋式的自我修正敘事，在績效檢討和團隊回顧時特別有說服力。
swaps: Every six months we discover we were still sugar-coating things.
In hindsight, what felt direct at the time really wasn't.
cards.pmNote: 回顧會議要問「半年前我們以為自己做到了什麼，其實沒做到」——這比列新問題更能抓到系統性盲點。
cards.episode: The power user’s guide to Codex: parallelizing workflows, planning techniques, advanced context engineering tips, automating code reviews, and more | Alexander Embiricos

alts.quote: So I actually ended up not letting the team run this experiment for six months so that we focus on lower hanging fruit. So that's a mistake on my end.
alts.zh: 所以我其實壓著這個實驗六個月沒讓團隊做，因為想先撿低垂的果實。這是我的錯。

alts.quote: And the big epiphany, we already talked about it, it shouldn't have taken me this long to realize that anytime an employee fails, it's your fault.
alts.zh: 我最大的頓悟——其實前面也提過——是我不該這麼晚才明白：只要有員工陣亡，那都是你的錯。

alts.quote: I feel really bad because I'm like, it should have been obvious. We should have been able to call a spade a spade and I guess speak truth to power.
alts.zh: 我到現在還是很懊惱，因為這件事本來就該一眼看穿。我們應該有辦法直話直說，向上把真話講出來。

cards.quote: So then the question is, how should we be candid? Okay, well, let's think of being candid as an act of kindness.
cards.zh: 所以問題變成：我們該怎麼坦白？後來想通了——把「坦白」當成一種善意的行為。
cards.why: 把兩個看似對立的價值（kind 與 candid）用 as an act of 綁在一起，直言就不再需要在善良與誠實之間選邊。這個句型 think of X as an act of Y 很好移植——把任何令人不安的行為重新歸類成一種美德。
swaps: Directness is the kind thing to do here.
Withholding the truth isn't kindness, it's avoidance.
cards.pmNote: 延遲難談的對話幾乎總是讓成本變高——把坦白重新定義成善意，是團隊敢給真回饋的文化前提。
cards.episode: The power user’s guide to Codex: parallelizing workflows, planning techniques, advanced context engineering tips, automating code reviews, and more | Alexander Embiricos

alts.quote: This is how we think about things. This is how we handle this type of behavior here. If that's hard for you, let's find you another job.
alts.zh: 我們就是這樣想事情的。這種狀況我們在這裡就是這樣處理的。如果你覺得很難接受，那我們一起幫你找個別的工作。

alts.quote: And it's not because people are bad people. I think most people are really well-intentioned. But what happens when you have people that join and you didn't really need them?
alts.zh: 這不是因為誰是壞人，我覺得大多數人動機都很好。但問題是：當你招了一批其實不需要的人，會發生什麼事？

alts.quote: I think we do a disservice when we say we're not good at speaking up because it's a skill like any other.
alts.zh: 我覺得我們說自己「不擅長發言」是在害自己，因為那跟其他技能沒有兩樣。

cards.pattern: We don't have to agree on [大方向], but [你真正在乎的條件]
cards.quote: We're very interested in folks who have already been thinking about what the future should look like with agents. And we don't have to agree on where we're going, but we want people who are very passionate.
cards.zh: 我們很想找那種已經在思考「agent 的未來該長什麼樣」的人。方向上我們不一定要有共識，但我們要真的在乎這件事的人。
cards.why: 明講「不必同意我」是很高階的招募與協作訊號——你把門檻從「立場一致」換成「投入程度」。don't have to agree on X, but 這個結構在跨團隊合作時也很好用：先解除對方的立場壓力，再講你真正的要求。
swaps: You don't have to share my view—you do have to have one.
Disagreement is fine. Indifference isn't.
cards.pmNote: 招人時測「有沒有觀點」比測「觀點對不對」有用——觀點會改，思考習慣不會。
cards.episode: The power user’s guide to Codex: parallelizing workflows, planning techniques, advanced context engineering tips, automating code reviews, and more | Alexander Embiricos

alts.quote: And I know this is going to trigger some people, but the truth is they don't want to work.
alts.zh: 我知道這句會讓一些人不爽，但事實就是——他們不想做事。

alts.quote: Something I caution people against though is don't use the data alone to figure out who the marginal user is.
alts.zh: 不過有件事我會提醒大家小心：不要只靠數據去判斷誰是邊際使用者。

alts.quote: And it's kind of building a house that you want every brick in the house to match. And if you go and try and take some bricks from someone else's house and stick it in your house, it's probably going to not look very matched.
alts.zh: 這有點像蓋房子，你會希望每一塊磚都是搭的。如果你跑去人家家裡搬幾塊磚塞進自己家，看起來大概就是不搭。

cards.pattern: Most people spend too much time on [大家都同意的部分] and not enough time on [真正有價值的部分]
cards.quote: Most writers, most course instructors spend too much time on the what and the why and not enough time on how.
cards.zh: 大部分寫作者、大部分課程講師，都花太多時間在「是什麼」跟「為什麼」，花太少時間在「怎麼做」。
cards.why: 這是一個「重新分配注意力」的開場句型——它不否定任何人，只說比例錯了，所以聽的人不會防衛。台灣人提案常寫成「我認為應該…」，這句改成診斷比例，一開口就站在後設位置。
swaps: We're over-indexed on the why and under-indexed on the how.
We keep re-litigating whether to do it instead of how we'd do it.
cards.pmNote: roadmap 會議上多數人已同意「這件事重要」，真正卡住的永遠是 how——把時間押在 how 才推得動決策。
cards.episode: Become a better communicator: Specific frameworks to improve your clarity, influence, and impact | Wes Kao (coach, entrepreneur, advisor)

alts.quote: and not to be too spiritual about this, but it really goes right to the issue of ego identification
alts.zh: 不是想把這件事講得太玄，但它真的直接踩到「自我認同」這個問題。

alts.quote: So when we reprogram ourselves to think in terms of opportunity cost, we are no longer thinking, 'Oh, is this a good use of my time?' Instead, you are thinking, 'Is this the best use of my time?'
alts.zh: 一旦改用機會成本思考，你就不再問「這樣用時間好不好？」，而是問「這是不是我時間最好的用法？」

alts.quote: speaking with adjacency, which means we're not going to match content to content. Instead, we're going to match theme, meaning or message.
alts.zh: 我把它叫做「鄰近敘事」，意思是我們不去對內容，而是去對主題、意義或訊息。

cards.pattern: There's already a point of view baked in, but you don't want it to be an accidental [point of view]
cards.quote: A lot of times when we write a sentence, there's actually already a point of view baked in, but you don't want it to be an accidental point of view.
cards.zh: 很多時候我們寫一句話，裡面其實已經藏了一個立場——但你不會希望那是一個「不小心跑出來的」立場。
cards.why: baked in（早就烤進去了）＋ accidental（不小心的）這組搭配，把「你以為自己中立其實不中立」講得很輕。用來提醒同事、或替自己的提案辯護都不傷人。
swaps: There's a recommendation hiding in here—let's make it explicit.
You're steering the reader whether you meant to or not.
cards.pmNote: framing 決定討論走向。同一份資料，寫法不同，會議結論就不同——所以立場要「刻意」而不是「不小心」。
cards.episode: Become a better communicator: Specific frameworks to improve your clarity, influence, and impact | Wes Kao (coach, entrepreneur, advisor)

alts.quote: So my two pieces of advice, anybody that's actually trying to do this is, A, state the problem, and, B, don't call it a strategy, call it an action agenda.
alts.zh: 我給真的要動手的人兩個建議：A，把問題講出來；B，不要叫它策略，叫它「行動議程」。

alts.quote: I think a lot of people think about markets almost like these bodies of water. And it's like, "Oh, it's this big body of water that we're going after." And I actually think that the most interesting markets, you have to think of them like currents.
alts.zh: 很多人把市場想成一片水域，覺得「喔，我們要去攻的是這一大片水」。但我覺得最有意思的市場，你得把它想成水流。

alts.quote: So for positioning work, I'm going to say something that is contentious, but I don't think it is at all.
alts.zh: 講到定位這件事，我要說一句大家可能覺得很有爭議的話——但我完全不覺得有爭議。

cards.quote: Is that your recommendation? Because if it is then great, because you're leading the reader to that conclusion. But if it's not, you're asking a leading question that is skewing the results.
cards.zh: 那是你的建議嗎？如果是，那很好，因為你正在把讀者帶往那個結論。但如果不是，那你就是在問一個誘導性的問題，會扭曲你收到的答案。
cards.why: 先給對方一條退路（if it is, then great），再指出問題（if it's not…）。這個 if A / if B 雙分支結構，讓一句本來很像指責的話變成純粹的釐清。
