swaps: Are you asking, or are you telling? Both are fine—just pick one.
Do you want input, or do you want a sign-off?
cards.pmNote: 問題怎麼問，決定你收到什麼答案。要真實回饋就別把答案寫進題目裡。
cards.episode: Become a better communicator: Specific frameworks to improve your clarity, influence, and impact | Wes Kao (coach, entrepreneur, advisor)

alts.quote: None of this is going to blow anyone's minds, I think, because it's very best practices. But it's easy to overlook when you're so focused on so many different steps of a process.
alts.zh: 這些應該不會讓誰驚呆，因為都是很基本的最佳實務。但當你同時盯著流程裡一大堆步驟時，就是很容易漏掉。

alts.quote: I sat for about a half a day and I thought, I think I can help here, drew out an org chart, put my name on the top, walked into my boss's office and said, "This is one potential solve of your marketing organization question."
alts.zh: 我想了大概半天，覺得我應該幫得上忙，就畫了一張組織圖，把自己放在最上面，走進我主管辦公室說：「這是你那個行銷組織問題的其中一個解法。」

alts.quote: So what we often encourage people to do is keep working the way you're working, but some future project, some low criticality project, try this new method on that.
alts.zh: 我們常建議的是：現在的做法照舊，但挑一個之後的、沒那麼要緊的專案，在那上面試新方法。

cards.pattern: [X] is not a specialized skill, it's a meta skill. That means the better you get at [X], the better [更大的東西] gets.
cards.quote: Speaking is not a specialized skill, it's a meta skill. That means that the better you get at speaking, the better your life gets.
cards.zh: 說話不是一項專門技能，它是一項後設技能。意思是：你說話越強，你的人生就越好。
cards.why: 把提案從「一個功能」升級成「一種槓桿」的標準做法：先否定小分類，再給大分類，最後用 That means 推出結論。三步走完，聽的人自己算完了投報率。
swaps: This isn't a feature, it's a platform bet.
Onboarding isn't a screen, it's a multiplier on everything downstream.
cards.pmNote: 提案要提高優先序，最有效的一招是重新歸類：從「一個需求」變成「一個會放大所有其他東西的底層能力」。
cards.episode: Why most public speaking advice is wrong—and how to finally overcome your speaking anxiety | Tristan de Montebello (CEO & co-founder of Ultraspeaking)

alts.quote: speaking with adjacency, which means we're not going to match content to content. Instead, we're going to match theme, meaning or message.
alts.zh: 我把它叫做「鄰近敘事」，意思是我們不去對內容，而是去對主題、意義或訊息。

alts.quote: How do I make this idea one click better? It's not about how do you do something radically, radically different, but taking ideas and then making it slightly better, slightly better.
alts.zh: 我要怎麼把這個想法再往上推一格？重點不是做出天差地遠的東西，而是接手別人的想法，再讓它好一點點。

alts.quote: None of this is going to blow anyone's minds, I think, because it's very best practices. But it's easy to overlook when you're so focused on so many different steps of a process.
alts.zh: 這些應該不會讓誰驚呆，因為都是很基本的最佳實務。但當你同時盯著流程裡一大堆步驟時，就是很容易漏掉。

cards.pattern: Instead of focusing on the symptoms of [X], I started to figure out what are the root causes that create these symptoms.
cards.quote: Instead of focusing on the symptoms of speaking, I started to try and figure out, well, what are the root causes that create these symptoms, and can I address those?
cards.zh: 與其盯著說話的「症狀」，我開始去找：造成這些症狀的根因是什麼？我有沒有辦法解決那個？
cards.why: symptoms / root causes 這組醫學隱喻在英文商業場合是萬用的，而且自帶說服力——沒有人會主張「我們就治症狀就好」。用 Instead of… I started to… 開場，還順便暗示你已經走過一輪。
swaps: We keep patching the symptom; I want to go one layer down.
Filler words are downstream of something else—let's fix that instead.
cards.pmNote: 把一串抱怨收斂成一個可解的根因，就是 problem statement 的工作。修症狀便宜但會一直復發。
cards.episode: Why most public speaking advice is wrong—and how to finally overcome your speaking anxiety | Tristan de Montebello (CEO & co-founder of Ultraspeaking)

alts.quote: speaking with adjacency, which means we're not going to match content to content. Instead, we're going to match theme, meaning or message.
alts.zh: 我把它叫做「鄰近敘事」，意思是我們不去對內容，而是去對主題、意義或訊息。

alts.quote: I think step one is the step that almost everyone misses on SEO, which is be the user. Try to understand who your user is.
alts.zh: 我覺得第一步就是幾乎每個人都跳過的那一步：去當那個使用者。先弄懂你的使用者是誰。

alts.quote: These are things we're going to do, not goals we're going to achieve. These are things we're going to do, action steps.
alts.zh: 這些是我們要做的事，不是我們要達成的目標。就是要做的事，是行動步驟。

cards.pattern: The old way is broken, and I haven't found anything out there that is innovating on this.
cards.quote: The old way I think is shitty. I think it's broken, and I haven't found anything out there that is innovating on this.
cards.zh: 舊的做法我覺得很爛。我覺得它是壞的，而且我沒看到市面上有任何人在改良它。
cards.why: 推新方案前先把舊方案的墓碑立好——而且第二句「我找過了，沒人在做」把你的主張從「意見」升級成「掃描過市場後的結論」。台灣人常直接跳到方案，少了這個真空。
swaps: The status quo here is genuinely broken, and nobody's touched it in years.
I looked around for prior art and came up empty—that's why I'm proposing this.
cards.pmNote: 提新方向前先製造真空：說清楚舊路為什麼壞掉，新路才有位置站。
cards.episode: Why most public speaking advice is wrong—and how to finally overcome your speaking anxiety | Tristan de Montebello (CEO & co-founder of Ultraspeaking)

alts.quote: I'll just run this as a thought experiment and you can see what you think on this, but it's like, are AI models themselves defensible?
alts.zh: 我把它當成一個思想實驗丟出來，你自己判斷——AI 模型本身到底有沒有護城河？

alts.quote: the best way to get feedback from people is not by asking what they think, but to put something concrete in front of them and then have them react to it, right?
alts.zh: 要拿到回饋，最好的方式不是問人家怎麼想，而是先擺一個具體的東西在他面前，讓他反應，對吧？

alts.quote: I actually think it's easier. Spicy take.
alts.zh: 我其實覺得更容易。這個看法比較嗆。

cards.pattern: Now, I'm biased when I say this, so take this with a pinch of salt, but [大膽主張]
cards.quote: Now, I'm biased when I'm going to say this, so take this with a pinch of salt, but I think the Accordion Method might be one of the things I'm the most proud of in my entire life.
cards.zh: 我要講的這件事我是有偏見的，所以你打個折聽——但我覺得手風琴法可能是我這輩子最引以為傲的東西之一。
cards.why: 先自己承認偏見，反而換到了講大話的許可證。這是英文說服裡最好用的一組槓桿：hedge 越誠實，後面的 claim 就能越大。
swaps: Obviously I'm not objective here, but I'd argue this is the single biggest lever we have.
Discount this however much you need to, but I think this is the most important thing on the list.
cards.pmNote: 你是提案人，聽眾本來就會替你的話打折。你自己先打，剩下的可信度就都是真的。
cards.episode: Why most public speaking advice is wrong—and how to finally overcome your speaking anxiety | Tristan de Montebello (CEO & co-founder of Ultraspeaking)

alts.quote: So for positioning work, I'm going to say something that is contentious, but I don't think it is at all.
alts.zh: 講到定位這件事，我要說一句大家可能覺得很有爭議的話——但我完全不覺得有爭議。

alts.quote: I'm going to tell my boss, on Monday, that I think we should do that. I'm going to use a little social capital and say we should do this.
alts.zh: 我禮拜一會跟我主管講，我覺得這個該做。我會動用一點我的政治額度，去替它說話。

alts.quote: I think going to college is great. I think this is a somewhat contrarian view within tech, maybe not in the broader economy.
alts.zh: 我覺得念大學很棒。我知道這在科技圈算是個有點逆風的看法，在一般社會可能就還好。

cards.pattern: Stop focusing as much on what you want to say and focus more on what you want [對象] to remember.
cards.quote: Stop focusing as much on what you want to say and focus more on what you want your audience to remember.
cards.zh: 別再那麼在意「你想說什麼」，多想想「你想讓聽眾記住什麼」。
cards.why: Stop focusing as much on A and focus more on B——注意是 as much，不是全盤否定，所以聽起來是調整而不是推翻。這個句型在改別人簡報、改 PRD 時都能直接套。
swaps: Optimize for what lands, not for what you cover.
The question isn't what we present, it's what they walk out with.
cards.pmNote: 簡報的成功指標不是「講完」，是「一週後對方還記得的那一句」。
cards.episode: Why most public speaking advice is wrong—and how to finally overcome your speaking anxiety | Tristan de Montebello (CEO & co-founder of Ultraspeaking)

alts.quote: I want you to pull the hiring manager aside and say, "Hey, Lenny, you're the hiring manager. I've thought about what the role is. I want to make sure I'm understanding it correctly.
alts.zh: 我要你把用人主管拉到一旁說：「我想過這個職位到底是什麼，我想確認我理解得對不對。我可以跟你分享一下嗎？」

alts.quote: So here's the really wonderful thing about moving from a coercive model to really, I guess you could say a model of curiosity, right? You want to be curious, not coercive.
alts.zh: 從一個高壓的模式，換成一個好奇的模式——你要的是好奇，不是強迫。

alts.quote: If you start your story with 'Our company is,' you focus on your solution. If you start with 'The problem we are solving is,' then you focus on the problem.
alts.zh: 如果你的故事開頭是「我們公司是…」，你的焦點就在解法。如果開頭是「我們要解決的問題是…」，焦點就在問題上。

cards.pattern: If you start your story with '[A]', you focus on [A的重點]. If you start with '[B]', you focus on [B的重點].
cards.quote: If you start your story with 'Our company is,' you focus on your solution. If you start with 'The problem we are solving is,' then you focus on the problem.
cards.zh: 如果你的故事開頭是「我們公司是…」，你的焦點就在解法。如果開頭是「我們要解決的問題是…」，焦點就在問題上。
cards.why: 把兩個開場白並排，讓聽眾自己看見差別——這種 If A… If B… 的對照結構不需要你下判斷，結論會自己浮出來。也是最容易背起來直接用的骨架。
swaps: 'We built…' puts the spotlight on us. 'Users can't…' puts it on them.
Lead with the metric and you'll get a metrics debate; lead with the user and you'll get a user debate.
cards.pmNote: 把「我們在做什麼」換成「我們解決什麼」，一句話就改變整場會議討論的軸線。
cards.episode: Lessons from a two-time unicorn builder, 50-time startup advisor, and 20-time company board member | Uri Levine (co-founder of Waze)

alts.quote: What is the unconstrained perfect solution to this burning problem?
alts.zh: 如果完全不設限，這個燒眉毛的問題最完美的解法長什麼樣？

alts.quote: Stop focusing as much on what you want to say and focus more on what you want your audience to remember.
alts.zh: 別再那麼在意「你想說什麼」，多想想「你想讓聽眾記住什麼」。

alts.quote: Past that point, I would argue: Just focus on the positional game.
alts.zh: 過了那個點之後，我會說：專心打位置戰就好。

cards.pattern: The way I think about it is [重新定義]—[常見信念] just controls [有限的部分].
cards.quote: The way I think about it is talent basically controls the slope of the curve, but most things are actually acquirable skills.
cards.zh: 我的想法是：天分只是決定那條曲線的斜率，但大多數東西其實都是可以習得的技能。
cards.why: The way I think about it is… 是英文裡最安全的「我要提出另一種看法了」開關——它把主張標成個人視角，對方不必先反駁你才能講話。後半把「天分」限縮成一個變數而不是門檻，等於偷偷改了整個題目。
swaps: The way I'd frame it is that budget sets the slope, not the ceiling.
I'd think of it less as a constraint and more as a coefficient.
cards.pmNote: 重新定義變數（門檻→斜率）是最省力的說服：不用推翻對方的事實，只要改變它在模型裡的位置。
cards.episode: Zigging vs. zagging: How HubSpot built a $30B company | Dharmesh Shah (co-founder/CTO)

alts.quote: Now, I'm biased when I'm going to say this, so take this with a pinch of salt, but I think the Accordion Method might be one of the things I'm the most proud of in my entire life.
alts.zh: 我要講的這件事我是有偏見的，所以你打個折聽——但我覺得手風琴法可能是我這輩子最引以為傲的東西之一。

alts.quote: I think a lot of people think about markets almost like these bodies of water. And it's like, "Oh, it's this big body of water that we're going after." And I actually think that the most interesting markets, you have to think of them like currents.
alts.zh: 很多人把市場想成一片水域，覺得「喔，我們要去攻的是這一大片水」。但我覺得最有意思的市場，你得把它想成水流。

alts.quote: You have to shift from doer to editor is the way I think about it.
alts.zh: 你必須從做事的人轉成當編輯——我是這樣看的。

cards.pattern: The best advice I've heard is [公認做法]. And one of our early zigs is we are going to do exactly the opposite of that.
cards.quote: Some of the best startup advice I've heard is startups should focus on one thing and be really, really exceptionally world-class at that one thing. And one of our early zigs is we are going to do exactly the opposite of that.
cards.zh: 我聽過最好的創業建議之一，就是新創應該專注在一件事，並且在那件事上做到世界級。而我們早期的其中一個「岔開」，就是完全反著做。
cards.why: 先真心誠意地把對手的論點講到最好（best advice I've heard），再宣布你要反著走。這種「先讚後反」讓你的反叛看起來是深思過的選擇，而不是沒讀過書。
swaps: Everything I believe about focus says don't do this. We did it anyway, and here's why.
The textbook answer is X. We're proposing not-X, deliberately.
cards.pmNote: 刻意違背通則之前，先證明你懂那條通則——否則團隊會把你的提案讀成無知而不是差異化。
cards.episode: Zigging vs. zagging: How HubSpot built a $30B company | Dharmesh Shah (co-founder/CTO)

alts.quote: None of this is going to blow anyone's minds, I think, because it's very best practices. But it's easy to overlook when you're so focused on so many different steps of a process.
alts.zh: 這些應該不會讓誰驚呆，因為都是很基本的最佳實務。但當你同時盯著流程裡一大堆步驟時，就是很容易漏掉。

alts.quote: I'm going to make a bold statement here. There is no such thing as a long feedback loop.
alts.zh: 我要講一句很大膽的話：世界上沒有「很長的回饋迴圈」這種東西。

alts.quote: How do you get the foot in the door?" And what I've found is you should make the smallest ask possible, which is the opposite of what 95% of people do.
alts.zh: 「你要怎麼把腳踏進門？」我發現的是：你的請求要越小越好，這跟 95% 的人做的正好相反。

cards.pattern: I'm not saying we should do it, but have we considered [另一條路]? You should at least know what [另一條路] would've been.
cards.quote: I'm not saying we should do it, but have we considered this alternate path? You should at least know what the zig would've been and have talked it through.
cards.zh: 我不是說我們該這麼做，但我們有認真考慮過另外那條路嗎？至少你應該知道「岔開」會長什麼樣子，而且真的討論過。
cards.why: I'm not saying we should do it, but… 是把新選項丟上桌卻不用背書的萬用開關——你只要求「討論過」，門檻低到沒人能拒絕，但選項已經進了會議紀錄。
swaps: I'm not advocating for it—I just want it on the table before we close.
Not a proposal, more of a stress test: what if we did the opposite?
cards.pmNote: 在收斂前強迫團隊列出「沒選的那條路」，是最便宜的 pre-mortem。
cards.episode: Zigging vs. zagging: How HubSpot built a $30B company | Dharmesh Shah (co-founder/CTO)

alts.quote: There's this thing in my head and I haven't fully validated it but I'm going to share it with you.
alts.zh: 我腦中有個想法，還沒完全驗證過，但我還是講給你聽。

alts.quote: So for positioning work, I'm going to say something that is contentious, but I don't think it is at all.
alts.zh: 講到定位這件事，我要說一句大家可能覺得很有爭議的話——但我完全不覺得有爭議。

alts.quote: I want you to pull the hiring manager aside and say, "Hey, Lenny, you're the hiring manager. I've thought about what the role is. I want to make sure I'm understanding it correctly.
alts.zh: 我要你把用人主管拉到一旁說：「我想過這個職位到底是什麼，我想確認我理解得對不對。我可以跟你分享一下嗎？」

cards.quote: You don't have to do the thing I'm asking, but it is something that I would do if I were you, or at least I would consider if I were you.
cards.zh: 你不一定要照我說的做，但如果我是你，我會做這件事——至少會認真考慮。
cards.why: 先解除壓力（you don't have to），再放進份量（I would do it if I were you）。這種「明講力度」的講法，讓資深者的隨口意見不會被當成聖旨——台灣人講「參考看看」常常反而更曖昧。
swaps: This is a suggestion, not a decision—no response needed.
Take it or leave it, but here's where I'd put my chips.
cards.pmNote: 資深者的一句隨口話，常被下游當成需求做三個月。明講「這只是建議」是省成本的溝通設計。
cards.episode: Zigging vs. zagging: How HubSpot built a $30B company | Dharmesh Shah (co-founder/CTO)

alts.quote: So for positioning work, I'm going to say something that is contentious, but I don't think it is at all.
alts.zh: 講到定位這件事，我要說一句大家可能覺得很有爭議的話——但我完全不覺得有爭議。

alts.quote: There's this thing in my head and I haven't fully validated it but I'm going to share it with you.
alts.zh: 我腦中有個想法，還沒完全驗證過，但我還是講給你聽。

alts.quote: the best way to get feedback from people is not by asking what they think, but to put something concrete in front of them and then have them react to it, right?
alts.zh: 要拿到回饋，最好的方式不是問人家怎麼想，而是先擺一個具體的東西在他面前，讓他反應，對吧？

cards.pattern: One of them is this thing that [X] is a [Y], period. Every [組織] builds two [Y]s.
cards.quote: One of them is this thing that culture is a product, period. Every company builds two products: one is the product they build for their customers, and the other is a product they build for their team.
cards.zh: 其中一個想法是：文化就是一個產品，就這樣。每家公司都在做兩個產品——一個給客戶，一個給團隊。
cards.why: period 放在句尾等於「不接受討價還價」，先把定義釘死，再用一個對稱結構（two products）把它變成可操作的東西。抽象名詞一旦被歸類成「產品」，所有產品方法論就直接可以套上去。
swaps: Onboarding is a product, full stop. It deserves a roadmap.
Internal tooling isn't overhead—it's a product with users.
cards.pmNote: 把非產品的東西宣告成產品（文化、內部工具、文件），就可以合法地要 NPS、要迭代、要排 roadmap。
cards.episode: Zigging vs. zagging: How HubSpot built a $30B company | Dharmesh Shah (co-founder/CTO)

alts.quote: The other exercise I used to take my students through was what I called value denial. Now, what is it that you should be able to buy but you can't?
alts.zh: 我以前會帶學生做另一個練習，我叫它「價值缺口」：有什麼是你照理該買得到、卻買不到的？

alts.quote: Here's the thing that I think is the easiest to change, is to realize the only thing that's ever supposed to happen in a meeting is the discussion part.
alts.zh: 我覺得最容易改的是這件事：認清一場會議裡唯一該發生的，只有「討論」。

alts.quote: There's this thing in my head and I haven't fully validated it but I'm going to share it with you.
alts.zh: 我腦中有個想法，還沒完全驗證過，但我還是講給你聽。

cards.pattern: Let's say we stipulate that's true. Just humor me for a minute. If you assume that's true, then a bunch of things follow.
cards.quote: Let's say we stipulate that that just happens to be true. Just humor me for a minute. If you assume that's true, then a bunch of things kind of follow from that postulate.
cards.zh: 我們先假設這是真的。先陪我一分鐘。如果你假設它是真的，那後面就會跟著推出一串結論。
cards.why: Just humor me for a minute 是英文會議裡的借時神器——你不要求對方同意前提，只借他一分鐘，推論跑完之後前提往往就自己站住了。台灣人多半會卡在「先說服前提」這一步。
swaps: Grant me the premise for two minutes and watch where it goes.
Suspend disbelief for a second—if this holds, here's what changes.
cards.pmNote: 策略提案常卡在前提爭論。先把推論跑完給大家看，前提的說服成本會大幅下降。
cards.episode: Zigging vs. zagging: How HubSpot built a $30B company | Dharmesh Shah (co-founder/CTO)

alts.quote: Now, I'm biased when I'm going to say this, so take this with a pinch of salt, but I think the Accordion Method might be one of the things I'm the most proud of in my entire life.
alts.zh: 我要講的這件事我是有偏見的，所以你打個折聽——但我覺得手風琴法可能是我這輩子最引以為傲的東西之一。

alts.quote: And as I saw the effectiveness of a post-mortem, that's what made me wonder, why do we need to wait until after things go wrong? Because why can't we extract some of these insights before they go wrong?
alts.zh: 看到事後檢討這麼有效之後，我就開始想：為什麼一定要等到事情出錯之後？為什麼不能在出錯之前就把這些洞見挖出來？

alts.quote: I'm going to tell my boss, on Monday, that I think we should do that. I'm going to use a little social capital and say we should do this.
alts.zh: 我禮拜一會跟我主管講，我覺得這個該做。我會動用一點我的政治額度，去替它說話。

cards.pattern: I'll put the most important point at the top, the TLDR, and then I'll say 'Context:' and put [脈絡] below.
cards.quote: So I'll usually put the most important point at the top, the TLDR, if you will, the gist and then I'll say context, colon, and then there might be multiple paragraphs of context below.
cards.zh: 我通常會把最重要的那點放最上面，也就是 TLDR、重點，然後寫「Context：」，下面可能會有好幾段脈絡。
cards.why: the TLDR, if you will 這個 if you will 是母語者用來替口語詞借正式場合的通行證。整句還順便交出了一個可以直接照抄的格式：結論在上、Context 在下、同意的人不必往下讀。
swaps: Bottom line up front, then context below for anyone who wants the reasoning.
Recommendation first. Everything under 'Background' is optional reading.
cards.pmNote: 分層寫作讓不同角色各取所需：同意的人看第一行就簽，想挑戰的人往下讀——兩邊都不浪費時間。
cards.episode: Become a better communicator: Specific frameworks to improve your clarity, influence, and impact | Wes Kao (coach, entrepreneur, advisor)

alts.quote: And the third thing is that I really believe that... I don't believe. I think we all know at this point that the most important thing for the growth of anything tech is retention.
alts.zh: 第三件事是我真的相信——不，不是相信。我覺得到這個時間點大家都已經知道了：科技產品成長最重要的就是留存。

alts.quote: I would argue the most important thing is to have a single name on that decision line, because that usually makes sure that you can get a decision very quickly.
alts.zh: 我會說最重要的一件事，是那條決策線上只放一個名字，因為那通常能確保你很快就拿到決定。

alts.quote: So you'll say, 'So to wrap up...' And your brain's going to fill in the gap. Or, 'In summary, so my point here is, so what I want you to remember.'
alts.zh: 你就說「所以總結一下…」，然後你的腦袋會自己把空格填完。或是「總之，我的重點是…」「我希望你記住的是…」。

cards.quote: Here's my recommendation, here's what I'm advocating for. And also, here are some downsides to that.
cards.zh: 這是我的建議，這是我在主張的東西。另外，這是它的一些缺點。
cards.why: 先亮立場再自曝缺點，順序不能反。先講缺點會讓人以為你沒把握；先講立場再補缺點，缺點反而變成「這人夠誠實」的證據。And also 的輕語氣也讓自曝不像認錯。
swaps: I'm recommending A. The honest cost of A is B.
Here's where I've landed—and here's what I'd be worried about if I were you.
cards.pmNote: 自己先講出 trade-off，會議上就沒人能靠「你沒想到 X」把你的提案打掉。
cards.episode: Become a better communicator: Specific frameworks to improve your clarity, influence, and impact | Wes Kao (coach, entrepreneur, advisor)

alts.quote: So having a shit draft is a million times more valuable than having all these great ideas. But it's also really painful.
alts.zh: 有一份爛草稿，比手上一堆很棒的點子有價值一百萬倍。但那個過程真的很痛。

alts.quote: I've learned that some of the companies we admire are not working the way we are, and maybe we should try this.
alts.zh: 我發現我們很欣賞的那幾家公司，做事方式跟我們並不一樣，也許我們可以試試看他們的做法。

alts.quote: So that's why I'm a huge fan of pre-mortems is, it's one of those very low downside, but very high upside things that I've experienced.
alts.zh: 所以我超推事前檢討：它就是那種下檔風險很低、上檔空間很大的做法。

cards.pattern: Is this a reversible decision, or is it one that's irreversible or expensive to reverse?
cards.quote: Is this a reversible decision or is this one that is irreversible or difficult to reverse or expensive to reverse?
cards.zh: 這是一個可以反悔的決定，還是一個不可逆、很難反悔、或反悔代價很高的決定？
cards.why: 把「要不要往上報」這種很政治的問題，換成一個中性的技術判準。三個並列（irreversible / difficult / expensive to reverse）也示範了英文如何用同義遞進撐住一個概念。
swaps: Is this a one-way door or a two-way door?
How expensive is it to undo this if we're wrong?
cards.pmNote: 可逆決策快做別開會，不可逆決策慢做多花力氣——這條分界線決定你該花多少政治資本。
cards.episode: Become a better communicator: Specific frameworks to improve your clarity, influence, and impact | Wes Kao (coach, entrepreneur, advisor)

alts.quote: I've never seen a product plan get to the truth of what it could do, but it will help you make a better decision than if you just guess.
alts.zh: 我沒看過哪份產品計畫真的算準過它能做到什麼，但它還是會讓你的決定比純用猜的好。

alts.quote: The calories you spend on a decision should be proportional to the consequences of that decision, pure and simple.
alts.zh: 你花在一個決定上的力氣，應該跟那個決定的後果成正比，就這麼簡單。

alts.quote: I would argue the most important thing is to have a single name on that decision line, because that usually makes sure that you can get a decision very quickly.
alts.zh: 我會說最重要的一件事，是那條決策線上只放一個名字，因為那通常能確保你很快就拿到決定。

cards.pattern: Your reader doesn't know which parts are FYIs, which parts are background, and what you actually want a response on.
cards.quote: Your reader doesn't know which parts are FYIs or which parts are background versus what is the thing that you want their response on.
cards.zh: 你的讀者根本分不出哪些是「知會一下」、哪些是背景，哪一段才是你要他回覆的。
cards.why: 用「對方的困惑」來當論點，比說「你寫得不清楚」有效十倍——因為它把責任放在結構上而不是人身上。三段並列（FYIs / background / response）也直接示範了該怎麼修。
swaps: Nobody can tell what's context and what's an ask.
Split it: FYI, background, and the one decision I need from you.
cards.pmNote: 把 FYI／背景／待決事項分開標示，收件人的回覆率會直接上升。
cards.episode: Become a better communicator: Specific frameworks to improve your clarity, influence, and impact | Wes Kao (coach, entrepreneur, advisor)

alts.quote: And so ever since then, we've been automating jobs and creating new jobs, and you can always see the job that's going to go away, and you don't know the new job because it doesn't exist yet.
alts.zh: 從那時候到現在，我們一直在自動化舊工作、也一直在長出新工作；而你永遠看得到那個要消失的工作，看不到新的，因為它還不存在。

alts.quote: And the third thing is that I really believe that... I don't believe. I think we all know at this point that the most important thing for the growth of anything tech is retention.
alts.zh: 第三件事是我真的相信——不，不是相信。我覺得到這個時間點大家都已經知道了：科技產品成長最重要的就是留存。

alts.quote: I would argue that the one thing AI can never have is agency because it doesn't have human motivations.
alts.zh: 我會說 AI 唯一永遠不會有的東西是能動性，因為它沒有人的動機。

cards.quote: Know that it's coming and make sure you land the plane.
cards.zh: 先知道它一定會來，然後確保你把飛機落好。
cards.why: land the plane 是英文會議裡最常聽到的收尾動詞（也常被主持人拿來催人收尾）。前半 Know that it's coming 把「結尾會失控」講成可預期的物理現象，於是解法變成準備而不是天分。
swaps: Let's land this before we run out of time.
Whatever happens in the middle, stick the ending.
cards.pmNote: 聽眾的印象由結尾決定（peak-end rule），所以簡報最該排練的是最後三十秒。
cards.episode: Why most public speaking advice is wrong—and how to finally overcome your speaking anxiety | Tristan de Montebello (CEO & co-founder of Ultraspeaking)

alts.quote: In a world where it's easier to build things, it's more important to make sure that your time is spent figuring out what you should be building in the first place.
alts.zh: 在一個「東西越來越好做」的世界裡，更重要的是先確保你把時間花在想清楚「到底該做什麼」。

alts.quote: By the way, the infrastructure piece, I know it's a nugget on the side but infrastructure is the product. Period.
alts.zh: 順帶一提，基礎建設這塊——我知道這是題外話——但基礎建設就是產品。就這樣。

alts.quote: So we can think there's people who don't know about it, there's people who do know about it but don't do it, and then there's people who do know about it, but do do it. And it's that last group that's so tiny.
alts.zh: 可以分成三種人：不知道這件事的、知道但不做的、知道又真的去做的。而最後那一群小得可憐。

cards.pattern: So to wrap up… / In summary, my point here is… / What I want you to remember is…
cards.quote: So you'll say, 'So to wrap up...' And your brain's going to fill in the gap. Or, 'In summary, so my point here is, so what I want you to remember.'
cards.zh: 你就說「所以總結一下…」，然後你的腦袋會自己把空格填完。或是「總之，我的重點是…」「我希望你記住的是…」。
cards.why: 這幾個 summary prompt 的價值在於：你先把句子的前半丟出去，腦袋被逼著補完後半。對英文非母語者尤其有用——不必先想好整句，開口就有結構。
swaps: Net-net, here's where I land.
If you take one thing from this, take this.
cards.pmNote: 英文會議插不上話、收不了尾，多半不是詞彙問題，是缺少現成的開頭骨架。
cards.episode: Why most public speaking advice is wrong—and how to finally overcome your speaking anxiety | Tristan de Montebello (CEO & co-founder of Ultraspeaking)

alts.quote: If I told you, I'm going to build an autonomous vehicle, and I said our team is 10 people, you should rightfully say, Varun, you're not serious. And you'd be right.
alts.zh: 如果我跟你說我要做自駕車，然後說團隊只有 10 個人，你完全應該回我：Varun，你不是認真的吧。而且你會是對的。

alts.quote: So I'll usually put the most important point at the top, the TLDR, if you will, the gist and then I'll say context, colon, and then there might be multiple paragraphs of context below.
alts.zh: 我通常會把最重要的那點放最上面，也就是 TLDR、重點，然後寫「Context：」，下面可能會有好幾段脈絡。

alts.quote: That's solving a problem for the company. That's not solving a career growth issue for an individual. And I think people who want to be promoted need to think in that orientation versus the other.
alts.zh: 那是在解決公司的問題，不是在解決個人的職涯成長問題。想升遷的人要用前面那種角度思考，不是後面那種。

cards.pattern: I genuinely believe that [大主張], but that doesn't mean [收回過度的部分].
cards.quote: I genuinely believe that every idea is awesome, but that doesn't mean I can do every idea.
cards.zh: 我真心覺得每個點子都很棒——但那不代表我每個都能做。
cards.why: I genuinely believe that… 是拉高信念強度的開關（比 I think 重很多），後面立刻用 but that doesn't mean 把範圍收回來。先給熱情再給紀律，講「取捨」時不會顯得冷血。
swaps: I genuinely think this is a great request, and I still can't take it this quarter.
I'm not disputing the value—I'm disputing the timing.
cards.pmNote: 擋需求時先真心肯定價值再談排序，對方才聽得進去「不是不做，是不是現在」。
cards.episode: Why most public speaking advice is wrong—and how to finally overcome your speaking anxiety | Tristan de Montebello (CEO & co-founder of Ultraspeaking)

alts.quote: So you don't have to believe in any of that stuff to believe that this is a giant deal.
alts.zh: 你完全不用相信那一整套說法，也可以相信這件事非常重大。

alts.quote: That sounds cliche. I think a lot of founders and startup people like to talk about the mission, and I get it, and I think it's real. But I really mean it.
alts.zh: 我知道這聽起來很老套。很多創辦人都愛談使命，我懂，我也覺得那是真的。但我是真心這樣講。

alts.quote: It doesn't make any sense to do things that are self-contradictory. And yet, people do it.
alts.zh: 做互相打架的事情根本說不通。但大家還是照做。

cards.quote: Focus is not about what we are doing, it's about what we are not doing. These are the hard decisions.
cards.zh: 專注不是關於我們在做什麼，是關於我們不做什麼。那才是難的決定。
cards.why: not about A, it's about B 是英文最短的重新定義句型，兩句話就把一個被用爛的詞（focus）換了內容。第二句補一刀，讓它從概念變成一個需要勇氣的行為。
swaps: Strategy is the list of things we're saying no to.
This roadmap is only real if something falls off it.
cards.pmNote: 策略即取捨。沒有砍掉東西的 roadmap，只是願望清單。
cards.episode: Lessons from a two-time unicorn builder, 50-time startup advisor, and 20-time company board member | Uri Levine (co-founder of Waze)

alts.quote: So having a shit draft is a million times more valuable than having all these great ideas. But it's also really painful.
alts.zh: 有一份爛草稿，比手上一堆很棒的點子有價值一百萬倍。但那個過程真的很痛。

alts.quote: This sounds, again, very simple but just like how you wouldn't fly a plane without instruments, why would you run your products without understanding the instrumentation and how it's doing.
alts.zh: 這聽起來很簡單，但就像你不會沒有儀表就開飛機一樣，為什麼你會在完全不看數據的情況下經營產品？

alts.quote: That sounds cliche. I think a lot of founders and startup people like to talk about the mission, and I get it, and I think it's real. But I really mean it.
alts.zh: 我知道這聽起來很老套。很多創辦人都愛談使命，我懂，我也覺得那是真的。但我是真心這樣講。

cards.quote: Start with the strongest point at the beginning. And by the way, finish with that as well.
cards.zh: 一開場就丟出你最強的那一點。順帶一提，結尾也用同一點。
cards.why: And by the way 在英文裡常是「我要補一個其實很重要的東西」的偽裝——語氣輕，份量重。整句是一條可以立刻照做的規則，不需要解釋就能用。
swaps: Lead with your best argument and close on it too.
Open strong, close on the same note—don't save it for the middle.
cards.pmNote: 投資人與主管在前幾秒就形成印象。把最強的證據藏在第八頁等於沒有。
cards.episode: Lessons from a two-time unicorn builder, 50-time startup advisor, and 20-time company board member | Uri Levine (co-founder of Waze)

alts.quote: The way I think about this that I've heard well described is just there's no silver bullets, just many lead bullets.
alts.zh: 我對這件事的想法——我聽過一個說得很好的講法——就是沒有銀色子彈，只有很多顆鉛彈。

alts.quote: I've learned that some of the companies we admire are not working the way we are, and maybe we should try this.
alts.zh: 我發現我們很欣賞的那幾家公司，做事方式跟我們並不一樣，也許我們可以試試看他們的做法。

alts.quote: By the way, the infrastructure piece, I know it's a nugget on the side but infrastructure is the product. Period.
alts.zh: 順帶一提，基礎建設這塊——我知道這是題外話——但基礎建設就是產品。就這樣。

cards.pattern: Most people are missing the most important [X]. It is [出乎意料的那個]. It's going to be [presented] for the longest period of time.
cards.quote: Most people are missing the most important slide of their presentation. The most important slide of your presentation is the first slide. This slide is going to be presented for the longest period of time.
cards.zh: 大部分人都漏掉了簡報裡最重要的那一頁。你簡報最重要的一頁，是第一頁。因為那一頁會在螢幕上停留最久。
cards.why: 三句遞進：先說「大家都漏了」製造懸念，再揭曉答案，最後給一個沒人能反駁的物理理由。理由是機制性的（停留時間最長），不是意見，所以你不需要辯論就贏了。
swaps: Everyone optimizes the demo and ignores the title slide people stare at for ten minutes.
The most-read line in your doc is the subject line.
cards.pmNote: 曝光時間最長的介面元素，往往是最少人優化的那個——簡報封面、email 標題、空狀態頁。
cards.episode: Lessons from a two-time unicorn builder, 50-time startup advisor, and 20-time company board member | Uri Levine (co-founder of Waze)

alts.quote: In a world where it's easier to build things, it's more important to make sure that your time is spent figuring out what you should be building in the first place.
alts.zh: 在一個「東西越來越好做」的世界裡，更重要的是先確保你把時間花在想清楚「到底該做什麼」。

alts.quote: If I told you, I'm going to build an autonomous vehicle, and I said our team is 10 people, you should rightfully say, Varun, you're not serious. And you'd be right.
alts.zh: 如果我跟你說我要做自駕車，然後說團隊只有 10 個人，你完全應該回我：Varun，你不是認真的吧。而且你會是對的。

alts.quote: That's the first-order thinking. Second-order thinking is thinking through the maintenance of that feature. The third-order thinking, which turns out to be the most important, is the other costs that complexity adds.
alts.zh: 那是第一層思考。第二層是去想這個功能的維護成本。第三層——結果證明是最重要的一層——是複雜度帶來的其他成本。

cards.pattern: Every time you [做X], mark your calendar for [期限] and ask yourself one question: knowing what I know today, would I [做同樣的決定]?
cards.quote: Every time that you hire someone new, mark your calendars for 30 days down the road and ask yourself one question: knowing what I know today, would I hire this person?
cards.zh: 每次你雇了新人，就在行事曆上標記三十天後，然後問自己一個問題：以我今天知道的事情，我還會雇這個人嗎？
cards.why: ask yourself one question 先把難題壓縮成單一問句，再用 knowing what I know today 把它變成一個沒有藉口的判斷。整句是「機制」而不是「建議」——他給的是一個會自動觸發的行事曆事件。
swaps: Knowing what we know now, would we still greenlight this?
Put a 30-day check-in on the calendar and answer one yes/no question.
cards.pmNote: 把難決策綁到固定時間點，可以避開「一直拖」這個預設值。沒有期限的檢討永遠不會發生。
cards.episode: Lessons from a two-time unicorn builder, 50-time startup advisor, and 20-time company board member | Uri Levine (co-founder of Waze)

alts.quote: And so ever since then, we've been automating jobs and creating new jobs, and you can always see the job that's going to go away, and you don't know the new job because it doesn't exist yet.
alts.zh: 從那時候到現在，我們一直在自動化舊工作、也一直在長出新工作；而你永遠看得到那個要消失的工作，看不到新的，因為它還不存在。

alts.quote: And just saying because dramatically boosted the percentage of the time that a person would let them cut the line. We're suckers for explanations, all of us.
alts.zh: 光是講出「因為」，別人讓他插隊的比例就大幅上升。我們每個人都吃「解釋」這一套。

alts.quote: In a world where it's easier to build things, it's more important to make sure that your time is spent figuring out what you should be building in the first place.
alts.zh: 在一個「東西越來越好做」的世界裡，更重要的是先確保你把時間花在想清楚「到底該做什麼」。

cards.pattern: I could become passively okay at [X]. I don't want to spend any years of my life becoming passively okay at something.
cards.quote: I don't want to spend any years of my life becoming passively okay at something.
cards.zh: 我不想花人生的任何幾年，只為了在某件事上變得「勉強還行」。
cards.why: passively okay（勉強還行）是一個自造但一聽就懂的貶義程度詞，比 mediocre 更精準也更不刺耳。整句用「時間成本」而不是「我不擅長」來拒絕，語氣是選擇不是逃避。
swaps: I'd rather be excellent at three things than passable at ten.
Those calories buy more somewhere else.
cards.pmNote: 機會成本的語言比能力的語言好用：「我把時間放在哪裡更有價值」永遠比「我不行」更有說服力。
cards.episode: Zigging vs. zagging: How HubSpot built a $30B company | Dharmesh Shah (co-founder/CTO)

alts.quote: My sense is if you want work-life balance, don't join one of these companies, because that's just not the way they work.
alts.zh: 我的感覺是，如果你想要工作生活平衡，就別加入這種公司，因為它們就不是那樣運作的。

alts.quote: And if you don't have them on your growth roadmap, you are going to be in some really big trouble over the next year to two years because your cost of acquisition is only going to go up.
alts.zh: 如果你的成長路線圖上沒有這些東西，未來一到兩年你會陷入大麻煩，因為你的獲客成本只會一路往上。

alts.quote: So you don't have to believe in any of that stuff to believe that this is a giant deal.
alts.zh: 你完全不用相信那一整套說法，也可以相信這件事非常重大。

cards.pattern: [X] does kill [Y]. Maybe not as quickly as other things, but much more reliably.
cards.quote: Complexity does kill companies. Maybe not as quickly as other things, but much more reliably than other things.
cards.zh: 複雜度真的會殺死公司。也許沒有其他東西那麼快，但可靠得多。
cards.why: 先讓一步（maybe not as quickly），再用一個更狠的維度贏回來（much more reliably）。這種「讓速度、要機率」的換維度反擊，是英文論證裡很高階的一招。does 的強調用法也值得學。
swaps: Tech debt won't kill us this quarter. It will kill us eventually, and on schedule.
Slower than a bad launch, but far more certain.
cards.pmNote: 慢性風險（複雜度、技術債）之所以難爭取資源，正是因為它不急。要贏就換維度講「必然性」。
cards.episode: Zigging vs. zagging: How HubSpot built a $30B company | Dharmesh Shah (co-founder/CTO)

alts.quote: I would argue in retrospect, absolutely, yes, there were opportunities that were left on the table, but in early days you leave good opportunities because you have to focus on other things.
alts.zh: 回頭看我會說，沒錯，確實有些機會被放掉了，但早期你就是會放掉好機會，因為你必須專注在別的事情上。

alts.quote: I've learned that some of the companies we admire are not working the way we are, and maybe we should try this.
alts.zh: 我發現我們很欣賞的那幾家公司，做事方式跟我們並不一樣，也許我們可以試試看他們的做法。

alts.quote: He thinks that a lot of the best recruiters in the world or the companies that attract talent, they put out this distinctive bad signal and it has to turn some people off. That's the key of a good, bad signal.
alts.zh: 他認為最會吸引人才的公司，都會刻意放出一個「不討喜的訊號」，而且一定要有人被勸退。這才是好的壞訊號的重點。

cards.pattern: That's the first-order thinking. Second-order is [X]. The third-order, which turns out to be the most important, is [Y].
cards.quote: That's the first-order thinking. Second-order thinking is thinking through the maintenance of that feature. The third-order thinking, which turns out to be the most important, is the other costs that complexity adds.
cards.zh: 那是第一層思考。第二層是去想這個功能的維護成本。第三層——結果證明是最重要的一層——是複雜度帶來的其他成本。
cards.why: first / second / third-order 是英文商業討論裡的階梯詞，一講出來就宣告「我比你多想了兩層」，而且不用貶低任何人。which turns out to be the most important 的插入語又替最後一層加了重量。
swaps: First-order: build cost. Second-order: upkeep. Third-order: every future decision gets harder.
The obvious cost is the dev time. The real cost is what it does to every roadmap after this.
cards.pmNote: 評估功能成本時要算到第三層：多一個產品，之後每一張圖表、每一次招聘、每一場行銷都要被切成兩份。
cards.episode: Zigging vs. zagging: How HubSpot built a $30B company | Dharmesh Shah (co-founder/CTO)

alts.quote: In a world where it's easier to build things, it's more important to make sure that your time is spent figuring out what you should be building in the first place.
alts.zh: 在一個「東西越來越好做」的世界裡，更重要的是先確保你把時間花在想清楚「到底該做什麼」。

alts.quote: And the third thing is that I really believe that... I don't believe. I think we all know at this point that the most important thing for the growth of anything tech is retention.
alts.zh: 第三件事是我真的相信——不，不是相信。我覺得到這個時間點大家都已經知道了：科技產品成長最重要的就是留存。

alts.quote: Most people are missing the most important slide of their presentation. The most important slide of your presentation is the first slide. This slide is going to be presented for the longest period of time.
alts.zh: 大部分人都漏掉了簡報裡最重要的那一頁。你簡報最重要的一頁，是第一頁。因為那一頁會在螢幕上停留最久。

cards.pattern: The calories you spend on [X] should be proportional to the consequences of [X], pure and simple.
cards.quote: The calories you spend on a decision should be proportional to the consequences of that decision, pure and simple.
cards.zh: 你花在一個決定上的力氣，應該跟那個決定的後果成正比，就這麼簡單。
cards.why: calories 當作「認知力氣」的計價單位是矽谷常見用法，比 effort 更具體。pure and simple 收尾等於「這條不用討論」，把一個可能很長的爭論直接封起來。
swaps: Let's not spend a week's worth of thinking on a decision we can reverse in an hour.
Match the process to the stakes.
cards.pmNote: 小決定開大會、大決定用直覺，是團隊效率最常見的錯配。
cards.episode: Zigging vs. zagging: How HubSpot built a $30B company | Dharmesh Shah (co-founder/CTO)

alts.quote: I've never seen a product plan get to the truth of what it could do, but it will help you make a better decision than if you just guess.
alts.zh: 我沒看過哪份產品計畫真的算準過它能做到什麼，但它還是會讓你的決定比純用猜的好。

alts.quote: I would argue the most important thing is to have a single name on that decision line, because that usually makes sure that you can get a decision very quickly.
alts.zh: 我會說最重要的一件事，是那條決策線上只放一個名字，因為那通常能確保你很快就拿到決定。

alts.quote: What I've found is that once you commit to a decision, you actually learn more post committing to that decision about what's going to work and not going to work, and you move out of the hypothetical.
alts.zh: 我發現的是，一旦你對一個決定拍板，你在拍板之後反而會學到更多——什麼會成、什麼不會成——而且你會離開純假設的狀態。

cards.pattern: The most common mistake people make is they think through [B] first without forcing themselves to think through [A].
cards.quote: The most common mistake people make is they think through the probability first without actually forcing themselves to think through the potential.
cards.zh: 大家最常犯的錯，是先想「成功機率」，卻沒有逼自己先想「這件事最大能長成什麼樣」。
cards.why: The most common mistake people make is… 是把個人主張升級成通則的萬用開場——你不是在說對方錯，是在說「這是普遍現象」。後半用順序（first / without）點出錯在哪，而不是錯什麼。
swaps: We're filtering on feasibility before we've sized the upside.
The usual failure mode is judging the odds before naming the prize.
cards.pmNote: 機會評估要先算 potential 再算 probability，否則高風險高報酬的選項會在還沒被看見前就被濾掉。
cards.episode: Zigging vs. zagging: How HubSpot built a $30B company | Dharmesh Shah (co-founder/CTO)

alts.quote: But the thing that I would argue folks that build really big companies have in common is they just really want it and they really believe in themselves and they really believe they can make it work.
alts.zh: 但我會說，那些做出真正大公司的人共通點是：他們就是非常想要，他們真的相信自己，也真的相信自己能做成。

alts.quote: In a world where it's easier to build things, it's more important to make sure that your time is spent figuring out what you should be building in the first place.
alts.zh: 在一個「東西越來越好做」的世界裡，更重要的是先確保你把時間花在想清楚「到底該做什麼」。

alts.quote: I think with hiring, it's funny, man, there's so much hiring advice online and you read it and you're like, "Yeah, this is super obvious." And then when you live it, you're suddenly like, "Aah, this is why people say this."
alts.zh: 招人這件事很好笑，網路上一堆建議，你看的時候都覺得「這不是廢話嗎」。等你真的經歷過，才會突然懂「喔，原來大家是這個意思」。

cards.pattern: If we just acknowledge reality and this person looks [X], they look [X]. That is data. Don't ignore that data.
cards.quote: If we just acknowledge reality and this person looks bored, they look bored, that is data. Don't ignore that data.
cards.zh: 如果我們願意面對現實——這個人看起來很無聊，那他就是很無聊。那是資料。別忽略那筆資料。
cards.why: 把「表情」正式升格成 data，等於偷偷擴大了證據的定義：定性訊號也算數。重複 they look bored 那一下是英文口語裡的「我不打算幫你留台階」節奏。
swaps: Their face is a data point. Log it.
Nobody asked a follow-up question. That's a signal, not noise.
cards.pmNote: 使用者研究裡的定性訊號跟數字一樣是資料。只承認可量化的東西，會系統性漏掉早期訊號。
cards.episode: Become a better communicator: Specific frameworks to improve your clarity, influence, and impact | Wes Kao (coach, entrepreneur, advisor)

alts.quote: Data is more like a compass than a GPS. If you look at data as a way of giving you the answer, you're always wrong. Wrong or slow, or sometimes both.
alts.zh: 數據比較像指南針，不是導航。如果你把數據當成會給你答案的東西，你不是錯就是慢，有時候兩者都有。

alts.quote: It's about saying, okay, if we have these themes of stuff that we want to work on, what do we know with confidence because the data tells us and what do we need to understand because we don't have the data?
alts.zh: 重點是要問：在我們想做的這些主題裡，哪些是數據講得夠清楚、我們有把握的？哪些是因為沒數據，所以還得先搞懂的？

alts.quote: It's not because my life is more interesting. It's because I have a better lens and I understand what to look for.
alts.zh: 不是因為我的生活變得比較精彩，是因為我的鏡頭變好了，我知道該找什麼。

cards.pattern: When you do a [平衡的呈現] but they're skewed and you leave things out, it makes the reader suspicious and they can't trust you anymore.
cards.quote: So when you do a pros and cons list, but they're skewed and you are leaving some things out of the cons list, it makes the reader suspicious and they can't trust you anymore.
cards.zh: 當你列出優缺點，但列得偏頗、缺點那欄漏了東西，讀者就會起疑，然後就再也不信你了。
cards.why: 它指出的是一個「假裝客觀反而更傷」的陷阱：偽裝的平衡比明講的立場更容易失去信任。suspicious → can't trust you anymore 的遞進，也把後果講到底。
swaps: A one-sided risk section reads worse than no risk section.
If the cons list is obviously curated, the pros stop counting.
cards.pmNote: 資料呈現的可信度是一次性的資產。被抓到選擇性呈現一次，之後你所有的數字都要重新被審一遍。
cards.episode: Become a better communicator: Specific frameworks to improve your clarity, influence, and impact | Wes Kao (coach, entrepreneur, advisor)

alts.quote: People aren't even getting to the third screen. They're stuck on the first screen because they can't even find the button that we think is so dead obvious.
alts.zh: 使用者根本走不到第三個畫面。他們卡在第一個畫面，因為連我們自認為超級明顯的那顆按鈕都找不到。

alts.quote: I'll caveat this by saying everyone's just figuring it out and it's a lot harder to figure it out when you're a larger organization than when you're much smaller and you get to run something yourself and there's pros and cons to both.
alts.zh: 我先加個但書：大家都還在摸索，而且組織越大越難摸索，比不上小團隊自己說了算——兩邊各有優缺點。

alts.quote: Companies I've invested in is a long list, and I love to give you names of companies that don't exist anymore because it's self-serving and a horrible survivorship bias to just list the good ones.
alts.zh: 我投資過的公司名單很長，我很願意告訴你那些已經倒掉的公司名字——因為只列出成功的那些，是自利、也是很糟的倖存者偏誤。

cards.pattern: It comes down to this metric that [某個專業社群] use called [X].
cards.quote: And it comes down to this metric that standup comedians use called LPM, laughs per minute. And there's actually a benchmark that you can say.
cards.zh: 最後歸結到一個站立喜劇演員在用的指標，叫 LPM——每分鐘笑聲數。而且真的有一個基準線可以對照。
cards.why: 從別的專業借一個指標過來，是把主觀領域變成可量測領域的標準招式。that [某群人] use called X 這個結構自帶權威，聽眾還沒判斷就先接受了它是真的指標。
swaps: There's a metric restaurants use for this called covers per hour.
Borrowing a term from logistics: what's our takt time here?
cards.pmNote: 把一個沒人量的東西定義成可量的指標，你就同時取得了討論它的主導權。
cards.episode: Zigging vs. zagging: How HubSpot built a $30B company | Dharmesh Shah (co-founder/CTO)

alts.quote: So there's a different metric that I like to use, which keys off of this idea that I think, again, people don't appreciate, which is cancellations grow faster than marketing.
alts.zh: 我比較喜歡用另一個指標，它是從一個大家常常沒放在心上的觀念推出來的：取消的成長速度比行銷快。

alts.quote: In fact, there's some early work on eBay that showed that if your first rating's negative, that could actually immediately cause an 8% hit on your immediate expected revenue, say nothing of long-term consequences.
alts.zh: 其實有一些早期針對 eBay 的研究顯示，如果你的第一則評價是負評，光是當下的預期營收就可能少 8%，長期的影響還沒算進去。

alts.quote: The basic principle with laser is that willpower is never going to win, and there's great research on this, but for now just trust me, you're not going to white-knuckle your way through not looking at Twitter when you're trying to work.
alts.zh: laser 的基本原理是：意志力永遠贏不了。這方面有很多很好的研究，但現在你先信我——你不可能靠硬撐來讓自己工作時不看 Twitter。

cards.quote: I have custom software that I've written that will say, 'Okay, here are the points at which the audience laughed.' Actually audibly laughed. That's the only way it counts.
cards.zh: 我自己寫了一套軟體，會告訴我「聽眾在哪些點笑了」。是真的出聲笑。只有出聲才算。
cards.why: Actually audibly laughed. That's the only way it counts. 兩個短句把量測標準收得死緊——這種「先給定義、再封住模糊地帶」的動作，是把數字變成證據的關鍵一步。
swaps: Only completed checkouts count. Adds-to-cart don't.
We count it when they come back on day seven. Nothing before that counts.
cards.pmNote: 指標的定義比指標本身重要。沒有把「什麼才算數」封死的數字，一定會被各方各自解讀。
cards.episode: Zigging vs. zagging: How HubSpot built a $30B company | Dharmesh Shah (co-founder/CTO)

alts.quote: They tend to have accomplished very difficult goals in very hostile environments. And it turns out that when you're starting a somewhat chaotic tech company, that's actually a very useful skill to have.
alts.zh: 這些人習慣在極度不友善的環境裡把很難的目標做出來。結果發現，開一家有點混亂的科技公司，這剛好是非常有用的能力。

alts.quote: It's not a statistically significant survey in general, but it will never go to 99% and one. That's fairly indicative that people are clicking the links, which surprises me.
alts.zh: 這份調查在統計上不算顯著，但它也不可能是 99 比 1。這蠻能說明大家真的有在點那些連結——這讓我有點意外。

alts.quote: You could have all the usage data in the world, that's going to tell you what's actually happening in your product, but it doesn't tell you why.
alts.zh: 就算你握有全世界的使用數據，它只會告訴你產品裡實際發生了什麼，不會告訴你為什麼。

cards.pattern: If you're solving for that ratio, there are two ways to improve it. One is [加分子]. Two is [減分母].
cards.quote: If you're solving literally for that ratio of laughs per minute, there are two ways to improve it. One is to add more laughs. Two is to decrease the number of words between laughs.
cards.zh: 如果你真的在解「每分鐘笑聲數」這個比值，只有兩種改法。一是增加笑點，二是減少笑點之間的字數。
cards.why: 把一個指標拆成分子分母，然後宣布「只有兩條路」——窮舉法讓討論從發散變收斂，而且暗示你已經想到底了。there are two ways to… 是很好用的收斂開關。
swaps: Conversion is a ratio: either more signups or fewer visitors we can't serve.
Two levers only—raise the numerator or shrink the denominator.
cards.pmNote: 北極星指標若是比值，行動就分兩類。講清楚你在動哪一邊，可以避開一整輪無效爭論。
cards.episode: Zigging vs. zagging: How HubSpot built a $30B company | Dharmesh Shah (co-founder/CTO)

alts.quote: So when it's a ratio and you decrease the denominator, the value of the ratio grows. And so, how do you decrease the denominator in this case where time is the denominator is you start working on things that take less time.
alts.zh: 這是一個比值，分母變小，比值就變大。那在這裡分母是時間，你要怎麼讓分母變小？你就開始挑那些花比較少時間的事情做。

alts.quote: Data is more like a compass than a GPS. If you look at data as a way of giving you the answer, you're always wrong. Wrong or slow, or sometimes both.
alts.zh: 數據比較像指南針，不是導航。如果你把數據當成會給你答案的東西，你不是錯就是慢，有時候兩者都有。

alts.quote: The basic principle with laser is that willpower is never going to win, and there's great research on this, but for now just trust me, you're not going to white-knuckle your way through not looking at Twitter when you're trying to work.
alts.zh: laser 的基本原理是：意志力永遠贏不了。這方面有很多很好的研究，但現在你先信我——你不可能靠硬撐來讓自己工作時不看 Twitter。

cards.pattern: I think [權威] says it more simply and elegantly, which is [引語].
cards.quote: I think Peter Thiel actually says it more simply and elegantly, which is, 'You need to be right about something that other people think you're wrong about for a very long time.'
cards.zh: 我覺得 Peter Thiel 講得更簡潔漂亮：「你得在一件別人認為你錯的事情上，長時間地正確。」
cards.why: says it more simply and elegantly 是引用權威時最漂亮的謙讓——你不是靠他的名氣，是說他表達得比你好。這樣借力不會顯得沒主見。
swaps: Bezos puts it better than I can: disagree and commit.
There's a cleaner version of this from Christensen—
cards.pmNote: 引用權威要引「說法」不要引「身分」。引身分是求庇護，引說法是加精度。
cards.episode: Zigging vs. zagging: How HubSpot built a $30B company | Dharmesh Shah (co-founder/CTO)

alts.quote: I like Sean Ellis's question of how disappointed would you be if this product disappeared? And I think it's if you have at least 40% of people respond that they'd be very disappointed, then you're on the right track.
alts.zh: 我喜歡 Sean Ellis 那一題：如果這個產品消失了，你會有多失望？如果至少 40% 的人回答「非常失望」，那你方向就是對的。

alts.quote: So there's a different metric that I like to use, which keys off of this idea that I think, again, people don't appreciate, which is cancellations grow faster than marketing.
alts.zh: 我比較喜歡用另一個指標，它是從一個大家常常沒放在心上的觀念推出來的：取消的成長速度比行銷快。

alts.quote: Data is more like a compass than a GPS. If you look at data as a way of giving you the answer, you're always wrong. Wrong or slow, or sometimes both.
alts.zh: 數據比較像指南針，不是導航。如果你把數據當成會給你答案的東西，你不是錯就是慢，有時候兩者都有。

cards.pattern: Are we in the top three in that category? If the answer is yes, that means we invested too much in that category.
cards.quote: Are we in the top three in the market in that category? If the answer is yes, that means we invested too much in that category.
cards.zh: 我們在那個品類裡有沒有進前三？如果答案是「有」，那代表我們在那個品類投太多了。
cards.why: 一個把常識反過來的判準——好成績當成警訊。這種反直覺指標之所以有說服力，是因為它只有在你的策略成立時才講得通，等於順便再證明一次策略。
swaps: If our API docs are best-in-class, we over-invested—that's not what we win on.
Being great at the thing we said we wouldn't compete on is a red flag.
cards.pmNote: 指標要對齊策略。all-in-one 的價值是整合，單點做到頂尖反而代表資源錯配。
cards.episode: Zigging vs. zagging: How HubSpot built a $30B company | Dharmesh Shah (co-founder/CTO)

alts.quote: We heard a couple comments from them, it was little murmurs. And I didn't realize at the time that was the signal that we did not have product market fit.
alts.zh: 我們只聽到他們零星幾句抱怨，就是一點小碎念而已。我當時沒意識到，那正是我們沒有 PMF 的訊號。

alts.quote: Companies I've invested in is a long list, and I love to give you names of companies that don't exist anymore because it's self-serving and a horrible survivorship bias to just list the good ones.
alts.zh: 我投資過的公司名單很長，我很願意告訴你那些已經倒掉的公司名字——因為只列出成功的那些，是自利、也是很糟的倖存者偏誤。

alts.quote: According to Harvard Law School, among venture-backed companies that have the standard best practices set up that you got from your lawyer, only 20% of founders are still the CEO three years after going public.
alts.zh: 根據哈佛法學院的研究，在那些照律師標準做法設立的創投公司裡，上市三年後還在當 CEO 的創辦人只有 20%。

cards.pattern: If they tell you '[敷衍的回應]', it's not a real problem.
cards.quote: If you tell someone, 'This is the problem I'm going to address,' and they will tell you, 'Oh, I know someone that has this problem,' it's not a real problem.
cards.zh: 如果你跟人說「這是我要解決的問題」，對方回你「喔，我知道有誰有這個問題」——那它就不是真問題。
cards.why: 給了一個可以當場判讀的訊號，而且訊號本身是一句台詞。把驗證標準寫成「對方會怎麼說」，比寫成抽象準則好用一百倍。
swaps: 'That'd be nice to have' means no.
If they can't name the last time it bit them, it isn't urgent.
cards.pmNote: 使用者訪談要聽的是「我上週就被這件事搞到」，不是「這聽起來很有用」。
cards.episode: Lessons from a two-time unicorn builder, 50-time startup advisor, and 20-time company board member | Uri Levine (co-founder of Waze)

alts.quote: The true test of whether the positioning's working is, if I'm sitting across from a qualified prospect and I tell the story, does the prospect get excited and want to buy something?
alts.zh: 定位有沒有效，真正的檢驗是：我坐在一個合格的潛在客戶對面把故事講完，他會不會眼睛一亮、想買東西？

alts.quote: It's about saying, okay, if we have these themes of stuff that we want to work on, what do we know with confidence because the data tells us and what do we need to understand because we don't have the data?
alts.zh: 重點是要問：在我們想做的這些主題裡，哪些是數據講得夠清楚、我們有把握的？哪些是因為沒數據，所以還得先搞懂的？

alts.quote: There was this unwritten rule of thumb that, hey, if it's not going to generate more than $100 million in revenue, it's not worth talking about it.
alts.zh: 當時有一條沒寫下來的潛規則：如果一件事帶不來一億美金以上的營收，就不值得拿出來討論。

cards.quote: If you create value, they will come back. If they're not coming back, that means that you are not creating value.
cards.zh: 如果你創造了價值，他們會回來。如果他們沒回來，那就代表你沒創造價值。
cards.why: 正向與逆否命題連著講，把一個指標變成邏輯上封閉的定義。這種寫法讓對方無處可躲——沒有「我們有價值只是用戶還沒發現」這個縫隙。
swaps: Retention is the receipt. No receipt, no value.
If it mattered, they'd be back. They're not back.
cards.pmNote: PMF 的單一指標是留存。所有其他數字都可以靠推廣買到，留存不行。
cards.episode: Lessons from a two-time unicorn builder, 50-time startup advisor, and 20-time company board member | Uri Levine (co-founder of Waze)

alts.quote: And so it's dropped by about half from 2000 to 2015 or so, and since then has come back to about 75% of the peak, adjusted for inflation.
alts.zh: 它從 2000 年到 2015 年左右大約掉了一半，之後回到高點的七成五左右，這是通膨調整後的數字。

alts.quote: So when you do a pros and cons list, but they're skewed and you are leaving some things out of the cons list, it makes the reader suspicious and they can't trust you anymore.
alts.zh: 當你列出優缺點，但列得偏頗、缺點那欄漏了東西，讀者就會起疑，然後就再也不信你了。

alts.quote: So when it's a ratio and you decrease the denominator, the value of the ratio grows. And so, how do you decrease the denominator in this case where time is the denominator is you start working on things that take less time.
alts.zh: 這是一個比值，分母變小，比值就變大。那在這裡分母是時間，你要怎麼讓分母變小？你就開始挑那些花比較少時間的事情做。

cards.pattern: In [這個場景], it's [小得多的比例]. Not [一般人以為的], [實際的]. So you're going to hear [N] times no until you hear one yes.
cards.quote: In investors, it's 1%. Not one third, 1%. So you're going to hear a hundred times no until you hear one yes.
cards.zh: 在投資人這邊，是 1%。不是三分之一，是 1%。所以你會聽到一百次「不」，才會聽到一次「好」。
cards.why: Not one third, 1% 這個「否定＋修正」的重述，把數字釘進聽眾腦裡。最後一句把百分比翻譯成「你會經歷幾次拒絕」，讓抽象比例變成可預期的體感。
swaps: Not 20%—2%. Which means 50 conversations per win.
Expect nine noes. Budget for them.
cards.pmNote: 把轉換率換算成「要跑幾輪」，才能真正管理團隊的期待與士氣。
cards.episode: Lessons from a two-time unicorn builder, 50-time startup advisor, and 20-time company board member | Uri Levine (co-founder of Waze)

alts.quote: If you say, 'I think this is going to take three months to launch' and I was thinking four weeks, you're never going to hear four weeks from me, ever.
alts.zh: 如果你說「我覺得要三個月」，而我原本想的是四週，那你永遠不會從我嘴裡聽到四週。永遠不會。

alts.quote: And I think it's if you have at least 40% of people respond that they'd be very disappointed, then you're on the right track.
alts.zh: 如果至少有 40% 的人回答「沒有這個東西會非常失望」，那你方向是對的。

alts.quote: The basic principle with laser is that willpower is never going to win, and there's great research on this, but for now just trust me, you're not going to white-knuckle your way through not looking at Twitter when you're trying to work.
alts.zh: laser 的基本原理是：意志力永遠贏不了。這方面有很多很好的研究，但現在你先信我——你不可能靠硬撐來讓自己工作時不看 Twitter。

cards.pattern: In order to improve, we need to speak with those that [失敗的那群]. Because they know something that we really need to know.
cards.quote: In order to improve, we need to speak with those that fail, those that were unsuccessful. Because they know something that we really need to know.
cards.zh: 想要進步，我們得去找那些失敗的人談——那些沒成功的。因為他們知道一件我們非常需要知道的事。
cards.why: 他不說「我們的取樣有偏差」，而說「他們知道一件我們需要知道的事」——把訪談流失用戶從方法論問題變成情報問題，聽起來就從糾錯變成尋寶。
swaps: The churned users are the ones holding the answer.
We keep interviewing the survivors. That's the bias.
cards.pmNote: 只訪談留下來的用戶＝倖存者偏差。要改善漏斗，必須訪談沒通過那一關的人。
cards.episode: Lessons from a two-time unicorn builder, 50-time startup advisor, and 20-time company board member | Uri Levine (co-founder of Waze)

alts.quote: It's about saying, okay, if we have these themes of stuff that we want to work on, what do we know with confidence because the data tells us and what do we need to understand because we don't have the data?
alts.zh: 重點是要問：在我們想做的這些主題裡，哪些是數據講得夠清楚、我們有把握的？哪些是因為沒數據，所以還得先搞懂的？

alts.quote: We know that something like 92% of developers are already using AI tools.
alts.zh: 我們知道大概有 92% 的開發者已經在用 AI 工具了。

alts.quote: And it turns out that according to Noam, Noam Wasserstein, 65% of startups fail because of conflict with founders or the founding team.
alts.zh: 根據 Noam Wasserstein 的研究，有 65% 的新創是死在創辦人或創始團隊之間的衝突。

cards.pattern: The symptom of not having [一件事] is usually [具體可見的病徵].
cards.quote: The symptom of not having a one thing is usually having a slide that says way too many things.
cards.zh: 「沒有一個核心重點」的症狀，通常就是一張塞了太多東西的投影片。
cards.why: The symptom of X is usually Y——把抽象缺陷對應到一個看得見的病徵，等於給了對方一個自我檢查工具。指出病徵比指責人溫和，但更難反駁。
swaps: The symptom of an unclear owner is a meeting that keeps getting rescheduled.
Bloated acceptance criteria usually mean we haven't agreed on the goal.
cards.pmNote: 一張投影片講不清一件事，代表想法還沒收斂——這時候該改的是思考，不是排版。
cards.episode: Why most public speaking advice is wrong—and how to finally overcome your speaking anxiety | Tristan de Montebello (CEO & co-founder of Ultraspeaking)

alts.quote: Number one is actually measuring it. I can't tell you how many times I suggest to a founder to track cohorts and that's a new thing.
alts.zh: 第一件事其實是去量它。我真的數不清有多少次我建議創辦人追蹤 cohort，結果那對他們是全新的東西。

alts.quote: Data is more like a compass than a GPS. If you look at data as a way of giving you the answer, you're always wrong. Wrong or slow, or sometimes both.
alts.zh: 數據比較像指南針，不是導航。如果你把數據當成會給你答案的東西，你不是錯就是慢，有時候兩者都有。

alts.quote: The basic principle with laser is that willpower is never going to win, and there's great research on this, but for now just trust me, you're not going to white-knuckle your way through not looking at Twitter when you're trying to work.
alts.zh: laser 的基本原理是：意志力永遠贏不了。這方面有很多很好的研究，但現在你先信我——你不可能靠硬撐來讓自己工作時不看 Twitter。

cards.pattern: That often comes in the form of an anecdote, or a data point that supports it, or a story that adds emotion.
cards.quote: That often comes in the form of an interesting anecdote or a data point that's going to support that, or a story that's going to add emotion or illustrate it.
cards.zh: 那通常會以一個有趣的軼事、一個支撐它的數據點、或一個能加上情緒或具體說明的故事的形式出現。
cards.why: 把「證據」列成三種可選形式（軼事／數據／故事），讓抽象的「請支撐你的主張」變成一份可勾選的清單。in the form of 也是英文裡列舉選項時很順的接法。
swaps: Back it with one number, one quote, or one story—pick whichever lands hardest.
Every claim needs weight behind it: data, anecdote, or demo.
cards.pmNote: 主張要有重量。數據負責可信、故事負責記憶、軼事負責具體——好提案三種都會用一點。
cards.episode: Why most public speaking advice is wrong—and how to finally overcome your speaking anxiety | Tristan de Montebello (CEO & co-founder of Ultraspeaking)

alts.quote: You could have all the usage data in the world, that's going to tell you what's actually happening in your product, but it doesn't tell you why.
alts.zh: 就算你握有全世界的使用數據，它只會告訴你產品裡實際發生了什麼，不會告訴你為什麼。

alts.quote: The true test of whether the positioning's working is, if I'm sitting across from a qualified prospect and I tell the story, does the prospect get excited and want to buy something?
alts.zh: 定位有沒有效，真正的檢驗是：我坐在一個合格的潛在客戶對面把故事講完，他會不會眼睛一亮、想買東西？

alts.quote: Data is more like a compass than a GPS. If you look at data as a way of giving you the answer, you're always wrong. Wrong or slow, or sometimes both.
alts.zh: 數據比較像指南針，不是導航。如果你把數據當成會給你答案的東西，你不是錯就是慢，有時候兩者都有。

cards.pattern: In fact, I wager you might only remember [極少的量] from that [經驗].
cards.quote: If you think about your last all hands, the last talk you saw, you probably don't remember much. In fact, I wager you might only remember one thing from that talk.
cards.zh: 回想你上一次的全員大會、上一場你聽的演講——你大概記不得多少。老實說，我敢賭你只記得一件事。
cards.why: 用聽眾自己的記憶當實驗樣本，證據就在對方腦袋裡，你不用引用任何研究。I wager 比 I bet 正式一點，帶點賭注的自信但不失禮。
swaps: Think back to last quarter's review—I'd wager you remember one number, tops.
Ask yourself what you retained from the last deck you sat through.
cards.pmNote: 沒有資料可引時，讓對方在腦中跑一次自己的經驗，是最便宜也最難反駁的證據。
cards.episode: Why most public speaking advice is wrong—and how to finally overcome your speaking anxiety | Tristan de Montebello (CEO & co-founder of Ultraspeaking)

alts.quote: And so, I think I probably shipped a lot of bad product those years, if I'm being completely honest.
alts.zh: 所以老實說，那幾年我大概出了不少爛產品。

alts.quote: I think people don't realize that there's a big difference between moving from 80% performance to 90% performance to 99% performance to 99.9% performance, and so on, and so on.
alts.zh: 我覺得大家沒意識到，從 80% 做到 90%、再到 99%、再到 99.9%，這幾段之間的差距有多大。

alts.quote: So there's a different metric that I like to use, which keys off of this idea that I think, again, people don't appreciate, which is cancellations grow faster than marketing.
alts.zh: 我比較喜歡用另一個指標，它是從一個大家常常沒放在心上的觀念推出來的：取消的成長速度比行銷快。

cards.pattern: Start right before [高潮的前一刻]. Get to the juicy part.
cards.quote: Start right before your friend left a Clif Bar out in their tent and you all almost got mauled by a bear. Get to the juicy part.
cards.zh: 從你朋友把能量棒留在帳篷外、你們差點被熊撲的前一刻開始講。直接切到最精彩的地方。
cards.why: 她不是教你「講短一點」，是給了一個可以照做的切點：熊出現的前一秒。Get to the juicy part 這種很口語的收尾也讓建議變成一句可以背的口令。
swaps: Start the story where it gets interesting, not where it started.
Cut everything before the moment things went wrong.
cards.pmNote: 策略敘事要從轉折點開場。背景鋪陳越長，聽眾越早離線。
cards.episode: Become a better communicator: Specific frameworks to improve your clarity, influence, and impact | Wes Kao (coach, entrepreneur, advisor)

alts.quote: Over the course of our life, because of all these little situations that happen, we start getting bugs in the software and we're not really upgrading our software.
alts.zh: 在人生的過程裡，因為發生了各種小事，我們的軟體開始長 bug，而我們也沒有真的在更新它。

alts.quote: I assume all the time, 100% of the time, that no one wants to hear anything I have to say.
alts.zh: 我永遠都假設——百分之百的場合都假設——沒有人想聽我講任何話。

alts.quote: I'd say that was the beginning of chapter two where it was we went from the company that could do no wrong to the company that could do no right, which was a big flip.
alts.zh: 我會說那就是第二章的開始——我們從「怎麼做都對」的公司，變成「怎麼做都錯」的公司，整個翻過來。

cards.quote: You really cut out all the parts that make people go dead in the eyes and just say the parts that make their eyes light up.
cards.zh: 你要做的就是把那些讓人眼神死掉的段落全砍掉，只留下讓人眼睛發亮的部分。
cards.why: go dead in the eyes / eyes light up 是一組完整的反義視覺對照，抽象的「無聊 vs 有趣」變成兩張看得見的臉。剪輯原則因此變得可以當場執行。
swaps: Keep the lines that make people lean in. Delete the rest.
Watch the room: cut wherever they check their phones.
cards.pmNote: 銷售說法、demo 腳本、上線公告都該用真人反應迭代——哪一句讓人眼睛亮，就把那句擴寫。
cards.episode: Become a better communicator: Specific frameworks to improve your clarity, influence, and impact | Wes Kao (coach, entrepreneur, advisor)

alts.quote: I assume all the time, 100% of the time, that no one wants to hear anything I have to say.
alts.zh: 我永遠都假設——百分之百的場合都假設——沒有人想聽我講任何話。

alts.quote: It doesn't matter if you think Bloomberg or Trump should be president. Do you think everyone should have access to great education? Most people would say yes.
alts.zh: 你覺得該讓 Bloomberg 還是 Trump 當總統，都無所謂。你覺得每個人都該有機會受好的教育嗎？大多數人會說會。

alts.quote: And one thing people make fun of me a lot for that I think is just a great example of extreme clarity is I never use bulleted lists because you can never refer to a bullet.
alts.zh: 有件事大家常笑我，但我覺得那正是「極度清楚」的最佳示範：我從來不用項目符號，因為你沒辦法指名某一個點。

cards.pattern: Over the course of our life, we start getting bugs in the software and we're not really upgrading our software.
cards.quote: Over the course of our life, because of all these little situations that happen, we start getting bugs in the software and we're not really upgrading our software.
cards.zh: 在人生的過程裡，因為發生了各種小事，我們的軟體開始長 bug，而我們也沒有真的在更新它。
cards.why: hardware / software 這組比喻把「你天生就會說話，只是被卡住了」講得無比清楚，而且完全不指責聽眾。對工程與產品出身的聽眾尤其有效——用他們的母語講心理學。
swaps: The hardware's fine. We just never patched the software.
It's not a capability gap, it's accumulated cruft.
cards.pmNote: 對技術聽眾說服時，借用他們熟悉的隱喻可以大幅降低理解成本。
cards.episode: Why most public speaking advice is wrong—and how to finally overcome your speaking anxiety | Tristan de Montebello (CEO & co-founder of Ultraspeaking)

alts.quote: As a very simple example, sorry, this is a little bit dark, but how restaurants want to turn over tables as fast as possible in order to maximize for the day? Hospitals actually want to do the same with patients.
alts.zh: 舉個很簡單的例子——抱歉這個講法有點黑暗——餐廳希望翻桌越快越好，好把一天的收益拉高。醫院對病床其實也是同一件事。

alts.quote: Start right before your friend left a Clif Bar out in their tent and you all almost got mauled by a bear. Get to the juicy part.
alts.zh: 從你朋友把能量棒留在帳篷外、你們差點被熊撲的前一刻開始講。直接切到最精彩的地方。

alts.quote: I call this habit “gossiping” to AI, because I fill in my copilot the same way I’d lean over and vent to a colleague sitting next to me.
alts.zh: 我把這個習慣叫做對 AI「講八卦」，因為我更新我的副駕的方式，就跟我側身跟隔壁同事抱怨一樣。

cards.pattern: It's like you had a very smooth flight and your landing was horrible. You're not going to remember the flight, you're going to remember the ending.
cards.quote: It's like you had a very smooth flight across the Atlantic and your landing was absolutely horrible. You're not going to remember the smooth flight, you're going to remember the ending.
cards.zh: 就像你飛越大西洋一路很平穩，結果降落爛透了。你不會記得那段平穩的飛行，你只會記得結尾。
cards.why: It's like… 開場、具體場景中段、最後用 not X, you're going to Y 收斂成原則。這三段式是英文口語裡把抽象心理效應講給人聽最穩的模板。
swaps: Great quarter, terrible QBR—guess which one gets remembered.
The launch went fine. The postmortem is what people will quote.
cards.pmNote: peak-end rule：一段體驗的評價由高峰與結尾決定。專案收尾與交付信值得額外投資。
cards.episode: Why most public speaking advice is wrong—and how to finally overcome your speaking anxiety | Tristan de Montebello (CEO & co-founder of Ultraspeaking)

alts.quote: I often use this analogy of if you're doing a home renovation, you can have the most beautiful rendering of the new bedroom. But if you haven't checked if there's electricity in that wall there or not, it's going to drastically change the cost and the time and everything.
alts.zh: 我常用一個比喻：你在裝修房子，臥室的效果圖可以做得美到不行。但如果你沒去確認那面牆裡到底有沒有電線，成本跟時間都會整個變樣。

alts.quote: We call it the bow and arrow technique because we think you can only remember one thing out of a talk and that it's very powerful to go through that framework or that kind of thinking when you're building a talk.
alts.zh: 我們把它叫做「弓與箭技巧」，因為我們認為一場演講聽眾只記得住一件事，而在準備演講時走過這套思考非常有效。

alts.quote: I think the hardest thing for a founder, challenge is not optional. You're going to be challenged, but the suffering is optional.
alts.zh: 對創辦人來說最難的是：挑戰不是選項，你一定會被挑戰；但要不要痛苦，是選項。

cards.quote: You want to be that tree in the storm that is not so rigid that if the wind is too strong it's going to break in half, but not so flexible that it's going to swing every which direction as soon as there's a gust.
cards.zh: 你要當風暴裡的那棵樹——不要硬到風一大就攔腰折斷，也不要軟到一陣風來就往每個方向亂晃。
cards.why: 用 not so X that… but not so Y that… 的雙邊界句型描述「剛剛好」，比說 balanced 精準得多。兩個失敗模式都被畫出來，聽眾自然知道要站哪裡。
swaps: Not so locked that we can't adapt, not so loose that the plan means nothing.
Firm on the goal, flexible on the path.
cards.pmNote: 描述「適度」時，畫出兩端的失敗樣態比形容中間值有效得多。
cards.episode: Why most public speaking advice is wrong—and how to finally overcome your speaking anxiety | Tristan de Montebello (CEO & co-founder of Ultraspeaking)

alts.quote: If you're trying to do it, the best way to tell a story about something that you want people to understand is to do what I call speaking with adjacency, which means we're not going to match content to content.
alts.zh: 如果你想讓別人理解某件事，最好的說故事方式是我所謂的「用鄰近性說話」——意思是我們不會拿內容去對內容。

alts.quote: I often use this analogy of if you're doing a home renovation, you can have the most beautiful rendering of the new bedroom. But if you haven't checked if there's electricity in that wall there or not, it's going to drastically change the cost and the time and everything.
alts.zh: 我常用一個比喻：你在裝修房子，臥室的效果圖可以做得美到不行。但如果你沒去確認那面牆裡到底有沒有電線，成本跟時間都會整個變樣。

alts.quote: You wouldn't want to be in a commercial airplane and hear the tower say to the pilot, 'I'm giving priority to the following three planes on runway five.' Right away, you know there's something wrong.
alts.zh: 你不會希望自己坐在飛機上，聽到塔台跟機師說：「我要給五號跑道上這三架飛機優先權。」你馬上就知道哪裡不對。

cards.pattern: Which reminds me of a [人名] quote that I love, where he says, '[引語]'
cards.quote: Which reminds me of a Kevin Kelly quote that I love where he says, 'Pros are just amateurs who've learned to recover gracefully from their mistakes.'
cards.zh: 這讓我想到我很喜歡的一句 Kevin Kelly 的話：「專業人士只是學會了優雅地從錯誤中恢復的業餘者。」
cards.why: Which reminds me of… 讓引用像是聯想而不是準備好的講稿，聽起來更自然。that I love 這三個字也表態了：我不是引權威，我是分享我信的東西。
swaps: That reminds me of a line I keep coming back to—
There's a quote I love that fits here:
cards.pmNote: 會議裡臨場接引語，比事先安排的引用更有說服力，因為它證明你真的在聽。
cards.episode: Why most public speaking advice is wrong—and how to finally overcome your speaking anxiety | Tristan de Montebello (CEO & co-founder of Ultraspeaking)

alts.quote: I'd say that was the beginning of chapter two where it was we went from the company that could do no wrong to the company that could do no right, which was a big flip.
alts.zh: 我會說那就是第二章的開始——我們從「怎麼做都對」的公司，變成「怎麼做都錯」的公司，整個翻過來。

alts.quote: He asked me one question which was something to the effect of, how does this make our users love Twitter more? Simple question. But then at that point I realized, yeah, we never really talked about that.
alts.zh: 他只問了我一個問題：這件事怎麼讓我們的使用者更愛 Twitter？很簡單的問題。但那一刻我才發現，我們從頭到尾沒真的談過這個。

alts.quote: Which is you bring a fruit to the reviewer and say, "Hey, here's a mango, what do you think?" And the reviewer says, "I actually don't like mangoes."
alts.zh: 你拿一個水果去給主管看：「欸，這是芒果，你覺得怎樣？」主管說：「我其實不喜歡芒果。」

cards.pattern: So I was thinking of an analogy for this, and one that I really like is imagine you're [日常場景].
cards.quote: So I was thinking of an analogy for this, and one that I really like is imagine you're redecorating your living room.
cards.zh: 我在想這件事的比喻，我很喜歡的一個是：想像你在重新佈置你的客廳。
cards.why: 這是英文裡最好用的「我要開始講比喻了」開關——先報備，聽眾就會切換到收比喻的模式，不會誤以為你離題。imagine you're… 再把他們拉進場景。
swaps: Here's the analogy I keep using: imagine you're packing for a trip.
Think of it like renovating a kitchen—
cards.pmNote: 把抽象方法論綁到一個人人有經驗的日常場景，是策略敘事最省力的傳播方式。
cards.episode: Why most public speaking advice is wrong—and how to finally overcome your speaking anxiety | Tristan de Montebello (CEO & co-founder of Ultraspeaking)

alts.quote: I often use this analogy of if you're doing a home renovation, you can have the most beautiful rendering of the new bedroom. But if you haven't checked if there's electricity in that wall there or not, it's going to drastically change the cost and the time and everything.
alts.zh: 我常用一個比喻：你在裝修房子，臥室的效果圖可以做得美到不行。但如果你沒去確認那面牆裡到底有沒有電線，成本跟時間都會整個變樣。

alts.quote: You kind of come up thinking you're the protagonist. You can be the protagonist in your life, but in the story of your work of a company, you are probably not the protagonist.
alts.zh: 你一路長大都以為自己是主角。你在自己的人生裡可以是主角，但在公司這個故事裡，你多半不是主角。

alts.quote: We call it the bow and arrow technique because we think you can only remember one thing out of a talk and that it's very powerful to go through that framework or that kind of thinking when you're building a talk.
alts.zh: 我們把它叫做「弓與箭技巧」，因為我們認為一場演講聽眾只記得住一件事，而在準備演講時走過這套思考非常有效。

cards.pattern: And suddenly I realized, 'Oh, [殘酷的事實]. This is not good. This is terrible.'
cards.quote: And I'm looking at this, and suddenly I realized, 'Oh, this speech, nobody cares about this. This is not a good speech. This is terrible.'
cards.zh: 我看著畫面，突然意識到：「喔，這篇講稿根本沒人在乎。這不是一篇好講稿。這爛透了。」
cards.why: 用現在式的內心獨白重演當下（不是「我後來發現」，而是把那句話原封搬出來），故事的轉折點就有了體感。三個越來越短的句子也模擬了心情崩塌的節奏。
swaps: And that's when it hit me: nobody was reading past the first paragraph.
Halfway through the recording I thought, oh no. This isn't working.
cards.pmNote: postmortem 或案例分享時，重演當下的想法比事後總結更有說服力，也更容易被記住。
cards.episode: Why most public speaking advice is wrong—and how to finally overcome your speaking anxiety | Tristan de Montebello (CEO & co-founder of Ultraspeaking)

alts.quote: He said, "I could have been a pretty good cartoonist or I could have been pretty good at business, but the fact that I was a cartoonist who understood business made me spectacularly great at making Dilbert."
alts.zh: 他說：「我可以當個還不錯的漫畫家，也可以當個還不錯的商業人，但因為我是一個懂商業的漫畫家，才讓我把呆伯特做到無人能及。」

alts.quote: And after all of that, which clearly means they wanted it to work, they're like, "No, bye." What? Just on an emotional level, you got to go, "Wait a minute, that's terrible."
alts.zh: 經歷了這一整串——這明明代表他們很想讓它成功——結果他們說「不用了，掰」。蛤？光是情緒上你就該有反應：等一下，這超糟的。

alts.quote: He was asked whether or not he was sleeping well at night and he said, 'Oh, yeah, I slept like a baby. I woke up every two hours and cried.'
alts.zh: 有人問他晚上睡得好不好，他說：「喔，超好，我睡得跟嬰兒一樣——每兩小時醒來哭一次。」

cards.quote: A good story is not about facts. It's about creating emotional engagement. It's about creating the sense that the listener would like to be part of this story.
cards.zh: 好故事不是關於事實。它是關於製造情緒上的連結。是讓聽的人覺得自己想要成為這個故事的一部分。
cards.why: not about X. It's about Y. It's about Z. 兩次重述層層加深，最後一層才是真正的定義（讓人想加入）。這種「否定一次、遞進兩次」的節奏很好背也很好用。
swaps: This isn't a status update. It's an invitation.
The pitch isn't the numbers—it's whether they want to be in the room when it works.
cards.pmNote: 願景敘事的成功標準不是「聽懂了」，是「想加入」。
cards.episode: Lessons from a two-time unicorn builder, 50-time startup advisor, and 20-time company board member | Uri Levine (co-founder of Waze)

alts.quote: You've started this company, it's been super successful, and then suddenly your employees don't want to wear your T-shirt anymore.
alts.zh: 你創了這家公司，它一路很成功，然後突然間，員工不想再穿你們公司的 T-shirt 了。

alts.quote: It's like you had a very smooth flight across the Atlantic and your landing was absolutely horrible. You're not going to remember the smooth flight, you're going to remember the ending.
alts.zh: 就像你飛越大西洋一路很平穩，結果降落爛透了。你不會記得那段平穩的飛行，你只會記得結尾。

alts.quote: And the story is like there's a frog at the bottom of the well. He looks up every night and he sees the world and he imagines he knows everything about the world.
alts.zh: 故事是這樣：有一隻青蛙住在井底。牠每天晚上抬頭看那一小塊天，就以為自己什麼都懂了。

cards.pattern: How do you make a story believable? With details. If there are no details, then this is not real.
cards.quote: How do you make a story make believe? With details. If there are no details, then this is not real.
cards.zh: 怎麼讓一個故事讓人信？用細節。沒有細節，那就不是真的。
cards.why: 自問自答（How do you…? With details.）是英文口語裡把重點推到最前面的方法。後面兩句一正一反再夾一次，一個原則就這樣被釘死。
swaps: Specificity is what makes it land. Vague stories sound made up.
Name the customer, name the day, name the number.
cards.pmNote: 使用者故事寫得越具體越可信。三行寫完的 use case，在會議上撐不住任何追問。
cards.episode: Lessons from a two-time unicorn builder, 50-time startup advisor, and 20-time company board member | Uri Levine (co-founder of Waze)

alts.quote: And the story is like there's a frog at the bottom of the well. He looks up every night and he sees the world and he imagines he knows everything about the world.
alts.zh: 故事是這樣：有一隻青蛙住在井底。牠每天晚上抬頭看那一小塊天，就以為自己什麼都懂了。

alts.quote: Let me tell you one not very happy story.
alts.zh: 我來講一個不太愉快的故事。

alts.quote: You kind of come up thinking you're the protagonist. You can be the protagonist in your life, but in the story of your work of a company, you are probably not the protagonist.
alts.zh: 你一路長大都以為自己是主角。你在自己的人生裡可以是主角，但在公司這個故事裡，你多半不是主角。

cards.pattern: He was asked [問題] and he said, '[出乎意料的回答]'
cards.quote: He was asked whether or not he was sleeping well at night and he said, 'Oh, yeah, I slept like a baby. I woke up every two hours and cried.'
cards.zh: 有人問他晚上睡得好不好，他說：「喔，超好，我睡得跟嬰兒一樣——每兩小時醒來哭一次。」
cards.why: 用一則笑話當證據。這種先鋪一個熟悉的說法（slept like a baby）再翻轉的結構，笑完的當下概念也被記住了——比任何形容詞都有效。
swaps: Someone asked how the launch went. 'Smoothly—if you don't count Tuesday.'
'How's the migration?' 'On track. Also on fire.'
cards.pmNote: 報告艱難處境時，一個自嘲的笑話可以同時傳達壓力與掌控感。
cards.episode: Lessons from a two-time unicorn builder, 50-time startup advisor, and 20-time company board member | Uri Levine (co-founder of Waze)

alts.quote: And the story is like there's a frog at the bottom of the well. He looks up every night and he sees the world and he imagines he knows everything about the world.
alts.zh: 故事是這樣：有一隻青蛙住在井底。牠每天晚上抬頭看那一小塊天，就以為自己什麼都懂了。

alts.quote: Yeah, every time you move up a league, your reward is a stronger and better opponent and potentially more unlevel playing field.
alts.zh: 每升上一個聯盟，你的獎賞就是一個更強的對手，而且場地可能還更不公平。

alts.quote: They're going to be like, 'Oh, well, it sounds like you put in your best effort.' But if you walk away early, people are like, 'What?'
alts.zh: 他們會說：「喔，聽起來你已經盡力了。」但如果你提早收手，大家的反應會是：「蛤？」

cards.pattern: In lay person's terms, [專業概念], I'm paraphrasing here, is that [白話版].
cards.quote: In lay person's terms, the second law of thermodynamics, I'm paraphrasing here, is that, 'Over time, unless you intervene, everything goes to crap.'
cards.zh: 用白話講，熱力學第二定律——我這是意譯——就是：隨著時間過去，除非你出手干預，不然一切都會爛掉。
cards.why: In lay person's terms 讓你可以借用一個硬概念的權威，同時用最白的話講；I'm paraphrasing here 則預先免責，避免被學術派抓字眼。兩個插入語一起，就能安全地把大詞拿來用。
swaps: In plain English, and I'm simplifying, compounding just means it gets easier later.
Roughly speaking—don't quote me to a physicist—
cards.pmNote: 跨職能溝通時，先宣告「我要講白話版」比講精確版更能推進會議。
cards.episode: Zigging vs. zagging: How HubSpot built a $30B company | Dharmesh Shah (co-founder/CTO)

alts.quote: I often use this analogy of if you're doing a home renovation, you can have the most beautiful rendering of the new bedroom. But if you haven't checked if there's electricity in that wall there or not, it's going to drastically change the cost and the time and everything.
alts.zh: 我常用一個比喻：你在裝修房子，臥室的效果圖可以做得美到不行。但如果你沒去確認那面牆裡到底有沒有電線，成本跟時間都會整個變樣。

alts.quote: I assume all the time, 100% of the time, that no one wants to hear anything I have to say.
alts.zh: 我永遠都假設——百分之百的場合都假設——沒有人想聽我講任何話。

alts.quote: Yeah, every time you move up a league, your reward is a stronger and better opponent and potentially more unlevel playing field.
alts.zh: 每升上一個聯盟，你的獎賞就是一個更強的對手，而且場地可能還更不公平。

cards.pattern: So the moral of the story is, [那一個決定]—can you imagine [被避開的巨大代價]?
cards.quote: So the moral of the story is, that one decision of simplifying, can you imagine the amount of politics we avoided?
cards.zh: 所以這個故事的寓意是：光是那一個「簡化」的決定，你能想像我們躲掉了多少辦公室政治嗎？
cards.why: 用問句當寓意收尾，比直接下結論更有力——聽眾必須自己在腦中估算那個數字，估完就等於同意了。moral of the story 也是明確的收束信號。
swaps: The takeaway: one rule up front saved us a hundred arguments later.
Do you know how many escalations that one default prevented?
cards.pmNote: 避開的成本很難量化，所以更要講成故事。你沒發生的災難，不會出現在任何 dashboard 上。
cards.episode: Zigging vs. zagging: How HubSpot built a $30B company | Dharmesh Shah (co-founder/CTO)

alts.quote: You kind of come up thinking you're the protagonist. You can be the protagonist in your life, but in the story of your work of a company, you are probably not the protagonist.
alts.zh: 你一路長大都以為自己是主角。你在自己的人生裡可以是主角，但在公司這個故事裡，你多半不是主角。

alts.quote: I always say you should have, what I call an elephant at the beginning of the story, which is actually a big spaceship shooting at a little spaceship or a police officer chasing a guy across a roof.
alts.zh: 我一直說你應該在故事開頭放一隻我稱為「大象」的東西——實際上就是一艘大太空船在射一艘小太空船，或是警察在屋頂上追一個人。

alts.quote: So I was thinking of an analogy for this, and one that I really like is imagine you're redecorating your living room.
alts.zh: 我在想這件事的比喻，我很喜歡的一個是：想像你在重新佈置你的客廳。

cards.pattern: Amazing product, [名字], and it had just one teeny tiny small problem, which is it didn't work.
cards.quote: Amazing product, GrowthBot, and it had just one teeny tiny small problem, which is it didn't work.
cards.zh: 超棒的產品，GrowthBot，只有一個小小小小的問題——它不能用。
cards.why: teeny tiny small 三個同義詞疊在一起是刻意的過度縮小，讓後面那句反差爆開。自嘲失敗案例時最好用的節奏，講完之後聽眾會更信你接下來的成功案例。
swaps: Beautiful launch. One minor detail: nobody used it.
Great strategy, tiny flaw—it was wrong.
cards.pmNote: 分享失敗案例時用自嘲收尾，可以保住可信度又不用防衛。
cards.episode: Zigging vs. zagging: How HubSpot built a $30B company | Dharmesh Shah (co-founder/CTO)

alts.quote: And after all of that, which clearly means they wanted it to work, they're like, "No, bye." What? Just on an emotional level, you got to go, "Wait a minute, that's terrible."
alts.zh: 經歷了這一整串——這明明代表他們很想讓它成功——結果他們說「不用了，掰」。蛤？光是情緒上你就該有反應：等一下，這超糟的。

alts.quote: I'd say that was the beginning of chapter two where it was we went from the company that could do no wrong to the company that could do no right, which was a big flip.
alts.zh: 我會說那就是第二章的開始——我們從「怎麼做都對」的公司，變成「怎麼做都錯」的公司，整個翻過來。

alts.quote: You kind of come up thinking you're the protagonist. You can be the protagonist in your life, but in the story of your work of a company, you are probably not the protagonist.
alts.zh: 你一路長大都以為自己是主角。你在自己的人生裡可以是主角，但在公司這個故事裡，你多半不是主角。

cards.pattern: My definition of [X] is [重新定義]. That's it.
cards.quote: So I have my definition of success I came up with years ago. Success is making the people who believed in you look brilliant. That's it.
cards.zh: 我幾年前想出了自己對成功的定義。成功就是：讓當初相信你的人看起來很有眼光。就這樣。
