cards.why: 把一個被用爛的詞（success）換成一個具體畫面（讓相信你的人看起來很聰明），焦點從自己轉到別人。That's it. 收尾則宣告不再補充——短、乾淨、可背。
swaps: My definition of a good launch: nobody who vouched for us regrets it.
Success here means the person who approved this gets to say 'told you so.'
cards.pmNote: 把成功定義成「讓支持你的人有面子」，會自然改變你對利害關係人的溝通頻率與誠實度。
cards.episode: Zigging vs. zagging: How HubSpot built a $30B company | Dharmesh Shah (co-founder/CTO)

alts.quote: It was kind of like, Bolt's this overnight success, seven years in the making.
alts.zh: 大概就是那句：Bolt 是一個醞釀了七年的一夜爆紅。

alts.quote: People act like having a startup fail is the worst thing that can happen to you. And man, that's not even in the top 10.
alts.zh: 大家都把「創業失敗」講得像是人生最慘的事。老實說，那連前十名都排不進去。

alts.quote: He said, "I could have been a pretty good cartoonist or I could have been pretty good at business, but the fact that I was a cartoonist who understood business made me spectacularly great at making Dilbert."
alts.zh: 他說：「我可以當個還不錯的漫畫家，也可以當個還不錯的商業人，但因為我是一個懂商業的漫畫家，才讓我把呆伯特做到無人能及。」

cards.pattern: How do I share enough context about my thought process so that [對方] has enough information to push back if needed?
cards.quote: How do I share enough context about my thought process and rationale so that my boss has enough information to be able to push back if needed or to be able to approve?
cards.zh: 我要怎麼把我的思路跟理由講到足夠，讓我主管有足夠資訊可以在需要時反對我、或是直接批准？
cards.why: 主動把「反對我」列進成功條件，是成熟提案者的訊號——你不是在避免挑戰，是在把挑戰的門檻降低。push back if needed 這個片語在英文職場幾乎每天都會用到。
swaps: I've included the reasoning so you can push back on the parts you disagree with.
Tell me where this breaks—that's what the context section is for.
cards.pmNote: 邀請反對比防堵反對安全。你希望反對意見出現在決策前，不是上線後。
cards.episode: Become a better communicator: Specific frameworks to improve your clarity, influence, and impact | Wes Kao (coach, entrepreneur, advisor)

alts.quote: And many of my design friends will push back on this and they'll say design should be its own thing and it should be an independent group and we should have three co-equal branches of government, and that's a solid argument as well
alts.zh: 我很多設計圈的朋友會反對，他們會說設計應該獨立成一個部門，跟產品、工程三權分立——那也是很有道理的論點。

alts.quote: I love it that you're starting with a spicy question here and let me share some more context behind it.
alts.zh: 我很喜歡你一開始就丟這麼辣的問題，讓我先把背後的脈絡補一下。

alts.quote: Sometimes I feel the need to defend that the process is not for process' sake, it's ultimately to help us all move faster and work better.
alts.zh: 有時候我得替流程辯護一下：流程不是為了流程而存在，它最終是要讓大家跑得更快、做得更好。

cards.pattern: Now they're looking at everything you said through the lens of [你自己種下的懷疑].
cards.quote: Now even if they had the best of experiences with your answer, now they're looking at everything you said through the lens of, oh, this person was kind of uncertain.
cards.zh: 就算他們原本對你的回答感受很好，現在他們也會透過「這個人好像沒把握」這個濾鏡，重新看你剛剛講的每一句話。
cards.why: through the lens of 是英文裡描述「詮釋框架」最常用的片語。整句解釋的是機制而不是後果——因為講清楚了機制，聽的人自己就會停止那個行為。
swaps: One hedge at the end recolours the whole answer.
They'll re-read your entire doc through that one caveat.
cards.pmNote: 溝通裡的「後設訊號」（你多有把握）會覆蓋內容本身。這是為什麼一句多餘的免責會很貴。
cards.episode: Why most public speaking advice is wrong—and how to finally overcome your speaking anxiety | Tristan de Montebello (CEO & co-founder of Ultraspeaking)

alts.quote: I remember somebody on social media said the problem with Benedict is his answer to everything is it depends. It's like, yeah, it does. It depends.
alts.zh: 我記得有人在社群上說：Benedict 的問題就是他對什麼都回答「看情況」。呃，本來就是啊。就是看情況。

alts.quote: Oftentimes when I see analysis from different product leaders or even data teams, you can drive a truck through it, literally drive a truck through it.
alts.zh: 我常看到一些產品主管、甚至數據團隊做的分析，那個漏洞大到可以開一台卡車過去，真的。

alts.quote: Now, don't get me wrong, I've built the experimentation platform at Lyft. I'm a guy who loves data and loves using it and looking at experiments.
alts.zh: 先別誤會我的意思——Lyft 的實驗平台就是我建的。我是個超愛用數據、愛看實驗的人。

cards.pattern: The solution is very simple. Don't share your insecurities. Put your best foot forward and stay in it the whole time.
cards.quote: The solution is very, very simple. The solution is just, don't share your insecurities. Put your best foot forward and stay in it the whole time.
cards.zh: 解法非常非常簡單：不要把你的不安全感講出來。拿出你最好的一面，然後從頭到尾維持住。
cards.why: 先宣告解法很簡單（降低對方的心理成本），再給三個祈使句。stay in it 這個超短的口令是刻意設計成可以在腦中自我提示用的。
swaps: Whatever's going on inside, don't broadcast it. Just keep going.
Hold the frame. They can't see what you're feeling.
cards.pmNote: 面對質疑時的內在慌張，聽眾其實看不出來——除非你自己講出來。
cards.episode: Why most public speaking advice is wrong—and how to finally overcome your speaking anxiety | Tristan de Montebello (CEO & co-founder of Ultraspeaking)

alts.quote: The best advice I could give you is, and this sounds so trite, but really it's true, is, stay as small as you can for as long as you can.
alts.zh: 我能給的最好建議是——這聽起來很老套，但真的是真的——能維持多小就維持多小，能撐多久就撐多久。

alts.quote: Another one, love him or hate him, one of the things that Elon Musk has said that I found it very valuable in my time.
alts.zh: 還有一個，不管你喜不喜歡他啦——馬斯克講過一句話，我覺得對我很受用。

alts.quote: It's like these things that seem so common sense are actually hard with what they're doing… a lot of the advice is common sense. That doesn't mean it's easy to put in motion.
alts.zh: 這些看起來根本是常識的東西，真的做起來很難……很多建議都是常識，但常識不代表容易落地。

cards.pattern: There's a caveat, small caveat. Maybe [很小的比例] need the opposite.
cards.quote: There's a caveat, small caveat. Maybe 10% of people in the workforce need the opposite.
cards.zh: 有個但書，小小的但書：可能有 10% 的職場人需要的是相反的建議。
cards.why: 先自己說出例外，反對者就沒東西可以拿來打你。關鍵是 small caveat 跟 maybe 10%——他承認了例外，同時把例外框得很小，主張的力道幾乎沒被削弱。
swaps: One caveat, and it's narrow: this doesn't hold for regulated markets.
Small asterisk—about one in ten teams should do the opposite.
cards.pmNote: 預先處理反對（pre-mortem）最有效的形式，是自己講出例外並且界定它的大小。
cards.episode: Why most public speaking advice is wrong—and how to finally overcome your speaking anxiety | Tristan de Montebello (CEO & co-founder of Ultraspeaking)

alts.quote: There's this rush to judgment upfront where people say, "Oh, it's therefore obvious that X, Y, Z. It's obvious that the moats are going to be in this area of the technology, but not in this other area."
alts.zh: 一開始大家都會急著下判斷，說「所以顯然就是 X、Y、Z」、「顯然護城河一定在這一塊，不會在那一塊」。

alts.quote: On Twitter, you'll see people say, "Oh, it's the most expensive use of everyone's time," but it's like, "Yep. But there's 0% fidelity loss in that.
alts.zh: 推特上會有人說：「那是最貴的一種時間使用方式。」但我的回答是：「對啊。可是這樣資訊零失真。」

alts.quote: But before that, I think getting to product-market fit, obviously there's a lot of methodology for doing it today that might make it a bit easier for people, but I still think it's fairly random and pretty dang hard.
alts.zh: 在那之前——我覺得要走到 PMF，現在當然有很多方法論可能讓大家輕鬆一點，但我還是認為它相當隨機，而且真的很難。

cards.pattern: I think that's an important question, and it's a question I hear a lot, because [對方顧慮的來源].
cards.quote: Yeah, I think that's an important question, and it's a question I hear a lot because we all know a bullshitter.
cards.zh: 我覺得那是一個重要的問題，而且我常常被問到——因為我們每個人都認識一個唬爛的人。
cards.why: 三段接招：肯定問題重要、說「我常被問」（表示不是被問倒）、然後點出顧慮的真正來源。第三段是關鍵——你把對方沒說出口的那一半講出來，他就會覺得你懂他。
swaps: That's the right question to ask, and I get it every time—because everyone's been burned by a rewrite that didn't ship.
Fair challenge, and a common one. Here's where it comes from.
cards.pmNote: 接住質疑的第一步不是回答，是先讓對方確認你理解他在擔心什麼。
cards.episode: Why most public speaking advice is wrong—and how to finally overcome your speaking anxiety | Tristan de Montebello (CEO & co-founder of Ultraspeaking)

alts.quote: I still think ChatGPT kind of sucks at writing and that's because it's bottlenecked by this creative reasoning.
alts.zh: 我還是覺得 ChatGPT 在寫作這件事上蠻爛的，而那是因為它卡在創造性推理這一關。

alts.quote: And I still think it is still cheaper than sending everybody to trainings and conferences all the time, and it has a lot of, yeah, ripple effects and network effects.
alts.zh: 而且我還是覺得，這比一天到晚把所有人送去上課、跑研討會便宜，而且它還有很多連鎖效應和網絡效應。

alts.quote: It's all the other stuff. And the PowerPoint is just like the task, but that's not what you hired them for.
alts.zh: 價值在其他所有事情上。投影片只是那個「任務」，但那不是你花錢請他們來做的事。

cards.quote: And he asked me, 'Do you want the right answer or the real answer?' Say, 'You know, I heard the right answer so many times, give me the real answer.'
cards.zh: 他問我：「你要聽正確答案，還是真實答案？」我說：「正確答案我聽過太多次了，給我真實的那個。」
cards.why: the right answer vs the real answer 這組對照極短又極有力，一問就把場面從公關模式切到誠實模式。你也可以反過來用——想講難聽話之前，先問對方這句。
swaps: Do you want the polished version or the honest one?
I can give you the answer that sounds good, or the one that's true.
cards.pmNote: 在會前先取得「講真話的許可」，比在會中硬講真話政治成本低得多。
cards.episode: Lessons from a two-time unicorn builder, 50-time startup advisor, and 20-time company board member | Uri Levine (co-founder of Waze)

alts.quote: And many of my design friends will push back on this and they'll say design should be its own thing and it should be an independent group and we should have three co-equal branches of government, and that's a solid argument as well
alts.zh: 我很多設計圈的朋友會反對，他們會說設計應該獨立成一個部門，跟產品、工程三權分立——那也是很有道理的論點。

alts.quote: The basic idea is bootstrapping is for lifestyle businesses that want to cash flow. Funding is for companies trying to create a billion dollars in annual revenue. And that answer offends everybody.
alts.zh: 基本想法是：自力經營是給想要現金流的生活型事業，募資是給要做到年營收十億美元的公司。而這個答案會得罪所有人。

alts.quote: And to have the ability to say, I heard you and your input, trust me, was incorporated into the decision, nevertheless, this is the path we're going to take.
alts.zh: 我聽到你說的了，你的意見真的有被放進這個決定裡。話雖如此，我們還是要走這條路。

cards.pattern: I think they're over-indexing on what they think it's like to [做某件事].
cards.quote: And I think they're over indexing on what they think it's like to be a publicly traded company.
cards.zh: 我覺得他們對「上市公司是什麼樣子」的想像，權重放太重了。
cards.why: over-index on 是矽谷會議室的高頻動詞，意思是「這件事在你的判斷裡佔太大權重」。它不說對方錯，只說比重錯——是英文裡最不傷人的反駁之一。
swaps: We might be over-indexing on one loud customer.
That risk is real, it's just weighted too heavily here.
cards.pmNote: 反駁「權重」比反駁「事實」安全。對方不必收回任何論點就能改變結論。
cards.episode: Zigging vs. zagging: How HubSpot built a $30B company | Dharmesh Shah (co-founder/CTO)

alts.quote: Yeah, I think that's an important question, and it's a question I hear a lot because we all know a bullshitter.
alts.zh: 我覺得那是一個重要的問題，而且我常常被問到——因為我們每個人都認識一個唬爛的人。

alts.quote: And optics is a good thing. So I'm not saying don't think about optics whatsoever, I think it's actually important to think about optics.
alts.zh: 而且「對外呈現」本身是好事。我不是說完全不要管呈現，我覺得那其實很重要。

alts.quote: I still think ChatGPT kind of sucks at writing and that's because it's bottlenecked by this creative reasoning.
alts.zh: 我還是覺得 ChatGPT 在寫作這件事上蠻爛的，而那是因為它卡在創造性推理這一關。

cards.pattern: And yes, there's certainly [代價] that we didn't have before. But there are actually benefits.
cards.quote: And yes, there's certainly a tax or things we have to do now as a publicly traded company that we didn't have to do as a privately traded company. But there are actually benefits.
cards.zh: 而且沒錯，身為上市公司確實有一些「稅」、一些我們以前不用做的事。但其實也是有好處的。
cards.why: And yes, there's certainly… 先把對方的顧慮完整承認一次（不是打折承認），But there are actually benefits 才有重量。actually 這個字暗示「這是大家沒想到的」，把反擊包成資訊而不是辯護。
swaps: Yes, there's a real cost here, and I'm not going to pretend otherwise. There's also an upside nobody's counting.
That tax is real. It also buys us something.
cards.pmNote: 承認代價要具體、要完整。含糊承認會讓對方覺得你根本沒聽懂他的顧慮。
cards.episode: Zigging vs. zagging: How HubSpot built a $30B company | Dharmesh Shah (co-founder/CTO)

alts.quote: It's like these things that seem so common sense are actually hard with what they're doing… a lot of the advice is common sense. That doesn't mean it's easy to put in motion.
alts.zh: 這些看起來根本是常識的東西，真的做起來很難……很多建議都是常識，但常識不代表容易落地。

alts.quote: Actually, all feedback I think is valid. People's feelings are valid, but it doesn't mean that you need to do something about all of those things.
alts.zh: 其實我覺得所有回饋都是有效的。別人的感受都是真的，但這不代表你每一項都得去處理。

alts.quote: That's a good idea, but we don't actually understand these three things before we start working on that. So maybe we should do understand work to make sure that that is actually the right idea.
alts.zh: 這個想法不錯，但在動手之前有三件事我們其實還沒搞懂。也許先做點「理解型的工作」，確認這真的是對的方向。

cards.pattern: So it sounds like [X] is necessary. Might not be sufficient, but it's necessary.
cards.quote: So it sounds like that's necessary. Might not be sufficient, but it's necessary.
cards.zh: 聽起來這是必要條件。不一定充分，但一定必要。
cards.why: 用 necessary / sufficient 這組詞把對方的反駁收下來，同時保住自己的推論——你不必證明強因果，只要卡住「非它不可」，論點就成立了。
swaps: It's a precondition, not a guarantee.
That alone won't get us there, but nothing gets there without it.
cards.pmNote: 機會評估時分清 necessary 與 sufficient，能讓論證不必過度承諾。
cards.episode: This will make you a better decision-maker | Annie Duke (author of “Thinking in Bets” and “Quit,” former pro poker player)

alts.quote: This sounds, again, very simple but just like how you wouldn't fly a plane without instruments, why would you run your products without understanding the instrumentation and how it's doing.
alts.zh: 這聽起來很簡單，但就像你不會沒有儀表就開飛機一樣，為什麼你會在完全不看數據的情況下經營產品？

alts.quote: He thinks that a lot of the best recruiters in the world or the companies that attract talent, they put out this distinctive bad signal and it has to turn some people off. That's the key of a good, bad signal.
alts.zh: 他認為最會吸引人才的公司，都會刻意放出一個「不討喜的訊號」，而且一定要有人被勸退。這才是好的壞訊號的重點。

alts.quote: That sounds cliche. I think a lot of founders and startup people like to talk about the mission, and I get it, and I think it's real. But I really mean it.
alts.zh: 我知道這聽起來很老套。很多創辦人都愛談使命，我懂，我也覺得那是真的。但我是真心這樣講。

cards.pattern: The answer is [很大的效果] — with a big if: if [條件成立].
cards.quote: So I think the answer is a lot with a big if, with an if you can get people to do it.
cards.zh: 我覺得答案是「效果很大」，但有一個很大的 if：前提是你真的能讓人去做。
cards.why: 先把對方想聽的結論給出來，再用 with a big if 把條件掛回去；比一開頭就講條件更容易被聽完，也保住你的可信度。
swaps: Huge — conditional on one thing.
A lot, and that 'if' is doing a lot of work.
cards.episode: This will make you a better decision-maker | Annie Duke (author of “Thinking in Bets” and “Quit,” former pro poker player)

alts.quote: That sounds cliche. I think a lot of founders and startup people like to talk about the mission, and I get it, and I think it's real. But I really mean it.
alts.zh: 我知道這聽起來很老套。很多創辦人都愛談使命，我懂，我也覺得那是真的。但我是真心這樣講。

alts.quote: I think with hiring, it's funny, man, there's so much hiring advice online and you read it and you're like, "Yeah, this is super obvious." And then when you live it, you're suddenly like, "Aah, this is why people say this."
alts.zh: 招人這件事很好笑，網路上一堆建議，你看的時候都覺得「這不是廢話嗎」。等你真的經歷過，才會突然懂「喔，原來大家是這個意思」。

alts.quote: The most common mistake people make is they think through the probability first without actually forcing themselves to think through the potential.
alts.zh: 大家最常犯的錯，是先想「成功機率」，卻沒有逼自己先想「這件事最大能長成什麼樣」。

cards.pattern: The way I talk about my ideas is to convey why I believe what I do, not to convince anybody that I'm right.
cards.quote: So the way that I'm supposed to talk about my ideas is to convey why I believe what I do, not to convince anybody that I'm right.
cards.zh: 我談我的想法，是要傳達我為什麼這樣相信，不是要說服誰我是對的。
cards.why: convey / convince 只差一個字，卻把你的發言從「爭輸贏」重新定義成「提供資訊」——會議上降溫又不退讓立場的關鍵句。
swaps: I'm sharing my reasoning, not lobbying.
Take this as input, not as a pitch.
cards.pmNote: 會議目標若設成 alignment，討論會變成 coercive；設成資訊交換才會出現真實分歧。
cards.episode: This will make you a better decision-maker | Annie Duke (author of “Thinking in Bets” and “Quit,” former pro poker player)

alts.quote: And again, everything I've just described, by the way, is just a very straightforward extrapolation of very basic economics. I'm not making any bold predictions of what I just said.
alts.zh: 我剛剛講的這一整串，其實只是最基本的經濟學往下推而已。我沒有在做什麼大膽預測。

alts.quote: If I told you, I'm going to build an autonomous vehicle, and I said our team is 10 people, you should rightfully say, Varun, you're not serious. And you'd be right.
alts.zh: 如果我跟你說我要做自駕車，然後說團隊只有 10 個人，你完全應該回我：Varun，你不是認真的吧。而且你會是對的。

alts.quote: And the way I describe a pre-mortem is that if you do a pre-mortem right, you will not have to do an ugly post-mortem.
alts.zh: 我都這樣講事前檢討：事前做對了，你就不必做那種很難看的事後檢討。

cards.pattern: There are people who don't know about [X], people who know but don't do it, and people who know and do it. That last group is tiny.
cards.quote: So we can think there's people who don't know about it, there's people who do know about it but don't do it, and then there's people who do know about it, but do do it. And it's that last group that's so tiny.
cards.zh: 可以分成三種人：不知道這件事的、知道但不做的、知道又真的去做的。而最後那一群小得可憐。
cards.why: 三段分層先擋掉「大家都知道了、沒有優勢」的質疑，最後一句反手把稀缺性變成你的論點。
swaps: Knowing it and doing it are two different populations.
The overlap between 'knows' and 'does' is where the edge is.
cards.episode: This will make you a better decision-maker | Annie Duke (author of “Thinking in Bets” and “Quit,” former pro poker player)

alts.quote: I think with hiring, it's funny, man, there's so much hiring advice online and you read it and you're like, "Yeah, this is super obvious." And then when you live it, you're suddenly like, "Aah, this is why people say this."
alts.zh: 招人這件事很好笑，網路上一堆建議，你看的時候都覺得「這不是廢話嗎」。等你真的經歷過，才會突然懂「喔，原來大家是這個意思」。

alts.quote: That's solving a problem for the company. That's not solving a career growth issue for an individual. And I think people who want to be promoted need to think in that orientation versus the other.
alts.zh: 那是在解決公司的問題，不是在解決個人的職涯成長問題。想升遷的人要用前面那種角度思考，不是後面那種。

alts.quote: And so ever since then, we've been automating jobs and creating new jobs, and you can always see the job that's going to go away, and you don't know the new job because it doesn't exist yet.
alts.zh: 從那時候到現在，我們一直在自動化舊工作、也一直在長出新工作；而你永遠看得到那個要消失的工作，看不到新的，因為它還不存在。

cards.pattern: The good news is you can reverse that: if I'm willing to [做那件麻煩事], think about what an edge I'll have over people who aren't.
cards.quote: Now, the good news is that you can then reverse that and say if I'm willing to do it, think about what an edge I'm going to have over people who aren't willing to do it, right?
cards.zh: 好消息是這件事可以反過來看：如果我願意做，想想我對那些不願意做的人會有多大的優勢。
cards.why: 把「大家都做不到」這個壞消息，用 you can reverse that 一句翻成「所以做得到的人有超額報酬」——提案被嫌太難時最好用。
swaps: Flip it around: the fact that it's hard is the moat.
That difficulty is exactly why it's worth doing.
cards.episode: This will make you a better decision-maker | Annie Duke (author of “Thinking in Bets” and “Quit,” former pro poker player)

alts.quote: If I told you, I'm going to build an autonomous vehicle, and I said our team is 10 people, you should rightfully say, Varun, you're not serious. And you'd be right.
alts.zh: 如果我跟你說我要做自駕車，然後說團隊只有 10 個人，你完全應該回我：Varun，你不是認真的吧。而且你會是對的。

alts.quote: You've got to be convinced of the certainty that you're going to win, and you've got to be willing to shift when things aren't working.
alts.zh: 你必須確信自己一定會贏，同時也必須願意在行不通的時候馬上換路。

alts.quote: What I've found talking to people who want to start what they think is a marketplace is that they think too much about a marketplace before they're a marketplace.
alts.zh: 我跟那些想做他們自認為是媒合平台的人聊下來，發現他們在還不是平台之前，就想太多平台的事。

cards.pattern: [X] is a prospective problem, not a retrospective one — even if we treat it like a retrospective one.
cards.quote: But of course, waste is a prospective problem, not a retrospective one, even if we treat it like a retrospective one.
cards.zh: 但浪費其實是關於未來的問題，不是關於過去的問題——即使我們都當成過去的問題在處理。
cards.why: 用 prospective / retrospective 這組對照重新定義關鍵詞，直接拆掉沉沒成本論證的地基；要砍專案時殺傷力最強的一句。
swaps: The waste is what you're about to spend, not what you've spent.
Sunk is sunk — the question is forward-looking.
cards.pmNote: 沉沒成本謬誤：若今天不會啟動這個專案，繼續投入的資源才是真正的浪費。
cards.episode: This will make you a better decision-maker | Annie Duke (author of “Thinking in Bets” and “Quit,” former pro poker player)

alts.quote: Even if we had no more progress today with models, which is absolutely not the case, but even if we had no more progress, we are way behind on product.
alts.zh: 就算模型從今天起完全不再進步——當然實際上完全不是這樣——就算真的不再進步，我們在產品上還是落後一大截。

alts.quote: Sometimes product managers hesitate to “waste people’s time” in sessions about goals, but I would argue it is the most valuable time to spend together.
alts.zh: 有時候產品經理會猶豫，覺得開會談目標是在「浪費大家時間」，但我會說那是最值得一起花的時間。

alts.quote: That's solving a problem for the company. That's not solving a career growth issue for an individual. And I think people who want to be promoted need to think in that orientation versus the other.
alts.zh: 那是在解決公司的問題，不是在解決個人的職涯成長問題。想升遷的人要用前面那種角度思考，不是後面那種。

cards.pattern: Human beings are notoriously good at trading off [長期] just to feel good in [短期]. That's why we're all [日常壞習慣].
cards.quote: But human beings are notoriously good at trading off the long run just to feel good in the short run. That's why we're all eating chocolate and cupcakes and stuff that we know is bad for us because it feels good.
cards.zh: 人類非常擅長犧牲長期，只為了短期舒服。所以我們才都在吃明知不好的巧克力跟杯子蛋糕。
cards.why: 抽象主張後面立刻接一個沒人能否認的日常例子，對方就很難說「我們團隊不會這樣」。
swaps: We're wired to buy comfort now and bill it to later.
It's the same reason none of us floss.
cards.episode: This will make you a better decision-maker | Annie Duke (author of “Thinking in Bets” and “Quit,” former pro poker player)

alts.quote: He thinks that a lot of the best recruiters in the world or the companies that attract talent, they put out this distinctive bad signal and it has to turn some people off. That's the key of a good, bad signal.
alts.zh: 他認為最會吸引人才的公司，都會刻意放出一個「不討喜的訊號」，而且一定要有人被勸退。這才是好的壞訊號的重點。

alts.quote: And so ever since then, we've been automating jobs and creating new jobs, and you can always see the job that's going to go away, and you don't know the new job because it doesn't exist yet.
alts.zh: 從那時候到現在，我們一直在自動化舊工作、也一直在長出新工作；而你永遠看得到那個要消失的工作，看不到新的，因為它還不存在。

alts.quote: And just saying because dramatically boosted the percentage of the time that a person would let them cut the line. We're suckers for explanations, all of us.
alts.zh: 光是講出「因為」，別人讓他插隊的比例就大幅上升。我們每個人都吃「解釋」這一套。

cards.pattern: You don't have to be [某種專家] to see that what they're really saying is [被迴避的真相].
cards.quote: Now, you don't have to be a Russian spy to see that what they're really saying is these guys aren't working together effectively and it's a problem.
cards.zh: 你不用是俄國間諜也看得出來，他們真正在講的是：這些人沒有好好合作，而這是個問題。
cards.why: 「你不用是 X 也看得出來」既把結論說破，又不讓對方覺得被當笨蛋——揭穿粉飾說法的溫和武器。
swaps: It doesn't take an insider to see what that really means.
Read that sentence again and it says the opposite.
cards.episode: Good Strategy, Bad Strategy | Richard Rumelt

alts.quote: Now, the good news is that you can then reverse that and say if I'm willing to do it, think about what an edge I'm going to have over people who aren't willing to do it, right?
alts.zh: 好消息是這件事可以反過來看：如果我願意做，想想我對那些不願意做的人會有多大的優勢。

alts.quote: And so ever since then, we've been automating jobs and creating new jobs, and you can always see the job that's going to go away, and you don't know the new job because it doesn't exist yet.
alts.zh: 從那時候到現在，我們一直在自動化舊工作、也一直在長出新工作；而你永遠看得到那個要消失的工作，看不到新的，因為它還不存在。

alts.quote: So having a shit draft is a million times more valuable than having all these great ideas. But it's also really painful.
alts.zh: 有一份爛草稿，比手上一堆很棒的點子有價值一百萬倍。但那個過程真的很痛。

cards.pattern: [X] is not [Y], it's something else. It's [Z]. And [Z] is not [Y].
cards.quote: But abstract, high-level goals, they're not strategy, they're something else. They're ambitions. And ambitions are not a strategy.
cards.zh: 抽象的高階目標不是策略，是別的東西。那叫野心。而野心不是策略。
cards.why: 三段遞進的否定：先說「不是」、再命名、再把命名打回原點。比直接說「你這不是策略」有力得多，也不必貶低對方。
swaps: That's a target, not a plan. And a target isn't a plan.
Call it what it is: an aspiration.
cards.pmNote: 目標≠策略；策略是診斷＋指導方針＋連貫行動。
cards.episode: Good Strategy, Bad Strategy | Richard Rumelt

alts.quote: The good news is, you're just like everybody else. The bad news is, you're mediocre just like everybody else.
alts.zh: 好消息是，你跟大家一樣；壞消息是，你跟大家一樣平庸。

alts.quote: If we go up to the 30,000-foot level, what are we doing here? What's our mission? We're building a private safety net for all those who've been laid off or let go.
alts.zh: 如果拉到三萬英尺的高度看，我們到底在做什麼？我們的使命是什麼？我們在為所有被裁員的人建一張民間的安全網。

alts.quote: I don't want to spend any years of my life becoming passively okay at something.
alts.zh: 我不想花人生的任何幾年，只為了在某件事上變得「勉強還行」。

cards.pattern: Correct statement. A real diagnosis would say 'because'. We jumped immediately to 'therefore'.
cards.quote: Okay, correct statement, we're falling behind. A real diagnosis would say, because. We jumped immediately to therefore.
cards.zh: 這句話沒錯，我們的確落後了。但真正的診斷會說「因為」。我們卻直接跳到「所以」。
cards.why: 先確認對方的陳述為真（不對抗），再用 because / therefore 兩個字精準指出邏輯缺口——質疑提案時火藥味最小、殺傷力最大的講法。
swaps: That's the symptom. What's the 'because'?
We've written the 'so what' before the 'why'.
cards.pmNote: 缺乏診斷是壞策略的第一大來源。
cards.episode: Good Strategy, Bad Strategy | Richard Rumelt

alts.quote: And just saying because dramatically boosted the percentage of the time that a person would let them cut the line. We're suckers for explanations, all of us.
alts.zh: 光是講出「因為」，別人讓他插隊的比例就大幅上升。我們每個人都吃「解釋」這一套。

alts.quote: But human beings are notoriously good at trading off the long run just to feel good in the short run. That's why we're all eating chocolate and cupcakes and stuff that we know is bad for us because it feels good.
alts.zh: 人類非常擅長犧牲長期，只為了短期舒服。所以我們才都在吃明知不好的巧克力跟杯子蛋糕。

alts.quote: And I think craft is a dessert that you get after the meal of does your thing solve a real problem in the world and are people clamoring, needing it badly?
alts.zh: 我覺得「做工精緻」是甜點，前面那頓正餐是：你的東西有沒有解決世界上真實的問題、有沒有人急著要它。

cards.pattern: We want [X], but we're scared of [X 的代價]. We want [Y], but we'd like to [走捷徑的版本].
cards.quote: We want to innovate, but we're scared of insight. We want to be the first, but we'd like to pick our strategy out of a list of common strategies for being first.
cards.zh: 我們想創新，卻害怕洞見。我們想搶第一，卻想從一張常見策略清單裡挑一個來當第一。
cards.why: 平行對句把「想要的」跟「不願付的代價」擺進同一句，逼對方自己看見矛盾，比直接指責有效得多。
swaps: We want the outcome without the uncomfortable part.
We say 'bold' and then ask for the template.
cards.episode: Good Strategy, Bad Strategy | Richard Rumelt

alts.quote: The most common mistake people make is they think through the probability first without actually forcing themselves to think through the potential.
alts.zh: 大家最常犯的錯，是先想「成功機率」，卻沒有逼自己先想「這件事最大能長成什麼樣」。

alts.quote: But the thing that I would argue folks that build really big companies have in common is they just really want it and they really believe in themselves and they really believe they can make it work.
alts.zh: 但我會說，那些做出真正大公司的人共通點是：他們就是非常想要，他們真的相信自己，也真的相信自己能做成。

alts.quote: In a world where it's easier to build things, it's more important to make sure that your time is spent figuring out what you should be building in the first place.
alts.zh: 在一個「東西越來越好做」的世界裡，更重要的是先確保你把時間花在想清楚「到底該做什麼」。

cards.pattern: It doesn't make any sense to [自相矛盾的做法]. And yet, people do it.
cards.quote: It doesn't make any sense to do things that are self-contradictory. And yet, people do it.
cards.zh: 做互相打架的事情根本說不通。但大家還是照做。
cards.why: And yet, people do it. 這種短句收尾，把批評從針對「你」變成針對「一種普遍現象」，對方比較不會豎起防衛。
swaps: On paper nobody would defend that. In practice we all do it.
It's obviously incoherent — and it's everywhere.
cards.pmNote: 連貫行動：策略裡的行動不該互相抵銷。
cards.episode: Good Strategy, Bad Strategy | Richard Rumelt

alts.quote: In a world where it's easier to build things, it's more important to make sure that your time is spent figuring out what you should be building in the first place.
alts.zh: 在一個「東西越來越好做」的世界裡，更重要的是先確保你把時間花在想清楚「到底該做什麼」。

alts.quote: And so ever since then, we've been automating jobs and creating new jobs, and you can always see the job that's going to go away, and you don't know the new job because it doesn't exist yet.
alts.zh: 從那時候到現在，我們一直在自動化舊工作、也一直在長出新工作；而你永遠看得到那個要消失的工作，看不到新的，因為它還不存在。

alts.quote: The most common mistake people make is they think through the probability first without actually forcing themselves to think through the potential.
alts.zh: 大家最常犯的錯，是先想「成功機率」，卻沒有逼自己先想「這件事最大能長成什麼樣」。

cards.pattern: You've got to be of two minds: convinced you're going to win, and willing to shift when things aren't working.
cards.quote: You've got to be convinced of the certainty that you're going to win, and you've got to be willing to shift when things aren't working.
cards.zh: 你必須確信自己一定會贏，同時也必須願意在行不通的時候馬上換路。
cards.why: 用「同時抱著兩種心態」把看似矛盾的兩個要求包成一種能力，避免被質疑「你到底是要堅持還是要轉彎」。
swaps: Hold both: total conviction and zero attachment.
Commit like you're right, listen like you're wrong.
cards.episode: Good Strategy, Bad Strategy | Richard Rumelt

alts.quote: Now, the good news is that you can then reverse that and say if I'm willing to do it, think about what an edge I'm going to have over people who aren't willing to do it, right?
alts.zh: 好消息是這件事可以反過來看：如果我願意做，想想我對那些不願意做的人會有多大的優勢。

alts.quote: If I told you, I'm going to build an autonomous vehicle, and I said our team is 10 people, you should rightfully say, Varun, you're not serious. And you'd be right.
alts.zh: 如果我跟你說我要做自駕車，然後說團隊只有 10 個人，你完全應該回我：Varun，你不是認真的吧。而且你會是對的。

alts.quote: So I think if you take all those steps back and you look at this from a journey perspective, there's no way that it won't be impacting search. It's just going to be hard to find.
alts.zh: 所以我覺得，只要你退開幾步、用「使用者旅程」的角度看，它不可能不影響搜尋。只是那個影響很難被指認出來。

cards.pattern: If you do [便宜的預防動作] right, you will not have to do an ugly [昂貴的補救動作].
cards.quote: And the way I describe a pre-mortem is that if you do a pre-mortem right, you will not have to do an ugly post-mortem.
cards.zh: 我都這樣講事前檢討：事前做對了，你就不必做那種很難看的事後檢討。
cards.why: 用「很難看的事後檢討」這個大家都痛過的畫面當代價，一句話完成成本效益論證。
swaps: An hour now buys you a week of cleanup later.
Pay for it in planning or pay for it in postmortems.
cards.pmNote: pre-mortem：專案啟動前假設它已失敗，反推失敗原因。
cards.episode: 4 questions Shreyas Doshi wishes he’d asked himself sooner | Former PM leader at Stripe, Twitter, Google

alts.quote: So the way that I'm supposed to talk about my ideas is to convey why I believe what I do, not to convince anybody that I'm right.
alts.zh: 我談我的想法，是要傳達我為什麼這樣相信，不是要說服誰我是對的。

alts.quote: What's interesting is that Silicon Valley has found a way to make the most profitable style of business the least profitable.
alts.zh: 有趣的是，矽谷居然有辦法把全世界最好賺的生意做成最不賺錢的生意。

alts.quote: And again, everything I've just described, by the way, is just a very straightforward extrapolation of very basic economics. I'm not making any bold predictions of what I just said.
alts.zh: 我剛剛講的這一整串，其實只是最基本的經濟學往下推而已。我沒有在做什麼大膽預測。

cards.quote: So that's why I'm a huge fan of pre-mortems is, it's one of those very low downside, but very high upside things that I've experienced.
cards.zh: 所以我超推事前檢討：它就是那種下檔風險很低、上檔空間很大的做法。
cards.why: low downside, high upside 是英文提案裡最省力的一句總結，直接處理「萬一沒用怎麼辦」這個沒說出口的反對。
swaps: Cheap to try, expensive to skip.
The worst case is we lose an hour.
cards.episode: 4 questions Shreyas Doshi wishes he’d asked himself sooner | Former PM leader at Stripe, Twitter, Google

alts.quote: In a world where it's easier to build things, it's more important to make sure that your time is spent figuring out what you should be building in the first place.
alts.zh: 在一個「東西越來越好做」的世界裡，更重要的是先確保你把時間花在想清楚「到底該做什麼」。

alts.quote: I'm just trying to argue this advice applied to a startup that's too early is actively not helpful.
alts.zh: 我只是想主張：把這套建議套在太早期的新創身上，是「主動有害」而不只是沒用。

alts.quote: And again, everything I've just described, by the way, is just a very straightforward extrapolation of very basic economics. I'm not making any bold predictions of what I just said.
alts.zh: 我剛剛講的這一整串，其實只是最基本的經濟學往下推而已。我沒有在做什麼大膽預測。

cards.pattern: We litigate the minutiae of [眼前的爭點], but we never recognize it's because we're thinking at different levels.
cards.quote: We litigate the minutiae of whatever issue we are discussing, but we never really recognize that it's because we are default thinking at different levels.
cards.zh: 我們一直在爭論眼前議題的枝微末節，卻沒發現真正的原因是雙方預設站在不同層次上。
cards.why: litigate the minutiae 把「一直吵細節」講得精準又不帶人身攻擊；後半把衝突歸因到結構而非個人，是拆解僵局的標準句。
swaps: We're arguing details when the disagreement is one level up.
We keep debating the 'how' while they're asking about the 'so what'.
cards.pmNote: 產品工作三層次：impact / execution / optics。衝突常來自雙方預設層次不同。
cards.episode: 4 questions Shreyas Doshi wishes he’d asked himself sooner | Former PM leader at Stripe, Twitter, Google

alts.quote: I would argue that the one thing AI can never have is agency because it doesn't have human motivations.
alts.zh: 我會說 AI 唯一永遠不會有的東西是能動性，因為它沒有人的動機。

alts.quote: In a world where it's easier to build things, it's more important to make sure that your time is spent figuring out what you should be building in the first place.
alts.zh: 在一個「東西越來越好做」的世界裡，更重要的是先確保你把時間花在想清楚「到底該做什麼」。

alts.quote: And if you don't have them on your growth roadmap, you are going to be in some really big trouble over the next year to two years because your cost of acquisition is only going to go up.
alts.zh: 如果你的成長路線圖上沒有這些東西，未來一到兩年你會陷入大麻煩，因為你的獲客成本只會一路往上。

cards.pattern: They don't care about [虛榮指標], they don't care about [另一個虛榮指標]. What they care about is [真正的體驗].
cards.quote: Customers don't care how big you are, they don't care how many transactions you've accumulated. What they care about is when they have a transaction with you, how happy do you make them?
cards.zh: 客戶不在乎你多大，也不在乎你累積了多少筆交易。他們在乎的是：這一次交易，你讓他多開心。
cards.why: 兩次否定先累積壓力，再用 What they care about is 翻轉到你要的重點——把討論從規模拉回體驗的標準句型。
swaps: Scale isn't the promise. The experience is.
None of that shows up in the customer's day.
cards.pmNote: happy GMV：只有帶來留存的交易額才算數。
cards.episode: The hierarchy of engagement | Sarah Tavel (Benchmark, Greylock, Pinterest)

alts.quote: And if you don't have them on your growth roadmap, you are going to be in some really big trouble over the next year to two years because your cost of acquisition is only going to go up.
alts.zh: 如果你的成長路線圖上沒有這些東西，未來一到兩年你會陷入大麻煩，因為你的獲客成本只會一路往上。

alts.quote: But the thing that I would argue folks that build really big companies have in common is they just really want it and they really believe in themselves and they really believe they can make it work.
alts.zh: 但我會說，那些做出真正大公司的人共通點是：他們就是非常想要，他們真的相信自己，也真的相信自己能做成。

alts.quote: In a world where it's easier to build things, it's more important to make sure that your time is spent figuring out what you should be building in the first place.
alts.zh: 在一個「東西越來越好做」的世界裡，更重要的是先確保你把時間花在想清楚「到底該做什麼」。

cards.pattern: [做法 A] is a lot harder, takes longer, but it's actually the path to [真正想要的結果].
cards.quote: And getting to $1,000,000 of GMV in a constrained market is a lot harder, takes longer, but it's actually the path to building something that endures.
cards.zh: 在一個受限的市場裡做到一百萬 GMV 難很多、也慢很多，但那才是真正做出能長久的東西的路。
cards.why: 主動把代價先講完（harder, takes longer），對方就沒東西可以反駁；最後一個 but 把代價轉成信任。
swaps: Slower on paper, faster to something real.
It costs more up front and it's the only version that compounds.
cards.episode: The hierarchy of engagement | Sarah Tavel (Benchmark, Greylock, Pinterest)

alts.quote: How big is the market opportunity to rewrite the software world order? It's trillions of dollars, or something, right? The world runs on software.
alts.zh: 重寫整個軟體世界秩序的市場機會有多大？大概是好幾兆美金吧。這個世界是靠軟體在跑的。

alts.quote: In a world where it's easier to build things, it's more important to make sure that your time is spent figuring out what you should be building in the first place.
alts.zh: 在一個「東西越來越好做」的世界裡，更重要的是先確保你把時間花在想清楚「到底該做什麼」。

alts.quote: If we go up to the 30,000-foot level, what are we doing here? What's our mission? We're building a private safety net for all those who've been laid off or let go.
alts.zh: 如果拉到三萬英尺的高度看，我們到底在做什麼？我們的使命是什麼？我們在為所有被裁員的人建一張民間的安全網。

cards.pattern: There really isn't a playbook — [每個案例都必須不同]. But there are first principles that they all share.
cards.quote: There really isn't a playbook. Every company, the ones that succeed have to be fundamentally different from anything that was before it. But there are these first principles of the ingredients that they all share.
cards.zh: 其實沒有什麼標準流程。真正成功的公司，本質上都必須跟前面所有人不一樣。但它們共有的基本要素是存在的。
cards.why: 先大方承認「沒有萬用解法」，再把自己的框架降級成「共通成分」——大幅降低被質疑「你這套哪來的普遍性」的風險。
swaps: No template survives contact with a real company — but the ingredients repeat.
You can't copy the plan; you can copy the constraints.
cards.episode: The hierarchy of engagement | Sarah Tavel (Benchmark, Greylock, Pinterest)

alts.quote: And the third thing is that I really believe that... I don't believe. I think we all know at this point that the most important thing for the growth of anything tech is retention.
alts.zh: 第三件事是我真的相信——不，不是相信。我覺得到這個時間點大家都已經知道了：科技產品成長最重要的就是留存。

alts.quote: So having a shit draft is a million times more valuable than having all these great ideas. But it's also really painful.
alts.zh: 有一份爛草稿，比手上一堆很棒的點子有價值一百萬倍。但那個過程真的很痛。

alts.quote: As an entrepreneur, a company, you actually don't have a choice whether you'll have a pricing conversation with your customer. The only thing in your control is when you will have it.
alts.zh: 身為創業者或公司，你其實沒有「要不要跟客戶談價格」的選擇權。你唯一能控制的是「什麼時候談」。

cards.pattern: I would underline it even — we get excited about [別人認為是缺點的東西].
cards.quote: I would underline it even, which is that we get excited about the markets, the opportunities, that might seem small from the outside.
cards.zh: 我甚至要再加重語氣：那些從外面看起來很小的市場、很小的機會，我們反而會興奮。
cards.why: 對方把你的立場講得比較溫和時，用 I would underline it even 主動加碼，比澄清更有力，也讓你的差異化立場更清楚。
swaps: I'd go further than that.
Not just tolerate it — we look for it.
cards.pmNote: 被低估的小市場通常沒有競爭，反而更容易 tip。
cards.episode: The hierarchy of engagement | Sarah Tavel (Benchmark, Greylock, Pinterest)

alts.quote: Even if we had no more progress today with models, which is absolutely not the case, but even if we had no more progress, we are way behind on product.
alts.zh: 就算模型從今天起完全不再進步——當然實際上完全不是這樣——就算真的不再進步，我們在產品上還是落後一大截。

alts.quote: I would argue in retrospect, absolutely, yes, there were opportunities that were left on the table, but in early days you leave good opportunities because you have to focus on other things.
alts.zh: 回頭看我會說，沒錯，確實有些機會被放掉了，但早期你就是會放掉好機會，因為你必須專注在別的事情上。

alts.quote: Small is not just a stepping stone, small is a great destination itself.
alts.zh: 「小」不只是通往別處的墊腳石，「小」本身就是一個很好的終點。

cards.pattern: It went from about a [50%] hit rate to [65]. That's a really big difference.
cards.quote: And in that case, it was from about a 50% hit rate to 65. So that's pretty huge, so that's a really big difference.
cards.zh: 那個案例是命中率從大約 50% 提到 65%。這個差距其實非常大。
cards.why: 給區間變化而不是單一數字，再自己補一句「這差距很大」替聽者解讀——不要假設對方會自動覺得你的數字了不起。
swaps: That's a fifteen-point move on a coin flip.
In a noisy domain, that's an enormous lift.
cards.pmNote: 結構化面試流程能顯著提高招募命中率（Kahneman 的研究）。
cards.episode: This will make you a better decision-maker | Annie Duke (author of “Thinking in Bets” and “Quit,” former pro poker player)

alts.quote: That's one out of 10, that's a 10% win rate.
alts.zh: 那就是十次成一次，也就是 10% 的成交率。

alts.quote: I think people don't realize that there's a big difference between moving from 80% performance to 90% performance to 99% performance to 99.9% performance, and so on, and so on.
alts.zh: 我覺得大家沒意識到，從 80% 做到 90%、再到 99%、再到 99.9%，這幾段之間的差距有多大。

alts.quote: They tend to have accomplished very difficult goals in very hostile environments. And it turns out that when you're starting a somewhat chaotic tech company, that's actually a very useful skill to have.
alts.zh: 這些人習慣在極度不友善的環境裡把很難的目標做出來。結果發現，開一家有點混亂的科技公司，這剛好是非常有用的能力。

cards.pattern: Have you ever had [結果 Y] that did not [前置條件 X]? And the answer is no.
cards.quote: But have you ever had a company that exited for more than a billion dollars that did not fund at Series A? And the answer is no.
cards.zh: 你有看過哪家出場超過十億、卻沒募到 A 輪的公司嗎？答案是沒有。
cards.why: 把資料整理成一個對方會自己去搜尋記憶的反問句，再由你補上答案——比直接丟統計數字更難反駁。
swaps: Name one that skipped that step.
I've never seen a case where that wasn't true.
cards.pmNote: 先行指標：找出與最終結果高度相關、但更早可觀測的事件。
cards.episode: This will make you a better decision-maker | Annie Duke (author of “Thinking in Bets” and “Quit,” former pro poker player)

alts.quote: Data is more like a compass than a GPS. If you look at data as a way of giving you the answer, you're always wrong. Wrong or slow, or sometimes both.
alts.zh: 數據比較像指南針，不是導航。如果你把數據當成會給你答案的東西，你不是錯就是慢，有時候兩者都有。

alts.quote: Never ever once have I seen a rebrand or redesign, especially of a marketing site, produce good performance results.
alts.zh: 我從來、一次都沒看過品牌重塑或改版——尤其是行銷官網——帶來好的成效數字。

alts.quote: And my first question to him as a product guy is like, "Wow, would you give me a million dollars to solve this problem?"
alts.zh: 身為做產品的人，我第一個問題是：「哇，那你願意花一百萬美元讓我解掉這個問題嗎？」

cards.pattern: If you say '[你的估計]' and I was thinking [很不同的估計], you're never going to hear [我的估計] from me. Ever.
cards.quote: If you say, 'I think this is going to take three months to launch' and I was thinking four weeks, you're never going to hear four weeks from me, ever.
cards.zh: 如果你說「我覺得要三個月」，而我原本想的是四週，那你永遠不會從我嘴裡聽到四週。永遠不會。
cards.why: 用第二人稱的具體場景當證據，把「資深的人會壓縮意見」這種抽象主張變成對方能在腦中重播的畫面；結尾單字句 Ever. 加重。
swaps: Once you've anchored, my number quietly moves to yours.
You'll never find out what I actually thought.
cards.pmNote: 錨定效應：先公開的估計會壓縮團隊真實意見的分佈，估時應先獨立收集。
cards.episode: This will make you a better decision-maker | Annie Duke (author of “Thinking in Bets” and “Quit,” former pro poker player)

alts.quote: He had gotten a quote from an agency for this, it was going to be 30 grand, and take six months. He had done in three weeks, and I think he spent 300 bucks on Bolt for the thing.
alts.zh: 他之前跟外包公司報價，要三萬美金、做六個月。結果他三個星期就做完了，在 Bolt 上大概花了三百塊美金。

alts.quote: The basic principle with laser is that willpower is never going to win, and there's great research on this, but for now just trust me, you're not going to white-knuckle your way through not looking at Twitter when you're trying to work.
alts.zh: laser 的基本原理是：意志力永遠贏不了。這方面有很多很好的研究，但現在你先信我——你不可能靠硬撐來讓自己工作時不看 Twitter。

alts.quote: In investors, it's 1%. Not one third, 1%. So you're going to hear a hundred times no until you hear one yes.
alts.zh: 在投資人這邊，是 1%。不是三分之一，是 1%。所以你會聽到一百次「不」，才會聽到一次「好」。

cards.pattern: As [權威] put it, most people won't [做 X] until it actually isn't a decision.
cards.quote: So as Richard Thaler put it, most people won't quit until it actually isn't a decision.
cards.zh: 就像 Richard Thaler 說的：大多數人要等到那已經不算一個選擇了，才會放手。
cards.why: As X put it 借權威，但真正的重點是那句話本身可以被複誦——引用時要挑「一句能記住的公式」，不是整段論文。
swaps: By the time they act, there was nothing left to decide.
People quit when quitting stops being optional.
cards.episode: This will make you a better decision-maker | Annie Duke (author of “Thinking in Bets” and “Quit,” former pro poker player)

alts.quote: They didn't actually put user acquisition spend behind TikTok until they had a product that was retentive, and then they know that they really wanted to maximize that. But every other social product has grown organically.
alts.zh: 他們是等到產品真的留得住人，才把獲客預算砸到 TikTok 上，然後才想把它極大化。但其他所有社群產品都是有機長出來的。

alts.quote: I think Peter Thiel actually says it more simply and elegantly, which is, 'You need to be right about something that other people think you're wrong about for a very long time.'
alts.zh: 我覺得 Peter Thiel 講得更簡潔漂亮：「你得在一件別人認為你錯的事情上，長時間地正確。」

alts.quote: The ultimate definition for me today of the love that somebody has for our product is they're willing to put their reputation on the line by telling people about it.
alts.zh: 對我來說，一個人有多愛你的產品，最終極的定義就是：他願意拿自己的名聲去替你背書，主動跟別人講。

cards.pattern: What you don't learn in school is [一個會翻轉評價的具體數字].
cards.quote: What you don't learn in school is he dropped the cost of a gallon of kerosene from $1 to 10 cents.
cards.zh: 學校不會教你的是：他把一加侖煤油的價格從一美元砍到十美分。
cards.why: 用「大家沒學到的那一個數字」推翻既定印象，比爭論立場有效；一個數量級的落差自己會說話。
swaps: The part that never makes the textbook is the number.
Everyone quotes the label; almost no one quotes the price curve.
cards.episode: Good Strategy, Bad Strategy | Richard Rumelt

alts.quote: It's about saying, okay, if we have these themes of stuff that we want to work on, what do we know with confidence because the data tells us and what do we need to understand because we don't have the data?
alts.zh: 重點是要問：在我們想做的這些主題裡，哪些是數據講得夠清楚、我們有把握的？哪些是因為沒數據，所以還得先搞懂的？

alts.quote: If you think about your last all hands, the last talk you saw, you probably don't remember much. In fact, I wager you might only remember one thing from that talk.
alts.zh: 回想你上一次的全員大會、上一場你聽的演講——你大概記不得多少。老實說，我敢賭你只記得一件事。

alts.quote: So to be clear, I don't explicitly see quantitative numbers around this.
alts.zh: 先講清楚，我並沒有真的看到這方面的量化數字。

cards.pattern: There's a [出處] saying that I like that says, '[一句格言]'.
cards.quote: There's an Arab saying that I like that says, 'He who forecasts the future lies, even if he tells the truth.'
cards.zh: 我很喜歡一句阿拉伯諺語：「預測未來的人是在說謊，即使他說的是實話。」
cards.why: 引諺語是承認不確定性又不顯得懦弱的低成本方式；加上 that I like 會讓引用變成個人立場，而不是賣弄。
swaps: There's a line I keep coming back to:
Someone put it better than I can:
cards.episode: Good Strategy, Bad Strategy | Richard Rumelt

alts.quote: It's about saying, okay, if we have these themes of stuff that we want to work on, what do we know with confidence because the data tells us and what do we need to understand because we don't have the data?
alts.zh: 重點是要問：在我們想做的這些主題裡，哪些是數據講得夠清楚、我們有把握的？哪些是因為沒數據，所以還得先搞懂的？

alts.quote: I mean there's not even a 100 million VMs to rent, on the planet. But there are a billion devices that you can run this stuff on.
alts.zh: 地球上根本租不到一億台虛擬機。但可以跑這些東西的裝置有十億台。

alts.quote: I'll caveat this by saying everyone's just figuring it out and it's a lot harder to figure it out when you're a larger organization than when you're much smaller and you get to run something yourself and there's pros and cons to both.
alts.zh: 我先加個但書：大家都還在摸索，而且組織越大越難摸索，比不上小團隊自己說了算——兩邊各有優缺點。

cards.pattern: There isn't a science of [X]. It's not like physics. It's not like [工程] where you can [寫下方程式].
cards.quote: It's very hard to think strategically about the situation you're in because there isn't a science of strategy. It's not like physics. It's not like engineering where we can write down the equations of stress on a beam.
cards.zh: 要對你所處的情況做策略思考很難，因為策略沒有一門科學。它不像物理。也不像工程——工程可以直接寫下樑的應力方程式。
cards.why: 用兩個「不像什麼」界定自己主張的證據標準，預先擋掉「你有沒有數據」這種質疑，同時說明為什麼得靠案例與歷史。
swaps: There's no closed-form solution here.
We're reasoning by analogy, not by formula — and that's the honest version.
cards.episode: Good Strategy, Bad Strategy | Richard Rumelt

alts.quote: I like Sean Ellis's question of how disappointed would you be if this product disappeared? And I think it's if you have at least 40% of people respond that they'd be very disappointed, then you're on the right track.
alts.zh: 我喜歡 Sean Ellis 那一題：如果這個產品消失了，你會有多失望？如果至少 40% 的人回答「非常失望」，那你方向就是對的。

alts.quote: I'll caveat this by saying everyone's just figuring it out and it's a lot harder to figure it out when you're a larger organization than when you're much smaller and you get to run something yourself and there's pros and cons to both.
alts.zh: 我先加個但書：大家都還在摸索，而且組織越大越難摸索，比不上小團隊自己說了算——兩邊各有優缺點。

alts.quote: Companies I've invested in is a long list, and I love to give you names of companies that don't exist anymore because it's self-serving and a horrible survivorship bias to just list the good ones.
alts.zh: 我投資過的公司名單很長，我很願意告訴你那些已經倒掉的公司名字——因為只列出成功的那些，是自利、也是很糟的倖存者偏誤。

cards.pattern: A sure-fire way of identifying [真正的病因] is when you put on a bandaid and the bandaid falls.
cards.quote: Now what tells me if something is seemingly an execution problem but not actually an execution problem, a sure fire way of identifying those is when you put on a bandaid and the bandaid falls.
cards.zh: 要判斷一件事表面上是執行問題、其實不是，最準的辨識法就是：你貼了 OK 繃，OK 繃掉了。
cards.why: 給對方一個可以自己驗證的判準，而不是要求他相信你；a sure-fire way of identifying 是把主觀判斷包裝成方法的句型。
swaps: If the same fix keeps unfixing itself, it wasn't the problem.
The tell is the recurrence, not the incident.
cards.pmNote: 反覆出現的執行問題，多半是策略、文化或人際問題的症狀。
cards.episode: 4 questions Shreyas Doshi wishes he’d asked himself sooner | Former PM leader at Stripe, Twitter, Google

alts.quote: They didn't actually put user acquisition spend behind TikTok until they had a product that was retentive, and then they know that they really wanted to maximize that. But every other social product has grown organically.
alts.zh: 他們是等到產品真的留得住人，才把獲客預算砸到 TikTok 上，然後才想把它極大化。但其他所有社群產品都是有機長出來的。

alts.quote: The basic principle with laser is that willpower is never going to win, and there's great research on this, but for now just trust me, you're not going to white-knuckle your way through not looking at Twitter when you're trying to work.
alts.zh: laser 的基本原理是：意志力永遠贏不了。這方面有很多很好的研究，但現在你先信我——你不可能靠硬撐來讓自己工作時不看 Twitter。

alts.quote: I have custom software that I've written that will say, 'Okay, here are the points at which the audience laughed.' Actually audibly laughed. That's the only way it counts.
alts.zh: 我自己寫了一套軟體，會告訴我「聽眾在哪些點笑了」。是真的出聲笑。只有出聲才算。

cards.pattern: When it's a ratio and you decrease the denominator, the value grows — so what we end up doing is [可預測的壞行為].
cards.quote: So when it's a ratio and you decrease the denominator, the value of the ratio grows. And so, how do you decrease the denominator in this case where time is the denominator is you start working on things that take less time.
cards.zh: 這是一個比值，分母變小，比值就變大。那在這裡分母是時間，你要怎麼讓分母變小？你就開始挑那些花比較少時間的事情做。
cards.why: 用「公式→機制→可預測行為」三步，把一個看起來是人的問題證明成制度必然的結果，對方就不需要替自己辯護。
swaps: The metric rewards speed, so speed is what you get.
Put time in the denominator and you've designed a quick-win machine.
cards.pmNote: 高槓桿角色應以「最小化機會成本」而非「正 ROI」做優先排序。
cards.episode: 4 questions Shreyas Doshi wishes he’d asked himself sooner | Former PM leader at Stripe, Twitter, Google

alts.quote: If you're solving literally for that ratio of laughs per minute, there are two ways to improve it. One is to add more laughs. Two is to decrease the number of words between laughs.
alts.zh: 如果你真的在解「每分鐘笑聲數」這個比值，只有兩種改法。一是增加笑點，二是減少笑點之間的字數。

alts.quote: But you should know when it's a vanity metric versus is this core to our growth engine? If this number goes up, does it mean the product is working?
alts.zh: 但你要分得出來：這是虛榮指標，還是我們成長引擎的核心？如果這個數字上升，代表產品真的成立了嗎？

alts.quote: Obviously in this case, it worked out great and there's survivorship bias and that doesn't mean that everyone should pivot all the time.
alts.zh: 當然這個案例後來結果很好，但這裡有倖存者偏誤，不代表每個人都該一直轉型。

cards.pattern: There was this unwritten rule of thumb that if it's not going to [達到門檻], it's not worth talking about.
cards.quote: There was this unwritten rule of thumb that, hey, if it's not going to generate more than $100 million in revenue, it's not worth talking about it.
cards.zh: 當時有一條沒寫下來的潛規則：如果一件事帶不來一億美金以上的營收，就不值得拿出來討論。
cards.why: 用「潛規則」當證據比引用政策更有說服力，因為它證明的是文化而不是文件；具體門檻數字讓「想得夠大」變得可操作。
swaps: Nobody wrote it down, but everyone knew the bar.
The unspoken filter was a number.
cards.episode: 4 questions Shreyas Doshi wishes he’d asked himself sooner | Former PM leader at Stripe, Twitter, Google

alts.quote: If you tell someone, 'This is the problem I'm going to address,' and they will tell you, 'Oh, I know someone that has this problem,' it's not a real problem.
alts.zh: 如果你跟人說「這是我要解決的問題」，對方回你「喔，我知道有誰有這個問題」——那它就不是真問題。

alts.quote: I mean there's not even a 100 million VMs to rent, on the planet. But there are a billion devices that you can run this stuff on.
alts.zh: 地球上根本租不到一億台虛擬機。但可以跑這些東西的裝置有十億台。

alts.quote: And it's not bad because it's not well-intentioned, but it's bad because it's not contextual.
alts.zh: 它不好，不是因為對方沒有善意，而是因為它沒有考慮你的處境。

cards.pattern: The test for me of whether [X 成立] is [兩個可觀察的判準].
cards.quote: The test for me, of whether you're building a product that has the ingredients to create a retentive product on a micro level, just at the user level, is that the product should get better the more you use it, and you'll have more to lose by leaving it.
cards.zh: 我判斷一個產品有沒有留存體質的標準是：用得越多它越好用，而且你越難離開它。
cards.why: The test for me is… 把個人判斷公開成一條可檢驗的標準，別人可以反駁標準而不是反駁你——把主觀意見升級成證據的句型。
swaps: My bar is simple:
Here's the check I run:
cards.pmNote: 留存體質＝accruing benefits（越用越好）＋ mounting loss（越難離開）。
cards.episode: The hierarchy of engagement | Sarah Tavel (Benchmark, Greylock, Pinterest)

alts.quote: The true test of whether the positioning's working is, if I'm sitting across from a qualified prospect and I tell the story, does the prospect get excited and want to buy something?
alts.zh: 定位有沒有效，真正的檢驗是：我坐在一個合格的潛在客戶對面把故事講完，他會不會眼睛一亮、想買東西？

alts.quote: Data is more like a compass than a GPS. If you look at data as a way of giving you the answer, you're always wrong. Wrong or slow, or sometimes both.
alts.zh: 數據比較像指南針，不是導航。如果你把數據當成會給你答案的東西，你不是錯就是慢，有時候兩者都有。

alts.quote: The basic principle with laser is that willpower is never going to win, and there's great research on this, but for now just trust me, you're not going to white-knuckle your way through not looking at Twitter when you're trying to work.
alts.zh: laser 的基本原理是：意志力永遠贏不了。這方面有很多很好的研究，但現在你先信我——你不可能靠硬撐來讓自己工作時不看 Twitter。

cards.pattern: I like [替代方法] — if at least [門檻數字], then you're on the right track.
cards.quote: I like Sean Ellis's question of how disappointed would you be if this product disappeared? And I think it's if you have at least 40% of people respond that they'd be very disappointed, then you're on the right track.
cards.zh: 我喜歡 Sean Ellis 那一題：如果這個產品消失了，你會有多失望？如果至少 40% 的人回答「非常失望」，那你方向就是對的。
cards.why: 否定一個常用指標時，一定要立刻給出替代方法和門檻值，否則會被當成純唱衰；then you're on the right track 是很輕的下結論方式。
swaps: Forget the score; ask the disappearance question.
The number I'd watch instead is:
cards.pmNote: Sean Ellis PMF 測試：≥40% 回答「非常失望」通常代表已達 product-market fit。
cards.episode: The hierarchy of engagement | Sarah Tavel (Benchmark, Greylock, Pinterest)

alts.quote: I think Peter Thiel actually says it more simply and elegantly, which is, 'You need to be right about something that other people think you're wrong about for a very long time.'
alts.zh: 我覺得 Peter Thiel 講得更簡潔漂亮：「你得在一件別人認為你錯的事情上，長時間地正確。」

alts.quote: I ran the question and it came back at only 7% of users saying they'd be very disappointed without the product.
alts.zh: 我把那個問題丟出去問，結果回來只有 7% 的使用者說「沒有這個產品會非常失望」。

alts.quote: It's very hard to think strategically about the situation you're in because there isn't a science of strategy. It's not like physics. It's not like engineering where we can write down the equations of stress on a beam.
alts.zh: 要對你所處的情況做策略思考很難，因為策略沒有一門科學。它不像物理。也不像工程——工程可以直接寫下樑的應力方程式。

cards.pattern: They didn't do [砸錢] until [前提成立]. But every other [類別] has [常規].
cards.quote: They didn't actually put user acquisition spend behind TikTok until they had a product that was retentive, and then they know that they really wanted to maximize that. But every other social product has grown organically.
cards.zh: 他們是等到產品真的留得住人，才把獲客預算砸到 TikTok 上，然後才想把它極大化。但其他所有社群產品都是有機長出來的。
cards.why: 主動舉出唯一的反例、再把它框成例外，等於先把對方最強的反駁拿走，剩下的規則就更站得住。
swaps: There's exactly one exception, and it proves the shape of the rule.
One company bought its way there. Everyone else earned it.
cards.episode: The hierarchy of engagement | Sarah Tavel (Benchmark, Greylock, Pinterest)

alts.quote: So as Richard Thaler put it, most people won't quit until it actually isn't a decision.
alts.zh: 就像 Richard Thaler 說的：大多數人要等到那已經不算一個選擇了，才會放手。

alts.quote: The ultimate definition for me today of the love that somebody has for our product is they're willing to put their reputation on the line by telling people about it.
alts.zh: 對我來說，一個人有多愛你的產品，最終極的定義就是：他願意拿自己的名聲去替你背書，主動跟別人講。

alts.quote: Now what tells me if something is seemingly an execution problem but not actually an execution problem, a sure fire way of identifying those is when you put on a bandaid and the bandaid falls.
alts.zh: 要判斷一件事表面上是執行問題、其實不是，最準的辨識法就是：你貼了 OK 繃，OK 繃掉了。

cards.pattern: Whether [X] has [小數字] or [大數字], it probably doesn't really change the experience for [使用者].
cards.quote: Whether Mechanical Turk has a hundred thousand Turkers or 5 million Turkers, it probably doesn't really change the experience for somebody who is using Mechanical Turk.
cards.zh: 不管 Mechanical Turk 上面有十萬個工人還是五百萬個，對使用的人來說體驗大概都一樣。
cards.why: 把數量拉到兩個極端來證明「量不是關鍵變數」——不需要任何資料就能完成的推論，資料不足時特別好用。
swaps: Ten times the supply, same experience — that tells you something.
If doubling it changes nothing, it isn't the lever.
cards.pmNote: 供給同質化的市集不會因為供給變多而變強，也就不容易 tip。
cards.episode: The hierarchy of engagement | Sarah Tavel (Benchmark, Greylock, Pinterest)

alts.quote: The ultimate definition for me today of the love that somebody has for our product is they're willing to put their reputation on the line by telling people about it.
alts.zh: 對我來說，一個人有多愛你的產品，最終極的定義就是：他願意拿自己的名聲去替你背書，主動跟別人講。

alts.quote: Whenever you talk to people who are at the company, they're always try to tell you the best version of the company. It's on you to triangulate that information, but you need both sides.
alts.zh: 你去問還在公司裡的人，他們永遠給你公司最好的那個版本。要交叉比對是你自己的責任，但兩邊的說法你都得聽到。

alts.quote: It turns out that 87% of buyers in our two and a half million sales calls we studied, either showed moderate or high levels of indecision.
alts.zh: 結果是，我們研究的兩百五十萬通銷售電話裡，有 87% 的買家表現出中度或高度的猶豫。

cards.pattern: I can't tell you how many times I [看到某現象] and [對方居然沒做過那件事].
cards.quote: Number one is actually measuring it. I can't tell you how many times I suggest to a founder to track cohorts and that's a new thing.
cards.zh: 第一件事其實是去量它。我真的數不清有多少次我建議創辦人追蹤 cohort，結果那對他們是全新的東西。
cards.why: 「我數不清有多少次」是把個人經驗轉成頻率證據的自然講法，在沒有統計資料時最實用。
swaps: More often than you'd think, the answer is 'we don't measure it'.
Nine times out of ten it's the first time anyone's asked.
cards.episode: The hierarchy of engagement | Sarah Tavel (Benchmark, Greylock, Pinterest)

alts.quote: You could have all the usage data in the world, that's going to tell you what's actually happening in your product, but it doesn't tell you why.
alts.zh: 就算你握有全世界的使用數據，它只會告訴你產品裡實際發生了什麼，不會告訴你為什麼。

alts.quote: They tend to have accomplished very difficult goals in very hostile environments. And it turns out that when you're starting a somewhat chaotic tech company, that's actually a very useful skill to have.
alts.zh: 這些人習慣在極度不友善的環境裡把很難的目標做出來。結果發現，開一家有點混亂的科技公司，這剛好是非常有用的能力。

alts.quote: I have custom software that I've written that will say, 'Okay, here are the points at which the audience laughed.' Actually audibly laughed. That's the only way it counts.
alts.zh: 我自己寫了一套軟體，會告訴我「聽眾在哪些點笑了」。是真的出聲笑。只有出聲才算。

cards.pattern: Don't call it [大詞], call it [具體可執行的詞].
cards.quote: So my two pieces of advice, anybody that's actually trying to do this is, A, state the problem, and, B, don't call it a strategy, call it an action agenda.
cards.zh: 我給真的要動手的人兩個建議：A，把問題講出來；B，不要叫它策略，叫它「行動議程」。
cards.why: 換掉一個名詞就換掉整場討論的期待值——提案卡住的時候，改名字常常比說服人有效。
swaps: Let's stop calling this a roadmap and call it a list of bets.
Rename it and the conversation changes.
cards.pmNote: 「行動議程」強迫團隊寫下要做的事，而不是希望發生的事。
cards.episode: Good Strategy, Bad Strategy | Richard Rumelt

alts.quote: A lot of times when we write a sentence, there's actually already a point of view baked in, but you don't want it to be an accidental point of view.
alts.zh: 很多時候我們寫一句話，裡面其實已經藏了一個立場——但你不會希望那是一個「不小心跑出來的」立場。

alts.quote: So for positioning work, I'm going to say something that is contentious, but I don't think it is at all.
alts.zh: 講到定位這件事，我要說一句大家可能覺得很有爭議的話——但我完全不覺得有爭議。

alts.quote: The way I think about it is talent basically controls the slope of the curve, but most things are actually acquirable skills.
alts.zh: 我的想法是：天分只是決定那條曲線的斜率，但大多數東西其實都是可以習得的技能。

cards.quote: These are things we're going to do, not goals we're going to achieve. These are things we're going to do, action steps.
cards.zh: 這些是我們要做的事，不是我們要達成的目標。就是要做的事，是行動步驟。
cards.why: 重複同一句加強界線，把提案的性質先定死，之後別人就很難把「希望發生的事」塞進來。
swaps: Verbs, not outcomes.
Every line here has an owner and a start date.
cards.episode: Good Strategy, Bad Strategy | Richard Rumelt

alts.quote: I think a lot of people think about markets almost like these bodies of water. And it's like, "Oh, it's this big body of water that we're going after." And I actually think that the most interesting markets, you have to think of them like currents.
alts.zh: 很多人把市場想成一片水域，覺得「喔，我們要去攻的是這一大片水」。但我覺得最有意思的市場，你得把它想成水流。

alts.quote: And a tiger is a threat that will actually kill us, just like a tiger would. So these are actual problematic things that could be really harmful to the product or the project.
alts.zh: 老虎是那種真的會弄死我們的威脅，就像真的老虎一樣。也就是真的會嚴重傷害產品或專案的問題。

alts.quote: speaking with adjacency, which means we're not going to match content to content. Instead, we're going to match theme, meaning or message.
alts.zh: 我把它叫做「鄰近敘事」，意思是我們不去對內容，而是去對主題、意義或訊息。

cards.pattern: The exercise I call [名字]: what is it that you should be able to buy but you can't?
cards.quote: The other exercise I used to take my students through was what I called value denial. Now, what is it that you should be able to buy but you can't?
cards.zh: 我以前會帶學生做另一個練習，我叫它「價值缺口」：有什麼是你照理該買得到、卻買不到的？
cards.why: 先替練習取名字再問問題，讓一個開放式提問變成可重複使用的工具——提想法時附上「怎麼再想一次」的方法，比想法本身更有價值。
swaps: What would you pay for today that nobody sells?
Where does money fail to buy the obvious thing?
cards.episode: Good Strategy, Bad Strategy | Richard Rumelt

alts.quote: Now, I'm biased when I'm going to say this, so take this with a pinch of salt, but I think the Accordion Method might be one of the things I'm the most proud of in my entire life.
alts.zh: 我要講的這件事我是有偏見的，所以你打個折聽——但我覺得手風琴法可能是我這輩子最引以為傲的東西之一。

alts.quote: One of them is this thing that culture is a product, period. Every company builds two products: one is the product they build for their customers, and the other is a product they build for their team.
alts.zh: 其中一個想法是：文化就是一個產品，就這樣。每家公司都在做兩個產品——一個給客戶，一個給團隊。

alts.quote: And as I saw the effectiveness of a post-mortem, that's what made me wonder, why do we need to wait until after things go wrong? Because why can't we extract some of these insights before they go wrong?
alts.zh: 看到事後檢討這麼有效之後，我就開始想：為什麼一定要等到事情出錯之後？為什麼不能在出錯之前就把這些洞見挖出來？

cards.pattern: It should [做到 X], but not [附帶的壞處]. It should [做到 X], but not [另一個壞處]. That's a little harder.
cards.quote: It should let in the air, good, but not the bugs, a screen. It should let in the air, but not the noise. That's a little harder.
cards.zh: 它應該讓空氣進來，但不讓蟲進來——所以要紗窗。它應該讓空氣進來，但不讓噪音進來。這個就比較難了。
cards.why: 用「要有 X，但不要 Y」的排比把需求規格講成一串取捨；最後一句 That's a little harder. 自己標出真正的難點在哪。
swaps: We want the upside of X without the tax of Y.
Same benefit, minus the side effect.
cards.pmNote: 從「完美版本應該長什麼樣」倒推，是找產品機會的實用練習。
cards.episode: Good Strategy, Bad Strategy | Richard Rumelt

alts.quote: So this is the simplest way to build a web app that's ever existed.
alts.zh: 所以這是有史以來做一個 web app 最簡單的方式。

alts.quote: So almost that it's like, I'm coming up with this on the spot, so it's not a good name, but chatter-driven development.
alts.zh: 有點像是——這名字是我現場亂想的，取得不好——「閒聊驅動開發」。

alts.quote: Here's the thing that I think is the easiest to change, is to realize the only thing that's ever supposed to happen in a meeting is the discussion part.
alts.zh: 我覺得最容易改的是這件事：認清一場會議裡唯一該發生的，只有「討論」。

cards.quote: Is there another way to look at this situation? Is there a bigger piece of wood over there than I can grab onto? That's the hard thing.
cards.zh: 這個情況有沒有別的看法？那邊有沒有一塊更大的浮木可以抓？難的就是這件事。
cards.why: 提替代方案時不直接否定現有診斷，而是把它比喻成「先抓到的那塊浮木」——保住對方的面子，同時打開第二個選項。
swaps: What's the second-best explanation?
We grabbed the first idea that floated by — is there a better one?
cards.pmNote: 先想到的診斷常只是「止住恐慌」的那一個，值得刻意再找第二個。
cards.episode: Good Strategy, Bad Strategy | Richard Rumelt

alts.quote: Here's the thing that I think is the easiest to change, is to realize the only thing that's ever supposed to happen in a meeting is the discussion part.
alts.zh: 我覺得最容易改的是這件事：認清一場會議裡唯一該發生的，只有「討論」。

alts.quote: Let's say we stipulate that that just happens to be true. Just humor me for a minute. If you assume that's true, then a bunch of things kind of follow from that postulate.
alts.zh: 我們先假設這是真的。先陪我一分鐘。如果你假設它是真的，那後面就會跟著推出一串結論。

alts.quote: So this is the simplest way to build a web app that's ever existed.
alts.zh: 所以這是有史以來做一個 web app 最簡單的方式。

cards.pattern: Here's the thing that I think is the easiest to change: [一個具體的小改動].
cards.quote: Here's the thing that I think is the easiest to change, is to realize the only thing that's ever supposed to happen in a meeting is the discussion part.
cards.zh: 我覺得最容易改的是這件事：認清一場會議裡唯一該發生的，只有「討論」。
cards.why: 用 the easiest to change 幫提案先降低採用門檻，聽的人在聽到內容之前就已經被告知「這不難」。
swaps: If we only change one thing, make it this.
The cheapest change with the biggest return is:
cards.pmNote: 會議三件事：discover / discuss / decide——只有 discuss 該在會議裡發生。
cards.episode: This will make you a better decision-maker | Annie Duke (author of “Thinking in Bets” and “Quit,” former pro poker player)

alts.quote: My most controversial opinion is that I think that AI is as big a deal as the internet or mobile. And only as big a deal as the internet or mobile.
alts.zh: 我最有爭議的一個看法是：AI 跟網路、行動裝置一樣重大——而且也「只」跟它們一樣重大而已。

alts.quote: Is there another way to look at this situation? Is there a bigger piece of wood over there than I can grab onto? That's the hard thing.
alts.zh: 這個情況有沒有別的看法？那邊有沒有一塊更大的浮木可以抓？難的就是這件事。

alts.quote: So this is the simplest way to build a web app that's ever existed.
alts.zh: 所以這是有史以來做一個 web app 最簡單的方式。

cards.pattern: I'm going to make a bold statement here. There is no such thing as [大家都當成前提的東西].
cards.quote: I'm going to make a bold statement here. There is no such thing as a long feedback loop.
cards.zh: 我要講一句很大膽的話：世界上沒有「很長的回饋迴圈」這種東西。
cards.why: 先標示「接下來這句很大膽」，等於幫聽眾預備好防衛心，反而讓極端主張更容易被聽完。
swaps: Let me say something that'll sound extreme:
I'll plant a flag here:
cards.pmNote: 長回饋迴圈可以主動縮短：找出與最終結果相關、但更早可觀測的必要條件。
cards.episode: This will make you a better decision-maker | Annie Duke (author of “Thinking in Bets” and “Quit,” former pro poker player)

alts.quote: There's this thing in my head and I haven't fully validated it but I'm going to share it with you.
alts.zh: 我腦中有個想法，還沒完全驗證過，但我還是講給你聽。

alts.quote: So for positioning work, I'm going to say something that is contentious, but I don't think it is at all.
alts.zh: 講到定位這件事，我要說一句大家可能覺得很有爭議的話——但我完全不覺得有爭議。

alts.quote: I want you to pull the hiring manager aside and say, "Hey, Lenny, you're the hiring manager. I've thought about what the role is. I want to make sure I'm understanding it correctly.
alts.zh: 我要你把用人主管拉到一旁說：「我想過這個職位到底是什麼，我想確認我理解得對不對。我可以跟你分享一下嗎？」

cards.pattern: [X] is great, but only if you attach [關鍵配套] with it. I just want to be super clear about that.
cards.quote: So a pre-mortem is great, but only if you attach a pre-commitment with it. So I just want to be super clear about that.
cards.zh: 事前檢討很棒，但前提是你要搭配一個事先承諾。這一點我想講得非常清楚。
cards.why: 推薦做法時同時綁上限制條件，避免對方只學走空殼；I just want to be super clear about that 是強調但不強勢的收尾。
swaps: Only worth doing if it comes with X.
Without the second half, it's theatre.
cards.pmNote: pre-mortem 要接上 kill criteria：預先定義看到哪些訊號就停或轉向。
cards.episode: This will make you a better decision-maker | Annie Duke (author of “Thinking in Bets” and “Quit,” former pro poker player)

alts.quote: And the genius of the pre-mortem ritual is the initial prompt. So it's not just about like, well, what could go wrong? The initial prompt is the genius.
alts.zh: 事前檢討真正厲害的地方在那個開場提示。它不只是問「可能哪裡會出錯」——關鍵就是提示怎麼下。

alts.quote: My most controversial opinion is that I think that AI is as big a deal as the internet or mobile. And only as big a deal as the internet or mobile.
alts.zh: 我最有爭議的一個看法是：AI 跟網路、行動裝置一樣重大——而且也「只」跟它們一樣重大而已。

alts.quote: I think going to college is great. I think this is a somewhat contrarian view within tech, maybe not in the broader economy.
alts.zh: 我覺得念大學很棒。我知道這在科技圈算是個有點逆風的看法，在一般社會可能就還好。

cards.pattern: The move is from [壞模式] to a model of [好模式]. You want to be [X], not [Y].
cards.quote: So here's the really wonderful thing about moving from a coercive model to really, I guess you could say a model of curiosity, right? You want to be curious, not coercive.
cards.zh: 從一個高壓的模式，換成一個好奇的模式——你要的是好奇，不是強迫。
cards.why: 用兩個押頭韻的形容詞（curious / coercive）把抽象的會議文化壓縮成一句口號：好記、好複誦、開會當場就能拿來擋人。
swaps: Ask, don't argue.
We're here to understand each other, not to win each other.
cards.episode: This will make you a better decision-maker | Annie Duke (author of “Thinking in Bets” and “Quit,” former pro poker player)

alts.quote: I want you to pull the hiring manager aside and say, "Hey, Lenny, you're the hiring manager. I've thought about what the role is. I want to make sure I'm understanding it correctly.
alts.zh: 我要你把用人主管拉到一旁說：「我想過這個職位到底是什麼，我想確認我理解得對不對。我可以跟你分享一下嗎？」

alts.quote: Stop focusing as much on what you want to say and focus more on what you want your audience to remember.
alts.zh: 別再那麼在意「你想說什麼」，多想想「你想讓聽眾記住什麼」。

alts.quote: So for positioning work, I'm going to say something that is contentious, but I don't think it is at all.
alts.zh: 講到定位這件事，我要說一句大家可能覺得很有爭議的話——但我完全不覺得有爭議。

cards.pattern: The genius of [做法] is [一個看似瑣碎的細節]. It's not just [大家以為的那個部分].
cards.quote: And the genius of the pre-mortem ritual is the initial prompt. So it's not just about like, well, what could go wrong? The initial prompt is the genius.
cards.zh: 事前檢討真正厲害的地方在那個開場提示。它不只是問「可能哪裡會出錯」——關鍵就是提示怎麼下。
cards.why: 介紹一個大家自認已經懂的做法時，指出「真正關鍵在某個小細節」，就能重新奪回聽眾的注意力。
swaps: The whole thing hinges on how you word the first question.
The magic isn't the meeting, it's the framing.
cards.pmNote: pre-mortem 提示語：「假設這個專案六個月後徹底失敗了，回頭看，是什麼害的？」
cards.episode: 4 questions Shreyas Doshi wishes he’d asked himself sooner | Former PM leader at Stripe, Twitter, Google

alts.quote: So a pre-mortem is great, but only if you attach a pre-commitment with it. So I just want to be super clear about that.
alts.zh: 事前檢討很棒，但前提是你要搭配一個事先承諾。這一點我想講得非常清楚。

alts.quote: None of this is going to blow anyone's minds, I think, because it's very best practices. But it's easy to overlook when you're so focused on so many different steps of a process.
alts.zh: 這些應該不會讓誰驚呆，因為都是很基本的最佳實務。但當你同時盯著流程裡一大堆步驟時，就是很容易漏掉。

alts.quote: So almost that it's like, I'm coming up with this on the spot, so it's not a good name, but chatter-driven development.
alts.zh: 有點像是——這名字是我現場亂想的，取得不好——「閒聊驅動開發」。

cards.pattern: A [新名詞] is [具體定義] — just like [字面上的東西] would.
cards.quote: And a tiger is a threat that will actually kill us, just like a tiger would. So these are actual problematic things that could be really harmful to the product or the project.
cards.zh: 老虎是那種真的會弄死我們的威脅，就像真的老虎一樣。也就是真的會嚴重傷害產品或專案的問題。
cards.why: 提案時發明一組具體的詞彙，讓團隊之後能用一個字帶出整個概念——語言本身就是採用率。
swaps: Let's name them so we can talk about them fast.
Give the risk a word and people will actually raise it.
cards.pmNote: pre-mortem 三詞：tiger（真威脅）／paper tiger（假警報）／elephant（沒人講的那件事）。
cards.episode: 4 questions Shreyas Doshi wishes he’d asked himself sooner | Former PM leader at Stripe, Twitter, Google

alts.quote: These are things we're going to do, not goals we're going to achieve. These are things we're going to do, action steps.
alts.zh: 這些是我們要做的事，不是我們要達成的目標。就是要做的事，是行動步驟。

alts.quote: The way I think about it is talent basically controls the slope of the curve, but most things are actually acquirable skills.
alts.zh: 我的想法是：天分只是決定那條曲線的斜率，但大多數東西其實都是可以習得的技能。

alts.quote: I think a lot of people think about markets almost like these bodies of water. And it's like, "Oh, it's this big body of water that we're going after." And I actually think that the most interesting markets, you have to think of them like currents.
alts.zh: 很多人把市場想成一片水域，覺得「喔，我們要去攻的是這一大片水」。但我覺得最有意思的市場，你得把它想成水流。

cards.pattern: We're no longer asking 'is this a good use of [資源]?' Instead we're asking 'is this the best use of [資源]?'
cards.quote: So when we reprogram ourselves to think in terms of opportunity cost, we are no longer thinking, 'Oh, is this a good use of my time?' Instead, you are thinking, 'Is this the best use of my time?'
cards.zh: 一旦改用機會成本思考，你就不再問「這樣用時間好不好？」，而是問「這是不是我時間最好的用法？」
cards.why: 只改一個形容詞（good→best）就重寫了決策標準，後面通常接一句 a subtle but profound shift——示範怎麼替自己的提案標註重要性。
swaps: Not 'is this worth doing' but 'is this the thing'.
Positive ROI is a low bar. Let's raise it.
cards.pmNote: 高槓桿角色的正 ROI 選項有上百個，優先排序該以最小化機會成本為準。
cards.episode: 4 questions Shreyas Doshi wishes he’d asked himself sooner | Former PM leader at Stripe, Twitter, Google

alts.quote: None of this is going to blow anyone's minds, I think, because it's very best practices. But it's easy to overlook when you're so focused on so many different steps of a process.
alts.zh: 這些應該不會讓誰驚呆，因為都是很基本的最佳實務。但當你同時盯著流程裡一大堆步驟時，就是很容易漏掉。

alts.quote: I'm going to tell my boss, on Monday, that I think we should do that. I'm going to use a little social capital and say we should do this.
alts.zh: 我禮拜一會跟我主管講，我覺得這個該做。我會動用一點我的政治額度，去替它說話。

alts.quote: the best way to get feedback from people is not by asking what they think, but to put something concrete in front of them and then have them react to it, right?
alts.zh: 要拿到回饋，最好的方式不是問人家怎麼想，而是先擺一個具體的東西在他面前，讓他反應，對吧？

cards.pattern: That's what made me wonder: why do we need to wait until [壞事發生] to [得到那個好處]?
cards.quote: And as I saw the effectiveness of a post-mortem, that's what made me wonder, why do we need to wait until after things go wrong? Because why can't we extract some of these insights before they go wrong?
cards.zh: 看到事後檢討這麼有效之後，我就開始想：為什麼一定要等到事情出錯之後？為什麼不能在出錯之前就把這些洞見挖出來？
cards.why: 用「我看到什麼→所以我開始想」的順序提案，讓新想法看起來是既有共識的自然延伸，而不是外來的入侵。
swaps: We already believe in X — why only after the fact?
Same exercise, different timing.
cards.episode: 4 questions Shreyas Doshi wishes he’d asked himself sooner | Former PM leader at Stripe, Twitter, Google

alts.quote: I think a lot of people think about markets almost like these bodies of water. And it's like, "Oh, it's this big body of water that we're going after." And I actually think that the most interesting markets, you have to think of them like currents.
alts.zh: 很多人把市場想成一片水域，覺得「喔，我們要去攻的是這一大片水」。但我覺得最有意思的市場，你得把它想成水流。

alts.quote: Let's say we stipulate that that just happens to be true. Just humor me for a minute. If you assume that's true, then a bunch of things kind of follow from that postulate.
alts.zh: 我們先假設這是真的。先陪我一分鐘。如果你假設它是真的，那後面就會跟著推出一串結論。

alts.quote: These are things we're going to do, not goals we're going to achieve. These are things we're going to do, action steps.
alts.zh: 這些是我們要做的事，不是我們要達成的目標。就是要做的事，是行動步驟。

cards.pattern: A lot of people think about [X] like [靜態比喻]. I actually think you have to think of them like [動態比喻].
cards.quote: I think a lot of people think about markets almost like these bodies of water. And it's like, "Oh, it's this big body of water that we're going after." And I actually think that the most interesting markets, you have to think of them like currents.
cards.zh: 很多人把市場想成一片水域，覺得「喔，我們要去攻的是這一大片水」。但我覺得最有意思的市場，你得把它想成水流。
cards.why: 「很多人這樣想／我覺得要那樣想」是最安全的反直覺開場：不否定任何人，只換一個比喻，而比喻換了結論就跟著換。
swaps: Most people picture a pond. I'd picture a river.
It's not how big the water is — it's which way it's moving.
cards.pmNote: 「Why now」＝市場裡正在改變、會推著你走的那股力量，比 TAM 更值得問。
cards.episode: The hierarchy of engagement | Sarah Tavel (Benchmark, Greylock, Pinterest)

alts.quote: None of this is going to blow anyone's minds, I think, because it's very best practices. But it's easy to overlook when you're so focused on so many different steps of a process.
alts.zh: 這些應該不會讓誰驚呆，因為都是很基本的最佳實務。但當你同時盯著流程裡一大堆步驟時，就是很容易漏掉。

alts.quote: I actually think it's easier. Spicy take.
alts.zh: 我其實覺得更容易。這個看法比較嗆。

alts.quote: These are things we're going to do, not goals we're going to achieve. These are things we're going to do, action steps.
alts.zh: 這些是我們要做的事，不是我們要達成的目標。就是要做的事，是行動步驟。

cards.pattern: You wouldn't want to be [高風險場景] and hear [把爛做法搬進那個場景]. Right away, you know there's something wrong.
cards.quote: You wouldn't want to be in a commercial airplane and hear the tower say to the pilot, 'I'm giving priority to the following three planes on runway five.' Right away, you know there's something wrong.
cards.zh: 你不會希望自己坐在飛機上，聽到塔台跟機師說：「我要給五號跑道上這三架飛機優先權。」你馬上就知道哪裡不對。
cards.why: 把辦公室裡沒人覺得奇怪的用法，搬到一個生死攸關的場景，荒謬感自己浮現——不用一句批評就完成了批評。
swaps: Try saying that sentence in an operating room.
Now imagine your surgeon has seventeen priorities.
cards.pmNote: priority 的原義是「第一」，一旦複數化就失去了排序功能。
cards.episode: Good Strategy, Bad Strategy | Richard Rumelt

alts.quote: I'd say that was the beginning of chapter two where it was we went from the company that could do no wrong to the company that could do no right, which was a big flip.
alts.zh: 我會說那就是第二章的開始——我們從「怎麼做都對」的公司，變成「怎麼做都錯」的公司，整個翻過來。

alts.quote: You want to be that tree in the storm that is not so rigid that if the wind is too strong it's going to break in half, but not so flexible that it's going to swing every which direction as soon as there's a gust.
alts.zh: 你要當風暴裡的那棵樹——不要硬到風一大就攔腰折斷，也不要軟到一陣風來就往每個方向亂晃。

alts.quote: If you're trying to do it, the best way to tell a story about something that you want people to understand is to do what I call speaking with adjacency, which means we're not going to match content to content.
alts.zh: 如果你想讓別人理解某件事，最好的說故事方式是我所謂的「用鄰近性說話」——意思是我們不會拿內容去對內容。

cards.pattern: That's a statement of value: you'd like [X]. I'd like to be taller than I am. I'd like to have more hair.
cards.quote: It's a statement of value, you would like to grow faster than you are. I'd like to be taller than I am. I'd like to have more hair.
cards.zh: 那是一句願望：你希望公司長得比現在快。我也希望自己長得比現在高。我也希望自己頭髮多一點。
cards.why: 用自嘲的平行例子拆解對方的說法，把「你這不是診斷」講得好笑而不傷人——自嘲是最安全的反駁載體。
swaps: I'd also like to be ten years younger.
That's a wish with a spreadsheet attached.
cards.episode: Good Strategy, Bad Strategy | Richard Rumelt

alts.quote: I'd say that was the beginning of chapter two where it was we went from the company that could do no wrong to the company that could do no right, which was a big flip.
alts.zh: 我會說那就是第二章的開始——我們從「怎麼做都對」的公司，變成「怎麼做都錯」的公司，整個翻過來。

alts.quote: I often use this analogy of if you're doing a home renovation, you can have the most beautiful rendering of the new bedroom. But if you haven't checked if there's electricity in that wall there or not, it's going to drastically change the cost and the time and everything.
alts.zh: 我常用一個比喻：你在裝修房子，臥室的效果圖可以做得美到不行。但如果你沒去確認那面牆裡到底有沒有電線，成本跟時間都會整個變樣。

alts.quote: And therefore envy is like wifi. It's like a hyperlocal service.
alts.zh: 所以說，嫉妒就像 wifi，是一種超在地的服務——只在很近的範圍內有訊號。

cards.pattern: For [結果] to happen, there has to be a source of power, there has to be a focus, and there has to be a target that can be affected.
cards.quote: To burn that black thread, there has to be a source of power, the sun. There has to be a focus. And it has to be a target that can be affected.
cards.zh: 要燒穿那根黑線，必須有能量來源，也就是太陽。必須有聚焦。而且必須是一個真的會被影響的目標。
cards.why: 用一個童年小故事把三個抽象條件掛在同一個畫面上：聽眾記住的是放大鏡，帶走的是三個條件。
swaps: Power, focus, and a target that actually burns.
Energy without focus is just a warm afternoon.
cards.pmNote: 策略三要素：力量來源、聚焦、可被影響的目標。
cards.episode: Good Strategy, Bad Strategy | Richard Rumelt

alts.quote: The ambition can often feel like this sun, like the heat of the sun that's trying to warm everything up. And I think that, really, what the best, ambitious founders do is they focus that ambition like a laser beam on a small market, the thimble.
alts.zh: 野心常常像太陽，想把整片海都曬熱。但最厲害的創辦人，是把同樣的野心像雷射一樣打在一個很小的市場上。

alts.quote: And at a high level, and this is me paraphrasing, so give me some license, but he's the source.
alts.zh: 大方向上——這是我自己轉述的，講得不精準請見諒——但源頭是他。

alts.quote: I'll give you a very small example again, just from Webflow, this idea of keyboard shortcuts, feels small, but that is a piece that creates a lot of love from user base who are power users.
alts.zh: 我再給你一個很小的例子，就 Webflow 的鍵盤快捷鍵。聽起來很小，但那正是讓重度使用者愛上產品的關鍵之一。

cards.pattern: The basic advice is: if you can't do [最難那一段], don't do [整件事], because that's where you'll fall off.
