cards.quote: And then the basic advice to a climber is if you can't do the crux, don't do the climb, because you're going to fall off there.
cards.zh: 攀岩最基本的建議是：如果你過不了關鍵段，就不要爬這條路線，因為你一定會在那裡掉下去。
cards.why: 借一個外行也懂的極端情境（會摔死）給出一條紀律，讓「先確認最難的部分做不做得到」聽起來不是保守，而是常識。
swaps: If the hardest part isn't solvable, the rest doesn't matter.
Start with the part that can kill the project.
cards.pmNote: crux＝整件事裡最難、也最決定成敗的那一段；先確認它是否可解。
cards.episode: Good Strategy, Bad Strategy | Richard Rumelt

alts.quote: I think the hardest thing for a founder, challenge is not optional. You're going to be challenged, but the suffering is optional.
alts.zh: 對創辦人來說最難的是：挑戰不是選項，你一定會被挑戰；但要不要痛苦，是選項。

alts.quote: I often use this analogy of if you're doing a home renovation, you can have the most beautiful rendering of the new bedroom. But if you haven't checked if there's electricity in that wall there or not, it's going to drastically change the cost and the time and everything.
alts.zh: 我常用一個比喻：你在裝修房子，臥室的效果圖可以做得美到不行。但如果你沒去確認那面牆裡到底有沒有電線，成本跟時間都會整個變樣。

alts.quote: It's like you had a very smooth flight across the Atlantic and your landing was absolutely horrible. You're not going to remember the smooth flight, you're going to remember the ending.
alts.zh: 就像你飛越大西洋一路很平穩，結果降落爛透了。你不會記得那段平穩的飛行，你只會記得結尾。

cards.pattern: Quit late and people say '[同情的話]'. Quit early and people say 'What?'
cards.quote: They're going to be like, 'Oh, well, it sounds like you put in your best effort.' But if you walk away early, people are like, 'What?'
cards.zh: 他們會說：「喔，聽起來你已經盡力了。」但如果你提早收手，大家的反應會是：「蛤？」
cards.why: 用兩句別人的台詞演出社會壓力的不對稱，比解釋「社會會懲罰提早放棄的人」有力十倍；引述對白是把論點戲劇化最快的方法。
swaps: Nobody questions a wreck. Everybody questions a clean exit.
Late quitters get sympathy; early quitters get raised eyebrows.
cards.pmNote: 砍專案的社會成本不對稱，是團隊拖太久才停損的主因之一。
cards.episode: This will make you a better decision-maker | Annie Duke (author of “Thinking in Bets” and “Quit,” former pro poker player)

alts.quote: If you're trying to do it, the best way to tell a story about something that you want people to understand is to do what I call speaking with adjacency, which means we're not going to match content to content.
alts.zh: 如果你想讓別人理解某件事，最好的說故事方式是我所謂的「用鄰近性說話」——意思是我們不會拿內容去對內容。

alts.quote: He was asked whether or not he was sleeping well at night and he said, 'Oh, yeah, I slept like a baby. I woke up every two hours and cried.'
alts.zh: 有人問他晚上睡得好不好，他說：「喔，超好，我睡得跟嬰兒一樣——每兩小時醒來哭一次。」

alts.quote: So I guess maybe for context, we had built this very nascent publisher motion where we were going out and helping people publish their rituals.
alts.zh: 先補個背景好了：我們當時做出了一套還很初期的「發布者」機制，我們會去幫大家把自己的儀式發布出來。

cards.pattern: As smart as [人] is, he couldn't see [新機會] until he quit [舊的東西]. That is a true cost of continuing.
cards.quote: And as smart as Stewart Butterfield is, he couldn't see Slack until he quit Glitch. And that is a true cost that he would've born of continuing with Glitch.
cards.zh: 連 Stewart Butterfield 這麼聰明的人，都是先關掉 Glitch 才看得見 Slack。而那就是繼續做下去真正的代價。
cards.why: 故事講完後用一句把「機會成本」這個抽象概念釘在一個具體的人身上；as smart as X is 先給對方最高評價，反而讓結論更難反駁。
swaps: He didn't find the next thing until he stopped defending the last one.
The cost wasn't the money — it was the idea he couldn't see yet.
cards.pmNote: 沉沒成本之外還有注意力的機會成本：不停掉舊的，你不會看到新的。
cards.episode: This will make you a better decision-maker | Annie Duke (author of “Thinking in Bets” and “Quit,” former pro poker player)

alts.quote: It's a bit like this really smart intern that refuses to read Slack and doesn't check Datadog or Sentry unless you ask it to.
alts.zh: 它有點像一個超聰明、但死不看 Slack、你不叫他他就不會去看 Datadog 或 Sentry 的實習生。

alts.quote: And so you go from this moment of the hard high cost of sales, pounding the pavement, to getting a list on a silver platter of restaurants to onboard. And that's that feeling of tipping, where all of a sudden something goes from being really freaking hard to so much easier.
alts.zh: 你會從那種一家一家敲門、成本超高的銷售，變成人家直接把一份餐廳名單端到你面前。那就是市場翻轉的感覺——某件事忽然從超級難變成輕鬆很多。

alts.quote: At Facebook in particular, I would find that every so often I would have to have what I called a Legos talk with someone where I would just see them start to ask these questions like, why are we hiring that person?
alts.zh: 特別是在 Facebook，我發現每隔一陣子就得跟某個人來一場我叫做「樂高談話」的對話——我會看到他們開始問：我們為什麼要招那個人？

cards.pattern: At the end of [看起來很順的那段時間], [人] writes a note and says, '[一句反直覺的判斷]'.
cards.quote: At the end of that six weeks, that Monday morning, Stewart Butterfield writes a note to his investors and co-founders and says, 'I woke up this morning with the dead certainty that Glitch was over.'
cards.zh: 六週結束的那個週一早上，Stewart Butterfield 寫信給投資人跟共同創辦人說：「我今天早上醒來，非常確定 Glitch 結束了。」
cards.why: 把時間點釘死（那個週一早上），再讓當事人自己說出結論——說故事時最有力的證據是主角的原話，不是你的評論。
swaps: On the morning it was going best, he wrote:
The numbers were up. His note said the opposite.
cards.episode: This will make you a better decision-maker | Annie Duke (author of “Thinking in Bets” and “Quit,” former pro poker player)

alts.quote: The ambition can often feel like this sun, like the heat of the sun that's trying to warm everything up. And I think that, really, what the best, ambitious founders do is they focus that ambition like a laser beam on a small market, the thimble.
alts.zh: 野心常常像太陽，想把整片海都曬熱。但最厲害的創辦人，是把同樣的野心像雷射一樣打在一個很小的市場上。

alts.quote: As a very simple example, sorry, this is a little bit dark, but how restaurants want to turn over tables as fast as possible in order to maximize for the day? Hospitals actually want to do the same with patients.
alts.zh: 舉個很簡單的例子——抱歉這個講法有點黑暗——餐廳希望翻桌越快越好，好把一天的收益拉高。醫院對病床其實也是同一件事。

alts.quote: You really cut out all the parts that make people go dead in the eyes and just say the parts that make their eyes light up.
alts.zh: 你要做的就是把那些讓人眼神死掉的段落全砍掉，只留下讓人眼睛發亮的部分。

cards.pattern: He asked one question: '[很簡單的問題]' Simple question. But at that point I realized we never really talked about that.
cards.quote: He asked me one question which was something to the effect of, how does this make our users love Twitter more? Simple question. But then at that point I realized, yeah, we never really talked about that.
cards.zh: 他只問了我一個問題：這件事怎麼讓我們的使用者更愛 Twitter？很簡單的問題。但那一刻我才發現，我們從頭到尾沒真的談過這個。
cards.why: 「一個簡單問題→我當場發現自己漏了什麼」是最有說服力的故事骨架，因為說故事的人是被打敗的那一方，聽的人不會有戒心。
swaps: One question, and the whole review changed shape.
He didn't argue. He just asked the question nobody had asked.
cards.episode: 4 questions Shreyas Doshi wishes he’d asked himself sooner | Former PM leader at Stripe, Twitter, Google

alts.quote: He was asked whether or not he was sleeping well at night and he said, 'Oh, yeah, I slept like a baby. I woke up every two hours and cried.'
alts.zh: 有人問他晚上睡得好不好，他說：「喔，超好，我睡得跟嬰兒一樣——每兩小時醒來哭一次。」

alts.quote: I'll give you a very small example again, just from Webflow, this idea of keyboard shortcuts, feels small, but that is a piece that creates a lot of love from user base who are power users.
alts.zh: 我再給你一個很小的例子，就 Webflow 的鍵盤快捷鍵。聽起來很小，但那正是讓重度使用者愛上產品的關鍵之一。

alts.quote: Which reminds me of a Kevin Kelly quote that I love where he says, 'Pros are just amateurs who've learned to recover gracefully from their mistakes.'
alts.zh: 這讓我想到我很喜歡的一句 Kevin Kelly 的話：「專業人士只是學會了優雅地從錯誤中恢復的業餘者。」

cards.pattern: [X] becomes a convenient excuse for us where we say, 'It's not me. I just don't have [X].'
cards.quote: So time becomes a convenient excuse for us where we say, 'Well, it's not me. It's just, I don't have time to work on it.'
cards.zh: 時間就變成一個很方便的藉口，我們會說：「不是我的問題，我只是沒時間做這件事。」
cards.why: 用「方便的藉口」點破自己（和大家）的說詞，再引述那句藉口的原話——先自曝再指認，聽眾就不會覺得被審判。
swaps: 'No bandwidth' is usually 'no confidence' in a nicer suit.
We blame the calendar because the real reason is scarier.
cards.pmNote: 高槓桿任務被拖延的真正原因常是害怕做不好，不是沒時間。
cards.episode: 4 questions Shreyas Doshi wishes he’d asked himself sooner | Former PM leader at Stripe, Twitter, Google

alts.quote: I assume all the time, 100% of the time, that no one wants to hear anything I have to say.
alts.zh: 我永遠都假設——百分之百的場合都假設——沒有人想聽我講任何話。

alts.quote: But weirdly, it was like you see the videos where there's the mushroom cloud in the distance. You see it. But you don't hear, or notice it.
alts.zh: 但很怪，那感覺就像影片裡遠方升起的蘑菇雲。你看得見。可是你聽不到，也沒真的感覺到。

alts.quote: I often use this analogy of if you're doing a home renovation, you can have the most beautiful rendering of the new bedroom. But if you haven't checked if there's electricity in that wall there or not, it's going to drastically change the cost and the time and everything.
alts.zh: 我常用一個比喻：你在裝修房子，臥室的效果圖可以做得美到不行。但如果你沒去確認那面牆裡到底有沒有電線，成本跟時間都會整個變樣。

cards.pattern: I started to feel this and it became like a pebble in my shoe — so I wrote it down, and that's where [框架] came from.
cards.quote: I just started to feel this and it became like a pebble in my shoe. I started just to go through that process that you've gone through many times before of writing and distilling it, and that's where I came up with this hierarchy.
cards.zh: 我一直有這個感覺，它就像鞋子裡的一顆小石頭。後來我就照那個寫下來、把它蒸餾的過程走一遍，這個框架就是這樣長出來的。
cards.why: 用一個身體感的比喻交代「我為什麼會有這套主張」；先講來源再講框架，聽的人會覺得這是被現實逼出來的，不是掰出來的。
swaps: It kept nagging at me until I had to write it down.
It was a splinter I couldn't leave alone.
cards.episode: The hierarchy of engagement | Sarah Tavel (Benchmark, Greylock, Pinterest)

alts.quote: So I have my definition of success I came up with years ago. Success is making the people who believed in you look brilliant. That's it.
alts.zh: 我幾年前想出了自己對成功的定義。成功就是：讓當初相信你的人看起來很有眼光。就這樣。

alts.quote: You've started this company, it's been super successful, and then suddenly your employees don't want to wear your T-shirt anymore.
alts.zh: 你創了這家公司，它一路很成功，然後突然間，員工不想再穿你們公司的 T-shirt 了。

alts.quote: People act like having a startup fail is the worst thing that can happen to you. And man, that's not even in the top 10.
alts.zh: 大家都把「創業失敗」講得像是人生最慘的事。老實說，那連前十名都排不進去。

cards.pattern: [特質] can feel like the sun trying to warm everything up. What the best [人] do is focus it like a laser beam on [很小的範圍].
cards.quote: The ambition can often feel like this sun, like the heat of the sun that's trying to warm everything up. And I think that, really, what the best, ambitious founders do is they focus that ambition like a laser beam on a small market, the thimble.
cards.zh: 野心常常像太陽，想把整片海都曬熱。但最厲害的創辦人，是把同樣的野心像雷射一樣打在一個很小的市場上。
cards.why: 不否定對方的野心，只換掉野心的形狀（太陽→雷射）——要人收斂範圍時最不傷人的講法。
swaps: Same energy, different aperture.
Don't lower the ambition — narrow the beam.
cards.pmNote: 市集起步要 thimble：小到能真的煮沸的一鍋水，而不是一整片海。
cards.episode: The hierarchy of engagement | Sarah Tavel (Benchmark, Greylock, Pinterest)

alts.quote: To burn that black thread, there has to be a source of power, the sun. There has to be a focus. And it has to be a target that can be affected.
alts.zh: 要燒穿那根黑線，必須有能量來源，也就是太陽。必須有聚焦。而且必須是一個真的會被影響的目標。

alts.quote: If you're trying to do it, the best way to tell a story about something that you want people to understand is to do what I call speaking with adjacency, which means we're not going to match content to content.
alts.zh: 如果你想讓別人理解某件事，最好的說故事方式是我所謂的「用鄰近性說話」——意思是我們不會拿內容去對內容。

alts.quote: The short version I think that works the best is almost like a U-curve where the X-axis is time and the Y-axis is level of involvement.
alts.zh: 最短的講法大概像一條 U 型曲線：橫軸是時間，縱軸是投入程度。

cards.pattern: You go from [很辛苦的舊狀態] to [輕鬆的新狀態]. And that's that feeling of [你要命名的概念].
cards.quote: And so you go from this moment of the hard high cost of sales, pounding the pavement, to getting a list on a silver platter of restaurants to onboard. And that's that feeling of tipping, where all of a sudden something goes from being really freaking hard to so much easier.
cards.zh: 你會從那種一家一家敲門、成本超高的銷售，變成人家直接把一份餐廳名單端到你面前。那就是市場翻轉的感覺——某件事忽然從超級難變成輕鬆很多。
cards.why: 故事講到轉折點後立刻替那個感覺命名（that's that feeling of tipping），讓聽眾之後可以用一個字回想整個故事。
swaps: One week you're begging; the next week they're calling.
That's the moment the pushing stops.
cards.pmNote: 市集 tipping point：在夠飽和的市場裡，供給方開始主動把需求帶進來。
cards.episode: The hierarchy of engagement | Sarah Tavel (Benchmark, Greylock, Pinterest)

alts.quote: And after all of that, which clearly means they wanted it to work, they're like, "No, bye." What? Just on an emotional level, you got to go, "Wait a minute, that's terrible."
alts.zh: 經歷了這一整串——這明明代表他們很想讓它成功——結果他們說「不用了，掰」。蛤？光是情緒上你就該有反應：等一下，這超糟的。

alts.quote: Over the course of our life, because of all these little situations that happen, we start getting bugs in the software and we're not really upgrading our software.
alts.zh: 在人生的過程裡，因為發生了各種小事，我們的軟體開始長 bug，而我們也沒有真的在更新它。

alts.quote: Yeah, so follow me on the detour to science world temporarily. If we all remember high school science classes, there was this concept of potential and kinetic energy.
alts.zh: 先跟我繞去科學世界一下。如果大家還記得高中物理，有個概念叫位能跟動能。

cards.pattern: Do you [做了決定] and then go to sleep like Rip Van Winkle, and wake up [十年] later and go, 'Hey, how'd that go?'
cards.quote: And I said, 'Oh, I'm sorry, do you invest? And then you go to sleep like Rip Van Winkle? And then you wake up 10 years later and you go, Hey, how'd that go?'
cards.zh: 我說：不好意思，你們是投完錢就像李伯大夢一樣睡著，十年後醒來說「欸，那個後來怎樣了？」嗎？
cards.why: 把對方的前提誇張演一遍讓它自己崩潰；開頭那句 Oh, I'm sorry 是禮貌緩衝，有了它後面才敢這麼嗆。
swaps: So nothing observable happens in between?
You invest, then you close your eyes for a decade?
cards.episode: This will make you a better decision-maker | Annie Duke (author of “Thinking in Bets” and “Quit,” former pro poker player)

alts.quote: So they would say, "Oh, your market's not big enough." And I would say, "It's going to be huge." And I'd add a new page in my pitch deck that said how big the market I believe was.
alts.zh: 他們會說：「你的市場不夠大。」我就說：「它會變超大。」然後我就在簡報裡加一頁，講我認為這市場有多大。

alts.quote: I remember somebody on social media said the problem with Benedict is his answer to everything is it depends. It's like, yeah, it does. It depends.
alts.zh: 我記得有人在社群上說：Benedict 的問題就是他對什麼都回答「看情況」。呃，本來就是啊。就是看情況。

alts.quote: But what I think that misses is, it assumes that you go and you do this analyst job for two years, and at the end of it you have a person who knows how to make models really well.
alts.zh: 但我覺得這個說法漏掉了一件事：它預設你得先當兩年分析師，兩年之後才會長出一個很會建模型的人。

cards.pattern: I heard you, and your input was incorporated into the decision. Nevertheless, this is the path we're going to take.
cards.quote: And to have the ability to say, I heard you and your input, trust me, was incorporated into the decision, nevertheless, this is the path we're going to take.
cards.zh: 我聽到你說的了，你的意見真的有被放進這個決定裡。話雖如此，我們還是要走這條路。
cards.why: nevertheless 是英文裡最好用的「接住之後不讓步」轉折詞：先確認對方被聽見，再把決定釘死，不必再解釋一次理由。
swaps: I hear you. Nevertheless, we're going this way.
That's real, and the decision stands.
cards.pmNote: disagree and commit：讓人覺得被聽見，跟接受他的結論，是兩件不同的事。
cards.episode: This will make you a better decision-maker | Annie Duke (author of “Thinking in Bets” and “Quit,” former pro poker player)

alts.quote: This is baby talk, but CEO after CEO will stand up and say, 'Well, we're going to grow and we're going to make a profit.'
alts.zh: 這根本是幼稚園程度，但一個又一個執行長還是會站上台說：「我們要成長，我們也要賺錢。」

alts.quote: So they would say, "Oh, your market's not big enough." And I would say, "It's going to be huge." And I'd add a new page in my pitch deck that said how big the market I believe was.
alts.zh: 他們會說：「你的市場不夠大。」我就說：「它會變超大。」然後我就在簡報裡加一頁，講我認為這市場有多大。

alts.quote: There's this rush to judgment upfront where people say, "Oh, it's therefore obvious that X, Y, Z. It's obvious that the moats are going to be in this area of the technology, but not in this other area."
alts.zh: 一開始大家都會急著下判斷，說「所以顯然就是 X、Y、Z」、「顯然護城河一定在這一塊，不會在那一塊」。

cards.pattern: What makes you think that you can succeed? '[空泛的理由].' Not good enough.
cards.quote: So what makes you think that you can succeed? Oh, I really want to succeed. Not good enough.
cards.zh: 那你憑什麼覺得自己會成功？「因為我真的很想成功。」——不夠。
cards.why: Not good enough. 三個字獨立成句，是英文裡最短的駁回；前面先自問自答一次，就不必針對在場的任何人。
swaps: Wanting it isn't an advantage.
That's motivation, not an edge.
cards.pmNote: 沒有不對稱優勢（asymmetry）就沒有勝算，努力本身不是策略。
cards.episode: Good Strategy, Bad Strategy | Richard Rumelt

alts.quote: And optics is a good thing. So I'm not saying don't think about optics whatsoever, I think it's actually important to think about optics.
alts.zh: 而且「對外呈現」本身是好事。我不是說完全不要管呈現，我覺得那其實很重要。

alts.quote: I mean, I don't want to act like I think this is easy, to be clear.
alts.zh: 我不想表現得好像我覺得這很簡單，先講清楚。

alts.quote: To me, I think it's a great accelerant when it's already working, but it can't fix it if people don't want to talk about your product.
alts.zh: 對我來說，那在本來就跑得動的時候是很好的加速器，但如果根本沒人想談論你的產品，它救不了你。

cards.pattern: This is baby talk, but [有頭有臉的人] after [人] will stand up and say '[自相矛盾的話]'.
cards.quote: This is baby talk, but CEO after CEO will stand up and say, 'Well, we're going to grow and we're going to make a profit.'
cards.zh: 這根本是幼稚園程度，但一個又一個執行長還是會站上台說：「我們要成長，我們也要賺錢。」
cards.why: 先承認「這道理很淺」，擋掉「這誰不知道」的反駁；再用 X after X 的重複證明它天天都在發生。
swaps: I know this is obvious. It's also everywhere.
Kindergarten logic — and it's in half the decks I read.
cards.episode: Good Strategy, Bad Strategy | Richard Rumelt

alts.quote: That's why you need your job search council. This is when you really need to ask for help because every bone in your body is going to say, "I'm not going to negotiate. That's going to make it worse," and it almost never does.
alts.zh: 這就是為什麼你需要求職小組。你全身上下每根骨頭都會喊：「我不要談判，談了只會更糟。」但幾乎從來不會更糟。

alts.quote: And to have the ability to say, I heard you and your input, trust me, was incorporated into the decision, nevertheless, this is the path we're going to take.
alts.zh: 我聽到你說的了，你的意見真的有被放進這個決定裡。話雖如此，我們還是要走這條路。

alts.quote: So they would say, "Oh, your market's not big enough." And I would say, "It's going to be huge." And I'd add a new page in my pitch deck that said how big the market I believe was.
alts.zh: 他們會說：「你的市場不夠大。」我就說：「它會變超大。」然後我就在簡報裡加一頁，講我認為這市場有多大。

cards.pattern: The theory is that if you [對方主張的做法], somehow [誇張到荒謬的機制] and [想要的結果] just happens.
cards.quote: The theory is that if you perfect yourself and somehow rays come out of your head and people will follow you, because you're so magnetic, and you're so perfect.
cards.zh: 那套理論是說：只要你把自己修煉到完美，頭上就會發出光芒，大家自然會跟隨你，因為你太有魅力、太完美了。
cards.why: 用誇張複述（把對方立場演成漫畫）來反駁；關鍵是誇張的是「機制」而不是「人」，所以不算人身攻擊。
swaps: Apparently the org chart resolves itself if you journal enough.
The implied mechanism is charisma osmosis.
cards.episode: Good Strategy, Bad Strategy | Richard Rumelt

alts.quote: I often tell people that I hate the word 'favorite' because it tells me to become limited in my mind. So I stay away from 'favorite', but I learn all the time from everybody.
alts.zh: 我常跟人說我討厭「最喜歡的」這個詞，因為它會逼我的腦袋變窄。所以我不用這個詞，但我隨時都在跟每個人學東西。

alts.quote: But if they come in on day one saying your strategy is all wrong, raises the question of, "Well then why did you join my team if you didn't believe in my strategy?"
alts.zh: 但如果他第一天就說你的策略整個都錯了，那就會讓人想問：既然你不相信這個策略，當初為什麼要加入我的團隊？

alts.quote: There's this rush to judgment upfront where people say, "Oh, it's therefore obvious that X, Y, Z. It's obvious that the moats are going to be in this area of the technology, but not in this other area."
alts.zh: 一開始大家都會急著下判斷，說「所以顯然就是 X、Y、Z」、「顯然護城河一定在這一塊，不會在那一塊」。

cards.quote: And by the way, everything I say here, I have been that person. So I have been that person who's procrastinated on an L task, whether it's the strategy or whether it's writing the PRD.
cards.zh: 順帶一提，我講的這些我自己都幹過。我就是那個會拖著高槓桿任務不做的人，不管是策略還是那份 PRD。
cards.why: 在別人開口說「你講得容易」之前先自曝，把「批評」轉成「共同的毛病」；後面再舉自己的具體例子讓它不像客套。
swaps: I'm describing myself here, to be clear.
Everything I just said, I've done wrong at least twice.
cards.episode: 4 questions Shreyas Doshi wishes he’d asked himself sooner | Former PM leader at Stripe, Twitter, Google

alts.quote: Not to say it's not better, but just this is the structure of it, and it kind of sets you up for bragging.
alts.zh: 我不是說它不好，我只是在講它的結構——這個結構會把你逼到一直自誇。

alts.quote: So they would say, "Oh, your market's not big enough." And I would say, "It's going to be huge." And I'd add a new page in my pitch deck that said how big the market I believe was.
alts.zh: 他們會說：「你的市場不夠大。」我就說：「它會變超大。」然後我就在簡報裡加一頁，講我認為這市場有多大。

alts.quote: And I always write them back and say like, "Please tell me the better term and popularize it and I'll use it. It's a great idea."
alts.zh: 我都回信說：「請你告訴我更好的講法，然後把它推廣開，我就會改用。這主意很好。」

cards.pattern: And [被你批評的東西] is a good thing. So I'm not saying don't [做它] whatsoever — I think it's actually important.
cards.quote: And optics is a good thing. So I'm not saying don't think about optics whatsoever, I think it's actually important to think about optics.
cards.zh: 而且「對外呈現」本身是好事。我不是說完全不要管呈現，我覺得那其實很重要。
cards.why: 批評一件事之前先替它平反一次，聽眾就不會把你歸類成反對派，之後你講的限制條件才聽得進去。
swaps: To be fair, it earns its place.
I'm not against it — I'm against it being the goal.
cards.pmNote: 內部 optics（讓人知道你在做什麼）本身有價值，問題在它變成目標本身。
cards.episode: 4 questions Shreyas Doshi wishes he’d asked himself sooner | Former PM leader at Stripe, Twitter, Google

alts.quote: I don't really agree and I still think it's wrong, but I'm committed to it." That's not actually commitment.
alts.zh: 「我其實不同意，我還是覺得這是錯的，但我會照做。」那並不是真正的承諾。

alts.quote: And to be clear, I don't think it's actually that dangerous right now.
alts.zh: 先講清楚，我不覺得現在真的有那麼危險。

alts.quote: The most important thing, three strategic pillars, I wouldn't change that. I would defend it using the framework, but if people are like, "there's really good arguments about the criteria that led to your ranking," then it's okay to reconsider it.
alts.zh: 最重要的那三根策略支柱，我不會改。我會用那套框架來守，但如果有人針對排序背後的評分標準提出很好的論證，那就可以重新考慮。

cards.pattern: There are very concrete instances where [對方是對的]. It's just that [在某種條件下], we ignore [你想加進來的因素].
cards.quote: So, there are very concrete instances where there is a real execution problem. It's just that in high performing organizations that are growing really fast, we ignore the other factors that might be at play.
cards.zh: 確實有非常具體的情況真的就是執行問題。只是在那種高效、又長得很快的組織裡，我們會忽略掉其他可能在作用的因素。
cards.why: 把對方的立場保留成「特例成立」，再用 It's just that… 輕輕把討論推回自己的主張——不需要贏，只需要把對方的適用範圍改小。
swaps: Sometimes it really is what it looks like. Just not usually.
Granted — and that's not what's happening here.
cards.pmNote: 多數「執行問題」其實是策略、文化或人際問題的表徵。
cards.episode: 4 questions Shreyas Doshi wishes he’d asked himself sooner | Former PM leader at Stripe, Twitter, Google

alts.quote: There's this rush to judgment upfront where people say, "Oh, it's therefore obvious that X, Y, Z. It's obvious that the moats are going to be in this area of the technology, but not in this other area."
alts.zh: 一開始大家都會急著下判斷，說「所以顯然就是 X、Y、Z」、「顯然護城河一定在這一塊，不會在那一塊」。

alts.quote: It's all the other stuff. And the PowerPoint is just like the task, but that's not what you hired them for.
alts.zh: 價值在其他所有事情上。投影片只是那個「任務」，但那不是你花錢請他們來做的事。

alts.quote: If you don't say yes, what you're essentially saying is, I am so presumptuous that I understand what's on the other side of that door already.
alts.zh: 你如果不答應，你其實等於在說：我狂妄到已經知道那扇門後面是什麼了。

cards.pattern: But the only way to build long-term value is [B]. It's that evolution that ends up changing who you focus on.
cards.quote: But the only way to build long-term enduring value with a marketplace is to corner the demand side. And so it's kind of a little bit that evolution of a marketplace that ends up changing who you focus on.
cards.zh: 但要做出長期能留住價值的市集，唯一的路是掌握需求端。所以那有點像是市集的演化，會慢慢改變你該把重心放在誰身上。
cards.why: 面對「到底供給重要還是需求重要」這種假二選一，不選邊，改用「演化階段」把兩個立場都保住，再把重心導向你要的那一端。
swaps: Both are true, just not at the same time.
That's the early game; this is the end game.
cards.pmNote: 市集早期靠供給破冰，長期價值來自掌握需求端。
cards.episode: The hierarchy of engagement | Sarah Tavel (Benchmark, Greylock, Pinterest)

alts.quote: So this kind of behavioral framing and nudging becomes important, it's not about deceiving your customers, but it's just about framing the products in such a way that it also appeals to the irrational side of the brain.
alts.zh: 這種行為框架跟推力很重要——它不是要騙客戶，而是把產品呈現得也能打到大腦不理性的那一面。

alts.quote: But I can understand why the hair stands up on the back of the neck a little bit thinking about it because, of course, if you give a senior engineer like, "Here's how I want you to go implement the schema"…
alts.zh: 但我理解為什麼你一想到這個就會汗毛豎起來——畢竟你如果去跟資深工程師說「這個 schema 我要你這樣實作」……

alts.quote: Not to say it's not better, but just this is the structure of it, and it kind of sets you up for bragging.
alts.zh: 我不是說它不好，我只是在講它的結構——這個結構會把你逼到一直自誇。

cards.pattern: If we could just have that be something [簡化後的樣子], that'd be huge.
cards.quote: And we're like, "If we could just have that be something, you click a link and it just boots in your browser, that'd be huge."
cards.zh: 我們就想：「如果這件事可以變成——你點一個連結，它就直接在瀏覽器裡開起來，那不得了。」
cards.why: 拋新點子時不要先講技術，先講「使用者最後只要做什麼動作」。If we could just… 把野心藏在 just 後面，聽起來像小事一樁；that'd be huge 才把賭注放大。
swaps: What if it were as simple as [一個動作]?
Imagine you just [動作] and it's done.
cards.pmNote: 提案先講 end-state 的操作畫面，比講架構更容易讓非技術的人買單。
cards.episode: Inside Bolt: From near-death to ~$40m ARR in 5 months—one of the fastest-growing products in history | Eric Simons (founder and CEO of StackBlitz)

alts.quote: How do I make this idea one click better? It's not about how do you do something radically, radically different, but taking ideas and then making it slightly better, slightly better.
alts.zh: 我要怎麼把這個想法再往上推一格？重點不是做出天差地遠的東西，而是接手別人的想法，再讓它好一點點。

alts.quote: speaking with adjacency, which means we're not going to match content to content. Instead, we're going to match theme, meaning or message.
alts.zh: 我把它叫做「鄰近敘事」，意思是我們不去對內容，而是去對主題、意義或訊息。

alts.quote: So for positioning work, I'm going to say something that is contentious, but I don't think it is at all.
alts.zh: 講到定位這件事，我要說一句大家可能覺得很有爭議的話——但我完全不覺得有爭議。

cards.pattern: What if there's a better way? What if we could reimagine [X] from the ground up?
cards.quote: And so the question just was what if there's a better way? What if we could reimagine this format from the ground up?
cards.zh: 所以問題就變成：有沒有更好的做法？我們有沒有可能把這個格式從頭重新想一遍？
cards.why: 連續兩個 what if 是升溫結構：第一句只問「有沒有更好的」，第二句才把範圍拉到 from the ground up。台灣人常一次講到底，反而讓人覺得太狂。
swaps: What if we started from scratch here?
What if the default isn't actually the right answer?
cards.pmNote: 重新定義既有品類時，先質疑 format 本身，比在既有 format 裡加功能更容易做出差異化。
cards.episode: “Dumbest idea I’ve heard” to $100M ARR: Inside the rise of Gamma | Grant Lee (CEO)

alts.quote: There's this thing in my head and I haven't fully validated it but I'm going to share it with you.
alts.zh: 我腦中有個想法，還沒完全驗證過，但我還是講給你聽。

alts.quote: How do I make this idea one click better? It's not about how do you do something radically, radically different, but taking ideas and then making it slightly better, slightly better.
alts.zh: 我要怎麼把這個想法再往上推一格？重點不是做出天差地遠的東西，而是接手別人的想法，再讓它好一點點。

alts.quote: the best way to get feedback from people is not by asking what they think, but to put something concrete in front of them and then have them react to it, right?
alts.zh: 要拿到回饋，最好的方式不是問人家怎麼想，而是先擺一個具體的東西在他面前，讓他反應，對吧？

cards.quote: We will do the work the night before it's due, so let's just make it due tomorrow. Can we turn tomorrow into today?
cards.zh: 反正大家都是死線前一晚才做，那我們乾脆把死線訂在明天。能不能把明天變成今天？
cards.why: 先講一個大家都承認的人性事實，再把它變成行動提案，對方很難反駁——因為前提是他自己也認的。最後那句短問句是催化劑，把提案交回給團隊。
swaps: Everyone ships the night before, so let's move the night up.
What would it take to do this today instead of next week?
cards.pmNote: 縮短 deadline 本身就是一種 scope 工具：時間壓縮會自動逼出優先順序。
cards.episode: Building product at Stripe: craft, metrics, and customer obsession | Jeff Weinstein (Product lead)

alts.quote: How do I make this idea one click better? It's not about how do you do something radically, radically different, but taking ideas and then making it slightly better, slightly better.
alts.zh: 我要怎麼把這個想法再往上推一格？重點不是做出天差地遠的東西，而是接手別人的想法，再讓它好一點點。

alts.quote: So for positioning work, I'm going to say something that is contentious, but I don't think it is at all.
alts.zh: 講到定位這件事，我要說一句大家可能覺得很有爭議的話——但我完全不覺得有爭議。

alts.quote: None of this is going to blow anyone's minds, I think, because it's very best practices. But it's easy to overlook when you're so focused on so many different steps of a process.
alts.zh: 這些應該不會讓誰驚呆，因為都是很基本的最佳實務。但當你同時盯著流程裡一大堆步驟時，就是很容易漏掉。

cards.pattern: If you are [不知道要衡量什麼], just make a [X] chart—emit a log line and count it.
cards.quote: If you are bored one day and you're not sure what to measure, just make a user having a bad day chart, emit a log line and count it as a bar chart.
cards.zh: 哪天你閒著、又不知道該量什麼，就做一張「使用者今天很衰」的圖表——打一行 log，堆成長條圖就好。
cards.why: 把一個抽象提案降級成「一行 log」這種零風險的動作，別人就沒有拒絕的理由。用 just 把提案的成本講到最小是關鍵。
swaps: Just start counting it and see what the shape looks like.
Emit an event for it and we'll argue about the definition later.
cards.pmNote: 「bad day 事件」是很好用的通用指標：先窮舉會讓使用者不爽的情境，再逐一消滅。
cards.episode: Building product at Stripe: craft, metrics, and customer obsession | Jeff Weinstein (Product lead)

alts.quote: I want you to pull the hiring manager aside and say, "Hey, Lenny, you're the hiring manager. I've thought about what the role is. I want to make sure I'm understanding it correctly.
alts.zh: 我要你把用人主管拉到一旁說：「我想過這個職位到底是什麼，我想確認我理解得對不對。我可以跟你分享一下嗎？」

alts.quote: I sat for about a half a day and I thought, I think I can help here, drew out an org chart, put my name on the top, walked into my boss's office and said, "This is one potential solve of your marketing organization question."
alts.zh: 我想了大概半天，覺得我應該幫得上忙，就畫了一張組織圖，把自己放在最上面，走進我主管辦公室說：「這是你那個行銷組織問題的其中一個解法。」

alts.quote: So what we often encourage people to do is keep working the way you're working, but some future project, some low criticality project, try this new method on that.
alts.zh: 我們常建議的是：現在的做法照舊，但挑一個之後的、沒那麼要緊的專案，在那上面試新方法。

cards.quote: I sort of wanted to ask myself, is it possible to break that divide between the haves and the have-nots and make this capability widely accessible through a procedural approach. And I have news for you. The answer is yes.
cards.zh: 我當時就問自己：有沒有可能打破「會的人／不會的人」這道分野，用一套流程讓這個能力變成人人都能上手？我告訴你，答案是可以。
cards.why: 先把問題升級成「有沒有可能」的大哉問，再用 And I have news for you 這個小停頓製造懸念，最後才給結論。這是講者控制節奏、不讓聽眾預先猜到答案的手法。
swaps: Is this actually a talent thing, or is it a process thing? It's a process thing.
Can this be taught? I'm going to argue yes.
cards.pmNote: 把「有沒有天分」的爭論改成「有沒有流程」，是把能力變成組織資產的第一步。
cards.episode: An operator’s guide to product strategy | Chandra Janakiraman (CPO at VRChat, ex-Meta, Headspace, Zynga)

alts.quote: How do you get the foot in the door?" And what I've found is you should make the smallest ask possible, which is the opposite of what 95% of people do.
alts.zh: 「你要怎麼把腳踏進門？」我發現的是：你的請求要越小越好，這跟 95% 的人做的正好相反。

alts.quote: I want you to pull the hiring manager aside and say, "Hey, Lenny, you're the hiring manager. I've thought about what the role is. I want to make sure I'm understanding it correctly.
alts.zh: 我要你把用人主管拉到一旁說：「我想過這個職位到底是什麼，我想確認我理解得對不對。我可以跟你分享一下嗎？」

alts.quote: The other exercise I used to take my students through was what I called value denial. Now, what is it that you should be able to buy but you can't?
alts.zh: 我以前會帶學生做另一個練習，我叫它「價值缺口」：有什麼是你照理該買得到、卻買不到的？

cards.pattern: [問題群] becomes the problem cluster, and [正向詞] becomes the opportunity framing of it.
cards.quote: So difficulty finding things becomes the cluster, the problem cluster and discovery becomes the opportunity sort of framing of it.
cards.zh: 所以「東西找不到」就是那個問題群集，而「探索性（discovery）」就是它翻成機會的講法。
cards.why: 同一件事講成 problem 是抱怨，講成 opportunity 是提案——差別只在換一個名詞。先蒐集問題再統一翻面，比一開始就叫大家想機會更有料。
swaps: The problem is X; the opportunity we'd call Y.
Framed positively, that whole cluster is just [名詞].
cards.pmNote: problem cluster → opportunity area 的翻面，是把 user pain 變成 roadmap 主題的標準動作。
cards.episode: An operator’s guide to product strategy | Chandra Janakiraman (CPO at VRChat, ex-Meta, Headspace, Zynga)

alts.quote: Now, I'm biased when I'm going to say this, so take this with a pinch of salt, but I think the Accordion Method might be one of the things I'm the most proud of in my entire life.
alts.zh: 我要講的這件事我是有偏見的，所以你打個折聽——但我覺得手風琴法可能是我這輩子最引以為傲的東西之一。

alts.quote: The way I think about it is talent basically controls the slope of the curve, but most things are actually acquirable skills.
alts.zh: 我的想法是：天分只是決定那條曲線的斜率，但大多數東西其實都是可以習得的技能。

alts.quote: So my two pieces of advice, anybody that's actually trying to do this is, A, state the problem, and, B, don't call it a strategy, call it an action agenda.
alts.zh: 我給真的要動手的人兩個建議：A，把問題講出來；B，不要叫它策略，叫它「行動議程」。

cards.quote: What is the unconstrained perfect solution to this burning problem?
cards.zh: 如果完全不設限，這個燒眉毛的問題最完美的解法長什麼樣？
cards.why: unconstrained 這個字先把「做不到啦」的討論擋在門外，burning 則交代了為什麼值得想。Jeff 接著補一句「畫火柴人就行」，提案和降低參與門檻要同一句講完。
swaps: If we had no constraints at all, what does this look like?
Sketch the ideal version—stick figures are fine.
cards.pmNote: 願景階段用 Sharpie 不用 Figma：低保真才不會讓討論卡在畫面細節。
cards.episode: Building product at Stripe: craft, metrics, and customer obsession | Jeff Weinstein (Product lead)

alts.quote: If you start your story with 'Our company is,' you focus on your solution. If you start with 'The problem we are solving is,' then you focus on the problem.
alts.zh: 如果你的故事開頭是「我們公司是…」，你的焦點就在解法。如果開頭是「我們要解決的問題是…」，焦點就在問題上。

alts.quote: So my two pieces of advice, anybody that's actually trying to do this is, A, state the problem, and, B, don't call it a strategy, call it an action agenda.
alts.zh: 我給真的要動手的人兩個建議：A，把問題講出來；B，不要叫它策略，叫它「行動議程」。

alts.quote: So difficulty finding things becomes the cluster, the problem cluster and discovery becomes the opportunity sort of framing of it.
alts.zh: 所以「東西找不到」就是那個問題群集，而「探索性（discovery）」就是它翻成機會的講法。

cards.quote: We use our gut instinct on like, "Hey, no one's asking for this, in meaningful numbers at least. But we think this is going to be a big deal."
cards.zh: 我們就靠直覺判斷：「這件事沒什麼人在要求——至少沒有多到有意義。但我們覺得它會是個大事。」
cards.why: 自己先把最強的反對意見（沒人要）講出來，還加上 in meaningful numbers at least 這種精準的自我限縮，接著才用 But we think 把賭注押下去。先認弱點再下注，比硬掰需求可信。
swaps: Nobody's requesting this, and I still think we should build it.
There's no demand signal here yet—that's kind of the point.
cards.pmNote: 使用者不會要求他們不知道可能存在的東西；純需求驅動的 roadmap 天生保守。
cards.episode: Inside Bolt: From near-death to ~$40m ARR in 5 months—one of the fastest-growing products in history | Eric Simons (founder and CEO of StackBlitz)

alts.quote: I'm going to tell my boss, on Monday, that I think we should do that. I'm going to use a little social capital and say we should do this.
alts.zh: 我禮拜一會跟我主管講，我覺得這個該做。我會動用一點我的政治額度，去替它說話。

alts.quote: My most controversial opinion is that I think that AI is as big a deal as the internet or mobile. And only as big a deal as the internet or mobile.
alts.zh: 我最有爭議的一個看法是：AI 跟網路、行動裝置一樣重大——而且也「只」跟它們一樣重大而已。

alts.quote: I think a lot of people think about markets almost like these bodies of water. And it's like, "Oh, it's this big body of water that we're going after." And I actually think that the most interesting markets, you have to think of them like currents.
alts.zh: 很多人把市場想成一片水域，覺得「喔，我們要去攻的是這一大片水」。但我覺得最有意思的市場，你得把它想成水流。

cards.pattern: So this is the simplest way to [做某事] that's ever existed.
cards.quote: So this is the simplest way to build a web app that's ever existed.
cards.zh: 所以這是有史以來做一個 web app 最簡單的方式。
cards.why: 最高級（simplest / ever existed）在英文商業場合是可以講的，但要跟前面的實作 demo 綁在一起講才不算吹牛。台灣人通常不敢下這種斷言，結果聽眾記不住重點。
swaps: This is the fastest anyone has ever been able to [動作].
I don't think there's ever been a lower-friction way to do this.
cards.pmNote: 一句話的 positioning statement 要能被 demo 當場驗證，否則就是行銷噪音。
cards.episode: Inside Bolt: From near-death to ~$40m ARR in 5 months—one of the fastest-growing products in history | Eric Simons (founder and CEO of StackBlitz)

alts.quote: Here's the thing that I think is the easiest to change, is to realize the only thing that's ever supposed to happen in a meeting is the discussion part.
alts.zh: 我覺得最容易改的是這件事：認清一場會議裡唯一該發生的，只有「討論」。

alts.quote: the best way to get feedback from people is not by asking what they think, but to put something concrete in front of them and then have them react to it, right?
alts.zh: 要拿到回饋，最好的方式不是問人家怎麼想，而是先擺一個具體的東西在他面前，讓他反應，對吧？

alts.quote: The old way I think is shitty. I think it's broken, and I haven't found anything out there that is innovating on this.
alts.zh: 舊的做法我覺得很爛。我覺得它是壞的，而且我沒看到市面上有任何人在改良它。

cards.quote: There are periods of time where you have to make judgment calls that are not going to be the consensus view. You got to have confidence in your convictions on how to best play the hand.
cards.zh: 有些時期你必須做出不會是主流看法的判斷。你得對自己怎麼打這手牌有信心。
cards.why: not going to be the consensus view 是很體面的講法——不說別人錯，只說「這次共識不站在我這邊」。play the hand 的牌局比喻把決策講成「有限資訊下的取捨」，而不是自信爆棚。
swaps: This won't be the popular call, and I still think it's the right one.
I know I'm offside on this one.
cards.pmNote: 逆共識決策要事後可檢驗：講清楚「如果我錯了會看到什麼」，才不是純賭。
cards.episode: Inside Bolt: From near-death to ~$40m ARR in 5 months—one of the fastest-growing products in history | Eric Simons (founder and CEO of StackBlitz)

alts.quote: In a world where it's easier to build things, it's more important to make sure that your time is spent figuring out what you should be building in the first place.
alts.zh: 在一個「東西越來越好做」的世界裡，更重要的是先確保你把時間花在想清楚「到底該做什麼」。

alts.quote: Most people are missing the most important slide of their presentation. The most important slide of your presentation is the first slide. This slide is going to be presented for the longest period of time.
alts.zh: 大部分人都漏掉了簡報裡最重要的那一頁。你簡報最重要的一頁，是第一頁。因為那一頁會在螢幕上停留最久。

alts.quote: My take on empty vessel names is they can be really memorable and they can be evocative of the emotion, but you have to do a lot more marketing work over time to make it mean something.
alts.zh: 我對「空殼型名字」的看法是：它們可以很好記、也能勾起情緒，但你得花更多行銷力氣，久了才會有意義。

cards.pattern: Every other [同類] has [X]. [我們這個] had nothing.
cards.quote: Every other platform, Mac has Xcode. Windows has Visual Studio. The web had nothing.
cards.zh: 其他每個平台都有：Mac 有 Xcode，Windows 有 Visual Studio。網頁什麼都沒有。
cards.why: 三個短句排比 + 最後一句急煞，是英文論證最省力的「缺口」寫法。不用形容詞，光靠清單就把空缺講得很痛。
swaps: Everyone else has a [X]. We have nothing.
Look at the list: A has it, B has it, C has it. Not us.
cards.pmNote: 機會評估最有力的證據，常常是「同類都有、只有這裡沒有」的結構性空缺。
cards.episode: Inside Bolt: From near-death to ~$40m ARR in 5 months—one of the fastest-growing products in history | Eric Simons (founder and CEO of StackBlitz)

alts.quote: That's solving a problem for the company. That's not solving a career growth issue for an individual. And I think people who want to be promoted need to think in that orientation versus the other.
alts.zh: 那是在解決公司的問題，不是在解決個人的職涯成長問題。想升遷的人要用前面那種角度思考，不是後面那種。

alts.quote: I genuinely believe that every idea is awesome, but that doesn't mean I can do every idea.
alts.zh: 我真心覺得每個點子都很棒——但那不代表我每個都能做。

alts.quote: Every time that you hire someone new, mark your calendars for 30 days down the road and ask yourself one question: knowing what I know today, would I hire this person?
alts.zh: 每次你雇了新人，就在行事曆上標記三十天後，然後問自己一個問題：以我今天知道的事情，我還會雇這個人嗎？

cards.pattern: If a picture is worth a thousand words, [更強的東西] is worth millions.
cards.quote: Because that just, if a picture is worth a thousand words, a live actual demo is worth millions.
cards.zh: 因為如果一張圖值一千字，那一個真的能跑的 demo 就值一百萬字。
cards.why: 把對方已經內建的老諺語當跳板，只換掉最後一格，聽眾零成本就接受了你的排序。這是「借梗升級」的標準句型。
swaps: If a demo is worth a thousand mocks, a live one is worth ten thousand.
If data beats opinions, a working prototype beats data.
cards.pmNote: PRD 附一個可點的 prototype，比寫十頁規格更能消除跨職能理解落差。
cards.episode: Inside Bolt: From near-death to ~$40m ARR in 5 months—one of the fastest-growing products in history | Eric Simons (founder and CEO of StackBlitz)

alts.quote: My sense is if you want work-life balance, don't join one of these companies, because that's just not the way they work.
alts.zh: 我的感覺是，如果你想要工作生活平衡，就別加入這種公司，因為它們就不是那樣運作的。

alts.quote: And if you don't have them on your growth roadmap, you are going to be in some really big trouble over the next year to two years because your cost of acquisition is only going to go up.
alts.zh: 如果你的成長路線圖上沒有這些東西，未來一到兩年你會陷入大麻煩，因為你的獲客成本只會一路往上。

alts.quote: And so ever since then, we've been automating jobs and creating new jobs, and you can always see the job that's going to go away, and you don't know the new job because it doesn't exist yet.
alts.zh: 從那時候到現在，我們一直在自動化舊工作、也一直在長出新工作；而你永遠看得到那個要消失的工作，看不到新的，因為它還不存在。

cards.pattern: How big is the market opportunity to [做這件事]? It's trillions of dollars. The world runs on [X].
cards.quote: How big is the market opportunity to rewrite the software world order? It's trillions of dollars, or something, right? The world runs on software.
cards.zh: 重寫整個軟體世界秩序的市場機會有多大？大概是好幾兆美金吧。這個世界是靠軟體在跑的。
cards.why: 自問自答＋一句沒有數字的收尾（The world runs on X），比一堆 TAM 投影片有力。最後那句是「不證自明的前提」，聽眾會自己補完推論。
swaps: What's the ceiling here? Basically every company that [X].
How big can this get? Everyone who [做某事] is a customer.
cards.pmNote: opportunity sizing 講到最後要能回到一句常識句，否則數字沒人記得住。
cards.episode: Inside Bolt: From near-death to ~$40m ARR in 5 months—one of the fastest-growing products in history | Eric Simons (founder and CEO of StackBlitz)

alts.quote: And getting to $1,000,000 of GMV in a constrained market is a lot harder, takes longer, but it's actually the path to building something that endures.
alts.zh: 在一個受限的市場裡做到一百萬 GMV 難很多、也慢很多，但那才是真正做出能長久的東西的路。

alts.quote: In a world where it's easier to build things, it's more important to make sure that your time is spent figuring out what you should be building in the first place.
alts.zh: 在一個「東西越來越好做」的世界裡，更重要的是先確保你把時間花在想清楚「到底該做什麼」。

alts.quote: And if you don't have them on your growth roadmap, you are going to be in some really big trouble over the next year to two years because your cost of acquisition is only going to go up.
alts.zh: 如果你的成長路線圖上沒有這些東西，未來一到兩年你會陷入大麻煩，因為你的獲客成本只會一路往上。

cards.quote: My one piece of advice is when you're early on, your mindset should almost be like you're trying to create a word of mouth machine. If you can get that part right, everything else becomes significantly easier.
cards.zh: 我唯一的建議是：早期你的心態應該是在打造一台「口碑機器」。這件事只要做對，其他所有事都會變得輕鬆很多。
cards.why: 把一堆待辦收斂成單一槓桿的萬用句型。everything else becomes significantly easier 是承諾報酬，不是承諾成功——語氣穩，不會被事後打臉。
swaps: Nail that one thing and the rest gets a lot cheaper.
Everything downstream depends on getting this right first.
cards.pmNote: 口碑（organic）是所有成長槓桿的乘數，付費獲客只是放大器不是引擎。
cards.episode: “Dumbest idea I’ve heard” to $100M ARR: Inside the rise of Gamma | Grant Lee (CEO)

alts.quote: I'm just trying to argue this advice applied to a startup that's too early is actively not helpful.
alts.zh: 我只是想主張：把這套建議套在太早期的新創身上，是「主動有害」而不只是沒用。

alts.quote: The good news is, you're just like everybody else. The bad news is, you're mediocre just like everybody else.
alts.zh: 好消息是，你跟大家一樣；壞消息是，你跟大家一樣平庸。

alts.quote: I think with hiring, it's funny, man, there's so much hiring advice online and you read it and you're like, "Yeah, this is super obvious." And then when you live it, you're suddenly like, "Aah, this is why people say this."
alts.zh: 招人這件事很好笑，網路上一堆建議，你看的時候都覺得「這不是廢話嗎」。等你真的經歷過，才會突然懂「喔，原來大家是這個意思」。

cards.pattern: What can you give them in that first [30 seconds] that earns you the next [30 seconds]?
cards.quote: And so what can you give them in that first 30 seconds that earns you the next 30 seconds and then the next 30 seconds?
cards.zh: 所以在最初的 30 秒裡，你要給他什麼，才能換到接下來的 30 秒、再接下來的 30 秒？
cards.why: earns you 這個動詞是重點：把使用者的注意力講成「必須賺來的」而不是理所當然的。重複三次「next 30 seconds」製造節奏，讓抽象原則變成可以複誦的口號。
swaps: Every screen has to buy you the next screen.
What do we give them up front that buys us the right to keep going?
cards.pmNote: onboarding 的目標不是教學，是盡快交付一次價值以換取繼續使用的許可。
cards.episode: “Dumbest idea I’ve heard” to $100M ARR: Inside the rise of Gamma | Grant Lee (CEO)

alts.quote: In a world where it's easier to build things, it's more important to make sure that your time is spent figuring out what you should be building in the first place.
alts.zh: 在一個「東西越來越好做」的世界裡，更重要的是先確保你把時間花在想清楚「到底該做什麼」。

alts.quote: And if you don't have them on your growth roadmap, you are going to be in some really big trouble over the next year to two years because your cost of acquisition is only going to go up.
alts.zh: 如果你的成長路線圖上沒有這些東西，未來一到兩年你會陷入大麻煩，因為你的獲客成本只會一路往上。

alts.quote: Most people are missing the most important slide of their presentation. The most important slide of your presentation is the first slide. This slide is going to be presented for the longest period of time.
alts.zh: 大部分人都漏掉了簡報裡最重要的那一頁。你簡報最重要的一頁，是第一頁。因為那一頁會在螢幕上停留最久。

cards.pattern: If your goal is [數字目標], then that becomes the goal. The goal is no longer [真正想要的].
cards.quote: If your goal is to double in headcount and add a hundred people to the company, then that becomes the goal. The goal is no longer to add the best people.
cards.zh: 如果你的目標是人數翻倍、加一百個人，那「一百個人」就會變成目標本身。目標就不再是找最好的人了。
cards.why: 同一個字 goal 重複三次，把「目標錯置」這個抽象問題講到具體。第二句用 no longer 點名被犧牲掉的那個東西，是反對錯誤 KPI 最乾淨的講法。
swaps: Set that as the target and the target is what you'll get—not the outcome.
The metric becomes the mission, and the mission quietly leaves.
cards.pmNote: 設 KPI 前先問「這個數字被最大化時，什麼會被犧牲」——Goodhart's law 的實務版。
cards.episode: “Dumbest idea I’ve heard” to $100M ARR: Inside the rise of Gamma | Grant Lee (CEO)

alts.quote: That's solving a problem for the company. That's not solving a career growth issue for an individual. And I think people who want to be promoted need to think in that orientation versus the other.
alts.zh: 那是在解決公司的問題，不是在解決個人的職涯成長問題。想升遷的人要用前面那種角度思考，不是後面那種。

alts.quote: He thinks that a lot of the best recruiters in the world or the companies that attract talent, they put out this distinctive bad signal and it has to turn some people off. That's the key of a good, bad signal.
alts.zh: 他認為最會吸引人才的公司，都會刻意放出一個「不討喜的訊號」，而且一定要有人被勸退。這才是好的壞訊號的重點。

alts.quote: In economics, people only do what their incentives told them to do. Broadly speaking, that is what they do. You get what you set out to measure.
alts.zh: 在經濟學裡，人只會做他們的誘因叫他們做的事。大致上就是這樣。你量什麼，就會得到什麼。

cards.pattern: A lot of people think about [X] on the [A] side, but the same thing applies on the [B] side.
cards.quote: A lot of founders think about not wanting to have a leaky bucket on the product side, but the same thing applies on the team side.
cards.zh: 很多創辦人都很在意產品端不要有「破桶子」，但同樣的道理在團隊這一端也成立。
cards.why: 把對方已經接受的比喻，原封不動搬到新的領域，是最省力的說服——你不用重新論證比喻本身。leaky bucket 一詞，聽的人腦中已經有畫面。
swaps: We measure churn on customers; nobody measures churn on teammates.
Same leak, different bucket.
cards.pmNote: 人員流動的隱形成本是脈絡損失（tribal knowledge），比重新招募的顯性成本高得多。
cards.episode: “Dumbest idea I’ve heard” to $100M ARR: Inside the rise of Gamma | Grant Lee (CEO)

alts.quote: Not having things be your idea I think is really powerful. I just talked to 50 customers who all yelled the same thing.
alts.zh: 讓這件事「不是你的點子」其實非常有力。我剛跟五十個客戶談過，他們全都在吼同一件事。

alts.quote: That sounds cliche. I think a lot of founders and startup people like to talk about the mission, and I get it, and I think it's real. But I really mean it.
alts.zh: 我知道這聽起來很老套。很多創辦人都愛談使命，我懂，我也覺得那是真的。但我是真心這樣講。

alts.quote: So I think the answer is a lot with a big if, with an if you can get people to do it.
alts.zh: 我覺得答案是「效果很大」，但有一個很大的 if：前提是你真的能讓人去做。

cards.quote: People don't really get out of bed for their second problem. They get out of bed for their first problem.
cards.zh: 人不會為了自己的第二號問題早起。他們只會為第一號問題早起。
cards.why: 兩句對仗、只換一個字，是英文格言體的標準做法——好記、好轉述，別人開會時會替你複誦。用具體動作（get out of bed）代替抽象的 priority。
swaps: Nobody switches tools for their third-biggest pain.
If it's not their number one, it's not a purchase.
cards.pmNote: 產品要瞄準使用者的第一順位痛點，第二順位的問題往往能忍到永遠。
cards.episode: Building product at Stripe: craft, metrics, and customer obsession | Jeff Weinstein (Product lead)

alts.quote: That's solving a problem for the company. That's not solving a career growth issue for an individual. And I think people who want to be promoted need to think in that orientation versus the other.
alts.zh: 那是在解決公司的問題，不是在解決個人的職涯成長問題。想升遷的人要用前面那種角度思考，不是後面那種。

alts.quote: Most people are missing the most important slide of their presentation. The most important slide of your presentation is the first slide. This slide is going to be presented for the longest period of time.
alts.zh: 大部分人都漏掉了簡報裡最重要的那一頁。你簡報最重要的一頁，是第一頁。因為那一頁會在螢幕上停留最久。

alts.quote: That's the first-order thinking. Second-order thinking is thinking through the maintenance of that feature. The third-order thinking, which turns out to be the most important, is the other costs that complexity adds.
alts.zh: 那是第一層思考。第二層是去想這個功能的維護成本。第三層——結果證明是最重要的一層——是複雜度帶來的其他成本。

cards.pattern: Craft is a dessert that you get after the meal of [先要成立的前提].
cards.quote: And I think craft is a dessert that you get after the meal of does your thing solve a real problem in the world and are people clamoring, needing it badly?
cards.zh: 我覺得「做工精緻」是甜點，前面那頓正餐是：你的東西有沒有解決世界上真實的問題、有沒有人急著要它。
cards.why: 用一個排序感很強的比喻（dessert / meal）來擋掉錯誤的優先順序，而不是直接說「你們搞錯重點」。要否定同事的偏好時，比喻比指正安全太多。
swaps: Polish is the dessert; product-market fit is the meal.
That's a second-order problem—we haven't solved the first-order one.
cards.pmNote: 在 PMF 前投資 craft 是常見的資源錯置：再美的介面也救不了沒人需要的產品。
cards.episode: Building product at Stripe: craft, metrics, and customer obsession | Jeff Weinstein (Product lead)

alts.quote: That's solving a problem for the company. That's not solving a career growth issue for an individual. And I think people who want to be promoted need to think in that orientation versus the other.
alts.zh: 那是在解決公司的問題，不是在解決個人的職涯成長問題。想升遷的人要用前面那種角度思考，不是後面那種。

alts.quote: He thinks that a lot of the best recruiters in the world or the companies that attract talent, they put out this distinctive bad signal and it has to turn some people off. That's the key of a good, bad signal.
alts.zh: 他認為最會吸引人才的公司，都會刻意放出一個「不討喜的訊號」，而且一定要有人被勸退。這才是好的壞訊號的重點。

alts.quote: That sounds cliche. I think a lot of founders and startup people like to talk about the mission, and I get it, and I think it's real. But I really mean it.
alts.zh: 我知道這聽起來很老套。很多創辦人都愛談使命，我懂，我也覺得那是真的。但我是真心這樣講。

cards.pattern: That is not a tier three issue. [使用者原話] should be sending alerts off in your whole psyche.
cards.quote: That is not a tier three issue. I am not able to run my business without getting on an airplane should be sending alerts off in your whole psyche.
cards.zh: 那不是什麼三級小事。「我不搭飛機就沒辦法開公司」這句話，應該讓你整個腦袋警鈴大作。
cards.why: 先用 not a tier three issue 把對方可能的低估講死，再把使用者原話當成句子的主詞丟回來。用別人的話當主詞，等於讓證據自己說話。
swaps: This isn't a papercut. This is a blocker.
If a customer says that sentence out loud, everything else stops.
cards.pmNote: 問題分級要用「使用者被卡住的程度」而不是「工程修復成本」來排。
cards.episode: Building product at Stripe: craft, metrics, and customer obsession | Jeff Weinstein (Product lead)

alts.quote: This sounds, again, very simple but just like how you wouldn't fly a plane without instruments, why would you run your products without understanding the instrumentation and how it's doing.
alts.zh: 這聽起來很簡單，但就像你不會沒有儀表就開飛機一樣，為什麼你會在完全不看數據的情況下經營產品？

alts.quote: But human beings are notoriously good at trading off the long run just to feel good in the short run. That's why we're all eating chocolate and cupcakes and stuff that we know is bad for us because it feels good.
alts.zh: 人類非常擅長犧牲長期，只為了短期舒服。所以我們才都在吃明知不好的巧克力跟杯子蛋糕。

alts.quote: He thinks that a lot of the best recruiters in the world or the companies that attract talent, they put out this distinctive bad signal and it has to turn some people off. That's the key of a good, bad signal.
alts.zh: 他認為最會吸引人才的公司，都會刻意放出一個「不討喜的訊號」，而且一定要有人被勸退。這才是好的壞訊號的重點。

cards.pattern: Not having things be your idea is really powerful. I just talked to 50 customers who all yelled the same thing.
cards.quote: Not having things be your idea I think is really powerful. I just talked to 50 customers who all yelled the same thing.
cards.zh: 讓這件事「不是你的點子」其實非常有力。我剛跟五十個客戶談過，他們全都在吼同一件事。
cards.why: 把提案的作者從自己換成客戶，反對你就變成反對客戶。yelled 這個動詞比 said 有情緒溫度，讓證據聽起來有壓力。
swaps: This isn't my opinion—it's what 40 people told us in a row.
I'm just the messenger here; the pattern is theirs.
cards.pmNote: 在大公司推新東西，去掉個人色彩可以降低政治阻力，也讓案子在你調職後還活著。
cards.episode: Building product at Stripe: craft, metrics, and customer obsession | Jeff Weinstein (Product lead)

alts.quote: And the third thing is that I really believe that... I don't believe. I think we all know at this point that the most important thing for the growth of anything tech is retention.
alts.zh: 第三件事是我真的相信——不，不是相信。我覺得到這個時間點大家都已經知道了：科技產品成長最重要的就是留存。

alts.quote: A lot of founders think about not wanting to have a leaky bucket on the product side, but the same thing applies on the team side.
alts.zh: 很多創辦人都很在意產品端不要有「破桶子」，但同樣的道理在團隊這一端也成立。

alts.quote: So we can think there's people who don't know about it, there's people who do know about it but don't do it, and then there's people who do know about it, but do do it. And it's that last group that's so tiny.
alts.zh: 可以分成三種人：不知道這件事的、知道但不做的、知道又真的去做的。而最後那一群小得可憐。

cards.pattern: Intrinsically [X] has no business value. It's basically a document with a few words. It starts accumulating value as you generate results.
cards.quote: Intrinsically strategy has no business value. It's basically a document with a few words. And I think it starts accumulating value as you generate business impact and results.
cards.zh: 策略本身沒有任何商業價值。它就是一份寫了幾個字的文件。它是在你做出business impact 之後，才開始累積價值的。
cards.why: 先自己踩自己一腳（no business value），信任度立刻上升，第三句的正面主張才站得住。這是資深者常用的「先卸武裝再下結論」。
swaps: On its own the doc is worth nothing; it earns value through execution.
Strategy is a hypothesis until the numbers say otherwise.
cards.pmNote: 策略文件的價值要靠執行結果回填；沒有驗證機制的策略等同於願望清單。
cards.episode: An operator’s guide to product strategy | Chandra Janakiraman (CPO at VRChat, ex-Meta, Headspace, Zynga)

alts.quote: So I think if you take all those steps back and you look at this from a journey perspective, there's no way that it won't be impacting search. It's just going to be hard to find.
alts.zh: 所以我覺得，只要你退開幾步、用「使用者旅程」的角度看，它不可能不影響搜尋。只是那個影響很難被指認出來。

alts.quote: I think with hiring, it's funny, man, there's so much hiring advice online and you read it and you're like, "Yeah, this is super obvious." And then when you live it, you're suddenly like, "Aah, this is why people say this."
alts.zh: 招人這件事很好笑，網路上一堆建議，你看的時候都覺得「這不是廢話嗎」。等你真的經歷過，才會突然懂「喔，原來大家是這個意思」。

alts.quote: So we can think there's people who don't know about it, there's people who do know about it but don't do it, and then there's people who do know about it, but do do it. And it's that last group that's so tiny.
alts.zh: 可以分成三種人：不知道這件事的、知道但不做的、知道又真的去做的。而最後那一群小得可憐。

cards.pattern: There's not even [N] [單位] on the planet. But there are [更大的數字] you can [做某事] on.
cards.quote: I mean there's not even a 100 million VMs to rent, on the planet. But there are a billion devices that you can run this stuff on.
cards.zh: 地球上根本租不到一億台虛擬機。但可以跑這些東西的裝置有十億台。
cards.why: 兩個數字對撞，中間只放一個 But——不解釋、不加形容詞，讓量級差自己說話。這種「供給上限 vs 需求規模」的證據結構在技術決策辯論裡特別好用。
swaps: There aren't enough X in existence. There are billions of Y.
The ceiling on that path is [數字]. This path doesn't have one.
cards.pmNote: 架構選型時，先算「這條路的物理上限」比較單位經濟更早見真章。
cards.episode: Inside Bolt: From near-death to ~$40m ARR in 5 months—one of the fastest-growing products in history | Eric Simons (founder and CEO of StackBlitz)

alts.quote: There's an Arab saying that I like that says, 'He who forecasts the future lies, even if he tells the truth.'
alts.zh: 我很喜歡一句阿拉伯諺語：「預測未來的人是在說謊，即使他說的是實話。」

alts.quote: There was this unwritten rule of thumb that, hey, if it's not going to generate more than $100 million in revenue, it's not worth talking about it.
alts.zh: 當時有一條沒寫下來的潛規則：如果一件事帶不來一億美金以上的營收，就不值得拿出來討論。

alts.quote: Obviously in this case, it worked out great and there's survivorship bias and that doesn't mean that everyone should pivot all the time.
alts.zh: 當然這個案例後來結果很好，但這裡有倖存者偏誤，不代表每個人都該一直轉型。

cards.pattern: He had gotten a quote for [價格] and [時間]. He had done it in [更短時間] and spent [更少錢].
cards.quote: He had gotten a quote from an agency for this, it was going to be 30 grand, and take six months. He had done in three weeks, and I think he spent 300 bucks on Bolt for the thing.
cards.zh: 他之前跟外包公司報價，要三萬美金、做六個月。結果他三個星期就做完了，在 Bolt 上大概花了三百塊美金。
cards.why: 拿一個真人的兩組報價做前後對照，比任何 benchmark 都有說服力，因為對方無法質疑「基準怎麼定」。先講舊報價再講新事實，順序不能反。
swaps: The quote was X. We did it for Y.
Their estimate was six months. It shipped in three weeks.
cards.pmNote: 價值主張最有力的證據是同一位客戶的「替代方案報價」，而不是市場平均值。
cards.episode: Inside Bolt: From near-death to ~$40m ARR in 5 months—one of the fastest-growing products in history | Eric Simons (founder and CEO of StackBlitz)

alts.quote: If you say, 'I think this is going to take three months to launch' and I was thinking four weeks, you're never going to hear four weeks from me, ever.
alts.zh: 如果你說「我覺得要三個月」，而我原本想的是四週，那你永遠不會從我嘴裡聽到四週。永遠不會。

alts.quote: If you think about your last all hands, the last talk you saw, you probably don't remember much. In fact, I wager you might only remember one thing from that talk.
alts.zh: 回想你上一次的全員大會、上一場你聽的演講——你大概記不得多少。老實說，我敢賭你只記得一件事。

alts.quote: You could have all the usage data in the world, that's going to tell you what's actually happening in your product, but it doesn't tell you why.
alts.zh: 就算你握有全世界的使用數據，它只會告訴你產品裡實際發生了什麼，不會告訴你為什麼。

cards.pattern: We heard a couple comments, it was little murmurs. I didn't realize at the time that was the signal that we did not have [X].
cards.quote: We heard a couple comments from them, it was little murmurs. And I didn't realize at the time that was the signal that we did not have product market fit.
cards.zh: 我們只聽到他們零星幾句抱怨，就是一點小碎念而已。我當時沒意識到，那正是我們沒有 PMF 的訊號。
cards.why: 把「反應很小」本身當成證據，是台灣人最少用、卻最有力的論證。murmurs（碎念）精準描述了「有回應但沒有溫度」，比說 not much feedback 具體太多。
swaps: Nobody complained. That was the finding.
The silence was the data point we should have read.
cards.pmNote: 服務中斷時的客訴強度是免費的 PMF 量測；沒人抱怨代表產品可被替代。
cards.episode: Building product at Stripe: craft, metrics, and customer obsession | Jeff Weinstein (Product lead)

alts.quote: They didn't actually put user acquisition spend behind TikTok until they had a product that was retentive, and then they know that they really wanted to maximize that. But every other social product has grown organically.
alts.zh: 他們是等到產品真的留得住人，才把獲客預算砸到 TikTok 上，然後才想把它極大化。但其他所有社群產品都是有機長出來的。

alts.quote: If the model gets it right 60% of the time, you build a very different product than if the model gets it right 95% of the time versus if the model gets it right 99.5% of the time.
alts.zh: 如果模型有六成的時候會做對，你做出來的產品，跟九成五、跟九成九點五的時候，會是完全不同的三個產品。

alts.quote: The ultimate definition for me today of the love that somebody has for our product is they're willing to put their reputation on the line by telling people about it.
alts.zh: 對我來說，一個人有多愛你的產品，最終極的定義就是：他願意拿自己的名聲去替你背書，主動跟別人講。

cards.pattern: For [價格], it would need to solve [X].
cards.quote: She might say, "Whoa, whoa, wait a second. Yeah, I like this thing, but not $10,000. For $10,000, it would need to solve X."
cards.zh: 她可能會說：「等一下、等一下。這東西我是喜歡，但不值一萬美金。要一萬美金的話，它得能解決 X 才行。」
cards.why: 把價格丟出去，讓對方自己說出真正的需求門檻——比任何訪談問題都準。這招的關鍵是價格要高到讓客氣話失效。
swaps: At that price, what would it have to do?
If this were $50k, what's the one thing it must nail?
cards.pmNote: 願付價格是最誠實的需求排序器；問「喜不喜歡」永遠得到客氣答案。
cards.episode: Building product at Stripe: craft, metrics, and customer obsession | Jeff Weinstein (Product lead)

alts.quote: Yeah, I mean, I can't promise that works for everyone, but again, in the very bespoke situation with Rujul, it worked really well.
alts.zh: 我不能保證這對每個人都有效，但在 Rujul 那個很特定的情況下，效果非常好。

alts.quote: And my first question to him as a product guy is like, "Wow, would you give me a million dollars to solve this problem?"
alts.zh: 身為做產品的人，我第一個問題是：「哇，那你願意花一百萬美元讓我解掉這個問題嗎？」

alts.quote: It's about saying, okay, if we have these themes of stuff that we want to work on, what do we know with confidence because the data tells us and what do we need to understand because we don't have the data?
alts.zh: 重點是要問：在我們想做的這些主題裡，哪些是數據講得夠清楚、我們有把握的？哪些是因為沒數據，所以還得先搞懂的？

cards.quote: And by the way, ready to pay is different than paying. Significantly different, significantly different.
cards.zh: 順帶一提，「準備好要付錢」跟「已經付錢」是兩回事。差非常多，非常多。
cards.why: 重複同一個詞兩次是英文口語裡的強調鍵，比加副詞自然。要打掉別人拿「客戶說願意買」當證據時，這句是最短的反擊。
swaps: Intent isn't revenue.
A signed LOI is not a wire transfer.
cards.pmNote: 驗證需求時只認已完成的交易；意向書、口頭承諾都屬於未驗證假設。
cards.episode: Building product at Stripe: craft, metrics, and customer obsession | Jeff Weinstein (Product lead)

alts.quote: Data is more like a compass than a GPS. If you look at data as a way of giving you the answer, you're always wrong. Wrong or slow, or sometimes both.
alts.zh: 數據比較像指南針，不是導航。如果你把數據當成會給你答案的東西，你不是錯就是慢，有時候兩者都有。

alts.quote: The basic principle with laser is that willpower is never going to win, and there's great research on this, but for now just trust me, you're not going to white-knuckle your way through not looking at Twitter when you're trying to work.
alts.zh: laser 的基本原理是：意志力永遠贏不了。這方面有很多很好的研究，但現在你先信我——你不可能靠硬撐來讓自己工作時不看 Twitter。

alts.quote: prospects who meet you in person have 10 to 30% higher willingness to pay than those who didn't. Churn for those folks who you meet in person is typically 20% lower than those folks who have never met you.
alts.zh: 跟你當面見過的潛在客戶，付費意願會高出 10 到 30%；見過面的客戶流失率通常比沒見過的低 20%。

cards.pattern: We took that number from [X]% to [Y]%. And you can look at [商業指標] plotted on the same timeframe and it's the same shape.
cards.quote: And over about 18 months, we took that number from 15% to 85. We basically just flipped it. And you can look at the market share plotted on the same timeframe and it's the same shape.
cards.zh: 大概十八個月，我們把那個數字從 15% 拉到 85%。基本上就是整個翻過來。而且你把市占率放在同一段時間軸上看，形狀是一樣的。
cards.why: 自己的過程指標＋外部的商業指標「同一個形狀」，是把 output 連到 outcome 最漂亮的證法。same shape 這個講法比 correlation 口語又不誇大。
swaps: We moved it from X to Y, and revenue traced the same curve.
Plot them together—the two lines rhyme.
cards.pmNote: 北極星指標要能和商業結果同形；否則就是團隊自嗨的過程指標。
cards.episode: Building product at Stripe: craft, metrics, and customer obsession | Jeff Weinstein (Product lead)

alts.quote: But you should know when it's a vanity metric versus is this core to our growth engine? If this number goes up, does it mean the product is working?
alts.zh: 但你要分得出來：這是虛榮指標，還是我們成長引擎的核心？如果這個數字上升，代表產品真的成立了嗎？

alts.quote: It's not because my life is more interesting. It's because I have a better lens and I understand what to look for.
alts.zh: 不是因為我的生活變得比較精彩，是因為我的鏡頭變好了，我知道該找什麼。

alts.quote: Whenever you talk to people who are at the company, they're always try to tell you the best version of the company. It's on you to triangulate that information, but you need both sides.
alts.zh: 你去問還在公司裡的人，他們永遠給你公司最好的那個版本。要交叉比對是你自己的責任，但兩邊的說法你都得聽到。

cards.pattern: If you accidentally leaked your dashboard, your customer would be ecstatic to learn that's what you were measuring.
cards.quote: And that if you accidentally leaked your dashboard to them, your customer would be ecstatic to learn that that's what you were measuring the whole time.
cards.zh: 而且如果你不小心把儀表板外流給客戶，他們看到你一直在量的是這個，只會欣喜若狂。
cards.why: 用一個「洩漏測試」來判斷指標好壞，把抽象的 customer-centric 變成可以當場執行的檢查。假設情境（if you accidentally…）讓批評不指向任何人。
swaps: Would you be proud to show this dashboard to the customer?
If this leaked, would it read as care or as extraction?
cards.pmNote: 好指標的檢驗法：客戶看到你在量它，會覺得被在乎而不是被榨取。
cards.episode: Building product at Stripe: craft, metrics, and customer obsession | Jeff Weinstein (Product lead)

alts.quote: If you present data with authority and that data is ridiculous, you don't just not get benefit for that. You lose a whole bunch of brownie points.
alts.zh: 如果你很有底氣地端出一份數據，結果那份數據很荒謬，你不只是沒加到分，還會倒扣一大堆好感度。

alts.quote: It's not a statistically significant survey in general, but it will never go to 99% and one. That's fairly indicative that people are clicking the links, which surprises me.
alts.zh: 這份調查在統計上不算顯著，但它也不可能是 99 比 1。這蠻能說明大家真的有在點那些連結——這讓我有點意外。

alts.quote: Number one is actually measuring it. I can't tell you how many times I suggest to a founder to track cohorts and that's a new thing.
alts.zh: 第一件事其實是去量它。我真的數不清有多少次我建議創辦人追蹤 cohort，結果那對他們是全新的東西。

cards.quote: I find proof of existence to be an incredibly powerful proof, rather than proof by theory or proof by debate. It's like, "Look, we did it one time."
cards.zh: 我覺得「存在性證明」比「理論證明」或「辯論證明」都有力太多。就是那種：「你看，我們真的做成一次了。」
cards.why: 借數學的 proof 三分法來分類論證強度，一句話就把會議室裡的空談降級。rather than 後面連放兩個對照組，殺傷力比只放一個大。
swaps: One working instance beats an hour of debate.
Let's stop arguing and produce one real example.
cards.pmNote: 跨部門僵局最快的解法是做出一個可驗證的最小實例，而不是再開一次對齊會。
cards.episode: Building product at Stripe: craft, metrics, and customer obsession | Jeff Weinstein (Product lead)

alts.quote: So when it's a ratio and you decrease the denominator, the value of the ratio grows. And so, how do you decrease the denominator in this case where time is the denominator is you start working on things that take less time.
alts.zh: 這是一個比值，分母變小，比值就變大。那在這裡分母是時間，你要怎麼讓分母變小？你就開始挑那些花比較少時間的事情做。

alts.quote: Turns out 90% of the time that we get distracted, it's not because of what's happening outside of us, but that most distraction begins from within boredom, loneliness, fatigue, uncertainty, anxiety.
alts.zh: 結果發現，我們分心的時候有 90% 不是因為外面發生了什麼，而是分心多半從內在開始——無聊、孤單、疲倦、不確定、焦慮。

alts.quote: It's not because my life is more interesting. It's because I have a better lens and I understand what to look for.
alts.zh: 不是因為我的生活變得比較精彩，是因為我的鏡頭變好了，我知道該找什麼。

cards.pattern: Is this a vanity metric versus is this core to our growth engine? If this number goes up, does it mean the product is working?
cards.quote: But you should know when it's a vanity metric versus is this core to our growth engine? If this number goes up, does it mean the product is working?
cards.zh: 但你要分得出來：這是虛榮指標，還是我們成長引擎的核心？如果這個數字上升，代表產品真的成立了嗎？
cards.why: 第二句是可以直接搬去任何會議的測試題——把「這指標好不好」翻譯成「它上升代表什麼」。用問句質疑指標，比說「這是虛榮指標」不傷人。
swaps: If this doubled tomorrow, would anything real change?
Does this number moving tell us the thing is working?
cards.pmNote: 虛榮指標的判準：上升時無法推論出任何使用者行為改變。
cards.episode: “Dumbest idea I’ve heard” to $100M ARR: Inside the rise of Gamma | Grant Lee (CEO)

alts.quote: It's about saying, okay, if we have these themes of stuff that we want to work on, what do we know with confidence because the data tells us and what do we need to understand because we don't have the data?
alts.zh: 重點是要問：在我們想做的這些主題裡，哪些是數據講得夠清楚、我們有把握的？哪些是因為沒數據，所以還得先搞懂的？

alts.quote: If you tell someone, 'This is the problem I'm going to address,' and they will tell you, 'Oh, I know someone that has this problem,' it's not a real problem.
alts.zh: 如果你跟人說「這是我要解決的問題」，對方回你「喔，我知道有誰有這個問題」——那它就不是真問題。

alts.quote: So when it's a ratio and you decrease the denominator, the value of the ratio grows. And so, how do you decrease the denominator in this case where time is the denominator is you start working on things that take less time.
alts.zh: 這是一個比值，分母變小，比值就變大。那在這裡分母是時間，你要怎麼讓分母變小？你就開始挑那些花比較少時間的事情做。

cards.quote: People aren't even getting to the third screen. They're stuck on the first screen because they can't even find the button that we think is so dead obvious.
cards.zh: 使用者根本走不到第三個畫面。他們卡在第一個畫面，因為連我們自認為超級明顯的那顆按鈕都找不到。
cards.why: 把使用者研究結果講成一個具體到不能反駁的畫面（第三頁／第一頁／那顆按鈕）。we think is so dead obvious 是自嘲，把團隊也拉進被打臉的行列，減少防衛心。
swaps: Nobody made it past step one.
Zero out of twenty found the button.
cards.pmNote: 可用性問題要用「幾人／幾步」呈現，比用滿意度分數更能推動修正。
cards.episode: “Dumbest idea I’ve heard” to $100M ARR: Inside the rise of Gamma | Grant Lee (CEO)

alts.quote: And when we do surveys, we'd find that 20, 30, 40% of people thought they were officially associated because how they were using our logo and presenting the brand and everything like that was very confusing to people.
alts.zh: 我們做調查的時候會發現，兩成、三成、四成的人以為他們跟我們有官方關係，因為他們用我們 logo 和呈現品牌的方式讓人很混淆。

alts.quote: So when you do a pros and cons list, but they're skewed and you are leaving some things out of the cons list, it makes the reader suspicious and they can't trust you anymore.
alts.zh: 當你列出優缺點，但列得偏頗、缺點那欄漏了東西，讀者就會起疑，然後就再也不信你了。

alts.quote: I think Peter Thiel actually says it more simply and elegantly, which is, 'You need to be right about something that other people think you're wrong about for a very long time.'
alts.zh: 我覺得 Peter Thiel 講得更簡潔漂亮：「你得在一件別人認為你錯的事情上，長時間地正確。」

cards.pattern: [產品] is this overnight success, [N] years in the making.
cards.quote: It was kind of like, Bolt's this overnight success, seven years in the making.
cards.zh: 大概就是那句：Bolt 是一個醞釀了七年的一夜爆紅。
cards.why: 把兩個互相矛盾的詞縫在一起（overnight / seven years），一句話同時交代了爆發力和苦工。這種自我矛盾式的標語特別容易被媒體和聽眾轉述。
swaps: A ten-year overnight success.
It looked instant. It took six years to get there.
cards.pmNote: 對外敘事要交代前置投入，否則會被誤讀成運氣，也會讓內部團隊的長期投資不被看見。
cards.episode: Inside Bolt: From near-death to ~$40m ARR in 5 months—one of the fastest-growing products in history | Eric Simons (founder and CEO of StackBlitz)

alts.quote: So I have my definition of success I came up with years ago. Success is making the people who believed in you look brilliant. That's it.
alts.zh: 我幾年前想出了自己對成功的定義。成功就是：讓當初相信你的人看起來很有眼光。就這樣。

alts.quote: He said, "I could have been a pretty good cartoonist or I could have been pretty good at business, but the fact that I was a cartoonist who understood business made me spectacularly great at making Dilbert."
alts.zh: 他說：「我可以當個還不錯的漫畫家，也可以當個還不錯的商業人，但因為我是一個懂商業的漫畫家，才讓我把呆伯特做到無人能及。」

alts.quote: You kind of come up thinking you're the protagonist. You can be the protagonist in your life, but in the story of your work of a company, you are probably not the protagonist.
alts.zh: 你一路長大都以為自己是主角。你在自己的人生裡可以是主角，但在公司這個故事裡，你多半不是主角。

cards.pattern: I was like, "Don't these people know [替代方案] exists?" And then it hit me. Those things are so complicated to use.
cards.quote: And I was like, "Don't these people know that Wix or Squarespace exists? Should I tell them?" And then it hit me. Those things are so complicated to use.
cards.zh: 我當時想：「這些人不知道有 Wix 或 Squarespace 嗎？要不要提醒他們一下？」然後我突然懂了——那些東西真的超難用。
cards.why: 先讓自己當笨蛋（我以為使用者搞錯了），再讓事實打臉自己，聽眾就會跟著一起「懂了」。And then it hit me 是英文敘事裡最好用的轉折開關。
swaps: I assumed they just didn't know better. Then I actually tried it myself.
My first reaction was to correct them. My second was to shut up and watch.
cards.pmNote: 使用者的「不合理行為」多半是在指出你沒看見的成本，不是無知。
cards.episode: Inside Bolt: From near-death to ~$40m ARR in 5 months—one of the fastest-growing products in history | Eric Simons (founder and CEO of StackBlitz)

alts.quote: Instacart signed up for Stripe with a Gmail address and then Covid happened and they delivered critical food to everyone when people were reasonably not allowed to go to the grocery store easily. So you just don't know what the next Gmail address is going to do.
alts.zh: Instacart 當年是用一個 Gmail 信箱註冊 Stripe 的；後來疫情來了，在大家不太能去超市的時候，是他們把關鍵的食物送到每個人手上。所以你根本不知道，下一個 Gmail 信箱會做出什麼。

alts.quote: If you're trying to do it, the best way to tell a story about something that you want people to understand is to do what I call speaking with adjacency, which means we're not going to match content to content.
alts.zh: 如果你想讓別人理解某件事，最好的說故事方式是我所謂的「用鄰近性說話」——意思是我們不會拿內容去對內容。

alts.quote: And one thing people make fun of me a lot for that I think is just a great example of extreme clarity is I never use bulleted lists because you can never refer to a bullet.
alts.zh: 有件事大家常笑我，但我覺得那正是「極度清楚」的最佳示範：我從來不用項目符號，因為你沒辦法指名某一個點。

cards.pattern: If someone dropped the food on your table, left, and never came with a bill, maybe I'm not going to recommend this to somebody else.
cards.quote: If someone just came by and dropped the food on your plate on the table, and just left and never came with a bill, I'm like, okay, maybe I'm not going to recommend this to somebody else.
cards.zh: 如果有人把菜往你桌上一放就走了，連帳單都沒來過，那我大概不會把這家推薦給別人。
cards.why: 用一個荒謬但完全具體的負面情境，去證明「產品好不等於體驗好」。台灣人講這件事通常用抽象詞（整體體驗、流程順暢），聽的人沒畫面。
swaps: Great food, no service—you still don't come back.
The product can be right and the experience still be broken.
cards.pmNote: onboarding 與收尾流程屬於產品體驗的一部分，會直接決定推薦意願。
cards.episode: “Dumbest idea I’ve heard” to $100M ARR: Inside the rise of Gamma | Grant Lee (CEO)

alts.quote: So I guess maybe for context, we had built this very nascent publisher motion where we were going out and helping people publish their rituals.
alts.zh: 先補個背景好了：我們當時做出了一套還很初期的「發布者」機制，我們會去幫大家把自己的儀式發布出來。

alts.quote: Instacart signed up for Stripe with a Gmail address and then Covid happened and they delivered critical food to everyone when people were reasonably not allowed to go to the grocery store easily. So you just don't know what the next Gmail address is going to do.
alts.zh: Instacart 當年是用一個 Gmail 信箱註冊 Stripe 的；後來疫情來了，在大家不太能去超市的時候，是他們把關鍵的食物送到每個人手上。所以你根本不知道，下一個 Gmail 信箱會做出什麼。

alts.quote: I think the hardest thing for a founder, challenge is not optional. You're going to be challenged, but the suffering is optional.
alts.zh: 對創辦人來說最難的是：挑戰不是選項，你一定會被挑戰；但要不要痛苦，是選項。

cards.quote: There's this thing from consumer advertising, which is you throw a consumer one egg, they can probably catch it. You throw them four or five eggs, they're probably going to drop all of them.
cards.zh: 廣告圈有個說法：你丟一顆蛋給消費者，他大概接得住；你一次丟四五顆，他大概會全部摔在地上。
cards.why: 一個五秒就懂的動作比喻，取代「訊息過載會降低轉換率」這種行話。全部用 you 當主詞，讓聽眾在腦中親自接那顆蛋。
swaps: One message lands. Five messages cancel each other out.
Give them one thing to hold.
cards.pmNote: 定位訊息一次只講一個價值主張，多講等於沒講。
cards.episode: “Dumbest idea I’ve heard” to $100M ARR: Inside the rise of Gamma | Grant Lee (CEO)

alts.quote: And after all of that, which clearly means they wanted it to work, they're like, "No, bye." What? Just on an emotional level, you got to go, "Wait a minute, that's terrible."
alts.zh: 經歷了這一整串——這明明代表他們很想讓它成功——結果他們說「不用了，掰」。蛤？光是情緒上你就該有反應：等一下，這超糟的。

alts.quote: You want to be that tree in the storm that is not so rigid that if the wind is too strong it's going to break in half, but not so flexible that it's going to swing every which direction as soon as there's a gust.
alts.zh: 你要當風暴裡的那棵樹——不要硬到風一大就攔腰折斷，也不要軟到一陣風來就往每個方向亂晃。

alts.quote: I think the hardest thing for a founder, challenge is not optional. You're going to be challenged, but the suffering is optional.
alts.zh: 對創辦人來說最難的是：挑戰不是選項，你一定會被挑戰；但要不要痛苦，是選項。

cards.pattern: The most valuable skill in [領域] is about to become obsolete.
cards.quote: And honestly, we kind came up with kind of a clickbaity sort of tweet. It was like the most valuable skill in business is about to become obsolete.
cards.zh: 老實說我們想了一個蠻標題黨的推文：「商業世界裡最有價值的技能，即將被淘汰。」
cards.why: 刻意留一個缺口（沒說是哪個技能），逼讀者點進來或留言反駁。Grant 自己用 clickbaity 承認手法，反而讓分享這招時不顯得油。
swaps: Everyone's about to stop doing [X]. Here's what replaces it.
The thing you're best at is about to stop mattering.
cards.pmNote: 發表新品時，製造可被反駁的觀點比宣布功能更容易取得演算法擴散。
cards.episode: “Dumbest idea I’ve heard” to $100M ARR: Inside the rise of Gamma | Grant Lee (CEO)

alts.quote: He said, "I could have been a pretty good cartoonist or I could have been pretty good at business, but the fact that I was a cartoonist who understood business made me spectacularly great at making Dilbert."
alts.zh: 他說：「我可以當個還不錯的漫畫家，也可以當個還不錯的商業人，但因為我是一個懂商業的漫畫家，才讓我把呆伯特做到無人能及。」

alts.quote: You kind of come up thinking you're the protagonist. You can be the protagonist in your life, but in the story of your work of a company, you are probably not the protagonist.
alts.zh: 你一路長大都以為自己是主角。你在自己的人生裡可以是主角，但在公司這個故事裡，你多半不是主角。

alts.quote: So I have my definition of success I came up with years ago. Success is making the people who believed in you look brilliant. That's it.
alts.zh: 我幾年前想出了自己對成功的定義。成功就是：讓當初相信你的人看起來很有眼光。就這樣。

cards.quote: And the story is like there's a frog at the bottom of the well. He looks up every night and he sees the world and he imagines he knows everything about the world.
cards.zh: 故事是這樣：有一隻青蛙住在井底。牠每天晚上抬頭看那一小塊天，就以為自己什麼都懂了。
cards.why: 用一則寓言開場，聽眾會自動進入「等結論」的狀態，你就取得了不被打斷的兩分鐘。井底之蛙是華人熟語，Grant 把它英譯後反而成了他的個人標記。
swaps: It's the frog-in-the-well problem.
We're describing the sky from the bottom of a well.
cards.pmNote: 策略討論前先擴大參照組，否則會在既有市場的邊界內做局部最佳化。
cards.episode: “Dumbest idea I’ve heard” to $100M ARR: Inside the rise of Gamma | Grant Lee (CEO)

alts.quote: He was asked whether or not he was sleeping well at night and he said, 'Oh, yeah, I slept like a baby. I woke up every two hours and cried.'
alts.zh: 有人問他晚上睡得好不好，他說：「喔，超好，我睡得跟嬰兒一樣——每兩小時醒來哭一次。」

alts.quote: I often use this analogy of if you're doing a home renovation, you can have the most beautiful rendering of the new bedroom. But if you haven't checked if there's electricity in that wall there or not, it's going to drastically change the cost and the time and everything.
alts.zh: 我常用一個比喻：你在裝修房子，臥室的效果圖可以做得美到不行。但如果你沒去確認那面牆裡到底有沒有電線，成本跟時間都會整個變樣。

alts.quote: And because of that and because of that... And I usually like to end it with, and finally, this was the last thing you left the world with.
alts.zh: 「很久以前……然後有一天……因為這樣、又因為這樣……最後，這就是你留給世界的東西。」

cards.pattern: [真實公司] signed up with a Gmail address and then [事件] happened. So you just don't know what the next Gmail address is going to do.
cards.quote: Instacart signed up for Stripe with a Gmail address and then Covid happened and they delivered critical food to everyone when people were reasonably not allowed to go to the grocery store easily. So you just don't know what the next Gmail address is going to do.
cards.zh: Instacart 當年是用一個 Gmail 信箱註冊 Stripe 的；後來疫情來了，在大家不太能去超市的時候，是他們把關鍵的食物送到每個人手上。所以你根本不知道，下一個 Gmail 信箱會做出什麼。
cards.why: 用一個超小的細節（Gmail 信箱）當故事的鉤子，再用同一個細節收尾，故事就變成一句可複誦的原則。這是「以小物件貫穿」的敘事技巧。
swaps: That account looked like nothing. It became [X].
You can't tell from the signup form who this turns into.
cards.pmNote: 自助註冊的長尾不能用當下的規模篩選；早期訊號和最終價值幾乎不相關。
cards.episode: Building product at Stripe: craft, metrics, and customer obsession | Jeff Weinstein (Product lead)

alts.quote: And I was like, "Don't these people know that Wix or Squarespace exists? Should I tell them?" And then it hit me. Those things are so complicated to use.
alts.zh: 我當時想：「這些人不知道有 Wix 或 Squarespace 嗎？要不要提醒他們一下？」然後我突然懂了——那些東西真的超難用。

alts.quote: If you're trying to do it, the best way to tell a story about something that you want people to understand is to do what I call speaking with adjacency, which means we're not going to match content to content.
alts.zh: 如果你想讓別人理解某件事，最好的說故事方式是我所謂的「用鄰近性說話」——意思是我們不會拿內容去對內容。

alts.quote: It doesn't matter if you think Bloomberg or Trump should be president. Do you think everyone should have access to great education? Most people would say yes.
alts.zh: 你覺得該讓 Bloomberg 還是 Trump 當總統，都無所謂。你覺得每個人都該有機會受好的教育嗎？大多數人會說會。

cards.quote: They said, "By the way, this is not a digital process yet. We're going to FedEx you an envelope and inside it is going to be the thing for you to sign.
cards.zh: 他們說：「先說一下，這段流程還沒有數位化。我們會用 FedEx 寄一個信封給你，裡面就是要請你簽名的文件。」
cards.why: Jeff 用這段客服對白來論證「產品不等於軟體」——故事講完只加一句 That is product。先講具體場景、再下一句抽象結論，順序反過來就沒力。
swaps: "Here's exactly what will happen, in what order, and what we need from you."
"This part is manual. Here's how we'll carry it for you."
cards.pmNote: 手動流程只要被設計過，也是產品的一部分；自動化不是體驗好壞的判準。
cards.episode: Building product at Stripe: craft, metrics, and customer obsession | Jeff Weinstein (Product lead)

alts.quote: If you're trying to do it, the best way to tell a story about something that you want people to understand is to do what I call speaking with adjacency, which means we're not going to match content to content.
alts.zh: 如果你想讓別人理解某件事，最好的說故事方式是我所謂的「用鄰近性說話」——意思是我們不會拿內容去對內容。

alts.quote: I think the hardest thing for a founder, challenge is not optional. You're going to be challenged, but the suffering is optional.
alts.zh: 對創辦人來說最難的是：挑戰不是選項，你一定會被挑戰；但要不要痛苦，是選項。

alts.quote: There's this thing from consumer advertising, which is you throw a consumer one egg, they can probably catch it. You throw them four or five eggs, they're probably going to drop all of them.
alts.zh: 廣告圈有個說法：你丟一顆蛋給消費者，他大概接得住；你一次丟四五顆，他大概會全部摔在地上。

cards.pattern: You bring a fruit to the reviewer and say, "Here's a mango, what do you think?" And the reviewer says, "I actually don't like mangoes."
