cards.quote: Which is you bring a fruit to the reviewer and say, "Hey, here's a mango, what do you think?" And the reviewer says, "I actually don't like mangoes."
cards.zh: 你拿一個水果去給主管看：「欸，這是芒果，你覺得怎樣？」主管說：「我其實不喜歡芒果。」
cards.why: 用幼稚到好笑的比喻去講一件很政治的事（審核來回浪費），因為好笑，被影射的主管也不會惱。這是資深者批評流程時最安全的包裝。
swaps: We keep bringing dishes to someone who never told us their diet.
Three rounds of review and we still don't know the criteria.
cards.pmNote: 提案前先做 leadership interview，可以省掉整輪「猜口味」的來回。
cards.episode: An operator’s guide to product strategy | Chandra Janakiraman (CPO at VRChat, ex-Meta, Headspace, Zynga)

alts.quote: I always say you should have, what I call an elephant at the beginning of the story, which is actually a big spaceship shooting at a little spaceship or a police officer chasing a guy across a roof.
alts.zh: 我一直說你應該在故事開頭放一隻我稱為「大象」的東西——實際上就是一艘大太空船在射一艘小太空船，或是警察在屋頂上追一個人。

alts.quote: I'd say that was the beginning of chapter two where it was we went from the company that could do no wrong to the company that could do no right, which was a big flip.
alts.zh: 我會說那就是第二章的開始——我們從「怎麼做都對」的公司，變成「怎麼做都錯」的公司，整個翻過來。

alts.quote: It doesn't matter if you think Bloomberg or Trump should be president. Do you think everyone should have access to great education? Most people would say yes.
alts.zh: 你覺得該讓 Bloomberg 還是 Trump 當總統，都無所謂。你覺得每個人都該有機會受好的教育嗎？大多數人會說會。

cards.pattern: Think of these [原型] as concept cars—they drive inspiration and give you small nuggets you can run with.
cards.quote: So think of these prototypes as these concept cars that really drive inspiration and potentially give you some small nuggets that you can run with.
cards.zh: 所以把這些原型想成概念車：它們的作用是帶來靈感，順便給你一些可以真的拿去用的小片段。
cards.why: 借一個外部產業的既有制度來替自己的做法取得正當性——別人不能說「這不切實際」，因為汽車業已經這樣做幾十年了。
swaps: These are concept cars, not next quarter's roadmap.
The point isn't to ship it; it's to see what people react to.
cards.pmNote: 探索性原型要明確標示「不會出貨」，否則會被誤當承諾而排進 roadmap。
cards.episode: An operator’s guide to product strategy | Chandra Janakiraman (CPO at VRChat, ex-Meta, Headspace, Zynga)

alts.quote: I think I'll give you a bit of a different one because I think this one is harder to spot and I think that's really interesting.
alts.zh: 我想給你一個不太一樣的例子，因為這個比較難被看出來，我覺得那才有意思。

alts.quote: I hate Jobs-to-be-Done, I think it is a terrible framework, I think no successful company has ever been built on top of JTBD and if you pick JTBD, you're probably doomed and I'll give you an example.
alts.zh: 我討厭 Jobs-to-be-Done，我覺得那是個爛框架，沒有一家成功公司是靠 JTBD 建起來的；你要是選了它，大概就完了——我給你一個例子。

alts.quote: I'll give you a very small example again, just from Webflow, this idea of keyboard shortcuts, feels small, but that is a piece that creates a lot of love from user base who are power users.
alts.zh: 我再給你一個很小的例子，就 Webflow 的鍵盤快捷鍵。聽起來很小，但那正是讓重度使用者愛上產品的關鍵之一。

cards.pattern: He would physically bring a chair over in a meeting and say, "The customer is sitting here."
cards.quote: He sometimes physically bring a chair over in a meeting and say, "The customer is sitting here," and you'd have to pretend.
cards.zh: 他有時候會在會議中真的搬一張椅子過來，說：「客戶就坐在這裡。」然後大家得配合演。
cards.why: 把抽象原則變成房間裡的一個物件，之後只要有人看那張椅子，論點就自動出現。要在組織裡植入一個價值觀，實體道具比一頁投影片持久。
swaps: Let's leave a seat for the customer in this room.
Who in this meeting is speaking for the person paying us?
cards.pmNote: 會議裡缺席的利害關係人需要指定代言人，否則內部方便性會壓過使用者利益。
cards.episode: Building product at Stripe: craft, metrics, and customer obsession | Jeff Weinstein (Product lead)

alts.quote: Which is you bring a fruit to the reviewer and say, "Hey, here's a mango, what do you think?" And the reviewer says, "I actually don't like mangoes."
alts.zh: 你拿一個水果去給主管看：「欸，這是芒果，你覺得怎樣？」主管說：「我其實不喜歡芒果。」

alts.quote: I call this habit “gossiping” to AI, because I fill in my copilot the same way I’d lean over and vent to a colleague sitting next to me.
alts.zh: 我把這個習慣叫做對 AI「講八卦」，因為我更新我的副駕的方式，就跟我側身跟隔壁同事抱怨一樣。

alts.quote: If your audience isn't wondering what you're about to say, they're no longer listening to you.
alts.zh: 如果台下的人沒有在好奇你下一句要講什麼，他們其實已經沒在聽你講話了。

cards.pattern: People will say [反對意見]. Yep. But there's 0% [損失] in that.
cards.quote: On Twitter, you'll see people say, "Oh, it's the most expensive use of everyone's time," but it's like, "Yep. But there's 0% fidelity loss in that.
cards.zh: 推特上會有人說：「那是最貴的一種時間使用方式。」但我的回答是：「對啊。可是這樣資訊零失真。」
cards.why: Yep 是一個完整的讓步，不辯解、不加 but I think——先把對方的批評百分之百接下來，再丟出他沒算進去的那一欄成本。台灣人常在讓步時偷偷加辯解，力道就散了。
swaps: You're right, it's expensive. It's also the only version with zero information loss.
Totally—and I'd pay that price again.
cards.pmNote: 全員會議的成本要跟「溝通失真的成本」一起比，不能只算人時。
cards.episode: Inside Bolt: From near-death to ~$40m ARR in 5 months—one of the fastest-growing products in history | Eric Simons (founder and CEO of StackBlitz)

alts.quote: There's this rush to judgment upfront where people say, "Oh, it's therefore obvious that X, Y, Z. It's obvious that the moats are going to be in this area of the technology, but not in this other area."
alts.zh: 一開始大家都會急著下判斷，說「所以顯然就是 X、Y、Z」、「顯然護城河一定在這一塊，不會在那一塊」。

alts.quote: And I always write them back and say like, "Please tell me the better term and popularize it and I'll use it. It's a great idea."
alts.zh: 我都回信說：「請你告訴我更好的講法，然後把它推廣開，我就會改用。這主意很好。」

alts.quote: But before that, I think getting to product-market fit, obviously there's a lot of methodology for doing it today that might make it a bit easier for people, but I still think it's fairly random and pretty dang hard.
alts.zh: 在那之前——我覺得要走到 PMF，現在當然有很多方法論可能讓大家輕鬆一點，但我還是認為它相當隨機，而且真的很難。

cards.quote: I just internalize this feeling that maybe he's right. Maybe something about what he's saying is actually correct.
cards.zh: 我心裡浮現一個念頭：也許他是對的。他講的東西裡，也許有某一部分真的成立。
cards.why: 被全盤否定時，先切出「他哪一部分是對的」而不是整包接受或整包反駁。something about what he's saying 是很精準的部分接受用語，可以直接搬去會議上。
swaps: There's a version of that critique that's right.
I don't agree with the conclusion, but the premise holds.
cards.pmNote: 把最刺耳的反對意見拆成「可證偽的部分」，往往就是策略的第一個輸入。
cards.episode: “Dumbest idea I’ve heard” to $100M ARR: Inside the rise of Gamma | Grant Lee (CEO)

alts.quote: That's a good idea, but we don't actually understand these three things before we start working on that. So maybe we should do understand work to make sure that that is actually the right idea.
alts.zh: 這個想法不錯，但在動手之前有三件事我們其實還沒搞懂。也許先做點「理解型的工作」，確認這真的是對的方向。

alts.quote: Actually, all feedback I think is valid. People's feelings are valid, but it doesn't mean that you need to do something about all of those things.
alts.zh: 其實我覺得所有回饋都是有效的。別人的感受都是真的，但這不代表你每一項都得去處理。

alts.quote: And optics is a good thing. So I'm not saying don't think about optics whatsoever, I think it's actually important to think about optics.
alts.zh: 而且「對外呈現」本身是好事。我不是說完全不要管呈現，我覺得那其實很重要。

cards.pattern: It's not just that [表面原因], it would be that they [真正原因].
cards.quote: And I'd say it's not just that the budget's too small, it would be that they put all their eggs in one basket.
cards.zh: 我會說，問題不只是預算太小，而是他們把所有雞蛋放在同一個籃子裡。
cards.why: 對方已經有一個診斷（預算不夠），你不否定它，只說「不只是」，再換上真正的原因。這比說 That's not the real problem 溫和很多，但效果一樣。
swaps: The budget isn't the constraint—the concentration is.
It's less about how much and more about how many bets.
cards.pmNote: 小預算的實驗要追求 bet 數量而不是單注大小，否則學不到分布。
cards.episode: “Dumbest idea I’ve heard” to $100M ARR: Inside the rise of Gamma | Grant Lee (CEO)

alts.quote: So they would say, "Oh, your market's not big enough." And I would say, "It's going to be huge." And I'd add a new page in my pitch deck that said how big the market I believe was.
alts.zh: 他們會說：「你的市場不夠大。」我就說：「它會變超大。」然後我就在簡報裡加一頁，講我認為這市場有多大。

alts.quote: Not to say it's not better, but just this is the structure of it, and it kind of sets you up for bragging.
alts.zh: 我不是說它不好，我只是在講它的結構——這個結構會把你逼到一直自誇。

alts.quote: Sometimes I feel the need to defend that the process is not for process' sake, it's ultimately to help us all move faster and work better.
alts.zh: 有時候我得替流程辯護一下：流程不是為了流程而存在，它最終是要讓大家跑得更快、做得更好。

cards.pattern: There's this stigma that [A] and [B] are at odds with each other. I very much follow the thought that [A] is [B].
cards.quote: I think there's this stigma that brand marketing and performance marketing are sort of at odds with each other. I very much follow the sort of thought that brand marketing is performance marketing.
cards.zh: 大家有一種成見，覺得品牌行銷和成效行銷是互相對立的。我個人非常認同的說法是：品牌行銷就是成效行銷。
cards.why: 先把二選一的框架命名為 stigma（成見），再用一句等式直接把二分法拆掉。要推翻假對立時，等式句（A is B）比「兩個都重要」有力太多。
swaps: People treat these as a trade-off. I don't think it is one.
It's not brand versus performance—brand is the input to performance.
cards.pmNote: 品牌投資的回報體現在成效行銷的素材產能與 CAC，只是歸因較慢。
cards.episode: “Dumbest idea I’ve heard” to $100M ARR: Inside the rise of Gamma | Grant Lee (CEO)

alts.quote: And so I think if there's anything that I would be accused of, it would be being over simplifying things.
alts.zh: 如果說我有什麼會被人批評的，大概就是我把事情簡化過頭了。

alts.quote: There's this rush to judgment upfront where people say, "Oh, it's therefore obvious that X, Y, Z. It's obvious that the moats are going to be in this area of the technology, but not in this other area."
alts.zh: 一開始大家都會急著下判斷，說「所以顯然就是 X、Y、Z」、「顯然護城河一定在這一塊，不會在那一塊」。

alts.quote: If you don't say yes, what you're essentially saying is, I am so presumptuous that I understand what's on the other side of that door already.
alts.zh: 你如果不答應，你其實等於在說：我狂妄到已經知道那扇門後面是什麼了。

cards.pattern: Of all the problems in the world, [這個抱怨] is on the top list of problems I want to have.
cards.quote: One, what a problem to have. Of all the problems in the world, "I'm overwhelmed by customer interest," is on the top list of problems I want to have.
cards.zh: 第一，這是多好的問題啊。世界上這麼多問題，「客戶熱情多到我應付不來」是我最想要的那幾個之一。
cards.why: 把對方的抱怨重新歸類成「別人求之不得的處境」，先卸掉情緒，再談解法。開頭那句 what a problem to have 是英文裡現成的重框裝置。
swaps: That's the good version of this problem.
I'd trade our problems for yours.
cards.pmNote: 抱怨的內容往往是需求訊號；先辨識它屬於「成功造成的問題」還是「失敗造成的問題」。
cards.episode: Building product at Stripe: craft, metrics, and customer obsession | Jeff Weinstein (Product lead)

alts.quote: Here's what I have a problem with. First of all, having a growth mindset is a very, very helpful thing.
alts.zh: 我要說的是我對它的哪一點有意見。首先，擁有成長心態本身是非常非常有幫助的事。

alts.quote: Now, obviously if you live in a small town and they capped the well and gave all the water to the data center, then you're really pissed off. But that's a planning problem. That's not a data center problem.
alts.zh: 當然，如果你住在小鎮上，井被封了、水全給了資料中心，那你當然火大。但那是都市規劃的問題，不是資料中心的問題。

alts.quote: the biggest misconception about customer research is I have to listen to them. You don't have to listen to them at all, you just have to understand where they are
alts.zh: 對客戶研究最大的誤解，是以為做了就得照客戶說的做。你完全不必照做，你只需要搞清楚他們現在站在哪裡。

cards.pattern: If someone has a strategy for [達成目標] that isn't [我的做法], I want to know about it, because [我的做法] is very hard.
cards.quote: If someone else has a strategy for moving revenue that isn't getting it from customers, I want to know about it because it's so hard to get it from customers.
cards.zh: 如果有人有辦法在不靠客戶的情況下推動營收，我很想知道，因為從客戶身上拿到營收真的太難了。
cards.why: 把「我是對的」翻成「我很想被證明錯」，姿態立刻從防守變開放，但實際上沒有讓步。這是資深者處理路線之爭最漂亮的一招。
swaps: If there's a cheaper path, genuinely tell me—this one is expensive.
I'd love to be wrong about this. Nobody's shown me the alternative.
cards.pmNote: 路線之爭要把舉證責任移轉：主張者說明機制，質疑者提出替代機制。
cards.episode: Building product at Stripe: craft, metrics, and customer obsession | Jeff Weinstein (Product lead)

alts.quote: Yeah, I think that's an important question, and it's a question I hear a lot because we all know a bullshitter.
alts.zh: 我覺得那是一個重要的問題，而且我常常被問到——因為我們每個人都認識一個唬爛的人。

alts.quote: But before that, I think getting to product-market fit, obviously there's a lot of methodology for doing it today that might make it a bit easier for people, but I still think it's fairly random and pretty dang hard.
alts.zh: 在那之前——我覺得要走到 PMF，現在當然有很多方法論可能讓大家輕鬆一點，但我還是認為它相當隨機，而且真的很難。

alts.quote: So this kind of behavioral framing and nudging becomes important, it's not about deceiving your customers, but it's just about framing the products in such a way that it also appeals to the irrational side of the brain.
alts.zh: 這種行為框架跟推力很重要——它不是要騙客戶，而是把產品呈現得也能打到大腦不理性的那一面。

cards.pattern: They wanted to minimize the support. I was like, "That's the product. The thing you're talking about is the product."
cards.quote: I was like, "That's the product. The thing you're talking about is the product."
cards.zh: 我就說：「那就是產品啊。你正在講的那個東西，就是產品本身。」
cards.why: 對方想消滅的東西，你直接改名成他最重視的東西——一句話把問題翻成資產。重複同一句話兩次是刻意的，讓對方來得及吸收這個轉向。
swaps: That's not overhead—that's the offering.
You're describing the feature, not the cost.
cards.pmNote: self-serve 流程中的高頻求助，往往是尚未被產品化的高價值服務環節。
cards.episode: Building product at Stripe: craft, metrics, and customer obsession | Jeff Weinstein (Product lead)

alts.quote: One, I think that's a really fantastic, maybe not counterpoint, but thing to call out.
alts.zh: 第一，我覺得你這個提得非常好——也不算是反駁啦，但確實是該點出來的一件事。

alts.quote: Now, obviously if you live in a small town and they capped the well and gave all the water to the data center, then you're really pissed off. But that's a planning problem. That's not a data center problem.
alts.zh: 當然，如果你住在小鎮上，井被封了、水全給了資料中心，那你當然火大。但那是都市規劃的問題，不是資料中心的問題。

alts.quote: And many of my design friends will push back on this and they'll say design should be its own thing and it should be an independent group and we should have three co-equal branches of government, and that's a solid argument as well
alts.zh: 我很多設計圈的朋友會反對，他們會說設計應該獨立成一個部門，跟產品、工程三權分立——那也是很有道理的論點。

cards.pattern: It's also not a sign of weakness. It's actually a sign of strength and humility to [做這件事].
cards.quote: And it's also not a sign of weakness. It's actually a sign of strength and humility to ask your leaders what you want.
cards.zh: 而且這不是示弱。主動去問你的主管想要什麼，其實是自信和謙遜的表現。
cards.why: 先講出對方心裡那句沒說出口的顧慮（這樣會不會顯得我很弱），再重新標籤。not X, actually Y 的重貼標籤句型，在說服猶豫的人時特別好用。
swaps: Asking early reads as senior, not junior.
That's not deferring—that's de-risking.
cards.pmNote: 提前對齊主管的成功定義，是降低專案政治風險最便宜的動作。
cards.episode: An operator’s guide to product strategy | Chandra Janakiraman (CPO at VRChat, ex-Meta, Headspace, Zynga)

alts.quote: It's like these things that seem so common sense are actually hard with what they're doing… a lot of the advice is common sense. That doesn't mean it's easy to put in motion.
alts.zh: 這些看起來根本是常識的東西，真的做起來很難……很多建議都是常識，但常識不代表容易落地。

alts.quote: And optics is a good thing. So I'm not saying don't think about optics whatsoever, I think it's actually important to think about optics.
alts.zh: 而且「對外呈現」本身是好事。我不是說完全不要管呈現，我覺得那其實很重要。

alts.quote: And to be clear, I don't think it's actually that dangerous right now.
alts.zh: 先講清楚，我不覺得現在真的有那麼危險。

cards.pattern: Its biggest strength is also somewhat its weakness, which is [同一個特質造成的問題].
cards.quote: I've also found that its biggest strength is also somewhat its weakness, which is these mock strategies tend to be pretty comprehensive and extensive.
cards.zh: 我也發現它最大的優點同時是它的缺點：這些模擬策略往往非常全面、非常詳盡。
cards.why: 在稱讚一個東西之後立刻用同一個特質做批評，聽起來像洞察而不是打槍。要否定一個大家正在熱捧的工具時，這是最不得罪人的路徑。
swaps: The thing that makes it good is the same thing that makes it unusable here.
It's comprehensive, and that's precisely the problem.
cards.pmNote: AI 產出的策略通常缺乏取捨；收斂與排除仍需人來承擔判斷責任。
cards.episode: An operator’s guide to product strategy | Chandra Janakiraman (CPO at VRChat, ex-Meta, Headspace, Zynga)

alts.quote: One of the comments was, "Benedict, this is 80 slides of saying we don't know," which is slightly facetious, but also kind of true.
alts.zh: 有人留言說：「Benedict，你這 80 張投影片就是在講『我們不知道』。」講得有點壞，但也算是實話。

alts.quote: So this kind of behavioral framing and nudging becomes important, it's not about deceiving your customers, but it's just about framing the products in such a way that it also appeals to the irrational side of the brain.
alts.zh: 這種行為框架跟推力很重要——它不是要騙客戶，而是把產品呈現得也能打到大腦不理性的那一面。

alts.quote: And for that reason, my advice is super lame, which is make really high quality content, which is not as actionable as I think people making content would ideally like.
alts.zh: 所以我的建議很沒創意，就是做出真正高品質的內容——我知道這對做內容的人來說不夠具體可執行。

cards.pattern: I wouldn't change [核心主張]. I would defend it using the framework, but if there are really good arguments about the criteria, then it's okay to reconsider.
cards.quote: The most important thing, three strategic pillars, I wouldn't change that. I would defend it using the framework, but if people are like, "there's really good arguments about the criteria that led to your ranking," then it's okay to reconsider it.
cards.zh: 最重要的那三根策略支柱，我不會改。我會用那套框架來守，但如果有人針對排序背後的評分標準提出很好的論證，那就可以重新考慮。
cards.why: 把「什麼情況下我會改」事先講清楚，你就同時顯得堅定又不固執。關鍵是把可協商的層級指定在標準，而不是結論。
swaps: The pillars aren't up for debate today; the weighting is.
Argue the criteria with me, not the conclusion.
cards.pmNote: 策略 rollout 階段的目的是落地不是重開討論；只開放對評分標準的挑戰。
cards.episode: An operator’s guide to product strategy | Chandra Janakiraman (CPO at VRChat, ex-Meta, Headspace, Zynga)

alts.quote: And optics is a good thing. So I'm not saying don't think about optics whatsoever, I think it's actually important to think about optics.
alts.zh: 而且「對外呈現」本身是好事。我不是說完全不要管呈現，我覺得那其實很重要。

alts.quote: There's this rush to judgment upfront where people say, "Oh, it's therefore obvious that X, Y, Z. It's obvious that the moats are going to be in this area of the technology, but not in this other area."
alts.zh: 一開始大家都會急著下判斷，說「所以顯然就是 X、Y、Z」、「顯然護城河一定在這一塊，不會在那一塊」。

alts.quote: On Twitter, you'll see people say, "Oh, it's the most expensive use of everyone's time," but it's like, "Yep. But there's 0% fidelity loss in that.
alts.zh: 推特上會有人說：「那是最貴的一種時間使用方式。」但我的回答是：「對啊。可是這樣資訊零失真。」

cards.pattern: It's going to take us years to do, but if we do it, we think this will change everything for [領域].
cards.quote: It's going to take us years to do, but if we do it, we think this will change everything for design.
cards.zh: 這件事會花我們好幾年；但如果做成了，我們認為這會徹底改變設計這件事。
cards.why: 先把成本講到最滿（years），再把報酬講到最大（change everything）——誠實的代價反而讓願景可信。這是深科技提案的標準骨架。
swaps: This is a multi-year build. If it works, the category changes.
It'll take longer than anyone wants. The payoff is the whole market.
cards.pmNote: 深技術賭注要同時交代時間成本與不對稱報酬，否則會被當成無限期研究。
cards.episode: Inside Bolt: From near-death to ~$40m ARR in 5 months—one of the fastest-growing products in history | Eric Simons (founder and CEO of StackBlitz)

alts.quote: But I think that I'd like to change that. I'd like to help change the mood. I'd like to help change the way we're thinking about things.
alts.zh: 但我會想去改變這件事。我想幫忙改變那個氛圍。我想幫忙改變我們思考事情的方式。

alts.quote: So since June, this is the worst it will ever be, the state of AI coding. And it's already this good.
alts.zh: 所以從六月到現在，AI 寫程式的水準就是它「最差」的時候了。而它已經這麼好了。

alts.quote: You want your product to live in their brain somewhere where when they think about, "Hey, I have to create a presentation." They come to you as the default tool.
alts.zh: 你會希望你的產品住在他們腦中的某個位置：當他們想到「我得做一份簡報」的時候，預設就是來找你。

cards.pattern: And what blew my mind is, it's not priced in. It's not reflected in [現況]. That is going to completely change.
cards.quote: And what blew my mind is, it's not priced in, to any of these companies out there. And it's not reflected in the org charts of all the software companies in the world right now. That is going to completely change.
cards.zh: 最讓我震驚的是：這件事根本還沒被 price in。它完全沒有反映在現在全世界軟體公司的組織圖上。而這會徹底改變。
cards.why: not priced in 是金融用語，借來講產業趨勢，暗示「你現在還有時間差」。中間那句把抽象趨勢落到一個可查證的物件（組織圖）上，願景就不空了。
swaps: Nobody has priced this in yet.
You can see it in the hiring plans—or rather, you can't.
cards.pmNote: 願景的可信度來自「現況與趨勢之間的落差證據」，組織圖與職缺是最好查的落差。
cards.episode: Inside Bolt: From near-death to ~$40m ARR in 5 months—one of the fastest-growing products in history | Eric Simons (founder and CEO of StackBlitz)

alts.quote: And it seemed really impossible that it would stay on the desktop, it would stay really complicated. And it just seemed so apparent to me that in the future it was going to be completely different.
alts.zh: 它會一直留在桌機上、一直這麼複雜，這件事在我看來根本不可能。我當時就覺得很明顯，未來一定會完全不一樣。

alts.quote: Imagine two years there's a newspaper, there's a journalist that covers this work, and there's a newspaper article that comes out. I want you to imagine the progress on all these strategic pillars and what the headline of that newspaper article looks like.
alts.zh: 想像兩年後有個記者來報導我們這段工作，寫成一篇報導。我要你想像那篇報導的標題會長什麼樣子。

alts.quote: So since June, this is the worst it will ever be, the state of AI coding. And it's already this good.
alts.zh: 所以從六月到現在，AI 寫程式的水準就是它「最差」的時候了。而它已經這麼好了。

cards.pattern: This is kind of the first time that you don't have to be [某種身分] to [做某件事].
cards.quote: This is kind of the first time that, you don't have to be technical to make production grade web, full-stack web and mobile apps.
cards.zh: 這大概是史上第一次，你不需要是工程背景，也能做出可上線等級的全端網頁和行動 App。
cards.why: 把願景寫成「誰被解禁了」而不是「什麼技術變強了」，聽眾才會在裡面看到自己。first time 一詞承擔了全部的份量。
swaps: You no longer need [身分] to do [事].
The permission requirement just disappeared.
cards.pmNote: 願景要指名被賦能的使用者族群，這也直接決定 GTM 的目標受眾。
cards.episode: Inside Bolt: From near-death to ~$40m ARR in 5 months—one of the fastest-growing products in history | Eric Simons (founder and CEO of StackBlitz)

alts.quote: You kind of want to have a ladder that goes all the way up to the moon, which is your crazy, wild vision. And then you want to have rungs that just work its way up step by step.
alts.zh: 你會希望有一把直達月球的梯子，那就是你那個瘋狂的大願景。然後你要有一階一階的橫桿，讓人可以一步一步往上爬。

alts.quote: And he would say, you have to aim for Chartres. You have to make something that is better than that. That should be your goal, not to just turn in something that's what you feel is good enough.
alts.zh: 他會說：你要對準夏特大教堂。你要做出比它更好的東西。那才是你的目標，而不是交出一個你自己覺得「還可以」的作品。

alts.quote: In deciding to turn Dropbox into this lab for distributed work, we're like, "Okay, when you open up your laptop in 2025, 2030, what do you see?"
alts.zh: 我們決定把 Dropbox 變成遠距工作的實驗室時，問的是：「二〇二五、二〇三〇年，你打開筆電的那一刻，看到的是什麼？」

cards.pattern: So since [時間點], this is the worst it will ever be. And it's already this good.
cards.quote: So since June, this is the worst it will ever be, the state of AI coding. And it's already this good.
cards.zh: 所以從六月到現在，AI 寫程式的水準就是它「最差」的時候了。而它已經這麼好了。
cards.why: 這是對抗「現在還不夠好」這類質疑的萬用句：不辯論現況，改辯論斜率。兩句都極短，念起來有敲定的感覺。
swaps: This is the floor, not the ceiling.
Judge the trajectory, not today's snapshot.
cards.pmNote: 評估新技術要看改善速率而不是當下能力，否則會系統性低估。
cards.episode: Inside Bolt: From near-death to ~$40m ARR in 5 months—one of the fastest-growing products in history | Eric Simons (founder and CEO of StackBlitz)

alts.quote: And he would say, you have to aim for Chartres. You have to make something that is better than that. That should be your goal, not to just turn in something that's what you feel is good enough.
alts.zh: 他會說：你要對準夏特大教堂。你要做出比它更好的東西。那才是你的目標，而不是交出一個你自己覺得「還可以」的作品。

alts.quote: It's going to take us years to do, but if we do it, we think this will change everything for design.
alts.zh: 這件事會花我們好幾年；但如果做成了，我們認為這會徹底改變設計這件事。

alts.quote: We should be cannibalizing the existing state of our product every six to 12 months. Every six to 12 months, it should make our existing product look silly.
alts.zh: 我們應該每六到十二個月就把自己現有的產品吃掉一次。每六到十二個月，新的東西就該讓舊的看起來很蠢。

cards.pattern: Could we help democratize [X]? That was sort of our north star.
cards.quote: And so we felt like that was the wrong, that didn't feel right, and so could we help democratize visual storytelling, visual communication? That was sort of our north star.
cards.zh: 我們覺得這件事不對勁，所以問：我們有沒有辦法讓視覺敘事、視覺溝通變得人人可用？那就是我們的北極星。
cards.why: 先講一句「這樣不對」的道德判斷，再把願景寫成一個問句——問句留了空間，聽起來像邀請加入而不是宣告。
swaps: Can we make [X] available to people who were locked out of it?
The north star is: nobody loses because they couldn't [做某事].
cards.pmNote: 使命敘事要指出一個具體的不公平，否則會退化成空泛的正面詞。
cards.episode: “Dumbest idea I’ve heard” to $100M ARR: Inside the rise of Gamma | Grant Lee (CEO)

alts.quote: And I think the thing that I love about a crazy big goal is that you feel completely inadequate before it.
alts.zh: 我最喜歡「瘋狂大目標」的一點，就是站在它面前你會覺得自己完全不夠格。

alts.quote: And he would say, you have to aim for Chartres. You have to make something that is better than that. That should be your goal, not to just turn in something that's what you feel is good enough.
alts.zh: 他會說：你要對準夏特大教堂。你要做出比它更好的東西。那才是你的目標，而不是交出一個你自己覺得「還可以」的作品。

alts.quote: I still feel like ChatGPT feels a little bit like MS-DOS, like we haven't built Windows yet. And it'll be obvious once we do.
alts.zh: 我還是覺得 ChatGPT 有點像 MS-DOS——我們的 Windows 還沒做出來。而且一旦做出來，大家馬上就會知道那就是了。

cards.pattern: You want your product to live in their brain where when they think "I have to [做某事]", they come to you as the default tool.
cards.quote: You want your product to live in their brain somewhere where when they think about, "Hey, I have to create a presentation." They come to you as the default tool.
cards.zh: 你會希望你的產品住在他們腦中的某個位置：當他們想到「我得做一份簡報」的時候，預設就是來找你。
cards.why: 把市占率這種抽象目標，改寫成「使用者腦中的一個觸發時刻」。live in their brain 這種略微擬人的講法，讓目標變得可以檢驗（他們什麼時候想到我們？）。
swaps: We want to own the moment right after they think [某念頭].
The goal is to be the reflex, not the option.
cards.pmNote: 品類預設地位的量測方式是品牌關鍵字直搜佔比，而非整體流量。
cards.episode: “Dumbest idea I’ve heard” to $100M ARR: Inside the rise of Gamma | Grant Lee (CEO)

alts.quote: So I guess there's two ways of planning. The way that you can plan is you can dream of what is the perfect vision of the future, what future do you want to exist in, what would you like the world to look like?
alts.zh: 我覺得規劃大概分兩種。一種是你去夢想那個最完美的未來——你想活在什麼樣的未來裡？你希望這個世界長什麼樣子？

alts.quote: It's going to take us years to do, but if we do it, we think this will change everything for design.
alts.zh: 這件事會花我們好幾年；但如果做成了，我們認為這會徹底改變設計這件事。

alts.quote: Imagine two years there's a newspaper, there's a journalist that covers this work, and there's a newspaper article that comes out. I want you to imagine the progress on all these strategic pillars and what the headline of that newspaper article looks like.
alts.zh: 想像兩年後有個記者來報導我們這段工作，寫成一篇報導。我要你想像那篇報導的標題會長什麼樣子。

cards.pattern: You can quit your job on a Sunday night and on Monday morning fill out this form and the next day be able to run a billion-dollar business.
cards.quote: So you can quit your job on a Sunday night, get the Sunday scaries, I'm done with this thing, and on Monday morning fill out this form and the next day be able to run a billion-dollar business.
cards.zh: 所以你可以星期天晚上辭掉工作——那種週日症候群發作、受夠了的心情——星期一早上填完這張表，隔天就能開始經營一間十億美金等級的公司。
cards.why: 願景寫成一個人的行事曆（週日／週一／隔天），聽眾自動代入自己。Sunday scaries 這種生活用語讓宏大的結論落地。
swaps: Quit on Friday, be operating on Tuesday.
The gap between deciding and operating goes to zero.
cards.pmNote: 把願景寫成使用者時間軸上的縮短，比講市場規模更能對齊團隊。
cards.episode: Building product at Stripe: craft, metrics, and customer obsession | Jeff Weinstein (Product lead)

alts.quote: And I think the thing that I love about a crazy big goal is that you feel completely inadequate before it.
alts.zh: 我最喜歡「瘋狂大目標」的一點，就是站在它面前你會覺得自己完全不夠格。

alts.quote: What does a day in the life of a user look like in five years? What does the product look like in five to 10 years? Why is the world better in 10 years?
alts.zh: 五年後，使用者的一天長什麼樣子？五到十年後，這個產品長什麼樣子？十年後，這個世界為什麼會更好？

alts.quote: And that ultimately, we understand what makes it a must-have product. And then what we're trying to do is build a flywheel around that must-have value.
alts.zh: 最終我們要弄清楚是什麼讓它變成「非有不可」的產品，然後圍繞那個非有不可的價值，去打造一個飛輪。

cards.pattern: Just shave a whole week off of [某流程] and you can kind of see [宏觀結果] being born sooner.
cards.quote: Just shave a whole week off of your company and you can kind of see GDP being born sooner.
cards.zh: 只要幫一家公司省下整整一個星期，你就能看到 GDP 更早一點被生出來。
cards.why: 把一個很小的產品改動（省一週）直接接到一個極大的名詞（GDP），落差本身就是修辭力量。being born 讓抽象的經濟指標有了畫面。
swaps: A week saved per company, multiplied by 50,000 companies.
Small friction removed at scale looks like macroeconomics.
cards.pmNote: 小改動的價值要乘上規模才看得出來；這也是平台型產品的論證方式。
cards.episode: Building product at Stripe: craft, metrics, and customer obsession | Jeff Weinstein (Product lead)

alts.quote: You kind of want to have a ladder that goes all the way up to the moon, which is your crazy, wild vision. And then you want to have rungs that just work its way up step by step.
alts.zh: 你會希望有一把直達月球的梯子，那就是你那個瘋狂的大願景。然後你要有一階一階的橫桿，讓人可以一步一步往上爬。

alts.quote: And that ultimately, we understand what makes it a must-have product. And then what we're trying to do is build a flywheel around that must-have value.
alts.zh: 最終我們要弄清楚是什麼讓它變成「非有不可」的產品，然後圍繞那個非有不可的價值，去打造一個飛輪。

alts.quote: Obviously, I skew very heavily towards earned channels just because once you stand that up, that's a gift that just keeps on giving and nobody can take that away from you.
alts.zh: 我明顯偏向自有通路，因為那個東西一旦架起來，就是一份會一直給你回報的禮物，而且沒有人拿得走。

cards.pattern: Imagine in two years there's a journalist that covers this work. Imagine what the headline of that newspaper article looks like.
cards.quote: Imagine two years there's a newspaper, there's a journalist that covers this work, and there's a newspaper article that comes out. I want you to imagine the progress on all these strategic pillars and what the headline of that newspaper article looks like.
cards.zh: 想像兩年後有個記者來報導我們這段工作，寫成一篇報導。我要你想像那篇報導的標題會長什麼樣子。
cards.why: 把「講願景」這件難事，換成「寫一個標題」這件人人做得到的事。標題的字數限制會自動逼出重點與白話，比要求大家「講清楚願景」有效。
swaps: Write the press release headline for two years from now.
If someone wrote about this in 2028, what's the first line?
cards.pmNote: newspaper headline / working-backwards press release 是把願景壓成可對齊語句的標準工具。
cards.episode: An operator’s guide to product strategy | Chandra Janakiraman (CPO at VRChat, ex-Meta, Headspace, Zynga)

alts.quote: You kind of want to have a ladder that goes all the way up to the moon, which is your crazy, wild vision. And then you want to have rungs that just work its way up step by step.
alts.zh: 你會希望有一把直達月球的梯子，那就是你那個瘋狂的大願景。然後你要有一階一階的橫桿，讓人可以一步一步往上爬。

alts.quote: And what blew my mind is, it's not priced in, to any of these companies out there. And it's not reflected in the org charts of all the software companies in the world right now. That is going to completely change.
alts.zh: 最讓我震驚的是：這件事根本還沒被 price in。它完全沒有反映在現在全世界軟體公司的組織圖上。而這會徹底改變。

alts.quote: You want your product to live in their brain somewhere where when they think about, "Hey, I have to create a presentation." They come to you as the default tool.
alts.zh: 你會希望你的產品住在他們腦中的某個位置：當他們想到「我得做一份簡報」的時候，預設就是來找你。

cards.pattern: What does a day in the life of a user look like in [五年後]? What does the product look like in [五到十年]? Why is the world better in [十年後]?
cards.quote: What does a day in the life of a user look like in five years? What does the product look like in five to 10 years? Why is the world better in 10 years?
cards.zh: 五年後，使用者的一天長什麼樣子？五到十年後，這個產品長什麼樣子？十年後，這個世界為什麼會更好？
cards.why: 三個問題有明顯的升溫順序：先具體（一天）、再形貌（產品）、最後才逼出價值判斷（世界為何更好）。訪談主管做願景時可以逐字照抄。
swaps: Walk me through a user's Tuesday, three years out.
What's the version of this that you'd be excited to tell people about?
cards.pmNote: big-S 願景訪談要問「一天的樣子」而不是「功能清單」，才會得到可設計的場景。
cards.episode: An operator’s guide to product strategy | Chandra Janakiraman (CPO at VRChat, ex-Meta, Headspace, Zynga)

alts.quote: So I guess there's two ways of planning. The way that you can plan is you can dream of what is the perfect vision of the future, what future do you want to exist in, what would you like the world to look like?
alts.zh: 我覺得規劃大概分兩種。一種是你去夢想那個最完美的未來——你想活在什麼樣的未來裡？你希望這個世界長什麼樣子？

alts.quote: We should be cannibalizing the existing state of our product every six to 12 months. Every six to 12 months, it should make our existing product look silly.
alts.zh: 我們應該每六到十二個月就把自己現有的產品吃掉一次。每六到十二個月，新的東西就該讓舊的看起來很蠢。

alts.quote: And he would say, you have to aim for Chartres. You have to make something that is better than that. That should be your goal, not to just turn in something that's what you feel is good enough.
alts.zh: 他會說：你要對準夏特大教堂。你要做出比它更好的東西。那才是你的目標，而不是交出一個你自己覺得「還可以」的作品。

cards.pattern: [X] is deterministic. When you [做動作], it either [成功] or it doesn't.
cards.quote: Software is deterministic. When you write code and you hit run, it either runs or it doesn't.
cards.zh: 軟體是確定性的。你寫完程式按下執行，它要嘛跑起來、要嘛跑不起來。
cards.why: 先給一個抽象性質（deterministic），立刻用一個五歲小孩都懂的動作解釋它。這種「術語＋白話對照」的雙句組，是把技術原因講給非技術聽的標準做法。
swaps: It's binary: it compiles or it doesn't.
There's a ground truth here, which is rare.
cards.pmNote: AI 在有客觀驗證訊號的領域進展最快；沒有 ground truth 的領域難以擴大訓練。
cards.episode: Inside Bolt: From near-death to ~$40m ARR in 5 months—one of the fastest-growing products in history | Eric Simons (founder and CEO of StackBlitz)

alts.quote: But then the job of the forward deployed engineer is not just to deploy software. It is not just to sell software. It is to actually solve the problem.
alts.zh: 前線工程師的工作不只是把軟體部署上去，也不只是把軟體賣出去，而是真的把問題解決掉。

alts.quote: So we try to build a team based on the needs of the work a bit, but then end up with a much smaller core.
alts.zh: 所以我們會盡量照工作本身的需求去組團隊，最後就會收斂成一個小很多的核心。

alts.quote: Maybe my best advice here is for founders to put themselves in the shoes of investors and just imagine what their life is like and how if you are in their shoes you would make decisions.
alts.zh: 我最好的建議大概是：創辦人去站在投資人的位置上，想像他們的日子長什麼樣、如果換成你會怎麼做決定。

cards.pattern: Until you see pull—people pulling the product out of your hands—you don't want to be spending money.
cards.quote: And I would just say generally, until you see pull, just people pulling the product out of your hands, you don't want to be spending money.
cards.zh: 我會說一個通則：在你看到「拉力」之前——就是人家把產品從你手上搶走那種——你都不該開始花錢。
cards.why: pull 這個抽象名詞馬上被一個具體動作重講一次（把產品從你手上搶走），聽眾就不會各自解讀。定義關鍵詞是解釋原因時最常被跳過的一步。
swaps: Wait for demand to pull before you push spend.
Nobody's ripping it out of our hands yet, so we're not spending yet.
cards.pmNote: 在 PMF 前提高 burn rate 會直接減少可嘗試的次數，也就是減少成功機率。
cards.episode: Inside Bolt: From near-death to ~$40m ARR in 5 months—one of the fastest-growing products in history | Eric Simons (founder and CEO of StackBlitz)

alts.quote: People often think that I get hired into later stage companies because I'm supposed to teach them how to operate like a big company, and in fact, I say I'm hired to remind them they can operate like a startup.
alts.zh: 大家常以為，公司找我去後期階段是要我教他們怎麼像大公司一樣運作；但其實我都說，我是被找去提醒他們，他們還可以像新創一樣運作。

alts.quote: He used to tell people, he said, "The key for career planning is," he said, "don't be fungible." He's an economist and so that was economic speaking. What that means essentially is don't be replaceable.
alts.zh: 他都跟人說：「職涯規劃的關鍵就是，別讓自己可被替換。」他是經濟學家，所以講得比較術語。白話講就是：別讓自己是可以隨便換掉的那個人。

alts.quote: He said that, "Hey, CJ, I'm hearing that a lot of people don't really understand why we are working on what we are working on," and that was it.
alts.zh: 他說：「欸 CJ，我聽到不少人其實不太明白，我們為什麼在做我們正在做的事。」就這樣，講完了。

cards.pattern: That just felt completely backwards. I should be spending 90% of the time on [重要的], 10% on [次要的].
cards.quote: And for me, that just felt completely backwards. I should be spending 90% of the time on the content, 10% maybe on the design and formatting.
cards.zh: 對我來說那整件事根本是反過來的。我應該把 90% 的時間花在內容上，設計排版頂多 10%。
cards.why: 用兩個數字把「不合理」講成可量測的失衡，比說 it's frustrating 有力太多。backwards 一詞暗示問題出在順序而不是程度。
swaps: The ratio is inverted.
We're spending the majority of our time on the minority of the value.
cards.pmNote: 產品機會常藏在使用者時間分配與價值分配不一致的地方。
cards.episode: “Dumbest idea I’ve heard” to $100M ARR: Inside the rise of Gamma | Grant Lee (CEO)

alts.quote: Maybe my best advice here is for founders to put themselves in the shoes of investors and just imagine what their life is like and how if you are in their shoes you would make decisions.
alts.zh: 我最好的建議大概是：創辦人去站在投資人的位置上，想像他們的日子長什麼樣、如果換成你會怎麼做決定。

alts.quote: It's not that you actually are going to watch it the whole time, but it gives you a mental model and makes you feel in control.
alts.zh: 並不是說你真的會全程盯著看，而是它讓你有一個心智模型，讓你覺得自己掌握著方向盤。

alts.quote: And I would just say generally, until you see pull, just people pulling the product out of your hands, you don't want to be spending money.
alts.zh: 我會說一個通則：在你看到「拉力」之前——就是人家把產品從你手上搶走那種——你都不該開始花錢。

cards.quote: Virtual office could get pretty good, but we would never beat that. And so we were almost limited in our own imagination about how good could this product be.
cards.zh: 虛擬辦公室可以做到不錯，但我們永遠贏不過真實見面。所以我們等於是被自己的想像力上限卡住了——這個產品最好能到哪裡。
cards.why: 解釋「為什麼砍掉另一條路」時，不講資源不足、不講市場小，而講「天花板在哪」。limited in our own imagination 這個講法把放棄講成清醒，不是失敗。
swaps: The ceiling on that one was someone else's product—real life.
We could win the category and still lose to the alternative.
cards.pmNote: 評估產品時要先找出真正的替代方案（含非產品的替代），再問能不能超越它。
cards.episode: “Dumbest idea I’ve heard” to $100M ARR: Inside the rise of Gamma | Grant Lee (CEO)

alts.quote: So if you take that viewpoint, then pricing needs to sit in the product function. This is my strong-held belief, one that probably won't change now.
alts.zh: 如果你接受那個看法，那定價就必須放在產品這一側。這是我很堅定的信念，大概不會再改了。

alts.quote: Yeah. Imagine, no such thing as a request from sales, yeah? No such thing as pressure of like, "We need this thing in order to upsell or to close this deal." Never.
alts.zh: 你想像一下：完全沒有業務來提需求，好嗎？也完全沒有那種「我們需要這個功能才能升級方案、才能成交」的壓力。從來沒有。

alts.quote: And I would just say generally, until you see pull, just people pulling the product out of your hands, you don't want to be spending money.
alts.zh: 我會說一個通則：在你看到「拉力」之前——就是人家把產品從你手上搶走那種——你都不該開始花錢。

cards.quote: But before you do that, you should think about, "Is this a problem I can invest five to 10 years into actually solving? Do I care deeply enough about it?"
cards.zh: 但在那之前你該先想：這是不是一個我願意投入五到十年去真正解決的問題？我對它在乎得夠深嗎？
cards.why: 用時間長度當篩子（five to 10 years），比問「你有沒有熱情」具體太多。兩個問句一外一內：第一個問可行性，第二個問動機。
swaps: Would I still want this problem in year seven?
Is this a decade-long problem or a good quarter?
cards.pmNote: 選題要看問題的耐久性；風口型題目在模型或平台變動後常整個消失。
cards.episode: “Dumbest idea I’ve heard” to $100M ARR: Inside the rise of Gamma | Grant Lee (CEO)

alts.quote: But then the job of the forward deployed engineer is not just to deploy software. It is not just to sell software. It is to actually solve the problem.
alts.zh: 前線工程師的工作不只是把軟體部署上去，也不只是把軟體賣出去，而是真的把問題解決掉。

alts.quote: People often think that I get hired into later stage companies because I'm supposed to teach them how to operate like a big company, and in fact, I say I'm hired to remind them they can operate like a startup.
alts.zh: 大家常以為，公司找我去後期階段是要我教他們怎麼像大公司一樣運作；但其實我都說，我是被找去提醒他們，他們還可以像新創一樣運作。

alts.quote: It's not that you actually are going to watch it the whole time, but it gives you a mental model and makes you feel in control.
alts.zh: 並不是說你真的會全程盯著看，而是它讓你有一個心智模型，讓你覺得自己掌握著方向盤。

cards.pattern: It is just so natural for our internal lingo to flow into the application over time. You need some counterbalance. It has to be an unnatural counterbalance.
cards.quote: It is just so natural for our internal mindset and lingo to flow into the application over time. And you need some counterbalance to get there. And I think it has to be an unnatural counterbalance.
cards.zh: 內部的思維和黑話會很自然地慢慢滲進產品裡。你需要某種抗衡的力量。而且我認為那必須是一種「不自然」的力量。
cards.why: 先把問題歸因給「自然」（不是誰的錯），再主張解方必須「不自然」（所以才需要制度）。這組 natural / unnatural 的對照，讓流程提案不像在指責團隊。
swaps: Drift is the default. You have to build something that fights it.
Nothing corrects this by itself—it needs a ritual.
cards.pmNote: 產品熵增需要制度化的外部視角（friction log、study group）才會被持續發現。
cards.episode: Building product at Stripe: craft, metrics, and customer obsession | Jeff Weinstein (Product lead)

alts.quote: I think the thing you really need to know is that for under 16-year-olds, if they want to change any of these defaults, they're going to have to get their parents' permission.
alts.zh: 我覺得你真正需要知道的是：未滿 16 歲的用戶如果想改這些預設值，必須先拿到父母同意。

alts.quote: People often think that I get hired into later stage companies because I'm supposed to teach them how to operate like a big company, and in fact, I say I'm hired to remind them they can operate like a startup.
alts.zh: 大家常以為，公司找我去後期階段是要我教他們怎麼像大公司一樣運作；但其實我都說，我是被找去提醒他們，他們還可以像新創一樣運作。

alts.quote: Yeah. Imagine, no such thing as a request from sales, yeah? No such thing as pressure of like, "We need this thing in order to upsell or to close this deal." Never.
alts.zh: 你想像一下：完全沒有業務來提需求，好嗎？也完全沒有那種「我們需要這個功能才能升級方案、才能成交」的壓力。從來沒有。

cards.quote: He said that, "Hey, CJ, I'm hearing that a lot of people don't really understand why we are working on what we are working on," and that was it.
cards.zh: 他說：「欸 CJ，我聽到不少人其實不太明白，我們為什麼在做我們正在做的事。」就這樣，講完了。
cards.why: I'm hearing that 把訊息來源模糊化，讓批評不指向任何個人；後半句刻意重複 working on 製造繞口感，反而讓「講不清楚」這件事被聽見。這是主管給重話卻不點火的講法。
swaps: I'm hearing some confusion about why this is the priority.
People can recite the roadmap. They can't explain it.
cards.pmNote: 團隊能背 roadmap 卻說不出 why，通常是缺策略而不是缺溝通。
cards.episode: An operator’s guide to product strategy | Chandra Janakiraman (CPO at VRChat, ex-Meta, Headspace, Zynga)

alts.quote: He used to tell people, he said, "The key for career planning is," he said, "don't be fungible." He's an economist and so that was economic speaking. What that means essentially is don't be replaceable.
alts.zh: 他都跟人說：「職涯規劃的關鍵就是，別讓自己可被替換。」他是經濟學家，所以講得比較術語。白話講就是：別讓自己是可以隨便換掉的那個人。

alts.quote: People often think that I get hired into later stage companies because I'm supposed to teach them how to operate like a big company, and in fact, I say I'm hired to remind them they can operate like a startup.
alts.zh: 大家常以為，公司找我去後期階段是要我教他們怎麼像大公司一樣運作；但其實我都說，我是被找去提醒他們，他們還可以像新創一樣運作。

alts.quote: And I would just say generally, until you see pull, just people pulling the product out of your hands, you don't want to be spending money.
alts.zh: 我會說一個通則：在你看到「拉力」之前——就是人家把產品從你手上搶走那種——你都不該開始花錢。

cards.pattern: Even though I really like a lot about [X], I'm going to say no.
cards.quote: And so even though I really like a lot about this, I'm going to say no." And I often think that founders think that there's some secret truth that's being held from them on why someone says no or they want more feedback.
cards.zh: 「就算我真的很喜歡這個東西的很多地方，我還是要說不。」我也常覺得，創辦人以為別人說不的背後藏著什麼沒告訴他的秘密，或想再要更多回饋。
cards.why: 拒絕前先把「我喜歡什麼」講具體（a lot about this），對方才知道你有認真看過；接著 I'm going to say no 用主動語態自己扛下決定，不推給流程或別人。台灣人常反過來——先鋪一堆理由，最後那句「不行」講得像被迫的。
cards.pmNote: 被拒絕後追問「還缺什麼」通常換不到不同結果，只會讓雙方都耗著；把 no 講清楚比講軟更仁慈。
cards.episode: Lessons from 1,000+ YC startups: Resilience, tar pit ideas, pivoting, more | Dalton Caldwell (Y Combinator, Managing Director)

alts.quote: So yeah, I think the only way you build something that matters that's going to change the world is if you find a big idea you believe in and you say no to everything else.
alts.zh: 我覺得要做出真正有份量、能改變世界的東西，唯一的路就是找到一個你相信的大想法，然後對其他所有東西說不。

alts.quote: if you want to change during the course of the quarter, if you want to disrupt our whole engineering product team, you can do it, but understand there's a high cost, and the later you do it in the quarter, the less successful it's going to be
alts.zh: 你想在季中改、想打亂整個工程團隊，可以啊，但你要知道代價很高——而且愈晚改，效果只會愈差。

alts.quote: We're not going to interrupt you with a popup that says like, "Do you want to save your changes," or any of that kind of stuff.
alts.zh: 我們不會用那種「你要儲存變更嗎？」的彈窗打斷你，那類東西都不會有。

cards.pattern: If it's not [品質門檻], we're not going to ship it.
cards.quote: If it's not lovable, we're not going to ship it.
cards.zh: 如果它還不到讓人喜歡的程度，我們就不會出。
cards.why: 把拒絕寫成一條條件句，界線就不是針對人而是針對標準——下次同一個人再來，他自己知道要先過那個門檻。lovable 這種具體形容詞也比「品質不夠」難含糊帶過。
cards.pmNote: 出貨門檻要用一個記得住的形容詞（lovable、not embarrassing），團隊才會自己檢查，而不是等你來擋。
cards.episode: Elena Verna 4.0

alts.quote: We're not going to show you that, but here are the middle grade books or whatever." There is a little bit of that.
alts.zh: 「我們不會給你看那個，但這裡有中年級的書之類的。」多少有一點那種味道。

alts.quote: We're going to have salespeople helping you through it, but we're not going to let you hire someone.
alts.zh: 我們會派業務協助你走完這段，但我們不會讓你去請一個人。

alts.quote: That's what we're going to focus on." And so no, we're not going to add five more features.
alts.zh: 「那就是我們要專注的地方。」所以不，我們不會再加五個功能。

cards.pattern: Sometimes I have to say no to [老闆/重要的人] and say, "I can't make it."
cards.quote: And sometimes I have to say no to Anton and say, "I can't make it," or, "I won't be there.
cards.zh: 有時候我就得對 Anton 說不，跟他說「我沒辦法」或「我不會到」。
cards.why: I can't make it 是狀況陳述、I won't be there 是意志陳述——後者更硬也更誠實。對上位者說不時多數人只敢用 can't（把責任推給行事曆），敢偶爾用 won't 的人反而被當成有優先順序的人。
cards.pmNote: 對主管說不要給「不能到」的事實，不要給「不想去」的評價；理由留給對方問。
cards.episode: Elena Verna 4.0

alts.quote: I can't really go into specifics a bunch with YouTube, but what I would say is this.
alts.zh: YouTube 那邊的細節我不太方便講，但我可以講的是這個。

alts.quote: let's say somebody commenting about your business, who does not understand the nuance of it, you can't be reacting to everything.
alts.zh: 假設有人在評論你的生意，但他根本不懂裡面的細節——你不可能每件事都去回應。

alts.quote: You can say, "Yes, I agree. That is a real problem. Yes, I think we could test this design with users."
alts.zh: 你可以說：「對，我同意，那確實是個真的問題。對，我覺得這個設計我們可以拿去跟使用者測。」

cards.pattern: We're not going to try this again because we literally did try everything we could to test [假設].
cards.quote: And if with all of that it didn't work, then you can say, "Hey, we're not going to try this again because we literally did try everything that we could to test this hypothesis.
cards.zh: 如果做到那樣還是沒用，你就可以說：「我們不會再試一次了，因為我們真的已經把能測的都測過了。」
cards.why: 拒絕重來的關鍵不是「這個沒用」，而是「我們窮盡了」——literally did try everything 把舉證責任翻給對方：你想再試，得先講出我們沒試過的那一招。
cards.pmNote: 要能講這句，前提是實驗過程有留紀錄；沒紀錄的失敗永遠會被要求再做一次。
cards.episode: Failure

alts.quote: We're not going to write out long-form content around everything related to dating because that's not the Tinder product.
alts.zh: 我們不會針對所有跟約會有關的東西寫長文，因為那不是 Tinder 這個產品。

alts.quote: Because if I'm not excited about what you you're doing, we're not going to work together.
alts.zh: 因為如果我對你在做的事沒有興奮感，我們就不會合作。

alts.quote: So yeah, I think the only way you build something that matters that's going to change the world is if you find a big idea you believe in and you say no to everything else.
alts.zh: 我覺得要做出真正有份量、能改變世界的東西，唯一的路就是找到一個你相信的大想法，然後對其他所有東西說不。

cards.pattern: We're so ambitious that we're not going to hold onto [還可以但不夠好的東西].
cards.quote: We're so ambitious that we're not going to hold onto a B+.
cards.zh: 我們野心大到不會抱著一個「B+」不放。
cards.why: 把砍掉包裝成「我們標準高」，拒絕就從損失變成宣示——對方不會覺得被否定，會覺得被拉高。so...that 的結構讓理由（ambitious）先出場，決定才落地。
cards.pmNote: 最難砍的不是爛專案，是「還可以」的專案；它們吃掉的是你做 A 的時間。
cards.episode: The hidden pattern behind successful products | Mark Pincus (Founder of Zynga)

alts.quote: But if a PM came to me with something that was drawn and kind of fully baked, my response was like, thanks for giving me that. Now I know exactly what we're not going to do.
alts.zh: 如果 PM 拿一張畫得很完整的圖來找我，我的回應是：謝謝你給我這個，現在我很清楚我們「不會」做成這樣。

alts.quote: And if with all of that it didn't work, then you can say, "Hey, we're not going to try this again because we literally did try everything that we could to test this hypothesis.
alts.zh: 如果做到那樣還是沒用，你就可以說：「我們不會再試一次了，因為我們真的已經把能測的都測過了。」

alts.quote: We're not going to write out long-form content around everything related to dating because that's not the Tinder product.
alts.zh: 我們不會針對所有跟約會有關的東西寫長文，因為那不是 Tinder 這個產品。

cards.pattern: We're not going to do something that doesn't align with [目標] in order to gain short term brownie points with [某方].
cards.quote: Or we're not going to do something unnatural or something that doesn't align with the business goals in order to gain any short term brownie points with investors.
cards.zh: 我們也不會為了在投資人面前拿一點短期的印象分，就去做不自然、或跟商業目標不一致的事。
cards.why: 拒絕短期作秀時，把對方的動機講白（short term brownie points）再否定它，比說「這樣不好」有殺傷力；in order to 把那個動作重新描述成「為了討好誰」，一講出來就沒人好意思堅持。
cards.pmNote: 被要求為了某場會議「先做個看得到的東西」時，先問這件事在會後還有沒有價值。
cards.episode: Product lessons from Waymo | Shweta Shrivastava (Waymo, Amazon, Cisco)

alts.quote: But if a PM came to me with something that was drawn and kind of fully baked, my response was like, thanks for giving me that. Now I know exactly what we're not going to do.
alts.zh: 如果 PM 拿一張畫得很完整的圖來找我，我的回應是：謝謝你給我這個，現在我很清楚我們「不會」做成這樣。

alts.quote: We're not going to interrupt you with a popup that says like, "Do you want to save your changes," or any of that kind of stuff.
alts.zh: 我們不會用那種「你要儲存變更嗎？」的彈窗打斷你，那類東西都不會有。

alts.quote: We're not going to get people necessarily building integrations just for us out of the gate unless we have a really compelling product around that.
alts.zh: 除非我們先把周邊產品做到真的夠有說服力，不然一開始不會有人專門為我們做整合。

cards.quote: Actively say no to solving the easy ones.
cards.zh: 要主動拒絕去解那些簡單的問題。
cards.why: actively 是全句的重點：不做簡單的事不會自然發生，得刻意去擋。把拒絕從「守」變成一個主動動作，也順帶說明了為什麼——簡單的問題誰都能解，解了沒有差異。
cards.pmNote: 團隊自然會漂向好解的問題，因為有成就感；排序時要主動把「容易但不重要」那格清空。
cards.episode: The unconventional Palantir principles that catalyzed a generation of startups

alts.quote: I am really hesitant to recommend any template. And what I'd say is these are principles for building it, not any prescribed formula.
alts.zh: 我真的很不願意推薦任何範本。我會說，這些是建構的原則，不是一套規定好的公式。

alts.quote: I don't think it's particularly productive to say, "Well, is it 20% bigger than the internet or 100%?" Those aren't productive conversations.
alts.zh: 去爭「它比網路大 20% 還是 100%」我覺得沒什麼意義，那種對話不會有產出。

alts.quote: I would say wait until it hurts more. If the unfamiliarity is the big problem with it, then maybe the things are fine.
alts.zh: 我會說：等到更痛再來。如果你最大的問題只是「不熟悉」，那可能表示現在其實還好。

cards.pattern: We're not going to [做 X], but here are [替代方案].
cards.quote: We're not going to show you that, but here are the middle grade books or whatever." There is a little bit of that.
cards.zh: 「我們不會給你看那個，但這裡有中年級的書之類的。」多少有一點那種味道。
cards.why: 拒絕後面緊接 but here are…，把對話從「要不要」拉回「那要哪個」。沒有替代方案的 no 會被反覆挑戰，有替代方案的 no 通常一次就過。
cards.pmNote: 擋需求時同時給一個「次好選項」，對方才有東西可以回報給他的老闆。
cards.episode: How to see like a designer: The hidden power of typography and logos | Jessica Hische (Lettering Artist, Author)

alts.quote: If it's not lovable, we're not going to ship it.
alts.zh: 如果它還不到讓人喜歡的程度，我們就不會出。

alts.quote: We're going to have salespeople helping you through it, but we're not going to let you hire someone.
alts.zh: 我們會派業務協助你走完這段，但我們不會讓你去請一個人。

alts.quote: That's what we're going to focus on." And so no, we're not going to add five more features.
alts.zh: 「那就是我們要專注的地方。」所以不，我們不會再加五個功能。

cards.pattern: We're going to [給的部分], but we're not going to [不給的部分].
cards.quote: We're going to have salespeople helping you through it, but we're not going to let you hire someone.
cards.zh: 我們會派業務協助你走完這段，但我們不會讓你去請一個人。
cards.why: 一句話裡同時放「給什麼」和「不給什麼」，範圍一次釘死；先講給的再講不給的，對方聽完記得的是自己拿到什麼。台灣人常只講不給的那半，聽起來像整件事被打回票。
cards.pmNote: 談範圍時把「支援」和「資源」分開講——願意投人力不等於願意加編制。
cards.episode: "Sell the alpha, not the feature": The enterprise sales playbook for $1M to $10M ARR | Jen Abel

alts.quote: If it's not lovable, we're not going to ship it.
alts.zh: 如果它還不到讓人喜歡的程度，我們就不會出。

alts.quote: We're not going to show you that, but here are the middle grade books or whatever." There is a little bit of that.
alts.zh: 「我們不會給你看那個，但這裡有中年級的書之類的。」多少有一點那種味道。

alts.quote: That's what we're going to focus on." And so no, we're not going to add five more features.
alts.zh: 「那就是我們要專注的地方。」所以不，我們不會再加五個功能。

cards.pattern: We're not going to [做 X] because that's not the [產品] product.
cards.quote: We're not going to write out long-form content around everything related to dating because that's not the Tinder product.
cards.zh: 我們不會針對所有跟約會有關的東西寫長文，因為那不是 Tinder 這個產品。
cards.why: 用「那不是我們的產品」當理由，拒絕的依據就從個人品味換成產品身分，對方沒得吵——要吵得先吵「我們是誰」。that's not the X product 很短，卻是最難反駁的一種理由。
cards.pmNote: 內容或功能要不要做，先問「這是不是我們的產品該負責的事」，再問流量或成本。
cards.episode: Rethinking SEO in the age of AI | Eli Schwartz (SEO advisor, author)

alts.quote: And if with all of that it didn't work, then you can say, "Hey, we're not going to try this again because we literally did try everything that we could to test this hypothesis.
alts.zh: 如果做到那樣還是沒用，你就可以說：「我們不會再試一次了，因為我們真的已經把能測的都測過了。」

alts.quote: We're not going to get people necessarily building integrations just for us out of the gate unless we have a really compelling product around that.
alts.zh: 除非我們先把周邊產品做到真的夠有說服力，不然一開始不會有人專門為我們做整合。

alts.quote: And also, we're not going to lock you into a cloud, you can choose." And obviously, that's what businesses want.
alts.zh: 「而且我們不會把你綁死在某一朵雲上，你可以自己選。」這顯然就是企業要的。

cards.pattern: That's what we're going to focus on. And so no, we're not going to add [更多 X].
cards.quote: That's what we're going to focus on." And so no, we're not going to add five more features.
cards.zh: 「那就是我們要專注的地方。」所以不，我們不會再加五個功能。
cards.why: 先重述已經同意的焦點，再說 no——拒絕就變成執行剛剛的共識，不是新的爭議。And so no 的 so 是全句樞紐：它讓 no 看起來是推論出來的，不是情緒。
cards.pmNote: 擋加功能時引用團隊自己定的焦點，比說資源不足有效——後者會招來「那我幫你要人」。
cards.episode: Father of the iPod and iPhone on building taste, judgment, and creativity in the AI era | Tony Fadell

alts.quote: We're not going to write out long-form content around everything related to dating because that's not the Tinder product.
alts.zh: 我們不會針對所有跟約會有關的東西寫長文，因為那不是 Tinder 這個產品。

alts.quote: And also, we're not going to lock you into a cloud, you can choose." And obviously, that's what businesses want.
alts.zh: 「而且我們不會把你綁死在某一朵雲上，你可以自己選。」這顯然就是企業要的。

alts.quote: If it's not lovable, we're not going to ship it.
alts.zh: 如果它還不到讓人喜歡的程度，我們就不會出。

cards.pattern: We're not going to interrupt you with [具體的干擾], or any of that kind of stuff.
cards.quote: We're not going to interrupt you with a popup that says like, "Do you want to save your changes," or any of that kind of stuff.
cards.zh: 我們不會用那種「你要儲存變更嗎？」的彈窗打斷你，那類東西都不會有。
cards.why: 講「我們不做什麼」時給一個大家都受過罪的具體畫面，比抽象的「我們重視體驗」有力十倍；結尾 or any of that kind of stuff 再把同類一起關掉，省得之後逐項再吵。
cards.pmNote: 產品原則要用反例寫才守得住：正面形容詞人人同意，反例才會擋下 PR。
cards.episode: Linear’s secret to building beloved B2B products | Nan Yu (Head of Product)

alts.quote: But if a PM came to me with something that was drawn and kind of fully baked, my response was like, thanks for giving me that. Now I know exactly what we're not going to do.
alts.zh: 如果 PM 拿一張畫得很完整的圖來找我，我的回應是：謝謝你給我這個，現在我很清楚我們「不會」做成這樣。

alts.quote: And so even though I really like a lot about this, I'm going to say no." And I often think that founders think that there's some secret truth that's being held from them on why someone says no or they want more feedback.
alts.zh: 「就算我真的很喜歡這個東西的很多地方，我還是要說不。」我也常覺得，創辦人以為別人說不的背後藏著什麼沒告訴他的秘密，或想再要更多回饋。

alts.quote: And also, we're not going to lock you into a cloud, you can choose." And obviously, that's what businesses want.
alts.zh: 「而且我們不會把你綁死在某一朵雲上，你可以自己選。」這顯然就是企業要的。

cards.pattern: We're not going to have an hour-long conversation about [小事].
cards.quote: We're not going to have an hour-long conversation about a support ticket.
cards.zh: 我們不會為了一張客服單開一小時的會。
cards.why: 把拒絕綁在「時間 × 事情大小」的比例上，聽起來就不是不在乎，而是不成比例。開會被歪樓時這句可以直接照抄。
cards.pmNote: 會議失控多半不是議題錯，是層級錯——個案要在會後單線處理，會上只談政策。
cards.episode: 10 lessons on bootstrapping a $200m business | Patrick Campbell (ProfitWell)

alts.quote: We're not going to write out long-form content around everything related to dating because that's not the Tinder product.
alts.zh: 我們不會針對所有跟約會有關的東西寫長文，因為那不是 Tinder 這個產品。

alts.quote: And when we got acquired, we had a conversation with our team where we said, we're going to of course embrace Spotify's culture and Spotify's core values, but we're not going to forget who we are as a team.
alts.zh: 被併購之後我們跟團隊談，說我們當然會擁抱 Spotify 的文化和核心價值，但我們不會忘記自己這個團隊是誰。

alts.quote: If it's not lovable, we're not going to ship it.
alts.zh: 如果它還不到讓人喜歡的程度，我們就不會出。

cards.quote: If the answer is no, just cancel it.
cards.zh: 如果答案是「不」，那就直接取消。
cards.why: If the answer is no 讓「不」變成一個測驗結果，而不是誰的立場；後半 just cancel it 用 just 把行動說得很輕，降低取消的心理成本。
cards.pmNote: 每個例會都該有一個「這週還有沒有必須一起決定的事？」的問句，沒有就取消。
cards.episode: How to fire people with grace, work through fear, and nurture innovation | Matt Mochary (CEO coach)

alts.quote: If the product manager and the designer are not available to be there during their product test, cancel the test. They need to be there.
alts.zh: 如果產品經理和設計師沒辦法到場，那這場使用者測試就取消。他們一定要在現場。

alts.quote: So if you can't answer the question about what is it that someone's going to do a search on, then don't do SEO, because SEO is about appealing to that user.
alts.zh: 所以如果你答不出「別人會搜什麼」這個問題，那就不要做 SEO——因為 SEO 就是在對那個使用者說話。

alts.quote: So I'm like, "Will anyone care in six months what we did here?" And the answer is no.
alts.zh: 所以我就想：「六個月後還有人會在乎我們這裡做了什麼嗎？」答案是不會。

cards.pattern: We're not going to lock you into [某個綁定], you can choose.
cards.quote: And also, we're not going to lock you into a cloud, you can choose." And obviously, that's what businesses want.
cards.zh: 「而且我們不會把你綁死在某一朵雲上，你可以自己選。」這顯然就是企業要的。
cards.why: 對客戶講「我們不做什麼」其實是承諾，不是拒絕——lock you into 精準點出對方最怕的事，後面補一句 you can choose 把控制權還回去。
cards.pmNote: B2B 的差異化常常不是多一個功能，而是少一個限制；先找出對手讓客戶最不舒服的那條綁約。
cards.episode: Max Schoenig

alts.quote: And so even though I really like a lot about this, I'm going to say no." And I often think that founders think that there's some secret truth that's being held from them on why someone says no or they want more feedback.
alts.zh: 「就算我真的很喜歡這個東西的很多地方，我還是要說不。」我也常覺得，創辦人以為別人說不的背後藏著什麼沒告訴他的秘密，或想再要更多回饋。

alts.quote: We're not going to write out long-form content around everything related to dating because that's not the Tinder product.
alts.zh: 我們不會針對所有跟約會有關的東西寫長文，因為那不是 Tinder 這個產品。

alts.quote: We're not going to interrupt you with a popup that says like, "Do you want to save your changes," or any of that kind of stuff.
alts.zh: 我們不會用那種「你要儲存變更嗎？」的彈窗打斷你，那類東西都不會有。

cards.pattern: I'm not willing to [付出 X], but I would [接受 Y].
cards.quote: I'm not willing to pay what I think the current tickets are, but I would take the risk.
cards.zh: 我不願意付我認為現在票價的那個價錢，但我願意承擔那個風險。
cards.why: I'm not willing to 把界線畫在「意願」而不是「能力」，比 I can't 更誠實也更難被說服；緊接 but I would… 立刻給出你願意付的另一種代價，談判就沒卡死。
cards.pmNote: 拒絕條件時同時報出你願意接受的替代代價（時間、風險、範圍），對方才知道還能不能談。
cards.episode: Taking control of your career | Ethan Evans (Amazon)

alts.quote: And so even though I really like a lot about this, I'm going to say no." And I often think that founders think that there's some secret truth that's being held from them on why someone says no or they want more feedback.
alts.zh: 「就算我真的很喜歡這個東西的很多地方，我還是要說不。」我也常覺得，創辦人以為別人說不的背後藏著什麼沒告訴他的秘密，或想再要更多回饋。

alts.quote: I'm not willing to be an activist.
alts.zh: 我不願意扮演那種要一直去衝撞的角色。

alts.quote: And so we had this idea that we came up with that would do it. I'm not going to let that one out.
alts.zh: 我們後來想到一個做得到的點子。那個我就不外流了。

cards.pattern: I'm not willing to be [某種角色].
cards.quote: I'm not willing to be an activist.
cards.zh: 我不願意扮演那種要一直去衝撞的角色。
cards.why: 拒絕「角色」比拒絕「單一任務」有效——一次講清楚就不用每件事再拒一次。willing 這個字承認你做得到、只是選擇不做，反而顯得有主體性。
cards.pmNote: 一直被叫去救火，問題通常出在你沒拒絕過那個角色，只拒絕過個別的火。
cards.episode: How to build a company that withstands any era | Eric Ries, Lean Startup author

alts.quote: I'm not willing to pay what I think the current tickets are, but I would take the risk.
alts.zh: 我不願意付我認為現在票價的那個價錢，但我願意承擔那個風險。

alts.quote: if you just want an hour of my time randomly, I'm sorry, honestly, I'm sorry, I don't have that hour of time
alts.zh: 如果你只是想隨機約我一小時，抱歉，真的很抱歉，我沒有那一小時。

alts.quote: So I'm like, "Will anyone care in six months what we did here?" And the answer is no.
alts.zh: 所以我就想：「六個月後還有人會在乎我們這裡做了什麼嗎？」答案是不會。

cards.pattern: We need to say no to a lot more of this [類別] work.
cards.quote: We need to say no to a lot more of this optional work.
cards.zh: 這種「可做可不做」的工作，我們得再多拒絕一些。
cards.why: 先幫工作貼上 optional 這個標籤，拒絕就變成分類問題而不是價值判斷；a lot more 也暗示現在拒得太少，是團隊集體要調的量，不是針對誰。
cards.pmNote: roadmap 上先把每一項標成 must / optional，砍的時候就不用重新辯論。
cards.episode: Jackie Bavaro on getting better at product strategy, what exactly is strategy, PM pitfalls to avoid, advancing your career, getting into management, and much more

alts.quote: And we know that eventually we need to get it, but we don't need it today. So we just say no to that.
alts.zh: 我們知道遲早得弄那個，但今天不需要。所以我們就直接說不。

alts.quote: And so even though I really like a lot about this, I'm going to say no." And I often think that founders think that there's some secret truth that's being held from them on why someone says no or they want more feedback.
alts.zh: 「就算我真的很喜歡這個東西的很多地方，我還是要說不。」我也常覺得，創辦人以為別人說不的背後藏著什麼沒告訴他的秘密，或想再要更多回饋。

alts.quote: And if with all of that it didn't work, then you can say, "Hey, we're not going to try this again because we literally did try everything that we could to test this hypothesis.
alts.zh: 如果做到那樣還是沒用，你就可以說：「我們不會再試一次了，因為我們真的已經把能測的都測過了。」

cards.pattern: Your job is to say no to [百分比] of things that get brought your way.
cards.quote: When I first started out in PM somebody, it's obviously a chestnut, but he pointed out that realistically when you're a product manager, your job is to say no to 90% of things that get brought your way.
cards.zh: 我剛入行做 PM 的時候，有人跟我說——雖然是老生常談——現實是，PM 的工作就是把送到你面前的事拒絕掉九成。
cards.why: 把拒絕寫成「職務內容」而不是「態度」，說 no 就不必每次都道歉；再加上 90% 這個數字，對方會知道被拒絕是常態，不是他特別倒楣。
cards.pmNote: 如果你這季的需求通過率遠高於一成，通常代表需求還沒被真正排序，只是被排隊。
cards.episode: Why great AI products are all about the data | Shaun Clowes (CPO Confluent, ex-Salesforce, Atlassian)

alts.quote: Pulling off other responsibilities is no problem. It's a good thing to do, especially as you grow, but never when you touch those three sacred things.
alts.zh: 把其他職責分出去完全沒問題，隨著規模變大這反而是好事——但前提是不能碰到那三件神聖不可讓的事。

alts.quote: I don't think it's particularly productive to say, "Well, is it 20% bigger than the internet or 100%?" Those aren't productive conversations.
alts.zh: 去爭「它比網路大 20% 還是 100%」我覺得沒什麼意義，那種對話不會有產出。

alts.quote: I would say wait until it hurts more. If the unfamiliarity is the big problem with it, then maybe the things are fine.
alts.zh: 我會說：等到更痛再來。如果你最大的問題只是「不熟悉」，那可能表示現在其實還好。

cards.pattern: Find [一個你相信的大方向] and say no to everything else.
cards.quote: So yeah, I think the only way you build something that matters that's going to change the world is if you find a big idea you believe in and you say no to everything else.
cards.zh: 我覺得要做出真正有份量、能改變世界的東西，唯一的路就是找到一個你相信的大想法，然後對其他所有東西說不。
cards.why: say no to everything else 把拒絕綁在一個已經選好的 yes 上——沒有那個 yes，所有的 no 都只是防守。被追問「為什麼不做」時，這也是最好的回法：因為我們選了那個。
cards.pmNote: 拒絕的說服力來自你講不講得出那個唯一的 yes；講不出來，你的 no 就只是沒空。
cards.episode: The 100-person AI lab that became Anthropic and Google's secret weapon | Edwin Chen (Surge AI)

alts.quote: And so even though I really like a lot about this, I'm going to say no." And I often think that founders think that there's some secret truth that's being held from them on why someone says no or they want more feedback.
alts.zh: 「就算我真的很喜歡這個東西的很多地方，我還是要說不。」我也常覺得，創辦人以為別人說不的背後藏著什麼沒告訴他的秘密，或想再要更多回饋。

alts.quote: We are about to launch something and then for example I or someone else goes to look at it and sees, "Oh, this doesn't feel right and we should fix it so I don't think we should launch this now."
alts.zh: 我們正要上線，然後我或別人去看了一眼，就會說：「這感覺不對，應該修一下，我覺得現在還不能上。」

alts.quote: Yeah, total waste of time. Yeah, I mean, unless there's a reason for it. So if you're a media company and traffic means that that number keeps going up, then yes, it matters.
alts.zh: 對，純粹浪費時間。嗯，除非真的有理由啦。如果你是媒體公司、流量就是那個一路往上的數字，那當然有意義。

cards.pattern: We're not going to drop this into [場景] where anybody and everybody can [做 X].
cards.quote: So we're not going to drop this into your Discord community where anybody and everybody can talk to it.
cards.zh: 所以我們不會把這個東西直接丟進你的 Discord 社群，讓任何人都能來跟它對話。
cards.why: 拒絕一個使用情境時，把最壞情況畫出來（anybody and everybody），對方自己就會同意；drop this into 這個動詞也帶著「隨便丟」的貶義，先把那個做法講得不負責任。
cards.pmNote: 早期產品要先講清楚「不支援的場景」，否則第一批災難用例會定義你的口碑。
cards.episode: From skeptic to true believer: How OpenClaw changed my life | Claire Vo

alts.quote: And when we got acquired, we had a conversation with our team where we said, we're going to of course embrace Spotify's culture and Spotify's core values, but we're not going to forget who we are as a team.
alts.zh: 被併購之後我們跟團隊談，說我們當然會擁抱 Spotify 的文化和核心價值，但我們不會忘記自己這個團隊是誰。

alts.quote: But if a PM came to me with something that was drawn and kind of fully baked, my response was like, thanks for giving me that. Now I know exactly what we're not going to do.
alts.zh: 如果 PM 拿一張畫得很完整的圖來找我，我的回應是：謝謝你給我這個，現在我很清楚我們「不會」做成這樣。

alts.quote: If you really need us to put us on the shelf and drop everything for a million dollar deal, we're a startup, we'll do it. But understand, just, is this really really what you want?
alts.zh: 如果你真的要我們把手上的東西全放下、為了這筆一百萬的案子全部重來，我們是新創，我們會做。但你想清楚——這真的是你要的嗎？

cards.pattern: We're not going to [做 A] or [做 B] or [做 C].
cards.quote: We're not going to create new changes to the product or create one time buys or reactivation emails.
cards.zh: 我們不會去動產品做新的改動，也不會做一次性購買或喚回信。
cards.why: 一次把三件事並列拒掉，比逐項拒絕省事，也讓大家看得出這是同一條界線而不是三個心情。並列的 or 讓清單聽起來還能繼續延伸——同類的都不做。
cards.pmNote: 一個實驗週期先宣告「這期不動的東西」，數據才讀得懂，否則歸因永遠有雜訊。
cards.episode: How to scrappily hire for, measure, and unlock growth | Crystal Widjaja, Gojek and Kumu

alts.quote: For what it's worth, we're not really motivated to try to create a self-improvement empire. This is not our full-time job. We just hope it works for you and is useful.
alts.zh: 順帶一提，我們並不是想搞一個自我成長帝國。這不是我們的正職。我們只是希望這對你有用。

alts.quote: We're not going to write out long-form content around everything related to dating because that's not the Tinder product.
alts.zh: 我們不會針對所有跟約會有關的東西寫長文，因為那不是 Tinder 這個產品。

alts.quote: We're not going to interrupt you with a popup that says like, "Do you want to save your changes," or any of that kind of stuff.
alts.zh: 我們不會用那種「你要儲存變更嗎？」的彈窗打斷你，那類東西都不會有。

cards.pattern: If we're not going to be good at [X], we'll just use [別人的方案].
cards.quote: But if we're not going to be good at a task and we think the open source is better or Anthropic's better, we'll go and just use the open source or Anthropic.
cards.zh: 但如果我們在某件事上就是做不好，而我們認為開源或 Anthropic 更好，那我們就直接去用開源或 Anthropic。
cards.why: 用「我們不會比較強」當拒絕理由，把自建 vs 外購的爭論從面子拉回能力比較；if…we'll just… 的結構讓決定聽起來是自動的，不是誰輸了。
cards.pmNote: 自建的門檻應該是「我們會不會比市面上最好的更好」，不是「我們做不做得出來」。
cards.episode: Building a magical AI code editor used by over 1 million developers in four months: The untold story of Windsurf | Varun Mohan (co-founder and CEO)

alts.quote: It's like, I don't think I can predict that. I think a much better use of my time is being very flexible and adaptable at a time like this.
alts.zh: 我不覺得我預測得了那個。我覺得我的時間花在保持彈性、快速調整上，回報高得多。

alts.quote: We're not going to settle for all the annoying bad technology that we use today.
alts.zh: 我們不會將就現在用的那些又爛又煩人的技術。

alts.quote: But if a PM came to me with something that was drawn and kind of fully baked, my response was like, thanks for giving me that. Now I know exactly what we're not going to do.
alts.zh: 如果 PM 拿一張畫得很完整的圖來找我，我的回應是：謝謝你給我這個，現在我很清楚我們「不會」做成這樣。

cards.pattern: We're not going to launch [某個大家都在做的東西].
cards.quote: We're not going to launch an AI sales agent.
cards.zh: 我們不會推出 AI 業務助理。
cards.why: 短句、不給理由、不加 hedge——當市場都在做同一件事時，最有力的表態就是直接點名那件事說不做。理由留到別人問，先讓立場站穩。
cards.pmNote: 面對熱潮，最省力的策略溝通是公開列出「我們不追的那幾樣」。
cards.episode: Inside OpenAI | Logan Kilpatrick (head of developer relations)

alts.quote: If it's not lovable, we're not going to ship it.
alts.zh: 如果它還不到讓人喜歡的程度，我們就不會出。

alts.quote: We're not going to show you that, but here are the middle grade books or whatever." There is a little bit of that.
alts.zh: 「我們不會給你看那個，但這裡有中年級的書之類的。」多少有一點那種味道。

alts.quote: We're going to have salespeople helping you through it, but we're not going to let you hire someone.
alts.zh: 我們會派業務協助你走完這段，但我們不會讓你去請一個人。

cards.pattern: Will anyone care in [時間] what we did here? And the answer is no.
cards.quote: So I'm like, "Will anyone care in six months what we did here?" And the answer is no.
cards.zh: 所以我就想：「六個月後還有人會在乎我們這裡做了什麼嗎？」答案是不會。
cards.why: 先問一個時間尺度的問題，再自己回答 no——拒絕就有了公開可檢驗的依據，而不是誰的偏好。用問句開場也讓對方有機會自己得出同樣結論。
cards.pmNote: 爭議事項先問「六個月後這件事還重要嗎」，多數辦公室政治型議題會自己消失。
cards.episode: The engineering mindset | Will Larson (Carta, Stripe, Uber, Calm, Digg)

alts.quote: If you need this feature, if you need this integration, I want you back in six months when you use this big product that isn't that great. But today, we're not the right solution for you.
alts.zh: 如果你需要這個功能、需要這個串接，那你先去用那個大廠的爛產品，六個月後再回來找我。今天我們不是適合你的解法。

alts.quote: So if you can't answer the question about what is it that someone's going to do a search on, then don't do SEO, because SEO is about appealing to that user.
alts.zh: 所以如果你答不出「別人會搜什麼」這個問題，那就不要做 SEO——因為 SEO 就是在對那個使用者說話。

alts.quote: If the answer is no, just cancel it.
alts.zh: 如果答案是「不」，那就直接取消。

cards.pattern: We're not going to settle for [現狀].
cards.quote: We're not going to settle for all the annoying bad technology that we use today.
cards.zh: 我們不會將就現在用的那些又爛又煩人的技術。
cards.why: settle for 是「將就」，這個動詞把拒絕現狀變成有骨氣的事而不是抱怨；配上具體對象（annoying bad technology）才不會淪為口號。
cards.pmNote: 對現狀的不滿要指名道姓才會變成需求，否則只會被當成士氣問題。
cards.episode: Building Lovable: $10M ARR in 60 days with 15 people | Anton Osika (co-founder and CEO)

alts.quote: If you need this feature, if you need this integration, I want you back in six months when you use this big product that isn't that great. But today, we're not the right solution for you.
alts.zh: 如果你需要這個功能、需要這個串接，那你先去用那個大廠的爛產品，六個月後再回來找我。今天我們不是適合你的解法。

alts.quote: And if with all of that it didn't work, then you can say, "Hey, we're not going to try this again because we literally did try everything that we could to test this hypothesis.
alts.zh: 如果做到那樣還是沒用，你就可以說：「我們不會再試一次了，因為我們真的已經把能測的都測過了。」

alts.quote: But if we're not going to be good at a task and we think the open source is better or Anthropic's better, we'll go and just use the open source or Anthropic.
alts.zh: 但如果我們在某件事上就是做不好，而我們認為開源或 Anthropic 更好，那我們就直接去用開源或 Anthropic。

cards.pattern: If the answer is no, [採取的行動] immediately.
cards.quote: If the answer is no, fire them immediately.
cards.zh: 如果答案是「不」，就馬上請他走。
cards.why: 條件句 + immediately 把「猶豫」這個選項直接刪掉；商業英語裡真正的狠不是用重話，是用時間副詞。
cards.pmNote: 這種一刀切的規則最適合拿來檢查自己在拖什麼——會拖，通常是因為答案其實已經是 no。
cards.episode: Lessons from a two-time unicorn builder, 50-time startup advisor, and 20-time company board member | Uri Levine (co-founder of Waze)

alts.quote: So if you can't answer the question about what is it that someone's going to do a search on, then don't do SEO, because SEO is about appealing to that user.
alts.zh: 所以如果你答不出「別人會搜什麼」這個問題，那就不要做 SEO——因為 SEO 就是在對那個使用者說話。

alts.quote: If the answer is no, just cancel it.
alts.zh: 如果答案是「不」，那就直接取消。

alts.quote: So I'm like, "Will anyone care in six months what we did here?" And the answer is no.
alts.zh: 所以我就想：「六個月後還有人會在乎我們這裡做了什麼嗎？」答案是不會。

cards.pattern: If I'm not excited about [X], we're not going to work together.
cards.quote: Because if I'm not excited about what you you're doing, we're not going to work together.
cards.zh: 因為如果我對你在做的事沒有興奮感，我們就不會合作。
cards.why: 把合作條件講成一條個人門檻，拒絕就不必針對案子本身評高低——你不是說它不好，你是說它不合你。
cards.pmNote: 接案或挑專案先設一條主觀門檻，可以省下大量「值不值得做」的內耗。
cards.episode: How to discover your superpowers, own your story, and unlock personal growth | Donna Lichaw (author of The Leader’s Journey)

alts.quote: And if with all of that it didn't work, then you can say, "Hey, we're not going to try this again because we literally did try everything that we could to test this hypothesis.
alts.zh: 如果做到那樣還是沒用，你就可以說：「我們不會再試一次了，因為我們真的已經把能測的都測過了。」

alts.quote: We're not going to write out long-form content around everything related to dating because that's not the Tinder product.
alts.zh: 我們不會針對所有跟約會有關的東西寫長文，因為那不是 Tinder 這個產品。

alts.quote: If it's not lovable, we're not going to ship it.
alts.zh: 如果它還不到讓人喜歡的程度，我們就不會出。

cards.pattern: We're not going to judge you on the basis of [某個指標].
cards.quote: We're not going to judge you on the basis of your OKRs.
cards.zh: 我們不會用你的 OKR 來評斷你。
cards.why: 主管版的「不做什麼」——先拿掉一個大家最怕的東西，人才敢設有野心的目標。on the basis of 比 by 正式，讓這句聽起來像制度承諾而不是一時好心。
cards.pmNote: OKR 一旦跟考績綁定，團隊就會開始設低標；要拿它當拉力，就得先公開拆掉這條連結。
cards.episode: Twitter’s former Head of Product opens up: being fired, meeting Elon, changing stagnant culture, building consumer product, more | Kayvon Beykpour

alts.quote: But if a PM came to me with something that was drawn and kind of fully baked, my response was like, thanks for giving me that. Now I know exactly what we're not going to do.
alts.zh: 如果 PM 拿一張畫得很完整的圖來找我，我的回應是：謝謝你給我這個，現在我很清楚我們「不會」做成這樣。

alts.quote: And if with all of that it didn't work, then you can say, "Hey, we're not going to try this again because we literally did try everything that we could to test this hypothesis.
alts.zh: 如果做到那樣還是沒用，你就可以說：「我們不會再試一次了，因為我們真的已經把能測的都測過了。」

alts.quote: We're so ambitious that we're not going to hold onto a B+.
alts.zh: 我們野心大到不會抱著一個「B+」不放。

cards.pattern: We're going to embrace [對方的東西], but we're not going to forget who we are.
cards.quote: And when we got acquired, we had a conversation with our team where we said, we're going to of course embrace Spotify's culture and Spotify's core values, but we're not going to forget who we are as a team.
cards.zh: 被併購之後我們跟團隊談，說我們當然會擁抱 Spotify 的文化和核心價值，但我們不會忘記自己這個團隊是誰。
cards.why: 先給足對方（of course embrace），再守住自己（but we're not going to forget）——順序反過來就會被聽成不合作。這是併購、改組、換老闆時最實用的一句。
cards.pmNote: 組織整併時要主動宣告「我們保留什麼」，不然團隊會自行猜測，士氣先掉。
cards.episode: Building Anchor, selling to Spotify, and lessons learned | Maya Prohovnik (Spotify’s Head of Podcast Product)

alts.quote: if you want to change during the course of the quarter, if you want to disrupt our whole engineering product team, you can do it, but understand there's a high cost, and the later you do it in the quarter, the less successful it's going to be
alts.zh: 你想在季中改、想打亂整個工程團隊，可以啊，但你要知道代價很高——而且愈晚改，效果只會愈差。

alts.quote: So we're not going to drop this into your Discord community where anybody and everybody can talk to it.
alts.zh: 所以我們不會把這個東西直接丟進你的 Discord 社群，讓任何人都能來跟它對話。

alts.quote: We're not going to have an hour-long conversation about a support ticket.
alts.zh: 我們不會為了一張客服單開一小時的會。

cards.pattern: We're not going to [得到 X] unless we [先做到 Y].
cards.quote: We're not going to get people necessarily building integrations just for us out of the gate unless we have a really compelling product around that.
cards.zh: 除非我們先把周邊產品做到真的夠有說服力，不然一開始不會有人專門為我們做整合。
cards.why: 拒絕一個過度樂觀的期待時，用 unless 把條件補上，就從潑冷水變成開條件；necessarily 這個副詞再留一點餘地，避免把話說死。
cards.pmNote: 生態系不會因為 API 開了就長出來；先算清楚對方為什麼要花工程時間接你。
cards.episode: Anthropic’s CPO on what comes next | Mike Krieger (co-founder of Instagram)

alts.quote: We're not going to write out long-form content around everything related to dating because that's not the Tinder product.
alts.zh: 我們不會針對所有跟約會有關的東西寫長文，因為那不是 Tinder 這個產品。

alts.quote: The point is growth can amplify great product market fit and growth can help you grow faster once you are already growing. But if you are slowing down, growth is going to be absolutely helpless to do anything.
alts.zh: 重點是：成長團隊可以放大本來就好的 PMF，可以讓已經在成長的東西長更快。但如果你正在衰退，成長團隊完全無能為力。

alts.quote: Or we're not going to do something unnatural or something that doesn't align with the business goals in order to gain any short term brownie points with investors.
alts.zh: 我們也不會為了在投資人面前拿一點短期的印象分，就去做不自然、或跟商業目標不一致的事。

cards.quote: Say no to stuff you’ve said yes to In the previous post, I shared a tactic for knowing when to say no: ask yourself, would I say yes if it were tomorrow?
cards.zh: 對那些你已經答應的事說不。上一篇我分享過一個判斷該不該拒絕的方法：問自己，如果這件事是明天，我還會答應嗎？
cards.why: 把「要不要拒絕」換算成一個時間測驗，情緒就退場了——遠期的 yes 之所以好答應，只是因為未來看起來很空。這句最狠的是它連已經答應的事都適用。
cards.pmNote: 每季重審一次已承諾事項，用「如果是明天」重問一次，通常能清掉兩成行事曆。
cards.episode: Part 2: Time management techniques that actually work

alts.quote: I always say to people don't come to me for management 101, I'm not the person to ask on how to run the most effective one-on-one with your people.
alts.zh: 我常跟人講：管理入門的東西不要來問我，怎麼把一對一開得最有效率，我不是那個該問的人。

alts.quote: You can say, "Yes, I agree. That is a real problem. Yes, I think we could test this design with users."
alts.zh: 你可以說：「對，我同意，那確實是個真的問題。對，我覺得這個設計我們可以拿去跟使用者測。」

alts.quote: Realistically when you're a product manager, your job is to say no to 90% of things that get brought your way. And so you're saying no to 90%, so you can say yes to 10%.
alts.zh: 說穿了，當產品經理的工作就是把送到你面前的九成東西拒絕掉——你拒絕九成，才有辦法對那一成說好。

cards.pattern: I say no to almost anything that isn't furthering [我的優先事項].
cards.quote: So I say no to almost anything that isn’t furthering these priorities.
cards.zh: 所以只要不是在推進這幾個優先事項的，我幾乎都會拒絕。
cards.why: almost anything 給自己留了例外空間，但 isn't furthering these priorities 把判準寫死——先講規則再講例外，比每次個案協商省力太多。
cards.pmNote: 把「我的優先事項」寫成三條公開的句子，別人自己就會過濾掉一半的請求。
cards.episode: Time management techniques that actually work

alts.quote: I am really hesitant to recommend any template. And what I'd say is these are principles for building it, not any prescribed formula.
alts.zh: 我真的很不願意推薦任何範本。我會說，這些是建構的原則，不是一套規定好的公式。

alts.quote: You can say, "Yes, I agree. That is a real problem. Yes, I think we could test this design with users."
alts.zh: 你可以說：「對，我同意，那確實是個真的問題。對，我覺得這個設計我們可以拿去跟使用者測。」

alts.quote: Realistically when you're a product manager, your job is to say no to 90% of things that get brought your way. And so you're saying no to 90%, so you can say yes to 10%.
alts.zh: 說穿了，當產品經理的工作就是把送到你面前的九成東西拒絕掉——你拒絕九成，才有辦法對那一成說好。

cards.pattern: You will see [對方說的趨勢] continue, but I still think there will be room for [我守的東西].
cards.quote: I think that you will see the functional lines continue to blur, but I still think there will be room for functions.
cards.zh: 我認為職能之間的界線會繼續模糊，但我還是覺得職能本身會有它的空間。
cards.why: 先把對方的趨勢完整承認（而且用 will，比對方還確定），再用 but I still think 守住自己那塊——讓步越大方，後面的堅持越有份量。
cards.pmNote: 面對「AI 會取代 X」這類大趨勢問句，最穩的回法是承認方向、限縮範圍。
cards.episode: Adam Mosseri: AI is a tailwind for authenticity

alts.quote: So I still think that concept is important and it seems to correlate with products going viral and taking off.
alts.zh: 所以我還是覺得那個概念很重要，而且它似乎跟產品爆紅、起飛是有相關的。

alts.quote: I still think ChatGPT kind of sucks at writing and that's because it's bottlenecked by this creative reasoning.
alts.zh: 我還是覺得 ChatGPT 在寫作這件事上蠻爛的，而那是因為它卡在創造性推理這一關。

alts.quote: But before that, I think getting to product-market fit, obviously there's a lot of methodology for doing it today that might make it a bit easier for people, but I still think it's fairly random and pretty dang hard.
alts.zh: 在那之前——我覺得要走到 PMF，現在當然有很多方法論可能讓大家輕鬆一點，但我還是認為它相當隨機，而且真的很難。

cards.pattern: "I don't really agree and I still think it's wrong, but I'm committed to it." That's not actually [名詞].
cards.quote: I don't really agree and I still think it's wrong, but I'm committed to it." That's not actually commitment.
cards.zh: 「我其實不同意，我還是覺得這是錯的，但我會照做。」那並不是真正的承諾。
cards.why: 引用一句大家都講過的場面話，再一刀切開它——That's not actually X 是拆穿場面話最短的公式。用在會議上比直接說「你根本沒買單」不傷人，因為批評的是那句話不是那個人。
cards.pmNote: disagree and commit 只有在「不同意」真的被聽完之後才成立，否則就只是加註免責聲明。
cards.episode: Unpacking Amazon’s unique ways of working | Bill Carr (author of Working Backwards)

alts.quote: And optics is a good thing. So I'm not saying don't think about optics whatsoever, I think it's actually important to think about optics.
alts.zh: 而且「對外呈現」本身是好事。我不是說完全不要管呈現，我覺得那其實很重要。

alts.quote: I still think ChatGPT kind of sucks at writing and that's because it's bottlenecked by this creative reasoning.
alts.zh: 我還是覺得 ChatGPT 在寫作這件事上蠻爛的，而那是因為它卡在創造性推理這一關。

alts.quote: And to be clear, I don't think it's actually that dangerous right now.
alts.zh: 先講清楚，我不覺得現在真的有那麼危險。

cards.pattern: I still think [舊的標準] is much more important than whether you're [新的標籤] or not.
cards.quote: I still think that things that we interviewed for in the past, a critical mindset, the ability to really understand deeply the technical nature of a problem is still much more important than whether you're a fully AI native programmer or not.
cards.zh: 我還是認為我們過去在面試裡看的那些東西——批判性的思維、能真正深入理解問題技術本質的能力——遠比你是不是一個完全 AI 原生的工程師重要得多。
cards.why: 反駁流行說法時不要否定它，改成排序（much more important than）；再把對方的說法降級成一個標籤（whether you're X or not），對比就出來了。
cards.pmNote: 招募標準被新技術帶著跑之前，先問這項能力三年後還算不算稀缺。
cards.episode: How Block is becoming the most AI-native enterprise in the world | Dhanji R. Prasanna

alts.quote: And I think one of the monikers we use internally is no, then go. As in just think through all the things that could go wrong, understand where scale will break, understand the things that might happen, and then move on anyway.
alts.zh: 我們內部有個口號叫「先說不，然後走」。把所有可能出錯的地方都想過一輪，知道規模在哪裡會斷，然後照樣往前。
