alts.quote: So I still think that concept is important and it seems to correlate with products going viral and taking off.
alts.zh: 所以我還是覺得那個概念很重要，而且它似乎跟產品爆紅、起飛是有相關的。

alts.quote: If you don't say yes, what you're essentially saying is, I am so presumptuous that I understand what's on the other side of that door already.
alts.zh: 你如果不答應，你其實等於在說：我狂妄到已經知道那扇門後面是什麼了。

cards.pattern: [A] is a different answer than [B], but I still think it's extremely valuable to [A].
cards.quote: I do still think studying computer science is a different answer than learning to code, but I would say I still think it's extremely valuable to study computer science.
cards.zh: 我確實仍然認為「唸資訊科學」跟「學寫程式」是兩個不同的答案，但我還是會說，唸資訊科學非常有價值。
cards.why: 對方把兩件事混為一談時，先拆開（a different answer than）再表態，就不會被對方的框架綁住。I do still think 裡的 do 是加強語氣，講出口時重音落在 do 上。
cards.pmNote: 被問「還需要 X 嗎」時先確認對方問的是哪一個 X；多數這類爭論其實是定義之爭。
cards.episode: He saved OpenAI, invented the “Like” button, and built Google Maps: Bret Taylor on the future of careers, coding, agents, and more

alts.quote: I don't really agree and I still think it's wrong, but I'm committed to it." That's not actually commitment.
alts.zh: 「我其實不同意，我還是覺得這是錯的，但我會照做。」那並不是真正的承諾。

alts.quote: I still think ChatGPT kind of sucks at writing and that's because it's bottlenecked by this creative reasoning.
alts.zh: 我還是覺得 ChatGPT 在寫作這件事上蠻爛的，而那是因為它卡在創造性推理這一關。

alts.quote: But before that, I think getting to product-market fit, obviously there's a lot of methodology for doing it today that might make it a bit easier for people, but I still think it's fairly random and pretty dang hard.
alts.zh: 在那之前——我覺得要走到 PMF，現在當然有很多方法論可能讓大家輕鬆一點，但我還是認為它相當隨機，而且真的很難。

cards.pattern: I still think [X] is important and it seems to correlate with [結果].
cards.quote: So I still think that concept is important and it seems to correlate with products going viral and taking off.
cards.zh: 所以我還是覺得那個概念很重要，而且它似乎跟產品爆紅、起飛是有相關的。
cards.why: 堅持之後補一句 it seems to correlate with…，用比較弱的因果詞（seems、correlate）把證據端出來——立場硬、證據軟，反而最難被推翻。
cards.pmNote: 沒有實驗證據時用 correlate 而不是 cause，可以守住立場又不會在數據會議上被打臉。
cards.episode: Gustav Söderström

alts.quote: I still think that things that we interviewed for in the past, a critical mindset, the ability to really understand deeply the technical nature of a problem is still much more important than whether you're a fully AI native programmer or not.
alts.zh: 我還是認為我們過去在面試裡看的那些東西——批判性的思維、能真正深入理解問題技術本質的能力——遠比你是不是一個完全 AI 原生的工程師重要得多。

alts.quote: Yeah, I think that's an important question, and it's a question I hear a lot because we all know a bullshitter.
alts.zh: 我覺得那是一個重要的問題，而且我常常被問到——因為我們每個人都認識一個唬爛的人。

alts.quote: And optics is a good thing. So I'm not saying don't think about optics whatsoever, I think it's actually important to think about optics.
alts.zh: 而且「對外呈現」本身是好事。我不是說完全不要管呈現，我覺得那其實很重要。

cards.pattern: I still think [X] kind of sucks at [Y], and that's because it's bottlenecked by [原因].
cards.quote: I still think ChatGPT kind of sucks at writing and that's because it's bottlenecked by this creative reasoning.
cards.zh: 我還是覺得 ChatGPT 在寫作這件事上蠻爛的，而那是因為它卡在創造性推理這一關。
cards.why: kind of 讓重話（sucks）不至於變成人身攻擊，後面 that's because 立刻給出機制——負評只要接上原因，就從情緒變成分析。
cards.pmNote: 批評對手或自家產品時一定要指出瓶頸在哪，否則會被當成品味之爭。
cards.episode: OpenAI researcher on why soft skills are the future of work | Karina Nguyen (Research at OpenAI, ex-Anthropic)

alts.quote: Yeah, I think that's an important question, and it's a question I hear a lot because we all know a bullshitter.
alts.zh: 我覺得那是一個重要的問題，而且我常常被問到——因為我們每個人都認識一個唬爛的人。

alts.quote: I don't really agree and I still think it's wrong, but I'm committed to it." That's not actually commitment.
alts.zh: 「我其實不同意，我還是覺得這是錯的，但我會照做。」那並不是真正的承諾。

alts.quote: But before that, I think getting to product-market fit, obviously there's a lot of methodology for doing it today that might make it a bit easier for people, but I still think it's fairly random and pretty dang hard.
alts.zh: 在那之前——我覺得要走到 PMF，現在當然有很多方法論可能讓大家輕鬆一點，但我還是認為它相當隨機，而且真的很難。

cards.pattern: This is a hill I would die on: [反直覺的主張].
cards.quote: Yeah, this is a hill that I would die on, which is that good process or sufficient process is actually something that speeds up a company rather than slow it down.
cards.zh: 這是我願意死守的一個立場：好的流程、或者說夠用的流程，其實會讓公司變快，而不是變慢。
cards.why: a hill I would die on 明確標示「這條我不讓」，讓對方知道現在不是在腦力激盪；後半用 rather than 把對方預設的結論直接對調，這是反直覺主張最乾淨的講法。
cards.pmNote: 一個團隊一年能守的「死守立場」大概兩三個，用超過就沒人當真。
cards.episode: Growth tactics from OpenAI and Stripe’s first marketer | Krithika Shankarraman

alts.quote: Actually, all feedback I think is valid. People's feelings are valid, but it doesn't mean that you need to do something about all of those things.
alts.zh: 其實我覺得所有回饋都是有效的。別人的感受都是真的，但這不代表你每一項都得去處理。

alts.quote: That's a good idea, but we don't actually understand these three things before we start working on that. So maybe we should do understand work to make sure that that is actually the right idea.
alts.zh: 這個想法不錯，但在動手之前有三件事我們其實還沒搞懂。也許先做點「理解型的工作」，確認這真的是對的方向。

alts.quote: And optics is a good thing. So I'm not saying don't think about optics whatsoever, I think it's actually important to think about optics.
alts.zh: 而且「對外呈現」本身是好事。我不是說完全不要管呈現，我覺得那其實很重要。

cards.pattern: But I still think we did the right thing there.
cards.quote: But I still think that we did the right thing there.
cards.zh: 但我還是覺得我們那時候做的是對的。
cards.why: 檢討完結果不如預期之後，用這句把「決策品質」和「結果」分開——承認結果差不等於承認判斷錯。there 限縮到那一次，避免聽起來在替所有決定辯護。
cards.pmNote: 事後檢討要分兩欄寫：決策當下有的資訊、事後才知道的資訊；只有前者能拿來評判人。
cards.episode: An inside look at Deel’s unprecedented growth | Meltem Kuran Berkowitz (Head of Growth)

alts.quote: Certainly earlier stages you often have to make compromises, but I still think it's worth paying attention to, right?
alts.zh: 早期階段當然常常得妥協，但我還是覺得這件事值得留意，對吧？

alts.quote: Well, I still think data network effects are underrated.
alts.zh: 嗯，我還是覺得資料網路效應被低估了。

alts.quote: I still think it comes back to product taste.
alts.zh: 我還是覺得最後還是回到產品品味這件事。

cards.pattern: Certainly [對方的處境] you often have to make compromises, but I still think it's worth paying attention to.
cards.quote: Certainly earlier stages you often have to make compromises, but I still think it's worth paying attention to, right?
cards.zh: 早期階段當然常常得妥協，但我還是覺得這件事值得留意，對吧？
cards.why: Certainly 開場是最有效率的讓步詞——一個字就把對方的例外全收下；worth paying attention to 則把要求降到最低（只要留意、不用照做），對方幾乎沒理由拒絕。
cards.pmNote: 提醒早期團隊補技術債或流程時，把要求降成「先看著」，比要求現在修容易被接受。
cards.episode: How to be more innovative | Sam Schillace (Microsoft deputy CTO, creator of Google Docs)

alts.quote: But before that, I think getting to product-market fit, obviously there's a lot of methodology for doing it today that might make it a bit easier for people, but I still think it's fairly random and pretty dang hard.
alts.zh: 在那之前——我覺得要走到 PMF，現在當然有很多方法論可能讓大家輕鬆一點，但我還是認為它相當隨機，而且真的很難。

alts.quote: But I still think that we did the right thing there.
alts.zh: 但我還是覺得我們那時候做的是對的。

alts.quote: I still think ChatGPT kind of sucks at writing and that's because it's bottlenecked by this creative reasoning.
alts.zh: 我還是覺得 ChatGPT 在寫作這件事上蠻爛的，而那是因為它卡在創造性推理這一關。

cards.pattern: Obviously there's a lot of [方法/工具] today that might make it easier, but I still think it's [仍然很難].
cards.quote: But before that, I think getting to product-market fit, obviously there's a lot of methodology for doing it today that might make it a bit easier for people, but I still think it's fairly random and pretty dang hard.
cards.zh: 在那之前——我覺得要走到 PMF，現在當然有很多方法論可能讓大家輕鬆一點，但我還是認為它相當隨機，而且真的很難。
cards.why: obviously 加 might 先把對方的樂觀完整說出來（而且講得比對方還公道），再用 but I still think 拉回現實。fairly random 這種帶保留的字眼讓悲觀結論不像唱衰。
cards.pmNote: 向主管報 PMF 進度時，先承認方法論的價值再說明不確定性，比一開場就講風險容易被聽進去。
cards.episode: The original growth hacker reveals his secrets | Sean Ellis (author of “Hacking Growth”)

alts.quote: It's like these things that seem so common sense are actually hard with what they're doing… a lot of the advice is common sense. That doesn't mean it's easy to put in motion.
alts.zh: 這些看起來根本是常識的東西，真的做起來很難……很多建議都是常識，但常識不代表容易落地。

alts.quote: Certainly earlier stages you often have to make compromises, but I still think it's worth paying attention to, right?
alts.zh: 早期階段當然常常得妥協，但我還是覺得這件事值得留意，對吧？

alts.quote: There's this rush to judgment upfront where people say, "Oh, it's therefore obvious that X, Y, Z. It's obvious that the moats are going to be in this area of the technology, but not in this other area."
alts.zh: 一開始大家都會急著下判斷，說「所以顯然就是 X、Y、Z」、「顯然護城河一定在這一塊，不會在那一塊」。

cards.pattern: I still think [X] is underrated.
cards.quote: Well, I still think data network effects are underrated.
cards.zh: 嗯，我還是覺得資料網路效應被低估了。
cards.why: underrated / overrated 是英語職場最省力的立場詞——不必證明對錯，只主張市場定價錯了，反駁的人得先舉證共識是對的。
cards.pmNote: 用 underrated/overrated 表態可以快速標出你的差異化觀點，很適合當 1:1 或面試的開場立場。
cards.episode: How to sell your ideas and rise within your company | Casey Winters, Eventbrite

alts.quote: And I still think it is still cheaper than sending everybody to trainings and conferences all the time, and it has a lot of, yeah, ripple effects and network effects.
alts.zh: 而且我還是覺得，這比一天到晚把所有人送去上課、跑研討會便宜，而且它還有很多連鎖效應和網絡效應。

alts.quote: But I still think that we did the right thing there.
alts.zh: 但我還是覺得我們那時候做的是對的。

alts.quote: Certainly earlier stages you often have to make compromises, but I still think it's worth paying attention to, right?
alts.zh: 早期階段當然常常得妥協，但我還是覺得這件事值得留意，對吧？

cards.pattern: I still think it comes back to [根本因素].
cards.quote: I still think it comes back to product taste.
cards.zh: 我還是覺得最後還是回到產品品味這件事。
cards.why: it comes back to X 是把發散的討論收回自己論點的收線句——不否定前面任何一個論點，只宣稱它們最終都指向同一個根。
cards.pmNote: 討論發散時用「這最後還是回到 X」收線，比說「我們離題了」更不得罪人。
cards.episode: How Anthropic’s product team moves faster than anyone else | Cat Wu (Head of Product, Claude Code)

alts.quote: But before that, I think getting to product-market fit, obviously there's a lot of methodology for doing it today that might make it a bit easier for people, but I still think it's fairly random and pretty dang hard.
alts.zh: 在那之前——我覺得要走到 PMF，現在當然有很多方法論可能讓大家輕鬆一點，但我還是認為它相當隨機，而且真的很難。

alts.quote: But I still think that we did the right thing there.
alts.zh: 但我還是覺得我們那時候做的是對的。

alts.quote: Certainly earlier stages you often have to make compromises, but I still think it's worth paying attention to, right?
alts.zh: 早期階段當然常常得妥協，但我還是覺得這件事值得留意，對吧？

cards.pattern: I still think it is cheaper than [對方的替代方案], and it has a lot of ripple effects.
cards.quote: And I still think it is still cheaper than sending everybody to trainings and conferences all the time, and it has a lot of, yeah, ripple effects and network effects.
cards.zh: 而且我還是覺得，這比一天到晚把所有人送去上課、跑研討會便宜，而且它還有很多連鎖效應和網絡效應。
cards.why: 面對成本質疑不要辯護價格，改成比較——cheaper than [對方現在在做的事] 把基準線換掉；再補 ripple effects 把難量化的好處放最後，先講贏數字再講價值。
cards.pmNote: 爭預算時先找出「現況的隱形成本」當比較基準，比直接論證投報率容易過關。
cards.episode: How to be the best coach to product people | Petra Wille (Strong Product People)

alts.quote: Yeah, I think that's an important question, and it's a question I hear a lot because we all know a bullshitter.
alts.zh: 我覺得那是一個重要的問題，而且我常常被問到——因為我們每個人都認識一個唬爛的人。

alts.quote: Well, I still think data network effects are underrated.
alts.zh: 嗯，我還是覺得資料網路效應被低估了。

alts.quote: But before that, I think getting to product-market fit, obviously there's a lot of methodology for doing it today that might make it a bit easier for people, but I still think it's fairly random and pretty dang hard.
alts.zh: 在那之前——我覺得要走到 PMF，現在當然有很多方法論可能讓大家輕鬆一點，但我還是認為它相當隨機，而且真的很難。

cards.pattern: Normally I want you all to feel great about [X], but I feel strongly about this path, so can we just try it and see how it goes?
cards.quote: If you’re uncomfortable, you could say something like “Normally, I want you all to feel great about the direction, but I feel strongly about this path, so can we just try it and see how it goes?
cards.zh: 如果你會不好意思，可以這樣說：「平常我希望大家都認同這個方向，但這條路我立場很強，我們就先試試看，看結果如何，好嗎？」
cards.why: 三步：先承認自己平常的原則（Normally…），再宣告這次是例外（I feel strongly），最後把賭注縮小成一次嘗試（just try it and see）。強行拍板最怕看起來像獨裁，這句用「例外」和「先試試」把代價降到最低。
cards.pmNote: 強推方向要明講「這次是我拍的」，事後才有人負責；模糊共識的失敗沒有人認帳。
cards.episode: Autonomy vs. direction - Issue 35

alts.quote: I definitely would not want anyone to feel joy. What I would say that's a close cousin to that is that enjoyment is such an important tool for productivity.
alts.zh: 我絕對不會要求任何人去感受喜悅。跟那個很接近、但我會這樣說的是：享受是生產力非常重要的工具。

alts.quote: Sometimes I feel the need to defend that the process is not for process' sake, it's ultimately to help us all move faster and work better.
alts.zh: 有時候我得替流程辯護一下：流程不是為了流程而存在，它最終是要讓大家跑得更快、做得更好。

alts.quote: Actually, all feedback I think is valid. People's feelings are valid, but it doesn't mean that you need to do something about all of those things.
alts.zh: 其實我覺得所有回饋都是有效的。別人的感受都是真的，但這不代表你每一項都得去處理。

cards.pattern: I'm going to kind of reject that premise, because I don't think [對方的前提] is true.
cards.quote: And so I'm going to kind of reject that premise, because I don't think design takes more time.
cards.zh: 所以我要說，我不太接受那個前提，因為我不認為設計會花比較多時間。
cards.why: reject that premise 把火力對準「問題本身」而不是對方——回答之前先宣告問題不成立；前面加 kind of 是英語裡的緩衝墊，讓這句硬話不至於變成挑釁。
cards.pmNote: 被問「為什麼你們比較慢」這種帶預設的問題，先拆前提再回答，否則你怎麼答都在承認它。
cards.episode: 35 years of product design wisdom from Apple, Disney, Pinterest, and beyond | Bob Baxley

alts.quote: I think sometimes people use data a lot or too much because they're worrying or they're afraid that, will I make the wrong choice? And I'm using data to make the choice for me.
alts.zh: 我覺得有時候大家用數據用得太兇，是因為他們在怕：萬一我選錯了怎麼辦？於是就讓數據替他們做決定。

alts.quote: Our loops are less tactical. In fact, if I'm being brutally honest, I think loops are kind of hard to achieve in B2B SaaS.
alts.zh: 我們的成長迴圈比較不那麼戰術。老實說，我覺得在 B2B SaaS 裡要做出真正的迴圈其實蠻難的。

alts.quote: I don't think there's any one thing that has happened. I think that a lot of times people ascribe a lot of momentum to a one time change or a single person.
alts.zh: 我不覺得有哪一件事是關鍵。很多時候大家會把一整段動能歸給某一次改動、或某一個人。

cards.pattern: How do we know that [大家預設的結論] would be true for us?
cards.quote: Well, how do we know that VR would be profitable for us?
cards.zh: 那我們怎麼知道 VR 對我們來說會賺錢？
cards.why: how do we know 用 we 把質疑變成集體求證，而不是「你憑什麼」；後面加 for us 又把泛用的市場說法拉回自家處境，這兩個字常常就足以讓提案卡住。
cards.pmNote: 任何引用外部趨勢的提案，都要能回答「為什麼這對我們也成立」。
cards.episode: The ultimate guide to OKRs | Christina Wodtke (Stanford)

alts.quote: How do we know there's an ROI to a better design here?
alts.zh: 我們怎麼知道在這裡做更好的設計是有投報率的？

alts.quote: Go and talk to that executive and say, "Look, I know you've told me to do this, but what would we observe if this was working versus not working? I'm here to help you with that."
alts.zh: 你可以去找那位主管說：「我知道你已經指定要做這個了，但如果它有效跟沒效，我們會分別看到什麼？這部分我可以幫你。」

alts.quote: So, I don't really care how high quality the initial MVP is because quality is defined by the customer. And if we don't know who our customer is, we literally don't know what the word quality means.
alts.zh: 所以第一版的 MVP 品質多高，我其實沒那麼在意，因為品質是由客戶定義的。如果我們連客戶是誰都不知道，我們根本不知道「品質」這兩個字是什麼意思。

cards.pattern: What would have to be true for [某個結果] to happen?
cards.quote: Then, the second question is, what would have to be true for the customer to want to pay us for that, to pay a premium ideally?
cards.zh: 接下來第二個問題是：要讓客戶願意為那個東西付錢、最好還是付溢價，什麼條件必須成立？
cards.why: what would have to be true 不評價提案好壞，只要求對方把隱含條件攤出來——它讓反對變成協作，是質疑上位者最安全的一句。
cards.pmNote: 用這句把爭論轉成一張「必須成立的條件清單」，接著就能排優先序、先去驗最脆弱的那條。
cards.episode: The surprising truth about what closes deals: Insights from 2.5m sales conversations | Matt Dixon (author of The Challenger Sale and The JOLT Effect)

alts.quote: You keep using the word advice, and I just want to, so for anybody who's listening, do not take my advice.
alts.zh: 你一直在用「建議」這個詞，我想借這個機會講一句：不要照我的建議做。

alts.quote: We're going to get to work on that, but can you tell me how are you measuring success? We want to make sure that what we do, you consider it successful.
alts.zh: 這件事我們會開始動工，不過可以先跟我說你是怎麼衡量成功的嗎？我們想確保做出來的東西，在你眼中算是成功。

alts.quote: I was talking to security leaders in our customer advisory board recently and I heard this piece of feedback and this is what it made me think about our strategy, what do you think about that?
alts.zh: 我最近跟客戶顧問委員會的資安主管聊，聽到一個回饋，這讓我重新想我們的策略——你怎麼看？

cards.pattern: What would have to be true for [具體數字目標] in [時間]?
cards.quote: What would have to be true for your business to reach $100M in revenue in one year?
cards.zh: 要讓你的生意在一年內做到一億美金營收，什麼條件必須成立？
cards.why: 同一個句型加上具體數字和期限，就從哲學問題變成算術題——對方得回頭算單價、數量、轉換率，很多「很大的市場」在這一步自己破功。
cards.pmNote: 檢驗一個機會的規模，用反推法（要達到 X 需要多少客戶）比引用市場報告可靠。
cards.episode: Your startup idea probably isn’t venture-scale

alts.quote: Why are we always looking to Navy SEALs to tell us how to run our business?
alts.zh: 我們為什麼老是要去看海豹部隊怎麼做，來決定自己公司該怎麼經營？

alts.quote: If a software project could get built in two to three weeks, what does that really mean about the true complexity of what you built? Unless you believe you are way smarter than everyone else, but I think that's hubris.
alts.zh: 如果一個軟體專案兩三週就能做出來，那它到底有多複雜、多難被取代？除非你相信自己比全世界聰明太多——但我覺得那叫自大。

alts.quote: Then, the second question is, what would have to be true for the customer to want to pay us for that, to pay a premium ideally?
alts.zh: 接下來第二個問題是：要讓客戶願意為那個東西付錢、最好還是付溢價，什麼條件必須成立？

cards.pattern: Have you tested the assumption that [對方的預設]?
cards.quote: Have you tested the assumption that enterprise users need all these features?” Don’t be afraid to ask challenging questions to assess how well aligned you are with leadership.
cards.zh: 「你們有驗證過『企業用戶需要這些功能』這個假設嗎？」別怕問挑戰性的問題，這能看出你跟領導層的想法有多接近。
cards.why: Have you tested…? 把質疑包裝成流程問題（做過沒？）而不是判斷問題（對不對？），對方就算沒做過也只會回「還沒」，不會覺得被否定。
cards.pmNote: 面試或空降初期用這句提問，既能看出組織的驗證習慣，又不會被當成挑釁。
cards.episode: The ultimate guide to negotiating your comp

alts.quote: All the advice used to be of the form, "Steve Jobs once did this thing, so if you do it too, you'll be like Steve Jobs." And it's like, well, he also wore the black turtleneck.
alts.zh: 以前的建議都是這個格式：「賈伯斯做過這件事，所以你也做，你就會變成賈伯斯。」我就想說，那他還穿黑色高領毛衣呢。

alts.quote: Well, inherent in your question is this assumption that design takes more time. And so I'm going to kind of reject that premise, because I don't think design takes more time.
alts.zh: 你這個問題裡本身就藏了一個假設：做設計會比較花時間。我要先否掉這個前提，因為我不覺得設計比較花時間。

alts.quote: It's funny that everyone complained about Google as this really, really smart, all-knowing LLM, and at the same time, they think they're dumb enough to fall for these guest posts.
alts.zh: 很好笑的是，大家一邊抱怨 Google 是那種超級聰明、什麼都知道的 LLM，一邊又覺得它笨到會被這些客座文章騙過去。

cards.pattern: What's the quickest test you can run to validate [假設]?
cards.quote: If there is disagreement — what’s the quickest test you can run to validate the assumption?
cards.zh: 如果有分歧——你能跑的最快的一個驗證是什麼？
cards.why: 爭執僵住時，把「誰對」換成「怎麼最快知道」；quickest 這個字尤其重要，它擋掉了「那我們做個完整研究」這種以驗證之名的拖延。
cards.pmNote: 會議上出現對立意見就直接切到這句，把爭論轉成一個當週做得完的實驗。
cards.episode: This Week #4: Motivating engineers to hit deadlines, PM career ladders, and aligning with execs

alts.quote: Why are we always looking to Navy SEALs to tell us how to run our business?
alts.zh: 我們為什麼老是要去看海豹部隊怎麼做，來決定自己公司該怎麼經營？

alts.quote: I feel like they operate under the assumption that people will always want the smartest model.
alts.zh: 我感覺他們是在「大家永遠都會想要最聰明的模型」這個假設下運作的。

alts.quote: But better how? You got to be able to articulate better.
alts.zh: 但「比較好」是好在哪？你得有辦法把「比較好」講清楚。

cards.pattern: That process is predicated on the assumption that [隱含前提].
cards.quote: And once again, that process is sort of predicated on the assumption that implementation is expensive and that you can really only afford to build once.
cards.zh: 再一次，那套流程其實是建立在一個假設上：實作很貴，而你其實只做得起一次。
cards.why: predicated on the assumption that… 是把對方沒說出口的前提翻上檯面的標準說法——你沒說他錯，只說他站在什麼東西上面；前提一旦被說出來，它就可以被檢查。
cards.pmNote: 質疑既有流程前先講出它成立的時代條件；很多流程不是錯，只是條件變了。
cards.episode: OpenAI Codex lead on the new shape of product work | Andrew Ambrosino

alts.quote: 90% of customers or people who we meet who claim to have a land and expand strategy are only landing. They're not expanding because they gave their farm away in the land.
alts.zh: 我們遇到宣稱自己有 land and expand 策略的人，九成其實只有 land。他們沒辦法 expand，因為一開始就把家當全給出去了。

alts.quote: All the advice used to be of the form, "Steve Jobs once did this thing, so if you do it too, you'll be like Steve Jobs." And it's like, well, he also wore the black turtleneck.
alts.zh: 以前的建議都是這個格式：「賈伯斯做過這件事，所以你也做，你就會變成賈伯斯。」我就想說，那他還穿黑色高領毛衣呢。

alts.quote: Well, inherent in your question is this assumption that design takes more time. And so I'm going to kind of reject that premise, because I don't think design takes more time.
alts.zh: 你這個問題裡本身就藏了一個假設：做設計會比較花時間。我要先否掉這個前提，因為我不覺得設計比較花時間。

cards.pattern: They operate under the assumption that [對手的預設].
cards.quote: I feel like they operate under the assumption that people will always want the smartest model.
cards.zh: 我感覺他們是在「大家永遠都會想要最聰明的模型」這個假設下運作的。
cards.why: operate under the assumption that 描述的是行為不是想法，指控就變得比較客觀；前面掛 I feel like 再降一級，適合在還沒有證據時先把問題放上桌。
cards.pmNote: 分析競爭對手時先寫出「他們的營運假設」，比列功能表更能預測他們下一步。
cards.episode: Max Schoenig

alts.quote: You're never going to always like your manager. The goal isn't to like your manager. Ideally, you respect them and they respect you, you feel like there's things that you can learn from them.
alts.zh: 你不可能永遠喜歡你的主管。重點本來就不是喜不喜歡，而是互相尊重、而且你從他身上學得到東西。

alts.quote: It would be safe to skip the priming step if we began the meeting under the assumption that everybody here is on the same page, has the same information, and generally speaking, intends for the same outcome.
alts.zh: 如果我們可以假設在座每個人都在同一頁上、拿到一樣的資訊、大致上也想要一樣的結果，那跳過暖身這一步是安全的。

alts.quote: I think people assume that there's a much more detailed semantic understanding of everybody's interests and preferences in the algorithm than there is.
alts.zh: 我覺得大家會以為演算法對每個人的興趣和偏好，有一套比實際上細膩得多的語意理解。

cards.pattern: What are the assumptions that led to folks believing that [某個決定] is the right idea?
cards.quote: I think that you need to understand in the event that it's a top-down strategy, what are the assumptions that led to folks believing that that is the right idea?
cards.zh: 我認為，如果那是一個由上而下的策略，你得去弄懂：是哪些假設讓大家相信那是對的方向？
cards.why: 挑戰高層決策時，把問題導向「當初的假設」而不是「這個決定」，你就從質疑者變成想理解的人；that led to folks believing 也預設了他們有理由，語氣立刻軟下來。
cards.pmNote: 接到上面丟下來的策略先做假設考古，找到最脆弱的那條假設，再拿數據去談。
cards.episode: Vision, conviction, and hype: How to build 0 to 1 inside a company | Mihika Kapoor (Product at Figma)

alts.quote: It's funny that everyone complained about Google as this really, really smart, all-knowing LLM, and at the same time, they think they're dumb enough to fall for these guest posts.
alts.zh: 很好笑的是，大家一邊抱怨 Google 是那種超級聰明、什麼都知道的 LLM，一邊又覺得它笨到會被這些客座文章騙過去。

alts.quote: I think there's this cult of lean, scrappy, fast, throw away your product quickly, keep moving. And I think at some level it's true, but a lot of times I see teams give up too early.
alts.zh: 現在有一種「精實、克難、快、東西不行就丟、繼續往前」的教派。某種程度上它是對的，但我常看到團隊太早就放棄了。

alts.quote: Your belief is that if we add buy now pay later, a lot more people will be able to buy and transact, and so it's going to pay off. Do I have that right?
alts.zh: 你的認定是：只要我們加了先買後付，會有更多人買得下去、成交量會上來，所以這筆投資划得來。我這樣理解對嗎？

cards.quote: That is such a good takeaway of just showing the leaders, here's the data, here's the assumptions that we're all betting on, and do you believe this can happen?
cards.zh: 那個心得真的很好：就是直接攤給高層看——這是數據，這是我們一起在賭的假設，你相信這件事會發生嗎？
cards.why: betting on 把「假設」講成賭注，責任就從你一個人身上分攤出去；最後那句 do you believe this can happen? 逼對方表態，避免計畫在沒有人真的相信的情況下被批准。
cards.pmNote: 送審計畫時附一張「我們在賭的假設」清單，比多做二十頁分析更能換到真正的承諾。
cards.episode: Billion dollar failures, and billion dollar success | Tom Conrad (Quibi, Pandora, Pets.com, Snap, Zero)

alts.quote: We're all sitting talking about it, and Tate says, "It's a low margin reseller, one time sells." "You can say dotcom all you like, it's a low margin reseller."
alts.zh: 大家在車上討論，Tate 說：「它就是個低毛利的經銷商，一次性買賣。你要講幾次『.com』都可以，它還是個低毛利經銷商。」

alts.quote: They would write principles such as move fast and I would always be, "Everyone likes to move fast." It is not a good principle actually because nobody can really disagree with this reasonably.
alts.zh: 他們會寫「快速行動」這種原則，我都會回：誰不喜歡快速行動？那其實不是好的原則，因為沒有人會合理地反對它。

alts.quote: We're going to get to work on that, but can you tell me how are you measuring success? We want to make sure that what we do, you consider it successful.
alts.zh: 這件事我們會開始動工，不過可以先跟我說你是怎麼衡量成功的嗎？我們想確保做出來的東西，在你眼中算是成功。

cards.pattern: This is the place to kick the tires of the assumptions behind [某個估算].
cards.quote: However, this is the place for a growth engineer to kick the tires of the assumptions behind the original T-shirt-size estimate.
cards.zh: 不過，這正是成長工程師該去踢一踢輪胎、檢查原本那個 T 恤尺碼估算背後假設的地方。
cards.why: kick the tires 是「動手驗一驗」的慣用語，帶點隨意感，用來質疑同事的估算不傷人；the assumptions behind X 則明確指出要查的是估算的依據，不是數字本身。
cards.pmNote: 工時估算要複查的是它假設的範圍與依賴，不是把數字往上加一倍。
cards.episode: Introducing DRICE: a modern prioritization framework

alts.quote: I think that you need to understand in the event that it's a top-down strategy, what are the assumptions that led to folks believing that that is the right idea?
alts.zh: 我認為，如果那是一個由上而下的策略，你得去弄懂：是哪些假設讓大家相信那是對的方向？

alts.quote: Well, I mean this is the irony of growth, is people think growth is overnight success and it's not. It is a lot of short wins and short-term execution for a longer-term gain.
alts.zh: 成長最諷刺的地方就在這：大家以為成長是一夜爆紅，其實不是。它是一堆短期的小勝仗，堆出長期的結果。

alts.quote: That is such a good takeaway of just showing the leaders, here's the data, here's the assumptions that we're all betting on, and do you believe this can happen?
alts.zh: 那個心得真的很好：就是直接攤給高層看——這是數據，這是我們一起在賭的假設，你相信這件事會發生嗎？

cards.quote: Ask if they understand your options, why you made your specific decision, and what would change your mind.
cards.zh: 問問他們懂不懂你有哪些選項、為什麼你做了那個決定，以及什麼會讓你改變想法。
cards.why: what would change your mind 逼對方講出自己的反證條件——講得出來代表他真的在推理，講不出來就是信仰。這也是自己該常問自己的一句。
cards.pmNote: 每份重大決策文件都該有一行「什麼證據會讓我們回頭」，之後爭論才有出口。
cards.episode: The definitive guide to mastering analytical thinking interviews

alts.quote: Everyone raised prices. The question I ask folks is, "Did you earn it?"
alts.zh: 大家都漲價了。但我會問一句：你憑什麼漲？（你賺到這個漲價了嗎？）

alts.quote: I was talking to security leaders in our customer advisory board recently and I heard this piece of feedback and this is what it made me think about our strategy, what do you think about that?
alts.zh: 我最近跟客戶顧問委員會的資安主管聊，聽到一個回饋，這讓我重新想我們的策略——你怎麼看？

alts.quote: The common knowledge was that you had to have at least a two-week wait for change approvals in order to get that stability. Turns out that's not right. It was just kind of an old wives' tale, right.
alts.zh: 過去大家都認為，變更審核至少要等兩週才能確保穩定。結果那是錯的。那就是個以訛傳訛的老說法。

cards.pattern: How do we know there's an ROI to [某個投入] here?
cards.quote: How do we know there's an ROI to a better design here?
cards.zh: 我們怎麼知道在這裡做更好的設計是有投報率的？
cards.why: 把 how do we know 直接接上 ROI，質疑就落在可計算的東西上；結尾的 here 把範圍限縮到這個案子，避免變成在否定整個設計投資。
cards.pmNote: 設計或技術投入要能講出對應的商業指標，否則永遠在預算會議上被排到最後。
cards.episode: Improve strategy, influence, and decision-making by understanding your brain | Evan LaPointe (founder of CORE Sciences)

alts.quote: But better how? You got to be able to articulate better.
alts.zh: 但「比較好」是好在哪？你得有辦法把「比較好」講清楚。

alts.quote: You're never going to always like your manager. The goal isn't to like your manager. Ideally, you respect them and they respect you, you feel like there's things that you can learn from them.
alts.zh: 你不可能永遠喜歡你的主管。重點本來就不是喜不喜歡，而是互相尊重、而且你從他身上學得到東西。

alts.quote: Well, how do we know that VR would be profitable for us?
alts.zh: 那我們怎麼知道 VR 對我們來說會賺錢？

cards.pattern: It would be safe to skip [某個步驟] if we began under the assumption that everybody is on the same page.
cards.quote: It would be safe to skip the priming step if we began the meeting under the assumption that everybody here is on the same page, has the same information, and generally speaking, intends for the same outcome.
cards.zh: 如果我們可以假設在座每個人都在同一頁上、拿到一樣的資訊、大致上也想要一樣的結果，那跳過暖身這一步是安全的。
cards.why: 用「如果那個假設成立，就可以省略」的句法反向指出假設不成立——不必說「大家其實沒共識」，聽的人自己會發現。三個並列條件（same page / same information / same outcome）把「有共識」拆成可檢查的項目。
cards.pmNote: 會議前先確認三件事：資訊一致、目標一致、決策權清楚；缺一項就會開成沒有結論的會。
cards.episode: Improve strategy, influence, and decision-making by understanding your brain | Evan LaPointe (founder of CORE Sciences)

alts.quote: I feel like they operate under the assumption that people will always want the smartest model.
alts.zh: 我感覺他們是在「大家永遠都會想要最聰明的模型」這個假設下運作的。

alts.quote: Well, inherent in your question is this assumption that design takes more time. And so I'm going to kind of reject that premise, because I don't think design takes more time.
alts.zh: 你這個問題裡本身就藏了一個假設：做設計會比較花時間。我要先否掉這個前提，因為我不覺得設計比較花時間。

alts.quote: It's funny that everyone complained about Google as this really, really smart, all-knowing LLM, and at the same time, they think they're dumb enough to fall for these guest posts.
alts.zh: 很好笑的是，大家一邊抱怨 Google 是那種超級聰明、什麼都知道的 LLM，一邊又覺得它笨到會被這些客座文章騙過去。

cards.quote: If you truly, truly want to solve a problem, get out of your building, get out of the assumptions, get out of your opinions.
cards.zh: 如果你真的、真的想解決一個問題，就走出你的辦公大樓，走出你的假設，走出你的意見。
cards.why: 三個同構的 get out of 把範圍從物理（building）推到認知（assumptions、opinions），節奏本身就是說服力——英語簡報裡三連排比是最容易複製的修辭。
cards.pmNote: 內部爭論超過兩輪還沒共識，通常代表缺的是使用者資料，不是更多會議。
cards.episode: The essence of product management | Christian Idiodi (SVPG)

alts.quote: You keep using the word advice, and I just want to, so for anybody who's listening, do not take my advice.
alts.zh: 你一直在用「建議」這個詞，我想借這個機會講一句：不要照我的建議做。

alts.quote: We're going to get to work on that, but can you tell me how are you measuring success? We want to make sure that what we do, you consider it successful.
alts.zh: 這件事我們會開始動工，不過可以先跟我說你是怎麼衡量成功的嗎？我們想確保做出來的東西，在你眼中算是成功。

alts.quote: It's one thing to say you're spending a lot of time looking outside the building. It's a whole other thing to hear from the places you don't normally hear from.
alts.zh: 說自己花很多時間在公司外面看，是一回事；真的去聽那些你平常聽不到的聲音，完全是另一回事。

cards.pattern: Maybe I disagree with [X], but they definitely have [值得肯定的地方].
cards.quote: Maybe I disagree with it, but they definitely have a coherent idea.
cards.zh: 我可能不同意這個看法，但他們的想法確實是自洽的。
cards.why: Maybe 把否決降級成個人立場，definitely 反而給對方一個不可否認的肯定。先讓對方的東西站得住，你的異議才不像在否定人。
cards.pmNote: 評估別家產品或別組方案時，先承認它內部邏輯一致，再談不同意，討論才不會變成攻防。
cards.episode: Thinking like a gardener not a builder, organizing teams like slime mold, the adjacent possible, and other unconventional product advice | Alex Komoroske (Stripe, Google)

alts.quote: So I think it's an unnecessary addition, but maybe I'm just being protective of my original idea.
alts.zh: 我覺得那是多此一舉的補充，不過也可能只是我在護著自己原本的想法啦。

alts.quote: So I'm going to disagree with Sedaris a little bit.
alts.zh: 這點我要跟 Sedaris 有一點不一樣的看法。

alts.quote: I'd maybe put it a little bit differently.
alts.zh: 我可能會換一個講法。

cards.pattern: I'm not convinced [某個假設會成立].
cards.quote: I'm not convinced I'm going to get Peter to use the app.
cards.zh: 我不太相信我真的能讓 Peter 用這個 app。
cards.why: I'm not convinced 把重擔放在「證據還沒說服我」，而不是「你錯了」；對方可以補證據翻盤，關係不會斷。
cards.pmNote: 質疑成長假設時，講「我還沒被說服」比「這行不通」更容易換到對方拿數據回來。
cards.episode: OpenAI Codex lead on the new shape of product work | Andrew Ambrosino

alts.quote: So I'm going to disagree with Sedaris a little bit.
alts.zh: 這點我要跟 Sedaris 有一點不一樣的看法。

alts.quote: You're focused on recent and I'm just going to push back. No, there's nothing terribly recent.
alts.zh: 你一直扣在「最近」這個點上，我要反過來擋一下——沒有，最近沒什麼特別的。

alts.quote: I'm not sure AR is going to be the right reference.
alts.zh: 我不確定 AR 會是對的參照對象。

cards.pattern: I'm not saying that [對方的做法] is not good, but sometimes there's a decision to be made.
cards.quote: I'm not saying that sales-led is not good, but sometimes there's a decision to be made.
cards.zh: 我不是說銷售驅動不好，但有時候就是得做出取捨。
cards.why: 先撤掉「你那套很爛」的解讀，再把問題升級成「這是個選擇題」。把價值判斷換成取捨判斷，對方就沒有立場可以捍衛。
cards.pmNote: 策略衝突多半不是好壞之爭，把它講成「要選一個」才逼得出決策。
cards.episode: Customer-led growth | Georgiana Laudi (Forget The Funnel)

alts.quote: Sometimes it can be as simple as like, is your mind made up on this or are you open to input? If the answer is like, "No, I'm pretty set that this is the answer," shut up.
alts.zh: 有時候簡單問一句就好：「這件事你已經決定了，還是還能聽意見？」如果對方說「我滿確定就是這個答案」，那就閉嘴。

alts.quote: I'm not saying that having a large market someday doesn't matter, of course it does eventually. But trying to be super pedantic about market size when it's a pre-seed company, it's just not something I'd put a lot of thought.
alts.zh: 我不是說市場總有一天要夠大這件事不重要，當然重要。但在一家 pre-seed 公司還在糾結市場規模算得多精確，我不會花太多心思在上面。

alts.quote: Hopefully, I don't come off as encouraging everyone to be like me. I'm not saying that at all. What I'm saying is, this is a way to be.
alts.zh: 希望我聽起來不是在鼓吹大家都要跟我一樣。我完全不是那個意思。我要說的是：這是一種活法。

cards.pattern: I did disagree with [X], but it's no excuse for me to [我的失禮行為].
cards.quote: Honestly, I did disagree with what you're saying, but it's no excuse for me to talk to you the way I did.
cards.zh: 老實說，我當時確實不同意你講的，但那不能當作我用那種態度跟你說話的藉口。
cards.why: 把「立場」跟「表達方式」切開來道歉：立場保住、行為認錯。台灣人常整包收回立場來換和平，結果下次還是會吵同一件事。
cards.pmNote: 吵完架的修補要分兩層講，否則你等於把技術判斷也一起撤回了。
cards.episode: A child psychologist’s guide to working with difficult adults | Dr. Becky Kennedy

alts.quote: I actually say I disagree with Naval on this because often, when you're part of a large organization, it's really hard to do great work and get recognized for it.
alts.zh: 我其實在這件事上跟 Naval 意見不同，因為在大組織裡，你常常很難既做出好成果又被看見。

alts.quote: Instead, it's my instinct to go the wrong way on challenge directly and to pretend that I agree when I disagree, and then I wind up in the worst place of all, manipulative insincerity.
alts.zh: 我的本能反而是在「直接挑戰」這件事上走錯邊——明明不同意卻裝作同意，最後掉進最糟的那一格：虛偽的操弄。

alts.quote: I think if you're building a product where it's not necessarily an AI- first product and you have some AI features that are on the side, but it's not the core of your value, I don't know that I would operate this way.
alts.zh: 如果你做的不是 AI 優先的產品，只是旁邊掛幾個 AI 功能、AI 不是核心價值，那我不確定我會這樣做。

cards.quote: Sorry, I don't buy it.
cards.zh: 抱歉，我不買單。
cards.why: Sorry 在這裡不是道歉，是「我要開火了」的節奏標記；I don't buy it 針對的是論證不是人。四個字把立場說完，不留模糊空間。
cards.pmNote: 短句反對比長篇鋪陳更能讓會議往下走——對方只需要回一件事：拿證據來。
cards.episode: How to build a company that withstands any era | Eric Ries, Lean Startup author

alts.quote: Yeah, sorry. Buy-in doesn't feel quite right to me, because buy-in feels like, oh, I've come to agree with you. And that's different from it's a part of me.
alts.zh: 抱歉，我覺得「buy-in（買單）」這個詞不太對。buy-in 聽起來像「我最後被你說服了」，那跟「這東西本來就是我的一部分」是兩回事。

alts.quote: I don't buy that, because I've met most people and most people are like, "Hell no," when they hear about my life.
alts.zh: 我不買單，因為我見過的大多數人，聽到我的生活方式時的反應都是「才不要」。

alts.quote: And don't get me wrong, I love those cultures, but they're all different cultures. They're very different cultures.
alts.zh: 別誤會，那些文化我都很欣賞，但它們彼此其實非常不一樣，真的差很多。

cards.pattern: Don't get me wrong, I'm not trying to talk people out of [做 X].
cards.quote: Again, don't get me wrong, I'm not trying to talk people out of doing it.
cards.zh: 再說一次，別誤會，我不是要勸大家別做這件事。
cards.why: 講完一串缺點後回頭補一句「我不是在勸退」，是替聽者的情緒收尾；Again 表示這已是第二次強調——重話講多了要重複貼標籤。
cards.pmNote: 給風險清單時要明講「這不是否決」，否則團隊會把資訊當成指令。
cards.episode: Leaving big tech to build the #1 technology newsletter | Gergely Orosz (The Pragmatic Engineer)

alts.quote: I'm curious what you think. I still don't think ideas are worth as much as maybe a lot of people think. I still think execution is really hard.
alts.zh: 我反而想聽你怎麼看。我還是不覺得點子有大家講的那麼值錢，我還是覺得執行才難。

alts.quote: And don't get me wrong, I think there's a lot of product folks out there who enjoy that modality of work, I'm not one of them.
alts.zh: 別誤會，我知道有很多產品人是真的喜歡那種工作方式的——我不是。

alts.quote: I'm not saying that having a large market someday doesn't matter, of course it does eventually. But trying to be super pedantic about market size when it's a pre-seed company, it's just not something I'd put a lot of thought.
alts.zh: 我不是說市場總有一天要夠大這件事不重要，當然重要。但在一家 pre-seed 公司還在糾結市場規模算得多精確，我不會花太多心思在上面。

cards.pattern: I disagree with myself constantly on [小事].
cards.quote: I disagree with myself constantly on small things.
cards.zh: 小事情上我常常自己跟自己意見不合。
cards.why: 把「改變立場」正常化成日常行為，等於預先解除「你上次不是這樣講」的攻擊。用 constantly 而不是 sometimes，才有立場彈性的感覺。
cards.pmNote: 領導者公開示範「改主意是常態」，團隊才敢在資料翻盤時改決策。
cards.episode: Jason Fried challenges your thinking on fundraising, goals, growth, and more

alts.quote: Yeah, it's definitely a huge part of it. There's a couple of things that I noticed get in the way.
alts.zh: 對，那絕對是很大一塊。不過我有注意到幾件事會卡住。

alts.quote: I'm not trying to diss anyone, but you'll see things that become fashionable really quickly because someone found success in this unfashionable space and then it becomes fashionable.
alts.zh: 我不是要酸誰，但你會看到有些東西紅得很快——因為有人在一個沒人做的領域做成了，然後它就變成流行。

alts.quote: I think my only build on that would be to say I think those core PM skills aren't necessarily the things that we have rewarded PMs for over the last five years, versus storytelling, alignment, strategy.
alts.zh: 我唯一想補的是：那些核心 PM 能力，其實不是我們過去五年在獎勵的東西——我們獎勵的是說故事、跨部門對齊、講策略。

cards.quote: Don't get me wrong, all that's very important.
cards.zh: 別誤會，那些都很重要。
cards.why: 六個字的緩衝包，用途是預告「我接下來要講的話聽起來會像在否定它」。英文的緩衝一定放在重話前面，放後面就來不及救。
cards.episode: Unorthodox PM wisdom: Automating user insights, unselling job candidates, logging every decision, more | Kevin Yien (Stripe, Square, Mutiny)

alts.quote: And don't get me wrong, I love those cultures, but they're all different cultures. They're very different cultures.
alts.zh: 別誤會，那些文化我都很欣賞，但它們彼此其實非常不一樣，真的差很多。

alts.quote: Again, don't get me wrong, I'm not trying to talk people out of doing it. But for me, a lot of this was luck.
alts.zh: 先說清楚，我不是想勸大家不要做。但對我來說，這裡面有很大一部分是運氣。

alts.quote: So, I think one needs to be a little bit cautious on what Dario says. And that's setting aside the cynical view that he's just doing that department stock, which I don't believe at all.
alts.zh: 我覺得對 Dario 講的話要保留一點。而且我這裡還先撇開那種比較酸的解讀——說他只是在替自家股價講話——那我完全不相信。

cards.pattern: It's my instinct to pretend that I agree when I disagree, and then I wind up in [最糟的位置].
cards.quote: Instead, it's my instinct to go the wrong way on challenge directly and to pretend that I agree when I disagree, and then I wind up in the worst place of all, manipulative insincerity.
cards.zh: 我的本能反而是在「直接挑戰」這件事上走錯邊——明明不同意卻裝作同意，最後掉進最糟的那一格：虛偽的操弄。
cards.why: 用第一人稱承認自己會裝同意，等於把台灣職場最常見的迴避行為命名成一個有代價的錯誤，聽起來不像在說教。
cards.pmNote: 「假裝同意」不是中立選項，它會被解讀成背書；不同意就要當場說。
cards.episode: Radical Candor: From theory to practice with author Kim Scott

alts.quote: I agree with you. I totally agree with you. Now, I think it's the human aspect though of boldness, seeing the future in a way that a thing trained on priors cannot.
alts.zh: 我同意你，完全同意。不過我覺得，人的那一塊——那種膽識、那種能看見未來的能力，是只學過去資料的東西做不到的。

alts.quote: Honestly, I did disagree with what you're saying, but it's no excuse for me to talk to you the way I did.
alts.zh: 老實說，我當時確實不同意你講的，但那不能當作我用那種態度跟你說話的藉口。

alts.quote: So far be it from me to disagree with Mike Tyson, but I think he's wrong.
alts.zh: 我哪敢跟泰森唱反調——但我覺得他錯了。

cards.pattern: Don't get me wrong, there's obviously a ton of value in [對方的做法].
cards.quote: Yeah, and don't get me wrong, there's obviously a ton of value in prototyping.
cards.zh: 嗯，別誤會，做原型當然有非常大的價值。
cards.why: obviously 是關鍵——它把讚美講成「這還用說」，快速帶過，不會讓聽者以為你要轉向支持；標籤貼完馬上可以接 but。
cards.pmNote: 反對前的肯定要短要快，講太久反而讓人以為結論是肯定。
cards.episode: The rise of the professional vibe coder (a new AI-era job) | Lazar Jovanovic (Professional Vibe Coder)

alts.quote: And don't get me wrong, I think there's a lot of product folks out there who enjoy that modality of work, I'm not one of them.
alts.zh: 別誤會，我知道有很多產品人是真的喜歡那種工作方式的——我不是。

alts.quote: And don't get me wrong, I love those cultures, but they're all different cultures. They're very different cultures.
alts.zh: 別誤會，那些文化我都很欣賞，但它們彼此其實非常不一樣，真的差很多。

alts.quote: Both things can be true. It's like, yeah, there's nothing perfect in product. However, it is true that some companies are healthier than others.
alts.zh: 這兩件事可以同時成立。對，產品這行沒有什麼是完美的；但同樣真實的是，有些公司確實比其他公司健康得多。

cards.pattern: I don't buy that, because I've [親身經驗], and [實際反應].
cards.quote: I don't buy that, because I've met most people and most people are like, "Hell no," when they hear about my life.
cards.zh: 我不買單，因為我見過的大多數人，聽到我的生活方式時的反應都是「才不要」。
cards.why: I don't buy that 之後立刻接 because + 第一手見聞，異議就從「感覺」升級成「證詞」；沒有 because 的 I don't buy that 只是在耍態度。
cards.pmNote: 反駁「大家都會想要 X」這種宣稱，最有效的武器是你實際訪談到的原話。
cards.episode: Redefining success, money, and belonging | Paul Millerd (The Pathless Path)

alts.quote: Yeah, sorry. Buy-in doesn't feel quite right to me, because buy-in feels like, oh, I've come to agree with you. And that's different from it's a part of me.
alts.zh: 抱歉，我覺得「buy-in（買單）」這個詞不太對。buy-in 聽起來像「我最後被你說服了」，那跟「這東西本來就是我的一部分」是兩回事。

alts.quote: So Lenny, I don't see it as a pivot because as we were joking in the beginning, I've been an employee, I was an operator there at early stage startups and now I'm a founder and I'm a VC.
alts.zh: Lenny，我不覺得那是轉彎——就像我們一開始開玩笑講的，我當過員工、在早期新創當過操盤手，現在是創辦人，也是投資人。

alts.quote: Something I caution people against though is don't use the data alone to figure out who the marginal user is.
alts.zh: 不過有件事我會提醒大家小心：不要只靠數據去判斷誰是邊際使用者。

cards.pattern: [某人的觀點] that I disagreed with a lot, but it was really interesting to think about it from a different perspective.
cards.quote: He just had an episode recently about a skeptical take on AI that I disagreed with a lot, but it was really interesting to think about it from a different perspective.
cards.zh: 他最近那集講了一個對 AI 很懷疑的觀點，我非常不同意，但從另一個角度想這件事真的很有意思。
cards.why: disagreed a lot 把不同意講到滿，後面再給價值；順序反過來就變成敷衍。推薦別人東西時保留自己的異議，反而讓推薦更可信。
cards.pmNote: 公開推薦跟自己立場相反的材料，是建立判斷力可信度最便宜的方法。
cards.episode: The secret to better AI prototypes: Why Tinder’s CPO starts with JSON, not design | Ravi Mehta (product advisor, previously EIR at Reforge)

alts.quote: I'm curious what you think. I still don't think ideas are worth as much as maybe a lot of people think. I still think execution is really hard.
alts.zh: 我反而想聽你怎麼看。我還是不覺得點子有大家講的那麼值錢，我還是覺得執行才難。

alts.quote: I don't know if this is a contrarian perspective, but I go to speak in a lot of universities.
alts.zh: 我不知道這算不算是個逆風的看法，但我常去很多大學演講。

alts.quote: I think some controversy is necessary and so I may be at a different point on that one.
alts.zh: 我覺得某種程度的爭議是必要的，所以這一題我的位置可能跟大家不太一樣。

cards.pattern: [對方重視的東西] is important, don't get me wrong, but as a [情境], we need to [我的主張].
cards.quote: The stability is important, don't get me wrong, but I do think that as a faster growing company, we need to consistently to reiterate not only the product but also our teams.
cards.zh: 穩定當然重要，別誤會，但我確實認為以一家成長更快的公司來說，我們要不斷迭代的不只是產品，還有團隊。
cards.why: don't get me wrong 插在句中而不是句首，讓肯定聽起來是順口補的、不是策略性的，重點還是留在 but 之後。
cards.pmNote: 「組織也要跟產品一樣迭代」是高速成長公司最常被忽略的重組理由。
cards.episode: Inside TikTok: Culture, strategy, monetization, and more | Ray Cao (Global Head of Monetization Product Strategy and Operations)

alts.quote: And don't get me wrong, I think there's a lot of product folks out there who enjoy that modality of work, I'm not one of them.
alts.zh: 別誤會，我知道有很多產品人是真的喜歡那種工作方式的——我不是。

alts.quote: I think if you're building a product where it's not necessarily an AI- first product and you have some AI features that are on the side, but it's not the core of your value, I don't know that I would operate this way.
alts.zh: 如果你做的不是 AI 優先的產品，只是旁邊掛幾個 AI 功能、AI 不是核心價值，那我不確定我會這樣做。

alts.quote: So far be it from me to disagree with Mike Tyson, but I think he's wrong.
alts.zh: 我哪敢跟泰森唱反調——但我覺得他錯了。

cards.pattern: I actually say I disagree with [權威] on this because [具體情境下的反例].
cards.quote: I actually say I disagree with Naval on this because often, when you're part of a large organization, it's really hard to do great work and get recognized for it.
cards.zh: 我其實在這件事上跟 Naval 意見不同，因為在大組織裡，你常常很難既做出好成果又被看見。
cards.why: 點名反對一個有名的人時，actually + on this 把範圍縮到單一議題，不是全面否定他；接著馬上給情境條件，讓異議變成「適用範圍之爭」。
cards.pmNote: 反對業界共識時，先限定情境（大組織 vs 小團隊），比正面對撞更容易被接受。
cards.episode: Hot takes and techno-optimism from tech’s top power couple | Sriram and Aarthi

alts.quote: Yeah, sorry. Buy-in doesn't feel quite right to me, because buy-in feels like, oh, I've come to agree with you. And that's different from it's a part of me.
alts.zh: 抱歉，我覺得「buy-in（買單）」這個詞不太對。buy-in 聽起來像「我最後被你說服了」，那跟「這東西本來就是我的一部分」是兩回事。

alts.quote: Honestly, I did disagree with what you're saying, but it's no excuse for me to talk to you the way I did.
alts.zh: 老實說，我當時確實不同意你講的，但那不能當作我用那種態度跟你說話的藉口。

alts.quote: Actually, it's not that it's harder to find, your stuff becomes less relevant. And that's the part about SEO that I'm excited about.
alts.zh: 其實不是變得比較難被找到，是你的東西變得沒那麼相關了。而這正是 SEO 讓我興奮的地方。

cards.pattern: My hot take is that for the vast majority of people, [反直覺結論].
cards.quote: But my hot take is that for the vast majority of people, they probably do not need a coach.
cards.zh: 但我的辣評是：對絕大多數人來說，他們大概並不需要教練。
cards.why: hot take 這個標籤先把話的位階降成「個人辣評」，換來的是可以直接否定一個熱門主張；再加 probably 留一條退路。標籤與重話同句，聽者來不及防禦。
cards.pmNote: 對「大家都在做的事」開火時，先自貼 hot take 標籤能大幅降低反彈成本。
cards.episode: How to make better decisions and build a joyful career | Ada Chen Rekhi (Notejoy, LinkedIn, SurveyMonkey)

alts.quote: Oh, I think this is my hot take. You hear people talking about craft and taste and product management, and it's all very wonderful. And I'm totally on board.
alts.zh: 喔，這大概是我的爭議發言了。大家都在談 craft、談品味、談產品管理，聽起來都很美好，我也完全買單——

alts.quote: And it's kind of building a house that you want every brick in the house to match. And if you go and try and take some bricks from someone else's house and stick it in your house, it's probably going to not look very matched.
alts.zh: 這有點像蓋房子，你會希望每一塊磚都是搭的。如果你跑去人家家裡搬幾塊磚塞進自己家，看起來大概就是不搭。

alts.quote: Maybe this is a hot take, but I feel like product market fit is independent of your marketplace dynamics.
alts.zh: 這可能是個辣評，但我覺得 PMF 跟你的平台供需動態其實是兩回事。

cards.pattern: I'm not saying [對方會誤以為我在說的極端主張], but [我真正的主張].
cards.quote: And I'm not saying agents cannot understand this or models are not capable enough to understand this, but there are really weird rules within enterprises that are not documented anywhere.
cards.zh: 我不是說 agent 理解不了這些，也不是說模型能力不夠，而是企業裡有一堆非常奇怪、根本沒寫在任何文件上的規則。
cards.why: 先把最容易被誤讀的兩個極端版本一次講掉，剩下的空間就只能照你的意思理解。這是「先貼標籤再開火」的完整版：否定誤讀 → but → 真正的主張。
cards.pmNote: 講技術限制時要指名「不是能力問題，是脈絡沒被寫下來」，才不會被聽成唱衰模型。
cards.episode: Aishwarya Naresh Reganti + Kiriti Badam

alts.quote: If you don't say yes, what you're essentially saying is, I am so presumptuous that I understand what's on the other side of that door already.
alts.zh: 你如果不答應，你其實等於在說：我狂妄到已經知道那扇門後面是什麼了。

alts.quote: I'm not saying that Arc is a commodity or we want it to be, but objectively web browsers are interchangeable.
alts.zh: 我不是說 Arc 是可替換的商品、也不是說我們希望它是，但客觀上瀏覽器就是可以互換的。

alts.quote: And optics is a good thing. So I'm not saying don't think about optics whatsoever, I think it's actually important to think about optics.
alts.zh: 而且「對外呈現」本身是好事。我不是說完全不要管呈現，我覺得那其實很重要。

cards.pattern: It's not [容易被誤會的對象] to be clear, but [真正的對象] ...
cards.quote: It's not LLMs to be clear, but there's engines like Stockfish these days that are just dramatically better than the top grand masters in the world.
cards.zh: 講清楚，那不是 LLM，但現在有像 Stockfish 那種引擎，已經遠遠強過世界頂尖大師。
cards.why: to be clear 插在誤會發生的那個詞後面，等於就地拆彈；不用另起一句解釋，節奏不會斷。
cards.episode: How to find hidden growth opportunities in your product | Albert Cheng (Duolingo, Grammarly, Chess.com)

alts.quote: Not to say it's not better, but just this is the structure of it, and it kind of sets you up for bragging.
alts.zh: 我不是說它不好，我只是在講它的結構——這個結構會把你逼到一直自誇。

alts.quote: Sometimes I feel the need to defend that the process is not for process' sake, it's ultimately to help us all move faster and work better.
alts.zh: 有時候我得替流程辯護一下：流程不是為了流程而存在，它最終是要讓大家跑得更快、做得更好。

alts.quote: And I always write them back and say like, "Please tell me the better term and popularize it and I'll use it. It's a great idea."
alts.zh: 我都回信說：「請你告訴我更好的講法，然後把它推廣開，我就會改用。這主意很好。」

cards.quote: To be clear, we're not building that, but it's a fun idea.
cards.zh: 先講清楚，我們沒有要做那個，但那是個有趣的點子。
cards.why: 談完一個假想產品後必須立刻切割，否則會被當成路線圖。先撤回承諾、再保住對方的面子，順序不能反。
cards.pmNote: 對外談論任何還沒承諾的東西，一定要當場加一句「我們沒有要做」。
cards.episode: The power user’s guide to Codex: parallelizing workflows, planning techniques, advanced context engineering tips, automating code reviews, and more | Alexander Embiricos

alts.quote: But, and this is the big but, no one has this at the early stages when they don't have a good idea and they don't have customers and it's objectively not working.
alts.zh: 但是——而且這是很大的一個「但是」——在最早期、還沒有好點子、沒有客戶、客觀上根本不 work 的時候，沒有人會有那種信念。

alts.quote: And I always write them back and say like, "Please tell me the better term and popularize it and I'll use it. It's a great idea."
alts.zh: 我都回信說：「請你告訴我更好的講法，然後把它推廣開，我就會改用。這主意很好。」

alts.quote: It's not LLMs to be clear, but there's engines like Stockfish these days that are just dramatically better than the top grand masters in the world.
alts.zh: 講清楚，那不是 LLM，但現在有像 Stockfish 那種引擎，已經遠遠強過世界頂尖大師。

cards.pattern: I'll caveat this by saying [限制條件], and there's pros and cons to both.
cards.quote: I'll caveat this by saying everyone's just figuring it out and it's a lot harder to figure it out when you're a larger organization than when you're much smaller and you get to run something yourself and there's pros and cons to both.
cards.zh: 我先加個但書：大家都還在摸索，而且組織越大越難摸索，比不上小團隊自己說了算——兩邊各有優缺點。
cards.why: I'll caveat this by saying 是明講「我要先降低這段話的適用範圍」，把後面的建議從普世法則降成情境經驗，聽者反而更願意採用。
cards.pmNote: 分享做法前先講清楚組織規模，能避免小公司照抄大公司流程。
cards.episode: How 80,000 companies build with AI: products as organisms, the death of org charts, and why agents will outnumber employees by 2026 | Asha Sharma (CVP of AI Platform at Microsoft)

alts.quote: Whenever you talk to people who are at the company, they're always try to tell you the best version of the company. It's on you to triangulate that information, but you need both sides.
alts.zh: 你去問還在公司裡的人，他們永遠給你公司最好的那個版本。要交叉比對是你自己的責任，但兩邊的說法你都得聽到。

alts.quote: It's very hard to think strategically about the situation you're in because there isn't a science of strategy. It's not like physics. It's not like engineering where we can write down the equations of stress on a beam.
alts.zh: 要對你所處的情況做策略思考很難，因為策略沒有一門科學。它不像物理。也不像工程——工程可以直接寫下樑的應力方程式。

alts.quote: Data is more like a compass than a GPS. If you look at data as a way of giving you the answer, you're always wrong. Wrong or slow, or sometimes both.
alts.zh: 數據比較像指南針，不是導航。如果你把數據當成會給你答案的東西，你不是錯就是慢，有時候兩者都有。

cards.pattern: Like, hot take: I think [X] ruins [Y].
cards.quote: I don't have Twitter, like hot take, I think Twitter ruins people's careers.
cards.zh: 我沒有 Twitter——講個辣評，我覺得 Twitter 會毀掉人的職涯。
cards.why: 火力全開的句子只用一個 like hot take 當前導，兩個字買下一整句攻擊。標籤越輕、後面能講的越重，這正是台灣人最缺的順序。
cards.episode: The ultimate guide to Martech | Austin Hay (Reforge, Ramp, Runway)

alts.quote: Oh, I think this is my hot take. You hear people talking about craft and taste and product management, and it's all very wonderful. And I'm totally on board.
alts.zh: 喔，這大概是我的爭議發言了。大家都在談 craft、談品味、談產品管理，聽起來都很美好，我也完全買單——

alts.quote: And don't get me wrong, I think there's a lot of product folks out there who enjoy that modality of work, I'm not one of them.
alts.zh: 別誤會，我知道有很多產品人是真的喜歡那種工作方式的——我不是。

alts.quote: I think this is an interesting thing that technical founders sometimes don't really like. They think sales is a very negative part of the process. I think it's not that black and white.
alts.zh: 技術背景的創辦人常常不太喜歡這件事，他們覺得業務是整個過程裡很負面的一塊。我覺得沒那麼非黑即白。

cards.pattern: Maybe this is a hot take, but I feel like [推翻常識的主張].
cards.quote: Maybe this is a hot take, but I feel like product market fit is independent of your marketplace dynamics.
cards.zh: 這可能是個辣評，但我覺得 PMF 跟你的平台供需動態其實是兩回事。
cards.why: Maybe this is a hot take 是替聽者預告「接下來要嚇到你」，他就會用聽新觀點的模式接收，而不是用找漏洞的模式。
cards.pmNote: 把 PMF 跟 marketplace 動態分開看，才不會用補貼掩蓋掉沒人要的產品。
cards.episode: How marketplaces win: Liquidity, growth levers, quality, and more | Benjamin Lauzier (Lyft, Thumbtack, Reforge)

alts.quote: Oh, I think this is my hot take. You hear people talking about craft and taste and product management, and it's all very wonderful. And I'm totally on board.
alts.zh: 喔，這大概是我的爭議發言了。大家都在談 craft、談品味、談產品管理，聽起來都很美好，我也完全買單——

alts.quote: But my hot take is that for the vast majority of people, they probably do not need a coach.
alts.zh: 但我的辣評是：對絕大多數人來說，他們大概並不需要教練。

alts.quote: This might be my hot take, but we do almost no estimating in order to hit deadlines.
alts.zh: 這可能算我的辣評：我們幾乎不做工時估算，照樣趕上死線。

cards.pattern: I want to be clear, the problem is not about [人], it's systemic.
cards.quote: And I think I want to be clear, in my mind the problem is obviously not about the practitioners, it's systemic.
cards.zh: 我想講清楚：在我看來問題不在第一線的人身上，是系統性的。
cards.why: 批評一個現象前先把人摘出來，重話就可以放心打在制度上；沒有這一句，同樣的內容會被現場的人聽成人身指控。
cards.pmNote: 做流程檢討前先宣告「不是在追究誰」，才拿得到真話。
cards.episode: How marketplaces win: Liquidity, growth levers, quality, and more | Benjamin Lauzier (Lyft, Thumbtack, Reforge)

alts.quote: I do want to be clear, it's one leader and their team who are accountable and responsible.
alts.zh: 我想把話講清楚：負責的就是一位負責人跟他的團隊。

alts.quote: This isn't funny, Hilary. This is a serious issue for a lot of people, and it's an emerging problem in some cases. And I think we should take it seriously.
alts.zh: 這不好笑。這對很多人來說是很嚴重的問題，而且在某些地方正在惡化。我覺得我們應該認真看待。

alts.quote: I think we do a disservice when we say we're not good at speaking up because it's a skill like any other.
alts.zh: 我覺得我們說自己「不擅長發言」是在害自己，因為那跟其他技能沒有兩樣。

cards.pattern: To be clear, I don't think it's actually that [嚴重] right now.
cards.quote: And to be clear, I don't think it's actually that dangerous right now.
cards.zh: 先講清楚，我不覺得現在真的有那麼危險。
cards.why: 講完一長串風險後必須校準時間軸，否則聽眾會把長期擔憂當成當下警報。actually 是用來對抗對方腦中已經升起的印象。
cards.pmNote: 談風險要把時間軸講出來，「現在」跟「三年後」的結論常常相反。
cards.episode: Benjamin Mann

alts.quote: And optics is a good thing. So I'm not saying don't think about optics whatsoever, I think it's actually important to think about optics.
alts.zh: 而且「對外呈現」本身是好事。我不是說完全不要管呈現，我覺得那其實很重要。

alts.quote: I don't really agree and I still think it's wrong, but I'm committed to it." That's not actually commitment.
alts.zh: 「我其實不同意，我還是覺得這是錯的，但我會照做。」那並不是真正的承諾。

alts.quote: That's a good idea, but we don't actually understand these three things before we start working on that. So maybe we should do understand work to make sure that that is actually the right idea.
alts.zh: 這個想法不錯，但在動手之前有三件事我們其實還沒搞懂。也許先做點「理解型的工作」，確認這真的是對的方向。

cards.pattern: I do want to be clear, it's [誰] who are accountable and responsible.
cards.quote: I do want to be clear, it's one leader and their team who are accountable and responsible.
cards.zh: 我想把話講清楚：負責的就是一位負責人跟他的團隊。
cards.why: I do want to be clear 的 do 是重音記號，用來把一句可能被和稀泥的分工宣告釘死。指名責任時語氣要平，資訊要硬。
cards.pmNote: 責任分散是專案失控的主因，宣告時要用單數（one leader）而不是「大家一起」。
cards.episode: Unpacking Amazon’s unique ways of working | Bill Carr (author of Working Backwards)

alts.quote: And I think I want to be clear, in my mind the problem is obviously not about the practitioners, it's systemic.
alts.zh: 我想講清楚：在我看來問題不在第一線的人身上，是系統性的。

alts.quote: Of course, I don't want to be cruel to the people who are putting their hearts into that work, because the Figma file is beautiful. It's just coming a little early.
alts.zh: 當然，我不想對那些真心投入的人太苛刻——那些 Figma 檔真的很漂亮。只是它來得太早了一點。

alts.quote: I noticed there's some PMs who will send an email and I read the email, I'm like, "What do you want me to do?
alts.zh: 我注意到有些 PM 寄信過來，我讀完心裡想的是：「所以你到底要我做什麼？」

cards.pattern: There are a few things that [A] do that annoy [B], and to be clear, I'm sure [B] annoy [A] just as much.
cards.quote: I would say there are a few things that PMs do that annoy engineers and to be clear, I am sure that engineers annoy PMs, just as much.
cards.zh: 我會說有幾件事是 PM 做了會惹惱工程師的——先講清楚，我相信工程師惹惱 PM 的程度也不遑多讓。
cards.why: 要批評一個職能，先把同樣的指控對稱地扣回自己這邊，聽眾就無法把它當派系攻擊。just as much 是關鍵，它保證雙方等重。
cards.pmNote: 跨職能檢討要先建立對稱性，否則會議會變成部門防衛戰。
cards.episode: The things engineers are desperate for PMs to understand | Camille Fournier (author of “The Manager’s Path,” ex-CTO at Rent the Runway)

alts.quote: Maybe this is a harsh thing to say, but I think very few companies have the talent caliber to be able to do that. So it might need to be adjusted if you were going to implement this.
alts.zh: 這樣講可能有點刺耳，但我覺得能做到這件事的公司真的很少。所以你要照搬的話，大概得先調整過。

alts.quote: So you have engineers now who are working on optimizing short form videos for higher engagement, and you sort of want to say to them like, "Hey, are you thinking about what this is doing to the brains of young children?"
alts.zh: 現在有一群工程師在優化短影音的互動率，你會有點想跟他們說：「欸，你有想過這對小朋友的腦袋在做什麼嗎？」

alts.quote: He said, "Well, two things. First, you were wrong. You were wrong to prioritize date over our reputation."
alts.zh: 他說：「兩件事。第一，你錯了。你不該把時程放在我們的商譽前面。」

cards.pattern: I think I probably [自己的爛紀錄], if I'm being completely honest.
cards.quote: And so, I think I probably shipped a lot of bad product those years, if I'm being completely honest.
cards.zh: 所以老實說，那幾年我大概出了不少爛產品。
cards.why: 這裡標籤放在句尾，是英文口語允許的另一種節奏——重話先出、誠實標籤收尾，效果是「我不是在博同情，只是陳述」。
cards.episode: Relentless curiosity, radical accountability, and HubSpot’s winning growth formula | Christopher Miller (VP of Product, Growth and AI)

alts.quote: But then, again, if I'm being honest to myself, I'm not making as good product decisions as I can.
alts.zh: 但話說回來，如果對自己誠實，我做的產品決策並沒有達到我能做到的水準。

alts.quote: If you think about your last all hands, the last talk you saw, you probably don't remember much. In fact, I wager you might only remember one thing from that talk.
alts.zh: 回想你上一次的全員大會、上一場你聽的演講——你大概記不得多少。老實說，我敢賭你只記得一件事。

alts.quote: I like Sean Ellis's question of how disappointed would you be if this product disappeared? And I think it's if you have at least 40% of people respond that they'd be very disappointed, then you're on the right track.
alts.zh: 我喜歡 Sean Ellis 那一題：如果這個產品消失了，你會有多失望？如果至少 40% 的人回答「非常失望」，那你方向就是對的。

cards.pattern: If I'm being brutally honest, I think [大家推崇的東西] is kind of hard to achieve in [情境].
cards.quote: In fact, if I'm being brutally honest, I think loops are kind of hard to achieve in B2B SaaS.
cards.zh: 其實老實不客氣地講，我覺得在 B2B SaaS 要做出成長迴圈是滿難的。
cards.why: brutally honest 是把火力調到最大的旋鈕，但後面搭 kind of 又降回來——英文常用「重標籤＋輕措辭」維持攻擊力又不失禮。
cards.pmNote: B2B SaaS 硬套消費級成長迴圈是常見誤植，多數成長還是靠銷售與帳號擴張。
cards.episode: Relentless curiosity, radical accountability, and HubSpot’s winning growth formula | Christopher Miller (VP of Product, Growth and AI)

alts.quote: So I think it's an unnecessary addition, but maybe I'm just being protective of my original idea.
alts.zh: 我覺得那是多此一舉的補充，不過也可能只是我在護著自己原本的想法啦。

alts.quote: I'm curious what you think. I still don't think ideas are worth as much as maybe a lot of people think. I still think execution is really hard.
alts.zh: 我反而想聽你怎麼看。我還是不覺得點子有大家講的那麼值錢，我還是覺得執行才難。

alts.quote: So this might mean that I think... I don't want to say that if you don't have experience, don't start one, but it's kind of true. So become an expert somewhere, somehow, before you start.
alts.zh: 我不想說「沒經驗就別開始」這種話……但其實有點是真的。所以動手前，先想辦法在某個地方變成專家。

cards.pattern: I'm not saying [X] doesn't matter, of course it does eventually.
cards.quote: So I'm not saying that having a large market someday doesn't matter, of course it does eventually.
cards.zh: 我不是說有一天有沒有大市場不重要，當然最後會很重要。
cards.why: of course it does 把讓步講得毫不勉強，聽者就不會停在這裡爭；讓步講得越乾脆，你越快能回到自己的主張。
cards.pmNote: 早期不必先證明 TAM，但要說清楚「不是不重要，是順序問題」。
cards.episode: Lessons from 1,000+ YC startups: Resilience, tar pit ideas, pivoting, more | Dalton Caldwell (Y Combinator, Managing Director)

alts.quote: I'm not saying it doesn't matter, but to me, again, it's more about that's a means to an end.
alts.zh: 我不是說那不重要，但對我來說，那比較是達成目的的手段。

alts.quote: And optics is a good thing. So I'm not saying don't think about optics whatsoever, I think it's actually important to think about optics.
alts.zh: 而且「對外呈現」本身是好事。我不是說完全不要管呈現，我覺得那其實很重要。

alts.quote: I'm not saying it's perfect, there's still a long road ahead of us, but we at least speak the same language.
alts.zh: 我不是說它已經完美，我們還有很長的路要走，但至少大家講的是同一種語言了。

cards.pattern: I'm not saying it's perfect, there's still a long road ahead of us, but at least [已經拿到的最小成果].
cards.quote: I'm not saying it's perfect, there's still a long road ahead of us, but we at least speak the same language.
cards.zh: 我不是說它已經完美，我們還有很長的路要走，但至少大家講的是同一種語言了。
cards.why: 三拍：不誇大 → 承認距離 → 守住底線成果。做進度報告時這是最穩的結構，因為它先把質疑講完，主管就沒有問題可以問。
cards.pmNote: 匯報半成品時，先量化「還沒到哪」，再定義「已經確定拿到什麼」。
cards.episode: How Block is becoming the most AI-native enterprise in the world | Dhanji R. Prasanna

alts.quote: And optics is a good thing. So I'm not saying don't think about optics whatsoever, I think it's actually important to think about optics.
alts.zh: 而且「對外呈現」本身是好事。我不是說完全不要管呈現，我覺得那其實很重要。

alts.quote: But before that, I think getting to product-market fit, obviously there's a lot of methodology for doing it today that might make it a bit easier for people, but I still think it's fairly random and pretty dang hard.
alts.zh: 在那之前——我覺得要走到 PMF，現在當然有很多方法論可能讓大家輕鬆一點，但我還是認為它相當隨機，而且真的很難。

alts.quote: I'm not saying it doesn't matter, but to me, again, it's more about that's a means to an end.
alts.zh: 我不是說那不重要，但對我來說，那比較是達成目的的手段。

cards.pattern: I'm not saying [極端版本], but I'm saying [真正要說的].
cards.quote: I'm not saying we should go back to the early 90's, but I'm saying it wasn't always like this.
cards.zh: 我不是說我們該回到九零年代初，我是說事情不是一直都長這樣。
cards.why: I'm not saying X, but I'm saying Y 是這整池的骨架句：同一個動詞重複兩次，把「你以為我在說的」跟「我真正在說的」並排，聽者不可能再誤讀。
cards.episode: Behind the founder: Drew Houston (Dropbox)

alts.quote: And I always write them back and say like, "Please tell me the better term and popularize it and I'll use it. It's a great idea."
alts.zh: 我都回信說：「請你告訴我更好的講法，然後把它推廣開，我就會改用。這主意很好。」

alts.quote: And optics is a good thing. So I'm not saying don't think about optics whatsoever, I think it's actually important to think about optics.
alts.zh: 而且「對外呈現」本身是好事。我不是說完全不要管呈現，我覺得那其實很重要。

alts.quote: So I'm not saying that having a large market someday doesn't matter, of course it does eventually.
alts.zh: 我不是說有一天有沒有大市場不重要，當然最後會很重要。

cards.pattern: Obviously, I'm not saying don't do [X], or don't do [Y].
cards.quote: Now, obviously, I'm not saying don't do SEO, or don't do SEM, so organic search or paid search.
cards.zh: 當然，我不是說不要做 SEO、也不是說不要做 SEM——就是自然搜尋跟付費搜尋。
cards.why: 唱衰一個通路之後最怕被斷章取義，所以要把「我沒有叫你停掉」逐項點名。obviously 讓這句聽起來像常識而不是補救。
cards.episode: Elena Verna on how B2B growth is changing, product-led growth, product-led sales, why you should go freemium not trial, what features to make free, and much more

alts.quote: And optics is a good thing. So I'm not saying don't think about optics whatsoever, I think it's actually important to think about optics.
alts.zh: 而且「對外呈現」本身是好事。我不是說完全不要管呈現，我覺得那其實很重要。

alts.quote: Now in general, I'm not saying that this is the only business model that is viable, but if you create value, you will figure out a business model.
alts.zh: 一般來說，我不是說這是唯一可行的商業模式，但只要你創造價值，商業模式你自然會找到。

alts.quote: Now, don't get me wrong, I've built the experimentation platform at Lyft. I'm a guy who loves data and loves using it and looking at experiments.
alts.zh: 先別誤會我的意思——Lyft 的實驗平台就是我建的。我是個超愛用數據、愛看實驗的人。

cards.pattern: I'm not saying [公司] is bad, but they used to have [某個價值], and it got lost.
cards.quote: I'm not saying Google's bad, but Google used to have this don't be evil ethos, and it got lost.
cards.zh: 我不是說 Google 很爛，但 Google 以前有「不作惡」那套精神，後來弄丟了。
cards.why: 標籤跟重話同一句：前半句撤掉人身攻擊，後半句用 used to… and it got lost 把批評講成「失落」而不是「墮落」，殺傷力更大但無法反駁。
cards.pmNote: 批評一家公司時，用「它自己曾經定下的標準」當尺，比用你的標準有力。
cards.episode: How to build a company that withstands any era | Eric Ries, Lean Startup author

alts.quote: Clearly, you're not so scared that you can't do anything, so I'm not buying it. I don't do it quite like that, I do it with a lot more love than that.
alts.zh: 很明顯你沒有害怕到什麼都做不了，所以這個說法我不買單。我實際上不會講得這麼硬，我會帶更多善意。

alts.quote: No, no, no. What they're saying is not that you're a bad product person, it's that you need to do a better job communicating or connecting.
alts.zh: 不不不。他們講的不是你是個爛 PM，而是你在溝通、在建立連結這件事上要做得更好。

alts.quote: Look, I don't have time to sugarcoat any feedback, and frankly, the best people I've worked with are the people who come into one-on-ones with me and yell at me and tell me I'm messing up.
alts.zh: 老實說，我沒空把回饋包糖衣；而且說真的，我合作過最好的人，都是會在一對一裡對我吼、直接說我哪裡搞砸了的人。

cards.pattern: I'm not saying one or the other was right or wrong, but as leaders we've got to get [最基本的問題] straight.
cards.quote: I'm not saying that one or the other was right or wrong, but as leaders in the organization, we've got to get some of the basic stories straight, including how do we fundamentally prioritize growth versus engagement versus monetization?
cards.zh: 我不是要說哪一邊對哪一邊錯，但身為組織的領導者，我們得先把一些最基本的故事講清楚——比如成長、互動、變現到底怎麼排順序。
cards.why: 先宣布「不評對錯」，就能把矛頭從兩派人轉到「你們沒有共識」這件事上，這是主管在兩個都很強的團隊之間開火的標準做法。
cards.pmNote: 兩派吵不完通常代表上層沒把優先順序講清楚，該修的是敘事不是人。
cards.episode: Gibson Biddle on his DHM product strategy framework, GEM roadmap prioritization framework, 5 Netflix strategy mini case studies, building a personal board of directors, and much more

alts.quote: And again, I'm not saying always, but sometimes it can happen that the thing that ends up shipping is the least common denominator that annoyed everybody the least amount, right?
alts.zh: 我不是說每次都這樣，但有時候最後出貨的東西，就是那個讓所有人都最不生氣的最小公約數。

alts.quote: I'm not saying I know the answer, but there was almost this refusal to look at what tech was doing from a political lens for a very long time.
alts.zh: 我不是說我知道答案，但有很長一段時間，大家幾乎是拒絕從政治的角度去看科技業在做什麼。

alts.quote: He said, "Well, two things. First, you were wrong. You were wrong to prioritize date over our reputation."
alts.zh: 他說：「兩件事。第一，你錯了。你不該把時程放在我們的商譽前面。」

cards.quote: First, big caveat, this is just super early.
cards.zh: 先講一個大但書：這還非常早期。
cards.why: 五個字的但書放在最前面，等於替接下來所有數字打上「暫時」的浮水印。台灣人常把這句放在講完之後，那時聽眾已經把數字記走了。
cards.pmNote: 早期數據要在開口前就標記不確定性，否則會被拿去當承諾。
cards.episode: Gustav Söderström

alts.quote: So don't confuse posting press releases even on very big websites with actual success.
alts.zh: 所以不要把「新聞稿被大網站登出來」跟真正的成功搞混。

alts.quote: And in that case, it was from about a 50% hit rate to 65. So that's pretty huge, so that's a really big difference.
alts.zh: 那個案例是命中率從大約 50% 提到 65%。這個差距其實非常大。

alts.quote: In fact, there's some early work on eBay that showed that if your first rating's negative, that could actually immediately cause an 8% hit on your immediate expected revenue, say nothing of long-term consequences.
alts.zh: 其實有一些早期針對 eBay 的研究顯示，如果你的第一則評價是負評，光是當下的預期營收就可能少 8%，長期的影響還沒算進去。

cards.quote: I mean, I don't want to act like I think this is easy, to be clear.
cards.zh: 我不想表現得好像我覺得這很簡單，先講清楚。
cards.why: 講完一套方法之後最容易招來的反彈是「你講得輕鬆」。先自己承認難度，反對意見就沒地方著力。
cards.episode: How to build a team that can “take a punch”: A playbook for building resilient, high-performing teams | Hilary Gridley (Head of Core Product, Whoop)

alts.quote: And to be clear, I don't think it's actually that dangerous right now.
alts.zh: 先講清楚，我不覺得現在真的有那麼危險。

alts.quote: To me, I think it's a great accelerant when it's already working, but it can't fix it if people don't want to talk about your product.
alts.zh: 對我來說，那在本來就跑得動的時候是很好的加速器，但如果根本沒人想談論你的產品，它救不了你。

alts.quote: In some ways, this sounds very puritanical, I don't mean it to sound this way, but there were lines that we didn't want to cross that just felt ethically not us, that I've seen other news players do more of.
alts.zh: 某種程度上這聽起來很清教徒，我不是要講成那樣，但確實有些線我們不想跨過去，那些做法感覺就不像我們——而我看到別的新聞產品做得更多。

cards.pattern: Now, to be clear, most of that is [毫不客氣的評價].
cards.quote: Now, to be clear, most of that is garbage in the real garbagey sense, right.
cards.zh: 先把話講清楚，那裡面大部分都是垃圾，字面意義上的垃圾。
cards.why: to be clear 在這裡不是緩衝，是加強——它宣告「我接下來要用精確的字」，於是 garbage 這種重話變成事實陳述而不是情緒發洩。
cards.episode: How to get press for your product | Jason Feifer (editor in chief of Entrepreneur magazine)

alts.quote: I got to tell you, the dominant failure case that I see in the real world is always, again and again, not enough detail.
alts.zh: 我得說，我在現實世界裡看到的主要失敗模式，一次又一次都是同一件事：細節給得不夠。

alts.quote: And I think I want to be clear, in my mind the problem is obviously not about the practitioners, it's systemic.
alts.zh: 我想講清楚：在我看來問題不在第一線的人身上，是系統性的。

alts.quote: I do want to be clear, it's one leader and their team who are accountable and responsible.
alts.zh: 我想把話講清楚：負責的就是一位負責人跟他的團隊。

cards.pattern: To be clear, not everyone ends up [最壞情況], but [我的解方].
cards.quote: To be clear, not everyone ends up in that level of depression, but the hack, if you will, is consciousness.
cards.zh: 先講清楚，不是每個人都會走到那種程度的憂鬱，但如果要說有什麼解法，那就是覺察。
cards.why: 講沉重案例時先把「這不會發生在每個人身上」講掉，避免聽眾把自己代入而關閉；接著才給方法。
cards.episode: How have I been complicit in creating the conditions I say I don’t want? | Jerry Colonna (CEO of Reboot, executive coach, former VC)

alts.quote: It's not LLMs to be clear, but there's engines like Stockfish these days that are just dramatically better than the top grand masters in the world.
alts.zh: 講清楚，那不是 LLM，但現在有像 Stockfish 那種引擎，已經遠遠強過世界頂尖大師。

alts.quote: And to be clear, I don't think it's actually that dangerous right now.
alts.zh: 先講清楚，我不覺得現在真的有那麼危險。

alts.quote: I mean, I don't want to act like I think this is easy, to be clear.
alts.zh: 我不想表現得好像我覺得這很簡單，先講清楚。

cards.quote: Now, to be clear, this is hard for me.
cards.zh: 先講清楚，這件事對我來說也很難。
cards.why: 在給建議的中途插一句「我自己也做不好」，能把講者從教練變回同路人，建議的接受度立刻改變。
cards.episode: How have I been complicit in creating the conditions I say I don’t want? | Jerry Colonna (CEO of Reboot, executive coach, former VC)

alts.quote: Now this is where I'm data informed, and I'm not data driven.
alts.zh: 這就是我所謂的「被數據啟發」，而不是「被數據驅動」。

alts.quote: The basic principle with laser is that willpower is never going to win, and there's great research on this, but for now just trust me, you're not going to white-knuckle your way through not looking at Twitter when you're trying to work.
alts.zh: laser 的基本原理是：意志力永遠贏不了。這方面有很多很好的研究，但現在你先信我——你不可能靠硬撐來讓自己工作時不看 Twitter。

alts.quote: Well, to be clear about my brand promise, because it's true, every word that has my name on it, I wrote.
alts.zh: 先把我的品牌承諾講清楚：每一個掛我名字的字，都是我寫的。

cards.pattern: I'm not saying it doesn't matter, but to me it's more about [真正的目的].
cards.quote: I'm not saying it doesn't matter, but to me, again, it's more about that's a means to an end.
cards.zh: 我不是說那不重要，但對我來說，那比較是達成目的的手段。
cards.why: 用 more about 而不是 not about，把爭論從「重不重要」轉成「排在哪一層」，對方就很難繼續捍衛。
cards.episode: Becoming a conscious leader: Leading without fear, finding your life’s objective function, and getting better at vision and strategy | John Mark Nickels (Uber, Waymo, DoorDash)

alts.quote: So I'm not saying that having a large market someday doesn't matter, of course it does eventually.
alts.zh: 我不是說有一天有沒有大市場不重要，當然最後會很重要。

alts.quote: And optics is a good thing. So I'm not saying don't think about optics whatsoever, I think it's actually important to think about optics.
alts.zh: 而且「對外呈現」本身是好事。我不是說完全不要管呈現，我覺得那其實很重要。

alts.quote: I'm not saying it's perfect, there's still a long road ahead of us, but we at least speak the same language.
alts.zh: 我不是說它已經完美，我們還有很長的路要走，但至少大家講的是同一種語言了。

cards.pattern: I'm not saying you have to [誇張到好笑的版本].
cards.quote: So I'm not saying you have to go to Bali and do 200 breathwork journeys.
cards.zh: 我不是說你得跑去峇里島做兩百次呼吸療程。
cards.why: 把對方可能有的抗拒具體誇大成一個好笑的畫面再否認，比抽象地說「沒有那麼誇張」有效——聽眾笑完就放下防備。
cards.episode: Managing nerves, anxiety, and burnout | Jonny Miller (Nervous System Mastery)

alts.quote: And optics is a good thing. So I'm not saying don't think about optics whatsoever, I think it's actually important to think about optics.
alts.zh: 而且「對外呈現」本身是好事。我不是說完全不要管呈現，我覺得那其實很重要。

alts.quote: So I'm not saying that having a large market someday doesn't matter, of course it does eventually.
alts.zh: 我不是說有一天有沒有大市場不重要，當然最後會很重要。

alts.quote: I'm not saying it's perfect, there's still a long road ahead of us, but we at least speak the same language.
alts.zh: 我不是說它已經完美，我們還有很長的路要走，但至少大家講的是同一種語言了。

cards.pattern: I'm not saying [自家產品] is a commodity or we want it to be, but objectively [殘酷事實].
cards.quote: I'm not saying that Arc is a commodity or we want it to be, but objectively web browsers are interchangeable.
cards.zh: 我不是說 Arc 是可替換的商品、也不是說我們希望它是，但客觀上瀏覽器就是可以互換的。
cards.why: 談自家產品的弱點時，先把「我不是在自貶」講掉，再用 objectively 把殘酷事實推給市場而不是自己。這是創辦人談競爭最安全的句型。
cards.pmNote: 承認品類同質化，才能把差異化的討論推到轉換成本與使用習慣上。
cards.episode: Competing with giants: An inside look at how The Browser Company builds product | Josh Miller (CEO)

alts.quote: And I'm not saying agents cannot understand this or models are not capable enough to understand this, but there are really weird rules within enterprises that are not documented anywhere.
alts.zh: 我不是說 agent 理解不了這些，也不是說模型能力不夠，而是企業裡有一堆非常奇怪、根本沒寫在任何文件上的規則。

alts.quote: And optics is a good thing. So I'm not saying don't think about optics whatsoever, I think it's actually important to think about optics.
alts.zh: 而且「對外呈現」本身是好事。我不是說完全不要管呈現，我覺得那其實很重要。

alts.quote: One, what a problem to have. Of all the problems in the world, "I'm overwhelmed by customer interest," is on the top list of problems I want to have.
alts.zh: 第一，這是多好的問題啊。世界上這麼多問題，「客戶熱情多到我應付不來」是我最想要的那幾個之一。

cards.pattern: To be clear, [X] is not the way the utopians think it will be or the dystopians think it will be.
cards.quote: And to be clear, I think we're looking at a world that's not radically transformed the way that, maybe, the utopians think that it will be or the dystopians think it will be.
cards.zh: 先講清楚，我認為我們面對的世界，不會像烏托邦派想的那樣被徹底改造，也不會像反烏托邦派想的那樣。
cards.why: 同時否定兩個極端，等於替自己畫出中間地帶，聽者無法把你歸到任一陣營再攻擊。
cards.episode: Marc Andreessen: The real AI boom hasn’t even started yet

alts.quote: One, I think that's a really fantastic, maybe not counterpoint, but thing to call out.
alts.zh: 第一，我覺得你這個提得非常好——也不算是反駁啦，但確實是該點出來的一件事。

alts.quote: I don't really agree and I still think it's wrong, but I'm committed to it." That's not actually commitment.
alts.zh: 「我其實不同意，我還是覺得這是錯的，但我會照做。」那並不是真正的承諾。

alts.quote: That's a good idea, but we don't actually understand these three things before we start working on that. So maybe we should do understand work to make sure that that is actually the right idea.
alts.zh: 這個想法不錯，但在動手之前有三件事我們其實還沒搞懂。也許先做點「理解型的工作」，確認這真的是對的方向。

cards.quote: I'm not saying I'm proud of that, but it just is.
cards.zh: 我不是說我以此為榮，但事實就是這樣。
cards.why: 承認一個不光彩的事實時，先切掉「炫耀」的解讀，再用 it just is 拒絕再解釋——不辯護，反而更可信。
cards.episode: How to fire people with grace, work through fear, and nurture innovation | Matt Mochary (CEO coach)

alts.quote: The true test of whether the positioning's working is, if I'm sitting across from a qualified prospect and I tell the story, does the prospect get excited and want to buy something?
alts.zh: 定位有沒有效，真正的檢驗是：我坐在一個合格的潛在客戶對面把故事講完，他會不會眼睛一亮、想買東西？

alts.quote: Now this is where I'm data informed, and I'm not data driven.
alts.zh: 這就是我所謂的「被數據啟發」，而不是「被數據驅動」。

alts.quote: It's about saying, okay, if we have these themes of stuff that we want to work on, what do we know with confidence because the data tells us and what do we need to understand because we don't have the data?
alts.zh: 重點是要問：在我們想做的這些主題裡，哪些是數據講得夠清楚、我們有把握的？哪些是因為沒數據，所以還得先搞懂的？

cards.pattern: I'm not saying I know the answer, but there was almost this refusal to [看見某件事].
cards.quote: I'm not saying I know the answer, but there was almost this refusal to look at what tech was doing from a political lens for a very long time.
cards.zh: 我不是說我知道答案，但有很長一段時間，大家幾乎是拒絕從政治的角度去看科技業在做什麼。
cards.why: 先放棄「我有解方」的高位，再指控一個集體盲點。沒有解方的批評如果不先自貶，很容易被回一句「那你說怎麼辦」堵死。
cards.pmNote: 提出你沒有解方的問題時，先聲明沒解方，才不會被要求當場提方案而閉嘴。
cards.episode: How Palantir built the ultimate founder factory | Nabeel S. Qureshi (founder, writer, ex-Palantir)

alts.quote: Look, I don't have time to sugarcoat any feedback, and frankly, the best people I've worked with are the people who come into one-on-ones with me and yell at me and tell me I'm messing up.
alts.zh: 老實說，我沒空把回饋包糖衣；而且說真的，我合作過最好的人，都是會在一對一裡對我吼、直接說我哪裡搞砸了的人。

alts.quote: I'm not saying that one or the other was right or wrong, but as leaders in the organization, we've got to get some of the basic stories straight, including how do we fundamentally prioritize growth versus engagement versus monetization?
alts.zh: 我不是要說哪一邊對哪一邊錯，但身為組織的領導者，我們得先把一些最基本的故事講清楚——比如成長、互動、變現到底怎麼排順序。

alts.quote: And again, I'm not saying always, but sometimes it can happen that the thing that ends up shipping is the least common denominator that annoyed everybody the least amount, right?
alts.zh: 我不是說每次都這樣，但有時候最後出貨的東西，就是那個讓所有人都最不生氣的最小公約數。

cards.pattern: This might be my hot take, but we do almost no [大家都在做的事].
cards.quote: This might be my hot take, but we do almost no estimating in order to hit deadlines.
cards.zh: 這可能算我的辣評：我們幾乎不做工時估算，照樣趕上死線。
cards.why: might 讓標籤更輕，換到的空間是直接否定一個行業標準做法，而且用「我們實際上就這樣做」當證據，比講道理難反駁。
cards.pmNote: 靠估算逼準時交付常是假象；改成縮小範圍與固定時間盒更可靠。
cards.episode: Linear’s secret to building beloved B2B products | Nan Yu (Head of Product)

alts.quote: But my hot take is that for the vast majority of people, they probably do not need a coach.
alts.zh: 但我的辣評是：對絕大多數人來說，他們大概並不需要教練。

alts.quote: Maybe this is a hot take, but I feel like product market fit is independent of your marketplace dynamics.
alts.zh: 這可能是個辣評，但我覺得 PMF 跟你的平台供需動態其實是兩回事。

alts.quote: So yeah, that's my hot take and hopefully I offend everyone.
alts.zh: 對，那就是我的辣評，希望我把大家都得罪了。

cards.quote: I'm pretty proud of that and I'm not saying that to brag.
cards.zh: 我對那件事滿自豪的——我這樣講不是要炫耀。
cards.why: 這是標籤放在後面的合法用法：先把成績講完，再解除炫耀的解讀。台灣人常因為怕被說炫耀乾脆不講成績，等於白做。
cards.pmNote: 講自己的成果時不要省略，補一句「不是要炫耀」就夠了。
cards.episode: Strategies for becoming less distracted and improving focus | Nir Eyal (author of Indistractable and Hooked)

alts.quote: And in that case, it was from about a 50% hit rate to 65. So that's pretty huge, so that's a really big difference.
alts.zh: 那個案例是命中率從大約 50% 提到 65%。這個差距其實非常大。

alts.quote: The true test of whether the positioning's working is, if I'm sitting across from a qualified prospect and I tell the story, does the prospect get excited and want to buy something?
alts.zh: 定位有沒有效，真正的檢驗是：我坐在一個合格的潛在客戶對面把故事講完，他會不會眼睛一亮、想買東西？

alts.quote: Now this is where I'm data informed, and I'm not data driven.
alts.zh: 這就是我所謂的「被數據啟發」，而不是「被數據驅動」。

cards.quote: So yeah, that's my hot take and hopefully I offend everyone.
cards.zh: 對，那就是我的辣評，希望我把大家都得罪了。
cards.why: 講完重話後用自嘲收尾，把「你冒犯到我了」這個回應自己先講掉，對方再說就顯得沒幽默感。
cards.episode: 10 lessons on bootstrapping a $200m business | Patrick Campbell (ProfitWell)

alts.quote: Hot take, paid is for everyone.
alts.zh: 辣評：付費行銷是每個人都該做的。

alts.quote: Hopefully, I don't come off as encouraging everyone to be like me. I'm not saying that at all. What I'm saying is, this is a way to be.
alts.zh: 希望我聽起來不是在鼓吹大家都要跟我一樣。我完全不是那個意思。我要說的是：這是一種活法。

alts.quote: Yeah, sorry. Buy-in doesn't feel quite right to me, because buy-in feels like, oh, I've come to agree with you. And that's different from it's a part of me.
alts.zh: 抱歉，我覺得「buy-in（買單）」這個詞不太對。buy-in 聽起來像「我最後被你說服了」，那跟「這東西本來就是我的一部分」是兩回事。

cards.pattern: It's super boring, but the biggest hot take is you just have to [簡單到無聊的做法].
cards.quote: It's super boring, but the biggest hot take is you just have to do something once a quarter.
cards.zh: 這超無聊，但最辣的評論就是：你每一季至少得動一次。
cards.why: 用 boring 當反標籤，反而讓「這件事無聊到大家都不做」變成攻擊點；hot take 不一定要語不驚人，也可以辣在它太簡單。
cards.pmNote: 定價的最大問題不是算法不夠好，是一整年沒動過。
cards.episode: 10 lessons on bootstrapping a $200m business | Patrick Campbell (ProfitWell)

alts.quote: I'm not saying that having a large market someday doesn't matter, of course it does eventually. But trying to be super pedantic about market size when it's a pre-seed company, it's just not something I'd put a lot of thought.
alts.zh: 我不是說市場總有一天要夠大這件事不重要，當然重要。但在一家 pre-seed 公司還在糾結市場規模算得多精確，我不會花太多心思在上面。

alts.quote: Oh, I think this is my hot take. You hear people talking about craft and taste and product management, and it's all very wonderful. And I'm totally on board.
alts.zh: 喔，這大概是我的爭議發言了。大家都在談 craft、談品味、談產品管理，聽起來都很美好，我也完全買單——
