alts.quote: And it's kind of building a house that you want every brick in the house to match. And if you go and try and take some bricks from someone else's house and stick it in your house, it's probably going to not look very matched.
alts.zh: 這有點像蓋房子，你會希望每一塊磚都是搭的。如果你跑去人家家裡搬幾塊磚塞進自己家，看起來大概就是不搭。

cards.quote: But I'm not telling you to say that to them, just to be clear.
cards.zh: 但我不是要你真的去對他們講這句話，先說清楚。
cards.why: 示範一個心裡的想法之後，馬上切割「這不是台詞」，避免對方照抄闖禍。這是教方法時最常漏掉的一句。
cards.episode: Land your dream job in today’s market: negotiation tactics, job search councils, and more | Phyl Terry (Author, “Never Search Alone”)

alts.quote: Not to say it's not better, but just this is the structure of it, and it kind of sets you up for bragging.
alts.zh: 我不是說它不好，我只是在講它的結構——這個結構會把你逼到一直自誇。

alts.quote: So they would say, "Oh, your market's not big enough." And I would say, "It's going to be huge." And I'd add a new page in my pitch deck that said how big the market I believe was.
alts.zh: 他們會說：「你的市場不夠大。」我就說：「它會變超大。」然後我就在簡報裡加一頁，講我認為這市場有多大。

alts.quote: And I always write them back and say like, "Please tell me the better term and popularize it and I'll use it. It's a great idea."
alts.zh: 我都回信說：「請你告訴我更好的講法，然後把它推廣開，我就會改用。這主意很好。」

cards.pattern: Don't hear this as [對方可能誤讀的敵意].
cards.quote: Now, again, don't hear this as antagonistic.
cards.zh: 再說一次，別把這句話聽成是在跟你作對。
cards.why: 直接指示對方「該怎麼聽」，比說「我沒有惡意」更強——它把解讀權從對方手上拿回來一半。again 表示這是重複的提醒。
cards.pmNote: 給難聽的回饋時先講「這不是對立」，能把對方從防衛模式拉回問題本身。
cards.episode: Land your dream job in today’s market: negotiation tactics, job search councils, and more | Phyl Terry (Author, “Never Search Alone”)

alts.quote: The only thing that's different is the insight that the founder has on the market, which is a hard pill to swallow. And I know that's hard to hear too.
alts.zh: 唯一的差別是創辦人對市場的洞察——這顆藥很難吞。我也知道這話很難聽。

alts.quote: Clearly, you're not so scared that you can't do anything, so I'm not buying it. I don't do it quite like that, I do it with a lot more love than that.
alts.zh: 很明顯你沒有害怕到什麼都做不了，所以這個說法我不買單。我實際上不會講得這麼硬，我會帶更多善意。

alts.quote: I got to tell you, the dominant failure case that I see in the real world is always, again and again, not enough detail.
alts.zh: 我得說，我在現實世界裡看到的主要失敗模式，一次又一次都是同一件事：細節給得不夠。

cards.pattern: I'm not saying just blow through [責任] and not [基本義務].
cards.quote: I'm not saying just blow through your meetings and not turn up for your one-on-ones.
cards.zh: 我不是說你可以把會議全部推掉、一對一也不出席。
cards.why: 給了很激進的建議之後，用最具體的失職行為當反例來畫界線，聽者就知道邊界在哪、不會走偏。
cards.episode: Superhuman's secret to success: Ignoring most customer feedback, manually onboarding every new user, obsessing over every detail, and positioning around a single attribute: speed | Rahul Vohra (CEO)

alts.quote: And optics is a good thing. So I'm not saying don't think about optics whatsoever, I think it's actually important to think about optics.
alts.zh: 而且「對外呈現」本身是好事。我不是說完全不要管呈現，我覺得那其實很重要。

alts.quote: So I'm not saying that having a large market someday doesn't matter, of course it does eventually.
alts.zh: 我不是說有一天有沒有大市場不重要，當然最後會很重要。

alts.quote: I'm not saying it's perfect, there's still a long road ahead of us, but we at least speak the same language.
alts.zh: 我不是說它已經完美，我們還有很長的路要走，但至少大家講的是同一種語言了。

cards.pattern: I'm not saying always, but sometimes what ends up shipping is the least common denominator.
cards.quote: And again, I'm not saying always, but sometimes it can happen that the thing that ends up shipping is the least common denominator that annoyed everybody the least amount, right?
cards.zh: 我不是說每次都這樣，但有時候最後出貨的東西，就是那個讓所有人都最不生氣的最小公約數。
cards.why: 用 not always / sometimes 把頻率降到最低，換來的是一句非常刺的組織批評；量詞退讓、內容不退讓，是英文開火的標準交換。
cards.pmNote: 共識驅動的決策容易產出最小公約數產品，需要有人被授權做不受歡迎的取捨。
cards.episode: Sanchan Saxena (VP of Product at Coinbase) on the inside story of how Airbnb made it through Covid; what he’s learned from Brian Chesky, Brian Armstrong, and Kevin Systrom; much more

alts.quote: I'm not saying that one or the other was right or wrong, but as leaders in the organization, we've got to get some of the basic stories straight, including how do we fundamentally prioritize growth versus engagement versus monetization?
alts.zh: 我不是要說哪一邊對哪一邊錯，但身為組織的領導者，我們得先把一些最基本的故事講清楚——比如成長、互動、變現到底怎麼排順序。

alts.quote: I'm not saying I know the answer, but there was almost this refusal to look at what tech was doing from a political lens for a very long time.
alts.zh: 我不是說我知道答案，但有很長一段時間，大家幾乎是拒絕從政治的角度去看科技業在做什麼。

alts.quote: I got to tell you, the dominant failure case that I see in the real world is always, again and again, not enough detail.
alts.zh: 我得說，我在現實世界裡看到的主要失敗模式，一次又一次都是同一件事：細節給得不夠。

cards.pattern: To be clear about my [承諾], every [最小單位] that has my name on it, I [親自做的].
cards.quote: Well, to be clear about my brand promise, because it's true, every word that has my name on it, I wrote.
cards.zh: 先把我的品牌承諾講清楚：每一個掛我名字的字，都是我寫的。
cards.why: to be clear about my X 把接下來的話定位成「規格說明」而不是自誇；後半句用最小單位（every word）當證據，無法打折。
cards.episode: Seth Godin's best tactics for building remarkable products, strategies, brands and more

alts.quote: And it's not bad because it's not well-intentioned, but it's bad because it's not contextual.
alts.zh: 它不好，不是因為對方沒有善意，而是因為它沒有考慮你的處境。

alts.quote: Yeah, I mean, I can't promise that works for everyone, but again, in the very bespoke situation with Rujul, it worked really well.
alts.zh: 我不能保證這對每個人都有效，但在 Rujul 那個很特定的情況下，效果非常好。

alts.quote: It's about saying, okay, if we have these themes of stuff that we want to work on, what do we know with confidence because the data tells us and what do we need to understand because we don't have the data?
alts.zh: 重點是要問：在我們想做的這些主題裡，哪些是數據講得夠清楚、我們有把握的？哪些是因為沒數據，所以還得先搞懂的？

cards.quote: So to be clear, I don't explicitly see quantitative numbers around this.
cards.zh: 先講清楚，我並沒有真的看到這方面的量化數字。
cards.why: 主動標記自己講的是觀察不是數據，接下來的判斷反而更被信任——把證據等級講明白是可信度的來源，不是弱點。
cards.pmNote: 分享趨勢判斷時先聲明「這不是數據」，能避免被引用成公司立場。
cards.episode: Sherwin Wu V2

alts.quote: It's not that I worked at groups that were particularly bad, Booking, Google Ads, other companies published numbers that are around 80 to 90% failure rate of ideas.
alts.zh: 不是說我待的團隊特別爛——Booking、Google Ads 這些公司公開的數字，點子的失敗率也都在八到九成左右。

alts.quote: It's about saying, okay, if we have these themes of stuff that we want to work on, what do we know with confidence because the data tells us and what do we need to understand because we don't have the data?
alts.zh: 重點是要問：在我們想做的這些主題裡，哪些是數據講得夠清楚、我們有把握的？哪些是因為沒數據，所以還得先搞懂的？

alts.quote: If you think about your last all hands, the last talk you saw, you probably don't remember much. In fact, I wager you might only remember one thing from that talk.
alts.zh: 回想你上一次的全員大會、上一場你聽的演講——你大概記不得多少。老實說，我敢賭你只記得一件事。

cards.pattern: If I'm being honest to myself, I'm not [達到自己的標準].
cards.quote: But then, again, if I'm being honest to myself, I'm not making as good product decisions as I can.
cards.zh: 但話說回來，如果對自己誠實，我做的產品決策並沒有達到我能做到的水準。
cards.why: honest to myself 比 honest 多一層——它把這句話定位成內部盤點而非對外表態，聽者不會覺得你在討拍。
cards.episode: Shreyas Doshi Live

alts.quote: And so, I think I probably shipped a lot of bad product those years, if I'm being completely honest.
alts.zh: 所以老實說，那幾年我大概出了不少爛產品。

alts.quote: The true test of whether the positioning's working is, if I'm sitting across from a qualified prospect and I tell the story, does the prospect get excited and want to buy something?
alts.zh: 定位有沒有效，真正的檢驗是：我坐在一個合格的潛在客戶對面把故事講完，他會不會眼睛一亮、想買東西？

alts.quote: Yeah, I mean, I can't promise that works for everyone, but again, in the very bespoke situation with Rujul, it worked really well.
alts.zh: 我不能保證這對每個人都有效，但在 Rujul 那個很特定的情況下，效果非常好。

cards.pattern: There's nothing wrong with [欲望], just to be clear, but then focus on [真正的槓桿].
cards.quote: And there's nothing wrong with wanting a promotion, just to be clear, and there's nothing wrong with being ambitious, but then focus on the impact.
cards.zh: 想升遷完全沒問題，先講清楚，有野心也完全沒問題——但那就把注意力放在影響力上。
cards.why: 先把對方的動機除罪化兩次，才有資格叫他改行為；如果直接說「別只想著升遷」，對方會先花力氣否認自己想升遷。
cards.pmNote: 談升遷輔導時要先承認欲望正當，才談得下去要做什麼。
cards.episode: Product lessons from Waymo | Shweta Shrivastava (Waymo, Amazon, Cisco)

alts.quote: It's not LLMs to be clear, but there's engines like Stockfish these days that are just dramatically better than the top grand masters in the world.
alts.zh: 講清楚，那不是 LLM，但現在有像 Stockfish 那種引擎，已經遠遠強過世界頂尖大師。

alts.quote: And so I think if there's anything that I would be accused of, it would be being over simplifying things.
alts.zh: 如果說我有什麼會被人批評的，大概就是我把事情簡化過頭了。

alts.quote: But if they come in on day one saying your strategy is all wrong, raises the question of, "Well then why did you join my team if you didn't believe in my strategy?"
alts.zh: 但如果他第一天就說你的策略整個都錯了，那就會讓人想問：既然你不相信這個策略，當初為什麼要加入我的團隊？

cards.quote: I want to be clear that I had seen that idea somewhere else, someone else, a blog post about it or something like that.
cards.zh: 我想講清楚，那個點子我是在別的地方看到的，是別人寫的一篇部落格之類的。
cards.why: 主動歸還功勞會提高其他說法的可信度；聽者的推論是「他連這種小事都要澄清，其他應該也沒誇大」。
cards.episode: Slack founder: Mental models for building products people love ft. Stewart Butterfield

alts.quote: The true test of whether the positioning's working is, if I'm sitting across from a qualified prospect and I tell the story, does the prospect get excited and want to buy something?
alts.zh: 定位有沒有效，真正的檢驗是：我坐在一個合格的潛在客戶對面把故事講完，他會不會眼睛一亮、想買東西？

alts.quote: And what Lomi does is you take your food scraps, and it turns out that depending on whose numbers you want to believe, in America, we throw away somewhere between 40 to 60% of our food.
alts.zh: 看你要相信誰的數字，在美國我們大概丟掉四成到六成的食物。

alts.quote: Never ever once have I seen a rebrand or redesign, especially of a marketing site, produce good performance results.
alts.zh: 我從來、一次都沒看過品牌重塑或改版——尤其是行銷官網——帶來好的成效數字。

cards.pattern: Hot take: [X] is for everyone.
cards.quote: Hot take, paid is for everyone.
cards.zh: 辣評：付費行銷是每個人都該做的。
cards.why: 兩個字的標籤加四個字的主張，是最短的開火句型。標籤前置讓對方知道這是刻意挑釁，反而不會生氣。
cards.episode: The ultimate guide to performance marketing | Timothy Davis (Shopify)

alts.quote: So yeah, that's my hot take and hopefully I offend everyone.
alts.zh: 對，那就是我的辣評，希望我把大家都得罪了。

alts.quote: I don't have Twitter, like hot take, I think Twitter ruins people's careers.
alts.zh: 我沒有 Twitter——講個辣評，我覺得 Twitter 會毀掉人的職涯。

alts.quote: But my hot take is that for the vast majority of people, they probably do not need a coach.
alts.zh: 但我的辣評是：對絕大多數人來說，他們大概並不需要教練。

cards.pattern: I'm not saying this is the only [方案] that is viable, but if you [做對的事], you will figure out [後面的問題].
cards.quote: Now in general, I'm not saying that this is the only business model that is viable, but if you create value, you will figure out a business model.
cards.zh: 一般來說，我不是說這是唯一可行的商業模式，但只要你創造價值，商業模式你自然會找到。
cards.why: 先放棄「唯一解」的宣稱，再把重點推回一個更高階的原則——這樣主張反而更難被個案反駁。
cards.pmNote: 早期別急著鎖定商業模式，先確認價值是否真實存在。
cards.episode: Lessons from a two-time unicorn builder, 50-time startup advisor, and 20-time company board member | Uri Levine (co-founder of Waze)

alts.quote: Now, obviously, I'm not saying don't do SEO, or don't do SEM, so organic search or paid search.
alts.zh: 當然，我不是說不要做 SEO、也不是說不要做 SEM——就是自然搜尋跟付費搜尋。

alts.quote: And optics is a good thing. So I'm not saying don't think about optics whatsoever, I think it's actually important to think about optics.
alts.zh: 而且「對外呈現」本身是好事。我不是說完全不要管呈現，我覺得那其實很重要。

alts.quote: So I'm not saying that having a large market someday doesn't matter, of course it does eventually.
alts.zh: 我不是說有一天有沒有大市場不重要，當然最後會很重要。

cards.pattern: To be clear, I'm not saying you should [極端行動]—I'm just saying [真正的主張].
cards.quote: And to be clear, I’m not saying you should quit building your strategic-thinking muscle—I’m just saying that AI will give you huge leverage here eventually.
cards.zh: 先講清楚，我不是說你該停止鍛鍊你的策略思考肌肉——我只是說，AI 早晚會在這裡給你巨大的槓桿。
cards.why: 破折號把「不是」跟「只是」拉在同一口氣裡，書面上等於不留給讀者誤讀的空白。I'm just saying 的 just 把主張縮到最小、最難反駁的版本。
cards.episode: How AI will impact product management

alts.quote: So I'm not saying that having a large market someday doesn't matter, of course it does eventually.
alts.zh: 我不是說有一天有沒有大市場不重要，當然最後會很重要。

alts.quote: But I can understand why the hair stands up on the back of the neck a little bit thinking about it because, of course, if you give a senior engineer like, "Here's how I want you to go implement the schema"…
alts.zh: 但我理解為什麼你一想到這個就會汗毛豎起來——畢竟你如果去跟資深工程師說「這個 schema 我要你這樣實作」……

alts.quote: To be clear, we're not building that, but it's a fun idea.
alts.zh: 先講清楚，我們沒有要做那個，但那是個有趣的點子。

cards.pattern: I use [產品]—I'm an investor, so I'm biased—but [推薦].
cards.quote: I now use, I'm an investor, so I'm biased, but Aura, A-U-R-A, which is a marketplace app.
cards.zh: 我現在用的是——我有投資，所以我立場不中立——Aura，A-U-R-A，一個市集型的 app。
cards.why: 利益揭露插在推薦的正中間，而不是講完才補；推薦一旦講完，揭露就變成事後補救。
cards.pmNote: 推薦任何你有利益關係的工具，揭露要早於推薦本身。
cards.episode: When and how to invest in new acquisition channels | Adam Grenier (Uber, MasterClass)

alts.quote: Now this is where I'm data informed, and I'm not data driven.
alts.zh: 這就是我所謂的「被數據啟發」，而不是「被數據驅動」。

alts.quote: So there's a different metric that I like to use, which keys off of this idea that I think, again, people don't appreciate, which is cancellations grow faster than marketing.
alts.zh: 我比較喜歡用另一個指標，它是從一個大家常常沒放在心上的觀念推出來的：取消的成長速度比行銷快。

alts.quote: The true test of whether the positioning's working is, if I'm sitting across from a qualified prospect and I tell the story, does the prospect get excited and want to buy something?
alts.zh: 定位有沒有效，真正的檢驗是：我坐在一個合格的潛在客戶對面把故事講完，他會不會眼睛一亮、想買東西？

cards.pattern: In the spirit of full disclosure, I'm familiar with [對象].
cards.quote: In the spirit of full disclosure, I'm familiar with Clary.
cards.zh: 本著完全揭露的精神，我跟 Clary 這家公司是熟的。
cards.why: familiar with 是刻意保守的說法——揭露關係但不細講程度，既完成誠信義務又不必攤開細節。
cards.episode: How to become a category pirate | Christopher Lochhead (author of Play Bigger, Niche Down, Category Pirates, more)

alts.quote: The true test of whether the positioning's working is, if I'm sitting across from a qualified prospect and I tell the story, does the prospect get excited and want to buy something?
alts.zh: 定位有沒有效，真正的檢驗是：我坐在一個合格的潛在客戶對面把故事講完，他會不會眼睛一亮、想買東西？

alts.quote: Now this is where I'm data informed, and I'm not data driven.
alts.zh: 這就是我所謂的「被數據啟發」，而不是「被數據驅動」。

alts.quote: If you tell someone, 'This is the problem I'm going to address,' and they will tell you, 'Oh, I know someone that has this problem,' it's not a real problem.
alts.zh: 如果你跟人說「這是我要解決的問題」，對方回你「喔，我知道有誰有這個問題」——那它就不是真問題。

cards.pattern: I'll be the first to tell you that, and I admit that [自己做過頭的地方].
cards.quote: And I'll be the first to tell you that, and I admit that this might have carried on too far.
cards.zh: 這件事我會第一個承認，我也承認這可能做得太過頭了。
cards.why: I'll be the first to tell you 是搶在批評者之前認錯，等於先把武器繳出去；後面的 admit 才是真正的內容。
cards.episode: Lessons from scaling Stripe | Claire Hughes Johnson (former COO of Stripe)

alts.quote: And I always write them back and say like, "Please tell me the better term and popularize it and I'll use it. It's a great idea."
alts.zh: 我都回信說：「請你告訴我更好的講法，然後把它推廣開，我就會改用。這主意很好。」

alts.quote: Here's what I have a problem with. First of all, having a growth mindset is a very, very helpful thing.
alts.zh: 我要說的是我對它的哪一點有意見。首先，擁有成長心態本身是非常非常有幫助的事。

alts.quote: And Twitter is designed for outrage getting likes. So I wouldn't read too much into it.
alts.zh: Twitter 這個場子本來就是設計來讓憤怒獲得按讚的。所以我不會太當一回事。

cards.pattern: This sounds so trite, but really it's true: [老生常談的建議].
cards.quote: The best advice I could give you is, and this sounds so trite, but really it's true, is, stay as small as you can for as long as you can.
cards.zh: 我能給的最好建議是——這聽起來很老套，但真的是真的——能維持多小就維持多小，能撐多久就撐多久。
cards.why: 先自己說「這聽起來很陳腔濫調」，聽者心裡那句吐槽就被講掉了，剩下的注意力才會放在建議本身。
cards.pmNote: 講經典建議前先承認它老套，比包裝成新洞見更有說服力。
cards.episode: Jason Fried challenges your thinking on fundraising, goals, growth, and more

alts.quote: And I'd say it's not just that the budget's too small, it would be that they put all their eggs in one basket.
alts.zh: 我會說，問題不只是預算太小，而是他們把所有雞蛋放在同一個籃子裡。

alts.quote: I'm not saying it's perfect, there's still a long road ahead of us, but we at least speak the same language.
alts.zh: 我不是說它已經完美，我們還有很長的路要走，但至少大家講的是同一種語言了。

alts.quote: So, if any of this sounds like "better than thou," it's not intended to.
alts.zh: 如果這些聽起來有點「我比你高尚」的味道，那不是我的本意。

cards.pattern: If any of this sounds like [對方可能感受到的傲慢], it's not intended to.
cards.quote: So, if any of this sounds like "better than thou," it's not intended to.
cards.zh: 如果這些聽起來有點「我比你高尚」的味道，那不是我的本意。
cards.why: 用條件句 if any of this sounds like… 把可能的冒犯講出來但不承認自己冒犯了，既道歉又不認錯，是英文很常用的雙軌處理。
cards.episode: Competing with giants: An inside look at how The Browser Company builds product | Josh Miller (CEO)

alts.quote: Not to say it's not better, but just this is the structure of it, and it kind of sets you up for bragging.
alts.zh: 我不是說它不好，我只是在講它的結構——這個結構會把你逼到一直自誇。

alts.quote: Sometimes I feel the need to defend that the process is not for process' sake, it's ultimately to help us all move faster and work better.
alts.zh: 有時候我得替流程辯護一下：流程不是為了流程而存在，它最終是要讓大家跑得更快、做得更好。

alts.quote: And I always write them back and say like, "Please tell me the better term and popularize it and I'll use it. It's a great idea."
alts.zh: 我都回信說：「請你告訴我更好的講法，然後把它推廣開，我就會改用。這主意很好。」

cards.pattern: I can't prove this, and [專家] may say that I'm wrong, but this is my best guess.
cards.quote: What I'm guessing, and I can't prove this, an LLM expert in the comments may say that I'm wrong, but this is my best guess as a non-educated person.
cards.zh: 我猜——我證明不了，留言區的 LLM 專家搞不好會說我錯了——但這是我這個非科班的人最好的猜測。
cards.why: 事先把最可能來砸場的人（專家）點名，等於先幫他們發過言；接著仍然把猜測講完。這是「沒有權威也能發表看法」的完整句型。
cards.pmNote: 在你不是專家的領域發表判斷時，先標記身分與可證性，反而更容易得到專家補充而不是嘲笑。
cards.episode: The rise of the professional vibe coder (a new AI-era job) | Lazar Jovanovic (Professional Vibe Coder)

alts.quote: Whenever you talk to people who are at the company, they're always try to tell you the best version of the company. It's on you to triangulate that information, but you need both sides.
alts.zh: 你去問還在公司裡的人，他們永遠給你公司最好的那個版本。要交叉比對是你自己的責任，但兩邊的說法你都得聽到。

alts.quote: We heard a couple comments from them, it was little murmurs. And I didn't realize at the time that was the signal that we did not have product market fit.
alts.zh: 我們只聽到他們零星幾句抱怨，就是一點小碎念而已。我當時沒意識到，那正是我們沒有 PMF 的訊號。

alts.quote: According to Harvard Law School, among venture-backed companies that have the standard best practices set up that you got from your lawyer, only 20% of founders are still the CEO three years after going public.
alts.zh: 根據哈佛法學院的研究，在那些照律師標準做法設立的創投公司裡，上市三年後還在當 CEO 的創辦人只有 20%。

cards.pattern: It's self-serving and a horrible survivorship bias to just list [成功的那些].
cards.quote: Companies I've invested in is a long list, and I love to give you names of companies that don't exist anymore because it's self-serving and a horrible survivorship bias to just list the good ones.
cards.zh: 我投資過的公司名單很長，我很願意告訴你那些已經倒掉的公司名字——因為只列出成功的那些，是自利、也是很糟的倖存者偏誤。
cards.why: 主動供出失敗案例，把「倖存者偏誤」這個詞當武器用在自己身上，之後你講的成功案例才有重量。
cards.pmNote: 引用案例時同時給出反例母數，別人才知道你的成功率不是零除。
cards.episode: 10 contrarian leadership truths every leader needs to hear | Matt MacInnis (Rippling)

alts.quote: It's about saying, okay, if we have these themes of stuff that we want to work on, what do we know with confidence because the data tells us and what do we need to understand because we don't have the data?
alts.zh: 重點是要問：在我們想做的這些主題裡，哪些是數據講得夠清楚、我們有把握的？哪些是因為沒數據，所以還得先搞懂的？

alts.quote: It's very hard to think strategically about the situation you're in because there isn't a science of strategy. It's not like physics. It's not like engineering where we can write down the equations of stress on a beam.
alts.zh: 要對你所處的情況做策略思考很難，因為策略沒有一門科學。它不像物理。也不像工程——工程可以直接寫下樑的應力方程式。

alts.quote: It's not that I worked at groups that were particularly bad, Booking, Google Ads, other companies published numbers that are around 80 to 90% failure rate of ideas.
alts.zh: 不是說我待的團隊特別爛——Booking、Google Ads 這些公司公開的數字，點子的失敗率也都在八到九成左右。

cards.pattern: This sounds very [負面標籤], I don't mean it to sound this way, but there were lines that we didn't want to cross.
cards.quote: In some ways, this sounds very puritanical, I don't mean it to sound this way, but there were lines that we didn't want to cross that just felt ethically not us, that I've seen other news players do more of.
cards.zh: 某種程度上這聽起來很清教徒，我不是要講成那樣，但確實有些線我們不想跨過去，那些做法感覺就不像我們——而我看到別的新聞產品做得更多。
cards.why: 先替自己的立場貼上最刺耳的標籤（puritanical），再否認語氣、但保留立場；最後那句對同業的暗批因為前面鋪好了，反而站得住。
cards.pmNote: 談產品倫理紅線時先自嘲道德潔癖，能讓標準聽起來像選擇而不是說教。
cards.episode: Anthropic’s CPO on what comes next | Mike Krieger (co-founder of Instagram)

alts.quote: I agree, look, having your soul at every little checkbox sounds like a high bar and in some ways it is.
alts.zh: 我同意，聽著，要求每一個小勾選框都灌注靈魂，聽起來標準很高，某種程度上也確實是。

alts.quote: I mean, I don't want to act like I think this is easy, to be clear.
alts.zh: 我不想表現得好像我覺得這很簡單，先講清楚。

alts.quote: If you don't say yes, what you're essentially saying is, I am so presumptuous that I understand what's on the other side of that door already.
alts.zh: 你如果不答應，你其實等於在說：我狂妄到已經知道那扇門後面是什麼了。

cards.pattern: This sounds like a commodity feature, and on the surface level it is.
cards.quote: This sounds like a commodity feature and on all surface level it is.
cards.zh: 這聽起來像個誰都有的功能，表面上看也確實是。
cards.why: 完全承認對方的第一印象（而且承認到底），才有資格接著講「但底下不一樣」。半推半就的承認會讓聽者停在懷疑。
cards.pmNote: 講差異化之前先大方承認表層同質，聽者才會願意聽細節。
cards.episode: Superhuman's secret to success: Ignoring most customer feedback, manually onboarding every new user, obsessing over every detail, and positioning around a single attribute: speed | Rahul Vohra (CEO)

alts.quote: You can imagine an engineer hearing me talk about how to run a meeting and all the canonical docs and just be like, "What? This sounds terrible."
alts.zh: 你可以想像一個工程師聽我在講怎麼開會、講那堆權威文件，心裡大概是：「蛤？這聽起來超糟。」

alts.quote: I know this sounds silly, but branded AirPods level of fancy swag.
alts.zh: 我知道這聽起來很蠢，但就是印上品牌的 AirPods 那種等級的高級贈品。

alts.quote: Here's what I have a problem with. First of all, having a growth mindset is a very, very helpful thing.
alts.zh: 我要說的是我對它的哪一點有意見。首先，擁有成長心態本身是非常非常有幫助的事。

cards.pattern: It worked out great, and there's survivorship bias—that doesn't mean that everyone should [照做].
cards.quote: Obviously in this case, it worked out great and there's survivorship bias and that doesn't mean that everyone should pivot all the time.
cards.zh: 當然這個案例後來結果很好，但這裡有倖存者偏誤，不代表每個人都該一直轉型。
cards.why: 講完自己的成功故事後主動貼上倖存者偏誤標籤，等於替聽眾做了風險提示；不做這件事，你的故事就會被當成通則。
cards.pmNote: 分享成功案例務必附上「這不是通則」，否則會誤導別人複製情境依賴的做法。
cards.episode: Slack founder: Mental models for building products people love ft. Stewart Butterfield

alts.quote: Yeah, I mean, I can't promise that works for everyone, but again, in the very bespoke situation with Rujul, it worked really well.
alts.zh: 我不能保證這對每個人都有效，但在 Rujul 那個很特定的情況下，效果非常好。

alts.quote: The basic principle with laser is that willpower is never going to win, and there's great research on this, but for now just trust me, you're not going to white-knuckle your way through not looking at Twitter when you're trying to work.
alts.zh: laser 的基本原理是：意志力永遠贏不了。這方面有很多很好的研究，但現在你先信我——你不可能靠硬撐來讓自己工作時不看 Twitter。

alts.quote: So when it's a ratio and you decrease the denominator, the value of the ratio grows. And so, how do you decrease the denominator in this case where time is the denominator is you start working on things that take less time.
alts.zh: 這是一個比值，分母變小，比值就變大。那在這裡分母是時間，你要怎麼讓分母變小？你就開始挑那些花比較少時間的事情做。

cards.pattern: [要講的事], and this sounds cruel, but I promise it wasn't.
cards.quote: My dad, again, to go back to my dad when I would write, and this sounds cruel, but I promise it wasn't.
cards.zh: 我爸——又要講回我爸——以前我在寫東西的時候，這聽起來很殘忍，但我保證不是那樣。
cards.why: 先預告聽者接下來會冒出的道德反應（很殘忍），再用 I promise 把解讀權要回來。講家庭或人事的敏感故事前少了這一句，聽眾會在中途下車。
cards.episode: Mastering product strategy and growing as a PM | Maggie Crowley (Toast, Drift, Tripadvisor)

alts.quote: And I always write them back and say like, "Please tell me the better term and popularize it and I'll use it. It's a great idea."
alts.zh: 我都回信說：「請你告訴我更好的講法，然後把它推廣開，我就會改用。這主意很好。」

alts.quote: I'm not saying we should go back to the early 90's, but I'm saying it wasn't always like this.
alts.zh: 我不是說我們該回到九零年代初，我是說事情不是一直都長這樣。

alts.quote: And many of my design friends will push back on this and they'll say design should be its own thing and it should be an independent group and we should have three co-equal branches of government, and that's a solid argument as well
alts.zh: 我很多設計圈的朋友會反對，他們會說設計應該獨立成一個部門，跟產品、工程三權分立——那也是很有道理的論點。

cards.pattern: I know this sounds silly, but [聽起來不重要卻有效的做法].
cards.quote: I know this sounds silly, but branded AirPods level of fancy swag.
cards.zh: 我知道這聽起來很蠢，但就是印上品牌的 AirPods 那種等級的高級贈品。
cards.why: I know this sounds silly 把聽者的白眼先翻掉，接著才敢講一個看起來不專業但真的有效的做法。
cards.episode: Lessons from Airtable’s unconventional growth strategy | Zoelle Egner

alts.quote: This sounds like a commodity feature and on all surface level it is.
alts.zh: 這聽起來像個誰都有的功能，表面上看也確實是。

alts.quote: So the idea is, basically, you write up a two-page plan for the project. You invite three or four smart folks who don't know anything about the project and their job is just to tear apart your plan.
alts.zh: 做法是：你先寫一份兩頁的專案計畫，然後找三四個完全不懂這個專案的聰明人來，他們的任務就是把你的計畫拆爛。

alts.quote: And that is never, ever, ever the reason. How do I know? Because they already looked at your homepage, read all the stuff, saw what you promised, looked at the pricing page and decided to buy it.
alts.zh: 那絕對、絕對不會是真正的原因。我怎麼知道？因為他們早就看過你的首頁、讀完那些內容、看過你承諾了什麼、也看過定價頁，然後決定買了。

cards.pattern: I'm not sure that it matches exactly to [對方的框架], but I can tell you [你確實握有的資訊].
cards.quote: I'm not sure that it matches exactly to functions, but I can tell you what we're seeing more of, we need more of.
cards.zh: 我不確定這能不能剛好對到各個職能，但我可以告訴你我們看到什麼在變多、我們需要什麼變多。
cards.why: 型1（劃範圍後補料）的教科書句：前半句只否定「對到你的分類方式」這一件事，後半句用 but I can tell you 立刻換上自己真正握有的第一手資料。不確定被限縮成格式問題，內容的權威沒有一起賠掉。
cards.pmNote: 被要求套用別人的框架回答時，可以拒絕框架但保留資料——這比硬套框架講出爛答案有用。
cards.episode: Netflix CPTO on AI and the future of product and tech roles | Elizabeth Stone

alts.quote: And there were some studies around this too, I think that there's, I think in, I'm not sure exactly, I just have to go check up on this.
alts.zh: 我不太確定，這個我得回去查一下。

alts.quote: I'm obviously limited on what exactly I can share, but it is true that our retention numbers are really exciting and that is actually the thing we look at.
alts.zh: 我能講的東西確實有限，不過可以說的是，我們的留存數字真的很好看，而且那正是我們在看的指標。

alts.quote: I can't speak to that whole period. But what I can tell you about what I'm feeling now is just an incredible sense of focus and urgency to deliver great products quickly.
alts.zh: 那一整段期間我沒辦法評論。但我可以告訴你現在的感受——一種非常強烈的專注感和急迫感，就是要快點把好產品交出去。

cards.pattern: I don't know what [別家公司] is doing, obviously, but I would be willing to bet money that they're doing [你的推斷].
cards.quote: Now, I don't know what Claude Code is doing, obviously, but I would be willing to bet money that they're doing something in the form of evals.
cards.zh: 我當然不知道 Claude Code 內部到底在幹嘛，但我敢拿錢賭他們一定有在做某種形式的 evals。
cards.why: 型1。obviously 這個字先承認「我當然沒有內線」，把不知道講成理所當然而不是失職；接著 bet money 把推測的力度直接拉滿。承認無知反而讓後面的斷言更可信。
cards.pmNote: 談競品時最專業的講法：明說自己沒有內部資訊，再給一個你願意押注的推論。
cards.episode: Why AI evals are the hottest new skill for product builders | Hamel Husain & Shreya Shankar (creators of the #1 eval course)

alts.quote: I don't know how to do it off the top of my head, but I can go and look at the code or I can have Claude look at the code and combine that with other things to solve new problems.
alts.zh: 我沒辦法直接憑印象講出來，但我可以去看程式碼，或叫 Claude 去看，再結合其他東西來解新問題。

alts.quote: And I don't know how much this matters in the future now, but there's this just elegance to functional programming and thinking in types, and this is just the way that I code, and the way that I can't stop thinking about coding.
alts.zh: 我不知道這件事在未來還有多重要，但函數式程式設計跟用型別思考就是有一種優雅，這就是我寫程式的方式，我沒辦法不這樣想。

alts.quote: We're going to go off and make this two-year, five-year, whatever, 10-year vision even, and we're going to point us towards something." But the way that the technology is changing now, we don't know what's going to happen in two years.
alts.zh: 我們本來會去做那種兩年、五年甚至十年的願景，把大家指向某個方向，但以現在技術變化的速度，我們根本不知道兩年後會發生什麼事。

cards.pattern: I don't know enough about it, but it wouldn't surprise me if [你的猜測].
cards.quote: I don't know enough about it, I don't know what it is, but it wouldn't surprise me if they harnessed inflections in some way that was disorienting to the incumbent.
cards.zh: 這件事我了解得不夠、我也不知道它到底是什麼，但如果他們用某種方式抓住了轉折點、把在位者打亂了，我不會意外。
cards.why: 型1。it wouldn't surprise me if 是英文裡強度最低的斷言之一——你等於說「這符合我的世界觀」而不是「我知道這是真的」。台灣人常在這種場合直接沉默，白白丟掉一次表達判斷的機會。
cards.pmNote: 對不熟的案例仍可貢獻判斷，只要把斷言強度降到「不會意外」這一級。
cards.episode: Pattern Breakers: How to find a breakthrough startup idea | Mike Maples, Jr. (Founding Partner at Floodgate, ex-Product at Silicon Graphics)

alts.quote: I don't think we should filter out AI content. I think we should let you know if content is AI content or not. That's hard, by the way.
alts.zh: 我不認為我們該把 AI 內容濾掉。我認為該做的是讓你知道這則內容是不是 AI 產的。順帶一提，這很難。

alts.quote: I don't know if I want to highlight any specific categories, but I can talk about some of the things that we've funded in the past that has real legs.
alts.zh: 我不確定我想特別點名哪些類別，但我可以聊聊我們過去投過、確實有搞頭的一些東西。

alts.quote: And then the other behavior, and I don't know if you've ever seen this in a doc, but in one way writeups that you see a lot is there'll be just a mega comment thread on the title of the doc.
alts.zh: 還有另一種行為——我不知道你有沒有在文件裡看過——就是在一頁式的書面報告上，常常會看到標題底下掛著一大串留言。

cards.quote: I don't know if I have the recipe for this, but I can just maybe share a few of the things that come to mind.
cards.zh: 我不確定我有沒有一套配方，但我可以分享幾個當下想到的東西。
cards.why: 型1。先否認自己有「系統化答案」（the recipe），再降級交付「幾個想到的點」。這招讓你不必先想出完整架構才敢開口，卻仍然有東西交出去。
cards.pmNote: 被問「你們的做法是什麼」而你其實沒有 SOP 時，用這句把答案降級成經驗分享，不要硬掰一套流程。
cards.episode: Building Substack | Sachin Monga (Substack, Facebook)

alts.quote: So I think it has to come with a place of knowing that you don't know everything and humility to say, "Hey, I need help." And it actually earns you a lot more credit than you think.
alts.zh: 我覺得這要來自一個認知：你不可能什麼都懂，還要有那個謙虛去說「嘿，我需要幫忙」。而且這其實比你想像的更會替你加分。

alts.quote: I don't know if I want to highlight any specific categories, but I can talk about some of the things that we've funded in the past that has real legs.
alts.zh: 我不確定我想特別點名哪些類別，但我可以聊聊我們過去投過、確實有搞頭的一些東西。

alts.quote: I haven't seen their CAD, so I don't know what it's like inside their device, but they do have a lot of things going on.
alts.zh: 我沒看過他們的 CAD 圖，所以我不知道他們裝置裡面長怎樣，但他們確實塞了很多東西進去。

cards.pattern: I don't know if I want to [對方要求的動作], but I can talk about [你願意給的].
cards.quote: I don't know if I want to highlight any specific categories, but I can talk about some of the things that we've funded in the past that has real legs.
cards.zh: 我不確定我想特別點名哪些類別，但我可以聊聊我們過去投過、確實有搞頭的一些東西。
cards.why: 型1，而且是把「不願意」包裝成「不確定」的版本：I don't know if I want to 其實是委婉的拒絕，後半句馬上提出替代方案，讓對方不會覺得被打槍。
cards.pmNote: 不想回答敏感問題（點名、數字、名單）時，用 I don't know if I want to… but I can… 換一個你願意講的角度。
cards.episode: Gustaf Alstromer

alts.quote: I don't know that I'm perfect at it, but I've learned to balance those things quite a bit more than I did in the past when I would just purely read from my questions and my rubric and not care about anything else.
alts.zh: 我不敢說我做得多完美，但我已經學會比以前平衡得多了——以前我只會照著自己的問題清單和評分表念，其他一概不管。

alts.quote: I don't know how many customer support folks we have, but it's not very many, 30, 40, I'm not sure, way smaller than you would have at any comparable company, and it's because we've automated a lot of our flows.
alts.zh: 我不知道我們有多少客服人力，但沒有很多，三十、四十吧，我不確定，總之比任何同等規模的公司都少很多，因為我們把很多流程自動化了。

alts.quote: I mean, I think Things probably, I'm just guessing, I don't know any of the numbers or whatever, but I would assume it makes between five and $25 million of revenue, which to a VC is not even worth considering a VC.
alts.zh: 我是說，Things 這款——我純粹在猜，數字我完全不知道——但我猜它一年營收大概在五百萬到兩千五百萬美金之間，這種規模對創投來說根本不值得看。

cards.pattern: I haven't seen [證據], so I don't know [結論], but [你從外部觀察到的].
cards.quote: I haven't seen their CAD, so I don't know what it's like inside their device, but they do have a lot of things going on.
cards.zh: 我沒看過他們的 CAD 圖，所以我不知道他們裝置裡面長怎樣，但他們確實塞了很多東西進去。
cards.why: 型1，而且先交代「為什麼不知道」（沒看過 CAD）。標明資訊來源的缺口，比只說「我不知道」專業得多——聽的人知道要補什麼才能讓你有答案。
cards.pmNote: 講不知道時附上原因（沒拿到資料／沒看過原始檔），對方就知道該給你什麼。
cards.episode: Why we’re at the beginning of the AI hardware boom | Caitlin Kalinowski (ex–OpenAI, Meta, Apple)

alts.quote: I don't know if you've ever seen just the UI of these things, but they're crazy complicated, and that's just for building a static website.
alts.zh: 我不知道你有沒有看過這些東西的介面，但它們複雜到誇張，而且這還只是為了做一個靜態網站。

alts.quote: And then the other behavior, and I don't know if you've ever seen this in a doc, but in one way writeups that you see a lot is there'll be just a mega comment thread on the title of the doc.
alts.zh: 還有另一種行為——我不知道你有沒有在文件裡看過——就是在一頁式的書面報告上，常常會看到標題底下掛著一大串留言。

alts.quote: I don't know how many customer support folks we have, but it's not very many, 30, 40, I'm not sure, way smaller than you would have at any comparable company, and it's because we've automated a lot of our flows.
alts.zh: 我不知道我們有多少客服人力，但沒有很多，三十、四十吧，我不確定，總之比任何同等規模的公司都少很多，因為我們把很多流程自動化了。

cards.pattern: I don't know that it's a perfect answer, but I think the reality is [你的答案].
cards.quote: I mean, look, I don't know that it's a perfect answer, but I think the reality is just that what kills most projects most early companies is stamina.
cards.zh: 我是說，我不確定這是不是完美的答案，但我覺得現實就是：殺死大多數專案、大多數早期公司的，是續航力。
cards.why: 型1。先貶低答案的完整度（not a perfect answer），再用 the reality is 把力道加回來。前後一降一升，聽起來是謙虛而不是沒把握。
cards.pmNote: 給一個你知道不完整但方向正確的答案時，先講不完美、再講你真的相信的那句。
cards.episode: The happiness and pain of product management | Noam Lovinsky (Grammarly, Facebook, YouTube, Thumbtack)

alts.quote: I mean, I think Things probably, I'm just guessing, I don't know any of the numbers or whatever, but I would assume it makes between five and $25 million of revenue, which to a VC is not even worth considering a VC.
alts.zh: 我是說，Things 這款——我純粹在猜，數字我完全不知道——但我猜它一年營收大概在五百萬到兩千五百萬美金之間，這種規模對創投來說根本不值得看。

alts.quote: It's very early, we don't know who's going to win.
alts.zh: 現在還很早期，我們不知道誰會贏。

alts.quote: And I don't know how to vet companies, I don't know how to really logically think through what space is going to take off or something like that, but I just do feel like I have a sense on people.
alts.zh: 我不知道怎麼審公司、也不知道怎麼有邏輯地判斷哪個領域會起飛，但我就是覺得我對人有直覺。

cards.pattern: I don't know, but I do think that [你的判斷].
cards.quote: I don't know, but I do think that trying to make big changes too quickly is a primary reason.
cards.zh: 我不知道，但我確實認為，想太快做太大的改變是主要原因之一。
cards.why: 型1最精簡的骨架：I don't know, but I do think。do 這個強調助動詞是關鍵——它讓後半句不只是意見，而是「這件事我是有想法的」。台灣人多半只講前半句就停住了。
cards.pmNote: 會議裡被問到沒把握的題目，最低成本的回答格式就是這一句。
cards.episode: Jason Fried challenges your thinking on fundraising, goals, growth, and more

alts.quote: And I don't know exactly when that will be, but I think we're pretty close.
alts.zh: 我不知道確切會是什麼時候，但我覺得已經很接近了。

alts.quote: I don't think we should filter out AI content. I think we should let you know if content is AI content or not. That's hard, by the way.
alts.zh: 我不認為我們該把 AI 內容濾掉。我認為該做的是讓你知道這則內容是不是 AI 產的。順帶一提，這很難。

alts.quote: So I think it has to come with a place of knowing that you don't know everything and humility to say, "Hey, I need help." And it actually earns you a lot more credit than you think.
alts.zh: 我覺得這要來自一個認知：你不可能什麼都懂，還要有那個謙虛去說「嘿，我需要幫忙」。而且這其實比你想像的更會替你加分。

cards.pattern: I don't know that I'm perfect at it, but I've learned to [你的進步].
cards.quote: I don't know that I'm perfect at it, but I've learned to balance those things quite a bit more than I did in the past when I would just purely read from my questions and my rubric and not care about anything else.
cards.zh: 我不敢說我做得多完美，但我已經學會比以前平衡得多了——以前我只會照著自己的問題清單和評分表念，其他一概不管。
cards.why: 型1的自評版：不確定的是「有多好」，確定的是「比以前好」。用相對進步取代絕對水準，是英文裡談自己能力最安全也最可信的方式。
cards.pmNote: 績效面談或自我介紹時，講「比過去進步了什麼」比講「我很擅長什麼」更難被質疑。
cards.episode: How to find hidden growth opportunities in your product | Albert Cheng (Duolingo, Grammarly, Chess.com)

alts.quote: So those will be custom for anything. And I hate to use the word, it depends because I think whenever consultants say it depends, they're just throwing their hands up and saying, "I don't really know."
alts.zh: 這些每家都不一樣。我很不想講「看情況」，因為顧問一講「看情況」，通常就是兩手一攤說「我其實不知道」。

alts.quote: I don't know if I want to highlight any specific categories, but I can talk about some of the things that we've funded in the past that has real legs.
alts.zh: 我不確定我想特別點名哪些類別，但我可以聊聊我們過去投過、確實有搞頭的一些東西。

alts.quote: However, I've read a few articles that have said that Google no longer does prioritize press releases in SEO, so I don't know how much that holds up.
alts.zh: 不過我讀過幾篇文章說 Google 現在 SEO 已經不會優先給新聞稿了，所以我不知道這個說法現在還成不成立。

cards.pattern: I don't know what their latest numbers are, but just in terms of [可觀察的量級], I would place [X] among [排序].
cards.quote: I don't know what their latest numbers are, but just in terms of the numbers of people and the number of activity, I would place our scale among the largest US companies.
cards.zh: 我不知道他們最新的數字是多少，但光看使用人數和活躍量，我會把我們的規模排進美國最大的那幾家公司裡。
cards.why: 型1。不知道的是精確數字，但他照樣敢下排序判斷——用 just in terms of 把比較基準講清楚，讓聽者知道這個判斷成立在什麼條件上。
cards.pmNote: 沒有精確數據時仍可比較量級；重點是明講你用什麼維度比。
cards.episode: Taxi mafias, cash vaults, and 100% MoM growth: The story behind Southeast Asia’s biggest startup | Kevin Aluwi (Gojek)

alts.quote: And I don't know how to vet companies, I don't know how to really logically think through what space is going to take off or something like that, but I just do feel like I have a sense on people.
alts.zh: 我不知道怎麼審公司、也不知道怎麼有邏輯地判斷哪個領域會起飛，但我就是覺得我對人有直覺。

alts.quote: I mean, I think Things probably, I'm just guessing, I don't know any of the numbers or whatever, but I would assume it makes between five and $25 million of revenue, which to a VC is not even worth considering a VC.
alts.zh: 我是說，Things 這款——我純粹在猜，數字我完全不知道——但我猜它一年營收大概在五百萬到兩千五百萬美金之間，這種規模對創投來說根本不值得看。

alts.quote: People always ask me, "How much time should I be spending on an assumption testing?" I don't know how to answer that question because for me, assumption testing and delivery are the same work.
alts.zh: 大家常問我：「假設驗證應該花多少時間？」我不知道怎麼回答這個問題，因為對我來說，假設驗證跟交付本來就是同一件工作。

cards.pattern: I don't know how many [X] we have, but it's not very many — [區間], I'm not sure — [比較基準], and it's because [原因].
cards.quote: I don't know how many customer support folks we have, but it's not very many, 30, 40, I'm not sure, way smaller than you would have at any comparable company, and it's because we've automated a lot of our flows.
cards.zh: 我不知道我們有多少客服人力，但沒有很多，三十、四十吧，我不確定，總之比任何同等規模的公司都少很多，因為我們把很多流程自動化了。
cards.why: 型1的高階版：不確定→給區間→再標一次不確定→給比較→給原因。他把「不知道確切數字」處理成兩秒的小事，重點全放在「為什麼這麼少」。
cards.pmNote: 數字不確定時給區間並附上比較對象，資訊價值幾乎等同精確值。
cards.episode: OpenAI’s CPO on how AI changes must-have skills, moats, coding, startup playbooks, more | Kevin Weil (CPO at OpenAI, ex-Instagram, Twitter)

alts.quote: I mean, I think Things probably, I'm just guessing, I don't know any of the numbers or whatever, but I would assume it makes between five and $25 million of revenue, which to a VC is not even worth considering a VC.
alts.zh: 我是說，Things 這款——我純粹在猜，數字我完全不知道——但我猜它一年營收大概在五百萬到兩千五百萬美金之間，這種規模對創投來說根本不值得看。

alts.quote: I don't know if I want to highlight any specific categories, but I can talk about some of the things that we've funded in the past that has real legs.
alts.zh: 我不確定我想特別點名哪些類別，但我可以聊聊我們過去投過、確實有搞頭的一些東西。

alts.quote: I haven't seen their CAD, so I don't know what it's like inside their device, but they do have a lot of things going on.
alts.zh: 我沒看過他們的 CAD 圖，所以我不知道他們裝置裡面長怎樣，但他們確實塞了很多東西進去。

cards.pattern: I don't know what percentile we're in, but it's got to be [方向性的判斷], based on [依據].
cards.quote: I don't know what percentile we're in, but it's got to be a very high percentile of per capita experiments run for a company, based on company size.
cards.zh: 我不知道我們落在第幾個百分位，但以公司規模來算，我們的人均實驗數一定落在非常高的百分位。
cards.why: 型1。it's got to be 是「憑推理必然如此」的語氣，比 I think 強、比 I know 弱，剛好放在「沒查過但很有把握」的位置。
cards.pmNote: 沒有 benchmark 資料時，用「以我們的規模來推」給一個方向性判斷，並講出推的依據。
cards.episode: Behind the product: Duolingo streaks | Jackson Shuttleworth (Group PM, Retention Team)

alts.quote: I don't know how many customer support folks we have, but it's not very many, 30, 40, I'm not sure, way smaller than you would have at any comparable company, and it's because we've automated a lot of our flows.
alts.zh: 我不知道我們有多少客服人力，但沒有很多，三十、四十吧，我不確定，總之比任何同等規模的公司都少很多，因為我們把很多流程自動化了。

alts.quote: We don't know if we're going to actually end up going, and based on the results whether we're going to actually move forward with investing in that area, but that's a body of work we can commit to.
alts.zh: 我們不知道最後會不會真的往那邊走、也要看結果才知道要不要真的投資那個領域，但那是一塊我們可以承諾投入的工作量。

alts.quote: I haven't seen their CAD, so I don't know what it's like inside their device, but they do have a lot of things going on.
alts.zh: 我沒看過他們的 CAD 圖，所以我不知道他們裝置裡面長怎樣，但他們確實塞了很多東西進去。

cards.pattern: I don't know exactly when [X] will be, but we're still in [目前階段], and it should be [粗略時程].
cards.quote: I don't know exactly when the Kindle release will be, but we're still in copy edits, but it should be done pretty soon.
cards.zh: 我不知道 Kindle 版確切什麼時候出，但我們還在潤稿階段，應該蠻快就好了。
cards.why: 型2（把不知道縮到一個點）：不知道的只有「確切日期」，其餘全部給滿——目前階段＋粗略時程。這是被追問時程時最好用的回答結構，既不承諾也不裝死。
cards.pmNote: 被追 deadline 而你真的不知道時，回「確切日期不知道＋目前卡在哪一關＋粗估」，比回「還在做」有用一百倍。
cards.episode: The things engineers are desperate for PMs to understand | Camille Fournier (author of “The Manager’s Path,” ex-CTO at Rent the Runway)

alts.quote: And I don't know exactly when that will be, but I think we're pretty close.
alts.zh: 我不知道確切會是什麼時候，但我覺得已經很接近了。

alts.quote: I don't know what percentile we're in, but it's got to be a very high percentile of per capita experiments run for a company, based on company size.
alts.zh: 我不知道我們落在第幾個百分位，但以公司規模來算，我們的人均實驗數一定落在非常高的百分位。

alts.quote: I don't know exactly which occasion this person is referring to, but I know I've used that analogy a few times.
alts.zh: 我不確定這位聽眾指的是哪一次，但我知道我用過那個比喻好幾次。

cards.quote: And I don't know exactly when that will be, but I think we're pretty close.
cards.zh: 我不知道確切會是什麼時候，但我覺得已經很接近了。
cards.why: 型2的最小單位：exactly 這一個字就把不確定從「會不會發生」縮到「什麼時候」。少了 exactly，整句就變成「這件事會不會成我不知道」，意思差很多。
cards.pmNote: exactly 是把不確定範圍縮小的關鍵字，寫進你的預設用語。
cards.episode: M&A, competition, pricing, and investing | Julia Schottenstein (dbt Labs)

alts.quote: I don't know exactly when the Kindle release will be, but we're still in copy edits, but it should be done pretty soon.
alts.zh: 我不知道 Kindle 版確切什麼時候出，但我們還在潤稿階段，應該蠻快就好了。

alts.quote: I'll let you know when we figure it out. We're hiring. I think there's so many interesting product problems here.
alts.zh: 等我們想通了再告訴你。我們還在徵人，這裡真的有一堆很有意思的產品問題。

alts.quote: I don't know, but I do think that trying to make big changes too quickly is a primary reason.
alts.zh: 我不知道，但我確實認為，想太快做太大的改變是主要原因之一。

cards.pattern: I don't know exactly which [細節] this person is referring to, but I know I've [你確實做過的事].
cards.quote: I don't know exactly which occasion this person is referring to, but I know I've used that analogy a few times.
cards.zh: 我不確定這位聽眾指的是哪一次，但我知道我用過那個比喻好幾次。
cards.why: 型2。被引用自己說過的話而想不起來出處時的標準處理：不確定的是「哪一次」，確定的是「我確實這樣講過」。承認記憶缺口但不否認立場。
cards.pmNote: 別人引用你講過的話而你沒印象時，先承認立場、再說想不起場合，不要整段否認。
cards.episode: Gustav Söderström

alts.quote: However, I've read a few articles that have said that Google no longer does prioritize press releases in SEO, so I don't know how much that holds up.
alts.zh: 不過我讀過幾篇文章說 Google 現在 SEO 已經不會優先給新聞稿了，所以我不知道這個說法現在還成不成立。

alts.quote: I don't know that I'm perfect at it, but I've learned to balance those things quite a bit more than I did in the past when I would just purely read from my questions and my rubric and not care about anything else.
alts.zh: 我不敢說我做得多完美，但我已經學會比以前平衡得多了——以前我只會照著自己的問題清單和評分表念，其他一概不管。

alts.quote: I don't know exactly when the Kindle release will be, but we're still in copy edits, but it should be done pretty soon.
alts.zh: 我不知道 Kindle 版確切什麼時候出，但我們還在潤稿階段，應該蠻快就好了。

cards.pattern: I don't know when [X] is going to happen and nobody else knows either, but when that happens, [必然的後果].
cards.quote: And I don't know when it's going to saturate and nobody else knows either, but when that happens, the next frontier is the physical world.
cards.zh: 我不知道它什麼時候會飽和，別人也都不知道，但等它飽和的那天，下一個戰場就是實體世界。
cards.why: 型2疊型5：先把不知道縮到「時間點」，再用 nobody else knows either 把這個未知變成產業共同的未知——於是不知道就不再是她的短處。然後把確定的部分（飽和之後會怎樣）講足。
cards.pmNote: 預測產業轉折時，把「時間點不可知」和「方向可知」拆開講，是最誠實也最有說服力的說法。
cards.episode: Why we’re at the beginning of the AI hardware boom | Caitlin Kalinowski (ex–OpenAI, Meta, Apple)

alts.quote: And so again, it's just like, I don't know, my view is I need to put a big discount on my forecasting ability on this one.
alts.zh: 所以這一題，我的看法是：我得把自己的預測能力先打一個大折扣。

alts.quote: I don't know how many customer support folks we have, but it's not very many, 30, 40, I'm not sure, way smaller than you would have at any comparable company, and it's because we've automated a lot of our flows.
alts.zh: 我不知道我們有多少客服人力，但沒有很多，三十、四十吧，我不確定，總之比任何同等規模的公司都少很多，因為我們把很多流程自動化了。

alts.quote: We don't know if we're going to actually end up going, and based on the results whether we're going to actually move forward with investing in that area, but that's a body of work we can commit to.
alts.zh: 我們不知道最後會不會真的往那邊走、也要看結果才知道要不要真的投資那個領域，但那是一塊我們可以承諾投入的工作量。

cards.pattern: I've read [來源] that said [說法], so I don't know how much that holds up.
cards.quote: However, I've read a few articles that have said that Google no longer does prioritize press releases in SEO, so I don't know how much that holds up.
cards.zh: 不過我讀過幾篇文章說 Google 現在 SEO 已經不會優先給新聞稿了，所以我不知道這個說法現在還成不成立。
cards.why: 型2。不確定的是「這個說法還剩多少效力」（how much that holds up），不是「有沒有這回事」。用程度而不是有無來下修，資訊仍然交得出去。
cards.pmNote: 轉述你沒親自驗證的行業說法時，用 how much that holds up 標記可信度，而不是整段不講。
cards.episode: The ultimate guide to PR | Emilie Gerber (founder of Six Eastern)

alts.quote: I don't know that I'm perfect at it, but I've learned to balance those things quite a bit more than I did in the past when I would just purely read from my questions and my rubric and not care about anything else.
alts.zh: 我不敢說我做得多完美，但我已經學會比以前平衡得多了——以前我只會照著自己的問題清單和評分表念，其他一概不管。

alts.quote: I don't know exactly which occasion this person is referring to, but I know I've used that analogy a few times.
alts.zh: 我不確定這位聽眾指的是哪一次，但我知道我用過那個比喻好幾次。

alts.quote: I don't know if I have the recipe for this, but I can just maybe share a few of the things that come to mind.
alts.zh: 我不確定我有沒有一套配方，但我可以分享幾個當下想到的東西。

cards.pattern: I don't know how much this matters going forward, but [你仍然相信的事].
cards.quote: And I don't know how much this matters in the future now, but there's this just elegance to functional programming and thinking in types, and this is just the way that I code, and the way that I can't stop thinking about coding.
cards.zh: 我不知道這件事在未來還有多重要，但函數式程式設計跟用型別思考就是有一種優雅，這就是我寫程式的方式，我沒辦法不這樣想。
cards.why: 型2的自貶版：把不確定放在「這件事還重不重要」，而不是「我懂不懂」。專業被時代質疑時，這個切法讓你既承認環境變了、又不否定自己的專業。
cards.pmNote: 技術典範轉移時談自己的老專長，質疑「重要性」比質疑「正確性」得體。
cards.episode: Boris Cherny

alts.quote: We're going to go off and make this two-year, five-year, whatever, 10-year vision even, and we're going to point us towards something." But the way that the technology is changing now, we don't know what's going to happen in two years.
alts.zh: 我們本來會去做那種兩年、五年甚至十年的願景，把大家指向某個方向，但以現在技術變化的速度，我們根本不知道兩年後會發生什麼事。

alts.quote: Now, I don't know what Claude Code is doing, obviously, but I would be willing to bet money that they're doing something in the form of evals.
alts.zh: 我當然不知道 Claude Code 內部到底在幹嘛，但我敢拿錢賭他們一定有在做某種形式的 evals。

alts.quote: If something is just purely code planning, there's not a great reason why we would be the best at that. I can't come up with a coherent argument for that.
alts.zh: 如果只是純粹的程式規劃，我想不出我們憑什麼會是最強的。這個我實在提不出一個站得住腳的論證。

cards.pattern: I don't know how much of that has to do with [某個變因] specifically though.
cards.quote: I don't know how much of that has to do with Facebook specifically though.
cards.zh: 不過我不知道這裡面有多少是 Facebook 本身造成的。
cards.why: 型2的歸因版：現象是真的、結論不否定，只把不確定放在「歸因比例」。這是英文會議裡最有殺傷力的溫和質疑之一，因為它逼對方去拆變因。
cards.pmNote: 看到成長數字被歸功給某個動作時，先問「有多少比例真的來自它」，而不是質疑數字本身。
cards.episode: Building Substack | Sachin Monga (Substack, Facebook)

alts.quote: I don't know, but I do think that trying to make big changes too quickly is a primary reason.
alts.zh: 我不知道，但我確實認為，想太快做太大的改變是主要原因之一。

alts.quote: And I don't know exactly when that will be, but I think we're pretty close.
alts.zh: 我不知道確切會是什麼時候，但我覺得已經很接近了。

alts.quote: So I don't know how much it costs, but it's definitely worth it.
alts.zh: 我不知道它多少錢，但絕對值得。

cards.quote: So I don't know how much it costs, but it's definitely worth it.
cards.zh: 我不知道它多少錢，但絕對值得。
cards.why: 型2最短的骨架：價格不知道、價值很確定。definitely 用來補償前半句的空白，讓整句聽起來是推薦而不是敷衍。
cards.pmNote: 推薦工具時價格記不得沒關係，關鍵是把價值判斷講得斬釘截鐵。
cards.episode: The non-technical PM’s guide to building with Cursor | Zevi Arnovitz (Meta)

alts.quote: It's very early, we don't know who's going to win.
alts.zh: 現在還很早期，我們不知道誰會贏。

alts.quote: I haven't seen their CAD, so I don't know what it's like inside their device, but they do have a lot of things going on.
alts.zh: 我沒看過他們的 CAD 圖，所以我不知道他們裝置裡面長怎樣，但他們確實塞了很多東西進去。

alts.quote: I mean, look, I don't know that it's a perfect answer, but I think the reality is just that what kills most projects most early companies is stamina.
alts.zh: 我是說，我不確定這是不是完美的答案，但我覺得現實就是：殺死大多數專案、大多數早期公司的，是續航力。

cards.pattern: We didn't [做某事] until — I don't know exactly — something like [粗估].
cards.quote: We didn't start really charging for subscriptions or having ads until, I don't know exactly, but something like year three.
cards.zh: 我們大概到第三年左右才真的開始收訂閱費、放廣告——我不記得確切時間了。
cards.why: 型2的插入版：I don't know exactly 直接塞在句子中間當括號用，不打斷敘事節奏；something like 再把數字轉成估值。台灣人常因為記不得確切年份就整句不敢講。
cards.pmNote: 講公司歷史時，用「大概第幾年」搭配一句 I don't know exactly，比停下來查資料更順。
cards.episode: Scaling Duolingo, embracing failure, and insight into Latin America’s tech scene | Gina Gotthilf (Latitud, Duolingo)

alts.quote: We're going to go off and make this two-year, five-year, whatever, 10-year vision even, and we're going to point us towards something." But the way that the technology is changing now, we don't know what's going to happen in two years.
alts.zh: 我們本來會去做那種兩年、五年甚至十年的願景，把大家指向某個方向，但以現在技術變化的速度，我們根本不知道兩年後會發生什麼事。

alts.quote: Now, I don't know what Claude Code is doing, obviously, but I would be willing to bet money that they're doing something in the form of evals.
alts.zh: 我當然不知道 Claude Code 內部到底在幹嘛，但我敢拿錢賭他們一定有在做某種形式的 evals。

alts.quote: I don't know exactly when the Kindle release will be, but we're still in copy edits, but it should be done pretty soon.
alts.zh: 我不知道 Kindle 版確切什麼時候出，但我們還在潤稿階段，應該蠻快就好了。

cards.pattern: I don't know how many people still [做某事], but it's [量級判斷] at this point.
cards.quote: I don't know how many people still sell perpetually licensed on premises software, but it's de minimis at this point.
cards.zh: 我不知道現在還有多少人在賣買斷式的地端授權軟體，但這個數字現在已經小到可以忽略了。
cards.why: 型2。數量不知道，但量級（小到可忽略）很確定。這種「不知道確數但知道數量級」的講法，在英文商業對話裡比報一個假數字更被信任。
cards.pmNote: 論證趨勢時，量級判斷（可忽略／絕大多數）比精確數字更耐得住追問。
cards.episode: He saved OpenAI, invented the “Like” button, and built Google Maps: Bret Taylor on the future of careers, coding, agents, and more

alts.quote: So, I don't know if supersystem is still the right exact analogy, but I think people just think of it as their AI.
alts.zh: 我不確定「超級系統」現在還是不是最精確的類比，但我覺得大家就是把它當成自己的 AI。

alts.quote: I don't know how many customer support folks we have, but it's not very many, 30, 40, I'm not sure, way smaller than you would have at any comparable company, and it's because we've automated a lot of our flows.
alts.zh: 我不知道我們有多少客服人力，但沒有很多，三十、四十吧，我不確定，總之比任何同等規模的公司都少很多，因為我們把很多流程自動化了。

alts.quote: I haven't seen their CAD, so I don't know what it's like inside their device, but they do have a lot of things going on.
alts.zh: 我沒看過他們的 CAD 圖，所以我不知道他們裝置裡面長怎樣，但他們確實塞了很多東西進去。

cards.pattern: I don't know if [術語] is still the right exact analogy, but I think people just think of it as [白話的說法].
cards.quote: So, I don't know if supersystem is still the right exact analogy, but I think people just think of it as their AI.
cards.zh: 我不確定「超級系統」現在還是不是最精確的類比，但我覺得大家就是把它當成自己的 AI。
cards.why: 型2的用詞版：不確定的是自己選的那個詞，不是背後的概念。把爭議壓在術語層，概念層就能繼續推進，不會整段被卡住。
cards.pmNote: 自創術語被挑戰時，先讓出術語、守住概念——多數爭執其實只是命名之爭。
cards.episode: Inside ChatGPT: The fastest-growing product in history | Nick Turley (Head of ChatGPT at OpenAI)

alts.quote: I don't know how many people still sell perpetually licensed on premises software, but it's de minimis at this point.
alts.zh: 我不知道現在還有多少人在賣買斷式的地端授權軟體，但這個數字現在已經小到可以忽略了。

alts.quote: I don't think we should filter out AI content. I think we should let you know if content is AI content or not. That's hard, by the way.
alts.zh: 我不認為我們該把 AI 內容濾掉。我認為該做的是讓你知道這則內容是不是 AI 產的。順帶一提，這很難。

alts.quote: So I think it has to come with a place of knowing that you don't know everything and humility to say, "Hey, I need help." And it actually earns you a lot more credit than you think.
alts.zh: 我覺得這要來自一個認知：你不可能什麼都懂，還要有那個謙虛去說「嘿，我需要幫忙」。而且這其實比你想像的更會替你加分。

cards.quote: I don't know what the right metaphor is here.
cards.zh: 我不知道這裡該用什麼比喻才對。
cards.why: 型2的極簡樣本：連比喻想不到都可以直接講出來，然後繼續說下去。英文會議允許你在句中承認「我還沒找到好說法」，這不算失分，反而讓聽者幫你補。
cards.pmNote: 想不到好比喻就直說，通常會有人幫你接上——這是把卡住轉成互動的便宜招。
cards.episode: How to unlock your product leadership skills | Ken Norton, Ex-Google

alts.quote: So, I don't know if supersystem is still the right exact analogy, but I think people just think of it as their AI.
alts.zh: 我不確定「超級系統」現在還是不是最精確的類比，但我覺得大家就是把它當成自己的 AI。

alts.quote: You should have 30 seconds for your play. Right? Don't ask me, I'm not a lawyer.
alts.zh: 應該有個三十秒的合理使用吧？別問我，我又不是律師。

alts.quote: I don't know if I have the recipe for this, but I can just maybe share a few of the things that come to mind.
alts.zh: 我不確定我有沒有一套配方，但我可以分享幾個當下想到的東西。

cards.quote: But I don't know that that's a total prerequisite.
cards.zh: 但我不覺得那是絕對的先決條件。
cards.why: 型3（用不確定包裝反對）。關鍵在 I don't know THAT（不是 if）——這個 that 在英文裡幾乎等於「我不同意」，只是語氣軟到不會啟動對方的防衛。台灣人幾乎只會用 if，於是永遠講不出這一層。
cards.pmNote: 別人把某個條件說成必要條件時，用 I don't know that it's a prerequisite 拆掉「必要」二字，而不是正面否認。
cards.episode: The things engineers are desperate for PMs to understand | Camille Fournier (author of “The Manager’s Path,” ex-CTO at Rent the Runway)

alts.quote: I think that as a smaller company, I don't know that that's the case.
alts.zh: 我覺得如果是規模比較小的公司，我不確定情況會是這樣。

alts.quote: I don't know that that's how it's going to play out.
alts.zh: 我不確定事情會這樣發展。

alts.quote: And I know this is going to trigger some people, but the truth is they don't want to work.
alts.zh: 我知道這句會讓一些人不爽，但事實就是——他們不想做事。

cards.pattern: I think that as [不同的情境], I don't know that that's the case.
cards.quote: I think that as a smaller company, I don't know that that's the case.
cards.zh: 我覺得如果是規模比較小的公司，我不確定情況會是這樣。
cards.why: 型3的加條件版：不直接說對方錯，而是先架出一個對方沒考慮到的情境（as a smaller company），再說在那個情境下不成立。反對被縮小成「適用範圍」問題。
cards.pmNote: 反對通則最有效的方式，是舉出一個它明顯不適用的情境，而不是宣稱它錯。
cards.episode: Anthropic’s $1B to $19B growth run: how Claude became the fastest-growing AI product in history | Amol Avasare

alts.quote: But I don't know that that's a total prerequisite.
alts.zh: 但我不覺得那是絕對的先決條件。

alts.quote: So, I think one needs to be a little bit cautious on what Dario says. And that's setting aside the cynical view that he's just doing that department stock, which I don't believe at all.
alts.zh: 我覺得對 Dario 講的話要保留一點。而且我這裡還先撇開那種比較酸的解讀——說他只是在替自家股價講話——那我完全不相信。

alts.quote: The stability is important, don't get me wrong, but I do think that as a faster growing company, we need to consistently to reiterate not only the product but also our teams.
alts.zh: 穩定當然重要，別誤會，但我確實認為以一家成長更快的公司來說，我們要不斷迭代的不只是產品，還有團隊。

cards.pattern: If you're building [另一種產品], I don't know that I would operate this way.
cards.quote: I think if you're building a product where it's not necessarily an AI- first product and you have some AI features that are on the side, but it's not the core of your value, I don't know that I would operate this way.
cards.zh: 如果你做的不是 AI 優先的產品，只是旁邊掛幾個 AI 功能、AI 不是核心價值，那我不確定我會這樣做。
cards.why: 型3。整段先把適用條件講得非常清楚，最後才用 I don't know that I would 收尾。這句實際上是「別照抄我剛講的做法」，但聽起來只是個人選擇。
cards.pmNote: 給建議時主動標出「這招在什麼情況下我不會用」，比事後被人踩雷有價值得多。
cards.episode: Anthropic’s $1B to $19B growth run: how Claude became the fastest-growing AI product in history | Amol Avasare

alts.quote: This is a tricky one. So, you're right that it's implied, but the thing is, in real life, if you make a commitment and you get alignment that we are going to spend six weeks of engineering time building this thing…
alts.zh: 這題很麻煩。你說得沒錯，那個確實是言下之意，但問題是，現實裡如果你已經做出承諾、也拿到共識要花六週工程時間……

alts.quote: Oh, I think this is my hot take. You hear people talking about craft and taste and product management, and it's all very wonderful. And I'm totally on board.
alts.zh: 喔，這大概是我的爭議發言了。大家都在談 craft、談品味、談產品管理，聽起來都很美好，我也完全買單——

alts.quote: Yeah, I don't think of them as an or. I think they have to be intersected because basically the way I think about it is you actually start with a problem.
alts.zh: 我不覺得這是二選一。我覺得這兩件事必須交集在一起，因為在我看來，你本來就是從一個問題開始。

cards.quote: I don't know that that's how it's going to play out.
cards.zh: 我不確定事情會這樣發展。
cards.why: 型3的預測版：對方講完一個推演，你用一句話表示不買單，但不必提出替代版本。這在英文會議裡是完全可接受的異議——反對不需要附帶解方。
cards.pmNote: 不同意某個預測但還沒想好替代版本時，先把不同意講出來，別等想好才說。
cards.episode: I’ve run 75+ businesses. Here’s why you’re probably chasing the wrong idea. | Andrew Wilkinson (co‑founder of Tiny)

alts.quote: And I know this is going to trigger some people, but the truth is they don't want to work.
alts.zh: 我知道這句會讓一些人不爽，但事實就是——他們不想做事。

alts.quote: But I don't know that that's a total prerequisite.
alts.zh: 但我不覺得那是絕對的先決條件。

alts.quote: I think that as a smaller company, I don't know that that's the case.
alts.zh: 我覺得如果是規模比較小的公司，我不確定情況會是這樣。

cards.pattern: I'm not sure that [某個做法] is one that works for every [對象].
cards.quote: I'm not sure that this pattern is one that works for every product.
cards.zh: 我不確定這個模式適用於每一種產品。
cards.why: 型3的普適性挑戰：不否定這個做法本身，只否定「每一個」。攻擊量詞是英文裡成本最低的反對法——對方通常會自己退讓到「當然不是每個」。
cards.pmNote: 別人講 best practice 時，質疑「是不是每個情況都適用」比質疑「這是不是好做法」容易被接受。
cards.episode: Mastering onboarding | Lauryn Isford (Head of Growth at Airtable)

alts.quote: And don't get me wrong, I think there's a lot of product folks out there who enjoy that modality of work, I'm not one of them.
alts.zh: 別誤會，我知道有很多產品人是真的喜歡那種工作方式的——我不是。

alts.quote: I'm not sure AR is going to be the right reference.
alts.zh: 我不確定 AR 會是對的參照對象。

alts.quote: I'm not sure if it's productive to continue to discussing right now.
alts.zh: 我不確定現在繼續討論這個有沒有生產力。

cards.pattern: I'm not sure [對方用的類比] is going to be the right reference.
cards.quote: I'm not sure AR is going to be the right reference.
cards.zh: 我不確定 AR 會是對的參照對象。
cards.why: 型3。整段爭論常常卡在雙方用了不同的類比，這句話直接把異議提到類比層——不吵結論，先吵你拿什麼來比。
cards.pmNote: 討論鬼打牆時，先檢查雙方的參照案例是不是同一個，往往比繼續辯結論快。
cards.episode: Geoffrey Moore on finding your beachhead, crossing the chasm, and dominating a market

alts.quote: I'm not sure if it's productive to continue to discussing right now.
alts.zh: 我不確定現在繼續討論這個有沒有生產力。

alts.quote: So I'm going to disagree with Sedaris a little bit.
alts.zh: 這點我要跟 Sedaris 有一點不一樣的看法。

alts.quote: You're focused on recent and I'm just going to push back. No, there's nothing terribly recent.
alts.zh: 你一直扣在「最近」這個點上，我要反過來擋一下——沒有，最近沒什麼特別的。

cards.pattern: …, which I'm not sure I would recommend, but [仍然介紹那個做法].
cards.quote: And the way Reid records, which I'm not sure I would recommend this, but he does it a little bit differently than you do.
cards.zh: Reid 錄音的方式——我不確定我會推薦這樣做——跟你的做法有點不一樣。
cards.why: 型3的插入版：把「我不推薦」壓縮成一個 which 子句塞進句中，既表態又不打斷敘事。中文很難這樣做，英文靠關係子句就辦到了。
cards.pmNote: 分享別人的做法但你不認同時，用一個插入子句標記立場，不必另起一段批評。
cards.episode: The rituals of great teams | Shishir Mehrotra of Coda, YouTube, Microsoft

alts.quote: So, I think one needs to be a little bit cautious on what Dario says. And that's setting aside the cynical view that he's just doing that department stock, which I don't believe at all.
alts.zh: 我覺得對 Dario 講的話要保留一點。而且我這裡還先撇開那種比較酸的解讀——說他只是在替自家股價講話——那我完全不相信。

alts.quote: I would soften it a little bit... I wouldn't say I'm not a fan of creating category.
alts.zh: 我會講得軟一點——我不會說我不喜歡做品類（category）這件事。

alts.quote: This is maybe going to come across a little bit flippant, but they can't stop you from sending an email technically. So I'm just going to send the email.
alts.zh: 這樣講可能有點輕佻，但嚴格來說他們也不能阻止我寄信。所以我就照寄。

cards.pattern: I'm not sure we're solving the right problem, but boy, we [做得很好的那件事].
cards.quote: I'm not sure we're solving the right problem, but boy, we run a great meeting." And it's not meant to diminish any of that.
cards.zh: 「我不確定我們解的是不是對的問題，但天啊，我們的會開得可真好。」而且這不是要否定那些努力。
cards.why: 型3裡殺傷力最強的一種：不否定執行品質，只把問題提到「我們解的是不是對的題」。用讚美當包裝紙的異議，讓被批評的人沒有防守點。
cards.pmNote: 團隊執行力很好卻沒成果時，這句是把討論拉回策略層的標準開場。
cards.episode: The rituals of great teams | Shishir Mehrotra of Coda, YouTube, Microsoft

alts.quote: I'm not sure if it's productive to continue to discussing right now.
alts.zh: 我不確定現在繼續討論這個有沒有生產力。

alts.quote: By the way, I'm being very mean to Figma so far in this conversation. There is a time when it's the right time for the Figma file.
alts.zh: 順帶一提，我到目前為止對 Figma 有點太兇了。Figma 檔是有它對的時機的。

alts.quote: Oh, I think this is my hot take. You hear people talking about craft and taste and product management, and it's all very wonderful. And I'm totally on board.
alts.zh: 喔，這大概是我的爭議發言了。大家都在談 craft、談品味、談產品管理，聽起來都很美好，我也完全買單——

cards.pattern: [列出你的成就], and as I look back at that, I'm not sure that's a good thing.
cards.quote: So much so that the company was number one on Glassdoor's best place to work, I was the number one CEO on Glassdoor, and as I look back at that, I'm not sure that's a good thing.
cards.zh: 誇張到公司在 Glassdoor 拿最佳職場第一名、我自己是第一名的 CEO，可是現在回頭看，我不確定那是件好事。
cards.why: 型3轉向自己：先把成就講足，再用 I'm not sure that's a good thing 整個翻過來。這種自我異議比批評別人更有說服力，也是英文簡報裡很常見的轉折裝置。
cards.pmNote: 要挑戰一個大家都認同的指標（員工滿意度、NPS），從自己曾經拿高分講起最有效。
cards.episode: Sequoia CEO coach: Why it’s never been easier to start a company, and never been harder to scale one | Brian Halligan (co-founder, HubSpot)

alts.quote: Now see, that's incorrect. That's only true if you only look at the proximate thing, which is project ended.
alts.zh: 你看，這就不對了。那句話只有在你只看最表面那層——也就是「專案結束了」——的時候才成立。

alts.quote: I don't know that I would look back at what I shipped back then or what we shipped back then, and say they were the best possible solutions or best possible product.
alts.zh: 我不確定我會回頭看當年出的東西，然後說那是最好的解法、最好的產品。

alts.quote: Thank you for advising me on the pros and cons. You work for me, you're my lawyer. I'd like to implement this thing.
alts.zh: 謝謝你把利弊分析給我。你是替我工作的、你是我的律師。我決定要做這件事。

cards.pattern: I don't know if I would say that you shouldn't [對方的結論].
cards.quote: So I don't know if I would say that you shouldn't go get a computer science degree.
cards.zh: 所以我不確定我會說你不應該去念資工學位。
cards.why: 型3的雙重否定：I don't know if I would say that you shouldn't。三層減震（不確定＋我會不會說＋不應該）把一個逆風的立場講得毫無攻擊性。文法看起來繞，但在英文會議裡完全自然。
cards.pmNote: 要反對一個正在流行的極端結論（別念書了、別做 X 了）時，用雙重否定把自己的位置放在中間。
cards.episode: Building a magical AI code editor used by over 1 million developers in four months: The untold story of Windsurf | Varun Mohan (co-founder and CEO)

alts.quote: I will say that when you say things are going well, I think we don't know the counterfactual.
alts.zh: 我要說一句：當你說事情進展順利的時候，我覺得我們並不知道反事實會是什麼。

alts.quote: I don't know that I would look back at what I shipped back then or what we shipped back then, and say they were the best possible solutions or best possible product.
alts.zh: 我不確定我會回頭看當年出的東西，然後說那是最好的解法、最好的產品。

alts.quote: I think if you're building a product where it's not necessarily an AI- first product and you have some AI features that are on the side, but it's not the core of your value, I don't know that I would operate this way.
alts.zh: 如果你做的不是 AI 優先的產品，只是旁邊掛幾個 AI 功能、AI 不是核心價值，那我不確定我會這樣做。

cards.pattern: I don't know if I would even use the dichotomy of [A] or [B].
cards.quote: And I don't know if I would even use the dichotomy of product-led growth, or sales-led growth, with Retool.
cards.zh: 我甚至不確定我會用「產品驅動成長 vs. 業務驅動成長」這種二分法來看 Retool。
cards.why: 型3裡層級最高的一種：不回答問題，而是質疑問題預設的二分法。even 是關鍵字，它標示「我要退一步講更基本的事」。
cards.pmNote: 被逼在兩個選項間表態時，先檢查這個二分法本身成不成立——多數策略爭論的病根在這裡。
cards.episode: How to foster innovation and big thinking | Eeke de Milliano (Retool, Stripe)

alts.quote: I think if you're building a product where it's not necessarily an AI- first product and you have some AI features that are on the side, but it's not the core of your value, I don't know that I would operate this way.
alts.zh: 如果你做的不是 AI 優先的產品，只是旁邊掛幾個 AI 功能、AI 不是核心價值，那我不確定我會這樣做。

alts.quote: I don't know that I would look back at what I shipped back then or what we shipped back then, and say they were the best possible solutions or best possible product.
alts.zh: 我不確定我會回頭看當年出的東西，然後說那是最好的解法、最好的產品。

alts.quote: The stability is important, don't get me wrong, but I do think that as a faster growing company, we need to consistently to reiterate not only the product but also our teams.
alts.zh: 穩定當然重要，別誤會，但我確實認為以一家成長更快的公司來說，我們要不斷迭代的不只是產品，還有團隊。

cards.pattern: I'm not sure if it's productive to continue discussing [X] right now.
cards.quote: I'm not sure if it's productive to continue to discussing right now.
cards.zh: 我不確定現在繼續討論這個有沒有生產力。
cards.why: 型3的喊停版：把「這個會該結束了」講成自己的不確定。指出流程有問題卻不指責任何人，是主持會議時最好用的一句。
cards.pmNote: 會議鬼打牆時用這句喊停，比說「我們沒時間了」更容易被接受，因為它談的是產值不是時間。
cards.episode: Scripts for difficult conversations: Giving hard feedback, navigating defensiveness, the three questions you should end every meeting with, more | Alisa Cohn (executive coach)

alts.quote: I'm not sure AR is going to be the right reference.
alts.zh: 我不確定 AR 會是對的參照對象。

alts.quote: I'm not sure we're solving the right problem, but boy, we run a great meeting." And it's not meant to diminish any of that.
alts.zh: 「我不確定我們解的是不是對的問題，但天啊，我們的會開得可真好。」而且這不是要否定那些努力。

alts.quote: By the way, I'm being very mean to Figma so far in this conversation. There is a time when it's the right time for the Figma file.
alts.zh: 順帶一提，我到目前為止對 Figma 有點太兇了。Figma 檔是有它對的時機的。

cards.pattern: I don't know that I would look back at [自己過去的東西] and say they were [高評價].
cards.quote: I don't know that I would look back at what I shipped back then or what we shipped back then, and say they were the best possible solutions or best possible product.
cards.zh: 我不確定我會回頭看當年出的東西，然後說那是最好的解法、最好的產品。
cards.why: 型3對準自己：用不確定的語氣否定自己過去的作品。這比直接說「那時候做得很爛」得體，也留了餘地——你否定的是「最好」這個評價，不是整段經歷。
cards.pmNote: 談自己的過往作品時，否定「最好」比否定「有價值」安全，也更誠實。
cards.episode: Relentless curiosity, radical accountability, and HubSpot’s winning growth formula | Christopher Miller (VP of Product, Growth and AI)

alts.quote: I think if you're building a product where it's not necessarily an AI- first product and you have some AI features that are on the side, but it's not the core of your value, I don't know that I would operate this way.
alts.zh: 如果你做的不是 AI 優先的產品，只是旁邊掛幾個 AI 功能、AI 不是核心價值，那我不確定我會這樣做。

alts.quote: So much so that the company was number one on Glassdoor's best place to work, I was the number one CEO on Glassdoor, and as I look back at that, I'm not sure that's a good thing.
alts.zh: 誇張到公司在 Glassdoor 拿最佳職場第一名、我自己是第一名的 CEO，可是現在回頭看，我不確定那是件好事。

alts.quote: So I don't know if I would say that you shouldn't go get a computer science degree.
alts.zh: 所以我不確定我會說你不應該去念資工學位。

cards.quote: I will say that when you say things are going well, I think we don't know the counterfactual.
cards.zh: 我要說一句：當你說事情進展順利的時候，我覺得我們並不知道反事實會是什麼。
cards.why: 型3＋型5的混血：用 we 而不是 you 提出異議（我們不知道，不是你不知道），把質疑轉成雙方共同的知識缺口。這是實驗文化裡最經典的一句反問。
cards.pmNote: 有人宣稱某個動作帶來成長時，先問「沒做這個動作的世界長什麼樣」——沒有對照組就沒有因果。
cards.episode: The ultimate guide to A/B testing | Ronny Kohavi (Airbnb, Microsoft, Amazon)

alts.quote: I think if you're building a product where it's not necessarily an AI- first product and you have some AI features that are on the side, but it's not the core of your value, I don't know that I would operate this way.
alts.zh: 如果你做的不是 AI 優先的產品，只是旁邊掛幾個 AI 功能、AI 不是核心價值，那我不確定我會這樣做。

alts.quote: So I don't know if I would say that you shouldn't go get a computer science degree.
alts.zh: 所以我不確定我會說你不應該去念資工學位。

alts.quote: So this might mean that I think... I don't want to say that if you don't have experience, don't start one, but it's kind of true. So become an expert somewhere, somehow, before you start.
alts.zh: 我不想說「沒經驗就別開始」這種話……但其實有點是真的。所以動手前，先想辦法在某個地方變成專家。

cards.pattern: I'm not an expert on [領域], so I'm not going to be able to comment to quite the degree that [別人] have.
cards.quote: I'm not an expert on MMM, so I'm not going to be able to comment to quite the degree that they have.
cards.zh: MMM 我不是專家，所以我沒辦法講到他們那個深度。
cards.why: 型4（先卸壓再遞資訊）：開口前先把對方的期待值調低，並且明講低到哪裡（不會像那些人那麼深）。這樣接下來講的任何東西都是加分，不會被拿去跟專家比。
cards.pmNote: 被問到跨領域問題時，先劃出自己能講到哪一層，再開始講。
cards.episode: The ultimate guide to Martech | Austin Hay (Reforge, Ramp, Runway)

alts.quote: Those are just numbers I'm putting out there. It's always going to be a gut call based on where you are.
alts.zh: 那些數字只是我隨口丟出來的。這終究是看你所在的位置做的直覺判斷。

alts.quote: Look, I won't claim to be an expert on this at all, but I think that with every technology that's come out, we've been able to harness it and it takes a lot of harnessing.
alts.zh: 我先講，我完全不敢說自己是這方面的專家，但我覺得每一種新技術出來，我們最後都有辦法駕馭它，只是那個駕馭要花很多力氣。

alts.quote: So I'm giving some heuristics, I'm giving some benchmarks, but your mileage is going to vary.
alts.zh: 我給的是一些經驗法則、一些對照基準，但你們的狀況一定會不一樣。

cards.pattern: I'm not an expert on this, but I think that [你的看法].
cards.quote: And I'm not an expert on this, but I think that AI has to do with why.
cards.zh: 我不是這方面的專家，但我覺得原因跟 AI 有關。
cards.why: 型4最基本的骨架。重點是 but 之後她照樣把觀點講完——I'm not an expert 在英文裡是進場門票，不是退場理由。台灣人常把它當成閉嘴的藉口。
cards.pmNote: 不是專家不等於不能表態；把它當成免責聲明，不是禁言令。
cards.episode: Why we’re at the beginning of the AI hardware boom | Caitlin Kalinowski (ex–OpenAI, Meta, Apple)

alts.quote: And there were some studies around this too, I think that there's, I think in, I'm not sure exactly, I just have to go check up on this.
alts.zh: 我不太確定，這個我得回去查一下。

alts.quote: Definitely don't bring me on here as a pricing expert, I think you have got better people for that.
alts.zh: 千萬別把我當定價專家找來，這題你應該去找更懂的人。

alts.quote: I'm not an expert on MMM, so I'm not going to be able to comment to quite the degree that they have.
alts.zh: MMM 我不是專家，所以我沒辦法講到他們那個深度。

cards.pattern: I'll be very honest, I'm not an expert in [領域], but I've thought a lot about it.
cards.quote: And I'll be very honest, I'm not an expert in education, but I just thought a lot about it.
cards.zh: 老實說，教育我不是專家，但我想過很多。
cards.why: 型4的補救版：卸壓之後立刻補上一個替代資格——不是專家，但花過很多時間想。這比單純的 I'm not an expert 站得住腳，因為你交出了另一種正當性。
cards.pmNote: 沒有頭銜時用「投入的時間與思考」當替代資格，這在英文語境是被接受的。
cards.episode: From ChatGPT to Instagram to Uber: The quiet architect behind the world’s most popular products | Peter Deng

alts.quote: I'll admit I'm definitely not an SEO expert. I've been fortunate to work with some of the best marketers in the world who I think are bonafide legends at this point
alts.zh: 我坦白說我絕對不是 SEO 專家。我只是很幸運跟一些世界頂尖的行銷人共事過，那些人到今天都算是真正的傳奇。

alts.quote: I'm not an expert on MMM, so I'm not going to be able to comment to quite the degree that they have.
alts.zh: MMM 我不是專家，所以我沒辦法講到他們那個深度。

alts.quote: There are plenty of agencies that go into the 50s and 60s a month, but that's just a whole nother world, and I'm not an expert on that part.
alts.zh: 也有很多代理商月費開到五、六萬美金，但那完全是另一個世界了，那一塊我不是專家。

cards.pattern: I could be wrong, but it feels different than [對照物].
cards.quote: I could be wrong, but it feels different than crypto.
cards.zh: 我可能錯，但這感覺跟加密貨幣不一樣。
cards.why: 型4。I could be wrong 四個字換來的是「我可以講一個沒有證據的直覺」的許可。feels 也是刻意的——他明說這是感覺不是分析。
cards.pmNote: 要講一個還沒有數據支持的直覺時，先說 I could be wrong，然後把直覺講完整。
cards.episode: Business strategy with Hamilton Helmer (author of 7 Powers)

alts.quote: Okay, that's a difficult and different question.
alts.zh: 好，這是個困難、而且性質不太一樣的問題。

alts.quote: I could be wrong about the ChatGPT prediction and what's going to happen there.
alts.zh: 我對 ChatGPT 那個預測、還有後續會怎樣，可能都是錯的。

alts.quote: Now, what I come back to, and I could be wrong, but what I come back to is we're talking through a medium, a mediated experience.
alts.zh: 我一直會回到的一點——我也可能是錯的——就是：我們是透過一個媒介在對話，一種被中介過的經驗。

cards.pattern: I could be wrong about [你剛給的預測].
cards.quote: I could be wrong about the ChatGPT prediction and what's going to happen there.
cards.zh: 我對 ChatGPT 那個預測、還有後續會怎樣，可能都是錯的。
cards.why: 型4的事後版：預測講完之後回頭補一句可能會錯。位置很重要——放在後面代表你不是不敢講，而是講完了願意認帳。
cards.pmNote: 給完預測後主動加一句「我可能錯」，比一開始就先怯場更能建立信任。
cards.episode: Brian Balfour: 10 lessons on career, growth, and life

alts.quote: We're going to go off and make this two-year, five-year, whatever, 10-year vision even, and we're going to point us towards something." But the way that the technology is changing now, we don't know what's going to happen in two years.
alts.zh: 我們本來會去做那種兩年、五年甚至十年的願景，把大家指向某個方向，但以現在技術變化的速度，我們根本不知道兩年後會發生什麼事。

alts.quote: And if you push a really experienced product director like that, they're going to go, "Good point, I don't. I'm going to go find out."
alts.zh: 你這樣逼一個真正資深的產品總監，他會說：「說得對，我確實不知道。我去查清楚。」

alts.quote: I could be wrong, but it feels different than crypto.
alts.zh: 我可能錯，但這感覺跟加密貨幣不一樣。

cards.pattern: I don't have a good answer for that because [原因], but my stock answer is [還是給一個].
cards.quote: I don't have a good answer for that because I just spent a lot of time using our internal products, but my stock answer is Granola.
cards.zh: 這題我沒有好答案，因為我大部分時間都在用我們自己的內部產品，不過我的罐頭答案是 Granola。
cards.why: 型4。承認沒有好答案＋交代原因＋照樣給一個並自嘲那是罐頭答案。三段都在降低期待，但問題確實被回答了——這是「不知道」跟「不回答」的差別。
cards.pmNote: 被問到你沒有真正意見的問題時，給一個並誠實標記它是罐頭答案，不要假裝那是深思熟慮的結論。
cards.episode: The AI-native startup: 5 products, 7-figure revenue, 100% AI-written code | Dan Shipper (co-founder/CEO of Every)

alts.quote: People always ask me, "How much time should I be spending on an assumption testing?" I don't know how to answer that question because for me, assumption testing and delivery are the same work.
alts.zh: 大家常問我：「假設驗證應該花多少時間？」我不知道怎麼回答這個問題，因為對我來說，假設驗證跟交付本來就是同一件工作。

alts.quote: I don't know how many customer support folks we have, but it's not very many, 30, 40, I'm not sure, way smaller than you would have at any comparable company, and it's because we've automated a lot of our flows.
alts.zh: 我不知道我們有多少客服人力，但沒有很多，三十、四十吧，我不確定，總之比任何同等規模的公司都少很多，因為我們把很多流程自動化了。

alts.quote: So again, I don't mean to overstate this, and I certainly don't mean to claim that there's some answer that's right for everybody, of course, but surely this is the right kind of question.
alts.zh: 我不想把這件事講得太滿，也絕對不是說有一個答案適用所有人——但這絕對是該問的那類問題。

cards.pattern: I'm just guessing, I don't know any of the numbers, but I would assume it makes between [下限] and [上限].
cards.quote: I mean, I think Things probably, I'm just guessing, I don't know any of the numbers or whatever, but I would assume it makes between five and $25 million of revenue, which to a VC is not even worth considering a VC.
cards.zh: 我是說，Things 這款——我純粹在猜，數字我完全不知道——但我猜它一年營收大概在五百萬到兩千五百萬美金之間，這種規模對創投來說根本不值得看。
cards.why: 型4的極致：連續三個卸壓（純猜／不知道數字／whatever），然後給出一個五倍寬的區間。寬區間本身就是誠實的訊號，比報一個假精確的數字可信。
cards.pmNote: 沒有資料卻必須估算時，把區間開寬並明說是猜的——假精確才是真正的信任殺手。
cards.episode: I’ve run 75+ businesses. Here’s why you’re probably chasing the wrong idea. | Andrew Wilkinson (co‑founder of Tiny)

alts.quote: We're going to go off and make this two-year, five-year, whatever, 10-year vision even, and we're going to point us towards something." But the way that the technology is changing now, we don't know what's going to happen in two years.
alts.zh: 我們本來會去做那種兩年、五年甚至十年的願景，把大家指向某個方向，但以現在技術變化的速度，我們根本不知道兩年後會發生什麼事。

alts.quote: I don't know how many customer support folks we have, but it's not very many, 30, 40, I'm not sure, way smaller than you would have at any comparable company, and it's because we've automated a lot of our flows.
alts.zh: 我不知道我們有多少客服人力，但沒有很多，三十、四十吧，我不確定，總之比任何同等規模的公司都少很多，因為我們把很多流程自動化了。

alts.quote: But had I had the same conversation five or 10 years ago with the team at Convoy like I don't know anything about trucking, I probably wouldn't have understood why that business was going to work.
alts.zh: 但如果我在五年、十年前跟 Convoy 那個團隊講同樣的話——像是我對貨運一無所知——我大概不會理解那門生意為什麼會成。

cards.pattern: I could be wrong on these numbers, but I think [具體數字] in [年份].
cards.quote: I could be wrong on these numbers, but I think average time to complete the driver application process was 21 days in 2013.
cards.zh: 這些數字我可能記錯，但我印象中 2013 年司機申請流程平均要花 21 天完成。
cards.why: 型4的書面版：寫作時同樣需要卸壓句，而且它讓你敢把具體數字寫進去。多數人是因為不敢寫錯就把數字整個拿掉，結果文章失去說服力。
cards.pmNote: 寫報告引用記憶中的數字時，加一句 I could be wrong on these numbers 就能保留具體性。
cards.episode: Growth inflections

alts.quote: I don't know about you, but literally every time I think to do this, there's a fight in my head of like, "Ah, do I really need to work out today?
alts.zh: 我不知道你怎麼樣，但我每次想到要做這件事，腦子裡都會吵一架：欸，我今天真的需要運動嗎？

alts.quote: I mean, I think Things probably, I'm just guessing, I don't know any of the numbers or whatever, but I would assume it makes between five and $25 million of revenue, which to a VC is not even worth considering a VC.
alts.zh: 我是說，Things 這款——我純粹在猜，數字我完全不知道——但我猜它一年營收大概在五百萬到兩千五百萬美金之間，這種規模對創投來說根本不值得看。

alts.quote: I don't think we should filter out AI content. I think we should let you know if content is AI content or not. That's hard, by the way.
alts.zh: 我不認為我們該把 AI 內容濾掉。我認為該做的是讓你知道這則內容是不是 AI 產的。順帶一提，這很難。

cards.pattern: [給出你知道的範圍], but that's just a whole nother world, and I'm not an expert on that part.
cards.quote: There are plenty of agencies that go into the 50s and 60s a month, but that's just a whole nother world, and I'm not an expert on that part.
cards.zh: 也有很多代理商月費開到五、六萬美金，但那完全是另一個世界了，那一塊我不是專家。
cards.why: 型4的收尾版：把卸壓句放在資訊之後，用來標記「我的知識邊界到這裡」。這樣聽的人知道再往下問你也答不了，省掉一輪無效追問。
cards.pmNote: 回答問題時主動畫出知識邊界，能避免對方一路追問到你露餡。
cards.episode: The ultimate guide to PR | Emilie Gerber (founder of Six Eastern)

alts.quote: I'll admit I'm definitely not an SEO expert. I've been fortunate to work with some of the best marketers in the world who I think are bonafide legends at this point
alts.zh: 我坦白說我絕對不是 SEO 專家。我只是很幸運跟一些世界頂尖的行銷人共事過，那些人到今天都算是真正的傳奇。

alts.quote: Look, I won't claim to be an expert on this at all, but I think that with every technology that's come out, we've been able to harness it and it takes a lot of harnessing.
alts.zh: 我先講，我完全不敢說自己是這方面的專家，但我覺得每一種新技術出來，我們最後都有辦法駕馭它，只是那個駕馭要花很多力氣。

alts.quote: I can't speak to that whole period. But what I can tell you about what I'm feeling now is just an incredible sense of focus and urgency to deliver great products quickly.
alts.zh: 那一整段期間我沒辦法評論。但我可以告訴你現在的感受——一種非常強烈的專注感和急迫感，就是要快點把好產品交出去。

cards.pattern: My guess is anybody who [處在同樣位置] is going to [你的推斷].
cards.quote: My guess is anybody who is sitting in their shoes owning their platform is going to follow the exact same playbook and the exact same reasoning.
cards.zh: 我猜任何人坐在他們的位置、擁有那個平台，都會照著一模一樣的劇本、一模一樣的邏輯走。
cards.why: 型4的關鍵發現：My guess is 是英文商業對話裡「不知道」的生產版本——它把承認無知的那半秒直接換成一個可以被討論的具體主張。這個池子裡出現二十幾次，幾乎都是這個用法。
cards.pmNote: 與其說「我不知道對方會怎麼做」，不如說 My guess is + 具體推論，讓團隊有東西可以反駁。
cards.episode: Brian Balfour: 10 lessons on career, growth, and life

alts.quote: And I'm not going to try to define agent exactly, but at least the stack that we think of it as having is you have this model, really smart reasoning model.
alts.zh: 我不打算給 agent 一個精準的定義，但至少我們認為它的堆疊長這樣：底下有一個很會推理的模型。

alts.quote: But had I had the same conversation five or 10 years ago with the team at Convoy like I don't know anything about trucking, I probably wouldn't have understood why that business was going to work.
alts.zh: 但如果我在五年、十年前跟 Convoy 那個團隊講同樣的話——像是我對貨運一無所知——我大概不會理解那門生意為什麼會成。
