alts.quote: My purely anecdotal guess is maybe 10 to 15% are good product companies, something like that.
alts.zh: 我純粹憑印象猜，大概一成到一成五算是好的產品公司吧，差不多這個量級。

cards.pattern: My guess is what you want to be doing is [推測對方的目標].
cards.quote: My guess is what you want to be doing is learning and creating and not spending a lot of time managing.
cards.zh: 我猜你真正想做的是學習跟創造，而不是花一堆時間在管理上。
cards.why: 型4的讀心版：用 My guess is 去猜對方的動機。因為標明是猜測，對方糾正你不會傷感情，猜對了則直接跳過三輪來回。
cards.pmNote: 猜測對方的意圖時一定要標記成猜測，否則會變成替人下定義。
cards.episode: LinkedIn’s product evolution and the art of building complex systems | Hari Srinivasan (LinkedIn)

alts.quote: I do want to apply a pretty severe caveat here though, which is, a decision log is not a replacement for building products. It's a additional complimentary thing that you can be doing on your own.
alts.zh: 不過我要加一個很重的但書：決策日誌不能取代真的去做產品。它只是你自己可以額外做的補充。

alts.quote: I don't have a good answer for that because I just spent a lot of time using our internal products, but my stock answer is Granola.
alts.zh: 這題我沒有好答案，因為我大部分時間都在用我們自己的內部產品，不過我的罐頭答案是 Granola。

alts.quote: People always ask me, "How much time should I be spending on an assumption testing?" I don't know how to answer that question because for me, assumption testing and delivery are the same work.
alts.zh: 大家常問我：「假設驗證應該花多少時間？」我不知道怎麼回答這個問題，因為對我來說，假設驗證跟交付本來就是同一件工作。

cards.pattern: My guess is — because I'm not a [專業身分] — that [大膽的判斷].
cards.quote: My guess is because I'm not a psychologist, I'm not a therapist, that you are modeling something that's happened in your life.
cards.zh: 我猜——因為我不是心理學家、也不是治療師——你其實是在複製你人生中發生過的某個模式。
cards.why: 型4。卸壓句直接插在 My guess is 和判斷之間，讓一個相當大膽、相當私人的判斷得以出口。沒有這個插入語，這句話會變成越界。
cards.pmNote: 要講一個踩到對方私領域的判斷前，先聲明你不具備那個專業身分。
cards.episode: How a great founder becomes a great CEO | Jonathan Lowenhar (co-founder of Enjoy The Work)

alts.quote: In a research paper, we'd have a discussion section, and this is where you get to guess. I would surmise, and we do this in the report, that it's probably because retail went through the retail apocalypse, right.
alts.zh: 我沒辦法告訴你原因。在論文裡這叫討論章節，也就是可以猜的地方。我的推測是——報告裡也是這樣寫的——大概是因為零售業經歷了那場零售末日。

alts.quote: And I guess it's kind of an embarrassing thing to say because everyone who's a startup founder thinks, my startup moves super fast and the talent bar is super high.
alts.zh: 說這話其實有點難為情，因為每個新創創辦人都覺得「我們超快、人才標準超高」。

alts.quote: I don't know how many customer support folks we have, but it's not very many, 30, 40, I'm not sure, way smaller than you would have at any comparable company, and it's because we've automated a lot of our flows.
alts.zh: 我不知道我們有多少客服人力，但沒有很多，三十、四十吧，我不確定，總之比任何同等規模的公司都少很多，因為我們把很多流程自動化了。

cards.quote: And there were some studies around this too, I think that there's, I think in, I'm not sure exactly, I just have to go check up on this.
cards.zh: 我不太確定，這個我得回去查一下。
cards.why: 型4的承諾版：不確定＋承諾去查。這句話把當下的空白轉成一個之後會補上的動作，讓「不知道」有了時間表。
cards.pmNote: 不確定的事說「我回去查」並且真的回頭補，是遠端協作裡最快累積信用的行為。
cards.episode: From ChatGPT to Instagram to Uber: The quiet architect behind the world’s most popular products | Peter Deng

alts.quote: I'll admit I'm definitely not an SEO expert. I've been fortunate to work with some of the best marketers in the world who I think are bonafide legends at this point
alts.zh: 我坦白說我絕對不是 SEO 專家。我只是很幸運跟一些世界頂尖的行銷人共事過，那些人到今天都算是真正的傳奇。

alts.quote: I'm not sure that it matches exactly to functions, but I can tell you what we're seeing more of, we need more of.
alts.zh: 我不確定這能不能剛好對到各個職能，但我可以告訴你我們看到什麼在變多、我們需要什麼變多。

alts.quote: And again, I'm not an expert in this and I think Erin Meyer wrote that book, The Culture Map. So you should just find what those people wrote because they're much smarter than I am about this.
alts.zh: 再說一次，我不是這方面的專家。Erin Meyer 寫過《文化地圖》那本書，你們應該直接去看他們寫的，他們比我懂太多了。

cards.pattern: We have [已經有的東西], but we don't know how to [還缺的那一步].
cards.quote: We have this name, but we don't know how to tell the story around it.
cards.zh: 我們有了這個名字，但我們不知道要怎麼把它的故事講出來。
cards.why: 型5（把未知升格成團隊的題目）：主詞從 I 換成 we，未知就從個人的失職變成組織的待辦。這一個代名詞的切換，是這個池子裡最值得台灣人學的一招。
cards.pmNote: 把「我不知道怎麼做」改成「我們還不知道怎麼做」，同一件事就從績效問題變成專案問題。
cards.episode: The power of strategic narrative | Andy Raskin

alts.quote: So I worked on Atlas for a bit. I don't work on it now. But a bit of the narrative here for me just to tell my story a bit was...
alts.zh: 我做過 Atlas 一陣子，現在沒在做了。不過就我自己的角度、講一下我的版本的話……

alts.quote: I don't know if I have the recipe for this, but I can just maybe share a few of the things that come to mind.
alts.zh: 我不確定我有沒有一套配方，但我可以分享幾個當下想到的東西。

alts.quote: I don't know, but I do think that trying to make big changes too quickly is a primary reason.
alts.zh: 我不知道，但我確實認為，想太快做太大的改變是主要原因之一。

cards.pattern: We don't know if we're going to [最終決定], but that's a body of work we can commit to.
cards.quote: We don't know if we're going to actually end up going, and based on the results whether we're going to actually move forward with investing in that area, but that's a body of work we can commit to.
cards.zh: 我們不知道最後會不會真的往那邊走、也要看結果才知道要不要真的投資那個領域，但那是一塊我們可以承諾投入的工作量。
cards.why: 型5的承諾版：結果不確定，但「這段探索工作」是可以承諾的。這句話解決了 PM 最常見的困境——上面要承諾、你只有假設。承諾過程，不承諾結論。
cards.pmNote: 無法承諾成果時，改成承諾一段有邊界的探索工作，這在英文語境是完全合法的答覆。
cards.episode: Behind the scenes of Calendly’s rapid growth | Annie Pearl (CPO)

alts.quote: And then for Q2, we don't know how Q1 is going to go, so we're just going to leave the objective there, but we're not going to get into the nitty-gritty OKRs.
alts.zh: 至於第二季，我們不知道第一季會跑成怎樣，所以我們就把目標先掛在那，但不會去細拆 OKR。

alts.quote: We're going to go off and make this two-year, five-year, whatever, 10-year vision even, and we're going to point us towards something." But the way that the technology is changing now, we don't know what's going to happen in two years.
alts.zh: 我們本來會去做那種兩年、五年甚至十年的願景，把大家指向某個方向，但以現在技術變化的速度，我們根本不知道兩年後會發生什麼事。

alts.quote: We're in the worst of all worlds where we are imperfectly executing and therefore, at the end of the day, the project might fail, but we don't know why.
alts.zh: 我們處在最糟的狀態：執行得不夠扎實，所以專案最後可能會失敗，但我們連為什麼失敗都不會知道。

cards.pattern: We don't know what [X] is going to be yet.
cards.quote: But we don't know what those specifications are going to be yet.
cards.zh: 但我們還不知道那些規格會長什麼樣。
cards.why: 型5的關鍵字是 yet：一個字就把「不知道」從狀態改成階段。沒有 yet，這句是坦白失敗；有了 yet，這句是進度回報。
cards.pmNote: 所有的「我們還不知道」都要加 yet，否則聽起來像永遠不會知道。
cards.episode: Reflections on a movement | Eric Ries (creator of the Lean Startup methodology)

alts.quote: It's very early, we don't know who's going to win.
alts.zh: 現在還很早期，我們不知道誰會贏。

alts.quote: So those will be custom for anything. And I hate to use the word, it depends because I think whenever consultants say it depends, they're just throwing their hands up and saying, "I don't really know."
alts.zh: 這些每家都不一樣。我很不想講「看情況」，因為顧問一講「看情況」，通常就是兩手一攤說「我其實不知道」。

alts.quote: I haven't seen their CAD, so I don't know what it's like inside their device, but they do have a lot of things going on.
alts.zh: 我沒看過他們的 CAD 圖，所以我不知道他們裝置裡面長怎樣，但他們確實塞了很多東西進去。

cards.pattern: If we don't know [前提], we literally don't know [連帶的後果].
cards.quote: And if we don't know who our customer is, we literally don't know what the word quality means.
cards.zh: 如果我們不知道客戶是誰，我們就真的不知道「品質」這個詞是什麼意思。
cards.why: 型5的推論版：把一個未知拿來當前提，推出第二個更痛的未知。他不是在承認無知，是在用無知證明某件事必須先解決。
cards.pmNote: 要說服團隊先做用戶研究時，證明「不知道用戶是誰」會讓下游所有判斷失去意義，比講方法論有效。
cards.episode: Reflections on a movement | Eric Ries (creator of the Lean Startup methodology)

alts.quote: I don't know how many customer support folks we have, but it's not very many, 30, 40, I'm not sure, way smaller than you would have at any comparable company, and it's because we've automated a lot of our flows.
alts.zh: 我不知道我們有多少客服人力，但沒有很多，三十、四十吧，我不確定，總之比任何同等規模的公司都少很多，因為我們把很多流程自動化了。

alts.quote: So those will be custom for anything. And I hate to use the word, it depends because I think whenever consultants say it depends, they're just throwing their hands up and saying, "I don't really know."
alts.zh: 這些每家都不一樣。我很不想講「看情況」，因為顧問一講「看情況」，通常就是兩手一攤說「我其實不知道」。

alts.quote: I don't know about you, but literally every time I think to do this, there's a fight in my head of like, "Ah, do I really need to work out today?
alts.zh: 我不知道你怎麼樣，但我每次想到要做這件事，腦子裡都會吵一架：欸，我今天真的需要運動嗎？

cards.pattern: For [下一期], we don't know how [這一期] is going to go, so we're just going to leave [粗的部分] and not get into [細的部分].
cards.quote: And then for Q2, we don't know how Q1 is going to go, so we're just going to leave the objective there, but we're not going to get into the nitty-gritty OKRs.
cards.zh: 至於第二季，我們不知道第一季會跑成怎樣，所以我們就把目標先掛在那，但不會去細拆 OKR。
cards.why: 型5的規劃版：讓未知直接決定計畫的顆粒度——不知道的部分就寫粗一點。這是把「承認不確定」轉成具體工作方法，而不只是一句免責聲明。
cards.pmNote: 規劃遠期目標時，用不確定程度決定要拆多細，別把每一季都拆到同樣顆粒度。
cards.episode: The ultimate guide to OKRs | Christina Wodtke (Stanford)

alts.quote: We don't know if we're going to actually end up going, and based on the results whether we're going to actually move forward with investing in that area, but that's a body of work we can commit to.
alts.zh: 我們不知道最後會不會真的往那邊走、也要看結果才知道要不要真的投資那個領域，但那是一塊我們可以承諾投入的工作量。

alts.quote: We're going to go off and make this two-year, five-year, whatever, 10-year vision even, and we're going to point us towards something." But the way that the technology is changing now, we don't know what's going to happen in two years.
alts.zh: 我們本來會去做那種兩年、五年甚至十年的願景，把大家指向某個方向，但以現在技術變化的速度，我們根本不知道兩年後會發生什麼事。

alts.quote: And I don't know when it's going to saturate and nobody else knows either, but when that happens, the next frontier is the physical world.
alts.zh: 我不知道它什麼時候會飽和，別人也都不知道，但等它飽和的那天，下一個戰場就是實體世界。

cards.pattern: The way [環境] is changing now, we don't know what's going to happen in [時間範圍].
cards.quote: We're going to go off and make this two-year, five-year, whatever, 10-year vision even, and we're going to point us towards something." But the way that the technology is changing now, we don't know what's going to happen in two years.
cards.zh: 我們本來會去做那種兩年、五年甚至十年的願景，把大家指向某個方向，但以現在技術變化的速度，我們根本不知道兩年後會發生什麼事。
cards.why: 型5用來挑戰既有流程：因為未知，所以那個規劃儀式該改。把不確定當成論據而不是藉口，這是型5跟單純抱怨的分界線。
cards.pmNote: 要求縮短規劃週期時，論據是環境的不可預測度，不是團隊沒空。
cards.episode: Jenny Wen

alts.quote: I mean, I think Things probably, I'm just guessing, I don't know any of the numbers or whatever, but I would assume it makes between five and $25 million of revenue, which to a VC is not even worth considering a VC.
alts.zh: 我是說，Things 這款——我純粹在猜，數字我完全不知道——但我猜它一年營收大概在五百萬到兩千五百萬美金之間，這種規模對創投來說根本不值得看。

alts.quote: And I don't know how to vet companies, I don't know how to really logically think through what space is going to take off or something like that, but I just do feel like I have a sense on people.
alts.zh: 我不知道怎麼審公司、也不知道怎麼有邏輯地判斷哪個領域會起飛，但我就是覺得我對人有直覺。

alts.quote: But had I had the same conversation five or 10 years ago with the team at Convoy like I don't know anything about trucking, I probably wouldn't have understood why that business was going to work.
alts.zh: 但如果我在五年、十年前跟 Convoy 那個團隊講同樣的話——像是我對貨運一無所知——我大概不會理解那門生意為什麼會成。

cards.pattern: A lot of times we don't know the outcome, especially with [某類工作].
cards.quote: Well, a lot of times we don't know the outcome, especially with AI native products.
cards.zh: 很多時候我們根本不知道結果會是什麼，尤其是做 AI 原生產品的時候。
cards.why: 型5的常態化：用 a lot of times 把不確定講成這類工作的常態，而不是這個專案的意外。常態化之後，團隊就不會把每一次未知都當成失控。
cards.pmNote: 把不確定性標記成這個產品類型的固有特徵，能省掉很多不必要的檢討。
cards.episode: The art of influence: The single most important skill that AI can’t replace | Jessica Fain (Webflow, ex-Slack)

alts.quote: So I think it has to come with a place of knowing that you don't know everything and humility to say, "Hey, I need help." And it actually earns you a lot more credit than you think.
alts.zh: 我覺得這要來自一個認知：你不可能什麼都懂，還要有那個謙虛去說「嘿，我需要幫忙」。而且這其實比你想像的更會替你加分。

alts.quote: I haven't seen their CAD, so I don't know what it's like inside their device, but they do have a lot of things going on.
alts.zh: 我沒看過他們的 CAD 圖，所以我不知道他們裝置裡面長怎樣，但他們確實塞了很多東西進去。

alts.quote: I don't know exactly which occasion this person is referring to, but I know I've used that analogy a few times.
alts.zh: 我不確定這位聽眾指的是哪一次，但我知道我用過那個比喻好幾次。

cards.pattern: We are [執行狀態], and therefore the project might fail, but we don't know why.
cards.quote: We're in the worst of all worlds where we are imperfectly executing and therefore, at the end of the day, the project might fail, but we don't know why.
cards.zh: 我們處在最糟的狀態：執行得不夠扎實，所以專案最後可能會失敗，但我們連為什麼失敗都不會知道。
cards.why: 型5的預警版：她指出真正的風險不是失敗，是「失敗了還學不到東西」。把未知本身描述成最貴的成本，這個框架比催進度有力得多。
cards.pmNote: 推動執行紀律時，最有力的論點是「這樣搞就算失敗我們也不知道原因」。
cards.episode: Meta’s Head of Product (and 29th employee) on working with Mark Zuckerberg, early growth tactics, why PMs are like conductors, and more | Naomi Gleit

alts.quote: We don't know if we're going to actually end up going, and based on the results whether we're going to actually move forward with investing in that area, but that's a body of work we can commit to.
alts.zh: 我們不知道最後會不會真的往那邊走、也要看結果才知道要不要真的投資那個領域，但那是一塊我們可以承諾投入的工作量。

alts.quote: And then for Q2, we don't know how Q1 is going to go, so we're just going to leave the objective there, but we're not going to get into the nitty-gritty OKRs.
alts.zh: 至於第二季，我們不知道第一季會跑成怎樣，所以我們就把目標先掛在那，但不會去細拆 OKR。

alts.quote: We're going to go off and make this two-year, five-year, whatever, 10-year vision even, and we're going to point us towards something." But the way that the technology is changing now, we don't know what's going to happen in two years.
alts.zh: 我們本來會去做那種兩年、五年甚至十年的願景，把大家指向某個方向，但以現在技術變化的速度，我們根本不知道兩年後會發生什麼事。

cards.pattern: The reason we are misaligned is that we don't know what [X] is.
cards.quote: So, we don't know what the strategy is.
cards.zh: 所以說，我們根本不知道策略是什麼。
cards.why: 型5的診斷版：把「大家不同調」重新歸因到「我們不知道策略是什麼」。用一個集體的未知取代互相指責，會議的溫度立刻降下來。
cards.pmNote: 團隊對不齊時先問「我們講得出策略是什麼嗎」，多數對齊問題的根在這裡而不在溝通。
cards.episode: 4 questions Shreyas Doshi wishes he’d asked himself sooner | Former PM leader at Stripe, Twitter, Google

alts.quote: I don't know if I have the recipe for this, but I can just maybe share a few of the things that come to mind.
alts.zh: 我不確定我有沒有一套配方，但我可以分享幾個當下想到的東西。

alts.quote: I don't know, but I do think that trying to make big changes too quickly is a primary reason.
alts.zh: 我不知道，但我確實認為，想太快做太大的改變是主要原因之一。

alts.quote: And I don't know exactly when that will be, but I think we're pretty close.
alts.zh: 我不知道確切會是什麼時候，但我覺得已經很接近了。

cards.pattern: We don't know what we don't know until we [某個動作].
cards.quote: And we don't know what we don't know until we ship it and we get opinions from the users.
cards.zh: 我們不知道自己不知道什麼，直到我們把東西出貨、拿到使用者的意見。
cards.why: 型5＋出貨論證：until 這個字把未知綁到一個具體行動上。這句話的功能不是承認無知，是替「先出貨再說」找到理由。
cards.pmNote: 說服團隊提早出貨時，把出貨定義成獲取未知資訊的手段，而不是完成度的宣告。
cards.episode: Father of the iPod and iPhone on building taste, judgment, and creativity in the AI era | Tony Fadell

alts.quote: We didn't start really charging for subscriptions or having ads until, I don't know exactly, but something like year three.
alts.zh: 我們大概到第三年左右才真的開始收訂閱費、放廣告——我不記得確切時間了。

alts.quote: I don't think we should filter out AI content. I think we should let you know if content is AI content or not. That's hard, by the way.
alts.zh: 我不認為我們該把 AI 內容濾掉。我認為該做的是讓你知道這則內容是不是 AI 產的。順帶一提，這很難。

alts.quote: So I think it has to come with a place of knowing that you don't know everything and humility to say, "Hey, I need help." And it actually earns you a lot more credit than you think.
alts.zh: 我覺得這要來自一個認知：你不可能什麼都懂，還要有那個謙虛去說「嘿，我需要幫忙」。而且這其實比你想像的更會替你加分。

cards.pattern: The answer is, we don't know yet, but I get excited about [兩三個方向].
cards.quote: And the answer is, we don't know, yet, but I get excited about two avenues.
cards.zh: 答案是：我們還不知道，但我對兩個方向感到興奮。
cards.why: 型5和型1的合體，也是回答策略性大哉問的標準結構：先誠實說還不知道，再交出你正在押注的方向。既不裝懂也不空手。
cards.pmNote: 被問到公司三年後長怎樣時，這是最好的答題格式——不知道＋我正在關注的兩條路。
cards.episode: Yuhki Yamashata

alts.quote: I mean, look, I don't know that it's a perfect answer, but I think the reality is just that what kills most projects most early companies is stamina.
alts.zh: 我是說，我不確定這是不是完美的答案，但我覺得現實就是：殺死大多數專案、大多數早期公司的，是續航力。

alts.quote: But we don't know what those specifications are going to be yet.
alts.zh: 但我們還不知道那些規格會長什麼樣。

alts.quote: People always ask me, "How much time should I be spending on an assumption testing?" I don't know how to answer that question because for me, assumption testing and delivery are the same work.
alts.zh: 大家常問我：「假設驗證應該花多少時間？」我不知道怎麼回答這個問題，因為對我來說，假設驗證跟交付本來就是同一件工作。

cards.quote: It's very early, we don't know who's going to win.
cards.zh: 現在還很早期，我們不知道誰會贏。
cards.why: 型5最短的樣本：把市場未定講成客觀階段（very early）而不是自己看不懂。同一件事換一個框架，聽起來就從無知變成判斷。
cards.pmNote: 評論競爭格局時，用「還在早期」框住不確定，比說「很難講」專業。
cards.episode: The ultimate guide to AEO: How to get ChatGPT to recommend your product | Ethan Smith (Graphite)

alts.quote: I haven't seen their CAD, so I don't know what it's like inside their device, but they do have a lot of things going on.
alts.zh: 我沒看過他們的 CAD 圖，所以我不知道他們裝置裡面長怎樣，但他們確實塞了很多東西進去。

alts.quote: I mean, look, I don't know that it's a perfect answer, but I think the reality is just that what kills most projects most early companies is stamina.
alts.zh: 我是說，我不確定這是不是完美的答案，但我覺得現實就是：殺死大多數專案、大多數早期公司的，是續航力。

alts.quote: So I don't know how much it costs, but it's definitely worth it.
alts.zh: 我不知道它多少錢，但絕對值得。

cards.pattern: It could be actually we don't know what moves [關鍵指標].
cards.quote: And it could be actually we don't know what moves retention.
cards.zh: 也有可能，其實我們根本不知道什麼會影響留存。
cards.why: 型5的自我懷疑版：用 it could be actually 把一個很傷的可能性（我們對核心指標沒有理解）輕輕放上桌。actually 標示這是一個大家都沒說破的想法。
cards.pmNote: 留存改不動時，先驗證「我們是否真的知道什麼驅動留存」，再繼續做實驗。
cards.episode: The secret to better AI prototypes: Why Tinder’s CPO starts with JSON, not design | Ravi Mehta (product advisor, previously EIR at Reforge)

alts.quote: So I think it has to come with a place of knowing that you don't know everything and humility to say, "Hey, I need help." And it actually earns you a lot more credit than you think.
alts.zh: 我覺得這要來自一個認知：你不可能什麼都懂，還要有那個謙虛去說「嘿，我需要幫忙」。而且這其實比你想像的更會替你加分。

alts.quote: We don't know if we're going to actually end up going, and based on the results whether we're going to actually move forward with investing in that area, but that's a body of work we can commit to.
alts.zh: 我們不知道最後會不會真的往那邊走、也要看結果才知道要不要真的投資那個領域，但那是一塊我們可以承諾投入的工作量。

alts.quote: I don't think we should filter out AI content. I think we should let you know if content is AI content or not. That's hard, by the way.
alts.zh: 我不認為我們該把 AI 內容濾掉。我認為該做的是讓你知道這則內容是不是 AI 產的。順帶一提，這很難。

cards.quote: And that requires analysis as much as analogy, and we are very much in the middle of that process and we don't know all of the answers.
cards.zh: 那需要的分析跟類比一樣多，而我們正在這個過程的中間，我們沒有掌握全部的答案。
cards.why: 型5。all of the answers 這個量詞很關鍵——不是「沒有答案」，是「沒有全部的答案」。承認缺口的同時保住已經有的部分。
cards.pmNote: 回報進度時用「還沒有全部答案」而不是「還沒有答案」，兩者給人的信心差很多。
cards.episode: Be fundamentally different, not incrementally better | Jag Duggal (Nubank, Facebook, Google, Quantcast)

alts.quote: I don't know exactly which occasion this person is referring to, but I know I've used that analogy a few times.
alts.zh: 我不確定這位聽眾指的是哪一次，但我知道我用過那個比喻好幾次。

alts.quote: So, I don't know if supersystem is still the right exact analogy, but I think people just think of it as their AI.
alts.zh: 我不確定「超級系統」現在還是不是最精確的類比，但我覺得大家就是把它當成自己的 AI。

alts.quote: We're in the worst of all worlds where we are imperfectly executing and therefore, at the end of the day, the project might fail, but we don't know why.
alts.zh: 我們處在最糟的狀態：執行得不夠扎實，所以專案最後可能會失敗，但我們連為什麼失敗都不會知道。

cards.pattern: There are so many dependencies and things outside of our control that we don't know if we could do it.
cards.quote: And there are so many dependencies and so many things outside of our control that we don't know if we could do it." And I said, "That's okay.
cards.zh: 有太多相依關係、太多我們控制不了的事，所以我們不知道自己做不做得到。
cards.why: 型5的談判版：把不確定歸因到「控制範圍外的相依」，這是團隊拒絕硬承諾時最站得住腳的說法——不是能力不足，是變數不在手上。
cards.pmNote: 被逼承諾時，把不確定歸到外部相依上，並要求對方一起處理那些相依。
cards.episode: The one question that saves product careers | Matt LeMay

alts.quote: I don't know if you've ever seen just the UI of these things, but they're crazy complicated, and that's just for building a static website.
alts.zh: 我不知道你有沒有看過這些東西的介面，但它們複雜到誇張，而且這還只是為了做一個靜態網站。

alts.quote: I don't know how many customer support folks we have, but it's not very many, 30, 40, I'm not sure, way smaller than you would have at any comparable company, and it's because we've automated a lot of our flows.
alts.zh: 我不知道我們有多少客服人力，但沒有很多，三十、四十吧，我不確定，總之比任何同等規模的公司都少很多，因為我們把很多流程自動化了。

alts.quote: I mean, I think Things probably, I'm just guessing, I don't know any of the numbers or whatever, but I would assume it makes between five and $25 million of revenue, which to a VC is not even worth considering a VC.
alts.zh: 我是說，Things 這款——我純粹在猜，數字我完全不知道——但我猜它一年營收大概在五百萬到兩千五百萬美金之間，這種規模對創投來說根本不值得看。

cards.quote: At that point, I was an interim CMO at Nero and I'm like, "I don't know how to do this." And it actually earns you a lot more credit than you think.
cards.zh: 那時候我在 Nero 當代理行銷長，我就說：「我不知道該怎麼做這件事。」結果這反而幫你賺到比你想像中多得多的信任。
cards.why: 型6的核心命題本身：把「我不會」講出口，換到的是信用而不是扣分。這個池子裡的資深人物幾乎都在做這件事，而台灣的職場直覺完全相反。
cards.pmNote: 空降或接手新領域時，第一時間承認不會，比撐三個月再被發現划算得多。
cards.episode: Elena Verna on how B2B growth is changing, product-led growth, product-led sales, why you should go freemium not trial, what features to make free, and much more

alts.quote: I don't know how many customer support folks we have, but it's not very many, 30, 40, I'm not sure, way smaller than you would have at any comparable company, and it's because we've automated a lot of our flows.
alts.zh: 我不知道我們有多少客服人力，但沒有很多，三十、四十吧，我不確定，總之比任何同等規模的公司都少很多，因為我們把很多流程自動化了。

alts.quote: I mean, I think Things probably, I'm just guessing, I don't know any of the numbers or whatever, but I would assume it makes between five and $25 million of revenue, which to a VC is not even worth considering a VC.
alts.zh: 我是說，Things 這款——我純粹在猜，數字我完全不知道——但我猜它一年營收大概在五百萬到兩千五百萬美金之間，這種規模對創投來說根本不值得看。

alts.quote: I don't think we should filter out AI content. I think we should let you know if content is AI content or not. That's hard, by the way.
alts.zh: 我不認為我們該把 AI 內容濾掉。我認為該做的是讓你知道這則內容是不是 AI 產的。順帶一提，這很難。

cards.pattern: Look, I don't know how to build this in [規模／範圍].
cards.quote: If you're traditionally trained in product management, this is what you'll do, which is, look, I don't know how to build this in 120 countries.
cards.zh: 如果你是傳統產品管理訓練出來的，你會這樣做：欸，我不知道怎麼在一百二十個國家做這件事。
cards.why: 型6。把不會做綁在一個具體的規模上（120 個國家），而不是籠統的「我不會」。範圍愈具體，愈像是在描述問題而不是在自白弱點。
cards.pmNote: 說自己做不到時一定要附上規模條件，否則會被聽成能力不足。
cards.episode: Sanchan Saxena (VP of Product at Coinbase) on the inside story of how Airbnb made it through Covid; what he’s learned from Brian Chesky, Brian Armstrong, and Kevin Systrom; much more

alts.quote: I mean, look, I don't know that it's a perfect answer, but I think the reality is just that what kills most projects most early companies is stamina.
alts.zh: 我是說，我不確定這是不是完美的答案，但我覺得現實就是：殺死大多數專案、大多數早期公司的，是續航力。

alts.quote: I don't know exactly which occasion this person is referring to, but I know I've used that analogy a few times.
alts.zh: 我不確定這位聽眾指的是哪一次，但我知道我用過那個比喻好幾次。

alts.quote: I don't know how to do it off the top of my head, but I can go and look at the code or I can have Claude look at the code and combine that with other things to solve new problems.
alts.zh: 我沒辦法直接憑印象講出來，但我可以去看程式碼，或叫 Claude 去看，再結合其他東西來解新問題。

cards.quote: I don't know how to scale this stuff.
cards.zh: 我不知道怎麼把這東西規模化。
cards.why: 型6最短的骨架。scale 這個動詞讓句子從「我不會做事」變成「我沒有做過這個量級」——同樣是承認，命中的卻是經驗而不是能力。
cards.pmNote: 把「不會」框在規模而不是能力上，通常換來的是資源而不是質疑。
cards.episode: Sanchan Saxena (VP of Product at Coinbase) on the inside story of how Airbnb made it through Covid; what he’s learned from Brian Chesky, Brian Armstrong, and Kevin Systrom; much more

alts.quote: I don't know if I have the recipe for this, but I can just maybe share a few of the things that come to mind.
alts.zh: 我不確定我有沒有一套配方，但我可以分享幾個當下想到的東西。

alts.quote: I don't know, but I do think that trying to make big changes too quickly is a primary reason.
alts.zh: 我不知道，但我確實認為，想太快做太大的改變是主要原因之一。

alts.quote: I don't know what their latest numbers are, but just in terms of the numbers of people and the number of activity, I would place our scale among the largest US companies.
alts.zh: 我不知道他們最新的數字是多少，但光看使用人數和活躍量，我會把我們的規模排進美國最大的那幾家公司裡。

cards.pattern: I'm in my early 20s, I have no idea how to [任務], but I ended up doing that.
cards.quote: I'm in my early 20s, I have no idea how to manage vendor relationships, but I ended up doing that.
cards.zh: 我才二十出頭，完全不知道怎麼管供應商關係，但我最後還是做了。
cards.why: 型6的敘事版：把過去的不會拿來當故事開頭。回頭講自己曾經完全不會，是英文裡建立親和力最常見的手法，也讓聽的人敢承認自己現在不會。
cards.pmNote: 帶新人時主動講自己當年多不會，是最便宜的心理安全感投資。
cards.episode: 4 questions Shreyas Doshi wishes he’d asked himself sooner | Former PM leader at Stripe, Twitter, Google

alts.quote: You'd think, I've been doing this for 10 years, I'd have a very snappy definition of it there, and I don't.
alts.zh: 你會以為我做了十年，應該早就有一句俐落的定義——結果我沒有。

alts.quote: Those are just numbers I'm putting out there. It's always going to be a gut call based on where you are.
alts.zh: 那些數字只是我隨口丟出來的。這終究是看你所在的位置做的直覺判斷。

alts.quote: And I don't mean to sound like I'm above it all and have figured it all out. It still drives my stress
alts.zh: 我不是想擺出一副「我早就超脫了、全都想通了」的樣子。那件事到現在還是讓我很焦慮。

cards.pattern: I don't know how to [X], I don't know how to [Y], but I just do feel like I have a sense on [你真正的強項].
cards.quote: And I don't know how to vet companies, I don't know how to really logically think through what space is going to take off or something like that, but I just do feel like I have a sense on people.
cards.zh: 我不知道怎麼審公司、也不知道怎麼有邏輯地判斷哪個領域會起飛，但我就是覺得我對人有直覺。
cards.why: 型6的交換版：連續兩個不會，換來一個很具體的會。這種「我不會 A 和 B，但我會 C」的結構，比單獨宣稱自己擅長 C 可信得多。
cards.pmNote: 講自己的強項前先誠實列出兩個弱項，可信度會高很多。
cards.episode: Inside ChatGPT: The fastest-growing product in history | Nick Turley (Head of ChatGPT at OpenAI)

alts.quote: We're going to go off and make this two-year, five-year, whatever, 10-year vision even, and we're going to point us towards something." But the way that the technology is changing now, we don't know what's going to happen in two years.
alts.zh: 我們本來會去做那種兩年、五年甚至十年的願景，把大家指向某個方向，但以現在技術變化的速度，我們根本不知道兩年後會發生什麼事。

alts.quote: I don't know what their latest numbers are, but just in terms of the numbers of people and the number of activity, I would place our scale among the largest US companies.
alts.zh: 我不知道他們最新的數字是多少，但光看使用人數和活躍量，我會把我們的規模排進美國最大的那幾家公司裡。

alts.quote: I mean, look, I don't know that it's a perfect answer, but I think the reality is just that what kills most projects most early companies is stamina.
alts.zh: 我是說，我不確定這是不是完美的答案，但我覺得現實就是：殺死大多數專案、大多數早期公司的，是續航力。

cards.pattern: I don't know how to do it off the top of my head, but I can go and [取得答案的方法].
cards.quote: I don't know how to do it off the top of my head, but I can go and look at the code or I can have Claude look at the code and combine that with other things to solve new problems.
cards.zh: 我沒辦法直接憑印象講出來，但我可以去看程式碼，或叫 Claude 去看，再結合其他東西來解新問題。
cards.why: 型6的現代版：把不會重新定義成「不在腦子裡」，然後展示自己有取得答案的路徑。在 AI 時代，會找答案的能力比記得答案更值錢，這句就是那個轉譯。
cards.pmNote: 被問到細節時，展示你的查找路徑而不是硬背——這在工程訪談裡是加分不是扣分。
cards.episode: An AI state of the union: We’ve passed the inflection point, dark factories are coming, and automation timelines | Simon Willison

alts.quote: Now, I don't know what Claude Code is doing, obviously, but I would be willing to bet money that they're doing something in the form of evals.
alts.zh: 我當然不知道 Claude Code 內部到底在幹嘛，但我敢拿錢賭他們一定有在做某種形式的 evals。

alts.quote: I don't know if I want to highlight any specific categories, but I can talk about some of the things that we've funded in the past that has real legs.
alts.zh: 我不確定我想特別點名哪些類別，但我可以聊聊我們過去投過、確實有搞頭的一些東西。

alts.quote: I haven't seen their CAD, so I don't know what it's like inside their device, but they do have a lot of things going on.
alts.zh: 我沒看過他們的 CAD 圖，所以我不知道他們裝置裡面長怎樣，但他們確實塞了很多東西進去。

cards.pattern: Had I [做過某事], like I don't know anything about [領域], I probably wouldn't have [結果].
cards.quote: But had I had the same conversation five or 10 years ago with the team at Convoy like I don't know anything about trucking, I probably wouldn't have understood why that business was going to work.
cards.zh: 但如果我在五年、十年前跟 Convoy 那個團隊講同樣的話——像是我對貨運一無所知——我大概不會理解那門生意為什麼會成。
cards.why: 型6的反省版：承認自己曾經因為不懂而錯過判斷。這種回顧式的承認在英文裡很受重視，因為它證明你會校正自己，而不只是會辯護。
cards.pmNote: 覆盤看走眼的案子時，指出當時缺的是哪一塊領域知識，比檢討決策流程具體。
cards.episode: Developing a growth model + marketplace growth strategy | Dan Hockenmaier (Faire, Thumbtack, Reforge)

alts.quote: We're going to go off and make this two-year, five-year, whatever, 10-year vision even, and we're going to point us towards something." But the way that the technology is changing now, we don't know what's going to happen in two years.
alts.zh: 我們本來會去做那種兩年、五年甚至十年的願景，把大家指向某個方向，但以現在技術變化的速度，我們根本不知道兩年後會發生什麼事。

alts.quote: I mean, I think Things probably, I'm just guessing, I don't know any of the numbers or whatever, but I would assume it makes between five and $25 million of revenue, which to a VC is not even worth considering a VC.
alts.zh: 我是說，Things 這款——我純粹在猜，數字我完全不知道——但我猜它一年營收大概在五百萬到兩千五百萬美金之間，這種規模對創投來說根本不值得看。

alts.quote: We don't know if we're going to actually end up going, and based on the results whether we're going to actually move forward with investing in that area, but that's a body of work we can commit to.
alts.zh: 我們不知道最後會不會真的往那邊走、也要看結果才知道要不要真的投資那個領域，但那是一塊我們可以承諾投入的工作量。

cards.pattern: I have no idea how to [做決定], freaking out.
cards.quote: I have no idea how to make a short list, freaking out.
cards.zh: 我完全不知道怎麼縮出一份候選名單，整個慌了。
cards.why: 型6替別人代言的版本：她在模擬買家的內心話。用第一人稱把使用者的「我不會」演出來，比說「使用者感到困惑」有畫面得多。
cards.pmNote: 做使用者洞察簡報時，用第一人稱把使用者的無助感講出來，遠比描述性的敘述有力。
cards.episode: April Dunford on product positioning, segmentation, and optimizing your sales process

alts.quote: At the highest level, I tend to be very short-term pessimistic, although I'll frame that short-term pessimistic and very long-term optimistic.
alts.zh: 從最高層次看，我大致上是短期悲觀、長期樂觀的。

alts.quote: Could I build that future? I had absolutely no idea
alts.zh: 我做得出那個未來嗎？我完全不知道。

alts.quote: I don't know, but I do think that trying to make big changes too quickly is a primary reason.
alts.zh: 我不知道，但我確實認為，想太快做太大的改變是主要原因之一。

cards.pattern: I don't know how to read a [基礎專業文件].
cards.quote: I don't know how to read a financial statement.
cards.zh: 我不會看財務報表。
cards.why: 型6裡最赤裸的一句：承認一個「你這個職位理應會」的基本能力缺口。這種等級的坦承通常出現在資深者身上——因為只有他們付得起這個代價，而付了之後別人就敢跟著承認。
cards.pmNote: 領導者承認一個基本能力的缺口，能立刻打開團隊的求助意願。
cards.episode: How a great founder becomes a great CEO | Jonathan Lowenhar (co-founder of Enjoy The Work)

alts.quote: I don't know that I'm perfect at it, but I've learned to balance those things quite a bit more than I did in the past when I would just purely read from my questions and my rubric and not care about anything else.
alts.zh: 我不敢說我做得多完美，但我已經學會比以前平衡得多了——以前我只會照著自己的問題清單和評分表念，其他一概不管。

alts.quote: However, I've read a few articles that have said that Google no longer does prioritize press releases in SEO, so I don't know how much that holds up.
alts.zh: 不過我讀過幾篇文章說 Google 現在 SEO 已經不會優先給新聞稿了，所以我不知道這個說法現在還成不成立。

alts.quote: I don't know if I have the recipe for this, but I can just maybe share a few of the things that come to mind.
alts.zh: 我不確定我有沒有一套配方，但我可以分享幾個當下想到的東西。

cards.pattern: I don't know how to answer that question because for me, [問題預設的兩件事] are the same thing.
cards.quote: People always ask me, "How much time should I be spending on an assumption testing?" I don't know how to answer that question because for me, assumption testing and delivery are the same work.
cards.zh: 大家常問我：「假設驗證應該花多少時間？」我不知道怎麼回答這個問題，因為對我來說，假設驗證跟交付本來就是同一件工作。
cards.why: 型6轉成型3：她說不知道怎麼回答，實際上是在指出問題本身的預設有錯。這是「我不會」最高階的用法——用自己的無能為力去揭露對方的框架問題。
cards.pmNote: 被問到一個預設就錯的問題時（例如某活動該佔幾成工時），先拆預設再回答。
cards.episode: Teresa Torres on how to interview customers, automating continuous discovery, the opportunity solution tree framework, making the case for user research, common interviewing mistakes, and much more

alts.quote: I don't have a good answer for that because I just spent a lot of time using our internal products, but my stock answer is Granola.
alts.zh: 這題我沒有好答案，因為我大部分時間都在用我們自己的內部產品，不過我的罐頭答案是 Granola。

alts.quote: But had I had the same conversation five or 10 years ago with the team at Convoy like I don't know anything about trucking, I probably wouldn't have understood why that business was going to work.
alts.zh: 但如果我在五年、十年前跟 Convoy 那個團隊講同樣的話——像是我對貨運一無所知——我大概不會理解那門生意為什麼會成。

alts.quote: I don't know about you, but literally every time I think to do this, there's a fight in my head of like, "Ah, do I really need to work out today?
alts.zh: 我不知道你怎麼樣，但我每次想到要做這件事，腦子裡都會吵一架：欸，我今天真的需要運動嗎？

cards.quote: And you just get wrapped around the axle of like, well, that sounds really good in theory, but I have no idea how to even start executing on this.
cards.zh: 然後你就整個卡死在那裡：這聽起來理論上很棒，可是我根本不知道要怎麼開始執行。
cards.why: 型6的卡關版：不是不同意這個想法，是不知道第一步在哪。把異議精確定位在 how to start，對方就知道要補的是執行路徑而不是說服你。
cards.pmNote: 聽到很漂亮但落不了地的策略時，說「我不知道第一步怎麼開始」，逼出具體的下一步。
cards.episode: Becoming a conscious leader: Leading without fear, finding your life’s objective function, and getting better at vision and strategy | John Mark Nickels (Uber, Waymo, DoorDash)

alts.quote: Is this positioning good or not?" And the problem with B2B tech companies is, well, unless I'm your buyer, I'm not the right person to ask.
alts.zh: 「這個定位到底好不好？」B2B 科技公司的問題在於——除非我就是你的買家，不然我根本不是該問的那個人。

alts.quote: My purely anecdotal guess is maybe 10 to 15% are good product companies, something like that.
alts.zh: 我純粹憑印象猜，大概一成到一成五算是好的產品公司吧，差不多這個量級。

alts.quote: Your job as manager and a leader is not to have all the answers. It is not to have all the answers, it is to get good at finding them.
alts.zh: 你當主管、當領導者的工作不是要有全部的答案。真的不是——是要變得很會把答案找出來。

cards.pattern: I don't know if you've ever seen [某個東西], but [它的重點].
cards.quote: I don't know if you've ever seen just the UI of these things, but they're crazy complicated, and that's just for building a static website.
cards.zh: 我不知道你有沒有看過這些東西的介面，但它們複雜到誇張，而且這還只是為了做一個靜態網站。
cards.why: 這是既有分型沒抓到的第七型：不確定的不是自己的知識，是「對方有沒有這個共同經驗」。它讓你在引用例子前先給對方一個不知道也沒關係的台階，於是解釋背景不會顯得看不起人。這個句式在全池出現超過七十次，是最高頻的完整句型。
cards.pmNote: 向不同背景的人舉例前先問一句「不知道你有沒有看過」，比直接開講或直接問「你知道嗎」都得體。
cards.episode: Inside Bolt: From near-death to ~$40m ARR in 5 months—one of the fastest-growing products in history | Eric Simons (founder and CEO of StackBlitz)

alts.quote: And then the other behavior, and I don't know if you've ever seen this in a doc, but in one way writeups that you see a lot is there'll be just a mega comment thread on the title of the doc.
alts.zh: 還有另一種行為——我不知道你有沒有在文件裡看過——就是在一頁式的書面報告上，常常會看到標題底下掛著一大串留言。

alts.quote: I haven't seen their CAD, so I don't know what it's like inside their device, but they do have a lot of things going on.
alts.zh: 我沒看過他們的 CAD 圖，所以我不知道他們裝置裡面長怎樣，但他們確實塞了很多東西進去。

alts.quote: And there are so many dependencies and so many things outside of our control that we don't know if we could do it." And I said, "That's okay.
alts.zh: 有太多相依關係、太多我們控制不了的事，所以我們不知道自己做不做得到。

cards.pattern: I don't know about you, but [你自己的經驗].
cards.quote: I don't know about you, but often the comments that I get with commit messages and PRs aren't super great.
cards.zh: 我不知道你怎麼樣，但我收到的 commit message 跟 PR 的註解常常都不怎麼樣。
cards.why: 第七型的變體：I don't know about you, but…。這句話的實際功能是「我要抱怨一件事，但先給你不同意的空間」。台灣人通常直接講「大家都覺得…」，反而更容易踩到人。
cards.pmNote: 要吐槽一個大家可能都有的痛點時，先用 I don't know about you 把它標成個人經驗。
cards.episode: The role of AI in product development | Ryan J. Salva (VP of Product at GitHub, Copilot)

alts.quote: I don't know if I have the recipe for this, but I can just maybe share a few of the things that come to mind.
alts.zh: 我不確定我有沒有一套配方，但我可以分享幾個當下想到的東西。

alts.quote: I don't know, but I do think that trying to make big changes too quickly is a primary reason.
alts.zh: 我不知道，但我確實認為，想太快做太大的改變是主要原因之一。

alts.quote: And I don't know exactly when that will be, but I think we're pretty close.
alts.zh: 我不知道確切會是什麼時候，但我覺得已經很接近了。

cards.pattern: I don't know about you, but literally every time I [做某事], [你的內心狀態].
cards.quote: I don't know about you, but literally every time I think to do this, there's a fight in my head of like, "Ah, do I really need to work out today?
cards.zh: 我不知道你怎麼樣，但我每次想到要做這件事，腦子裡都會吵一架：欸，我今天真的需要運動嗎？
cards.why: 第七型用在自我揭露：先問對方是不是也這樣，再講一個有點難堪的內心戲。這個順序讓自我揭露變成邀請，而不是傾倒。
cards.pmNote: 要在會議裡承認一個很人性的弱點時，先用 I don't know about you 把它轉成共同經驗的邀請。
cards.episode: Building beautiful products with Stripe’s Head of Design | Katie Dill (Stripe, Airbnb, Lyft)

alts.quote: So I think it has to come with a place of knowing that you don't know everything and humility to say, "Hey, I need help." And it actually earns you a lot more credit than you think.
alts.zh: 我覺得這要來自一個認知：你不可能什麼都懂，還要有那個謙虛去說「嘿，我需要幫忙」。而且這其實比你想像的更會替你加分。

alts.quote: People always ask me, "How much time should I be spending on an assumption testing?" I don't know how to answer that question because for me, assumption testing and delivery are the same work.
alts.zh: 大家常問我：「假設驗證應該花多少時間？」我不知道怎麼回答這個問題，因為對我來說，假設驗證跟交付本來就是同一件工作。

alts.quote: I don't think we should filter out AI content. I think we should let you know if content is AI content or not. That's hard, by the way.
alts.zh: 我不認為我們該把 AI 內容濾掉。我認為該做的是讓你知道這則內容是不是 AI 產的。順帶一提，這很難。

cards.pattern: I don't know if you've ever seen this in [某個場景], but [你觀察到的行為模式].
cards.quote: And then the other behavior, and I don't know if you've ever seen this in a doc, but in one way writeups that you see a lot is there'll be just a mega comment thread on the title of the doc.
cards.zh: 還有另一種行為——我不知道你有沒有在文件裡看過——就是在一頁式的書面報告上，常常會看到標題底下掛著一大串留言。
cards.why: 第七型用來引入一個觀察到的模式。先確認對方可能沒看過，接著把場景描述得很具體，聽者就算沒經驗也能跟上。
cards.pmNote: 描述一個組織壞習慣時，先把場景講具體再下判斷，比直接下標籤有效。
cards.episode: What sets great teams apart | Lane Shackleton (CPO of Coda)

alts.quote: I don't know if you've ever seen just the UI of these things, but they're crazy complicated, and that's just for building a static website.
alts.zh: 我不知道你有沒有看過這些東西的介面，但它們複雜到誇張，而且這還只是為了做一個靜態網站。

alts.quote: I haven't seen their CAD, so I don't know what it's like inside their device, but they do have a lot of things going on.
alts.zh: 我沒看過他們的 CAD 圖，所以我不知道他們裝置裡面長怎樣，但他們確實塞了很多東西進去。

alts.quote: I don't know how many customer support folks we have, but it's not very many, 30, 40, I'm not sure, way smaller than you would have at any comparable company, and it's because we've automated a lot of our flows.
alts.zh: 我不知道我們有多少客服人力，但沒有很多，三十、四十吧，我不確定，總之比任何同等規模的公司都少很多，因為我們把很多流程自動化了。

cards.pattern: I don't know if this is a contrarian perspective, but [你的立場].
cards.quote: I don't know if this is a contrarian perspective, but I go to speak in a lot of universities.
cards.zh: 我不知道這算不算是個逆風的看法，但我常去很多大學演講。
cards.why: 第七型跟型3的交界：不確定的是「我這個看法算不算異類」。先把自己標成可能的少數派，聽的人會準備好接收不同意見，反而比較不會反射性反駁。
cards.pmNote: 要講一個可能不受歡迎的看法時，先標記它可能是少數意見，比包裝成共識安全。
cards.episode: How to own your career growth and become a powerful product leader | Deb Liu, Ancestry (ex-Facebook, PayPal)

alts.quote: And I know this is going to trigger some people, but the truth is they don't want to work.
alts.zh: 我知道這句會讓一些人不爽，但事實就是——他們不想做事。

alts.quote: I'm curious what you think. I still don't think ideas are worth as much as maybe a lot of people think. I still think execution is really hard.
alts.zh: 我反而想聽你怎麼看。我還是不覺得點子有大家講的那麼值錢，我還是覺得執行才難。

alts.quote: He just had an episode recently about a skeptical take on AI that I disagreed with a lot, but it was really interesting to think about it from a different perspective.
alts.zh: 他最近那集講了一個對 AI 很懷疑的觀點，我非常不同意，但從另一個角度想這件事真的很有意思。

cards.pattern: We went from only [X] to [Y].
cards.quote: So we went from only 5% of people using the product to 50%.
cards.zh: 我們從只有 5% 的人在用這個產品，變成 50%。
cards.why: only 放在起點數字前面，一個字就把「原本有多慘」講完了；終點數字直接接在 to 後面、不再加任何形容詞，讓落差自己說話。
cards.pmNote: 報成長一定要給起點。沒有起點的終點數字，對方無法判斷這是你做的還是本來就會發生的。
cards.episode: The original growth hacker reveals his secrets | Sean Ellis (author of “Hacking Growth”)

alts.quote: And our beta waiting list went from 5,000 to 85,000 people overnight.
alts.zh: 我們的 beta 候補名單一夜之間從五千人變成八萬五千人。

alts.quote: I think the other thing is really asking yourself, "What do I do that no one else in this organization can do?" There are lots of things that I do that other people in the organization can do.
alts.zh: 另外一件事是問自己：「我做的哪些事，是這個組織裡其他人做不到的？」我做的很多事，其實別人也能做。

alts.quote: We at IMVU, we shipped product 50 times a day on average at a time when people were lucky to be doing it monthly if they were really advanced.
alts.zh: 我們在 IMVU 平均一天出貨 50 次，那個年代大家能做到一個月一次就算很先進了。

cards.pattern: The end result of that phase was our [指標 A] went from [X] to [Y], and our [指標 B] went from [X] to [Y].
cards.quote: And so the end result of that phase, which is from 2018 to maybe late 2021, 2022, was our retention went from about 60% to 90%, and our NPS went from 16 to 50.
cards.zh: 那個階段最後的結果是，我們的留存率從大約 60% 上到 90%，NPS 從 16 上到 50。
cards.why: 兩個指標並排講，一個量行為一個量感受，互相當佐證。about 只加在第一個數字上——估的就標估的，記得精確的就不加，精確度標示得很準。
cards.pmNote: 留存和滿意度一起動，才排除得掉「只是把難搞的客戶趕走」這種解讀。
cards.episode: An inside look at Mixpanel’s product journey | Vijay Iyengar (Head of Product)

alts.quote: I realized that my best bet in terms of actually adding value was not to be another cook in the kitchen trying to figure that out, but to move into the next step of the journey, which nobody was paying attention to.
alts.zh: 我意識到，我真正能加值的方式，不是再擠進廚房當第 N 個廚師，而是往旅程的下一步走——那一步根本沒人在顧。

alts.quote: So we cut down basically 50% of test runs this way, which is pretty great, and we're not warming the planet as much with all these unnecessary CPU cycles being wasted on tests.
alts.zh: 我們用這個方法把測試執行次數砍掉大概一半。

alts.quote: So I like to give the Super Bowl example because one of our customers, Ramp, had a 43X increase in traffic when their ad went live.
alts.zh: 我很喜歡舉超級盃這個例子，因為我們有個客戶 Ramp，廣告一上流量就漲了 43 倍。

cards.pattern: There was one day where I brought [X] from [A] to [B], with statistical significance.
cards.quote: There was one day where I brought one page from three to 12% conversion rate with statistical significance.
cards.zh: 有一天我把某個頁面的轉換率從 3% 拉到 12%，而且有統計顯著性。
cards.why: 用 there was one day where 把大成果縮回一個具體場景，聽起來像在講故事而不是邀功；結尾補 with statistical significance，先把「你怎麼知道不是雜訊」這個問題堵掉。
cards.pmNote: 小樣本的漂亮數字最容易被打槍。主動講顯著性，比等人問再解釋強得多。
cards.episode: Scaling Duolingo, embracing failure, and insight into Latin America’s tech scene | Gina Gotthilf (Latitud, Duolingo)

alts.quote: We want to remove the field that was like an open text fields where we're asking people an open-ended question and we improved conversion by 40% page over page.
alts.zh: 我們把那個開放式問答欄位拿掉，逐頁比較之下轉換率提升了 40%。

alts.quote: So Webflow, we saw a 6X conversion rate difference between LLM traffic and Google Search traffic.
alts.zh: 以 Webflow 來說，我們看到 LLM 來的流量跟 Google 搜尋來的流量，轉換率差了六倍。

alts.quote: We hadn't even gotten there and the trial-to-paid conversion rate increased 40%, and we didn't touch it.
alts.zh: 我們根本還沒做到那一步，試用轉付費的轉換率就漲了 40%，而且我們完全沒動它。

cards.pattern: By [做了什麼], we have seen a [X]% increase in [指標].
cards.quote: So by improving the quality of the checkout experience through details small and large, we have seen a 10.5% increase in business' revenue from an older form of checkout to a newer form of checkout.
cards.zh: 靠著把結帳體驗的品質從大大小小的細節改好，我們看到商家營收提升了 10.5%。
cards.why: by + 動名詞開頭先講做法，數字留到主句才出現，數字因此是「做法的結果」而不是憑空宣稱。10.5 保留小數點，比講 10% 更像真的量過。
cards.pmNote: 體驗細節難以立案，因為它沒有單一功能可以掛。把一整批細節綁成一個做法、對到一個營收數字，才拿得到資源。
cards.episode: Building beautiful products with Stripe’s Head of Design | Katie Dill (Stripe, Airbnb, Lyft)

alts.quote: So by improving a creator's first and second month revenue by 25%, we were then able to improve their overall value on Patreon by an equivalent amount, which is pretty massive.
alts.zh: 所以把創作者第一、第二個月的收入提升 25% 之後，我們就能把他們在 Patreon 的整體價值也拉高差不多的幅度。

alts.quote: But where I started understanding deeply the dynamics of the marketplace was actually my experience and the one job I've had that not been in the creator or art or these big consumer platforms.
alts.zh: 但我真正開始深入理解市集的運作機制，其實是在那份唯一不屬於創作者、藝術或大型消費平台的工作裡。

alts.quote: I don't want to make it seem like it was me against everyone because that was definitely not the case. I think the starting engineers and designers on that team really cared about the quality of what they built too.
alts.zh: 我不想講得好像是我一個人對抗全世界，完全不是那樣。那個團隊的工程師跟設計師本來就很在乎品質。

cards.pattern: We doubled [指標] while also [通常會被犧牲的另一件事].
cards.quote: We doubled our upgrade rate from our starter plan to our pro plan while also increasing the price of the pro plan.
cards.zh: 我們把從入門方案升級到專業方案的比例翻倍，而且同時還把專業方案漲價了。
cards.why: 重點在 while also——它把成果從「一個數字變好」升級成「在通常互相衝突的兩件事上同時贏」，難度不必自己說，句型已經說了。
cards.pmNote: 升級率和價格通常反向。同時動兩個而不掉，代表價值主張真的成立，不是靠折扣買來的。
cards.episode: How to price your product | Naomi Ionita (Menlo Ventures)

alts.quote: We doubled our growth rate and last year we were in the low double digits.
alts.zh: 我們把成長率翻倍，去年大概是十幾趴那個區間。

alts.quote: There was one day where I brought one page from three to 12% conversion rate with statistical significance.
alts.zh: 有一天我把某個頁面的轉換率從 3% 拉到 12%，而且有統計顯著性。

alts.quote: So Webflow, we saw a 6X conversion rate difference between LLM traffic and Google Search traffic.
alts.zh: 以 Webflow 來說，我們看到 LLM 來的流量跟 Google 搜尋來的流量，轉換率差了六倍。

cards.pattern: We [做了什麼] [X] times a day on average, at a time when people were lucky to be doing it [Y].
cards.quote: We at IMVU, we shipped product 50 times a day on average at a time when people were lucky to be doing it monthly if they were really advanced.
cards.zh: 我們在 IMVU 平均一天出貨 50 次，那個年代大家能做到一個月一次就算很先進了。
cards.why: 50 這個數字本身沒有意義，是後面 at a time when… 補上當年的業界基準，落差才成立；on average 三個字讓它不像挑出來的最好那一天。
cards.pmNote: 講速度類的成績，一定要附上當時的產業基準，否則聽的人是用今天的標準在評你當年的事。
cards.episode: Reflections on a movement | Eric Ries (creator of the Lean Startup methodology)

alts.quote: My one learning there that has stuck with me, and I think can work for other people too, is that it's not just about doing things that actually matter, and learning. It's about being able to tell the story.
alts.zh: 那段經驗裡有一個一直留在我身上的體悟，我覺得對別人也適用：重點不只是去做真正重要的事、去學東西，還要能把這件事講成一個故事。

alts.quote: if I had to guess how people might talk about that, if I wasn't in the room, maybe they would cite that, but it's tough to say.
alts.zh: 如果要我猜、我不在場的時候別人會怎麼講這件事，他們可能會提到那個吧——但很難說。

alts.quote: So we went from only 5% of people using the product to 50%.
alts.zh: 我們從只有 5% 的人在用這個產品，變成 50%。

cards.pattern: We had around [起點], and we scaled from there to [終點].
cards.quote: We had around 4 million in ARR, and we scaled from there to 1 billion.
cards.zh: 我們當時大概 400 萬 ARR，然後從那裡一路做到 10 億。
cards.why: from there 兩個字把兩個數字接成一條線，而不是兩個各自漂浮的成績。around 只掛在起點上——起點記不清可以承認，終點要講死。
cards.pmNote: 在履歷或面試裡講規模，起點比終點更能證明你是推動的人而不是搭上車的人。
cards.episode: Inside monday.com’s transformation: radical transparency, impact over output, and their path to $1B ARR | Daniel Lereya (Chief Product and Technology Officer)

alts.quote: Like I mentioned, I think we scaled this exponentially to become, I think again, the fourth-largest rental fleet in the U.S.
alts.zh: 我們把這塊做起來，最後變成全美第四大的租賃車隊。

alts.quote: Hey, I noticed that we have this problem. I fixed it.
alts.zh: 嘿，我注意到我們有這個問題，我把它處理掉了。

alts.quote: I think the other thing is really asking yourself, "What do I do that no one else in this organization can do?" There are lots of things that I do that other people in the organization can do.
alts.zh: 另外一件事是問自己：「我做的哪些事，是這個組織裡其他人做不到的？」我做的很多事，其實別人也能做。

cards.pattern: We [倍數動詞] our [名詞].
cards.quote: We tripled our company size.
cards.zh: 我們把公司規模變成三倍。
cards.why: 英文有一整排把倍數塞進動詞的字（double / triple / 10x），一個動詞就把幅度講完，不必寫成 increased by 200%。台灣人習慣用形容詞（大幅成長），換成這個動詞立刻變成可查證的宣稱。
cards.pmNote: 組織規模三倍是背景資訊，不是成績。它的作用是替後面所有的管理難題定調。
cards.episode: Elena Verna 4.0

alts.quote: And we were able to say, "Oh, we shipped 65 improvements this week, this sprint." And that felt really, really aligned with what they were trying to accomplish from a company perspective as well.
alts.zh: 我們可以說：「這一週、這個 sprint，我們出了 65 個改善。」

alts.quote: Hey, I noticed that we have this problem. I fixed it.
alts.zh: 嘿，我注意到我們有這個問題，我把它處理掉了。

alts.quote: I think the other thing is really asking yourself, "What do I do that no one else in this organization can do?" There are lots of things that I do that other people in the organization can do.
alts.zh: 另外一件事是問自己：「我做的哪些事，是這個組織裡其他人做不到的？」我做的很多事，其實別人也能做。

cards.pattern: We doubled [指標], and last year we were in the [區間描述].
cards.quote: We doubled our growth rate and last year we were in the low double digits.
cards.zh: 我們把成長率翻倍，去年大概是十幾趴那個區間。
cards.why: 前半用倍數講幅度，後半用 low double digits 補絕對值。不方便給精確數字時，英文有一整套區間語（low / mid / high + double digits）可以誠實地講個大概。
cards.pmNote: 只講倍數不講基期是老招，內行人一定會追問。自己先把區間補上，可信度差很多。
cards.episode: How Intercom rose from the ashes by betting everything on AI | Eoghan McCabe (founder and CEO)

alts.quote: We doubled our upgrade rate from our starter plan to our pro plan while also increasing the price of the pro plan.
alts.zh: 我們把從入門方案升級到專業方案的比例翻倍，而且同時還把專業方案漲價了。

alts.quote: Candidly, one of the development areas for me, and it could be downstream because I do have this analogy of how to be a PM, is that the growth feedback or the constructive feedback for me is really learning when to lead from the front more.
alts.zh: 老實說，我自己的成長項目之一——這可能跟我對 PM 的那套比喻有關——別人給我的建設性回饋是：我要學會什麼時候該站到前面帶。

alts.quote: We hadn't even gotten there and the trial-to-paid conversion rate increased 40%, and we didn't touch it.
alts.zh: 我們根本還沒做到那一步，試用轉付費的轉換率就漲了 40%，而且我們完全沒動它。

cards.pattern: It was [X] days from when we decided to [做 A] to when we [做完 A].
cards.quote: So, it was 10 days from when we decided we were going to ship to when we shipped.
cards.zh: 從我們決定要出貨，到真的出貨，中間是 10 天。
cards.why: 沒有講「我們動作很快」，而是把「快」換成兩個時間點之間的天數；from when… to when… 這個結構順便把量測的起訖點定義清楚，別人沒得挑毛病。
cards.pmNote: 週期時間是最好講也最難造假的效率指標，因為起訖點都寫在句子裡。
cards.episode: Inside ChatGPT: The fastest-growing product in history | Nick Turley (Head of ChatGPT at OpenAI)

alts.quote: I've rarely regretted going deep in something that isn't quite my job. The worst case scenario is I've learned something new that I will never use.
alts.zh: 去深入研究那些不完全屬於我職責的東西，我幾乎沒後悔過。最糟的情況也不過是學到一個以後用不到的東西。

alts.quote: And this sounds like a fairytale. And if you do this, I guarantee you're not going to get the same results. In fact, you'll probably see way smaller numbers.
alts.zh: 這聽起來像童話。如果你照做，我可以保證你不會拿到一樣的結果——很可能數字會小很多。

alts.quote: And for us, even at scale, again going back to more than 50% of new signups still come through word of mouth.
alts.zh: 對我們來說，就算做到這個規模，還是有超過一半的新註冊是從口碑來的。

cards.pattern: We scaled this to become the [第 N 大] [類別] in [範圍].
cards.quote: Like I mentioned, I think we scaled this exponentially to become, I think again, the fourth-largest rental fleet in the U.S.
cards.zh: 我們把這塊做起來，最後變成全美第四大的租賃車隊。
cards.why: 拿不出絕對數字時，用排名加範圍當數字（第四大／全美）。排名的好處是聽的人不必知道基準就能定位你在哪裡。
cards.pmNote: 公司不讓你講絕對數字時，排名、佔比、倍數是三個還能講的替代品。
cards.episode: How marketplaces win: Liquidity, growth levers, quality, and more | Benjamin Lauzier (Lyft, Thumbtack, Reforge)

alts.quote: And I raised my hand and I said, "I'll IC this. I think I know what we need."
alts.zh: 我就舉手說：「這個我自己下去做。我大概知道我們需要什麼。」

alts.quote: I think those people tend to get lost in organizations. So if that describes you, just remember to say what you did.
alts.zh: 這種人在組織裡很容易被淹沒。所以如果你就是這種人，記得一定要把你做過的事講出來。

alts.quote: My one learning there that has stuck with me, and I think can work for other people too, is that it's not just about doing things that actually matter, and learning. It's about being able to tell the story.
alts.zh: 那段經驗裡有一個一直留在我身上的體悟，我覺得對別人也適用：重點不只是去做真正重要的事、去學東西，還要能把這件事講成一個故事。

cards.pattern: I led [職務名稱], so [具體到什麼規模／範圍].
cards.quote: I led Alexa International, so scaling Alexa and Echo to six more countries.
cards.zh: 我帶 Alexa 國際部門，也就是把 Alexa 跟 Echo 推到另外六個國家。
cards.why: I led X 後面接 so + 動名詞，把頭銜立刻翻譯成一件可以數的事。頭銜是公司內部語言，數字才是外面的人聽得懂的。
cards.pmNote: 自我介紹時頭銜後面永遠要接一個範圍或數字，否則對方無法判斷那個頭銜有多大。
cards.episode: What it takes to become a top 1% PM | Ian McAllister (Uber, Amazon, Airbnb)

alts.quote: What I didn't tell is that there was at least six years of accidental work behind this. I started a blog six years before... Actually, I've always been blogging since I graduated.
alts.zh: 我沒講的是，這背後至少有六年、不是刻意規劃的累積。我在那之前六年就開始寫部落格了——其實我從畢業就一直在寫。

alts.quote: Hey, I noticed that we have this problem. I fixed it.
alts.zh: 嘿，我注意到我們有這個問題，我把它處理掉了。

alts.quote: I think the other thing is really asking yourself, "What do I do that no one else in this organization can do?" There are lots of things that I do that other people in the organization can do.
alts.zh: 另外一件事是問自己：「我做的哪些事，是這個組織裡其他人做不到的？」我做的很多事，其實別人也能做。

cards.pattern: We shipped [X] [單位] this [時間單位].
cards.quote: And we were able to say, "Oh, we shipped 65 improvements this week, this sprint." And that felt really, really aligned with what they were trying to accomplish from a company perspective as well.
cards.zh: 我們可以說：「這一週、這個 sprint，我們出了 65 個改善。」
cards.why: 把「做了很多」換成一個可以數的單位（改善項），再掛上時間單位，句子就從一次性成果變成一個節奏。
cards.pmNote: 沒有大功能可報的季度，用可數的小單位加時間單位，比講「持續優化」有用。
cards.episode: The art of influence: The single most important skill that AI can’t replace | Jessica Fain (Webflow, ex-Slack)

alts.quote: Well, it's very generous of you. I wouldn't say... look, we've done some really good work, some good work so far at YouTube, and it's been a journey.
alts.zh: 你太抬舉我了。我不會這樣講啦——我們在 YouTube 是做了一些不錯的成績，過程也蠻曲折的。

alts.quote: I just want to say, I'm this Nigerian girl. I don't have an MBA, I didn't work in consulting, and I'm here, right?
alts.zh: 我只想說：我就是個奈及利亞女生。我沒有 MBA，也沒做過顧問業，但我人就在這裡。

alts.quote: We tripled our company size.
alts.zh: 我們把公司規模變成三倍。

cards.pattern: We cut down basically [X]% of [成本項] this way.
cards.quote: So we cut down basically 50% of test runs this way, which is pretty great, and we're not warming the planet as much with all these unnecessary CPU cycles being wasted on tests.
cards.zh: 我們用這個方法把測試執行次數砍掉大概一半。
cards.why: basically 掛在數字前是口語版的「大約」，比 approximately 自然得多；this way 把數字綁回前面講過的做法，避免數字脫離脈絡被亂引用。
cards.pmNote: 省成本的成果要綁在做法上。單獨的「省了 50%」會被追問到底省在哪。
cards.episode: How Block is becoming the most AI-native enterprise in the world | Dhanji R. Prasanna

alts.quote: Yeah, I mean, I don't want to overstate it, but they basically said all the early stuff we did to grow TikTok was based on your writing.
alts.zh: 我不想講得太誇張，不過他們基本上是說：TikTok 早期做的成長工作，都是照你寫的東西做的。

alts.quote: Well, first of all, thank you for saying all that. That's giving me too much credit, but I like the idea that it's going to balance out the too little credit I ostensibly get somewhere else, that's great.
alts.zh: 首先謝謝你這樣說。你太抬舉我了——不過我喜歡這個說法，就當作是補回我在別的地方被低估的部分吧。

alts.quote: So by improving a creator's first and second month revenue by 25%, we were then able to improve their overall value on Patreon by an equivalent amount, which is pretty massive.
alts.zh: 所以把創作者第一、第二個月的收入提升 25% 之後，我們就能把他們在 Patreon 的整體價值也拉高差不多的幅度。

cards.pattern: We hadn't even [做到那一步] and [指標] increased [X]%, and we didn't touch it.
cards.quote: We hadn't even gotten there and the trial-to-paid conversion rate increased 40%, and we didn't touch it.
cards.zh: 我們根本還沒做到那一步，試用轉付費的轉換率就漲了 40%，而且我們完全沒動它。
cards.why: 兩個否定句夾一個數字——前面說「我們還沒做到那步」，後面說「我們根本沒碰它」，40% 反而被襯得更強。這是講成果時很難得的謙虛版本。
cards.pmNote: 意外的成長要照實說是意外。硬把它算成自己的功勞，等對方查到真因你就沒有信用了。
cards.episode: Customer-led growth | Georgiana Laudi (Forget The Funnel)

alts.quote: There was one day where I brought one page from three to 12% conversion rate with statistical significance.
alts.zh: 有一天我把某個頁面的轉換率從 3% 拉到 12%，而且有統計顯著性。

alts.quote: So Webflow, we saw a 6X conversion rate difference between LLM traffic and Google Search traffic.
alts.zh: 以 Webflow 來說，我們看到 LLM 來的流量跟 Google 搜尋來的流量，轉換率差了六倍。

alts.quote: It was just such a rare opportunity, but I wouldn't have gotten those opportunities if I just let them promote me or I followed a strategy where I was just focused on trying to get the biggest title.
alts.zh: 那真的是很難得的機會，但如果我當初只是讓他們幫我升職、或只想著拿最大的頭銜，我根本拿不到那些機會。

cards.pattern: We improved [指標] by [X]%, [比較基準] over [比較基準].
cards.quote: We want to remove the field that was like an open text fields where we're asking people an open-ended question and we improved conversion by 40% page over page.
cards.zh: 我們把那個開放式問答欄位拿掉，逐頁比較之下轉換率提升了 40%。
cards.why: page over page（或 quarter over quarter、year over year）是英文報成果的標配尾巴，它回答「跟什麼比」。沒有這個尾巴的百分比，內行人一律當作沒說。
cards.pmNote: 百分比一定要附比較基準。同一個 40%，逐頁比和逐年比是兩件完全不同的事。
cards.episode: Using behavioral science to improve your product | Kristen Berman (Irrational Labs)

alts.quote: There was one day where I brought one page from three to 12% conversion rate with statistical significance.
alts.zh: 有一天我把某個頁面的轉換率從 3% 拉到 12%，而且有統計顯著性。

alts.quote: I think the other thing is really asking yourself, "What do I do that no one else in this organization can do?" There are lots of things that I do that other people in the organization can do.
alts.zh: 另外一件事是問自己：「我做的哪些事，是這個組織裡其他人做不到的？」我做的很多事，其實別人也能做。

alts.quote: Conversion rates go from 60% to 90% over the course of a few weeks of just optimizing that and putting more content there.
alts.zh: 轉換率會在幾週內從 60% 上到 90%，就只是把那塊優化一下、多放點內容進去。

cards.pattern: That simple idea increased [指標] by about [X]%.
cards.quote: That simple idea increased revenue by about 12%.
cards.zh: 那個很簡單的點子，讓營收提升了大約 12%。
cards.why: 主詞是 that simple idea 而不是 we——功勞給點子不給自己，數字反而更可信；about 讓 12% 不必假裝精確。
cards.pmNote: 小改動配大數字是實驗文化最有說服力的證據，因為它同時證明了「值得試」和「試很便宜」。
cards.episode: The ultimate guide to A/B testing | Ronny Kohavi (Airbnb, Microsoft, Amazon)

alts.quote: And so the idea of launching web really drove and actually increased Instagram's growth by 10% the minute we launched it.
alts.zh: 推出網頁版這件事，在我們上線的那一刻就讓 Instagram 的成長多了 10%。

alts.quote: It's not about you, it's about the idea. And don't be afraid to stand behind the idea.
alts.zh: 重點不是你，是那個想法。而且不要怕站在那個想法後面。

alts.quote: So by improving the quality of the checkout experience through details small and large, we have seen a 10.5% increase in business' revenue from an older form of checkout to a newer form of checkout.
alts.zh: 靠著把結帳體驗的品質從大大小小的細節改好，我們看到商家營收提升了 10.5%。

cards.pattern: We've cut [X] down by [Y]%.
cards.quote: We've cut our human escalation from our support infrastructure down by 50%.
cards.zh: 我們把客服系統轉真人處理的比例砍掉了一半。
cards.why: 成果是「變少」時用 cut … down by，不要用 reduced 再堆一串名詞。現在完成式 we've 表示這是已經到手、而且還在持續的狀態。
cards.pmNote: 自動化的成效要用「轉人工比例」這種對外部有感的指標講，不要用內部處理量。
cards.episode: Behind the founder: Marc Benioff

alts.quote: Well, it's very generous of you. I wouldn't say... look, we've done some really good work, some good work so far at YouTube, and it's been a journey.
alts.zh: 你太抬舉我了。我不會這樣講啦——我們在 YouTube 是做了一些不錯的成績，過程也蠻曲折的。

alts.quote: So we cut down basically 50% of test runs this way, which is pretty great, and we're not warming the planet as much with all these unnecessary CPU cycles being wasted on tests.
alts.zh: 我們用這個方法把測試執行次數砍掉大概一半。

alts.quote: Hey, I noticed that we have this problem. I fixed it.
alts.zh: 嘿，我注意到我們有這個問題，我把它處理掉了。

cards.pattern: [做法] increased [指標] by [X]% the minute we launched it.
cards.quote: And so the idea of launching web really drove and actually increased Instagram's growth by 10% the minute we launched it.
cards.zh: 推出網頁版這件事，在我們上線的那一刻就讓 Instagram 的成長多了 10%。
cards.why: the minute we launched it 是時間證據——它排除了「可能是其他因素」的解讀，等於用半句話做了因果宣稱。
cards.pmNote: 上線瞬間的階梯式跳動，是沒做 A/B test 時最強的因果證據。
cards.episode: Unorthodox frameworks for growing your product, career, and impact | Bangaly Kaba (YouTube, Instagram, Facebook, Instacart)

alts.quote: That simple idea increased revenue by about 12%.
alts.zh: 那個很簡單的點子，讓營收提升了大約 12%。

alts.quote: What I didn't tell is that there was at least six years of accidental work behind this. I started a blog six years before... Actually, I've always been blogging since I graduated.
alts.zh: 我沒講的是，這背後至少有六年、不是刻意規劃的累積。我在那之前六年就開始寫部落格了——其實我從畢業就一直在寫。

alts.quote: But where I started understanding deeply the dynamics of the marketplace was actually my experience and the one job I've had that not been in the creator or art or these big consumer platforms.
alts.zh: 但我真正開始深入理解市集的運作機制，其實是在那份唯一不屬於創作者、藝術或大型消費平台的工作裡。

cards.pattern: [指標] go from [X] to [Y] over the course of [時間] of just [做法].
cards.quote: Conversion rates go from 60% to 90% over the course of a few weeks of just optimizing that and putting more content there.
cards.zh: 轉換率會在幾週內從 60% 上到 90%，就只是把那塊優化一下、多放點內容進去。
cards.why: 用現在式 go 而不是過去式 went，把一次成果講成「這件事通常會這樣」的通則；just 放在做法前面，暗示投入不大、回報很大。
cards.pmNote: 把個案講成通則要很小心：只有在你看過多個案例時才能用現在式，否則會被抓到以偏概全。
cards.episode: How to scrappily hire for, measure, and unlock growth | Crystal Widjaja, Gojek and Kumu

alts.quote: We want to remove the field that was like an open text fields where we're asking people an open-ended question and we improved conversion by 40% page over page.
alts.zh: 我們把那個開放式問答欄位拿掉，逐頁比較之下轉換率提升了 40%。

alts.quote: We hadn't even gotten there and the trial-to-paid conversion rate increased 40%, and we didn't touch it.
alts.zh: 我們根本還沒做到那一步，試用轉付費的轉換率就漲了 40%，而且我們完全沒動它。

alts.quote: One, I hate to be this person, but I'll point to a few of my papers.
alts.zh: 第一，我很不想當那種人，但我還是要推薦一下我自己的幾篇論文。

cards.pattern: [指標] went from [X] to [Y] overnight.
cards.quote: And our beta waiting list went from 5,000 to 85,000 people overnight.
cards.zh: 我們的 beta 候補名單一夜之間從五千人變成八萬五千人。
cards.why: overnight 是這句唯一的形容詞，其他全交給兩個絕對數字。用絕對人數而不是百分比，是因為十七倍聽起來抽象，5,000 到 85,000 有畫面。
cards.pmNote: 早期指標用絕對數字比用倍數誠實，因為基期太小的時候倍數會騙人。
cards.episode: Behind the founder: Drew Houston (Dropbox)

alts.quote: So we went from only 5% of people using the product to 50%.
alts.zh: 我們從只有 5% 的人在用這個產品，變成 50%。

alts.quote: I think the other thing is really asking yourself, "What do I do that no one else in this organization can do?" There are lots of things that I do that other people in the organization can do.
alts.zh: 另外一件事是問自己：「我做的哪些事，是這個組織裡其他人做不到的？」我做的很多事，其實別人也能做。

alts.quote: Beyond those cosmetics, the biggest thing I see particularly at higher levels is people talk about what they have done but not why it mattered.
alts.zh: 撇開那些表面功夫，我在比較資深的層級看到最大的問題是：大家只講自己做了什麼，不講那件事為什麼重要。

cards.pattern: [客戶] had a [X]X increase in [指標] when [事件].
cards.quote: So I like to give the Super Bowl example because one of our customers, Ramp, had a 43X increase in traffic when their ad went live.
cards.zh: 我很喜歡舉超級盃這個例子，因為我們有個客戶 Ramp，廣告一上流量就漲了 43 倍。
cards.why: 43X 這種奇怪的數字比 40X 可信，因為它明顯是量出來的不是講出來的；前面掛 I like to give the… example，表示這是他固定會用的證據，不是臨時想的。
cards.pmNote: 客戶案例要留一個帶精確數字的當常備彈藥，講第二十次跟第一次一樣有力。
cards.episode: Everyone’s an engineer now: Inside v0’s mission to create a hundred million builders | Guillermo Rauch (founder and CEO of Vercel, creators of v0 and Next.js)

alts.quote: Looking back, my career has been a little bit like a bingo card. I've always been looking to fill in boxes I didn't have filled because I felt like that would make me a better professional.
alts.zh: 回頭看，我的職涯有點像一張賓果卡。我一直在補那些還沒被填滿的格子，因為我覺得那會讓我變成更好的專業工作者。

alts.quote: I don't want to make it seem like it was me against everyone because that was definitely not the case. I think the starting engineers and designers on that team really cared about the quality of what they built too.
alts.zh: 我不想講得好像是我一個人對抗全世界，完全不是那樣。那個團隊的工程師跟設計師本來就很在乎品質。

alts.quote: And so the end result of that phase, which is from 2018 to maybe late 2021, 2022, was our retention went from about 60% to 90%, and our NPS went from 16 to 50.
alts.zh: 那個階段最後的結果是，我們的留存率從大約 60% 上到 90%，NPS 從 16 上到 50。

cards.pattern: Probably the stat I'm most proud of is [數字＋事實].
cards.quote: But probably the stat I'm most proud of, and the hardest thing to make happen out of all of that was we acquired 70% of the users that found out about Wise last month through word of mouth.
cards.zh: 大概是我最自豪、也最難做到的一個數字：上個月知道 Wise 的使用者裡，有 70% 是靠口碑來的。
cards.why: 先講「這是我最自豪的數字」，等於替聽的人做了排序，你不必把所有成績念一遍；再補 the hardest thing to make happen，把難度也標出來——難度是數字的第二個維度。
cards.pmNote: 口碑佔比是少數難以造假的成長指標，因為它沒辦法用預算買出來。
cards.episode: How to drive word of mouth | Nilan Peiris (CPO of Wise)

alts.quote: And I'm not saying that's the thing that made it happen, but I will say very quickly after that, we became very close partners and ultimately they acquired me.
alts.zh: 我不是說就是因為這件事才成的，但我可以說，那之後我們很快就變成很緊密的夥伴，最後他們把我們買下來了。

alts.quote: And for us, even at scale, again going back to more than 50% of new signups still come through word of mouth.
alts.zh: 對我們來說，就算做到這個規模，還是有超過一半的新註冊是從口碑來的。

alts.quote: So at any given point in time, I probably give myself a B to B-, and sometimes it's a C and sometimes it's a D, and sometimes it's an A, and I'm really plugging away, but it's totally an ongoing challenge.
alts.zh: 任何時間點上，我大概給自己 B 到 B-，有時候 C、有時候 D，偶爾也有 A，我真的一直在努力，但這就是個持續的挑戰。

cards.pattern: By improving [近端指標] by [X]%, we were then able to improve [終端指標] by an equivalent amount.
cards.quote: So by improving a creator's first and second month revenue by 25%, we were then able to improve their overall value on Patreon by an equivalent amount, which is pretty massive.
cards.zh: 所以把創作者第一、第二個月的收入提升 25% 之後，我們就能把他們在 Patreon 的整體價值也拉高差不多的幅度。
cards.why: 兩個數字之間用 we were then able to 串成因果鏈，讓一個局部改善連到公司真正在乎的大指標；by an equivalent amount 避免重複講一次 25%，同時把等價關係講清楚。
cards.pmNote: 早期指標要能推到 LTV，你的專案才有預算。中間那條因果鏈是說服 CFO 的關鍵。
cards.episode: How to build a high-performing growth team | Adam Fishman (Patreon, Lyft, Imperfect Foods)

alts.quote: I realized that my best bet in terms of actually adding value was not to be another cook in the kitchen trying to figure that out, but to move into the next step of the journey, which nobody was paying attention to.
alts.zh: 我意識到，我真正能加值的方式，不是再擠進廚房當第 N 個廚師，而是往旅程的下一步走——那一步根本沒人在顧。

alts.quote: So by improving the quality of the checkout experience through details small and large, we have seen a 10.5% increase in business' revenue from an older form of checkout to a newer form of checkout.
alts.zh: 靠著把結帳體驗的品質從大大小小的細節改好，我們看到商家營收提升了 10.5%。

alts.quote: So we cut down basically 50% of test runs this way, which is pretty great, and we're not warming the planet as much with all these unnecessary CPU cycles being wasted on tests.
alts.zh: 我們用這個方法把測試執行次數砍掉大概一半。

cards.pattern: We launched at [X], and now we're down to about [Y].
cards.quote: We launched at 0.5%, and now we're down to about 0.35%.
cards.zh: 我們上線時是 0.5%，現在降到大概 0.35%。
cards.why: 這是「愈低愈好」的指標該怎麼講——down to 是關鍵字，它讓聽的人立刻知道降低是成就；起點用 launched at 標定，等於自己給了基準線。
cards.pmNote: 費率、錯誤率這種愈低愈好的指標，起點一定要講，否則對方不知道 0.35% 是好是壞。
cards.episode: How to drive word of mouth | Nilan Peiris (CPO of Wise)

alts.quote: But now I am making more in compensation that I made at Uber. Part of it is just luck, part of this is situational.
alts.zh: 但我現在的收入比在 Uber 的時候還高。其中一部分純粹是運氣，一部分是時機造成的。

alts.quote: So we cut down basically 50% of test runs this way, which is pretty great, and we're not warming the planet as much with all these unnecessary CPU cycles being wasted on tests.
alts.zh: 我們用這個方法把測試執行次數砍掉大概一半。

alts.quote: We want to remove the field that was like an open text fields where we're asking people an open-ended question and we improved conversion by 40% page over page.
alts.zh: 我們把那個開放式問答欄位拿掉，逐頁比較之下轉換率提升了 40%。

cards.pattern: Even at scale, more than [X]% of [指標] still come through [管道].
cards.quote: And for us, even at scale, again going back to more than 50% of new signups still come through word of mouth.
cards.zh: 對我們來說，就算做到這個規模，還是有超過一半的新註冊是從口碑來的。
cards.why: even at scale 加 still 是一組——它預先回答了「那是早期才有的吧」這個反駁。先把質疑講掉，數字才守得住。
cards.pmNote: 口碑佔比在規模化後通常會被付費管道稀釋。沒被稀釋才是真正的訊號。
cards.episode: “Dumbest idea I’ve heard” to $100M ARR: Inside the rise of Gamma | Grant Lee (CEO)

alts.quote: But probably the stat I'm most proud of, and the hardest thing to make happen out of all of that was we acquired 70% of the users that found out about Wise last month through word of mouth.
alts.zh: 大概是我最自豪、也最難做到的一個數字：上個月知道 Wise 的使用者裡，有 70% 是靠口碑來的。

alts.quote: I've rarely regretted going deep in something that isn't quite my job. The worst case scenario is I've learned something new that I will never use.
alts.zh: 去深入研究那些不完全屬於我職責的東西，我幾乎沒後悔過。最糟的情況也不過是學到一個以後用不到的東西。

alts.quote: I was going to start by saying, I've been wrong about tons of things, but I buried those out back behind the shed.
alts.zh: 我本來想說，我看走眼的次數多到數不清啦，只是那些我都埋在後院工具間後面了。

cards.pattern: We ran an anonymous [量測方式], [多久之後], and we had a [X]% [結果].
cards.quote: We ran an anonymous employee survey, I think 15 or 16 months after I started aggressively working through the org and rebuilding the org and rebuilding the culture, and we had a 98 to 99% approval of management, leadership and new strategy.
cards.zh: 我們做了一次匿名員工調查，大概是我開始大刀闊斧整頓組織、重建文化的十五、十六個月之後，結果是九成八到九成九的人認可管理層、領導層跟新策略。
cards.why: 先講量測方法（anonymous）與時間點，最後才給數字——順序決定可信度，數字先出來的話聽的人會先懷疑量法。98 to 99% 用區間，是因為他真的記不清，不假裝。
cards.pmNote: 文化類成果最容易被質疑是自我感覺良好。匿名、時間點、樣本三件事講齊，數字才站得住。
cards.episode: How Intercom rose from the ashes by betting everything on AI | Eoghan McCabe (founder and CEO)

alts.quote: And for us, even at scale, again going back to more than 50% of new signups still come through word of mouth.
alts.zh: 對我們來說，就算做到這個規模，還是有超過一半的新註冊是從口碑來的。

alts.quote: And I'm not saying that's the thing that made it happen, but I will say very quickly after that, we became very close partners and ultimately they acquired me.
alts.zh: 我不是說就是因為這件事才成的，但我可以說，那之後我們很快就變成很緊密的夥伴，最後他們把我們買下來了。

alts.quote: It was just such a rare opportunity, but I wouldn't have gotten those opportunities if I just let them promote me or I followed a strategy where I was just focused on trying to get the biggest title.
alts.zh: 那真的是很難得的機會，但如果我當初只是讓他們幫我升職、或只想著拿最大的頭銜，我根本拿不到那些機會。

cards.pattern: We saw a [X]X difference in [指標] between [A] and [B].
cards.quote: So Webflow, we saw a 6X conversion rate difference between LLM traffic and Google Search traffic.
cards.zh: 以 Webflow 來說，我們看到 LLM 來的流量跟 Google 搜尋來的流量，轉換率差了六倍。
cards.why: 不講任何一邊的絕對值，只講兩邊的倍數差。不方便公開真實數字時，差距倍數是可以講的版本，而且它本來就是聽的人真正想知道的。
cards.pmNote: 新管道要爭預算，講轉換率差距比講流量絕對值有效——流量小但質量高，是最好的立案理由。
cards.episode: The ultimate guide to AEO: How to get ChatGPT to recommend your product | Ethan Smith (Graphite)

alts.quote: There was one day where I brought one page from three to 12% conversion rate with statistical significance.
alts.zh: 有一天我把某個頁面的轉換率從 3% 拉到 12%，而且有統計顯著性。

alts.quote: We hadn't even gotten there and the trial-to-paid conversion rate increased 40%, and we didn't touch it.
alts.zh: 我們根本還沒做到那一步，試用轉付費的轉換率就漲了 40%，而且我們完全沒動它。

alts.quote: We doubled our upgrade rate from our starter plan to our pro plan while also increasing the price of the pro plan.
alts.zh: 我們把從入門方案升級到專業方案的比例翻倍，而且同時還把專業方案漲價了。

cards.pattern: At the peak, we had [X]% of users [負面行為] per day.
cards.quote: And at the peak, we had 3% of users deleting their accounts per day.
cards.zh: 最嚴重的時候，我們每天有 3% 的使用者在刪帳號。
cards.why: 講自己的壞數字時加 at the peak，同時標出最糟的一刻和「那已經過去了」；per day 這個單位讓 3% 從小數字變成災難——單位選擇本身就是論證。
cards.pmNote: 壞數字換算成日頻率才看得出嚴重性。3% 聽起來還好，每天 3% 是一個月歸零。
cards.episode: How to consistently go viral: Nikita Bier’s playbook for winning at consumer apps (co-founder of TBH, Gas, advisor, investor)

alts.quote: There was one day where I brought one page from three to 12% conversion rate with statistical significance.
alts.zh: 有一天我把某個頁面的轉換率從 3% 拉到 12%，而且有統計顯著性。

alts.quote: But probably the stat I'm most proud of, and the hardest thing to make happen out of all of that was we acquired 70% of the users that found out about Wise last month through word of mouth.
alts.zh: 大概是我最自豪、也最難做到的一個數字：上個月知道 Wise 的使用者裡，有 70% 是靠口碑來的。

alts.quote: We at IMVU, we shipped product 50 times a day on average at a time when people were lucky to be doing it monthly if they were really advanced.
alts.zh: 我們在 IMVU 平均一天出貨 50 次，那個年代大家能做到一個月一次就算很先進了。

cards.pattern: We had something like [X]% [壞指標], [補充定義], [對象].
cards.quote: We had something like 40% churn, revenue churn, our core product.
cards.zh: 我們的核心產品當時大概有 40% 的流失，是營收流失。
cards.why: 講到 churn 立刻補一句 revenue churn 把口徑釘死。同一個字在不同公司算法不同，講壞數字時尤其要先定義，否則對方會往更糟的方向想。
cards.pmNote: 客戶流失和營收流失可以差很遠。報流失一定要先講是哪一種，否則後面的討論全是雞同鴨講。
cards.episode: An inside look at Mixpanel’s product journey | Vijay Iyengar (Head of Product)

alts.quote: I've rarely regretted going deep in something that isn't quite my job. The worst case scenario is I've learned something new that I will never use.
alts.zh: 去深入研究那些不完全屬於我職責的東西，我幾乎沒後悔過。最糟的情況也不過是學到一個以後用不到的東西。

alts.quote: Yeah, this is not something I'd ever say about myself. It's nice that someone else would say it, but it's a mysterious thing.
alts.zh: 這種話我自己絕對講不出口。有別人這樣說當然開心，不過這東西其實挺玄的。

alts.quote: So by improving the quality of the checkout experience through details small and large, we have seen a 10.5% increase in business' revenue from an older form of checkout to a newer form of checkout.
alts.zh: 靠著把結帳體驗的品質從大大小小的細節改好，我們看到商家營收提升了 10.5%。

cards.pattern: [好消息], but at just the [某一步] we had a [X]% drop off rate.
cards.quote: We found a demand generation channel that was really cheap and the economics looked great, but at just the download step we had a 90% drop off rate.
cards.zh: 我們找到一個獲客管道，很便宜、帳算起來很漂亮，但光是下載那一步我們就掉了九成的人。
cards.why: 好消息用形容詞講（cheap、looked great），壞消息用數字講。這個不對稱是刻意的，讓 90% 落在句子最後一個位置，整段的重量都壓在它身上。
cards.pmNote: 管道經濟模型漂亮但漏斗某一步崩掉，是最常見的假陽性。要指名是哪一步，不要只說轉換不好。
cards.episode: The original growth hacker reveals his secrets | Sean Ellis (author of “Hacking Growth”)

alts.quote: I realized that my best bet in terms of actually adding value was not to be another cook in the kitchen trying to figure that out, but to move into the next step of the journey, which nobody was paying attention to.
alts.zh: 我意識到，我真正能加值的方式，不是再擠進廚房當第 N 個廚師，而是往旅程的下一步走——那一步根本沒人在顧。

alts.quote: We doubled our upgrade rate from our starter plan to our pro plan while also increasing the price of the pro plan.
alts.zh: 我們把從入門方案升級到專業方案的比例翻倍，而且同時還把專業方案漲價了。

alts.quote: So we cut down basically 50% of test runs this way, which is pretty great, and we're not warming the planet as much with all these unnecessary CPU cycles being wasted on tests.
alts.zh: 我們用這個方法把測試執行次數砍掉大概一半。

cards.pattern: I ran the question and it came back at only [X]% of [對象] saying [具體反應].
cards.quote: I ran the question and it came back at only 7% of users saying they'd be very disappointed without the product.
cards.zh: 我把那個問題丟出去問，結果回來只有 7% 的使用者說「沒有這個產品會非常失望」。
cards.why: it came back at 把數字寫成「跑出來的結果」而不是「我認為」；only 一個字就把這個數字的意義（不夠）標好，不必再加一句評論。
cards.pmNote: Sean Ellis 問卷的門檻是 40%。7% 代表產品市場契合根本還沒開始，不是差一點。
cards.episode: The original growth hacker reveals his secrets | Sean Ellis (author of “Hacking Growth”)

alts.quote: I like Sean Ellis's question of how disappointed would you be if this product disappeared? And I think it's if you have at least 40% of people respond that they'd be very disappointed, then you're on the right track.
alts.zh: 我喜歡 Sean Ellis 那一題：如果這個產品消失了，你會有多失望？如果至少 40% 的人回答「非常失望」，那你方向就是對的。

alts.quote: And my first question to him as a product guy is like, "Wow, would you give me a million dollars to solve this problem?"
alts.zh: 身為做產品的人，我第一個問題是：「哇，那你願意花一百萬美元讓我解掉這個問題嗎？」

alts.quote: We saw more like 30 to 40% engagement rate drops for likes and reposts in A-B tests we were ran when showing a post with or without a note, which is just crazy big.
alts.zh: 我們在 A/B 測試裡看到的比較像是 30 到 40% 的互動率下降，就是按讚跟轉發，比較有掛註記跟沒掛註記的貼文——這個幅度大得誇張。

cards.pattern: If you have at least [X]% of people [反應], then you're on the right track.
cards.quote: And I think it's if you have at least 40% of people respond that they'd be very disappointed, then you're on the right track.
cards.zh: 如果至少有 40% 的人回答「沒有這個東西會非常失望」，那你方向是對的。
cards.why: if…then 把一個數字變成一條可判定的門檻；at least 標出這是下限而不是目標值，聽的人才知道 41% 和 80% 在這條規則裡是同一邊。
cards.pmNote: 門檻型指標的價值在於它能結束辯論。沒有門檻的數字，每個人都能自己解讀成對自己有利的方向。
cards.episode: The hierarchy of engagement | Sarah Tavel (Benchmark, Greylock, Pinterest)

alts.quote: I think Peter Thiel actually says it more simply and elegantly, which is, 'You need to be right about something that other people think you're wrong about for a very long time.'
alts.zh: 我覺得 Peter Thiel 講得更簡潔漂亮：「你得在一件別人認為你錯的事情上，長時間地正確。」

alts.quote: In investors, it's 1%. Not one third, 1%. So you're going to hear a hundred times no until you hear one yes.
alts.zh: 在投資人這邊，是 1%。不是三分之一，是 1%。所以你會聽到一百次「不」，才會聽到一次「好」。

alts.quote: It's very hard to think strategically about the situation you're in because there isn't a science of strategy. It's not like physics. It's not like engineering where we can write down the equations of stress on a beam.
alts.zh: 要對你所處的情況做策略思考很難，因為策略沒有一門科學。它不像物理。也不像工程——工程可以直接寫下樑的應力方程式。

cards.pattern: The companies that [結果] almost always had more than [X]% [條件].
cards.quote: Whereas the companies that grew the fastest almost always had more than 40%, very disappointed.
cards.zh: 反過來說，成長最快的那些公司，幾乎每一家的「非常失望」比例都超過 40%。
cards.why: almost always 是誠實的強度標示——不是 always，也不是 sometimes。把數字掛在一群公司的共同特徵上，比掛在單一案例上難反駁得多。
cards.pmNote: 引用門檻時要一併講反面樣本，否則對方會問「那沒過門檻但成功的呢」。
cards.episode: Superhuman's secret to success: Ignoring most customer feedback, manually onboarding every new user, obsessing over every detail, and positioning around a single attribute: speed | Rahul Vohra (CEO)

alts.quote: Data is more like a compass than a GPS. If you look at data as a way of giving you the answer, you're always wrong. Wrong or slow, or sometimes both.
alts.zh: 數據比較像指南針，不是導航。如果你把數據當成會給你答案的東西，你不是錯就是慢，有時候兩者都有。

alts.quote: I like Sean Ellis's question of how disappointed would you be if this product disappeared? And I think it's if you have at least 40% of people respond that they'd be very disappointed, then you're on the right track.
alts.zh: 我喜歡 Sean Ellis 那一題：如果這個產品消失了，你會有多失望？如果至少 40% 的人回答「非常失望」，那你方向就是對的。

alts.quote: I ran the question and it came back at only 7% of users saying they'd be very disappointed without the product.
alts.zh: 我把那個問題丟出去問，結果回來只有 7% 的使用者說「沒有這個產品會非常失望」。

cards.pattern: Of these [樣本], [X]% failed to [達成目標].
cards.quote: Of these experiments, 92% failed to improve the metric that we were trying to move.
cards.zh: 這些實驗裡面，有 92% 沒能推動我們原本想推動的指標。
cards.why: Of these… 開頭先把分母講清楚，百分比才有意義；用 failed to 而不是 didn't succeed，語氣直接，是講壞數字時的標準做法。
cards.pmNote: 實驗失敗率是團隊該公開的基準線。它讓每一次成功的價值被正確定價，也讓失敗不必被隱藏。
cards.episode: The ultimate guide to A/B testing | Ronny Kohavi (Airbnb, Microsoft, Amazon)

alts.quote: In order to improve, we need to speak with those that fail, those that were unsuccessful. Because they know something that we really need to know.
alts.zh: 想要進步，我們得去找那些失敗的人談——那些沒成功的。因為他們知道一件我們非常需要知道的事。

alts.quote: The basic principle with laser is that willpower is never going to win, and there's great research on this, but for now just trust me, you're not going to white-knuckle your way through not looking at Twitter when you're trying to work.
alts.zh: laser 的基本原理是：意志力永遠贏不了。這方面有很多很好的研究，但現在你先信我——你不可能靠硬撐來讓自己工作時不看 Twitter。

alts.quote: It's about saying, okay, if we have these themes of stuff that we want to work on, what do we know with confidence because the data tells us and what do we need to understand because we don't have the data?
alts.zh: 重點是要問：在我們想做的這些主題裡，哪些是數據講得夠清楚、我們有把握的？哪些是因為沒數據，所以還得先搞懂的？

cards.pattern: It's not that [自我防衛的解釋]—[其他來源] published numbers that are around [X]%.
cards.quote: It's not that I worked at groups that were particularly bad, Booking, Google Ads, other companies published numbers that are around 80 to 90% failure rate of ideas.
cards.zh: 不是說我待的團隊特別爛——Booking、Google Ads 這些公司公開的數字，點子的失敗率也都在八到九成左右。
cards.why: 先把「是不是你們特別爛」這個質疑講出來再否掉，然後才引外部公開數字。published numbers 三個字把證據等級標成「可查證」，比 I've heard 高一階。
cards.pmNote: 自家難看的數字要放在同業公開數字旁邊講，否則它會被當成能力問題而不是行業常態。
cards.episode: The ultimate guide to A/B testing | Ronny Kohavi (Airbnb, Microsoft, Amazon)

alts.quote: Companies I've invested in is a long list, and I love to give you names of companies that don't exist anymore because it's self-serving and a horrible survivorship bias to just list the good ones.
alts.zh: 我投資過的公司名單很長，我很願意告訴你那些已經倒掉的公司名字——因為只列出成功的那些，是自利、也是很糟的倖存者偏誤。

alts.quote: And it's not bad because it's not well-intentioned, but it's bad because it's not contextual.
