alts.zh: 它不好，不是因為對方沒有善意，而是因為它沒有考慮你的處境。

alts.quote: So to be clear, I don't explicitly see quantitative numbers around this.
alts.zh: 先講清楚，我並沒有真的看到這方面的量化數字。

cards.pattern: [X]% of [對象] in our [樣本量] we studied [結論].
cards.quote: It turns out that 87% of buyers in our two and a half million sales calls we studied, either showed moderate or high levels of indecision.
cards.zh: 結果是，我們研究的兩百五十萬通銷售電話裡，有 87% 的買家表現出中度或高度的猶豫。
cards.why: 樣本量塞在主詞裡（in our two and a half million sales calls），數字跟證據強度同時出現，聽的人不必再問「你研究了幾筆」。
cards.pmNote: B2B 的最大競爭者常常不是別家，是客戶「先不決定」。這個數字把它從直覺變成可立案的問題。
cards.episode: The surprising truth about what closes deals: Insights from 2.5m sales conversations | Matt Dixon (author of The Challenger Sale and The JOLT Effect)

alts.quote: They did something recently that showed that roughly half of companies that instituted a pricing change saw at least a 25% increase in ARR.
alts.zh: 他們最近做了一份研究，顯示做過定價調整的公司裡，大概有一半 ARR 至少成長了 25%。

alts.quote: Whether Mechanical Turk has a hundred thousand Turkers or 5 million Turkers, it probably doesn't really change the experience for somebody who is using Mechanical Turk.
alts.zh: 不管 Mechanical Turk 上面有十萬個工人還是五百萬個，對使用的人來說體驗大概都一樣。

alts.quote: In fact, there's some early work on eBay that showed that if your first rating's negative, that could actually immediately cause an 8% hit on your immediate expected revenue, say nothing of long-term consequences.
alts.zh: 其實有一些早期針對 eBay 的研究顯示，如果你的第一則評價是負評，光是當下的預期營收就可能少 8%，長期的影響還沒算進去。

cards.pattern: They did something recently that showed that roughly [比例] of [對象] saw at least a [X]% increase in [指標].
cards.quote: They did something recently that showed that roughly half of companies that instituted a pricing change saw at least a 25% increase in ARR.
cards.zh: 他們最近做了一份研究，顯示做過定價調整的公司裡，大概有一半 ARR 至少成長了 25%。
cards.why: 一句話裡放兩層數字——多少比例的公司，各自拿到多少幅度；roughly 和 at least 各修飾一層，讓兩個數字的精確度分開標示。
cards.pmNote: 定價是唯一不必增加成本就能動的成長槓桿，卻是最少被碰的。這種兩層數字最適合拿來推動它。
cards.episode: How to price your product | Naomi Ionita (Menlo Ventures)

alts.quote: It turns out that 87% of buyers in our two and a half million sales calls we studied, either showed moderate or high levels of indecision.
alts.zh: 結果是，我們研究的兩百五十萬通銷售電話裡，有 87% 的買家表現出中度或高度的猶豫。

alts.quote: Now what tells me if something is seemingly an execution problem but not actually an execution problem, a sure fire way of identifying those is when you put on a bandaid and the bandaid falls.
alts.zh: 要判斷一件事表面上是執行問題、其實不是，最準的辨識法就是：你貼了 OK 繃，OK 繃掉了。

alts.quote: Whether Mechanical Turk has a hundred thousand Turkers or 5 million Turkers, it probably doesn't really change the experience for somebody who is using Mechanical Turk.
alts.zh: 不管 Mechanical Turk 上面有十萬個工人還是五百萬個，對使用的人來說體驗大概都一樣。

cards.pattern: They did a survey on over [樣本量], and they looked at for a [X]% improvement on [變數], how did it impact [結果]?
cards.quote: They did a survey once on I think it was over 500 SaaS companies, and they looked at for a 1% improvement on acquisition, retention, and monetization, how did it impact a company's bottom line?
cards.zh: 他們做過一次調查，樣本我記得是五百多家 SaaS 公司，看的是獲客、留存、變現各改善 1%，分別會怎麼影響公司的獲利。
cards.why: 把研究設計講出來（樣本量、自變數、應變數）再給結論，聽的人可以自己判斷這個數字能推到多遠；I think it was 誠實標出記憶不確定的部分。
cards.pmNote: 同樣的 1%，投在變現上的回報通常遠高於獲客。知道這個順序，資源配置的辯論會短很多。
cards.episode: How to price your product | Naomi Ionita (Menlo Ventures)

alts.quote: We would predict, based on the data that we're seeing, that over 80% of companies will miss their Q4 goals.
alts.zh: 根據我們看到的資料，我們會預測有超過八成的公司達不到第四季的目標。

alts.quote: The ultimate definition for me today of the love that somebody has for our product is they're willing to put their reputation on the line by telling people about it.
alts.zh: 對我來說，一個人有多愛你的產品，最終極的定義就是：他願意拿自己的名聲去替你背書，主動跟別人講。

alts.quote: So there's a different metric that I like to use, which keys off of this idea that I think, again, people don't appreciate, which is cancellations grow faster than marketing.
alts.zh: 我比較喜歡用另一個指標，它是從一個大家常常沒放在心上的觀念推出來的：取消的成長速度比行銷快。

cards.pattern: We found that if you went from [X] to [Y], there was an [Z]% chance [結果].
cards.quote: And we found that if you went from zero ASN to one, there was an 80% chance we saw you again in the next month.
cards.zh: 我們發現，只要你從零個好友變成一個，下個月我們再看到你的機率就有 80%。
cards.why: 把數字寫成機率而不是平均值——if…then 加 % chance 讓對方可以直接拿去做決策；we found that 是最低調的證據標籤，暗示這是資料看出來的不是猜的。
cards.pmNote: 把留存拆成「跨過某個動作門檻的機率」，比追總留存率更能指出該做什麼功能。
cards.episode: The hidden pattern behind successful products | Mark Pincus (Founder of Zynga)

alts.quote: Yeah, I mean, I can't promise that works for everyone, but again, in the very bespoke situation with Rujul, it worked really well.
alts.zh: 我不能保證這對每個人都有效，但在 Rujul 那個很特定的情況下，效果非常好。

alts.quote: If you think about your last all hands, the last talk you saw, you probably don't remember much. In fact, I wager you might only remember one thing from that talk.
alts.zh: 回想你上一次的全員大會、上一場你聽的演講——你大概記不得多少。老實說，我敢賭你只記得一件事。

alts.quote: But then, again, if I'm being honest to myself, I'm not making as good product decisions as I can.
alts.zh: 但話說回來，如果對自己誠實，我做的產品決策並沒有達到我能做到的水準。

cards.pattern: According to [來源], among [限定範圍], only [X]% [結果] [時間點].
cards.quote: According to Harvard Law School, among venture-backed companies that have the standard best practices set up that you got from your lawyer, only 20% of founders are still the CEO three years after going public.
cards.zh: 根據哈佛法學院的研究，在那些照律師標準做法設立的創投公司裡，上市三年後還在當 CEO 的創辦人只有 20%。
cards.why: 來源、範圍、數字、時間點四件事按這個順序排，每一項都在縮小這個數字適用的地方；among 那一段限定條件是關鍵——沒有它，20% 會被亂用。
cards.pmNote: 引用外部統計時，限定範圍比來源更重要。範圍不講清楚，數字很快就會被別人拿去支持相反的結論。
cards.episode: How to build a company that withstands any era | Eric Ries, Lean Startup author

alts.quote: I think there's a stat that some growth person put out there years ago, which is that on average only 20 to 30% of experiments of growth team runs might be successful.
alts.zh: 有個數字是好幾年前某個做成長的人提出來的，說平均而言成長團隊跑的實驗只有兩到三成會成功。

alts.quote: If you say, 'I think this is going to take three months to launch' and I was thinking four weeks, you're never going to hear four weeks from me, ever.
alts.zh: 如果你說「我覺得要三個月」，而我原本想的是四週，那你永遠不會從我嘴裡聽到四週。永遠不會。

alts.quote: Whenever you talk to people who are at the company, they're always try to tell you the best version of the company. It's on you to triangulate that information, but you need both sides.
alts.zh: 你去問還在公司裡的人，他們永遠給你公司最好的那個版本。要交叉比對是你自己的責任，但兩邊的說法你都得聽到。

cards.pattern: We found that [X]% of [同業] have [問題], which [後果].
cards.quote: We found that 99% of the top e-commerce sites have errors in their checkout flow that actually hinder more impactful, more seamless, quicker checkout, and therefore higher conversion with their customers.
cards.zh: 我們發現，頂尖電商網站裡有 99% 的結帳流程有錯誤，這些錯誤讓結帳沒辦法更順、更快，也就拉低了轉換率。
cards.why: 99% 這種極端數字要立刻接上「所以會怎樣」，否則聽起來像唬人；therefore 把問題連到對方在乎的指標上，數字才有行動含義。
cards.pmNote: 「連最強的同業都有這個問題」是推動體驗投資最好用的框，因為它把議題從補破洞變成搶優勢。
cards.episode: Building beautiful products with Stripe’s Head of Design | Katie Dill (Stripe, Airbnb, Lyft)

alts.quote: prospects who meet you in person have 10 to 30% higher willingness to pay than those who didn't. Churn for those folks who you meet in person is typically 20% lower than those folks who have never met you.
alts.zh: 跟你當面見過的潛在客戶，付費意願會高出 10 到 30%；見過面的客戶流失率通常比沒見過的低 20%。

alts.quote: And it comes down to this metric that standup comedians use called LPM, laughs per minute. And there's actually a benchmark that you can say.
alts.zh: 最後歸結到一個站立喜劇演員在用的指標，叫 LPM——每分鐘笑聲數。而且真的有一個基準線可以對照。

alts.quote: So as Richard Thaler put it, most people won't quit until it actually isn't a decision.
alts.zh: 就像 Richard Thaler 說的：大多數人要等到那已經不算一個選擇了，才會放手。

cards.pattern: The epiphany I had was, they had a stat, which is [X]% of [對象] don't [做某事].
cards.quote: So when Tony and Evan walked into my office originally, the epiphany I had was, well, they had a stat, which is 93% of the restaurants in the United States don't deliver.
cards.zh: Tony 跟 Evan 走進我辦公室的時候，我當下的頓悟來自他們手上一個數字：全美有 93% 的餐廳不做外送。
cards.why: they had a stat, which is… 是英文引數字最省事的接法——先宣告「接下來是一個數字」，聽的人自動切換到記憶模式。用「不做某事」的比例劃出市場空白，比講市場規模更有說服力。
cards.pmNote: 市場空白用「多少比例還沒做這件事」來描述，比 TAM 更能說服人，因為它直接對應到可觸及的供給。
cards.episode: Hard truths about building in the AI era | Keith Rabois (Khosla Ventures)

alts.quote: So there's a different metric that I like to use, which keys off of this idea that I think, again, people don't appreciate, which is cancellations grow faster than marketing.
alts.zh: 我比較喜歡用另一個指標，它是從一個大家常常沒放在心上的觀念推出來的：取消的成長速度比行銷快。

alts.quote: I think there's a stat that some growth person put out there years ago, which is that on average only 20 to 30% of experiments of growth team runs might be successful.
alts.zh: 有個數字是好幾年前某個做成長的人提出來的，說平均而言成長團隊跑的實驗只有兩到三成會成功。

alts.quote: Yeah, I mean, I can't promise that works for everyone, but again, in the very bespoke situation with Rujul, it worked really well.
alts.zh: 我不能保證這對每個人都有效，但在 Rujul 那個很特定的情況下，效果非常好。

cards.pattern: We found that [A] and [B] both get boosted by about [X]% when [條件], and it lasts [持續多久].
cards.quote: So we found the connection and productivity, they both get boosted by about 30% when you bring people together but intentionally, and it lasts them months.
cards.zh: 我們發現，連結感跟生產力兩個都會提升大約 30%，前提是你要有意識地把人聚在一起，而且效果可以持續好幾個月。
cards.why: 條件（but intentionally）和持續時間（lasts them months）才是這句真正的內容。一個百分比只講幅度，加上條件和半衰期才是可用的知識。
cards.pmNote: 遠距團隊的實體聚會要爭預算，關鍵不是「有效」，是效果能撐幾個月——那決定了該辦幾次。
cards.episode: Lessons from Atlassian: Launching new products, getting buy-in, and staying ahead of the competition | Megan Cook (head of product, Jira)

alts.quote: Whenever you talk to people who are at the company, they're always try to tell you the best version of the company. It's on you to triangulate that information, but you need both sides.
alts.zh: 你去問還在公司裡的人，他們永遠給你公司最好的那個版本。要交叉比對是你自己的責任，但兩邊的說法你都得聽到。

alts.quote: The ultimate definition for me today of the love that somebody has for our product is they're willing to put their reputation on the line by telling people about it.
alts.zh: 對我來說，一個人有多愛你的產品，最終極的定義就是：他願意拿自己的名聲去替你背書，主動跟別人講。

alts.quote: So there's a different metric that I like to use, which keys off of this idea that I think, again, people don't appreciate, which is cancellations grow faster than marketing.
alts.zh: 我比較喜歡用另一個指標，它是從一個大家常常沒放在心上的觀念推出來的：取消的成長速度比行銷快。

cards.pattern: We know that something like [X]% of [對象] are already [做某事].
cards.quote: We know that something like 92% of developers are already using AI tools.
cards.zh: 我們知道大概有 92% 的開發者已經在用 AI 工具了。
cards.why: something like 讓 92% 這種精確數字不必負全責，是引用二手數字時的安全閥；already 一個字就把數字轉成時間壓力。
cards.pmNote: 採用率高到這個程度時，該辯論的已經不是要不要導入，而是治理和標準。
cards.episode: The future of AI in software development | Inbal Shani (CPO of GitHub)

alts.quote: In order to improve, we need to speak with those that fail, those that were unsuccessful. Because they know something that we really need to know.
alts.zh: 想要進步，我們得去找那些失敗的人談——那些沒成功的。因為他們知道一件我們非常需要知道的事。

alts.quote: The true test of whether the positioning's working is, if I'm sitting across from a qualified prospect and I tell the story, does the prospect get excited and want to buy something?
alts.zh: 定位有沒有效，真正的檢驗是：我坐在一個合格的潛在客戶對面把故事講完，他會不會眼睛一亮、想買東西？

alts.quote: It's about saying, okay, if we have these themes of stuff that we want to work on, what do we know with confidence because the data tells us and what do we need to understand because we don't have the data?
alts.zh: 重點是要問：在我們想做的這些主題裡，哪些是數據講得夠清楚、我們有把握的？哪些是因為沒數據，所以還得先搞懂的？

cards.pattern: [X]% of [對象] [做 A] as opposed to [B].
cards.quote: 80% of customers buy to avoid pain or reduce risk as opposed to increased upside, which is a good thing for startup founders to understand.
cards.zh: 有 80% 的客戶是為了避免痛苦或降低風險而買，不是為了增加好處，這件事創辦人很值得理解。
cards.why: as opposed to 把百分比變成一個二選一的對照，聽的人自動算出另一邊是 20%；後面補 which is a good thing for X to understand，直接標示這個數字該被誰拿去用。
cards.pmNote: 定位文案寫成「幫你多賺」通常比寫成「幫你少賠」弱，因為買單的人多半是在解決風險。
cards.episode: What world-class GTM looks like in 2026 | Jeanne DeWitt Grosser (Vercel, Stripe, Google)

alts.quote: The true test of whether the positioning's working is, if I'm sitting across from a qualified prospect and I tell the story, does the prospect get excited and want to buy something?
alts.zh: 定位有沒有效，真正的檢驗是：我坐在一個合格的潛在客戶對面把故事講完，他會不會眼睛一亮、想買東西？

alts.quote: Never ever once have I seen a rebrand or redesign, especially of a marketing site, produce good performance results.
alts.zh: 我從來、一次都沒看過品牌重塑或改版——尤其是行銷官網——帶來好的成效數字。

alts.quote: It's about saying, okay, if we have these themes of stuff that we want to work on, what do we know with confidence because the data tells us and what do we need to understand because we don't have the data?
alts.zh: 重點是要問：在我們想做的這些主題裡，哪些是數據講得夠清楚、我們有把握的？哪些是因為沒數據，所以還得先搞懂的？

cards.pattern: Turns out [X]% of the time that [現象], it's not because of [直覺答案], but [真正原因].
cards.quote: Turns out 90% of the time that we get distracted, it's not because of what's happening outside of us, but that most distraction begins from within boredom, loneliness, fatigue, uncertainty, anxiety.
cards.zh: 結果發現，我們分心的時候有 90% 不是因為外面發生了什麼，而是分心多半從內在開始——無聊、孤單、疲倦、不確定、焦慮。
cards.why: turns out 是英文裡「我本來也以為不是這樣」的信號，用它開頭，數字自帶反直覺的框；not because of A but B 的對照句型讓 90% 有了指向，而不只是一個大小。
cards.pmNote: 問題歸因錯了，解法一定錯。把分心歸到外部觸發，做出來的就是封鎖 App 這種沒用的功能。
cards.episode: Strategies for becoming less distracted and improving focus | Nir Eyal (author of Indistractable and Hooked)

alts.quote: And it's not bad because it's not well-intentioned, but it's bad because it's not contextual.
alts.zh: 它不好，不是因為對方沒有善意，而是因為它沒有考慮你的處境。

alts.quote: It's about saying, okay, if we have these themes of stuff that we want to work on, what do we know with confidence because the data tells us and what do we need to understand because we don't have the data?
alts.zh: 重點是要問：在我們想做的這些主題裡，哪些是數據講得夠清楚、我們有把握的？哪些是因為沒數據，所以還得先搞懂的？

alts.quote: So when it's a ratio and you decrease the denominator, the value of the ratio grows. And so, how do you decrease the denominator in this case where time is the denominator is you start working on things that take less time.
alts.zh: 這是一個比值，分母變小，比值就變大。那在這裡分母是時間，你要怎麼讓分母變小？你就開始挑那些花比較少時間的事情做。

cards.pattern: I can tell you that [X]% of people that [做 A] actually [做 B].
cards.quote: But I can tell you that 98% of people that write opportunities write them as solutions.
cards.zh: 我可以跟你說，寫「機會」的人裡面有 98% 其實寫的是解法。
cards.why: I can tell you that 是把自己的經驗當證據來源，等於說「這個數字沒有論文，但我看過夠多」。用在你有大量一手觀察、卻拿不出研究的時候。
cards.pmNote: 機會和解法混寫，會讓探索直接跳到執行。這是機會樹最常見的失敗模式。
cards.episode: Teresa Torres on how to interview customers, automating continuous discovery, the opportunity solution tree framework, making the case for user research, common interviewing mistakes, and much more

alts.quote: Whenever you talk to people who are at the company, they're always try to tell you the best version of the company. It's on you to triangulate that information, but you need both sides.
alts.zh: 你去問還在公司裡的人，他們永遠給你公司最好的那個版本。要交叉比對是你自己的責任，但兩邊的說法你都得聽到。

alts.quote: You could have all the usage data in the world, that's going to tell you what's actually happening in your product, but it doesn't tell you why.
alts.zh: 就算你握有全世界的使用數據，它只會告訴你產品裡實際發生了什麼，不會告訴你為什麼。

alts.quote: Number one is actually measuring it. I can't tell you how many times I suggest to a founder to track cohorts and that's a new thing.
alts.zh: 第一件事其實是去量它。我真的數不清有多少次我建議創辦人追蹤 cohort，結果那對他們是全新的東西。

cards.pattern: There's a stat that [模糊來源] put out there years ago, which is that on average only [X]% [結果].
cards.quote: I think there's a stat that some growth person put out there years ago, which is that on average only 20 to 30% of experiments of growth team runs might be successful.
cards.zh: 有個數字是好幾年前某個做成長的人提出來的，說平均而言成長團隊跑的實驗只有兩到三成會成功。
cards.why: 來源記不清時就照實說 some growth person… years ago，反而比硬掰出處可信；might 掛在句尾再降一階強度——這是引用弱證據的完整配套。
cards.pmNote: 拿不確定的行業數字當背景可以，但別拿它當決策依據。標示清楚，別人才知道能靠多重。
cards.episode: Relentless curiosity, radical accountability, and HubSpot’s winning growth formula | Christopher Miller (VP of Product, Growth and AI)

alts.quote: So there's a different metric that I like to use, which keys off of this idea that I think, again, people don't appreciate, which is cancellations grow faster than marketing.
alts.zh: 我比較喜歡用另一個指標，它是從一個大家常常沒放在心上的觀念推出來的：取消的成長速度比行銷快。

alts.quote: According to Harvard Law School, among venture-backed companies that have the standard best practices set up that you got from your lawyer, only 20% of founders are still the CEO three years after going public.
alts.zh: 根據哈佛法學院的研究，在那些照律師標準做法設立的創投公司裡，上市三年後還在當 CEO 的創辦人只有 20%。

alts.quote: In fact, there's some early work on eBay that showed that if your first rating's negative, that could actually immediately cause an 8% hit on your immediate expected revenue, say nothing of long-term consequences.
alts.zh: 其實有一些早期針對 eBay 的研究顯示，如果你的第一則評價是負評，光是當下的預期營收就可能少 8%，長期的影響還沒算進去。

cards.pattern: According to [具名研究者], [X]% of [對象] [結果] because of [原因].
cards.quote: And it turns out that according to Noam, Noam Wasserstein, 65% of startups fail because of conflict with founders or the founding team.
cards.zh: 根據 Noam Wasserstein 的研究，有 65% 的新創是死在創辦人或創始團隊之間的衝突。
cards.why: 具名到人（而不只是「有研究指出」）是提高證據等級最便宜的方法；名字唸兩次是口語裡自然的自我修正，不必怕。
cards.pmNote: 創辦人衝突的殺傷力遠高於一般人以為的。共同創辦協議該在還很好的時候就談。
cards.episode: Scripts for difficult conversations: Giving hard feedback, navigating defensiveness, the three questions you should end every meeting with, more | Alisa Cohn (executive coach)

alts.quote: In order to improve, we need to speak with those that fail, those that were unsuccessful. Because they know something that we really need to know.
alts.zh: 想要進步，我們得去找那些失敗的人談——那些沒成功的。因為他們知道一件我們非常需要知道的事。

alts.quote: Turns out 90% of the time that we get distracted, it's not because of what's happening outside of us, but that most distraction begins from within boredom, loneliness, fatigue, uncertainty, anxiety.
alts.zh: 結果發現，我們分心的時候有 90% 不是因為外面發生了什麼，而是分心多半從內在開始——無聊、孤單、疲倦、不確定、焦慮。

alts.quote: It's not because my life is more interesting. It's because I have a better lens and I understand what to look for.
alts.zh: 不是因為我的生活變得比較精彩，是因為我的鏡頭變好了，我知道該找什麼。

cards.pattern: If [條件] [X]% of the time, you [結果 A]—than if it's [Y]%, versus [Z]%.
cards.quote: If the model gets it right 60% of the time, you build a very different product than if the model gets it right 95% of the time versus if the model gets it right 99.5% of the time.
cards.zh: 如果模型有六成的時候會做對，你做出來的產品，跟九成五、跟九成九點五的時候，會是完全不同的三個產品。
cards.why: 三個數字排成階梯，論點不是任何一個數字，而是「跨過某條線後性質會變」。重複整個 if 子句三次在中文會顯得囉唆，在英文口語裡是刻意的節奏，讓聽的人跟上每一階。
cards.pmNote: AI 產品設計的第一個問題是準確率落在哪一段，因為那決定要不要有人審、能不能自動執行。
cards.episode: OpenAI’s CPO on how AI changes must-have skills, moats, coding, startup playbooks, more | Kevin Weil (CPO at OpenAI, ex-Instagram, Twitter)

alts.quote: We heard a couple comments from them, it was little murmurs. And I didn't realize at the time that was the signal that we did not have product market fit.
alts.zh: 我們只聽到他們零星幾句抱怨，就是一點小碎念而已。我當時沒意識到，那正是我們沒有 PMF 的訊號。

alts.quote: I think Peter Thiel actually says it more simply and elegantly, which is, 'You need to be right about something that other people think you're wrong about for a very long time.'
alts.zh: 我覺得 Peter Thiel 講得更簡潔漂亮：「你得在一件別人認為你錯的事情上，長時間地正確。」

alts.quote: I like Sean Ellis's question of how disappointed would you be if this product disappeared? And I think it's if you have at least 40% of people respond that they'd be very disappointed, then you're on the right track.
alts.zh: 我喜歡 Sean Ellis 那一題：如果這個產品消失了，你會有多失望？如果至少 40% 的人回答「非常失望」，那你方向就是對的。

cards.pattern: People don't realize there's a big difference between moving from [X] to [Y] to [Z].
cards.quote: I think people don't realize that there's a big difference between moving from 80% performance to 90% performance to 99% performance to 99.9% performance, and so on, and so on.
cards.zh: 我覺得大家沒意識到，從 80% 做到 90%、再到 99%、再到 99.9%，這幾段之間的差距有多大。
cards.why: 用一串遞增的數字取代「後面愈來愈難」這個抽象說法；people don't realize 開頭先把對方放在「你可能沒想過」的位置，數字才不像在說教。
cards.pmNote: 最後那幾個 9 的成本通常是前面全部的好幾倍。訂品質目標時要先問這個產品真的需要幾個 9。
cards.episode: The 100-person AI lab that became Anthropic and Google's secret weapon | Edwin Chen (Surge AI)

alts.quote: So there's a different metric that I like to use, which keys off of this idea that I think, again, people don't appreciate, which is cancellations grow faster than marketing.
alts.zh: 我比較喜歡用另一個指標，它是從一個大家常常沒放在心上的觀念推出來的：取消的成長速度比行銷快。

alts.quote: The best comparison I can give is, there is a world of difference between reading a report about a lime cook and then standing with a lime cook.
alts.zh: 我能給的最好對照是：讀一份關於廚房廚師的報告，跟真的站在他旁邊，是天差地遠的兩件事。

alts.quote: I think Peter Thiel actually says it more simply and elegantly, which is, 'You need to be right about something that other people think you're wrong about for a very long time.'
alts.zh: 我覺得 Peter Thiel 講得更簡潔漂亮：「你得在一件別人認為你錯的事情上，長時間地正確。」

cards.pattern: We saw [X] to [Y]% drops in [指標] in A-B tests when showing [A] with or without [B].
cards.quote: We saw more like 30 to 40% engagement rate drops for likes and reposts in A-B tests we were ran when showing a post with or without a note, which is just crazy big.
cards.zh: 我們在 A/B 測試裡看到的比較像是 30 到 40% 的互動率下降，就是按讚跟轉發，比較有掛註記跟沒掛註記的貼文——這個幅度大得誇張。
cards.why: in A-B tests… with or without 把量測方法直接寫進句子，是證據等級最高的講法之一；more like 放在數字前，表示他在修正剛剛被講出來的較小數字。
cards.pmNote: 內容治理功能要證明有效，只能靠對照組。沒有 with or without 的比較，效果永遠說不清。
cards.episode: An inside look at X’s Community Notes | Keith Coleman (VP of Product) and Jay Baxter (ML Lead)

alts.quote: I ran the question and it came back at only 7% of users saying they'd be very disappointed without the product.
alts.zh: 我把那個問題丟出去問，結果回來只有 7% 的使用者說「沒有這個產品會非常失望」。

alts.quote: So there's a different metric that I like to use, which keys off of this idea that I think, again, people don't appreciate, which is cancellations grow faster than marketing.
alts.zh: 我比較喜歡用另一個指標，它是從一個大家常常沒放在心上的觀念推出來的：取消的成長速度比行銷快。

alts.quote: It's not a statistically significant survey in general, but it will never go to 99% and one. That's fairly indicative that people are clicking the links, which surprises me.
alts.zh: 這份調查在統計上不算顯著，但它也不可能是 99 比 1。這蠻能說明大家真的有在點那些連結——這讓我有點意外。

cards.pattern: There's some early work on [對象] that showed that if [條件], that could cause an [X]% hit on [指標].
cards.quote: In fact, there's some early work on eBay that showed that if your first rating's negative, that could actually immediately cause an 8% hit on your immediate expected revenue, say nothing of long-term consequences.
cards.zh: 其實有一些早期針對 eBay 的研究顯示，如果你的第一則評價是負評，光是當下的預期營收就可能少 8%，長期的影響還沒算進去。
cards.why: some early work 誠實標示這是初步研究，所以配 could 而不是 will；say nothing of… 收尾把「還有沒量到的部分」講出來，讓 8% 變成下限而不是全貌。
cards.pmNote: 雙邊市場的新供給方最脆弱的就是前幾筆評價。這是新手保護機制值得做的量化依據。
cards.episode: Marketplace lessons from Uber, Airbnb, Bumble, and more | Ramesh Johari (Stanford professor, startup advisor)

alts.quote: And it comes down to this metric that standup comedians use called LPM, laughs per minute. And there's actually a benchmark that you can say.
alts.zh: 最後歸結到一個站立喜劇演員在用的指標，叫 LPM——每分鐘笑聲數。而且真的有一個基準線可以對照。

alts.quote: I think there's a stat that some growth person put out there years ago, which is that on average only 20 to 30% of experiments of growth team runs might be successful.
alts.zh: 有個數字是好幾年前某個做成長的人提出來的，說平均而言成長團隊跑的實驗只有兩到三成會成功。

alts.quote: Some of my colleagues also did a paper that showed that you can do certain tasks, like build an HTTP server 50% faster, but I don't think that's what productivity's about when you're using an AI tool, frankly.
alts.zh: 我有些同事也做過一篇論文，顯示某些任務——像是架一個 HTTP server——可以快 50%，但老實說我不覺得用 AI 工具談生產力是在談這個。

cards.pattern: We did an analysis where one out of [X] [對象] drive roughly [Y]% of [結果].
cards.quote: So we did an analysis where one out of 20 landing pages drive roughly 85% of all your traffic.
cards.zh: 我們做過一個分析，每二十個到達頁裡面就有一個帶來了大約 85% 的全站流量。
cards.why: 一句話同時用「幾分之幾」和「百分比」兩種數字——前者講數量少，後者講影響大，兩個一撞就是集中度；roughly 只掛在需要它的那一個上。
cards.pmNote: SEO 的產出高度集中。把力氣平均分給所有頁面，是最常見也最貴的錯誤。
cards.episode: The ultimate guide to AEO: How to get ChatGPT to recommend your product | Ethan Smith (Graphite)

alts.quote: Now this is where I'm data informed, and I'm not data driven.
alts.zh: 這就是我所謂的「被數據啟發」，而不是「被數據驅動」。

alts.quote: I had a spreadsheet that I maintained for the first year of the publication, where I listed, for every article, how much did my annual revenue go up a week later. So tracking what was the impact.
alts.zh: 電子報第一年我維護了一份表，把每一篇文章對應到一週後年營收增加了多少。就是在追蹤 impact。

alts.quote: If you think about your last all hands, the last talk you saw, you probably don't remember much. In fact, I wager you might only remember one thing from that talk.
alts.zh: 回想你上一次的全員大會、上一場你聽的演講——你大概記不得多少。老實說，我敢賭你只記得一件事。

cards.pattern: [某人] did a paper that showed [X]% faster on [具體任務], but I don't think that's what [大概念] is about.
cards.quote: Some of my colleagues also did a paper that showed that you can do certain tasks, like build an HTTP server 50% faster, but I don't think that's what productivity's about when you're using an AI tool, frankly.
cards.zh: 我有些同事也做過一篇論文，顯示某些任務——像是架一個 HTTP server——可以快 50%，但老實說我不覺得用 AI 工具談生產力是在談這個。
cards.why: 先把對自己不利的數字完整講出來，再劃界說它量的不是重點。這比質疑數字本身有力，因為你沒有否認資料，你否認的是它的適用範圍。
cards.pmNote: 用單一任務加速當生產力證據，會讓團隊去優化那個任務。指標選錯，行為就會跟著錯。
cards.episode: How to measure AI developer productivity in 2025 | Nicole Forsgren

alts.quote: So there's a different metric that I like to use, which keys off of this idea that I think, again, people don't appreciate, which is cancellations grow faster than marketing.
alts.zh: 我比較喜歡用另一個指標，它是從一個大家常常沒放在心上的觀念推出來的：取消的成長速度比行銷快。

alts.quote: It's very hard to think strategically about the situation you're in because there isn't a science of strategy. It's not like physics. It's not like engineering where we can write down the equations of stress on a beam.
alts.zh: 要對你所處的情況做策略思考很難，因為策略沒有一門科學。它不像物理。也不像工程——工程可以直接寫下樑的應力方程式。

alts.quote: I think there's a stat that some growth person put out there years ago, which is that on average only 20 to 30% of experiments of growth team runs might be successful.
alts.zh: 有個數字是好幾年前某個做成長的人提出來的，說平均而言成長團隊跑的實驗只有兩到三成會成功。

cards.pattern: For people who [做了 A], [X]% [結果]，versus [Y]% who didn't.
cards.quote: And for people who completed a quiz, 53% of them went on to purchase versus 37% who didn't complete.
cards.zh: 有做完測驗的人，後來有 53% 去購買；沒做完的只有 37%。
cards.why: versus 後面那個對照組是整句的重點。只給 53% 沒有意義，兩個數字並排才構成證據——中文常只講前半，英文職場預期你把對照組一起端出來。
cards.pmNote: 這種相關性不等於因果：也可能本來就想買的人才會做完測驗。要主張因果得靠隨機分派。
cards.episode: Using behavioral science to improve your product | Kristen Berman (Irrational Labs)

alts.quote: prospects who meet you in person have 10 to 30% higher willingness to pay than those who didn't. Churn for those folks who you meet in person is typically 20% lower than those folks who have never met you.
alts.zh: 跟你當面見過的潛在客戶，付費意願會高出 10 到 30%；見過面的客戶流失率通常比沒見過的低 20%。

alts.quote: Whenever you talk to people who are at the company, they're always try to tell you the best version of the company. It's on you to triangulate that information, but you need both sides.
alts.zh: 你去問還在公司裡的人，他們永遠給你公司最好的那個版本。要交叉比對是你自己的責任，但兩邊的說法你都得聽到。

alts.quote: And I think it's if you have at least 40% of people respond that they'd be very disappointed, then you're on the right track.
alts.zh: 如果至少有 40% 的人回答「沒有這個東西會非常失望」，那你方向是對的。

cards.pattern: We would predict, based on the data that we're seeing, that over [X]% of [對象] will [結果].
cards.quote: We would predict, based on the data that we're seeing, that over 80% of companies will miss their Q4 goals.
cards.zh: 根據我們看到的資料，我們會預測有超過八成的公司達不到第四季的目標。
cards.why: based on the data that we're seeing 這個插入語把預測跟資料綁在一起，同時 we're seeing 的現在進行式暗示資料還在變。講未來的數字時，這是既有底氣又留餘地的標準做法。
cards.pmNote: 對外做預測要把資料來源和時效講清楚，否則猜錯一次，之後所有數字都會被打折。
cards.episode: How to hit revenue targets in a recession | Sahil Mansuri (Bravado)

alts.quote: They did a survey once on I think it was over 500 SaaS companies, and they looked at for a 1% improvement on acquisition, retention, and monetization, how did it impact a company's bottom line?
alts.zh: 他們做過一次調查，樣本我記得是五百多家 SaaS 公司，看的是獲客、留存、變現各改善 1%，分別會怎麼影響公司的獲利。

alts.quote: Data is more like a compass than a GPS. If you look at data as a way of giving you the answer, you're always wrong. Wrong or slow, or sometimes both.
alts.zh: 數據比較像指南針，不是導航。如果你把數據當成會給你答案的東西，你不是錯就是慢，有時候兩者都有。

alts.quote: Now this is where I'm data informed, and I'm not data driven.
alts.zh: 這就是我所謂的「被數據啟發」，而不是「被數據驅動」。

cards.pattern: [大數字], which is equivalent to [換算成有感的單位].
cards.quote: $1.4 trillion flows through Stripe annually, which is equivalent to over 1% of the entire global GDP.
cards.zh: 每年有 1.4 兆美元流經 Stripe，相當於全球 GDP 的 1% 以上。
cards.why: 1.4 兆這種數字大到沒有感覺，which is equivalent to 把它換算成一個人腦掂量得動的比例。凡是超過人腦尺度的數字，英文都預期你附一個換算。
cards.pmNote: 介紹來賓或公司規模時，換算比原始數字有用。聽眾記得住的是比例，不是位數。
cards.episode: 35 years of product design wisdom from Apple, Disney, Pinterest, and beyond | Bob Baxley

alts.quote: The basic principle with laser is that willpower is never going to win, and there's great research on this, but for now just trust me, you're not going to white-knuckle your way through not looking at Twitter when you're trying to work.
alts.zh: laser 的基本原理是：意志力永遠贏不了。這方面有很多很好的研究，但現在你先信我——你不可能靠硬撐來讓自己工作時不看 Twitter。

alts.quote: I have custom software that I've written that will say, 'Okay, here are the points at which the audience laughed.' Actually audibly laughed. That's the only way it counts.
alts.zh: 我自己寫了一套軟體，會告訴我「聽眾在哪些點笑了」。是真的出聲笑。只有出聲才算。

alts.quote: I now use, I'm an investor, so I'm biased, but Aura, A-U-R-A, which is a marketplace app.
alts.zh: 我現在用的是——我有投資，所以我立場不中立——Aura，A-U-R-A，一個市集型的 app。

cards.pattern: That's one out of [X], that's a [Y]% [指標名稱].
cards.quote: That's one out of 10, that's a 10% win rate.
cards.zh: 那就是十次成一次，也就是 10% 的成交率。
cards.why: 同一件事講兩次，第二次換成一個有名字的指標（win rate）——這一步把體感翻譯成可以拿去比較的東西。開會時把對方隨口講的次數當場換算成率，是很強的一招。
cards.pmNote: 把軼事換算成率，是讓討論從「感覺如何」跳到「跟基準比如何」最快的方法。
cards.episode: "Sell the alpha, not the feature": The enterprise sales playbook for $1M to $10M ARR | Jen Abel

alts.quote: And in that case, it was from about a 50% hit rate to 65. So that's pretty huge, so that's a really big difference.
alts.zh: 那個案例是命中率從大約 50% 提到 65%。這個差距其實非常大。

alts.quote: They tend to have accomplished very difficult goals in very hostile environments. And it turns out that when you're starting a somewhat chaotic tech company, that's actually a very useful skill to have.
alts.zh: 這些人習慣在極度不友善的環境裡把很難的目標做出來。結果發現，開一家有點混亂的科技公司，這剛好是非常有用的能力。

alts.quote: You could have all the usage data in the world, that's going to tell you what's actually happening in your product, but it doesn't tell you why.
alts.zh: 就算你握有全世界的使用數據，它只會告訴你產品裡實際發生了什麼，不會告訴你為什麼。

cards.pattern: So that's like a [X]%-plus reduction in [指標].
cards.quote: So that's like a 90%-plus reduction in total cost there.
cards.zh: 所以那大概是總成本降低九成以上。
cards.why: 別人講完一長串細節後，用 so that's like a…% 把它收成一個數字，等於幫全場做結論；-plus 後綴表示「至少」，讓你在不確定精確值時仍敢講。
cards.pmNote: 會議裡最有價值的動作之一，是把別人的敘述當場收成一個可記的數字。沒人做，那段討論就白開。
cards.episode: What world-class GTM looks like in 2026 | Jeanne DeWitt Grosser (Vercel, Stripe, Google)

alts.quote: Wait, reduction of cognitive load." Maybe even if 10% of people get confused to get 90% of people far faster through this process is a big win and a great opportunity cost trade off.
alts.zh: 就算有 10% 的人會被搞混，只要能讓 90% 的人快很多地走完這個流程，那還是大勝，機會成本上很划算。

alts.quote: I have custom software that I've written that will say, 'Okay, here are the points at which the audience laughed.' Actually audibly laughed. That's the only way it counts.
alts.zh: 我自己寫了一套軟體，會告訴我「聽眾在哪些點笑了」。是真的出聲笑。只有出聲才算。

alts.quote: That often comes in the form of an interesting anecdote or a data point that's going to support that, or a story that's going to add emotion or illustrate it.
alts.zh: 那通常會以一個有趣的軼事、一個支撐它的數據點、或一個能加上情緒或具體說明的故事的形式出現。

cards.pattern: [指標 A] is less than [X], [指標 B] is greater than [Y].
cards.quote: Regretted churn's less than 10%, NRR is greater than 110%.
cards.zh: 後悔型流失低於 10%，淨收入留存高於 110%。
cards.why: 用 less than / greater than 把兩個指標寫成一組門檻，句子短到像規格表。講標準時不給區間、只給邊界，對方才知道自己過了沒。
cards.pmNote: 把「產品市場契合」寫成一組可查的門檻，才能停掉那種每季重來一次的定性辯論。
cards.episode: A framework for finding product-market fit | Todd Jackson (First Round Capital)

alts.quote: It's not because my life is more interesting. It's because I have a better lens and I understand what to look for.
alts.zh: 不是因為我的生活變得比較精彩，是因為我的鏡頭變好了，我知道該找什麼。

alts.quote: They tend to have accomplished very difficult goals in very hostile environments. And it turns out that when you're starting a somewhat chaotic tech company, that's actually a very useful skill to have.
alts.zh: 這些人習慣在極度不友善的環境裡把很難的目標做出來。結果發現，開一家有點混亂的科技公司，這剛好是非常有用的能力。

alts.quote: So don't confuse posting press releases even on very big websites with actual success.
alts.zh: 所以不要把「新聞稿被大網站登出來」跟真正的成功搞混。

cards.pattern: It's got to be north of [X], ideally like more than [Y].
cards.quote: It's got to be north of 5%, ideally like more than 7%.
cards.zh: 至少要在 5% 以上，理想的話最好超過 7%。
cards.why: north of 是商業口語裡「高於」的說法，比 above 更有份量；先給及格線再給理想線，兩個數字分工——一個是拒絕的依據，一個是努力的方向。
cards.pmNote: 訂目標同時給及格線和理想線，團隊才不會把理想線當唯一標準，然後每季都覺得自己失敗。
cards.episode: How to grow a subscription business | Yuriy Timen (Grammarly, Canva, Airtable)

alts.quote: And it's not bad because it's not well-intentioned, but it's bad because it's not contextual.
alts.zh: 它不好，不是因為對方沒有善意，而是因為它沒有考慮你的處境。

alts.quote: It's about saying, okay, if we have these themes of stuff that we want to work on, what do we know with confidence because the data tells us and what do we need to understand because we don't have the data?
alts.zh: 重點是要問：在我們想做的這些主題裡，哪些是數據講得夠清楚、我們有把握的？哪些是因為沒數據，所以還得先搞懂的？

alts.quote: If you tell someone, 'This is the problem I'm going to address,' and they will tell you, 'Oh, I know someone that has this problem,' it's not a real problem.
alts.zh: 如果你跟人說「這是我要解決的問題」，對方回你「喔，我知道有誰有這個問題」——那它就不是真問題。

cards.pattern: I'll actually call out that only [X]% of people reported that [反面情況].
cards.quote: And I'll actually call out, first of all, that only 3% of people reported that AI hasn't shifted their identity.
cards.zh: 我想特別點出來一件事：只有 3% 的人回報說 AI 沒有動搖他們的職業認同。
cards.why: 從反面切——不講 97% 的人受影響，而是講只有 3% 沒受影響。同一份資料換個方向講，衝擊完全不同；I'll call out 是主動點名一個數字，等於告訴聽眾「這個要記」。
cards.pmNote: 同一份資料的正反兩種講法都不算造假，但會導向不同的行動。挑哪一面講本身就是主張。
cards.episode: How tech workers actually feel about AI in 2026 | Annual AI sentiment survey (Noam Segal)

alts.quote: In fact, there's some early work on eBay that showed that if your first rating's negative, that could actually immediately cause an 8% hit on your immediate expected revenue, say nothing of long-term consequences.
alts.zh: 其實有一些早期針對 eBay 的研究顯示，如果你的第一則評價是負評，光是當下的預期營收就可能少 8%，長期的影響還沒算進去。

alts.quote: I have custom software that I've written that will say, 'Okay, here are the points at which the audience laughed.' Actually audibly laughed. That's the only way it counts.
alts.zh: 我自己寫了一套軟體，會告訴我「聽眾在哪些點笑了」。是真的出聲笑。只有出聲才算。

alts.quote: If you think about your last all hands, the last talk you saw, you probably don't remember much. In fact, I wager you might only remember one thing from that talk.
alts.zh: 回想你上一次的全員大會、上一場你聽的演講——你大概記不得多少。老實說，我敢賭你只記得一件事。

cards.pattern: When we do surveys, we'd find that [X], [Y], [Z]% of people [反應].
cards.quote: And when we do surveys, we'd find that 20, 30, 40% of people thought they were officially associated because how they were using our logo and presenting the brand and everything like that was very confusing to people.
cards.zh: 我們做調查的時候會發現，兩成、三成、四成的人以為他們跟我們有官方關係，因為他們用我們 logo 和呈現品牌的方式讓人很混淆。
cards.why: 連丟三個數字（20, 30, 40）不是含糊，是在講「每次調查的結果都落在這個範圍」。重複做的量測要用區間報，硬給單一數字反而不誠實。
cards.pmNote: 品牌混淆是可以量的。量出來才有辦法判斷商標維權該投多少資源。
cards.episode: The creator of WordPress opens up about becoming an internet villain, why he’s taking a stand, and the future of open source | Matt Mullenweg (founder and CEO, Automattic)

alts.quote: People aren't even getting to the third screen. They're stuck on the first screen because they can't even find the button that we think is so dead obvious.
alts.zh: 使用者根本走不到第三個畫面。他們卡在第一個畫面，因為連我們自認為超級明顯的那顆按鈕都找不到。

alts.quote: Well, to be clear about my brand promise, because it's true, every word that has my name on it, I wrote.
alts.zh: 先把我的品牌承諾講清楚：每一個掛我名字的字，都是我寫的。

alts.quote: The ultimate definition for me today of the love that somebody has for our product is they're willing to put their reputation on the line by telling people about it.
alts.zh: 對我來說，一個人有多愛你的產品，最終極的定義就是：他願意拿自己的名聲去替你背書，主動跟別人講。

cards.pattern: It's dropped by about half from [年] to [年], and since then has come back to about [X]% of the peak, adjusted for [口徑].
cards.quote: And so it's dropped by about half from 2000 to 2015 or so, and since then has come back to about 75% of the peak, adjusted for inflation.
cards.zh: 它從 2000 年到 2015 年左右大約掉了一半，之後回到高點的七成五左右，這是通膨調整後的數字。
cards.why: 兩段趨勢、一個基準點（the peak）、一個口徑註記（adjusted for inflation）。最後那三個字是專業與否的分水嶺——它先回答了內行人一定會問的問題。
cards.pmNote: 跨十年的數字沒有調整口徑就等於沒調整。先講口徑，別人才會信你其他的數字。
cards.episode: A rational conversation on where AI is actually going | Benedict Evans

alts.quote: Whenever you talk to people who are at the company, they're always try to tell you the best version of the company. It's on you to triangulate that information, but you need both sides.
alts.zh: 你去問還在公司裡的人，他們永遠給你公司最好的那個版本。要交叉比對是你自己的責任，但兩邊的說法你都得聽到。

alts.quote: It's not a statistically significant survey in general, but it will never go to 99% and one. That's fairly indicative that people are clicking the links, which surprises me.
alts.zh: 這份調查在統計上不算顯著，但它也不可能是 99 比 1。這蠻能說明大家真的有在點那些連結——這讓我有點意外。

alts.quote: If you create value, they will come back. If they're not coming back, that means that you are not creating value.
alts.zh: 如果你創造了價值，他們會回來。如果他們沒回來，那就代表你沒創造價值。

cards.pattern: Depending on whose numbers you want to believe, [X] to [Y]% of [對象] [結果].
cards.quote: And what Lomi does is you take your food scraps, and it turns out that depending on whose numbers you want to believe, in America, we throw away somewhere between 40 to 60% of our food.
cards.zh: 看你要相信誰的數字，在美國我們大概丟掉四成到六成的食物。
cards.why: depending on whose numbers you want to believe 是最誠實的引用法——承認各家統計不一致，然後給區間。這樣講反而讓人相信你查過不只一個來源。
cards.pmNote: 市場規模的估計本來就分歧。給區間並說明分歧來源，比挑一個對自己最有利的數字安全。
cards.episode: How to become a category pirate | Christopher Lochhead (author of Play Bigger, Niche Down, Category Pirates, more)

alts.quote: I want to be clear that I had seen that idea somewhere else, someone else, a blog post about it or something like that.
alts.zh: 我想講清楚，那個點子我是在別的地方看到的，是別人寫的一篇部落格之類的。

alts.quote: It's not that I worked at groups that were particularly bad, Booking, Google Ads, other companies published numbers that are around 80 to 90% failure rate of ideas.
alts.zh: 不是說我待的團隊特別爛——Booking、Google Ads 這些公司公開的數字，點子的失敗率也都在八到九成左右。

alts.quote: It turns out that 87% of buyers in our two and a half million sales calls we studied, either showed moderate or high levels of indecision.
alts.zh: 結果是，我們研究的兩百五十萬通銷售電話裡，有 87% 的買家表現出中度或高度的猶豫。

cards.pattern: Even if [X]% of people [代價], to get [Y]% of people [好處] is a big win.
cards.quote: Wait, reduction of cognitive load." Maybe even if 10% of people get confused to get 90% of people far faster through this process is a big win and a great opportunity cost trade off.
cards.zh: 就算有 10% 的人會被搞混，只要能讓 90% 的人快很多地走完這個流程，那還是大勝，機會成本上很划算。
cards.why: 把取捨寫成兩個百分比的交換，代價先講、收益後講；even if 開頭表示你已經先承認了對方會提的反對意見。
cards.pmNote: 設計決策卡住時，多半是因為沒人願意講出「我們接受多少人被犧牲」。把它寫成數字，決策才做得下去。
cards.episode: Lessons on building product sense, navigating AI, optimizing the first mile, and making it through the messy middle | Scott Belsky (Adobe, Behance)

alts.quote: So there's a different metric that I like to use, which keys off of this idea that I think, again, people don't appreciate, which is cancellations grow faster than marketing.
alts.zh: 我比較喜歡用另一個指標，它是從一個大家常常沒放在心上的觀念推出來的：取消的成長速度比行銷快。

alts.quote: The basic principle with laser is that willpower is never going to win, and there's great research on this, but for now just trust me, you're not going to white-knuckle your way through not looking at Twitter when you're trying to work.
alts.zh: laser 的基本原理是：意志力永遠贏不了。這方面有很多很好的研究，但現在你先信我——你不可能靠硬撐來讓自己工作時不看 Twitter。

alts.quote: People aren't even getting to the third screen. They're stuck on the first screen because they can't even find the button that we think is so dead obvious.
alts.zh: 使用者根本走不到第三個畫面。他們卡在第一個畫面，因為連我們自認為超級明顯的那顆按鈕都找不到。

cards.pattern: The way [大家原本學的做法] is what I call [兩三個字的貶義命名].
cards.quote: And the traditional structure, the way I learned how to pitch in business school, I think the way most people did is what I call the arrogant doctor.
cards.zh: 而傳統的結構，也就是我在商學院學到的提案方式，我想大部分人學到的也是——我把它叫做「傲慢的醫生」。
cards.why: 先把對方熟悉的做法完整描述一遍，最後才丟出命名。名字是貶義的（arrogant doctor），一旦全場接受這個詞，舊做法就自帶羞恥感，你不必再逐點反駁。
cards.pmNote: 要淘汰一個舊做法，替它取一個難聽的名字比列舉它的缺點有效。
cards.episode: The power of strategic narrative | Andy Raskin

alts.quote: If you're trying to do it, the best way to tell a story about something that you want people to understand is to do what I call speaking with adjacency, which means we're not going to match content to content.
alts.zh: 如果你想讓別人理解某件事，最好的說故事方式是我所謂的「用鄰近性說話」——意思是我們不會拿內容去對內容。

alts.quote: It doesn't matter if you think Bloomberg or Trump should be president. Do you think everyone should have access to great education? Most people would say yes.
alts.zh: 你覺得該讓 Bloomberg 還是 Trump 當總統，都無所謂。你覺得每個人都該有機會受好的教育嗎？大多數人會說會。

alts.quote: I call this habit “gossiping” to AI, because I fill in my copilot the same way I’d lean over and vent to a colleague sitting next to me.
alts.zh: 我把這個習慣叫做對 AI「講八卦」，因為我更新我的副駕的方式，就跟我側身跟隔壁同事抱怨一樣。

cards.pattern: And I call this shift the shift from [舊狀態] to [新狀態].
cards.quote: And I call this shift the shift from the old game to the new game.
cards.zh: 我把這個轉變稱為「從舊遊戲到新遊戲」的轉變。
cards.why: 命名的不是東西，是「轉變」本身。A→B 的兩詞對比讓聽眾自動站到 B 那一邊——沒有人想留在 old game。
cards.pmNote: 策略敘事的第一步不是講產品，是先讓所有人同意世界變了。
cards.episode: The power of strategic narrative | Andy Raskin

alts.quote: I often use this analogy of if you're doing a home renovation, you can have the most beautiful rendering of the new bedroom. But if you haven't checked if there's electricity in that wall there or not, it's going to drastically change the cost and the time and everything.
alts.zh: 我常用一個比喻：你在裝修房子，臥室的效果圖可以做得美到不行。但如果你沒去確認那面牆裡到底有沒有電線，成本跟時間都會整個變樣。

alts.quote: In the book, I call it the force that no one controls, but everyone obeys.
alts.zh: 在書裡，我把它叫做「沒有人控制、但所有人都服從的那股力量」。

alts.quote: I always say you should have, what I call an elephant at the beginning of the story, which is actually a big spaceship shooting at a little spaceship or a police officer chasing a guy across a roof.
alts.zh: 我一直說你應該在故事開頭放一隻我稱為「大象」的東西——實際上就是一艘大太空船在射一艘小太空船，或是警察在屋頂上追一個人。

cards.pattern: That is what I call [命名], and it's really important to distinguish between [好的那個] and [壞的那個].
cards.quote: That is what I call obnoxious aggression, and it's really important to distinguish between radical candor and obnoxious aggression.
cards.zh: 那個我稱之為「討人厭的攻擊」，而區分「徹底坦率」跟「討人厭的攻擊」非常重要。
cards.why: 命名之後立刻加一句「這兩個一定要分清楚」，把自己的詞升格成一組必要的分類工具；聽的人不接受這個詞，就沒辦法繼續討論下去。
cards.pmNote: 兩個概念被混為一談時，PM 的第一步是分別替它們命名。
cards.episode: Radical Candor: From theory to practice with author Kim Scott

alts.quote: And the difference between v0 and a lot of other tools is that yes, you do have the code and code is very important, but I call it code last rather than code first.
alts.zh: v0 跟很多工具的差別在於：對，你確實有程式碼，程式碼也很重要，但我把它叫做「程式碼最後」而不是「程式碼優先」。

alts.quote: Also, price is not just the number on the webpage. It's easy to think that, but how it's structured is just as important, how the product's positioned is just as important.
alts.zh: 還有，價格不是只有網頁上那個數字。很容易這樣以為，但怎麼收費、產品怎麼定位，重要程度完全一樣。

alts.quote: Right now we kind of have this dichotomy between what I call investor controlled companies and founder controlled companies.
alts.zh: 我們現在有一個二分：我稱之為「投資人控制的公司」跟「創辦人控制的公司」。

cards.pattern: I call it [A] and not [B] because if I [用 B 會發生的具體場景], I'm implying [難堪的言外之意].
cards.quote: To me, I call it candor and not truth because if I march into a room and I say, "Lenny, I'm going to tell you the truth." I'm kind of implying I've got a pipeline to God and you don't know anything.
cards.zh: 對我來說，我叫它「坦率」而不是「真相」，因為如果我走進一個房間說：「Lenny，我要告訴你真相。」我等於在暗示我有一條直通上帝的專線，而你什麼都不懂。
cards.why: 用「我叫它 A 不叫 B」直接處理選詞，再演一段用錯詞會有多難看。命名的理由用場景演出來，比解釋定義更有說服力。
cards.episode: Radical Candor: From theory to practice with author Kim Scott

alts.quote: So there's, I wouldn't say a checklist, but there's a series of questions that I asked to diagnose why is growth slowing in this order, because it's one of these things where the first one that's a problem, if you don't fix that, it doesn't matter if you fix one of the ones below.
alts.zh: 我不會說那是一張檢查清單，但我確實有一組問題，會照順序問下去診斷成長為什麼變慢——因為只要最前面那個沒修，後面修再多都沒用。

alts.quote: I often say most communication in business is round white and flavorless, intentionally so, because a lot of people are afraid to stand out.
alts.zh: 我常說，商業場合的溝通大多是圓的、白的、沒有味道的——而且是故意的，因為大家都怕突出。

alts.quote: Let's just say there's a product manager and nobody's ever coached this poor person, and so they really don't know much.
alts.zh: 我們就假設有一個產品經理，從來沒有人帶過他，所以他其實懂得不多。

cards.pattern: I call it the [名詞] that [沒人做得到的事], but [大家都在做的事].
cards.quote: In the book, I call it the force that no one controls, but everyone obeys.
cards.zh: 在書裡，我把它叫做「沒有人控制、但所有人都服從的那股力量」。
cards.why: 名字本身就是一句完整的描述，聽一次就記住。一個內建矛盾的長名字，往往比一個生硬的縮寫更容易傳播。
cards.episode: How to build a company that withstands any era | Eric Ries, Lean Startup author

alts.quote: It doesn't matter if you think Bloomberg or Trump should be president. Do you think everyone should have access to great education? Most people would say yes.
alts.zh: 你覺得該讓 Bloomberg 還是 Trump 當總統，都無所謂。你覺得每個人都該有機會受好的教育嗎？大多數人會說會。

alts.quote: And the traditional structure, the way I learned how to pitch in business school, I think the way most people did is what I call the arrogant doctor.
alts.zh: 而傳統的結構，也就是我在商學院學到的提案方式，我想大部分人學到的也是——我把它叫做「傲慢的醫生」。

alts.quote: I always say you should have, what I call an elephant at the beginning of the story, which is actually a big spaceship shooting at a little spaceship or a police officer chasing a guy across a roof.
alts.zh: 我一直說你應該在故事開頭放一隻我稱為「大象」的東西——實際上就是一艘大太空船在射一艘小太空船，或是警察在屋頂上追一個人。

cards.pattern: Right now we have this dichotomy between what I call [A 型] and [B 型].
cards.quote: Right now we kind of have this dichotomy between what I call investor controlled companies and founder controlled companies.
cards.zh: 我們現在有一個二分：我稱之為「投資人控制的公司」跟「創辦人控制的公司」。
cards.why: 先宣告「現在只有這兩個選項」，再各給一個名字——這一步是為了下一句端出第三種。命名一組二分法，是為了讓你的新選項有位置站。
cards.pmNote: 提新方案前先把現有選項命名並窮舉，新方案才不會被當成第 N 個雜訊。
cards.episode: How to build a company that withstands any era | Eric Ries, Lean Startup author

alts.quote: The way to summarize that is if you look at all the startup stories that we have at YC and all the companies we funded over all the years, the underlying theme is that rationally the founder should have given up at some point.
alts.zh: 要總結的話：如果你看 YC 所有的創業故事、這些年投的所有公司，底下共通的主題是——照理性判斷，創辦人早就該在某個時間點放棄了。

alts.quote: That is what I call obnoxious aggression, and it's really important to distinguish between radical candor and obnoxious aggression.
alts.zh: 那個我稱之為「討人厭的攻擊」，而區分「徹底坦率」跟「討人厭的攻擊」非常重要。

alts.quote: So Google missed the opportunity of social mobile apps like WhatsApp, like Snapchat, etc and for me this story kind of was the epitome of what I call today, opinion-based development.
alts.zh: Google 錯過了 WhatsApp、Snapchat 這類社交手機 app 的機會，對我來說這個故事就是我今天所說的「意見驅動開發」的極致代表。

cards.pattern: We have what I call the [法則名], which is a situation where [一句話定義].
cards.quote: We have what I call the law of sustainable growth, which is a situation where new customers come as a natural side effect of the actions of past customers.
cards.zh: 我們有一個我稱之為「可持續成長法則」的東西，指的是新客戶會是舊客戶行為的自然副產品。
cards.why: 名字取得像物理定律（the law of...），再用 which is a situation where 一句話定義。取名成 law，暗示這不是意見而是規律。
cards.episode: Reflections on a movement | Eric Ries (creator of the Lean Startup methodology)

alts.quote: So we did this recent reorg where now we have what I call the fast thinking group, which officially is called AI platform, but it really means we want to just ship a bunch of new capabilities on a near weekly basis.
alts.zh: 我們最近重組，現在有一個我叫做「快思考小組」的團隊，正式名稱是 AI 平台，但它真正的意思是我們想每週左右就出一批新能力。

alts.quote: So there's, I wouldn't say a checklist, but there's a series of questions that I asked to diagnose why is growth slowing in this order, because it's one of these things where the first one that's a problem, if you don't fix that, it doesn't matter if you fix one of the ones below.
alts.zh: 我不會說那是一張檢查清單，但我確實有一組問題，會照順序問下去診斷成長為什麼變慢——因為只要最前面那個沒修，後面修再多都沒用。

alts.quote: I call it a LinkedIn crush where you're really excited to post the job on LinkedIn, but you're deeply unexcited about doing the job.
alts.zh: 我把它叫做「LinkedIn 迷戀」——你超級興奮想把那個職缺 po 上 LinkedIn，但對真的去做那份工作完全提不起勁。

cards.pattern: I have this notion of what I call [自創詞].
cards.quote: I have this notion of what I call SoloWare.
cards.zh: 我有一個概念，我把它叫做 SoloWare（單人軟體）。
cards.why: notion 這個字先幫你降低風險——我不是在下定義，只是有個概念。台灣人講自創詞常直接丟出來，加上 I have this notion of 會讓對方願意聽完再判斷。
cards.episode: Zigging vs. zagging: How HubSpot built a $30B company | Dharmesh Shah (co-founder/CTO)

alts.quote: So in positioning work we call this competitive alternatives.
alts.zh: 在定位這門工作裡，我們把這個叫做「競爭替代方案」。

alts.quote: We call it sugar-coated broccoli.
alts.zh: 我們把它叫做「糖衣花椰菜」。

alts.quote: We call it internally the hamster wheel of content creation.
alts.zh: 我們內部把它叫做「內容生產的倉鼠滾輪」。

cards.pattern: This story was the epitome of what I call [X-based 命名].
cards.quote: So Google missed the opportunity of social mobile apps like WhatsApp, like Snapchat, etc and for me this story kind of was the epitome of what I call today, opinion-based development.
cards.zh: Google 錯過了 WhatsApp、Snapchat 這類社交手機 app 的機會，對我來說這個故事就是我今天所說的「意見驅動開發」的極致代表。
cards.why: 先講一個大家都知道的失敗案例，再把它命名成一類病（opinion-based development）。案例當證據、命名當結論，順序不能反。
cards.episode: Becoming evidence-guided | Itamar Gilad (Gmail, YouTube, Microsoft)

alts.quote: To me, I call it candor and not truth because if I march into a room and I say, "Lenny, I'm going to tell you the truth." I'm kind of implying I've got a pipeline to God and you don't know anything.
alts.zh: 對我來說，我叫它「坦率」而不是「真相」，因為如果我走進一個房間說：「Lenny，我要告訴你真相。」我等於在暗示我有一條直通上帝的專線，而你什麼都不懂。

alts.quote: Right now we kind of have this dichotomy between what I call investor controlled companies and founder controlled companies.
alts.zh: 我們現在有一個二分：我稱之為「投資人控制的公司」跟「創辦人控制的公司」。

alts.quote: So we can accidentally spend a lot of our time thinking about features that are very deep in the user adoption journey. And so we can kind of end up oversolving for that.
alts.zh: 我們很容易不小心把時間都花在使用者旅程很後段的功能上，結果就在那一段過度投入了。

cards.pattern: But it's not what I call the [術語], the [術語] measures [你的定義].
cards.quote: But it's not what I call the North Star metric, the North Star metric measures how much value we create for the market.
cards.zh: 但那不是我說的北極星指標；北極星指標衡量的是我們為市場創造了多少價值。
cards.why: 別人已經在用這個詞、但用錯了，這句是把詞搶回來的標準做法：先否認對方的用法，馬上補上自己的定義。
cards.pmNote: 團隊誤用術語時，糾正定義比糾正結論有效。
cards.episode: Becoming evidence-guided | Itamar Gilad (Gmail, YouTube, Microsoft)

alts.quote: I think that the issue is, it's not just about product market fit, it is about achieving a product market pricing fit.
alts.zh: 我覺得問題在於：重點不只是 product-market fit，而是要做到 product-market-pricing fit。

alts.quote: That is what I call obnoxious aggression, and it's really important to distinguish between radical candor and obnoxious aggression.
alts.zh: 那個我稱之為「討人厭的攻擊」，而區分「徹底坦率」跟「討人厭的攻擊」非常重要。

alts.quote: The way I learned how to pitch in business school, and I think the way most people did, is what I call the arrogant doctor.
alts.zh: 我在商學院學到的提案方式——我想大部分人學的也是——就是我說的「傲慢醫生」那一套。

cards.pattern: In [領域] work we call this [術語].
cards.quote: So in positioning work we call this competitive alternatives.
cards.zh: 在定位這門工作裡，我們把這個叫做「競爭替代方案」。
cards.why: 用 we 而不是 I，把命名說成整個專業社群的共識，聽的人比較不會覺得是你臨時發明的。短短一句就把對話拉進你的地盤。
cards.episode: April Dunford on product positioning, segmentation, and optimizing your sales process

alts.quote: I have this notion of what I call SoloWare.
alts.zh: 我有一個概念，我把它叫做 SoloWare（單人軟體）。

alts.quote: We call it sugar-coated broccoli.
alts.zh: 我們把它叫做「糖衣花椰菜」。

alts.quote: We call it internally the hamster wheel of content creation.
alts.zh: 我們內部把它叫做「內容生產的倉鼠滾輪」。

cards.pattern: We call this the [命名] because this person's job is to [職責].
cards.quote: We call this the champion in the account because this person, their job is to get consensus and champion the deal across everybody, including their boss, who's the actual economic buyer, the person that writes the check.
cards.zh: 我們把這個人叫做「客戶內部的擁護者」，因為他的工作就是在所有人之間建立共識、替這筆案子背書，包括他的老闆——那個真正掏錢的經濟決策者。
cards.why: 命名一個角色，用 because 把職責講清楚，順便把另一個角色（economic buyer）也一併定義。一句話建立兩個座標，之後討論就有共同語言。
cards.pmNote: 複雜的採購流程要先把角色命名，才談得下去。
cards.episode: April Dunford on product positioning, segmentation, and optimizing your sales process

alts.quote: I call it a LinkedIn crush where you're really excited to post the job on LinkedIn, but you're deeply unexcited about doing the job.
alts.zh: 我把它叫做「LinkedIn 迷戀」——你超級興奮想把那個職缺 po 上 LinkedIn，但對真的去做那份工作完全提不起勁。

alts.quote: And we are, I mean we are busy, but we call it the busy bandwagon because it feels like you should be busy.
alts.zh: 我們確實很忙，但我們把它叫做「忙碌從眾車」，因為那感覺就像你應該要很忙。

alts.quote: I call it sort of a half-built strategy because too much strategy ties you down and too little strategy, you're too responsive to everything.
alts.zh: 我把它叫做某種「蓋一半的策略」，因為策略太多會把你綁死，策略太少你又會什麼都想回應。

cards.pattern: I call it a [命名] where you're really excited to [表面的動作], but you're deeply unexcited about [真正的工作].
cards.quote: I call it a LinkedIn crush where you're really excited to post the job on LinkedIn, but you're deeply unexcited about doing the job.
cards.zh: 我把它叫做「LinkedIn 迷戀」——你超級興奮想把那個職缺 po 上 LinkedIn，但對真的去做那份工作完全提不起勁。
cards.why: 名字帶畫面（LinkedIn crush），定義用「對 X 超興奮、對 Y 完全沒勁」的反差把毛病點破。被講中的人會笑，而不是防衛。
cards.pmNote: 招人前先確認你想要的是這個職位，還是只想要「有這個職位」這件事。
cards.episode: The high-growth handbook: Molly Graham’s frameworks for leading through chaos, change, and scale

alts.quote: We call this Right for Wrong, doing the right thing for the wrong reason, where the right thing may be completing the flow, but the wrong reason is seeing that error message go away.
alts.zh: 我們把這個叫做「對事錯因」——用錯誤的理由做對的事。對的事可能是完成流程，錯的理由是想讓那個錯誤訊息消失。

alts.quote: One of the things that I think when you're doing interviewing, one way to think about it, I call it home court, away court, neutral court, you want interviews to balance in all those different spheres.
alts.zh: 面試的時候有一個思考方式，我把它叫做「主場、客場、中立場」，你會希望面試在這幾個場域之間取得平衡。

alts.quote: You just feel more like you're running through mud like, "Ah, God, we're just still doing so much work and it's not having as much of an impact."
alts.zh: 那種感覺比較像在爛泥裡跑步——「天啊，我們明明還是做了這麼多事，但影響力就是沒以前大。」

cards.pattern: At [公司], I would have to have what I called a [命名] with someone where I would see them start to [徵兆].
cards.quote: At Facebook in particular, I would find that every so often I would have to have what I called a Legos talk with someone where I would just see them start to ask these questions like, why are we hiring that person?
cards.zh: 特別是在 Facebook，我發現每隔一陣子就得跟某個人來一場我叫做「樂高談話」的對話——我會看到他們開始問：我們為什麼要招那個人？
cards.why: 命名一種「反覆發生的對話」，並用觸發它的徵兆來定義。名字加上觸發時機，別人下次遇到就知道該開哪一場會。
cards.episode: The high-growth handbook: Molly Graham’s frameworks for leading through chaos, change, and scale

alts.quote: But weirdly, it was like you see the videos where there's the mushroom cloud in the distance. You see it. But you don't hear, or notice it.
alts.zh: 但很怪，那感覺就像影片裡遠方升起的蘑菇雲。你看得見。可是你聽不到，也沒真的感覺到。

alts.quote: Over the course of our life, because of all these little situations that happen, we start getting bugs in the software and we're not really upgrading our software.
alts.zh: 在人生的過程裡，因為發生了各種小事，我們的軟體開始長 bug，而我們也沒有真的在更新它。

alts.quote: It's a bit like this really smart intern that refuses to read Slack and doesn't check Datadog or Sentry unless you ask it to.
alts.zh: 它有點像一個超聰明、但死不看 Slack、你不叫他他就不會去看 Datadog 或 Sentry 的實習生。

cards.pattern: We call it [具體意象的複合詞].
cards.quote: We call it sugar-coated broccoli.
cards.zh: 我們把它叫做「糖衣花椰菜」。
cards.why: 五個字的一句話，兩個具體名詞疊出張力（好吃的糖衣＋沒人想吃的花椰菜）。把抽象概念壓成兩個能吃能看的東西，是命名最強的形式。
cards.episode: Notion’s lost years, its near collapse during Covid, staying small to move fast, the joy and suffering of building horizontal, more | Ivan Zhao (CEO and co-founder)

alts.quote: I have this notion of what I call SoloWare.
alts.zh: 我有一個概念，我把它叫做 SoloWare（單人軟體）。

alts.quote: So in positioning work we call this competitive alternatives.
alts.zh: 在定位這門工作裡，我們把這個叫做「競爭替代方案」。

alts.quote: We call it internally the hamster wheel of content creation.
alts.zh: 我們內部把它叫做「內容生產的倉鼠滾輪」。

cards.pattern: We call it internally the [意象] of [你要批評的事].
cards.quote: We call it internally the hamster wheel of content creation.
cards.zh: 我們內部把它叫做「內容生產的倉鼠滾輪」。
cards.why: internally 這個字很有用——它暗示這是自家人私下的講法，比正式術語更可信，也更容易被對方借去用。
cards.episode: Monetizing passions, scaling marketplaces, and stories from a creator economy vet | Camille Hearst (Spotify, Patreon, Apple, YouTube)

alts.quote: I have this notion of what I call SoloWare.
alts.zh: 我有一個概念，我把它叫做 SoloWare（單人軟體）。

alts.quote: So in positioning work we call this competitive alternatives.
alts.zh: 在定位這門工作裡，我們把這個叫做「競爭替代方案」。

alts.quote: We call it sugar-coated broccoli.
