cards.pattern: We call it the [命名] because it feels like you should [大家默認該做的事].
cards.quote: And we are, I mean we are busy, but we call it the busy bandwagon because it feels like you should be busy.
cards.zh: 我們確實很忙，但我們把它叫做「忙碌從眾車」，因為那感覺就像你應該要很忙。
cards.why: 先承認事實（我們是真的忙），再命名那個機制，最後用 because it feels like 指出它是感覺不是事實。三步走完，批評就不像抱怨。
cards.episode: Making time for what matters | Jake Knapp and John Zeratsky (authors of Sprint and Make Time, co-founders of Character Capital)

alts.quote: We call this the champion in the account because this person, their job is to get consensus and champion the deal across everybody, including their boss, who's the actual economic buyer, the person that writes the check.
alts.zh: 我們把這個人叫做「客戶內部的擁護者」，因為他的工作就是在所有人之間建立共識、替這筆案子背書，包括他的老闆——那個真正掏錢的經濟決策者。

alts.quote: I call it sort of a half-built strategy because too much strategy ties you down and too little strategy, you're too responsive to everything.
alts.zh: 我把它叫做某種「蓋一半的策略」，因為策略太多會把你綁死，策略太少你又會什麼都想回應。

alts.quote: So I purposely chose the word complicit because complicit does not mean responsible, and that's a really important distinction.
alts.zh: 我是刻意選「共謀」這個詞的，因為共謀不等於負責，這個區別非常重要。

cards.pattern: We call this [簡稱], [完整定義], where [A] may be [例子], but [B] is [例子].
cards.quote: We call this Right for Wrong, doing the right thing for the wrong reason, where the right thing may be completing the flow, but the wrong reason is seeing that error message go away.
cards.zh: 我們把這個叫做「對事錯因」——用錯誤的理由做對的事。對的事可能是完成流程，錯的理由是想讓那個錯誤訊息消失。
cards.why: 命名→展開定義→各給一個例子，三層一次講完。簡稱先出手，是為了讓後面的例子有東西可以掛。
cards.pmNote: 行為數據看起來達標，動機可能完全不是你以為的那個。
cards.episode: Using behavioral science to improve your product | Kristen Berman (Irrational Labs)

alts.quote: One of the things that I think when you're doing interviewing, one way to think about it, I call it home court, away court, neutral court, you want interviews to balance in all those different spheres.
alts.zh: 面試的時候有一個思考方式，我把它叫做「主場、客場、中立場」，你會希望面試在這幾個場域之間取得平衡。

alts.quote: I call it a LinkedIn crush where you're really excited to post the job on LinkedIn, but you're deeply unexcited about doing the job.
alts.zh: 我把它叫做「LinkedIn 迷戀」——你超級興奮想把那個職缺 po 上 LinkedIn，但對真的去做那份工作完全提不起勁。

alts.quote: So we did this recent reorg where now we have what I call the fast thinking group, which officially is called AI platform, but it really means we want to just ship a bunch of new capabilities on a near weekly basis.
alts.zh: 我們最近重組，現在有一個我叫做「快思考小組」的團隊，正式名稱是 AI 平台，但它真正的意思是我們想每週左右就出一批新能力。

cards.pattern: They need to lean into what I call [反直覺命名], which is [用一個問句定義].
cards.quote: And I think they really need to lean into what I call lazy leadership, which is how do I get away from the things I hate as quickly as humanly possible?
cards.zh: 我覺得他們真的該擁抱我說的「懶惰式領導」——也就是：我要怎麼用人類可能最快的速度，擺脫我討厭的那些事？
cards.why: 把一個貶義詞拿來當褒義（lazy leadership），再用第一人稱問句定義它。問句定義比名詞定義好記，因為可以直接拿去問自己。
cards.episode: I’ve run 75+ businesses. Here’s why you’re probably chasing the wrong idea. | Andrew Wilkinson (co‑founder of Tiny)

alts.quote: One of the things that I think when you're doing interviewing, one way to think about it, I call it home court, away court, neutral court, you want interviews to balance in all those different spheres.
alts.zh: 面試的時候有一個思考方式，我把它叫做「主場、客場、中立場」，你會希望面試在這幾個場域之間取得平衡。

alts.quote: The way I learned how to pitch in business school, and I think the way most people did, is what I call the arrogant doctor.
alts.zh: 我在商學院學到的提案方式——我想大部分人學的也是——就是我說的「傲慢醫生」那一套。

alts.quote: And so I think a lot of it comes down to not the things you try, but how you deeply understand the problem that's preventing someone from using your product effectively.
alts.zh: 所以我覺得關鍵不在你試了哪些招，而在你有多深地搞懂「是什麼擋住使用者用好你的產品」。

cards.pattern: I call it a [命名] because too much [X] [壞處], and too little [X], [另一個壞處].
cards.quote: I call it sort of a half-built strategy because too much strategy ties you down and too little strategy, you're too responsive to everything.
cards.zh: 我把它叫做某種「蓋一半的策略」，因為策略太多會把你綁死，策略太少你又會什麼都想回應。
cards.why: 要命名一個中庸的位置很難，她用「兩邊都太糟」把中間那塊撐出來。sort of 是保護色，讓這個半成品的名字聽起來像思考中而不是定論。
cards.episode: The ultimate guide to OKRs | Christina Wodtke (Stanford)

alts.quote: We call this the champion in the account because this person, their job is to get consensus and champion the deal across everybody, including their boss, who's the actual economic buyer, the person that writes the check.
alts.zh: 我們把這個人叫做「客戶內部的擁護者」，因為他的工作就是在所有人之間建立共識、替這筆案子背書，包括他的老闆——那個真正掏錢的經濟決策者。

alts.quote: I call it a LinkedIn crush where you're really excited to post the job on LinkedIn, but you're deeply unexcited about doing the job.
alts.zh: 我把它叫做「LinkedIn 迷戀」——你超級興奮想把那個職缺 po 上 LinkedIn，但對真的去做那份工作完全提不起勁。

alts.quote: And we are, I mean we are busy, but we call it the busy bandwagon because it feels like you should be busy.
alts.zh: 我們確實很忙，但我們把它叫做「忙碌從眾車」，因為那感覺就像你應該要很忙。

cards.pattern: This is a trick, I call this the [命名].
cards.quote: This is a trick, I call this the brain transplant.
cards.zh: 這是個小技巧，我把它叫做「腦移植」。
cards.why: 先說 This is a trick 把期待值降到「小撇步」，再丟一個誇張的名字。低承諾＋高記憶點的組合，最容易被別人拿去複述。
cards.episode: From skeptic to true believer: How OpenClaw changed my life | Claire Vo

alts.quote: I have this notion of what I call SoloWare.
alts.zh: 我有一個概念，我把它叫做 SoloWare（單人軟體）。

alts.quote: So in positioning work we call this competitive alternatives.
alts.zh: 在定位這門工作裡，我們把這個叫做「競爭替代方案」。

alts.quote: We call it sugar-coated broccoli.
alts.zh: 我們把它叫做「糖衣花椰菜」。

cards.pattern: Yes, you do have [X] and [X] is important, but I call it [X] last rather than [X] first.
cards.quote: And the difference between v0 and a lot of other tools is that yes, you do have the code and code is very important, but I call it code last rather than code first.
cards.zh: v0 跟很多工具的差別在於：對，你確實有程式碼，程式碼也很重要，但我把它叫做「程式碼最後」而不是「程式碼優先」。
cards.why: 先讓步（對，我們也有 code），再把爭點從「有沒有」換成「順序」。命名成 X last rather than X first，一句話就把整個產品定位講完。
cards.pmNote: 產品差異化講不清楚時，試著把比較軸從「有無」換成「先後」。
cards.episode: Everyone’s an engineer now: Inside v0’s mission to create a hundred million builders | Guillermo Rauch (founder and CEO of Vercel, creators of v0 and Next.js)

alts.quote: That is what I call obnoxious aggression, and it's really important to distinguish between radical candor and obnoxious aggression.
alts.zh: 那個我稱之為「討人厭的攻擊」，而區分「徹底坦率」跟「討人厭的攻擊」非常重要。

alts.quote: Right now we kind of have this dichotomy between what I call investor controlled companies and founder controlled companies.
alts.zh: 我們現在有一個二分：我稱之為「投資人控制的公司」跟「創辦人控制的公司」。

alts.quote: Then finally I did what I call the cocktail party test, which is to look at the cocktail parties and to watch how people pitch your product to other people.
alts.zh: 最後我做了一件我叫做「雞尾酒會測試」的事——去看那些雞尾酒會，觀察別人怎麼把你的產品推薦給其他人。

cards.pattern: We have what I call the [綽號], which officially is called [正式名稱], but it really means [實際目的].
cards.quote: So we did this recent reorg where now we have what I call the fast thinking group, which officially is called AI platform, but it really means we want to just ship a bunch of new capabilities on a near weekly basis.
cards.zh: 我們最近重組，現在有一個我叫做「快思考小組」的團隊，正式名稱是 AI 平台，但它真正的意思是我們想每週左右就出一批新能力。
cards.why: 同時給三層：綽號、正式名、真正在幹嘛。綽號負責記憶、正式名負責對外、but it really means 負責講真話。
cards.pmNote: 組織命名要能同時對外交代、對內動員，通常需要兩個名字。
cards.episode: How we restructured Airtable’s entire org for AI | Howie Liu (co-founder and CEO)

alts.quote: We have what I call the law of sustainable growth, which is a situation where new customers come as a natural side effect of the actions of past customers.
alts.zh: 我們有一個我稱之為「可持續成長法則」的東西，指的是新客戶會是舊客戶行為的自然副產品。

alts.quote: We call this Right for Wrong, doing the right thing for the wrong reason, where the right thing may be completing the flow, but the wrong reason is seeing that error message go away.
alts.zh: 我們把這個叫做「對事錯因」——用錯誤的理由做對的事。對的事可能是完成流程，錯的理由是想讓那個錯誤訊息消失。

alts.quote: One of the things that I think when you're doing interviewing, one way to think about it, I call it home court, away court, neutral court, you want interviews to balance in all those different spheres.
alts.zh: 面試的時候有一個思考方式，我把它叫做「主場、客場、中立場」，你會希望面試在這幾個場域之間取得平衡。

cards.pattern: You should have what I call [意象命名], which is [兩個具體畫面].
cards.quote: I always say you should have, what I call an elephant at the beginning of the story, which is actually a big spaceship shooting at a little spaceship or a police officer chasing a guy across a roof.
cards.zh: 我一直說你應該在故事開頭放一隻我稱為「大象」的東西——實際上就是一艘大太空船在射一艘小太空船，或是警察在屋頂上追一個人。
cards.why: 命名之後不給定義、直接給兩個畫面。概念很抽象時，兩個具體例子比一句定義更能讓人抓到邊界。
cards.episode: How to tell better stories | Matthew Dicks (Storyworthy)

alts.quote: I'd say that was the beginning of chapter two where it was we went from the company that could do no wrong to the company that could do no right, which was a big flip.
alts.zh: 我會說那就是第二章的開始——我們從「怎麼做都對」的公司，變成「怎麼做都錯」的公司，整個翻過來。

alts.quote: Which is you bring a fruit to the reviewer and say, "Hey, here's a mango, what do you think?" And the reviewer says, "I actually don't like mangoes."
alts.zh: 你拿一個水果去給主管看：「欸，這是芒果，你覺得怎樣？」主管說：「我其實不喜歡芒果。」

alts.quote: As a very simple example, sorry, this is a little bit dark, but how restaurants want to turn over tables as fast as possible in order to maximize for the day? Hospitals actually want to do the same with patients.
alts.zh: 舉個很簡單的例子——抱歉這個講法有點黑暗——餐廳希望翻桌越快越好，好把一天的收益拉高。醫院對病床其實也是同一件事。

cards.pattern: The best way to [目標] is to do what I call [動名詞命名], which means we're not going to [大家會做的事].
cards.quote: If you're trying to do it, the best way to tell a story about something that you want people to understand is to do what I call speaking with adjacency, which means we're not going to match content to content.
cards.zh: 如果你想讓別人理解某件事，最好的說故事方式是我所謂的「用鄰近性說話」——意思是我們不會拿內容去對內容。
cards.why: which means 後面接的是「不做什麼」而不是「做什麼」。用否定來定義，聽的人會自己去猜正確答案，注意力反而更集中。
cards.episode: How to tell better stories | Matthew Dicks (Storyworthy)

alts.quote: You want to be that tree in the storm that is not so rigid that if the wind is too strong it's going to break in half, but not so flexible that it's going to swing every which direction as soon as there's a gust.
alts.zh: 你要當風暴裡的那棵樹——不要硬到風一大就攔腰折斷，也不要軟到一陣風來就往每個方向亂晃。

alts.quote: They're going to be like, 'Oh, well, it sounds like you put in your best effort.' But if you walk away early, people are like, 'What?'
alts.zh: 他們會說：「喔，聽起來你已經盡力了。」但如果你提早收手，大家的反應會是：「蛤？」

alts.quote: They said, "By the way, this is not a digital process yet. We're going to FedEx you an envelope and inside it is going to be the thing for you to sign.
alts.zh: 他們說：「先說一下，這段流程還沒有數位化。我們會用 FedEx 寄一個信封給你，裡面就是要請你簽名的文件。」

cards.pattern: And before you know it, you have what I call a [縫合怪命名].
cards.quote: And before you know it, you have what I call a Franken deck.
cards.zh: 然後你還沒回過神，就得到一份我叫做「科學怪人簡報」的東西。
cards.why: before you know it 把責任推給流程而不是人，接著用一個滑稽的名字收尾。批評別人的產出時，先讓它聽起來像自然而然發生的意外。
cards.episode: Pattern Breakers: How to find a breakthrough startup idea | Mike Maples, Jr. (Founding Partner at Floodgate, ex-Product at Silicon Graphics)

alts.quote: To me, I call it candor and not truth because if I march into a room and I say, "Lenny, I'm going to tell you the truth." I'm kind of implying I've got a pipeline to God and you don't know anything.
alts.zh: 對我來說，我叫它「坦率」而不是「真相」，因為如果我走進一個房間說：「Lenny，我要告訴你真相。」我等於在暗示我有一條直通上帝的專線，而你什麼都不懂。

alts.quote: The way I learned how to pitch in business school, and I think the way most people did, is what I call the arrogant doctor.
alts.zh: 我在商學院學到的提案方式——我想大部分人學的也是——就是我說的「傲慢醫生」那一套。

alts.quote: The problem is not like what should my goal be or how should I figure out what to do with my life? They usually know, but it's very hard to actually make time for those things.
alts.zh: 問題不在於「我的目標該是什麼」或「我這輩子要幹嘛」。這個大家其實都知道。問題是很難真的挪出時間去做那些事。

cards.pattern: I did what I call the [場景] test, which is to [具體動作].
cards.quote: Then finally I did what I call the cocktail party test, which is to look at the cocktail parties and to watch how people pitch your product to other people.
cards.zh: 最後我做了一件我叫做「雞尾酒會測試」的事——去看那些雞尾酒會，觀察別人怎麼把你的產品推薦給其他人。
cards.why: 把一個做法命名成 test，它就從個人習慣升格成可複製的方法。which is to 後面一定要接動作，不然名字撐不住。
cards.pmNote: 定性訊號也可以制度化：命名它、寫下步驟，它才會被重複執行。
cards.episode: Superhuman's secret to success: Ignoring most customer feedback, manually onboarding every new user, obsessing over every detail, and positioning around a single attribute: speed | Rahul Vohra (CEO)

alts.quote: The way I learned how to pitch in business school, and I think the way most people did, is what I call the arrogant doctor.
alts.zh: 我在商學院學到的提案方式——我想大部分人學的也是——就是我說的「傲慢醫生」那一套。

alts.quote: I think most people don't like product managers often because they haven't experienced good product managers.
alts.zh: 我覺得多數人不喜歡 PM，多半是因為他們沒遇過真正好的 PM。

alts.quote: We have what I call the law of sustainable growth, which is a situation where new customers come as a natural side effect of the actions of past customers.
alts.zh: 我們有一個我稱之為「可持續成長法則」的東西，指的是新客戶會是舊客戶行為的自然副產品。

cards.pattern: One way to think about it, I call it [A], [B], [C], you want [事情] to balance across all of them.
cards.quote: One of the things that I think when you're doing interviewing, one way to think about it, I call it home court, away court, neutral court, you want interviews to balance in all those different spheres.
cards.zh: 面試的時候有一個思考方式，我把它叫做「主場、客場、中立場」，你會希望面試在這幾個場域之間取得平衡。
cards.why: 一次命名三個位置，而且借用大家都懂的球賽比喻。三分法比二分法更難被反駁，因為它看起來像盤點而不是立場。
cards.episode: The rituals of great teams | Shishir Mehrotra of Coda, YouTube, Microsoft

alts.quote: And I think they really need to lean into what I call lazy leadership, which is how do I get away from the things I hate as quickly as humanly possible?
alts.zh: 我覺得他們真的該擁抱我說的「懶惰式領導」——也就是：我要怎麼用人類可能最快的速度，擺脫我討厭的那些事？

alts.quote: We call this Right for Wrong, doing the right thing for the wrong reason, where the right thing may be completing the flow, but the wrong reason is seeing that error message go away.
alts.zh: 我們把這個叫做「對事錯因」——用錯誤的理由做對的事。對的事可能是完成流程，錯的理由是想讓那個錯誤訊息消失。

alts.quote: The way I learned how to pitch in business school, and I think the way most people did, is what I call the arrogant doctor.
alts.zh: 我在商學院學到的提案方式——我想大部分人學的也是——就是我說的「傲慢醫生」那一套。

cards.pattern: We call it the [意象] technique because we think [背後的信念].
cards.quote: We call it the bow and arrow technique because we think you can only remember one thing out of a talk and that it's very powerful to go through that framework or that kind of thinking when you're building a talk.
cards.zh: 我們把它叫做「弓與箭技巧」，因為我們認為一場演講聽眾只記得住一件事，而在準備演講時走過這套思考非常有效。
cards.why: because 後面接的是信念而不是定義——你買不買這個名字，取決於你同不同意那個前提。把命名的理由放在前提上，比放在功能上更難推翻。
cards.episode: Why most public speaking advice is wrong—and how to finally overcome your speaking anxiety | Tristan de Montebello (CEO & co-founder of Ultraspeaking)

alts.quote: And one thing people make fun of me a lot for that I think is just a great example of extreme clarity is I never use bulleted lists because you can never refer to a bullet.
alts.zh: 有件事大家常笑我，但我覺得那正是「極度清楚」的最佳示範：我從來不用項目符號，因為你沒辦法指名某一個點。

alts.quote: I think the hardest thing for a founder, challenge is not optional. You're going to be challenged, but the suffering is optional.
alts.zh: 對創辦人來說最難的是：挑戰不是選項，你一定會被挑戰；但要不要痛苦，是選項。

alts.quote: You kind of come up thinking you're the protagonist. You can be the protagonist in your life, but in the story of your work of a company, you are probably not the protagonist.
alts.zh: 你一路長大都以為自己是主角。你在自己的人生裡可以是主角，但在公司這個故事裡，你多半不是主角。

cards.pattern: The idea behind what I call the [命名] method is that you should [具體做法].
cards.quote: So the idea behind what I call the state change method is that you should punctuate your monologues with state changes.
cards.zh: 我所謂的「狀態轉換法」背後的想法是：你應該在自己的長篇獨白中間，穿插一些狀態轉換。
cards.why: the idea behind X is that... 把名字跟原理分開講，聽的人可以只買原理、不買名字，接受門檻低很多。
cards.episode: Become a better communicator: Specific frameworks to improve your clarity, influence, and impact | Wes Kao (coach, entrepreneur, advisor)

alts.quote: The more massive an object, the more energy it takes to change its direction. This is why big companies move slowly.
alts.zh: 物體越重，要改變它的方向就要越多能量。這就是為什麼大公司動得慢。

alts.quote: I often use this analogy of if you're doing a home renovation, you can have the most beautiful rendering of the new bedroom. But if you haven't checked if there's electricity in that wall there or not, it's going to drastically change the cost and the time and everything.
alts.zh: 我常用一個比喻：你在裝修房子，臥室的效果圖可以做得美到不行。但如果你沒去確認那面牆裡到底有沒有電線，成本跟時間都會整個變樣。

alts.quote: And the traditional structure, the way I learned how to pitch in business school, I think the way most people did is what I call the arrogant doctor.
alts.zh: 而傳統的結構，也就是我在商學院學到的提案方式，我想大部分人學到的也是——我把它叫做「傲慢的醫生」。

cards.pattern: I call this habit “[日常動詞]”, because I [做法] the same way I'd [大家都做過的日常動作].
cards.quote: I call this habit “gossiping” to AI, because I fill in my copilot the same way I’d lean over and vent to a colleague sitting next to me.
cards.zh: 我把這個習慣叫做對 AI「講八卦」，因為我更新我的副駕的方式，就跟我側身跟隔壁同事抱怨一樣。
cards.why: 用一個沒人會拿來講工作的日常動詞當名字，再用 the same way I'd... 把它接回一個大家都做過的動作。名字越不正式，越容易被記住。
cards.episode: Build your personal AI copilot

alts.quote: As a very simple example, sorry, this is a little bit dark, but how restaurants want to turn over tables as fast as possible in order to maximize for the day? Hospitals actually want to do the same with patients.
alts.zh: 舉個很簡單的例子——抱歉這個講法有點黑暗——餐廳希望翻桌越快越好，好把一天的收益拉高。醫院對病床其實也是同一件事。

alts.quote: Over the course of our life, because of all these little situations that happen, we start getting bugs in the software and we're not really upgrading our software.
alts.zh: 在人生的過程裡，因為發生了各種小事，我們的軟體開始長 bug，而我們也沒有真的在更新它。

alts.quote: He sometimes physically bring a chair over in a meeting and say, "The customer is sitting here," and you'd have to pretend.
alts.zh: 他有時候會在會議中真的搬一張椅子過來，說：「客戶就坐在這裡。」然後大家得配合演。

cards.pattern: That's not a [對方認定的類別] problem.
cards.quote: That's not a data center problem.
cards.zh: 那不是資料中心的問題。
cards.why: 六個字就把整場討論的分析單位換掉。不反駁對方的結論，只否認他們正在討論的類別——對方得先證明類別，才回得到原本的論點。
cards.pmNote: 討論卡住時，先確認大家在解的是不是同一類問題。
cards.episode: A rational conversation on where AI is actually going | Benedict Evans

alts.quote: I hate success stories. I love problem solving stories. And that's why when I talk to an entrepreneur, I expect them to be really open about that stuff.
alts.zh: 我討厭成功故事。我喜歡解決問題的故事。所以我跟創業者聊的時候，會期待他們願意把難的部分講出來。

alts.quote: And that's the thing they used to say, "Hey, leadership, this is the problem statement. Here's what we think how might we solve this big problem and here's what we think it looks like when we ship it." That's a mini-vision.
alts.zh: 「各位主管，這是問題陳述。我們認為可以怎麼解這個大問題，還有我們認為做出來會長什麼樣。」這就是一個小型願景。

alts.quote: And so in that case, someone like me who's an advisor comes in and is like, "That's right, it's not a marketing problem, it's company strategy problem.
alts.zh: 所以那種情況下，像我這種顧問進去就會說：「沒錯，這不是行銷的問題，這是公司策略的問題。」

cards.pattern: It's not a [部門 A] problem, it's a [部門 B] problem.
cards.quote: And so in that case, someone like me who's an advisor comes in and is like, "That's right, it's not a marketing problem, it's company strategy problem.
cards.zh: 所以那種情況下，像我這種顧問進去就會說：「沒錯，這不是行銷的問題，這是公司策略的問題。」
cards.why: 換分析單位最直接的句型：否認一個部門、指定另一個部門。把問題從行銷搬到策略，等於把解法的層級也一起搬高。
cards.pmNote: 問題被掛在哪個部門，決定了誰有權力解它。
cards.episode: How to achieve hypergrowth in your business and career | Carilu Dietrich (Atlassian, Miro, Segment, 1Password)

alts.quote: And so I think a lot of it comes down to not the things you try, but how you deeply understand the problem that's preventing someone from using your product effectively.
alts.zh: 所以我覺得關鍵不在你試了哪些招，而在你有多深地搞懂「是什麼擋住使用者用好你的產品」。

alts.quote: So there's, I wouldn't say a checklist, but there's a series of questions that I asked to diagnose why is growth slowing in this order, because it's one of these things where the first one that's a problem, if you don't fix that, it doesn't matter if you fix one of the ones below.
alts.zh: 我不會說那是一張檢查清單，但我確實有一組問題，會照順序問下去診斷成長為什麼變慢——因為只要最前面那個沒修，後面修再多都沒用。

alts.quote: Everyone that I know says they have a bottom of funnel problem. It's never a bottom of funnel problem. It's a top of funnel problem.
alts.zh: 我認識的每個人都說自己是漏斗底部有問題。從來都不是漏斗底部的問題，是漏斗頂端的問題。

cards.pattern: It's never a [X] problem.
cards.quote: It's never a bottom of funnel problem.
cards.zh: 那永遠不會是漏斗底部的問題。
cards.why: never 比 not 更狠——不只這次不是，是從來都不是。用在你想一次終結某個常見誤診的時候。
cards.episode: "Sell the alpha, not the feature": The enterprise sales playbook for $1M to $10M ARR | Jen Abel

alts.quote: And so in that case, someone like me who's an advisor comes in and is like, "That's right, it's not a marketing problem, it's company strategy problem.
alts.zh: 所以那種情況下，像我這種顧問進去就會說：「沒錯，這不是行銷的問題，這是公司策略的問題。」

alts.quote: It's never about one finding in isolation.
alts.zh: 重點從來都不是單獨一個發現。

alts.quote: The problem is not like what should my goal be or how should I figure out what to do with my life? They usually know, but it's very hard to actually make time for those things.
alts.zh: 問題不在於「我的目標該是什麼」或「我這輩子要幹嘛」。這個大家其實都知道。問題是很難真的挪出時間去做那些事。

cards.pattern: Most people asked the wrong question, which was, "[原本的問題]?" The answer to that is [不理想的結果].
cards.quote: When people were reference checking Max, often most VCs asked the wrong question, which was, "Was Max a good employee?" The answer to that is very mixed.
cards.zh: 大家在對 Max 做背景查核時，多數創投問錯了問題，他們問的是：「Max 是個好員工嗎？」那個答案褒貶不一。
cards.why: 不說對方錯，說他們問錯問題，再把那個問題原句引出來。引號讓錯誤的問題現形，下一句你就可以放上正確的問題。
cards.episode: Hard truths about building in the AI era | Keith Rabois (Khosla Ventures)

alts.quote: I think most people don't like product managers often because they haven't experienced good product managers.
alts.zh: 我覺得多數人不喜歡 PM，多半是因為他們沒遇過真正好的 PM。

alts.quote: Then finally I did what I call the cocktail party test, which is to look at the cocktail parties and to watch how people pitch your product to other people.
alts.zh: 最後我做了一件我叫做「雞尾酒會測試」的事——去看那些雞尾酒會，觀察別人怎麼把你的產品推薦給其他人。

alts.quote: But that's the wrong question, because you can do a lot of bad things that will improve revenue.
alts.zh: 但那是錯的問題，因為你可以做很多爛事，一樣能讓營收變好。

cards.pattern: Same [對象], wrong [輸入], wrong [輸出].
cards.quote: Same person, wrong question, wrong result.
cards.zh: 同一個人，問錯問題，得到錯的結論。
cards.why: 三個名詞片語、沒有動詞，像一句格言。變因只換一個（問題），結果就變了，等於用一句話證明「問題比答案重要」。
cards.episode: Hard truths about building in the AI era | Keith Rabois (Khosla Ventures)

alts.quote: But that's the wrong question, because you can do a lot of bad things that will improve revenue.
alts.zh: 但那是錯的問題，因為你可以做很多爛事，一樣能讓營收變好。

alts.quote: Success is an output of a lot of failures, but the question is, how much time do you have to fail?
alts.zh: 成功是一堆失敗的產物，但問題是：你有多少時間可以失敗？

alts.quote: Sometimes I wonder if the challenges and the opportunities are exactly the same.
alts.zh: 我有時候會想，所謂的挑戰跟機會，會不會根本是同一件事。

cards.pattern: But that's the wrong question, because you can [照這個問題會導出的荒謬做法].
cards.quote: But that's the wrong question, because you can do a lot of bad things that will improve revenue.
cards.zh: 但那是錯的問題，因為你可以做很多爛事，一樣能讓營收變好。
cards.why: 說對方問錯問題之後，一定要立刻給理由，否則就是耍賴。這裡的理由是反例——照這個問題走會得到明顯荒謬的答案。
cards.pmNote: 指標選錯，優化得越用力，離目標越遠。
cards.episode: The ultimate guide to A/B testing | Ronny Kohavi (Airbnb, Microsoft, Amazon)

alts.quote: And so I think a lot of it comes down to not the things you try, but how you deeply understand the problem that's preventing someone from using your product effectively.
alts.zh: 所以我覺得關鍵不在你試了哪些招，而在你有多深地搞懂「是什麼擋住使用者用好你的產品」。

alts.quote: So there's, I wouldn't say a checklist, but there's a series of questions that I asked to diagnose why is growth slowing in this order, because it's one of these things where the first one that's a problem, if you don't fix that, it doesn't matter if you fix one of the ones below.
alts.zh: 我不會說那是一張檢查清單，但我確實有一組問題，會照順序問下去診斷成長為什麼變慢——因為只要最前面那個沒修，後面修再多都沒用。

alts.quote: Success is an output of a lot of failures, but the question is, how much time do you have to fail?
alts.zh: 成功是一堆失敗的產物，但問題是：你有多少時間可以失敗？

cards.pattern: That's the real question: what does [大家都在用的詞] mean?
cards.quote: That's the real question, what does engagement mean?
cards.zh: 那才是真正的問題：engagement 到底是什麼意思？
cards.why: 把一個大家天天在用、卻沒人定義過的詞挑出來問。指標名詞常常是團隊最大的隱藏分歧點。
cards.episode: Using behavioral science to improve your product | Kristen Berman (Irrational Labs)

alts.quote: But that's the wrong question, because you can do a lot of bad things that will improve revenue.
alts.zh: 但那是錯的問題，因為你可以做很多爛事，一樣能讓營收變好。

alts.quote: Finding a new manager is always an option, but I guess sometimes the real question is, is actually spending time to try to understand what is your manager optimizing?
alts.zh: 換一個主管永遠是個選項，但我想有時候真正的問題是：要不要花時間去搞懂你的主管到底在最佳化什麼？

alts.quote: The real question here isn’t about tech, or specific resources, it’s about position.
alts.zh: 這裡真正的問題不在技術，也不在特定資源，而在位置。

cards.pattern: [對方想到的解法] is always an option, but sometimes the real question is [換一個問題].
cards.quote: Finding a new manager is always an option, but I guess sometimes the real question is, is actually spending time to try to understand what is your manager optimizing?
cards.zh: 換一個主管永遠是個選項，但我想有時候真正的問題是：要不要花時間去搞懂你的主管到底在最佳化什麼？
cards.why: 先承認對方的解法可行（is always an option），再換問題。給對方留了退路，換框架就不像否定。
cards.episode: Unorthodox frameworks for growing your product, career, and impact | Bangaly Kaba (YouTube, Instagram, Facebook, Instacart)

alts.quote: And so I think a lot of it comes down to not the things you try, but how you deeply understand the problem that's preventing someone from using your product effectively.
alts.zh: 所以我覺得關鍵不在你試了哪些招，而在你有多深地搞懂「是什麼擋住使用者用好你的產品」。

alts.quote: Success is an output of a lot of failures, but the question is, how much time do you have to fail?
alts.zh: 成功是一堆失敗的產物，但問題是：你有多少時間可以失敗？

alts.quote: The problem is not like what should my goal be or how should I figure out what to do with my life? They usually know, but it's very hard to actually make time for those things.
alts.zh: 問題不在於「我的目標該是什麼」或「我這輩子要幹嘛」。這個大家其實都知道。問題是很難真的挪出時間去做那些事。

cards.quote: You can ask the question behind the question.
cards.zh: 你可以去問那個問題背後的問題。
cards.why: 一句話把「換框架」這個動作本身命名出來。在會議上當成提議說出口，比直接換題目更不冒犯。
cards.episode: How to ask the right questions, project confidence, and win over skeptics | Paige Costello (Asana, Intercom, Intuit)

alts.quote: That's the real question, what does engagement mean?
alts.zh: 那才是真正的問題：engagement 到底是什麼意思？

alts.quote: Success is an output of a lot of failures, but the question is, how much time do you have to fail?
alts.zh: 成功是一堆失敗的產物，但問題是：你有多少時間可以失敗？

alts.quote: When people were reference checking Max, often most VCs asked the wrong question, which was, "Was Max a good employee?" The answer to that is very mixed.
alts.zh: 大家在對 Max 做背景查核時，多數創投問錯了問題，他們問的是：「Max 是個好員工嗎？」那個答案褒貶不一。

cards.pattern: The real question here isn't about [A], or [B], it's about [C].
cards.quote: The real question here isn’t about tech, or specific resources, it’s about position.
cards.zh: 這裡真正的問題不在技術，也不在特定資源，而在位置。
cards.why: 連續否定兩個大家會先想到的答案，第三個才是你的。兩次否定是為了讓第三個看起來像窮舉之後的結論。
cards.episode: How to communicate tradeoffs so leaders will listen

alts.quote: Finding a new manager is always an option, but I guess sometimes the real question is, is actually spending time to try to understand what is your manager optimizing?
alts.zh: 換一個主管永遠是個選項，但我想有時候真正的問題是：要不要花時間去搞懂你的主管到底在最佳化什麼？

alts.zh: 那才是真正的問題：engagement 到底是什麼意思？

alts.quote: Success is an output of a lot of failures, but the question is, how much time do you have to fail?
alts.zh: 成功是一堆失敗的產物，但問題是：你有多少時間可以失敗？

cards.pattern: And it turns out, [X], it's not a separate problem.
cards.quote: And it turns out, eval, it's not a separate problem.
cards.zh: 結果發現，evals 並不是一個獨立的問題。
cards.why: 否認的不是類別而是「獨立性」——它不是另一件事，它就長在你正在做的事情裡。用來擋掉「那個之後再處理」很好用。
cards.pmNote: 被排到 backlog 最下面的事，常常是因為它被誤認成一個獨立專案。
cards.episode: Al Engineering 101 with Chip Huyen (Nvidia, Stanford, Netflix)

alts.quote: The problem is not like what should my goal be or how should I figure out what to do with my life? They usually know, but it's very hard to actually make time for those things.
alts.zh: 問題不在於「我的目標該是什麼」或「我這輩子要幹嘛」。這個大家其實都知道。問題是很難真的挪出時間去做那些事。

alts.quote: So there's, I wouldn't say a checklist, but there's a series of questions that I asked to diagnose why is growth slowing in this order, because it's one of these things where the first one that's a problem, if you don't fix that, it doesn't matter if you fix one of the ones below.
alts.zh: 我不會說那是一張檢查清單，但我確實有一組問題，會照順序問下去診斷成長為什麼變慢——因為只要最前面那個沒修，後面修再多都沒用。

alts.quote: Everyone that I know says they have a bottom of funnel problem. It's never a bottom of funnel problem. It's a top of funnel problem.
alts.zh: 我認識的每個人都說自己是漏斗底部有問題。從來都不是漏斗底部的問題，是漏斗頂端的問題。

cards.pattern: [對象] has [看起來符合的特徵], but it's never a true [類別].
cards.quote: Shopify has a third-party ecosystem and things like that, but it's never a true platform.
cards.zh: Shopify 有第三方生態系之類的東西，但它從來都不是一個真正的平台。
cards.why: 先承認表面證據，再否認類別歸屬。爭論的焦點被換成「什麼才算 true X」，而定義權在你手上。
cards.episode: The creator of WordPress opens up about becoming an internet villain, why he’s taking a stand, and the future of open source | Matt Mullenweg (founder and CEO, Automattic)

alts.quote: The problem is not like what should my goal be or how should I figure out what to do with my life? They usually know, but it's very hard to actually make time for those things.
alts.zh: 問題不在於「我的目標該是什麼」或「我這輩子要幹嘛」。這個大家其實都知道。問題是很難真的挪出時間去做那些事。

alts.quote: So there's, I wouldn't say a checklist, but there's a series of questions that I asked to diagnose why is growth slowing in this order, because it's one of these things where the first one that's a problem, if you don't fix that, it doesn't matter if you fix one of the ones below.
alts.zh: 我不會說那是一張檢查清單，但我確實有一組問題，會照順序問下去診斷成長為什麼變慢——因為只要最前面那個沒修，後面修再多都沒用。

alts.quote: Everyone that I know says they have a bottom of funnel problem. It's never a bottom of funnel problem. It's a top of funnel problem.
alts.zh: 我認識的每個人都說自己是漏斗底部有問題。從來都不是漏斗底部的問題，是漏斗頂端的問題。

cards.pattern: It's never about [單一的東西] in isolation.
cards.quote: It's never about one finding in isolation.
cards.zh: 重點從來都不是單獨一個發現。
cards.why: in isolation 是關鍵字：不是說那個發現不重要，是說它不能單獨看。適合用在別人拿一個數據就想下結論的時候。
cards.episode: Marketplace lessons from Uber, Airbnb, Bumble, and more | Ramesh Johari (Stanford professor, startup advisor)

alts.quote: Everyone that I know says they have a bottom of funnel problem. It's never a bottom of funnel problem. It's a top of funnel problem.
alts.zh: 我認識的每個人都說自己是漏斗底部有問題。從來都不是漏斗底部的問題，是漏斗頂端的問題。

alts.quote: Shopify has a third-party ecosystem and things like that, but it's never a true platform.
alts.zh: Shopify 有第三方生態系之類的東西，但它從來都不是一個真正的平台。

alts.quote: One is people set this goal, I want to be promoted the next thing, or I want to lead this big project. And those are bad goals, because it's not in your control. A good goal is what you can do.
alts.zh: 有一種是設「我要升到下一級」或「我要主導那個大專案」。這些是壞目標，因為不在你的掌控裡。好目標是你自己做得到的事。

cards.pattern: You take the thing you're responsible for and you just do one zoom out of [X] and question that.
cards.quote: But you take the thing you're responsible for and you just do one zoom out of the problem you're solving and question that.
cards.zh: 你就拿你負責的那件事，把你在解的問題往外拉一層，然後質疑那一層。
cards.why: one zoom out 把「拉高視角」量化成一個動作——只往外一層，不是無限上綱。這讓換框架變成可執行的步驟而不是態度。
cards.pmNote: 往外拉一層通常就夠了；拉太多層會變成不切實際的策略討論。
cards.episode: Netflix CPTO on AI and the future of product and tech roles | Elizabeth Stone

alts.quote: You're never trying to solve a problem of simplifying. And simplifying might be a solution, but it can never be a problem on its own.
alts.zh: 你不會是在解決「簡化」這個問題。簡化可能是一種解法，但它本身永遠不會是問題。

alts.quote: I hate success stories. I love problem solving stories. And that's why when I talk to an entrepreneur, I expect them to be really open about that stuff.
alts.zh: 我討厭成功故事。我喜歡解決問題的故事。所以我跟創業者聊的時候，會期待他們願意把難的部分講出來。

alts.quote: And that's the thing they used to say, "Hey, leadership, this is the problem statement. Here's what we think how might we solve this big problem and here's what we think it looks like when we ship it." That's a mini-vision.
alts.zh: 「各位主管，這是問題陳述。我們認為可以怎麼解這個大問題，還有我們認為做出來會長什麼樣。」這就是一個小型願景。

cards.pattern: We don't obsess over [眼前的指標], because if you zoom out and out and out, [眼前的東西] will be inconsequential.
cards.quote: And then we also don't obsess over absolute numbers, because if we're successful, if you zoom out and out and out, any point in time will be inconsequential and small.
cards.zh: 我們也不會執著於絕對數字，因為如果我們成功了，你一直往外拉、再往外拉，任何一個時間點都會顯得無足輕重。
cards.why: zoom out and out and out 用重複製造尺度感，把時間軸拉到讓對方的焦慮自己消失。這是用視角處理情緒，不是用數據。
cards.episode: Competing with giants: An inside look at how The Browser Company builds product | Josh Miller (CEO)

alts.quote: The way to summarize that is if you look at all the startup stories that we have at YC and all the companies we funded over all the years, the underlying theme is that rationally the founder should have given up at some point.
alts.zh: 要總結的話：如果你看 YC 所有的創業故事、這些年投的所有公司，底下共通的主題是——照理性判斷，創辦人早就該在某個時間點放棄了。

alts.quote: And so then the first few pages became very much more problem-based because if people don't understand the problem then they can't understand or care about your solution.
alts.zh: 所以前面幾頁後來就大改成以「問題」為主，因為人如果不懂那個問題，就不可能懂、也不可能在乎你的解法。

alts.quote: I think most people don't like product managers often because they haven't experienced good product managers.
alts.zh: 我覺得多數人不喜歡 PM，多半是因為他們沒遇過真正好的 PM。

cards.pattern: If you look beyond [短期視角] and zoom out and think about [更高的參照組], you realize [結論].
cards.quote: And if you look beyond the short term and like, "Okay, what are the numbers for this quarter?" And you zoom out and you think about what are the very best products out there, you realize this is how they all operate.
cards.zh: 如果你不只看短期、不只問「這一季的數字怎樣」，而是往外拉、去想想市面上最好的產品是怎麼運作的，你會發現它們全都是這樣做的。
cards.why: 換的不是問題而是參照組——從「這季數字」換成「最好的產品」。用 you realize 收尾，結論聽起來像對方自己想通的。
cards.episode: Anthropic’s $1B to $19B growth run: how Claude became the fastest-growing AI product in history | Amol Avasare

alts.quote: I completely agree with what Gustav said, but to look at this from a different frame, I think is that the founders lose hope.
alts.zh: 我完全同意 Gustav 講的，但換一個框架來看，我覺得真正的原因是創辦人失去了希望。

alts.quote: One of the things that I think when you're doing interviewing, one way to think about it, I call it home court, away court, neutral court, you want interviews to balance in all those different spheres.
alts.zh: 面試的時候有一個思考方式，我把它叫做「主場、客場、中立場」，你會希望面試在這幾個場域之間取得平衡。

alts.quote: And then we also don't obsess over absolute numbers, because if we're successful, if you zoom out and out and out, any point in time will be inconsequential and small.
alts.zh: 我們也不會執著於絕對數字，因為如果我們成功了，你一直往外拉、再往外拉，任何一個時間點都會顯得無足輕重。

cards.pattern: I would argue that what we're seeing is us trying to use [舊做法] in [新情境] that doesn't really fit yet.
cards.quote: In fact, I would argue that what we're seeing in the industry is us trying to use mature playbooks from the end stage of the last tech era in one that doesn't really fit yet.
cards.zh: 事實上我會說，我們在業界看到的，是大家拿上一個科技時代末期的成熟劇本，套進一個還不適合的新時代。
cards.why: I would argue 把主觀判斷包裝成論證的一步，聽起來像推導出來的。後面接的是對現況的診斷，不是對人的批評。
cards.episode: Thinking like a gardener not a builder, organizing teams like slime mold, the adjacent possible, and other unconventional product advice | Alex Komoroske (Stripe, Google)

alts.quote: I'm just trying to argue this advice applied to a startup that's too early is actively not helpful.
alts.zh: 我只是想主張：把這套建議套在太早期的新創身上，是「主動有害」而不只是沒用。

alts.quote: And so ever since then, we've been automating jobs and creating new jobs, and you can always see the job that's going to go away, and you don't know the new job because it doesn't exist yet.
alts.zh: 從那時候到現在，我們一直在自動化舊工作、也一直在長出新工作；而你永遠看得到那個要消失的工作，看不到新的，因為它還不存在。

alts.quote: I would argue that the one thing AI can never have is agency because it doesn't have human motivations.
alts.zh: 我會說 AI 唯一永遠不會有的東西是能動性，因為它沒有人的動機。

cards.pattern: The way I think about this, that I've heard well described, is [一句話的原則].
cards.quote: The way I think about this that I've heard well described is just there's no silver bullets, just many lead bullets.
cards.zh: 我對這件事的想法——我聽過一個說得很好的講法——就是沒有銀色子彈，只有很多顆鉛彈。
cards.why: 中間插一句 that I've heard well described，把功勞讓給別人，自己的立場反而更容易被接受。借來的說法比自創的說法阻力小。
cards.episode: Humanizing product development | Adriel Frederick (Reddit, Lyft, Facebook)

alts.quote: And again, everything I've just described, by the way, is just a very straightforward extrapolation of very basic economics. I'm not making any bold predictions of what I just said.
alts.zh: 我剛剛講的這一整串，其實只是最基本的經濟學往下推而已。我沒有在做什麼大膽預測。

alts.quote: There's no way that you can lower the cost of content creation and increase the scale of distribution and not see this emerge, this creator economy I think emerge.
alts.zh: 你不可能同時把內容製作成本壓低、又把發行規模放大，然後這個東西——創作者經濟——不出現。

alts.quote: So I think if you take all those steps back and you look at this from a journey perspective, there's no way that it won't be impacting search. It's just going to be hard to find.
alts.zh: 所以我覺得，只要你退開幾步、用「使用者旅程」的角度看，它不可能不影響搜尋。只是那個影響很難被指認出來。

cards.pattern: My take on [議題] is they can be [優點 1] and [優點 2], but you have to [代價].
cards.quote: My take on empty vessel names is they can be really memorable and they can be evocative of the emotion, but you have to do a lot more marketing work over time to make it mean something.
cards.zh: 我對「空殼型名字」的看法是：它們可以很好記、也能勾起情緒，但你得花更多行銷力氣，久了才會有意義。
cards.why: My take on X is 直接宣告這是我的判斷，不假裝客觀。先給兩個優點再用 but 收代價，聽起來像評估過而不是偏好。
cards.episode: The art of building legendary brands | Arielle Jackson (Google, Square, Marketer in Residence at First Round Capital)

alts.quote: In a world where it's easier to build things, it's more important to make sure that your time is spent figuring out what you should be building in the first place.
alts.zh: 在一個「東西越來越好做」的世界裡，更重要的是先確保你把時間花在想清楚「到底該做什麼」。

alts.quote: And getting to $1,000,000 of GMV in a constrained market is a lot harder, takes longer, but it's actually the path to building something that endures.
alts.zh: 在一個受限的市場裡做到一百萬 GMV 難很多、也慢很多，但那才是真正做出能長久的東西的路。

alts.quote: That sounds cliche. I think a lot of founders and startup people like to talk about the mission, and I get it, and I think it's real. But I really mean it.
alts.zh: 我知道這聽起來很老套。很多創辦人都愛談使命，我懂，我也覺得那是真的。但我是真心這樣講。

cards.pattern: The thing that I would argue [某群人] have in common is they [特質 1] and they [特質 2].
cards.quote: But the thing that I would argue folks that build really big companies have in common is they just really want it and they really believe in themselves and they really believe they can make it work.
cards.zh: 但我會說，那些做出真正大公司的人共通點是：他們就是非常想要，他們真的相信自己，也真的相信自己能做成。
cards.why: 把 I would argue 塞進句子中間當插入語，主張聽起來不像宣言而像分析的一部分。台灣人習慣把 I think 放句首，這個位置更資深。
cards.episode: Lessons from 1,000+ YC startups: Resilience, tar pit ideas, pivoting, more | Dalton Caldwell (Y Combinator, Managing Director)

alts.quote: The most common mistake people make is they think through the probability first without actually forcing themselves to think through the potential.
alts.zh: 大家最常犯的錯，是先想「成功機率」，卻沒有逼自己先想「這件事最大能長成什麼樣」。

alts.quote: I would argue that the more power you have, the more moral responsibility you have to actually pause and figure out what it is that you're doing to be complicit in creating the conditions you say you don't want.
alts.zh: 我會說，你擁有的權力越大，你就越有道德責任停下來，弄清楚你到底做了什麼，才讓你嘴上說不想要的那些狀況得以成立。

alts.quote: My sense is if you want work-life balance, don't join one of these companies, because that's just not the way they work.
alts.zh: 我的感覺是，如果你想要工作生活平衡，就別加入這種公司，因為它們就不是那樣運作的。

cards.pattern: I would argue the most important thing is to [做法], because that usually makes sure [結果].
cards.quote: I would argue the most important thing is to have a single name on that decision line, because that usually makes sure that you can get a decision very quickly.
cards.zh: 我會說最重要的一件事，是那條決策線上只放一個名字，因為那通常能確保你很快就拿到決定。
cards.why: the most important thing 是排序宣告，很容易招來反駁，所以後面立刻用 because 給機制。主張＋機制一起出手，對方才有東西可以討論。
cards.pmNote: 一個決策只掛一個名字（DRI），是加快決策最便宜的做法。
cards.episode: LinkedIn’s product evolution and the art of building complex systems | Hari Srinivasan (LinkedIn)

alts.quote: I would argue that the one thing AI can never have is agency because it doesn't have human motivations.
alts.zh: 我會說 AI 唯一永遠不會有的東西是能動性，因為它沒有人的動機。

alts.quote: In a world where it's easier to build things, it's more important to make sure that your time is spent figuring out what you should be building in the first place.
alts.zh: 在一個「東西越來越好做」的世界裡，更重要的是先確保你把時間花在想清楚「到底該做什麼」。

alts.quote: And just saying because dramatically boosted the percentage of the time that a person would let them cut the line. We're suckers for explanations, all of us.
alts.zh: 光是講出「因為」，別人讓他插隊的比例就大幅上升。我們每個人都吃「解釋」這一套。

cards.pattern: I would argue that just by [小動作], we usually have a slightly better [結果] than [現況].
cards.quote: I would argue that just by breaking the question to these two questions we usually have a slightly better discussion than just my idea is better than yours.
cards.zh: 我會說，光是把這個問題拆成這兩個問題，我們通常就能有比「我的點子比你的好」稍微好一點的討論。
cards.why: 提案的力道刻意壓低：just by、slightly better。承諾小、阻力小，對方要試的成本也小——這是推動流程改變的標準話術。
cards.episode: Becoming evidence-guided | Itamar Gilad (Gmail, YouTube, Microsoft)

alts.quote: How do I make this idea one click better? It's not about how do you do something radically, radically different, but taking ideas and then making it slightly better, slightly better.
alts.zh: 我要怎麼把這個想法再往上推一格？重點不是做出天差地遠的東西，而是接手別人的想法，再讓它好一點點。

alts.quote: And so the question just was what if there's a better way? What if we could reimagine this format from the ground up?
alts.zh: 所以問題就變成：有沒有更好的做法？我們有沒有可能把這個格式從頭重新想一遍？

alts.quote: I sat for about a half a day and I thought, I think I can help here, drew out an org chart, put my name on the top, walked into my boss's office and said, "This is one potential solve of your marketing organization question."
alts.zh: 我想了大概半天，覺得我應該幫得上忙，就畫了一張組織圖，把自己放在最上面，走進我主管辦公室說：「這是你那個行銷組織問題的其中一個解法。」

cards.pattern: What I've found is you should [做法], which is the opposite of what most people do.
cards.quote: How do you get the foot in the door?" And what I've found is you should make the smallest ask possible, which is the opposite of what 95% of people do.
cards.zh: 「你要怎麼把腳踏進門？」我發現的是：你的請求要越小越好，這跟 95% 的人做的正好相反。
cards.why: what I've found is 把建議說成經驗歸納而不是規則。結尾的 which is the opposite of what most people do 製造反差，讓建議顯得值得記。
cards.episode: Leveraging mentors to uplevel your career | Jules Walter (YouTube, Slack)

alts.quote: I sort of wanted to ask myself, is it possible to break that divide between the haves and the have-nots and make this capability widely accessible through a procedural approach. And I have news for you. The answer is yes.
alts.zh: 我當時就問自己：有沒有可能打破「會的人／不會的人」這道分野，用一套流程讓這個能力變成人人都能上手？我告訴你，答案是可以。

alts.quote: I want you to pull the hiring manager aside and say, "Hey, Lenny, you're the hiring manager. I've thought about what the role is. I want to make sure I'm understanding it correctly.
alts.zh: 我要你把用人主管拉到一旁說：「我想過這個職位到底是什麼，我想確認我理解得對不對。我可以跟你分享一下嗎？」

alts.quote: Some of the best startup advice I've heard is startups should focus on one thing and be really, really exceptionally world-class at that one thing. And one of our early zigs is we are going to do exactly the opposite of that.
alts.zh: 我聽過最好的創業建議之一，就是新創應該專注在一件事，並且在那件事上做到世界級。而我們早期的其中一個「岔開」，就是完全反著做。

cards.pattern: What I've found is that once you [動作], you actually [反直覺的好處], and you move out of the [壞狀態].
cards.quote: What I've found is that once you commit to a decision, you actually learn more post committing to that decision about what's going to work and not going to work, and you move out of the hypothetical.
cards.zh: 我發現的是，一旦你對一個決定拍板，你在拍板之後反而會學到更多——什麼會成、什麼不會成——而且你會離開純假設的狀態。
cards.why: 主張本身是反直覺的（先決定再學習），所以用 What I've found is 開頭，把它降格成個人觀察，反而更好推銷。
cards.pmNote: 拿不定主意時，決策本身就是最快的資訊來源。
cards.episode: Becoming more strategic, navigating difficult colleagues, harnessing founder mode, and more | Anneka Gupta (Chief Product Officer at Rubrik)

alts.quote: What's interesting is that Silicon Valley has found a way to make the most profitable style of business the least profitable.
alts.zh: 有趣的是，矽谷居然有辦法把全世界最好賺的生意做成最不賺錢的生意。

alts.quote: I've never seen a product plan get to the truth of what it could do, but it will help you make a better decision than if you just guess.
alts.zh: 我沒看過哪份產品計畫真的算準過它能做到什麼，但它還是會讓你的決定比純用猜的好。

alts.quote: But, what I've found is when you build a product, most founders, and most teams kind of stop when it works.
alts.zh: 但我發現的是，做產品的時候，大部分創辦人跟團隊在「能用了」的那一刻就停了。

cards.pattern: What I've found is when you [情境], most [群體] kind of stop when [不夠的標準].
cards.quote: But, what I've found is when you build a product, most founders, and most teams kind of stop when it works.
cards.zh: 但我發現的是，做產品的時候，大部分創辦人跟團隊在「能用了」的那一刻就停了。
cards.why: 用 most founders 當主詞而不是 you，聽的人可以先同意、再自己對號入座。kind of 讓這個指控軟一點，但意思一點都沒少。
cards.episode: How to drive word of mouth | Nilan Peiris (CPO of Wise)

alts.quote: And that what I've found over the years with founders is that they start to use Proven, Better, New to justify a wrong idea.
alts.zh: 我這些年在創辦人身上發現的是，他們會開始拿「已驗證、更好、全新」這套框架去合理化一個錯的點子。

alts.quote: I've never seen a product plan get to the truth of what it could do, but it will help you make a better decision than if you just guess.
alts.zh: 我沒看過哪份產品計畫真的算準過它能做到什麼，但它還是會讓你的決定比純用猜的好。

alts.quote: A lot of founders think about not wanting to have a leaky bucket on the product side, but the same thing applies on the team side.
alts.zh: 很多創辦人都很在意產品端不要有「破桶子」，但同樣的道理在團隊這一端也成立。

cards.pattern: What I've found talking to [對象] is that they [錯誤行為] before they [前提條件].
cards.quote: What I've found talking to people who want to start what they think is a marketplace is that they think too much about a marketplace before they're a marketplace.
cards.zh: 我跟那些想做他們自認為是媒合平台的人聊下來，發現他們在還不是平台之前，就想太多平台的事。
cards.why: What I've found + talking to 直接把樣本來源講出來，這句主張就有了資料感。X before they're X 的重複句式讓錯誤一目了然。
cards.episode: Marketplace lessons from Uber, Airbnb, Bumble, and more | Ramesh Johari (Stanford professor, startup advisor)

alts.quote: What I've found is, oftentimes when you go into corporate environments, like people start becoming very sterile in the facts that they provide.
alts.zh: 我發現的是，很多時候你走進大公司的環境，大家提供的事實會開始變得很無菌、很乾。

alts.quote: That's solving a problem for the company. That's not solving a career growth issue for an individual. And I think people who want to be promoted need to think in that orientation versus the other.
alts.zh: 那是在解決公司的問題，不是在解決個人的職涯成長問題。想升遷的人要用前面那種角度思考，不是後面那種。

alts.quote: Now, the good news is that you can then reverse that and say if I'm willing to do it, think about what an edge I'm going to have over people who aren't willing to do it, right?
alts.zh: 好消息是這件事可以反過來看：如果我願意做，想想我對那些不願意做的人會有多大的優勢。

cards.pattern: I tend to think that if [組織安排], [後果].
cards.quote: I tend to think that if design reports into Product, the UX suffers.
cards.zh: 我傾向認為，如果設計團隊回報給產品，使用者體驗會受害。
cards.why: I tend to think 比 I think 更留餘地，用在會得罪人的組織主張上剛好。短句、沒有修飾，立場很清楚但語氣不硬。
cards.episode: How Ramp builds product

alts.quote: A lot of founders think about not wanting to have a leaky bucket on the product side, but the same thing applies on the team side.
alts.zh: 很多創辦人都很在意產品端不要有「破桶子」，但同樣的道理在團隊這一端也成立。

alts.quote: That's solving a problem for the company. That's not solving a career growth issue for an individual. And I think people who want to be promoted need to think in that orientation versus the other.
alts.zh: 那是在解決公司的問題，不是在解決個人的職涯成長問題。想升遷的人要用前面那種角度思考，不是後面那種。

alts.quote: That sounds cliche. I think a lot of founders and startup people like to talk about the mission, and I get it, and I think it's real. But I really mean it.
alts.zh: 我知道這聽起來很老套。很多創辦人都愛談使命，我懂，我也覺得那是真的。但我是真心這樣講。

cards.pattern: I would argue that the one thing [X] can never have is [Y] because [理由].
cards.quote: I would argue that the one thing AI can never have is agency because it doesn't have human motivations.
cards.zh: 我會說 AI 唯一永遠不會有的東西是能動性，因為它沒有人的動機。
cards.why: the one thing... can never have 是很強的斷言，前面掛 I would argue 就變成一個可以被辯論的命題。強主張＋弱框架，是聰明的組合。
cards.episode: An AI state of the union: We’ve passed the inflection point, dark factories are coming, and automation timelines | Simon Willison

alts.quote: I would argue the most important thing is to have a single name on that decision line, because that usually makes sure that you can get a decision very quickly.
alts.zh: 我會說最重要的一件事，是那條決策線上只放一個名字，因為那通常能確保你很快就拿到決定。

alts.quote: And so ever since then, we've been automating jobs and creating new jobs, and you can always see the job that's going to go away, and you don't know the new job because it doesn't exist yet.
alts.zh: 從那時候到現在，我們一直在自動化舊工作、也一直在長出新工作；而你永遠看得到那個要消失的工作，看不到新的，因為它還不存在。

alts.quote: Your reader doesn't know which parts are FYIs or which parts are background versus what is the thing that you want their response on.
alts.zh: 你的讀者根本分不出哪些是「知會一下」、哪些是背景，哪一段才是你要他回覆的。

cards.pattern: I would argue that the more [X] you have, the more [Y] you have to [動作].
cards.quote: I would argue that the more power you have, the more moral responsibility you have to actually pause and figure out what it is that you're doing to be complicit in creating the conditions you say you don't want.
cards.zh: 我會說，你擁有的權力越大，你就越有道德責任停下來，弄清楚你到底做了什麼，才讓你嘴上說不想要的那些狀況得以成立。
cards.why: the more X, the more Y 的比例句型讓主張聽起來像原則而不是指責。對象是「有權力的人」這個類別，不是在場的某個人。
cards.episode: How have I been complicit in creating the conditions I say I don’t want? | Jerry Colonna (CEO of Reboot, executive coach, former VC)

alts.quote: As an entrepreneur, a company, you actually don't have a choice whether you'll have a pricing conversation with your customer. The only thing in your control is when you will have it.
alts.zh: 身為創業者或公司，你其實沒有「要不要跟客戶談價格」的選擇權。你唯一能控制的是「什麼時候談」。

alts.quote: But the thing that I would argue folks that build really big companies have in common is they just really want it and they really believe in themselves and they really believe they can make it work.
alts.zh: 但我會說，那些做出真正大公司的人共通點是：他們就是非常想要，他們真的相信自己，也真的相信自己能做成。

alts.quote: And so ever since then, we've been automating jobs and creating new jobs, and you can always see the job that's going to go away, and you don't know the new job because it doesn't exist yet.
alts.zh: 從那時候到現在，我們一直在自動化舊工作、也一直在長出新工作；而你永遠看得到那個要消失的工作，看不到新的，因為它還不存在。

cards.pattern: My sense is [預測], kind of like how [已經在發生的類比].
cards.quote: My sense is I think managers will be able to manage much larger teams in this world, kind of like how software engineers are managing 20 to 30 Codexes.
cards.zh: 我的感覺是，在這個世界裡主管有辦法管理大得多的團隊，有點像現在軟體工程師同時在管 20 到 30 個 Codex。
cards.why: My sense is 明說這是直覺不是證據；後面用一個已經在發生的事當類比，把預測變得可想像。預測沒有數據時，類比就是你的證據。
cards.episode: Sherwin Wu V2

alts.quote: So for positioning work, I'm going to say something that is contentious, but I don't think it is at all.
alts.zh: 講到定位這件事，我要說一句大家可能覺得很有爭議的話——但我完全不覺得有爭議。

alts.quote: I sat for about a half a day and I thought, I think I can help here, drew out an org chart, put my name on the top, walked into my boss's office and said, "This is one potential solve of your marketing organization question."
alts.zh: 我想了大概半天，覺得我應該幫得上忙，就畫了一張組織圖，把自己放在最上面，走進我主管辦公室說：「這是你那個行銷組織問題的其中一個解法。」

alts.quote: My most controversial opinion is that I think that AI is as big a deal as the internet or mobile. And only as big a deal as the internet or mobile.
alts.zh: 我最有爭議的一個看法是：AI 跟網路、行動裝置一樣重大——而且也「只」跟它們一樣重大而已。

cards.pattern: My sense is if you want [X], don't [動作], because that's just not the way [對象] work.
cards.quote: My sense is if you want work-life balance, don't join one of these companies, because that's just not the way they work.
cards.zh: 我的感覺是，如果你想要工作生活平衡，就別加入這種公司，因為它們就不是那樣運作的。
cards.why: My sense is 先把責任降到個人觀察，接著給一句非常直接的建議。軟開頭＋硬建議，是講不中聽的話時最好用的組合。
cards.episode: Elena Verna 4.0

alts.quote: And so ever since then, we've been automating jobs and creating new jobs, and you can always see the job that's going to go away, and you don't know the new job because it doesn't exist yet.
alts.zh: 從那時候到現在，我們一直在自動化舊工作、也一直在長出新工作；而你永遠看得到那個要消失的工作，看不到新的，因為它還不存在。

alts.quote: I don't want to spend any years of my life becoming passively okay at something.
alts.zh: 我不想花人生的任何幾年，只為了在某件事上變得「勉強還行」。

alts.quote: I've learned that some of the companies we admire are not working the way we are, and maybe we should try this.
alts.zh: 我發現我們很欣賞的那幾家公司，做事方式跟我們並不一樣，也許我們可以試試看他們的做法。

cards.pattern: Sometimes people hesitate to [做某事], but I would argue it is [完全相反的評價].
cards.quote: Sometimes product managers hesitate to “waste people’s time” in sessions about goals, but I would argue it is the most valuable time to spend together.
cards.zh: 有時候產品經理會猶豫，覺得開會談目標是在「浪費大家時間」，但我會說那是最值得一起花的時間。
cards.why: 先把對方的顧慮用引號原句寫出來，再用 but I would argue 反轉。引號讓那個顧慮看起來是別人的想法，你反駁的就不是在場的人。
cards.episode: This Week #10: Keeping designers and engineers excited about metrics + Transitioning from DS to PM 🕺

alts.quote: Most people are missing the most important slide of their presentation. The most important slide of your presentation is the first slide. This slide is going to be presented for the longest period of time.
alts.zh: 大部分人都漏掉了簡報裡最重要的那一頁。你簡報最重要的一頁，是第一頁。因為那一頁會在螢幕上停留最久。

alts.quote: In a world where it's easier to build things, it's more important to make sure that your time is spent figuring out what you should be building in the first place.
alts.zh: 在一個「東西越來越好做」的世界裡，更重要的是先確保你把時間花在想清楚「到底該做什麼」。

alts.quote: I would argue that the more power you have, the more moral responsibility you have to actually pause and figure out what it is that you're doing.
alts.zh: 我會主張：你握有的權力越大，你就越有道德責任停下來，搞清楚自己在做什麼。

cards.pattern: You have to shift from [舊角色] to [新角色] is the way I think about it.
cards.quote: You have to shift from doer to editor is the way I think about it.
cards.zh: 你必須從做事的人轉成當編輯——我是這樣看的。
cards.why: 把 is the way I think about it 放句尾當補丁：先講完主張，再補一句「這是我的看法」。順序反過來，主張的力道就不會被開場的 hedge 吃掉。
cards.pmNote: 團隊變大時，PM 的產出從「做東西」變成「判斷東西」。
cards.episode: How to build trust and grow as a product leader | Fareed Mosavat (Reforge, Slack, Instacart, Zynga, Pixar)

alts.quote: The way I think about it is talent basically controls the slope of the curve, but most things are actually acquirable skills.
alts.zh: 我的想法是：天分只是決定那條曲線的斜率，但大多數東西其實都是可以習得的技能。

alts.quote: the best way to get feedback from people is not by asking what they think, but to put something concrete in front of them and then have them react to it, right?
alts.zh: 要拿到回饋，最好的方式不是問人家怎麼想，而是先擺一個具體的東西在他面前，讓他反應，對吧？

alts.quote: The old way I think is shitty. I think it's broken, and I haven't found anything out there that is innovating on this.
alts.zh: 舊的做法我覺得很爛。我覺得它是壞的，而且我沒看到市面上有任何人在改良它。

cards.pattern: What I've found over the years with [對象] is that they start to use [框架] to justify [錯誤].
cards.quote: And that what I've found over the years with founders is that they start to use Proven, Better, New to justify a wrong idea.
cards.zh: 我這些年在創辦人身上發現的是，他們會開始拿「已驗證、更好、全新」這套框架去合理化一個錯的點子。
cards.why: over the years 是時間背書，讓觀察聽起來有樣本數。指出的是「框架被拿去護航」而不是「這個框架不好」，批評更精準。
cards.episode: The hidden pattern behind successful products | Mark Pincus (Founder of Zynga)

alts.quote: But, what I've found is when you build a product, most founders, and most teams kind of stop when it works.
alts.zh: 但我發現的是，做產品的時候，大部分創辦人跟團隊在「能用了」的那一刻就停了。

alts.quote: What I've found is, oftentimes when you go into corporate environments, like people start becoming very sterile in the facts that they provide.
alts.zh: 我發現的是，很多時候你走進大公司的環境，大家提供的事實會開始變得很無菌、很乾。

alts.quote: What I've found talking to people who want to start what they think is a marketplace is that they think too much about a marketplace before they're a marketplace.
alts.zh: 我跟那些想做他們自認為是媒合平台的人聊下來，發現他們在還不是平台之前，就想太多平台的事。

cards.pattern: Past that point, I would argue: just focus on [唯一該做的事].
cards.quote: Past that point, I would argue: Just focus on the positional game.
cards.zh: 過了那個點之後，我會說：專心打位置戰就好。
cards.why: 先設一個時間界線（past that point），再給一句極短的建議。條件明確的建議比全稱建議更容易被採納。
cards.episode: Tobi Lutke

alts.quote: Stop focusing as much on what you want to say and focus more on what you want your audience to remember.
alts.zh: 別再那麼在意「你想說什麼」，多想想「你想讓聽眾記住什麼」。

alts.quote: If you start your story with 'Our company is,' you focus on your solution. If you start with 'The problem we are solving is,' then you focus on the problem.
alts.zh: 如果你的故事開頭是「我們公司是…」，你的焦點就在解法。如果開頭是「我們要解決的問題是…」，焦點就在問題上。

alts.quote: A lot of times when we write a sentence, there's actually already a point of view baked in, but you don't want it to be an accidental point of view.
alts.zh: 很多時候我們寫一句話，裡面其實已經藏了一個立場——但你不會希望那是一個「不小心跑出來的」立場。

cards.pattern: What I've found is, oftentimes when you [情境], people start [問題行為].
cards.quote: What I've found is, oftentimes when you go into corporate environments, like people start becoming very sterile in the facts that they provide.
cards.zh: 我發現的是，很多時候你走進大公司的環境，大家提供的事實會開始變得很無菌、很乾。
cards.why: oftentimes 把頻率講清楚（常常但不是每次），這一步讓主張站得住。批評的對象是環境造成的行為，不是人的能力。
cards.episode: Jeetu Patel

alts.quote: What I've found talking to people who want to start what they think is a marketplace is that they think too much about a marketplace before they're a marketplace.
alts.zh: 我跟那些想做他們自認為是媒合平台的人聊下來，發現他們在還不是平台之前，就想太多平台的事。

alts.quote: And that what I've found over the years with founders is that they start to use Proven, Better, New to justify a wrong idea.
alts.zh: 我這些年在創辦人身上發現的是，他們會開始拿「已驗證、更好、全新」這套框架去合理化一個錯的點子。

alts.quote: What I've found is that once you commit to a decision, you actually learn more post committing to that decision about what's going to work and not going to work, and you move out of the hypothetical.
alts.zh: 我發現的是，一旦你對一個決定拍板，你在拍板之後反而會學到更多——什麼會成、什麼不會成——而且你會離開純假設的狀態。

cards.pattern: I would argue in retrospect, yes, there were [遺憾], but [當時的理由].
cards.quote: I would argue in retrospect, absolutely, yes, there were opportunities that were left on the table, but in early days you leave good opportunities because you have to focus on other things.
cards.zh: 回頭看我會說，沒錯，確實有些機會被放掉了，但早期你就是會放掉好機會，因為你必須專注在別的事情上。
cards.why: 先大方承認損失（absolutely, yes），再解釋當時的取捨。承認在前、辯護在後，聽起來像檢討而不是找藉口。
cards.episode: Lessons from Airtable’s unconventional growth strategy | Zoelle Egner

alts.quote: Complexity does kill companies. Maybe not as quickly as other things, but much more reliably than other things.
alts.zh: 複雜度真的會殺死公司。也許沒有其他東西那麼快，但可靠得多。

alts.quote: I'm just trying to argue this advice applied to a startup that's too early is actively not helpful.
alts.zh: 我只是想主張：把這套建議套在太早期的新創身上，是「主動有害」而不只是沒用。

alts.quote: But human beings are notoriously good at trading off the long run just to feel good in the short run. That's why we're all eating chocolate and cupcakes and stuff that we know is bad for us because it feels good.
alts.zh: 人類非常擅長犧牲長期，只為了短期舒服。所以我們才都在吃明知不好的巧克力跟杯子蛋糕。

cards.pattern: Can I actually jump in real quick because [為什麼值得打斷——通常是稱讚對方剛講的東西]?
cards.quote: Can I actually jump in real quick because that's a really cool framework that I haven't heard before, this idea of fuel and engine from a marketing perspective.
cards.zh: 我可以插一下嗎？因為這個框架真的很酷，我以前沒聽過——就是行銷上「燃料 vs 引擎」這個想法。
cards.why: 插話三段式的完整範例：請求（Can I jump in）＋時間承諾（real quick）＋理由（because 後面整段都在誇對方）。理由是利他的，所以打斷聽起來像加分而不是搶麥。
cards.pmNote: 會議上打斷別人前先把「為什麼現在打斷」講出來，對方才不會覺得被搶話。
cards.episode: How to build a powerful marketing machine | Emily Kramer (Asana, Carta, MKT1)

alts.quote: I want to come back real quick to the activation metric because it's something that a lot of people somewhat misuse and think maybe incorrectly about.
alts.zh: 我想快速回到啟用指標那件事，因為很多人其實在誤用它、想錯方向。

alts.quote: Now can I jump in here, please? Because then people are like, "But how do I do this?"
alts.zh: 我可以在這邊插一句嗎？因為接下來大家一定會問：「那我到底該怎麼做？」

alts.quote: Just one quick interjection there is that when I coined growth hacking, I did not think of it as a bunch of one-off hacks.
alts.zh: 這邊我快速插一句：我當初造 growth hacking 這個詞的時候，並不是指一堆一次性的小花招。

cards.pattern: I want to ask you one question about [主題] real quick and I'll keep it short just because I know we're going to run out of time.
cards.quote: So I want to ask you one question about hiring marketing real quick and I'll keep it short just because I know we're going to run out of time.
cards.zh: 我想快速問一個關於行銷招募的問題，我會講短一點，因為我知道我們時間快不夠了。
cards.why: 時間承諾講了兩次（real quick、I'll keep it short），再用 because 把理由歸給「時間快到了」這個雙方共同的限制，而不是自己想講。
cards.pmNote: 會議尾聲要硬塞議題，先自報「我只佔一分鐘」再說要問什麼，主持人比較不會擋。
cards.episode: The art of building legendary brands | Arielle Jackson (Google, Square, Marketer in Residence at First Round Capital)

alts.quote: So one other follow up question real quick on the hiring and then I want to talk about one other bucket of work.
alts.zh: 我想快速再追一個關於招募的問題，然後我想聊另一塊工作。

alts.quote: I'm not going to interrupt the flow conversation. I'm just going to summarize in Zoom chat this is what I've heard, and this is what I think we're saying in this conversation.
alts.zh: 我不打斷大家的討論節奏，我直接在 Zoom 聊天室整理一下我聽到的、以及我認為我們在談的東西。

alts.quote: And I'm like, "Time out. What you're going to do is raise prices again. You just told me you 12x-ed the price and nothing observable changed."
alts.zh: 我就說：「等一下。你接下來要做的是再漲一次價。你剛剛才跟我說你把價格拉了十二倍，結果什麼都沒變。」

cards.pattern: Let me throw in a question real quick before we get to [下一段].
cards.quote: Let me throw in a question real quick before we get to the last piece.
cards.zh: 在進到最後一段之前，我快速丟一個問題。
cards.why: throw in 把問題講成「順手丟進去」，份量很輕；before we get to… 同時承諾了插話的結束點，對方知道議程沒被打亂。
cards.episode: How Snyk built a product-led growth juggernaut | Ben Williams (VP of Product at Snyk)

alts.quote: Let me take two tangents here real quick.
alts.zh: 我快速岔兩個題。

alts.quote: Just one quick interjection there is that when I coined growth hacking, I did not think of it as a bunch of one-off hacks.
alts.zh: 這邊我快速插一句：我當初造 growth hacking 這個詞的時候，並不是指一堆一次性的小花招。

alts.quote: I'm taking us off track, but I want to go a little deeper with this.
alts.zh: 我知道這樣會離題，但我想在這裡多挖一點。

cards.pattern: Let me follow that thread real quickly because [為什麼值得追].
cards.quote: Let me follow that thread real quickly because that's really interesting.
cards.zh: 我快速追一下那條線，因為那真的很有意思。
cards.why: 請求＋時間承諾＋理由三段全在一句話裡，只用十來個字。thread（線頭）是英文會議裡指「剛剛那個沒講完的點」最常用的字。
cards.episode: From ChatGPT to Instagram to Uber: The quiet architect behind the world’s most popular products | Peter Deng

alts.quote: Can I actually jump in real quick because that's a really cool framework that I haven't heard before, this idea of fuel and engine from a marketing perspective.
alts.zh: 我可以插一下嗎？因為這個框架真的很酷，我以前沒聽過——就是行銷上「燃料 vs 引擎」這個想法。

alts.quote: Now can I jump in here, please? Because then people are like, "But how do I do this?"
alts.zh: 我可以在這邊插一句嗎？因為接下來大家一定會問：「那我到底該怎麼做？」

alts.quote: So yeah, anyway, sorry, that's just a rant, but you should try it.
alts.zh: 總之，抱歉，剛剛那段只是我在碎念——但你真的該試試看。

cards.quote: Can I double click on that though for a second?
cards.zh: 我可以就那一點再往下鑽一下嗎？就一下下。
cards.why: 來賓反過來打斷主持人。though 表示「我知道你想往下走」，for a second 是時間承諾。double click 在科技業會議＝「就這點再深入」。
cards.pmNote: double click on X 幾乎是英文產品會議的標配動詞，比 dig deeper 更常聽到。
cards.episode: He saved OpenAI, invented the “Like” button, and built Google Maps: Bret Taylor on the future of careers, coding, agents, and more

alts.quote: Just to double click on that one real quick, so what you're describing for the visual is you're presenting here's our options, here's our three options on a slide.
alts.zh: 這點我很快追一下——你剛說的那個視覺化，意思是你把三個選項放在一張投影片上對吧？

alts.quote: I have a few follow up questions along those lines, but before we do that I want to double click on this friction logging process.
alts.zh: 我沿著這條線還有幾個追問，但在那之前，我想先就這個 friction logging 的流程往下鑽。

alts.quote: So is that my legacy? Yeah, and maybe there's some ego implicit in that, but can I go on for just a bit on this?
alts.zh: 所以那算是我的 legacy 嗎？算吧，裡面可能也有一點自我——不過我可以再多講一下嗎？

cards.pattern: I just want to highlight real quick, [對方剛講的東西] is really important.
cards.quote: I just want to highlight real quick, this phrasing is really important.
cards.zh: 我想快速標一下重點——這個講法真的很關鍵。
cards.why: 插話的理由是「幫大家畫重點」，完全利他。just want to highlight 把自己降級成一支螢光筆，不是來搶發言權的。
cards.pmNote: 幫別人的話畫重點是最安全的插話理由，因為打斷的受益者是全場而不是你。
cards.episode: An operator’s guide to product strategy | Chandra Janakiraman (CPO at VRChat, ex-Meta, Headspace, Zynga)

alts.quote: So I want to ask you one question about hiring marketing real quick and I'll keep it short just because I know we're going to run out of time.
alts.zh: 我想快速問一個關於行銷招募的問題，我會講短一點，因為我知道我們時間快不夠了。

alts.quote: I'm taking us off track, but I want to go a little deeper with this.
alts.zh: 我知道這樣會離題，但我想在這裡多挖一點。

alts.quote: Just one quick interjection there is that when I coined growth hacking, I did not think of it as a bunch of one-off hacks.
alts.zh: 這邊我快速插一句：我當初造 growth hacking 這個詞的時候，並不是指一堆一次性的小花招。

cards.pattern: I'm going to jump in real quick just to highlight [對方剛講的重點].
cards.quote: I'm going to jump in real quick just to highlight what you're talking...
cards.zh: 我快速插一下，只是想把你剛剛講的重點標出來……
cards.why: 用直述句（I'm going to）不徵求同意，但立刻用 just to highlight 說明目的是替對方放大。強度比 Can I jump in 高，風險靠理由抵銷。
cards.episode: How to measure AI developer productivity in 2025 | Nicole Forsgren

alts.quote: I'm going to take a quick tangent down the being the first PM route real quick.
alts.zh: 我要快速岔題，往「第一位 PM」那條路走一下。

alts.quote: And I'm like, "Time out. What you're going to do is raise prices again. You just told me you 12x-ed the price and nothing observable changed."
alts.zh: 我就說：「等一下。你接下來要做的是再漲一次價。你剛剛才跟我說你把價格拉了十二倍，結果什麼都沒變。」

alts.quote: So a downside we haven't mentioned, but I'm just going to call it out, is holiday.
alts.zh: 有一個我們還沒提到的缺點，我就直接講出來——就是休假。

cards.pattern: I want to come back real quick to [先前的點] because [為什麼大家需要它].
cards.quote: I want to come back real quick to the activation metric because it's something that a lot of people somewhat misuse and think maybe incorrectly about.
cards.zh: 我想快速回到啟用指標那件事，因為很多人其實在誤用它、想錯方向。
cards.why: come back to 表示「這是回收，不是開新戰場」；because 後面講的是聽眾的困惑，不是自己的好奇心。
cards.episode: Meta’s Head of Product (and 29th employee) on working with Mark Zuckerberg, early growth tactics, why PMs are like conductors, and more | Naomi Gleit

alts.quote: So I want to ask you one question about hiring marketing real quick and I'll keep it short just because I know we're going to run out of time.
alts.zh: 我想快速問一個關於行銷招募的問題，我會講短一點，因為我知道我們時間快不夠了。

alts.quote: Just one quick interjection there is that when I coined growth hacking, I did not think of it as a bunch of one-off hacks.
alts.zh: 這邊我快速插一句：我當初造 growth hacking 這個詞的時候，並不是指一堆一次性的小花招。

alts.quote: Now can I jump in here, please? Because then people are like, "But how do I do this?"
alts.zh: 我可以在這邊插一句嗎？因為接下來大家一定會問：「那我到底該怎麼做？」

cards.quote: I want to talk about just one other topic real quick and then we'll wrap this up.
cards.zh: 我想再快速聊一個主題，然後我們就收尾。
cards.why: just one other＋and then we'll wrap this up，把剩下的議程長度講死，對方知道這是最後一次被打斷。
cards.pmNote: 「還有一件事，講完就結束」是延長會議時最不惹人厭的說法。
cards.episode: How Shopify builds a high-intensity culture | Farhan Thawar (VP and Head of Eng)

alts.quote: So I want to ask you one question about hiring marketing real quick and I'll keep it short just because I know we're going to run out of time.
alts.zh: 我想快速問一個關於行銷招募的問題，我會講短一點，因為我知道我們時間快不夠了。

alts.quote: I'm taking us off track, but I want to go a little deeper with this.
alts.zh: 我知道這樣會離題，但我想在這裡多挖一點。

alts.quote: Just one quick interjection there is that when I coined growth hacking, I did not think of it as a bunch of one-off hacks.
alts.zh: 這邊我快速插一句：我當初造 growth hacking 這個詞的時候，並不是指一堆一次性的小花招。

cards.pattern: Let me take [數量] tangents here real quick.
cards.quote: Let me take two tangents here real quick.
cards.zh: 我快速岔兩個題。
cards.why: 先把「岔題」講明並報出數量（two），聽的人就能預期什麼時候回主線。不報數量的岔題才是讓人焦慮的那種。
cards.episode: How to show up in any room with a low heart rate: Silicon Valley’s missing etiquette playbook | Sam Lessin

alts.quote: Let me throw in a question real quick before we get to the last piece.
alts.zh: 在進到最後一段之前，我快速丟一個問題。

alts.quote: Just one quick interjection there is that when I coined growth hacking, I did not think of it as a bunch of one-off hacks.
alts.zh: 這邊我快速插一句：我當初造 growth hacking 這個詞的時候，並不是指一堆一次性的小花招。

alts.quote: I'm taking us off track, but I want to go a little deeper with this.
alts.zh: 我知道這樣會離題，但我想在這裡多挖一點。

cards.pattern: I'm going to take a quick tangent down the [主題] route.
cards.quote: I'm going to take a quick tangent down the being the first PM route real quick.
cards.zh: 我要快速岔題，往「第一位 PM」那條路走一下。
cards.why: take a tangent down [X] route 明講岔題的方向，等於先給地圖再走。逐字稿裡 real quick 重複出現，是真實口語的冗贅，不必學。
cards.episode: Why not asking for what you want is holding you back | Kenneth Berger (exec coach, first PM at Slack)

alts.quote: I'm going to jump in real quick just to highlight what you're talking...
alts.zh: 我快速插一下，只是想把你剛剛講的重點標出來……

alts.quote: So a downside we haven't mentioned, but I'm just going to call it out, is holiday.
alts.zh: 有一個我們還沒提到的缺點，我就直接講出來——就是休假。

alts.quote: I'm not going to interrupt the flow conversation. I'm just going to summarize in Zoom chat this is what I've heard, and this is what I think we're saying in this conversation.
alts.zh: 我不打斷大家的討論節奏，我直接在 Zoom 聊天室整理一下我聽到的、以及我認為我們在談的東西。

cards.quote: There's a couple more things you mentioned that I want to come back to real quick.
cards.zh: 你剛剛提到還有幾件事，我想快速繞回去。
cards.why: 把插話包裝成「回收你自己講過的東西」，主權還在對方身上；a couple more 又預告了長度。
cards.episode: Unorthodox PM wisdom: Automating user insights, unselling job candidates, logging every decision, more | Kevin Yien (Stripe, Square, Mutiny)

alts.quote: Before we get to the next topic, I wanted to come back to the stats that you had real quick.
alts.zh: 在進到下一個主題之前，我想快速回到你剛剛給的那些數字。

alts.quote: I'm taking us off track, but I want to go a little deeper with this.
alts.zh: 我知道這樣會離題，但我想在這裡多挖一點。

alts.quote: And one core idea I don't think we've mentioned yet is that we strongly believe in people's intuition about how they should spend their time if they have the chance.
alts.zh: 還有一個核心想法我覺得我們還沒提到：我們非常相信一個人只要有機會，他自己知道時間該花在哪。

cards.pattern: Real quick on [主題], I was going to ask this.
cards.quote: Real quick on the Vine and Periscope point, I was going to ask this.
cards.zh: 快速回到 Vine 和 Periscope 那個點，我本來想問這個。
cards.why: Real quick on [主題] 把時間承諾和話題座標壓成一個前綴，兩個字就完成定位，是英文會議裡最省力的插話開頭。
cards.episode: Twitter’s former Head of Product opens up: being fired, meeting Elon, changing stagnant culture, building consumer product, more | Kayvon Beykpour

alts.quote: So I want to ask you one question about hiring marketing real quick and I'll keep it short just because I know we're going to run out of time.
alts.zh: 我想快速問一個關於行銷招募的問題，我會講短一點，因為我知道我們時間快不夠了。

alts.quote: I'm not going to interrupt the flow conversation. I'm just going to summarize in Zoom chat this is what I've heard, and this is what I think we're saying in this conversation.
alts.zh: 我不打斷大家的討論節奏，我直接在 Zoom 聊天室整理一下我聽到的、以及我認為我們在談的東西。

alts.quote: And I'm like, "Time out. What you're going to do is raise prices again. You just told me you 12x-ed the price and nothing observable changed."
alts.zh: 我就說：「等一下。你接下來要做的是再漲一次價。你剛剛才跟我說你把價格拉了十二倍，結果什麼都沒變。」

cards.pattern: Real quick on [主題] because [理由].
cards.quote: Real quick on Yahoo because it makes me think about it.
cards.zh: 快速講一下 Yahoo，因為它讓我想到這件事。
cards.why: 只剩三個成分：時間承諾＋主題＋because 理由。示範這個公式可以縮到多短還成立。
cards.episode: 4 questions Shreyas Doshi wishes he’d asked himself sooner | Former PM leader at Stripe, Twitter, Google

alts.quote: I want to come back real quick to the activation metric because it's something that a lot of people somewhat misuse and think maybe incorrectly about.
alts.zh: 我想快速回到啟用指標那件事，因為很多人其實在誤用它、想錯方向。

alts.quote: Just one quick interjection there is that when I coined growth hacking, I did not think of it as a bunch of one-off hacks.
alts.zh: 這邊我快速插一句：我當初造 growth hacking 這個詞的時候，並不是指一堆一次性的小花招。

alts.quote: I'm not going to interrupt the flow conversation. I'm just going to summarize in Zoom chat this is what I've heard, and this is what I think we're saying in this conversation.
alts.zh: 我不打斷大家的討論節奏，我直接在 Zoom 聊天室整理一下我聽到的、以及我認為我們在談的東西。

cards.pattern: So one other follow up question real quick on [主題] and then I want to talk about [下一塊].
cards.quote: So one other follow up question real quick on the hiring and then I want to talk about one other bucket of work.
cards.zh: 我想快速再追一個關於招募的問題，然後我想聊另一塊工作。
cards.why: 插話的同時報出下一站，等於把主持棒還回去；對方知道這不是一串失控的追問。
cards.episode: How a great founder becomes a great CEO | Jonathan Lowenhar (co-founder of Enjoy The Work)

alts.quote: So I want to ask you one question about hiring marketing real quick and I'll keep it short just because I know we're going to run out of time.
alts.zh: 我想快速問一個關於行銷招募的問題，我會講短一點，因為我知道我們時間快不夠了。

alts.quote: Just one quick interjection there is that when I coined growth hacking, I did not think of it as a bunch of one-off hacks.
alts.zh: 這邊我快速插一句：我當初造 growth hacking 這個詞的時候，並不是指一堆一次性的小花招。

alts.quote: It gets easier. I don't want to go off too much of a tangent, but the thing you have to remember is that pricing is not this knob that you can turn separate from the rest of your strategy.
alts.zh: 是會變簡單。我不想扯太遠，但有件事一定要記得：定價不是一個可以單獨轉的旋鈕，它跟整套策略是連在一起的。

cards.pattern: Before we get to the next topic, I wanted to come back to [先前的東西] real quick.
cards.quote: Before we get to the next topic, I wanted to come back to the stats that you had real quick.
cards.zh: 在進到下一個主題之前，我想快速回到你剛剛給的那些數字。
cards.why: 用過去式 I wanted 而不是 I want，把需求講得像早就存在、只是在等一個空檔，聽起來比較不急。
cards.episode: How to hit revenue targets in a recession | Sahil Mansuri (Bravado)

alts.quote: I want to come back real quick to the activation metric because it's something that a lot of people somewhat misuse and think maybe incorrectly about.
alts.zh: 我想快速回到啟用指標那件事，因為很多人其實在誤用它、想錯方向。

alts.quote: Just one quick interjection there is that when I coined growth hacking, I did not think of it as a bunch of one-off hacks.
alts.zh: 這邊我快速插一句：我當初造 growth hacking 這個詞的時候，並不是指一堆一次性的小花招。

alts.quote: So is that my legacy? Yeah, and maybe there's some ego implicit in that, but can I go on for just a bit on this?
alts.zh: 所以那算是我的 legacy 嗎？算吧，裡面可能也有一點自我——不過我可以再多講一下嗎？

cards.quote: That's an awesome story, just to comment in that real quick.
cards.zh: 那故事太棒了，我快速針對它講一句。
cards.why: 先給評價再要發言權，讚美就是插話的入場券；just to comment 把自己限縮成「只留一句評論」。
cards.episode: Behind the product: Duolingo streaks | Jackson Shuttleworth (Group PM, Retention Team)

alts.quote: Can I actually jump in real quick because that's a really cool framework that I haven't heard before, this idea of fuel and engine from a marketing perspective.
alts.zh: 我可以插一下嗎？因為這個框架真的很酷，我以前沒聽過——就是行銷上「燃料 vs 引擎」這個想法。

alts.quote: So yeah, anyway, sorry, that's just a rant, but you should try it.
alts.zh: 總之，抱歉，剛剛那段只是我在碎念——但你真的該試試看。

alts.quote: Can I share one story about candidate market fit-
alts.zh: 我可以分享一個關於「候選人市場適配」的故事嗎？

cards.pattern: I have a few follow up questions along those lines, but before we do that I want to double click on [某個點].
cards.quote: I have a few follow up questions along those lines, but before we do that I want to double click on this friction logging process.
cards.zh: 我沿著這條線還有幾個追問，但在那之前，我想先就這個 friction logging 的流程往下鑽。
cards.why: 先宣告「我手上有排隊的問題」再插隊，等於公開自己的議程；被打斷的人知道之後還有什麼在等。
cards.pmNote: 講出你手上有幾個待問的問題，是主持會議時控制節奏最簡單的手法。
cards.episode: Building a culture of excellence | David Singleton (CTO of Stripe)

alts.quote: Anything you want to double click on before we get to our very exciting lightning round?
alts.zh: 在進到快問快答之前，有沒有什麼你想再深入講的？

alts.quote: Can I double click on that though for a second?
alts.zh: 我可以就那一點再往下鑽一下嗎？就一下下。

alts.quote: It gets easier. I don't want to go off too much of a tangent, but the thing you have to remember is that pricing is not this knob that you can turn separate from the rest of your strategy.
alts.zh: 是會變簡單。我不想扯太遠，但有件事一定要記得：定價不是一個可以單獨轉的旋鈕，它跟整套策略是連在一起的。

cards.quote: Before we get to that, before we get to that real quick-
cards.zh: 在講那個之前——在講那個之前，等一下——
cards.why: 真實搶話的樣子：重複同一句、句尾被截斷。母語者插話時也不是完整句子，而是把 Before we get to that 講兩次直到對方停下來。
cards.pmNote: 線上會議搶話要靠重複短句佔住聲道，一次講完整長句通常會被蓋掉。
cards.episode: 5 essential questions to craft a winning strategy | Roger Martin (author, advisor, speaker)

alts.quote: Real quick on Yahoo because it makes me think about it.
alts.zh: 快速講一下 Yahoo，因為它讓我想到這件事。

alts.quote: Just one quick interjection there is that when I coined growth hacking, I did not think of it as a bunch of one-off hacks.
alts.zh: 這邊我快速插一句：我當初造 growth hacking 這個詞的時候，並不是指一堆一次性的小花招。

alts.quote: I'm taking us off track, but I want to go a little deeper with this.
alts.zh: 我知道這樣會離題，但我想在這裡多挖一點。

cards.pattern: Anything you want to double click on before we get to [下一段]?
cards.quote: Anything you want to double click on before we get to our very exciting lightning round?
cards.zh: 在進到快問快答之前，有沒有什麼你想再深入講的？
cards.why: 反向操作——把插話權讓給對方。切段落之前留一個開口，比直接推進更不會漏掉重要的東西。
cards.pmNote: 換議題前問一句「還有什麼想補的」，比事後被追加意見便宜得多。
cards.episode: He saved OpenAI, invented the “Like” button, and built Google Maps: Bret Taylor on the future of careers, coding, agents, and more

alts.quote: I have a few follow up questions along those lines, but before we do that I want to double click on this friction logging process.
alts.zh: 我沿著這條線還有幾個追問，但在那之前，我想先就這個 friction logging 的流程往下鑽。

alts.quote: Can I double click on that though for a second?
alts.zh: 我可以就那一點再往下鑽一下嗎？就一下下。

alts.quote: It gets easier. I don't want to go off too much of a tangent, but the thing you have to remember is that pricing is not this knob that you can turn separate from the rest of your strategy.
alts.zh: 是會變簡單。我不想扯太遠，但有件事一定要記得：定價不是一個可以單獨轉的旋鈕，它跟整套策略是連在一起的。

cards.quote: Can you just remind us real quick while we're on there?
cards.zh: 趁我們還在講這個，你可以快速幫我們複習一下嗎？
cards.why: 把插話變成請對方講——風險轉嫁給自己（是我們忘了）；while we're on there 又說明現在問最有效率。
cards.episode: Become a better communicator: Specific frameworks to improve your clarity, influence, and impact | Wes Kao (coach, entrepreneur, advisor)

alts.quote: Just to double click on that one real quick, so what you're describing for the visual is you're presenting here's our options, here's our three options on a slide.
alts.zh: 這點我很快追一下——你剛說的那個視覺化，意思是你把三個選項放在一張投影片上對吧？

alts.quote: Just one quick interjection there is that when I coined growth hacking, I did not think of it as a bunch of one-off hacks.
alts.zh: 這邊我快速插一句：我當初造 growth hacking 這個詞的時候，並不是指一堆一次性的小花招。

alts.quote: I'm not going to interrupt the flow conversation. I'm just going to summarize in Zoom chat this is what I've heard, and this is what I think we're saying in this conversation.
alts.zh: 我不打斷大家的討論節奏，我直接在 Zoom 聊天室整理一下我聽到的、以及我認為我們在談的東西。

cards.pattern: I think that's the key part, but let me pause there and then I'll talk about [下一段].
cards.quote: I think that's the key part, but let me pause there and then I'll talk a little bit about ChatGPT and some of my reasoning behind that.
cards.zh: 我覺得那是關鍵的部分，但我先停在這裡，然後再來講一點 ChatGPT 和我背後的理由。
cards.why: 自己講太久時的自我收斂：先標出重點（that's the key part）、主動讓出發言權（let me pause there）、再預告下一段。台灣人常一路講到沒氣才停。
cards.episode: Brian Balfour: 10 lessons on career, growth, and life

alts.quote: Sometimes I'm like, "Who's owning this?" And it's like people don't know. That's why I think it's very important to have a single-threaded owner.
alts.zh: 有時候我問「這件事誰在 own？」結果大家都不知道。這就是為什麼一定要有一個單一負責人。

alts.quote: Is everyone in agreement with that or is there some dissent about whether that's an accurate portrayal of where we've landed with this conversation?
alts.zh: 大家都同意嗎？還是有人覺得我這樣描述我們的結論並不準確？

alts.quote: But before we do that, let me just summarize maybe the top five attributes and kind of traits you just shared, and then I have a two part question around this.
alts.zh: 在進到那個之前，我先把你剛剛講的五個特質整理一次，然後我有一個兩段式的問題。

cards.quote: And again, just to summarize where we're at, just to give people the advice we've shared so far.
cards.zh: 再一次，快速摘要一下我們現在講到哪，把目前分享過的建議整理給大家。
