cards.why: 摘要的理由是利他（give people），不是「我要確認」。where we're at 把摘要定位成進度回報，聽起來像服務而不是打斷。
cards.episode: Aishwarya Naresh Reganti + Kiriti Badam

alts.quote: Let me just try to summarize what you shared, this five step framework.
alts.zh: 我試著把你剛剛講的整理一下，這個五步驟的框架。

alts.quote: So just to summarize so people can have just a very short definition of this framework.
alts.zh: 所以快速總結一下，讓大家可以有一個很短的定義知道這個框架是什麼。

alts.quote: Is everyone in agreement with that or is there some dissent about whether that's an accurate portrayal of where we've landed with this conversation?
alts.zh: 大家都同意嗎？還是有人覺得我這樣描述我們的結論並不準確？

cards.pattern: To close out this thread on [主題], just to summarize your advice here.
cards.quote: Okay, so to close out this thread on engineering leaders, finding the right balance, just to summarize your advice here.
cards.zh: 好，那就把工程主管怎麼拿捏平衡這條線收掉，快速總結一下你的建議。
cards.why: close out this thread 明講「這一段要關掉了」，摘要就成了關門動作而不是新的討論；接著才進下一個主題，段落感很清楚。
cards.pmNote: 會議每收掉一段就摘要一次，比最後才總結更能避免同一件事被重講。
cards.episode: The things engineers are desperate for PMs to understand | Camille Fournier (author of “The Manager’s Path,” ex-CTO at Rent the Runway)

alts.quote: So just to summarize the audit that you do, I wrote some notes as you were talking, and maybe we can keep going from that point.
alts.zh: 所以快速總結一下你做的那套盤點——你講的時候我有做筆記——然後我們可以從那個點繼續往下。

alts.quote: Let me just try to summarize what you shared, this five step framework.
alts.zh: 我試著把你剛剛講的整理一下，這個五步驟的框架。

alts.quote: So put succinctly, stay attached to the growth and hold mindset a little loosely.
alts.zh: 簡單講就是：緊抓成長，心態就抓鬆一點。

cards.pattern: So just to summarize so people can have a very short definition of [框架].
cards.quote: So just to summarize so people can have just a very short definition of this framework.
cards.zh: 所以快速總結一下，讓大家可以有一個很短的定義知道這個框架是什麼。
cards.why: so people can… 把摘要的受益者指定成第三方，講者就不會覺得你在幫他的話瘦身。
cards.episode: The full-stack PM | Anuj Rathi (Swiggy, Jupiter Money, Flipkart)

alts.quote: Let me just try to summarize what you shared, this five step framework.
alts.zh: 我試著把你剛剛講的整理一下，這個五步驟的框架。

alts.quote: Okay, so let me summarize things that you've taught us so far. One is think about publications that go to people that will buy your thing. Two is don't think of it broad thing.
alts.zh: 好，我來把你目前教我們的整理一下。第一，挑那些會接觸到你買家的媒體。第二，不要只想到媒體這個層級。

alts.quote: Sometimes I'm like, "Who's owning this?" And it's like people don't know. That's why I think it's very important to have a single-threaded owner.
alts.zh: 有時候我問「這件事誰在 own？」結果大家都不知道。這就是為什麼一定要有一個單一負責人。

cards.pattern: So, just to summarize, the main benefits are [1], [2], [3].
cards.quote: So, just to summarize, the main benefits are focuses you, lines, creates a cadence and creates a learning cycle.
cards.zh: 所以總結一下，主要好處是：讓你聚焦、對齊、建立節奏，還有創造一個學習循環。
cards.why: 摘要最安全的形式是把對方的話變成清單。動詞開頭排比（focuses / lines / creates）讓幾個好處聽起來是同一層級。
cards.episode: The ultimate guide to OKRs | Christina Wodtke (Stanford)

alts.quote: Let me just try to summarize what you shared, this five step framework.
alts.zh: 我試著把你剛剛講的整理一下，這個五步驟的框架。

alts.quote: But before we do that, let me just summarize maybe the top five attributes and kind of traits you just shared, and then I have a two part question around this.
alts.zh: 在進到那個之前，我先把你剛剛講的五個特質整理一次，然後我有一個兩段式的問題。

alts.quote: Yeah. So it works like this. I start with competitive alternatives.
alts.zh: 對，運作方式是這樣：我從「競爭替代方案」開始。

cards.pattern: So just to summarize [對方講的東西], I wrote some notes as you were talking, and maybe we can keep going from that point.
cards.quote: So just to summarize the audit that you do, I wrote some notes as you were talking, and maybe we can keep going from that point.
cards.zh: 所以快速總結一下你做的那套盤點——你講的時候我有做筆記——然後我們可以從那個點繼續往下。
cards.why: 補上「我剛剛在做筆記」等於出示證據，摘要的可信度立刻不同；結尾再把球丟回去（keep going from that point），摘要就不會變成結案。
cards.pmNote: 摘要時說出你邊聽邊記，對方會更願意讓你代表他的意思。
cards.episode: The ultimate guide to adding a PLG motion | Hila Qu (Reforge, GitLab)

alts.quote: So basically my long answer to your question, maybe boring answer is that I think starting next year, we're going to see early adopters starting to hockey stick their productivity.
alts.zh: 所以我這個落落長、可能還有點無聊的答案就是：我覺得從明年開始，早期採用者的生產力會開始往上翹。

alts.quote: But before we do that, let me just summarize maybe the top five attributes and kind of traits you just shared, and then I have a two part question around this.
alts.zh: 在進到那個之前，我先把你剛剛講的五個特質整理一次，然後我有一個兩段式的問題。

alts.quote: Is everyone in agreement with that or is there some dissent about whether that's an accurate portrayal of where we've landed with this conversation?
alts.zh: 大家都同意嗎？還是有人覺得我這樣描述我們的結論並不準確？

cards.pattern: So just to summarize what you shared, which I was just writing as you were talking, [重點].
cards.quote: So just to summarize what you shared, which I was just writing as you were talking about the things that essentially help Stripe build this incredible team.
cards.zh: 所以總結一下你分享的——你講的時候我就在寫——那些讓 Stripe 能建出這支超強團隊的東西。
cards.why: which I was just writing as you were talking 插在中間，一邊爭取整理的時間，一邊證明摘要不是臨時編的。
cards.episode: Building a culture of excellence | David Singleton (CTO of Stripe)

alts.quote: Let me just try to summarize what you shared, this five step framework.
alts.zh: 我試著把你剛剛講的整理一下，這個五步驟的框架。

alts.quote: So to your question, you're a feature team. You want to give it a shot, be in a real product team. These are the four things you need to go out and do.
alts.zh: 回到你的問題：你在一支功能團隊，想試試看真正的產品團隊怎麼運作——那你要去做的就是這四件事。

alts.quote: But before we do that, let me just summarize maybe the top five attributes and kind of traits you just shared, and then I have a two part question around this.
alts.zh: 在進到那個之前，我先把你剛剛講的五個特質整理一次，然後我有一個兩段式的問題。

cards.pattern: So I was taking notes as you were talking and there's kind of these [數量] items just to summarize.
cards.quote: So I was taking notes as you were talking and there's kind of these four items just to summarize.
cards.zh: 你講的時候我一直在記筆記，總結起來大概是這四項。
cards.why: 先報數量（four items）再展開，聽的人知道要等幾個點；先講數字也逼自己真的收斂到四個。
cards.pmNote: 摘要前先報數量，是讓別人願意閉嘴聽完的最短前綴。
cards.episode: Building high-performing teams | Melissa Tan (Webflow, Dropbox, Canva)

alts.quote: So to your question, you're a feature team. You want to give it a shot, be in a real product team. These are the four things you need to go out and do.
alts.zh: 回到你的問題：你在一支功能團隊，想試試看真正的產品團隊怎麼運作——那你要去做的就是這四件事。

alts.quote: But before we do that, let me just summarize maybe the top five attributes and kind of traits you just shared, and then I have a two part question around this.
alts.zh: 在進到那個之前，我先把你剛剛講的五個特質整理一次，然後我有一個兩段式的問題。

alts.quote: Let me just try to summarize what you shared, this five step framework.
alts.zh: 我試著把你剛剛講的整理一下，這個五步驟的框架。

cards.pattern: Just to summarize in case people didn't totally catch it, basically, [第一層], [第二層], [第三層].
cards.quote: Just to summarize in case people didn't totally catch it, basically, layer one is focus, layer two, tip the market, layer three, dominate the market.
cards.zh: 總結一下，怕大家沒完全抓到——基本上第一層是聚焦，第二層是把市場推倒，第三層是主宰市場。
cards.why: in case people didn't totally catch it 把「沒聽懂」的責任放到聽眾（含自己）身上，而不是暗示對方講得不清楚。這就是重述技術的核心：風險留給自己。
cards.episode: The hierarchy of engagement | Sarah Tavel (Benchmark, Greylock, Pinterest)

alts.quote: Okay, so let me summarize things that you've taught us so far. One is think about publications that go to people that will buy your thing. Two is don't think of it broad thing.
alts.zh: 好，我來把你目前教我們的整理一下。第一，挑那些會接觸到你買家的媒體。第二，不要只想到媒體這個層級。

alts.quote: Sometimes I'm like, "Who's owning this?" And it's like people don't know. That's why I think it's very important to have a single-threaded owner.
alts.zh: 有時候我問「這件事誰在 own？」結果大家都不知道。這就是為什麼一定要有一個單一負責人。

alts.quote: Two people owning a goal is no one owning a goal. One person owns the goal, who is it?
alts.zh: 兩個人一起扛一個目標，等於沒人在扛。這個目標只能有一個人負責——是誰？

cards.quote: So just to summarize really quick, I have the list here in front of me.
cards.zh: 所以快速總結一下，我這邊手上有清單。
cards.why: 摘要也要給時間承諾（really quick），並宣告手上有清單，等於預告接下來是條列而不是即興發揮。
cards.episode: How to be the best coach to product people | Petra Wille (Strong Product People)

alts.quote: I actually want to double down on that thread, but just to summarize, I have the list here.
alts.zh: 我其實想順著那條線再往下挖，但先總結一下，清單我這邊有。

alts.quote: Let me just try to summarize what you shared, this five step framework.
alts.zh: 我試著把你剛剛講的整理一下，這個五步驟的框架。

alts.quote: Yeah. So it works like this. I start with competitive alternatives.
alts.zh: 對，運作方式是這樣：我從「競爭替代方案」開始。

cards.quote: So just to summarize and make it super clear.
cards.zh: 所以總結一下，把它講到超清楚。
cards.why: 把摘要的目的講出來（make it super clear），對方就知道你不是要改寫他的話，是要幫他把話講死。
cards.episode: An inside look at X’s Community Notes | Keith Coleman (VP of Product) and Jay Baxter (ML Lead)

alts.quote: Let me just try to summarize what you shared, this five step framework.
alts.zh: 我試著把你剛剛講的整理一下，這個五步驟的框架。

alts.quote: So just to summarize so people can have just a very short definition of this framework.
alts.zh: 所以快速總結一下，讓大家可以有一個很短的定義知道這個框架是什麼。

alts.quote: And then the DRI's job is to take all that input and make a decision.
alts.zh: 然後 DRI 的工作就是把所有意見收進來，然後做決定。

cards.quote: I actually want to double down on that thread, but just to summarize, I have the list here.
cards.zh: 我其實想順著那條線再往下挖，但先總結一下，清單我這邊有。
cards.why: 先宣告「還要繼續」再摘要，摘要就不會被誤讀成結束的訊號。這是同時想收斂又不想結束話題時的解法。
cards.episode: Business strategy with Hamilton Helmer (author of 7 Powers)

alts.quote: And one last thing to touch on, you said something really important about pull, and I want to double down on that.
alts.zh: 還有最後一件事，你剛剛講到「拉力」那個點很重要，我想把它再放大講。

alts.quote: So just to summarize really quick, I have the list here in front of me.
alts.zh: 所以快速總結一下，我這邊手上有清單。

alts.quote: So to replay the system overall highlight is about the thing you want to make time for today. The most important thing today, laser is about creating barriers to distraction.
alts.zh: 把整套系統再跑一遍：highlight 是你今天最想騰出時間做的那件事；laser 是替干擾設路障。

cards.pattern: So, just to summarize, what would be [具體欄位] again, just if someone's taking notes and wants to [做出成品]?
cards.quote: So, just to summarize, what would be the headings again, just if someone's taking notes and wants to create the rule template?
cards.zh: 所以總結一下，那些標題到底是什麼？如果有人在做筆記、想照著做一份模板的話。
cards.why: 摘要收尾不是句號而是問號——把最關鍵的細節再要一次，理由是「有人要照著做」，所以不算刁難。
cards.episode: Mastering product strategy and growing as a PM | Maggie Crowley (Toast, Drift, Tripadvisor)

alts.quote: And again, just to summarize where we're at, just to give people the advice we've shared so far.
alts.zh: 再一次，快速摘要一下我們現在講到哪，把目前分享過的建議整理給大家。

alts.quote: Let me just try to summarize what you shared, this five step framework.
alts.zh: 我試著把你剛剛講的整理一下，這個五步驟的框架。

alts.quote: So put succinctly, stay attached to the growth and hold mindset a little loosely.
alts.zh: 簡單講就是：緊抓成長，心態就抓鬆一點。

cards.pattern: So just to wrap things up, is there anything else you thought would be fun to share before we get to [下一段]?
cards.quote: So just to wrap things up, is there anything else that you thought would be fun to share or maybe a piece of wisdom you want to leave listeners with before we get to a very exciting lightning round?
cards.zh: 那就準備收尾了——還有什麼你覺得好玩、想分享的，或想留給大家的一句話，然後我們才進快問快答？
cards.why: 收尾不要自己講完，最後一個開口留給對方。anything else… before we get to X 同時關門和開門，對方知道只剩一發。
cards.pmNote: 會議結束前問一句「還有什麼沒講到的」，能撈回大部分事後才冒出來的問題。
cards.episode: Thinking like a gardener not a builder, organizing teams like slime mold, the adjacent possible, and other unconventional product advice | Alex Komoroske (Stripe, Google)

alts.quote: So to your question, you're a feature team. You want to give it a shot, be in a real product team. These are the four things you need to go out and do.
alts.zh: 回到你的問題：你在一支功能團隊，想試試看真正的產品團隊怎麼運作——那你要去做的就是這四件事。

alts.quote: So maybe this is a way to come back to your question about what's the output of the shaping session, it's like it's shaped if we can give this to a technical person and they say, "Yeah, I know what to go build now."
alts.zh: 所以回到你剛剛問的「shaping session 的產出是什麼」：判準是——把它交給一個技術的人，他會說「好，我知道要蓋什麼了」。

alts.quote: So to replay the system overall highlight is about the thing you want to make time for today. The most important thing today, laser is about creating barriers to distraction.
alts.zh: 把整套系統再跑一遍：highlight 是你今天最想騰出時間做的那件事；laser 是替干擾設路障。

cards.pattern: I want to try to wrap up our first [bucket／段落].
cards.quote: I want to try to wrap up our first bucket.
cards.zh: 我想把第一塊先收掉。
cards.why: bucket（桶／塊）把長對話切成段，收尾就變成「收這一段」而不是「結束談話」；try to 再降低一層強度。
cards.pmNote: 長會議用 bucket 切段、每段各自收尾，比最後統一收斂實際得多。
cards.episode: The AI paradox: More automation, more humans, more work | Dan Shipper

alts.quote: Let me just try to summarize what you shared, this five step framework.
alts.zh: 我試著把你剛剛講的整理一下，這個五步驟的框架。

alts.quote: Here's what I heard from all of you. I'm listening, I hear this and here's what I want to do about it.
alts.zh: 以下是我從各位那裡聽到的。我有在聽，我聽到了，接下來我打算這樣做。

alts.quote: So to your question, you're a feature team. You want to give it a shot, be in a real product team. These are the four things you need to go out and do.
alts.zh: 回到你的問題：你在一支功能團隊，想試試看真正的產品團隊怎麼運作——那你要去做的就是這四件事。

cards.quote: I know I keep saying we're going to wrap this up, but here's a question and if it doesn't work, we'll get rid of it.
cards.zh: 我知道我一直說要收尾了，但這裡有個問題——如果行不通，我們就把它砍掉。
cards.why: 先自曝「我已經說過要收尾很多次」化解尷尬，再給對方一個逃生門（行不通就刪掉），破例延長就沒有壓力。
cards.episode: How Snyk built a product-led growth juggernaut | Ben Williams (VP of Product at Snyk)

alts.quote: So let's take a step back. The fear is, if I can reflect back to your original question, the fear is if I go there, I don't know what's going to happen as a consequence of that.
alts.zh: 我們退一步看。如果我把你原本的問題回映給你，那個恐懼是：如果我真的往下探，我不知道會發生什麼後果。

alts.quote: So basically my long answer to your question, maybe boring answer is that I think starting next year, we're going to see early adopters starting to hockey stick their productivity.
alts.zh: 所以我這個落落長、可能還有點無聊的答案就是：我覺得從明年開始，早期採用者的生產力會開始往上翹。

alts.quote: So maybe this is a way to come back to your question about what's the output of the shaping session, it's like it's shaped if we can give this to a technical person and they say, "Yeah, I know what to go build now."
alts.zh: 所以回到你剛剛問的「shaping session 的產出是什麼」：判準是——把它交給一個技術的人，他會說「好，我知道要蓋什麼了」。

cards.pattern: So just to wrap up on that, I'm curious, [收尾問題]?
cards.quote: So just to wrap up on that, I'm curious, where do you think this goes long term for you?
cards.zh: 那這段就收在這裡——我好奇，長期來看你覺得這會走到哪？
cards.why: 收尾語和一個往前看的問題綁在一起，段落結束的同時話題自然轉場，中間沒有空白。
cards.episode: Leaving big tech to build the #1 technology newsletter | Gergely Orosz (The Pragmatic Engineer)

alts.quote: Sometimes I'm like, "Who's owning this?" And it's like people don't know. That's why I think it's very important to have a single-threaded owner.
alts.zh: 有時候我問「這件事誰在 own？」結果大家都不知道。這就是為什麼一定要有一個單一負責人。

alts.quote: I'm going to mirror back the tips you just shared, and there's actually a secondary tip that I think is the more interesting piece.
alts.zh: 我把你剛剛給的建議重述一遍——而且我覺得裡面藏了一個更有意思的第二層建議。

alts.quote: I'm in too many conversations where I'm like, "Who is on the hook for this decision? Who cares if this decision is made?" It's not like six people with consensus. Who is the person?
alts.zh: 我參加過太多會議，我會問：「這個決定是誰扛？誰真的在乎它有沒有被做出來？」不是六個人共識，是哪一個人？

cards.pattern: Okay, so [一段完整的重述] is what I'm hearing.
cards.quote: Okay, so if you're feeling anxious right now, this is an exercise you can do and you'll feel less anxious in like five minutes is what I'm hearing.
cards.zh: 好，所以如果你現在覺得焦慮，這是一個你可以做的練習，大概五分鐘後就會沒那麼焦慮——我聽到的是這樣。
cards.why: 長重述最怕講到一半被打斷，所以整段照肯定句講完，最後才掛上 is what I'm hearing。這證明句尾式免責真正的功能是「保住前半句的語氣」。
cards.episode: Brian Chesky's secret mentor who died 9 times, started the Burning Man board, and built the world's first midlife wisdom school | Chip Conley (founder of MEA)

alts.quote: The reason I'm a little confused, just because I want to get it right, is what I'm hearing, which maybe isn't what you said
alts.zh: 我有點不確定，純粹是想弄清楚——我聽到的（可能不是你講的意思）是……

alts.quote: What I'm hearing is step one is just get your kind of peer leaders aligned behind something that may not obviously be something your leaders want you to do, is that right?
alts.zh: 我聽到的是：第一步就是先把同層的主管拉到同一邊，就算那件事你的上面不見得想要你做——是這樣嗎？

alts.quote: I say something to you like, "Lenny, I think what I'm hearing you say is you're off and you're thinking, screw you, Matt.
alts.zh: 我會對你說：「Lenny，我想我聽到你在說的是——你火了，你心裡在想：去你的，Matt。」

cards.pattern: So the fact that [某個手段] helped you [某個結果] is what I'm hearing.
cards.quote: So the fact that you pushed him out helped you get a better deal is what I'm hearing.
cards.zh: 所以是因為你把他推出去，才讓你談到更好的條件——我聽到的是這樣。
cards.why: 敏感歸因（把功勞算在某個手段上）用句尾免責最安全：先把因果講清楚，再讓對方決定要不要收下這個版本。
cards.episode: First interview with Scale AI’s CEO: $14B Meta deal, what’s working in enterprise AI, and what frontier labs are building next | Jason Droege

alts.quote: The reason I'm a little confused, just because I want to get it right, is what I'm hearing, which maybe isn't what you said
alts.zh: 我有點不確定，純粹是想弄清楚——我聽到的（可能不是你講的意思）是……

alts.quote: So kind of what I'm hearing is a lot of the work is giving humans more information versus giving machine learning algorithms more information and there's a lot more leverage potentially there, giving humans more ways to tweak and dial.
alts.zh: 所以我聽到的大概是：很多工作其實是給人更多資訊，而不是給機器學習演算法更多資訊，而那裡的槓桿可能大得多。

alts.quote: What I'm hearing is step one is just get your kind of peer leaders aligned behind something that may not obviously be something your leaders want you to do, is that right?
alts.zh: 我聽到的是：第一步就是先把同層的主管拉到同一邊，就算那件事你的上面不見得想要你做——是這樣嗎？

cards.pattern: So kind of what I'm hearing is [重述].
cards.quote: So kind of what I'm hearing is a lot of the work is giving humans more information versus giving machine learning algorithms more information and there's a lot more leverage potentially there, giving humans more ways to tweak and dial.
cards.zh: 所以我聽到的大概是：很多工作其實是給人更多資訊，而不是給機器學習演算法更多資訊，而那裡的槓桿可能大得多。
cards.why: 前置版本要靠 kind of 降溫，才不會一開口就宣告「我來總結你」。這正是前置式的代價：得多付一個緩衝詞。
cards.episode: Humanizing product development | Adriel Frederick (Reddit, Lyft, Facebook)

alts.quote: What I'm hearing is step one is just get your kind of peer leaders aligned behind something that may not obviously be something your leaders want you to do, is that right?
alts.zh: 我聽到的是：第一步就是先把同層的主管拉到同一邊，就算那件事你的上面不見得想要你做——是這樣嗎？

alts.quote: So just to mirror back what I'm hearing, there's this, if you visualize this curve at the bottom, it's like I don't even know what this is.
alts.zh: 所以把我聽到的鏡射回去：如果你把那條曲線想像出來，最底下那段就是——我根本不知道這是什麼。

alts.quote: The reason I'm a little confused, just because I want to get it right, is what I'm hearing, which maybe isn't what you said
alts.zh: 我有點不確定，純粹是想弄清楚——我聽到的（可能不是你講的意思）是……

cards.pattern: What I'm hearing is [重述], is that right?
cards.quote: What I'm hearing is step one is just get your kind of peer leaders aligned behind something that may not obviously be something your leaders want you to do, is that right?
cards.zh: 我聽到的是：第一步就是先把同層的主管拉到同一邊，就算那件事你的上面不見得想要你做——是這樣嗎？
cards.why: 前置 What I'm hearing is 開頭、句尾 is that right? 收尾，兩端都留門。長重述用這個雙夾結構最穩。
cards.episode: How to sell your ideas and rise within your company | Casey Winters, Eventbrite

alts.quote: The reason I'm a little confused, just because I want to get it right, is what I'm hearing, which maybe isn't what you said
alts.zh: 我有點不確定，純粹是想弄清楚——我聽到的（可能不是你講的意思）是……

alts.quote: Okay, so if you're feeling anxious right now, this is an exercise you can do and you'll feel less anxious in like five minutes is what I'm hearing.
alts.zh: 好，所以如果你現在覺得焦慮，這是一個你可以做的練習，大概五分鐘後就會沒那麼焦慮——我聽到的是這樣。

alts.quote: So kind of what I'm hearing is a lot of the work is giving humans more information versus giving machine learning algorithms more information and there's a lot more leverage potentially there, giving humans more ways to tweak and dial.
alts.zh: 所以我聽到的大概是：很多工作其實是給人更多資訊，而不是給機器學習演算法更多資訊，而那裡的槓桿可能大得多。

cards.pattern: If I were to reflect back what I'm hearing, it's [重述].
cards.quote: Just to close the loop on this advice around getting better at vision and strategy, if I were to reflect back what I'm hearing its be very self-aware about what you are not strong at, say openness.
cards.zh: 就把「怎麼變得更擅長願景與策略」這段收掉——如果讓我把聽到的反映回去，就是：對自己不擅長的地方要非常自覺，比如開放性。
cards.why: 用假設語氣 If I were to reflect back 把重述變成一個「提議的動作」，對方可以在你講完前就喊停。這是把風險框成自己的最高階版本。
cards.episode: Improve strategy, influence, and decision-making by understanding your brain | Evan LaPointe (founder of CORE Sciences)

alts.quote: I say something to you like, "Lenny, I think what I'm hearing you say is you're off and you're thinking, screw you, Matt.
alts.zh: 我會對你說：「Lenny，我想我聽到你在說的是——你火了，你心裡在想：去你的，Matt。」

alts.quote: The reason I'm a little confused, just because I want to get it right, is what I'm hearing, which maybe isn't what you said
alts.zh: 我有點不確定，純粹是想弄清楚——我聽到的（可能不是你講的意思）是……

alts.quote: So kind of what I'm hearing is a lot of the work is giving humans more information versus giving machine learning algorithms more information and there's a lot more leverage potentially there, giving humans more ways to tweak and dial.
alts.zh: 所以我聽到的大概是：很多工作其實是給人更多資訊，而不是給機器學習演算法更多資訊，而那裡的槓桿可能大得多。

cards.pattern: So just to mirror back what I'm hearing, [重述].
cards.quote: So just to mirror back what I'm hearing, there's this, if you visualize this curve at the bottom, it's like I don't even know what this is.
cards.zh: 所以把我聽到的鏡射回去：如果你把那條曲線想像出來，最底下那段就是——我根本不知道這是什麼。
cards.why: mirror back 是英文會議裡「重述」的正式說法，比 summarize 更明確地表示「我不加料，只是照鏡子」。
cards.pmNote: mirror back / reflect back 都表示原樣反映，用在敏感對話比 summarize 安全。
cards.episode: Slack founder: Mental models for building products people love ft. Stewart Butterfield

alts.quote: So kind of what I'm hearing is a lot of the work is giving humans more information versus giving machine learning algorithms more information and there's a lot more leverage potentially there, giving humans more ways to tweak and dial.
alts.zh: 所以我聽到的大概是：很多工作其實是給人更多資訊，而不是給機器學習演算法更多資訊，而那裡的槓桿可能大得多。

alts.quote: The reason I'm a little confused, just because I want to get it right, is what I'm hearing, which maybe isn't what you said
alts.zh: 我有點不確定，純粹是想弄清楚——我聽到的（可能不是你講的意思）是……

alts.quote: What I'm hearing is step one is just get your kind of peer leaders aligned behind something that may not obviously be something your leaders want you to do, is that right?
alts.zh: 我聽到的是：第一步就是先把同層的主管拉到同一邊，就算那件事你的上面不見得想要你做——是這樣嗎？

cards.pattern: I think what I'm hearing you say is [對方沒說出口的情緒].
cards.quote: I say something to you like, "Lenny, I think what I'm hearing you say is you're off and you're thinking, screw you, Matt.
cards.zh: 我會對你說：「Lenny，我想我聽到你在說的是——你火了，你心裡在想：去你的，Matt。」
cards.why: 用重述把對方不敢講的情緒講出來，而且把 I think what I'm hearing you say is 掛在前面，講錯了也只是「我的理解」。
cards.pmNote: 幫對方說出他不方便說的話，是把暗火拉到檯面上最快的方式。
cards.episode: How to fire people with grace, work through fear, and nurture innovation | Matt Mochary (CEO coach)

alts.quote: Just to close the loop on this advice around getting better at vision and strategy, if I were to reflect back what I'm hearing its be very self-aware about what you are not strong at, say openness.
alts.zh: 就把「怎麼變得更擅長願景與策略」這段收掉——如果讓我把聽到的反映回去，就是：對自己不擅長的地方要非常自覺，比如開放性。

alts.quote: You're sitting in the meeting and you're like, "This is a dumb question. Everyone's going to think I'm an idiot." But then you get brave and you ask it and it turns out it wasn't a dumb question.
alts.zh: 你坐在會議裡想：「這問題也太蠢，問了大家會覺得我是白痴。」結果你鼓起勇氣問了，才發現根本不是蠢問題。

alts.quote: What I'm hearing is step one is just get your kind of peer leaders aligned behind something that may not obviously be something your leaders want you to do, is that right?
alts.zh: 我聽到的是：第一步就是先把同層的主管拉到同一邊，就算那件事你的上面不見得想要你做——是這樣嗎？

cards.quote: And correct me if I'm wrong.
cards.zh: 講錯的話你糾正我。
cards.why: 重述技術的最小單位。單獨一句就能用，通常擺在一段可能記錯的事實之前或之後。
cards.episode: How to achieve hypergrowth in your business and career | Carilu Dietrich (Atlassian, Miro, Segment, 1Password)

alts.quote: So I'm not saying they didn't get the exact monthly number wrong. I'm saying they got it wrong by many factors.
alts.zh: 我不是在說他們只是月份的確切數字抓錯。我是說他們錯了好幾個量級。

alts.quote: Correct me if I'm spreading misinformation, but is that right?
alts.zh: 如果我在散播錯誤資訊就糾正我——是這樣嗎？

alts.quote: Backing up a little bit, we jumped right in. I'm curious how you even describe positioning, what the heck is positioning?
alts.zh: 稍微倒回去一下——我們一開始就直接跳進來了。我很好奇你會怎麼定義「定位」這件事？

cards.pattern: [事實前半], correct me if I'm wrong, [最可能記錯的細節].
cards.quote: You just left Wealthfront and you launched the podcast maybe a year and a half ago, correct me if I'm wrong, by a year and a half ago.
cards.zh: 你剛離開 Wealthfront，然後大概一年半前開了 podcast——講錯糾正我——大概一年半前。
cards.why: correct me if I'm wrong 插在句子中間，剛好卡在最可能記錯的數字旁邊，等於就地標示不確定的位置，而不是整句都打折。
cards.episode: Launching and growing a podcast | Chris Hutchins (All the Hacks, Wealthfront, Google)

alts.quote: The reason I'm a little confused, just because I want to get it right, is what I'm hearing, which maybe isn't what you said
alts.zh: 我有點不確定，純粹是想弄清楚——我聽到的（可能不是你講的意思）是……

alts.quote: Correct me if I'm spreading misinformation, but is that right?
alts.zh: 如果我在散播錯誤資訊就糾正我——是這樣嗎？

alts.quote: What I'm hearing is basically you give those responsibilities to the engineers, designer, and maybe other functions within the team. Is that right?
alts.zh: 我聽到的意思基本上是：你們把那些責任分給工程師、設計師，可能還有團隊裡其他角色。我理解對嗎？

cards.pattern: Something I heard from someone that worked at [公司], correct me if this is not correct, [轉述內容].
cards.quote: Something I heard from someone that worked at Intercom, correct me if this is not correct, you've always been very anti-bot in the customer support business because you didn't like how impersonal it was.
cards.zh: 我聽在 Intercom 待過的人說——不對的話糾正我——你一直很反對客服機器人，因為你覺得那太沒有人味。
cards.why: 講二手資訊時免責要更重：先揭露來源（我聽某人說），再掛 correct me if this is not correct。來源和不確定性一起給，對方才不會覺得你在放話。
cards.pmNote: 轉述聽來的事情時，把來源和不確定性一起講出來，比含糊帶過更能保護自己。
cards.episode: How Intercom rose from the ashes by betting everything on AI | Eoghan McCabe (founder and CEO)

alts.quote: The reason I'm a little confused, just because I want to get it right, is what I'm hearing, which maybe isn't what you said
alts.zh: 我有點不確定，純粹是想弄清楚——我聽到的（可能不是你講的意思）是……

alts.quote: I explicitly do not mean read a bunch of other PM artifacts. You're not going to become a better writer by reading PRDs or whatever it is or support articles. It needs to be writing that compels.
alts.zh: 我明確講：我不是叫你去讀一堆 PM 文件。讀 PRD 不會讓你變成更好的作者。你要讀的是那種會推著你行動的文字。

alts.quote: What I'm hearing is step one is just get your kind of peer leaders aligned behind something that may not obviously be something your leaders want you to do, is that right?
alts.zh: 我聽到的是：第一步就是先把同層的主管拉到同一邊，就算那件事你的上面不見得想要你做——是這樣嗎？

cards.quote: Correct me if I'm spreading misinformation, but is that right?
cards.zh: 如果我在散播錯誤資訊就糾正我——是這樣嗎？
cards.why: 把 wrong 換成 spreading misinformation 是自嘲式的升級：誇大自己可能犯的錯，反而讓氣氛變輕。
cards.episode: Building Substack | Sachin Monga (Substack, Facebook)

alts.quote: The reason I'm a little confused, just because I want to get it right, is what I'm hearing, which maybe isn't what you said
alts.zh: 我有點不確定，純粹是想弄清楚——我聽到的（可能不是你講的意思）是……

alts.quote: Okay, so if you're feeling anxious right now, this is an exercise you can do and you'll feel less anxious in like five minutes is what I'm hearing.
alts.zh: 好，所以如果你現在覺得焦慮，這是一個你可以做的練習，大概五分鐘後就會沒那麼焦慮——我聽到的是這樣。

alts.quote: What I'm hearing is step one is just get your kind of peer leaders aligned behind something that may not obviously be something your leaders want you to do, is that right?
alts.zh: 我聽到的是：第一步就是先把同層的主管拉到同一邊，就算那件事你的上面不見得想要你做——是這樣嗎？

cards.quote: I want to follow that thread, but first of all, I want to also add, and correct me if you disagree with this.
cards.zh: 我想追那條線，但首先我想補充一點——你不同意的話就說。
cards.why: 這裡要免責的不是事實而是觀點，所以用 correct me if you disagree 而不是 if I'm wrong。在別人的話上加自己的看法時，用這個版本比較準。
cards.episode: Inside Bolt: From near-death to ~$40m ARR in 5 months—one of the fastest-growing products in history | Eric Simons (founder and CEO of StackBlitz)

alts.quote: Does that resonate at all?
alts.zh: 這樣講有打中什麼嗎？

alts.quote: The reason I'm a little confused, just because I want to get it right, is what I'm hearing, which maybe isn't what you said
alts.zh: 我有點不確定，純粹是想弄清楚——我聽到的（可能不是你講的意思）是……

alts.quote: What I'm hearing is step one is just get your kind of peer leaders aligned behind something that may not obviously be something your leaders want you to do, is that right?
alts.zh: 我聽到的是：第一步就是先把同層的主管拉到同一邊，就算那件事你的上面不見得想要你做——是這樣嗎？

cards.pattern: Just to make sure I understand what you're saying there, you're saying [重述].
cards.quote: Just to make sure I understand what you're saying there, you're saying generally maybe third party tools limit what you can do, which set you up for hardship later.
cards.zh: 我確認一下我有聽懂你的意思：你是說一般來說第三方工具會限制你能做的事，之後會讓你很痛苦。
cards.why: 把「怕聽錯」的責任完全放在自己身上（make sure I understand），對方就沒有被指責表達不清的空間；接著用 you're saying 把重述標成引述。
cards.pmNote: 這句幾乎不會出錯，是英文會議裡最泛用的確認開頭。
cards.episode: The ultimate guide to Martech | Austin Hay (Reforge, Ramp, Runway)

alts.quote: So just to make sure we hear what you're saying, you're saying all of the code of these 95% engineers at OpenAI is written by AI, it's written and then they review it.
alts.zh: 我確認一下我們有聽懂你的意思——你是說 OpenAI 那 95% 工程師寫的程式碼全都是 AI 寫的，寫完他們再 review？

alts.quote: To set the answer up, I'll give you a super brief history of Make Time.
alts.zh: 為了鋪陳我的答案，我先講一段 Make Time 的超簡短來歷。

alts.quote: The reason I'm a little confused, just because I want to get it right, is what I'm hearing, which maybe isn't what you said
alts.zh: 我有點不確定，純粹是想弄清楚——我聽到的（可能不是你講的意思）是……

cards.pattern: Just to make sure I heard you right, [重述]?
cards.quote: And then just to make sure I heard you right, these five stages are roughly the same across role, so designers have the same five and they're described similarly.
cards.zh: 然後確認一下我有沒有聽對：這五個階段跨角色大致相同，設計師也是同樣五個、描述也差不多？
cards.why: I heard you right 比 I understand 更聚焦在「接收」這一端，適合用在你要覆述一組具體事實或數字的時候。
cards.episode: What sets great teams apart | Lane Shackleton (CPO of Coda)

alts.quote: So just to make sure we hear what you're saying, you're saying all of the code of these 95% engineers at OpenAI is written by AI, it's written and then they review it.
alts.zh: 我確認一下我們有聽懂你的意思——你是說 OpenAI 那 95% 工程師寫的程式碼全都是 AI 寫的，寫完他們再 review？

alts.quote: Satisfaction could be like, "I know this thing has to get done, and I got it done." Joy could be like, "Man, that was great." And they're in the same family, but they're cousins.
alts.zh: 「滿足」比較像：我知道這件事非做不可，而我做完了。「喜悅」比較像：哇，那真的太棒了。它們算同一家族，但只是表親。

alts.quote: I talk about what I like to call the magic questions, but the thing about magic questions is they're not actually questions, they're statements and they end with, "Do you agree?" Or "Is that right?"
alts.zh: 我把它叫做「魔法問句」，但重點是它們根本不是問句——它們是敘述句，結尾加上「你同意嗎？」或「我理解得對嗎？」

cards.pattern: Just to make sure we understand, when you say [對方的詞], what should people be thinking of?
cards.quote: Just to make sure we understand, when you say judgment, what should people be thinking of when you talk about judgment?
cards.zh: 我們確認一下：你說的 judgment，大家該想到的是什麼？
cards.why: 主詞用 we 而不是 I，把不懂的人擴大成全場；再用 when you say X 引述對方原字，問定義就不會像挑毛病。
cards.pmNote: 會議上遇到定義模糊的詞，用「當你說 X，你指的是什麼」比「X 是什麼意思」有禮貌得多。
cards.episode: Why half of product managers are in trouble | Nikhyl Singhal (Meta, Google)

alts.quote: Just to make sure I understand what you're saying there, you're saying generally maybe third party tools limit what you can do, which set you up for hardship later.
alts.zh: 我確認一下我有聽懂你的意思：你是說一般來說第三方工具會限制你能做的事，之後會讓你很痛苦。

alts.quote: I say something to you like, "Lenny, I think what I'm hearing you say is you're off and you're thinking, screw you, Matt.
alts.zh: 我會對你說：「Lenny，我想我聽到你在說的是——你火了，你心裡在想：去你的，Matt。」

alts.quote: Let me refine that a little bit more. It's more about giving people the information that they can use for decisions that they alone are good at...
alts.zh: 我把那個講法再修得精準一點。重點比較是：給人們他們才擅長的那類決策所需要的資訊。

cards.pattern: So just to make sure we hear what you're saying, you're saying [覆述那個難以置信的事實].
cards.quote: So just to make sure we hear what you're saying, you're saying all of the code of these 95% engineers at OpenAI is written by AI, it's written and then they review it.
cards.zh: 我確認一下我們有聽懂你的意思——你是說 OpenAI 那 95% 工程師寫的程式碼全都是 AI 寫的，寫完他們再 review？
cards.why: 聽到難以置信的數字時，先聲明是自己要確認，再逐項覆述一次。覆述本身就是最禮貌的質疑。
cards.episode: Sherwin Wu V2

alts.quote: Just to make sure I understand what you're saying there, you're saying generally maybe third party tools limit what you can do, which set you up for hardship later.
alts.zh: 我確認一下我有聽懂你的意思：你是說一般來說第三方工具會限制你能做的事，之後會讓你很痛苦。

alts.quote: Just for folks that are listening, just to calibrate what size of company you're talking about selling to here.
alts.zh: 為了讓聽的人有個基準——你剛剛講的是賣給多大規模的公司？

alts.quote: Does that resonate at all?
alts.zh: 這樣講有打中什麼嗎？

cards.pattern: And just to be clear, I'm not [利益關係], I'm just [真正的動機].
cards.quote: And just to be clear, I'm not an investor, I'm just excited about this thing.
cards.zh: 先說清楚，我不是投資人，我只是對這東西很興奮。
cards.why: just to be clear 也可以用來澄清自己：講完一段像在推銷的話之後主動揭露利益關係，可信度反而上升。
cards.pmNote: 推薦任何東西前先講清楚你跟它的關係，是最便宜的信任成本。
cards.episode: How marketplaces win: Liquidity, growth levers, quality, and more | Benjamin Lauzier (Lyft, Thumbtack, Reforge)

alts.quote: Backing up a little bit, we jumped right in. I'm curious how you even describe positioning, what the heck is positioning?
alts.zh: 稍微倒回去一下——我們一開始就直接跳進來了。我很好奇你會怎麼定義「定位」這件事？

alts.quote: So I'm not saying they didn't get the exact monthly number wrong. I'm saying they got it wrong by many factors.
alts.zh: 我不是在說他們只是月份的確切數字抓錯。我是說他們錯了好幾個量級。

alts.quote: I'm not saying that we should not take customer feedback, that's very different.
alts.zh: 我不是說不要聽客戶回饋——那是完全不同的兩件事。

cards.pattern: Just to be clear, I love [你接下來要批評的東西].
cards.quote: Just to be clear, I love Claude.
cards.zh: 先說清楚，我很愛 Claude。
cards.why: 批評一個東西之前先表態喜歡它，後面的批評才會被當成建議而不是攻擊。四個字就完成立場宣告。
cards.episode: Brian Balfour: 10 lessons on career, growth, and life

alts.quote: Two things I'd love to clarify.
alts.zh: 有兩件事我想澄清一下。

alts.quote: I love this answer. So what I'm hearing is, essentially, if you're amazing at any of these three roles, you will do well.
alts.zh: 我很喜歡這個回答。所以我聽到的意思，簡單講就是：這三個角色你任何一個做到頂尖，都會過得很好。

alts.quote: Yeah. To be clear, we're not building that, but it's a fun idea.
alts.zh: 喔對，先說清楚，我們沒有要做這個，只是覺得這想法很好玩。

cards.quote: I guess just to be clear, are these the same thing in your mind with different words?
cards.zh: 我想確認一下：在你心裡，這兩個是同一件事、只是換個詞嗎？
cards.why: 對方用了兩個近義詞時最該問的一句。in your mind 把問題限定在對方的定義體系裡，不是要他接受你的分類。
cards.episode: Business strategy with Hamilton Helmer (author of 7 Powers)

alts.quote: Satisfaction could be like, "I know this thing has to get done, and I got it done." Joy could be like, "Man, that was great." And they're in the same family, but they're cousins.
alts.zh: 「滿足」比較像：我知道這件事非做不可，而我做完了。「喜悅」比較像：哇，那真的太棒了。它們算同一家族，但只是表親。

alts.quote: And then just to make sure I heard you right, these five stages are roughly the same across role, so designers have the same five and they're described similarly.
alts.zh: 然後確認一下我有沒有聽對：這五個階段跨角色大致相同，設計師也是同樣五個、描述也差不多？

alts.quote: Please note that don't mix transparency and fairness with being predictable. Those are very different things.
alts.zh: 請注意，不要把「透明與公平」跟「可預測」混為一談。這是兩件很不一樣的事。

cards.quote: Talk a little bit about that just to make sure that point is clear.
cards.zh: 那部分再講一點，確保這個點是清楚的。
cards.why: 反過來把澄清的工作交回給對方：不說「我沒聽懂」，而說「為了確保這點清楚」，聽起來是為全場要，不是自己跟不上。
cards.episode: How tech workers actually feel about AI in 2026 | Annual AI sentiment survey (Noam Segal)

alts.quote: Backing up a little bit, we jumped right in. I'm curious how you even describe positioning, what the heck is positioning?
alts.zh: 稍微倒回去一下——我們一開始就直接跳進來了。我很好奇你會怎麼定義「定位」這件事？

alts.quote: And if it's helpful, let me break down the question a little bit.
alts.zh: 如果有幫助的話，我把這個問題拆開來講一下。

alts.quote: Just to make sure I understand what you're saying there, you're saying generally maybe third party tools limit what you can do, which set you up for hardship later.
alts.zh: 我確認一下我有聽懂你的意思：你是說一般來說第三方工具會限制你能做的事，之後會讓你很痛苦。

cards.pattern: Just to clarify what you just said, what do you mean when you say [對方的詞]?
cards.quote: Just to clarify what you just said, what do you mean when you say citation strategy is different?
cards.zh: 我釐清一下你剛剛講的：你說引用策略不一樣，是什麼意思？
cards.why: 先宣告動作（Just to clarify），再用 when you say 引述原字，最後才問 what do you mean。三段順序固定，是問定義最不刺人的排法。
cards.episode: The ultimate guide to AEO: How to get ChatGPT to recommend your product | Ethan Smith (Graphite)

alts.quote: And when you say unconventional, what do you mean?
alts.zh: 你說「非典型」的時候，指的是什麼？

alts.quote: So put another way, it defines what are the alternatives to what you do? How are you different?
alts.zh: 換個講法：它定義的是——你的替代方案有哪些？你跟它們差在哪？

alts.quote: Two things I'd love to clarify.
alts.zh: 有兩件事我想澄清一下。

cards.pattern: There's so many threads I want to follow here, but maybe on just this last one, when you say [對方的詞], what do you mean by that?
cards.quote: There's so many threads I want to follow here, but maybe on just this last one, when you say taste, what do you mean by that?
cards.zh: 這裡有好多條線我都想追，不過就挑最後那一條吧——你說的 taste，指的是什麼？
cards.why: 先講「你講的東西太多我都想追」是包裝過的讚美，再宣告只挑一條，最後才問定義。問短問題前的鋪陳，決定對方願意答多長。
cards.episode: Thinking like a gardener not a builder, organizing teams like slime mold, the adjacent possible, and other unconventional product advice | Alex Komoroske (Stripe, Google)

alts.quote: The reason I'm a little confused, just because I want to get it right, is what I'm hearing, which maybe isn't what you said
alts.zh: 我有點不確定，純粹是想弄清楚——我聽到的（可能不是你講的意思）是……

alts.quote: I read the email, I'm like, "What do you want me to do? Is this an FYI? Are you saying there's a problem? Do you want me to help?"
alts.zh: 我讀完信心想：「你到底要我做什麼？這是知會嗎？你是在說有問題嗎？還是你要我幫忙？」

alts.quote: And when you say unconventional, what do you mean?
alts.zh: 你說「非典型」的時候，指的是什麼？

cards.pattern: And when you say [對方的詞], what do you mean?
cards.quote: And when you say unconventional, what do you mean?
cards.zh: 你說「非典型」的時候，指的是什麼？
cards.why: when you say [對方的詞] 是關鍵——問的是他用的那個字，不是他整個論點，範圍小到不可能被當成挑戰。
cards.episode: Lessons from Airtable’s unconventional growth strategy | Zoelle Egner

alts.quote: Just to clarify what you just said, what do you mean when you say citation strategy is different?
alts.zh: 我釐清一下你剛剛講的：你說引用策略不一樣，是什麼意思？

alts.quote: I got the feedback that I needed to be more strategic. I was like, "Okay, great. What does being more strategic mean?" And nobody could tell me.
alts.zh: 我收到的回饋是「要更有策略性」。我心想：好啊，那「更有策略性」到底是什麼意思？結果沒有人講得出來。

alts.quote: Okay, what do you mean by this? Are you talking about inner and outer loop? Are you talking about friction?
alts.zh: 好，你指的是什麼意思？你講的是內外迴圈嗎？還是講摩擦成本？

cards.quote: Can you say more about that?
cards.zh: 這部分可以多說一點嗎？
cards.why: 不預設方向、不給判斷，只是要更多——最安全的追問。它和 what do you mean 的差別是：一個要更多，一個要更準。
cards.episode: How 80,000 companies build with AI: products as organisms, the death of org charts, and why agents will outnumber employees by 2026 | Asha Sharma (CVP of AI Platform at Microsoft)

alts.quote: So put another way, it defines what are the alternatives to what you do? How are you different?
alts.zh: 換個講法：它定義的是——你的替代方案有哪些？你跟它們差在哪？

alts.quote: Backing up a little bit, we jumped right in. I'm curious how you even describe positioning, what the heck is positioning?
alts.zh: 稍微倒回去一下——我們一開始就直接跳進來了。我很好奇你會怎麼定義「定位」這件事？

alts.quote: And if it's helpful, let me break down the question a little bit.
alts.zh: 如果有幫助的話，我把這個問題拆開來講一下。

cards.quote: Oh, say more about that.
cards.zh: 喔，那個再多說一點。
cards.why: 去掉 Can you 之後只剩祈使句，配上開頭的 Oh，聽起來是被勾起興趣而不是下命令。熟人之間最常見的版本。
cards.episode: Brian Balfour: 10 lessons on career, growth, and life

alts.quote: So put another way, it defines what are the alternatives to what you do? How are you different?
alts.zh: 換個講法：它定義的是——你的替代方案有哪些？你跟它們差在哪？

alts.quote: Backing up a little bit, we jumped right in. I'm curious how you even describe positioning, what the heck is positioning?
alts.zh: 稍微倒回去一下——我們一開始就直接跳進來了。我很好奇你會怎麼定義「定位」這件事？

alts.quote: What I'm hearing is the core issues, we're not able to feel our emotion.
alts.zh: 我聽到的重點是：核心問題在於我們沒辦法真的感受到自己的情緒。

cards.quote: What does success look like to you?
cards.zh: 對你來說，成功長什麼樣子？
cards.why: 不問目標（goal）而問「長什麼樣子」，逼對方描述可辨識的畫面而不是抽象名詞；加上 to you 又把它從公司標準轉成個人標準。
cards.pmNote: 專案啟動時先問成功長什麼樣，比先問要做什麼功能更能避免後期爭執。
cards.episode: Scripts for difficult conversations: Giving hard feedback, navigating defensiveness, the three questions you should end every meeting with, more | Alisa Cohn (executive coach)

alts.quote: I always ask, "What worked? What didn't work?"
alts.zh: 我每次都會問：哪裡有用？哪裡沒用？

alts.quote: So which game do you want to play? Let's just start there.
alts.zh: 所以你想玩哪一種賽局？我們就從這裡開始。

alts.quote: What else can people do to become better storytellers in business? I know this is a big question, but let's see where it goes.
alts.zh: 在商業場合還可以怎麼把故事講得更好？我知道這題很大，但我們就看看會聊到哪。

cards.pattern: What does success look like for [眼前這件事]?
cards.quote: What does success look like for the thing you're trying to do here?
cards.zh: 你想在這裡做成的那件事，成功長什麼樣子？
cards.why: for the thing you're trying to do here 把範圍縮到眼前這件事，對方不用回答人生哲學，回答率高很多。
cards.episode: A guide to difficult conversations, building high-trust teams, and designing a life you love | Rachel Lockett

alts.quote: And then there'll be some other thing that happens that causes you to reinstall it, and that's totally fine, because you're being deliberate about it and you're paying attention.
alts.zh: 然後某天會發生某件事讓你又把它裝回來——那完全沒問題，因為你是刻意這樣做的，你有在注意。

alts.quote: When I joined Microsoft many years ago, the first thing I noticed was that Outlook was very buggy and I asked people what's going on?
alts.zh: 我很多年前剛進微軟的時候，第一件注意到的事就是 Outlook 超多 bug，我就去問大家：這是怎麼回事？

alts.quote: So first of all, if you're asking whether you should pivot or not you probably know the answer already.
alts.zh: 首先，如果你在問「該不該轉向」，你八成心裡已經有答案了。

cards.quote: And it's the short, medium, lon-term in product, but it's what are you optimizing for today, this quarter, this year?
cards.zh: 產品上分短中長期，但問題就是：你今天、這一季、今年，到底在最佳化什麼？
cards.why: 同一個問題套三個時間尺度，逼對方承認短期和長期在最佳化不同的東西——衝突通常就藏在那個落差裡。
cards.pmNote: 「你在最佳化什麼」比「你的目標是什麼」更能問出真正的取捨。
cards.episode: Driving alignment and urgency within teams, work-life balance, and the changing PM landscape | Nikita Miller (The Knot, Trello)

alts.quote: always be working back from, in one year from now, what will I wish I had been learning today? Two years, five years?
alts.zh: 永遠從未來往回推：一年後的我，會希望今天的我在學什麼？兩年後呢？五年後呢？

alts.quote: One of the things I ask a lot in product review when someone says, "Hey, we want to run an experiment," is, "Okay, what do we do if it's green? What do we do if it's red?"
alts.zh: 有人說「我們想跑個實驗」，我在產品評審上最常問的就是：「如果結果是綠的我們做什麼？紅的又做什麼？」

alts.quote: So if your partner comes to you and says that marketing plan or that product roadmap that you put together, not good, do you take it as the plan is not good and let's talk about what we can actually do to fix it?
alts.zh: 如果你的夥伴跟你說，你做的行銷計畫或產品路線圖不好，你會理解成「這份計畫不好，我們來談怎麼修」嗎？

cards.quote: You usually need a goal in mind, like what are you optimizing for?
cards.zh: 你通常心裡得先有個目標，也就是——你到底在最佳化什麼？
cards.why: 先講前提（need a goal in mind）再把問題丟出來，like 讓它聽起來像順口舉例，不像質詢。
cards.episode: What differentiates the highest-performing product teams | John Cutler (Amplitude, The Beautiful Mess)

alts.quote: If there's nothing here, totally cool. But is there something that you changed Mark's mind about?
alts.zh: 如果沒有的話完全沒關係。不過，有沒有哪件事是你改變了 Mark 的想法的？

alts.quote: And it's the short, medium, lon-term in product, but it's what are you optimizing for today, this quarter, this year?
alts.zh: 產品上分短中長期，但問題就是：你今天、這一季、今年，到底在最佳化什麼？

alts.quote: I always ask, "What worked? What didn't work?"
alts.zh: 我每次都會問：哪裡有用？哪裡沒用？

cards.pattern: What are you optimizing for when you [具體情境]?
cards.quote: What are you optimizing for when you think a thought that would help someone improve and you avoid giving it to them because it would make you uncomfortable?
cards.zh: 當你腦中冒出一個對別人有幫助的想法，卻因為講出來會讓自己不舒服而不講——那一刻你在最佳化什麼？
cards.why: 把 what are you optimizing for 接在一段具體情境後面，對方沒辦法用抽象答案閃過，只能承認自己在最佳化「自己的舒適」。
cards.pmNote: 教練式提問的殺傷力來自前面那段情境描述，不是問句本身。
cards.episode: 10 contrarian leadership truths every leader needs to hear | Matt MacInnis (Rippling)

alts.quote: "Hey, help me understand how you came to that conclusion because here's my reaction to that." So, you're honest, but you're also curious.
alts.zh: 「嘿，幫我理解你是怎麼得出這個結論的，因為我的反應是這樣。」——你既誠實，也保持好奇。

alts.quote: I'll say, "I want to run a theory by you. Do you think that the reason why you are really interested in this or you made that decision is actually because of this other thing that you told me a little bit about?"
alts.zh: 我會說：「我想跟你對一個猜測。你會這麼在意這件事、或做了那個決定，會不會其實是因為你剛剛提到的另一件事？」

alts.quote: Let me tell you what a director does. And you're going to work with me over the next couple of months to do those things because I am promoting you to do the job, not to learn the job.
alts.zh: 我先跟你講總監到底在做什麼。接下來這幾個月你要跟我一起把那些事做一遍——因為我升你是要你來做這個職位，不是來學這個職位。

cards.pattern: How do you know that you have [某個問題] and that you should focus on [某個解法]?
cards.quote: How do you know that you have a positioning problem and that you should focus on positioning?
cards.zh: 你怎麼知道自己有定位問題、而且該把力氣放在定位上？
cards.why: 一句問兩層：怎麼判斷問題存在、怎麼判斷這是現在最該修的。第二層才是真正逼人交出判準的地方。
cards.episode: April Dunford on product positioning, segmentation, and optimizing your sales process

alts.quote: So first of all, if you're asking whether you should pivot or not you probably know the answer already.
alts.zh: 首先，如果你在問「該不該轉向」，你八成心裡已經有答案了。

alts.quote: I try to focus them less around whatever happened and more on what is the action that you can take next to counter program the narrative that you are afraid that this other person has of you.
alts.zh: 我會把他的注意力從「已經發生的事」拉開，改放到：你接下來可以做什麼動作，去反寫你擔心對方對你形成的那個印象。

alts.quote: And then I would say, what are you world-class at and how do you know that you're at that? And the second part is almost more important.
alts.zh: 然後我會問：你在什麼事情上是世界級的？你怎麼知道自己是？第二個問題其實更重要。

cards.pattern: How do you know if it's a [框架的 A] or a [框架的 B]?
cards.quote: How do you know if it's a one way or a two way door decision?
cards.zh: 你怎麼知道這是一扇單向門還是雙向門的決策？
cards.why: how do you know 配上一個既有框架（單向／雙向門），對方不用從零解釋，只要說出判準就好。
cards.pmNote: 單向門＝難以回頭的決策要慢；雙向門＝可回復的決策要快。
cards.episode: Nickey Skarstad (Airbnb, Etsy, Shopify, Duolingo) on translating vision into goals, operationalizing product quality, second-order decisions, brainstorming, influence, and much more

alts.quote: It's like why was this decision made? Why do you think the decision was made? And I might ask, "Do you think it was the right decision or did you agree on it?"
alts.zh: 像是：這個決定為什麼會做？你覺得為什麼會這樣決定？然後我可能會問：你覺得那是對的決定嗎？你當時同意嗎？

alts.quote: How do you know when it's time to hire someone?
alts.zh: 你怎麼知道什麼時候該招人了？

alts.quote: So first of all, if you're asking whether you should pivot or not you probably know the answer already.
alts.zh: 首先，如果你在問「該不該轉向」，你八成心裡已經有答案了。

cards.pattern: Something that I always think about with people in your shoes is just how do you [做到 X] and how do you know [判準]?
cards.quote: Something that I always think about with people in your shoes is just how do you not get overwhelmed and how do you know what to pay attention to?
cards.zh: 我常常在想，處在你這個位置的人——你怎麼做到不被淹沒？又怎麼知道該注意什麼？
cards.why: with people in your shoes 把問題從「你」擴大成「所有在這位置的人」，對方回答時不必先承認自己有困難，防禦性大幅降低。
cards.episode: How to win in the AI era: Ship a feature every week, embrace technical debt, ruthlessly cut scope, and create magic your competitors can't copy | Gaurav Misra (CEO and co-founder of Captions)

alts.quote: I often think about this phrase, which is people don't care what you know until they know that you care.
alts.zh: 我常想到這句話：在別人知道你在乎之前，他們不會在乎你懂什麼。

alts.quote: What we ask people in general is we say, what do you think? We don't say, what do you know? We often say, what do you think?
alts.zh: 我們一般會問人「你怎麼想？」我們不會問「你知道什麼？」我們最常問的就是「你怎麼想？」

alts.quote: People call me sometimes they're like "I want to know if I have product market fit." Well, the fact that you have time to call me and ask me this question already tells me the answer.
alts.zh: 有人打給我說：「我想知道我們有沒有 PMF。」嗯，你有空打這通電話問我，這件事本身就給了答案。

cards.pattern: How do you know you'll actually make money on [這個東西]?
cards.quote: And I remember going and pitching our ideas and the VC asked me, how do you know you'll actually make money on this innovation?
cards.zh: 我還記得我們去提案，那個投資人問我：你怎麼知道這個創新真的能賺到錢？
cards.why: 投資人版的 how do you know——不否定點子，只要求證據來源。這句話幾乎可以貼在任何一份提案的最後一頁。
cards.pmNote: 提案前先自問一次「我怎麼知道這會賺錢」，答不出來就是資料還沒做。
cards.episode: Pricing your AI product: Lessons from 400+ companies and 50 unicorns | Madhavan Ramanujam

alts.quote: Okay, so I noticed that I needed to change that at some point, and actually found a solution, again, late in my career, but I found a solution, because I asked myself this question, which is, "Why am I so busy?
alts.zh: 我注意到我某個時間點需要改掉這個，後來真的找到解法——雖然是職涯很後期才找到——因為我問了自己一個問題：「我為什麼這麼忙？」

alts.quote: When I joined Microsoft many years ago, the first thing I noticed was that Outlook was very buggy and I asked people what's going on?
alts.zh: 我很多年前剛進微軟的時候，第一件注意到的事就是 Outlook 超多 bug，我就去問大家：這是怎麼回事？

alts.quote: So if your partner comes to you and says that marketing plan or that product roadmap that you put together, not good, do you take it as the plan is not good and let's talk about what we can actually do to fix it?
alts.zh: 如果你的夥伴跟你說，你做的行銷計畫或產品路線圖不好，你會理解成「這份計畫不好，我們來談怎麼修」嗎？

cards.pattern: [一個殘酷的前提], so how do you know [判準]?
cards.quote: Most work is wasted in AEO, so how do you know what's not wasted?
cards.zh: AEO 上大多數的工都是白做的——那你怎麼知道哪些沒白做？
cards.why: 先給一個殘酷前提再問，問題就不是挑戰對方而是共同面對現實；so 把前提和問句黏成因果。
cards.episode: The ultimate guide to AEO: How to get ChatGPT to recommend your product | Ethan Smith (Graphite)

alts.quote: But if I said you had to write a spec for your career, what's in there? What are your milestones? What are the skills?
alts.zh: 如果我要你替自己的職涯寫一份 spec，裡面會有什麼？你的里程碑是什麼？需要哪些技能？

alts.quote: So first of all, if you're asking whether you should pivot or not you probably know the answer already.
alts.zh: 首先，如果你在問「該不該轉向」，你八成心裡已經有答案了。

alts.quote: And then I would say, what are you world-class at and how do you know that you're at that? And the second part is almost more important.
alts.zh: 然後我會問：你在什麼事情上是世界級的？你怎麼知道自己是？第二個問題其實更重要。

cards.pattern: How do you know when it's time to [做某個決定]?
cards.quote: How do you know when it's time to hire someone?
cards.zh: 你怎麼知道什麼時候該招人了？
cards.why: how do you know when it's time to X 是最通用的時機類骨架：把「該不該」換成「怎麼判斷」，對方就得交出訊號而不是意見。
cards.episode: Building a magical AI code editor used by over 1 million developers in four months: The untold story of Windsurf | Varun Mohan (co-founder and CEO)

alts.quote: One of the things I ask a lot in product review when someone says, "Hey, we want to run an experiment," is, "Okay, what do we do if it's green? What do we do if it's red?"
alts.zh: 有人說「我們想跑個實驗」，我在產品評審上最常問的就是：「如果結果是綠的我們做什麼？紅的又做什麼？」

alts.quote: People call me sometimes they're like "I want to know if I have product market fit." Well, the fact that you have time to call me and ask me this question already tells me the answer.
alts.zh: 有人打給我說：「我想知道我們有沒有 PMF。」嗯，你有空打這通電話問我，這件事本身就給了答案。

alts.quote: How do you know if it's a one way or a two way door decision?
alts.zh: 你怎麼知道這是一扇單向門還是雙向門的決策？

cards.quote: Walk me through what's living in your head right now.
cards.zh: 帶我走一遍你現在腦子裡裝的東西。
cards.why: 不問「你怎麼想」而問「腦子裡現在住著什麼」，把對方的混亂正當化，他就不用先整理好才敢開口。
cards.episode: "Sell the alpha, not the feature": The enterprise sales playbook for $1M to $10M ARR | Jen Abel

alts.quote: Walk me through how you go about tackling this or solving this." For me, I like that question because it gives me a sense of how you think.
alts.zh: 「帶我走一遍你會怎麼下手處理這件事。」我喜歡這個問題，因為它讓我看得到你怎麼想。

alts.quote: But if I said you had to write a spec for your career, what's in there? What are your milestones? What are the skills?
alts.zh: 如果我要你替自己的職涯寫一份 spec，裡面會有什麼？你的里程碑是什麼？需要哪些技能？

alts.quote: always be working back from, in one year from now, what will I wish I had been learning today? Two years, five years?
alts.zh: 永遠從未來往回推：一年後的我，會希望今天的我在學什麼？兩年後呢？五年後呢？

cards.quote: Walk me through how you go about tackling this or solving this." For me, I like that question because it gives me a sense of how you think.
cards.zh: 「帶我走一遍你會怎麼下手處理這件事。」我喜歡這個問題，因為它讓我看得到你怎麼想。
cards.why: walk me through 要的是過程不是答案；後半句自己點破為什麼——過程才看得出思考方式，答案只看得出記憶力。
cards.pmNote: 面試或評估時問流程不問結論，比較難被準備好的答案矇過去。
cards.episode: The essence of product management | Christian Idiodi (SVPG)

alts.quote: I'll say, "I want to run a theory by you. Do you think that the reason why you are really interested in this or you made that decision is actually because of this other thing that you told me a little bit about?"
alts.zh: 我會說：「我想跟你對一個猜測。你會這麼在意這件事、或做了那個決定，會不會其實是因為你剛剛提到的另一件事？」

alts.quote: Walk me through what's living in your head right now.
alts.zh: 帶我走一遍你現在腦子裡裝的東西。

alts.quote: Okay, so I noticed that I needed to change that at some point, and actually found a solution, again, late in my career, but I found a solution, because I asked myself this question, which is, "Why am I so busy?
alts.zh: 我注意到我某個時間點需要改掉這個，後來真的找到解法——雖然是職涯很後期才找到——因為我問了自己一個問題：「我為什麼這麼忙？」

cards.quote: "Hey, help me understand how you came to that conclusion because here's my reaction to that." So, you're honest, but you're also curious.
cards.zh: 「嘿，幫我理解你是怎麼得出這個結論的，因為我的反應是這樣。」——你既誠實，也保持好奇。
cards.why: help me understand 把「我不同意」翻譯成「我還沒跟上」；後面加 because here's my reaction 又不隱藏立場，所以不是假裝中立。
cards.pmNote: 反對別人前先讓對方講一遍推導過程，多數爭執會在那段裡自己散掉。
cards.episode: A guide to difficult conversations, building high-trust teams, and designing a life you love | Rachel Lockett

alts.quote: Let me tell you what a director does. And you're going to work with me over the next couple of months to do those things because I am promoting you to do the job, not to learn the job.
alts.zh: 我先跟你講總監到底在做什麼。接下來這幾個月你要跟我一起把那些事做一遍——因為我升你是要你來做這個職位，不是來學這個職位。

alts.quote: What are you optimizing for when you think a thought that would help someone improve and you avoid giving it to them because it would make you uncomfortable?
alts.zh: 當你腦中冒出一個對別人有幫助的想法，卻因為講出來會讓自己不舒服而不講——那一刻你在最佳化什麼？

alts.quote: To ensure we’re aligned, could you help me understand the specific percentage or number of shares that represents?
alts.zh: 為了確保我們有對齊，可以幫我理解那代表的具體百分比或股數嗎？

cards.quote: I'm not going to let that slide, but I'm going to say, "Help me understand why that is a good idea," and I'm going to press on that.
cards.zh: 我不會放它過去，但我會說：「幫我理解為什麼那是個好主意」，然後我會一直壓那個點。
cards.why: 示範 help me understand 是施壓工具而不是禮貌詞——句子外面包著客氣，裡面是 press on that。
cards.episode: A guide to difficult conversations, building high-trust teams, and designing a life you love | Rachel Lockett

alts.quote: Let me tell you what a director does. And you're going to work with me over the next couple of months to do those things because I am promoting you to do the job, not to learn the job.
alts.zh: 我先跟你講總監到底在做什麼。接下來這幾個月你要跟我一起把那些事做一遍——因為我升你是要你來做這個職位，不是來學這個職位。

alts.quote: I'm asking them, "What do you do for joy? Are you doing something every single day that's bringing you joy in your life?" And if they say no, I'm like, "That's a problem."
alts.zh: 我會問他們：「你都做什麼讓自己開心？你每天有沒有一件事是讓你有樂趣的？」如果回答沒有，我就會說：「那這是個問題。」

alts.quote: put a calendar invite, let it renew every three months. You're going to snooze it a couple of times, I get it, I've seen this many, many times before. But just do something, even if it's super small.
alts.zh: 開一個行事曆邀請，每三個月自動重複。你一定會按掉個幾次，我懂，我看過太多次了。但就是做點什麼，再小都好。

cards.quote: You could tell, he's like, "Help me understand this part of your thinking."
cards.zh: 你看得出來，他就會說：「幫我理解你這一段的思路。」
cards.why: 把範圍限縮到 this part of your thinking，不是整個人整件事——質疑一個段落，比質疑一個結論安全得多。
cards.episode: A guide to difficult conversations, building high-trust teams, and designing a life you love | Rachel Lockett

alts.quote: To ensure we’re aligned, could you help me understand the specific percentage or number of shares that represents?
alts.zh: 為了確保我們有對齊，可以幫我理解那代表的具體百分比或股數嗎？

alts.quote: I'm like, "I'm not surprised to hear that. Tell me how you did it."
alts.zh: 我就說：「我一點都不意外。你跟我說說你們是怎麼做的。」

alts.quote: "Hey, help me understand how you came to that conclusion because here's my reaction to that." So, you're honest, but you're also curious.
alts.zh: 「嘿，幫我理解你是怎麼得出這個結論的，因為我的反應是這樣。」——你既誠實，也保持好奇。

cards.pattern: To ensure we're aligned, could you help me understand [你要的具體數字]?
cards.quote: To ensure we’re aligned, could you help me understand the specific percentage or number of shares that represents?
cards.zh: 為了確保我們有對齊，可以幫我理解那代表的具體百分比或股數嗎？
cards.why: 談判要數字時最軟的問法：先給理由（確保雙方對齊），再用 help me understand 把「你講得太模糊」轉成「我需要幫忙」。
cards.pmNote: 談 offer 的股票時百分比和股數都要問到，只給其中一個等於沒給。
cards.episode: The ultimate guide to negotiating your comp

alts.quote: "Hey, help me understand how you came to that conclusion because here's my reaction to that." So, you're honest, but you're also curious.
alts.zh: 「嘿，幫我理解你是怎麼得出這個結論的，因為我的反應是這樣。」——你既誠實，也保持好奇。

alts.quote: You could tell, he's like, "Help me understand this part of your thinking."
alts.zh: 你看得出來，他就會說：「幫我理解你這一段的思路。」

alts.quote: What are you optimizing for when you think a thought that would help someone improve and you avoid giving it to them because it would make you uncomfortable?
alts.zh: 當你腦中冒出一個對別人有幫助的想法，卻因為講出來會讓自己不舒服而不講——那一刻你在最佳化什麼？

cards.pattern: I noticed that in the last [three] [sprint planning meetings], you [具體行為].
cards.quote: For example, I noticed that in the last three sprint planning meetings, you didn't invite me to those conversations or share with me the roadmap.
cards.zh: 舉個例子，我注意到最近三次的 sprint 規劃會議，你都沒有找我進去談，也沒有把 roadmap 分享給我。
cards.why: 不說「你老是把我排除在外」，改成可數的次數加上可查證的行為。對方要反駁得先反駁事實，而事實通常反駁不了，情緒就不會先被點燃。
cards.pmNote: 要給難聽的回饋前先湊滿三個具體事例；少於三次就先觀察不要開口。
cards.episode: A guide to difficult conversations, building high-trust teams, and designing a life you love | Rachel Lockett

alts.quote: I noticed immediately that Meena was spending her whole day helping her teammates and putting her own priorities last.
alts.zh: 我一眼就注意到，Meena 整天都在幫隊友，把自己的優先事項擺到最後。

alts.quote: To suggest an idea, use language with your manager like, “I noticed that we are often late on projects because we forget to account for vacation schedules and then someone critical is out.
alts.zh: 我注意到我們專案常常延遲，因為我們排程時忘了把休假算進去，然後關鍵的人剛好就不在。

alts.quote: I noticed there's some PMs who will send an email and I read the email, I'm like, "What do you want me to do?
alts.zh: 我注意到有些 PM 寄信過來，我讀完心裡想的是：「所以你到底要我做什麼？」

cards.pattern: I noticed that we are often [問題], because we [系統性原因].
cards.quote: To suggest an idea, use language with your manager like, “I noticed that we are often late on projects because we forget to account for vacation schedules and then someone critical is out.
cards.zh: 我注意到我們專案常常延遲，因為我們排程時忘了把休假算進去，然後關鍵的人剛好就不在。
cards.why: 主詞用 we、原因指向流程而不是某個人，所以這句聽起來是在描述一個共同的系統缺陷。後面接提案時，就不會被讀成指責。
cards.pmNote: 向上提案的標準三段：先描述模式，再給解法，最後問要不要我來做。
cards.episode: The Magic Loop

alts.quote: But shortly after we started Character, I noticed that, while Design Sprints are awesome for solving problems, building prototypes, and testing ideas, founders at the very beginning of big projects need more.
alts.zh: 但我們開了 Character 沒多久，我就注意到：Design Sprint 很適合解問題、做原型、測想法，但大專案最初期的創辦人需要的不只這些。

alts.quote: I care so much about you and I'm giving you this feedback because I want you to be successful and I want you to be able to reach the pinnacle of what I know you can accomplish.
alts.zh: 我非常在乎你，我給你這個回饋是因為我希望你成功、希望你能走到我知道你能到的高度。

alts.quote: And then you flip to your development areas because no one calls them weaknesses.
alts.zh: 然後你翻到「待發展面向」那一頁——因為沒人會直接叫它「缺點」。

cards.pattern: Yes, you [做錯的那件事], but that's not on you.
cards.quote: And the mistake I made was not reaching out to him and really reassuring him of, "Yes, you wrote the bug, but that's not on you.
cards.zh: 我犯的錯是沒有去找他、好好安撫他說：「對，bug 是你寫的，但這不該算在你頭上。」
cards.why: 先承認事實不打模糊仗，再用 that's not on you 把責任從人移到系統。台灣主管為了安慰常說「沒事啦不是你的問題」，那是否認事實，對方反而更不安。
cards.pmNote: 事故檢討的分界線：行為可以檢討，責任歸屬要指向系統，否則之後沒人敢碰高風險的東西。
cards.episode: Taking control of your career | Ethan Evans (Amazon)

alts.quote: And I think the error that people make more often than not is they are actually too stuck on their own product vision. That's the mistake I've seen a little bit more actually than the other way around.
alts.zh: 我覺得大家最常犯的錯，是太黏著自己原本的產品願景。這個錯我看到的，其實比反過來的那種多一點。

alts.quote: The only thing that's different is the insight that the founder has on the market, which is a hard pill to swallow. And I know that's hard to hear too.
alts.zh: 唯一的差別是創辦人對市場的洞察——這顆藥很難吞。我也知道這話很難聽。

alts.quote: I respect that, and I relate to it in some ways with my own trying to get attention for my own work. But, "I deserve this" that's not a good tactical decision for your business.
alts.zh: 我尊重這種心情，我自己在推廣作品時也有過。但「我值得」不是一個好的商業決策理由。

cards.pattern: I noticed we have [this problem / this opportunity].
cards.quote: I noticed we have this opportunity.
cards.zh: 我注意到我們有這個機會。
cards.why: 把要講的事包成一個中性觀察，句子短到可以直接丟進 Slack。同一個骨架套 problem 是提醒、套 opportunity 是提案，措詞成本一樣。
cards.pmNote: 主動回報問題時附上你打算怎麼處理，才會被讀成負責而不是抱怨。
cards.episode: Taking control of your career | Ethan Evans (Amazon)

alts.quote: I asked her once, I said, "I noticed that you never answer questions when we do these presentations."
alts.zh: 我有一次問她：「我注意到，我們在做這些簡報的時候，你從來不回答問題。」

alts.quote: And one thing that I noticed, a lot of people just don't know what you built.
alts.zh: 我注意到一件事：很多人根本不知道你做了什麼。

alts.quote: I noticed immediately that Meena was spending her whole day helping her teammates and putting her own priorities last.
alts.zh: 我一眼就注意到，Meena 整天都在幫隊友，把自己的優先事項擺到最後。

cards.pattern: One thing that I noticed — a lot of people just don't [X].
cards.quote: And one thing that I noticed, a lot of people just don't know what you built.
cards.zh: 我注意到一件事：很多人根本不知道你做了什麼。
cards.why: One thing that I noticed 是把刺耳的話降溫的最短前綴，它把批評縮小成「一個觀察」而不是「一個總評」。拿掉這幾個字，整句就變成人身攻擊。
cards.pmNote: 「沒人知道你做了什麼」在組織裡幾乎永遠是真的；預設要花在推廣上的力氣跟做出來一樣多。
cards.episode: Al Engineering 101 with Chip Huyen (Nvidia, Stanford, Netflix)

alts.quote: Hey, Lenny. You probably didn't know, but I don't really like when people comment on my shirt.
alts.zh: 嘿 Lenny，你可能不知道，我其實不太喜歡別人評論我的衣服。

alts.quote: The only thing that's different is the insight that the founder has on the market, which is a hard pill to swallow. And I know that's hard to hear too.
alts.zh: 唯一的差別是創辦人對市場的洞察——這顆藥很難吞。我也知道這話很難聽。

alts.quote: Clearly, you're not so scared that you can't do anything, so I'm not buying it. I don't do it quite like that, I do it with a lot more love than that.
alts.zh: 很明顯你沒有害怕到什麼都做不了，所以這個說法我不買單。我實際上不會講得這麼硬，我會帶更多善意。

cards.pattern: I noticed there's some [角色] who will [行為], and I'm like, "[讀完心裡的疑問]"
cards.quote: I noticed there's some PMs who will send an email and I read the email, I'm like, "What do you want me to do?
cards.zh: 我注意到有些 PM 寄信過來，我讀完心裡想的是：「所以你到底要我做什麼？」
cards.why: some PMs 把對象泛化，被講的人會自己對號入座但沒有被公開點名。再用「我心裡的 OS」呈現後果，比直接說「你信寫得很爛」有效。
cards.pmNote: 每封對外的信都要有一句明確的 ask，否則收件人的預設動作是不動作。
cards.episode: Crafting a compelling product vision | Ebi Atawodi (YouTube, Netflix, Uber)

alts.quote: I care so much about you and I'm giving you this feedback because I want you to be successful and I want you to be able to reach the pinnacle of what I know you can accomplish.
alts.zh: 我非常在乎你，我給你這個回饋是因為我希望你成功、希望你能走到我知道你能到的高度。

alts.quote: I do want to be clear, it's one leader and their team who are accountable and responsible.
alts.zh: 我想把話講清楚：負責的就是一位負責人跟他的團隊。

alts.quote: So you have engineers now who are working on optimizing short form videos for higher engagement, and you sort of want to say to them like, "Hey, are you thinking about what this is doing to the brains of young children?"
alts.zh: 現在有一群工程師在優化短影音的互動率，你會有點想跟他們說：「欸，你有想過這對小朋友的腦袋在做什麼嗎？」

cards.pattern: I noticed that [人] was [行為 A] and [行為 B].
cards.quote: I noticed immediately that Meena was spending her whole day helping her teammates and putting her own priorities last.
cards.zh: 我一眼就注意到，Meena 整天都在幫隊友，把自己的優先事項擺到最後。
cards.why: 兩個並列的行為描述就足以構成一個模式，不必加形容詞（too nice、沒有界線）。形容詞是評價、會被防衛；行為是資料、可以一起看。
cards.pmNote: 過度幫忙的人在績效檢討常吃虧；主管的責任是把它講成可調整的行為，而不是個性。
cards.episode: On asking for help (even when you really don’t want to)

alts.quote: For example, I noticed that in the last three sprint planning meetings, you didn't invite me to those conversations or share with me the roadmap.
alts.zh: 舉個例子，我注意到最近三次的 sprint 規劃會議，你都沒有找我進去談，也沒有把 roadmap 分享給我。

alts.quote: At one point I noticed I was spending six to 7% of my week on these areas, these areas where I can truly be world-class at.
alts.zh: 有一陣子我注意到，我一週只花百分之六到七的時間在這些領域上——那些我真的能做到世界頂尖的領域。

alts.quote: I asked her once, I said, "I noticed that you never answer questions when we do these presentations."
alts.zh: 我有一次問她：「我注意到，我們在做這些簡報的時候，你從來不回答問題。」

cards.pattern: I noticed [身體訊號] as you [表面上在做的事].
cards.quote: In our session, I noticed his tight smile (a common deflection when we’re uncomfortable with anger) as he calmly outlined all the operational reasons why Corey shouldn’t join.
cards.zh: 在諮詢時我注意到他那個緊繃的微笑（我們對憤怒感到不自在時常見的迴避），而他還冷靜地列出所有 Corey 不該加入的營運理由。
cards.why: 把「你其實在生氣」講成「我看到一個緊繃的微笑」。身體訊號是雙方都觀察得到的，動機不是——講動機一定會吵起來。
cards.pmNote: 會議上出現「講得很有道理但情緒不對」時先處理情緒，那串理由通常是事後合理化。
cards.episode: Why you’re so angry at work (and what to do about it)

alts.quote: The only answer I think one can have is, don't stick your head in the sand and say, "I hate all of this stuff," because that gives you a great feeling of moral superiority.
alts.zh: 我覺得唯一的答案是：別把頭埋進沙子裡說「我討厭這些東西」，因為那只會讓你很有道德優越感。

alts.quote: And it's not because people are bad people. I think most people are really well-intentioned. But what happens when you have people that join and you didn't really need them?
alts.zh: 這不是因為誰是壞人，我覺得大多數人動機都很好。但問題是：當你招了一批其實不需要的人，會發生什麼事？

alts.quote: And again, I'm not saying always, but sometimes it can happen that the thing that ends up shipping is the least common denominator that annoyed everybody the least amount, right?
alts.zh: 我不是說每次都這樣，但有時候最後出貨的東西，就是那個讓所有人都最不生氣的最小公約數。

cards.pattern: I noticed the term '[對方的原話]' in our discussions.
cards.quote: I noticed the term ‘significant equity’ in our discussions.
cards.zh: 我注意到我們談的過程中出現了「可觀的股權」這個說法。
cards.why: 引用對方用過的原字，再逼他自己定義。不說「你講得很模糊」，只把那個詞挑出來放到桌上，對方就得補上數字。
cards.pmNote: 談薪、談範圍都一樣：先鎖定對方用過的模糊詞再要求量化，比自己先出價安全。
cards.episode: The ultimate guide to negotiating your comp

alts.quote: For example, I noticed that in the last three sprint planning meetings, you didn't invite me to those conversations or share with me the roadmap.
alts.zh: 舉個例子，我注意到最近三次的 sprint 規劃會議，你都沒有找我進去談，也沒有把 roadmap 分享給我。

alts.quote: To suggest an idea, use language with your manager like, “I noticed that we are often late on projects because we forget to account for vacation schedules and then someone critical is out.
alts.zh: 我注意到我們專案常常延遲，因為我們排程時忘了把休假算進去，然後關鍵的人剛好就不在。

alts.quote: I noticed there's some PMs who will send an email and I read the email, I'm like, "What do you want me to do?
alts.zh: 我注意到有些 PM 寄信過來，我讀完心裡想的是：「所以你到底要我做什麼？」

cards.pattern: I noticed myself starting to feel [情緒] after the [第三、第四次].
cards.quote: I noticed myself starting to feel angry after the third, fourth, then fifth instance.
cards.zh: 我注意到自己在第三次、第四次、然後第五次之後開始生氣。
cards.why: 把自己的情緒也當成觀察對象，並且附上次數。這樣講出來的不是「我很不爽」，而是「有一個累積到臨界的模式」，後者對方可以一起解。
cards.pmNote: 抱怨要有計數器：第一次是意外，第三次才是議題，說得出次數才有討論的資格。
cards.episode: Why you’re so angry at work (and what to do about it)

alts.quote: For example, I noticed that in the last three sprint planning meetings, you didn't invite me to those conversations or share with me the roadmap.
alts.zh: 舉個例子，我注意到最近三次的 sprint 規劃會議，你都沒有找我進去談，也沒有把 roadmap 分享給我。

alts.quote: To suggest an idea, use language with your manager like, “I noticed that we are often late on projects because we forget to account for vacation schedules and then someone critical is out.
alts.zh: 我注意到我們專案常常延遲，因為我們排程時忘了把休假算進去，然後關鍵的人剛好就不在。

alts.quote: I noticed there's some PMs who will send an email and I read the email, I'm like, "What do you want me to do?
alts.zh: 我注意到有些 PM 寄信過來，我讀完心裡想的是：「所以你到底要我做什麼？」

cards.pattern: Every time we [對使用者的要求], that's a failure on our part.
cards.quote: I just think every time we make a demand on the audience, that's a failure on our part.
cards.zh: 我就是覺得，每次我們對觀眾提出一個要求，那都是我們自己的失敗。
cards.why: 把責任預設在自己這邊的句型。that's a failure on our part 跟 that's not on you 是同一組工具：先把責任歸屬釘死，討論才不會變成互相指認。
cards.pmNote: 使用者「不會用」幾乎都是設計問題；把每個需要教學的地方都記成一個 bug。
cards.episode: 35 years of product design wisdom from Apple, Disney, Pinterest, and beyond | Bob Baxley

alts.quote: And I think the error that people make more often than not is they are actually too stuck on their own product vision. That's the mistake I've seen a little bit more actually than the other way around.
alts.zh: 我覺得大家最常犯的錯，是太黏著自己原本的產品願景。這個錯我看到的，其實比反過來的那種多一點。

alts.quote: This is how we think about things. This is how we handle this type of behavior here. If that's hard for you, let's find you another job.
alts.zh: 我們就是這樣想事情的。這種狀況我們在這裡就是這樣處理的。如果你覺得很難接受，那我們一起幫你找個別的工作。

alts.quote: And so here's where I think we go off the rails in marketing.
alts.zh: 而我覺得行銷就是在這一步脫軌的。

cards.quote: I think it's so easy to personalize anything, and it can also come across as really stressed when you're like, hey, I noticed you were on such and such podcast, and that was when they were previously two roles behind.
cards.zh: 我覺得現在要客製化任何東西都太容易了，但它也可能顯得很刻意——像是「嘿，我注意到你上過某某 podcast」，結果那是他兩個職位以前的事。
cards.why: I noticed 只有在觀察是新的、跟現在相關時才有效；拿過期資訊當開場，反而暴露你是批次寄送。
cards.pmNote: 冷開發信的客製化要押在對方「這個月在煩什麼」，不是他的履歷。
cards.episode: "Sell the alpha, not the feature": The enterprise sales playbook for $1M to $10M ARR | Jen Abel

alts.quote: I think we do a disservice when we say we're not good at speaking up because it's a skill like any other.
alts.zh: 我覺得我們說自己「不擅長發言」是在害自己，因為那跟其他技能沒有兩樣。

alts.quote: This isn't funny, Hilary. This is a serious issue for a lot of people, and it's an emerging problem in some cases. And I think we should take it seriously.
alts.zh: 這不好笑。這對很多人來說是很嚴重的問題，而且在某些地方正在惡化。我覺得我們應該認真看待。

alts.quote: So when the feedback is coming like raw, they know that it's in their best interest because I've shown them enough times that I genuinely care about the person behind the role.
alts.zh: 所以當回饋很生硬地丟過來，他們知道那是為他們好——因為我已經用夠多次證明，我在乎的是角色背後那個人。

cards.pattern: I noticed that, while [既有方法] is awesome for [X], [對象] need more.
cards.quote: But shortly after we started Character, I noticed that, while Design Sprints are awesome for solving problems, building prototypes, and testing ideas, founders at the very beginning of big projects need more.
cards.zh: 但我們開了 Character 沒多久，我就注意到：Design Sprint 很適合解問題、做原型、測想法，但大專案最初期的創辦人需要的不只這些。
cards.why: 要說「這套方法不夠用」，先花一整句真心稱讚它擅長的地方，再用 need more 而不是 doesn't work。批評既有標準時，攻擊面越小越容易被接受。
cards.pmNote: 提新框架先界定舊框架的適用範圍，不要否定它——否定會讓所有既得使用者變成你的反對者。
cards.episode: Introducing the Foundation Sprint: From the creators of the Design Sprint

alts.quote: To suggest an idea, use language with your manager like, “I noticed that we are often late on projects because we forget to account for vacation schedules and then someone critical is out.
alts.zh: 我注意到我們專案常常延遲，因為我們排程時忘了把休假算進去，然後關鍵的人剛好就不在。

alts.quote: And it's not because people are bad people. I think most people are really well-intentioned. But what happens when you have people that join and you didn't really need them?
alts.zh: 這不是因為誰是壞人，我覺得大多數人動機都很好。但問題是：當你招了一批其實不需要的人，會發生什麼事？

alts.quote: I think it's so easy to personalize anything, and it can also come across as really stressed when you're like, hey, I noticed you were on such and such podcast, and that was when they were previously two roles behind.
alts.zh: 我覺得現在要客製化任何東西都太容易了，但它也可能顯得很刻意——像是「嘿，我注意到你上過某某 podcast」，結果那是他兩個職位以前的事。

cards.pattern: At one point I noticed I was spending [6 to 7%] of my week on [真正該做的事].
cards.quote: At one point I noticed I was spending six to 7% of my week on these areas, these areas where I can truly be world-class at.
cards.zh: 有一陣子我注意到，我一週只花百分之六到七的時間在這些領域上——那些我真的能做到世界頂尖的領域。
cards.why: 對自己的批評用百分比說，不用形容詞。數字讓「我時間分配有問題」變成一個可以被修的數字，而不是一種自責的情緒。
cards.pmNote: 要改變時間分配，先量出現況比例；沒有基準線的「我要更專注」一週後就回到原點。
cards.episode: Superhuman's secret to success: Ignoring most customer feedback, manually onboarding every new user, obsessing over every detail, and positioning around a single attribute: speed | Rahul Vohra (CEO)

alts.quote: I asked her once, I said, "I noticed that you never answer questions when we do these presentations."
alts.zh: 我有一次問她：「我注意到，我們在做這些簡報的時候，你從來不回答問題。」

alts.quote: I noticed immediately that Meena was spending her whole day helping her teammates and putting her own priorities last.
alts.zh: 我一眼就注意到，Meena 整天都在幫隊友，把自己的優先事項擺到最後。

alts.quote: And so here's where I think we go off the rails in marketing.
alts.zh: 而我覺得行銷就是在這一步脫軌的。

cards.quote: If you can tell me what you're working on and ask me at the end of a meeting specifically what I noticed then that is much better."
cards.zh: 如果你可以先跟我說你在忙什麼，然後在會議結束時具體問我注意到了什麼，那效果好得多。
cards.why: 這是「怎麼跟人要回饋」的說明書：先給脈絡、指定時間點、把問題縮小到 what I noticed。開放式的「給我一點回饋」只會拿到客套話。
cards.pmNote: 要回饋要指定範圍與時機；範圍越窄，拿到的東西越可用。
cards.episode: Radical Candor: From theory to practice with author Kim Scott

alts.quote: I asked them, think about one of the biggest mistakes you've made, truly, the more painful the better. And tell me what the mistake was.
alts.zh: 我會請對方想一個自己犯過最大的錯——說真的，越痛越好——然後告訴我那個錯是什麼。

alts.quote: Let me tell you what a director does. And you're going to work with me over the next couple of months to do those things because I am promoting you to do the job, not to learn the job.
alts.zh: 我先跟你講總監到底在做什麼。接下來這幾個月你要跟我一起把那些事做一遍——因為我升你是要你來做這個職位，不是來學這個職位。

alts.quote: One of the things to ask oneself is what draws me to this position in the first place?
alts.zh: 有個可以問自己的問題是：當初到底是什麼把我吸引到這個位置的？

cards.pattern: I would've asked before I [看作品／下判斷], when I noticed that [對方的訊號].
cards.quote: So it's not always the right thing to ask questions, but I would've tried to ask it before I had examined the work when I noticed that he looked uncomfortable himself.
cards.zh: 所以問問題不見得永遠是對的，但我會希望在我檢視他的作品之前就先問——就在我注意到他自己也很不安的那個時候。
cards.why: 把提問的時機釘在一個訊號上（對方看起來不安），而不是等自己已經有結論。你一旦看完作品才開口，任何問題聽起來都像在鋪陳批評。
cards.pmNote: 檢視成果前先問「你自己覺得哪裡最沒把握」，會拿到最快的路徑，也省掉一輪防衛。
cards.episode: Radical Candor: From theory to practice with author Kim Scott

alts.quote: I always ask, "What worked? What didn't work?"
alts.zh: 我每次都會問：哪裡有用？哪裡沒用？

alts.quote: It's like why was this decision made? Why do you think the decision was made? And I might ask, "Do you think it was the right decision or did you agree on it?"
alts.zh: 像是：這個決定為什麼會做？你覺得為什麼會這樣決定？然後我可能會問：你覺得那是對的決定嗎？你當時同意嗎？

alts.quote: put a calendar invite, let it renew every three months. You're going to snooze it a couple of times, I get it, I've seen this many, many times before. But just do something, even if it's super small.
alts.zh: 開一個行事曆邀請，每三個月自動重複。你一定會按掉個幾次，我懂，我看過太多次了。但就是做點什麼，再小都好。

cards.pattern: I was looking at [你的公開資料], and I noticed that you [具體模式].
cards.quote: I was looking at your LinkedIn and your career history, and I noticed that you've worked for a different billionaire every decade of your life.
cards.zh: 我看了你的 LinkedIn 跟你的職涯，我注意到你人生每十年都在幫一個不同的億萬富翁工作。
cards.why: 先報出「我做了功課」的來源，再講一個對方自己可能沒歸納過的模式。這比 Tell me about your career 有效十倍，因為它已經替對方想好一個角度。
cards.pmNote: 使用者訪談同理：先講你從資料看到什麼，再請對方修正你，比開放式問題拿到的東西具體。
cards.episode: How Shopify builds a high-intensity culture | Farhan Thawar (VP and Head of Eng)

alts.quote: There's another topic I definitely wanted to spend a little time on, which is this interesting trend that I noticed when I was looking at your LinkedIn and your background.
alts.zh: 還有一個主題我很想花點時間談，就是我在看你的 LinkedIn 跟背景時注意到的一個有趣趨勢。

alts.quote: You ask questions like, what's the hardest you've ever worked to get something done and why? And that does differentiate a lot of people, a lot of people don't actually have a great answer to that.
alts.zh: 你可以問這種問題：你這輩子為了完成某件事最拚的一次是什麼？為什麼？這題真的很能分辨人，很多人其實答不太出來。

alts.quote: I'm asking them, "What do you do for joy? Are you doing something every single day that's bringing you joy in your life?" And if they say no, I'm like, "That's a problem."
alts.zh: 我會問他們：「你都做什麼讓自己開心？你每天有沒有一件事是讓你有樂趣的？」如果回答沒有，我就會說：「那這是個問題。」

cards.pattern: The first thing I noticed was [X], and I asked people what's going on?
cards.quote: When I joined Microsoft many years ago, the first thing I noticed was that Outlook was very buggy and I asked people what's going on?
cards.zh: 我很多年前剛進微軟的時候，第一件注意到的事就是 Outlook 超多 bug，我就去問大家：這是怎麼回事？
cards.why: 新人最有價值的資產是還沒被同化的眼睛。先講 I noticed 再問 what's going on，不帶批評、只要解釋，老鳥才會告訴你真正的原因。
cards.pmNote: 到職前 90 天把所有「這什麼怪東西」記下來，那份清單三個月後再也寫不出來。
cards.episode: Becoming evidence-guided | Itamar Gilad (Gmail, YouTube, Microsoft)

alts.quote: You ask questions like, what's the hardest you've ever worked to get something done and why? And that does differentiate a lot of people, a lot of people don't actually have a great answer to that.
alts.zh: 你可以問這種問題：你這輩子為了完成某件事最拚的一次是什麼？為什麼？這題真的很能分辨人，很多人其實答不太出來。

alts.quote: put a calendar invite, let it renew every three months. You're going to snooze it a couple of times, I get it, I've seen this many, many times before. But just do something, even if it's super small.
alts.zh: 開一個行事曆邀請，每三個月自動重複。你一定會按掉個幾次，我懂，我看過太多次了。但就是做點什麼，再小都好。

alts.quote: And I remember going and pitching our ideas and the VC asked me, how do you know you'll actually make money on this innovation?
alts.zh: 我還記得我們去提案，那個投資人問我：你怎麼知道這個創新真的能賺到錢？

cards.pattern: I found a solution because I asked myself this question: "[一個很笨但很真的問題]"
cards.quote: Okay, so I noticed that I needed to change that at some point, and actually found a solution, again, late in my career, but I found a solution, because I asked myself this question, which is, "Why am I so busy?
cards.zh: 我注意到我某個時間點需要改掉這個，後來真的找到解法——雖然是職涯很後期才找到——因為我問了自己一個問題：「我為什麼這麼忙？」
cards.why: 教練式問題不必聰明。把一個你已經抱怨很久的狀態改寫成一個真的要回答的問句，就是全部的技巧。
cards.pmNote: 「我為什麼這麼忙」的答案通常是你在補別人流程的洞；先找洞，不要先找時間管理法。
cards.episode: Shreyas Doshi Live

alts.quote: I'll say, "I want to run a theory by you. Do you think that the reason why you are really interested in this or you made that decision is actually because of this other thing that you told me a little bit about?"
alts.zh: 我會說：「我想跟你對一個猜測。你會這麼在意這件事、或做了那個決定，會不會其實是因為你剛剛提到的另一件事？」

alts.quote: And I remember going and pitching our ideas and the VC asked me, how do you know you'll actually make money on this innovation?
alts.zh: 我還記得我們去提案，那個投資人問我：你怎麼知道這個創新真的能賺到錢？

alts.quote: There's another topic I definitely wanted to spend a little time on, which is this interesting trend that I noticed when I was looking at your LinkedIn and your background.
alts.zh: 還有一個主題我很想花點時間談，就是我在看你的 LinkedIn 跟背景時注意到的一個有趣趨勢。

cards.pattern: There's another topic I definitely wanted to spend a little time on, which is [X].
cards.quote: There's another topic I definitely wanted to spend a little time on, which is this interesting trend that I noticed when I was looking at your LinkedIn and your background.
cards.zh: 還有一個主題我很想花點時間談，就是我在看你的 LinkedIn 跟背景時注意到的一個有趣趨勢。
cards.why: 換題目前先宣告「我要換題目、而且這是我事前準備的」。definitely wanted to 傳達這不是臨時起意，對方會給更完整的答案。
cards.pmNote: 會議中轉場先報一句「接下來談 X、大概花幾分鐘」，能省掉一半的偏題。
cards.episode: Humanizing product development | Adriel Frederick (Reddit, Lyft, Facebook)

alts.quote: I was looking at your LinkedIn and your career history, and I noticed that you've worked for a different billionaire every decade of your life.
alts.zh: 我看了你的 LinkedIn 跟你的職涯，我注意到你人生每十年都在幫一個不同的億萬富翁工作。

alts.quote: Okay, so I noticed that I needed to change that at some point, and actually found a solution, again, late in my career, but I found a solution, because I asked myself this question, which is, "Why am I so busy?
alts.zh: 我注意到我某個時間點需要改掉這個，後來真的找到解法——雖然是職涯很後期才找到——因為我問了自己一個問題：「我為什麼這麼忙？」
