alts.quote: People call me sometimes they're like "I want to know if I have product market fit." Well, the fact that you have time to call me and ask me this question already tells me the answer.
alts.zh: 有人打給我說：「我想知道我們有沒有 PMF。」嗯，你有空打這通電話問我，這件事本身就給了答案。

cards.quote: Why not think about this bigger?" And every time we talked about something important, he talked about that.
cards.zh: 「為什麼不把這件事想得更大一點？」而且每次我們談到重要的事，他都會講這句。
cards.why: 四個字的教練式問題。Why not 把舉證責任丟回去：你要停在小的版本，得說出理由。台灣人習慣說「可以再想大一點」（建議），英文這句是問句，逼對方自己回答。
cards.pmNote: 主管重複問同一個問題，久了會變成團隊的預設思考步驟，比寫在文件裡有效。
cards.episode: Why we’re at the beginning of the AI hardware boom | Caitlin Kalinowski (ex–OpenAI, Meta, Apple)

alts.quote: I'm asking them, "What do you do for joy? Are you doing something every single day that's bringing you joy in your life?" And if they say no, I'm like, "That's a problem."
alts.zh: 我會問他們：「你都做什麼讓自己開心？你每天有沒有一件事是讓你有樂趣的？」如果回答沒有，我就會說：「那這是個問題。」

alts.quote: put a calendar invite, let it renew every three months. You're going to snooze it a couple of times, I get it, I've seen this many, many times before. But just do something, even if it's super small.
alts.zh: 開一個行事曆邀請，每三個月自動重複。你一定會按掉個幾次，我懂，我看過太多次了。但就是做點什麼，再小都好。

alts.quote: I often think about this phrase, which is people don't care what you know until they know that you care.
alts.zh: 我常想到這句話：在別人知道你在乎之前，他們不會在乎你懂什麼。

cards.quote: We'll see what comes to mind, no pressure, you can skip them too if you want.
cards.zh: 看你想到什麼，沒有壓力，不想答的也可以跳過。
cards.why: 提問前先明講「可以不答」。給了退路，對方反而更願意講——因為他確定這不是被逼的。台灣人習慣把客套放在句首（「方便的話」），英文的退路放在問題後面才像真的。
cards.pmNote: 使用者訪談的標準開場；先給退出權，敏感問題的回答率反而更高。
cards.episode: Frameworks for product differentiation, team building, and thinking from first principles | Ayo Omojola (Carbon Health, Cash App)

alts.quote: I would really love to become a people manager someday. What do you suggest that I work on now so that I'll be ready when the opportunity comes up?
alts.zh: 我以後很想帶人。你建議我現在可以先練哪些東西，等機會來的時候我已經準備好了？

alts.quote: I picked you because I really trust you to be a sound source of truthful advice and give me some feedback. So I really value that. Do you mind spending a couple of minutes and just giving me some thoughts on this?
alts.zh: 我會找你，是因為我真的很信任你會給我誠實的建議跟回饋，這對我很有價值。可以請你花個幾分鐘，給我一點想法嗎？

alts.quote: And you can feel free to let me know if it's too much of an aside.
alts.zh: 如果太離題了，你隨時可以跟我說。

cards.pattern: Are you able to share [敏感的事]?
cards.quote: So are you able to share what went down there with the story of what happened, how it went, and where things are at now?
cards.zh: 所以你方便說一下那邊發生了什麼事嗎——事情經過、後來怎麼樣、現在到哪了？
cards.why: Are you able to 問的是「能不能」而不是「願不願意」，對方可以用「我不能講」擋掉，不必說「我不想講」。這是英文裡最省人情的敏感問題句型。
cards.pmNote: 問競品、問離職原因、問未公開數字都用這個殼；對方拒絕時你也沒有損失關係。
cards.episode: Lessons from scaling Uber and Opendoor | Brian Tolkin (Head of Product at Opendoor, ex-Uber)

alts.quote: It might be easier if I just go, I might be able to save you some time and some energy if I just joined you.
alts.zh: 也許我直接去比較快，我一起進去的話，說不定可以幫你省下一些時間跟力氣。

alts.quote: Give yourself two to three months at the minimum, ideally more like six months, to really optimize it back to a good standing where it can potentially outperform.
alts.zh: 至少給自己兩到三個月，最好是六個月，把它優化回到好的水準、甚至超越原本的表現。

alts.quote: And I want you to say, "This is great. I want to talk about money, but before we do, I want to think about some of the things that will set me up to see succeed in this role.
alts.zh: 我要你這樣說：「這很好。我想談薪水，但在那之前，我想先談談有哪些東西能讓我在這個角色上成功。」

cards.pattern: Feel free to [動作], but don't feel like that's required to [目標].
cards.quote: So feel free to reach out to us if you have questions, but don't feel like that's required to be a good YC applicant.
cards.zh: 有問題歡迎來找我們，但不要覺得一定要這樣做才算是好的申請人。
cards.why: 大部分 feel free to 只是客套；加上 but don't feel like that's required 才真的把壓力拿掉。沒有第二句，對方會把邀請讀成一個隱形的評分項目。
cards.pmNote: 任何「歡迎參加」的內部活動都該補一句不參加不影響評價，否則它實質上是強制的。
cards.episode: Gustaf Alstromer

alts.quote: So instead of just sending the link, I usually start the email with something like looking forward to connecting, feel free to share, sometimes you're available or if easier, you can choose to find time on my calendar using the Calendly link here.
alts.zh: 所以我不會只丟一個連結，我通常這樣開頭：很期待跟你聊，你可以直接給我幾個方便的時間，或者比較省事的話，也可以用這裡的 Calendly 連結直接約。

alts.quote: Sounds like more of a six than a five?” Feel free to adjust the criteria on the charts as you go—the default labels above are just a starting point.
alts.zh: 「聽起來比較像六分而不是五分？」你可以邊做邊調整圖表上的評分標準——上面那些預設標籤只是個起點。

alts.quote: We always keep this kind of mentality internal is that we're still a young company, we want to grow and you can feel free to talk to anyone.
alts.zh: 我們內部一直維持這種心態：我們還是家年輕公司、我們想長大，所以你要找誰談都可以。

cards.pattern: Feel free to share some times you're available, or if easier, you can [用我的行事曆連結].
cards.quote: So instead of just sending the link, I usually start the email with something like looking forward to connecting, feel free to share, sometimes you're available or if easier, you can choose to find time on my calendar using the Calendly link here.
cards.zh: 所以我不會只丟一個連結，我通常這樣開頭：很期待跟你聊，你可以直接給我幾個方便的時間，或者比較省事的話，也可以用這裡的 Calendly 連結直接約。
cards.why: 給兩條路、而且明說哪一條比較省事（if easier），對方就不必猜你希望他選哪個。只丟 Calendly 連結，地位高的一方會覺得被當成下屬。
cards.pmNote: 約會議給「你給時間」與「用我的連結」兩個選項，是跨階級邀約最不失禮的預設。
cards.episode: Behind the scenes of Calendly’s rapid growth | Annie Pearl (CPO)

alts.quote: But do feel free to pay them for their time, especially if the project is being done on their own time.
alts.zh: 不過真的可以付費給他們，尤其是這份作業是佔用他們自己時間做的。

alts.quote: It might be easier if I just go, I might be able to save you some time and some energy if I just joined you.
alts.zh: 也許我直接去比較快，我一起進去的話，說不定可以幫你省下一些時間跟力氣。

alts.quote: So feel free to reach out to us if you have questions, but don't feel like that's required to be a good YC applicant.
alts.zh: 有問題歡迎來找我們，但不要覺得一定要這樣做才算是好的申請人。

cards.quote: We always keep this kind of mentality internal is that we're still a young company, we want to grow and you can feel free to talk to anyone.
cards.zh: 我們內部一直維持這種心態：我們還是家年輕公司、我們想長大，所以你要找誰談都可以。
cards.why: 事前授權。把「可以越級、可以跨部門」講在前面，之後就不必每次都問；沒明講的話，多數人的預設是不行。
cards.pmNote: 資訊流通的預設值要寫下來；沒有明講的權限，在多數組織等於不存在。
cards.episode: Inside TikTok: Culture, strategy, monetization, and more | Ray Cao (Global Head of Monetization Product Strategy and Operations)

alts.quote: I want to make sure I've got air cover from the highest people in the company setting the culture.
alts.zh: 我要確定最高層那些定文化的人會幫我掩護。

alts.quote: And I want you to say, "This is great. I want to talk about money, but before we do, I want to think about some of the things that will set me up to see succeed in this role.
alts.zh: 我要你這樣說：「這很好。我想談薪水，但在那之前，我想先談談有哪些東西能讓我在這個角色上成功。」

alts.quote: So feel free to reach out to us if you have questions, but don't feel like that's required to be a good YC applicant.
alts.zh: 有問題歡迎來找我們，但不要覺得一定要這樣做才算是好的申請人。

cards.pattern: If that doesn't work out, here's the rollback plan, and here's the maximum [損失].
cards.quote: And then I propose a little contingency plan, like hey, if that doesn't work out, here's the rollback plan, here's the maximum impact it will have done in a negative way, which is not going to be too much.
cards.zh: 然後我會提一個小小的備案：如果沒成，這是回滾計畫，這是最壞情況下的負面影響——而且不會太大。
cards.why: 要人點頭最快的方法，是先幫他算好「說 yes 最多會賠多少」。給對方一條退場路線，等於把決定從賭注改成試驗。
cards.pmNote: 提案附回滾計畫與損失上限，是把審批從「要不要冒險」改成「值不值得試」的標準做法。
cards.episode: AI and product management | Marily Nika (Meta, Google)

alts.quote: Okay. I would like to carve 20% of my time listening and I'm happy to do this work 80% of the time.
alts.zh: 好，我想切出兩成的時間去聽，另外八成的時間我很樂意投入手上的工作。

alts.quote: What do you think about us doing an experiment? For the next quarter or two, why don't you let us try running like this? If it goes well, great; if it doesn't, no harm.
alts.zh: 我們來做個實驗你覺得如何？接下來一兩季，讓我們試著用這種方式跑跑看。順利的話很好，不順利也沒損失，我們就退回原本的做法。

alts.quote: But do feel free to pay them for their time, especially if the project is being done on their own time.
alts.zh: 不過真的可以付費給他們，尤其是這份作業是佔用他們自己時間做的。

cards.pattern: It's totally fine if it's [粗糙的樣子] at first.
cards.quote: It’s totally fine if it’s messy and random at first.
cards.zh: 一開始亂七八糟、東一塊西一塊也完全沒關係。
cards.why: 跟人要初稿時先把品質門檻明講到很低。不講，對方會用自己想像中的標準做，然後遲交或乾脆不交。
cards.pmNote: 要 draft 一定要附上「可接受的最低品質」，否則你收到的是延遲，不是品質。
cards.episode: Flywheels, flywheels, flywheels

alts.quote: What would it take, Lenny? How can we get going on Riverside? What would it take?
alts.zh: 那要怎樣才成呢，Lenny？我們要怎麼把 Riverside 這件事推動起來？要什麼條件你才點頭？

alts.quote: Lenny, you can say, "Hey, are you open to 450? That was really what I was hoping for.
alts.zh: 你可以說：「你們可以接受 450 嗎？這其實是我原本期待的數字。這件事我們可以談嗎？」

alts.quote: We always keep this kind of mentality internal is that we're still a young company, we want to grow and you can feel free to talk to anyone.
alts.zh: 我們內部一直維持這種心態：我們還是家年輕公司、我們想長大，所以你要找誰談都可以。

cards.pattern: Feel free to adjust [X] as you go — the defaults are just a starting point.
cards.quote: Sounds like more of a six than a five?” Feel free to adjust the criteria on the charts as you go—the default labels above are just a starting point.
cards.zh: 「聽起來比較像六分而不是五分？」你可以邊做邊調整圖表上的評分標準——上面那些預設標籤只是個起點。
cards.why: 交出方法論的同時交出改它的權力。明說 default 只是起點，使用者才敢改；不明說，多數人會照著做到不合用為止然後放棄。
cards.pmNote: 內部模板一定要標示哪些欄位可以刪；沒標的欄位會被當成規定。
cards.episode: Introducing the Foundation Sprint: From the creators of the Design Sprint

alts.quote: So feel free to reach out to us if you have questions, but don't feel like that's required to be a good YC applicant.
alts.zh: 有問題歡迎來找我們，但不要覺得一定要這樣做才算是好的申請人。

alts.quote: So instead of just sending the link, I usually start the email with something like looking forward to connecting, feel free to share, sometimes you're available or if easier, you can choose to find time on my calendar using the Calendly link here.
alts.zh: 所以我不會只丟一個連結，我通常這樣開頭：很期待跟你聊，你可以直接給我幾個方便的時間，或者比較省事的話，也可以用這裡的 Calendly 連結直接約。

alts.quote: We always keep this kind of mentality internal is that we're still a young company, we want to grow and you can feel free to talk to anyone.
alts.zh: 我們內部一直維持這種心態：我們還是家年輕公司、我們想長大，所以你要找誰談都可以。

cards.pattern: But do feel free to [X], especially if [條件].
cards.quote: But do feel free to pay them for their time, especially if the project is being done on their own time.
cards.zh: 不過真的可以付費給他們，尤其是這份作業是佔用他們自己時間做的。
cards.why: do feel free 比 feel free 多一個 do，語氣從「我允許」變成「我鼓勵」。差一個字，對方對「要不要做」的判讀就不同。
cards.pmNote: 請人做面試作業就該付費，這是招募品牌最便宜的投資。
cards.episode: How to interview product managers

alts.quote: So instead of just sending the link, I usually start the email with something like looking forward to connecting, feel free to share, sometimes you're available or if easier, you can choose to find time on my calendar using the Calendly link here.
alts.zh: 所以我不會只丟一個連結，我通常這樣開頭：很期待跟你聊，你可以直接給我幾個方便的時間，或者比較省事的話，也可以用這裡的 Calendly 連結直接約。

alts.quote: So feel free to reach out to us if you have questions, but don't feel like that's required to be a good YC applicant.
alts.zh: 有問題歡迎來找我們，但不要覺得一定要這樣做才算是好的申請人。

alts.quote: We always keep this kind of mentality internal is that we're still a young company, we want to grow and you can feel free to talk to anyone.
alts.zh: 我們內部一直維持這種心態：我們還是家年輕公司、我們想長大，所以你要找誰談都可以。

cards.pattern: Feel free to let me know if it's too much of [一個岔題／太細節].
cards.quote: And you can feel free to let me know if it's too much of an aside.
cards.zh: 如果太離題了，你隨時可以跟我說。
cards.why: 自己主動遞出中止鍵。講一段可能沒人想聽的細節前先給對方喊停的權力，你就不必邊講邊猜對方的表情。
cards.pmNote: 簡報講到細節前先問「要多深」，比講完才發現方向錯了省時間。
cards.episode: How to foster innovation and big thinking | Eeke de Milliano (Retool, Stripe)

alts.quote: If not, feel free to talk to any manager, whether your own or somebody else.
alts.zh: 如果不行的話，你可以去找任何一位主管談，不管是不是你自己的主管。

alts.quote: Feel free to use it next time you feel this same problem.
alts.zh: 下次你再碰到同樣問題的時候，隨時可以拿去用。

alts.quote: So instead of just going to someone saying, "Hey, can you be a mentor?" Coming to me and say, "Do you know someone who's actually really good at changing the way teams work or really good at communicating a new vision that I can talk to?"
alts.zh: 與其跑去問人家「你可以當我的 mentor 嗎」，不如問：「你認識誰特別擅長改變團隊運作方式、或特別會傳達新願景，可以讓我請教一下嗎？」

cards.pattern: Feel free to talk to any [對象], whether your own or somebody else.
cards.quote: If not, feel free to talk to any manager, whether your own or somebody else.
cards.zh: 如果不行的話，你可以去找任何一位主管談，不管是不是你自己的主管。
cards.why: 明說「可以繞過我」。給求助者一條不必經過你的路，等於承認你不是唯一解，也讓對方不必為了保護關係而不敢求助。
cards.pmNote: 求助管道一定要有第二條不經過直屬主管的路，否則主管本身是問題時就無解。
cards.episode: Taking control of your career | Ethan Evans (Amazon)

alts.quote: And you can feel free to let me know if it's too much of an aside.
alts.zh: 如果太離題了，你隨時可以跟我說。

alts.quote: Feel free to use it next time you feel this same problem.
alts.zh: 下次你再碰到同樣問題的時候，隨時可以拿去用。

alts.quote: I would really love to become a people manager someday. What do you suggest that I work on now so that I'll be ready when the opportunity comes up?
alts.zh: 我以後很想帶人。你建議我現在可以先練哪些東西，等機會來的時候我已經準備好了？

cards.pattern: This is all up to you, but [一句很短的忠告].
cards.quote: My uncle and aunt were coming in, and they're encouraging me, "This is all up to you, but try not to lose it all on night number one," which was good advice to give me.
cards.zh: 我叔叔阿姨要來，他們鼓勵我說：「這都是你自己決定，不過盡量不要第一晚就全輸光。」後來覺得這建議給得很好。
cards.why: 先交出決定權，再給一句很短的忠告。順序很重要：先講忠告再補「當然看你」會像客套，先說 up to you 反而讓後面那句聽得進去。
cards.pmNote: 給建議前先確認對方是決策者，可以大幅降低建議被當成干預的機率。
cards.episode: How a great founder becomes a great CEO | Jonathan Lowenhar (co-founder of Enjoy The Work)

alts.quote: I picked you because I really trust you to be a sound source of truthful advice and give me some feedback. So I really value that. Do you mind spending a couple of minutes and just giving me some thoughts on this?
alts.zh: 我會找你，是因為我真的很信任你會給我誠實的建議跟回饋，這對我很有價值。可以請你花個幾分鐘，給我一點想法嗎？

alts.quote: So first of all, when you're in the early innings, you'll actually get more useful advice often from your peers because they're going through the same thing.
alts.zh: 首先，在很前期的階段，你從同輩那裡拿到的建議其實比較有用，因為他們正在經歷一模一樣的事。

alts.quote: So instead of just going to someone saying, "Hey, can you be a mentor?" Coming to me and say, "Do you know someone who's actually really good at changing the way teams work or really good at communicating a new vision that I can talk to?"
alts.zh: 與其跑去問人家「你可以當我的 mentor 嗎」，不如問：「你認識誰特別擅長改變團隊運作方式、或特別會傳達新願景，可以讓我請教一下嗎？」

cards.pattern: What you do is up to you, but by [下次見面前], you should have [動作].
cards.quote: What you do is up to you, but by the next time we talk, you should have made a move.” We considered our options: shut down, restart, or sell the company.
cards.zh: 「怎麼做由你決定，但下次我們談之前，你應該已經動了。」我們評估了選項：關掉、重來，或把公司賣掉。
cards.why: 自主權給滿，但時間點鎖死。up to you 管的是「做什麼」，by the next time we talk 管的是「什麼時候」——兩者分開，就能既不越權又不放生。
cards.pmNote: 對不歸你管的人施加推力，唯一能拿的槓桿是時間點，不是內容。
cards.episode: Startup to exit: Lessons from a first-time founder

alts.quote: Feel free to use it next time you feel this same problem.
alts.zh: 下次你再碰到同樣問題的時候，隨時可以拿去用。

alts.quote: If this job were open, I'd like to be considered for it.
alts.zh: 如果這個職位有空缺，我希望能被列入考慮。

alts.quote: If they had reached out to me and said, "I know you don't know me. I have this small software company. I'm not well-connected, but I would love your advice on how to grow this business and what you would do if you were in my shoes,"
alts.zh: 如果他們寫信說：「我知道你不認識我。我有間小軟體公司，我人脈也不廣，但我很想聽聽你對怎麼把它做大的建議——如果你是我會怎麼做？」

cards.pattern: Feel free to use it next time you [遇到同樣狀況].
cards.quote: Feel free to use it next time you feel this same problem.
cards.zh: 下次你再碰到同樣問題的時候，隨時可以拿去用。
cards.why: 給工具而不是給指令，並且附上一個觸發時機（next time you…）。建議會被記住是因為它綁在情境上，不是因為它有道理。
cards.pmNote: 分享方法時附上使用時機，採用率遠高於只講方法本身。
cards.episode: Strategies for becoming less distracted and improving focus | Nir Eyal (author of Indistractable and Hooked)

alts.quote: And you can feel free to let me know if it's too much of an aside.
alts.zh: 如果太離題了，你隨時可以跟我說。

alts.quote: If not, feel free to talk to any manager, whether your own or somebody else.
alts.zh: 如果不行的話，你可以去找任何一位主管談，不管是不是你自己的主管。

alts.quote: What you do is up to you, but by the next time we talk, you should have made a move.” We considered our options: shut down, restart, or sell the company.
alts.zh: 「怎麼做由你決定，但下次我們談之前，你應該已經動了。」我們評估了選項：關掉、重來，或把公司賣掉。

cards.quote: Who needs to do what by when?
cards.zh: 誰要在什麼時候之前做什麼？
cards.why: 會議結尾唯一必問的一句。六個字同時鎖三個欄位：人、事、時間。中文的「那就先這樣」把三個欄位一起留白。
cards.pmNote: 沒有這句的會議一律視為沒有結論；把它做成會議紀錄的固定欄位。
cards.episode: Scripts for difficult conversations: Giving hard feedback, navigating defensiveness, the three questions you should end every meeting with, more | Alisa Cohn (executive coach)

alts.quote: Two people owning a goal is no one owning a goal. One person owns the goal, who is it?
alts.zh: 兩個人一起扛一個目標，等於沒人在扛。這個目標只能有一個人負責——是誰？

alts.quote: I'm in too many conversations where I'm like, "Who is on the hook for this decision? Who cares if this decision is made?" It's not like six people with consensus. Who is the person?
alts.zh: 我參加過太多會議，我會問：「這個決定是誰扛？誰真的在乎它有沒有被做出來？」不是六個人共識，是哪一個人？

alts.quote: But really, we want to help people answer the question at work, "Who is doing what by when, and why?" So that notion of clarity of purpose, clarity of plan, progress, and responsibility are often so painful in people's work lives.
alts.zh: 我們真正想幫人在工作上回答的問題是：誰、在什麼時候之前、要做什麼、為什麼？所以目的清楚、計畫清楚、進度與責任清楚，這些在多數人的工作裡都非常痛苦。

cards.quote: But really, we want to help people answer the question at work, "Who is doing what by when, and why?" So that notion of clarity of purpose, clarity of plan, progress, and responsibility are often so painful in people's work lives.
cards.zh: 我們真正想幫人在工作上回答的問題是：誰、在什麼時候之前、要做什麼、為什麼？所以目的清楚、計畫清楚、進度與責任清楚，這些在多數人的工作裡都非常痛苦。
cards.why: 在標準的 what by when 後面多加一個 why。前三個管執行，why 管的是有人想砍這件事時它還站不站得住。
cards.pmNote: 待辦清單只有人跟時間，在改優先序時會全面崩潰；每一項都要能追回到一個理由。
cards.episode: How to ask the right questions, project confidence, and win over skeptics | Paige Costello (Asana, Intercom, Intuit)

alts.quote: Two people owning a goal is no one owning a goal. One person owns the goal, who is it?
alts.zh: 兩個人一起扛一個目標，等於沒人在扛。這個目標只能有一個人負責——是誰？

alts.quote: I'm in too many conversations where I'm like, "Who is on the hook for this decision? Who cares if this decision is made?" It's not like six people with consensus. Who is the person?
alts.zh: 我參加過太多會議，我會問：「這個決定是誰扛？誰真的在乎它有沒有被做出來？」不是六個人共識，是哪一個人？

alts.quote: So basically my long answer to your question, maybe boring answer is that I think starting next year, we're going to see early adopters starting to hockey stick their productivity.
alts.zh: 所以我這個落落長、可能還有點無聊的答案就是：我覺得從明年開始，早期採用者的生產力會開始往上翹。

cards.pattern: Use [某些字眼] as an automatic signal to pause and clarify who will do what by when.
cards.quote: When you hear these words, use them as an automatic signal to pause and clarify who will do what by when.
cards.zh: 當你聽到這些字眼，就把它當成一個自動訊號：停下來，把誰在什麼時候之前做什麼講清楚。
cards.why: 把追問變成觸發式反應，而不是每次都要鼓起勇氣。英文會議裡 we'll circle back、let's align、someone should 都是這種訊號詞。
cards.pmNote: 為模糊語言建一份觸發清單，聽到就當場補欄位，比會後補紀錄有效。
cards.episode: Introducing the GAIN framework for feedback: an evidence-based approach to giving feedback that people love, appreciate, and act on

alts.quote: Two people owning a goal is no one owning a goal. One person owns the goal, who is it?
alts.zh: 兩個人一起扛一個目標，等於沒人在扛。這個目標只能有一個人負責——是誰？

alts.quote: I'm in too many conversations where I'm like, "Who is on the hook for this decision? Who cares if this decision is made?" It's not like six people with consensus. Who is the person?
alts.zh: 我參加過太多會議，我會問：「這個決定是誰扛？誰真的在乎它有沒有被做出來？」不是六個人共識，是哪一個人？

alts.quote: I think that's the key part, but let me pause there and then I'll talk a little bit about ChatGPT and some of my reasoning behind that.
alts.zh: 我覺得那是關鍵的部分，但我先停在這裡，然後再來講一點 ChatGPT 和我背後的理由。

cards.pattern: Who's the DRI, who needs to weigh in, and who's going to be the helper?
cards.quote: Who's the DRI and who needs to weigh in and who's going to be the helper?
cards.zh: 誰是 DRI？誰需要表達意見？誰是幫手？
cards.why: 一次把三種角色分開問。多數爭執其實是「有意見的人以為自己有決定權」，這句話把 weigh in 跟 decide 明確切開。
cards.pmNote: DRI＝directly responsible individual，一件事只能有一個；weigh in 的人可以很多。
cards.episode: How to build a powerful marketing machine | Emily Kramer (Asana, Carta, MKT1)

alts.quote: We pick the best person who's most capable of driving an initiative forward, regardless of the function to be the DRI.
alts.zh: 我們挑最有能力把一件事推動下去的人當 DRI，不管他是哪個部門的。

alts.quote: Sometimes I'm like, "Who's owning this?" And it's like people don't know. That's why I think it's very important to have a single-threaded owner.
alts.zh: 有時候我問「這件事誰在 own？」結果大家都不知道。這就是為什麼一定要有一個單一負責人。

alts.quote: I'm going to mirror back the tips you just shared, and there's actually a secondary tip that I think is the more interesting piece.
alts.zh: 我把你剛剛給的建議重述一遍——而且我覺得裡面藏了一個更有意思的第二層建議。

cards.quote: And then the DRI's job is to take all that input and make a decision.
cards.zh: 然後 DRI 的工作就是把所有意見收進來，然後做決定。
cards.why: 定義職責時把「收集」跟「決定」綁在同一句。只講決定會被讀成獨裁，只講收集會變成無限協商。
cards.pmNote: 共識不是決策機制；DRI 要負責聽完，但不必等到所有人都同意。
cards.episode: Sanchan Saxena (VP of Product at Coinbase) on the inside story of how Airbnb made it through Covid; what he’s learned from Brian Chesky, Brian Armstrong, and Kevin Systrom; much more

alts.quote: As a PM, your job is to just cut as much scope as possible to make it possible to hit that deadline.
alts.zh: 身為 PM，你的工作就是盡可能砍範圍，讓那個死線變成做得到。

alts.quote: Here's what I heard from all of you. I'm listening, I hear this and here's what I want to do about it.
alts.zh: 以下是我從各位那裡聽到的。我有在聽，我聽到了，接下來我打算這樣做。

alts.quote: So just to summarize and make it super clear.
alts.zh: 所以總結一下，把它講到超清楚。

cards.pattern: We trust the [角色], whoever that is, to make the decision.
cards.quote: We trust the DRI, whoever that DRI is, to make the decision.
cards.zh: 不管 DRI 是誰，我們都信任那個人做決定。
cards.why: whoever that is 把信任綁在角色上而不是特定的人身上。這樣新人接手時不必重新爭取授權。
cards.pmNote: 授權寫在角色上而不是人身上，組織才能換人不換制度。
cards.episode: Sanchan Saxena (VP of Product at Coinbase) on the inside story of how Airbnb made it through Covid; what he’s learned from Brian Chesky, Brian Armstrong, and Kevin Systrom; much more

alts.quote: So to replay the system overall highlight is about the thing you want to make time for today. The most important thing today, laser is about creating barriers to distraction.
alts.zh: 把整套系統再跑一遍：highlight 是你今天最想騰出時間做的那件事；laser 是替干擾設路障。

alts.quote: I'm in too many conversations where I'm like, "Who is on the hook for this decision? Who cares if this decision is made?" It's not like six people with consensus. Who is the person?
alts.zh: 我參加過太多會議，我會問：「這個決定是誰扛？誰真的在乎它有沒有被做出來？」不是六個人共識，是哪一個人？

alts.quote: Who's the DRI and who needs to weigh in and who's going to be the helper?
alts.zh: 誰是 DRI？誰需要表達意見？誰是幫手？

cards.pattern: We pick the best person …, regardless of the function, to be the DRI.
cards.quote: We pick the best person who's most capable of driving an initiative forward, regardless of the function to be the DRI.
cards.zh: 我們挑最有能力把一件事推動下去的人當 DRI，不管他是哪個部門的。
cards.why: regardless of the function 是先把「這應該是 PM 的事」這種部門本位擋掉。指定負責人時先講選人標準再講人選，爭議會小很多。
cards.pmNote: DRI 依推動能力指派而非職稱，是跨部門專案不卡住的關鍵設計。
cards.episode: Inside the expert network training every frontier AI model | Garrett Lord (Handshake CEO)

alts.quote: Who's the DRI and who needs to weigh in and who's going to be the helper?
alts.zh: 誰是 DRI？誰需要表達意見？誰是幫手？

alts.quote: Sometimes I'm like, "Who's owning this?" And it's like people don't know. That's why I think it's very important to have a single-threaded owner.
alts.zh: 有時候我問「這件事誰在 own？」結果大家都不知道。這就是為什麼一定要有一個單一負責人。

alts.quote: So maybe this is a way to come back to your question about what's the output of the shaping session, it's like it's shaped if we can give this to a technical person and they say, "Yeah, I know what to go build now."
alts.zh: 所以回到你剛剛問的「shaping session 的產出是什麼」：判準是——把它交給一個技術的人，他會說「好，我知道要蓋什麼了」。

cards.pattern: [專案] are driven by a single DRI.
cards.quote: Projects are driven by a single DRI, and execution steps are done in parallel as much as possible.
cards.zh: 每個專案都由單一一位 DRI 推動，執行步驟盡可能平行進行。
cards.why: a single 這個字是重點。英文寫制度時會刻意把數量寫出來，因為「負責人」在沒有限定時很容易變成兩個以上，然後就沒有人負責。
cards.pmNote: 一件事兩個負責人等於零個負責人；共同負責是最常見的組織失能。
cards.episode: How Perplexity builds product

alts.quote: As a PM, your job is to just cut as much scope as possible to make it possible to hit that deadline.
alts.zh: 身為 PM，你的工作就是盡可能砍範圍，讓那個死線變成做得到。

alts.quote: Sometimes I'm like, "Who's owning this?" And it's like people don't know. That's why I think it's very important to have a single-threaded owner.
alts.zh: 有時候我問「這件事誰在 own？」結果大家都不知道。這就是為什麼一定要有一個單一負責人。

alts.quote: Who's the DRI and who needs to weigh in and who's going to be the helper?
alts.zh: 誰是 DRI？誰需要表達意見？誰是幫手？

cards.pattern: My feeling on [X] is don't have too many of them, and when you do, it's a P0.
cards.quote: So, my feeling on deadlines is don't have too many of them, and when you do, it's a P0.
cards.zh: 我對死線的看法是：不要訂太多，但一旦訂了，那就是 P0。
cards.why: 先限制數量再提高強度。英文表達立場常用這種「少而硬」的結構，比「每個都很重要」可信，因為它顯示你願意放棄一些東西。
cards.pmNote: 死線的可信度來自稀有度；每季一到兩個真死線，其餘用目標日期。
cards.episode: Linear’s secret to building beloved B2B products | Nan Yu (Head of Product)

alts.quote: I'm in too many conversations where I'm like, "Who is on the hook for this decision? Who cares if this decision is made?" It's not like six people with consensus. Who is the person?
alts.zh: 我參加過太多會議，我會問：「這個決定是誰扛？誰真的在乎它有沒有被做出來？」不是六個人共識，是哪一個人？

alts.quote: Sometimes I'm like, "Who's owning this?" And it's like people don't know. That's why I think it's very important to have a single-threaded owner.
alts.zh: 有時候我問「這件事誰在 own？」結果大家都不知道。這就是為什麼一定要有一個單一負責人。

alts.quote: So maybe this is a way to come back to your question about what's the output of the shaping session, it's like it's shaped if we can give this to a technical person and they say, "Yeah, I know what to go build now."
alts.zh: 所以回到你剛剛問的「shaping session 的產出是什麼」：判準是——把它交給一個技術的人，他會說「好，我知道要蓋什麼了」。

cards.pattern: Your job is to cut as much scope as possible to make it possible to hit [that deadline].
cards.quote: As a PM, your job is to just cut as much scope as possible to make it possible to hit that deadline.
cards.zh: 身為 PM，你的工作就是盡可能砍範圍，讓那個死線變成做得到。
cards.why: 把「守住日期」翻譯成「砍東西」。英文職場對死線的預設反應是調整範圍而不是加班——這是台灣人最需要重寫的一條預設。
cards.pmNote: 時間、範圍、品質三選二；日期定死時，唯一能動的變數就是範圍。
cards.episode: Linear’s secret to building beloved B2B products | Nan Yu (Head of Product)

alts.quote: And then the DRI's job is to take all that input and make a decision.
alts.zh: 然後 DRI 的工作就是把所有意見收進來，然後做決定。

alts.quote: So just to summarize and make it super clear.
alts.zh: 所以總結一下，把它講到超清楚。

alts.quote: Projects are driven by a single DRI, and execution steps are done in parallel as much as possible.
alts.zh: 每個專案都由單一一位 DRI 推動，執行步驟盡可能平行進行。

cards.pattern: For [新產品上線], you got quality, features, deadline — choose two.
cards.quote: Well, another thing that Evan taught me was that for a new launch, you got quality, features, deadline, choose two.
cards.zh: Evan 教我的另一件事是：新產品上線，品質、功能、死線，三個裡面挑兩個。
cards.why: 把取捨講成一條規則而不是一次談判。choose two 讓對方變成共同決策者，他不能三個都要，但可以決定放掉哪一個。
cards.pmNote: 上線前讓利害關係人當場選兩個，比事後解釋為什麼砍功能省事得多。
cards.episode: Dylan Field live at Config: Intuition, simplicity, and the future of design

alts.quote: Okay, so let me summarize things that you've taught us so far. One is think about publications that go to people that will buy your thing. Two is don't think of it broad thing.
alts.zh: 好，我來把你目前教我們的整理一下。第一，挑那些會接觸到你買家的媒體。第二，不要只想到媒體這個層級。

alts.quote: And one last thing to touch on, you said something really important about pull, and I want to double down on that.
alts.zh: 還有最後一件事，你剛剛講到「拉力」那個點很重要，我想把它再放大講。

alts.quote: As a PM, your job is to just cut as much scope as possible to make it possible to hit that deadline.
alts.zh: 身為 PM，你的工作就是盡可能砍範圍，讓那個死線變成做得到。

cards.quote: Sometimes we say deadlines are a gift.
cards.zh: 我們有時候會說，死線是一種禮物。
cards.why: 把一個大家覺得討厭的東西重新命名成禮物，是提出不受歡迎機制時最短的框架句。台灣人習慣先道歉（「不好意思要訂個時間」），英文則是先重新定義它的價值。
cards.pmNote: 死線減少的是選項而不是時間；對拖延與無限討論都是解藥。
cards.episode: Using behavioral science to improve your product | Kristen Berman (Irrational Labs)

alts.quote: I still may insert myself and say, "Hey, let me pause here for a second and try to capture what has been said." This is what I've heard.
alts.zh: 我還是會切進去說：「欸，我先暫停一下，把剛剛講的整理一下。」以下是我聽到的。

alts.quote: Sometimes I'm like, "Who's owning this?" And it's like people don't know. That's why I think it's very important to have a single-threaded owner.
alts.zh: 有時候我問「這件事誰在 own？」結果大家都不知道。這就是為什麼一定要有一個單一負責人。

alts.quote: So maybe this is a way to come back to your question about what's the output of the shaping session, it's like it's shaped if we can give this to a technical person and they say, "Yeah, I know what to go build now."
alts.zh: 所以回到你剛剛問的「shaping session 的產出是什麼」：判準是——把它交給一個技術的人，他會說「好，我知道要蓋什麼了」。

cards.pattern: What shall we build by when, and what are the resources?
cards.quote: They talk about what shall we build by when, what are the resources?
cards.zh: 他們談的是：我們要在什麼時候之前做出什麼、資源有多少？
cards.why: by when 跟 resources 綁在一起問。只問時間不問資源，對方只能用加班回答；兩個一起問，才叫在談計畫。
cards.pmNote: 承諾日期前先確認資源；沒有資源欄位的時程表都是願望清單。
cards.episode: Becoming evidence-guided | Itamar Gilad (Gmail, YouTube, Microsoft)

alts.quote: So maybe this is a way to come back to your question about what's the output of the shaping session, it's like it's shaped if we can give this to a technical person and they say, "Yeah, I know what to go build now."
alts.zh: 所以回到你剛剛問的「shaping session 的產出是什麼」：判準是——把它交給一個技術的人，他會說「好，我知道要蓋什麼了」。

alts.quote: I think that's the key part, but let me pause there and then I'll talk a little bit about ChatGPT and some of my reasoning behind that.
alts.zh: 我覺得那是關鍵的部分，但我先停在這裡，然後再來講一點 ChatGPT 和我背後的理由。

alts.quote: So just to summarize what you shared, which I was just writing as you were talking about the things that essentially help Stripe build this incredible team.
alts.zh: 所以總結一下你分享的——你講的時候我就在寫——那些讓 Stripe 能建出這支超強團隊的東西。

cards.pattern: What I'm hearing from them is that you're [行為], and not letting them know [X].
cards.quote: So what I'm hearing from them is that you're missing deadlines on a regular basis and not letting them know you're missing the deadlines, and that also you're not fully keeping your team up to speed.
cards.zh: 所以我從他們那邊聽到的是：你經常錯過死線，而且錯過的時候沒有讓他們知道，另外你也沒有讓你的團隊完全掌握狀況。
cards.why: What I'm hearing from them 把訊息來源說清楚，你是轉述不是評判。真正的指控在後半句——不是遲交，是遲交而沒說。
cards.pmNote: 職場上遲交是常態，沒預警才是信任破口；delay 要在死線前講，不是死線後解釋。
cards.episode: Scripts for difficult conversations: Giving hard feedback, navigating defensiveness, the three questions you should end every meeting with, more | Alisa Cohn (executive coach)

alts.quote: Then you're pushing deadlines out, and you're making your marketing team very sad.
alts.zh: 然後你就開始一直往後延，把行銷團隊搞得很難過。

alts.quote: I'm just going to bump you up to the 100-video plan. Let me know if you have any questions.
alts.zh: 我就直接幫你升到 100 支影片的方案囉。有問題再跟我說。

alts.quote: You know what? We should ship. It's embarrassing, but that's strictly less bad than not getting the feedback you wanted.
alts.zh: 我覺得就出吧。是很難看沒錯，但這比拿不到你要的回饋還是好一點。

cards.pattern: I've talked to you multiple times about [X], and I've talked to you multiple times about [Y].
cards.quote: I've talked to you multiple times about coordinating with your peers and not having them surprised about missed deadlines, and I've talked to you multiple times about keeping your team in the loop on different things.
cards.zh: 關於跟同儕協調、不要讓他們對你錯過死線感到意外，我已經跟你談過很多次；關於讓你的團隊掌握各種進度，我也跟你談過很多次。
cards.why: 同一個句式重複兩次，是在當場建立紀錄。這種話出現時通常代表下一步是正式流程——英文職場用結構而不是音量來表示嚴重性。
cards.pmNote: 同一件事講到第三次就要書面化；純口頭提醒沒有累積效力。
cards.episode: Scripts for difficult conversations: Giving hard feedback, navigating defensiveness, the three questions you should end every meeting with, more | Alisa Cohn (executive coach)

alts.quote: Then you're pushing deadlines out, and you're making your marketing team very sad.
alts.zh: 然後你就開始一直往後延，把行銷團隊搞得很難過。

alts.quote: Hopefully I'm not making this sound too daunting. I'm just really trying to lay out all the mistakes I've made.
alts.zh: 希望我沒有把這件事講得太嚇人。我只是想把我自己踩過的坑全部攤出來。

alts.quote: By the way, a very, very successful company for a new set of products has a 50% hit rate. So half of you are going to come back in a year and have a different job. Do you have the resilience to do that?
alts.zh: 順帶一提，一家非常成功的公司做新產品的成功率大概是五成。所以你們有一半的人一年後會換一份工作。你們有那個韌性嗎？

cards.pattern: We were given a pretty strict deadline …, and I pushed it out [three times].
cards.quote: I definitely don't think it was obvious to everyone, and I can definitely say that because we were given a pretty strict deadline that we needed to launch by and I pushed it out three times.
cards.zh: 我完全不覺得這對所有人來說是顯而易見的，我敢這樣說是因為我們當初拿到一個很硬的上線死線，而我把它往後推了三次。
cards.why: 報壞消息時自己把次數講出來。I pushed it out three times 沒有任何形容詞跟藉口，數字本身就是誠意；模糊化（「有稍微延一點」）反而會被追問。
cards.pmNote: 延期要主動報次數與新日期；被問出來的延期，代價是自己說的三倍。
cards.episode: Unorthodox PM wisdom: Automating user insights, unselling job candidates, logging every decision, more | Kevin Yien (Stripe, Square, Mutiny)

alts.quote: It was pretty obvious after six months this thing was a bit of a zombie product walking, and the least I could have done is said, "This thing is dead." We could have called it dead way earlier.
alts.zh: 半年後就很明顯這是個活死人產品了，我至少可以做的，就是講一句：這個東西已經死了。我們早就該宣布它死亡。

alts.quote: And at Uber, I learned this because, it pains me to say this, but really the price and the ETA at Uber was the product.
alts.zh: 我在 Uber 學到這件事——講出來我自己都有點痛——但價格跟預估時間，那才是 Uber 真正的產品。

alts.quote: I would be honest with people and say some patience is required. However, there is a lot you can do. A lot is in your control.
alts.zh: 我會誠實地說：這需要一點耐心。不過，你能做的事很多，很多都在你的掌控裡。

cards.pattern: You're pushing deadlines out, and you're making [下游團隊] very sad.
cards.quote: Then you're pushing deadlines out, and you're making your marketing team very sad.
cards.zh: 然後你就開始一直往後延，把行銷團隊搞得很難過。
cards.why: 講延期的後果時指名被害的下游團隊。抽象的「會有影響」沒人會動，講出「誰會被害到」才會。very sad 是刻意的輕描淡寫，在英文裡反而更刺。
cards.pmNote: 排程變動要算下游成本（行銷檔期、業務承諾、客服準備），那才是延期真正的價格。
cards.episode: Linear’s secret to building beloved B2B products | Nan Yu (Head of Product)

alts.quote: So what I'm hearing from them is that you're missing deadlines on a regular basis and not letting them know you're missing the deadlines, and that also you're not fully keeping your team up to speed.
alts.zh: 所以我從他們那邊聽到的是：你經常錯過死線，而且錯過的時候沒有讓他們知道，另外你也沒有讓你的團隊完全掌握狀況。

alts.quote: We are a series A startup. We are pushing really hard at product-market fit. The expectation here is going to be that you're online at 10:00, that you can occasionally hop on a meeting on a Saturday or Sunday."
alts.zh: 「我們是 A 輪新創。我們正在拚產品市場契合。這裡的預期是你晚上十點還在線上，週六日偶爾也要開會。」

alts.quote: Hopefully I'm not making this sound too daunting. I'm just really trying to lay out all the mistakes I've made.
alts.zh: 希望我沒有把這件事講得太嚇人。我只是想把我自己踩過的坑全部攤出來。

cards.pattern: Be careful punishing people who don't — otherwise people will [自我保護的行為].
cards.quote: But be careful punishing people who don’t — otherwise people will pad deadlines or ship crappy code.
cards.zh: 但要小心處罰沒達成的人——不然大家就會開始把時程灌水，或是交出爛程式碼。
cards.why: 反對一個管理做法時，直接講它會誘發的行為，而不是講它「不好」。otherwise 後面那句是預測，預測可以驗證，價值判斷不行。
cards.pmNote: 只獎不罰是刻意設計：處罰未達成會直接換來估時灌水，之後那份資料就再也不能用了。
cards.episode: This Week #4: Motivating engineers to hit deadlines, PM career ladders, and aligning with execs

alts.quote: It's so hard to give a founder hard feedback. Who wants to be the bearer of bad news?
alts.zh: 要給創辦人難聽的回饋真的很難。誰想當那個報壞消息的人？

alts.quote: I would be honest with people and say some patience is required. However, there is a lot you can do. A lot is in your control.
alts.zh: 我會誠實地說：這需要一點耐心。不過，你能做的事很多，很多都在你的掌控裡。

alts.quote: We can't just cut the scope and say, "Oh, well now, we managed to ship inside of six weeks." That's going to kill everybody's morale.
alts.zh: 我們不能就這樣砍掉範圍，然後說「你看，我們六週內出貨了」。那會把所有人的士氣打死。

cards.pattern: We feel it's trying to drive [X] via [壞方法] versus via [好方法].
cards.quote: We feel it’s trying to drive urgency via artificial deadlines versus via value to the customer.
cards.zh: 我們覺得它是在用人造的死線去製造急迫感，而不是用對客戶的價值。
cards.why: 批評用 A versus B 的對比句，聽起來像在比較方法而不是在否定人。We feel 又把它標成團隊觀點，留了被說服的空間。
cards.pmNote: 內部否決一個做法時同時給出你認為對的那條路，否則會被當成純粹擋案。
cards.episode: How Gong builds product

alts.quote: Hopefully I'm not making this sound too daunting. I'm just really trying to lay out all the mistakes I've made.
alts.zh: 希望我沒有把這件事講得太嚇人。我只是想把我自己踩過的坑全部攤出來。

alts.quote: Then you're pushing deadlines out, and you're making your marketing team very sad.
alts.zh: 然後你就開始一直往後延，把行銷團隊搞得很難過。

alts.quote: So what I'm hearing from them is that you're missing deadlines on a regular basis and not letting them know you're missing the deadlines, and that also you're not fully keeping your team up to speed.
alts.zh: 所以我從他們那邊聽到的是：你經常錯過死線，而且錯過的時候沒有讓他們知道，另外你也沒有讓你的團隊完全掌握狀況。

cards.pattern: I was often running against the deadline, barely finishing it — which is not what I was expecting.
cards.quote: So I was working on parallel things at the same time, and I was often running against the deadline, I was barely finishing it, which is not what I was expecting initially.
cards.zh: 所以我同時在做好幾件事，常常都是在跟死線賽跑、勉強趕完，這跟我一開始預期的完全不一樣。
cards.why: 承認自己判斷失準時用 which is not what I was expecting 收尾。它把問題定位在「我的預估錯了」而不是「事情很難」，聽起來是誠實而不是抱怨。
cards.pmNote: 個人產能的估計誤差多半來自沒算平行任務的切換成本。
cards.episode: Leaving big tech to build the #1 technology newsletter | Gergely Orosz (The Pragmatic Engineer)

alts.quote: The last handoff meeting we had, you didn’t share any background customer research, which I failed to flag at the time.
alts.zh: 上次交接會議你沒有分享任何背景使用者研究，而我當下也沒有把這件事提出來。

alts.quote: I definitely don't think it was obvious to everyone, and I can definitely say that because we were given a pretty strict deadline that we needed to launch by and I pushed it out three times.
alts.zh: 我完全不覺得這對所有人來說是顯而易見的，我敢這樣說是因為我們當初拿到一個很硬的上線死線，而我把它往後推了三次。

alts.quote: I've talked to you multiple times about coordinating with your peers and not having them surprised about missed deadlines, and I've talked to you multiple times about keeping your team in the loop on different things.
alts.zh: 關於跟同儕協調、不要讓他們對你錯過死線感到意外，我已經跟你談過很多次；關於讓你的團隊掌握各種進度，我也跟你談過很多次。

cards.quote: I say to the person, “Let’s come up with an arbitrary deadline!” We both know it’s made up, but there’s a weird gravitational pull once you’ve put a date out there.
cards.zh: 我會跟對方說：「我們來訂一個隨便的死線吧！」我們都知道那是編的，但日期一旦放上去，就會有一種奇怪的引力。
cards.why: 明講「這是假的」反而讓它有效。承認任意性，對方就不必花力氣質疑合理性，可以直接把它當成一個共同的推力接受。
cards.pmNote: 重要但不緊急的事需要人造死線；公開承認它是人造的，能避免它被當成正式承諾。
cards.episode: Part 2: Time management techniques that actually work

alts.quote: So find some friend of yours that's like, "I'm tweeting about your podcast on Friday, or I'm going to include you in my newsletter next month." And give yourself an artificial deadline or even a real deadline to just put a stake in the ground.
alts.zh: 去找一個朋友，讓他說「我週五要發推介紹你的 podcast」或「我下個月電子報會提到你」，然後給自己一個人造死線——甚至真的死線——先把樁打下去。

alts.quote: What do you think about us doing an experiment? For the next quarter or two, why don't you let us try running like this? If it goes well, great; if it doesn't, no harm.
alts.zh: 我們來做個實驗你覺得如何？接下來一兩季，讓我們試著用這種方式跑跑看。順利的話很好，不順利也沒損失，我們就退回原本的做法。

alts.quote: the number one mistake is hiring a head of growth, giving them no resources and expecting them to pull rabbit out of their hat.
alts.zh: 最常見的錯誤，就是找了一個成長負責人來，什麼資源都不給，然後期待他變魔術。

cards.quote: It’s important to have the person doing the work pick the deadline so that it’s a date that works for them.
cards.zh: 重要的是讓實際做事的人自己挑那個日期，這樣才會是他做得到的時間。
cards.why: 日期由執行者說出口，承諾才成立。你指定的日期是你的期待，他說出口的日期才是他的承諾——只有後者有心理約束力。
cards.pmNote: 要日期不要自己填空白；問「你覺得什麼時候合理」再談判，達成率比直接指派高。
cards.episode: Part 2: Time management techniques that actually work

alts.quote: Okay. I would like to carve 20% of my time listening and I'm happy to do this work 80% of the time.
alts.zh: 好，我想切出兩成的時間去聽，另外八成的時間我很樂意投入手上的工作。

alts.quote: What do you think about us doing an experiment? For the next quarter or two, why don't you let us try running like this? If it goes well, great; if it doesn't, no harm.
alts.zh: 我們來做個實驗你覺得如何？接下來一兩季，讓我們試著用這種方式跑跑看。順利的話很好，不順利也沒損失，我們就退回原本的做法。

alts.quote: And then I propose a little contingency plan, like hey, if that doesn't work out, here's the rollback plan, here's the maximum impact it will have done in a negative way, which is not going to be too much.
alts.zh: 然後我會提一個小小的備案：如果沒成，這是回滾計畫，這是最壞情況下的負面影響——而且不會太大。

cards.pattern: Provide context on [X], but give each [負責人] full autonomy to handle [新狀況].
cards.quote: Provide context on specific projects, meetings, and other workstreams, but give each DRI full autonomy to handle any new decisions that come up in their area.
cards.zh: 把具體專案、會議跟其他工作流的脈絡交代清楚，但要給每位 DRI 完全的自主權，去處理他們範圍內新冒出來的決定。
cards.why: 交接時 context 給滿、決定權放掉。這句把兩件常被混在一起的事分開：資訊要給，決策不要留在自己手上。
cards.pmNote: 交接文件只寫「怎麼做」會讓代理人卡住；要寫「為什麼這樣做」加上明確的授權範圍。
cards.episode: How to create an exceptional coverage plan for your parental leave

alts.quote: Give yourself two to three months at the minimum, ideally more like six months, to really optimize it back to a good standing where it can potentially outperform.
alts.zh: 至少給自己兩到三個月，最好是六個月，把它優化回到好的水準、甚至超越原本的表現。

alts.quote: I say to the person, “Let’s come up with an arbitrary deadline!” We both know it’s made up, but there’s a weird gravitational pull once you’ve put a date out there.
alts.zh: 我會跟對方說：「我們來訂一個隨便的死線吧！」我們都知道那是編的，但日期一旦放上去，就會有一種奇怪的引力。

alts.quote: So find some friend of yours that's like, "I'm tweeting about your podcast on Friday, or I'm going to include you in my newsletter next month." And give yourself an artificial deadline or even a real deadline to just put a stake in the ground.
alts.zh: 去找一個朋友，讓他說「我週五要發推介紹你的 podcast」或「我下個月電子報會提到你」，然後給自己一個人造死線——甚至真的死線——先把樁打下去。

cards.pattern: Establish clearly how much time you will need, and understand that if you go beyond this deadline, [後果].
cards.quote: When you get the term sheet, you should establish clearly how much time you will need and understand that if you go beyond this deadline, the term sheet could be withdrawn.
cards.zh: 拿到 term sheet 的時候，你應該明確講好你需要多少時間，並且清楚知道超過這個期限，term sheet 是可能被收回的。
cards.why: 談時間要同時談「超過會怎樣」。英文的時間承諾預設帶著後果條款；只講日期不講後果，對方會自己想像一個更嚴厲的版本。
cards.pmNote: 對外承諾期限時把逾期後果寫出來，逼雙方確認這個日期是不是真的可行。
cards.episode: A playbook for fundraising

alts.quote: Instead of saying, "Look, your span of control, you have nine direct reports, you need leverage here. I have a lot of credibility with this side of the product organization. I think we could be doing more if this position existed."
alts.zh: 換成這樣講：「你看你的管理幅度，你手下有九個直屬，你需要有人幫你分擔。我在產品組織這一邊累積了不少信任。我覺得如果有這個職位，我們可以做得更多。」

alts.quote: I love setting a fast pace at the company, but in order to do that with confidence, I need at least one day every week that I'm entirely unplugged.
alts.zh: 我很喜歡替公司設一個快節奏，但要有信心這樣衝，我每週至少需要一天完全斷線。

alts.quote: So find some friend of yours that's like, "I'm tweeting about your podcast on Friday, or I'm going to include you in my newsletter next month." And give yourself an artificial deadline or even a real deadline to just put a stake in the ground.
alts.zh: 去找一個朋友，讓他說「我週五要發推介紹你的 podcast」或「我下個月電子報會提到你」，然後給自己一個人造死線——甚至真的死線——先把樁打下去。

cards.pattern: Our push to them was to [具體改動] to [達成的效果].
cards.quote: And so, our push to them was to add a deadline to help people show up.
cards.zh: 所以我們對他們的建議就是：加一個截止時間，讓人真的會出現。
cards.why: our push to them was to… 把建議講成一個明確立場，而不是「我們有討論到」。這句同時交代了你主張什麼、以及主張要換到什麼。
cards.pmNote: 報告顧問或跨團隊工作時，先講你推的那一件事，再講理由與資料。
cards.episode: Using behavioral science to improve your product | Kristen Berman (Irrational Labs)

alts.quote: I want to make sure I've got air cover from the highest people in the company setting the culture.
alts.zh: 我要確定最高層那些定文化的人會幫我掩護。

alts.quote: I say to the person, “Let’s come up with an arbitrary deadline!” We both know it’s made up, but there’s a weird gravitational pull once you’ve put a date out there.
alts.zh: 我會跟對方說：「我們來訂一個隨便的死線吧！」我們都知道那是編的，但日期一旦放上去，就會有一種奇怪的引力。

alts.quote: So find some friend of yours that's like, "I'm tweeting about your podcast on Friday, or I'm going to include you in my newsletter next month." And give yourself an artificial deadline or even a real deadline to just put a stake in the ground.
alts.zh: 去找一個朋友，讓他說「我週五要發推介紹你的 podcast」或「我下個月電子報會提到你」，然後給自己一個人造死線——甚至真的死線——先把樁打下去。

cards.pattern: Give yourself an artificial deadline … to just put a stake in the ground.
cards.quote: So find some friend of yours that's like, "I'm tweeting about your podcast on Friday, or I'm going to include you in my newsletter next month." And give yourself an artificial deadline or even a real deadline to just put a stake in the ground.
cards.zh: 去找一個朋友，讓他說「我週五要發推介紹你的 podcast」或「我下個月電子報會提到你」，然後給自己一個人造死線——甚至真的死線——先把樁打下去。
cards.why: 求助的內容不是幫忙做事，而是幫忙製造一個對外的日期。put a stake in the ground 是英文裡「先定一個之後還可以再改的點」的固定說法。
cards.pmNote: 拖延的解法是把私人承諾換成公開承諾；找一個會公開提到你的人是最便宜的方式。
cards.episode: Launching and growing a podcast | Chris Hutchins (All the Hacks, Wealthfront, Google)

alts.quote: Give yourself two to three months at the minimum, ideally more like six months, to really optimize it back to a good standing where it can potentially outperform.
alts.zh: 至少給自己兩到三個月，最好是六個月，把它優化回到好的水準、甚至超越原本的表現。

alts.quote: I say to the person, “Let’s come up with an arbitrary deadline!” We both know it’s made up, but there’s a weird gravitational pull once you’ve put a date out there.
alts.zh: 我會跟對方說：「我們來訂一個隨便的死線吧！」我們都知道那是編的，但日期一旦放上去，就會有一種奇怪的引力。

alts.quote: I love setting a fast pace at the company, but in order to do that with confidence, I need at least one day every week that I'm entirely unplugged.
alts.zh: 我很喜歡替公司設一個快節奏，但要有信心這樣衝，我每週至少需要一天完全斷線。

cards.pattern: The biggest mistakes I've made have been [做了什麼] and thinking, I can do this better.
cards.quote: The biggest mistakes I've made have been going into business models where other people have repeatedly failed and thinking, I can do this better.
cards.zh: 我犯過最大的錯，都是跳進那種別人一再失敗的商業模式，然後心想：我可以做得比他們好。
cards.why: 認錯認到「當時腦子裡那句話」為止。把自己的傲慢原句引出來，比講「我判斷失準」具體一百倍，也讓人相信你真的復盤過。
cards.pmNote: 「別人都做不起來但我可以」通常不是洞見，先去查別人失敗的真正原因。
cards.episode: I’ve run 75+ businesses. Here’s why you’re probably chasing the wrong idea. | Andrew Wilkinson (co‑founder of Tiny)

alts.quote: Yeah, I messed up. But I know I'm still a good person and a good worker. Yes, I made a mistake, but I'm going to move on.
alts.zh: 對，我搞砸了。但我知道我還是個好人、也還是個好的工作者。對，我犯了錯，但我要往前走。

alts.quote: And of course at the time I thought this was one of the biggest mistakes in my whole career.
alts.zh: 當然，我當下覺得那是我整個職涯裡最大的錯誤之一。

alts.quote: Someone else is like, "I'd pay $5,000 for those 10 units of value." So, the biggest mistake was a lot of mistakes compounded.
alts.zh: 另一個人會說：「那十個單位的價值我願意付五千美金。」所以最大的錯，其實是很多個小錯疊出來的。

cards.pattern: I had a very strong identity of myself as [身分], and nope, I was wrong.
cards.quote: I had a very strong identity of myself as this AI infrastructure product guy, and I was working in this space and nope, I was wrong.
cards.zh: 我曾經很強烈地認定自己就是那個「做 AI 基礎設施產品的人」，人也真的在這個領域裡——結果呢，我錯了。
cards.why: 錯的不是一個決定，是一整個身分認同。nope 這個口語詞讓沉重的自我否定聽起來乾脆，而不是自憐。
cards.episode: Making Meta | Andrew ‘Boz’ Bosworth (CTO)

alts.quote: Probably for me, I think my time at Instacart was probably not my best time. I think I went to Instacart with a vision of what I felt the product could be, but I was not aware or in tune with what the DNA of the company was.
alts.zh: 對我來說，Instacart 那段大概是我狀態最不好的時候。我帶著一套「產品應該長成什麼樣」的想像進去，卻沒真的看懂那家公司的 DNA 是什麼。

alts.quote: But what can you do, if not look back on it and say, "Yeah, I was wrong.
alts.zh: 那你還能怎麼辦呢？不就是回頭看著它說一句：對，我那時錯了。

alts.quote: With this new information, it was clear to me her team was right and I was wrong.
alts.zh: 有了這個新資訊之後，我很清楚是她的團隊對、我錯了。

cards.quote: And I was wrong by the way.
cards.zh: 順帶一提，我那時是錯的。
cards.why: by the way 把認錯降級成順口一提：不打斷敘事、不索取安慰，但紀錄留下了。台灣人常把認錯做成一個儀式，反而讓對方要花力氣安慰你。
cards.episode: Making Meta | Andrew ‘Boz’ Bosworth (CTO)

alts.quote: I came in thinking I was supposed to behave the way I behaved at Apple, which is very direct, fighting hard.
alts.zh: 我進去的時候以為我該照在 Apple 的那一套來——非常直接、硬碰硬地爭。

alts.quote: I was wrong on the total population.
alts.zh: 我在總人口數那一項判斷錯了。

alts.quote: Then just to admit, "Okay, I was wrong.
alts.zh: 然後就是承認一句：好吧，我錯了。

cards.quote: I failed at tons of stuff.
cards.zh: 我失敗過一堆事。
cards.why: 四個字的資歷宣告。英文職場把「講得出自己失敗過多少」當能力訊號，講得越輕描淡寫，越顯得你站得穩。
cards.episode: Lessons from 1,000+ YC startups: Resilience, tar pit ideas, pivoting, more | Dalton Caldwell (Y Combinator, Managing Director)

alts.quote: I failed year after year trying to make the team, trying to make the boat.
alts.zh: 我年復一年地失敗，一直想擠進校隊、想上那條船。

alts.quote: The biggest mistakes I've made have been going into business models where other people have repeatedly failed and thinking, I can do this better.
alts.zh: 我犯過最大的錯，都是跳進那種別人一再失敗的商業模式，然後心想：我可以做得比他們好。

alts.quote: So what I was doing and what science knows were very different things, and that's why I failed in those cases.
alts.zh: 我當時在做的事，跟科學界已知的事，是兩回事——所以那幾次我才會失敗。

cards.pattern: I was wrong on [具體是哪一項].
cards.quote: I was wrong on the total population.
cards.zh: 我在總人口數那一項判斷錯了。
cards.why: on 後面接的名詞把錯誤縮到單一變數上：承認得乾脆，同時也劃清了沒錯的部分。台灣人習慣整包說「我搞砸了」，等於把對的部分一起丟掉。
cards.pmNote: 覆盤時把錯誤定位到單一假設，模型其他部分才留得下來。
cards.episode: Rethinking SEO in the age of AI | Eli Schwartz (SEO advisor, author)

alts.quote: And I was wrong by the way.
alts.zh: 順帶一提，我那時是錯的。

alts.quote: Here's the way in which I was wrong.
alts.zh: 我來說一下我是哪裡錯了。

alts.quote: Then just to admit, "Okay, I was wrong.
alts.zh: 然後就是承認一句：好吧，我錯了。

cards.pattern: What I was doing and what [權威來源] knows were very different things, and that's why I failed.
cards.quote: So what I was doing and what science knows were very different things, and that's why I failed in those cases.
cards.zh: 我當時在做的事，跟科學界已知的事，是兩回事——所以那幾次我才會失敗。
cards.why: 把失敗接到一個可檢驗的落差上（我做的 vs 已知的），因果就成立了。沒有因果的認錯只是情緒表態。
cards.episode: Improve strategy, influence, and decision-making by understanding your brain | Evan LaPointe (founder of CORE Sciences)

alts.quote: And then the second piece of advice I would give I think we should have been talking to potential acquirers from the beginning and sharing our vision and what we were trying to accomplish because we started those quite late in our journey as a company.
alts.zh: 我要給的第二個建議是：我覺得我們一開始就該去跟潛在的收購方聊，分享我們的願景跟想達成的事。我們啟動得太晚了。

alts.quote: And just owning things ends up being more painful in the short run, but then some painful hours can save painful years.
alts.zh: 把責任認下來，短期一定比較痛；但幾個難熬的小時，可以省下難熬的好幾年。

alts.quote: I got to tell you, I had no idea how unique we were until I was outside and there are so many things.
alts.zh: 我得說，直到我離開之後，我才知道我們當時有多特殊——太多事情都是。

cards.pattern: I have a note called Failure Resume, and I wrote down all the times I failed.
cards.quote: I wrote down, I have a note on my phone called Failure Resume, and I wrote down all the times I failed and it is depressing.
cards.zh: 我手機裡有一則筆記叫「失敗履歷」，我把每次失敗都記下來——看了很沮喪。
cards.why: 用一個具體物件（手機備忘錄的名字）承載失敗，比任何形容詞可信。結尾 it is depressing 沒有硬轉正面，那份不修飾正是可信度來源。
cards.episode: How Shopify builds a high-intensity culture | Farhan Thawar (VP and Head of Eng)

alts.quote: We were like, "You know what? If we had just tested that, we would have all known that this was a super lame badge." And I was like, "Why are we not testing our experiments?"
alts.zh: 我們就說：「欸，我們如果當初有自己測一下，早就知道這個徽章有夠遜。」我就問：「所以我們為什麼沒有在測自己的實驗？」

alts.quote: The biggest mistakes I've made have been going into business models where other people have repeatedly failed and thinking, I can do this better.
alts.zh: 我犯過最大的錯，都是跳進那種別人一再失敗的商業模式，然後心想：我可以做得比他們好。

alts.quote: So what I was doing and what science knows were very different things, and that's why I failed in those cases.
alts.zh: 我當時在做的事，跟科學界已知的事，是兩回事——所以那幾次我才會失敗。

cards.pattern: I failed year after year trying to [目標].
cards.quote: I failed year after year trying to make the team, trying to make the boat.
cards.zh: 我年復一年地失敗，一直想擠進校隊、想上那條船。
cards.why: year after year 把失敗從一次事件變成一段長度，重複的 trying to 讓人聽見那個節奏。這是講失敗最有畫面的方式。
cards.episode: How to break out of autopilot and create the life you want | Graham Weaver (Stanford GSB professor, founder of Alpine Investors)

alts.quote: So I actually ended up not letting the team run this experiment for six months so that we focus on lower hanging fruit. So that's a mistake on my end.
alts.zh: 所以我其實壓著這個實驗六個月沒讓團隊做，因為想先撿低垂的果實。這是我的錯。

alts.quote: I failed at tons of stuff.
alts.zh: 我失敗過一堆事。

alts.quote: And then the second piece of advice I would give I think we should have been talking to potential acquirers from the beginning and sharing our vision and what we were trying to accomplish because we started those quite late in our journey as a company.
alts.zh: 我要給的第二個建議是：我覺得我們一開始就該去跟潛在的收購方聊，分享我們的願景跟想達成的事。我們啟動得太晚了。

cards.quote: And of course at the time I thought this was one of the biggest mistakes in my whole career.
cards.zh: 當然，我當下覺得那是我整個職涯裡最大的錯誤之一。
cards.why: at the time 這三個字把「當時的評價」跟「現在的評價」分開，等於預告後面會翻案。講失敗先標好時間層，故事才有轉折空間。
cards.episode: Jackie Bavaro on getting better at product strategy, what exactly is strategy, PM pitfalls to avoid, advancing your career, getting into management, and much more

alts.quote: The biggest mistakes I've made have been going into business models where other people have repeatedly failed and thinking, I can do this better.
alts.zh: 我犯過最大的錯，都是跳進那種別人一再失敗的商業模式，然後心想：我可以做得比他們好。

alts.quote: Someone else is like, "I'd pay $5,000 for those 10 units of value." So, the biggest mistake was a lot of mistakes compounded.
alts.zh: 另一個人會說：「那十個單位的價值我願意付五千美金。」所以最大的錯，其實是很多個小錯疊出來的。

alts.quote: Probably for me, I think my time at Instacart was probably not my best time. I think I went to Instacart with a vision of what I felt the product could be, but I was not aware or in tune with what the DNA of the company was.
alts.zh: 對我來說，Instacart 那段大概是我狀態最不好的時候。我帶著一套「產品應該長成什麼樣」的想像進去，卻沒真的看懂那家公司的 DNA 是什麼。

cards.pattern: I screwed up [次數], but it still turned out [結果].
cards.quote: But I screwed up twice, but it still turned out pretty good.
cards.zh: 我搞砸了兩次，不過最後結果還是不錯。
cards.why: 壞消息跟結果同一句給完，對方不用懸著。數字（twice）讓認錯有邊界，不會被想像成無限大。
cards.episode: Making time for what matters | Jake Knapp and John Zeratsky (authors of Sprint and Make Time, co-founders of Character Capital)

alts.quote: And sometimes it's okay to just say, "Hey, we screwed up here.
alts.zh: 有時候就直接說「欸，我們這邊搞砸了」，這樣是可以的。

alts.quote: And the good news bad news is that's true. That is absolutely true.
alts.zh: 好消息也是壞消息：那是真的。千真萬確。

alts.quote: Nobody wants to hear it. Everybody wants to just think about these really cool models and how smart they are. But really it's just the hard work of getting really good data to the LLMs.
alts.zh: 沒有人想聽這個。大家都只想談那些很酷的模型有多聰明。但說到底，這就是把好資料餵給 LLM 的苦工。

cards.quote: And sometimes it's okay to just say, "Hey, we screwed up here.
cards.zh: 有時候就直接說「欸，我們這邊搞砸了」，這樣是可以的。
cards.why: 用 we 不用 I，是團隊層級的認錯；here 把範圍釘在一個點上。講完就停、不接解釋——解釋等對方問。
cards.pmNote: 對客戶或跨部門認錯，第一段只講事實與範圍，原因與補救分到第二段。
cards.episode: Jeetu Patel

alts.quote: In those stages, the experience can be a little janky or it's not that polished, but we're okay with it because we are saying, "It's not finished. We just want to get your feedback early so we can make it better."
alts.zh: 那個階段體驗可能有點卡、不太精緻，但我們可以接受，因為我們有先講清楚：「這還沒完成，我們只是想早點拿到你的回饋，好把它做得更好。」

alts.quote: But I screwed up twice, but it still turned out pretty good.
alts.zh: 我搞砸了兩次，不過最後結果還是不錯。

alts.quote: It's so hard to give a founder hard feedback. Who wants to be the bearer of bad news?
alts.zh: 要給創辦人難聽的回饋真的很難。誰想當那個報壞消息的人？

cards.quote: Here's the way in which I was wrong.
cards.zh: 我來說一下我是哪裡錯了。
cards.why: 認錯之後最關鍵的一句：不是再道歉一次，是準備交出錯誤的結構。英文職場真正給分的，是這句後面接的內容。
cards.episode: Moving fast and navigating uncertainty | Jeremy Henrickson (Rippling, Coinbase)

alts.quote: I came in thinking I was supposed to behave the way I behaved at Apple, which is very direct, fighting hard.
alts.zh: 我進去的時候以為我該照在 Apple 的那一套來——非常直接、硬碰硬地爭。

alts.quote: And so maybe I picked the wrong term in calling it growth hacking, but I think it at least opened the conversation to getting more people thinking about growth in a different way.
alts.zh: 所以也許我當初取 growth hacking 這個名字是取錯了，但至少它打開了對話，讓更多人開始用不同的方式想成長這件事。

alts.quote: I was wrong on the total population.
alts.zh: 我在總人口數那一項判斷錯了。

cards.quote: You're just coming into this journey and you should be humble and you should be learning and you should be saying, "Oops, I screwed up over here." And that's okay.
cards.zh: 你才剛踏上這條路，本來就該保持謙虛、持續學，而且該說得出「唉呀，我這邊搞砸了」——那是沒關係的。
cards.why: Oops 這個字把認錯的重量調到日常等級。And that's okay 是說給團隊聽的許可證，讓認錯變成組織允許的行為，而不是個人風險。
cards.episode: Manik Gupta (ex-CPO Uber, Google Maps) on how to build consumer apps, why it’s useful to be optimistic about technology, creating inflections in your PM career, the changing CPO role, and more

alts.quote: And then the second piece of advice I would give I think we should have been talking to potential acquirers from the beginning and sharing our vision and what we were trying to accomplish because we started those quite late in our journey as a company.
alts.zh: 我要給的第二個建議是：我覺得我們一開始就該去跟潛在的收購方聊，分享我們的願景跟想達成的事。我們啟動得太晚了。

alts.quote: And I'll tell you, ProfitWell, this was a big mistake. Yes, it was a great exit, we sold for over $200 million, et cetera, but we probably, if we had taken money, we could have had a billion-dollar exit
alts.zh: 老實說 ProfitWell 這件事是個大失誤。是啦，出場很漂亮，賣了兩億多美元，但如果我們當初有拿錢，可能會是十億等級的出場。

alts.quote: So what I was doing and what science knows were very different things, and that's why I failed in those cases.
alts.zh: 我當時在做的事，跟科學界已知的事，是兩回事——所以那幾次我才會失敗。

cards.pattern: People loved it, but it was too [問題], and so we failed.
cards.quote: People loved it, but it was too ambitious and so we failed.
cards.zh: 大家很喜歡它，但我們做得太貪心了，所以失敗了。
cards.why: 好消息在前、壞消息在後，而且失敗歸因到自己的野心，不是市場或使用者。台灣人習慣反過來歸因外部，英文聽起來就像在找藉口。
cards.pmNote: 「使用者喜歡但我們還是死了」通常是範圍問題，不是需求問題。
cards.episode: The hidden pattern behind successful products | Mark Pincus (Founder of Zynga)

alts.quote: These are reaching millions of people, their websites get many, many, many millions of unique visitors each month. That does not mean that your story is going to be read by millions of people.
alts.zh: 這些媒體確實觸及上百萬人，網站每個月幾百萬不重複訪客。但這不代表你那篇報導會被上百萬人看到。

alts.quote: Hopefully I'm not making this sound too daunting. I'm just really trying to lay out all the mistakes I've made.
alts.zh: 希望我沒有把這件事講得太嚇人。我只是想把我自己踩過的坑全部攤出來。

alts.quote: I would be honest with people and say some patience is required. However, there is a lot you can do. A lot is in your control.
alts.zh: 我會誠實地說：這需要一點耐心。不過，你能做的事很多，很多都在你的掌控裡。

cards.quote: But what can you do, if not look back on it and say, "Yeah, I was wrong.
cards.zh: 那你還能怎麼辦呢？不就是回頭看著它說一句：對，我那時錯了。
cards.why: 用反問把認錯講成唯一合理的選項，聽的人不會覺得你在自責，而會覺得你在講常識。
cards.episode: The one question that saves product careers | Matt LeMay

alts.quote: Yeah, I messed up. But I know I'm still a good person and a good worker. Yes, I made a mistake, but I'm going to move on.
alts.zh: 對，我搞砸了。但我知道我還是個好人、也還是個好的工作者。對，我犯了錯，但我要往前走。

alts.quote: I don't want them to leave it at, "It was a big loss." You want to say, "What I learned from that is now I always run a load test, and I've had many successful launches since then."
alts.zh: 我不希望他只停在「那是一次很大的損失」。你應該說：我從那件事學到，現在我一定會先跑壓力測試，後來的好幾次上線都沒再出過同樣的問題。

alts.quote: I had a very strong identity of myself as this AI infrastructure product guy, and I was working in this space and nope, I was wrong.
alts.zh: 我曾經很強烈地認定自己就是那個「做 AI 基礎設施產品的人」，人也真的在這個領域裡——結果呢，我錯了。

cards.quote: Someone else is like, "I'd pay $5,000 for those 10 units of value." So, the biggest mistake was a lot of mistakes compounded.
cards.zh: 另一個人會說：「那十個單位的價值我願意付五千美金。」所以最大的錯，其實是很多個小錯疊出來的。
cards.why: 拒絕把失敗簡化成單一原因。compounded 暗示錯誤是複利，越晚發現越貴——比「我判斷錯了」多帶了一個機制。
cards.episode: What AI means for your product strategy | Paul Adams (CPO of Intercom)

alts.quote: The biggest mistakes I've made have been going into business models where other people have repeatedly failed and thinking, I can do this better.
alts.zh: 我犯過最大的錯，都是跳進那種別人一再失敗的商業模式，然後心想：我可以做得比他們好。

alts.quote: And of course at the time I thought this was one of the biggest mistakes in my whole career.
alts.zh: 當然，我當下覺得那是我整個職涯裡最大的錯誤之一。

alts.quote: Yeah, I messed up. But I know I'm still a good person and a good worker. Yes, I made a mistake, but I'm going to move on.
alts.zh: 對，我搞砸了。但我知道我還是個好人、也還是個好的工作者。對，我犯了錯，但我要往前走。

cards.pattern: And so I failed [某個人].
cards.quote: Next question." And so I failed him.
cards.zh: 「下一題。」——所以我等於辜負了他。
cards.why: fail 後面直接接人，講的不是任務失敗而是辜負一個人。英文裡這是最重的一種認錯，因為承認的是關係上的責任。
cards.episode: How to be more innovative | Sam Schillace (Microsoft deputy CTO, creator of Google Docs)

alts.quote: The biggest mistakes I've made have been going into business models where other people have repeatedly failed and thinking, I can do this better.
alts.zh: 我犯過最大的錯，都是跳進那種別人一再失敗的商業模式，然後心想：我可以做得比他們好。

alts.quote: So what I was doing and what science knows were very different things, and that's why I failed in those cases.
alts.zh: 我當時在做的事，跟科學界已知的事，是兩回事——所以那幾次我才會失敗。

alts.quote: I wrote down, I have a note on my phone called Failure Resume, and I wrote down all the times I failed and it is depressing.
alts.zh: 我手機裡有一則筆記叫「失敗履歷」，我把每次失敗都記下來——看了很沮喪。

cards.quote: Then just to admit, "Okay, I was wrong.
cards.zh: 然後就是承認一句：好吧，我錯了。
cards.why: just 把認錯降到「只是一個小動作」的等級。英文常用 just 卸掉一件事的心理重量，讓它變成可以隨手做的事。
cards.episode: Slack founder: Mental models for building products people love ft. Stewart Butterfield

alts.quote: And guess what? It's all okay. It's not a loss, it's a lesson.
alts.zh: 然後你知道嗎？那都沒關係。那不是損失，那是一課。

alts.quote: And I was wrong by the way.
alts.zh: 順帶一提，我那時是錯的。

alts.quote: I was wrong on the total population.
alts.zh: 我在總人口數那一項判斷錯了。

cards.pattern: I failed for somewhere between [X] and [Y] years before getting to this point.
cards.quote: I failed for, I don't know, somewhere between 10 and 15 years before getting to this point.
cards.zh: 我大概失敗了……我也不確定，十到十五年吧，才走到現在這一步。
cards.why: 給失敗一個模糊但很長的區間，反而比精確數字更真——真的失敗很久的人本來就記不清是從哪一年開始的。
cards.episode: OpenAI Codex lead on the new shape of product work | Andrew Ambrosino

alts.quote: Yeah, I messed up. But I know I'm still a good person and a good worker. Yes, I made a mistake, but I'm going to move on.
alts.zh: 對，我搞砸了。但我知道我還是個好人、也還是個好的工作者。對，我犯了錯，但我要往前走。

alts.quote: I don't want them to leave it at, "It was a big loss." You want to say, "What I learned from that is now I always run a load test, and I've had many successful launches since then."
alts.zh: 我不希望他只停在「那是一次很大的損失」。你應該說：我從那件事學到，現在我一定會先跑壓力測試，後來的好幾次上線都沒再出過同樣的問題。

alts.quote: So it's someone that as a leader, you are in the hot seat and you can take accountability. So if some of these things don't pan out, it's on you and not on your team, and give your team permission to fail.
alts.zh: 身為領導者，你就是坐在火線上、要負起責任的人。如果這些事沒成，那是你的責任，不是團隊的責任——同時給團隊失敗的許可。

cards.pattern: With this new information, it was clear to me [對方] was right and I was wrong.
cards.quote: With this new information, it was clear to me her team was right and I was wrong.
cards.zh: 有了這個新資訊之後，我很清楚是她的團隊對、我錯了。
cards.why: 把認錯綁在「新資訊」上：不是我當初笨，是條件變了。書面體最安全的收回方式，同時把功勞明確給出去。
cards.episode: Autonomy vs. direction - Issue 35

alts.quote: So it's someone that as a leader, you are in the hot seat and you can take accountability. So if some of these things don't pan out, it's on you and not on your team, and give your team permission to fail.
alts.zh: 身為領導者，你就是坐在火線上、要負起責任的人。如果這些事沒成，那是你的責任，不是團隊的責任——同時給團隊失敗的許可。

alts.quote: I had a very strong identity of myself as this AI infrastructure product guy, and I was working in this space and nope, I was wrong.
alts.zh: 我曾經很強烈地認定自己就是那個「做 AI 基礎設施產品的人」，人也真的在這個領域裡——結果呢，我錯了。

alts.quote: But what can you do, if not look back on it and say, "Yeah, I was wrong.
alts.zh: 那你還能怎麼辦呢？不就是回頭看著它說一句：對，我那時錯了。

cards.pattern: [具體事實], which I failed to flag at the time.
cards.quote: The last handoff meeting we had, you didn’t share any background customer research, which I failed to flag at the time.
cards.zh: 上次交接會議你沒有分享任何背景使用者研究，而我當下也沒有把這件事提出來。
cards.why: 給別人負面回饋的同一句裡，先認下自己那一份漏失。which I failed to… 讓對方不必先防守，接下來的對話才會是問題導向而不是攻防。
cards.pmNote: 回饋要綁在具體會議與具體缺件上，不要綁在「你總是」。
cards.episode: Introducing the GAIN framework for feedback: an evidence-based approach to giving feedback that people love, appreciate, and act on

alts.quote: Look, we haven't shipped any. Last three years, the only thing our customers have really meaningfully seen from our product is a price increase. What the hell are we doing?
alts.zh: 你看，我們什麼都沒出。過去三年，客戶從我們產品上真正感受到的只有一件事：漲價。我們到底在幹嘛？

alts.quote: So I was working on parallel things at the same time, and I was often running against the deadline, I was barely finishing it, which is not what I was expecting initially.
alts.zh: 所以我同時在做好幾件事，常常都是在跟死線賽跑、勉強趕完，這跟我一開始預期的完全不一樣。

alts.quote: I'm just going to bump you up to the 100-video plan. Let me know if you have any questions.
alts.zh: 我就直接幫你升到 100 支影片的方案囉。有問題再跟我說。

cards.pattern: I used to think it was [A] versus [B], but now I realize they [新關係].
cards.quote: Yeah, I used to think it was versus, but now I realize that they combine really well.
cards.zh: 對，我以前覺得這兩個是互斥的，但現在我發現它們其實搭得很好。
cards.why: 收回立場最短的完整結構：舊判斷＋轉折＋新判斷，一句講完。台灣人常只講新結論，聽的人不知道你其實走過舊的那條路。
cards.pmNote: 「A vs B」的框架本身常是假二選一；發現兩者能疊加，通常就是策略的轉折點。
cards.episode: How to find hidden growth opportunities in your product | Albert Cheng (Duolingo, Grammarly, Chess.com)

alts.quote: Which is I used to think something and then some stuff happened and now I think a new thing.
alts.zh: 就是：我以前這樣想，後來發生了一些事，現在我改成那樣想。

alts.quote: And I used to think leadership was the same, which is, well, it's not about you as a leader, it's about who are you bringing along on your journey?
alts.zh: 我以前也以為領導力是同一回事——就是說，重點不在你這個領導者身上，而在你把誰一起帶上路。

alts.quote: Four or five years ago, I would've said, well, personal skills, nothing. It's all the environment. I used to be one of those particular people.
alts.zh: 四五年前我會說：個人能力根本不重要，全都是環境造成的。我以前就是那一派的人。

cards.pattern: I used to think I was [自我評價].
cards.quote: I used to think I was very curious, and I'm a learner and I'll seek out information.
cards.zh: 我以前覺得自己很有好奇心，是那種會主動去找資料、愛學習的人。
cards.why: 把「我以前對自己的認知」也當成可以收回的立場——不是收回一個主張，是收回一張自我標籤。這比認錯更難，也更有份量。
cards.episode: Lessons from scaling Stripe | Claire Hughes Johnson (former COO of Stripe)

alts.quote: Yeah, I used to think it was versus, but now I realize that they combine really well.
alts.zh: 對，我以前覺得這兩個是互斥的，但現在我發現它們其實搭得很好。

alts.quote: Which is I used to think something and then some stuff happened and now I think a new thing.
alts.zh: 就是：我以前這樣想，後來發生了一些事，現在我改成那樣想。

alts.quote: When I was younger and I was starting off, I used to think it's all about the product.
alts.zh: 我年輕、剛入行的時候，以為一切就是產品而已。

cards.pattern: I used to think [X] was [舊定義], which is [把舊定義攤開].
cards.quote: And I used to think leadership was the same, which is, well, it's not about you as a leader, it's about who are you bringing along on your journey?
cards.zh: 我以前也以為領導力是同一回事——就是說，重點不在你這個領導者身上，而在你把誰一起帶上路。
cards.why: 講完舊立場後用 which is 把它攤開，聽的人才知道你要收回的到底是哪一塊。只講「我以前想錯了」沒有資訊量。
cards.episode: How to discover your superpowers, own your story, and unlock personal growth | Donna Lichaw (author of The Leader’s Journey)

alts.quote: I used to think my insecurity was a downfall and I would just hide it and try to pretend it's not there.
alts.zh: 我以前覺得自己的不安全感是個致命傷，就一直把它藏起來，假裝它不存在。

alts.quote: Four or five years ago, I would've said, well, personal skills, nothing. It's all the environment. I used to be one of those particular people.
alts.zh: 四五年前我會說：個人能力根本不重要，全都是環境造成的。我以前就是那一派的人。

alts.quote: Yeah, I used to think it was versus, but now I realize that they combine really well.
alts.zh: 對，我以前覺得這兩個是互斥的，但現在我發現它們其實搭得很好。

cards.pattern: That's the biggest 180 I've changed my mind on, but I change my mind all the time.
cards.quote: I think that's the biggest major fundamental 180 degree change that I've changed my mind on, but I changed my mind all the time.
cards.zh: 那大概是我立場整個一百八十度翻過來、最大的一次改變，不過我本來就一天到晚在改想法。
cards.why: 先把這次改變標成「最大的一次」給它份量，再補一句「我一直在改」解除防衛，讓改變想法看起來是習慣而不是意外。
cards.episode: Jason Fried challenges your thinking on fundraising, goals, growth, and more

alts.quote: I agree, I've changed my mind. You're right. You just saw it in a way that I hadn't seen.
alts.zh: 我同意，我改變想法了。你是對的，你看到的角度是我原本沒看到的。

alts.quote: By the way, I will say on the Peter one, I've come much more around to Peter's point of view. I would probably argue that one quite a bit differently today than I did, and I would give his view, I think, a lot more credit.
alts.zh: 順帶一提，Peter 那場辯論，我現在比較站到他那邊了。同樣的題目今天要我講，我會講得很不一樣，也會給他的看法多很多分數。

alts.quote: No, I mean I've shared that enough, but I used to not talk about it before because I used to think that I would get some sympathy for that.
alts.zh: 不會，這件事我講得夠多了。不過我以前不太提，因為我當時覺得講了會被同情。

cards.pattern: I've since [轉向]. I used to [舊做法], and now [新做法].
cards.quote: And then I've since gone, I used to do a lot of interviews at startup school on stage with people, and now the podcast.
cards.zh: 後來我就轉了——我以前常在 Startup School 的台上跟人做訪談，現在改成 podcast。
cards.why: I've since… 是英文裡最輕的轉向詞，不帶懊悔也不用解釋，適合講「我換做法了」而不是「我以前錯了」。
cards.episode: The social radar: Y Combinator’s secret weapon | Jessica Livingston (co-founder of Y Combinator, author, podcast host)

alts.quote: Four or five years ago, I would've said, well, personal skills, nothing. It's all the environment. I used to be one of those particular people.
alts.zh: 四五年前我會說：個人能力根本不重要，全都是環境造成的。我以前就是那一派的人。

alts.quote: Yeah, I used to think it was versus, but now I realize that they combine really well.
alts.zh: 對，我以前覺得這兩個是互斥的，但現在我發現它們其實搭得很好。

alts.quote: Which is I used to think something and then some stuff happened and now I think a new thing.
alts.zh: 就是：我以前這樣想，後來發生了一些事，現在我改成那樣想。

cards.pattern: I used to not talk about it, because I used to think [當初的動機].
cards.quote: No, I mean I've shared that enough, but I used to not talk about it before because I used to think that I would get some sympathy for that.
cards.zh: 不會，這件事我講得夠多了。不過我以前不太提，因為我當時覺得講了會被同情。
cards.why: 收回的是「當初為什麼不講」的動機，等於把自己的心理計算攤在桌上。英文職場把這種動機層級的坦白視為高可信度訊號。
cards.episode: Kunal Shah on winning in India, second-order thinking, the philosophy of startups, and more

alts.quote: Which is I used to think something and then some stuff happened and now I think a new thing.
alts.zh: 就是：我以前這樣想，後來發生了一些事，現在我改成那樣想。

alts.quote: By the way, I will say on the Peter one, I've come much more around to Peter's point of view. I would probably argue that one quite a bit differently today than I did, and I would give his view, I think, a lot more credit.
alts.zh: 順帶一提，Peter 那場辯論，我現在比較站到他那邊了。同樣的題目今天要我講，我會講得很不一樣，也會給他的看法多很多分數。

alts.quote: And I used to think leadership was the same, which is, well, it's not about you as a leader, it's about who are you bringing along on your journey?
alts.zh: 我以前也以為領導力是同一回事——就是說，重點不在你這個領導者身上，而在你把誰一起帶上路。

cards.pattern: I used to think [X], then [發生了什麼], and now I think [Y].
cards.quote: Which is I used to think something and then some stuff happened and now I think a new thing.
cards.zh: 就是：我以前這樣想，後來發生了一些事，現在我改成那樣想。
cards.why: 這是「改變想法」的最小骨架——舊想法、觸發事件、新想法。缺了中間那段就只是翻供；有了它才叫推理。
cards.pmNote: 對主管改口徑時，中間那段（發生了什麼）才是他真正要的東西。
cards.episode: How to tell better stories | Matthew Dicks (Storyworthy)

alts.quote: Yeah, I used to think it was versus, but now I realize that they combine really well.
alts.zh: 對，我以前覺得這兩個是互斥的，但現在我發現它們其實搭得很好。

alts.quote: And I used to think leadership was the same, which is, well, it's not about you as a leader, it's about who are you bringing along on your journey?
alts.zh: 我以前也以為領導力是同一回事——就是說，重點不在你這個領導者身上，而在你把誰一起帶上路。

alts.quote: No, I mean I've shared that enough, but I used to not talk about it before because I used to think that I would get some sympathy for that.
alts.zh: 不會，這件事我講得夠多了。不過我以前不太提，因為我當時覺得講了會被同情。

cards.pattern: I used to think [我的某個特質] was [缺點], and I would just [當初的隱藏行為].
cards.quote: I used to think my insecurity was a downfall and I would just hide it and try to pretend it's not there.
cards.zh: 我以前覺得自己的不安全感是個致命傷，就一直把它藏起來，假裝它不存在。
cards.why: 不只講舊想法，還講舊想法讓自己做了什麼（藏、裝沒事）。行為細節讓收回立場變得可信，否則聽起來像場面話。
cards.episode: An inside look at Deel’s unprecedented growth | Meltem Kuran Berkowitz (Head of Growth)

alts.quote: And I used to think leadership was the same, which is, well, it's not about you as a leader, it's about who are you bringing along on your journey?
alts.zh: 我以前也以為領導力是同一回事——就是說，重點不在你這個領導者身上，而在你把誰一起帶上路。

alts.quote: When I was younger and I was starting off, I used to think it's all about the product.
alts.zh: 我年輕、剛入行的時候，以為一切就是產品而已。

alts.quote: No, I mean I've shared that enough, but I used to not talk about it before because I used to think that I would get some sympathy for that.
alts.zh: 不會，這件事我講得夠多了。不過我以前不太提，因為我當時覺得講了會被同情。

cards.pattern: What I have come to believe — and this differs from what I used to believe — is [新立場].
cards.quote: But what I have come to believe and this differs from what I used to believe is especially if you're working in a big company, you are one of the many thousands of employees in there.
cards.zh: 但我後來相信的事——這跟我以前相信的不一樣——是：如果你在大公司，你就只是那幾千個員工裡的一個。
cards.why: 把「我改變過」做成插入句塞在主張中間，重點仍落在新主張上。適合會議上改口徑：既標記了轉變，又不讓整段變成道歉。
cards.episode: Hot takes and techno-optimism from tech’s top power couple | Sriram and Aarthi

alts.quote: It's this weird tightrope where you're pushing for a future that you believe is true, but all the while you're getting new information. You need to kill the beliefs that you had.
alts.zh: 這是一條很怪的鋼索：你一邊在推動一個你相信會成真的未來，一邊又不斷收到新資訊。你得親手殺掉自己原本的信念。

alts.quote: If you had asked me when I first started the company, it would've been an enthusiastic hell yes. I totally recommend. Now, I have a couple asterisks on top of it.
alts.zh: 如果你在我剛創業的時候問我，答案會是超級肯定的「絕對推薦」。現在的話，我會加上幾個但書。

alts.quote: By the way, I will say on the Peter one, I've come much more around to Peter's point of view. I would probably argue that one quite a bit differently today than I did, and I would give his view, I think, a lot more credit.
alts.zh: 順帶一提，Peter 那場辯論，我現在比較站到他那邊了。同樣的題目今天要我講，我會講得很不一樣，也會給他的看法多很多分數。

cards.pattern: When I was [人生階段], I used to think it's all about [X].
cards.quote: When I was younger and I was starting off, I used to think it's all about the product.
cards.zh: 我年輕、剛入行的時候，以為一切就是產品而已。
cards.why: 先給時間定錨再講舊想法，等於幫舊想法找到合理的位置——那個階段會這樣想是正常的。這讓收回立場不傷自己的專業形象。
cards.episode: A framework for PM skill development | Vikrama Dhiman (Gojek)

alts.quote: Four or five years ago, I would've said, well, personal skills, nothing. It's all the environment. I used to be one of those particular people.
alts.zh: 四五年前我會說：個人能力根本不重要，全都是環境造成的。我以前就是那一派的人。

alts.quote: And I used to think leadership was the same, which is, well, it's not about you as a leader, it's about who are you bringing along on your journey?
alts.zh: 我以前也以為領導力是同一回事——就是說，重點不在你這個領導者身上，而在你把誰一起帶上路。

alts.quote: I used to think my insecurity was a downfall and I would just hide it and try to pretend it's not there.
alts.zh: 我以前覺得自己的不安全感是個致命傷，就一直把它藏起來，假裝它不存在。

cards.pattern: Telling someone "I no longer need you to [X]" makes them nervous.
cards.quote: Change is constant, but telling someone, "I no longer need you to do that," it makes them a little bit nervous.
cards.zh: 變動是常態，但跟一個人說「我不再需要你做那件事了」，還是會讓他有點不安。
cards.why: 先承認改變決定會踩到人，再去講怎麼講。英文職場改口徑時通常先處理對方的感受，才處理事實。
cards.pmNote: 撤掉別人的工作範圍等於動到他的安全感；改 scope 先講「為什麼改」再講「改成什麼」。
cards.episode: Understanding the role of product ops | Christine Itwaru (Pendo)

alts.quote: By the way, I will say on the Peter one, I've come much more around to Peter's point of view. I would probably argue that one quite a bit differently today than I did, and I would give his view, I think, a lot more credit.
alts.zh: 順帶一提，Peter 那場辯論，我現在比較站到他那邊了。同樣的題目今天要我講，我會講得很不一樣，也會給他的看法多很多分數。

alts.quote: I think that's the biggest major fundamental 180 degree change that I've changed my mind on, but I changed my mind all the time.
alts.zh: 那大概是我立場整個一百八十度翻過來、最大的一次改變，不過我本來就一天到晚在改想法。

alts.quote: But I no longer have to provide the first-round feedback I once did, since the draft has already undergone several rounds of what are essentially my suggestions before I even touch it.
alts.zh: 但我已經不必再給以前那種第一輪回饋了，因為草稿在我碰到之前，已經跑過好幾輪等同我意見的修改。

cards.pattern: I no longer have to [舊工作], since [前提已經改變].
cards.quote: But I no longer have to provide the first-round feedback I once did, since the draft has already undergone several rounds of what are essentially my suggestions before I even touch it.
cards.zh: 但我已經不必再給以前那種第一輪回饋了，因為草稿在我碰到之前，已經跑過好幾輪等同我意見的修改。
cards.why: 書面體的收回：不講「我想法變了」，講「前提變了所以我的工作變了」。把改變歸因於環境，不是歸因於自己判斷失準。
cards.episode: How to become a supermanager with AI

alts.quote: Even if I don't agree with the feedback, what is the insight that I'm missing? How am I wrong about this? What would be true for this other person to be right?
alts.zh: 就算我不同意那個回饋，我也會問：我漏掉了什麼洞見？我哪裡想錯了？要怎麼樣，對方才會是對的？

alts.quote: If you had asked me when I first started the company, it would've been an enthusiastic hell yes. I totally recommend. Now, I have a couple asterisks on top of it.
alts.zh: 如果你在我剛創業的時候問我，答案會是超級肯定的「絕對推薦」。現在的話，我會加上幾個但書。

alts.quote: And it stunned me into silence because essentially that is and was SEO, and then that forced me to really pivot my thinking around what SEO might be.
alts.zh: 那句話讓我當場說不出話，因為 SEO 本來、現在也確實就是那樣。也就是那一刻逼我重新想：SEO 到底可以是什麼。

cards.pattern: Unless I'm [某個身分], I'm not the right person to ask.
cards.quote: Is this positioning good or not?" And the problem with B2B tech companies is, well, unless I'm your buyer, I'm not the right person to ask.
cards.zh: 「這個定位到底好不好？」B2B 科技公司的問題在於——除非我就是你的買家，不然我根本不是該問的那個人。
cards.why: 拒絕的不是問題，是自己的資格。指出「該問誰」比含糊給意見更有價值，也把對話推去對的人身上。
cards.pmNote: 定位的唯一評審是買家，不是同事、也不是投資人。
cards.episode: April Dunford on product positioning, segmentation, and optimizing your sales process

alts.quote: I don't understand what this is, and I'm not the right person for this role," and it turned out, nobody understood exactly what was going on.
alts.zh: 「我看不懂這是什麼，我也不是這個職位該找的人」——結果發現，根本沒有人真的搞懂在發生什麼事。

alts.quote: You should have 30 seconds for your play. Right? Don't ask me, I'm not a lawyer.
alts.zh: 應該有個三十秒的合理使用吧？別問我，我又不是律師。

alts.quote: My purely anecdotal guess is maybe 10 to 15% are good product companies, something like that.
alts.zh: 我純粹憑印象猜，大概一成到一成五算是好的產品公司吧，差不多這個量級。

cards.pattern: But what I can do is [我能給的那一件事].
cards.quote: But what I can do is I can give you one wish.
cards.zh: 但我能做的是——我可以給你一個願望。
cards.why: But what I can do is… 是英文把「不能」翻成「能」的轉軸。先劃界線再馬上給替代品，對方就不會停在被拒絕的感覺上。
cards.episode: How to break out of autopilot and create the life you want | Graham Weaver (Stanford GSB professor, founder of Alpine Investors)

alts.quote: I mean, look, there is literally no magic answer to that. I wish that there was, but there is not. There's no format.
alts.zh: 老實說，這題沒有什麼神奇答案。我也希望有，但就是沒有。也沒有什麼固定格式。

alts.quote: Yes, so I am biased. I think they should have the right people give them advice on SEO.
alts.zh: 對，我確實有利益關係。但我還是覺得他們應該找對的人來給 SEO 建議。

alts.quote: So I'll give you a contention and a plausible way we get there, but as for how it happens, who knows?
alts.zh: 我可以給你一個主張，還有一條看起來說得通的路徑，但實際上會怎麼發生，誰知道。

cards.pattern: I can't speak to [X] because I'm not allowed to, but [我還能給的].
cards.quote: So I can't speak to specific clients because I'm not allowed to talk about the work that we've done in large part, but that would be one example.
cards.zh: 我沒辦法談具體的客戶，因為我們做過的案子大部分不能講，但那會是一個例子。
cards.why: 把「不能講」明確歸因於保密義務而不是自己不想講，對方就不會覺得被防。結尾仍丟出一點東西，不讓話題死掉。
cards.episode: Mastering paid growth | Jonathan Becker (Thrive Digital)

alts.quote: I can't speak to that whole period. But what I can tell you about what I'm feeling now is just an incredible sense of focus and urgency to deliver great products quickly.
alts.zh: 那一整段期間我沒辦法評論。但我可以告訴你現在的感受——一種非常強烈的專注感和急迫感，就是要快點把好產品交出去。

alts.quote: I don't know if I want to highlight any specific categories, but I can talk about some of the things that we've funded in the past that has real legs.
alts.zh: 我不確定我想特別點名哪些類別，但我可以聊聊我們過去投過、確實有搞頭的一些東西。
